Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 2 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the next verses of Sūrat l-Baqarah. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 2:81: 81- Yes is proof of what they denied about the Fire touching them for a long time and a long age in a more general way, to be like proof of the invalidity of their statement, and it is specific to the answer to the denial whoever earns a bad deed ugly, and the difference between it and sin is that it may be said in what is intended by the self, and sin is predominant in what is intended by the accident because it is from error, and earning is: bringing benefit. And its connection to the bad is in the manner of his saying: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment. "And his sin encompassed him" means it took control of him and encompassed all of his conditions until he became as if he was surrounded by it, with nothing of his aspects being free from it. This is only true in the case of the disbeliever because even if someone else has nothing but the belief of his heart and the admission of his tongue, the sin does not encompass him. That is why the early Muslims interpreted it as disbelief. The realization of that is that whoever commits a sin and does not desist from it, it will drag him to repeat the same sin and become immersed in it and commit what is greater than it, until the sins take control of him and take hold of his heart, so he becomes naturally inclined towards sins, approving of them and believing that there is no pleasure other than them, hating those who prevent him from them and denying those who advise him in them, as God the Most High said: "Then the end of those who did evil was the worst, because they denied the signs of God. Nafi' read his sins. It was read his sins" with the heart and assimilation in both. Then those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein in the Hereafter, just as they abide therein in its causes in this world. They will abide therein eternally, permanently, or they will remain there for a long time. As you can see, the verse does not contain any proof that the person who commits a major sin will abide eternally, nor does the one before it.
2:82: 82- And those who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally. It is the custom of God Almighty to follow up His promise with His threat, so that His mercy may be hoped for and His punishment may be feared. The conjunction of deeds with faith indicates that it is outside its meaning.
2:83: 83- "And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel, 'You shall not worship except God.'" This is a statement in the sense of a prohibition, as in the Almighty's saying: "And let no scribe or witness be harmed." It is more eloquent than an explicit prohibition, because it implies that the one being prohibited hastened to end, so it is a statement about it, and it is supported by the reading: Do not worship. And the conjunction of "say" to it is in the sense of saying: And it was said: Its meaning is that they should not worship, so when it was deleted, it was raised, as in His saying: Oh, you who deter, I attend the battle and witness the pleasures. Are you immortal? It is indicated by the reading: that you shall not worship, so it is a substitute for the covenant, or an object of it by deleting the preposition. It was said that it is the answer to an oath indicated by the meaning, as if he said: And We made them swear that they would not worship. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, Abu ‘Amr, ‘Asim, and Ya’qub read it with a ta’, narrating what they were addressed with, and the rest with a ya’ because they are absent. And to parents, good treatment is related to an implied word, which is: And you do good, or do good. “And relatives, orphans, and the needy” is in apposition to parents. And orphans is the plural of orphan, like friend and companion, and it is rare. Miskin is a passive participle from sukoon, as if poverty silenced it. And say to the people good meaning a good word, and he called it good for emphasis. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read Hasan with two fathahs. "Hasan is read with two dhammahs, which is the language of the people of Hijaz, and Husna is on the source like Bushra", and what is meant by it is what is in it is good manners and guidance. "And establish prayer and give zakat" meaning by them what was imposed on them in their religion. "Then you turned away" in the manner of turning away, and perhaps the address is to those of them who were present during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and before them in the manner of turning away, meaning you turned away from the covenant and rejected it. "Except a few of you" meaning by it those who established Judaism in its original form before the abrogation, and those of them who converted to Islam. "And you are turning away" people whose habit is turning away from loyalty and obedience. The origin of turning away is going from confrontation to the direction of display.
2:84: 84- "And when We took your covenant, you shall not shed your blood nor expel yourselves from your homes" in the manner previously mentioned, and what is meant by it is that some of them shall not attack each other by killing or expelling one another from their homeland. Rather, He made killing another man killing himself, because of his connection to him by lineage or religion, or because it requires retaliation. It was said that its meaning is do not commit what makes it permissible to shed your blood and expel you from your homes, or do not do what ruins you and turns you away from eternal life, for it is killing in reality, and do not commit what prevents you from Paradise, which is your home, for it is the real expulsion. "Then you acknowledged the covenant and admitted its obligation, and you are witnesses" is an emphasis like your saying: So-and-so acknowledged as a witness against himself. It was said that you, the present ones, are witnesses to the acknowledgment of your ancestors, so attributing the acknowledgment to them is metaphorical.
2:85: 85-"Then you are these" is an exclusion of what they committed after the covenant and the acknowledgment of it and the testimony to it. And you are the subject and these is its predicate, meaning that you are after that these deficient ones, like your saying you are that man who did such and such. The change in the description is in the place of the change in the self, and their number is in consideration of what is attributed to them in their presence and in consideration of what will be narrated about them in their absence. And the Almighty's saying: "You kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes" is either a state and the agent in it is the meaning of the indication, or an explanation of this sentence. It was said: These is an emphasis, and the predicate is the sentence. It was said that it means those and the sentence is its connection and the whole is the predicate, and "you kill" was read as an exaggeration. "You cooperate against them in sin and aggression is a state of the subject of you expel", or of its object, or both. And cooperation is cooperation from the back. Asim, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it by deleting one of the two ta's. It was read with the pronunciation of it, and you show off with the meaning of you show off. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them. It was narrated that Qurayzah were allies of the Aws, and Nadir were allies of the Khazraj. So if they fought, each group would help its allies in killing, destroying homes, and expelling their people. And if one of the two groups was taken prisoner, they would gather around him until they ransomed him. And it was said that its meaning is if they come to you as captives in the hands of the devils, you would rush to rescue them with guidance and preaching while you waste yourselves, like the Almighty’s saying: Do you enjoin righteousness upon the people and forget yourselves? And Hamzah read asra which is the plural of asir like jareeh and jarha, and asara is its plural like sakra and sakara. And it was said that it is also the plural of asir, and it is as if he likened it to the lazy person and the plural of its plural. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamza and Ibn Aam read you ransom them as and it is forbidden for you to expel them connected to His statement and you expel a party of you from their homes, and what is between them is an interruption, and the pronoun refers to the matter, or is vague and is explained by you expel them, or refers to what is indicated by you expel them from the source. And their expulsion is a substitute or clarification Do you then believe in some of the Scripture? meaning ransom. "And you disbelieve in some" meaning the sanctity of fighting and exile. "Then what is the reward for whoever does that among you except disgrace in the life of this world" such as killing Qurayzah and taking them captive, and expelling Banu Nadir, and imposing the jizya on others. The root of disgrace is humiliation that is shameful, and therefore it is used in both of them. "And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the severest punishment" because their disobedience is more severe. "And God is not unaware of what you do" confirming the threat, meaning God, the Most High, is watching and does not ignore their actions. Asim read in the narration of al-Mufaddal, you will be returned to the address because of his saying "from you". Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr, Khalaf, and Ya'qub work on the pronoun referring to whom.
2:86: 86- "Those are the ones who have purchased the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter." They preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter. "The punishment will not be lightened for them" by canceling the jizya in this world, and the torture in the Hereafter. "Nor will they be aided" by removing both from them.
2:87: 87- And We gave Moses the Book meaning the Torah and followed him up with messengers meaning We sent messengers after him, as the Almighty said: Then We sent Our messengers in succession. It is said that he followed him, and he followed him with it if he followed him from the back, like his sin from the sin And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs the clear miracles such as raising the dead and healing the blind and the leper, and informing of the unseen. Or the Gospel, and Jesus in Hebrew is Absho'. And Mary means servant, and in Arabic it is for women like Al-Zir is for men. Ru'yah said: I said to Al-Zir that Mary did not reach him. Its weight is Mufa`il since Fa`il was not established, and Aydanahu and Qawwanihu, and Aydanahu was read with a long vowel with the Holy Spirit with the Holy Spirit as you say: Hatim al-Jud, and a man of truth, and he meant by it Gabriel, and it was said: the spirit of Jesus, peace be upon him, and he described it with it because of its purity from the touch of Satan, or because of its honor with God Almighty and that is why he added it to himself Almighty, or because the loins and wombs did not contain it, or the Gospel, or the greatest name of God with which he revived the dead, and Ibn Kathir read al-Quds with a sukun in the entire Qur’an So every time there comes to you a messenger with what your souls do not desire with what you do not like. It is said hawwa with a kasra if he loves, hawwa with a fatha, hawwa with a damma if he falls. And the hamza was placed between the fa and what it is connected to as a rebuke to them for following that with this and astonishment at their condition, and it is possible that it is a resumption and the fa is for conjunction with what is understood, you were arrogant about faith and following the messengers. A party you denied, such as Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them. The fa is for causality or detail. And a party you killed, such as Zechariah and John, peace be upon them. It was mentioned in the present tense to narrate the past situation, to bring it to mind, for the matter is terrible. Or to take into account the pauses, or to indicate that you are still in it, for you are hovering around killing Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had I not protected him from you. For this reason, you bewitched him and poisoned the sheep for him.
2:88: 88- And they said, 'Our hearts are covered' covered with natural coverings that what you have brought cannot reach them nor can they comprehend it, borrowed from the uncircumcised who is not circumcised. It was said that its origin is ghalaf, the plural of ghalaf, so it was lightened. The meaning is that they are vessels for knowledge. They do not hear knowledge except that they comprehend it, nor do they understand what they say. Or we are independent of what is in them from others. Rather, God has cursed them for their disbelief is a response to what they said, and the meaning is that they were created with the innate nature and the ability to accept the truth, but God let them down with their disbelief and nullified their readiness, or that they did not refuse to accept what they say due to a defect in it, but rather because God the Most High let them down with their disbelief as He the Most High said: So He made them deaf and blinded their sight, or they are cursed disbelievers, so where do they get the claim of knowledge and independence from you? So little do they believe So little faith they believe, and what is more is for exaggeration in the smallness, which is their belief in some of the Book. It was said: He meant by little nothingness.
2:89: 89- And when there came to them a Book from God meaning the Qur'an confirming what was with them of their Book, and it was read in the accusative case as a state of the Book because it is specific to the description, and the answer to lama is omitted and indicated by the answer to the second lama". "And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved" meaning they used to pray for victory against the polytheists and say: O God, grant us victory through the Prophet of the End of Time described in the Torah. Or they would grant victory to them and inform them that a Prophet would be sent from among them, and his time had drawn near. The "seen" is for emphasis and to indicate that the subject is asking about himself. "So when there came to them what they recognized" of the truth. "They disbelieved in it" out of envy and fear for leadership. "So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers meaning upon them, and the apparent was brought to indicate that they were cursed for their disbelief, so the lam" is for the covenant, and it is permissible for it to be for the genus and they enter into it as a primary entry because the speech is about them.
2:90: 90- "What a miserable thing they have purchased for themselves is an indefinite noun meaning something that distinguishes the subject of the implied bad, and bought" is its description and meaning they sold, or bought according to their assumption, for they assumed that they had saved themselves from punishment by what they did. "That they should disbelieve in what God has revealed is what is specifically blamed out of envy seeking what is not theirs and envy, and this is the reason for that they should disbelieve rather than bought" for the separation. "That God should send down" for sending down, meaning they envied Him for God to send down. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Sahl and Ya'qub read it with a light pronunciation. "From His grace" meaning the revelation. "Upon whomever He wills of His servants" on whom He chose for the message. "So they incurred wrath upon wrath" for disbelief and envy of the one who is the best of creation. It was said: Because of their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, after Jesus, peace be upon him, or after their saying that Ezra was the son of God. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment, meaning their humiliation, unlike the punishment of the sinner, which is a purification of his sins.
2:91: 91- And when it is said to them, 'Believe in what God has revealed,' meaning all the revealed books. "They say, 'We believe in what has been revealed to us,' meaning the Torah. 'And they disbelieve in what is beyond it.'" is a state of the pronoun in they said, and behind is originally made a circumstance, and is added to the subject, meaning what is hidden by it, which is His creation, and to the object, meaning what is hidden by it, which is in front of Him. Therefore, it is considered one of the opposites. And it is the truth, the pronoun refers to what is beyond it, and what is meant by it is the Qur'an. Confirming what is with them, is a state of emphasis that includes rejecting their statement, for when they disbelieved in what agrees with the Torah, they disbelieved in it. Say, 'Then why did you kill the prophets of God before, if you were believers?' is an objection to them regarding killing the prophets while claiming to believe in the Torah, which does not justify it. Rather, it was attributed to them because it was the action of their fathers, and that they were pleased with it and determined to do it. Nafi' alone read that the report of God is with a hamza throughout the Qur'an.
2:92: 92- And Moses came to you with clear proofs meaning the verses mentioned in the Almighty's saying: And We gave Moses nine clear signs "Then you took the calf meaning as a god after him after Moses came, or went to the mountain and you were wrongdoers" is a state, meaning you took the calf wrongfully by worshipping it, or by neglecting the verses of God Almighty, or an objection meaning and you are a people whose habit is injustice. The context of the verse is also to invalidate their saying "We believe in what was revealed to us" and to draw attention to the fact that their method with the Messenger was the method of their ancestors with Moses, peace be upon them, not to repeat the story and so on after it.
2:93: 93- "And when We took your covenant and raised the Mount over you, [saying], 'Take what We have given you with determination and listen.'" That is, We said to them: Take what you have been commanded to do in the Torah with earnestness and listen with obedience. "They said, 'We hear your word and disobey your command.' And they made the calf drink into their hearts." Love for it engulfed them and its image was ingrained in their hearts, due to their intense passion for it, just as dye engulfs a garment and drink ingrains the depths of the body. And in their hearts: a statement of the place of intoxication, as God Almighty says: They only eat fire into their bellies “because of their disbelief” because of their disbelief, and that is because they were anthropomorphists, or incarnates, and they did not see a body more amazing than it, so what the Samaritan suggested to them took root in their hearts. Say, ‘Evil is that which your faith enjoins upon you’ meaning the Torah, and the specific thing being blamed is omitted, such as this command, or what includes it and other uglinesses of theirs listed in the three verses, obligating them if you are believers is a confirmation of the criticism of their claim to believe in the Torah, and its meaning is if you are believers in it, it did not command you to do these uglinesses, nor does it permit you to do them because of your belief in it, or if you are believers in it, then evil is that which your belief in it enjoins upon you, because the believer should not engage in anything except what his belief requires, but belief in it does not command it, so then you are not believers.
2:94: 94- "Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively for you" specifically for you as you said: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew and its accusative is in the state of the home. Outside of the people the rest of them, and the lam is for the genus, or the Muslims and the lam is for the covenant. Then wish for death if you are truthful because whoever is certain that he is from the people of Paradise longs for it, and loves to be freed from the home of impurities, as Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: I do not care whether I fall upon death, or death falls upon me. And Ammar, may God be pleased with him, said at Siffin: Now I will meet the beloved Muhammad and his party. And Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, said when he summarized: (A beloved has come in need. He who regrets will not succeed) meaning: on wishing, especially if he knows that it is safe for him and no one else shares it with him.
2:95: 95- And they will never wish for it because of what their hands have put forth of the causes of Hellfire, such as disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Qur'an, and distorting the Torah. And since the working hand is specific to man, a tool for his ability through which he performs all his deeds and most of his benefits, he used it to refer to the soul sometimes and to ability at other times, and this sentence is information about the unseen and it was as he reported, because if they wished, it would have been transmitted and become famous, for wishing is not an act of the heart to be hidden, rather it is to say: I wish for such and such, and if it were in the heart, they would have said: We wished. And from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, If they wished for death, every person would choke on his saliva and die on the spot, and no Jew would remain on the face of the earth. "And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers" is a threat to them and a warning that they are wrongdoers in claiming what is not theirs, and denying it from those who do.
2:96: 96- And you will find them the most greedy of people for life from the one who finds with his mind running the course of knowledge, and its objects are they and the most greedy of people, and the indefiniteness of life because it is intended by it an individual of its individuals, which is: the prolonged life: and it was read with the lam. And of those who associate others with God is carried on the meaning as if he said: more greedy of people for life than those who associate others with God. And mentioning it individually is for emphasis, for if you are very greedy since they did not know anything but the immediate life, and the increase in rebuke and reprimand, then when their greed increased - and they acknowledge the punishment on the greed of the deniers - this indicates their knowledge that they are going to the Fire, and it is permissible that it is intended and more greedy than those who associate others with God, so greed was deleted because the first indicates it, and that it is the predicate of a deleted subject whose description is one of them would like on the basis that what is intended by those who associate others with God is the Jews because they said: Ezra is the son of God, meaning: and among them are people one of whom would like, and it is for the first two a statement of the increase of their greed in the manner of resumption. If he were to live a thousand years is a story of their friendship. If means if only and its original form was if he were to live a thousand years, so it was made in the third person because of his saying he would like, like your saying he swore by God that they would do so. And it is not to remove him from the punishment that he live a thousand years is the pronoun referring to one of them, and that he live a thousand years is the subject of that he live a thousand years, meaning that none of them can remove him from the punishment by his living a thousand years, or because of what he indicates. That he live a thousand years is a substitute for it. Or from them, and that he live a thousand years is its explanation. The original form of sanah is sanwah because of their saying sanawat. It was said sanah like jibnah because of their saying sanahtuhu and sanahat an-nakhlah if the years come upon it, and zahzah means distancing. And God is Seeing of what they do so He will reward them.
2:97: 97-"Say: Who is an enemy to Gabriel? It was revealed about Abdullah bin Suriya. He asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about whom the revelation comes down to? He said: Gabriel. He said: That is our enemy, he has been our enemy many times, and the most severe of that was when it was revealed to our Prophet that Jerusalem would be destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar, so we sent someone to kill him. He saw him in Babylon and Gabriel pushed him away. He said: If your Lord has commanded him to destroy you, then he should not give you power over him. Otherwise, why would you kill him?" It was said: “Omar, may God be pleased with him, entered the Jewish schools one day and asked them about Gabriel. They said: He is our enemy who reveals our secrets to Muhammad and he is the one who brings down all the suffering and torment, and Michael is the one who brings fertility and peace. He said: What is their status with God? They said: Gabriel is on his right and Michael is on his left and there is enmity between them. He said: If they are as you say, then they are not enemies, and you are more disbelieving than donkeys. Whoever is an enemy to one of them is an enemy of God. Then Omar returned and found that Gabriel had preceded him with the revelation, so he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Your Lord has agreed with you, O Omar.” There are eight languages for Gabriel, four of which are recited in: the well-known Gabriel like Salsabil, the recitation of Hamza and Al-Kisa’i, and Gabriel with a kasra on the ra’ and deleting the hamza, the recitation of Ibn Kathir, and Gabriel like Jahmush, the recitation of Asim, according to the narration of Abu Bakr, and Gabriel like Qandeel, the recitation of the rest. And four in the anomalies: Gabriel as Gabriel, and Gabriel and Jibreen and it was prevented from being declined due to foreignness, and the definite article, and its profession is Abdullah. For He has revealed it the first prominent one is for Gabriel, and the second is for the Qur’an, and its omission is not mentioned indicating the magnificence of its status as if due to its specificity and extreme fame it did not need to be mentioned previously. Upon your heart for it is the first to receive revelation, and the place of understanding and memorization, and its right was upon my heart but it came as a narration of the speech of God Almighty as if he said: Say what I have spoken By the permission of God by His command, or His facilitation is a state of its subject He revealed it. Confirming what was before it and guidance and good tidings for the believers are conditions of its object, and it appears that the answer to the condition is for He revealed it, and the meaning is that whoever among them is hostile to Gabriel has cast off his bond of fairness, or has disbelieved in what he has of the Book by being hostile to him for his revelation to you, because it is the revelation of a Book confirming the previous Books, so the answer was omitted and its cause was established in its place, or whoever is hostile to him, the reason for his hostility is that he revealed it to you. And it was said that it was omitted, such as: So let him die of rage, or he is an enemy to me and I am an enemy to him, as he said:
2:98: 98- Whoever is an enemy to God and His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael - then indeed, God is an enemy to the disbelievers. By enmity to God, he meant opposition out of stubbornness, or enmity to those close to His worship. The speech began with mentioning them to magnify their status, as in the Almighty's saying: And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should please Him. He mentioned the two angels separately because of their excellence, as if they were of a different kind, and to draw attention to the fact that enmity to one and to all is the same in disbelief and incurring enmity from God, the Almighty, and that whoever is an enemy to one of them is as if he is an enemy to all of them, since the obligation for their enmity and love in reality is one, and because the argument was between them. He put the apparent in place of the implicit to indicate that God, the Almighty, was an enemy to them because of their disbelief, and that enmity to the angels and messengers is disbelief. Nafi` read Mika`il as Mika`il, and Abu `Amr, Ya`qub, and `Asim, according to the narration of Hafs, read it as Mika`il as Mi`ad, and the rest read it as Mika`il with a hamza and a ya` after it. Mika`il was read as Mika`il, Mika`il as Mika`il, and Mika`il.
2:99: 99- "And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses, and none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient." That is, the rebellious disbelievers. When defiant is used in a type of sin, it indicates its enormity, as if it is exceeding its limit. It was revealed about Ibn Suriya when he said to his Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, "You have not brought us anything that we recognize, and no verse has been sent down to you for us to follow you."
2:100: 100- "Or whenever they made a covenant" The hamza is for denial, and the waw is for connecting to something omitted, the meaning of which is they disbelieved in the verses and whenever they made a covenant, and it was read with the waw silent on the basis that the meaning is except for those who were wicked, "Or whenever they made a covenant", and it was read they made a covenant and they made a covenant. "A group of them threw it away broke it, and the origin of the word nabdh is to throw it away, but it is more common in what is forgotten, and a group only said it because some of them did not break it, But most of them do not believe" is a response to what is imagined that the group are the minority, or that those who did not throw it away openly are believers in it secretly.
2:101: 101- "And when there came to them a Messenger from God confirming what was with them" such as Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them. "A party of those who were given the Scripture cast away the Book of God" meaning the Torah, because their disbelief in the Messenger confirming it was disbelief in it in what confirms it, and cast away what is in it of the obligation to believe in the Messengers supported by the signs. And it was said that what was with the Messenger, peace be upon him, was the Qur'an. "Behind their backs" is an example of their turning away from it completely, turning away from what is thrown behind their backs for not paying attention to it. "As if they do not know" that it is the Book of God, meaning that their knowledge of it is solid, but they ignore it out of stubbornness. Know that God the Almighty indicated in the two verses that the generation of the Jews is divided into four groups: a group that believed in the Torah and fulfilled its rights like the believers of the People of the Book, and they are the minority indicated by His statement: "But most of them do not believe." A group that openly rejected its covenants and transgressed its limits out of rebellion and immorality, and they are the ones meant by His statement: "A party of them cast it aside." A group that did not openly reject it, but they cast it aside out of ignorance of it, and they are the majority. A group that held fast to it outwardly and cast it aside secretly, knowing the situation, out of transgression and stubbornness, and they are the ones who ignored it.
2:102: 102- And they followed what the devils recited is in apposition to rejecting, meaning they rejected the Book of God and followed the books of magic that the devils from the jinn or mankind read or follow, or both. During the reign of Solomon meaning his era, and it is recited as a story of a past situation. It was said: They used to eavesdrop and add lies to what they heard, and they would tell them to the priests who would write them down and teach the people. This became widespread during the reign of Solomon, peace be upon him, until it was said: The jinn know the unseen, and that Solomon's kingdom was completed with this knowledge, and that the jinn, mankind, and the wind were subject to him by it. And Solomon did not disbelieve is a denial of those who claimed that, and magic was expressed as disbelief to indicate that it was disbelief, and that whoever was a prophet was protected from it. But the devils disbelieved by using it, and Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read but with a light l, and the devils was raised. They teach people magic as a means of seduction and misguidance. The sentence is a state of the pronoun. What is meant by magic is that which is obtained by drawing closer to Satan, which a person cannot do independently. This is only established by someone who is compatible with him in terms of spark and evil soul. For compatibility is a condition for solidarity and cooperation, and by this the magician is distinguished from the prophet and the saint. As for what is astonishing, as the masters of tricks do with the help of tools and medicines, or what the sleight-of-hand shows, then it is not blameworthy. Calling it magic is an act of metaphor, or because of the subtlety in it, because in the original its cause is hidden. And what was revealed to the two angels is in apposition to magic, and what is meant by them is one, and the apposition is for the difference in consideration, or what is meant by it is a stronger type than it, or for what you recite. They are two angels who were sent down to teach magic as a test from God to the people, and to distinguish it from a miracle. And what was narrated that they were two human beings, and lust was mixed in them, so they exposed themselves to a woman called: Zahra, so she led them to sins and polytheism, then she ascended to the sky with what she learned from them, so it is narrated from the Jews and perhaps it is from the symbols of the ancients and its solution is not hidden from those with insight. And it was said: Two men were called angels in consideration of their righteousness, and this is supported by the reading of the two angels with the kasra. And it was said: What was sent down is a negation conjoined with what Solomon disbelieved in, denying the Jews in this story. In Babylon is an adverb, or a state of the two angels, or the pronoun in was sent down and it is well known that it is a city in the blackness of Kufa. Harut and Marut is an explanatory apposition for the two angels, and their inflection was prevented due to the action and foreignness, and if they were from hert and mart with the meaning of the kasra, they would have been inflected. And whoever made ma a negation replaced them with devils instead of some, and what is between them is an objection and it was read with the nominative on them Harut and Marut. And they do not teach anyone until they say, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’ So its meaning according to the first is that they do not teach anyone until they advise him and tell him, We are only a test from God. So whoever learns from us and acts upon it is a disbeliever, and whoever learns from us and avoids acting upon it is steadfast in faith, so do not disbelieve by believing in its permissibility and acting upon it. This is evidence that learning magic and what is not permissible to follow is not forbidden, but rather the prohibition is on following it and acting upon it. According to the second, they do not teach anyone until they say, We are only a trial, so do not be like us. “And they learn from them” is the pronoun for what it indicates from someone. That by which they separate between a man and his wife meaning from magic that which is the cause of their separation. And they do not harm thereby anyone except by God’s permission because it and other causes are not effective in and of themselves, but by His command and making. Bidari was read as an addition to someone, and the preposition was made part of it and the separation was by the circumstance. And they learn what harms them because they intend it to be an action, or because knowledge often leads to action and does not benefit them since merely knowing it is not intended nor beneficial in both worlds. And in it, it is more appropriate to avoid it. And they certainly knew meaning the Jews. For whoever bought it meaning he exchanged what the devils recited for the Book of God Almighty. And it is more apparent that the lam is the lam of initiation, and they knew about the action for him there is no share in the Hereafter. "And evil is that for which they sold themselves" it is possible to mean both meanings based on what was mentioned. "If they had known" they thought about it, or they knew its ugliness specifically, or the right to what follows it of punishment, and what is established for them first on the oath of affirmation is the instinctive mind or general knowledge that the action is ugly, or the punishment is arranged without verification. And it was said, its meaning is if they were to act according to their knowledge, for whoever does not act according to what he knows is like someone who did not know.
2:103: 103- And if they had believed in the Messenger and the Book. And feared God by abandoning sins, such as rejecting the Book of God and following magic. A reward from God would be better is the answer to if, and its original form is they would have been rewarded with a reward from God better than what they sold themselves for. The verb was deleted and the rest was composed as a nominal sentence to indicate the permanence of the reward and the certainty of its goodness. The preferred word was deleted out of respect for the preferred one so that it would not be attributed to him, and the reward was indefinite because the meaning of something of the reward is better. It was said: if is for wishing, and for a reward is a subject statement. For a reward was read as consultation, and the reward is a reward and a reward because the doer of good will be rewarded if they only knew that the reward from God is better than what they are in, and they knew but their ignorance was due to their abandonment of contemplation or acting on knowledge.
2:104: 104- "O you who have believed, do not say, 'Ra'ina' but say, 'Unzurna'." Shepherding is the preservation of others for their own benefit. The Muslims used to say to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, "Ra'ina, meaning, watch over us" and take our time with what he taught us until we understand it. The Jews heard it, so they assumed it and addressed him with it, intending to attribute it to rashness, or to insult him with the Hebrew word they used to curse him with, which is "Ra'ina. The believers were forbidden from it and were ordered to do something that would convey that benefit and would not accept confusion, which is Unzurna meaning look at us. Or Anzarna from Nazar" if he waited for him. "Unzurna was read from Inzaar meaning, Give us time so that we may preserve. Ra'una was read in the plural form for respect, and Ra'ina with the tanween means a word with rashness in relation to Ra'na which is impetuousness, because it resembles their saying Ra'ina" and causes insults. And listen and listen well so that you do not need to seek consideration, or listen with acceptance, not like the Jews, or listen to what you have been commanded to do seriously so that you do not return to what you have been forbidden from. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment, meaning those who took the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, lightly and insulted him.
2:105: 105- "The disbelievers among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists do not wish" was revealed to refute a group of Jews who showed affection for the believers, and claimed that they wished them well. Affection is the love of something while wishing for it, and therefore it is used in both cases. "Min" is for clarification, as in the Almighty's saying: "It was not for those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord is the object of yud, and the first min" is added for comprehensiveness, and the second is for the beginning, and good was explained as revelation. The meaning is that they envy you for it and do not wish for any of it to be sent down to you, and as for knowledge and harm, and perhaps what is meant by it is what is general in that. "And God singles out for His mercy whom He wills" He invites him to inform him and teaches him wisdom and supports him, nothing is required of Him, and no one has a right over Him. "And God is the possessor of great bounty" indicating that prophethood is from bounty, and that the deprivation of some of His servants is not His bounty, but rather due to His will and what is known in them of His wisdom.
2:106: 106-Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten was revealed when the polytheists or Jews said: Do you not see that Muhammad orders his companions to do something then forbids them from it and orders the opposite. Abrogation in the language is: removing the image from something and establishing it in something else, like the shadow abrogating the sun and transfer, and from it reincarnation. Then it was used for each of them like your saying: the wind abrogated the trace, and abrogated the book. Abrogation of the verse is a statement of the end of worship by reading it, or the ruling derived from it, or both. And its being forgotten is its removal from the hearts, and what is a conditional imperative for us to abrogate, erected by it as a direct object. Ibn Amir read what we abrogate from ansakh, meaning we order you or Gabriel to abrogate it, or we find it abrogated, and Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr nansa'uha meaning we delay it from an-nasu'. It was read nansaha meaning we make someone forget it, and nansaha meaning you, and tansaha in the passive form, and nansukaha with the two objects implied na’t bi-khair minha or mathulha meaning what is better for the servants in benefit and reward, or similar to it in reward. Abu Amr read it by changing the hamza to an alif. did you not know that God is over all things competent? He is able to abrogate and bring something similar to the abrogated, or something better than it. The verse indicates the permissibility of abrogation and delaying revelation, as the origin is that an and what it includes are limited to possible matters. This is because the rulings were legislated and the verses were revealed for the benefit of the servants and to perfect their souls as a favor and mercy from God. This differs according to the eras and people, such as the causes of livelihood, as what is beneficial in one era may be harmful in another era. Those who forbade abrogation without a substitute or with a heavier substitute argued that the abrogation of the Book and the Sunnah is what is brought in place of it, and the Sunnah is not like that, and all of them are weak, as it is possible that the absence of a ruling or something heavier is better. Abrogation may be known by other means, and the Sunnah is something that God Almighty brought, and what is meant by good and similar is not what is like that in the wording. The Mu'tazila are on the occurrence of the Qur'an, as change and variation are among its requirements. I answer: They are among the accidents of matters related to the meaning that exists in the eternal self.
2:107: 107- Do you not know? The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is him and his nation, because He said: And what is [the matter] with you? He only singled it out because He is the most knowledgeable of them and the source of their knowledge. That to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He does what He wills and rules as He wills, and it is like evidence for His saying: Indeed, God is over all things competent. Or for the permissibility of abrogation, and that is why He left out the conjunction. And you have not besides God any protector or helper. Rather, He is the One who owns your affairs and directs them in a way that is good for you. The difference between the protector and the helper is that the protector may be too weak to help, and the helper may be a stranger to the one being helped, so there is a generality between them in one respect.
2:108: 108-Or do you want to ask your Messenger as Moses was asked before? Or is it equivalent to the hamza in did you not know? meaning: Did you not know that He is the Owner of all affairs, capable of all things, He commands and forbids as He wills, or do you know and suggest the question as the Jews suggested to Moses, peace be upon him? Or is it disconnected and what is meant is that he advises them to trust in Him and leave the suggestion to Him. It was said: It was revealed about the People of the Book when they asked that God send down a book from the sky to them. And it was said: About the polytheists when they said, We will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book that we can read. "And whoever exchanges faith for disbelief has certainly strayed from the right path." And whoever abandons trust in the clear verses and doubts them and suggests other than them, has strayed from the straight path until he fell into disbelief after faith. The meaning of the verse is: Do not suggest, lest you go astray from the middle of the path, and misguidance leads you far from the goal and exchanging faith for disbelief. It was read as yabadal from abdal.
2:109: 109- And many of the People of the Scripture wish meaning their rabbis that they would turn you back, for if replaces in in meaning but not in wording: after you have believed, as disbelievers apostates, and it is a state of the pronoun of the addressees out of envy the reason for wish. From themselves may be related to wish, meaning they wished that from themselves and their desires, not because of religiousness and inclination towards the truth. Or out of envy, meaning extreme envy emanating from the origin of their souls after the truth has become clear to them through the miracles and attributes mentioned in the Torah. So pardon and overlook pardon is leaving the punishment of the sinner, and pardon is leaving the reproach of him until God brings about His command which is permission to fight them and impose the jizyah on them, or to kill Banu Qurayzah and expel Banu Nadir. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that it was abrogated by the verse of the sword, and there is a consideration in it because the command is not absolute, Indeed, God is over all things competent, so He is able to take revenge on them.
2:110: 110- And establish prayer and give zakat is in apposition to so forgive as if he ordered them to be patient, disobedient, and seek refuge in God Almighty through worship and righteousness. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves such as prayer and charity. Prepare is read from prepare "you will find it with God" meaning its reward. God is Seeing of what you do. No work is lost with Him. It was read with the letter ya and it is a warning.
2:111: 111- And they said is in apposition to and wished, and the pronoun refers to the People of the Book, the Jews and Christians. None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian is a conjunction between the statements of the two groups as in the Almighty's saying: And they said, Be Jews or Christians trusting in the understanding of the listener, and Hawd is the plural of Ha'idh like A'wadh and A'idh, and the singularity of the implied noun in Kan" and the plural of the predicate is due to the consideration of the word and meaning. "Those are their wishes" is a reference to the aforementioned wishes, which is that no good will descend upon the believers from their Lord, and that such wishes are their wishes, and the sentence is an interjection and the wish is a verbal noun from the verb "to wish like adhookah and ajubah". "Say, Bring your proof for your exclusivity to enter Paradise. If you are truthful in your claim, because every statement without evidence is not proven.
2:112: 112- Bala is proof of what they denied about others entering Paradise Whoever submits his face to God sincerely devotes himself to Him, or his intention, and its origin is the limb and is a doer of good in his work then he will have his reward which was promised to him for his work with his Lord fixed from his Lord, it will not be lost or diminished, and the sentence is the answer to man if it is conditional and its predicate if it is relative. The fa in it is because it includes the meaning of the condition, so the response is by saying: Bala alone, and it is good to stop on it. It is permissible for man aslam to be the subject of an implied verb like Bala whoever submits will enter it and there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve in the Hereafter.
2:113: 113- And the Jews said, 'The Christians are not upon anything,' and the Christians said, 'The Jews are not upon anything,' meaning, upon a matter that is valid and reliable. It was revealed when Najran came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Jewish rabbis came to them and they debated and discussed that. And they recite the Scripture The waw is for the state, and the Scripture is for the genus, meaning: they said that while they were people of knowledge and the Scripture. Likewise like that those who do not know said like their saying like the idol worshippers and the deniers. He rebuked them for their stubbornness and imitating the ignorant. If it is said: Why did he rebuke them when they were truthful, for both religions after abrogation are nothing? I said: They did not mean that, but rather each group intended by it to invalidate the religion of the other from its origin, and to disbelieve in his prophet and his book, even though what was not abrogated from them is true and must be accepted and acted upon. So God will judge separate between them “between the two groups” on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they differed by allocating to each group what is appropriate for it of punishment. And it was said that His judgment between them is that he will call them liars and put them in the Fire.
2:114: 114- And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God is general for everyone who destroys a mosque, or strives to disable a place designated for prayer. It was revealed about the Romans when they invaded Jerusalem and destroyed it and killed its people. Or about the polytheists when they prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from entering the Sacred Mosque in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah that his name be mentioned in it is the second object of prevented and sought to destroy it by demolition, or disabling those meaning the preventers it was not for them to enter it except in fear it was not appropriate for them to enter it except with fear and humility, let alone dare to destroy it, or it was not right for them to enter it except in fear of the believers that they would attack them, let alone prevent them from it, or it was not for them in the knowledge and judgment of God, so it is a promise to the believers of victory and the liberation of the mosques from them and He fulfilled His promise. It was said: Its meaning is the prohibition of allowing them to enter the mosque, and the imams differed about it. Abu Hanifa permitted it and Malik forbade it, and Al-Shafi’i distinguished between the Sacred Mosque and others. For them in this world is disgrace killing and captivity, or that by imposing the jizya. And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment because of their disbelief and injustice.
2:115: 115- And to God belong the East and the West meaning by them the two sides of the earth, meaning that the whole earth belongs to Him, and no place is exclusive to Him. If you are prevented from praying in the Sacred Mosque or Al-Aqsa Mosque, then the earth has been made a place of prostration for you. So wherever you turn in any place you turn towards the Qiblah there is the Face of God meaning His direction which He has commanded, for the possibility of turning is not exclusive to a mosque or a place. Or there is His Essence: meaning He is All-Knowing of what is done therein. Indeed, God is Vast by His encompassing of things. Or by His mercy He wants to expand upon His servants. Knowing of their interests and their actions in all places. And from Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, that it was revealed regarding the prayer of the traveler on a mount: And it was said: Regarding a people who were blind to the Qiblah, so they prayed in different directions, then when morning came they realized their mistake. Based on this, if the mujtahid makes a mistake and then the mistake becomes clear to him, he is not obligated to make up for it. It was said that it is a prelude to the abrogation of the Qiblah and the exoneration of the worshipped from being in the space of its direction.
2:116: 116- And they said, 'God has taken a son.' It was revealed when the Jews said, Ezra is the son of God, and the Christians said, The Messiah is the son of God, and the polytheists of the Arabs said, The angels are the daughters of God. Its conjunction with the Jews said, or a prohibition, or the meaning of the Almighty's saying, And who is more unjust? Ibn Amir read without the waw, Glory be to Him, to absolve Him of that, as it requires likening, need, and the speed of annihilation. Do you not see that the celestial bodies - despite their possibility and annihilation - since they were permanent as long as the world existed, did not take what would be for them like a son, taking animals and daughters, by choice or by nature. Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. This is a response to what they said, and evidence of its corruption. The meaning is that He, the Most High, is the Creator of whatever is in the heavens and the earth, which includes the angels, Ezra, and the Messiah. All are obedient to Him. Submissive, they do not refrain from His will and creation. Everything that has this characteristic is not similar to its necessary component in itself, so it does not have a son, because it is the right of a son to be similar to his father. Rather, He came with what is not for those who have knowledge. He said obedient in order to emphasize those who have knowledge, belittling their status. The nunation of every is a substitute for the added to it, meaning everything in them. It is possible that it is intended for everyone whom they made a son to Him, obedient and committed to servitude, so it is an obligation after establishing the proof. The verse indicates the corruption of what they said in three ways, and the jurists used it as evidence that whoever owns his son is freed from him, because the Most High denied the son by affirming ownership, and that requires their contradiction.
2:117: 117-The Originator of the heavens and the earth is their Creator, and His counterpart is the All-Hearing in His saying: The security of Rayhana, the All-Hearing Supplicant, keeps me awake and my companions awake Or the Creator of His heavens and His earth, from the innovations of the Creator, and it is a fourth argument. Its statement is that the father is the element of the son who is affected by the separation of his matter from him, and God, glory be to Him, is the Creator of all things, the absolute doer, free from being affected, so He cannot be a father. And creativity: is the invention of something not from something all at once, and it is more appropriate for this subject than the making which is: the composition of images not by the element, and the formation which is by change and in time mostly. And the word Badi’ was read in the genitive case as a substitute for the pronoun in lahu. And the word Badi’ is in the accusative case as a praise. And when He decrees a matter means He wills something. The root of decree is the completion of something in power, as in the Almighty’s saying: And your Lord has decreed, or in action, as in the Almighty’s saying: So He ordained them as seven heavens. It is used to refer to the divine will’s attachment to the existence of something in that He necessitates it. Then He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. From the perfect kāna meaning to create, so it occurs. What is meant by it is not the reality of a command or compliance, but rather the representation of the occurrence of what His will is attached to without delay by obeying the one commanded without stopping. It contains the meaning of innovation, and an allusion to a fifth argument, which is that taking a child is something that occurs in stages and a delay, and His action is independent of that. Ibn ‘Amir read faykūn with a fathah on the nūn. Know that the reason for this misguidance is that the masters of the previous religions used to call God Almighty the Father, considering Him to be the first cause, until they said that the Father is the lesser Lord, and God Almighty is the greater Lord. Then the ignorant among them thought that what was meant by it was the meaning of birth, so they believed that by imitation, and therefore the one who said it was an unbeliever and he was forbidden from it absolutely, to cut off the source of corruption.
2:118: 118- "And those who do not know said," meaning the ignorant polytheists, or the ignorant ones from the People of the Book. "Why does God not speak to us? Why does God not speak to us as He speaks to the angels, or reveal to us that you are His Messenger? Or a sign come to us?" An argument for your truthfulness. The first is arrogance, and the second is denial, because the signs of God that were given to them were disdain and stubbornness. "Likewise said those before them, from the past nations, like their saying, So they said, 'Show us God plainly.' Can your Lord send down to us a table spread with food from the heaven? Their hearts are alike," the hearts of these and those before them in blindness and stubbornness. It was read with a shaddah on the shin. "We have certainly made clear the verses for a people who are certain," meaning who seek certainty, or are certain of the truths, without doubt or stubbornness. It indicates that they did not say this because of the ambiguity in the verses or to seek more certainty, but rather they said it out of arrogance and stubbornness.
2:119: 119- Indeed, We have sent you with the truth embodied and supported by it. As a bringer of good tidings and a warner So do not worry about them if they persist and are stubborn. And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire Why did they not believe after you delivered the message. Nafi' and Ya'qub read: Do not ask, as a prohibition to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from asking about the condition of his parents. Or as a glorification of the punishment of the disbelievers, as if it is so terrible that he is unable to tell about it, or the listener cannot be patient to hear report of it, so he is forbidden from asking. Hellfire: the blazing fire.
2:120: 120- And never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you until you follow their religion is an exaggeration in making the Messenger (peace be upon him) despair of their Islam, for if they were not pleased with him until he followed their religion, how would they follow his religion? Perhaps they said something like that, so God spoke about them, and that is why He said: Say as an instruction for the answer. Indeed, the guidance of God is the guidance meaning the guidance of God, which is Islam, is the guidance to the truth, not what you call for. And if you were to follow their desires their false opinions. The religion is what God has prescribed for His servants through the tongues of His prophets, from the word I dictated the book if you dictated it, and desire is an opinion that follows fame after what has come to you of knowledge meaning the revelation, or the religion whose authenticity is known. You will have from God neither a protector nor a helper who will ward off His punishment from you, and this is the answer to if.
2:121: 121- Those to whom We gave the Scripture meaning the believers of the People of the Scripture recite it with its true recitation by observing the wording without distortion and contemplating its meaning and acting in accordance with it, and it is an implied state and the predicate is what follows it, or a predicate on the basis that what is meant by the relative pronoun are the believers of the People of the Scripture those believe in it with their Scripture without the distorters. And whoever disbelieves in it with distortion and disbelief in what confirms it then those are the losers since they purchased disbelief with faith.
2:122: 122- O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.
2:123: 123- And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all, nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be aided. When he began their story with the command to remember blessings, fulfill their rights, beware of wasting them, and fear the Hour and its terrors, he repeated that and concluded his speech with them with it, exaggerating the advice and indicating that this was the gist of the matter and the intended meaning of the story.
2:124: 124- And when his Lord tested Abraham with words He charged him with His commands and intentions, and the test in origin is the assignment of a difficult matter of affliction, but since it necessitates testing for those who are ignorant of the consequences, it was thought that they were synonymous, and the pronoun refers to Abraham, and it is good because it comes first in wording even if it comes after in rank, because the condition is one of the two precedences, and words may be applied to meanings, so they were interpreted as the thirty praiseworthy qualities mentioned in the Almighty's saying: The repentant, the worshippers and the Almighty's saying: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women to the end of the verse, and His saying: The believers have succeeded to His saying: Those are the inheritors as they were interpreted in His saying: Then Adam received from his Lord words and the ten that are from His Sunnahs, and the rituals of Hajj, and the planets, and the two moons, and circumcision, and the slaughter of a child, and the fire, and the migration. However, the Almighty treated him with them as one who is tested by them and by what is included in the verses that follow them. And Abraham, his Lord, was read as if he called upon his Lord with words such as, Show me how You give life to the dead. “Make this a secure city,” to see if He would answer him. Ibn Amir read Abraham with an alif for all of what is in this surah. So he completed them, so he performed them completely and fulfilled them as they should be, because the Almighty said, And Abraham, who fulfilled. In the last reading, the pronoun refers to his Lord, meaning He gave him everything he called upon. He said, ‘Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people.’ This is a resumption if it is implied, as it is as if it was said: So what did his Lord say when he completed them, so he was answered with that? Or an explanation of his saying, He was tested, so the words are what he mentioned about the Imamate, purifying the House, raising its foundations, and Islam. If you put it in the accusative case, it is said that the whole is a sentence conjoined to what preceded it, or a maker from ja'ala which has two objects, and the Imam is the name of the one who is followed and his Imamate is general and eternal, since no prophet was sent after him except that he was from his descendants who were commanded to follow him. He said, And from my descendants is conjoined with the kaf, meaning and some of my descendants, as you say, And Zayd, in response to I will honor you". The descendants are the offspring of a man, so it is verbal or verbal, and its second ra was changed to a ya as in "I have been given". From the dhar, meaning to separate, or verbal or verbal, and its hamza was changed from the dhartha, meaning to create. And my descendants were read with the kasra, and this is a language. "He said, My covenant does not include the wrongdoers" is an answer to his request, and a warning that there may be oppressors from his descendants, and that they will not attain the Imamate because it is a trust from God Almighty and a covenant, and the oppressor is not entitled to it, and only the righteous and pious among them attain it. It is evidence of the infallibility of the prophets from major sins before the mission, and that the immoral person is not fit for leadership. It was read as the oppressors and the meaning is the same, since whatever has befallen you, you have attained.
2:125: 125- And when We made the House meaning the Kaaba, it was prevalent over it like the star over the Pleiades. A place of return for people a place of return to which the prominent visitors or their likes return, or a place of reward where they are rewarded for performing Hajj and Umrah. It was read: Mathabat, meaning because it is the place of return for everyone. And security and a place of security where its people are not exposed, as God Almighty said: A secure sanctuary. And people are snatched from around them, or a place of security from the torment of the Hereafter, since Hajj nullifies what came before it, first the offender who takes refuge in it is held accountable until he leaves, and this is the school of Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him. And take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer with the intention of saying, or in apposition to the understood as an agent for when, or an objection in apposition to an implied meaning, repent to it and take, on the basis that the address is to the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is a recommended matter, and the Station of Abraham is the stone on which is the trace of his foot, or the place where the stone was when he stood on it and called the people to Hajj, or the building of the House was raised and it is its location today. It was narrated that “peace and blessings of God be upon him took the hand of Omar, may God be pleased with him, and said: This is the Station of Abraham, so Omar said: Should we not take it as a place of prayer, so he said: I was not commanded to do that, and the sun did not set until it descended.” It was said that what was meant by it was the command to perform the two rak’ahs of the circumambulation, because Jabir narrated that, peace and blessings of God be upon him, When he finished his circumambulation, he went to the Station of Abraham and prayed two rak’ahs behind it and he recited And take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, has two opinions regarding their obligation. It was said: The Station of Abraham is the entire Sanctuary. It was said that the Hajj stations and their being a place of prayer are to be supplicated in and draw closer to God the Almighty. Nafi and Ibn Amir read and take in the past tense in apposition to we made, meaning: and the people took his designated station, meaning the Kaaba, as a qiblah to which they pray. And We enjoined upon Abraham and Ishmael We commanded them. Purify My House It is possible that an is an explanatory particle to include the covenant with the meaning of the statement, meaning purify it from idols and impurities and what is not appropriate for it, or purify it. For those who circumambulate around it. And those who stay there residing near it, or those who stay in it. And bowing and prostrating meaning those who pray, the plural of bowing and prostrating.
2:126: 126- "And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this' meaning the city, or the place. 'A secure city', as God Almighty says, 'In a life of contentment.' Or make its people secure, as you say: a sleeping night. 'And provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day.'" He substituted for whoever believes "his people" a substitute for some for specification. "He said, 'And whoever disbelieves' is in apposition to believed." The meaning is, provide whoever disbelieves. Abraham, peace be upon him, compared provision to leadership, so God Almighty pointed out that provision is a worldly mercy that includes the believer and the disbeliever, unlike leadership and advancement in religion. Or a subject that includes the meaning of condition, “So let him enjoy himself a little” is its predicate, and if disbelief is not a reason for enjoyment, it is a reason for reducing it, by making him confined to the fortunes of this world and not using it to attain reward, and for this reason, Then He will compel him to the punishment of the Fire is conjoined to it, meaning He will force him to it as one who is compelled by his disbelief and his loss of the blessings He has given him, and a little is accusative as a source, or an adverb. And it was read in the imperative form in both of them as being from the supplication of Abraham, and in said is his pronoun. Ibn Amir read So let him enjoy himself from amta’a. And it was read Fanata’u thumma natadruhu, and Ijtarahu with a kasra on the hamza according to the language of those who break the letters of the present tense, and Ijtarahu with the assimilation of the dad, which is weak because the letters Damma Shafar are assimilated into what is adjacent to them, but not vice versa. "And what an evil destination" is the one specifically blamed, which is the torment.
2:127: 127- And when Abraham was raising the foundations of the House is a narration of a past situation, and foundations is the plural of base, which is the foundation, a predominant characteristic of sitting, meaning stability, and perhaps it is a metaphor for the opposite of standing, and from it God made you sit, and raising it the building on it, as it transfers it from a low state to a high state, and it is possible that it is intended to mean the foundations of the building, as every foundation is a base that is placed on it and its construction raises it. It was said that what is intended is to raise its status and show its honor by glorifying it, and calling people to an argument. In the ambiguity of the foundations and their clarification, there is magnification of its status. And Ishmael was reaching for the stones, but since he had an input into the building, it was conjoined with it. It was said: They build on two sides, or alternately. Our Lord, accept from us means they say, Our Lord, accept from us, and it was read with it and the sentence is a state of them. Indeed, You are the Hearer of our supplication, The Knower of our intentions.
2:128: 128- Our Lord, and make us Muslims to You sincerely to You, from aslam who submitted, or submissive who surrendered from aslama who submitted and obeyed, and what is meant is to seek an increase in sincerity and submission, or to remain steadfast in it. It was read Muslims who were Muslims so that what is meant is themselves and Hajar. Or that the dual is one of the levels of the plural. And from our descendants, a nation devoted to You meaning, make some of our descendants. The descendants were singled out for supplication because they are more deserving of compassion, and because if they are righteous, the followers will be righteous through them. Some of them were singled out because they knew that there was darkness in their descendants, and they knew that divine wisdom does not require agreement on sincerity and total devotion to God Almighty, because that is what confuses livelihood. Therefore, it was said: If it were not for fools, the world would have been ruined. It was also said: He meant by the nation the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is possible that from is for clarification, as in the Almighty’s statement: God has promised those among you who believe He placed it before the clarifying one, and separated the conjunction from the conjoined one, as in the Almighty’s statement: He created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof. “And show us” is from ra’a meaning to see or know, and therefore it did not go beyond two objects. Our rites are our acts of worship in the Hajj, or our slaughterhouses. The ritual is originally the ultimate in worship and it became common in the Hajj because of the difficulty and distance from custom in it. Ibn Kathir and Al-Wasosi read on the authority of Abu Amr and Yaqub, Arna, by analogy with faj in faj a thigh in a thigh, and this is unfair because the kasra is transferred from the dropped hamza, which is evidence of it. Al-Duri read on the authority of Abu Amr, with a shortened form, Wa ta’ab ‘alayna, as a request for repentance for their offspring, or for what they had neglected inadvertently. Perhaps they said it to demean themselves and guide their offspring, Indeed, You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful, for whoever repents.
2:129: 129- Our Lord, and send among them among the Muslim nation a messenger from among themselves and none was sent from their descendants except Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he is the one to whom their supplication was answered as he said, may God bless him and grant him peace, I am the supplication of Abraham, the good report of Jesus, and the vision of my mother. "He recites to them Your verses" he reads to them and conveys to them what is revealed to him of the evidence of monotheism and prophethood. "And teaches them the Book" the Qur'an. "And wisdom" what perfects their souls of knowledge and rulings. "And purifies them" from polytheism and sins. "Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might" who cannot be defeated or overcome in what He wills. "The Wise" is the One who rules for it.
2:130: 130-And whoever turns away from the religion of Abraham is a rejection and denial that anyone would turn away from his clear and brilliant religion, meaning that no one would turn away from his religion. Except he who belittles himself except he who despises himself, humiliates himself, and belittles himself. Al-Mubarrad and Tha'lab said that belittling with the kasra is transitive and with the damma is intransitive, and what is stated in the hadith supports this: Pride is to belittle the truth and to look down on people. It was said: Its origin is belittling himself in the nominative case, then it was made accusative as a distinction, such as his opinion was deceived and his head ached, and the saying of Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani: And we take after him the tail of a life that has a back that has no hump Or foolishness in himself, so it is accusative by removing the preposition. And the exception is in the place of the nominative on the chosen instead of the pronoun in yaghriba because it is in the meaning of negation, And We have chosen him in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. An argument and explanation for that, for whoever was the best of the servants in this world, and was witnessed to for his uprightness and righteousness on the Day of Resurrection, he was deserving of being followed, and no one would turn away from him except a fool, or a foolish person who humiliated himself through ignorance and turning away from looking.
2:131: 131- "When his Lord said to him, 'Submit,' he said, 'I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.' is an adverb for We chose him, or an explanation for it, or it is accusative with the omission of remember." It is as if it was said: Remember that time so that you may know that he is the chosen, righteous one who deserves leadership and advancement, and that he attained what he attained by taking the initiative to submit and to be sincere in his secret when his Lord called him and brought to his mind the signs leading to the knowledge that calls to Islam. It was narrated that it was revealed when Abdullah bin Salam called his two nephews, Salamah and Muhajir, to Islam, and Salamah and Abu Muhajir became Muslims.
2:132: 132- "And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons" The recommendation is to do something to someone else that is good and pious, and its root is connection. It is said: he enjoined it upon him, and he separated it, as if the testator connects an action to the action of the one being recommended, and the pronoun in it refers to the religion, or to his saying I have submitted according to the interpretation of the word, or the sentence.
