Nafi and Ibn Amir read and he enjoined, and the first is more eloquent. "And Jacob" is in apposition to Abraham, meaning and he also enjoined it upon his sons. It was read in the accusative case as one of those whom Abraham enjoined, "O my son." According to the Basrans' omission of the saying, it is related to the Kufians because it is a type of it and its counterpart is: Two men from Duba told us that they saw a naked man. In the broken form, the sons of Abraham were four: Ishmael, Isaac, Midian, and Midan. It was said: eight. It was said: fourteen. And the sons of Jacob were twelve: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Shesukhor, Paul, Taphtoni, Don, Kodah, Osher, Benjamin, and Joseph. Indeed, God has chosen for you the religion The religion of Islam, which is the best of religions, as God Almighty says: So do not die except as Muslims. Its appearance is the prohibition of dying in a state contrary to Islam, and what is meant is the prohibition of being in a state contrary to that when they die, and the command to remain steadfast in Islam, like your saying: Do not pray except while you are humble, changing the phrase to indicate that their death, not in Islam, is a death in which there is no good, and that it is His right that it not befall them, and similar to it in the command is: Die and you are a martyr. It was narrated that the Jews said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you not know that Jacob advised his sons to follow Judaism on the day he died, so this was revealed.
2:133: 133- "Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob? The word am" is disconnected and the meaning of the hamza in it is denial, meaning you were not present when death approached Jacob and he said to his sons what he said, so why did you not call Judaism against him? Or it is connected and omitted, meaning were you absent or were you witnesses. It was said: The address is to the believers and the meaning is you did not witness that, but you only learned about it through revelation. "Hadr" was read with a kasra. When he said to his sons instead of when he was present. “What will you worship after me?” meaning: something you will worship. He meant by this to confirm them in monotheism and Islam, and to take their covenant to remain steadfast in them. He will not be asked about anything unless it is known. If it is known, it is specific to the rational ones if asked about their specification. If asked about their description, it is said: Is Zaid a scholar or a doctor? “They said: We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.” It is agreed upon that He exists, is divine, and that His worship is obligatory. Ishmael was counted among his fathers, giving precedence to the father and grandfather, or because he is like a father, based on his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: A man’s paternal uncle is like his father. Like “He said, peace and blessings be upon him, about Al-Abbas, may God be pleased with him: This is the remainder of my fathers.” And it was read as the God of your father, as it is plural with the waw and the nun, as he said: When our voices became clear, we cried and offered our fathers Or singular and Ibrahim alone is an apposition. One God instead of God of your fathers, as in the Almighty’s saying: By the forelock, a lying forelock. Its benefit is to state monotheism and to negate the illusion arising from repeating the complement due to the difficulty of connecting it to the genitive and emphasizing it, or the accusative case for specificity. And we are Muslims to Him is a state of the subject of we worship Him, or its object, or both of them, and it is possible that it is an objection.
2:134: 134- That is a nation that has passed on meaning Abraham, Jacob and their sons. The nation originally meant the group and was called thus because groups follow it. For it is what it has earned, and for you is what you have earned each one will be rewarded for his work, and the meaning is that your affiliation with them does not necessitate that you benefit from their work, but rather you benefit by agreeing with them and following them, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: People do not come to me with their deeds and you come to me with your lineages "And you will not be asked about what they used to do" meaning you will not be held accountable for their bad deeds just as you are not rewarded for their good deeds.
2:135: 135- "And they said, 'Be Jews or Christians.' The absent pronoun refers to the People of the Book, and the or" is for variation, and the meaning is that their statement is one of these two statements. The Jews said, "Be Jews. And the Christians said, Be Christians. You will be guided." The answer to the command. "Say, 'Rather, the religion of Abraham.'" That is, rather, it will be the religion of Abraham, meaning the people of his religion, or rather, we will follow the religion of Abraham. It was read in the nominative case, meaning his religion is our religion, or the opposite, or we are his religion, meaning we are the people of his religion. "Hanif" inclining from falsehood to the truth. A state of the noun or the noun, as in the Almighty's saying: "And We will remove whatever is in their breasts of resentment, [so] they will be brothers. And he was not of the polytheists." An allusion to the People of the Book and others, for they claim to follow him while they are polytheists.
2:136: 136- Say, 'We believe in God.' The address is to the believers, as God Almighty says: If they believe in the same as you believe. "And what was revealed to us" the Qur'an, it was mentioned first because it was the first in relation to us, or a reason for believing in something else. "And what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes" the scrolls, and even though they were revealed to Abraham, since they were worshippers of its details and included under its rulings, it was also revealed to them, just as the Qur'an was revealed to us. The tribes are the plural of tribe, which is the grandchild, meaning the grandchildren of Jacob, or his sons and their offspring, for they are the grandchildren of Abraham and Isaac. "And what was given to Moses and Jesus" the Torah and the Gospel, their mention is singular by a more eloquent ruling because their matter in relation to Moses and Jesus is different from what came before, and the dispute occurred in them. "And what was given to the prophets" all of those mentioned among them and those not mentioned. "From their Lord" revealed to them from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, such as the Jews, so we believe in some and disbelieve in others. One is in the context of general negation, so it is permissible to add between to it. And we are to Him, meaning to God. Submitting, obedient and sincere.
2:137: 137-If they believe in the same as you believe in, then they have been guided is a form of incapacitation and rebuke, like the Almighty's saying: Then produce a surah like it, since there is no like what the Muslims believe in, and no religion is like the religion of Islam. It was said: The ba' is for the instrument without the transitive, and the meaning is if you seek faith in a way that guides to the truth like your way, since the unity of purpose does not reject multiple ways, or it is added for emphasis like the Almighty's saying: The recompense for an evil is the like thereof. The meaning is: “If they believe in God with a belief like your belief in Him, or the example is inserted as in His statement: “And a witness from among the Children of Israel testifies to the like of it” meaning to it, and the one who recites what you believe in testifies to it. But if they turn away, then they are in dissension meaning if they turn away from the belief, or from what you say to them, then they are only in dissension of the truth, which is opposition and opposition, for each one of the dissenters is in a different sect from the other. Then God will suffice you against them as consolation and reassurance for the believers, and a promise to them of preservation and victory over those who oppose them. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing either from the completion of the promise, meaning that He hears what you say and knows your sincerity, and He will inevitably reward you, or a threat to those who turn away, meaning that He hears what they express and knows what they conceal, and He will punish them for it.
2:138: 138- The dye of God meaning God dyed us with His dye, which is the nature of God Almighty upon which He created people, for it is the adornment of man just as the dye is the adornment of the dyed, or God guided us with His guidance and guided us with His proof, or He purified our hearts with faith with His purification, and He called it a dye because the dye appeared on the dyed, and it entered their hearts as dye enters a garment, or for similarity, for the Christians used to dip their children in yellow water which they called baptism and they said: It is a purification for them and by it their Christianity is confirmed, and it was put in the accusative case as a source confirming His saying We believe, and it was said as an enticement, and it was said as a substitute for the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him. And who is better than God at dyeing? There is no dye like His dyeing. And we are His worshippers. This is an allusion to them, meaning we do not associate anything with Him as you associate anything with Him. It is in apposition to We believe, and that requires His saying the dye of God to enter into the object of say. And for those who make it an incitement or a substitute, they should imply say in apposition to adhere, or follow the religion of Abraham. And say we believe is in apposition to follow, so that there is no need for disjointed structure or poor arrangement.
2:139: 139- "Say: Do you argue with us? About God?" About His affair and His choosing a prophet from among the Arabs rather than you? It was narrated that the People of the Book said: All the prophets are from us. If I were a prophet, you would be from us. So the verse was revealed: "And He is our Lord and your Lord." He has no special status over any people. He bestows His mercy upon whomever He wills of His servants. "And for us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds." It is not far-fetched that He honors us with our deeds, as if He obligated them to adhere to every doctrine they adopt, in order to silence and rebuke them. For the honor of prophethood is either a favor from God to whomever He wills, and everyone is equal in it, or it is the bestowal of a right upon those who are prepared for it by persevering in obedience and adorning themselves with sincerity. Just as you have deeds that God may consider in giving them, we also have deeds. "And we are sincere to Him," monotheists, singling Him out with faith and obedience rather than you.
2:140: 140- Or do you say that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the tribes were Jews or Christians? The am is disconnected and the hamza is for denial. According to Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs with the ta, it is possible that it is equivalent to the hamza in Do you argue with us, meaning which of the two matters do you argue with, or claim Judaism or Christianity against the prophets. Say, Are you more knowing or is God? The two matters were denied from Abraham by saying: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian and it was argued against by saying: And the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him. And those who are conjoined with him are his followers in religion according to agreement. And who is more unjust than he who conceals a testimony he has from God? meaning God to Abraham about monotheism and innocence from Judaism and Christianity, and the meaning is that no one is more unjust than the People of the Book, because they concealed this testimony. Or from us if we concealed this testimony, and in it is an allusion to their concealing God’s testimony for Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding his prophethood in their books and elsewhere, and from is for beginning as in the Almighty’s saying: Disavowal from God and His Messenger. “And God is not unaware of what you do” is a warning to them, and it was read with the letter ya.
2:141: 141- "That is a nation that has passed on. It shall have what it earned, and you shall have what you earn. And you will not be asked about what they used to do." This is a repetition of the exaggeration in warning and deterrence against what has become ingrained in human nature of boasting about one's fathers and relying on them. It was said: The address is to them in what came before, and in this verse there is a warning for us against following their example. It was also said: What is meant by the nation in the first is the prophets, and in the second is the ancestors of the Jews and Christians.
2:142: 142- The foolish among the people will say whose dreams have become dim, and who have taken them lightly by imitation and turning away from looking. He means by this those who deny the change of the Qiblah from among the hypocrites, Jews and polytheists. The benefit of presenting the report with it is to settle the soul, prepare the answer and show the miracle. What has turned them away what has diverted them. From their Qiblah which they were facing meaning the Holy House, and the Qiblah is originally the state in which a person faces, so it became a custom for the place towards which one turns for prayer. Say, 'To God belongs the East and the West' no place is specific to Him over another place with an intrinsic characteristic that prevents another from establishing His position, but rather the point is in the impression of His command and not the specificity of the place. He guides whom He wills to a straight path which is what wisdom approves, and what interest requires from turning towards the Holy House at one time, and the Kaaba at another.
2:143: 143- And also refers to the concept of the previous verse, that is, just as We made you guided to the straight path, or made your qiblah the best qiblah. We made you a middle nation that is, the best, or just, purified by knowledge and action. It is originally a name for a place where the area is equal from the sides, then it was borrowed for the praiseworthy qualities because they fall between the two extremes of excess and deficiency, such as generosity between extravagance and miserliness, and courage between rashness and cowardice, then it was applied to the one who is described by them, equal in it the singular and the plural, and the masculine and feminine like all the names that are described by it, and it was used as evidence that consensus is an argument, because if what they agreed upon was false, then their justice would be undermined by it. So that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you is a reason for making, meaning that you may know by contemplating what He has set up for you of arguments, and what He has sent down to you from the Book, that He, the Most High, has not been stingy with anyone nor has He wronged anyone, but rather He has made clear the ways and sent the messengers, so they conveyed and advised. But those who disbelieved were driven by misery to follow desires, and to turn away from the signs, so you bear witness to that over your contemporaries and those before you, or after you. It was narrated that “on the Day of Resurrection, the nations will deny the message of the prophets, so God will demand from them proof of the message - and He knows them best - to establish the argument against the deniers. Then the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be brought and testify, and the nations will say: How did you know? They will say: We know that from the information of God Almighty in His Book, which speaks through the tongue of His truthful Prophet. Then Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be brought and asked about the state of his nation, and he will testify to their justice.” And this testimony, even though it is for them, but since the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, was like a watchful observer over his nation, it was preceded by Ali, and the connection was presented to indicate their exclusivity, so the Messenger will be a witness against them. And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face meaning the direction you used to face, which is the Kaaba, for he, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray toward it in Mecca, then when he migrated, he was ordered to pray toward the rock in order to win over the Jews. Or the rock, according to the saying of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: “His qiblah in Mecca was Jerusalem, except that he made the Kaaba between him and it. So what is reported about it is the first abrogating qiblah, and the second abrogated qiblah. The meaning is that the origin of your command is to face the Kaaba, and we did not make Jerusalem your qiblah.” Except that We may test the people thereby and know who follows you in praying towards it from who turns back on his heels. “Except that We may test the people thereby and know who follows you in praying towards it from who turns back from your religion in devotion to the Qiblah of his fathers.” Or So that We may know now who follows the Messenger from who does not follow him, and there was no obstacle that would disappear with its disappearance. According to the first, its meaning is: We did not return you to what you were upon except to know who is steadfast in Islam from who turns back on his heels due to his anxiety and weakness of faith. If it is said: How can His knowledge be the ultimate in generalities while He has always been All-Knowing? I say: This and similar things are in consideration of the current connection which is the basis of the reward, and the meaning is so that Our knowledge is connected to it existing. It was said: So that His Messenger and the believers may know, but He attributed it to Himself because they are His special ones, or to distinguish the firm from the unstable, like the Most High’s saying: So that God may distinguish the wicked from the good. So He placed knowledge in the place of the distinction caused by it, and the reading of to know in the passive form bears witness to it, and knowledge either means knowledge, or is suspended from what is in from the meaning of interrogation, or its second object is from those who turn away, meaning so that We may know who follows the Messenger, distinguished from those who turn away. And if it were a great sin "if is the lightened form of the heavy sin, and the lam" is the separator. The Kufians said that it is the negative and the "lam" means except. The pronoun is for what is indicated by the Almighty's saying: "And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face" of making, or apostasy, or turning, or transferring, or the qiblah. "Lakbira was read with the nominative case, so kan" would be redundant. "Except for those whom God has guided" to the wisdom of the rulings, who are steadfast in faith and following. "And God would not let your faith go to waste" meaning your steadfastness in faith. It was said: Your faith in the abrogated qiblah, or your prayers towards it, because it was narrated: "When he, peace be upon him, turned towards the Kaaba, they said: How about those who died, O Messenger of God, before the transfer from our brothers? So the verse Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful was revealed. He does not waste their rewards nor does he abandon their righteousness. Perhaps he presented al-Ra'uf which is more eloquent in preserving the separators. The two imams, Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs read al-Ra'uf with a long vowel, and the rest with a short vowel.
2:144: 144- We may see perhaps we may see turning your face toward the sky turning your face toward the sky in anticipation of revelation, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be terrified and expect his Lord to turn him toward the Kaaba, because it was the qiblah of his father Abraham, and the oldest of the two qiblahs and the most conducive to the Arabs' faith, and to oppose the Jews, and that indicates the perfection of his manners as he waited and did not ask We will surely turn you to a qiblah so that we may enable you to face it from your saying: I have turned it to such and such, if you make it its governor, or We will make you face its direction that pleases it you love it and long for it, for religious purposes that agree with the will and wisdom of God. Turn your face turn your face. Toward the Sacred Mosque similarly. It was said: The original meaning of shatr is for what is separated from something if it is separated, and dar shatruf means separate from the dar, then it was used for its side, even if it is not separated like the rain, and the forbidden is forbidden, meaning it is forbidden to fight in it, or it is forbidden for the oppressors to attack it, and the mosque was mentioned without the Kaaba because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in Medina, and the distant one was sufficient for him to take into account the direction, because facing it was difficult for him due to the stinginess of the near one. It was narrated: “He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, and prayed towards the Holy House for sixteen months, then he turned towards the Kaaba in Rajab after noon, two months before the Battle of Badr.” “He prayed with his companions in the mosque of Bani Salamah two rak’ahs of noon, so he turned in prayer and faced the gutter, and the men and women exchanged their rows, so the mosque was called the mosque of the two Qiblahs.” And wherever you are, turn your faces towards it. The Messenger was specifically addressed to glorify him and fulfill his desire, then he generalized it explicitly to clarify the generality of the ruling and to confirm the matter of the Qiblah and to make the nation follow. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. That he, may God bless him and grant him peace, prays towards the two Qiblahs, and the pronoun indicates transformation or direction. And God is not unaware of what you do. A promise and a threat to both groups. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read it with the letter ya.
2:145: 145- And if you brought to those who were given the Scripture every sign proof and argument that the Kaaba is a qiblah, and the lam is used to introduce an oath, they would not follow your qiblah is an answer to the implied oath, and the oath and its answer are the answer to the condition, and the meaning is they did not abandon your qiblah for a doubt that you remove with an argument, but they only opposed you out of stubbornness and obstinacy. And you are not a follower of their qiblah to cut off their desires, for they said: If you remained on our qiblah, we would hope that you would be our companion whom we are waiting for, to deceive him and hope that he would return, and their qiblahs, although multiple, are united in falsehood and opposition to the truth. And some of them are not a follower of the qiblah of others for the Jews face the rock, and the Christians face the rising of the sun. It is not expected that they will agree with you, just as it is not expected that they will agree with you, because each party is stubborn in what it is doing. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, hypothetically and estimatingly, meaning: And if you were to follow them, for example, after the truth has become clear to you and revelation has come to you, then you would be among the wrongdoers. He emphasized his threat and exaggerated it in seven ways: First: Bringing the lam that introduces the oath. Second: The implied oath. Third: The letter of confirmation, which is that. Fourth: Its composition of a verbal sentence and a nominal sentence. Fifth: Bringing the lam in the report. Sixth: He made him one of the wrongdoers, and did not say that you are a wrongdoer because being included with them would give the impression of the occurrence of types of injustice. Seventh: The restriction to the coming of knowledge, in order to magnify the known truth, and to encourage people to follow it and warn against following desires, and to find it horrifying that sins are committed by prophets.
2:146: 146- Those to whom We gave the Scripture meaning their scholars know him the pronoun refers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though it was not mentioned previously because the speech indicates it. It was said that it refers to knowledge, or the Qur'an, or transformation as they know their sons testifies to the first: that is, they know him by his descriptions as they know their sons, they do not confuse them with others. On the authority of Omar, may God be pleased with him, that he asked Abdullah bin Salam, may God be pleased with him, about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: I know him better than I know my son. He said: Why? He said: Because I do not doubt that Muhammad is a prophet. As for my son, perhaps his mother has betrayed him. And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know is a specification for those who are obstinate and an exception for those who believe.
2:147: 147- The truth is from your Lord is a new statement, and the truth is either a subject whose predicate is from your Lord and the lam is for the covenant, and the reference is to what the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is upon, or the truth that they conceal, or for the genus. The meaning is that the truth is what has been proven to be from God Almighty, like what you are upon, not what has not been proven, like what the People of the Book are upon, or its predicate is a deleted subject, meaning it is the truth. And from your Lord is a state, or a predicate after a predicate. It was read in the accusative as a substitute for the first, or the object of they know "so do not be among the doubters" who doubt that it is from your Lord, or in their concealment of the truth while knowing it, and what is not meant by it is a prohibition of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from doubting it, because it is not expected from him and is not intentional or chosen, but rather either the realization of the matter and that it is such that no observer doubts it, or a command to the nation to acquire knowledge that removes doubt in the most eloquent way.
2:148: 148- And for every direction and for every nation a direction, or for every group of Muslims a direction and side of the Kaaba, and the tanween is a substitute for the addition He is its master one of the two objects is omitted, meaning He is its master, or God Almighty is its master. And it was read: And for every direction with the addition, and the meaning is that every direction God is its master, and the lam is added for emphasis to compensate for the weakness of the agent. Ibn Amir read: its master meaning he is the master of that direction, meaning he has taken charge of it. So race to do good deeds such as facing the qiblah and other things that will bring happiness in both worlds, or the virtuous directions, which are those parallel to the Kaaba. Wherever you may be, God will bring you all together meaning: in whatever place you may be, whether in agreement or disagreement, where parts are united or separated, God will gather you to the place of assembly for recompense. Or wherever you may be in the depths of the earth or the tops of mountains, He will take your souls. Or wherever you may be in the opposite directions, God will bring you all together and make your prayers as if they are in one direction. Indeed, God is over all things competent so He is able to cause death, give life, and bring together.
2:149: 149- And from wherever you set out and from wherever you set out for travel turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque when you pray and indeed and and indeed this matter is the truth from your Lord, and God is not unaware of what you do Abu Amr read it with the letter ya and the rest with the letter ta". 7
2:150: 150-"And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it." This ruling was repeated due to its multiple reasons, for God Almighty mentioned three reasons for the change. The first is to glorify the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, by seeking his pleasure, and the divine custom that the people of every religion and the one who calls to a religion should turn toward it and be distinguished by it. And to refute the arguments of the opponents, as we will explain. And He linked each reason with its effect, just as the meaning is linked with each one of its evidences, approximately, although the qiblah has a role. Abrogation is one of the places of temptation and doubt, so it is more appropriate to emphasize its matter and repeat it again and again. "So that the people will have no argument against you is a reason for His saying then turn," and the meaning is that turning from the rock to the Kaaba refutes the Jews' argument that the one described in the Torah's qiblah is the Kaaba, and that Muhammad denies our religion and follows us in our qiblah. And the polytheists that he claims the religion of Abraham and opposes his Qiblah, except those who are unjust among them, an exception from the people, meaning so that no one among the people will have an argument except the obstinate ones among them, as they say, he did not turn to the Kaaba except out of inclination to the religion of his people and love for his country, or it changed his mind and he returned to the Qiblah of his fathers and is about to return to their religion. And he called this an argument like the saying of the Most High: Their argument is invalid with their Lord, because they present it in its context. And it was said that the argument means the argument. And it was said that the exception is to exaggerate in denying the argument completely like his saying: There is no fault in them, except that their swords have nicks from the clashing of the battalions. Knowing that the oppressor has no argument, and it was read: Except those who are unjust among them. As a resumption with the letter of warning. Do not fear them. Do not fear them, for their attacks will not harm you. And fear Me. Do not disobey what I have commanded you. And that I may complete My favor upon you and that you may be guided. The reason for an omitted word is that I have commanded you to complete My favor upon you and that I desire your guidance, or it is in apposition to an implied reason such as: And fear Me so that I may protect you from them and complete My favor upon you, or so that it will not be. In the hadith, The completion of the favor is entering Paradise. And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, the completion of the favor is death as a Muslim.
2:151: 151- As We have sent among you a Messenger from among you is connected to what came before it, meaning, "And to complete My favor upon you in the matter of the Qiblah, or in the Hereafter as I completed it by sending a Messenger from among you, or in what comes after it as I reminded you of sending, so remember Me. "He recites to you Our verses and purifies you" He carries you to what makes you pure, He presented it in consideration of the intention and delayed it in the call of Abraham, peace be upon him, in consideration of the action "And teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you that which you did not know" by thought and contemplation, since there is no way to know it except through revelation, and the action was repeated to indicate that it is another type.
2:152: 152- Remember Me with obedience. I will remember you with reward. And be grateful to Me for what I have bestowed upon you. And do not be ungrateful by denying blessings and disobeying the command.
2:153: 153- O you who have believed, seek help through patience from sins and self-interests, and prayer which is the mother of all acts of worship and the ascension of the believers, and the communion with the Lord of the Worlds. Indeed, God is with the patient with victory and the answering of supplications.
2:154: 154- "And do not say of those who are killed in the way of God, 'They are dead,'" meaning they are dead. "Rather, they are alive. But you perceive not," what is their state? This is a warning that their life is not in the body nor of the same kind as what animals sense, but rather it is something that cannot be perceived by reason, but rather by revelation. And from Al-Hasan (Indeed, the martyrs are alive with their Lord. Their provisions are presented to their souls, and the spirit and joy reach them, just as the fire is presented to the souls of the people of Pharaoh, morning and evening, and pain and suffering reach them.) The verse was revealed about the martyrs of Badr, and they were fourteen. It indicates that the souls are substances that exist in themselves, different from what is sensed in the body, and they remain perceptible after death. The majority of the Companions and Followers agreed on this, and the verses and Sunnahs spoke of it. And on this, the martyrs were singled out for their special closeness to God the Most High, and for increased joy and dignity.
2:155: 155- And We will surely test you and We will surely afflict you with the affliction of those who test your conditions, will you be patient in the face of affliction and submit to the decree? with something of fear and hunger meaning with a little of that, and He only made it small in relation to what He protected them from in order to make it easier for them, and to show them that His mercy will not leave them, or in relation to what will befall their opponents in the Hereafter, and He only informed them of it before it happened so that they would prepare themselves for it. And a loss of wealth and lives and fruits is a conjunction of something, or fear, and from Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, fear is the fear of God, and hunger is the fasting of Ramadan, and the loss is from wealth, charity and zakat, and from lives: diseases, and from fruits, the death of children. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “When a servant’s child dies, God Almighty says to the angels: ‘Have you taken the soul of My servant’s child?’ They say: ‘Yes.’ God Almighty says: ‘Have you taken the fruit of his heart?’ They say: ‘Yes.’ God Almighty says: ‘What did My servant say?’ They say: ‘He praised You and sought refuge in You.’ God Almighty says: ‘Build for My servant a house in Paradise, a house of praise.’ And give good tidings to the patient.”
2:156: 156- Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, 'Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return.' The address is to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to whomever brings him good report. The word calamity includes any harm that befalls a person, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Everything that harms a believer is a calamity for him. Patience is not by saying return to God with the tongue, but rather by it and in the heart, by imagining what he was created for, and that he will return to his Lord, and remembering God's blessings upon him so that he sees that what remains for him is many times what he was restored to, so it becomes easy for him, and he submits to it, and the one who is given good report is omitted and indicated.
2:157: 157-Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. Prayer is originally a supplication, and from God the Most High is purification and forgiveness. It is pluralized to indicate its abundance and variety. What is meant by mercy is kindness and goodness. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever seeks refuge in God from a calamity, God will compensate for his calamity, make his end good, and grant him a righteous successor whom He wills. "And those are the ones who are guided" to the truth and right path, as they seek refuge in God and submit to the decree of God the Most High.
2:158: 158- Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are two mountains in Mecca. Among the symbols of God are signs of His rituals, the plural of sha'irah which is a mark. So whoever performs Hajj or 'Umrah Hajj linguistically means intention, and 'Umrah means visiting. So they are predominant in the Shari'ah for intending the House and visiting it in the two specific ways. There is no blame upon him for walking between them Isaf was on As-Safa and Na'ilah was on Marwah, and the people of the Jahiliyyah used to touch them when they walked. When Islam came and the idols were broken, the Muslims were embarrassed to walk between them, so this was revealed. There is consensus that it is prescribed in Hajj and 'Umrah, but the difference of opinion is over its obligation. Ahmad reported that it is a Sunnah, and Anas and Ibn 'Abbas may God be pleased with them reported it, based on his saying: There is no blame upon him, as it is understood from it that he has a choice, which is weak, because denying blame indicates permissibility that is included in the meaning of obligation, so it does not negate it. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said that it is obligatory and must be compensated for by blood. Malik and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them, said that it is a pillar based on the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Strive, for God has prescribed striving for you. “And whoever volunteers good” means he performs an act of obedience, whether it is obligatory or voluntary, or does more than what God has prescribed for him of Hajj or Umrah, or Tawaf, or volunteers to do Sa’i if we say that it is a Sunnah. Good is in the accusative case because it is an attribute of a deleted source, or by deleting the preposition and connecting the verb to it, or by making the verb transitive because it includes the meaning of came or did. Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read it, and its original form is yatadhu’, so it was assimilated like yatawuf. For God is Appreciative, Knowing rewards for obedience that is not hidden from Him.
2:159: 159- Those who conceal such as the Jewish rabbis. What We have sent down of clear proofs such as the verses bearing witness to the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And guidance and what guides to the obligation to follow it and believe in it. After We have made it clear to the people We have summarized it. In the Book in the Torah. Those are cursed by God and cursed by those who curse meaning those who are able to curse them from the angels and the two heavy burdens.
2:160: 160- Except for those who repent from concealing and all that must be repented from and put right what they corrupted by making up for it. And make clear what God made clear in their book so that their repentance would be complete. It was said that what they innovated from repentance was to erase the mark of disbelief from themselves and for their peers to follow their example. Then those I will turn to with acceptance and forgiveness. And I am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful the one who goes to great lengths in accepting repentance and bestowing mercy.
2:161: 161- Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers meaning, and those who did not repent from the concealers until they died, upon them is the curse of God and the angels and the people all together The curse from God has been established upon them, and whoever among His creation takes His curse into account. It was said, the first cursed them while they were alive, and this cursed them while they were dead. And it was read, and the angels and the people all together in apposition to the place of the name of God because it is the subject in meaning, like your saying, I liked the beating of Zaid and Amr, or the subject of an implied verb like and the angels curse them.
2:162: 162- They will abide therein meaning in the curse, or in the fire. The omission of it before mentioning it is to magnify its importance and to intimidate it, or to suffice with the indication of the curse upon it. The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved meaning they will not be given respite, or they will not wait to apologize, or they will not be looked at with mercy.
2:163: 163- And your God is one God is a general address, meaning the one among you who deserves to be worshipped is one, with no partner who can be worshipped or called a god. There is no god but He is a confirmation of oneness, and a way to remove the notion that there is a god in existence but who does not deserve to be worshipped. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful is like an argument against it, because since He is the Master of all blessings, their origins and branches, and everything else is either a blessing or a benefactor, no one else deserves to be worshipped except Him. These are two other pieces of report for His saying your God, or for an omitted subject. It was said that when the polytheists heard it, they were amazed and said: If you are truthful, then bring us a sign by which we will know your truthfulness. So it was revealed.
2:164: 164- Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth The heavens and the individuals of the earth are plural, because they are separate layers in themselves, different in reality, unlike the two earths. And the alternation of night and day is their succession, as in the Almighty's saying: He made the night and the day in succession. "And the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people meaning that which benefits them, or with that which benefits them, and the intention is to provide evidence from the sea and its conditions, and to specify the mention of the ship" because it is the reason for delving into it and learning about its wonders, and for this reason it is presented before mentioning rain and clouds, because their origin is the sea in most cases, and the feminization of "the ship" because it means a ship. It was read with two dammahs according to the original, or the plural, and the dammah of the plural is not the dammah of the singular according to the investigators. "And what God has sent down from the sky of water" from the first for the beginning, and the second for clarification. And the sky includes the ship and the clouds and the direction of the height. And He revived thereby the earth after its death with plants and dispersed therein every kind of creature is in apposition to sent down, as if he used as evidence the descent of rain and the formation of plants by it and the dispersion of animals in the earth, or revived, because the creatures grow through fertility and live through life. Dispersion means spreading and dispersing. And the disposition of the winds in their auras and conditions. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it in the singular. And the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth do not descend or disperse, although nature requires one of them until the command of God Almighty comes. It was said: The clouds controlled by their turning in the atmosphere by the will of God Almighty, and its derivation is from the clouds because some of them drag others. Signs for a people who reason who ponder them and look at them with the eyes of their minds. And it was reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Woe to the one who reads this verse and is distracted by it meaning he did not ponder it. Know that the evidence of these verses for the existence of God and His Oneness is from many aspects that would take a long time to explain in detail. The general statement is that they are: possible matters, each of which exists in a specific way from possible aspects and different ways. For example, it is possible that the heavens, or some of them like the earth, do not move, and that they move in the opposite direction of their movements, and that the region becomes a circle passing through the poles, and that it does not have a peak or a nadir at all. In this way, due to its simplicity and the equality of its parts, it must have a powerful and wise director who creates it according to what His wisdom calls for and His will requires, transcending the opposition of others, since if there was a god with Him who is able to do what the other is able to do. If their wills agree, then if the action is theirs, then it is necessary for two influencers to come together on one effect. If it is for one of them, then it is necessary to give preference to the doer without a preference and to exclude the other, which is contrary to His divinity. If they differ, then it is necessary to contradict and chase each other, as indicated by His Almighty saying: If there were within them gods besides God, they both would have been ruined. The verse draws attention to the honor of the science of theology and its people, and urges research and consideration into it.
2:165: 165- And among mankind are those who take for themselves rivals to God of idols. It was said that they were the leaders whom they obeyed, based on the Almighty's statement: When those who were followed disassociated themselves from those they followed Perhaps what is meant is more general than both of them, which is what distracts him from God. They love them they glorify them and obey them as the love of God as glorifying Him and inclining to obey Him, meaning they treat Him and them equally in love and obedience. Love is the inclination of the heart from love, it was borrowed for the grain of the heart, then love was derived from it because it affected it and became rooted in it. The love of the servant for God the Almighty is the desire to obey Him and to take care to obtain what pleases Him, and the love of God for the servant is the desire to honor him and use him in obedience, and to protect him from sins. And those who believe are stronger in love for God because their love for God Almighty does not cease, unlike the love of rivals, which is for corrupt, imaginary purposes that disappear at the slightest cause. Therefore, they would turn away from their gods to God Almighty during times of hardship, and they would worship the idol for a time, then reject it for something else. And if only those who did wrong could see And if only these wrongdoers knew about taking rivals to God when they see the punishment when they witness it on the Day of Resurrection. And the future was made to follow the course of the past because it will be realized, as God Almighty said: And the companions of Paradise will call out. All power belongs to God is the object of sees, and the answer to if is omitted. That is, if they knew that all power belongs to God, when they saw the punishment, they would regret it intensely. It was said that it is the object of the answer and the two objects are omitted, and the meaning is: And if those who did wrong saw that their rivals do not benefit, they would know that all power belongs to God, and no one else benefits or harms. Ibn Amir, Nafi' and Ya'qub read: And if you saw as an address to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that is, if you saw that, you would see a great matter. Ibn Amir: When they see is in the passive form, and Ya'qub: If with the kasra, and so is and that God is severe in punishment as a new sentence, or the statement is omitted.
2:166: 166- When those who followed disavowed those who followed instead of when they see, meaning when the led disavowed the followers. It was read the opposite way, meaning the followers disavowed the leaders. And they saw the punishment meaning seeing it, and the waw is for the state, and it has been implied. It was said, it is in apposition to disavowed. And the causes were cut off from them may be in apposition to disavowed, or they saw, and the waw is for the state, and the first is more apparent. The causes: the connection that was between them from the followers and the agreement on the religion, and the purposes calling for that. The origin of the cause: the rope by which one climbs the tree. It was read and was cut off in the passive form.
2:167: 167- And those who followed said, 'If only we had another chance to return, we could disown them as they disowned us.' "If" is for wishing, and therefore it was answered with the letter fa, meaning, if only we had another chance to return to the world, we could disown them. "Likewise" is like those terrible opinions. "God will show them their deeds as regrets for them. Regrets, and they are the third object of see" if it is from the vision of the heart, otherwise it is a condition. "And they will not come out of the Fire. Its original form is and they will not come out," so it was changed to this expression, to exaggerate the eternity and despair of salvation and returning to the world.
2:168: 168- O mankind, eat from whatever is on the earth [that is] lawful. This was revealed about a people who forbade themselves fine foods and clothing. Halal is the object of eat, or an adjective of a deleted source, or a state of what is on the earth. Min is for partiality, since everything on the earth is eaten good, which is deemed good by the law or by upright desire. Since halal indicates the first. And do not follow the footsteps of Satan, do not follow his example in following desires, forbidding what is lawful and permitting what is unlawful. Nafi', Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Bazzi, and Abu Bakr read it with a sukoon on the ta, where it occurred. They are two dialects for the plural of khutwa, which is what is between the feet of the sinner. It was read with two dammahs and a hamza, making the dammah of the ta’ as if it were on it, and with two fathahs, as it is the plural of khatwa, which is the time of khatwa. Indeed, he is a clear enemy to you. The enmity is apparent to those with insight, even if he appears to be loyal to the one who misleads him. That is why he called him a guardian in the Almighty’s saying: Their allies are the false gods.
2:169: 169- He only orders you to do evil and immorality is a statement of his enmity and the necessity of avoiding following him. The command was used metaphorically to adorn him and send them to evil, belittling their opinion and degrading their status. Evil and immorality are what the mind rejects and the Shari'ah finds ugly. The conjunction is due to the difference between the two descriptions, as evil is due to the mind being concerned about it, and immorality is due to its being found ugly. It was said: evil includes all ugly things, and immorality is what exceeds the limit in ugliness among the major sins. It was said: the first is what has no limit, and the second is what has been legislated for. And that you say about God what you do not know such as taking rivals, making forbidden things permissible, and forbidding good things. It is evidence of the prohibition of following conjecture completely. As for the mujtahid following what he leads to based on conjecture based on a Shari'ah-based evidence, its obligation is definite, and conjecture is in a way as we explained in the books of Usul.
2:170: 170-And when it is said to them, Follow what God has revealed," the pronoun refers to the people, and the address is changed from them to call out their misguidance, as if he turned to the rational people and said to them: Look at these fools, what do they answer? "They say, Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing, what we found them doing. It was revealed about the polytheists who were ordered to follow the Qur'an and all the other proofs and verses that God revealed, but they turned to imitation. It was said about a group of Jews whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called to Islam, but they said: Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing because they were better than us and more knowledgeable. Based on this, what God revealed includes the Torah because it also calls to Islam. Or even if their fathers did not understand anything and were not guided, the waw is for the state, or the conjunction. The hamza is for response and amazement. The answer to if is omitted, meaning if their fathers were ignorant and did not think about the matter of religion, nor were they guided to the truth, they would have followed them. This is evidence of the prohibition of imitation for those who are able to consider and exert effort. As for following others in religion if it is known by some evidence that they are correct, such as the prophets and those who exert effort in rulings, then in reality it is not imitation but rather following what God has revealed.
2:171: 171- And the example of those who disbelieve is like the example of one who cries to something that hears nothing but a call and a cry with the omission of an added noun, meaning: And the example of the caller of those who disbelieve is like the example of one who cries, or the example of those who disbelieve is like the example of the animals that cries. The meaning is that the disbelievers, because they are preoccupied with imitation, do not pay attention to what is recited to them, nor do they ponder what is decided with them, so they are in that like the animals that are cawed at, so they hear the sound but do not know its significance, and sense the call but do not understand its meaning. It was said that it is a representation of them in following their fathers according to their apparent state, ignorant of its reality, like the animals that hear the sound but do not understand what is beneath it. Or their representation in their calling to the idols, like the cawer in his caw, which is the sounding of the animals, and this suffices for the implication, but it is not supported by his saying nothing but a call and a cry, because the idols do not hear, unless it is made from the category of compound representation. Deaf, dumb and blind is a noun of blame. They do not understand means actually, due to the lack of vision.
2:172: 172- O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you. Since He has made the command broad for all people and permitted them what is on earth, evil of what was forbidden to them, He commanded the believers among them to seek out the good things which they have been provided with and to fulfill their rights, so He said: And be grateful to God for what He has provided you with and made lawful for you. If it is Him that you worship. If it is true that you single Him out for worship and acknowledge that He is the Master of blessings, then His worship is not complete except with gratitude. So what is connected to an action is the command to be grateful for its completion, and it is nonexistent when it is not. And from the Prophet, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, "God the Most High says, 'Indeed, I and mankind and the jinn are in a momentous matter. I create and others worship Me, and I provide and others thank Me.'"
2:173: 173- He has only forbidden you dead animals to eat or benefit from them. It is that which died without being slaughtered. The hadith included with it what is clearly alive. Fish and locusts were excluded by custom or by the exception of the Shari'a. The prohibition added to the object indicates by custom the prohibition of dealing with it absolutely except for what is specified by evidence, such as dealing with tanned animals. Blood and the flesh of swine The meat was mentioned specifically because it is the most eaten of the animal and the rest of its parts are like those attached to it. And that which is dedicated to other than God meaning raising the voice when slaughtering it for an idol. The origin of the ihram is seeing the crescent moon, it is said: the crescent moon and I declared it. However, since it is customary to raise the voice with takbir when it is seen, it was called ihram, then it was said to raise the voice even if it is for someone other than him. But whoever is forced by necessity, without desiring anything by monopolizing another forced person. Asim, Abu Amr and Hamzah read with a kasra on the letter nun z: nor did he return to satiate hunger or thirst. It was said: not a transgressor against the ruler. Nor did he return to robbing the road. Based on this, it is not permissible for the sinner to travel, and this is the apparent view of the Shafi’i school of thought and the statement of Ahmad, may God have mercy on them both. There is no sin upon him in consuming it. Indeed, God is Forgiving for what he did. Merciful by permitting it. If it is said: It only indicates restricting the ruling to what was mentioned, and how many prohibitions were not mentioned. I say: What is meant is restricting the prohibition to what was mentioned of what they deemed permissible, not absolutely, or restricting its prohibition to a state of choice, as if it was said: These things were only forbidden to you unless you were compelled to do them.
2:174: 174- "Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book and exchange it for a small price" a lowly exchange. "Those eat nothing into their bellies except the Fire" either in the present case, because they ate what is associated with the Fire because it is a punishment for it, so it is as if he ate the Fire, as in His saying: I would eat blood if I did not smite you with a distant rival, the destination of the earring is good, the spreader It means blood money. Or in the final destination, meaning they will eat nothing on the Day of Resurrection but fire. The meaning of in their bellies is: filling their bellies. It is said: he ate in his stomach and he ate in some of his stomach, as in the saying: Eat together and you will be forgiven And God will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection refers to His anger, and hints at their being deprived of the honor and closeness to God when they meet Him. Nor will He purify them does not praise them. And for them is a painful punishment painful.
2:175: 175- Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance in this world. And punishment in exchange for forgiveness in the Hereafter, by concealing the truth for worldly purposes and purposes. How patient they are in the Fire. He is amazed at their state in being confused by the requirements of the Fire without caring. And what is complete and raised by the beginning, and its specification is like the specification of their saying. Evil is this fang Or interrogative and what follows it is the predicate, or relative and what follows it is a connection and the predicate is omitted.
2:176: 176- That is because God sent down the Book with the truth meaning that this punishment is because God sent down the Book with the truth and they rejected it by denying it or concealing it. And those who differed over the Book the lam in it is either for the genus, and their difference is their belief in some of God's books and their disbelief in others. Or it is for the covenant, and the reference is either to the Torah, and they differed in the sense that they deviated from the straight path in interpreting it, or they deviated from what God sent down in its place, meaning they distorted what is in it. Or it is to the Qur'an and their difference in it, their saying magic, and saying, and speech taught to a human being, and legends of the ancients. are in a far schism are in a far disagreement from the truth.
2:177: 177- Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west. "Righteousness" is every act that is good, and the address is to the People of the Book, for they have frequently discussed the matter of the Qiblah when it was changed, and each group claimed that righteousness is turning toward its Qiblah, so God Almighty responded to them and said, Righteousness is not what you are upon, for it has been abrogated, but righteousness is what God has made clear and the believers follow. And it was said that it is general for them and the Muslims, meaning righteousness is not limited to the matter of the Qiblah, or is not the great righteousness that it is good for you to be oblivious to its matter other than its matter, and Hamzah and Hafs read "righteousness in the accusative case but righteousness is he who believes in God and the Last Day and the angels and the Book and the prophets" meaning but the righteousness that should be concerned with is the righteousness of he who believes in God, or but the righteous is he who believes, and this is supported by the reading of the one who read but the righteous. The first is more appropriate and better. What is meant by the Book is the genus, or the Qur'an. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read "but with a lightened vowel and raised righteousness. And give wealth out of love for it" meaning out of love for money. When he was asked which charity is best, he said, "That you give it while you are healthy and stingy, hoping to live and fearing poverty." It was said that the pronoun refers to God, or to the source. The preposition and noun are in the place of the state. "Relatives and orphans" means those among them who are in need, and it was not restricted to avoid confusion. He mentioned relatives first because giving to them is better, as he said, peace and blessings be upon him, "Your charity given to a poor person is charity, and to your relatives it is two things: charity and maintaining ties of kinship. The needy is the plural of the needy", which is the one who has been made inhabited by friendship, and its root is permanent stillness, like the drunkard is the one who is always drunk. "The wayfarer" is the traveler, so called because he stays on the road, just as the highwayman is called the son of the road. It was said that the guest is the one who is fed up with the way. "And the beggars" are those who are forced by need to beg, and he, peace and blessings be upon him, said, "The beggar has a right, even if he comes on his horse. And in the necks" and in freeing them with the help of those who have been freed, or releasing captives, or buying slaves to free them. "And establishes the prayer" the obligatory prayer. "And gives the zakat" it is possible that what is meant by it and his saying: "And gives the wealth" is the obligatory zakat, but the purpose of the first is to explain its expenditures, and of the second is to perform it and encourage it. It is possible that what is meant by the first is voluntary charity or rights that were in the wealth other than zakat. In the hadith: "Zakat has abrogated all charity. And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made a covenant is in apposition to whoever believes. And those who are patient in poverty and hardship" is in the accusative case for praise and is not in apposition because patience is superior to all other deeds. Al-Azhari said: poverty in wealth is like poverty, and hardship in the soul is like sickness. "And at the time of battle" the time of fighting the enemy. "Those are the ones who are truthful" in religion and following the truth and seeking righteousness. "And those are the righteous" from disbelief and all other vices. The verse, as you can see, is a collection of all human words, indicating them explicitly or implicitly. They are, in their multiplicity and complexity, limited to three things: sound belief, good treatment, and self-discipline. The first is indicated by His saying: Whoever believes in God to and the prophets. The second is indicated by His saying: And gives wealth to and for the freeing of slaves. The third is indicated by His saying: And establishes prayer to the end. Therefore, the one who performs it is described as truthful in view of his faith and belief in piety, considering his interaction with people and dealings with the Truth. And this is what he referred to in his saying, peace be upon him, Whoever acts according to this verse has completed his faith.
2:178: 178- "O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution for those murdered: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female." In the pre-Islamic era, there was a blood feud between two tribes of the Arabs, and one of them had a long history with the other, so they swore, We will kill the free among you for the slave for the female. When Islam came, they went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for judgment, and it was revealed, and he ordered them to take revenge. It does not indicate that a free man should not be killed for a slave, nor a male for a female, just as it does not indicate the opposite, because the concept, where the purpose of the specification did not appear, was to specify the ruling, and we have explained what the purpose was. Rather, Malik and Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with them, forbade killing a free man for a slave, whether he was his slave or someone else's slave, because of what was narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him: A man killed his slave, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, flogged him and banished him for a year and did not retaliate for him. It was narrated that he said: It is from the Sunnah that a Muslim should not be killed for a person with a covenant, nor a free man for a slave. And because Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, did not kill a free man for a slave among the companions without any objection. And by analogy to the parties, and whoever accepts its evidence, then he has no claim to abrogation by the saying of God the Almighty: A life for a life because it is a narration of what is in the Torah, so it does not abrogate what is in the Qur’an. The Hanafis used it as evidence that the requirement of premeditated murder is retaliation alone, and this is weak because what is obligatory based on choice is true of it as being obligatory and written, and therefore it was said that choosing between what is obligatory and something else is not abrogation of its obligation. And it was read wrote in the active form and retaliation in the accusative, and so is every verb that came in the Qur’an. So whoever is pardoned by his brother anything meaning any of the pardon, because pardon is obligatory. Its benefit is to indicate that some of the pardon is like complete pardon in dropping the retaliation. And it was said that pardon means left, and something is the object, and this is weak because it was not proven that pardoning something means leaving it, but rather he pardoned it. And the word forgave is transitive to the offender and to the sin. God the Almighty said, God has forgiven you and said, God has forgiven what is past. So if it is transitive to the sin, it is transitive to the offender with the letter lam and it is understood from the verse as if it was said: So whoever has been forgiven for his crime on behalf of his brother, meaning the blood money avenger. And he mentioned him with the expression of brotherhood established between them in terms of nationality and Islam to show compassion and kindness to him. Then follow up with kindness and pay it to him with goodness. That is, let there be following, or the matter is following. What is meant by it is the command of the forgiver to ask for the blood money with kindness and not be violent, and the forgiven to pay it with kindness: that is, not to delay or reduce. And in it is evidence that blood money is one of the requirements of intention, otherwise the command to pay it would not have been made conditional on absolute forgiveness. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, has two opinions on the issue. That meaning the ruling mentioned in forgiveness and blood money. A mitigation from your Lord and a mercy because of what is in it of facilitation and benefit. It was said that retaliation was prescribed for the Jews alone, and forgiveness was prescribed for the Christians in general. This nation was given the choice between them and the blood money to make things easier for them and to determine the ruling according to their ranks. But whoever transgresses after that meaning kills after the pardon and taking the blood money, will have a painful punishment in the Hereafter. It was said that in this world he will inevitably be killed, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him, I will not pardon anyone who kills after taking the blood money.
2:179: 179- And there is life for you in retaliation is a statement of the utmost eloquence and rhetoric in that it makes one thing the place of its opposite, and defines retaliation and denies life, to indicate that in this type of ruling there is a great kind of life, because knowledge of it deters the killer from killing, so it is the reason for the life of two souls. And because they used to kill someone other than the killer, and the group for one, so strife would arise between them. So if retaliation is taken from the killer, the rest would be safe, so that would be the reason for their life. According to the first, there is an implication in it, and according to the second, there is a specification. It was said: What is meant by it is the afterlife, because if the killer is retaliated against in this world, he will not be held accountable for it in the afterlife. And there is life for you in retaliation may be two pieces of report for life, and one of them may be report and the other a connection to it, or a state of the pronoun hidden in it. And it was read in the stories, meaning in what was told to you of the ruling on killing, life, or in the Qur'an, life for the hearts. O you of understanding those with perfect minds. He called them to contemplate the wisdom of retribution in preserving lives and protecting souls. Perhaps you will become righteous in preserving retribution, ruling by it, and submitting to it, or in refraining from retribution and refraining from killing.
2:180: 180- It is prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you meaning its causes are present and its signs appear. If he leaves behind wealth meaning money. It was said a lot of money, because it was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that a slave of his wanted to make a will and he had seven hundred dirhams, but he prevented him and said: God, the Most High, said, If he leaves behind wealth and wealth is a lot of money. And on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that a man wanted to make a will, so she asked him how much money he had, and he said, Three thousand. She said, How many are your dependents? He said, Four. She said, God, the Most High, said, If he leaves behind wealth and that this is a small thing, so leave it for your dependents. "The will is for parents and relatives is raised by wrote, and the masculine of its action is for separation, or on the interpretation that he wills, or the will, and that is why the referent was mentioned in His statement, So whoever changes it. The agent in if is the meaning of wrote", not the will, because it precedes it. It was said that it is a subject and its predicate is for the parents, and the sentence is the answer to the condition by implying the fa, like his saying: Whoever does good deeds, God will reward them, and evil is recompensed for evil in the sight of God. It was replied that if it is true, it is one of the necessities of poetry. This ruling was in the beginning of Islam, but it was abrogated by the verse on inheritance and by the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “Indeed, God has given the one who has a right his right. Beware, there is no bequest for an heir.” There is a view on this, because the verse on inheritance does not contradict it, but rather confirms it in that it indicates the priority of the bequest in general, and the hadith is from the individual narrators, and the acceptance of the ummah of it does not make it equal to the mutawatir. Perhaps he who interpreted the bequest as what God has commanded of the inheritance of parents and relatives has reserved it by saying: God commands you. Or as the bequest of the dying person to them to provide what God has commanded them to do in a reasonable manner with justice, so that he does not give preference to the rich, nor does he exceed a third. A right upon the righteous is a confirmed source, meaning that is a right.
2:181: 181- But whoever changes it another of the guardians and witnesses. After he has heard it meaning it has reached him and he has verified it, then the sin is upon those who change it so the sin of the changed will or the change is only upon those who change it because they are the ones who have deviated and violated the law. Indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing is a warning to the one who changes it unjustly.
2:182: 182- So whoever fears a testator i.e. expects and knows, from their saying I fear that the sky will send. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Ya'qub and Abu Bakr read a testator with emphasis. Janfan meaning a mistake in the will. Or sin deliberately committing injustice. So reconcile between them between those to whom the testator directed by making them follow the path of the Shari'ah. There is no sin upon him in this change, because it is a false change to the truth, unlike the first. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful is a promise to the reformer, and the mention of forgiveness is in agreement with the mention of sin and the action is of the same type as what is sinful.
2:183: 183- O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you meaning the prophets and nations since Adam, peace be upon him, and it confirms the ruling and encourages action and makes the soul happy. Fasting in the language means abstaining from what the soul is inclined to, and in the Shari'ah: abstaining from things that break the fast during the day, as they are most of what the soul desires. That you may guard against sins, as fasting breaks the desire that is its beginning, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, So let him fast, for fasting is a shield for him or failure to perform it due to its originality and precedence.
2:184: 184- A few days are timed with a known number, or few. A little money is counted as a number and a lot is a trivial amount. Its accusative is not with fasting because of the separation between them, but with the implication of fast because fasting indicates it, and what is meant by it is Ramadan or what was obligatory to fast before it was obligatory and was abrogated by it, which is Ashura or three days of every month, or as it was written on the circumstance, or that it is a second object for was prescribed for you on the spaciousness. It was said that its meaning is your fasting is like their fasting in the number of days, because it was narrated: Ramadan was prescribed for the Christians, and it occurred in extreme cold or heat, so they changed it to spring and added twenty expiations to it to change it. It was said that they added that for a death that befell them. So whoever among you is ill with an illness that harms or makes fasting difficult. Or on a journey or a traveler, and in it is an allusion to the fact that whoever travels during the day does not break his fast. Then a number of other days means he must fast the number of days of illness, or of travel from other days if he breaks the fast. The condition, the complement, and the complement to it were omitted because they are known. It was read in the accusative case, meaning let him fast a number, and this is by way of concession. It was said that it is obligatory, and this is the view of the Zahiris, and Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him said the same. And upon those who are able to do it means upon those who are able to fast if they break the fast. The ransom is the feeding of a poor person means half a sa' of wheat or a sa' of other than it according to the jurists of Iraq, and a mudd according to the jurists of Hijaz. They were initially given concession for that when they were ordered to fast, but it was difficult for them because they were not accustomed to it, then it was abrogated. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read according to the narration of Ibn Dhakwan by adding the ransom to the food and pluralizing the poor. Ibn Amir read, according to the narration of Hisham, masakeen without adding the ransom to the food, and the rest without adding it and unifying masakeen. It was read yatuwaqunhu meaning they burden him and they imitate him in the roads, meaning the energy or necklace, and yatuwaqunhu meaning they burden him, or they imitate him and they imitate him with assimilation, and yatuwaqunhu and yatuwaqunhu on the basis that their origin is yatuwaqunhu from fa’il and taf’il meaning they imitate him and they imitate him, and according to these readings, a second meaning is possible, which is the permission for those who are tired and exhausted by fasting - and they are the elderly and the old - to break the fast and pay the ransom, so it is fixed and the famous reading was interpreted by it, meaning they fast it to the best of their ability and capacity. So whoever volunteers good so he added to the ransom. It is so the volunteering or the good. “It is better for him and that you fast” you who are able, or those who are able and you have exerted your energy. Or those who are permitted to break the fast so that the sick and the traveler fall under it. It is better for you than the ransom or volunteering good or both of them and from delaying it to make up for it. If you knew what virtue there is in fasting and the release of conscience, and its answer is omitted and indicated by what preceded it, i.e. you chose it. And it was said that its meaning is if you are people of knowledge and contemplation, you would know that fasting is better for you than that.
2:185: 185- The month of Ramadan is a subject whose predicate is what follows it, or a predicate of a deleted subject, the meaning of which is that is the month of Ramadan, or a substitute for fasting by deleting the complement, i.e. fasting is prescribed for you, the fasting of the month of Ramadan. It was read in the accusative case with the omission of fast, or as an object, and that you fast and there is weakness in it, or a substitute for a numbered day. The month: from fame, and Ramadan: the source of ramadh if it burns, so the month was added to it and made a proper noun and prevented from being declined for being a proper noun and the alif and the nun, just as da'iyah in ibn da'iyah was prevented as a proper noun for the crow for being a proper noun and feminine, and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, Whoever fasts Ramadan is based on the deletion of the complement to avoid confusion, and they called it that either because they are burning in it from the heat of hunger and thirst, or because sins are burning in it, or because it falls during the days of the heat of Ramadan when they transferred the names of the months from the ancient language. In which the Qur’an was revealed means that its revelation began in it, and that was the Night of Decree, or it was revealed in it all at once to the lowest heaven and then it was revealed in stages to the earth, or the Qur’an was revealed concerning it, which is His statement: Fasting is prescribed for you.
