And on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “The scrolls of Abraham, peace be upon him, were revealed on the first night of Ramadan, and the Torah was revealed on the sixth, and the Gospel on the thirteenth, and the Qur’an on the twenty-fourth.” And the relative clause is the predicate of the subject or its description, and the predicate is whoever witnesses, and the fa is for describing the subject with what includes the meaning of the condition. And in it is an indication that the revelation in it is the reason for it being specific to the obligation of fasting. A guidance for mankind and clear proofs of guidance and criterion are two states of the Qur’an, that it was revealed while it is guidance for mankind, a miracle and clear verses that guide to the truth and differentiate between it and falsehood with what it contains of wisdom and rulings. So whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it. So whoever is present in the month and is not traveling, let him fast it. The original is So whoever witnesses it, let him fast it. For you, the apparent is placed in place of the first implied for emphasis, and the accusative is in the circumstance, and the preposition is omitted, and the second pronoun is in the accusative for expansion. It was said: So whoever witnesses the crescent of the month, let him fast it, as a direct object, like your saying: I witnessed the Friday prayer, meaning its prayer. So And whoever is ill or on a journey, then an equal number of other days is specific to it, because the traveler and the ill are among those who witness the month. Perhaps the repetition is for that reason, or so that it is not thought that it was abrogated, as is its context. God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship meaning He wants to make it easy for you and not make it difficult. For that reason He permitted breaking the fast when traveling and sick. And that you may complete the number and glorify God for having guided you, and perhaps you will be grateful. Give reasons for an omitted verb indicated by what came before, that is, and explain the whole of what was mentioned about the command of the witness to fast the month and the permission to make up for it and to observe the number of days he broke his fast in, and the permission to complete the number to the end is by way of wrapping up, for His saying and that you may complete the number is the reason for the command to observe the number, and that you may glorify God is the reason for the command to make up for it and explaining how it is done, and perhaps you will be grateful is the reason for the permission and facilitation. Or the verbs are each for its action, or conjoined with an implied reason such as to make it easy for you, or to know what you know and to complete the number, and it is permissible to conjoin with ease, that is, He wants you to complete it, like His saying, They want to extinguish the light of God. The meaning of glorification is to magnify God by praising and thanking Him, and for this reason it is transitive with ala. It was said that it is the Takbir of the Day of Eid al-Fitr, and it was said that it is the Takbir at the beginning of the month of Ramadan and what the source and the report may contain, meaning that which He guided you to. And from Asim, according to the narration of Abu Bakr, And that you may complete it with emphasis. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 3 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the next verses of Sūrat l-Baqarah. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 2:186: - And when My servants ask you concerning Me, indeed I am near. That is, say to them, I am near. This is a representation of His perfect knowledge of the actions and words of His servants and His awareness of their conditions in a state of His nearness to them. It was narrated that a Bedouin said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Is our Lord near so that we may commune with Him, or is He far so that we may call upon Him? So the verse was revealed, I answer the call of the caller when he calls upon Me. This is a confirmation of the nearness and a promise to the caller to be answered. So let them respond to Me if I call them to faith and obedience, just as I answer them when they call upon Me for their important matters. And let them believe in Me is an order to be steadfast and persistent in it. Perhaps they will be guided hoping to attain guidance, which is attaining the truth. It was read with the opening of the shin and its breaking. Know that when the Almighty commanded them to fast the month and observe the number, and urged them to perform the duties of glorification and thanks, He followed it with this verse, indicating that the Almighty is aware of their conditions, hears their words, answers their prayers, and rewards them for their deeds, as confirmation of this and urging it. Then He explained the rulings of fasting, saying:
2:187: 187- It is lawful for you on the night of fasting to have sexual relations with your wives. It was narrated that when the Muslims spent the evening, it was lawful for them to eat, drink, and have sexual intercourse until they prayed the last 'Isha' prayer or went to sleep. Then, 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, went after 'Isha' and regretted it. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and apologized to him. Some men stood up and confessed to what they had done after 'Isha'. So the following was revealed: "The night of fasting: the night in which you become fasting." And 'Isha' is a euphemism for sexual intercourse, because it is almost never devoid of 'Isha', which is disclosing what should be euphemistically referred to. It was transitive with 'Ila' because it includes the meaning of 'Isha', and it was preferred here to condemn what they had committed, and that is why he called it 'Treachery.'" And the rufuth was read: They are clothing for you and you are clothing for them. This is a resumption explaining the reason for the permissibility, which is the lack of patience with them, and the difficulty of avoiding them due to the frequent mixing and intense contact. And since the man and woman embrace and each one embraces the other, it was likened to clothing. Al-Ja’di said: If the bedfellow bends her elbow, she bends and becomes his garment. Or because each one of them covers the other's condition and prevents him from immorality. "God knows that you were betraying yourselves" you wronged yourselves by exposing them to punishment, and reducing their share of reward, and betrayal is more eloquent than betrayal, like acquisition is from earnings. "Then He turned to you" when you repented for what you committed. "And pardoned you" and erased its trace from you. "So now have sexual relations with them" when the prohibition was abrogated from you, and in it is evidence of the permissibility of abrogating the Sunnah by the Qur'an, and direct contact: the contact of the skin is a metaphor for intercourse. "And seek what God has decreed for you" and seek what He has destined for you and established in the Preserved Tablet of children, and the meaning is that the purpose of direct contact should be children, because it is the wisdom behind the creation of desire. And marriage was prescribed to satisfy desire, and it was said to prohibit withdrawal, and it was said about non-compulsory intercourse: and the meaning is and seek the place which God has decreed for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread. He likened the first thing that appears of the dawn crossing the horizon and the darkness of night that extends with it to two threads, white and black. He was satisfied with explaining the white thread by saying of dawn instead of explaining the black thread, because it indicates it. Thus, they departed from metaphor to representation. It is possible that min is for partiality, because what appears is some of the dawn. And what was narrated that it was revealed and it was not revealed from dawn, so men took two threads, black and white, and they continued to eat and drink until they could distinguish them, so it was revealed, if it is authentic, then perhaps it was before the beginning of Ramadan and delaying the explanation until the time of need is permissible, or it was sufficient first with their fame in that and then the explanation was stated because it was confused for some of them and in permitting intercourse until dawn there is evidence of the permissibility of delaying the ritual bath until that time and the validity of the fast of the one who is ritually impure in the morning. Then complete the fast until the night is a statement of the end of its time, and taking the night out of it negates the fast of continuous prayer. And do not have intercourse with them while you are in retreat in the mosques in retreat therein, and retreat is staying in the mosque with the intention of drawing near to God. What is meant by intercourse is sexual intercourse. According to Qatadah, a man would perform I’tikaf and go out to his wife and have intercourse with her, then return, so they were forbidden from that. This is evidence that I’tikaf is in the mosque and is not specific to a mosque rather than a mosque. And that intercourse is forbidden in it and spoils it because the prohibition in acts of worship leads to corruption. These are the limits set by God, meaning the rulings that were mentioned. So do not approach them. He forbade approaching the limit separating truth from falsehood lest falsehood come close to it, let alone transgress it. As the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, “Every king has a sanctuary, and God’s sanctuary is His prohibitions. So whoever grazes around the sanctuary is likely to fall into it.” This is more eloquent than his statement, So do not transgress them. It is possible that by the limits set by God he means His prohibitions and prohibitions. Likewise, such is the clarification, God makes clear His verses to the people that they may fear disobeying the commands and prohibitions.
2:188: 188- And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly meaning, do not consume one another's wealth in a manner that God has not permitted. And between is an accusative of circumstance, or a state of wealth. And send it to the rulers is in apposition to the prohibited, or is an accusative with the implication that, and ad-dila means throwing, meaning, do not send its ruling to the rulers. To consume by arbitration. A group is a sect. Of the wealth of the people in sin in a way that necessitates sin, such as false testimony and a false oath, or while you are immersed in sin. And you know that you are wrongdoers, because committing a sin while knowing it is worse. It was narrated that Abdun Al-Hadrami claimed a piece of land from Imru’ Al-Qais Al-Kindi, but he had no evidence. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that Imru’ Al-Qais should swear an oath. He wanted to do so, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price, so he refrained from swearing and handed the land over to Abdun. So this was revealed. This is evidence that the ruling of a judge is not enforceable inwardly, and it is supported by his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: “I am only a human being, and you bring your disputes to me. Perhaps some of you are more eloquent in presenting his argument than others, so I rule in his favor based on what I hear from him. So if I rule in his favor with something that is the right of his brother, I rule in his favor with a piece of fire.”
2:189: 189-They ask you about the new moons. Muadh bin Jabal and Tha'laba bin Ghanam asked him and said: What is the matter with the crescent moon that appears thin like a thread, then increases until it is equal, then continues to decrease until it returns to how it appeared? "Say: They are measurements of time for mankind and for Hajj." They asked about the wisdom in the changing state of the moon and its changing condition, so God commanded him to answer that the apparent wisdom in that is that they are landmarks for people to use to time their affairs, and landmarks for the timed acts of worship by which their times are known. Especially Hajj, as time is observed in it for performing and fulfilling. And the timings: the plural of miqat, from time, and the difference between it and the duration and time: that the absolute duration is the extension of the movement of the heavens from its beginning to its end. And time: a divided period, and time: the time appointed for a matter. And righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs. Nafi', Abu Amr, Warsh, and Hafs read it with a damma on the ba', and the rest read it with a kasra. But righteousness is of him who fears God. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read with a light but and a raised righteousness. When the Ansar entered ihram, they would not enter a house or a tent from its door, but would enter from a hole or an opening behind it, and they would consider that righteousness. So he explained to them that it was not righteousness, but rather righteousness is of he who fears the forbidden and desires. The connection between it and what came before it is that they asked about the two matters. Or that when he mentioned that they were the times of Hajj, and this was also one of their actions during Hajj, he mentioned it as a digression. Or that when they asked about what did not concern them and was not related to the knowledge of the Prophet and left asking about what concerned them and was specific to the knowledge of the Prophet, he followed it with mentioning the answer to what they asked, drawing attention to the fact that it was appropriate for them to ask such things and to be concerned with knowledge of them. Or that what was meant by it was to draw attention to their reversal in the question by likening their situation to the situation of someone who left the door of the house and entered from behind it. The meaning is: And righteousness is not that you reverse your questions, but righteousness is of he who fears that and does not dare to do something like it. And enter houses through their doors, for there is no righteousness in turning away, so approach matters from their proper perspective. And fear God, in changing His rulings and objecting to His actions. That you may succeed, so that you may attain guidance and righteousness.
2:190: 190- And fight in the cause of God strive to exalt His word and glorify His religion. Those who fight you It was said: That was before they were ordered to fight all the polytheists, the fighters among them and the ones who block their way. It was also said that its meaning is those who are hostile to you in fighting and it is expected from them, not others like the elderly, children, monks, women, or all the infidels, because they are about to fight the Muslims and intend to do so. The first is supported by what was narrated: That the polytheists repelled the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah, and they made peace with him on the condition that he would return the next year and they would leave Mecca - may God honor it - for him for three days, so he returned for the Umrah of Al-Qada' and the Muslims feared that they would not fulfill their promise to them and they would fight them in the Sacred Sanctuary or the Sacred Month, and they hated that, so And transgress not was revealed by initiating fighting, or by fighting in a treaty, or by surprise without being invited, or by mutilating, or by killing someone you were forbidden to kill. God does not love the aggressors. He does not want good for them.
2:191: 191-And kill them wherever you find them wherever you find them in a sanctuary or in a lawful place. The root of the word thaqaf is: skill in understanding something, whether it is knowledge or action. It includes the meaning of victory, and that is why it is used in this context. He said: If you find me, kill me, for whoever finds me will not live forever. And expel them from where they expelled you meaning from Mecca, and this was done to those who did not convert to Islam on the day of the conquest. And persecution is worse than killing meaning the trial that a person is tempted by, such as expulsion from one’s homeland, is more difficult than killing because of its constant fatigue and the pain it causes to the soul. It was said that its meaning is their association with you in the sanctuary and their preventing you from it is worse than your killing them in it. And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there meaning do not initiate fighting with them and violate the sanctity of al-Masjid al-Haram. And if they fight you, then kill them do not bother fighting them, then they are the ones who violated its sanctity. Hamzah and al-Kisa’i read “And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there. If they fight you” meaning until they kill some of you, like their saying We killed Banu Asad. “Such is the recompense of the disbelievers” like that is their recompense, they will be treated like what they did.
2:192: 192-If they desist from fighting and disbelief, then God is Forgiving and Merciful He will forgive them what has passed.
2:193: 193- And fight them until there is no more fitnah polytheism and religion is for God purely for Him, with no share in it for Satan. But if they desist from polytheism, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers meaning, do not transgress against those who desist, as it is not right to wrong anyone except the wrongdoer, so He put the reason in place of the ruling. And the punishment for injustice was called by its name for the sake of similarity, like His statement: But whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you. Or that if you attack those who desist, you become wrongdoers and the matter will be reversed against you, and the first fa is for consequence and the second is for punishment.
2:194: 194- A sacred month for a sacred month The polytheists fought them in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah in Dhul-Qi'dah, and it was their time to go out for the Umrah of Qada' in that month, and they hated to fight them in that month because of its sanctity, so they were told, This month is for that, and violating it is for violating it, so do not pay attention to it. "And sacred things are subject to retaliation" is an argument against it, meaning every sacred thing that must be preserved is subject to retaliation. So when they violated the sanctity of your month by turning away, do the same to them, and enter upon them by force and kill them if they fight you. As He said: "And whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you" and this is the gist of the statement. "And fear God" regarding the Ansar and do not transgress to what He has not given you permission. "And know that God is with the righteous" He protects them and reforms their affairs.
2:195: 195- And spend in the way of God and do not withhold completely. And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction by extravagance and wasting your livelihood, or by refraining from war and spending in it, because that strengthens the enemy and gives them power to destroy them. It is supported by what was narrated on the authority of Abu Ayoub Al-Ansari may God be pleased with him that he said: When God made Islam victorious and its people increased, we returned to our families and our wealth to reside in them and improve them. So it was revealed, or withholding and the love of wealth, for it leads to the supported destruction. Therefore, miserliness was called destruction, and in origin it is the end of something in corruption. And throwing: is throwing something, and it was transitive with ila to include the meaning of ending, and the ba is an extra letter and what is meant by hands are the souls, and destruction, perdition and destruction are one and the same, so it is a source like harm and pleasure, meaning do not throw yourselves into destruction. And it was said: Its meaning is do not let it take hold of your hands, or do not throw yourselves into it with your hands, so the object was deleted. And do good your deeds and morals, or be generous to those in need. Indeed, God loves the doers of good.
2:196: 196- And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God meaning, perform them in full, completing the rituals for the sake of God Almighty, and on this basis it indicates their obligation and is supported by the reading of those who read And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God, and what Jabir may God be pleased with him narrated "It was said, O Messenger of God, is Umrah obligatory like Hajj? He said: No, but if you perform Umrah it is better for you." This is opposed by what was narrated that a man said to Umar may God be pleased with him, I found Hajj and Umrah written down for me, so I entered into Ihram for both of them, so he said: I have been guided to the Sunnah of your Prophet. It cannot be said that he explained that they were written down by saying I entered into Ihram for them, so it is permissible for the obligation to be due to his entering into Ihram for them, because he arranged the entering into Ihram for the finding, and that indicates that it is the cause of the entering into Ihram and not the other way around. It was said that completing them is that you make ihram for them from your family circle, or that you separate a journey for each of them, or that you strip them for them without mixing them with a worldly purpose, or that the spending is lawful. If you are prevented means you are prevented. It is said that the enemy prevented him and detained him if he imprisoned him and prevented him from proceeding, like he stopped him and prevented him. What is meant is the enemy’s confinement according to Malik and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them, based on the Almighty’s saying: And when you are safe and its revelation in Al-Hudaybiyyah, and the saying of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them: There is no confinement except the enemy’s confinement and every prevention from an enemy or illness or other than that according to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, based on what was narrated from him, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, Whoever breaks or is lame has become ihram, so he must perform Hajj the following year. It is weak and is interpreted as meaning that the condition of ihram is based on his saying, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, to Duba’ah bint Al-Zubayr, “Perform Hajj and stipulate and say: O God, my place is where You have detained me.” And whatever is easy of the sacrifice, so you must do what is easy, or what is obligatory is what is easy. Or sacrifice what is easy. The meaning is that if the pilgrim is prevented and wants to exit ihram by slaughtering a sacrificial animal that is easy for him, from his own body, a cow or a sheep, according to the majority of scholars. Because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) slaughtered it in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah, and it is from the permissible areas. According to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, he sends it and assigns the one sent by him a day of guidance. When the day comes and he thinks that he has slaughtered, he exits ihram, based on the words of God, the Most High: And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal reaches its place. That is, do not exit ihram until you know that the sacrificial animal sent to the Sacred Sanctuary has reached its place, meaning the place where it is slaughtered. The first scholars interpreted the arrival of the sacrificial animal to mean slaughtering it where slaughtering is permissible, whether it is permissible in the Sacred Sanctuary or in the Sacred Sanctuary. Limiting it to the sacrificial animal is evidence of not making up the fast. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said that it is obligatory to make up the fast. The place in the kasra refers to place and time. The sacrificial animal is the plural of hadiyyah, like jady and jidya. It was read from the sacrificial animal, the plural of hadiyyah, like mount in mount. And whoever among you is ill, an illness that requires shaving his head. Or he has an injury to his head such as a wound or lice. "Then he must pay a ransom if he shaves. "From fasting or charity or sacrifice" is an explanation of the type of ransom. As for its amount, it was narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Ka'b ibn Ujrah, "Perhaps your vermin has hurt you. He said, Yes, O Messenger of God. He said, Shave and fast for three days or give a faraqah in charity to six poor people or sacrifice a sheep." The faraqah is three sa'. "Then when you are safe" from being prevented. Or you are in a state of ease and security. "Whoever performs 'Umrah until Hajj" whoever enjoys and benefits from drawing closer to God through 'Umrah before benefiting from drawing closer to God through Hajj during its months. It was said: whoever enjoys after being released from his 'Umrah by permitting the prohibitions of ihram until he enters ihram for Hajj. "Whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal" is obligatory for him because of the enjoyment, so it is a compensation blood that he slaughters when he enters ihram for Hajj and he does not eat from it. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said that if he regrets performing a ritual, it is like a sacrifice. But whoever does not find meaning the sacrificial animal. Then fast three days during Hajj during the days of being busy with it after entering ihram and before becoming released. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said in its months between the two ihrams, and it is preferable to fast the seventh, eighth and ninth of Dhul-Hijjah. Fasting on the Day of Sacrifice and the days of Tashreeq is not permissible according to the majority. And seven when you return to your families, which is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, or you have set out and finished your work, which is his second opinion and the school of Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him. Seven was read in the accusative case in apposition to the place of three days. “Those are ten” is the gist of the calculation, and its benefit is that no one should imagine that the and means or, like when you say, I sat with Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin. And to know the number as a whole as he knew in detail, for most Arabs did not know how to count, and that what is meant by seven is the number without the multitude, so complete is used for them as an emphatic description that indicates exaggeration in preserving the number, or indicating the perfection of ten, for it is the first complete number, for with it the ones end and their ranks are completed, or restricted, restricting the perfection of its replacement from the sacrifice. That is a reference to the ruling mentioned with us. And enjoyment according to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, because there is no enjoyment or qiran for those present at the Sacred Mosque according to him, so whoever does that, that is, enjoyment from them, then he must offer a blood money for a crime. For those whose families are not present at the Sacred Mosque is whoever is from the Haram at the distance of shortening according to us, for whoever is at less then he is a resident in the Haram, or in its ruling. And from his residence behind the Miqat according to him and the people of the solution according to Tawus and other than the Meccan according to Malik. And fear God in preserving His commands and prohibitions, especially in Hajj, and know that God is severe in penalty for whoever does not fear Him, so that He may prevent you from disobeying Him, due to knowledge of Him.
2:197: 197- Hajj months means its time. Like saying the cold is two months. Information is well-known and they are: Shawwal, Dhul-Qi'dah, and nine of Dhul-Hijjah on the night of sacrifice according to us, and the ten according to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, and all of Dhul-Hijjah according to Malik. Based on the disagreement that what is meant by its time is the time of his ihram, or the time of his actions and rituals, or what is not appropriate for other rituals in general, then Malik disliked Umrah in the rest of Dhul-Hijjah. And Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, even though he approved of ihram before Shawwal, he disliked it. And the two months and part of a month were called months to establish some in place of all, or to generalize the collection to what is above one. Whoever makes Hajj obligatory in them whoever makes it obligatory upon himself by entering ihram in them according to us, or by Talbiyah or market the sacrificial animal according to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, and it is evidence for what Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, went with and that whoever enters ihram for Hajj must complete it. No obscenity No sexual intercourse, or no obscene speech. No immorality No going beyond the limits of the Shariah with bad deeds and committing forbidden acts. No disputation No quarreling with servants and companions. During Hajj During its days, the negation of the three is intended as a prohibition for exaggeration and to indicate that they are real, so that they should not be, and whatever of them is ugly in themselves, in Hajj it is more ugly, like wearing silk in prayer and singing while reciting the Qur’an, because it is a departure from the requirements of nature and habit to pure worship. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and the first two read it with the nominative case meaning: There should be no obscenity or immorality. The third read it with the fat-ha meaning except to inform of the absence of disagreement in Hajj, and that is because Quraysh used to form an alliance with the rest of the Arabs and stand at the sacred monument, so the disagreement was removed by ordering them to also stand at Arafat. And whatever good you do, God knows it He urged goodness followed by the prohibition of evil to be used as evidence and in its place. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. And take provisions for your return with fear of God, for it is the best provision. It was said: It was revealed about the people of Yemen who used to hide themselves and not take provisions, and they used to say: We trust in God, and so they would be a burden on the people. So they were commanded to take provisions and to avoid insisting on asking and burdening the people. And fear God, O you of understanding. For the issue of understanding is the fear of God and fearing Him. He urged them to fear God, then commanded them to aim for God Almighty by it, and to disavow everything other than Him, and this is what the mind requires, free from the impurities of desires, and for this reason He specifically addressed the people of understanding.
2:198: 198- There is no blame upon you if you seek i.e. in tabtaghwa i.e. ask. Benefit from your Lord a gift and provision from Him, meaning profit from trade. It was said: Ukaz, Majannah and Dhu al-Majaz were their markets in the pre-Islamic period, which they held during the Hajj seasons, and their livelihoods were from them. When Islam came, they felt guilty about it, so it was revealed. And when you pour from Arafat you pour from it in abundance, from afdah al-maa if you poured it in abundance. Its origin is afdahtum anfusakum, so the object was deleted as was deleted in dafa'at min al-Basrah. Arafat is a plural noun, like adhra'at, and it is only with a nun and a kasra, and it contains the science and femininity because the plural tanween is the tanween of comparison, not the tanween of empowerment, and therefore it is pluralized with the lam, and the loss of the kasra follows the loss of the tanween without compensation due to the lack of inflection, and here it is not like that. Or because the feminization is either with the mentioned taa', which is not a taa of feminization. Rather, it is with the alif before it, a sign of the feminine plural, or an implied construction as in Su’ad, and it is not correct to estimate it because the mentioned prevents it from being like a substitute for it due to its being specific to the feminine like the ta’ of bint, and the standing place was called Arafat because it is a description of Abraham, peace be upon him, so when he saw him, he recognized him, or because Gabriel, peace be upon him, was circling with him in the sacred sites, so when he showed him to him, he said, I have recognized you, or because Adam and Eve met there and got to know each other. Or because people get to know each other there. Arafat is for exaggeration in that, and it is one of the improvised names unless it is made the plural of ‘Arif, and in it is evidence of the obligation of standing there because the ifada does not happen except after it, and it is commanded by the Almighty’s saying: Then hasten, or it is an introduction to the commanded remembrance, and there is a view in it because the remembrance is not obligatory, but rather recommended. And if it is assumed that it is obligatory, then it is a restricted obligation, not an absolute obligation until its introduction is obligatory, and the command to do it is not absolute. So remember God by uttering the Talbiyah, Tahlil, and supplication. And it was said: by the two ‘Isha’ prayers. At Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram is a mountain on which the Imam stands and it is called Qazah. It was said: It is between the two valleys of Arafat and Wadi Muhsir. The first is supported by what Jabir narrated: That when he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed Fajr - meaning at Muzdalifah - in the early morning, he rode his camel until he reached Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram, then he supplicated, glorified and praised God, and he did not stop standing until it became light. It was called Al-Mash'ar because it is a landmark of worship, and it was described as Al-Haram because of its sanctity. The meaning of At Al-Mash'ar Al-Haram: what is next to it and close to it, for it is better. Otherwise, all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing except Wadi Muhsir. And remember Him as He has guided you as He taught you, or remember Him with good remembrance as He has guided you with good guidance to the rituals and other things. Ma is a source or a collective. And if you were before it meaning guidance. Among the astray meaning ignorant of faith and obedience. An is the lightened form of the heavy one and lam is the distinguishing feature. It was said that an is negative and lam means except, as in the Almighty’s saying: And we think you are among the liars.
2:199: 199- Then proceed from where the people proceed meaning from Arafat, not from Muzdalifah. The address is with Quraysh, they used to stand in Jam' and the rest of the people in Arafat and they saw that as superiority over them, so they were ordered to be equal to them. And then because of the difference between the two proceeds, as in your saying, Be good to the people then do not be good to anyone but a generous person. And it was said: From Muzdalifah to Mina after proceeding from Arafat to it, and the address is general. And the people was read with a kasra, meaning the forgetful, meaning Adam from the statement of the Most High: So he forgot and the meaning is that proceeding from Arafat is an ancient law, so do not change it. And seek forgiveness from God for your ignorance in changing the rituals and the like. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful He forgives the sin of the one who seeks forgiveness and bestows His blessings upon him.
2:200: 200-And when you have completed your rites So when you have completed the Hajj rituals and are done with them. Then remember God as you remember your fathers So remember Him often and exaggerate in it as you do in mentioning your fathers in boasting. When the Arabs completed their rites, they would stand in Mina between the mosque and the mountain and mention the glories of their fathers and the good days of their lives. Or more remembrance is either a genitive in apposition to the remembrance, making the remembrance a remembrancer, figuratively and meaning: So remember God as you remember your fathers or as a remembrance more intense and eloquent than it. Or according to what is added to it in weakness meaning or as the remembrance of a people more intense in remembrance than you. Or it is accusative in apposition to your fathers and remembrance from the verb mentioned meaning or as your remembrance more intense in remembrance than your fathers. Or by an implied noun indicated by the meaning, estimated as: Or be more intense in remembrance of God than your fathers. “Some people say, ‘Our Lord, give us in this world,’ make our giving and our grant in this world, ‘and he will have no share or portion in the Hereafter,’ meaning no share or portion because his concern is limited to this world, or he seeks a share.”
2:201: 201- "And among them is he who says, 'Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good,' meaning health, sufficiency, and the granting of good. 'And in the Hereafter that which is good,' meaning reward and mercy. 'And save us from the punishment of the Fire,' with forgiveness and pardon. 'Ali may God be pleased with him said, 'A good woman in this world is a righteous woman, and in the Hereafter a beautiful woman. 'And the punishment of the Fire is a bad woman.' Al-Hasan said, 'A good woman in this world is knowledge and worship, and in the Hereafter it is Paradise. 'And save us from the punishment of the Fire,' meaning, 'Preserve us from desires and sins,' and the things that lead to the Fire are examples of what is meant by it.
2:202: 202- Those refers to the second group. It was said to them. They will have a share of what they have earned meaning of the same kind and it is their recompense, or because of it, as God Almighty said: Because of their sins they were drowned or from what they called for, We give them from it what We have determined, so the call is called an acquisition because it is from the deeds. And God is swift in reckoning He will hold the servants accountable for their great number and the great number of their deeds in the span of a moment, or He is about to establish the Resurrection and hold the people accountable, so hasten to do acts of obedience and earn good deeds.
2:203: 203- And remember God during the appointed days glorify Him after the prayer and when slaughtering the sacrifices and throwing the pebbles and other things during the days of Tashreeq. But whoever hastens whoever hastens to depart. In two days the day of Qarr and the day after it, meaning whoever departs on the second day of Tashreeq after throwing the pebbles according to us, and before dawn according to Abu Hanifa. There is no sin upon him for hastening. And whoever delays, there is no sin upon him and whoever delays in departing until he throws the pebbles on the third day after noon, Abu Hanifa said: It is permissible to advance his throwing before noon. The meaning of negating the sin of hastening and delaying is the choice between them and the response to the people of ignorance, for among them are those who have sinned in haste and among them are those who have sinned in delay. For whoever fears God meaning what was mentioned of the choice, or of the rulings for whoever fears God because he is the pilgrim in truth and benefits from it, or for its sake so that he will not be harmed by abandoning what concerns him from them. And fear God in all your affairs so that He may take care of you. And know that you will be gathered to Him for recompense after resurrection. The root of gathering is to gather and join together what is dispersed.
2:204: 204-And among the people is he whose speech pleases you He pleases you and is great in your soul, and astonishment: is a confusion that a person experiences due to his ignorance because of the one he is astonished at. In the life of this world is related to speech, meaning what he says about worldly matters and the means of livelihood, or in the meaning of the world, then it is intended by claiming love and showing faith, or you like it, meaning you like his speech in this world for its sweetness and eloquence, but you do not like it in the Hereafter because of the astonishment and stuttering that befalls him, or because he is not permitted to speak. And he calls God to witness as to what is in his heart He swears and calls God to witness that what is in his heart is in agreement with his speech. And he is the most hostile opponent He is very hostile and argumentative towards the Muslims, and the argument is quarrelling, and it is possible that it is the plural of opponent like difficult and difficult meaning the most hostile opponent. It was said that it was revealed about Al-Akhnas bin Shuraik Al-Thaqafi, who was handsome in appearance and sweet in speech, and he was loyal to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he claimed to be a Muslim. It was said about all the hypocrites.
2:205: 205-And if he takes over he turns away and leaves you. It was said: if he is defeated and becomes a governor. He strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and livestock as Al-Akhns did with Thaqeef when he destroyed their crops and destroyed their livestock, or as evil governors do by killing and destroying, or by injustice until God prevents the rain with his evil, destroying crops and livestock. And God does not love corruption He does not approve of it, so beware of His anger with him.
2:206: 206- And when it is said to him, 'Fear God,' pride in sin takes hold of him. His haughtiness and the zeal of the Age of Ignorance drive him to commit the sin he is commanded to perfect, stubbornly, from your saying, 'I took him with such-and-such' if you compelled him to do it and forced him to do it. Hell is sufficient for him is sufficient for him as a punishment and torment. Hell is a name for the abode of punishment, and it is originally synonymous with fire. It was said that it is an Arabization. And what an evil resting place is the answer to an implied oath, and the one specifically blamed is omitted because it is known, and the resting place is a bed. It was said that it is what one treads on for one in a state of ritual impurity.
2:207: 207- And among the people is he who sells himself he sells it, that is, he spends it in jihad or enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong until he is killed seek[ing] the pleasure of God seeking His pleasure. It was said that it was revealed about Suhaib ibn Sinan the Roman, the polytheists captured him and tortured him to make him apostatize, so he said: "Indeed, I am an old man. It will not benefit you if I am with you, nor will it harm you if I am against you, so leave me as I am and take my money." So they accepted it from him and he came to Medina. And God is Kind to His servants as He guided them to such a purchase and charged them with jihad, thus exposing them to the reward of the warriors and martyrs.
2:208: 208-"O you who have believed, enter into peace completely." "Peace" with kasra and fatha means surrender and obedience, and therefore it is used in peace and Islam. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Al-Kisa'i opened it and the rest closed it. Kafah is the name of the sentence because it prevents the parts from separating, a state of the pronoun, or peace because it is feminine like war. He said: Peace takes what you are satisfied with, but war suffices you with its breaths of hunger. The meaning is: Submit to God and obey Him completely, outwardly and inwardly, and the address is to the hypocrites. Or enter Islam completely and do not mix anything else with it. The address is to the believers among the People of the Book, for after their conversion to Islam they venerated the Sabbath and forbade camels and their milk. Or in all of God’s laws by believing in all of the prophets and books, and the address is to the People of the Book. Or in all of the branches of Islam and its rulings, so do not neglect anything, and the address is to the Muslims. And do not follow the footsteps of Satan by dividing and separating. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy with apparent enmity.
2:209: 209- If you slip from entering into peace. After the clear proofs have come to you the verses and arguments that testify that it is the truth. Then know that God is Exalted in Might revenge is not beyond His power. Wise He does not take revenge except with justice.
2:210: 210- Do they wait? is an interrogative in the sense of negation, and that is why it came after it. Unless God comes to them meaning His command or His punishment comes to them, as in the Almighty's saying: Or the command of your Lord comes "So Our punishment came to them or God brings them His punishment, so the thing brought was omitted to indicate it with the Almighty's saying, such as Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise In the shade" is the plural of shade like qala and qalala which is what shades you, and it was read shade like qalal. "From the clouds" is the white cloud, and the punishment comes to them in it because it is a place of mercy, so if the punishment comes from it, it is more terrible because evil comes from where one does not expect it is more difficult, so how about if it comes from where one expects good. "And the angels" because they are the intermediaries in bringing His command, or the ones who truly bring His punishment. It was read in the accusative case in apposition to "shade or clouds". "And the matter was decided." The matter of their destruction was completed and finished. The past tense was put in the place of the future because of its proximity and the certainty of its occurrence. It was read "and the matter was decided" in apposition to the angels. "And to God all matters return. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu Amr, and Asim read it in the passive form as if it were from returning. The rest read it in the active form with the feminine gender except for Ya'qub as if it were from returning." It was also read in the masculine and passive form.
2:211: 211- "Ask the Children of Israel" is an order to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone, and the purpose of this question is to rebuke them. "How many clear signs have We given them? A clear miracle, or a sign in the books that testifies to the truth and correctness at the hands of the prophets, and how many" is a report or interrogative statement and its place is the accusative as a direct object or the nominative as a beginning with the deletion of the referent from good to the subject. And a sign is its distinguishing feature. And "from" is for separation. "And whoever changes the favor of God" meaning the signs of God, for they are the cause of guidance, which is the greatest of blessings, making them the cause of misguidance and the increase of filth, or by distortion and deviant contemplation. "After it came to him" after it reached him and he was able to know it, and in it is an allusion that they changed it after they understood it, and therefore it was said that it is estimated that they changed it. "And whoever changes then God is severe in penalty" so He punishes him with the most severe punishment because he committed the most serious crime.
2:212: 212- The life of this world has been made attractive to those who disbelieve. It has become beautiful in their eyes and its love has been instilled in their hearts until they have fallen in love with it and turned away from anything else. The one who makes it attractive in reality is God Almighty, since there is nothing but that He is the doer. This is indicated by the reading of make attractive in the active form, and both Satan, the animal force, and what God created in it of beautiful matters and delicious things are made attractive by the display. And they ridicule those who believe meaning the poor believers like Bilal, Ammar and Suhaib, meaning they despise them and mock them for their rejection of this world and their eagerness for the Hereafter. Min is for the beginning, as if they made the mockery begin with them. And those who feared God are above them on the Day of Resurrection because they are in the highest heavens while they are in the lowest depths, or because they are in honor while they are in humiliation, or because they are arrogant towards them and mock them as they mocked them in this world. He only said And those who feared God after saying of those who believed to indicate that they are fearful and that their superiority is due to fear of God. And God provides for whom He wills in both abodes. Without account without measure, so He gives them plenty in this world as a means of enticement at times and as a test at other times.
2:213: 213- Mankind was one nation agreeing on the truth between Adam and Idris or Noah or after the flood, or agreeing on ignorance and disbelief during the period of Idris or Noah. So God sent the prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners meaning they differed then God sent, and it was only deleted because of the significance of His statement regarding what they differed about, and from Ka'b (that which I know of the number of prophets is one hundred and twenty-four thousand and those sent from among them are three hundred and thirteen and those mentioned in the Qur'an by the name of the proper name are twenty-eight). And He sent down with them the Book meaning by this the genus and does not mean that He sent down with each one a book specific to him, because most of them did not have a book specific to them, but rather they took books from those before them. With the truth is a state of the Book, meaning mixed with the truth and bearing witness to it. To judge between the people meaning God, or the sent prophet, or his Book. In what they differed over in the truth in which they differed, or in what was confusing to them. And what they differed over in the truth, or the Book. Except for those who were given it meaning the Book revealed to remove the difference, meaning they reversed the matter and made what was revealed a mixture of difference and a reason for its strengthening. After the clear proofs had come to them, out of envy among themselves out of envy among themselves and injustice due to their eagerness for the world. So God guided those who believed to that over which they differed meaning to the truth over which those who differed differed. Of the truth clarification of what they differed over. By His permission by His command or by His will and kindness. And God guides whom He wills to a straight path its follower does not go astray.
2:214: 214- Or do you think that you will enter Paradise? He addressed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers with it after mentioning the differences of the nations with the prophets after the coming of the verses, encouraging them to remain steadfast despite their opposition. Or is disconnected and the meaning of the hamza in it is denial. And when it has not come to you and it has not come to you, and the origin of when is when was added to them what and in it there is expectation and therefore it was made opposite to had. The likeness of those who passed on before you their state which is like in hardship. They were touched by poverty and hardship is a statement of it on the resumption. And they were shaken and were disturbed severely by the hardships that befell them. Until the Messenger and those who believed with him say because of the extreme hardship and the length of time such that the ropes of patience were cut. Nafi' read Yaqool in the nominative case as a narration of a past state like you saying He was sick until they did not hope for it. When will God's victory is a delay for it because of its delay. Indeed, the victory of God is near. This is a resumption of the intention of the statement, meaning that this was said to them to help them in their request for immediate victory. It indicates that reaching God Almighty and winning honor with Him is by rejecting desires and pleasures, and enduring hardships and practicing asceticism, as the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said, Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and Hell is surrounded by desires.
2:215: 215-They ask you what they should spend On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both (that Amr bin Al-Jamuh Al-Ansari was an old man with great wealth, so he said, O Messenger of God, what do we spend from our wealth and where do we put it? So the verse was revealed: "Say: Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer." He was asked about the spender, so he answered by stating the recipient because it is more important, since the expenditure is considered by its consideration, and because it was in Amr's question, even though it was not mentioned in the verse, and the recipient was limited to what was included in his statement, Whatever you spend of good. "And whatever you do of good" is in the sense of a condition. "Indeed, God is Knowing of it." His answer is that if you do good, God knows its nature and will pay its reward, and there is nothing in the verse that contradicts the obligation of zakat to be abrogated by it.
2:216: 216- Fighting has been enjoined upon you, although it is hateful to you. It is difficult for you and hateful by nature, and it is a source of description for exaggeration, or a verb with the meaning of a passive participle like bread. It is read with the fat-ha as a language in it like weakness and weakness, or with the meaning of compulsion metaphorically as if they were forced to do it due to its severity and great hardship like the Almighty's saying: His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship. "And perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you." It is everything that they were charged with, because nature dislikes it and it is the basis of their goodness and the reason for their success. "And perhaps you like a thing and it is bad for you." It is everything that they were forbidden from, because the soul loves it and desires it and it leads it to ruin. "Perhaps" was mentioned because if the soul is trained, the matter will be reversed upon it. "And God knows" what is best for you. "And you do not know" that, and in it is evidence that rulings follow the prevailing interests even if they are not known.
2:217: 217-"They ask you about the sacred month." It was narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, "sent Abdullah bin Jahsh, his cousin, on a raid in Jumada al-Akhira - two months before Badr - to lie in wait for a caravan of the Quraysh in which was Amr bin Abdullah al-Hadrami and three others with him. They killed him and took two captives and resumed the caravan, which contained some of the merchandise of Taif. This was the first of Rajab, and they thought it was Jumada al-Akhira. The Quraysh said, Muhammad has made the sacred month permissible, a month in which the fearful are safe and the people are terrified about their livelihoods. This was difficult for the people of the raid and they said, We will not leave until our repentance is revealed. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, returned the caravan and the captives. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, When this was revealed, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, took the spoils, and it was the first spoils in Islam." The questioners were the polytheists who wrote to him about this, denouncing and reproaching him, and it was said that they were the people of the raid. "Fighting in it" is a substitute for including the sacred month. It was read about fighting with the repetition of the agent. "Say, 'Fighting in it is a great sin.'" That is, a great sin. The most likely is that it was abrogated by the Almighty's saying: "Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them." This is contrary to what Ata' said, which is the abrogation of the specific by the general, and there is a difference of opinion about it. The first is to prevent the verse from indicating the prohibition of fighting in the sacred month absolutely, because fighting in it is an indefinite noun in the scope of an established verse, so it is not general. "And turning away" is to divert and prevent. "From the path of God" that is, Islam, or what leads the servant to God, the Most High, of acts of obedience. "And disbelieve in it" that is, in God. "And the Sacred Mosque" is intended to mean the complement, that is, and turning away and the Sacred Mosque, as Abu Dawud said: Every man you think is a man, and a fire lit at night is a fire It is not appropriate to connect it to the path of God because connecting his statement and disbelieved in it to and turned away prevents it, since connecting to the relative pronoun does not precede connecting to the relative clause nor to the ha’ in it, because connecting to the genitive pronoun is only done by repeating the preposition. And expelling his people from it the people of the Sacred Mosque, who are the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers. Greater in the sight of God than what the secret police did by mistake and based on conjecture, and it is report about the four things counted among the major sins of Quraysh. And more effective than what is equal in singular and plural and masculine and feminine. And persecution is greater than killing meaning what you are committing of expulsion and polytheism is more terrible than what they committed of killing the Hadrami. And they will not cease fighting you until they turn you back from your religion is report about the continuity of the enmity of the disbelievers towards them and that they will not stop from it until they turn them back from their religion, and even is for explanation like your saying I will worship God until I enter Paradise. If they are able This is a ruling out of their ability, like the saying of one who is confident in his strength: On his horn, if you defeat me, do not spare me, and a sign that they will not turn them back. And whoever among you turns back from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever - for those, their deeds have become worthless. He restricted apostasy to death in the nullification of deeds, as is the doctrine of Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. What is meant by it are beneficial deeds. It was read Habatat with a fat-ha, which is a language for it. In this world because what they imagined is invalid and the worldly benefits of Islam are lost. And in the Hereafter because the reward is lost. And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally like all the disbelievers.
2:218: 218- Indeed, those who believed was also revealed about the secret missionaries, because it was thought that if they were saved from sin, they would have no reward. And those who emigrated and fought in the cause of God The relative pronoun was repeated to emphasize the emigration and the fighting, as if they were independent in achieving hope. Those are the ones who hope for the mercy of God His reward. He established hope for them to indicate that the work is not binding or decisive in meaning, especially since the point of reference is the endings. And God is Forgiving for what they did wrong and lacked caution. Merciful in generously rewarding and recompense.
2:219: 219- They ask you about wine and gambling. It was narrated that the verse was revealed in Mecca: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision. So the Muslims began to drink it. Then Umar, Muadh, and a group of the Companions said: Give us your fatwa, O Messenger of God, about wine, for it takes away the mind and wastes money. So this verse was revealed, and some people drank it and others left it. Then Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf invited some of them and they drank and became drunk. One of them led the prayer and recited: “Say: O you disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship.” Then Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated was revealed. Then “Say: Who drinks it?” Then Utbah ibn Malik invited Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas with a group of people and when they got drunk they boasted and recited poetry. He recited a satire of the Ansar. An Ansari hit him with a camel’s jawbone and wounded him. He complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: O God, give us a clear explanation about wine. Then the following verse was revealed: Indeed, wine and gambling until His saying: Will you then desist? Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: We have desisted, O Lord. Wine is originally a source of khamarah if it conceals it. Grape and date juice is called by it when it becomes strong and boils as if it intoxicates the mind, just as it is called sakr because it intoxicates, i.e., it blocks it. It is absolutely forbidden, as is everything that intoxicates according to most scholars. Abu Hanifa may God have mercy on him said: The infusion of raisins and dates, if it is cooked until two-thirds of it is gone, then it becomes very sweet to drink without getting drunk. Maysir is also a verbal noun like al-mu’ad, and gambling is called this because it takes someone else’s money easily or robs him of his ease. The meaning is that they ask you about their dealings, as God swt says: Say about them, meaning about their dealings. A great sin, in that it leads to deviating from what is commanded and committing what is forbidden. Hamza and al-Kisa’i often read it with a tha. “And benefits for people,” from earning money, music, enjoyment, and befriending young men, and in wine in particular, it encourages the cowardly, provides chivalry, and strengthens nature. And their sin is greater than their benefit, meaning the corruption that arises from them is greater than the expected benefits from them. For this reason, it was said that it is the forbidden for wine, because if the corruption outweighs the benefit, it necessitates the prohibition of the act. It is more apparent that this is not the case, as mentioned above, regarding the invalidation of the Mu’tazila school of thought. And they ask you what they should spend. It was also said that Amr ibn al-Jamuh asked first about the spender and the spender, then he asked about how to spend. “Say: ‘Pardon.’ Pardon is the opposite of effort, and from it is said of the easy land, which is that he spends what he is able to give and does not reach the point of effort. He said: Pardon me, you will maintain my affection, and do not speak ill of me when I get angry. It was narrated that a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a golden egg that he had obtained in some of the spoils of war and said: Take it from me as charity. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him until he repeated it several times. Then he said, “Give it to me,” angry. So he took it and threw it away in a way that if it had struck him it would have wounded him. Then he said: “One of you brings all his wealth and gives it in charity and sits begging from people. Charity is only from what is left on my back.” Abu Amr read al-‘afu in the nominative case. Thus does God make clear to you the verses, meaning like what He made clear that forgiveness is better than effort, or what was mentioned of the rulings. The kaf in the accusative case is an attribute of a deleted source, meaning an explanation like this explanation. The sign and the one being addressed are singular based on the interpretation of the tribe and the plural, so that you may reflect on the evidence and rulings.
2:220: 220-"In this world and the Hereafter" in the affairs of both abodes, so you take what is best in both, and avoid what harms you and does not benefit you, or harms you more than it benefits you. "And they ask you about orphans when the verse was revealed, Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly" they avoided mixing with orphans and taking care of their affairs, so that was difficult for them, so that was mentioned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the verse was revealed, "Say, 'Improvement for them is best'" meaning interfering with them to reform them, or reforming their property is better than avoiding them. "And if you mix with them, they are your brothers" urging mixing, meaning that they are your brothers in religion and it is the right of a brother to mix with a brother. It was said that what is meant by mixing is marriage. "And God knows the corrupter from the reformer." A warning and a promise to those who associate with them to corrupt and reform, meaning He knows their situation and will punish them for it. "And if God had willed, He could have forced you. That is, if God had willed to force you, He would have forced you, meaning He would have burdened you with what is difficult for you, from 'anat" which means hardship, and it would not have been permissible for you to interfere with them. "Indeed, God is Exalted in Might." Victorious and able to force. "Wise." He rules as wisdom requires and as capacity allows.
2:221: 221-And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe meaning, do not marry them. It is read with the dammah meaning, do not marry them to Muslims. Polytheistic women include the People of the Book because the People of the Book are polytheists, as God the Almighty says: And the Jews say, 'Ezra is the son of God,' and the Christians say, 'The Messiah is the son of God.' to His saying: Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him. But He made it specific for them by His saying: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture. It was narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, sent Murthad al-Ghanawi to Mecca to expel some Muslims from it, and Anaq came to him, and he loved her in the pre-Islamic era, and she said: Will you not be alone? He said: Islam has come between us. She said: Would you like to marry me? He said: "Yes, but seek the permission of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him." So he sought his permission, and the verse was revealed: And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist. That is, a believing woman, whether she is free or a slave, for all people are God's slaves and slave girls. And even if you were to be pleased with her with her beauty and features, and the waw is for the state, and even with the meaning of if, and it is common. And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe and do not marry believing women from among them until they believe, and this is general. And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even if he pleases you is a reason for the prohibition of associating with them, and an encouragement to associating with the believers. Those is a reference to the polytheistic men and women mentioned. They invite to the Fire meaning disbelief that leads to the Fire, so it is not appropriate to befriend them or marry them. And God meaning and His allies, meaning the believers, the noun was omitted and the noun to which it was added was used in its place to magnify their status. Invites to Paradise and forgiveness meaning to the belief and action that lead to them, so they are the most deserving of associating. By His permission meaning by the success and facilitation of God the Most High, or by His decree and will. And He makes clear His verses to the people that perhaps they will be reminded so that they will remember, or so that they will be at a level that is hoped for by remembering due to what He has instilled in the minds of the inclination towards good and opposing desires.
2:222: 222- "And they ask you about menstruation" It was narrated (that the people of ignorance did not live with menstruating women nor eat with them, as the Jews and Magians did, and this continued until Abu Al-Dahdah asked a group of the Companions about that, and then it was revealed. Menstruation is a source like coming and spending the night, and perhaps the Almighty mentioned they ask you without the waw three times, because the first questions were at different times and the last three were at the same time, so He mentioned them with the plural letter. "Say, it is a harmful thing" meaning menstruation is something disgusting and harmful to whoever approaches it out of aversion to it. "So keep away from women during menstruation" so avoid having intercourse with them, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "You were only commanded to keep away from having intercourse with them when they menstruate, and He did not command you to expel them from the houses as the non-Arabs do." This is the moderation between the excess of the Jews and the negligence of the Christians, as they used to have intercourse with them and did not care about menstruation. Rather, he described it as harm and based the ruling on it with the letter fa to indicate that it is the cause. And do not approach them until they are pure is an emphasis on the ruling and a clarification of its purpose, which is that they should bathe after the cessation. This is clearly indicated by the reading of Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Asim in the narration of Ibn Abbas, They should be pure meaning they should be purified, meaning they should bathe, and in compliance with his statement, Then when they have purified themselves, then come to them, as it requires the latter to be permissible to come after bathing. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, said that if she is pure for most of her period, it is permissible to come to her before bathing. From where God has commanded you meaning from what God has commanded you to do and made permissible for you. Indeed, God loves those who repent from sins. And He loves those who purify themselves meaning those who are pure from indecencies and filth, such as intercourse with a menstruating woman and coming in places other than those where one comes.
2:223: 223- Your women are a place of cultivation for you places of cultivation for you. He likened them to it, likening what is placed in their wombs of sperm to seeds. Come to your place of cultivation meaning come to them as you come to the place of cultivation, and it is like an explanation of the Almighty's saying: Come to them from where God has commanded you "However you wish" from any direction you wish. It was narrated (that the Jews used to say: Whoever has intercourse with his wife from behind in her vagina, her child will be cross-eyed, so this was mentioned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and so it was revealed). "And send forth for yourselves" what is stored up for you of reward. It was said that it is seeking a child. It was also said that it is saying the name of God upon intercourse. "And fear God" by avoiding His disobedience. "And know that you will meet Him" so provide yourself with what will not disgrace you. "And give good tidings to the believers" those who are perfect in faith with honor and eternal bliss. The Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to advise them and give good tidings to those who believed him and obeyed his command.
2:224: 224- "And do not make God an object of your oaths to prevent you from being righteous and fearing God and making peace between people." It was revealed about Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him when he swore not to spend on Mastih because of his slander against Aisha may God be pleased with them both, or about Abdullah bin Rawahah who swore not to speak to his son-in-law Bashir bin Al-Nu'man and not to make peace between him and his sister. The word arda is a verb meaning the object, like fist, and is used for something that is exposed without something and for something that is exposed to something. The meaning of the verse according to the first is And do not make God an obstacle to the types of good that you have sworn to, so what is meant by oath is the matters that are sworn to, like his saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Ibn Samurah If you swear an oath and then see something better than it, then do what is better and expiate for your oath. And that with its connection is an explanatory apposition for it, and the lam is a connection of the subject because of the meaning of objection in it, and it is possible that it is for the reason and that is related to the verb or to the subject, meaning do not make God subject to you being righteous because of your faith in Him, and according to the second, do not make Him subject to your oaths so that you squander it by swearing by Him a lot, and for this reason He condemned swearing with His saying: And do not obey every worthless oath-taker, and that you be righteous is a reason for the prohibition, meaning He forbade you from it in order to your righteousness and piety and to reform between people, for swearing is daring towards God Almighty, and the one who is daring towards it is not righteous and piety nor can he be trusted to reform between people, and God is Hearing of your oaths, Knowing of your intentions.
2:225: 225- God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths means idle talk that is not taken into account from the words of others, and idle oaths are those that were not agreed upon as was said by the tongue, or spoken out of ignorance of its meaning, such as the Arabs saying: No, by God and yes, by God, just to emphasize His saying: But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned and the meaning is that God will not hold you accountable for punishment or expiation for what you did not intend, but He will hold you accountable for both or one of them for what you intended of faith and what your hearts agreed upon with your tongues. Abu Hanifa said: idle talk is when a man swears based on his false assumption, and the meaning is that He will not punish you for the oaths you erred in, but He will punish you for what you deliberately lied about. And God is Forgiving as He did not hold you accountable for idle talk, Forbearing as He did not hasten to hold you accountable for an oath that was serious, waiting for repentance.
2:226: 226- For those who swear not to have intercourse with their wives meaning they swear not to have intercourse with them. Ila' is an oath, and its transitivity is with 'ala, but since this section includes the meaning of distance, it is transitive with min. Wait four months is the subject and what precedes it is its predicate, or the subject of the circumstance, contrary to what was mentioned previously. Waiting means waiting and stopping, and it was added to the circumstance in a broad sense, meaning that the master has the right to remain in this period, so he is not required to return the marriage, nor to divorce. Therefore, Al-Shafi'i said: There is no Ila' except in more than four months, and this is supported by If they return they go back on the oath by breaking it, then God is Forgiving and Merciful the master bears the sin of breaking it if he atones, or what he intended by the Ila' of harming the woman and the like, by the group that is like repentance.
2:227: 227- And if they decide to divorce and if they are silent about his intention then God is Hearing of their divorce and Knowing of their intention in it, and Abu Hanifa said: The oath is for four months or more, and its ruling is that if the master fulfills the period with intercourse if he is able, and with a promise if he is unable, then the oath is valid and the one who had intercourse must atone, otherwise she is separated after that with one divorce. And with us, he is required after the period to do one of the two things, and if he refuses them, the judge divorces him.
2:228: 228- And the divorced women means those who have been consummated with and who have menstruated, because the verses and reports indicate that the ruling for others is different from what was mentioned. They wait is a predicate with the meaning of a command, and the change in the phrase is for emphasis and to indicate that it is something that must be complied with, as if the addressee intended to comply with the command and inform about it, like your saying in supplication: May God have mercy on you, and its construction on the subject increases its emphasis.
