With themselves is an arousal and a urging for them to wait, because women's souls are longing for men, so they were commanded to suppress them and make them wait. Three menstrual periods is an accusative of circumstance, or the direct object. That is, they wait for it to pass. Menstrual periods is the plural of menstruation and it is used for menstruation, like his saying, peace be upon him: Leave prayer during your menstrual periods and for purity between two menstrual periods, like the saying of Al-A'sha: You inherited wealth and honor in the neighborhood because of the menstrual periods of your women that were lost in it. Its origin is the transition from purity to menstruation, which is what is meant by it in the verse because it indicates the purity of the womb, not menstruation, as the Hanafis said, based on the Almighty’s saying, So divorce them at their waiting period, meaning the time of their waiting period. The permissible divorce does not occur during menstruation. As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, The divorce of a slave woman is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstrual periods, it cannot be contradicted by what the two sheikhs narrated in the story of Ibn Umar, “Order him to take her back, then to keep her until she is pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure, then if he wishes, he may keep her after he wishes, and divorce her before he touches her. This is the waiting period for which God, the Most High, has commanded women to be divorced.” The analogy would have been to mention it in the form of paucity, which is the menstrual periods, but they are more expansive in that and use each of the two constructions in place of the other. Perhaps the ruling, since it includes divorcees who have menstrual periods, includes the meaning of abundance, so its construction is good. It is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs of children or menstruation in order to hasten the waiting period and nullify the right of return. Rather, it is a warning that it contradicts faith, and that a believer should not dare to do so and should not do so. And their husbands meaning the husbands of divorced women. have more right to return them to marriage and return to them. However, if the divorce is revocable according to the verse that follows, then the pronoun is more specific than the one to whom it is returned and there is no prohibition in it, as if the apparent meaning was repeated and made specific. Ba’ulah is the plural of ba’l and the ta’ is for the feminine of the plural like ummah and khawlah, or a source from your saying ba’l hasan a good husband describing it, or it is used in place of the deleted noun, meaning and the people of their husbands, and af’al here means the subject. In that meaning during the waiting period. If they desire reconciliation by taking them back, not to harm the woman. What is meant by it is not the condition of intending reconciliation for taking them back, but rather urging it and preventing the intention of harm. And women have rights similar to those against them according to what is equitable. That is, they have rights over men like their rights over them in obligation and entitlement to demand from them, not in kind. And men have a degree over them. An increase in right and preference in it, because their rights in themselves and their rights are the dowry, sufficiency, refraining from harming, and the like, or honor and virtue because they are their protectors and guardians and share with them the purpose of marriage and are equal in virtue of care and spending. And God is Exalted in Might. He is able to take revenge on whoever violates the rulings. Wise. He legislates them for wisdom and in the interests.
2:229: 229- Divorce twice meaning two revocable divorces, as it was narrated that "the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked, 'Where is the third?' He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, 'Or release with kindness.'" It was said that its meaning is the legal divorce, one divorce after another with separation, and for this reason the Hanafis said that combining two and three divorces is an innovation. Then keep with kindness by taking her back and treating her well, and this supports the first meaning. Or release her with kindness by the third divorce, or by not taking her back until she becomes clear, and according to the latter meaning, it is a new ruling and an absolute choice followed by teaching them how to divorce. And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them meaning from the charity. It was narrated that Jamila bint Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul hated her husband Thabit bin Qais, so she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Neither I nor Thabit have anything in common with me. By God, I do not find fault with him in religion or character, but I hate disbelief in Islam, and I cannot bear it out of hatred. I lifted the side of the tent and saw him approaching with a group of men. He was the tallest of them, the shortest of them in stature, and the ugliest of them in face. So I came down and divorced him in exchange for a garden that he had given her as a dowry.” The address is to the rulers and the taking and giving are attributed to them because they are the ones who order them during litigation. It was said that it is an address to the husbands, and what follows is an address to the rulers, which confuses the system of the popular reading. Except that they fear meaning the spouses, and it was read suspect which supports the interpretation of fear as suspicion. That they do not establish the limits of God means abandoning the establishment of His rulings from the duties of marriage. Hamzah and Yaqub read yakhāfā in the passive voice and replaced its connection with the pronoun with a substitute for inclusion. It was read takhāfā and taqīmā with the second-person ta'ā, if you fear O rulers, that they will not uphold the limits of God, then there is no blame upon them concerning that with which she ransomed herself on the man in taking what she ransomed herself with and divorced herself, and on the woman in giving him. those are the limits of God referring to what he has set of rulings. do not transgress them do not transgress them by disobeying them. and whoever transgresses the limits of God - then those are the wrongdoers following the prohibition with a threat, exaggerating the threat. Know that the apparent meaning of the verse indicates that khul' is not permissible except for dislike and discord, nor with everything that the husband leads her to let alone the extra, and this is supported by the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Any woman who asks her husband for a divorce without a good reason, the fragrance of Paradise will be forbidden to her. And what was narrated that “he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said to Jamila: Will you return his garden to him? She said: I will return it and add to it. He, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: As for the extra, no.” The majority disliked it, but they carried it out, because preventing the contract does not indicate its corruption, and that it is valid with the wording of ransom, because God Almighty called it ransom. And there is disagreement as to whether if it is done without the wording of divorce, is it annulment or divorce? And whoever considers it annulment relied on his saying:
2:230: 230- If he divorces her then his following the khul' after mentioning the two divorces requires that it be a fourth divorce if the khul' was a divorce. And it is more apparent that it is a divorce because it is a separation by the husband's choice, so it is like a divorce with compensation, and his saying if he divorces her is related to his saying: Divorce is twice or an explanation of his saying: or release with kindness the mention of the khul' interrupted between them indicating that the divorce occurs for free sometimes and for compensation other times, and the meaning is if he divorces her after the two. Then she is not lawful to him after that after that divorce. Until she marries another husband until she marries another, and marriage is based on both of them like marriage, and those who limited themselves to the contract, such as Ibn al-Musayyab, relied on its appearance, and the majority agreed that it is necessary to have a relationship, as it was narrated: "The wife of Rifa'ah said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Rifa'ah divorced me and my divorce was final, and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr married me and he had what he had like the hem of a garment. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you want to go back to Rifa'ah? She said: Yes. He said: No, until you taste his honey and he tastes your honey." So the verse is absolute and restricted by the Sunnah, and it is possible that marriage is interpreted as having a relationship, and the contract is derived from the wording of the husband. The wisdom in this ruling is to deter haste in divorce and returning to the woman who has been divorced three times and desiring her, and marriage on the condition of tahlil is invalid according to the majority. Abu Hanifa permitted it with dislike, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the tahlil and the one for whom it is tahlil is done. But if he divorces her the second husband there is no blame upon them if they return that each of the woman and the first husband return to the other by marrying, if they think that they can keep within the limits of God if they think that they can keep within the limits of God that God has set and legislated of marital rights. The interpretation of thinking as knowledge here is not sound because the consequences of matters are unseen and are thought but not known, and because it is not said I knew that Zayd would stand because an is used to indicate expectation, which contradicts knowledge. And those are the limits of God meaning the rulings mentioned. He makes them clear to a people who know who understand and know based on knowledge.
2:231: 231- And if you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term meaning the end of their waiting period. The term is used for the period and its end, so it is said for the lifespan of a person and for the death with which it ends. He said: Every living thing has a complete life span and dies when its appointed time has come to an end. Puberty is reaching something, and it may be said to be close to it in terms of spaciousness, which is what is meant in the verse to make it valid or to be arranged according to it. Then keep them on acceptable terms or release them on acceptable terms, because there is no keeping after the expiry of the term, and the meaning is take them back without harm, or leave them until their waiting period ends without prolonging it, and it is a repetition of the ruling in some form to pay attention to it. And do not keep them with harm, and do not take them back with the intention of harming them, as if the divorcer leaves the woman in waiting until the term approaches and then takes her back so that the waiting period is prolonged for her, so he forbade it after ordering its opposite as an exaggeration. And the accusative of harm is on the cause or the state meaning harming. So that you may transgress is to wrong them by prolonging it or forcing them to ransom, and the lam is related to harm because what is meant is to restrict it. And whoever does that has wronged himself by exposing himself to punishment. And do not take the verses of God in jest by turning away from them and being lax in acting upon what is in them, such as saying to someone who does not find the matter satirical, You are only mocking, as if he forbade mockery and intended by it to command the opposite. It was said, A man would marry, divorce, and free a slave, and he would say, ‘I was playing.’ And from him, peace and blessings be upon him: “There are three things which are serious in earnest and serious in jest: divorce, marriage, and freeing a slave.” And remember the favor of God upon you, which includes guidance and the mission of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, with gratitude and fulfilling its rights. And what has been revealed to you of the Book and wisdom, the Qur’an and Sunnah, He singled them out for mention to show their honor. He admonishes you thereby, with what has been revealed to you. And fear God and know that God is Knowing of all things, as an emphasis and a threat.
2:232: 232- And if you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term meaning their waiting period has expired, and from Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, the context of the two statements indicates the separation of the two puberties. And do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands is addressed to the guardians, as it was narrated that it was revealed about Mu'qil ibn Yasar when he prevented his sister Jamila from returning to her first husband by renewing the marriage contract. This is evidence that the woman does not marry herself, because if she was able to do so, the guardian's preventing her would have no meaning, and it is not contradicted by attributing the marriage to them because it is dependent on their permission. It was said that the husbands who prevent their wives after the waiting period has passed and do not let them marry out of aggression and force, because it is the answer to his statement And if you divorce women. It was said that it is the guardians and the husbands. It was said that it is all people, and the meaning is: This matter does not exist among you, because if it exists among them and they are satisfied with it, they are the ones who do it. And the restriction is the confinement and constriction, from it the restriction of the hen if her eggs are laid and do not come out. If they agree among themselves meaning the addressees and the women, and it is a circumstance because they marry or do not prevent them. With what is acceptable as the law knows and chivalry approves, a state of the raised pronoun, or an attribute of a deleted source, or an agreement that is acceptable. And in it is an indication that preventing marriage to someone who is not a match is not forbidden. That is a reference to what was mentioned previously, and the address is to everyone according to the interpretation of the tribe, or each one, or that the kaf is for the sake of addressing. And the difference between the present and the past without specifying the addressees, or to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the manner of his saying: O Prophet, when you divorce women to indicate that the reality of what is referred to is something that hardly everyone can imagine. He who among you believes in God and the Last Day is admonished by it because he is the one who is admonished by it and benefits. That meaning acting in accordance with what was mentioned. Purer for you is more beneficial. And purer from the filth of sins. And God knows what is beneficial and good. And you do not know because of the deficiency of your knowledge.
2:233: 233- And mothers shall breastfeed their children is a command expressed by the report for emphasis and its meaning is recommendation, or obligation, so it is specific to when the boy is not breastfed except by his mother or he does not have a wet nurse, or the father is unable to hire a wet nurse. Mothers include divorcees and others. It was said that it is specific to them because the discussion is about them. Two complete years is emphasized by the attribute of perfection because it is something that is tolerated. For whoever wants to complete the breastfeeding is a statement of the one to whom the ruling is directed, meaning for whoever wants to complete the breastfeeding, or related to them breastfeeding, then the father is obligated to breastfeed as maintenance, and the mother breastfeeds for him. It is evidence that the maximum period of breastfeeding is two years and there is no consideration for it after that and that it is permissible for it to be less than that. And upon the one for whom the child is born meaning the one for whom the child is born, meaning the father, because the child is born to him and is attributed to him. The change in the phrase is to indicate the meaning that requires the obligation of breastfeeding and the expenses of the wet nurse on him. Their provision and clothing is a wage for them, and there is a difference of opinion regarding hiring a mother, so Al-Shafi'i permitted it and Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, forbade it as long as she is a wife or in her waiting period. With what is reasonable according to what the ruler sees and what he can fulfill. No soul is charged except [with that within] its capacity is an explanation for the obligation of provision and the restriction to what is reasonable, and evidence that God, the Most High, does not charge a servant with what he cannot bear, and that does not prevent its possibility. No mother shall be harmed because of her child, nor shall a father because of his child is a detailed explanation and confirmation of it, meaning that neither of them burdens the other with what is beyond his capacity, nor harms him because of the child. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ya'qub read La tadhar in the nominative case instead of saying La takalafa, and its origin according to both readings is tadharar with a kasra in the active form or a fatha in the passive form, and according to the first view it is permissible for it to mean tadhar and the ba' is from its connection, meaning that the parents do not harm the child by being excessive in taking care of him or falling short in what is appropriate for him. La tadhar was read with sukoon and with emphasis on the intention of stopping and with it with alleviation on the basis that he who harms him will harm him, and adding the boy to her sometimes and to him other times is to show compassion for them towards him, and to draw attention to the fact that it is appropriate for them to agree on improving him and showing compassion, so they should not harm him, or be harmed because of him. And upon the heir is the same is in apposition to his saying and upon him is meant their sustenance and clothing, and what is between them is an intervening reason. What is meant by the heir is the father's heir, which is the boy, meaning the expenses of the wet nurse from his money if the father dies. It was said that the remainder of the parents from his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, And make him the heir from us, and both sayings agree with the school of thought of al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, since he has no expenses except for childbirth. It was said that it is the child's heir, and Ibn Abi Layla went to him. It was said that it is his heir who is forbidden from him, and this is the school of thought of Abu Hanifa. It was said that it is his agnates, and Abu Zayd said that, and that is an indication of what is obligatory upon the father of sustenance and clothing. But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation meaning a weaning that is issued by their mutual consent and consultation between them before the two years, and consultation, consultation, advice and counsel are extracting an opinion, from the word sharat al-‘asal if you extract it. There is no blame upon them in that, and their mutual consent is considered in consideration of the child’s well-being, and to be careful that one of them does something that will harm him for a purpose or otherwise. And if you wish to have wet nurses for your children meaning you may have wet nurses for your children. It is said that the woman breastfed the child and she had him wet nursed, like you say God made my need successful and I made it successful for him, so the first object was deleted because it is not needed. There is no blame upon you in it, and its generality indicates that the husband may have the child wet nursed and prevent the wife from breastfeeding. If you surrender to the wet nurses. What you have given what you intended to give, like the Almighty’s saying When you rise to prayer and Ibn Kathir’s reading is what you have been given from ata ihsanan if he did it. It was read you have been given meaning what God has given you and enabled you to do as a reward. In a reasonable manner is the relative clause of you have been given, meaning in the manner that is customarily accepted and approved by the Shari’ah. The answer to the condition is omitted and is indicated by what precedes it. The condition of giving is not for the permissibility of breastfeeding, but rather for following what is best and most appropriate for the child. And fear God is an exaggeration in preserving what has been legislated in the matter of children and wet nurses. And know that God is Seeing of what you do is an exhortation and a threat.
2:234: 234- And those among you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days. That is, the wives of those, or those among you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait after them, like their saying, The fat is two dirhams' worth of ghee. It was read yatuwafu with the opening of the ya', meaning they complete their terms, and the feminine of the ten is based on the nights because they are the most beautiful months and days, and therefore they never use the masculine in such a case, going to the days, so they say I fasted ten and this is supported by the saying of God the Almighty: You remained only ten then You remained only a day, and perhaps what is required for this estimation is that the fetus usually moves for three months if it is male, and for four if it is female, so the longer of the two terms is considered, and ten is added to it as a precaution since its movement may weaken in the beginning so that it is not felt, and the generality of the wording requires the equality of the Muslim woman and the woman of the Book in it, as Al-Shafi'i said, and the free woman and the slave woman as Al-Asamm said, and the pregnant woman and others, but analogy required halving the period for the slave woman, and the consensus specified the pregnant woman from it based on the saying of God the Almighty: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth, and on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, that she observes the longer of the two terms as a precaution. And when they have reached their term meaning their waiting period has ended. There is no blame upon you O Imams or all Muslims. For what they do with themselves of exposing themselves to the suitors and all the other things that are forbidden to them during the waiting period. In an acceptable manner in a manner that is not denounced by the Shari’ah, and its implication is that if they do something that is denounced, then they must refrain from it, and if they fall short, then they are to blame. And God is Aware of what you do so He will reward you for it.
2:235: 235- And there is no blame upon you for what you suggest of proposing marriage to women Insinuation and allusion are to suggest the intended meaning with something for which it was not intended literally or metaphorically, such as the questioner saying I greet you, and allusion is indicating something by mentioning its requirements and concomitants, such as saying long-necked for long, and much-ashed for hospitable. And the sermon with the damma and kasra is the name of the state, except that the damma is specific to the sermon and the kasra is the request of the woman, and what is meant by women who are waiting for death, and alluding to proposing to her is to say to her that you are beautiful or hypocritical and my intention is to marry and the like. Or you concealed it within yourselves or you concealed it in your hearts and did not mention it explicitly or alludingly. God knows that you will mention them and you will not be patient in remaining silent about them and about the desire for them, and in it is a type of rebuke. But do not make an appointment with them secretly is a correction to an omitted word indicated by you will mention them meaning, mention them, but do not make an appointment with them for marriage or intercourse. Secret refers to intercourse because it is something that is made easy, and then to the contract because it is the cause of it. It was said that its meaning is, do not make an appointment with them in secret, on the basis that the meaning of an appointment in secret is an appointment with something that is considered reprehensible. Except that you say a well-known word meaning that you hint and do not state it explicitly, and the exception from it is omitted, meaning: do not make an appointment with them except a well-known appointment, or except a promise with a well-known word. It was said that it is an exception disconnected from secretly, and it is weak because it leads to your saying, Do not make an appointment with them except hinting, and it is not a promise. It is evidence of the prohibition of explicitly proposing to a woman in her waiting period, and the permissibility of hinting to her if she is in her waiting period following death. There is a difference of opinion regarding a woman in her waiting period following a final separation, but the most apparent view is that it is permissible. And do not resolve to tie the knot of marriage mentioning the intention is an exaggeration in the prohibition of the contract, meaning, do not resolve to tie the knot of marriage. It was said that its meaning is: Do not sever the marriage bond, for the root of determination is to cut. Until the written term has come to an end until the waiting period that has been written has ended. And know that God knows what is within yourselves of determination to do what is not permissible. So beware of Him and do not resolve. And know that God is Forgiving to whoever resolves but does not do it out of fear of God, the Most High. Forbearing He does not hasten to punish you.
2:236: 236-There is no blame upon you no responsibility for the dowry. It was said that it is a burden because there is no innovation in divorce before touching. It was said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, often forbade knocking, so he thought that there was hardship in it, so he denied If you divorce women before you have touched them meaning have not had intercourse with them. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read tamaasoohunna with a damma on the ta' and a long meem in the entire Quran. Or impose for them a dowry unless you impose, or until you impose, or you impose. The duty is the name of the dowry, and duty is an accusative of the object with the meaning of fa'ila with the meaning of maf'ul. The ta' is to transfer the word from descriptive to nominal, and it is possible that it is a source. The meaning is that there is no responsibility on the divorcer from demanding the dowry if the divorced woman was not touched and he did not name a dowry for her, because if she were touched, then the named dowry would be effective, or the dowry of her peers. If she was not touched but was named for her, then she is entitled to half of the named amount. The explicit meaning of the verse negates the obligation in the first case, and its implication requires obligation in general in the last two. And provide for them is in apposition to the implied meaning, so divorce them and provide for them. The wisdom in requiring the provision of provision is to make up for the distress of divorce, and its estimation is delegated to the opinion of the judge, and this is supported by his statement: The wealthy person is responsible for his ability and the poor person is responsible for his ability, meaning that both the wealthy person and the poor person who is in a tight situation must do what they can and what is appropriate for them. This is indicated by his statement, peace be upon him, to an Ansari who divorced his wife who was given permission before he touched her. Provide for her with your skullcap. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, said: It is a shield, a blanket, and a veil according to the situation, unless the dowry of her peers is less than that, then she is entitled to half the dowry of her peers. The implication of the verse requires specifying the provision of provision for the woman who was given permission and whom the husband did not touch. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, included with her in one of his two opinions the woman who was touched, the woman who was given permission and others by analogy, and this takes precedence over the implied meaning. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Hafs and Ibn Dhakwan read with a fat-ha on the dal: mta’aan enjoyment. By what is right in the manner that is approved by the Shari’ah and chivalry. Haqq truly is an attribute of mata’aan, or a confirmed source, meaning that is truly right. Ala al-mushsinun upon the doers of good are those who do good to themselves by hastening to comply, or to divorced women by enjoying themselves. He called them doers of good before the action to indicate proximity, as an encouragement and incitement.
2:237: 237- And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry When he mentioned the ruling on the delegated woman, he followed it with the ruling on her sharer. Then half of what you specified meaning, for them, or the duty is half of what you specified for them, and it is evidence that the wing is denied and then followed by the dowry and that there is no enjoyment with the division because it is her sharer unless they remit meaning the divorced women, then they do not take anything, and the formula is subject to masculinity and femininity, and the difference in the first is that the waw is a pronoun and the nun is a sign of raising, the second is the lam of the verb and the nun is a pronoun of the verb, built and therefore the an here and the accusative of the conjoined to it did not affect it. Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract remits meaning the husband who owns the contract and its solution from what is returned to him by the division, so he gives her the dowry in full, and it indicates that the divorce before touch is optional for the husband and is not divided by itself, and some of our companions and the Hanafis went to it. It was said that it is the guardian who concludes their marriage contract, if the woman is young. This is an old statement by Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. And to pardon is closer to righteousness. This supports the first view. The husband’s pardon is clear in terms of choice, and on the other hand it is an expression of an increase over the right. Calling it pardon is either due to the reciprocity or because they give the dowry to the women when they get married. Whoever divorces before consummation is entitled to get half back, but if he does not get it back, then he has pardoned her. On the authority of Jubayr ibn Mut’im, that he married a woman and divorced her before consummation, so he completed her dowry and said, I am more deserving of pardon. “And do not forget to be generous to one another.” That is, do not forget to be generous to one another. Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do. He will not waste your generosity and kindness.
2:238: 238-Guard the prayers by performing them on time and regularly. Perhaps the command to do so is in the folds of the rulings on children and spouses so that they are not distracted from them by being busy with their own affairs. The middle prayer means the middle one between them, or the best of them in particular, which is the afternoon prayer, based on the Prophet's (peace be upon him) saying on the Day of the Confederates: "They distracted us from the middle prayer, the afternoon prayer. May God fill their homes with fire." Its virtue is due to the many people being busy at its time, and the angels gathering. It was said that the noon prayer is because it is in the middle of the day and was the most difficult prayer for them, so it was the best, based on the Prophet's (peace be upon him) saying: The best of acts of worship are the most difficult. It was said that the dawn prayer is because it is between the daytime and nighttime prayers and falls within the common boundary between them and because it is witnessed. It was said that the sunset prayer is because it is the middle one in number and the odd number of the day. It was said that the night prayer is because it is between two nights, falling at the ends of the night. On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, “used to recite: ‘The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer.’” So it is one of the four prayers that was specifically mentioned with the afternoon prayer because of their unique merit. It was read in the accusative case for specificity and praise. And stand before God in prayer. Devoted remembering Him in standing, and devotion is remembrance in it. It was said that they were humble. Ibn al-Musayyab said that what is meant by it is devotion in the morning prayer.
2:239: 239- If you fear an enemy or otherwise. Then on foot or riding pray on foot or riding. On foot is the plural of rajil or rajul with the same meaning as qayyim and qiyam. It is evidence of the obligation of prayer during combat, and this is what Al-Shafi'i may God be pleased with him agreed with. Abu Hanifa may God have mercy on him said that one should not pray while walking or combat unless it is possible to stand. When you are safe and your fear is removed. Then remember God pray the prayer of safety or thank Him for safety as He taught you remembrance like what He taught you of the laws and how to pray in the states of fear and safety. Or thanks equivalent to it. Ma is a source or relative. What you did not know is the object of taught you.
2:240: 240 And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, a bequest for their wives Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza and Hafs read it in the accusative case on the basis of And those of you who die, they make a bequest, or To make a bequest, or God has prescribed for them a bequest, or He has obligated those who die to make a bequest. This is supported by the reading He has prescribed for you a bequest for your wives, a provision for a year in its place. The rest read it in the nominative case on the basis of And the bequest of those who die, or And their ruling is a bequest, or And those who die are entitled to a bequest, or A bequest has been prescribed for them, or A provision for a year was read instead of it. Provision for a year is in the accusative case with they bequeath if it is implied, otherwise with the bequest and with provision according to the reading of the one who read it because it means enjoyment. Other than the exit instead of it, or a confirmed source like your saying this saying is other than what you say, or a condition of their wives, meaning other than the exits, and the meaning is: that it is obligatory for those who die to bequeath before they die to their wives that they enjoy after them for a year with housing and maintenance, and this was in the beginning of Islam, then the period was abrogated by His saying: four months and ten and although it was earlier in recitation it was later in revelation, and the maintenance was dropped by her inheriting a quarter or an eighth, and housing for her after that is established according to us contrary to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him. If they go out from the husbands' home. There is no blame upon you O Imams. In what they do with themselves such as applying perfume and not observing mourning. From what is right of what the Shari'ah did not denounce, and this indicates that she was not obligated to stay in the husband's home and mourn for him, but rather she had the choice between staying and taking maintenance or going out and not doing so. And God is Almighty He takes revenge on whoever opposes Him among them. Hakim takes care of their interests.
2:241: 241-And for divorced women is a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the righteous. He established the provision for all divorced women after that, or he made it obligatory for one of them, and singling out some of the general in the ruling does not make it specific unless we allow the specification of the explicit with the implied. Therefore, Ibn Jubayr made it obligatory for every divorced woman, and he began others with what includes the obligatory and recommended provision. Some people said that what is meant is the maintenance of the waiting period, and it is possible that the lam is for the covenant and the repetition is for emphasis or for the repetition of the issue.
2:242: 242- Likewise referring to the previous rulings on divorce and waiting period. God makes clear to you His signs He promised that He will make clear to His servants the evidence and rulings that they need in this life and the hereafter. That you may understand that you may understand them and use reason in them.
2:243: 243-Have you not seen? is an expression of astonishment and confirmation for those who heard their story from the People of the Book and the masters of history. It may also be addressed to those who did not see or hear, as it has become an example of astonishment. To those who left their homes. He means the people of Dawardan, a village before Wasit, where a plague struck, so they fled, and God killed them and then revived them so that they would take heed and be certain that there is no escape from God Almighty's decree and destiny. Or a people from the Children of Israel whose king called them to jihad, so they fled for fear of death, so God killed them for eight days and then revived them. And they were thousands, meaning many thousands. It was said ten. It was said thirty. It was said seventy. It was said they were united, plural of thousand or thousand like qa'id and qa'ud, and the waw is for the state. Hadr al-Mawt is an object for it. Then God said to them, 'Die' meaning, He said to them, 'Die', so they died, as He said, Be, and it was. The meaning is that they died the death of one man, without a reason, by the command and will of God. It was said that an angel called them, but it was attributed to God to frighten and intimidate them. Then He revived them. It was said that Ezekiel, peace be upon him, passed by the people of Dawardan, and their bones were exposed and their limbs were scattered. He was amazed by that, so God revealed to him to call out to them, Stand up by the permission of God. So he called out, and they stood up, saying, "Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. There is no god but You." The benefit of the story is to encourage Muslims to strive and expose themselves to martyrdom, and to urge them to trust and submit to fate. Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind, as He revived them so that they would consider and succeed, and He related to them their situation so that they would see. But most people are not grateful, meaning they do not thank Him as they should. It is possible that what is meant by gratitude is consideration and insight.
2:244: 244- And fight in the cause of God When He made clear that fleeing from death is not a salvation from it and that what is destined will inevitably happen, He ordered them to fight, for if their time comes, it will be in the cause of God, otherwise victory and reward will be theirs. And know that God is Hearing of what the one who lags behind and the one who forerunner says. Knowing of what they conceal, and He is behind the recompense.
2:245: 245- Who is the one who lends to God? "Who is an interrogative nominative in the subject position, and that is its predicate, and who" is an attribute of that or its substitute, and God's lending is an example of presenting the work by which one seeks reward. "A good loan" is a good loan coupled with sincerity and goodness of heart, or a lawful and good loan. It was said: The good loan is by striving and spending in the way of God. "He will multiply it for him" so he will multiply his reward. He brought it out in the form of overcoming for exaggeration, and Asim read it in the accusative case as an answer to the question based on the meaning, for "Who is the one who lends to God is in the meaning of Will God lend to anyone?" Ibn Kathir read it in the nominative and stressed form, and Ibn Amir and Yaqub in the accusative case. "Many times over" is an abundance that only God, the Most High, can estimate. It was said that one is seven hundred, and multiples is the plural of double and its accusative is in the state of the accusative pronoun, or the second object to include the doubling of the meaning of becoming or the source on the basis that double is a source name and its plural is for diversification. And God contracts and expands He is stingy with some and expands with others according to what His wisdom requires, so do not be stingy with Him in what He has expanded upon you so that He does not change your condition. Nafi’, Al-Kisa’i, Al-Bazzi and Abu Bakr read it with a sad and the same is in Al-A’raf in the words of God Almighty: And He increased you in creation abundantly “And to Him you will be returned” so He will reward you according to what you have put forth.
2:246: 246-Have you not seen the assembly of the Children of Israel? "The assembly is a group who gather to consult, and it does not have a singular like the people, and min" is for partiality. "After Moses means after his death, and min" is for beginning. "When they said to a prophet of theirs" he is Joshua, or Simeon, or Samuel, peace be upon them. "Send us a king, and we will fight in the way of God appoint for us a prince with whom we can rise up to fight, who will manage its affairs and issue in it according to his opinion, and the jussive of naqtal" is for the answer. It was read in the nominative case as a state, meaning send him to us, desiring to fight, and "yaqatil with the letter ya is jussive and nominative as the answer and description of malakan". "He said, Is it possible that if fighting is decreed upon you, you will not fight? The condition separated asa and its predicate, and the meaning is I expect you to be cowardly about fighting if it is decreed upon you, so he introduced hal" as a verb of expectation, asking about what is expected with him, confirming and affirming. Nafi' read "asatum with the letter sin". They said, "Why should we not fight in the cause of God when we have been driven out from our homes and our children?" That is, what purpose do we have in abandoning fighting when we have been presented with what it requires and urges of being driven out from our homelands and separated from our children? This is because Goliath and the giants with him were living on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea between Egypt and Palestine. They defeated the Children of Israel, took their homes, captured their children, and took four hundred and forty of the sons of kings captive. "But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned back, except for a few of them" three hundred and thirteen, the number of the people of Badr. "And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers" is a warning to them for their wrongdoing in abandoning jihad.
2:247: 247- And their prophet said to them, 'Indeed, God has sent you Talut as a king.' Talut is a Hebrew name like David, and he made it a verb from the word 'tall', meaning to push away. It was narrated that when their prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called upon God to make him king, he brought a stick by which to measure who would rule over them, and none could match it except Talut. They said, 'How can he have kingship over us?' How did he get that and deserve it? And we are more deserving of kingship than he, and he has not been given an abundance of wealth. The fact is that I am more deserving of kingship than him, in inheritance and position, and he is poor, with no wealth to support himself with. They only said that because Talut was a poor shepherd, a water-carrier, or a tanner, from the sons of Benjamin, and the prophecy and kingship were not among them. Rather, the prophecy was among the sons of Levi, son of Jacob, and the kingship was among the sons of Judah, and among them were people from the two tribes. "He said, 'God has chosen him over you and has increased him abundantly in knowledge and stature. And God gives His kingdom to whomever He wills. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.'" When they ruled out his possession due to his poverty and the fall of his lineage, he responded to them. First, that the main point is that God, the Most High, has chosen him and has selected him over you, and He knows best what is in your best interests. Second, that the condition is abundant knowledge to enable him to know political matters, and a large body to be more dangerous to hearts, and stronger in resisting the enemy and enduring wars, not what you mentioned. And God has increased him in both of them, and the man standing would stretch out his hand and reach his head. Third, that God, the Most High, is the absolute owner of the kingdom, so He can give it to whomever He wills. Fourth, that He is of vast grace, and He gives to the poor and enriches them. He knows who is worthy of kingship, whether relative or otherwise.
2:248: 248- And their prophet said to them when they asked him for proof that He, the Most High, chose Talut and made him king over them. The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you. The chest is a noun derived from to return, which means to return, as it continues to return to what comes out of it. It is not a noun of action due to paucity, such as salsal and qalaq. Whoever reads it with the ha may have substituted it for it as he substituted the ta of femininity due to their sharing in whispering and increase. He means by it the box of the Torah, which was made of shamshad wood covered with gold, about three cubits by two cubits. In it is tranquility from your Lord. The pronoun refers to the coming, meaning that in its coming there is tranquility and reassurance for you, or to the Ark, meaning that what you are reassured by is deposited in it, which is the Torah. When Moses, peace be upon him, fought, he would bring it forward, so the souls of the Children of Israel would be at peace and they would not flee. It was said that it was an image of emerald or ruby, with a head and a tail like a cat's head and tail and two wings, so it groaned and the ark was carried towards the enemy and they followed it, and when it settled they stood firm and calmed down and victory descended. It was said that it was an image of the prophets from Adam to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon them. It was said that the ark is the heart and the tranquility is what is in it of knowledge and sincerity and its arrival at the destination of his heart is a place of knowledge and dignity after it was not there. And the remainder of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind is the scraps of the tablets and the staff of Moses and his clothes and the turban of Aaron, and their family are their sons or themselves. The family is inserted to magnify their status, or the prophets of the Children of Israel because they are their cousins. The angels carried it. It was said that God raised it after Moses, and the angels descended with it while they were looking at it. It was also said that it was with their prophets after him, seeking victory through it until they corrupted and the infidels defeated them over it. It was in the land of Goliath until God made Saul the king, and a calamity befell them until five cities were destroyed. They took the Ark as a bad omen, so they placed it on two bulls, and the angels drove them to Saul. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers. It is possible that it is part of the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and that it is the beginning of a speech from God, the Most High, the Most Great. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 4 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Baqarah, and the first verses of Sūrat āl ʿIm'rān. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. Portions of this work have been translated using AI (machine-assisted translation) and post-edited for clarity and accuracy. 2:249: 249- When Talut departed with the soldiers he separated with them from his country to fight the giants, and its origin is to separate himself from it, but when it was used frequently, its object was deleted and it became like an intransitive verb. It was narrated that he said to them, None shall go out with me except the active, free young man. Eighty thousand of those he had chosen gathered around him, and it was summer, so they took the desert and asked him to make a river flow for them. "He said, 'Indeed, God is testing you with a river.' He will treat you as one who is tested by what you have suggested. 'Whoever drinks from it is not of me.' He is not one of my followers, or he is not united with me. 'And whoever does not taste it is of me.' That is, whoever does not taste it from the taste of something if he tastes it as food or drink. The poet said: If you wish, I have not tasted a drop of water or a cold.' And he only knew that by revelation if he was a prophet as it was said, or by the Prophet's information, peace and blessings be upon him. "Except for he who takes a handful with his hand is an exception to his statement, So whoever drinks from it. The second clause was presented to emphasize it, as the Saabiyyun presented it to the report of his statement, Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews", and the meaning is the permission for a little but not a lot. Ibn Amir and the Kufians read "a handful" with a damma on the ghain. "So they drank from it except a few of them" meaning they drank from it, since the origin of drinking from it is to be in the middle, and the generalization of the first is to connect the exception, or they drank from it excessively except a few of them. It was read with the nominative case based on the meaning, since his statement, "So they drank from it" is in the meaning of they did not obey him, and the few were three hundred and thirteen men. It was said three thousand. It was said: a thousand. It was narrated that whoever limited himself to a handful was given a cup for his drinking and his water container, and whoever did not limit himself to it, his lips became black and he was not able to continue. And so is the world for the one intending the Hereafter. "So when he and those who believed with him had passed it" meaning the few who did not disobey him. "They said" meaning some of them to each other. We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers, because of their great number and strength. Those who think they will meet God said, meaning the sincere ones among them who were certain of meeting God and expected His reward, or knew that they would be martyred soon and meet God the Most High, said. It was said: They are the few who stood firm with him, and the pronoun in they said refers to the many who abandoned him, as an apology for staying behind and discouraging the few, as if they were talking to him and the river was between them. How often has a small company overcome a large one by God’s permission, by His wisdom and facilitation. How many can be a statement or a question, and who is a clarifier or an addition. A group is a division of people from fa’wa meaning to split its head, or from fa’a meaning to return, so its weight is fa’ah or fulah. And God is with the patient, with victory and reward.
2:250: 250- And when they came forward to face Goliath and his soldiers," meaning they appeared to them and approached them. "They said, 'Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.'" They turned to God Almighty with supplication, and in it is a powerful arrangement, as they first asked for patience to be poured into their hearts, which is the essence of the matter, then for steadfastness in the pitfalls of war caused by it, then for victory over the enemy, which usually results from both.
2:251: 251- So they defeated them by God's permission so they defeated them with His victory, or accompanying His victory over them in response to their prayer. And David killed Goliath It was said: Isha was in the army of Talut with six of his sons, and David was the seventh of them and he was young and tending sheep, so God revealed to their prophet that he was the one who would kill Goliath, so he asked his father for him and he came and three stones had spoken to him on the way and they said to him that you will kill Goliath with us, so he carried them in his saddlebags and threw them at him and killed him, then Talut married him to his daughter. And God gave him the kingdom meaning the kingdom of the Children of Israel and they had not gathered together in a kingdom before David. And wisdom meaning prophecy. And taught him of whatever He willed such as narration and the speech of animals and birds. “And had it not been that God, glory be to Him, repels some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted. But God is full of bounty to the worlds.” And had it not been that He, glory be to Him, repels some people by means of others and gives victory to the Muslims over the infidels and prevents their corruption, they would have been victorious and spread corruption on the earth, or the earth would have been corrupted by their evil. Nafi’ read here and in al-Hajj 22:God’s defense.
2:252: 252- These are the signs of God referring to what was narrated about the story of the thousands, the kingship of Saul, the coming of the Ark, the defeat of the giants, and David killing Goliath. We recite them to you in truth in the exact manner that the People of the Book and the masters of history do not doubt. And indeed, you are among the messengers because you were tested with them without knowing or hearing.
2:253: 253- Those messengers refers to the group whose stories are mentioned in the surah, or the one known to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the group of messengers, and the lam is for comprehensiveness. We preferred some of them over others by giving them a special virtue that no one else has. Among them is he to whom God spoke as a preference, and he is Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: Moses and Muhammad, may God bless them both, God spoke to Moses on the night of confusion and at the mountain, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the ascension when he was two bow lengths away or nearer and there was a great distance between them, and it was read God spoke and God spoke in the accusative case, because he spoke to God as God spoke to him, and therefore it was said God spoke to him in the sense of speaking to him. And He raised some of them in degrees by giving him preference over others in multiple ways, or in distant ranks. And he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for He singled him out with the general call, the many arguments, the continuous miracles, the successive signs with the passage of time, and the scientific and practical virtues that are beyond counting. The vagueness is to magnify his status as if he is the specific knowledge of this description that does not need specification. It was said: Abraham, peace be upon him, He singled him out with the trait that is the highest of ranks. It was also said: Idris, peace be upon him, because God Almighty said: And We raised him to a high station. It was also said: The messengers of resolve. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. He singled him out with specification because the Jews and Christians were excessive in belittling and glorifying him, and He made his miracles the reason for his preference because they are clear proofs and great miracles that no one else has gathered. And if God had willed, meaning He had guided all people. Those after them would not have fought one another, after the messengers. After the clear proofs had come to them, meaning the clear miracles because of their differences in religion and their misleading of one another. “But they differed. Some of them believed” by His guidance to adhere to the religion of the prophets as a favor. And some of them disbelieved by turning away from it by abandoning it. And if God had willed, they would not have fought He repeated it for emphasis. But God does what He wills He guides whomever He wills as a favor, and abandons whomever He wills as justice. The verse is evidence that the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, are of different ranks, and that it is permissible to prefer some of them over others, but with a decisive factor because the consideration of conjecture is with regard to action and that events are in the hand of God, the Most High, and are subject to His will, whether good or evil, faith or disbelief.
2:254: 254- O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided for you" what is obligatory for you to spend. "Before there comes a Day in which there is no trading, no friendship, no intercession" before a Day comes in which you will not be able to make up for what you have neglected, nor be saved from its punishment, since there is no trading in it so that you can obtain what you spend, or ransom yourself with it from the punishment, nor friendship until your friends help you with it or forgive you for it, nor intercession "except for he to whom the Most Gracious has given permission and whose word He is pleased with" until you speak about intercessors who will intercede for you in reducing what is on your debts. The three of them were raised with the intention of generalization because they are in the estimation an answer: Is there trading in it? Or friendship? Or intercession? Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ya'qub opened it according to the original. And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers. He means that those who abandon zakat are the wrongdoers who wronged themselves, or put the money in the wrong place and spent it in the wrong way. So he put the disbelievers in its place to make things difficult for them and threaten them, like his saying: And whoever disbelieves instead of and whoever does not perform Hajj and to indicate that abandoning zakat is one of the characteristics of the disbelievers, because the Most High said: And woe to the polytheists * Who do not give zakat.
2:255: 255-God, there is no god but He is a subject and predicate, and the meaning is that He is the only One deserving of worship, and no one else. There is a difference of opinion regarding salvation, as to whether it implies an example for the latter in existence or whether it is correct for it to exist. The Living is the One who can know and determine, and everything that is correct for Him is obligatory and does not cease due to His impossibility of power and possibility. The Self-Sustaining is the One who is constantly in charge of managing creation and preserving it, so He is responsible for whoever undertakes the matter if he preserves it. And al-Qiyam and al-Qayyim were read. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep drowsiness is a lethargy that precedes sleep. Ibn al-Ruqa'a said: And Sinan, I mean sleepiness, I saw a squint in his eye, but he is not asleep Sleep is a condition that the animal is exposed to from the relaxation of the nerves of the brain from the moisture of the rising vapors, so that the apparent senses stop feeling at all, and the Sunnah is presented before it and the measure of exaggeration is its opposite in the order of existence, and the sentence is a negation of the likeness and an affirmation of His being alive and self-sustaining, for whoever is overcome by drowsiness or sleep is the one who is deprived of life and deficient in preservation and management, and therefore the conjunction was left in it and in the sentences that follow it To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is a confirmation of His self-sustaining and an argument with it for His uniqueness in divinity, and what is meant by what is in them is within their reality or outside of them and is established in them, so it is more eloquent than His saying: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, “Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission?” is a statement of the greatness of His status, glory be to Him, and that no one is equal to Him or comes close to Him, and is independent in repelling what He wants through intercession and submission, let alone obstructing Him through stubbornness or opposition, i.e. quarreling. He knows what is before them and what is behind them what is before them and what is after them, or vice versa because you are the receiver of the future and the one who has turned away from the past, or the affairs of this world, and the affairs of the Hereafter or vice versa, or what they sense and what they understand, or what they perceive and what they do not perceive, and the pronoun refers to what is in the heavens and the earth, because in them are rational beings, or what is indicated by that from the angels and prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge of His information. Except what He wills that they know, and He connected it to what came before it because their combination indicates His uniqueness with complete intrinsic knowledge indicating His Oneness, glory be to Him, the Most High. His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth a depiction of His greatness and an abstract representation like the Almighty’s saying: And they have not appraised God with His true appraisal “And the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand” There is no throne in reality, nor is there a seat. It was said that His throne is a metaphor for His knowledge or His kingdom, taken from the throne of the world and the kingdom. It was said that it is a body in front of the Throne, and that is why it was called a Kursi, surrounding the seven heavens, because of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: “The seven heavens and the seven earths are not compared to the Kursi except as a ring in a desert, and the superiority of the Throne over the Kursi is like the superiority of that desert over that ring.” Perhaps it is the sphere known as the sphere of the zodiac, and it is originally the name of what one sits on and is not superior to the seat of the one sitting, as if it is attributed to the Kursi, which is the padded one. And it does not burden Him means it does not weigh Him down, taken from the word awd which means crookedness. He preserved them means He preserved the heavens and the earth, so the subject was deleted and the infinitive was added to the object. And He is the Most High the One who is exalted above rivals and likenesses. The Great the One who is despised in comparison to Him, everything else besides Him. This verse includes the most important divine issues, as it indicates that He, the Most High, is One in divinity, characterized by life, necessary for Himself and the creator of others, as the Self-Sustainer is the One who sustains Himself and establishes others, free from bias and incarnation, free from change and weakness, not compatible with ghosts and not affected by what affects spirits, the Owner of the Kingdom and the Kingdom, the Creator of the principles and branches, the Possessor of severe power, with whom no one intercedes except he who permits Him, the Knower of all things, their clear and hidden, their whole and their parts, the Vast in kingdom and power, everything that is right for Him to own and be able to do, no difficulty harms Him, and no matter distracts Him, He is exalted above what He comprehends, and He is great and cannot be encompassed by understanding, and for this reason the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “The greatest verse in the Qur’an is the Throne Verse. Whoever recites it, God sends an angel who writes down his good deeds and erases his bad deeds until the next day from that hour.” He said, “Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every prescribed prayer, nothing will prevent him from entering Paradise except death. No one will be persistent in reciting it except a friend or a worshipper. Whoever recites it when he goes to bed, God will make him, his neighbor, his neighbor’s neighbor, and the houses around him safe.”
2:256: 256- There is no compulsion in religion because compulsion is forcing another to do an action in which he sees no good that would compel him to do it, but the right way has become distinct from the wrong way faith is distinguished from disbelief by clear verses, and the evidence indicates that faith is the right way that leads to eternal happiness and disbelief is the wrong way that leads to eternal misery, and when this becomes clear to the wise person, his soul rushes to faith in order to attain happiness and salvation, and he does not need compulsion or coercion. And before informing about the meaning of the prohibition, that is, do not hate in religion, and it is either general and abrogated by His saying, Fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh with them, or specific to the People of the Book, as it was narrated (that an Ansari had two sons who converted to Christianity before the mission, then they came to Medina and their father stuck to them and said: By God, I will not leave you until you become Muslims, but they refused, so they argued before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Ansari said: O Messenger of God, will my heels enter the Fire while I am looking at him? So it was revealed and he left them alone). So whoever disbelieves in Taghut in Satan, or idols, or everything that is worshipped besides God, or turns away from the worship of God Almighty. So the word taghut is derived from tyranny, and his eye and his blame are turned upside down. And believes in God in monotheism and believing in the Messengers. He has grasped the firmest handhold seeking to hold back from himself with the firm handhold from the strong rope, and it is borrowed for holding on to the truth from correct vision and sound opinion. It has no break It has no interruption. It is said, I broke it and it broke. “And God is All-Hearing” of words, All-Knowing of intentions. Perhaps it is an enumeration of hypocrisy.
2:257: 257- God is the ally of those who believe He loves them, or He takes care of their affairs, and what is meant by them is the one who desires to believe and it is established in his knowledge that he believes. He brings them out with His guidance and success. From darknesses the darkness of ignorance and following desires and accepting whispers and doubts that lead to disbelief. To the light to the guidance connected to faith, and the sentence is a predicate after a predicate, or a state of what is hidden in the predicate, or of the relative, or of both of them, or a clear resumption, or a confirmation of the guardianship. And those who disbelieve, their allies are the Taghut meaning the devils, or the misguiders from desires and Satan and others. They bring them out from the light into darknesses from the light that they were given by nature, to disbelief and corruption of readiness and preoccupation with desires, or from the light of clear proofs to the darkness of doubts and suspicions. It was said: It was revealed about a people who apostatized from Islam, and attributing the expulsion to the tyrant on the basis of causation does not negate the connection of His Almighty power and will to it. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. This is a threat and a warning, and perhaps the fact that it is not met with a promise to the believers is to magnify their status.
2:258: 258-Have you not seen him who argued with Abraham about his Lord? Astonishment at the argument with Nimrod and his foolishness. That God gave him the kingdom because He gave him, that is, He made him arrogant by giving him the kingdom and made him argue, or he argued for it as thanks to Him in the opposite way, like saying you opposed me because I was good to you, or the time that God gave him the kingdom is his argument against those who denied giving God the kingdom, the infidels from the Mu'tazila. When Abraham said is an adverb for argued, or a substitute for that God gave him the kingdom in the second way. My Lord is He who gives life and causes death by creating life and death in bodies. Hamza read Rabb without the ya. He said, I give life and cause death by pardoning the killing and by killing. Nafi' read Ana without the alif. Abraham said, 'God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.' Abraham, peace be upon him, turned away from objecting to his corrupt opposition to arguing with what he is not capable of, in this manner of deception, in order to avoid trouble. In reality, it is a shift from a hidden example to a clear example of His abilities that no one else can bring, not from one argument to another. Perhaps Nimrod claimed that he was able to do everything that God does, so Abraham refuted him with that, but what prompted him to do that was the king's arrogance and foolishness, or his belief in incarnation. It was said that when Abraham, peace be upon him, broke the idols, he imprisoned them for days, then took them out to burn them. He said to him, Who is your Lord to whom you call? and he had a need for Him. Then the one who disbelieved was dumbfounded. So he became dumbfounded. It was read, Then he was dumbfounded, meaning, I overcame Abraham the disbeliever. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people, those who wronged themselves by refusing to accept guidance. It was said that He will not guide them to the path of argument or the path of salvation, or the path to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection.
2:259: 259-"Or like the one who passed by a village its meaning is or have you seen the like of the one so it was deleted because of the indication of have you not seen" on it, and it was specified with the letter of comparison because the one who denies the revival is many and the one who is ignorant of its manner is more than can be counted, unlike the one who claims divinity, and it was said that the kaf is added and the meaning of the speech is have you not seen the one who argued or the one who passed. And it was said that it is an appositive carried on the meaning as if it was said: Have you not seen the like of the one who argued, or the like of the one who passed. And it was said: It is from the speech of Abraham, he mentioned it as an answer to his opposition and its meaning is or if you revive, then revive like the revival of God Almighty who passed by a village. And he is Uzair bin Sharhya. Or Al-Khidr, or a disbeliever in the resurrection. And his arrangement with Nimrod supports this. And the village is the Holy House when Nebuchadnezzar destroyed it. And it was said that it is the village from which thousands came out. And it was said other than them and its derivation is from villages which is the plural. "And it is empty on its thrones" empty, its walls falling on its roofs. "He said, 'How will God revive this after its death?'" In recognition of the inability to know the way to revive, and in awe of the power of the reviver if the speaker is a believer, and inconceivable if he is an unbeliever. "How" is in the accusative case as an adverbial phrase meaning when or as a state meaning how. "So God caused him to die for a hundred years" So He caused him to remain dead for a hundred years, or God caused him to die so he remained dead for a hundred years. "Then He resurrected him" with the resurrection. "He said, 'How long did you remain?'" The speaker is God and it is permissible for Him to speak to him even if he is an unbeliever because he believed after the resurrection or was close to believing. It was said that he was an angel or a prophet. "He said, 'I remained a day or part of a day,'" as one who thinks. It was said that he died at noon and was resurrected after a hundred, before sunset, so he said before looking at the sun a day, then he turned and saw the rest of it, so he said, "or part of a day," in contrast. "He said, 'Rather, you have remained a hundred years. So look at your food and your drink; it has not become stale.' It has not changed with the passage of time, and its derivation is from the word sunnah. The letter ha is original if you consider the lam of sunnah to be a ha, and a silent ha if you consider a waw. It was said that its origin is lam yatasanna from stained mud, so the third nun was replaced with a vowel like taqdaa al-bazi." The pronoun is singular because food and drink are like one kind. It was said that his food was figs and grapes, and his drink was juice or milk, and everything remained the same. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "lam yatasanna without the letter ha" in the connection. "And look at your donkey," how its bones have dispersed, or look at it intact in its place as you tied it up. We preserved it without water and fodder as we preserved food and drink from changing. The first is more indicative of the situation and more appropriate for what follows. "And that We may make you a sign for the people," meaning, We did that to make you a sign. It was narrated that he came to his people on his donkey and said, I am Ezra, but they denied him. He recited the Torah from memory, and no one had memorized it before him. They recognized him by that and said, He is the son of God. It was said that when he returned to his home, he was a young man and his children were old men. When he told them something, they said, A story of a hundred years. “And look at the bones,” meaning the bones of the donkey, or the dead whom he was amazed at having been brought back to life. How We resurrect them, meaning how We resurrect them, or how We raise some of them on top of others and ride them on them. How is the object of resurrected, and the sentence is a state of the bones, meaning: look at them as they are brought back to life. Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, Abu Amr, and Ya’qub read We resurrect them from God resurrects the dead, and it was read We resurrect them from Nashr meaning spread. “Then We clothed them with flesh. Then when it became clear to him,” the subject of it became clear is implied and explained by what follows, the meaning of it is, “So when it became clear to him that God has power over all things.” He said, I know that God has power over all things. The first was omitted because the second indicated it, or what preceded it explains it, So when what was unclear to him became clear to him. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read, He said, I know, as a command, addressing her, or he himself addressed her with it as a way of rebuking her.
2:260: 260- And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead,' he only asked that so that his knowledge would become evident. It was said that when Nimrod said, I give life and cause death, he said to him, Indeed, God Almighty's revival is the return of the soul to its body. So he said that so that his heart would be reassured about the answer if he was asked about it again. He said, 'Do you not believe?' that I am able to give life by reconstructing and reviving. He said that to him and he knew that he had drowned people in faith so that he would answer with what he answered so that the listeners would know his purpose. He said, 'Yes, but so that my heart may be reassured.' That is, yes I believed, but I asked that to increase my insight and calm the heart of the one who sees the revelation or the evidence. He said, 'Take four birds.' It was said, a peacock, a rooster, a crow, and a dove. Some of them mentioned the eagle instead of the dove, and in it is an allusion to the fact that reviving the soul with eternal life is only achieved by killing the love of lusts and decorations, which is a characteristic of the peacock, and the famous attack of the rooster, and the baseness of the soul and the remoteness of hope, which is characteristic of the crow, and the haughtiness and haste to desire, which is characteristic of the dove.
