And he only singled out the bird because it is closer to man and gathers the characteristics of the animal, and the bird is a source named after it or a plural like companions. Fasrahinna ilayk means,... Hunting necks is not a trick among them, but the tips of spears depict it. And he said: A branch that becomes good and a barrier as if it were on a lion, the branches of the vineyards. The reading of Fasrahunna with a damma or a kasra on the sad is two dialects, with a shaddah on the ra from sara yasrahu and yasrahu if he gathered it and fasrahunna is from tasriya which is also a collection. Then place on every mountain a part of them meaning then divide them and distribute their parts on the mountains that are in your presence. It was said that there were four. And it was said that there were seven. Abu Bakr read jaz'u and jaz'u with a damma on the zay wherever it occurred. Then call them say to them come by the permission of God the Most High. They will come to you running running quickly, flying or walking. It was narrated that he ordered that they be slaughtered, their feathers plucked, and they cut them up, and he would hold their heads, and mix the rest of their parts and distribute them on the mountains, then he would call them. So he did that as an indication that whoever wants to revive himself with eternal life must turn to the physical powers, kill them and mix some of them with others until their strength is broken, and they will obey him quickly when he calls them with the call of reason or the law. It is sufficient for you as a witness to the virtue of Abraham, peace be upon him, and the blessing of humility in supplication and good manners in asking. God Almighty showed him what He wanted to show him immediately in the easiest way, and showed him honored after He had caused him to die for a hundred years. And know that God is Exalted in Might He is not unable to do what He wants. Wise He has the utmost wisdom in everything He does and leaves.
2:261: 261- The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain of corn meaning their spending is like a grain of corn, or their example is like that of one who sows a grain of corn, with the addition omitted. It produces seven ears of corn, in each ear a hundred grains The production is attributed to the grain because it is one of the causes, just as it is attributed to the earth and water. The one who produces in reality is God, the Most High, and the meaning is that a stalk emerges from it, each of which branches out seven branches, each of which has an ear containing a hundred grains. This is a metaphor that does not necessarily occur, and it may be in the case of corn and millet, in wheat, in productive lands. And God multiplies that multiplication for whom He wills by His grace and according to the state of the spender in terms of his sincerity and effort, and because of the difference in the amounts of reward for deeds. And God is Bountiful He does not find it difficult to obtain what He bestows of increase. Knowing of the intention of the spender and the amount of his spending.
2:262: 262- Those who spend their wealth in the way of God and do not follow up what they have spent with reminders or injury. It was revealed about Uthman, may God be pleased with him, as he equipped the Army of Hardship with a thousand camels with their saddlebags and saddles. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, as he brought the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, four thousand dirhams as charity. Representation means that one is considered to have done good to someone. Injury means that one is arrogant towards him because of what he has bestowed upon him. There is a difference between spending and leaving reminders and injury. They will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve. Perhaps the letter fa was not included in it, and what was attributed to it included the meaning of a condition, giving the impression that they are worthy of that even if they did not do it, so how would it be for them if they did it.
2:263: 263- A kind word is a nice response. And forgiveness is overlooking the beggar and the need, or attaining forgiveness from God by a nice response, or pardon from the beggar by making an excuse and forgiving his response. Better than charity followed by injury is report about them, and it is correct to begin with the indefinite noun because it is specific to the description. And God is Rich from spending on those and harming. Forbearing from treating those who do good and harm with punishment.
2:264: 264- O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury. Do not invalidate their reward with either of them. Like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in God and the Last Day. Like the invalidity of the hypocrite who shows off in his spending and does not want thereby the pleasure of God Almighty or the reward of the Hereafter, or similar to the one who spends to be seen by people, and the kaf is in the accusative case as a source or a state, and showing off is accusative as a direct object or a state meaning showing off or the source, meaning spending showing off. "So his example" meaning the example of the hypocrite in his spending is like the example of a smooth rock. "On which there is dust and a downpour falls" heavy rain. "And it leaves it solid" smooth and free of dust. “They are not able to do anything of what they have earned.” They do not benefit from what they have done out of hypocrisy, nor do they find any reward for it. The pronoun refers to the one who spends, considering the meaning, because what is meant by it is the genus, or the group, as in His statement: Those whose blood was shed in Falaj are the people, all the people, O Umm Khalid. And God does not guide the disbelieving people to goodness and guidance. It is an allusion to the fact that showing off, showing off, and causing harm in spending are characteristics of the disbelievers, and the believer must avoid them.
2:265: 265- The parable of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of God and to strengthen themselves and to strengthen some of themselves in faith, for wealth is the brother of the soul, so whoever spends his wealth for the sake of God strengthens some of himself, and whoever spends his wealth and his soul strengthens all of it, or to confirm Islam and to achieve the reward, starting from the origin of their souls, and in it is an alert that the wisdom of spending for the spender is to purify the soul from miserliness and love of money. Like a garden on a high place meaning, and the example of the spending of these people in zakat is like an orchard on a high place, for its trees are more beautiful to look at and its fruit is more fragrant. Ibn Amir and Asim read on a high place with the fat-ha and it was read with the kasra and all three of them are dialects in it. A heavy downpour struck it heavy rain. It brought forth its fruit its fruits. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu Amr read it with the sukoon for ease. Twice twice as much as you used to bear fruit because of the downpour. What is meant by double is the same as what is meant by one pair in the Almighty’s saying: Of every pair, two. It was said: four times its like, and its accusative is in the state of being multiplied. But if no downpour strikes it, then a drizzle means that it strikes it, or what strikes it is dew, or a drizzle that is sufficient for it due to the generosity of its origin and the coolness of its air due to its high place. It is the small raindrops, and the meaning is that the expenditures of these people are pure with God and are not wasted under any circumstances, even if they vary in consideration of what is added to them from its conditions. It is possible that the representation of their state with God is like Paradise on the hill and their expenditures, many and few, are excessive in their closeness to the downpour and dew. And God is Seeing of what you do is a warning against showing off and an encouragement to sincerity.
2:266: 266- Would any of you like the hamza in it is for denial to have a garden of palm trees and grapes with rivers flowing beneath it, and for him in it all kinds of fruits He made the garden from them with what is in it of other trees, to make them superior to each other due to their honor and the abundance of their benefits, then he mentioned that it has all kinds of fruits to indicate that it contains all kinds of trees, and it is possible that what is meant by fruits is the benefits and old age befalls him meaning old age, because poverty and poverty in old age are more difficult, and the waw is for the state or for conjunction based on the meaning, so it is as if it was said: Would any of you like to have a garden and be old? and have weak offspring young, they are not able to earn. and a hurricane in it containing fire struck it and it was burned is a conjunction to struck it, or it is based on the meaning. A hurricane is a violent wind that reflects from the earth to the sky, round like a column. The meaning is to represent the state of someone who does good deeds and adds to them what nullifies them, such as envy and harm, in regret and sorrow. Then, when the Day of Resurrection comes and his need for them becomes intense, he will find them nullified by a state like this. The most similar to him is the one who wanders in secret in the world of the kingdom, and ascends with his thought to the side of the Almighty, then turns back on his heels to the world of falsehood and turns to what is other than the truth and makes his efforts scattered in vain. Thus does God make clear to you the verses that you may reflect. That is, that you may reflect on them and take heed from them.
2:267: 267- O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned from its lawful or good things. And from that which We have produced for you from the earth meaning, and from the good things which We have produced for you from grains, fruits, and minerals, so the complement was omitted because it was mentioned before. And do not aim at the bad thereof meaning, do not aim at the bad thereof, meaning from the money, or from that which We have produced for you. And it is specified for that because the difference in it is greater, and it was read, Do not aim at and Do not aim at with a damma on the ta'. You spend is an implied state of the subject of aimmamwa, and it is permissible for it to be related to it from it and the pronoun is for the bad and the sentence is a state of it. And you are not taking it meaning, and your condition is that you do not take it in your rights because of its badness. Unless you close your eyes to it except that you are tolerant of it, a metaphor from the one who closed his gaze if he lowered it. It was read taghamdhu meaning bear closing your eyes, or be found closing your eyes. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: They used to give in charity the husks and pits of dates, but they were forbidden from doing so. And know that God is independent of your spending, and He only commands you to do so for your benefit. Praiseworthy for accepting and rewarding it.
2:268: 268- The devil promises you poverty in spending, and the promise is originally common in good and evil. Poverty is read with damma and sukoon and with two dhammahs and two fathahs. And he orders you to immorality and entices you to be stingy, and the Arabs call the miserly one fahish. It was said that it means sins. And God promises you forgiveness from Him meaning He promises you forgiveness for your sins in spending. And bounty a replacement better than what you spent in this world, or in the hereafter. And God is Vast meaning He is Vast in bounty for whoever spends. Knowing of his spending.
2:269: 269- He grants wisdom means achieving knowledge and perfecting it. Whom He wills is the first object of the verb, to emphasize the second object. And whomever is granted wisdom is the object because it is intended. Jacob read it with a kasra, meaning whoever God grants wisdom. He has been granted much good meaning: much good? Because the best of both worlds has been granted to him. And he does not remember nor is he admonished by what was narrated of the verses, or he does not think, for the one who thinks is like the one who remembers what God has placed in his heart of knowledge by force. Except for those of understanding those with pure minds free from the impurities of illusion and inclination to following desires.
2:270: 270- And whatever you spend little or much, secretly or openly, in right or wrong. Or whatever you vow conditionally or unconditionally, in obedience or disobedience. God knows it and will reward you for it. And for the wrongdoers who spend in sins and make vows therein, or who withhold charity and do not fulfill vows. Any helpers from God who will support them and protect them from His punishment.
2:271: 271- If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good. The good thing is to disclose them. Ibn Amir, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with a fatha on the noon and a kasra on the 'ayn according to the original. Abu Bakr, Abu Amr and Qaloon read it with a kasra on the noon and a sukoon on the 'ayn. It was narrated from them with a kasra on the noon and a hidden vowel on the 'ayn, which is more correct. But if you conceal it and give it to the poor, meaning you give it while concealing it. It is better for you, concealing it is better for you. This is in voluntary charity and for the one who is not known for his wealth, as giving the intended benefit to someone else is better to remove suspicion from him. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, A secret voluntary charity is better than its public nature seventy times, and an obligatory charity, its public nature is better than its secret nature twenty-five times. And He will expiate for you some of your misdeeds. Ibn Amir and Asim read it in the narration of Hafs with the letter Ya, meaning, And God expiates, or concealment. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Asim read it in the narration of Ibn Ayyash and Yaqub with the letter Noun, in the nominative case, as a verbal noun in the beginning or a nominative noun conjoined with what comes after the letter Fa, meaning, And We expiate. Nafi', Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read it in the subjunctive mood, in the place of the letter Fa and what comes after it. It was read with the letter Ta, in the nominative and subjunctive, and the verb refers to charity. And God is Aware of what you do, encouraging secrecy.
2:272: 272- You are not responsible for their guidance You are not required to make people guided, but you are responsible for guidance and urging them to do good deeds, and forbidding them from doing evil deeds such as showing off, harming others, and spending evil deeds. But God guides whom He wills is clear that guidance is from God Almighty and by His will, and that it is specific to some people and not others. And whatever you spend of good of known spending and is for yourselves it is for yourselves and no one else will benefit from it, so do not show off to it and do not spend evil deeds. And you do not spend except seeking the countenance of God is a state, and it is as if he said and whatever you spend of good is for yourselves, not spending except seeking the countenance of God and seeking His reward. Or it is a conjunction to what came before it, meaning your spending is only for seeking His countenance, so why do you show off with it and spend evil deeds. It was said: negation in the sense of prohibition. And whatever you spend in good will be repaid to you in full its reward is multiplied many times over, so it is a confirmation of the previous condition, or what is left for the spender in response to the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): O God, grant to the spender a replacement, and to the withholder a loss. It was narrated that some Muslims had in-laws and foster parents among the Jews, and they used to spend on them, but when they converted to Islam they hated to benefit them, so this was revealed. This is not in relation to what is obligatory, as for what is obligatory, it is not permissible to spend it on the disbelievers. And you will not be wronged meaning you will not reduce the reward for your spending.
2:273: 273- For the poor is related to an omitted word, meaning, dedicate what you spend to the poor, or make what you spend for the poor, or your charity for the poor. Those who are restricted in the cause of God are restricted by jihad. They are unable because of their preoccupation with it. Strikes in the land going about in it to earn a living. It was said that they were the people of the Suffa, who were about four hundred of the poor immigrants who lived in the Suffa of the mosque, spending their time learning and worshipping. They used to go out in every expedition that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out. The ignorant would think them because of their condition, and Ibn Amir, Asim, and Hamzah read with the seen open. Rich from self-restraint because of their self-restraint from asking, You will recognize them by their mark from weakness and shabby condition, and the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone. They do not ask people insistently. Insistence, which is to persist with the one being asked until he gives him, from their saying He gave me from the excess of what he has, meaning he gave me from the excess of what he has. The meaning is that they do not ask, and if they ask out of necessity, they do not insist. It was said: It is a negation of both matters, like his saying: There is no love that does not follow its lighthouse He put it in the accusative case as a source, as it is a type of question, or as a state. Whatever good you spend, God is Knowing of it. It encourages spending, especially on these people.
2:274: 274-Those who spend their wealth by night and by day, secretly and publicly meaning they fill all times and conditions with good. It was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, as a charity of forty thousand dinars, ten by night and ten by day, ten in secret and ten in public. It was said about the Commander of the Faithful, Ali, may God be pleased with him: He only owned four dirhams, so he gave away a dirham by night and a dirham by day, a dirham secretly and a dirham publicly. It was said: Regarding tying horses in the way of God and spending on them. They will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve is the report of those who spend, and the fa is for causality. It was said for the conjunction and the report is omitted, meaning, and among them are those, and therefore it is permissible to stop at and publicly.
3:131: 275- Those who consume interest meaning those who take it, and eating is mentioned because it is the greatest benefit of money, and because interest is common in foods and is an increase in the term, such as selling food, or cash for cash on term, or in compensation, such that one of them is sold for more of the same type, and it was written with the waw like in prayer for emphasis in language and the alif was added after it to resemble the waw of the plural. They do not rise if they are raised from their graves. Except as he rises whom Satan has beaten to pieces except standing like the standing of the possessed, and it is mentioned according to what they claim that Satan beats a person and he is struck down, and beating is a type of inconsistency like the beating of the blind. From the touch meaning madness, and this is also from their leaders that the jinn touches him and his mind becomes confused and for this reason it was said: the man went mad. It is related to they do not rise meaning they do not rise from the affliction that is upon them due to eating usury, or they rise or stumble, so their rising and falling are like those who are possessed, not because their minds are disturbed, but because God has increased in their bellies what they have eaten of usury, so it has weighed them down. That is because they said, 'Trade is only like usury' meaning that this punishment is because they have put usury and trade in one chain to lead to profit, so they have made it permissible. The original was that usury is only like trade, but it was reversed for the sake of exaggeration, as if they had made usury the original and compared it to trade. The difference between them is that whoever gives two dirhams for one dirham has wasted a dirham, and whoever buys a commodity worth one dirham for two dirhams, perhaps the need for it, or the expectation of its popularity, will make up for this loss. And God has permitted trade and forbidden usury is a denial of their equalization, and the invalidation of the analogy by opposing the text. But whoever receives an admonition from his Lord so whoever receives an admonition from God the Most High and a warning, like the denial of usury. He stopped. So he was admonished and followed the prohibition. He will have what is past. He took the prohibition and cannot take it back. What is in the nominative case is in the adverbial phrase if you make min a relative pronoun, and in the subject if you make it a conditional, according to the opinion of Sibawayh, since the adverbial phrase is not dependent on what preceded it. And his affair is with God. He will reward him for stopping if he accepted the admonition and had sincere intentions. It was said that He will judge his affair and you have no objection to it. And whoever returns to permitting usury, since the discussion is about it. Then those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. Because they disbelieved in Him. 131 And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers by avoiding following them and engaging in their actions. It is a warning that the Fire is specifically prepared for the disbelievers and, incidentally, for the sinners.
2:276: 276- God destroys usury takes away its blessing and destroys the money that goes into it. And increases charity multiplies its reward and blesses what it is given for. And from him, peace and blessings be upon him, God accepts charity and increases it as one of you increases his foal. And from him, peace and blessings be upon him, Zakat never decreases wealth. "And God does not love" is not pleased and does not love His love for those who repent. "Every disbeliever" insists on making forbidden things permissible. "Sinful" preoccupied with committing it.
2:277: 277- Indeed, those who have believed in God and His Messenger and what came to them from Him. And done righteous deeds and established prayer and gave zakah He connected it to what includes them because they are superior to all other righteous deeds. They will have their reward with their Lord, and no fear will there be concerning them from what comes. Nor will they grieve over what is lost.
2:278: 278-O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of interest and leave the remainder of what you stipulated from people of interest. If you are believers in your hearts, then the evidence of this is compliance with what you were commanded to do. It was narrated: Thaqeef had money owed to some of the Quraysh, so they demanded the money and interest from them at the market. So this was revealed.
2:279: 279- But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger meaning, then be aware of it, from the verb to be informed if he knows about it, and Hamza and Asim read in the narration of Ibn Ayyash fa'adhunu meaning, then be aware of it to others, from the verb adhan which means listening, as it is one of the ways of knowledge, and the indefiniteness of harb is for glorification, and this requires that the educator fight after being asked to repent until he returns to the command of God, like the rebel, and it does not require his disbelief. It was narrated that when it was revealed, Thaqeef said, We have no hand in waging war against God and His Messenger. "And if you repent" from doubt and believing that it is permissible. "Then you shall have your capital. You shall not be wronged" by taking the increase. "And you shall not be wronged" by delaying or decreasing, and it is understood from it that if they do not repent, then they do not have their capital, and this is correct according to what we said, because the one who insists on making it permissible is an apostate and his money is spoils:
2:280: 280- "And if he is in hardship" and if a debtor is in hardship. It is read "in hardship" meaning if the debtor is in hardship. "Then a reprieve" the ruling is a reprieve, or upon you is a reprieve, or let it be a reprieve which is the reprieve. It is read "Fananaziruhu as a report meaning the one who deserves it is the one who is waiting for him, or the one who is waiting for him by way of lineage and Fananaziruhu" as a matter meaning then forgive him with a reprieve. "To ease is ease, and Nafi' and Hamzah read with a damma on the seen, and they are two dialects like Mashriqah and Mashriqah". It is read with them both added by deleting the taa when added like his saying: "They broke their promise to God". "And that you give in charity" by acquitting. Asim read with a lightened "sad". "Better for you" is more rewarding than a reprieve, or better than what you take because its reward is doubled and permanent. It was said: What is meant by charity is delaying it, based on the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, A Muslim man’s debt is not settled and he delays it except that he will have a charity for every day, “if you only knew,” what is in it of the beautiful and abundant remembrance.
2:281: 281-And fear a Day when you will be returned to God the Day of Resurrection, or the Day of Death, so prepare for your destination to it. Abu Amr and Yaqub read with the opening of the taa and the kasra of the jim. Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned the reward for what it did of good or evil and they will not be wronged by reducing the reward and doubling the punishment. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both (it is the last verse that Gabriel, peace be upon him, revealed and he said, Put it at the beginning of the two hundred and eightyth of the cow) and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lived after that for twenty-one days, and it was said eighty-one days, and it was said seven days, and it was said three hours.
2:282: 282- "O you who have believed, when you contract a debt" meaning if you contract a debt with one another, you say: I contracted a debt with him if I dealt with him on credit, giving or taking. The benefit of mentioning the debt is that there is no suspicion of recompense from the debt and it is known that it is deferred and immediate, and that it is the motive for the scribes and the reference of the pronoun "write it is for a specified term" of known days and months, not for the harvest and the arrival of the pilgrims. "Write it" because it is more reliable and prevents dispute, and the majority are of the view that it is recommended. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him that what is meant by it is the Muslim and he said that when God forbade usury, He permitted Salam. "And let a scribe write between you with justice" one who writes the balance, neither adding nor subtracting, and it is in reality an order for the debtors to choose a scribe who is a knowledgeable religious scholar so that he can produce a trustworthy written document that is just according to the Shari'ah. "And no scribe should refuse" and no one should refuse to write. To write as God taught him like what God taught him of writing documents, or not to refuse to benefit people with his writing as God benefited him by teaching it, like His statement: And do good as God has done good to you. “So let him write” that taught writing. He ordered it after forbidding refusing it for emphasis, and it is permissible for the kaf to be connected to the order, so the prohibition against abstaining from it is absolute and then the order is restricted. And let him upon whom the right is dictate and let the one dictating be the one upon whom the right is because he is the one who acknowledges and is witnessed against, and dictation and dictation are one and the same. And let him fear God, his Lord meaning the one dictating or the writer. And let him not withhold or reduce anything from it meaning from the right, or from what was dictated to him. If the one upon whom the right is a fool lacking in mind and extravagant. Or weak a young boy or an old man who is mentally ill. Or he is unable to dictate or is unable to dictate himself due to muteness or ignorance of the language. Then let his guardian dictate with justice meaning the one who is in charge of his affairs and takes his place from a guardian if he is a child or mentally unsound, or an agent or translator if he is unable. This is evidence of the application of representation in the admission and perhaps it is specific to what the guardian or agent undertakes. And bring to witness two witnesses and demand that two witnesses testify to the religion. From among your men from among the Muslim men, and this is evidence of the condition of the witnesses being Muslims and this is the opinion of most scholars. Abu Hanifa said: The testimony of some infidels against others is acceptable. But if they are not two men if the two witnesses are not two men. A man and two women let him testify or let a man and two women testify, and this is specific to money according to us and to everything other than the prescribed punishments and retaliation according to Abu Hanifa. From among the witnesses whom you accept because you know of their justice. "That one of them should go astray, then one of them should remind the other." The reason for considering the number is because if one of them goes astray in her testimony, because she forgets it, the other reminds her. The reason in reality is the reminder, but since going astray was the cause of it, it was given the same status as their saying: I prepared the weapon lest an enemy should come, so I could repel him. It is as if it was said: The intention is that one of them should remind the other if she goes astray. This indicates the deficiency of their minds and lack of control. Hamzah read "that one of them should go astray" as a condition, then she should remind the other, in the nominative case. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read "then she should remind" from the remembrances. "And the witnesses should not refuse when they are called upon" to give testimony or bear witness. They were called witnesses before bearing witness, in order to bring it closer to the status of reality. "Ma" is an additional word. "And do not tire of writing it down", and do not tire of writing down the debt, the truth, or the Book, due to the large number of your debts. It was said that boredom is a metaphor for laziness because it is a characteristic of the hypocrite, and therefore the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The believer does not say ‘I was lazy’ “small or large” whether the right was small or large, or whether the writer was brief or full. Until its due date until the time it is due which the debtor acknowledged. That is a reference to you writing it down. More just with God is more just. And more upright for testimony and more established for it and more helpful in establishing it, and they are both built from aqsat and aqama not in analogy, or from qasit meaning of having justice and upright. The waw is correct in aqwam as it is correct in the expression of astonishment because of its rigidity. And more likely that you do not doubt and closer to not doubting the type of debt, its amount, its due date, the witnesses, and the like. Except if it is a present trade which you carry on among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it down. An exception to the command to write it down. Present trade includes transactions for a debt or in kind, and its management among yourselves is their dealing with it hand to hand, meaning: unless you carry on a transaction hand to hand, then there is no problem with you writing it down, because it is far from dispute and forgetfulness. Asim put trade in the accusative case as the predicate and the noun is implied, meaning except that the trade is a present trade, like his saying: Banu Asad, do you know our affliction if it is ever more terrible? The rest raised it as the name and the predicate, you manage it or as the complete was. And bear witness when you make a transaction this transaction, or absolutely because it is more cautious. The orders in this verse are recommended according to most of the imams. It was said: It is for obligation, then there was a difference of opinion regarding its rulings and abrogation. And let neither the scribe nor the witness be harmed It is possible for both constructions, and the evidence for that is that it was read and let not be harmed with the kasra and the fatha. It is a prohibition on them from leaving the answer and distorting and changing the writings and the testimony, or a prohibition on harming them such as if they are hastening from their task and are forced to go beyond what has been set for them, and the scribe is not given his wages, and the witness the expense of coming wherever he is. And if you do harm or what you have been forbidden from. It is wickedness on your part leaving obedience and not right for you. And fear God in disobeying His command and prohibition. And God will teach you His rulings that include your interests. And God is All-Knowing of everything. The word God was repeated in the three sentences because they are independent. The first is an exhortation to piety, the second is a promise of His blessings, and the third is an exaltation of His status. And because it is more closely related to exaltation than to metaphor.
2:283: 283- And if you are on a journey meaning travelers. And you cannot find a scribe, then a pledge is taken then the one who is trusted is a pledge, or upon you is a pledge, or let a pledge be taken. This condition is not to require travel in the pledge as Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak, may God have mercy on them, thought, because he, peace be upon him, pawned his armor in Medina to a Jew for twenty sa' of barley that he took for his family, but rather to establish the trust for the pledge in place of the trust of writing in the journey which is likely to be insufficient. The majority are of the view that the possession in it is not owned. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read farahan like saqf and both of them are the plural of rahan meaning mortgaged. It was read with the ha silent for the sake of alleviation. If some of you trust others meaning some of the creditors some of the debtors and he is satisfied with his trustworthiness without the pledge. Let him who is trusted discharge his trust meaning his debt, he called it a trust because he trusted him by not mortgaging it. The word whoever is trusted was read by changing the hamza to a ya’, and the word whoever is trusted was read by assimilating the ya’ to the ta’, which is a mistake because the word that is changed from the hamza is governed by its rule and is not assimilated. And let him fear God, his Lord in betrayal and denial of the truth, and there are exaggerations in it. And do not conceal testimony O witnesses, or debtors, and testimony is their testimony against themselves. And whoever conceals it, then his heart is sinful meaning his heart is sinful or his heart is sinful. The sentence is the predicate of in and the sin is attributed to the heart because concealment and its counterparts are: the eye is a fornicator and the ear is a fornicator. Or for exaggeration, because it is the chief of the organs and its actions are the greatest actions, and it is as if it was said: the sin took hold of his soul and took over the most honorable of its parts, and surpassed all his sins. The word his heart was read in the accusative case like the beauty of his face. And God is Knowing of what you do is a threat.
2:284: 284- To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth in creation and dominion. And if you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it meaning what is in it of evil and the intention to do it, forgiveness and punishment will be arranged for it. God will call you to account for it on the Day of Resurrection. And it is an argument against those who deny accountability, such as the Mu'tazila and the Rafidah. Then He forgives whom He wills His forgiveness. And He punishes whom He wills His punishment, and it is explicit in denying the necessity of punishment. Ibn Amir, Asim, and Ya'qub raised them as a resumption, and the rest of them made them jussive in apposition to the answer to the condition, and whoever made them jussive without a fa made them a substitute for it, indicating part of the whole or inclusion, like his saying: When you come to visit us in our homes, you will find abundant firewood and a blazing fire. Assimilation of the letter Raa into the letter Laam is a mistake, as the letter Raa is only assimilated into its like. And God is over all things competent means He is able to bring to life and to hold people to account.
2:285: 285- The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord is a testimony and explicit statement from God Almighty on the validity of his faith and reliance on it, and that he is firm in his matter and has no doubt about it. And the believers - all of them believe in God and His angels and His books and His messengers There is no ambiguity in that the believers is connected to the Messenger, so the pronoun that the tanween replaces refers to the Messenger and the believers, or it is made a subject, so the pronoun refers to the believers. And by consideration, it is correct for each to occur with its predicate as the predicate of the subject, and the Messenger is singled out in the ruling either to glorify him or because his faith is based on observation and vision, and their faith is based on contemplation and inference. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read and his book meaning the Qur'an, or the genus. The difference between it and the plural is that it is common in the singular of the genus and the plural in its plurals, and for this reason it is said: the book is more than the books. We make no distinction between any of His messengers meaning they say do not make a distinction. And Yaqub read la yfarq with a ya’, on the basis that the verb is for all. And it was read la yfarqoon based on its meaning, like the Almighty’s saying: And all will come to Him in submission. One in the meaning of the plural because it occurs in a context of negation, like the Almighty’s saying: So none of you can prevent Him from it. That is why bayn entered into it, and what is meant is the negation of the difference by affirmation and denial. And they said, ‘We hear,’ we responded. And we obeyed, your command. Your forgiveness, our Lord, forgive us with Your forgiveness, or we seek Your forgiveness. And to You is the destination, the return after death, which is an acknowledgment from them of the resurrection.
2:286: 286- God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity except what its capacity can bear out of grace and mercy, or what is less than its capacity so that it can be expanded and made easy for it, as God the Almighty says: God intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship which indicates that the impossible does not occur and does not indicate that it is impossible. For it is what it has earned of good. And upon it is what it has acquired of evil, no one benefits from its obedience and no one is harmed by its disobedience except God. The specification of earning to good and acquisition to evil is because there is a possibility of earning and the soul desires evil and is drawn to it, so it is more diligent in obtaining it and works, unlike good. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake. That is, do not impose blame upon us for what led us to forget or make a mistake due to negligence or carelessness, or for ourselves, since it is not rational to prevent being blamed for them. Sins are like poisons, so just as consuming them leads to destruction—even if it was a mistake—committing sins is not unlikely to lead to punishment, even if it was not a decision. However, the Almighty promised to overlook it out of mercy and grace, so it is permissible for a person to supplicate with it for continuity and reliance on the blessing in it. This is supported by the meaning of his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, Mistakes and forgetfulness have been lifted from my nation. “Our Lord, and place not upon us a burden.” A heavy burden that constrains its owner, that is, it confines him in his place. He means by it the difficult duties. It was read and do not burden with emphasis for emphasis. As You imposed it upon those before us means a burden like You imposed it upon those before us, or like what You imposed upon them, so it is a description of a burden, and what is meant by it is what the Children of Israel were charged with, such as killing people, cutting off the place of impurity, fifty prayers a day and night, and spending a quarter of the wealth on zakat, or what befell them of hardships and trials. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear of affliction and punishment, or of the duties that human capacity cannot fulfill, and this indicates the permissibility of imposing what is unbearable, otherwise he would not have been asked to be relieved of it, and the emphasis here is to make the verb transitive to the second object. And pardon us and erase our sins. And forgive us and cover our faults and do not disgrace us by holding us accountable. And have mercy upon us and be kind to us and be gracious to us. You are our Master our master. So give us victory over the disbelieving people because it is the right of the master to give victory to his allies over the enemies, or what is meant by it is the generality of the disbelievers. It was narrated that when he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) supplicated with these supplications, it was said to him after every word he did. And it was narrated from him (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “God revealed two verses from the treasures of Paradise. The Most Gracious wrote them with His hand two thousand years before He created the creation. Whoever recites them after the last evening prayer, they will suffice him for the night prayer.” And it was narrated from him (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever recites the two verses from the end of Surat Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him. This refutes the statement of those who dislike saying Surat Al-Baqarah, and he said: It should be said the surah in which the cow is mentioned, as he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The surah in which the cow is mentioned is the tent of the Qur’an, so learn it, for learning it is a blessing, and abandoning it is a regret, and the magicians will never be able to do it. It was said: O Messenger of God, and who are the magicians? He said: The magicians.”
3:2: 2- God, there is no god but He The opening of the meem in the famous version was not valid, but it was right to stop on it to cast the movement of the hamza on it to indicate that it is in the ruling of the fixed, because it was dropped for the sake of alleviation, not for the sake of gradation, because the meem is in the ruling of stopping like their saying one two by casting the movement of the hamza on the dal, not because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, because it is not objectionable in the chapter of stopping, and therefore the meem was not moved in the lam. And it was read with a kasra on the assumption of moving it because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Abu Bakr read with a sukoon on it and starting with what comes after it according to the original. The Living, the Eternal It was narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The greatest name of God is in three surahs: in al-Baqarah 2:God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Eternal", and in Al Imran 3:God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Eternal", and in Ta-Ha 20:"And faces are humbled before the Living, the Eternal,.
3:3: 3 He sent down to you the Book the Qur'an in stars. In truth with justice, or with truthfulness in his information, or with proven arguments that it is from God and it is in the place of the state. Confirming what was before it of the books. And He sent down the Torah and the Gospel as a whole to Moses and Jesus. Their derivation from wara and najl, and their weight with tafa'ala and fa'il is arbitrary because they are foreign, and this is supported by the fact that the Gospel was read with a fatha on the hamza and it is not from the structures of Arabic, and Abu Amr, Ibn Dhakwan and Al-Kisa'i read the Torah with imala in the entire Qur'an and Nafi' and Hamza between the two pronunciations except Qaloon who read it with a fatha like the reading of the rest.
3:4: 4 Before before the revelation of the Qur'an. A guidance for mankind in general, if we say that we worship according to the law of those before us, otherwise it refers to their people. And He sent down the Criterion meaning the type of divine books, for they distinguish between truth and falsehood. He mentioned that after mentioning the three books to include everything else, as if he said: And He sent down everything by which truth is distinguished from falsehood, or the Psalms or the Qur'an. He repeated mentioning it as a description of it, praising and glorifying it, and demonstrating its virtue in that it shares with them the fact that it is a revealed revelation and is distinguished by being a miracle that distinguishes between the truthful and the false, or miracles. Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God from His revealed books and others. For them is a severe punishment because of their disbelief. And God is Exalted in Might Dominant and does not prevent punishment. The One with Revenge is such that no other avenger can do anything like Him. Revenge is the punishment of the criminal, and the verb from it is naqām with the fathah and the kasrah. It is a threat that was brought after establishing monotheism and pointing to what is the mainstay in proving prophethood, to magnify the matter and deter from turning away from it.
3:5: 5 Indeed, nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven meaning anything that exists in the world, whether completely or partially, whether faith or disbelief. He referred to it as heaven and earth because the senses do not go beyond them, and he mentioned the earth first as an ascension from the lowest to the highest, and because what is meant by the mention is what is committed in it. It is like evidence that He is alive.
3:6: 6 And His saying: It is He who shapes you in the wombs however He wills meaning from different shapes, as evidence of the Self-Sustainer, and evidence that He is All-Knowing of the perfection of His action in creating the fetus and shaping it. And it was read as your shaping meaning your shaping of Himself and His worship. There is no god but He because no one else knows all that He knows and is not able to do what He does. The Almighty, the Wise is an indication of the perfection of His power and the limit of His wisdom. It was said: This is an argument against those who claim that Jesus was a god, because when the delegation of Najran argued with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about him, the surah was revealed, from the beginning of which there are more than eighty verses confirming what he argued with them and answering their doubts.
3:7: 7 "It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are precise." Its wording is precise by being free from ambiguity and ambiguity. They are the mothers of the Book. Its origin is such that others can be traced back to it, and analogy is that mothers are so separated according to the interpretation of each one, or that all are in the position of one verse. And others that are ambiguous are ambiguous, and their intended meaning is not clear - due to ambiguity or contradiction of the apparent meaning - except by examination and consideration, so that the merit of the scholars becomes apparent in them, and their eagerness increases to strive to contemplate them and acquire the knowledge that depends on deducing what is intended by them, so that they attain by them - and by tiring their minds in extracting their meanings, and reconciling what is between them and the precise verses - the highest degrees. As for the Almighty’s saying: “Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses are perfected,” its meaning is that they are protected from corruption of meaning and weakness of wording. His saying: A Book that is similar, its meaning is that some of it resembles others in the correctness of meaning and the eloquence of wording. And another is the plural of another, and it was not declined because it is a description that was modified from the other, and it does not necessarily require knowing it, because its meaning is that analogy is to know and not to know, not that it is in the meaning of the definite or from another of As for those in whose hearts is deviation, deviation from the truth like the innovators. They follow that which is ambiguous thereof, so they cling to its apparent meaning or to a false interpretation. Seeking discord, seeking to tempt people away from their religion by doubting and confusing and contradicting the clear with the ambiguous. And seeking its interpretation, and seeking that they interpret it according to what they desire. It is possible that the motive for following is the combination of the two requests, or each one of them in succession. The first suits the obstinate and the second suits the ignorant. And he does not know its interpretation, which is what it must be carried on. Except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge meaning those who are steadfast and established in it. Whoever stops at except God interprets the ambiguous as what God has kept knowledge to Himself: such as the duration of the world, the time of the Hour, and the characteristics of numbers such as the number of the guards, or as an exchange for the decisive, although its apparent meaning is not intended and does not indicate what is intended. They say, 'We believe in it' is a resumption of the position of the firmly rooted, is the state of them or the predicate or you made it the subject. All is from our Lord meaning all of the ambiguous and the decisive are from Him, and none will remember except those of understanding is praise for those firmly rooted in the quality of their minds and good insight, and an indication of what they have prepared for guidance to its interpretation, which is the mind being free from the veils of the senses, and the connection of the verse to what preceded it in that it depicts the soul with knowledge and its education, and what preceded it in depicting the body and its formation, or it is an answer to the Christians' steadfastness in the manner of the Almighty's saying: And His Word which He bestowed on Mary and a spirit from Him. It is also an answer to his saying that he has no father but God, so it is necessary that He is his father, because He, the Most High, is the one who shapes the embryos however He wills, so He shapes them.
3:8: 8 Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate from the article of the firm-rooted. It was said: It is a resumption and the meaning is do not let our hearts deviate from the path of truth to follow the ambiguous with an interpretation that you do not accept. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The heart of the son of Adam is between two fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills, He will make him stay on the truth and if He wills, He will make him deviate from it." It was said: Do not test us with afflictions that will cause our hearts to deviate. After You have guided us to the truth and faith in both parts. From the decisive and ambiguous, and after is the accusative of the circumstance, and when is in the position of the genitive with its addition to it. It was said that it means if. And grant us mercy from Yourself to draw us closer to You and we win it with You, or success to remain steadfast on the truth or forgiveness of sins. Indeed, You are the Giver for every question, and in it is evidence that guidance and misguidance are from God and that He is generous with what He bestows upon His servants and nothing is required of Him.
3:9: 9 Our Lord, You will surely gather mankind for a Day for the reckoning of a Day or for its recompense. There is no doubt about it in the occurrence of the Day and what it contains of gathering and recompense, drawing attention to the fact that most of their purpose in the two requests is related to the Hereafter, for it is the goal and the wealth. Indeed, God does not fail in His promise for divinity contradicts it, and to indicate it and to glorify the promised one, there is a color of speech, and the threat was used as evidence. It was answered that the threat of the wicked is conditional upon not pardoning, for separate evidence, just as it is conditional upon not repenting, in agreement.
3:10: 10 Indeed, those who disbelieve is general for the disbelievers. It was said that what is meant by it is the delegation of Najran, or the Jews, or the polytheists of the Arabs. Their wealth and their children will not avail them at all against God meaning from His mercy, or from His obedience in the sense of substitution, or from His punishment. And those are the fuel of the Fire its firewood. It was read with the dammah meaning the people of its fuel.
3:11: 11 Like the way of Pharaoh's people is connected to what came before it, meaning it will not suffice for those, or kindle with them as you kindle with those, or a resumption in the nominative case, the estimated way of these people is like their way of disbelief and torment, and it is a source of perseverance in work if one toils in it, so it was transferred to the meaning of the matter. And those before them is in apposition to Pharaoh's people. It was said that it is a resumption. They denied Our signs, so God seized them for their sins is a state with the implied had, or a resumption explaining their state, or a predicate of if you begin with those before them. And God is severe in penalty is an exaggeration of the punishment and an increase in the fear of the disbelievers.
3:12: 12 Say to those who disbelieve, 'You will be overcome and gathered together to Hell.' That is, say to the polytheists of Mecca, 'You will be overcome,' meaning on the day of Badr. It was also said to the Jews, for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gathered them after Badr in the market of Banu Qaynuqa' and warned them that what happened to Quraysh would happen to them. They said, 'Do not be deceived by the fact that you have struck ignorant people who have no knowledge of war. If you fight us, you will know that we are the people.' So it was revealed. And God fulfilled His promise to them by killing Qurayza, expelling Banu Nadir, conquering Khaybar, and imposing the jizyah on those other than them, which is one of the signs of prophethood. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with a ya' in both of them, as if the command was to tell them what he had been told of their threat in his own words. And an evil resting place is the completion of what is said to them, or a resumption and the estimation of an evil resting place is Hell or what they have prepared for themselves.
3:13: 13 There has already been for you a sign The address is to the Quraysh or the Jews, and it was said to the believers. In two companies that met on the day of Badr. "One company fighting in the cause of God and the other disbelieving. They saw them as twice their number" The polytheists saw the believers as twice the number of the polytheists, and it was close to a thousand, or twice the number of the Muslims, and they were three hundred and a few, and that was after they had diminished them in their eyes until they dared to attack them and turned to them, whenever they met them they increased in their eyes until they were defeated, as reinforcement from God the Most High for the believers, or the believers saw the polytheists as twice the number of the believers, and they were three times their number, so that they would prove to them and be certain of the victory that God promised them in His saying: But if there are a hundred of you, patient, they will overcome two hundred. This is supported by the reading of Nafi’ and Ya’qub with the letter ta’, and it was read with both of them in the passive form, meaning that God shows them, or shows you that with His power, and a group in the accusative case as a substitute for two groups and the accusative case as a specification, or a state of the subject of the verb they turned away. “Ra’y al-‘ayn” means a clear, witnessed vision. And God supports with His victory whom He wills His victory as He supported the people of Badr. Indeed in that means the reduction and increase, or the predominance of the few who are ill-equipped over the many who are armed, and the fact that the event was a sign also bears this possibility, and it is possible that the matter occurred as the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us. A lesson for those of vision meaning a lesson for those with insight. And it was said to those who saw them.
3:14: 14 The love of desires has been made attractive to people meaning the desired things. He called them desires as an exaggeration and an allusion that they were so immersed in loving them that they loved their desire, as God Almighty said: I loved the love of good. And the one who makes things attractive is God Almighty because He is the Creator of actions and motives, and perhaps He made them attractive as a test, or because they are a means to happiness in the Hereafter if they are in a way that God Almighty approves of, or because they are among the reasons for livelihood and the survival of the species. And it was said that it is Satan, because the verse is in the context of blame. Al-Jubba'i distinguished between what is permissible and what is forbidden. Of women and children, and heaped-up sums of gold and silver, and branded horses, and livestock and tillage is a statement of desires, and a heap is a lot of money. And it was said that it is one hundred thousand dinars. And it was said that it is a bull's fill of musk. And there is disagreement as to whether it is an action or a sandal, and the heaped-up sum is taken from it for emphasis, as they say a scattered pearl. The marked, marked from the mark, or the marked from the mark of the animal, or the marked. And the livestock are camels, cows, and sheep. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, referring to what was mentioned. And with God is the best return, meaning the place of return, and it is an incitement to exchange what He has of true, eternal pleasures for the deceitful, fleeting desires.
3:15: 15 "Say: Shall I inform you of something better than that?" He means by it to state that the reward of God is better than the pleasures of this world. For those who fear God are gardens with rivers flowing beneath them, wherein they abide eternally. A resumption to explain what is better, and it is possible for the lam to be related to good and for gardens to be raised above what is gardens, and this is supported by the reading of jarrha instead of good. "And purified spouses" from what is abhorrent in women. "And pleasure from God" Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr in the entire Qur'an with a damma on the ra' except for the second letter in Al-Ma'idah, which is the Almighty's saying: "His pleasure is paths of peace" with a kasra on the ra', and they are two languages. And God is All-Seeing of His servants, meaning their deeds, so He rewards the doer of good and punishes the doer of evil, or the conditions of those who fear God, for that reason He has prepared gardens for them. And He has drawn attention in this verse to His blessings, the least of which is the enjoyment of worldly life, and the highest of which is the pleasure of God Almighty, as He Almighty says: And the pleasure of God is greater, and the middle of which is Paradise and its delights.
3:16: 16 Those who say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.' This is an attribute of the righteous, or of the servants, or praise in the accusative or nominative case. And in arranging the question based on mere belief, there is evidence that it is sufficient to deserve forgiveness or prepare for it.
3:17: 17 The patient, the truthful, the obedient, the spenders, and those who seek forgiveness before dawn is a limitation of the stations of the seeker in the best order, for his dealings with God the Most High are either supplication or request, and supplication is either with the soul, which is preventing it from vices and confining it to virtues, and patience includes both, or with the body, which is either verbal, which is truthfulness, or practical, which is obedience, or with money, which is spending in the ways of goodness, or with request, then by seeking forgiveness because forgiveness is the greatest of requests, indeed the common denominator of them, and the interposition of the waw between them is to indicate the independence of each one of them and their perfection in it, or because of the difference in those described by it, and the specification of the pre-dawn hours because supplication in them is closer to being answered, because worship at that time is more difficult and the soul is purer and the fear is more comprehensive for those who strive. It was said that they used to pray until dawn, then seek forgiveness and supplicate.
3:18: 18 God bears witness that there is no god but He He demonstrated His Oneness by establishing the evidence indicating it and sending down the verses that speak of it. And the angels by acknowledging it. And those of knowledge by believing in it and arguing for it. This is similar in explanation and revelation to the testimony of a witness. Establishing justice Establishing justice in His division and judgment. Its accusative case is in the state of God, and it is permissible to single it out and it is not permissible to say Zaid and Umar came riding to avoid confusion, like the Almighty's saying: And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift. Or from he and the factor in it is the meaning of the sentence, i.e. he is the one who is standing alone, or he is the most deserving because it is a confirmed state, or on praise, or the description of the negated and in it is weakness for the separation and it is included in what is witnessed to if you make it a description, or a state of the pronoun. And establishing justice was read as a substitute for he the deleted report. There is no god but He. He repeated it for emphasis and to further pay attention to knowing the evidence of monotheism and ruling by it after establishing the argument, and to build upon it his saying: The Almighty, the Wise. So that he knows that He is the One described by them, and He presented the Almighty to present knowledge of His power over knowledge of His wisdom, and He raised them as a substitute for the pronoun or description for the agent of witness. It was narrated about their merit that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Their owner will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and God Almighty will say: This servant of Mine has a covenant with Me, and I am the most deserving of fulfilling the covenant. Let My servant enter Paradise.” It is evidence of the distinction of knowledge of the principles of religion and the honor of its people.
3:19: 19Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam is a renewed sentence confirming the first, meaning that there is no religion acceptable to God except Islam, which is monotheism and adopting the law that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. Al-Kisa'i read it with the fatha as a substitute for the whole if he interpreted Islam as faith, or what it includes, and a substitute for inclusion if he interpreted it as the law. It was read that it is with the kasra and that with the fatha as the action falling on the second, and the objection between them or the implementation of the witness in the manner of said sometimes and learned other times to include their meanings. And those who were given the Scripture did not differ from the Jews and Christians, or from the masters of the book that came before in Islam, so some said that it is true and some said that it is specific to the Arabs and others denied it absolutely, or in monotheism, so a third of the Christians And the Jews said, ‘Ezra is the son of God’ and it was said that they are the people of Moses who differed after him and it was said that they are the Christians who differed about the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him except after knowledge had come to them meaning after they knew the truth of the matter and were able to know it through the signs and arguments. Out of envy among themselves out of envy among them and seeking leadership, not because of doubt or concealment of the matter. And whoever disbelieves in the signs of God - then indeed, God is swift in account a warning to whoever disbelieves among them.
3:20: 20If they dispute with you about religion, or argue with you about it after you have established the proofs. Say, 'I have submitted my face to God' I have devoted myself and my entire being to Him, and I do not associate anyone else with Him. It is the straight religion that the proofs have established and the verses and messengers have called to. The face is used to refer to the soul because it is the most noble of the outward organs and the manifestation of the faculties and senses. And whoever follows is in apposition to the ta' in aslamtu and is good for separation, or an object with it. And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered who do not have a book like the polytheists of the Arabs. Have you submitted as I submitted when the proof was made clear to them, or are you still in your disbelief? Similar to it is His statement: Then will you not desist? In it is a reproach to them for their dullness or obstinacy. If they submit, then they are rightly guided they have benefited themselves by taking them out of misguidance. But if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance. That is, they will not harm you, since all you have to do is convey, and you have conveyed. And God is Seeing of His servants. A promise and a threat.
3:21: 21Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets without right and kill those who enjoin justice among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment. They are the People of the Book who were in his time, peace be upon him. He killed the first of them, the prophets and their followers, and they were pleased with him and intended to kill the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the believers, but God protected them. A similar example has been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Hamza read and they fight those who... Sibawayh forbade the inclusion of the letter fa in the predicate of in kalita and perhaps, and that is why the predicate was said.
3:22: 22 Those are the ones whose deeds have been lost in this world and the Hereafter is like saying Zaid, so understand that he is a righteous man. The difference is that it does not change the meaning of the beginning, unlike them. And they will have no helpers to ward off the punishment from them.
3:23: 23 Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture meaning the Torah or the genus of heavenly books, and min is for partiality or clarification. The indefiniteness of the portion can mean glorification or disparagement. They are called to the Book of God to judge between them The caller is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Book of God is the Qur'an, or the Torah, as it was narrated "that he, peace and blessings be upon him, entered their schools and Nu'aym ibn Amr and Al-Harith ibn Zayd said to him, "What religion are you on? He said, On the religion of Abraham. They said, Abraham was Jewish. He said, Come to the Torah, for it is between us and you. But they refused, so it was revealed. It was said that it was revealed about stoning. It was read to judge in the passive form, so the difference between them is evidence that the auditory evidence is an argument in the fundamentals. Then a group of them will turn away is an exclusion of their turning away, even though they know that returning to Him is obligatory. And they are turning away and they are people who are accustomed to turning away, and the sentence is a state of a group, and it was only permissible because it was specified by the description.
3:24: 24And that is a reference to turning away and turning away. Because they said, 'The Fire will not touch us except for a few days' because they made the matter of punishment easy for themselves due to this false belief and empty greed. And they were deceived in their religion by what they used to invent that the Fire would not touch them except for a few days, or that their fathers the prophets would intercede for them, or that God Almighty promised Jacob, peace be upon him, that He would not punish his children except to fulfill an oath.
3:25: 25 How then, when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt? A sign of the enormity of what will surround them in the Hereafter and a refutation of their saying, The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. It was narrated that the first banner to be raised on the Day of Resurrection from the banners of the infidels will be the banner of the Jews. God will disgrace them before all witnesses and then order them to the Fire. And every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned. The recompense for what it earned. This is evidence that worship is not nullified and that the believer will not remain in the Fire forever, because the full compensation of his faith and deeds will not take place in the Fire or before entering it, so it is after salvation from it. And they will not be wronged. The pronoun for every is a negation of the meaning because it is in the meaning of every human being.
3:26: 26Say, O God The meem replaces Ya, and therefore they do not come together. It is one of the characteristics of this name, like the entry of Ya upon it with the definite article and the cutting of its hamza and the taa of the oath. It was said: Its origin is O God, grant me security with good, so it was lightened by deleting the letter of address and the dependents of the verb and its hamza. Master of the Kingdom acts in what can be acted upon as owners act in what they own. It is a second address according to Sibawayh, as the meem, according to him, prevents description. You give the kingdom to whomever You will and take the kingdom away from whomever You will You give it to whomever You will and take it back, so the first kingdom is general and the other two are parts of it. It was said: What is meant by the kingdom is prophecy, and taking it away is transferring it from one people to another. And You honor whomever You will and humiliate whomever You will in this world and the hereafter, or in both of them with victory and retreat, success and failure. In Your hand is goodness, for You are over all things competent. He mentioned good alone because it is decreed in itself, and evil is decreed by accident, since there is no partial evil unless it includes complete good, or to observe politeness in speech, or because the speech occurred in it, as it was narrated: “When he, peace be upon him, drew the trench and cut forty cubits for every ten, and they began to dig, a huge rock appeared in it that the pickaxes had not worked on, so they directed Salman to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, to inform him, so he, peace be upon him, came and took the pickaxe from it and struck it a blow that split it. And lightning flashed from it that lit up what was between its two lava fields as if it were a lamp in the interior of a dark house, so he said, “Allahu Akbar” and the Muslims said with him, and he said, The palaces of Al-Hirah were lit up for me from it as if they were the fangs of dogs. Then he struck the second time and said, The red palaces of the land of the Romans were lit up for me from it. Then he struck the third time and said, “The palaces of Sana’a were lit up for me from it, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, informed me that my nation will prevail over all of them, so be glad.” The hypocrites said, Do you not marvel at your omen, and falsehood promises you and tells you that it sees? From Yathrib, the palaces of Al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra, and that they will be opened to you, and you are only digging the trench out of division, so it was revealed.” He pointed out that evil is also in his hand by saying, Indeed, you are capable of all things.
3:27: 27 "You cause the night to enter the day and cause the day to enter the night. You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living. And You provide for whom You will without account." He followed that with a statement of His ability to punish night and day: to bring one into the other by succession or increase and decrease. And to bring the living out of the dead and vice versa. To create animals from their materials and cause them to die, or to create the animal from the sperm and the sperm from it. It was said: to bring the believer out of the disbeliever and the disbeliever out of the believer. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Abu Bakr read "the dead" with a light pronunciation.
3:28: 28 Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies They forbade them from being allies due to kinship and pre-Islamic friendship and the like, so that their love and hatred would only be for the sake of God, or from seeking their help in conquest and other religious matters. Other than the believers indicates that they are the most deserving of allegiance, and that their allegiance is an alternative to allegiance to the disbelievers. And whoever does that meaning taking them as allies. has nothing to do with God meaning in His allegiance to something that could be called allegiance, for allegiance to two enemies cannot come together. He said: You call me your enemy and then claim that I am your friend. No one can be more loyal to you. Except that you fear them with a fear except that you fear. And he read from their side what must be feared, or fear. And the verb is transitive with min because it means beware and fear. And Yaqub read the rest. He forbade befriending them outwardly and inwardly at all times except at the time of fear, because showing befriending them is permissible at that time as Jesus, peace be upon him, said: Be in the middle and walk to the side. And God warns you of Himself, and to God is the final destination. So there is no ugliness and mention of the self, so that it is known that what is warned against is a punishment issued by the Almighty, so no attention is paid to what is warned against from the disbelievers other than that.
3:29: 29Say: Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it, God knows it." That is, He knows your innermost thoughts regarding the allegiance of the infidels and other matters, whether you conceal them or reveal them. "And He knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth." In the knowledge of your secrets and your public matters. "And God is over all things competent." So He is able to punish you if you do not desist from what you have been forbidden. The verse is an explanation of the Almighty's saying: "And God warns you of Himself." It is as if He said and warns you of its negation because it is characterized by an intrinsic knowledge that encompasses all information, and an intrinsic power that encompasses all capabilities, so do not dare to disobey Him, because there is no sin except that He is aware of it and able to punish for it.
3:30: 30On the Day every soul will find present what it has done of good and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that day was a great distance. "On the Day is in the accusative case with wish", meaning every soul will wish that on the Day it will find its records of deeds, or the reward for its deeds of good and evil, present, if between it and that Day, which is for it, was a great distance, or with an implied word such as "remember, and wish is a state of the pronoun in worked or a predicate of what it has done of evil, and wish is restricted to what it has done of good and what is not conditional because wish" is raised. It was read "wish" and based on this it is correct to be conditional, but applying it to the predicate is more appropriate in meaning because it is a narration of a happening and more in line with the popular reading. "And God warns you of Himself" is repeated for emphasis and reminder. "And God is Kind to His servants" is an indication that God Almighty only forbade them out of mercy for them and consideration for their goodness, or that He is the Possessor of forgiveness and the Possessor of painful punishment, so one hopes for His mercy and fears His punishment.
3:31: 31"Say: If you love God, then follow me." Love is the soul's inclination towards something because of the perfection it has perceived in it, such that it leads it to do what brings it closer to Him. When the servant knows that true perfection is only for God, and that everything he sees as perfection in himself or someone else is from God, with God, and to God, then his love will only be for God and in God. This necessitates the will to obey Him and the desire for what brings him closer to Him. Therefore, love was interpreted as the will to obey and was made a requirement for following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his worship and keenness to obey him. God will love you and forgive you your sins. This is an answer to the command, meaning that He will be pleased with you and will remove the veils from your hearts by overlooking what you have neglected, bringing you closer to the side of His glory and placing you in the vicinity of His holiness. He expressed this with love by way of metaphor or comparison. And God is Forgiving and Merciful for those who love Him by obeying Him and following His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated that it was revealed when the Jews said, We are the children of God and His beloved. It was also said that it was revealed about the delegation from Najran when they said, We only worship Christ out of love for God. It was also said that it was about people who claimed during his time, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they loved God, so they were commanded to make their words confirmed by deeds.
