3:32: 32 "Say: Obey God and the Messenger. But if they turn away" This may be in the past or present tense, meaning if you turn away. Then God does not love the disbelievers. He is not pleased with them nor does He praise them. He did not say He does not love them for the purpose of generality and indicating that turning away is disbelief. Rather, from this perspective, he negates God's love and that His love is specific to the believers.
3:33: 33Indeed, God chose Adam, Noah, the family of Abraham, and the family of Imran over the worlds with the message and spiritual and physical characteristics, and therefore they were able to do what others were not able to do. When He made obedience to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, obligatory and explained that it brings about the love of God, He followed that by explaining their virtues as an encouragement to it, and with that He provided evidence of their superiority over the angels, and the family of Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and their children. And the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered among them, and the family of Imran Moses and Aaron, sons of Imran, son of Izhar, son of Qahath, son of Levi, son of Jacob, or Jesus, and his mother Mary, daughter of Imran, son of Mathan, son of Eleazar, son of Abi-Yudh, son of Jozan, son of Zerubbabel, son of Salian, son of Ushiah, son of Manishken, son of Hezka, son of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, son of Joram, son of Isha, son of Rajim, son of Solomon, son of David, son of Ishi, son of Obed, son of Salmon, son of Jaaz, son of Nahshon, son of Ammiad, son of Ram, son of Hasrum, son of Pharez, son of Judah, son of Jacob, peace be upon him, and there were one thousand eight hundred years between the two Imrans.
3:34: 34 Descendants, some from others is a state or a substitute for the two gods or from them and from Noah, meaning that they are one descendants branching out from each other. It was said that some from each other in religion. And descendants is a child, and it applies to the singular and the plural is fa'ila from dhar or fa'ula from dhar, its hamza was replaced with a ya', then the waw was changed to a ya' and assimilated. And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing of people's words and deeds, so He chooses whoever is upright in speech and action, or He is All-Hearing of the words of Imran's wife and All-Knowing of her intention.
3:35: 35 When the wife of Imran said, 'My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb.' So the particle idh is in the accusative case for the dispute. It was said that it is in the accusative case by implying remember. This is Hannah bint Faqudha, the grandmother of Jesus, peace be upon him. Imran bin Yashar had a daughter named Mary, who was older than Moses and Aaron. It was thought that what was meant was his wife, and it was supported by the guardianship of Zachariah, as he was a contemporary of Ibn Mathan and married his daughter Isha. Both John and Jesus, peace be upon them, were cousins from their father. It was narrated that she was an old, barren woman. While she was in the shade of a tree, she saw a bird feeding its chick, so she longed for a child and wished for one, so she said: O God, I have a vow from You that if You grant me a child, I will give him in charity to the Holy House so that he may be one of its servants. So Mary became pregnant and Imran died. This vow was permissible in their time for young boys, so perhaps she based the matter on estimation or requested a liberated male, freed for his service, not to be occupied with anything, or devoted to worship and his appointment in the present case. So accept from me what I vowed. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing of my words and intentions.
3:36: 36 And when she delivered her, she said, 'My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female,' for the pronoun for what was in her womb and its feminization because it was a female, and it is permissible for female to be in the accusative case as a state of it because its feminization is known from it in, for the state and its owner are one in essence. Or on the interpretation of feminine like the soul and the pregnant woman. She only said it out of regret and sorrow to her Lord because she was hoping to give birth to a male and for that reason she vowed to free him. And God knows best what she delivered, meaning the thing she delivered. It is a resumption from God Almighty to magnify its subject and to make her ignorant of its matter. Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read from Asim and Yaqub laid as if it was from her speech to console herself, meaning perhaps God Almighty had a secret in it, or the female was better. And laid was read as if it was addressed to God Almighty. And the male is not like the female is an explanation of his saying And God knows best meaning the male that you requested is not like the female that you gave, and the lam in both of them is for the covenant and it is possible that it is from her saying with the meaning and the male and female are not the same in what you vowed so the lam is for the gender. And I have named her Mary is in apposition to what preceded it from her statement and what is between them is an interjection, and she only mentioned that to her Lord to draw closer to Him and to ask Him to protect her and reform her so that her action would be in accordance with her name because Mary in their language means: worship. And in it is evidence that the name, the named, and the naming are different matters. And I seek refuge for her in You I protect her with Your protection. And her offspring from Satan the accursed the banished, and the origin of stoning is throwing stones. And from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, No child is born except that Satan touches him at birth, so he cries from his touch except Mary and her son. Its meaning is that Satan hopes to seduce every newborn who is affected by him except Mary and her son because God Almighty protected them by the blessing of this seeking refuge.
3:37: 37 And her Lord accepted her He was pleased with her in the vow instead of the remembrance. With good acceptance meaning with a good face in which vows are accepted, which is her establishment in the place of remembrance, or receiving her immediately after her birth before she grows up and is fit for the custodianship. It was narrated that when Hannah gave birth to her, she wrapped her in a rag and carried her to the mosque and placed her with the rabbis and said: Here is this vow, so they competed over her because she was the daughter of their leader and the one who brought their sacrifices, for the children of Mathan were the leaders and kings of the children of Israel, so Zachariah said: I have more right to her, her aunt is with me, but they refused except by drawing lots, and they were twenty-seven, so they went to a river and cast their pens, and Zachariah's pen floated and their pens sank, so Zachariah took care of her. It is permissible for it to be a source on the assumption of an added meaning with good acceptance, and for it to be accepted in the sense of received like to pass and hasten, meaning so he took her at the beginning of her matter when she was born with good acceptance. And caused her to grow well is a metaphor for raising her in a way that would suit her in all her circumstances. And caused Zakariya to be her guardian. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Asim stressed the fa, and they shortened Zakariya except for Asim in the narration of Ibn Ayish, so that the subject is God Almighty and Zakariya is the object, meaning He made him her guardian and guarantor of her interests. The rest lightened it. They extended Zakariya in the nominative case. Whenever Zakariya entered upon her the sanctuary meaning the room that was built for her, or the mosque, or the most honorable and prominent of its places, it was called that because it is the place of fighting Satan, as if she was placed in the most honorable place in the Holy House. He found with her provision is the answer to whenever and its subject. It was narrated that no one would enter upon her except him, and when he went out, he would close seven doors on her, and he would find with her the fruits of winter in the summer and vice versa. He said, O Mary, from where did you get this? From where did you get this provision that comes at an unusual time while the doors are closed on you, and this is evidence of the permissibility of the honor for his friends. This made Zachariah's miracle so that he would be confused about the matter. She said, 'It is from God.' So do not rule it out. It was said that she spoke when she was young, like Jesus, peace be upon him, and she never breastfed, and her sustenance was sent down to her from Paradise. God provides for whom He wills without account, without estimating its abundance, or without deserving it as a favor. It is possible that it was from her words or from the words of God Almighty. It was narrated: "That Fatima, may God be pleased with her, presented to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, two loaves of bread and a piece of meat, so he returned to her and said: Come here, my daughter. So she uncovered the plate and it was filled with bread and meat. He said to her: Where did you get this? She said: It is from God. God provides for whom He wills without account. He said: Praise be to God who made you similar to the lady of the women of the Children of Israel. Then he gathered Ali, Al-Hassan, and Al-Hussein, and gathered his family to him until they were full and the food remained as it was, so she gave generously to her neighbors."
3:38: 38 There Zachariah called upon his Lord in that place, or time, as here and then and where are borrowed for time, when he saw the honor of Mary and her status with God Almighty. He said, 'My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring' as He had granted it to the barren old woman Hannah. And it was said that when he saw the fruits out of season, he realized that it was permissible for a barren woman to give birth to an old man, so he asked and said, Grant me from Yourself offspring, because it was not in the usual ways and by the usual means. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication the Answerer. 5- And I feared the allies meaning his cousins and they were the worst of the Children of Israel, so he feared that they would not improve his succession over his nation and would change their religion for them. From behind me after my death, and from Ibn Kathir with extension and shortening with the opening of the ya' and it is related to something omitted, or with the meaning of the allies, meaning I feared the actions of the allies behind me, or those who are in charge of the matter after me. And it was read I feared the allies behind me meaning they were few and unable to establish the religion after me, or they were few and went before me, so based on this the circumstance was related to I feared. And my wife was barren did not give birth. So grant me from Yourself for something like it is not hoped for except from Your grace and perfect power, for my wife and I are not fit to give birth. A successor from my loins.
3:39: 39 "The angels called him" meaning from their kind, as they say Zaid is riding the horse. The caller was Gabriel alone. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read "Fanadah" with imala and masculine. "While he was standing praying in the sanctuary meaning standing in prayer, and praying" is an adjective of standing or a predicate or another state or a state of the pronoun in standing. "That God gives you good tidings of Yahya" meaning that God. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with kasra intending to say, or because calling is a type of it. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read "Yabashkur", and Yahya is a foreign name, and even if it is made Arabic, it is prevented from being declined due to the definition and the weight of the verb. "Confirming a word from God" meaning Jesus, peace be upon him. He was called that because he was found by His command, the Most High, without a father, so he resembled the innovations that are the world of command, or by the Book of God. It was called a word, as it was said, the word of Al-Huwaidara for his poem. And a master who rules his people and excels them, and he was superior to all people in that he never committed a sin. And chaste who exaggerated in restraining himself from desires and amusements. It was narrated that in his youth he passed by some boys who invited him to play, but he said: I was not created for playing. And a prophet from among the righteous growing up among them or being among those who did not commit any major or minor sin.
3:40: 40 He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a boy?' as a way of excluding the usual, or as a great deal of wonder, or as a question about how it happened. And old age has overtaken me. Old age has overtaken me and affected me. He was ninety-nine years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. And my wife is barren. She does not give birth, from barrenness, which means cutting off, because she has no children. He said, 'Thus does God do what He wills.' That is, He does what He wills of wonders, such as that action, which is creating a child from a perishing old man and a barren old woman, or as you and your wife are in terms of old age and barrenness, He does what He wills of creating a child. Or Thus is God is a subject and predicate, meaning God is like this attribute, and He does what He wills is an explanation of it. Or Thus is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning the matter is thus, and God does what He wills is an explanation of it.
3:41: 41 "He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign'" a sign by which I know the rope so that I may receive it with cheerfulness and gratitude and remove the hardship of waiting. "He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days'" meaning you will not be able to speak to people for three days, but he held his tongue from speaking to them specifically so that he would devote the period to remembering God Almighty and thanking Him, fulfilling the right of the blessing. It is as if he said, 'Your sign is that your tongue will be held except from thanking.' The best answer is what is derived from the question. "Except a symbol" is a gesture like a hand or head, and its origin is movement, and from it the symbols of the sea and the exception is disconnected and it was said connected and what is meant by speech is what indicates the pronoun. It was read: "a symbol" with two fat-has like servants, the plural of a symbol, and a symbol like messengers, the plural of symbols, as a state of it and of people, meaning they are symbolizing each other, like his saying: Whenever you meet two people, your cheeks tremble and fly away And remember your Lord often during the days of imprisonment. It confirms what preceded it and explains its purpose. Restricting the command to frequently indicates that it does not indicate repetition. And glorify God in the evening from noon until sunset. It was said from the afternoon or sunset until the middle of the night has passed. And early from sunrise until noon. It was read with the opening of the hamza, the plural of bakr like sahar and ashar.
3:42: 42 "And when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds,' they spoke to her verbally as an honor to her. Whoever denies the honor claims that this was a miracle for Zachariah or a harbinger of the prophethood of Jesus, peace be upon him, for the consensus is that He, glory be to Him, did not appoint a woman as a prophet, as He, glory be to Him, says: "And We did not send before you, except men." It was said that they inspired her, and the first selection was accepting her from her mother, and no female was accepted before her, and freeing her for worship and making her rich with the provision of Paradise from earning and purifying her from what is abhorrent in women. The second was guiding her and sending angels to her, and singling her out with the noble honors like a father without a father, and clearing her of what the Jews accused her of by making the child speak and making her and her son a sign for the worlds.
3:43: 43 O Mary, be devout toward your Lord, and prostrate and bow with those who bow. She was commanded to pray in congregation by mentioning its pillars, to emphasize its preservation. Prostration was mentioned before bowing, either because it is so in their law, or to draw attention to the fact that the letter waw does not require order, or to link bow with those who bow, to indicate that those who do not bow in their prayer are not praying. It was said that what is meant by qunut is to maintain obedience, as in the Almighty’s saying: Is he who is devout during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing? And prostration is prayer, as in the Almighty’s saying: And at the ends of prostration. And bowing is humility and submission.
3:44: 44 This is from the report of the unseen which We reveal to you, meaning what We mentioned of the stories of the unseen that you did not know except through revelation. And you were not with them when they cast their pens, their cups for casting lots. It was said that they cast lots with the pens with which they used to write the Torah as a blessing. What is meant is to establish that it was a revelation by way of mocking those who deny it, since the path of knowledge is the observed events and hearing and not hearing is known and there is no doubt about it among them, so it remains that the accusation is based on the possibility of seeing, and no sane person would suspect it. Which of them will be responsible for Mary? is related to an omitted word indicated by they cast their pens, meaning they cast them to know, or say, Which of them will be responsible for Mary. "And you were not with them when they disputed," competing over her care.
3:45: 45 When the angels said instead of the first When they said and what is between them is an objection, or of When they dispute on the basis that the dispute and the good report occurred in a wide period of time, like your saying I met him in such and such a year. O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary. Messiah is his title, and it is one of the honorable titles like the Truthful. Its origin in Hebrew is Messiah, which means: the blessed. Jesus is the Arabization of Joshua, and they are both derived from wiping, because they wiped someone with blessing or with what purified him from sins, or he wiped the ground and did not stand in a place, or Gabriel wiped him, from the whiteness which is covered with redness, a futile effort. And the son of Mary, since it is a characteristic that distinguishes the distinction of names, it is organized in its chain, and it does not contradict the multiplicity of the report and the singularity of the subject, because it is a generic noun with an addition, and it is possible that it is intended that the one by whom he is known and distinguished from others are these three, because the name is the sign of the named and distinguishes him from others. It is possible that Jesus is the report of a deleted subject and the son of Mary is his description. Rather, it was said the son of Mary and the address to her is to indicate that he is born without a father, because children are attributed to fathers and are not attributed to the mother except if the father is missing. Highly respected in this world and the Hereafter is a state of the word, which, even though it is indefinite, is described, and its masculinity is for the sake of meaning. Highly respected in this world is prophethood, and in the Hereafter it is intercession. And among those brought near to God. It was said that it is a reference to his high status in Paradise or his being raised to heaven and the company of the angels.
3:46: 46 And he will speak to the people in the cradle and as an adult meaning he will speak to them while he is a child and an adult, the speech of the prophets without any difference. The cradle is a source for what is prepared for the boy in his bed. It was said that he was raised as a young man, and what is meant is as an adult after his descent, and his different, contradictory states were mentioned as guidance that he is isolated from divinity. And of the righteous is a third state of the word or its pronoun that speaks.
3:47: 47 She said, 'My Lord, how can I have a son when no man has touched me?' This was astonishment, or a normal exclusion, or a question about whether it would be through marriage or otherwise. He said, 'Thus does God create what He wills.' The speaker was Gabriel, or God Almighty, and Gabriel narrated to her the words of God Almighty. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is. This is an indication that just as God Almighty is able to create things gradually through causes and materials, He is also able to create them all at once without that.
3:48: 48 And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel. This is a subjective statement mentioned to please her heart and remove the fear of blame that worried her when she learned that she would give birth without a husband, or in apposition to He gives you good tidings, or a distinguished person. "The Book" means the scribes or the type of revealed books. The two books were singled out for their excellence. Nafi' and Asim read "and He will teach him with a ya."
3:49: 49 And a messenger to the Children of Israel, that I have come to you with a sign from your Lord is accusative with an implied subject meaning to say, which is: And he says I sent a messenger that I have come to you, or by conjoining with the previous states implying the meaning of speech, so it is as if he said: And a speaker that I have come to you, and the specification of the Children of Israel for the specificity of his mission to them or to respond to those who claimed that he was sent to others. That I create for you from clay like the form of a bird is accusative instead of that I have come to you, or genitive instead of sign, or nominative on it that I create for you and the meaning is: I determine for you and form things like the form of a bird, and Nafi' read that I with a kasra so I breathe into it the pronoun is for the kaf meaning into that similar thing. So it becomes a bird by the permission of God so it becomes alive and flying by the command of God, he pointed out with it that its revival is from God Almighty and not from him. Nafi' read here and in Al-Ma'idah bird with the alif and the hamza. And I heal the blind and the leper the blind is the one who was born blind or the one whose eye was anointed. It was narrated that thousands of patients would sometimes gather around him, whoever could bear it would come to him and whoever could not, Jesus, peace be upon him, would come to him, and he would not be treated except by supplication. And I bring the dead to life by God’s permission he repeated by God’s permission to dispel the illusion of divinity, because bringing to life is not of the same kind as human actions. And I inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses of the unseen aspects of your conditions that you have no doubt about. Indeed in that is a sign for you if you are believers successful in believing, because others do not benefit from miracles, or believing in the truth and not being stubborn.
3:50: 50 "And confirming what came before me of the Torah is in apposition to a Messenger in both ways, or is accusative by the implication of a verb indicated by I have come to you" meaning I have come to you confirming. "And to make lawful for you" is understood by its implication, or is returned to his saying: "I have come to you with a sign, or is in apposition to the meaning of confirming" like their saying I have come to you apologizing and to please your heart. "Some of what was forbidden to you" meaning in the law of Moses, peace be upon him, such as fats, droppings, fish, camel meat, and working on the Sabbath, and it indicates that his law abrogates the law of Moses, peace be upon him, and this does not negate its being a confirmation of the Torah, just as the abrogation of some parts of the Qur'an by others does not return to it with contradiction and falsehood, for abrogation in reality is clarification and specification in times "And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear God and obey me."
3:51: 51 "Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path." That is, I have come to you with another sign that your Lord has inspired, which is His statement: Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord. It is the call to the truth agreed upon among the messengers, distinguishing between the prophet and the magician. Or I have come to you with a sign that God is my Lord and your Lord. His statement: So fear God and obey me is an objection, and it appears that it is a repetition of His statement: I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, that is, I have come to you with a sign after another of what I have mentioned to you. The first is to prepare the argument and the second is to bring it closer to the ruling, and therefore He arranged upon it with the letter fa His statement, the Most High: So fear God, that is, when I have come to you with the apparent miracles and dazzling signs, then fear God in opposition and obey me in what I have called you to. Then He began the call and referred to it with the general statement, saying: Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, indicating the completion of the theoretical power with the true belief whose goal is monotheism. And He said: So worship Him, indicating the completion of the scientific power, for By adhering to obedience, which is carrying out the commands and refraining from the prohibitions, then he decided that by explaining that combining the two matters is the path that is known for its righteousness, and similar to that is his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, Say, ‘I believe in God,’ then be steadfast.
3:52: 52 When Jesus perceived disbelief on their part he realized their disbelief with him, which is what is perceived by the senses. "He said: Who are my helpers to God?" Taking refuge in God Almighty or going or joining Him, and it is permissible for the preposition to be related to my helpers implying the meaning of addition, that is, from those who add themselves to God Almighty in my support. It was said that here to means with or in or the lam and the disciples said the man's disciples are his special ones from the houris which is pure whiteness, and from it the Hawariyat for the urban women because of the purity of their colors. The companions of Jesus, peace be upon him, from the Jews were called by this name. It was said that they are short-skinned people who whiten the clothes, that is, they whiten them. We are the helpers of God meaning the helpers of the religion of God. We have believed in God, and bear witness that we are Muslims to bear witness for us on the Day of Resurrection when the messengers bear witness for their people and against them.
3:53: 53 Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and have followed the Messenger, so register us among the witnesses. That is, among those who bear witness to Your oneness, or with the prophets who bear witness for their followers, or with the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for they are witnesses over the people.
3:54: 54 And they plotted meaning those Jews who were aware of the disbelief, so they appointed someone to kill him by treachery. And God plotted when He raised Jesus, peace be upon him, and cast his likeness on those who intended to assassinate him until he was killed. And plotting, in that it is originally a trick by which someone brings harm to another, is not attributed to God except by way of comparison and duplication. And God is the best of plotters the most powerful of them in plotting and the most capable of causing harm from where he least expects.
3:55: 55 "When God said" is an adverb for God's deception or the best of deceptions, or the implied as it happened. "O Jesus, I will take you" meaning I will complete your term and postpone you to your appointed term, protecting you from their killing, or taking you from the earth from the time my wealth is taken, or taking you while asleep as it was narrated that he was raised while asleep, or causing you to die to the heavens and to him the Christians went. "And raise you to Me" to the place of My honor and the seat of My angels. "And purify you from those who disbelieve" from their bad behavior or intentions. "And make those who follow you superior to those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection" He assists them with argument or the sword in most cases, and his followers are those who believed in his prophethood from the Muslims and Christians and until now you have not heard of the Jews prevailing over them nor have they achieved a kingdom or state. "Then to Me is your return" the pronoun refers to Jesus, peace be upon him, and those who followed him and those who disbelieved in him, and the ones addressed are mostly absent. "Then I will judge between you concerning that over which you differed" of the matter of religion.
3:56: 56 As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
3:57: 57 And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their reward in full. An explanation of the ruling and a detailed explanation of it. Hafs read He will pay them with a ya. And God does not love the wrongdoers. A confirmation of that.
3:58: 58 That refers to what came before of the report of Jesus and others, and it is the subject of its predicate. We recite it to you and his saying: of the signs is a state of the ha' and it is possible for the predicate and we recite it to be a state on the condition that the agent has the meaning of the indication and that they are two predicates and that it is subject to an implied word that explains it. And the wise remembrance that includes the ruling, or the decisive that is prevented from being flawed, meaning the Qur'an. And it was said the tablet.
3:59: 59 "The likeness of Jesus before God is as the likeness of Adam." His strange affair is like the affair of Adam, peace be upon him. "He created him from dust" is a sentence explaining the metaphor and clarifying what the likeness is, which is that he was created without a father, just as Adam was created from dust without a father or a mother. He likened his condition to something stranger than it, to silence the opponent and to cut off the materials of doubt. The meaning is that He created his mold from dust. "Then He said to him, 'Be.' That is, He created him as a human being, as God Almighty says, Then We produced him as another creation." Or He determined his formation from dust, then He created him. It is permissible for it to be "then" due to the delay of the report, not the informant. "So it is" is a narration of a past situation.
3:60: 60 The truth is from your Lord is an omitted predicate, meaning it is the truth. It was said that the truth is the subject and from your Lord is its predicate, meaning the truth mentioned from God Almighty. So do not be among those who doubt is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a way of provocation to increase steadfastness or to every listener.
3:61: 61 So whoever disputes with you from the Christians. About it in Jesus. After what has come to you of knowledge meaning the clear proofs that necessitate knowledge. "Then say: Come" come with opinion and determination. We will call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves meaning each one of us and you will call himself and the dearest of his family and those closest to his heart to the Mubahala and carry it out. He only put them before the souls because a man risks his life for them and fights for them. Then we will implore meaning we will implore each other by cursing the liar among us. And the word bahala with the dammah and fathah means cursing and its origin is leaving from their saying bahalat an-naqa if you leave it without a squeak. And we will place the curse of God upon the liars is a conjunction in which there is clarification. It was narrated that when they were called to the Mubahala, they said, Let us see. When they had finished, they said to the follower - who had their opinion - What do you think? He said, “By God, you have recognized his prophethood, and he has come to you with the decisive factor in the matter of your companion. By God, no people engage in Mubahala with a prophet except that they perish. If you refuse except to adhere to your religion, then say farewell to the man and depart. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had come in the morning embracing Al-Husayn, holding the hand of Al-Hasan, and Fatima walking behind him and Ali, may God be pleased with him, behind her, and he was saying, ‘When I call, then say Amen.’ Their bishop said, ‘O group of Christians, I see faces that if they asked God, the Most High, to remove a mountain from its place, He would remove it, so do not engage in Mubahala, lest you perish.’ So they submitted to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and offered him the tribute of two thousand red garments and thirty iron shields. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if they engaged in Mubahala, they would be transformed into monkeys and pigs, and fire would be set on them.” The valley is a fire, and God will eradicate Najran and its people, even the birds on the trees.” This is evidence of his prophethood and the virtue of those he brought from his family.
3:62: 62 This meaning what was narrated of the story of Jesus and Mary. It is the true story in its entirety is the predicate of in, or it is a chapter indicating that what he mentioned regarding the matter of Jesus and Mary is true, unlike what they mentioned, and what follows it is the predicate and the lam entered into it because it is closer to the subject than the ink, and its origin is that it enters into the subject And there is no god but God He stated in it the additional of for the sake of completeness, to confirm the response to the Christians in their trinity And God is the Exalted in Might, the Wise No one else is equal to Him in complete power and consummate wisdom to share with Him in divinity.
3:63: 63But if they turn away, then indeed, God is Knowing of the corrupters. This is a threat to them, and the apparent is placed in place of the implicit to indicate that turning away from the arguments and turning away from monotheism is corruption of religion and belief, leading to the corruption of the soul and even to the corruption of the world.
3:64: 64Say, O People of the Book refers to the People of the Two Books. It was said that he meant the delegation of Najran, or the Jews of Medina. Come to a word that is equitable between us and you in which the messengers and books do not differ, and what follows explains it that we worship none but God that we unify Him in worship and be sincere in it. And that we associate nothing with Him and that we do not make anyone else a partner with Him in deserving worship, nor do we see Him as worthy of being worshipped. And that some of us take others as lords besides God and we do not say that Ezra is the son of God, nor that the Messiah is the son of God, and we do not obey the rabbis in what they have innovated of prohibiting and permitting because each of them is a human being like us. It was narrated that when the verse They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides God was revealed, Adi bin Hatim said: We did not worship them, O Messenger of God. He said: Did they not make what was lawful for you and what was forbidden, so you would accept their word? He said: Yes. He said: That is it. Then if they turn away from monotheism. Then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims.’ That is, the proof is binding on you, so acknowledge that we are Muslims without you, or acknowledge that you are disbelievers in what the books have spoken and what the messengers have agreed upon. Note Look at what he took into account in this story of exaggeration in guidance and good gradation in argumentation between: First, the conditions of Jesus, peace be upon him, and the stages that he went through that contradicted divinity, then he mentioned what would solve their knots and remove their doubts. When he saw their stubbornness and obstinacy, he called them to the Mubahalah with a kind of miracle. Then when they turned away from it and submitted to some submission, he returned to them with guidance and took an easier path, and he made it obligatory by calling them to what Jesus, the Gospel, and all the other prophets and books agreed upon. Then when he did not find that on them either and he knew that the signs and warnings would not suffice for them, he turned away from that and said, Then say, ‘Bear witness that we are Muslims.’
3:65: 65 O People of the Scripture, why do you dispute about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? The Jews and Christians disputed about Abraham, peace be upon him, and each group claimed that he was from them. They brought their case to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, and this was revealed. The meaning is that Judaism and Christianity reported that the Torah and the Gospel were revealed to Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them, and Abraham was a thousand years before Moses and Jesus was two thousand years before them, so how could this be the case for them? Do you not understand? So you claim the impossible.
3:66: 66 "Here you are, you have argued about that of which you have knowledge. So why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge?" Ha is a letter of warning with which they alerted to their state of which they were unaware. You is the subject and these is its predicate and you have argued is another clause explaining the first. That is, you are these fools and the explanation of your foolishness is that you have argued about that of which you have knowledge, which you found in the Torah and the Gospel, out of stubbornness, or you claim that it was mentioned in the Torah. So why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge and which is not mentioned in your book of the religion of Abraham? It was said that these means those and argued is its connection. It was said that Here you is originally A'ntum as a question to express astonishment at their foolishness, so the hamza was changed to a ha. Nafi and Abu Amr read ha antum where it was pronounced with a long vowel without a hamza, and Warsh with a shorter vowel, and Qunbal with a hamza without an alif after the ha’, and the rest with a long vowel and a hamza, and Al-Bazzi with a short vowel on its original form. And God knows what you have argued about. And you do not know and you are ignorant of it.
3:67: 67 Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian is a statement based on what he established from the evidence. But he was one inclining toward truth deviating from false beliefs. A Muslim submissive to God, and it does not mean that he was of the religion of Islam, otherwise the obligation would have been shared. And he was not of the polytheists is an allusion to the fact that they were polytheists because they associated Ezra and the Messiah with him, and it is a response to the polytheists' claim that they were of the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him.
3:68: 68 The people who are most deserving of Abraham are the most special to him and the closest to him. From the word wali which means closeness. Those who followed him from his nation. And this Prophet and those who believed because they agreed with him in most of what he legislated for them in principle. And the Prophet was read in the accusative case in apposition to the ha in followed him, and in the genitive case in apposition to Abraham. And God is the ally of the believers He supports them and rewards them with goodness for their faith.
3:69: 69 A party of the People of the Scripture wish they could mislead you. It was revealed about the Jews when they invited Hudhayfah, Ammar, and Muadh to Judaism. If means that. They only mislead themselves. Misguidance does not overtake them and its consequences only return to them, as their punishment is doubled by it, or They only mislead their likes. "And they do not perceive" its burden and the fact that its harm is limited to them.
3:70: 70 O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the signs of God in what the Torah and the Gospel stated and indicated the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while you bear witness that they are the signs of God, or in the Qur'an, and you bear witness to His description in the two books, or you know by the miracles that it is the truth.
3:71: 71 O People of the Scripture, why do you mix truth with falsehood? by distorting and presenting falsehood in its true form, or by failing to distinguish between them. It was read Talabsiwun with emphasis and Talabsiwun with a fatha on the ba, meaning you mix truth with falsehood, as in his saying, peace be upon him, Like a wearer of two garments of falsehood. "And you conceal the truth" the prophethood of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and his description. "And you know" knowing what you conceal.
3:72: 72 "And a party of the People of the Scripture said, 'Believe in that which was revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day,' meaning they showed belief in the Qur'an at the beginning of the day. 'And disbelieve in it at its end that perhaps they will return.' And disbelieve in it at its end that perhaps they will doubt their religion, thinking that you have returned due to a defect that has become apparent to you.' What is meant by the party is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Malik ibn al-Sayf. They said to their companions when the qiblah was changed: 'Believe in what was revealed to them regarding praying towards the Ka'bah and pray towards it at the beginning of the day, then pray towards the rock at its end that perhaps they will say, 'They are more knowledgeable than us, and they have returned,' and they will return." It was said that twelve of the rabbis of Khaybar conspired to enter Islam at the beginning of the day and say at its end. We looked in our book and consulted our scholars, but we did not find Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, with the description that was mentioned in the Torah, perhaps his companions would doubt him.
3:73: 73 "And do not believe except to those who follow your religion" and do not acknowledge the belief of your heart except to the people of your religion, or do not show your faith in the face of the day to those who are on your religion, for their return is more hopeful and important. "Say, 'Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God'" He guides whomever He wills to faith and makes him steadfast in it. "That someone should be given the like of what you have been given" is related to something omitted, meaning that you plotted that and said that someone should be given, the meaning is that envy led you to that or that you should not believe, meaning do not show your faith that someone should be given the like of what you have been given except to your followers, and do not spread it to the Muslims lest their steadfastness increase, nor to the polytheists lest it call them to Islam. His statement, "Say, 'Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God' is an objection indicating that their plotting is of no avail, or the predicate of that" on the basis that the guidance of God is a substitute for the guidance. Ibn Kathir's reading of "that someone should be given" as a question for reprimand supports the first interpretation, that is, unless someone is given to you. "In was read as a negative, so it is from the speech of the group, that is, and do not believe except for those who follow your religion, and say to them, No one has been given what you have been given. Or they argue with you before your Lord is in apposition to that someone should be given" according to the first two interpretations, and according to the third, its meaning is: until they argue with you before your Lord and refute your argument before your Lord. The waw is the pronoun for someone because it is in the sense of the plural, since what is meant by it is not their followers. "Say, 'Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God. He gives it to whom He wills. And God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.'" Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 5 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the next verses of Sūrat āl ʿIm'rān. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. Portions of this work have been translated using AI (machine-assisted translation) and post-edited for clarity and accuracy. While an ongoing effort has been made to ensure fidelity to the original text, minor variations, or mistakes may be found. 3:74: 74 He chooses for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty. A response and refutation of what they claimed with clear evidence.
3:75: 75 And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will return it to you such as Abdullah bin Salam, to whom a Qurayshite entrusted one thousand two hundred ounces of gold and he returned it to him. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you such as Nahas bin Azura, to whom another Qurayshite entrusted a dinar and he denied it. It was said that those who are trusted with much money are the Christians, since trustworthiness is common among them, and the traitors with little money are the Jews, since treachery is common among them. Hamzah, Abu Bakr, and Abu Amr read yu'udhu 'ilak and la yu'udhu 'ilak with a sukoon on the ha' and Qalun with the stealing of the kasra of the ha' and likewise it was narrated from Hafs and the rest with the full kasra. Except as long as you stand over him except for the period of time you stand over his head, exaggerating in demanding litigation, pleading, and presenting evidence. That is an indication of not returning the payment indicated by his saying will not return it. Because they said because of their saying. There is no blame or rebuke against us concerning the unlettered ones meaning, there is no blame or rebuke against us concerning those who are not from the People of the Book - and who are not of our religion. And they tell a lie about God by claiming that while they know that they are lying, because they considered it permissible to oppress those who opposed them and said: There was no sanctity for them in the Torah. It was said that the Jews dealt with a man from Quraysh, and when he converted to Islam, they took legal action against them and they said: Your right is forfeited since you abandoned your religion,” and they claimed that this was also in their book. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when this verse was revealed: “The enemies lied. There is nothing in the days of ignorance that is not under my feet except for the trust, for it is returned to the righteous and the wicked.”
3:76: 76 "Yes" is proof of what they denied, i.e. yes, there is a way for them. "Whoever fulfills his covenant and fears God - then indeed, God loves the righteous. A resumption confirming the sentence that yes filled in for, and the genitive pronoun for whoever or for God and the generality of the righteous replaced the one who returned from the reward to whoever", and I feel that piety is the essence of the matter and it includes fulfillment and other things such as performing duties and avoiding prohibitions.
3:77: 77 Those who exchange "the covenant of God" what they have pledged to God of belief in the Messenger and fulfillment of trusts. "and their oaths and what they have sworn by saying, By God, we will believe in him and support him, for a small price" the enjoyment of this world. "Those will have no portion in the Hereafter, nor will God speak to them" with what pleases them or with anything at all, and that the angels will ask Him on the Day of Resurrection, or they will not benefit from the words and verses of God. It appears that it is a metaphor for His anger with them, as He says: "nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection", for whoever is angry with someone else and belittles him, He turns away from him and from speaking to him and turning towards him, just as whoever is arrogant towards someone else, speaks to him and looks at him a lot. "nor will He purify them nor praise them and for them is a painful punishment" for what they did. It was said: It was revealed about rabbis who distorted the Torah and changed the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the ruling on trusts and other things, and they took bribes for that. It was also said: It was revealed about a man who displayed goods in the market and swore that he had bought them for something he had not bought them for. It was also said: It was revealed about a dispute that took place between Al-Ash'ath bin Qais and a Jew over a well or land, and the oath was directed at the Jew.
3:78: 78 And indeed, among them is a group meaning the distorters such as Ka'b, Malik, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab. They twist their tongues with the Book twisting it by reading it, so they incline it away from the revealed text to the distorted text, or they bend it with something resembling the Book. Yalawn was read by changing the damma waw to a hamza, then lightening it by deleting it and placing its vowel on the consonant before it. That you may think it is from the Book, but it is not from the Book is the pronoun for the distorted text indicated by the statement they twist. That you may think it was read with a ya' and the pronoun also refers to the names. And they say it is from God, but it is not from God is an emphasis in His statement: And it is not from the Book and a denunciation of them and a clarification because they claim that explicitly, not implicitly, meaning that it was not revealed from Him. This does not mean that the servant's action is not the action of God Almighty. And they tell lies about God while they know is an emphasis and recording of them lying about God and doing so intentionally.
3:79: 79 It is not for a human being that God should give him the Book and wisdom and prophethood and then he should say to the people, 'Be my servants instead of God.' This is a lie and a response to His servant Jesus, peace be upon him. It was said, "Abu Rafi' al-Qurazi and Sayyid al-Najrani said, 'O Muhammad, do you want us to worship you and take you as a Lord?' He said, 'God forbid that we should worship other than God and that we should command the worship of other than God. For that is not what He sent me to do, nor did He command me to do that.' So it was revealed." It was said, "A man said, 'O Messenger of God, we greet you as we greet one another. Should we not prostrate to you?' He said, 'It is not appropriate to prostrate to anyone other than God. Rather, honor your Prophet and acknowledge the truth to its people.'" But be rabbis. But he says, Be rabbis. The word rabbi is attributed to the Lord by adding the letter alif and the letter nun, like al-Laythani and al-Raqbani, and it is the perfect one in knowledge and action. Because you have taught the Book and because you have studied it because you are teachers of the Book and because you are students of it, the benefit of teaching and learning is knowing the truth and goodness for belief and action. Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, Abu Amr, and Ya’qub read you teach in the sense of knowing. You study was read from teaching and you study from adris meaning studied like akram and karam, and it is possible that the famous reading also has this meaning on the assumption that because you have taught it to the people.
3:80: 80 And He does not command you to take the angels and the prophets as lords. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Asim, and Yaqub put it in the accusative case in apposition to Then He says. The la is an additional particle to emphasize the meaning of negation in His statement it was not, meaning it was not for a human being to be called by God to be a prophet and then command people to worship Himself and command to take the angels and the prophets as lords, or it is not an additional particle to mean that he does not have the right to command to worship Him or to command to take his equals as lords, rather he forbids it and it is lower than worship. The rest put it in the accusative case as a resumption, and the situation is possible. Abu Amr read it according to its origin according to the narration of Al-Duri by stealing the damma. Does He command you to disbelieve? is a denial, and the pronoun in it refers to humans and it was said to God. After you are Muslims is evidence that the address is to the Muslims and they are those who have asked permission to prostrate to Him.
3:81: 81 "And when God took a covenant from the prophets, 'Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him. '" It was said that it is on its face value, and if this is the ruling of the prophets, then the nations are more deserving of it. It was said that its meaning is that God the Most High took the covenant from the prophets and their nations and dispensed with mentioning them instead of mentioning the nations. It was said that adding the covenant to the prophets is adding it to the subject, and the meaning is, and when God took the covenant that the prophets confirmed with their nations. It was said that what is meant is the children of the prophets with the deletion of the added, and they are the children of Israel, or He called them prophets in mockery because they used to say, "We are more deserving of prophethood than Muhammad because we are the people of the Book and the prophets were from us. The lam in lama" is used for an oath because taking the covenant means swearing, and what is possible is the conditional and you must believe, it is the answer to the oath and the condition and it is possible for the report. Hamza read "lamma with a kasra on the basis that lamma is a source, meaning because of my giving you some of you the Book, then the coming of a messenger confirming him, God took the covenant that you should believe in him and support him", or it is a relative pronoun meaning God took it for what I gave you and a messenger came to you confirming him. "lamma was read with the meaning when I gave you, or for the sake of what I gave you, on the basis that its origin is lamma" with assimilation, so one of the three meems was deleted due to the difficulty. Nafi' read "ataynakum" with a nun and an alif together. "He said, Did you acknowledge and take upon yourself My covenant for that? meaning My pledge, it was named thus because it is called yasir, meaning it tightens. It was read with a damma, which is either a dialect in it like ‘abara and ‘abara about the plural of isaar which is what is tightened with. They said, We acknowledged. He said, Then bear witness." meaning, let some of you bear witness to one another with the acknowledgment. Al-Hattāb said in "li-l-mala'iq. And I am with you among the witnesses." I am also a witness to your acknowledgment and your bearing witness, and it is a great emphasis and warning.
3:82: 82 But whoever turns away after that after the covenant, confirmation, acknowledgment, and testimony. Then those are the wicked the rebellious unbelievers.
3:83: 83 "Do they seek other than the religion of God? is in apposition to the previous sentence, and the hamza is between them for denial, or something is omitted, meaning Do you turn to God and seek other than the religion of God?" The object is presented because it is the intended meaning of the denial, and the verb is in the third person according to Abu Amr and Asim in the narration of Hafs and Yaqub, and with the ta' according to the rest, based on the estimation of "and say to him. And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion." That is, willingly by looking and following the argument, and reluctantly by the sword and witnessing what compels one to Islam, such as moving a mountain, realizing drowning, and looming over death. Or chosen like the angels and believers, and subjugated like the disbelievers, for they are not able to refrain from what He has decreed for them. "And to Him they will be returned." It was read with the ya', so that the pronoun refers to whoever.
3:84: 84 "Say: We believe in God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and the prophets from their Lord." An order to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform about himself and his followers with faith, and the Qur'an as it was revealed to him through the mediation of its delivery to them, and also what is attributed to one of the group may be attributed to them, or to speak about itself in the manner of kings out of reverence for it, and the revelation as it is transitive with ila because it ends with the messengers is transitive with ala because it is from above, and the one who was sent down to him, peace be upon him, was presented before the one sent down to the rest of the messengers because he is the one who is known and the standard is upon him We make no distinction between any of them in belief and denial. And we are Muslims to Him obedient or sincere in his worship.
3:85: 85 And whoever desires other than Islam as religion meaning other than monotheism and submission to the rule of God. Never will it be accepted from him, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers falling into loss. The meaning is that the one who turns away from Islam and seeks something other than it is missing out on benefit and falling into loss by invalidating the sound nature upon which people were created. It is used as evidence that faith is Islam, since if it were other than it, it would not be accepted. The answer is that it negates the acceptance of every religion that differs from it, not the acceptance of everything that differs from it. Perhaps religion is also for deeds.
3:86: 86 How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief and testified that the Messenger was true and clear proofs had come to them? It is unlikely that God would guide them, for the one who deviates from the truth after it has been made clear to him is immersed in misguidance and far from guidance. It was said that it is a denial and rejection of it, and that requires that the repentance of the apostate not be accepted. And they testified is in apposition to what is in their belief of the meaning of the verb and its equivalent, so I believed and I was, or a state with the omission of qad from disbelieved, and in both cases it is evidence that the admission with the tongue is outside the reality of faith. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people who wronged themselves by neglecting to consider and placing disbelief in place of faith, so how about the one to whom the truth came and he recognized it and then turned away from it.
3:87: 87 Their recompense is that upon them is the curse of God and the angels and of mankind, all together. Its explicit meaning indicates that it is permissible to curse them, and its implication indicates that it is not permissible to curse others. Perhaps the difference is that they are naturally infidels, forbidden from guidance, and denied mercy altogether, unlike others. What is meant by people are the believers or the general public, for the infidel is also cursed by the one who denies the truth and apostatizes from it, but he does not know the truth specifically.
3:88: 88 They will abide therein eternally in the curse, or punishment, or Hellfire, even though it is not permissible to mention them because the speech indicates them. The punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
3:89: 89 Except for those who repent after that meaning after apostasy. And put right what they corrupted, and it is permissible that it does not have an object meaning and entered into righteousness. Then God is Forgiving accepting his repentance. Merciful showing favor to him. It was said that it was revealed about Al-Harith bin Suwaid when he regretted his apostasy and sent to his people to ask if there is repentance for me, so his brother Al-Jalas sent him the verse and he returned to Madinah and repented.
3:90: 90 "Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief" such as the Jews who disbelieved in Jesus and the Gospel after believing in Moses and the Torah, then increased in disbelief in Muhammad and the Qur'an, or disbelieved in Muhammad after they believed in him before his mission then increased in disbelief by persisting and obstinacy and slandering him and turning away from faith and breaking the covenant, or like a people who apostatized and went to Mecca then increased in disbelief by saying we will await for Muhammad the vicissitudes of fate or we will return to him and we will be hypocritical with him by showing it. "Their repentance will not be accepted" because they do not repent, or they do not repent except when they are on the verge of destruction, so the non-acceptance of their repentance was referred to as non-acceptance as a harshness in their case and to highlight their condition in the image of those who have despaired of mercy, or because their repentance is nothing but hypocrisy due to their apostasy and increased disbelief, and for this reason the letter "fa" was not included in it. "And those are the ones who are astray" those who persist in misguidance.
3:91: 91 Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers - never will an earth full of gold be accepted from one of them. Since death in disbelief was a reason for not accepting the ransom, the letter fa was inserted here to indicate this, and filling something is what fills it. And gold is in the accusative case as a distinction. It is read in the nominative case as a substitute for filling or as a predicate for something omitted. And if he ransomed himself with it is based on the meaning as if it was said: No ransom will be accepted from any of them even if he ransomed himself with the earth full of gold, or it is conjoined with an implied meaning: No ransom will be accepted from any of them even if he ransomed himself with the earth full of gold even if he offered it in this world even if he ransomed himself with it from the punishment in the hereafter, or what is meant is if he ransomed himself with something similar, as in the saying of the Most High: Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and something like it and the like is omitted and is often intended because two like things are considered one thing, those will have a painful punishment as an exaggeration in warning and despair because the one from whom the ransom is not accepted may be pardoned as a kindness, and they will have no helpers in repelling the punishment, and of is an additional word for comprehensiveness.
3:92: 92 "You will never attain righteousness" meaning you will never attain the true righteousness which is the perfection of goodness, or you will never attain the righteousness of God the Most High which is mercy, pleasure and Paradise. "Until you spend from that which you love" meaning money, or what is general and other than that, such as spending one's status in helping people, one's body in obeying God and one's life in His path. It was narrated that "when this was revealed, Abu Talha came and said: O Messenger of God, the most beloved of my wealth to me is Bayruha, so put it where God shows you. He said: Good, good, that is profitable or profitable wealth, and I think that you should give it to your relatives. Zaid ibn Haritha came with a horse that he loved and said: This is for the sake of God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loaded Usama ibn Zaid on it. Zaid said: I only wanted to give it in charity. He, peace be upon him, said: God has accepted it from you." This indicates that spending the most beloved wealth on the closest of relatives is better, and that the verse includes obligatory and recommended spending. Some of what you love was read, and it indicates that min is for partiality and may be for clarification. And whatever you spend of anything meaning of anything beloved or otherwise, and min is for clarifying what. God is Knowing of it so He will reward you according to it.
3:93: 93 All food meaning the foodstuffs and what is meant is to eat them. It was lawful for the Children of Israel lawful for them, and it is a source of description and therefore the singular and plural and masculine and feminine are the same in it. God Almighty said: They are not lawful for them. "Except what Israel made unlawful" Jacob. "For himself" such as camel meat and milk. It was said that he had sciatica and vowed that if he recovered he would not eat the food he loved most and that was what he loved most. It was said that he did that for treatment with the advice of doctors. It was used as evidence by those who permitted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to exert himself, and the one who prevented him from saying that with God's permission in it is like forbidding it from the beginning. "Before the Torah was revealed" meaning before it was revealed, including the prohibition of what was prohibited to them due to their injustice and transgression, as punishment and severity. This is a response to the Jews in their claim of innocence from what was criticized against them in the Almighty’s saying: "Then because of the wrongdoing of those who are Jews, We prohibited for them [certain] good things" and His saying: "And for those who are Jews, We prohibited every animal with claws" the two verses, by saying that they were not the first to whom it was prohibited, but rather it was prohibited to Noah and Abraham and those after him until the matter reached us, so it was prohibited to us as it was prohibited to those before us. In it is the prevention of abrogation and the attack on the claim of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to agree with Abraham, peace be upon him, in permitting camel meat and milk. "Say: Bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful" He ordered to argue with them with their book and to rebuke them for what is in it that what was not prohibited was prohibited to them due to their injustice. It was narrated that when he, peace be upon him, said this to them, they were astonished and did not dare to bring out the Torah. This is evidence of his prophethood.
3:94: 94 So whoever invents a lie against God innovates it against God Almighty by claiming that He prohibited that before the Torah was revealed to the Children of Israel and before them. After that after the proof was imposed on them. Then those are the wrongdoers who do not do justice to themselves and deny the truth after it has become clear to them.
3:95: 95 "Say: God has spoken the truth" is an allusion to their lie, meaning that it is proven that God is truthful in what He revealed and you are the liars. So follow the religion of Abraham, the upright meaning the religion of Islam which is originally the religion of Abraham, or similar to his religion until you are free from Judaism which forced you to distort and be stubborn in order to achieve worldly goals, and obligated you to forbid good things which God Almighty made lawful for Abraham and those who followed him. And he was not of the polytheists is an allusion to the fact that following him is obligatory in pure monotheism and uprightness in religion and avoiding excess and deficiency, and an allusion to the polytheism of the Jews.
3:96: 96 The first House established for mankind means established for worship and made a place of worship for them, and the one who established it is God the Most High. This is indicated by the fact that it was read in the active form. For the one in Makkah for the house in Makkah, which is a language in Makkah like Nabit and Namit, and a regular and final matter and a constant and necessary and it was said that it is the location of the mosque. Makkah is the city from Bakkah if it is crowded, or from Bakkah if it is crushed, for it makes the necks of tyrants weep. It was narrated: "That peace be upon him was asked about the first house established for mankind, and he said: The Sacred Mosque, then the Holy House. And he was asked how much time was between them, and he said forty years." And it was said that the first to build it was Abraham, then it was demolished and a people from Jurhum built it, then the Amalekites, then the Quraysh. And it was said that it was the first house built by Adam, then it was obliterated in the flood, then Abraham built it. It was said: There was a house in its place before Adam called Ad-Dhirah, which the angels would circumambulate. When Adam descended, he was ordered to perform Hajj and circumambulate around it, and he was raised in the flood to the fourth heaven, and the angels of the heavens would circumambulate around it. This does not fit the meaning of the verse. It was said that what is meant is that it is the first house in honor, not in time. Blessed is full of goodness and benefit for whoever performs Hajj, Umrah, and I’tikaf there and circumambulates around it, a state of what is hidden in the circumstance. And a guidance for the worlds because it is their qiblah and their place of worship, and because it contains amazing signs, as He said:
3:97: 97 In it are clear signs such as the deviation of birds from parallel to the House throughout the ages, and that the predatory beasts mingle with the game in the sanctuary and do not interfere with it, and that every tyrant who intended evil against it, God Almighty subdued him like the owners of the elephant. The sentence explains the guidance, or another condition. The Station of Abraham is a deleted subject, the predicate of which is either the Station of Abraham, or a substitute for the signs, a substitute for some of the whole. It was said that it is an explanatory apposition to A, what is meant by the signs is the trace of the foot in the solid rock and its sinking into it up to the ankles, and its being singled out for this softness among the rocks and its preservation without the rest of the traces of the prophets and its preservation despite the multitude of its enemies for thousands of years. This is supported by the fact that it was read as a clear sign of monotheism. The reason for this trace is that when the building of the Kaaba was raised, he stood on this stone to be able to lift the stones, so his feet sank into it. And whoever enters it shall be safe is an introductory clause, or a conditional clause in meaning connected to a station because it means that whoever enters it is safe, i.e. whoever enters it is safe, or it contains clear signs, the station of Abraham and whoever enters it is safe. He limited himself to mentioning them from the many signs and omitted mentioning others, such as his saying, peace be upon him, "Three things have been made beloved to me from your world: perfume, women, and the comfort of my eyes in prayer" because in them there is no need for anything else in both worlds, the effect remains for all time and security from punishment on the Day of Resurrection. He, peace be upon him, said, Whoever dies in one of the two sanctuaries, will be raised on the Day of Resurrection safe. According to Abu Hanifa, whoever is required to be killed for apostasy or retaliation or other and takes refuge in the sanctuary is not addressed, but he is forced to leave. And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by the people with a kasra, which is the language of Najd. Whoever can afford it instead of people instead of some instead of all is specified for it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) explained the ability as the provisions and the mount and he supports the statement of Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him that it is money. Therefore, he made it obligatory to delegate time if he finds a wage for someone to delegate. Malik may God have mercy on him said that it is with the body, so it is obligatory for whoever is able to walk and earn money on the way. Abu Hanifa may God have mercy on him said that it is the sum of the two matters. The pronoun in to him is the House, or the Hajj, and everything that comes to something is its way. And whoever disbelieves, then indeed, God is independent of the worlds. He put disbelief in place of whoever does not perform Hajj to emphasize its obligation and to make it more severe for those who abandon it. Therefore, he, peace be upon him, said, Whoever dies without performing Hajj, let him die, if he wishes, as a Jew or a Christian. The matter of Hajj has been emphasized in this verse in many ways, in the form of a report, and its presentation in the nominal form and its presentation in a way that indicates that it is a right that is obligatory for God, the Most High, upon the necks of the people, and the generalization of the ruling first and then its specification second, as it is like a clarification after illusion and repetition and repetition of what is intended, and calling the abandonment of Hajj disbelief in that it is the action of the disbelievers, and the mention of independence, as in this place is one of those things that indicate hatred and abandonment, and his saying: from the worlds indicates it because of what it contains of exaggeration of generalization and indication of independence from it through proof and the feeling of the greatness of the wrath, because it is a difficult task that combines breaking the soul, tiring the body, spending money, detaching oneself from desires, and turning to God. It was narrated that when the beginning of the verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered the leaders of the religions and addressed them, saying, God Almighty has prescribed Hajj for you, so perform Hajj. One religion believed in it and five religions disbelieved in it. Then the verse was revealed: And whoever disbelieves.
3:98: 98 Say, 'O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God?' That is, in His auditory and rational verses that indicate the truthfulness of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he claims of the obligation of Hajj and other things. The specific address to the People of the Scripture is evidence that their disbelief is more hideous, because their knowledge of the verses is stronger and if they claim that they believe in the Torah and the Gospel, then they are disbelievers in them. And God is Witness over what you do. The fact is that He is a Witness who is aware of your deeds and will reward you for them. Distortion and secrecy will not benefit you.
3:99: 99 Say, 'O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of God those who believe?' The address and question were repeated to exaggerate the rebuke and deny their excuse, and to indicate that each of the two matters is ugly in itself and independently brings about punishment, and the way of God in His true religion that we are commanded to follow is Islam. It was said that they were tempting the believers and causing them to be incited between them until they came to the Aws and Khazraj and reminded them of the enmity and warfare between them in the pre-Islamic period so that they would return to the same and devise a plan to avert them from it. Seeking to make it crooked is a state of the waw, meaning seeking to make it crooked by confusing people and making them think that there is a deviation from the truth in it, by preventing abrogation and changing the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the like, or by causing incitement among the believers so that their word would differ and their religious matter would be disrupted.
