And you are witnesses It is the path of God the Most High, and turning away from it is misguidance and leading others astray, or you are just before the people of your religion, who trust your words and cite you as witnesses in cases. And God is not unaware of what you do is a warning to them, and since the evil in the first verse was their disbelief, which they openly declare, He concluded it by saying: And God is Witness over what you do. And since in this verse it was their turning the believers away from Islam, which they were hiding and scheming to do, He said: And God is not unaware of what you do.
3:100: 100 "O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back, after your belief, to disbelief. This was revealed about a group of Aws and Khazraj who were sitting and talking. Shas bin Qais the Jew passed by them and their friendship and gathering angered him, so he ordered a young Jew to sit with them and remind them of the Day of Bu'ath and recite to them some of what was said about it. The Aws were victorious that day, so he did so. The people argued and boasted and got angry and said, Weapons, weapons. A great number of people gathered with the two tribes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions turned to them and said, Do you abandon ignorance while I am among you after God has honored you with Islam and cut off from you the matter of ignorance and united your hearts? They realized that it was a temptation from Satan and a plot from their enemy, so they laid down their weapons and sought forgiveness and embraced each other and left with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace." God addressed them Himself after He commanded the Messenger to address the People of the Book, to demonstrate the greatness of their status and to make them feel that they are the most deserving of God addressing them and speaking to them.
3:101: 101 And how can you disbelieve while the verses of God are recited to you and among you is His Messenger? Denial and astonishment at their disbelief when they have all the reasons that call them to faith and turn them away from disbelief. And whoever holds fast to God and whoever clings to his religion or seeks refuge in Him in all his affairs. has certainly been guided to a straight path he has inevitably been guided.
3:102: 102 "O you who have believed, fear God as He should be feared." The fear of Him that He should be feared and what is required of it, which is to exhaust one's ability in performing one's duty and avoiding forbidden things, as He said: "So fear God as much as you are able." And on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him: It is to obey and not disobey, to thank and not be ungrateful, and to remember and not forget. And it was said: It is to keep obedience away from attention and from expecting reward for it. And in this matter there is an emphasis on the prohibition of obeying the People of the Book, and the origin of piety is waqiyyah, so its waw with a dammah was changed to a ta' as in taw'adah and takhamah and the ya' to an alif. "And do not die except as Muslims" meaning, do not be in a state other than the state of Islam if death overtakes you, for the prohibition of what is restricted by a state or other may be directed towards the action itself sometimes and the restriction at other times and it may be directed towards the group without them, and likewise the negation.
3:103: 103"And hold fast to the rope of God all together" in the religion of Islam, or in His Book, as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The Qur'an is the strong rope of God." He used the rope as a metaphor for it, as holding fast to it is a reason for salvation from ruin, just as holding fast to the rope is a reason for safety from ruin, trusting in it and relying on it is holding fast as a nomination for metaphor. "All together united upon it and do not be divided" meaning do not be divided from the truth by differences occurring among you like the People of the Book, or do not be divided as you were in the Age of Ignorance, fighting one another, or do not mention what necessitates division and removes familiarity. "And remember the favor of God upon you" which includes guidance and success to Islam, which leads to harmony and the removal of rancor. "When you were enemies" in the Age of Ignorance, fighting. "He brought your hearts together" through Islam. "And by His grace you became brothers" loving one another and united in brotherhood in God. It was said that the Aws and Khazraj were brothers, and enmity arose between their children and wars continued for one hundred and twenty years until God extinguished it with Islam and united them with His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. "And you were on the brink of a pit of fire" on the verge of falling into the fire of Hell because of your disbelief, for if death had overtaken you in that state, you would have fallen into the fire. "So He saved you from it" with Islam. The pronoun refers to the pit, or the fire, or the lip. Its feminine form is due to the feminine of what it is added to, or because it means the lip, for the lip of a well and its lip are its edge, like the side and the side, and its root is shafu, so the waw was changed to an alif in the masculine and deleted in the feminine. "Thus" is the clarification. "God makes clear to you His signs" His evidence. "That you may be guided" meaning your steadfastness in guidance and your increase in it.
3:104: 104 And let there be among you a group of people inviting to good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. "Min" is for partiality, because enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong are communal obligations, and because not everyone is qualified for it, as the one who undertakes it has conditions that are not shared by the entire nation, such as knowledge of the rulings, the levels of accountability, how to implement them, and the ability to carry them out. He addressed everyone and asked some of them to do something to indicate that it is obligatory on everyone, even if they left it outright, they would all be sinful, but it is dropped by the action of some of them, and so on with everything that is a communal obligation. Or for clarification, meaning, and be a group of people inviting, as God Almighty said: "You are the best nation produced for mankind. You enjoin what is right." And calling to good includes calling to what is good for religion or the world, and linking enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong to it is linking the specific to the general to indicate its virtue. "Those are the successful ones" who are distinguished by complete success. It was narrated that he, peace be upon him, "was asked who is the best of people, so he said: He who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong, and who fears God the most and maintains ties of kinship." Enjoining what is right is obligatory or recommended according to what is enjoined. Forbidding what is wrong is all obligatory because everything that is forbidden by the Shari'ah is forbidden. It is more apparent that the sinner must forbid what he is committing because he must abandon it and forbid it, so abandoning one does not cancel the obligation of the other.
3:105: 105 And do not be like those who divided and differed like the Jews and Christians who differed about monotheism, transcendence, and the conditions of the Hereafter, as you know. After the clear proofs had come to them the verses and arguments that clarify the truth and require agreement upon it. It is more apparent that the prohibition therein is specific to division in the fundamentals and not the branches, based on his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, The difference of opinion among my nation is a mercy and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, Whoever strives and is correct will have two rewards, and whoever errs will have one reward. "And for those is a great punishment" a warning to those who divided and a threat against imitating them.
3:106: 106 On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black is in the accusative case with the meaning of the verb for them, or with the implied mention. The whiteness of faces and its blackness are two metaphors for the appearance of the joy of happiness and the gloom of fear in it. It was said that the people of truth will be marked by the whiteness of faces and the record and the radiance of skin and the light running between His hands and His right hand, and the people of falsehood by the opposites of that. As for those whose faces will turn black, did you disbelieve after your belief? meaning that it will be said to them, Did you disbelieve? The hamza is for rebuke and astonishment at their state, and they are the apostates or the People of the Book who disbelieved in the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, after their belief in him before his mission, or all the disbelievers disbelieved after they acknowledged him when he made them witness against themselves or they were able to believe by looking at the evidence and verses. Then taste the punishment is an order of humiliation. For what you used to disbelieve because of your disbelief or as a punishment for your disbelief.
3:107: 107 And as for those whose faces will be white, they will be in the mercy of God meaning Paradise and eternal reward. He expressed this with mercy as a warning that even if the believer spends his life in obeying God the Most High, he will not enter Paradise except by His mercy and grace. The proper arrangement would have been to mention them first, but the intention was for the beginning and end of the speech to be about the adornment of the believers and their reward. They will abide therein eternally It was narrated as a resumption for emphasis, as if it was said: How will they be there? So he said: They will abide therein eternally.
3:108: 108These are the verses of God contained in His promise and threat. We recite them to you in truth mixed with the truth, with no doubt about them. And God does not desire injustice for the worlds since injustice is impossible for Him because nothing is due to Him, so He would be wronged by its deficiency, nor would He be prevented from anything, so He would be wronged by its action, because He is the absolute owner, as He said.
3:109: 109To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to God all matters will return. So He will reward each person according to what He has promised and threatened him with.
3:110: 110 "You were the best nation" indicates their goodness in the past and does not indicate a break that occurred, as in the Almighty's saying: "Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful." It was said that you were in the knowledge of God or in the Preserved Tablet, or among the previous nations. "Brought out to mankind" means made manifest to them. "You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong is a resumption that explains their being the best nation", or a second piece of report for you were. "And you believe in God" includes belief in everything that must be believed in, because belief in Him is only right and taken into account if belief in everything that one is commanded to believe in is obtained. He only delayed it and it is right to be presented because he intended by mentioning it to indicate that they enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong out of faith in God and belief in Him and manifesting His religion. This verse was used as evidence that consensus is a proof because it requires that they enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong, since the lam in both of them is for comprehensiveness, so if they agreed on falsehood, their matter would be contrary to that. And if the People of the Scripture had believed as they should have believed, it would have been better for them faith would have been better for them than what they are in. Among them are believers like Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions. But most of them are wicked rebellious in disbelief. This sentence and the one after it are mentioned by way of digression.
3:111: 111 They will not harm you except a slight harm" a slight harm such as stabbing and threatening. "And if they fight you, they will turn their backs" they will be defeated and will not harm you by killing or taking you captive. "Then they will not be aided" then there will be no one to aid them against you or repel your violence from them, negating their harm except what is by saying and he decided that if they rose to fight, their defeat would be upon them, then he informed that their end would be weakness and betrayal. And it was read "do not be aided in apposition to they turn on the basis that then" is for the slackness in the rank, so the lack of victory is restricted to fighting them, and this verse is one of the unseen things that agree with reality since that was the case of Qurayza, Nadir, Banu Qaynuqa' and the Jews of Khaybar.
3:112: 112 "Humiliation has been imposed upon them" the squandering of life, wealth and family, or the humiliation of clinging to falsehood and the jizya. "Wherever they are found they are found except by a rope from God and a rope from the people" an exception from the most general of the general conditions, meaning humiliation has been imposed upon them in most conditions except for those who hold fast, or are clothed in the protection of God or the writing that He gave them and the protection of the Muslims, or the religion of Islam and following the path of the believers. "And they incurred the wrath of God" they returned with it deserving it. "And poverty has been imposed upon them" so it surrounds them like a house that is stricken upon its people, and the Jews are mostly poor and needy. "That" is an indication of what was mentioned about the humiliation and poverty and the incurring of wrath. "Because they disbelieved in the signs of God and killed the prophets without right" because of their disbelief in the signs and their killing of the prophets. And the restriction without right, although it is so in reality, to indicate that it was not right according to their belief either. That meaning disbelief and killing. Because they disobeyed and were transgressing because of their disobedience and transgression of the limits of God, as insisting on minor sins leads to major sins and continuing in them leads to disbelief. It was said that its meaning is that the humiliation in this world and the response to wrath in the hereafter, as is explained by their disbelief and killing, is caused by their disobedience and transgression, since they are also addressed by the branches.
3:113: 113They are not equal in equality and the pronoun refers to the People of the Book. Among the People of the Book is a community standing is a resumption to explain the negation of equality, and the upright and just community is from I established the stick and it stood and they are those who submitted from them. They recite the verses of God during the hours of the night and they prostrate they recite the Qur'an in their night prayers. It was expressed by recitation during the hours of the night with prostration to be clearer and more eloquent in praise. It was said that what is meant is the Isha prayer because the People of the Book pray it, as it was narrated that "he, peace and blessings be upon him, delayed it and then went out and saw the people waiting for the prayer, so he said: As for there is no one among the people of religions who remembers God at this hour except you."
3:114: 114 They believe in God and the Last Day, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and hasten to good deeds. Other characteristics of a nation described with characteristics that were not found in the Jews, for they deviated from the truth, did not worship at night, were polytheists with God, were atheists in His attributes, described the Last Day in a manner other than its attribute, were lenient in seeking reward, and were slow to do good deeds. And those are among the righteous, meaning those described with these qualities, whose conditions are good with God and who deserve His pleasure and praise.
3:115: 115And whatever good they do, they will never be denied it so it will not be lost nor will its reward be diminished at all. This is called ungratefulness just as the fulfillment of the reward is called gratitude. It is transitive with two objects because it includes the meaning of deprivation. Hafs, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read And whatever good they do, they will never be denied it with a ya' and the rest read it with a ta'. And God is Knowing of the righteous as good report for them and a notification that piety is the beginning of goodness and good deeds, and that the winner with God is the one who has piety.
3:116: 116 Indeed, those who disbelieve - neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God of punishment, or of enrichment, so it is a source. And those are the companions of the Fire, its abiding companions. They will abide therein eternally.
3:117: 117 Like what they spend what the infidels spend as an act of worship, or to boast and gain fame, or the hypocrites out of hypocrisy or fear. In this worldly life like a wind in which there is a chill severe cold and it is common to use it for a cold wind like the chill, so it is originally a source of description or a description of the cold for exaggeration like saying a cold chill. It struck the crops of a people who wronged themselves by disbelief and sins and destroyed them as a punishment for them because destruction from anger is more severe, and what is meant is to liken what they spent in its loss to the crops of the infidels which the chill struck and uprooted it and left them no benefit in it in this world or the hereafter, and it is from the compound simile and Shalk did not care about giving the word of simile to the wind without the crops, and it is permissible to estimate it like a destroying wind which is the crops. And God did not wrong them, but they wrong themselves. That is, He did not wrong the spenders by wasting their expenses, but they wronged themselves by not spending them in a way that would be taken into account. Or He did not wrong the owners of the crops by destroying it, but they wronged themselves by committing what deserved punishment. And it was read but meaning, but they wrong themselves. And it is not permissible to estimate the pronoun of the matter because it is not deleted except in poetic necessity, as in His saying: You are not one of those whose hearts are filled with love, but whoever sees your eyelids falls in love.
3:118: 118 O you who have believed, do not take as intimates a friend A confidant, which is someone whom a man knows his secrets with confidence, it is likened to the lining of a garment as it is likened to a slogan. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The Ansar are a slogan and the people are a covering. "From without you from without the Muslims, and it is related to don't take", or to an omitted word which is a description of the confidant, meaning a confidant who is from without you. "They will spare no effort in corrupting you meaning they will not fall short in corrupting you, and alo" means falling short and its origin is to be transitive with a preposition and to two objects like their saying: I will not spare you advice to include the meaning of prevention or deficiency. "And they wish for what you have suffered they wish for your suffering, which is severe harm and hardship, and ma" is a source. "Hatred has already appeared from their mouths" meaning in their speech because they cannot control themselves due to their excessive hatred. "And what their hearts conceal is greater" than what appeared because in turn it is not from deliberation and choice. We have made clear to you the signs indicating the obligation of sincerity and loyalty to believers and hostility to disbelievers. If you understand what has been made clear to you. The four sentences came as resumptions of the explanation, and it is possible that the first three are attributes of the inner circle.
3:119: 119 "Here you are, you love them but they do not love you" meaning, you are the ones who are wrong in befriending the infidels and you love them but they do not love you, a statement of their mistake in befriending them, and it is a second piece of report or report for "them" and the sentence is report for you like you say: you are Zaid, you greet him, or its connection or a state and the agent in it has the meaning of indication, and it is permissible for "them" to be made accusative by an implied verb that is explained by what follows it and the sentence is report. "And you believe in the entire Book" in the genus of the entire Book, and it is a state of those who do not love you and the meaning is: they do not love you and the fact is that you believe in their book also so what is wrong with you that you love them and they do not believe in your book, and in it is a rebuke that they are more steadfast in their falsehood than you are in your right. "And when they meet you they say, We believe" hypocritically and deceitfully and when they are alone they bite their fingertips at you out of rage because of him, regretting and remorse since they did not find a way to take revenge. Say, ‘Die in your rage.’ This is a supplication against them for their rage to continue and increase by multiplying the power of Islam and its people until they are destroyed by it. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts. He knows what is in their breasts of hatred and resentment. This could be part of what is said, i.e., say to them that God is Knowing of what is more hidden than what you hide of biting your fingers in rage, or it could be outside of it, meaning, say that to them and do not be surprised that I have informed you of their secrets, for I am Knowing of what is more hidden than their inner selves.
3:120: 120 If good befalls you, it distresses them, but if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. A statement of the extent of their enmity to the point that they envy the good and benefit that befell them, and rejoice at the harm and hardship that befell them. And if you are patient in their enmity, or in the hardships of the obligations. And fear their friendship, or what God, the Almighty, has forbidden you. Their plot will not harm you at all by the grace of God, the Almighty, and His promised protection for the patient and the God-fearing. And because the glory in the matter, trained in fear and patience, is less agitated in order to run after the opponent, and the dammah of the ra' is for following like the dammah of the maddah. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu Amr, and Ya'qub read will not harm you from dararahu yadhiruhu. Indeed, God is encompassing of what they do of patience, fear of God, and other things. Encompassing meaning His knowledge encompasses, so He will reward you for what you are worthy of. It was read with the letter ya meaning of what they do in your enmity, He is All-Knowing and will punish them for it.
3:121: 121 And when you went forth in the morning meaning, remember when you went forth. From your family meaning from the room of Aisha, may God be pleased with her. A place for the believers means to settle them. Or to level and prepare for them. This is supported by the reading with the letter lam. Seats for fighting means stations and places for it. Seat and station may be used to mean place in the broad sense, as in the Almighty's saying: In a seat of truth and His saying: Before you rise from your place. "And God is Hearing" of your words. "Aleem" your intentions It was narrated that the polytheists descended on Uhud on Wednesday - the twelfth of Shawwal in the third year of the Hijra - so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted his companions, and he had called Abdullah bin Ubay bin Salul and had not called him before, so he and most of the Ansar said: Stay, O Messenger of God, in Medina and do not go out to them, for by God, we have not gone out from it to an enemy except that he has killed some of us, and he has not entered it upon us except that we have killed some of them, so how is it while you are among us? So leave them, for if they stay, they will stay in a prison, and if they enter, the men will fight them and the women and children will throw stones at them, and if they return, they will return disappointed. Some of them indicated to go out, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw in my dream a slaughtered cow around me, so I interpreted it as good, and I saw a dent in the fly of my sword, so I interpreted it as defeat, and I saw as if I put my hand in a strong shield, so I interpreted it as Medina, so if you see that you should stay in Medina and leave them, then the men said They missed Badr and God honored them with martyrdom on the day of Uhud. Let us go out to our enemies. They exaggerated until he entered and put on his cloak. When they saw that, they regretted their exaggeration and said, Do, O Messenger of God, what you saw. He said, It is not appropriate for a prophet to put on his cloak and then put it down until he fights. So he went out after the Friday prayer and became at the valley of Uhud on Saturday. He camped in the valley and turned his back and his army to Uhud and straightened their ranks. He put Abdullah ibn Jubayr in charge of the archers and said, Sprinkle arrows away from us so that they do not come to us from behind.
3:122: 122 When you intended is related to his saying: All-Hearing, All-Knowing or in place of When you went forth. "Two parties from among you" Banu Salamah from the Khazraj, and Banu Haritha from the Aws, were the two wings of the army. "That you should fail" means that you should become cowardly and weak. It was narrated that "he, peace and blessings be upon him, went out with about a thousand men and promised them victory if they were patient. When they reached the shore, Ibn Abi was defeated with three hundred men and said: Why should we kill ourselves and our children? Amr Ibn Hazm Al-Ansari followed them and said: I call upon you by God and Islam in your Prophet and yourselves. Ibn Abi said: If we knew of fighting, we would have followed you. The two tribes intended to follow him, but God protected them and they went with the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him." It appears that it was not a determination, as God Almighty said: And God is their Guardian, meaning He protected them from following that step. It is also possible that it means God is their Supporter, so why should they fail and not put their trust in God? And in God let the believers put their trust, meaning let them put their trust in Him and not put their trust in anyone else so that He may support them as He supported them at Badr.
3:123: 123And God had already helped you at Badr is a reminder of some of the benefits of trust. Badr is a body of water between Mecca and Medina that belonged to a man called Badr, so it was named after him. And you were weak is a state of the pronoun. He said weak and did not say weak to draw attention to their small number despite their weakness due to the weakness of their situation and the scarcity of mounts and weapons. So fear God in steadfastness. That you may be grateful by your fear of what He has bestowed upon you of His victory, or perhaps you may be grateful for God's blessings upon you. So He put gratitude in place of blessing because it is its cause.
3:124: 124When you said to the believers is an adverb for your victory. It was said that it is a second substitute for when you went forth on the basis that their saying to them on the day of Uhud was with the condition of patience and piety from disobedience, so when they were not patient about the spoils and disobeyed the command of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, the angels did not descend. Will it not suffice you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down denying that it was not enough for them, but rather lan was brought to indicate that they were like those who had despaired of victory due to their weakness and fewness and the strength and large numbers of the enemy. It was said that God reinforced them on the day of Badr first with a thousand angels, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand. Ibn Amir read sent down with emphasis for multiplication or gradualness.
3:125: 125Yes is an affirmation for what comes after no, meaning yes is enough for you. Then He promised them more patience and piety, urging them on and strengthening their hearts, saying: If you are patient and fear God and they come to you meaning the polytheists. All at once from this hour, and it is originally a source from the word farat al-qadr meaning it boiled, so it was used metaphorically for speed and then used for a state in which there is no hesitation or delay, and the meaning is that they will come to you immediately. Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels in the case of their coming without delay or delay. Marked is marked from tasweem which is showing the mark of something, based on the Prophet's saying, peace and blessings be upon him, to his companions: Mark, for the angels have marked. Or sent from tasweem meaning the name. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Asim, and Ya'qub read it with a kasra on the waw.
3:126: 126 And God has not made it and He has not made your support with angels. except as good tidings for you except as good tidings for you of victory. And that your hearts may be reassured thereby and that they may find peace in it from fear. And victory is only from God not from equipment and numbers, and it is a warning that there is no need for support in their victory, but rather He has provided them with support and promised it to them as a sign to them and a binding on their hearts, since the general public looks more to the causes and urges them not to care about what is delayed from them. The Mighty who cannot be overcome in His decrees. The Wise who supports and lets down with or without a middle ground according to wisdom and interest.
3:127: 127 To cut off a portion of those who disbelieved is related to your victory, or And what is victory if the lam in it is for the covenant, and the meaning is to reduce them by killing some and taking others captive, which is what happened on the day of Badr when seventy of their leaders were killed and seventy were taken captive. Or to suppress them or to disgrace them, and suppression is intense anger, or a weakness that occurs in the heart, and the or is for variation without hesitation so they turn back disappointed so they are defeated with no hope.
3:128: 128You have no part in the matter is an objection. Or He turns to them in mercy or punishes them is in apposition to His statement or suppresses them, and the meaning is that God is the Master of their matter, so He will either destroy them or suppress them or turn to them in mercy if they submit or punish them if they persist, and you have no part in their matter, but you are a slave commanded to warn them and fight them. It is possible that it is in apposition to the command or something with the implied that, meaning you have no part in their matter or turn to them in mercy or punish them. Or you have no part in their matter, or turn to them in mercy or punish them. And that or means except that. Meaning you have no part in their matter unless God turns to them in mercy and you are happy with it or punishes them and you are healed from them. It was narrated that Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas wounded him on the day of Uhud and broke his front tooth, so he began wiping the blood from his face and saying, How can a people succeed who have stained the face of their Prophet with blood?" So it was revealed. It was said that they were to invoke curses upon them, but God forbade them because He knew that among them were those who would believe. For they are wrongdoers, and they deserved to be punished for their wrongdoing.
3:129: 129 And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth in creation and dominion, so His is the command, not yours. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills is explicit in denying the necessity of punishment, and the restriction to repentance or not is like the opposite of it. And God is Forgiving and Merciful to His servants, so do not rush to pray against them.
3:130: 130 O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied. Do not increase it repeatedly, and perhaps the specification is according to reality. A man among them used to increase it for a term, then he would add another increase to it until the small amount consumed the debtor's money. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Yaqub read doubled. "And fear God" in what I have forbidden you from. "That you may succeed" hoping for success.
3:132: 132 And obey God and the Messenger that you may receive mercy. He followed the threat with the promise, intimidating against disobedience and encouraging obedience. Perhaps and perhaps in such cases there is evidence of the difficulty of attaining what was made report for.
3:133: 133And hasten they hastened and came. To forgiveness from your Lord to that which deserves forgiveness, such as Islam, repentance, and sincerity. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read hasten without the waw. And a Paradise as wide as the heavens and the earth meaning its width is like their width, and the width is mentioned to exaggerate its description of spaciousness in the manner of metaphor, because it is less than length. And according to Ibn 'Abbas, like seven heavens and seven earths if some of them were connected to others, prepared for the righteous it was prepared for them, and in it is evidence that Paradise was created and that it is outside this world.
3:134: 134 "Those who spend" is a praiseworthy description of the righteous, or praise in the accusative or nominative. "In prosperity and adversity in both states of ease and hardship, or in all circumstances, since man is never without pleasure or harm, meaning they are never without spending what they are able to, whether little or much, and those who restrain anger" are those who hold it back and are sufficient to carry it out even though they are able, from the verb kazmat al-qarya, which means to fill it and strengthen its head. And from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "Whoever restrains anger when he is able to save it, God will fill his heart with security and faith. And those who pardon people" are those who leave the punishment of those who deserve to be held accountable. And from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "These are few in my nation except for those whom God protects" and they were many in the nations that came before. "And God loves the doers of good" is possible and includes these, and the covenant, so the reference is to them.
3:135: 135 And those who, when they commit an immorality an extremely ugly act such as adultery. or wrong themselves by committing any sin, and it has been said that the immorality is a major sin and the wrong of the self is a minor one, and perhaps the immorality is what is transitive and the wrong of the self is not like that. remember God remember His threat or His judgment or His great right. and seek forgiveness for their sins by regretting and repenting. And who forgives sins except God is an interrogative with the meaning of negation inserted between the two conjoined words, and what is meant by it is describing Him, the Most High, with the breadth of mercy and the generality of forgiveness and urging seeking forgiveness and promising to accept repentance. and did not persist in what they did and did not persist in their sins without seeking forgiveness, according to the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, He who seeks forgiveness will not persist, even if he returns to it seventy times a day. "And they know" is the state of those who persist, meaning they did not persist in the uglyness of their action, knowing it.
3:136: 136 Those - their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. This is report for those if you begin with it, and a renewed sentence explaining what came before it if you connect it to the righteous, or to those who spend. It is not necessary that Paradise is prepared for the righteous and the repentant as a reward for them that those who persist will not enter it, just as it is not necessary that Hell is prepared for the disbelievers as a reward for them that no one else will enter it. The indefiniteness of the word gardens in the first place indicates that what they are is less than what the righteous are described with those qualities mentioned in the previous verse. It is sufficient for you to distinguish between the two groups that He separated their verse by stating that they are doers of good and deserving of God’s love, because they preserved the limits of the Shari’ah and went beyond to specialize in His good deeds. He separated the verse for these people by saying: And excellent is the reward of the workers, because the one who makes up for his shortcomings is like the one who works to obtain some of what he missed. How great is the difference between the doer of good and the one who makes up for it, the beloved and the hired worker. Perhaps the replacement of the word reward with reward is for this reason, and what is specifically praised is omitted, its meaning is and excellent is the reward of the workers, meaning forgiveness and the gardens.
3:137: 137There have already been precedents before you events that God Almighty established for the nations that denied, such as His Almighty saying, "And they were killed with a terrible killing. The precedent of God for those who passed on before." And it was said that nations said: People have not witnessed a virtue like yours, nor have they seen anything like it in the past. So travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied so that you may take heed from what you see of the effects of their destruction.
3:138: 138 This is a statement for the people and a guidance and an admonition for the righteous. This is a reference to his saying, It has already passed away, or the meaning of his saying, So look, meaning that while it is a statement for the deniers, it is an increase in insight into the admonition for the righteous, or to what was summarized regarding the matter of the righteous and the repentant, and his saying, It has already passed away is an interjectional clause to urge faith and repentance, and it was said to refer to the Qur'an.
3:139: 139 And do not weaken and do not grieve is a consolation for them for what happened to them on the day of Uhud, and the meaning is do not weaken in jihad because of what happened to you and do not grieve for those among you who were killed. And you are the superior and your situation is that you are higher than them in status, because you are on the truth and your fighting is for God and your dead are in Paradise, and they are on falsehood and their fighting is for Satan and their dead are in Hell, or because you killed more of them on the day of Badr than they killed of you today, or you are the superior in the end, so it is good report for them of victory and triumph. If you are believers is related to the prohibition, meaning do not weaken if your faith is sound, because it requires the strength of the heart by trusting in God or in those who are superior.
3:140: 140 If a wound should touch you, a wound similar to it has already touched the people. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Ibn Ayyash read it on the authority of Asim with a damma on the qaf, and the rest with a fatha. They are two dialects like weakness and weakness. It was said that with a fatha it means wounds and with a damma it means their pain. The meaning is that if they afflicted you on the day of Uhud, you afflicted them on the day of Badr like it. Then they did not weaken or become cowardly, so you are more deserving of not being weakened, for you hope from God what they do not hope for. It was said that both of the two attacks were on the day of Uhud, because the Muslims had taken revenge on them before they disobeyed the command of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And these days We alternate among the people We distribute them among them as an indication for these sometimes and for those at other times, like His saying: One day against us, one day for us, one day for women, one day for eagles And deliberation is like repetition. It is said, I deliberated something among them, so they traded it. Days can be described as descriptions or report, and we alternated it can be report or condition. What is meant by it is times of victory and triumph. And that God may know those who believe is in apposition to an omitted reason, meaning, We alternated it so that it would be such and such, and And that God may know as an indication that the reason for it is not one, and that what befalls the believer in it is what he does not know, or the verb that is explained by it is omitted, meaning, And that those who are steadfast in faith may be distinguished from those who are on the edge of our action. The purpose in its likes and opposites is not to prove or deny His knowledge, but rather to prove or deny what is known by way of proof. It was said that its meaning is to teach them knowledge to which the reward is related, which is knowledge of the existing thing. And He takes from among you witnesses, and He honors some of you with martyrdom, meaning the martyrs of Uhud, or He takes from among you witnesses who are just because of what they have encountered of steadfastness and righteousness in hardships. And God does not love the wrongdoers who conceal something other than what they show, or the disbelievers, which is an objection, and it contains a warning that God Almighty does not support the disbelievers in truth, but rather He sometimes defeats them to lure them in and test the believers.
3:141: 141 And that God may purify those who believe to cleanse them and purify them from sins if the state is against them. And destroy the disbelievers and destroy them if it is against them. And the destruction is the reduction of something little by little.
3:142: 142 Or do you think that you will enter Paradise? Rather, you thought, and its meaning is denial. And God has not yet made known those among you who strive and when you strive, and in it is evidence that jihad is a communal obligation, and the difference between when and when is that it expects the action in the future. He knows was read with the opening of the mim on the basis that its original form is ya'alumun, so the nun was deleted. And He knows the patient was in the accusative case with the omission of an on the basis that the waw is for the plural. It was read with the nominative case on the basis that the waw is for the state, as if he said: And when you strive and you are patient.
3:143: 143 And you were wishing for death meaning war, for it is one of the causes of death, or death by martyrdom. The address is to those who did not witness Badr and wished to witness with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they might attain the honor that the martyrs of Badr attained, so they insisted on going out on the day of Uhud. Before you met him before you witnessed him and knew his severity. You saw him while you were looking meaning you saw him witnessing him when those of your brothers were killed before you, and it is a rebuke to them for wishing for war and causing it, then they were cowards and fled from it, or for wishing for martyrdom, for wishing for it is wishing for the victory of the infidels.
3:144: 144 And Muhammad is no more than a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. So they will pass away just as they passed away by death or murder. Then if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Denying their apostasy and turning back on their heels from the religion because of his passing away by death or murder after their knowledge of the passing away of the messengers before him and the continuation of their religion by adhering to it. It was said that the fa' is for causality and the hamza is to deny that they would make the passing away of the messengers before him a reason for their turning back on their heels after his death. It was narrated that when Abdullah bin Qami’ah Al-Harithi threw a stone at the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), breaking his front tooth and splitting his face, Mus’ab bin Umair may God be pleased with him defended him, and he was the standard-bearer, until Ibn Qami’ah killed him, and he thought that he had killed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he said: I have killed Muhammad, and a cryer cried out: Muhammad has been killed. So the people retreated and the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) began calling the servants of God to me, so thirty of his companions rallied to him and protected him until they drove the polytheists away from him, and the rest dispersed, and some of them said: I wish Ibn Abi would take a guarantee for us from Abu Sufyan. And some of the hypocrites said: If he had been a prophet, he would not have been killed. Return to your brothers and your religion. Anas bin An-Nadr, the uncle of Anas bin Malik may God be pleased with them both, said: O people, if Muhammad is killed, then the Lord of Muhammad is alive and will not die, and what will you do with life after him? So fight for what he fought for. Then he said: O God, I apologize to You for what they say and I disavow him before You, and he grabbed his sword and fought until he was killed. So it was revealed. And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm God at all by his apostasy, but rather he will harm himself. And God will reward the grateful for the blessing of Islam by remaining steadfast in it, like Anas and his ilk.
3:145: 145 And no soul can die except by God's permission except by the will of God Almighty or by His permission to the Angel of Death, peace and blessings be upon him, to take his soul, and the meaning is that every soul has a specified term in His knowledge and judgment. They will not delay an hour nor will they advance it by refraining from fighting or rushing forward. In it is an incitement and encouragement to fight, and a promise to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, of preservation and delaying the term. A book is a confirmed source, as the meaning is that death was written in a book. Deferred is an attribute of it, meaning temporary, not advanced or delayed. And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof is an allusion to those who were preoccupied with the spoils on the day of Uhud, as the Muslims attacked the polytheists and defeated them and began to plunder, so when the archers saw that, they turned to plunder and left their place, so the polytheists took advantage and attacked them from behind them and defeated them. And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof meaning from its reward. And We will reward the grateful those who were grateful for God’s blessings and nothing distracted them from jihad.
3:146: 146 And how many originally, the letter kaf was added to it and it became the meaning of how much and the nun is a tanween that is fixed in writing in a way that is not analogous. Ibn Kathir read and how many as ka'an and the reason for that is changing the change of the single word like their saying wa'amli in la'amri, so it became ka'in then the second ya' was deleted for the sake of alleviation then the other ya' was replaced with an alif as was replaced from ta'i from a prophet to clarify it. Many rabbiyoon fought with him rabbiyoon are knowledgeable, pious, or worshippers of their Lord. It was said groups and the rabbiyoon is attributed to the rabbah which is the group for emphasis. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu Amr and Ya'qub read killed and its attribution to rabbiyoon or the pronoun of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and with him rabbiyoon is a state of it and the first is supported by the fact that it was read with emphasis and rabbiyoon was read with fatha as is the original and with damma which is one of the changes in attribution like kasra. They did not lose heart for what befell them in the cause of God. They did not slacken nor did their resolve break when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or some of them were killed. They did not weaken against the enemy or in religion. They did not submit nor did they yield to the enemy. Its root is istakana from sukoon because the submissive person is still with his companion so that he can do with him what he wants. The alif is from the full fatha or istakana from kawn because he asks himself to be for the one who submits to him. This is a definition of what befell them when the rumors spread of his killing, may God bless him and grant him peace. And God loves the patient so He grants them victory and magnifies their status.
3:147: 147 And their only statement was that they said, 'Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our transgression in our affair and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.' That is, their only statement, despite their steadfastness and strength in religion and their being rabbis, was this statement, which was attributing the sins and transgression to themselves in order to belittle them and attributing what had befallen them to their evil deeds and seeking forgiveness for them, then seeking steadfastness in the places of war and victory over the enemy in order to be out of submission and purity, so that it would be closer to being answered. And their statement was made good because what they said is more well-known, indicating the aspect of the relation and the time of the event.
3:148: 148 "So God gave them the reward of this world and the best reward of the Hereafter. And God loves the doers of good." So God gave them, because of their seeking forgiveness and turning to God, victory, spoils, honor, and good reputation in this world, and Paradise and bliss in the Hereafter. He made its reward special with good, indicating its grace and that it is the one that is taken into account by God.
3:149: 149 "O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back" that is, to disbelief. "on your heels, and you will turn back as losers." It was revealed regarding the words of the hypocrites to the believers when they were defeated: Return to your religion and your brothers. If Muhammad had been a prophet, he would not have been killed. It was also said that you should submit to Abu Sufyan and his followers and seek their protection, so that they will return you to their religion. It was also said that it is general regarding obeying the disbelievers and submitting to their rule, as it leads to agreeing with them.
3:150: 150"Rather, God is your protector" Your helper. It was read in the accusative case, meaning, "Rather, obey God, your protector. And He is the best of helpers. So, they were satisfied with Him, without the guardianship and support of anyone else.
3:151: 151 We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve meaning what was cast into their hearts of fear on the day of Uhud until they stopped fighting and returned without a reason, and Abu Sufyan called out, O Muhammad, our meeting is the next Badr season if you wish, so he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: God willing. And it was said that when they returned and were on some of the way, they regretted it and resolved to return to them to eradicate them, so God cast terror into their hearts. Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read with the dammah according to the original in the entire Qur'an, because they associated partners with God because of their associating partners with Him. For which He has not sent down any authority meaning gods for whom there is no proof for their associating partners with Him and for which He has not sent down any authority, and it is like His saying: You don't see the lizard flourishing in it The root of sultanate is power, from which comes the word sultanate, meaning the force of its ignition, and salaat, meaning the sharpness of the tongue. And their abode is the Fire, and wretched is the abode of the wrongdoers. That is, their abode, so the apparent was placed in place of the implicit for emphasis and explanation.
3:152: 152 And God has fulfilled His promise to you meaning, He promised you victory on condition of piety and patience, and this was the case until the archers disagreed. When the polytheists approached, the archers began to shoot arrows at them, while the rest struck them with swords until they were defeated and the Muslims were on their heels. When you were killing them by His permission you were killing them, from His sense if he invalidated his sense. Until when you were weak you became cowardly and your opinion weakened, or you turned to the spoils, for greed is from weakness of mind. And you disputed about the matter means the archers differed when the polytheists were defeated. Some of them said, What is our position here? Others said, We will not disobey the command of the Messenger. So their leader remained in his place with a group of less than ten, and the rest went out to plunder, which is what is meant by His statement, And you disobeyed after He had shown you what you love of victory and spoils and the defeat of the enemy. The answer to if is omitted, which is He tested you. Among you are those who desire this world and they are those who leave the center for the spoils. And among you are those who desire the Hereafter and they are those who are steadfast in preserving the command of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He turned you away from them then He restrained you from them until the situation changed and they overcame you. To test you for the calamities and to test your steadfastness in faith at that time. And He has pardoned you out of favor and because He knows of your regret for disobeying. And God is full of bounty to the believers He favors them with pardon, or in all circumstances, whether He has given them or against them, since testing is also mercy.
3:153: 153 When you ascend is related to your diversion, or to test you, or to something that is estimated, such as remember. Ascension means going and being far away on earth. It is said: We ascended in Mecca and Medina. And do not look back on anyone No one stops for anyone nor waits for him. And the Messenger calls you He used to say to me, servants of God, I am the Messenger of God, whoever returns will have Paradise. In your rear In your rear or in your other group. So He rewarded you with grief for grief In apposition to your diversion, and the meaning is So God rewarded you for your failure and disobedience with grief connected to grief, from grief over killing and wounding and the victory of the polytheists and the rumor of killing the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or So He rewarded you with grief because of the grief you made the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taste by your disobedience to him. So that you may not grieve for what has escaped you or what has befallen you so that you may practice patience in times of hardship, so that you may not grieve later for a lost benefit or a subsequent harm. It was said that la is an additional word, and the meaning is so that you may regret what you have missed of victory and booty, and what you have suffered of injury and defeat as a punishment for you. It was said that the pronoun in atabakum refers to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that he consoled you in your grief, so he was grieved by what was revealed to you, just as you were grieved by what was revealed to him, and he did not stir up trouble in you for your disobedience, as a consolation for you, so that you may not grieve for what you have missed of victory or for what you have suffered of defeat. And God is Acquainted with what you do He is All-Knowing of your actions and what you intended by them.
3:154: 154 Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security, drowsiness. God sent down upon you security until drowsiness overcame you. Abu Talha said: Drowsiness overcame us in the ranks until the sword would fall from the hand of one of us and he would grab it, then it would fall and he would grab it. Security is security in the accusative case as the object and drowsiness is a substitute for it or it is the object, and security is a state of it that comes before it or an object for it or a state of those addressed in the sense of those with security or that it is a plural of secure, great and righteous. Security was read with a sukoon on the meem as if it were the time in the command overwhelms a group of you meaning drowsiness. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with a ta' in response to security. The group are the true believers. A group are the hypocrites. Their souls have worried them their souls have caused them to fall into worries, or what concerns them is nothing but themselves and seeking their deliverance. They think about God other than the truth, the thought of the Age of Ignorance is another description of a group or state or a resumption of the explanation of what came before it, and other than the truth is in the accusative case as a source, meaning: they think about God other than the true thought that is right to think about Him, and the thought of the Age of Ignorance is its substitute, and it is the thought specific to the Age of Ignorance religion and its people. They say meaning to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is a substitute for they think. Do we have any part in the matter? Do we have any share in what God has commanded and promised of victory and triumph? It was said: Ibn Abi was informed of the killing of Banu Khazraj and he said that, and the meaning is that we were prevented from managing and disposing of ourselves by our own choice, so nothing of the matter remains for us, or will this oppression be removed from us so that we will have any part of the matter? "Say: The matter is entirely God's" meaning the true victory is for God the Most High and for His friends, for the party of God are the victorious, or the judgment is His, so He does what He wills and rules as He wills, and it is an objection. Abu Amr and Yaqub read it all in the nominative case as the beginning. They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you is a state of the pronoun they say, meaning they say, showing that they are seeking guidance and seeking victory, nullifying denial and lie. They say meaning within themselves and when some of them are alone with others, and it is a substitute for they conceal or a resumption of the explanation of it. If we had any part in the matter as Muhammad promised or claimed that the matter is entirely for God and His friends, or if we had choice and planning and did not leave as Ibn Abi and others did. We would not have been killed here we would not have been defeated, or those of us who were killed in this battle would not have been killed. Say, 'If you had been in your houses, those upon whom killing was decreed would have gone forth to their places of death' meaning those upon whom killing was decreed by God and which He wrote in the Preserved Tablet would have gone forth to their places of death, and staying in the city would not have benefited them, and none of them would have escaped, for He has decreed and managed all matters in His previous judgment, and there is no objection to His judgment. And that God may test what is in your hearts and to examine what is in your hearts and reveal their secrets of sincerity and hypocrisy. This is the reason for an omitted verb, meaning, And He did that to test or in apposition to an omitted verb, meaning, to reveal the fulfillment of the decree or for many interests and for the test, or so that you will not grieve. “And that He may purify what is in your hearts” and to reveal it and distinguish it or rid it of whispers. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts of their secrets, rarely revealing them. It contains a promise and a threat and a warning that He does not need to test, and He only did that to train the believers and reveal the state of the hypocrites.
3:155: 155 Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met, Satan caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. That is, the reason for those who were defeated on the day of Uhud was that Satan asked them to slip, so they obeyed him and committed sins to deceive the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, by abandoning their position and being greedy for the spoils or life, so they prevented support and strength of heart. It was said that Satan caused them to turn back because of sins they had committed, for sins lead to one another, just like obedience. It was also said that he caused them to slip because of the mention of past sins they had committed, so they hated to fight before sincerely repenting and leaving the injustice. And God has pardoned them because of their repentance and apology. Indeed, God is Forgiving of sins, Forbearing, He does not hasten to punish sins so that people may repent.
3:156: 156 O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved meaning the hypocrites. And they said to their brothers for their sake and in them, and the meaning of their brothers is their agreement in lineage or doctrine when they traveled in the land if they traveled in it and went far for trade or other, and it was right because of his saying they said, but it came as a narration of the past situation or they were a raid plural of raid is ka'a and af. If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed the verbal noun of said indicates that their brothers were not addressed by it. That God may make that a regret in their hearts is related to they said on the basis that the lam is the lam of consequence like it in that he may be an enemy and a grief for them, or do not be, meaning do not be like them in uttering that saying and belief in order to make it a regret in their hearts in particular, so that is an indication of what their saying indicates of belief. It was said that it refers to what the prohibition indicates, i.e. do not be like them, so that God may make the fact that you are not like them a regret in their hearts, for opposing and contradicting them is what saddens them. And God gives life and causes death is a response to their statement, i.e. He is the one who influences life and death, not residence and travel, for He, the Most High, may give life to the traveler and the fighter and cause death to the resident and the seated. And God is Seeing of what you do is a threat to the believers that they should be like them. Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read it with the letter ya as a warning to those who disbelieved.
3:157: 157 And if you are killed in the way of God or die meaning if you die in His way. Nafi', Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read with a kasra on the meem from mata yamāt. For forgiveness from God and mercy are better than what they accumulate. The answer to the oath, which is the same as the reward. The meaning is: Travel and conquest are not among the things that bring death and advance the appointed time. If that happens in the way of God, then what you attain of forgiveness and mercy through death is better than what you accumulate of the world and its benefits, even if you do not die. Hafs read with a ya'.
3:158: 158 And if you die or are killed meaning in whatever way you perish, to God you will be gathered to your deity to whom you turned and sacrificed your souls for His sake and not for anyone else. You will inevitably be gathered, and He will pay your recompense and magnify your reward. Nafi', Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read mutam with a kasra.
3:159: 159 "So by mercy from God, you were gentle with them meaning, by mercy, and ma" is an additional emphasis, warning and indication that his gentleness with them was only by mercy from God, which is to control his temper and enable him to be gentle with them until he was saddened by them after they disobeyed him. "And if you had been rude" ill-tempered and harsh. "Harsh in heart" harsh. "They would have dispersed from around you" they would have dispersed from you and would not have been at ease with you. "So pardon them" in what pertains to you. "And ask forgiveness for them" in what belongs to God. "And consult them in the matter" meaning in the matter of war, since the discussion is about it, or in what it is appropriate to consult in, seeking their opinion and comforting their souls and preparing for the tradition of consultation in the nation. "So when you have decided" if you have settled your soul on something after consultation. "Then rely upon God" in carrying out your matter according to what is best for you, because no one knows it except Him. It was read as if you resolve to speak, meaning if I resolve something for you and specify it for you, then put your trust in God and do not consult anyone about it. Indeed, God loves those who trust so He will support them and guide them to righteousness.
3:160: 160 If God helps you as He helped you on the day of Badr. No one can overcome you so no one can overcome you. But if He forsakes you as He forsook you on the day of Uhud. Who is there that can help you after Him? after His forsake, or after God, meaning if you go beyond Him, then you will have no helper. This is a warning of what is required for trust and an incitement to do what deserves help from God and a warning against what brings about His forsake. And upon God let the believers put their trust so let them put their trust in Him specifically because they know that they have no helper but Him and believe in Him.
3:161: 161 And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war It is not authentic for a prophet to betray in the spoils of war, for prophethood contradicts betrayal. It is said that he took something from the spoils of war, he took it secretly, and what is meant by it is either the innocence of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from what he was accused of, as it was narrated that a red velvet was lost on the day of Badr, so some of the hypocrites said that perhaps the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had taken it, or the archers thought so on the day of Uhud when they left the position for the spoils and said, "We fear that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, will say, 'Whoever takes something, it belongs to him,' and he will not divide the spoils of war." Or the exaggeration in the prohibition to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, based on what was narrated that he sent out scouts, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the spoils and divided them among those with him, but he did not divide them among the scouts, so this was revealed. So calling the deprivation of some of those who deserved it theft is a second exaggeration and severity. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah and Ya'qub read an yaghl in the passive voice, and the meaning is: It is not right for him to be found as a thief or to be attributed to ghulul. And whoever commits ghulul will bring what he has thwarted on the Day of Resurrection he will bring what he has thwarted, carrying it on his neck as mentioned in the hadith, or what he has borne of its burden and sin. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned meaning it will be given the full recompense for what it has earned. It would have been more appropriate for what came before it to say Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, but the ruling was generalized to be like proof of the intended meaning and to exaggerate it, because if every earner is rewarded for his work, then the thief, despite the enormity of his crime, is more deserving of that. And they will not be wronged so the reward of their obedient ones will not be diminished nor will the punishment of their disobedient ones be increased.
3:162: 162 Is he who pursues the pleasure of God through obedience like he who returns "with wrath from God because of sins and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination" The difference between it and the reference is that the destination must be different from the first case, but the reference is not like that.
3:163: 163They are of degrees with God. They were likened to degrees because of the difference between them in reward and punishment, or they have degrees. And God is Seeing of what they do. He knows their deeds and their degrees are issued by them, so He rewards them according to them.
3:164: 164 God has conferred a great favor upon the believers" He bestowed a great favor upon those who believed with the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from his people, and He singled them out, although the blessing of the mission was general, in order to increase their benefit from it. "God has conferred a great favor" was read as the predicate of a deleted subject, such as from him or he sent him. "When He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves" from their lineage, or from their race, an Arab like them, so that they would understand his words easily and be aware of his state of truthfulness and honesty, proud of him. It was read from "theirselves", meaning from the most noble of them, because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was from the most noble of the tribes and clans of the Arabs. "Recites to them His verses" meaning the Qur'an after they were ignorant and had not heard the revelation. "And purifies them" purifies them from the filth of character and bad beliefs and deeds. "And teaches them the Book and wisdom" meaning the Qur'an and the Sunnah. And they were before in clear error. “In” is the lightened form of the heavy one, and lam is the distinguishing factor. The meaning is that they were before the mission of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in clear error.
3:165: 165 Or when a disaster struck you, although you had suffered twice as much, you said, 'How is this? ' The hamza is for rebuke and confirmation, and the waw is a conjunction for the sentence on what came before in the story of Uhud or on something omitted, such as you did such and such and you said, and when is its adverb added to what struck you, meaning you said when a disaster struck you, which was the killing of seventy of you on the day of Uhud, and the situation is that you received double on the day of Badr from the killing of seventy and the capture of seventy. How did this strike us when God promised us victory? "Say, 'It is from yourselves. '" That is, from what yourselves committed of disobeying the order by abandoning the position, for the promise was conditional upon steadfastness and obedience, or choosing to leave the city. And from Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding your choosing the ransom on the day of Badr. Indeed, God is over all things competent. He is able to give victory and prevent it, and to strike you and strike from you.
3:166: 166And what befell you on the day the two armies met the armies of Muslims and the armies of polytheists, meaning the Day of Uhud. was by permission of God so it will happen by His decree or His release of the infidels. He called it permission because it is one of its requirements. And that He might make evident the believers.
3:167: 167And that those who are hypocrites may be known and that the believers and hypocrites may be distinguished, so that the faith of some may be revealed and the disbelief of others may be revealed. And it will be said to them is an apodosis to hypocrites and is included in the relative clause or a subject statement. Come, fight in the cause of God or defend dividing the matter among them and giving them a choice between fighting for the Hereafter or defending lives and property. It was said that its meaning is fight the disbelievers or repel them by increasing the number of the mujahideen, because the large number of people terrifies the enemy and defeats him. They said, 'If we knew how to fight, we would have followed you' If we knew what could be called fighting, we would have followed you in it, but what you are doing is not fighting, but throwing lives into destruction, or if we were good at fighting, we would have followed you in it, and they only said it out of deceit and mockery. They are nearer to disbelief that Day than to faith because of their failure and their words, for they were the first signs that appeared from them indicating their disbelief. It was said that they are closer to supporting the unbelievers than they are to the believers, since their failure and their words strengthen the polytheists and discourage the believers. They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts they show something other than what they conceal, their hearts do not agree with their tongues in faith. Adding the words to the mouths is an emphasis and a depiction. And God knows best what they conceal of hypocrisy. And what they secretly say to one another, He knows it in detail with obligatory knowledge, and you know it in general with signs.
3:168: 168 Those who said is raised instead of the waw of they conceal, or it is accusative as a censure or description of those who were hypocrites, or it is genitive instead of the pronoun in with their mouths or their hearts as in his saying: If there was a generous Hatem among the people, Hatem would be stingy with water. For their brothers meaning for their sake, meaning those who were killed on the Day of Uhud from their relatives or from their kind. And they sat is a state implied by qad meaning they said they were sitting from fighting. If they had obeyed us in sitting in the city. They would not have been killed just as we were not killed. Hashim read they were not killed with a shaddah on the ta’. “Say: Then avert death from yourselves, if you should be truthful” meaning if you are truthful that you are able to avert killing from those who have been decreed for them, then avert death and its causes from yourselves, for it is more appropriate for you. The meaning is that sitting is not a substitute for death, for the causes of death are many, just as fighting can be a cause of destruction and sitting is a cause of salvation. The opposite may be the case.
3:169: 169 "And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead." This was revealed about the martyrs of Uhud. It was also said that it was about the martyrs of Badr, and the address is to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone. It was read with the letter "ya" based on its attribution to the pronoun of the Messenger, or to whomever is considered, or to those who were killed. The first object is omitted because it is originally a subject that can be omitted based on the context. Ibn Amir read "killed" with emphasis due to the large number of speakers. "Rather, they are alive" meaning, rather, they are alive. It was read with the accusative meaning, rather, I think that they are alive. "With their Lord" with closeness to Him. "They are provided for" from Paradise, which is an emphasis on their being alive.
3:170: 170 Rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty" which is the honor of martyrdom, winning eternal life, being close to God Almighty, and enjoying the bliss of Paradise. "And they rejoice" they are pleased with the good report. "For those who have not yet joined them" meaning their believing brothers who were not killed so that they could join them. "From behind them" meaning those who are behind them in time or rank. "There is no fear for them, nor shall they grieve is a substitute for those" and the meaning is: they rejoice in what has become clear to them about the matter of the Hereafter and the state of those believers they left behind them, which is that if they die or are killed they are alive with a life that is not troubled by the fear of something bad happening, nor the sadness of missing out on something beloved. The verse indicates that man is not a tangible structure, but rather an essence that is perceived in itself and does not perish with the destruction of the body, and his perception, pain and pleasure do not depend on it. This is supported by the Almighty’s statement about the people of Pharaoh: The Fire will be exposed to them Al-Baqarah 2:170. And what Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him narrated that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The souls of the martyrs are in the bodies of green birds that frequent the rivers of Paradise, eat from its fruits and take refuge in hanging lanterns in the shade of the Throne. And whoever denies this and sees the soul only as a wind and an exposure said that they are alive on the Day of Resurrection, but they were described thus in the present moment because of its realization and proximity, or alive through remembrance or faith. In it is an exhortation to jihad and an encouragement to martyrdom and an incentive to increase obedience and praise for those who wish for their brothers what they have been blessed with, and good tidings for the believers of success.
3:171: 171 They rejoice He repeated it for emphasis and to attach to it what is an explanation of his saying: There is no fear for them. It is possible that the first is regarding the condition of their brothers and this is regarding the condition of themselves. With a blessing from God as a reward for their deeds. And bounty as an addition to it, like the Almighty's saying: For those who do good is the best and more. And their indefiniteness is for emphasis. And that God does not allow to be lost the reward of the believers is from the group of those who rejoice in it, in apposition to bounty. Al-Kisa'i read it with the kasra as an interjecting resumption indicating that this is a reward for them for their faith, indicating that the deeds of the one who has no faith are nullified and his rewards are lost.
3:172: 172 "Those who responded to God and the Messenger after the wound had befallen them" is an attribute of the believers, or an accusative of praise or a subject whose predicate is. "For those among them who do good and fear God is a great reward" in its entirety and from the statement, and the purpose of mentioning the two attributes is praise and explanation, not restriction, because all of those who responded were good and fear God. It was narrated that "when Abu Sufyan and his companions returned and reached Ar-Rawha, they regretted it and intended to return, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of that, so he urged his companions to go out in search of him and said, Let none go out with us except those who were present with us yesterday.
