It was said that what is meant by it are male and female slaves and it is the plural of child. Those who say, ‘Our Lord, take us out of this city whose people are oppressors and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper.’ So God answered their prayer by making it easy for some of them to leave for Medina and by appointing for those who remained of them the best protector and helper by opening Mecca to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He took charge of them and supported them, then appointed ‘Atab ibn Asid over them, so he protected them and supported them until they became the most honored of its people. The city is Mecca and the oppressor is its description, and its masculinity is to masculinize what it is attributed to, because if the active participle or the passive participle is applied to someone other than the one to whom it belongs, it is like a verb that is masculine or feminine according to what it does.
4:76: 76 Those who believe fight in the cause of God in order to reach God, the Most High. Those who disbelieve fight in the cause of Taghut in order to reach Satan. Then fight the allies of Satan When He mentioned the purpose of the two groups, He ordered His allies to fight the allies of Satan, then He encouraged them by saying: Indeed, the plot of Satan has ever been weak meaning that his plot against the believers, in addition to the plot of God, the Most High, against the disbelievers, is weak, so do not pay attention to it, so do not fear His allies, for their reliance is on the weakest and most feeble thing.
4:77: 77"Have you not considered those who were told, 'Restrain your hands' meaning from fighting. "And establish prayer and give zakah" and busy themselves with what you have been commanded to do. "But when fighting was prescribed for them, at once a party of them feared the people as they feared God" they feared the disbelievers that they would kill them just as they feared God that He would send down His punishment upon them. "If is an answer to the surprise answer to what and a party is the subject of them and its description is and they fear" in the sense that they fear the people like the people who fear God from Him. "Or a greater fear" is in apposition to it if you make it a state, but if you make it a source then no. The comparative if it places what follows it in the accusative case is not of its type, but rather it is in apposition to the name of God, the Most High, meaning: and like the fear of God, the Most High, or like a greater fear than Him, assuming "O God" unless you make the fear inherent in fear like their saying: "very, very" meaning they fear the people with a fear like the fear of God, the Most High, or a fear more intense than the fear of God, the Most High. And they will say, ‘Our Lord, why have You decreed fighting upon us? Why have You not delayed us for a short term?’ This was an extension of the period of abstention from fighting out of fear of death. It is possible that they did not say it out loud, but rather said it to themselves, so God Almighty spoke about them. Say, ‘The enjoyment of this world is little.’ It is fleeting, “and the Hereafter is better for him who fears God. And you will not be wronged a thread.” That is, you will not be deprived of the slightest bit of your reward, so do not desire it, or of your appointed terms. Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read nor will they be wronged because of the precedence of the third person.
4:78: 78 Wherever you may be, death will overtake you. It was read with the nominative case, deleting the fa as in his saying: Whoever does good deeds, God will thank them. Or as a subject, and wherever it is connected to do not wrong. “Even if you were in lofty towers” in palaces or high fortresses, and towers are originally houses on the edges of palaces, from tabarrujt a woman if she appeared. It was read mushaydah with a kasra on the ya’ describing it with the description of its doer, like their saying: a female poet’s poem, and mushaydah from shed al-qasr if he raised it. And if good befalls them, they say, ‘This is from God,’ and if evil befalls them, they say, ‘This is from you.’ Just as good and evil fall on obedience and disobedience, they fall on blessing and affliction, and they are what is meant in the verse, that is: If a blessing such as fertility befalls them, they attribute it to God, the Most High, and if a affliction befalls them such as drought, they attribute it to you and say, It is only because of your bad luck, as the Jews said: Since Muhammad entered Medina, its fruits have decreased and its prices have risen. Say, ‘All is from God.’ That is, He expands and contracts according to His will. What is the matter with these people that they can hardly understand a statement that they are being admonished with, which is the Qur’an? If they understood it and pondered its meanings, they would know that everything is from God Almighty, or a statement like animals that do not understand, or an event from the vicissitudes of time, so they think about it and know that the One who contracts and expands is God Almighty.
4:79: 79Whatever good befalls you O human being. It is from God meaning a favor from Him, for everything a person does in terms of obedience is not equivalent to the blessing of existence, so how can it necessitate anything else? That is why the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "No one will enter Paradise except by the mercy of God the Most High. It was said: Not even you? He said: Not even me." And whatever evil befalls you of affliction. It is from yourself because it is the cause of it, as it is brought about by sins. This does not contradict the words of God the Most High: "Say: All is from God", for all is from Him in creation and delivery. However, the good is kindness and gratitude, and the evil is recompense and vengeance, as Aisha may God be pleased with her said: "No Muslim is afflicted with fatigue or exhaustion, or a thorn that pricks him, or even the lace of his sandal breaking, except for a sin. And God forgives more." As you can see, the two verses do not constitute an argument for us or the Mu'tazila. And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger is a state intended to emphasize if the preposition is attached to the verb, and to generalize if it is attached to it, i.e. a messenger to all mankind, as in the Almighty’s saying: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to mankind. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case as a verbal noun, as in His saying: And not outside of the false speech. “And sufficient is God as Witness” of your message by putting miracles in the accusative case.
4:80: 80Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God because he, peace and blessings be upon him, is in fact a messenger, and the command is God, the Most High. It was narrated that "he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever loves me has loved God, and whoever obeys me has obeyed God. He said: The hypocrites have committed polytheism and he forbade it, he only wants us to take him as a lord as the Christians took Jesus as a lord so it was revealed. "And whoever turns away" from obeying him. "We have not sent you over them as a guardian" to preserve their deeds and hold them accountable for them. You are only responsible for conveying the message and for Us is the reckoning, and it is a state of the kaf.
4:81: 81 And they say when you command them to do something. Obedience means our command or from us to obey, and its origin is the accusative as a source and its nominative to indicate steadfastness. So when they leave you they go out. Then a party of them has committed a sin meaning they have fabricated something other than what you say, or what she said to you of acceptance and guarantee of obedience, and spending the night is either from spending the night because matters are managed at night, or from the house of poetry, or the built house because it is arranged and managed. Abu Amr and Hamza read the house of a party with assimilation because of their proximity in the exit. And God records what they spend the night He records it in their records for recompense, or in the sum of what is revealed to you so that you may know their secrets. So turn away from them pay little attention to them or avoid them. And put your trust in God in all matters, especially their affair. And God is sufficient as a Disposer of affairs He will suffice you from their harm and will take revenge on you from them.
4:82: 82 Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an? Reflect upon its meanings and consider what is in it? The root of contemplation is looking at the backs of something. If it had been from other than God meaning, if it had been the speech of humans as the infidels claim. They would have found in it much discrepancy in terms of contradiction in meaning and disparity in composition. Some of it is eloquent and some of it is weak, some of it is difficult to oppose and some of it is easy, some of its future report matches reality and some of it does not, and the mind agrees with some of its rulings and not others, as indicated by induction due to the deficiency of human power. Perhaps it is mentioned here to draw attention to the fact that the difference in the rulings that preceded it is not due to a contradiction in the ruling, but rather due to the difference in circumstances in the ruling and interests.
4:83: 83 And if there came to them report of security or fear of what necessitated security or fear. They broadcast it they spread it as some of the weak Muslims used to do if they heard report of the expeditions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them of what was revealed to him of a promise of victory, or a threat from the infidels, they broadcast it because of their lack of resolve. The ba is an additional letter or to include the meaning of speaking. And if they had referred it that is, if they had referred that report. To the Messenger and to those in authority among them to his opinion and the opinion of his senior companions who were insightful in matters, or the princes. For his knowledge they would have known what they were told in whatever way it is mentioned. Those who deduce it from among them they extract its measures through their experiences and insights. It was said that they heard the rumours of the hypocrites and spread them, so they would have a bad effect on the Muslims. If they had referred it to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to those in authority among them so that they could hear it from them and wonder if it would have been spread, then those who deduce it from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those in authority would have known about it, meaning: they would have extracted its knowledge from their side. The origin of deduction is the extraction of Nabat: which is water, which comes out of the well when it is first dug. And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy by sending the Messenger and revealing the books. You would have followed Satan and disbelief and misguidance. Except a few meaning except a few of you whom God favored with a sound mind that guided them to the truth and right path, and protected them from following Satan, like Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl and Waraqah ibn Nawfal. Or except a few followers, rarely.
4:84: 84Then fight in the cause of God lest they become discouraged and leave you alone. You are not tasked with anything but yourself except your own actions. It does not harm you to oppose them and stay behind, so go forward to jihad even if no one helps you, for God will support you, not the soldiers. It was narrated that "he, peace and blessings be upon him, called the people in the Battle of Badr al-Sughra to go out, but some of them disliked him, so it was revealed. So he, peace and blessings be upon him, went out, and with him were only seventy, not looking back on anyone." It was read La takalluf in the jussive mood, and La nakalluf with the nun in the active voice, meaning we do not task you with anything but your own actions, not I do not task anyone but yourself, because of his saying: And urge the believers to fight, since you are only responsible for their matter with the incitement. Perhaps God will restrain the violence of those who disbelieved meaning Quraysh, and he did so by casting terror into their hearts until they returned. And God is more severe in violence than Quraysh. And more severe in punishment in torment than them, and it is a rebuke and threat to those who do not follow him. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 7 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Nisāa, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Māidah. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. 4:85: 85Whoever intercedes for a good cause he takes care of the rights of a Muslim and repels harm from him or brings him benefit seeking the face of God Almighty, including supplication for a Muslim. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever supplicates for his Muslim brother in his absence, his supplication will be answered and the angel will say to him, And for you is the same. He will have a share of it" which is the reward of intercession and the means to the good that comes from it. "And whoever intercedes for an evil cause" meaning something forbidden. "He will have a share of it" a share of its burden equal in amount. "And God is Able to do all things from the verb aqat if it means has power." He said: And I refrained from holding a grudge against him, and I was hateful of his wrongdoing. Or a martyr and protector, and its derivation is from the word sustenance because it strengthens and protects the body.
4:86: 86 And if you are greeted with a greeting, greet with one better than it or return it. The majority of scholars agree that it is in the case of peace, and it indicates that it is obligatory to respond either with something better than it, which is to add to it and the mercy of God. If the Muslim says it, he adds and His blessings, which is the end, or to return something similar to it, as it was narrated that "a man said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Peace be upon you. He said: And upon you be peace and the mercy of God. Another said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God. He said: And upon you be peace and the mercy of God and His blessings. Another said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings. He said: And upon you. The man said: You have failed me, so where is what God the Most High said and recited the verse? So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have not left me any excess, so I returned to you something similar." This is because it includes the sections of demands that are free from harm and the benefits are obtained and established, and from this it was said, or to hesitate between greeting a Muslim with some of the greeting and greeting him with the entire greeting, and this obligation is on the sufficiency and since peace is prescribed, it is not rejected in the sermon, reading the Qur’an, in the bathroom, when relieving oneself and the like. The greeting is originally a source of May God give you life for the report of life, then it was used for ruling and supplication with that, then it was said for every supplication and it was prevalent in peace. It was said that what is meant by the greeting is the gift and the obligation of reward or return to the one who gave it, and it is an old saying of Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him. Indeed, God is ever, over all things, an Accountant He will hold you accountable for the greeting and other things.
4:87: 87 God, there is no god but He is a subject and predicate, or God is a subject and predicate He will surely gather you together on the Day of Resurrection meaning God, and God will surely gather you from the graves on the Day of Resurrection, or arriving at it or on the Day of Resurrection, and there is no god but He, an objection. And the rising and the resurrection are like the students and the students, which is the rising of people from the graves or for the reckoning. There is no doubt about it in the day or in the gathering, so it is a state of the day, or an attribute of the source. And who is more truthful than God in statement is a denial that anyone is more truthful than Him, for lying does not enter into His statement in any way because it is a deficiency and it is impossible for God.
4:88: 88So what is the matter with you regarding the hypocrites? So what is the matter with you that you are divided regarding the matter of the hypocrites. In two groups meaning two groups and you did not agree on their disbelief, and that is because some of them asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to go out to the desert to seize the city, and when they went out they continued to travel, stage by stage, until they caught up with the polytheists, and the Muslims differed regarding their conversion to Islam. It was said that it was revealed regarding those who stayed behind on the day of Uhud, or regarding a group of people who migrated and then returned, complaining of seizing the city and longing for their homeland, or a group who showed Islam and then refrained from migrating. Two groups is a state of its agent for you, like saying: What is wrong with you standing? In the hypocrites is a state of two groups meaning divided among them, or from the pronoun meaning so what is the matter with you that you are divided regarding them, and the meaning of separation is derived from two groups. And God has turned them back for what they have earned. He returned them to the rule of the infidels, or He turned them back by sending them to the Fire. The root of raks is to return something upside down. Do you want to guide one whom God has sent astray? To make him one of the guided ones. And he whom God sends astray, you will not find for him a way to guidance.
4:89: 89 And they wish that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved. They wished that you would disbelieve as they disbelieved. So you would be equal with them so that you would be equal with them in misguidance, and it is an appositive to disbelieve. If it had been in the accusative case as an answer to the wish, it would have been permissible. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the cause of God. So do not befriend them until they believe and you have confirmed their faith by emigrating for the sake of God and His Messenger, not for worldly purposes. The cause of God is that which He has commanded us to follow. But if they turn away from the apparent faith by emigrating or from showing faith. Then seize them and kill them wherever you find them like all the disbelievers. And do not take from among them any friend or helper meaning, completely avoid them and do not accept any friend or help from them.
4:90: 90 Except those who reach a people between you and whom there is a treaty is an exception to His statement, So seize them and kill them, meaning: except those who reach and go to a people with whom you have a treaty, and refrain from fighting you. The people are Khuza'ah. It was said: they are the Aslamites, because when he left for Mecca, peace and blessings be upon him, he called upon Hilal bin Uwaimir Al-Aslami on the condition that he would not help him or help against him, and whoever sought refuge with him would have a neighbor like his wealth. It was said: they are the sons of Bakr bin Zaid Manat. Or they came to you is an appositive to the connection, meaning or those who came to you refraining from fighting you and fighting their people. He excluded from the command to seize and kill those who left the fighters and joined the treaty-holders, or came to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and refrained from fighting the two groups, or in a manner as if it was said: except those who reach a people with whom there is a treaty, or a people refraining from fighting for you and against you. The first is more apparent because of His statement, If they withdraw from you. It was read without the conjunction as an adjective after an adjective or a statement of they pray or a resumption. They have constricted their chests is a state with the implied may and it is indicated by the fact that it was read They have constricted their chests and the constrictions of their chests, or a statement of they came to you. It was said that it is an adjective of something omitted, meaning they came to you as people whose chests were constricted, and they are Banu Mudlij who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, not fighting. Constriction is narrowness and contraction. That they may fight you or fight their people meaning from that or because or out of dislike that they fight you. And if God had willed, He would have given them power over you by strengthening their hearts, expanding their chests, and removing fear from them. So they would have fought you and did not refrain from you. But if they withdraw from you and do not fight you if they do not confront you. “And they throw peace to you” means surrender and obedience. Then God has not made for you a way over them so He has not given you permission to seize them and kill them.
4:91: 91 "You will find others who want to give you security and give security to their people." They are Asad and Ghatafan, and it was said that Banu Abd al-Dar came to Medina and showed Islam in order to give security to the Muslims, but when they returned, they disbelieved. "Every time they were returned to the fitnah," they called to disbelief and to fighting the Muslims. "They relapsed into it," they returned to it and turned into it the ugliest heart. "But if they do not withdraw from you and offer you peace, and throw away their covenant with you, and restrain their hands," from fighting you. "Then seize them and kill them wherever you find them," wherever you are able to do so, because merely restraining does not necessitate denying exposure. "And those We have given you clear authority over," a clear argument in exposing them to killing and captivity due to the appearance of their enmity and the clarity of their disbelief and treachery, or an apparent authority where We have given you permission[*1] to kill them. In the book, an ear with tanween I think wrong
4:92: 92 "And it is not for a believer" and what is right for him and is not his business. "To kill a believer" unjustly. "Except by mistake" because it is on his offer, and its accusative is in the state or the object for it, meaning: he does not kill him in any case except by mistake, or he does not kill him for a reason except by mistake or as a description of a deleted source, meaning by mistaken killing. It was said that "what was" negates the meaning of prohibition, and the exception is disconnected, meaning but if he kills him by mistake, then his punishment is what is mentioned, and the mistake is that which is not harmed by the intention to the action or the person or is not intended to cause the loss of the soul usually, or is not intended to cause a harm such as throwing a Muslim into the ranks of the infidels while being ignorant of his Islam, or is it the action of an undutiful person. "Khata was read with a long vowel and khata" like a stick with a light hamza, and the verse was revealed about Ayyash bin Abi Rabi'ah, the brother of Abu Jahl from his mother, he met Harith bin Zaid on the road and he had converted to Islam and Ayyash did not know about him so he killed him. And whoever kills a believer by mistake, the freeing of a slave means that it is his duty or obligation to free a slave. Freeing means emancipation. A free man is like a freed slave for a noble person, such as a free man of the face for the noblest part of it. He was called this because nobility is in the free and baseness is in the slaves. The neck is used to refer to the soul, just as it is used to refer to the head. A believing woman is considered a Muslim, even if she is young. A blood money paid to her family is paid to his heirs, who divide it like other inheritances, based on the statement of Dahhak ibn Sufyan al-Kalabi: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to me ordering me to give the wife of Ashim al-Dababi an inheritance from her husband’s blood money.” It is on the agnates, and if there is none, then on the public treasury, and if there is none, then on his money. Unless they give him the blood money unless they give him the blood money. Pardoning her is called charity as an encouragement to do so and as a reminder of its virtue. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every good deed is charity. It is related to him, or a Muslim woman, meaning that the blood money must be paid by him or he must hand it over to his family, except in the case of their giving him charity. Or his time, then it is in the accusative case as a state of the killer, the family, or the circumstance. But if he is from a people at war with you and he is a believer, then the freeing of a believing slave, meaning that if the believer who was killed is from a people who are infidels at war, or among their ranks and his faith is not known, then his killer must pay expiation without paying blood money to his family, since there is no inheritance between him and them and because they are at war. But if he is from a people with whom you have a treaty, then a ransom must be paid to his family and the freeing of a believing slave, meaning that if he is from a people who are infidels with whom you have a treaty, or a protected person, then his ruling is the ruling of Muslims in the obligation of expiation and blood money. This may be in the case when the one killed is a protected person, or he has a Muslim heir. But whoever does not find a slave, meaning that he does not own her or what can reach her. Then fasting two consecutive months. He must fast two consecutive months. Repentance is in the accusative case as a direct object, meaning that it was prescribed as repentance, from God has accepted your repentance if he accepts his repentance. Or as a verbal noun, meaning that God has accepted your repentance, or as a state with the omission of an adjective, meaning that he must fast two consecutive months as a repentance. From God is its description. And God is Knowing of his condition. Wise in what He commanded regarding his affair.
4:93: 93 And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and the wrath and the curse of God are upon him, and a great punishment is prepared for him because of the great threat it contains. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said: The repentance of the one who intentionally kills a believer is not accepted. Perhaps he meant to be strict, as it was narrated from him otherwise. The majority are of the opinion that it is specific to the one who does not repent, as God the Almighty said: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and similar to it, and it is from us, either it is specific to the one who considers it permissible, as mentioned by Ikrimah and others, and it is supported by the fact that it was revealed about Muqays ibn Dhubabah, who found his brother Hisham killed in Banu al-Najjar, and his killer was not found, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to pay him his blood money, so they paid it to him, then he attacked a Muslim and killed him and returned to Mecca as an apostate, or what is meant by eternity is a long stay, as the evidence is clear that the punishment of the disobedient Muslims does not last.
4:94: 94 "O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God" you travel and go to war. "Then verify" seek clarification of the matter and its confirmation and do not hasten it. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read "Fa-thabatu in both places here, and in Al-Hujurat from the word tattabat". "And do not say to one who offers you peace" to one who greets you with the greeting of Islam. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read "As-Salam" without the alif, meaning submission and obedience, and peace was also interpreted by it. "I am not a believer", but I did that seeking refuge. "Mu'minan" was read with the fat-ha, meaning offering him security. "Seeking the goods of the worldly life you seek his wealth, which is a fleeting wreck, and it is a state of the pronoun in Ta-thaqulu" indicating what is driving them to hasten and abandon verification. "Then with God are spoils" for you. "Abounding" We will make you independent of killing the likes of him for his wealth. Thus were you before meaning when you first entered Islam, you uttered the two testimonies of faith, thus protecting your blood and your wealth without your tongues knowing that your hearts were in agreement. Then God has bestowed His favor upon you by being known for your faith and uprightness in religion. Then verify and do to those who entered Islam as God did to you, and do not rush to kill them thinking that they entered it out of fear and caution, for the survival of a disbeliever is easier for God than the killing of a Muslim. Repeating it is to emphasize the gravity of the matter and to base the ruling on what was mentioned about their condition. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted knowing it and its purpose, so do not rush to kill and be cautious in it. It was narrated that the army of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, attacked the people of Fadak, so they fled and Murdas remained, confident in his Islam. When he saw the horses, he took his sheep to a mountain peak and climbed up. When they caught up with him and shouted God Almighty, he shouted God Almighty and came down and said: There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God, peace be upon you. Usama killed him and drove away his sheep. It was also said that it was revealed about Muqdad, who passed by a man with his spoils and wanted to kill him, so he said: There is no god but God. So he killed him and said: He wished he could flee with his family and his money. It is evidence of the validity of the faith of one who is forced, and that one who strives hard may make mistakes and that his mistakes are forgiven.
4:95: 95 Those who sit at home are not equal from war. Of the believers is in the position of a state of those who sit at home or of the pronoun in it. Others than those who are disabled in the nominative case is an attribute of those who sit at home because it does not mean a specific group of people or a substitute for it. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Al-Kisa'i read it in the accusative case as a state or exception and it was read in the genitive case as an attribute of the believers or a substitute for it. And on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit that it was revealed and there were none in it other than those who are disabled, so Ibn Umm Maktum said: How is it that he was blind and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was overcome by revelation in his assembly, and his thigh fell on my thigh until I feared that it would crush it, then he was relieved and said: Write Those of the believers who sit at home are not equal, other than those who are disabled "and those who strive in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives" meaning there is no equality between them and those who sit at home without a reason. Its benefit is to remind them of the difference between them so that the one who sits at home may desire jihad to raise his rank and be proud of the decline of his status. God has favored those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home by a degree. This is a sentence explaining what was negated in it. The ones who sit is based on the previous restriction, and degree is in the accusative case by removing the preposition, meaning by degree, or in the verbal noun because it includes the meaning of preference and is used as a time in it, or in the state meaning those with a degree. And both are from those who sit at home and the mujahideen. God has promised the best the best reward, which is Paradise, because of the goodness of their belief and the purity of their lineage. The difference is in the increase in the work that requires more reward. And God has favored those who strive with their wealth over those who sit at home by a great reward. It is in the accusative case as in the verbal noun because fadl means reward, or its second object because it includes the meaning of giving, as if it was said: And He gave them, in addition to those who sit at home, a great reward.
4:96: 96 Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy each one of them is a substitute for reward, and it is permissible for degrees to be in the accusative case as a source like you say I struck him with whips, and reward as a state of it preceded it because it is indefinite, and forgiveness and mercy as a source with an implied subject, so he repeated the preference of the mujahideen, and exaggerated in it in general and in detail to magnify jihad and encourage it. It was said: The first is what He granted them in this world of spoils, victory and good reputation, and the second is what He made for them in the hereafter. It was said that what is meant by the first degree is the elevation of their status with God, the Most High, and by the degrees are their homes in Paradise. It was said that the first sitters are the weak and the second sitters are those who were permitted to stay behind, being satisfied with others. It was said that the first mujahideen are those who fought the infidels and the last are those who fought themselves, and based on his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, We have returned from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad. "And God is Forgiving" for what they may have neglected. "Merciful" in what he promised them.
4:97: 97 Indeed, those whom the angels take in death can be in the past or present tense, and tawafahum and tawafahum are read in the present tense and wafayt meaning that God takes the angels' souls in full, meaning that He enables them to take them in full, so they take them in full. Wrongdoers to themselves in the case of their wronging themselves by not migration and agreeing with the infidels, for it was revealed about people from Mecca who converted to Islam but did not migrate when migration was obligatory. They said the angels as a rebuke to them. In what were you? meaning in what were you in your worldly affairs? They said, We were oppressed in the land." They apologized for what they were rebuked for, due to their weakness and inability to migrate, or to manifest the religion and raise the word of God. "They said" meaning the angels as a denial and rebuke to them. "Was not the earth of God spacious enough for you to migrate therein?" to another country, as the migrants to Medina and Abyssinia did. "Then their abode is Hell" for abandoning their duty and helping the disbelievers. It is the predicate of "inna and the fa" in it because the name includes the meaning of condition. And they said in what you were is a state of the angels with the omission of "qad" or the predicate said and the pronoun is omitted, meaning they said to them, and it is a sentence conjoined to the sentence before it and inferred from it. "And evil is their destination" their destination is the fire of Hell. And in the verse is evidence of the obligation of migration from a place where a man is unable to establish his religion. And from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "Whoever flees for his religion from one land to another, even if it is a handspan of land, Paradise is due to him, and he was the companion of his father Abraham and his prophet Muhammad, may God bless them both."
4:98: 98 Except for the weak among men, women and children is an interrupted exception because they are not included in the relative pronoun and the pronoun refers to them. The mention of the child, if it means slaves, is clear, and if it means young boys, is to exaggerate the matter and indicate that they are on the verge of the obligation of migration, because if they reach maturity and are able to migrate, then there is no escape for them from it and that their guardians must migrate with them whenever possible. They are unable to find a plan nor are they guided to a way is a description of the weak, since there is no time limit for it, or a state of it or of what is hidden in it. The ability to find a plan is finding the reasons for migration and what it depends on, and finding the way is knowing the path by itself or by evidence.
16:110: 99 So those, perhaps God will pardon them. He mentioned the word covetousness and the word pardon as an indication that abandoning migration is a serious matter, so much so that the one forced has the right not to feel safe and to watch for an opportunity and attach his heart to it. And God is Pardoning and Forgiving. 110. Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted meaning they were tortured, like Ammar, may God be pleased with him, with guardianship and victory, and then to differentiate the situation of these from the situation of those, and Ibn Amir read they were persecuted with the fat-ha, meaning after the believers were tortured, like the Hadrami who forced his master to apostatize, then converted to Islam and emigrated. Then they struggled and were patient in the struggle and what befell them of hardships. Indeed, your Lord, after that after the emigration, struggle and patience. Forgiving for what they did before. Merciful gracious to them as a reward for what they did after.
4:100: 100 And whoever emigrates for the cause of God will find on the earth many [alternative] locations. Shifting from ragham, which is dust. It was said that it is a path that he takes against his people, meaning he leaves them in spite of their noses, and it is also from ragham. And abundance in provision and manifesting religion. And whoever emigrates from his home as an emigrant to God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him It was read overtakes him in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning then he overtakes him, and in the accusative case as an implied that, like his saying: I will leave my home in Bani Tamim and go to Hijaz to rest His reward has become due to God, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. Occurrence and obligation are close in meaning, and the meaning is: his reward has become due to God, the Most High, as is the obligatory matter. The noble verse was revealed about Jundub bin Damrah. His sons carried him on a bed, heading to Madinah. When he reached At-Tan’im, he was on the verge of death, so he clapped his right hand over his left and said: O God, this is for you and this is for Your Messenger. I pledge allegiance to You on what Your Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged allegiance to. Then he died.
4:101: 101 And if you travel throughout the land you travel. There is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer by halving its rak'ahs and denying any hardship in that indicates its permissibility but not its obligation, and this is supported by the fact that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, completed it while traveling. And that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, "performed Umrah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: O Messenger of God, I shortened and completed it, and I fasted and broke my fast. He said: Well done, Aisha." Abu Hanifa made it obligatory based on the statement of Omar, may God be pleased with him: The prayer of travel is two complete rak'ahs, not shortened, on the tongue of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and based on the statement of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that when prayer was first made obligatory, it was made obligatory as two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs, so it was left on while traveling and increased while at home. Their apparent meaning contradicts the noble verse. If it is correct, then the first is interpreted as being like the complete one in validity and sufficiency, and the second does not deny the permissibility of the increase, so there is no need to interpret the verse. They were accustomed to the four, so it was likely that they would think that the two rak'ahs of travel were shortened and incomplete, so performing them was called shortening according to their assumption. And negating sins in it is to treat their souls with it, and the minimum travel in which four rak'ahs are shortened is according to us and six according to Abu Hanifa. And it was read Taqasra from aqsar meaning shortened, and from as-salat is an attribute of something omitted, meaning: something of the prayer according to Sibawayh, and the object of Taqasra is an addition according to Al-Akhfash. If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you - indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy on the condition that the majority are considered at that time, and therefore its meaning was not considered as it was not considered in the statement of God the Most High: But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, then there is no blame upon them for that by which they ransom themselves and the Sunnahs have agreed on its permissibility also in a state of security. And it was read from as-salat that an yiftankum bi ghayr that you fear, meaning that he dislikes that he tempts you: which is fighting and exposing oneself to what is disliked. [*1] Written as is in The book I think is wrong. The correct one is To perfume without the letter Baa.
4:102: 102 And if you are among them and lead them in prayer relates to the concept of the specificity of the prayer of fear in the presence of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, due to the virtue of the congregation, and most of the jurists are of the opinion that God Almighty taught the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, how to do it so that the imams after him would follow him, for they are his representatives, and their presence would be like his presence. Then let a group of them stand with you So make them two groups, so let one of them stand with you and pray, and the other group stands, and mentioning the first group indicates them. When they prostrate means those who are praying. Then let them be meaning those who are not praying. Behind you guarding you, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who are praying, so the one addressed is predominant. And let another group come who have not prayed because they are busy guarding. Let them pray with you appears to indicate that the imam prays twice, with each group once, as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did at Batn Nakhl. If what is meant is that he prays in each rak'ah, if the prayer is two rak'ahs, then the way to do it is to pray one rak'ah with the first one and wait standing until they complete their prayer individually and go to face the enemy, and the other one comes and completes the second rak'ah with them. Then he waits sitting until they complete their prayer and greet them, as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did at Dhat al-Riqa'. Abu Hanifah may God be pleased with him said: He prays one rak'ah with the first one, then this one goes and stands facing the enemy, and the other one comes and prays one rak'ah with him, and completes his prayer, then returns to face the enemy, and the first one comes and performs the second rak'ah without recitation and completes its prayer, then returns and the other one comes and performs the rak'ah with recitation and completes its prayer. And let them take their precautions and their weapons. He made caution a tool with which to fortify themselves in battles, so He combined it with weapons in the obligation to take them. Similar to it is the statement of the Most High: And those who have established themselves in the home and in the faith. "Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage so that they could attack you with a single attack." They wished that they could catch you by surprise during your prayer so that they could attack you with a single attack. This is a statement of the reason for which they were ordered to take precautions and take weapons. "And there is no blame upon you if you are harmed by rain or you are ill for you to lay down your weapons." A license for them to lay them down if taking them is difficult for them because of rain or illness. This supports that the order to take precautions is obligatory and not recommended. "And take your precautions." He ordered them, however, to take precautions so that the enemy does not attack them. God has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment. He promised the believers victory over the disbelievers after the command to be firm so that their hearts would be strengthened and so that they would know that the command to be firm was not because of their weakness or the superiority of their enemy, but because it is their duty to maintain the rituals of vigilance and contemplation in matters and to put their trust in God Almighty.
4:103: 103 "So when you have completed the prayer" you have performed it and finished it. "Then remember God standing, sitting, and lying on your sides" so continue to remember God in all circumstances, or if you want to perform the prayer and the fear is intense then perform it however you can, standing, fighting and striking, sitting, throwing, and lying on your sides. “Through them.” So when you are reassured, your hearts will be calmed from fear. Establish prayer, so be just and preserve its pillars and conditions and perform it completely. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times, an obligation limited in time and it is not permissible to deviate from its times under any circumstances. This is evidence that what is meant by the remembrance is prayer and that it is obligatory to perform it during combat and in turmoil in battle, and an explanation for the command to perform it however possible. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said that the warrior does not pray until he is reassured.
4:104: 104 And do not weaken and do not become weak. In seeking out the people in seeking out the infidels by fighting. If you are suffering, then they are suffering as you are suffering, and you hope from God that which they do not hope for is an obligation on them and a rebuke for their laziness in it, because the harm of fighting is between the two parties and is not limited to them, and they hope from God because of it to show the religion and to deserve wealth that their enemy does not hope for, so they should be more desirous of war and more patient in it. If you are is read with the fat-ha meaning do not weaken because you are suffering, and His saying then they are suffering is a reason for the prohibition of weakness because of it. The verse was revealed at Badr al-Sughra. And God is Knowing of your deeds and your consciences. Wise in what He commands and forbids.
4:105: 105 Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between people. It was revealed about Ta'mah ibn Ubayraq from Banu Thafar. He stole a shield from his neighbor Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man in a bag of flour. The flour began to scatter from a hole in it and he hid it with Zayd ibn al-Sameen the Jew. The shield was sought with Ta'mah but was not found. He swore that he had not taken it and that he had no knowledge of it. They left him and followed the traces of the flour until he reached the house of the Jew and took it. He said, He gave it to Ta'mah. Some Jews testified for him. Banu Thafar said, "Let us go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him to argue on behalf of your companion." They said, If you do not do so, he will be destroyed and disgraced, and the Jew will be acquitted. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, understood that he should do what God has shown you with what God has made known to you and revealed to you. Seeing does not mean knowing, otherwise it would require three objects. And do not be an advocate for the traitors meaning for their sake and to defend them for the innocent.
4:106: 106 And I seek forgiveness from God for what I intended to do. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful to those who seek forgiveness.
4:107: 107 And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves betray themselves, for the consequences of their betrayal will return upon them, or make the sin a betrayal of them as it was made an injustice against them, and the pronoun refers to Ta'mah and his likes or to him and his people, for they shared in the sin as they testified to his innocence and argued on his behalf. Indeed, God does not love one who is a traitor exaggerating in betrayal and persisting in it. Sinful immersed in it. It was narrated that Ta'mah fled to Mecca and apostatized and dug a hole in a wall there to steal from his family, but the wall fell on him and killed him.
4:108: 108 They hide from people They hide from them out of shyness and fear. And they do not hide from God Nor are they ashamed of Him, and He is more deserving of being ashamed and feared. And He is with them Their secret is not hidden from Him, so there is no way with Him except to leave what He finds ugly and for which He will be held accountable. When they spend the night They plot and visit. What is not pleasing of speech Of accusing the innocent, false oaths, and false testimony. And God is encompassing of what they do Nothing escapes Him.
4:109: 109 "Here you are" subject and predicate. "You argued for them in the worldly life a clause explaining the occurrence of these" as a predicate or a relative clause for those who make it a relative clause. "Then who will argue for them with God on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their advocate" an advocate who protects them from punishment.
4:110: 110 And whoever does evil ugly, causing harm to others. Or wrongs himself with what is specific to him and does not extend beyond him. It was said that what is meant by evil is less than polytheism, and by wrongdoing is polytheism. It was said: small and big. Then seeks forgiveness from God by repentance. He will find God Forgiving of his sins. Merciful and gracious to him. In it is an urging for Ta'mah and his people to repent and seek forgiveness.
4:111: 111 And whoever commits sin, he commits it only against himself so it does not extend beyond him and its consequences, as God Almighty says: And if you do evil, it is against you. "And God is Knowing and Wise" so He is All-Knowing of his actions and Wise in his punishment.
4:112: 112 And whoever commits a sin small or unintentional, or a major sin or what was intentional, and then throws it at an innocent person as Ta'mah threw at Zayd, and the pronoun was made singular in place of or. "has incurred slander and a manifest sin" because of throwing at an innocent person and acquitting the sinful soul, and therefore he made them equal even if the one was committed without the other.
4:113: 113 And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy by informing you of what they are upon through revelation, and the pronoun refers to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. A party of them meaning from Banu Thafar would have resolved to mislead you from judging with truth despite their knowledge of the situation, and the sentence is the answer to had it not been and the intention in it is not to deny their resolve but to deny its effect on it. And they mislead none but themselves because it is not what made you slip from the truth and its consequences returned upon them. And they do not harm you at all for God, the Most High, the Most Great, protected you and what crossed your mind was your reliance on the apparent meaning of the matter and not a bias in the judgment, and from something is in the accusative case as a source, meaning any harm. And God has sent down upon you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you did not know of the hidden matters, or of the matters of religion and rulings. And the grace of God upon you is great because there is no grace greater than prophethood.
4:114: 114 There is no good in much of their private conversation from their private conversations, as God Almighty says: And when they are in private conversation or from their private conversations, so His saying: Except for he who enjoins charity or righteousness is based on the deletion of an adjective, meaning except for a private conversation from an order, or on the disconnection meaning but whoever enjoins charity, then in his private conversation is goodness, and righteousness is everything that the Shari'ah approves of and reason does not reject. And He interpreted it here as a loan, helping the distressed, voluntary charity, and all that it was interpreted as. Or reconciliation between people or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of God - then We are going to give him a great reward The speech is based on the command and the reward is arranged according to the action and the consideration of the command in terms of it being a connection to it, and the action is restricted to saying to seek the pleasure of God Almighty, because actions are according to intentions and whoever does good for show and reputation does not deserve a reward from God for it. The reward was described as great, as a reminder of the insignificance of the worldly benefits he missed. Hamza and Abu Amr read yu’tihi with a ya’.
4:115: 115 And whoever contradicts the Messenger opposes him, from the side, for each of the two who differ is on a side other than the side of the other. After guidance has become clear to him the truth has become clear to him by standing on the miracles. And follows a way other than the way of the believers other than what they are upon of belief or action. We will give him what he has taken We will make him a guardian of what he has taken upon of misguidance, and we will leave between him and what he has chosen. And we will drive him into Hell and we will enter him into it. And it was read with the opening of the noon from prayer. And an evil destination is Hell. The verse indicates the prohibition of disobeying consensus, because God Almighty has imposed a severe threat on disobedience and following a path other than that of the believers, either because each of them is prohibited, or one of them, or the combination of both. The second is invalid, as it is ugly to say that whoever drinks alcohol and eats bread deserves the punishment. Likewise the third, because disobedience is prohibited, whether or not something else is added to it. If following a path other than theirs is prohibited, then following their path is obligatory, because abandoning following their path by someone who knows their path is following a path other than theirs. I have discussed this in detail in Marsad al-Afham ila Mabdil al-Ahkam.
4:116: 116 God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. He repeated it for emphasis, or for the story of Ta'mah. It was said, "An old man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I am an old man exhausted by sins. However, I have not associated anything with God since I knew Him and believed in Him, and I have not taken anyone as a guardian besides Him, and I have not committed sins out of boldness, and I have not imagined for the blink of an eye that I could escape from God. I am regretful and repentant, so what do you see in my state before God, the Most High, the Most Great? Then the verse was revealed, "And whoever associates anything with God has certainly strayed far astray." From the truth, for association is the greatest type of misguidance and the furthest from correctness and rectitude. It was only mentioned in the first verse that he fabricated because it is connected to the story of the People of the Book, and the origin of their association was a type of fabrication, which is the claim of adoption by God, the Most High, the Most Great. 4:117: 117 They invoke besides Him only female idols meaning Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, Manat, and the like. Every tribe had an idol that they worshipped and called the female of the Banu So-and-so. This was either because their names were feminine, as he said: And what was mentioned, if it becomes fat, it is a female, very stubborn, and has no molars. It meant the tick, which was small and was called a tick, and when it grew it was called a nipple, or because it was inanimate and inanimate objects are feminine because they resemble females but have no benefit, and perhaps the Almighty mentioned it with this name to alert that they worship what they call females because it is passive and does not act, and it is the right of the worshipped to be an agent and not a passive one, to be evidence of the extremes of their ignorance and extreme foolishness. And it was said that what was meant was the angels because they said: The angels are the daughters of God, the Almighty, and it is the plural of female like rabab and rabbi, and female was read for the sake of monotheism and that we on the basis that it is the plural of feminine like khabath and khabeeth, and wthana with the lightening and wthana with the emphasis and it is the plural of wthana like Assad and Asad and Asad, and athna and athna with them on the conversion of the waw because of its damma as a hamza. And if they call upon and that they worship by worshipping her. “Except a rebellious devil,” because he is the one who ordered them to worship it and tempted them to do so, so it is as if obeying him in that is worshipping him. The rebellious and rebellious are the ones who do not cling to good. The origin of the construction is for association. From this comes a beardless palace, “a beardless boy,” and a beardless tree, meaning one whose leaves are scattered.
4:118: 118 May God curse him is a second description of Satan. And he said, 'I will surely take from among Your servants a prescribed portion.' This is connected to him, meaning a rebellious Satan, combining the curse of God, and this statement indicating the extreme hostility of his people. God Almighty first proved that polytheism is an extreme misguidance by way of explanation, that what they associate with Him is affected and does not do an action voluntarily, and this contradicts divinity in the utmost contradiction, for the deity should be an agent and not a passive one. Then He proved that it is the worship of Satan, which is the most horrible misguidance for three reasons. The first: that he is a willful person immersed in misguidance and does not cling to anything of goodness and guidance, so obeying him is misguidance far from guidance. The second: that he is cursed for his misguidance, so obeying him does not bring about anything but misguidance and cursing. The third: that he is extremely hostile and strives to destroy them, and his friendship with someone like this is extremely misguidance, let alone worshipping him. The presumed and definite is a share that is determined for me and an obligation from their saying an obligation for him in giving.
4:119: 119 And I will mislead them from the truth. And I will arouse in them false hopes such as long life and no resurrection or punishment. And I will command them to slit the ears of cattle they will slit them to forbid what God has made lawful. This is an expression of what the Arabs used to do with the lakes and the sawa'ib, and an indication of the forbidding of what has been made lawful and the deficiency of everything that was created perfect in actuality or potential. And I will command them to change the creation of God of His face, image or description. This includes what has been said about gouging out the eye of the protector, castrating slaves, tattooing, tattooing, sodomy, crushing, and the like, and worshipping the sun and the moon, and changing the nature of God, the Most High, which is Islam, and using the limbs and powers in what does not bring perfection to the soul nor does it bring it nearness to God, the Most High. The generality of the wording prohibits castration absolutely, but the jurists have made a specific exception to castrating animals out of necessity. The four sentences are a narration of what Satan mentioned verbally or did to him in action. And whoever takes Satan as a friend instead of God by preferring what he calls to over what God has commanded and by going beyond obeying God to obeying him. He has certainly suffered a manifest loss if he wastes his capital and exchanges his place in Paradise for a place in Hell.
4:120: 120 He promises them" what he does not accomplish. "And he gives them hopes" of what they do not attain. "And Satan promises them nothing but delusion" which is showing benefit when there is harm in it. This promise is either through corrupt thoughts, or through the tongues of his followers.
4:121: 121 Their abode is Hell, and they will find no escape from it. It is a modifier and an escape from the verb haas which means to deviate from it, and it is not a relative clause because it is a place name, and if it is made a source, it does not work in what precedes it.
4:122: 122 "And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. The promise of God is true." That is, His promise is a promise and that is truly true. The first is an affirmation of itself because the content of the nominal sentence before it is a promise, and the second is an affirmation of something else. It is permissible to make the relative pronoun accusative with a verb that is explained by what comes after it. God promised by His saying We will admit them because it means We promise them their admission, and truly as a state of the source. And who is more truthful than God in statement? is an affirming and eloquent sentence. The purpose of the verse is to oppose the false satanic promises of his companions with the true promise of God to His friends, and to exaggerate in emphasizing it to encourage the servants to attain it.
4:123: 123 Not by your desires nor by the desires of the People of the Book meaning that what God has promised of reward is not attained by your desires, O Muslims, nor by the desires of the People of the Book, but rather it is attained by faith and righteous deeds. It was said: Faith is not by wishing, but rather what is established in the heart and proven by deeds. It was narrated (that the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted. The People of the Book said: Our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book came before your Book, and we are closer to God than you. The Muslims said: We are closer to you than you. Our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our Book supersedes the previous books), so it was revealed. It was said: The address is to the polytheists and this is indicated by their previous mention, i.e. the matter is not according to the wishes of the polytheists, which is their saying there is no Paradise and no Hell, and their saying if the matter is as these people claim we will be better than them and in a better state, nor according to the wishes of the People of the Book, which is their saying: None will enter Paradise except he who is a Jew or a Christian and their saying: The Fire will not touch us except for a few days then he confirmed that and said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it sooner or later because it was narrated that “when it was revealed Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: So who will be saved with this, O Messenger of God? He, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Are you not sad, are you not sick, are you not afflicted with opinions? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: That is it.” And he will not find for himself besides God a protector or a helper and he will not find for himself if he exceeds the friendship and support of God someone who will befriend him and help him in repelling the punishment from him.
4:124: 124 And whoever does righteous deeds some or some of them, for not everyone is able to do all of them and is not charged with them. Whether male or female is in the position of a state of the implied in works, and from is for clarification or from the righteous deeds, i.e. whether male or female, and from is for the beginning. And he is a believer is a state of the condition of coupling the work with it in calling for the mentioned reward and drawing attention to the fact that it is not taken into account without it in it. Then those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, even as much as a speck by reducing any of the reward, and if the reward of the obedient is not reduced, then it is more appropriate that the punishment of the disobedient will not be increased, because the rewarder is the most merciful of the merciful, and therefore it was limited to mentioning it after the reward. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Abu Bakr read enter Paradise here and in Ghafir and Maryam with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the kha, and the rest with a fatha on the ya and a damma on the kha.
4:125: 125 And who is better in religion than he who submits himself to God? He devotes himself to God, not knowing any lord other than Him. It was said that he offered his face to Him in prostration. In this questioning there is an indication that this is the limit of human strength. And he is a doer of good, doing good deeds and abandoning evil. And follows the religion of Abraham, which is in agreement with the religion of Islam, the authenticity of which is agreed upon. Hanif, deviating from all other religions, and it is a state of the follower or of the religion or Abraham. And God took Abraham as a friend, He chose him and singled him out with an honor similar to the honor of a friend with his friend. He only mentioned him repeatedly and did not imply glorification of his status and explicitly stating that he is the one being praised. Friendship is from the characteristics, for it is a desire to penetrate the soul and mix with it. It was said from the defect, if one of the two friends fills the defect of the other, or from the friend, which is the path in the sand, then they accompany each other on the path, or from the friend in the sense of the characteristic, then they agree on the characteristics. The sentence is a resumption that was brought to encourage following his religion, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to indicate that he is the ultimate in beauty and the ultimate perfection of mankind. It was narrated that Abraham, peace be upon him, sent to a close friend of his in Egypt during a crisis that had befallen the people, and he was distinguished from him. His close friend said: If Abraham wanted this for himself, I would have done it, but he wants it for the guests, and what has befallen the people has befallen us. So his servants passed by a soft plain and filled it with small baskets out of shyness from the people. When they told Abraham, the report upset him, and his eyes overcame him and he slept. Sarah went to one of her baskets and brought out small baskets and baked bread. Abraham, peace be upon him, woke up and smelled the bread, so he said: Where did you get this from? She said: From your Egyptian close friend, but rather it is from the two close friends of God Almighty, so God named him a close friend.
4:126: 126 And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth creation and dominion. He chooses from them whomever He wills and whatever He wills. It was said that it is connected to the mention of the workers, establishing the obligation of His obedience on the people of the heavens and the earth, and the perfection of His power is to reward them for their deeds. And God is encompassing of all things encompassing knowledge and power, so He was aware of their deeds and rewarded them for their good and evil.
4:127: 127 And they ask you about women about their inheritance, since the reason for its revelation "is that Uyaynah ibn Hisn came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Tell us that you give the daughter half and the sister half, and we only inherit from those who witness the fighting and allow the spoils, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Thus I was commanded." "Say: God gives you a fatwa about them" He explains to you His ruling on them, and fatwa is the clarification of what is unclear. And what is recited to you in the Book is an appositive to the name of God Almighty, or its pronoun implied in gives you a fatwa, and it is permissible for separation, so the fatwa is attributed to God Almighty and to what is in the Qur’an from His saying, God commands you and the like, and the single action is attributed to two different agents with two different considerations, and its equivalent is Zayd enriched me and their giving, or a resumption to magnify what is recited to them, on the basis that what is recited to you is the subject and in the Book is its predicate. It means the Preserved Tablet. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case, meaning He explains to you what He dictates to you, or in the genitive case, as if it were said: And I swear by what is recited to you in the Book. It is not permissible to conjoin it with the genitive case, in them, because it is incorrect in wording. The meaning of in the orphan women is the relative clause of is recited, if the relative clause is conjoined with what precedes it, meaning is recited to you regarding them, otherwise in them is a substitute for in them, or another relative clause to give you a fatwa, meaning God gives you a fatwa regarding them because of the orphan women, as you say: I spoke to you today about Zayd. This addition has the meaning of from, because it is an addition of something to its kind. It was read in my mother with two ya’s, meaning in my mother, so its hamza was changed to a ya’. “Those whom you do not give what is written for them” means what is prescribed for them of inheritance. And you desire to marry them whether to marry them or not to marry them, because the guardians of orphans desire them if they are beautiful and eat their wealth, otherwise they prevent them in the hope of their inheritance. And the waw may be interpreted as a state or a conjunction, and there is no evidence in it for the permissibility of marrying an orphan girl, since the desire to marry her does not necessarily mean that the contract was concluded while she was young. And the weak among the children is an conjunction to the orphan women and the Arabs did not inherit them as they did not inherit women. And that you stand up for orphans with justice is also an appositive to it, meaning: And He orders you or what is recited regarding that you stand up, this is if you make orphans a connection to one of them, but if you make it a substitute, then the correct way is to make them both accusative in appositive to the position of in them, and it is permissible to make and that you stand up accusative by implying a verb, meaning: And He orders you to stand up, and it is an address to the imams to look after them and fulfill their rights, or to stand up fairly in their matter. And whatever good you do, then indeed, God is ever Knowing of it, a promise to whoever prefers good in that.
4:128: 128 And if a woman fears her husband she expects from him because of the signs that appear to her, and woman is the subject of an action that is explained by the apparent meaning. Nushooz means avoiding her and being too proud to be with her out of dislike for her and denying her rights. Or turning away by reducing her company and conversation. "There is no blame upon them if they make peace between themselves" that they reconcile by reducing some of the dowry, or a portion, or giving him something to win him over. The Kufians read an sehliha from asla bain al-mutanatha'inu, and based on this it is permissible for sehliha to be in the accusative case as a direct object, and between them is a circumstance or state of it or as a source as in the first reading and the direct object between them or it is deleted. It was read yisliha from aslaha meaning to reconcile. And reconciliation is better than separation or bad treatment or quarrel. It is not permissible to mean preference, but rather to clarify that it is one of the good things, just as quarreling is one of the evils, and this is an objection. Likewise, His statement: And the souls have brought forth greed, and therefore the lack of similarity between them is forgiven. The first is to encourage reconciliation, and the second is to pave the way for an excuse for bargaining. The meaning of bringing forth greed is to make it present to him and natural to him, so that the woman hardly allows him to turn away from her and fall short in her rights, nor does the man allow him to keep her and fulfill her rights as he should if he hates her or loves someone else. And if you do good in your company. And fear rebellion, turning away, and lacking in rights. Indeed, God is ever, of what you do of doing good and quarreling. Aware of it and of the purpose in it, so He will reward you for it. He established His being aware of their actions in place of His affirming them for them, which is in reality the answer to the condition, establishing the cause in place of the effect.
4:129: 129 "And you will never be able to be fair between wives" because justice means that there is no deviation at all, and that is impossible. Therefore, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to divide between his wives fairly and say: "This is my division of what I own, so do not hold me accountable for what you own and I do not own. Even if you are keen" that is, on seeking that and going to extremes in it. "Do not incline completely" by abandoning what is possible and being unjust to what is desired from her, because what cannot be attained in its entirety should not be abandoned in its entirety. "Leave her as one in suspense" who is neither married nor divorced. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Whoever has two wives and is inclined towards one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side of him leaning. And if you amend" what you were corrupting in their affairs. "And fear God" in the future. "Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful" He will forgive you for what has passed of your inclination.
4:130: 130 And if they separate and it was read: And if each of them separates from the other. "God will enrich each" of them from the other with a substitute or consolation. "From His abundance" His wealth and power. "And God is Bountiful and Wise" Powerful and perfect in His actions and judgments.
4:131: 131 And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is a warning of the perfection of His vastness and power. And We have already enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you meaning the Jews and Christians, and those before them, and the Scripture is for the genus and of is related to We enjoined upon or to they were given and the context of the verse is to emphasize the command to be sincere. And you is in apposition to those. To fear God by fearing God, and it is possible that that is an explanatory particle because the recommendation is in the sense of saying. And if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth meaning saying, meaning: And We said to them and to you that you should disbelieve, for God is the Owner of all sovereignty and is not harmed by your disbelief and disobedience, just as He does not benefit from your gratitude and piety, and He only enjoined upon you out of His mercy, not out of His need. Then He confirmed that by saying: And God is Rich from the creation and their worship. Praiseworthy in His essence, praiseworthy even if He is not praised.
4:132: 132 And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He mentioned it thirdly to indicate that He is Rich and Praiseworthy, for all creatures demonstrate their need for His Richness and what He bestowed upon them of existence and various characteristics and perfections on Him as being Praiseworthy.
