And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs. refers to His statement, God enriches each from His abundance, for He entrusted them with their sufficiency and what is between them is an affirmation of that.
4:133: 133 "If He wills, He can take you away, O people. He will annihilate you, and the object of wills" is omitted and indicated by the answer. "And He will bring others." And He will create another people or another creation in place of the people. "And God is over that" from annihilation and creation. "Powerful." Eminent in power, nothing is beyond His power, and this is also a confirmation of His wealth and power, and a threat to those who disbelieve in Him and disobey His command. It was said: It is addressed to those Arabs who opposed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its meaning is the meaning of the Almighty's saying: "And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people," because it was narrated: "When it was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck his hand on the back of Salman and said: They are the people of this one."
4:134: 134 Whoever desires the reward of this world is like the mujahid who strives for the spoils. With God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. So why should he seek the lesser of the two? Let him seek them both, as if he says: Our Lord, give us in this world that which is good and in the Hereafter that which is good, or let him seek the more honorable of the two, for whoever strives sincerely for God, the Most High, the Most Great, the spoils will not miss him, and in the Hereafter he will have what is beside him, nothing. Or with God are two abodes, so He gives each one what he wants, as the Most High says: Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter - We increase for him in his harvest (al-Baqarah 2:134), And God is Hearing and Seeing, Knowing of the purposes, so He rewards each one according to his intention.
4:135: 135 O you who have believed, be persistent in justice persevering in justice and striving to establish it. Witnesses for God in truth, establishing your testimonies for the sake of God, the Most High, and this is a second piece of report or a state. Even if it is against yourselves even if the testimony is against yourselves by admitting to it, because testimony is a statement of the truth whether it is against him or someone else. Or parents and relatives even if it is against your parents and relatives. If that is, the one against whom the testimony is testified or each one of him and the one for whom the testimony is testified, he is rich or poor then do not refrain from establishing the testimony, or do not be unjust in it out of bias or compassion. God is more worthy of them both the rich and the poor and of looking after them. If testifying against them or for them was not good for Him, He would not have legislated it. This is the reason for the answer, and it was established in its place. The pronoun in them both refers to what was mentioned, which is the genus of the rich and the poor, not to Him. Otherwise, it would have been alone. What bears witness to this is that it was read God is more worthy of them. "So do not follow desire, lest you turn away" because you turn away from the truth or dislike to turn away from justice. "And if you twist" your tongues from testifying to the truth or the rule of justice. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Abu Amr, Asim, and Al-Kisa'i read it with a sukoon on the lam and after it the first waw is damma and the second is sukoon. Hamzah and Ibn Amir read "And if you turn away" meaning if you turn away to establish the testimony and perform it. "Or turn away" from performing it. "For God is ever, with what you do, Knowing" so He will reward you for it.
4:136: 136 O you who have believed is addressed to the Muslims, or to the hypocrites, or to the believers of the People of the Book, as it was narrated: Ibn Salam and his companions said, O Messenger of God: We believe in you and your book and in Moses and the Torah and Ezra, and we disbelieve in everything else. So it was revealed. Believe in God and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down to His Messenger and the Book which He sent down before Be steadfast in believing in that and continue with it, or believe in it with your hearts as you believed with your tongues, or believe with a general belief that includes the books and messengers, for belief in each part is faith, and the first book is the Qur’an and the second is the genus. Nafi' and the Kufians read: which He sent down and which He sent down with the opening of the noon, the hamza, and the zay, and the rest with the damma of the noon, the hamza, and the kasra of the zay. And whoever disbelieves in God and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day meaning whoever disbelieves in any of that. He has gone far astray from the goal to the point that he can hardly find his way back.
4:137: 137 Those who believed meaning the Jews believed in Moses, peace be upon him. Then they disbelieved when they worshipped the calf. Then they believed after his return to them. Then they disbelieved in Jesus, peace be upon him. Then they increased in disbelief in Muhammad, peace be upon him, or a people who repeatedly apostatized and then persisted in disbelief and increased in their persistence in error. God would not forgive them nor guide them to a way since it is unlikely that they would repent from disbelief and remain steadfast in faith, for their hearts were struck with disbelief and their insights were blinded to the truth, not that if they were sincere in faith, it would not be accepted from them and they would not be forgiven. The predicate of was in such cases is omitted and the letter lam is attached to it, such as: God was not willing to forgive them.
4:138: 138 Give the hypocrites tidings that they will have a painful punishment. This indicates that the verse is about the hypocrites, who believed outwardly and disbelieved in secret time after time, then increased in their insistence on hypocrisy and corrupting matters for the believers. The placement of give the hypocrites in place of warned is to mock them.
4:139: 139 Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers in the accusative case, or in the nominative case for blame, meaning that I mean those or they are those. Do they seek honor with them? Do they seek honor through their friendship? For honor belongs entirely to God. No one is honored except he whom God has honored, and He has written honor for His allies, saying: And to God belongs honor and to His Messenger and to the believers. He does not pay attention to the honor of others in comparison to them.
4:140: 140 And it has been revealed to you in the Book meaning the Qur'an. Asim read was revealed and the rest read was revealed in the passive form and the subject is in place of its subject. That when you hear the verses of God which is the lightened form and the meaning is that when you hear. disbelieve in them and mock at them are two states of the verses that were brought to restrict the prohibition of sitting in His statement: So do not sit with them until they engage in another conversation which is the reward of the condition if the one sitting with him is mocking, stubborn and not hopeful, and the goal supports it. This is a reminder of what was revealed to them in Mecca from His statement: And when you see those who engage in discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them the verse. The pronoun in with them refers to the disbelievers indicated by His statement disbelieve in them and mock at them. Indeed, you are like them in sin because you are able to turn away from them and deny them, or disbelieve if you are satisfied with that, or because those who sit with those who engage in the Qur’an from the rabbis were hypocrites, and this is indicated by: Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together meaning those who sit and those who are seated with them. And then it is cancelled because it occurs between the noun and the predicate, and therefore the verb and the singular like them were not mentioned after it, because it is like a source or for the sake of sufficiency in addition to the plural. And it was read with the fat-ha on the construction because of its addition to a construction like the Almighty’s saying: like you speak.
4:141: 141 Those who lie in wait for you are waiting for something to happen to you, and it is a substitute for those who take, or an attribute of the hypocrites and the disbelievers, or a blame raised or lowered or a subject whose predicate is. And if you have a victory from God, they will say, Were we not with you" supporting you, so give us a share of what you have gained. "And if the disbelievers have a share" of the war, then it is a contest. "They will say, Did we not gain control over you? That is, they said to the disbelievers: Did we not defeat you and be able to kill you, so we spared you? Gaining control is domination, and the analogy would have been to say istihaadh to gain control is yastadhah to gain control, so it came according to the original. And we protect you from the believers by letting them down by imagining what weakened their hearts and our delay in supporting them, so they made us share in what you gained. The victory of the Muslims was called a victory and the victory of the disbelievers was called a share because of their lowly fortune, because it is limited to a worldly matter that quickly passes away. So God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers. Then or in this world, and what is meant by the way is the argument, and our companions used it as evidence of the invalidity of the purchase of a Muslim by a disbeliever. The Hanafis hold that separation occurs by the apostasy itself, and this is weak because it does not negate the possibility that it could happen if he returns to faith before the waiting period has passed.
4:142: 142 "The hypocrites seek to deceive God, but He will deceive them." This was discussed at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. "And when they stand up for prayer, they stand lazily," sluggishly as if forced to do something. "Lazy" is read with a fat-ha, and they are the plural of lazy. "They show off to people," to make them think they are believers. Showing off is a reciprocal verb with the meaning of activation, like na'am and na'am, or for comparison, for the hypocrite shows the one he is showing off his work while he shows him his approval. "And they do not remember God except a little," for the hypocrite does not act except in the presence of the one he is showing off to, and this is the least of his states, or because their remembrance with the tongue is little in comparison to the remembrance with the heart. It was said that what is meant by remembrance is prayer. It was said that remembrance in it is that they do not remember in it except for glorification and taslim.
4:143: 143 "Wavering between that is a state of the waw of showing off" like his saying: "And they do not remember" meaning they show off to them not remembering, wavering or the waw of remembering or accusative of blame, and the meaning: wavering between faith and disbelief from the wavering which is to make something disturbed, and its origin is which means expulsion. And it was read with a kasra on the dhal meaning they waver their hearts or their religion or they waver like their saying: Salsal meaning to rattle. And it was read with the non-voweled dhal meaning they took sometimes in a deluge and sometimes in a deluge which is the way. "Neither to these nor to these" neither attributed to the believers nor to the disbelievers, or not going to one of the two groups completely. "And he whom God sends astray - you will not find for him a way" to the truth and the right, and similar to it is the saying of the Most High: "And he for whom God has not appointed light - for him there is no light."
4:144: 144 O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. For that is the action and religion of the hypocrites, so do not imitate them. Do you want to make for God a clear authority over you? A clear argument, for their allegiance is evidence of hypocrisy or an authority that will impose His punishment upon you.
4:145: 145 The hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire which is the level at the bottom of Hell, and it is only that way because they are the most evil of the disbelievers, as they added to disbelief mockery of Islam and deceit of the Muslims. As for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "Three things, whoever has them is a hypocrite, even if he fasts and prays and claims to be a Muslim: whoever lies when he speaks, breaks his promise, and betrays when he is entrusted" and the like, it is from the aspect of comparison and emphasis, and its seven levels were called levels because they are successive and one above the other. The Kufians read it with a sukoon on the ra', which is a language, and like the line and the line, and the movement is more appropriate because it is pluralized as idrak. And you will not find for them a helper to take them out of it.
4:146: 146 Except for those who repent from hypocrisy. And put right what they corrupted of their secrets and conditions while they were hypocrites. And hold fast to God and trust in Him or adhere to His religion. And make their religion sincere for God they do not desire by their obedience anything but His noble face, glory be to Him, the Most High. Then those will be with the believers and among their number in both abodes. And God will give the believers a great reward so they will share in it with them.
4:147: 147 What would God do with your punishment if you were grateful and believed? Would He satisfy his anger with it, or repel harm with it, or bring about benefit with it, while He is the Rich and Exalted above benefit or harm? The one who persists in his disbelief is only punished because his persistence in it is like a bad temperament that leads to illness. If he removes it with faith and gratitude - and denies himself of it - he is freed from its consequences. He only presented gratitude because the one who looks first realizes the blessing, so he gives vague thanks, then he looks carefully until he knows the benefactor and believes in him. And God is Ever Appreciative Rewarding, accepting the little and giving the abundant. Knowing of the truth of your gratitude and faith.
4:148: 148 God does not like the public mention of evil except by one who has been wronged. Except by one who has been wronged by praying against the wrongdoer and complaining about him. It was narrated that a man hosted some people and they did not feed him, so he complained about them and was reprimanded for it. So it was revealed and it was read from the wronged in the active form, so the exception is disconnected, meaning but the wrongdoer does what God does not like. And God is All-Hearing of the words of the wronged. All-Knowing of the wrongdoer.
4:149: 149 If you disclose good obedience and righteousness. Or conceal it or do it secretly. Or pardon an offense you will be held accountable for it, and this is what is intended. The mention of disclosing good and concealing it is an encouragement for it, and therefore He based His statement on it. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Powerful meaning He often pardons sinners despite His perfect ability to take revenge, so you are more deserving of that. It is an urging for the wronged to pardon after He has permitted him to wait, based on noble morals.
4:150: 150 Those who disbelieve in God and His messengers and want to make distinction between God and His messengers by believing in God and disbelieving in His messengers. And they say, 'We believe in some and disbelieve in others' We believe in some of the prophets and disbelieve in others. And they want to take a path in between a middle path between belief and disbelief, not a middle way: for the truth does not differ, for belief in God, the Most High, the Most Great, is not complete except by belief in His messengers and believing in what they conveyed from Him in detail and in general. So the one who disbelieves in some of that is like the one who disbelieves in all of it in misguidance, as God, the Most High, said: So what is there after the truth except misguidance?
4:151: 151 Those are the disbelievers They are the ones who are complete in disbelief, their belief is of no importance. Truly is a source confirming something else or an attribute of the source of the disbelievers, meaning: They are the ones who disbelieved truly, that is, with certainty and certainty. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
4:152: 152 And those who believed in God and His messengers and made no distinction between any of them their opposites and their counterparts, and the word between was used on one, and it requires multiple because of its generality, as it occurred in the context of negation. Those, He will give them their rewards promised to them, and it begins with sawfa to emphasize the promise and indicate that it will inevitably happen, even if it is delayed. Hafs, on the authority of Asim, and Qaloon, on the authority of Yaqub, read it with the letter ya to color the address. And God is Forgiving for what they neglected. Merciful to them by doubling their good deeds.
4:153: 153 The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. It was revealed about the Jewish rabbis. They said: If you are truthful, then bring us a book from the heaven in its entirety, just as Moses, peace be upon him, brought it. It was also said: A book written in heavenly script on tablets, just as the Torah was, or a book that we can see when it is revealed, or a book to us with our own eyes that you are the Messenger of God. They asked Moses something greater than that. The answer to an implied condition, meaning: If you find what they asked of you too great, they asked Moses, peace be upon him, something greater than that. This question, even though it was from their fathers, was attributed to them because they were taking their doctrine and following their guidance. The meaning is that their lineage is deeply rooted in that and that what they suggested to you was not the first of their ignorance and fantasies. They said, 'Show us God plainly.' Plainly, we will show Him, we will see Him plainly, or openly, witnessing Him. Then the thunderbolt seized them. A fire that came from the heaven and destroyed them. Because of their injustice because of their injustice, which is their stubbornness and their asking for what is impossible in the state they were in. This does not necessitate the absolute impossibility of seeing. Then they took the calf after the clear proofs had come to them. This is the second crime that their predecessors also committed, and the clear proofs are miracles, and it is not permissible to apply it to the Torah since it had not yet come to them. So We pardoned that and gave Moses clear authority. Clear authority over them when He commanded them to kill themselves in repentance for taking it.
4:154: 154 And We raised the mountain above them with their covenant because of their covenant so that they would accept it. And We said to them, Enter the gate, prostrating on the tongue of Moses, and the mountain was overshadowed by them. And We said to them, Do not transgress on the Sabbath on the tongue of David, peace be upon him. It is possible that it was intended on the tongue of Moses when the mountain overshadowed them, for the Sabbath was legislated, but transgression and transformation occurred during the time of David, peace be upon him. Warsh read from Nafi' Do not transgress on the basis that its original form is do not transgress, so the ta' was assimilated into the dal. Qaloon read by concealing the vowel of the 'ayn and doubling the dal, and the text from him is with the sukoon. And We took from them a firm covenant on that, which is their saying we hear and obey.
4:155: 155 Because they broke their covenant meaning they disobeyed and broke it, so We did to them what We did because of their breaking it. Ma is an additional word for emphasis, and the ya is related to the deleted verb. It is possible that it is related to We forbade them good things, so the prohibition is because of the deficiency. What is connected to it is due to injustice, not to what is indicated by His statement: Rather, God has set a seal upon them like they do not believe because it is a response to their saying Our hearts are covered, so it is from the relative clause, and their saying is connected to the accusative, so it does not work on its neighbor. And their disbelief in the signs of God in the Qur'an or what came in their book. And their killing of the prophets without right and their saying Our hearts are covered" are vessels for knowledge, or in coverings from what they call us to. "Rather, God has set a seal upon them because of their disbelief", so He made them veiled from knowledge, or He let them down and prevented them from being guided to ponder the signs and remember in the sermons. They do not believe except a few of them, such as Abdullah bin Salam, or a little faith, as it is not worth mentioning due to its deficiency.
4:156: 156 And their disbelief in Jesus, peace be upon him, and it is conjoined with and their disbelief because it is one of the reasons for nature, or with His saying: Then because of their violation and it is permissible to conjoin the whole of this and what is conjoined to it with the whole of what preceded it and the repetition of the mention of disbelief is an indication of the repetition of their disbelief, for they disbelieved in Moses, then in Jesus, then in Muhammad, peace be upon him. And their saying against Mary a great slander meaning their attribution of adultery to her.
4:157: 157 "And their saying, 'We have killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of God,'" meaning, according to their claim, and it is possible that they said it in mockery, and similar to it is that your Messenger who was sent to you is insane, and that it is a renewal from God Almighty in praising him, or placing a good mention in place of their ugly mention. "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it appeared to them as if they were." It was narrated (that a group of Jews insulted him and his mother, so he invoked God Almighty upon them, and God Almighty transformed them into monkeys and pigs. The Jews gathered to kill him, so God Almighty informed him that He would raise him to heaven, so he said to his companions: Which of you would be pleased to have my likeness cast upon him, so he would be killed and crucified and enter Paradise? So one of them stood up, and God cast his likeness upon him, so he was killed and crucified). It was said: He was a hypocrite who went out to guide him, so God cast his likeness on him, so he was captured, crucified, and killed. It was also said: The Jewish Titanus entered a house where he was and did not find him, and God cast his likeness on him, so when he went out, he thought that he was Jesus, so he was captured and crucified. And similar miracles are not unlikely in the time of prophethood, but God Almighty condemned them for what the speech indicated of their audacity towards God Almighty, and their intention to kill his prophet supported by dazzling miracles, and their boasting about him, not for their saying this according to their calculations, and like is attributed to the preposition and noun as if it was said but they made a comparison between Jesus and the one killed or in the matter according to the saying of the one who said: No one was killed but rumors of his killing spread among the people, or to the pronoun of the one killed to indicate that we killed someone. "And those who differed about it" regarding Jesus, peace be upon him, when that incident occurred, people differed. Some of the Jews said: He was a liar, so we killed him for real. Others hesitated, so some of them said: If this is Jesus, then where is our companion? Some of them said: The face is the face of Jesus and the body is the body of our companion. And whoever heard from him that God Almighty raises me to the heavens said: He was raised to the heavens. And some people said: The humanity was crucified and the divinity ascended. "In doubt about it" is in doubt. And doubt, as it is applied to what one of its two sides is not likely, is applied to absolute hesitation, and to what is opposite to knowledge. Therefore, He confirmed it by saying: "They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption" is a discontinuous exception, meaning, but they follow assumption. It is permissible to interpret doubt as ignorance and knowledge as the belief that the soul is content with, whether it is certain or otherwise, so the exception is connected. "And they did not kill him for certain a certain killing as they claimed in their saying We killed the Messiah", or certain. It was said that its meaning is what they knew for certain, like the poet's saying: That is what the scholars say about it, and I have killed them with my knowledge, that is certain. From their saying, I killed something knowingly and I slaughtered it knowingly if you want to exaggerate your knowledge.
4:158: 158 Rather, God raised him up to Himself and a denial of his killing and confirmation of his being raised up. And God is Exalted in Might He is not overcome by what He wills. Wise in what He planned for Jesus, peace be upon him.
4:159: 159 And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death meaning, there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him, so His saying will surely believe in him is a divisive clause that describes one and the second pronoun refers to him, and the first refers to Jesus, peace be upon him. The meaning is that there is none from the Jews and Christians but that he will surely believe that Jesus is the servant of God and His Messenger before he dies, even if it is until his soul is taken away and his belief will not benefit him. This is supported by the fact that it was read but that he will surely believe in him before his death with a damma on the letter nun because one is in the sense of a plural, and this is like a threat to them and an exhortation to treat faith in him before they are forced to do so and their belief will not benefit them. It was said that the two pronouns refer to Jesus, peace be upon him, and the meaning is that when he descends from the heavens, all people of religions will believe in him. It was narrated that when the Antichrist emerges, he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will descend from the sky and destroy him, and no one from the People of the Book will remain who will not believe in him, until the religion is one, which is the religion of Islam, and security will prevail until lions graze with camels, tigers with cows, wolves with sheep, and children play with snakes. He will remain on earth for forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them, so he will testify against the Jews that they lied and against the Christians that they called him the son of God.
4:160: 160 Then because of the wrongdoing of those who are Jews meaning because of any wrongdoing on their part. We prohibited for them [certain] good things which had been lawful to them meaning what He mentioned in His statement, And because of their averting many from the way of God many people or averting.
4:161: 161 And their taking of usury, although they were forbidden from it Usury was forbidden to them as it is forbidden to us, and in it is evidence that the prohibition indicates the prohibition. And their consuming of people's wealth unjustly through bribery and other forbidden means. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment without those who repent and believe.
4:162: 162 But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them such as Abdullah bin Salam and his companions. And the believers meaning among them or among the Muhajireen or Ansar. They believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you is the predicate of the subject. And those who establish prayer is in the accusative case for praise if they believe is made the predicate for those, or in apposition to what was revealed to you and what is meant by them are the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, meaning: they believe in the books and the prophets. It was read in the nominative case in apposition to the firmly rooted or to the pronoun in they believe or as a subject and the predicate Those We will give them. And those who give zakat is in the nominative case for one of the reasons mentioned. And the believers in God and the Last Day is presented before it belief in the prophets and books and what confirms it from following the laws because it is the intended meaning of the verse. Those We will give them a great reward for combining correct belief and righteous deeds. Hamza read We will give them with the ya.
4:163: 163 "Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him." This is an answer to the People of the Book regarding their suggestion that a book be sent down to them from heaven, and an argument against them that his command to reveal was like that of all the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. "And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon." He mentioned them specifically, while including the prophets, out of respect for them, for Abraham was the first of those of resolve among them, and Jesus was the last of them, and the rest are the most honorable and famous of the prophets. "And We gave David the Psalms. Hamza read Zabur" with a dammah, which is the plural of Zabar, meaning written.
4:164: 164 "And messengers" is in the accusative case with an implied noun that indicates We have revealed to you, like We have sent, or it is explained by: "We have already related them to you before" meaning before this surah or today. "And messengers We have not related them to you, and God spoke to Moses directly" which is the highest level of revelation that He singled out Moses from among them, and He favored Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by giving him the same as He gave each one of them.
4:165: 165 Messengers, bringing good tidings and warnings is an accusative of praise or by implying that we sent, or as a state, and messengers is a prelude to what comes after it, like saying I passed by Zayd, a righteous man. So that people will have no argument against God after the messengers and they will say, Why did you not send us a messenger to alert us and teach us what we did not know? It is a warning that the mission of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, to the people is necessary because everyone is unable to perceive the details of interests and most are unable to perceive their generalities. The lam is related to We sent or to His saying bringing good tidings and warnings, and argument is the noun of was and its predicate is for people or against God and the other is a state, and it is not permissible for it to be related to an argument because it is a source and after is a circumstance for it or an attribute. And God is Exalted in Might He is not overcome in what He wills. Wise in what He planned of the matter of prophethood and He distinguished each prophet with a type of revelation and miracle.
4:166: 166 But God bears witness is a correction of the meaning of what came before it, as if when they were stubborn with me by asking for a book to be sent down to them from the sky, and he argued with them by saying Indeed, We have revealed to you he said: They do not bear witness, but God bears witness, or they denied it, but God confirms it and confirms it. With what has been sent down to you of the miraculous Qur'an indicating your prophethood. It was narrated that when Indeed, We have revealed to you was revealed, they said: We do not bear witness to you, so it was sent down. He sent it down with His knowledge He sent it down while it was clothed in His special knowledge, which is the knowledge of its composition in a system that no eloquent speaker is capable of, or in a state of him preparing for prophethood and deserving the book to be sent down to him, or in His knowledge that people need in their livelihood and their covenants, so the preposition and the noun in the first two are a state of the subject and in the third a state of the object, and the sentence is like the explanation of what came before it and the angels bear witness also to your prophethood. It is a warning that they would like to know the validity of the claim of prophethood in a way that does not require contemplation and reflection. This type is one of the characteristics of the angels, and there is no way for a human being to know such things except through thought and contemplation. If these people had come with correct contemplation, they would have known your prophethood and testified to it, just as the angels knew and testified. And sufficient is God as a witness. That is, what He established of proofs for the validity of your prophethood is sufficient without relying on anyone else as evidence.
4:167: 167 Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God have certainly strayed far astray. Because they combined straying and leading others astray, and because the one who leads others astray is more deeply immersed in straying and further from abandoning it.
4:168: 168 Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, by denying his prophethood, or the people by turning them away from what is good for them and their salvation, or more generally than that. The verse indicates that the disbelievers are addressed by the branches, as what is meant by them are those who combine disbelief and injustice. God would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to a way.
4:169: 169 Except the path of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally forever. His previous ruling and inevitable promise were that whoever dies in disbelief will abide eternally in the Fire and will abide eternally in a predestined state. And that is easy for God. It is not difficult for Him nor is it too great for Him.
4:170: 170 O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord. When he established the matter of prophethood and explained the path leading to knowledge of it and the threat of those who deny it, he addressed the people in general with the call and the obligation of the argument and the promise of response and the threat of rejection. So believe, it is better for you. That is, a belief that is better for you or do something better for you than what you are doing. It was said that its meaning is that belief will be better for you, but the Basrans prevented it because kana is not deleted with its name except in what is necessary and because it leads to the condition and its response. And if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. That is, if you disbelieve, He is independent of you and is not harmed by your disbelief, just as He does not benefit from your belief. He pointed out His independence by saying: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, which includes what they contain and what they ride on from it. And God is Knowing of their conditions. Wise in what He planned for them.
4:171: 171 O People of the Scripture, do not go to extremes in your religion. The address is to both groups. The Jews went to extremes in belittling Jesus, peace be upon him, to the point that they accused him of being born from a mother's womb, and the Christians went to extremes in elevating him to the point that they took him as a god. It was said that the address was to the Christians in particular, as this is more in keeping with His statement: And do not say about God except the truth. Meaning, absolving Him of having a wife or a son. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was only a messenger of God and His word which He directed to Mary. He conveyed it to her and made it her. And a spirit from Him and the possessor of a spirit issued from Him through the mediation of what runs the course of the origin and substance for Him, and it was said that it was called a spirit because it revived the dead or the hearts. So believe in God and His messengers and do not say, 'Three' meaning the gods are three: God, Christ, and Mary. This is attested to by the words of God Almighty: Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as gods besides God' or God is three if it is true that they say God is three hypostases[*1] the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and they mean the Father in person, the Son is knowledge, and the Holy Spirit is life. Stop from the trinity. It is better for you He made it accusative as mentioned before. God is only one God meaning one in person, there is no multiplicity in Him in any way. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth a kingdom and creation that is not comparable to anything of that, so He takes Him as a son. And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs is a reminder of His independence from a son, for there is a need for Him to be a disposer of affairs for His Father, and God Almighty is sufficient in preserving things, independent of anyone who creates or assists Him. [*1] I think it is wrong and investigation is required. Because I didn't guess right...
4:172: 172 "The Messiah will not be ashamed" He will not be ashamed, from wiping away the tears if you remove them with your finger so that he does not see their trace on you. "To be a slave of God" from being a slave to Him, for his servitude is an honor that he boasts about, but rather for humiliation and disdain in the servitude of others. It was narrated that "the delegation of Najran said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Why do you criticize our companion? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And who is your companion? They said: Jesus, peace be upon him. He, peace be upon him, said: And what should I say? They said: You say that he is the slave and messenger of God. He said: It is not shameful to be the slave of God. They said: Yes. Then it was revealed: Nor the angels brought near in apposition to the Messiah, meaning that the angels brought near will not be ashamed to be slaves of God, and it was used as evidence by those who claimed that he preferred the angels over the prophets, peace be upon them. He said: Its context is to refute the Christians’ statement that Christ was elevated from a position of servitude, and that requires that the conjoined be of a higher degree than the conjoined to, so that their not refusing is like evidence of his not refusing. The answer to that is that the verse is to refute the worshippers of Christ and the angels, so that is not correct, even if we accept that it is specific to the Christians. Perhaps he intended by the conjoining to exaggerate by considering the multiplication without glorification, like your saying: The prince has become, and neither a leader nor a subordinate opposes him. If he intended by it glorification, then his ultimate aim is to give preference to those close to him from the angels, who are the cherubim who are around the throne, or those of them who are of a higher rank from the angels over Christ from the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. This does not require the preference of one gender over the other absolutely, and the dispute over it is and whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant and whoever rises above it, and arrogance is less than disdain, and that is why it is conjoined to it, and it is only used in terms of entitlement, unlike arrogance, which may be by entitlement. Then He will gather them all to Him so He will reward them.
4:173: 173 "As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their reward in full and increase them from His bounty. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper." A detailed account of the general recompense indicated by the content of the speech, as if he said, then He will gather them all together to Him on the Day when the servants are gathered for recompense, or for their recompense, for the reward of those who are in return for their kindness is a punishment for them with grief and regret.
4:174: 174 O mankind, there has come to you a proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a clear light. By proof he meant miracles, and by light he meant the Qur’an, meaning that the evidence of reason and the evidence of transmission have come to you, and you have no excuse or reason left. It was said: The proof is religion, or the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the Qur’an.
4:175: 175 But as for those who believed in God and held fast to Him, He will admit them into mercy from Him in a reward He has decreed in return for their faith and deeds, a mercy from Him, not a fulfillment of an obligatory right and grace an additional kindness to Him and He will guide them to Him to God, and it was said to the Promised One. A straight path is Islam and obedience in this world, and the path to Paradise in the Hereafter.
4:176: 176 "They ask you" i.e. in the case of kalalah, it was deleted because the answer indicated it. It was narrated that "Jabir ibn Abdullah was sick and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited him and said: I am kalalah, so what should I do with my money? So it was revealed" and it is the last ruling to be revealed. "Say: God gives you a ruling concerning kalalah" its explanation was previously mentioned at the beginning of the surah. "If a man dies and leaves no child but has a sister, she shall have half of what he leaves A man was raised by a verb that is explained by the apparent meaning, and he has no child is a description of him or a condition of what is implied in he died, and the and in and he has" may be a condition or a conjunction, and what is meant by the sister is the sister from both parents or the father because he made her brother an agnate and the son of the mother is not an agnate, and the son is according to its apparent meaning, because even if the sister inherits with the daughter according to most scholars - except Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both - she does not inherit half. "And he inherits her" i.e. and the man inherits if the matter is the other way around. If she has no child, whether male or female, if it is meant that he inherits from her, he inherits all of her money, otherwise it is meant for the male, since the daughter does not exclude the brother. The verse, just as it did not indicate that brothers are dropped without a son, did not indicate that they are not dropped because of him. The Sunnah indicated that they do not inherit with the father. The same is the meaning of His statement, Say, ‘God gives you a ruling concerning those who are not descendants,’ if it is interpreted as meaning the deceased. But if there are two of them, for them are two-thirds of what he leaves. The pronoun refers to those who inherit by brotherhood, and its dual form is interpreted in the meaning. The benefit of informing about it as two is to draw attention to the fact that the ruling is based on the number, not on young or old, etc. And if they are brothers, men and women, the male shall have the share of two females. Its origin is that if they are brothers and sisters, the male is predominant. God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, meaning that God makes clear to you your error, which is your nature when you are left alone with your natures, so that you guard against it and seek to contradict it, or He makes clear to you the truth and what is right, lest you go astray. It was said that so that you do not go astray, so la was deleted, and this is the opinion of the Kufians. And God is Knowing of all things, so He knows the interests of His servants in life and death. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Whoever recites Surat An-Nisa, it is as if he has given charity to every believing man and woman, and inherited an inheritance, and was given a reward like one who bought a freed slave, and was absolved of polytheism, and was, in the will of God Almighty, among those whom He overlooks.”
5:1: 1 O you who have believed, fulfill contracts. Fulfillment is carrying out the requirements of the covenant, as well as fulfillment and a binding covenant. Al-Hutay'ah said: A people who, when they make a contract with their neighbor, tighten the knot and burden him with hardship. Its origin is combining two things so that it is difficult to separate, and perhaps what is meant is Contracts include the contracts that God the Almighty has made with His servants and imposed on them of obligations, and what they make between themselves of contracts of trusts and transactions and the like that must be fulfilled, or it is better if we take the matter as common between obligation and recommendation. Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock is a detail of contracts, and the beast is every living creature that cannot distinguish. It was said that it is every quadruped, and adding it to livestock is for clarification, like saying: a silk garment, and its meaning is the beast from the livestock. They are the eight pairs, and the gazelle is included with them, and the wild beasts roost. It was said that they are what is meant by the beast and the like that resembles livestock in ruminating and lacking fangs, and adding it to livestock is for the close resemblance. Except what is recited to you except what is forbidden that is recited to you, like the Almighty’s saying: Forbidden to you is dead meat or except what is recited to you its prohibition. Except for the forbidden game is a state of the pronoun in for you and it was said from the waw of fulfill and it was said an exception and in it is arbitrariness and the game may be the source and the object. And you are in a sacred place is a state of what is implied in my place, and the sacred place is the plural of haram, which is the forbidden. Indeed, God decrees what He wills of making permissible or forbidden.
5:2: 2 "O you who have believed, do not violate the rites of God" meaning the rituals of Hajj, the plural of rite, which is the name of everything that is marked, i.e. made a symbol by which the actions of Hajj are named and agreed upon because they are the signs of Hajj and the flags of its ritual. It was said that it is the religion of God, based on the words of the Most High: "And whoever honors the rites of God" meaning His religion. It was also said that it is His obligations that He has set for His servants. "Nor the sacred month" by fighting in it or by postponing. "Nor the sacrificial animal" what is offered to the Kaaba, the plural of gift like a young goat in all the seriousness of the herding. "Nor the necklaces" meaning those with necklaces from the sacrificial animal, and its conjunction with the sacrificial animal is for specificity because it is the most honorable of the sacrificial animal, or the necklaces themselves, and the prohibition of making them permissible is an exaggeration in the prohibition of exposing the sacrificial animal, and similar to it is the words of the Most High: "And let them not display their adornment". Necklaces are the plural of necklace, which is what is hung on the sacrificial animal such as a sandal, tree bark, or other things to indicate that it is a sacrificial animal and not to interfere with it. Nor those who are at the Sacred House intending to visit it. They seek bounty from their Lord and approval that He may reward them and be pleased with them. The sentence is in the position of a state of the implied in Amin and not a description of it, because it is an agent. The preferred view is that the described active participle does not act, and its benefit is to denounce the attack of someone of this nature, drawing attention to the one who prevents it. It was said that its meaning is that they seek from God provision through trade and approval, according to their claim, since it was narrated that the verse was revealed in the year of the judgment regarding the pilgrims of Yamamah when the Muslims intended to attack them because among them was Al-Hutaym bin Shuraih bin Dhubay’ah, who had driven away the camels of Madinah. Based on this, the verse is abrogated. It was read tabtaghoon addressing the believers, And when you have finished the ritual state, hunt. So, it is about hunting after the end of the ritual state of ihram. The intention of permission here from the command does not necessarily indicate the command that comes after the prohibition on permission in general. It was read with a kasra on the fa’ to cast the connecting vowel on it, which is very weak. It was read halaltum it is said the forbidden state has finished and become permissible. wa la yujurmankum it is not to burden you or not to make you gain. Shanan qawm the intensity of their hatred and enmity, and it is a verbal noun added to the object or subject. Ibn Amir and Ismail from Nafi’ and Ibn Ayyash from Asim read with a sukoon on the nun, and it is also a verbal noun of kaliyan or na’t meaning: hated people, and fa’laan in the description is more common like ‘atshan’ and ‘sakran. that they prevented you from the Sacred Mosque because they prevented you from it in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read with a kasra on the hamza as an intervening condition that makes its answer unnecessary. wa la yujurmankum. "That you transgress with revenge, and it is the second object of yajrimnakum, as it is transitive to one or to two, like kasab". Whoever reads "yajrimnakum with a damma on the ya" makes it transferred from transitive to a direct object with a hamza to two objects. "And cooperate in righteousness and piety" in forgiving, overlooking, following the matter, and avoiding desires. "And do not cooperate in sin and aggression" to seek revenge. "And fear God; indeed, God is severe in penalty", so His vengeance is more severe.
5:3: 3 He has forbidden you dead animals is an explanation of what is recited to you, and dead animals are those from which the soul has departed without being slaughtered. And blood means spilled blood, as God the Almighty says: or blood poured forth, and the people of ignorance used to pour it into the intestines and roast them. And the flesh of swine and that which has been dedicated to other than God with it meaning raising the voice to other than God with it, like their saying: In the name of Al-Lat and Al-Uzza when slaughtering it. And the strangled means that which died by strangulation. And the beaten means that which was struck with something like wood or stone until it died from its beating if it was struck. And the fallen means that which fell from a height or into a well and died. And the gored means that which was gored by another and died from the goring, and the ta' in it is for transfer. And that which a wild beast has eaten means that which a wild beast has eaten from and died, and it indicates that if the game animals eat what they have hunted, it is not permissible. Except what you have slaughtered except what you have found slaughtered and in it there is a stable life from that. It was said that the exception is specific to what the beast has eaten. And the slaughter in the Sharia is to cut the throat and esophagus with a sharp tool. And that which is slaughtered on altars The altar is one of the altars, which are stones that were erected around the House and they slaughtered on them and they consider that an offering. It was said that they are idols and on means the lam or on its origin with the estimation and what was slaughtered is named on the idols. It was said that it is a plural and the singular is nasab. And that you seek division by arrows meaning it is forbidden for you to seek division by arrows, and that is because if they intend to do something, they draw three lots. Written on one of them is: My Lord has commanded me. On the other is: My Lord has forbidden me. And the third is a fool. If the command is issued, they continue with that, and if the prohibition is issued, they avoid it, and if the fool is issued, they postpone it a second time. So the meaning of seeking division is to seek to know what has been divided for them and not what has not been divided for them by the arrows. It was said that it is the drawing of camels by arrows on the known shares, and the singular of the arrows is zalam like a camel and zalam like a sard. That is transgression refers to the use of divination, and it is transgression because it is entering into the knowledge of the unseen and misguidance in believing that this is a path to it, and a slander against God, the Most High, if God is meant by my Lord, and ignorance and polytheism if it is meant by an idol or forbidden gambling or consuming what was forbidden to them. Today does not refer to a specific day, and it was revealed after the afternoon of Friday in Arafat during the Farewell Pilgrimage. Those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion meaning that it will be invalidated and you will turn back from it through the trickery of these evils and others, or that they will overcome you in it. So do not fear them that they will prevail over you. And fear Me and sincerely fear Me. Today I have perfected your religion for you by giving victory and making it victorious over all religions, or by specifying the principles of beliefs and stopping at the foundations of the laws and the rules of ijtihad. And I have completed My favor upon you by guidance and success or by completing the religion or by conquering Mecca and demolishing the beacons of ignorance. And I have approved for you Islam as religion I have chosen it for you as a religion from among the religions, and it is the religion with God and no other. But whoever is forced is connected to the mention of the forbidden things, and what is between them is an objection to what necessitates avoiding them, which is that consuming them is an act of disobedience, and their prohibition is part of the perfect religion, complete blessing, and acceptable Islam. The meaning is: So whoever is forced to consume any of these forbidden things, in a state of famine “without inclining toward sin” “without inclining toward it or deviating toward it by eating them for pleasure or exceeding the limit of the concession as He says: “without transgressing [their duty] nor exceeding [the limits of] transgression.” Then God is Forgiving and Merciful He will not hold him accountable for eating them.
5:4: 4 They ask you what is lawful for them since the question includes the meaning of saying, it is applied to the sentence, and the discussion of what has already been mentioned, and he said to them and did not say to us in the narrative, because they ask you is in the third person, and both aspects are permissible in similar cases, and the one being asked is what is lawful for them from the foods, as if when what was forbidden to them was recited to them, they asked about what was lawful for them. "Say: Lawful for you are the good things" what sound natures do not find repugnant or repel from, and from its implication the repugnant things of the Arabs are forbidden, or what no text or analogy indicates are forbidden. And what you have taught of the birds of prey is in apposition to the good things if you make what a relative pronoun, assuming that you have taught the game, and a conditional sentence if you make it a condition and its answer is so eat and the birds of prey are the prey of their owners from the four-legged beasts and birds with dogs teaching them to hunt, and the dog is the one who trains the birds of prey and harms them with hunting. Derived from the word dog, because discipline is more effective in it, or because every beast is called a dog, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O God, send upon it a dog from among your dogs. Its accusative case is in the state of you taught them, and its benefit is the exaggeration of the teaching. You teach them is a second state or a resumption. From what God taught you of tricks and methods of discipline, because knowledge of them is inspired by God Almighty or acquired by the mind, which is a gift from Him, glory be to Him, or from what God taught you to learn from following the game by sending its owner, and that it be deterred by his deterrence and turn away by his supplication and hold on to the game and not eat from it. So eat from what they catch for you which is what you did not eat from. "Because of what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Adi bin Hatim: If he eats from it, do not eat from it, for he has only held it for himself. Most jurists agreed with this view. Some of them said: This is not a condition for wild birds because it is impossible to discipline them to this extent. Others said: It is not a condition at all. And mention the name of God over it. The pronoun refers to what you know, and the meaning is: mention the name of God over it when you release it or when you hold it, meaning mention the name of God over it if you realize that it has been slaughtered. And fear God in His prohibitions. Indeed, God is swift in account. He will hold you accountable for what is great and small.
5:5: 5 Today, all good things are lawful for you, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you includes slaughtered animals and other things, and includes those who were given the Scripture, the Jews and Christians. Ali, may God be pleased with him, excluded the Christians of Banu Taghlib and said: They are not Christians, and they only took from them the drinking of wine. The Magians are not included in that, even though they were included in the report on the jizya, according to the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Treat them as you treat the People of the Scripture, except for marrying their women and eating their slaughtered animals. "And your food is lawful for them", so you do not have to feed them or sell them, and if it was forbidden to them, that would not be permissible. "And chaste women from among the believers" meaning free or chaste women, and specifying them was a motive for what is best. "And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you" even if they were warlike. Ibn Abbas said that warlike women are not permissible. "When you have given them their dowries" their dowries, and restricting the permissibility to giving them is to emphasize its obligation and to encourage what is best. It was said that what is meant by giving it is to commit to it, chaste, free through marriage. Not fornicators, not public in their adultery. Nor taking lovers, secretly, and a lover is a friend for both males and females. And whoever disbelieves in the faith, his work has become worthless, and he, in the Hereafter, will be among the losers. By faith he means the laws of Islam, and by disbelief he means denying it and abstaining from it.
5:6: 6 O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer meaning if you intend to stand, as God Almighty says: So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed. He expressed the intention of the action caused by it for the sake of brevity and to alert whoever wants to worship that he should hasten to do it, such that the action is not separated from the intention, or if you intend to pray because turning to something and standing for it is an intention for it, and the apparent meaning of the verse requires ablution for everyone standing for prayer even if he is not in a state of ritual impurity, and the consensus is to the contrary because of what was narrated "that he, peace and blessings be upon him, prayed the five prayers with one ablution on the day of the conquest, so Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: You did something that you did not do, so he said: I did it intentionally." It was said that it is absolute and intended to be restricted, and the meaning is if you rise to prayer in a state of ritual impurity. It was said that the command in it is for encouragement. It was said that it was at the beginning then it was abrogated, and it is weak because of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: Al-Ma'idah is from the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, so make lawful what is lawful in it and forbid what is unlawful in it. "Wash your faces." They ordered water to be poured over them, and there is no need to rub them, contrary to Malik. "And your hands to the elbows." The majority of scholars agree that the elbows are included in what is washed. Therefore, it was said that "to" means with, as in the Almighty's saying: "And He will add strength to your strength." Or it is related to something omitted, which is: And your hands are added to the elbows. If that were the case, there would be no further benefit to the meaning of specification or mentioning it, because the absolute hand includes it. It was said: to indicates the goal absolutely, and as for its inclusion in the ruling or its exit from it, it has no indication of it, but it is known from outside and was not in the verse. The hands were included in it, so it was ruled to include it as a precaution. It was said that to indicates the goal, requiring its exit, otherwise it would not be a goal, as in the Almighty's saying: "Then grant respite until ease." And the Almighty's saying: "Then complete the fast until the night." However, since the verse here is not distinguished from the one with the goal, it must be included as a precaution. "And wipe your heads." The ba' is an addition. It was said that it is for partiality, because it is the difference between your saying I wiped the handkerchief and with the handkerchief, and its face is that it is said that it indicates the inclusion of the action with the meaning of sticking, as if it was said: And stick the wiping to your heads, and that does not require comprehensiveness, unlike if it was said: And wipe your heads, because it is like his saying: Then wash your faces. The scholars differed regarding the amount of what is obligatory. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, made it obligatory: The least that the name falls on, taking certainty. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him: Wiping a quarter of the head, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, wiped his forehead, which is close to a quarter. Malik, may God be pleased with him: Wiping all of it, taking precaution. And your feet to the ankles Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, Hafs, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub made it the subject of it in apposition to your faces, and it is supported by: the widespread Sunnah, the actions of the Companions, the saying of most of the Imams, and the specification, because wiping was not limited. The rest of them have used it in the accusative case, and there is much similar to it in the Qur’an and poetry, such as the Almighty’s saying: The torment of a painful day and Hoor al-‘Ayn in the accusative case in the reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa’i, and their saying a ruined lizard’s hole. Grammarians have a chapter on that, and its benefit is to point out that one should be moderate in pouring water over her and wash her with a washing close to wiping, and in the separation between him and his two brothers there is an allusion to the necessity of order. It has been read in the nominative case on and your feet washed. And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, then purify yourselves and wash yourself. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you find no water, then seek clean earth and wipe your faces and hands with it its explanation has been given previously, and perhaps its repetition is to connect the speech in explaining the types of purification. God does not intend to make difficulty for you meaning He does not intend the command to purify oneself for prayer or the command to perform dry ablution to make things difficult for you. But He intends to purify you to clean you, or to purify you from sins, because ablution expiates sins, or to purify you with dust if you are unable to purify yourself with water. The object of intends is omitted in both instances, and the lam is for the reason. It was said that it is an addition, and the meaning is: God does not intend to make it difficult for you, so that He does not permit you to perform tayammum, but He intends to purify you, and this is weak, because an cannot be understood after the addition. And to complete His favor upon you to complete through His law that which purifies your bodies and expiates your sins, His favor upon you in religion, you were given His concessions and His favors upon you through His obligations. Perhaps you will be grateful for His favor. The verse includes seven matters, all of which are dual: two types of purification, the original and the alternative. The original is two types, comprehensive and non-comprehensive. Non-comprehensive, in terms of the action, is washing and wiping, and in terms of the place, is limited and unlimited. Their tools are liquid and solid, their cause is minor and major ritual impurity, the reason for switching to the alternative is illness or travel, and the promise for them is the purification of sins and the completion of the blessing. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 8 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the next verses of Sūrat l-Māidah. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 5:7: 7 And remember the favor of God upon you with Islam to remind you of the benefactor and encourage you to thank Him. And His covenant which He bound you with when you said, We hear and we obey" meaning the covenant that He took from the Muslims when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged them to hear and obey in hardship and ease, in comfort and in distress, or His covenant on the night of Aqaba or the Pledge of Ridwan. "And fear God" in forgetting His favor and breaking His covenant. "Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts" meaning their secrets, so He will reward you for it in addition to your obvious deeds.
5:8: 8 O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for God, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people incite you not to be just. He made it transitive with the preposition 'ala because it includes the meaning of burden, and the meaning is that the intensity of your hatred for the polytheists does not lead you to abandon justice towards them, so you transgress against them by committing what is not permissible, such as mutilation, slander, killing women and children, and breaking a covenant out of revenge for what is in your hearts. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. That is, justice is nearer to righteousness. He explicitly commanded them to be just and explained that it is a place of righteousness after He forbade them from injustice and explained that it is a requirement of desire. If this is for justice with the disbelievers, then what do you think about justice with the believers? "And fear God. Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do." He will reward you accordingly. The repetition of this ruling is either due to a difference in reason, as it was said that the first was revealed regarding the polytheists and this regarding the Jews, or to increase the interest in justice and exaggeration and in extinguishing the fire of anger.
5:9: 9 God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and a great reward. The second object of the promise was omitted because the statement for them is forgiveness is sufficient, as it is a new sentence that clarifies it. It was said that the sentence is in the place of the object, as the promise is a type of statement, as if he said: He promised them this statement.
5:10: 10 And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire. This is part of His Almighty habit, that the state of one of the two groups follows the state of the other, fulfilling the right of the call, and in it is more promise for the believers and comfort for their hearts.
5:11: 11 O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you. It was narrated (that the polytheists saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions at Usfan, standing together for the noon prayer. When they prayed, they regretted that they had not attacked them and intended to attack them when they stood up for the afternoon prayer. God responded to their plot by sending down upon them the prayer of fear). The verse is an allusion to that, and it was said that it is an allusion to what was narrated "that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Quraiza with the four caliphs to borrow from them for the sake of the Muslims whom Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri had killed, thinking that they were polytheists. They said: Yes, O Abu al-Qasim, sit down so that we may feed you and lend you money. They made him sit down and intended to kill him, but Amr ibn Jahash went to a large millstone and threw it at him, but God held back his hand. Gabriel came down and informed him, so he went out." It was said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped at a place and hung his weapon on a tree, and the people dispersed from him. Then a Bedouin came and drew his sword and said: Who can protect you from me? He said: God! Then Gabriel dropped it from his hand, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and said: Who can protect you from me? He said: No one. I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Then the verse was revealed: “When a people were about to stretch out their hands against you” to kill and destroy. It is said that he stretched out his hand towards him if he struck him and stretched out his tongue towards him if he insulted him. So he restrained their hands from you He prevented them from being extended towards you and repelled their harm from you. And fear God, and in God let the believers put their trust for He is sufficient to bring about good and repel evil.
5:12: 12And God took a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders witnesses from each tribe who would investigate and search for the conditions of his people, or guarantors who would guarantee that they would fulfill what they were commanded to do. It was narrated that when the Children of Israel were finished with Pharaoh and settled in Egypt, God Almighty commanded them to march to Jericho in the land of Ash-Sham, which was inhabited by the Canaanite giants. He said: I have written it for you as a home and a settlement, so go out to it and fight those in it, for I will support you. He commanded Moses, peace be upon him, to take from each tribe a guarantor for them to fulfill what they were commanded to do. So he took a covenant from them and chose from them the leaders and marched with them. When he approached the land of Canaan, he sent the leaders to spy on the report, and he forbade them from telling their people. They saw great bodies and severe violence, so they were afraid and returned and told their people and broke the covenant except for Caleb, son of Joseph, from the tribe of Judah, and Joshua, son of Nun, from the tribe of Ephraim, son of Joseph. “And God said, ‘Indeed, I am with you’ in victory ‘if you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them’ meaning, support them and strengthen them. Its root is ‘dhab’ and from it comes ‘ta’zir’. ‘And lend God a goodly loan’ by spending in the way of goodness. A loan may be a source or a direct object. ‘I will surely remove from you your misdeeds’ is an answer to the oath indicated by the lam in ‘if’ which is used as an answer to the condition. ‘And I will surely admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever disbelieves after that’ after that emphatic condition upon which the great promise is suspended. ‘Among you has certainly strayed from the right path’ a straying that has no doubt or excuse, unlike someone who disbelieved before that, as it is possible for him to have a doubt and imagine that he has an excuse.
5:13: 13 So because they broke their covenant, We cursed them. We expelled them from Our mercy, or transformed them, or imposed on them the jizyah. And We made their hearts hard. They do not react to the signs and warnings. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read Qasiyyah, which is either an exaggeration of Qasiyyah or in the sense of bad, from their saying Qasi Dirham if it is adulterated. It is also from Qasiyyah, because the adulterated has dryness and hardness. It was read Qasiyyah by following the Qaf to the Seen. "They distort the words from their places" is a resumption to explain the hardness of their hearts, because there is no hardness more severe than changing the words of God Almighty and slandering them. It is possible that it is a state of the object of "We cursed them, not of the hearts, because there is no pronoun for it, so it is And they forgot a portion" and left a full share. "From what they were reminded of" from the Torah, or from following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the meaning is that they distorted the Torah and left their share of what was revealed to them and did not attain it, and it was said that it means that they distorted it and some of it slipped from their memory due to its bad luck, because it was narrated that Ibn Masoud said: A person may forget some knowledge due to disobedience, and he recited this verse. "And you will not cease to find treachery among them" treachery among them, or a treacherous group or a traitor, and the taa is for emphasis. The meaning is that treachery and betrayal are their custom and the custom of their ancestors, and you will not cease to see that from them. "Except a few of them" who did not deceive, and they are those who believed among them, and it was said that it is an exception to His statement: "And We made their hearts hard So pardon them and overlook" if they repent and believe or make a covenant and commit to paying the jizyah. It was said: It is absolute and was abrogated by the verse of the sword. "Indeed, God loves the doers of good" is an explanation for the command to pardon and an urging of it and a warning that pardoning the treacherous disbeliever is a virtue and a failure to pardon others.
5:14: 14 And among those who said, 'We are Christians,' We took their covenant." That is, We took from the Christians their covenant as We took from those before them. It was said that its meaning is, "And among those who said, 'We are Christians,' is a people We took. He only said, They said, 'We are Christians,' to indicate that they called themselves that, claiming to support God Almighty. But they forgot a portion of that of which they had been reminded, so We incited." So We obligated from inciting something if it stuck to it. "Between them is enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection" between the sects of the Christians, who are Nestorians, Jacobites, and Melkites, or between them and the Jews. "And God will inform them of what they used to do" with the reward and punishment.
5:15: 15 O People of the Book meaning the Jews and Christians, and the Book is singular because it is for the genus. There has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Book I was Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse of stoning in the Torah and the good report of Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Ahmad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Gospel.
