And He pardons much of what you conceal and does not tell about it if there is no religious necessity for it, or about many of you so that he is not held accountable for his crime. There has come to you from God a light and a clear Book meaning the Qur'an, for it is the one that dispels the darkness of doubt and misguidance and the Book with a clear miracle. It was said that by the light he means Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
5:16: 16 God guides thereby The pronoun is singular because what is meant by them is one, or because they are like one in ruling. Whoever follows His pleasure is whoever follows His pleasure through faith among them. "The paths of peace" are the paths of safety from punishment, or the paths of God. And He brings them out from darkness into the light from the types of disbelief to Islam. By His permission by His will and success. And He guides them to a straight path a path that is the closest path to God Almighty and leads to Him inevitably.
5:17: 17 "They have certainly disbelieved who say that God is the Messiah, the son of Mary." They are those who said that there is unity among them, and it was said that none of them stated it explicitly, but since they claimed that there is divinity in him and said there is no god but God, one, it was necessary for them to be the Messiah, so the consequence of their statement was attributed to them to clarify their ignorance and expose their belief. "Say, 'Then who has control over anything from God?' So who can prevent anything from His power and will? If He willed to destroy the Messiah" Jesus. "The son of Mary and his mother and everyone on the earth together." He used this as evidence of the corruption of their minds and his statement: that the Messiah is capable, subdued, and subject to annihilation like all other possibilities, and whoever is like that is isolated from divinity. “And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and God is over all things competent.” This is to remove any doubt that they had about His command. The meaning is that He, glory be to Him, is absolutely capable of creating from nothing, just as He created the heavens and the earth, and from an origin, just as He created what is between them. He creates from an origin that is not of His kind, like Adam and many animals, and from an origin that is similar to Him, either from a male alone, like He created Eve, or from a female alone, like Jesus, or from them, like all other people.
5:18: 18 "And the Jews and Christians said, 'We are the sons of God and His beloved ones,' the followers of his sons Ezra and the Messiah, as was said to the followers of Ibn al-Zubayr, the beloved ones or those close to Him, as close as children are to their fathers. And more explanation of that has been given previously in Surat Al-Imran. "Say, 'Then why does He punish you for your sins?'" That is, if what you claim is true, then why does He punish you for your sins? For whoever is in this position does not do what necessitates his punishment. He punished you in this world by killing, capturing, and transforming, and you acknowledged that He will punish you in the Fire for a number of days. "Rather, you are human beings from among those He created," from among those whom God Almighty created. "He forgives whom He wills," and they are those who believed in Him and His messengers. "And He punishes whom He wills," and they are those who disbelieved. The meaning is that He treats you as He treats all other people, with no advantage for you with Him. "And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them," all of them are equal in being His creation and His dominion. And to Him is the final destination. So He will reward the doer of good for his good and the doer of evil for his evil.
5:19: 19 "O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you" meaning the religion, and it was omitted because it was made clear to you or what you concealed and it was omitted because it was mentioned before. It is possible that the object is not estimated to have the meaning of making clear to you and the sentence is in the position of the state, meaning Our Messenger came to you making clear to you. "After a period of messengers is related to came to you, meaning he came to you at a time of slackening in sending and interruption of revelation, or it is explained as a state of the pronoun in it, lest you say, 'There has not come to us any bearer of good tidings or a warner'" out of dislike for you to say that and make an excuse with it. "There has come to you a bearer of good tidings and a warner is related to something omitted, meaning do not make an excuse with what has come to us", for it has come to you. And God is capable of all things. He is able to send successively, as He did between Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them, when there were between them one thousand seven hundred years and a thousand prophets, and to send over a period of time, as He did between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, when there were between them six hundred or five hundred and sixty-nine years and four prophets, three from the Children of Israel and one from the Arabs, Khalid ibn Sinan al-Absi. And in the verse there is gratitude to them by sending them when the traces of revelation had been extinguished and they were in dire need of it.
5:20: 20 "And when Moses said to his people, 'O my people, remember the favor of God upon you when He made among you prophets,' and guided you and honored you through them. He did not send to any nation what He sent to the Children of Israel of prophets. 'And made you kings,' meaning, He made from you or among you. And the kings multiplied among them as the prophets multiplied after Pharaoh until they killed John and intended to kill Jesus. And it was said that when they were slaves in the hands of the Copts, God saved them and made them masters of themselves and their affairs, He called them kings. 'And He gave you what He had not given to anyone in the worlds,' from splitting the sea, shading the clouds, sending down manna and quails, and the like of what God gave them. And it was said that what is meant by the worlds are the worlds of their time.
5:21: 21 O my people, enter the Holy Land The land of Jerusalem was named thus because it was the residence of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, and the dwelling place of the believers. It was said that it was the Mount and what was around it. It was said that it was Damascus, Palestine, and some of Jordan. It was said that it was the Levant. Which God has ordained for you He divided it for you or wrote on the tablet that it would be a dwelling place for you, but if you believe and obey, according to what He said to them after they disobeyed, then it is forbidden to them. "And do not turn back" and do not turn back in fear of the tyrants. It was said that when they heard their condition from the leaders, they cried and said: If only we had died in Egypt, come, let us appoint a leader over us who will turn us back to Egypt, or do not turn back from your religion by disobedience and lack of trust in God Almighty. "Then you will turn back as losers" The reward of the two abodes. It is permissible in "then you will turn back" to use the subjunctive mood as a conjunction and the accusative as a response.
5:22: 22 They said, O Moses, indeed therein is a people who are tyrannical" who are overpowering and cannot be resisted. The tyrant is the active participle of "jabaruhu ala amar meaning to compel" and he is the one who compels people to do what he wants. "And indeed, we will not enter it until they leave it. But if they leave it, then we will enter" because we have no power over them.
5:23: 23 Two men said, Caleb and Joshua. Of those who fear" meaning they fear God Almighty and are pious to Him. It was said that two of the tyrants converted to Islam and went to Moses, peace be upon him. According to this, the waw is for the Children of Israel and the reference to the relative pronoun is omitted, meaning of those whom the Children of Israel fear. It is supported by the fact that it was read "those who fear" with the damma, meaning those who are frightened. According to the first meaning, this would be from fearing, meaning those who fear God Almighty by reminding or who are frightened by the threat. "God bestowed His favor upon them" with faith and steadfastness, which is a second description of the two men or an objection. "Enter upon them through the gate" the gate of their village, meaning surprise them and press them in the strait and prevent them from the desert. And when you enter it, you will be victorious. Because it is difficult for them to attack in the narrow places due to the size of their bodies, and because they are bodies without hearts, and it is possible that their knowledge of that came from the report of Moses, peace be upon him, and his saying: God has decreed for you, or from what they knew of the habit of God Almighty in supporting His messengers, and what they knew of His doing for Moses, peace be upon him, in subduing his enemies. And upon God rely, if you are believers, meaning believers in Him and believing in His promise.
5:24: 24 They said, O Moses, we will never enter it." They denied their entry for emphasis and perpetuity. "As long as they are in it" instead of some. "Then go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting right here." They said that out of contempt for God and His Messenger and indifference to them. It was said that it meant go, you and your Lord will help you.
5:25: 25 He said, 'My Lord, I have no control over anyone except myself and my brother.' He said this as a complaint of his grief and sorrow to God Almighty because his people had opposed him and he had despaired of them, and there remained with him no one who agreed with him whom he could trust except Aaron, peace be upon him, and the two men mentioned, even though they agreed with him, he could not trust them because of what he had suffered from the fickleness of his people. It is possible that what is meant by my brother is the one who befriends me in religion and enters into it. It is possible that it is accusative in apposition to myself, or on the name of in and nominative in apposition to the pronoun in I do not have control, or on the place of in and its name, and its genitive according to the Kufians in apposition to the pronoun in myself. "So separate us from the wicked people" by ruling for us as we deserve and ruling against them as they deserve, or by distancing us from them and freeing us from their company.
5:26: 26" He said, Then the Holy Land is forbidden to them they will not enter it or own it because of their disobedience. Forty years they will wander in the land The circumstantial factor is either forbidden, so the prohibition is temporary and not permanent, so it does not contradict the apparent meaning of his statement, which God has ordained for you, and this is supported by what was narrated: that Moses, peace be upon him, went after him with those who remained from the Children of Israel and conquered Jericho, and stayed there as long as God willed, then he died. It was said that he died in the wilderness, and when he was dying, he informed them that Joshua would be a prophet after him and that God Almighty commanded him to fight the giants, so Joshua went with them and killed the giants and all of Ash-Sham became for the Children of Israel, or they will wander, meaning they will walk in it confused and not seeing a way, so the prohibition is absolute. It was said that none of those who said, We will not enter it entered the Holy Land, but rather they perished in the wilderness, and the giants fought their children. It was narrated that they stayed for forty years in six farsakhs, walking from morning to evening, until they reached where they had departed from him, and the clouds shaded them from the sun and a pillar of light rose at night to give them light. Their food was manna and quails and their water was from the stone they carried. Most of them agree that Moses and Aaron were with them in the wilderness, but that it was a spirit for them and an increase in their status, and a punishment for them, and that they died in it. Aaron died, and Moses died a year after him. Then Joshua entered Jericho after three months and the leaders died in it suddenly except for Caleb and Joshua. So do not grieve over the wicked people is what Hatib attributed to Moses, peace be upon him, when he regretted praying against them and explained that they deserved it because of their wickedness.
5:27: 27 And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam Cain and Abel. God Almighty inspired Adam to marry each of them to the twin of the other, but Cain was angry with him because his twin was more beautiful. So Adam said to them: Offer a sacrifice, and which of you will accept it and marry it? So Abel's sacrifice was accepted by sending down fire and consuming it, so Cain became even more angry and did what he did. It was said that the two sons of Adam were not returned to them because of his lineage and that they were two men from the Children of Israel, and that is why He said: We prescribed for the Children of Israel. "By truth" is an adjective of a deleted source, meaning a recitation that is clothed in truth, or a state of the dhamma in atal, or of naba', meaning clothed in truth, in agreement with what is in the books of the ancients. "When they offered a sacrifice" is an adverb for report, or a state of it, or a substitute for the omission of an added word, meaning recite to them their report, the report of that time. The sacrifice is the name of what is offered to God, the Most High, from a sacrifice or other, just as sweets are the name of what is sweetened, meaning it is given. It is originally a source, and that is why it was not dualized. It was said that its meaning is if each of them offered a sacrifice. It was said that Cain was a farmer and offered worse wheat than him, and Abel was a milker and offered a fat camel. "So it was accepted from one of them and not accepted from the other" because he was displeased with the judgment of God, the Most High, and did not purify his intention in his sacrifice and intended the worst thing he had. "He said, I will surely kill you He threatened him with killing because of his extreme envy of him for his sacrifice being accepted, and that is why. He said, God only accepts from those who fear Him. In response, that is, you only came from yourself by abandoning piety, not from me, so why did you kill me? This indicates that the envious person should see his deprivation as a result of his shortcomings and strive to obtain what will make the envied person fortunate, not to remove his fortune, because that would harm him and not benefit him, and that obedience is only accepted from a believing, pious person.
5:28: 28 "If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me, I will not stretch out my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds." It was said that Abel was stronger than him, but he hesitated to kill him and surrendered to him out of fear of God, the Most High, because defense was not yet permissible, or because he forbade what was better. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Be the servant of God who is killed, and do not be the servant of God who kills. Rather, he said: I will not stretch out in response to If you should stretch out to absolve himself of this heinous act completely, and to avoid being described with it and being called by it. Therefore, he emphasized the negation with the letter baa.
5:29: 29 "I want you to bear my sin and your sin, so you will be among the companions of the Fire. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers." A second explanation for refraining from opposition and resistance. The meaning is that I only surrender to you out of a desire that you bear my sin if I were to stretch out my hand against you, and your sin by stretching out your hand against me, and the like of what they said is clear. So upon the aggressor is the sin of the wronged one, unless he retaliates. It was said that the meaning of with my sin is the sin of killing me, and with your sin for which your sacrifice was not accepted, and both are in the place of the state, meaning that you return covered with the two sins, bearing them. Perhaps he did not mean his brother's disobedience and misery, but rather he intended with this speech that if that was inevitable, then I wanted it to be for you, not for me. So what is meant by the self is that it should not be for him, that it should be for his brother. It is permissible that what is meant by the sin is his punishment, and wanting the punishment of the disobedient is permissible.
5:30: 30 So his soul willingly accepted him to kill his brother So he made it easy and made it spacious for him from the pasture that is obedient to him if it is spacious. And it was read So he willingly as an agent with the meaning of a verb, or that he killed his brother as if he called her to go ahead with it and she obeyed him, and for him to increase the connection like you say I preserved his money for Zaid. So he killed him and became one of the losers in religion and in this world, as he remained banished and sad for the rest of his life. It was said that Abel was killed when he was twenty years old at the Hira Pass. And it was said: in Basra in the location of the Great Mosque.
5:31: 31 So God sent a raven to dig in the ground to show him how to hide his brother's private parts. It was narrated that when he killed him, he was confused about his situation and did not know what to do with him, as he was the first of the sons of Adam to die. So God sent two ravens, and they fought, and one of them killed the other. Then he dug a hole for him with his beak and feet, then threw him into the hole. The pronoun in to see refers to God, the Most High, or to the raven. How is the case of the pronoun in to hide? The sentence is the second object of to see! What is meant by his brother's private parts is his dead body, as it is something that is ugly to see. He said, 'Woe to me!' is a word of grief and regret, and the alif in it is a substitute for the ya of the speaker. The meaning is, 'Woe to me! Come, for this is your time.' Woe and woe is destruction. Am I unable to be like this crow and cover the shame of my brother? I cannot find the like of what I am guided to. His saying, so I can cover is in apposition to I am and is not the answer to the question, as the meaning here is not if I were unable I would have covered. It was read with a sukoon on so I cover or with a sukoon on the accusative case for ease. So he became among those who regretted killing him because of what he suffered in it of confusion about his matter and carrying him on his neck for a year or more according to what was said, and his discipleship of the crow and the blackening of his color and his parents’ disowning him, as it was narrated that when he killed him his body turned black, so Adam asked him about his brother, and he said, I was not his guardian. He said, Rather, you killed him and that is why your body turned black. He disowned him and remained after that for a hundred years without laughing and not achieving what he did for him.
5:32: 32 For that reason We decreed upon the Children of Israel because of which We decreed upon them, and the root of the verb ajal is an evil if he committed it, and it is used to explain crimes, like their saying, whoever caused you to do something, meaning whoever caused you to do something, then it was expanded and used in every explanation, and min is an introductory particle related to Our Book, meaning the beginning of the books and the emergence of for that reason. That whoever kills a soul unless for a soul, meaning without killing a soul, necessitates retaliation. Or corruption in the land or without corruption in it, such as polytheism or highway robbery. It is as if he had killed all mankind in that he violated the sanctity of blood and established killing, and emboldened people to do it, or in that killing one and killing all are equal in bringing about the wrath of God Almighty and the great punishment. And whoever saves a life, it is as if he had saved all of mankind. That is, whoever causes its life to continue by pardoning or preventing killing, or rescuing from some cause of destruction, it is as if he had done that to all of mankind. The purpose of this is to magnify the killing of a soul and its revival in the hearts, to intimidate against exposing it and to encourage people to defend it. And indeed, Our messengers came to them with clear proofs, but indeed, many of them after that were transgressors upon the earth. That is, after We prescribed this great severity upon them for such crimes, and We sent to them messengers with clear signs to confirm the matter and renew the covenant so that they would protect themselves from it, and many of them are transgressors upon the earth in killing and do not care about it. Thus, the story is connected to what came before it, and transgression is straying from the limit of moderation in the matter.
5:33: 33 The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger meaning they wage war against their allies, who are the Muslims, is to wage war against them as a form of glorification. The root of war is plunder, and what is meant here is highway robbery. It has been said that it is stubbornness in theft, even if it is in Egypt. And they strive to cause corruption in the land meaning corruptors, and it is permissible to put it in the accusative case as a reason or a source because their striving was corruption, so it is as if it was said: And they cause corruption in the land. That they be killed meaning as retribution without crucifixion if they single out killing. Or crucified meaning crucified with killing if they kill and take money. The jurists have a difference of opinion as to whether he is killed and crucified or crucified alive and left or stabbed until he dies. Or their hands and feet are cut off on opposite sides their right hands and left feet are cut off if they take money and do not kill. Or be banished from the land They are banished from one country to another so that they are unable to settle in one place if they limit themselves to intimidation. Abu Hanifa interpreted banishment as imprisonment, and the or in the verse is detailed. It was said that it is for choice and the imam has a choice between these punishments for every highway robber. That is for them disgrace in this world Humiliation and disgrace. And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment because of the enormity of their sins.
5:34: 34 Except for those who repent before you have power over them is an exception specific to what is right for God Almighty and is indicated by His Almighty saying: So know that God is Forgiving and Merciful. As for killing in retaliation, it is for the guardians, and its obligation is dropped by repentance, not its permissibility. Restricting repentance to precedence over power indicates that after power it does not drop the punishment, even if it drops the punishment, and that the verse is about the Muslims because the repentance of the polytheist wards off punishment from him before and after power.
5:35: 35 O you who have believed, fear God and seek the means of approach to Him meaning that which you use to attain His reward and to draw near to Him by doing acts of obedience and abandoning sins, from the word wasal meaning to draw near to Him. In the hadith, the means of approach is a station in Paradise. "And strive in His cause" by fighting His apparent and hidden enemies. "That you may succeed" by reaching God, the Most High, and attaining His honor.
5:36: 36 Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is on the earth of all kinds of wealth. And the like thereof with it, they would ransom themselves thereby to make it a ransom for themselves. from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. The lam is related to an omitted word that is called for by if, since the meaning is if it were proven that they had what is on the earth. The unification of the pronoun in by it and the mentioned is two things: either to make it the course of a demonstrative pronoun in the like of the Most High's saying: A prison between that. Or because the waw and the like thereof have the meaning of with. "What is accepted from them is an answer, and even with what is within its scope is the predicate of if," and the sentence is a representation of the necessity of the punishment for them and that they have no way to escape from it. "And for them is a painful punishment" is an explicit statement of what is intended by it, and so is His saying:
5:37: 37 "They want to get out of the Fire, but they will not get out of it. And for them is a lasting punishment." It was read they will get out from to get out. Rather, he said and they will not get out instead of and they will not get out for emphasis.
5:38: 38 And the male thief, the female thief, cut off their hands. Two sentences according to Sibawayh, since the meaning of what is recited to you is the male thief, meaning their ruling. And a sentence according to Al-Mubarrad, and the fa' is for causality, the predicate entered because they include the meaning of the condition, since the meaning is: the one who stole and the one who stole. And it was read in the accusative, which is the preferred one in similar cases, because the construction does not occur as a predicate except with an implication and interpretation. Theft: taking someone else’s money secretly. Amputation is only required if it is from a safe place and the thing taken is a quarter of a dinar or its equivalent, based on the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Amputation for a quarter of a dinar or more. Scholars have differed on this, based on hadeeths that have been reported on this subject, and I have discussed this in detail in Sharh al-Masabih. What is meant by hands is faith, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him: their oaths. Therefore, it is permissible to put the plural in place of the dual, as in the statement of God the Almighty: For indeed, your hearts have become corrupted. It is sufficient to use the dual of the object to which it is added. The hand is the name for the entire limb, and for this reason the Khawarij went to the view that the part that was cut off is the shoulder, while the majority are of the view that it is the wrist, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) brought a thief and ordered that his right hand be cut off. A punishment for what they have earned, a scourge from God is in the accusative case as a direct object or a verbal noun, indicating their action, so cut off. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.
5:39: 39 But whoever repents from the thief. After his wrongdoing that is, after his theft. And reforms his matter by investigating the consequences and resolving not to return to it. "Then God will accept his repentance. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful" He accepts his repentance and will not punish him in the Hereafter. As for cutting off the hand, it is not dropped according to the majority because it includes the right of the one from whom it was stolen.
5:40: 40 Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? Al-Hattāb refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone. He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and God is over all things competent. He presented punishment before forgiveness, giving in the order of what came before, or because the deserving of punishment comes first, or because what is meant by it is cutting off, and it is in this world.
5:41: 41 O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you meaning the actions of those who fall into disbelief quickly, i.e. in showing it if they find an opportunity. Of those who say, 'We believe' with their mouths, but their hearts do not believe meaning of the hypocrites. The baa is related to they said, 'We do not believe' and the waw can be interpreted as a state or a conjunction. Of those who are Jews is an apposition to of those who said "listeners to falsehood" is an omitted predicate, meaning they are listeners, and the pronoun refers to both groups, or to those who hasten. It is permissible for it to be a subject and of those who is its predicate, meaning of the Jews are a people who listen, and the lam in it is for lying, either added for emphasis or to imply that listening means acceptance, i.e., they are receptive to what the rabbis fabricate, or for the reason and the object is omitted, i.e., they listen to your words in order to lie to you in them. listening to another people who have not come to you meaning to another group of Jews who did not attend your meeting and turned away from you out of arrogance and excessive hatred. The meaning is either listening to them and accepting their words, or listening to you to solve them and convey them to them. It is permissible for the lam to be connected to the lie because the second listening is repeated for emphasis, meaning: listening to them to lie to another people. distorting words from their proper places meaning they distort them from the places in which God placed them, either verbally: by neglecting them or changing their position, or in meaning: by interpreting them in a way other than what is intended and applying them in a place other than their intended place. The sentence is another description of a people or a description of listening or a state of the pronoun in it or a resumption that has no position, or in the nominative case as report of something omitted, meaning they distort. Likewise, they say, ‘If you are given this, then take it’ meaning if you are given this distortion, then accept it and act upon it. "And if you do not give it to him but Muhammad gave you a fatwa contrary to it then beware" that is, beware of accepting what he gave you. It was narrated that "a nobleman from Khaybar committed adultery with a noblewoman and they were both married, so they disliked stoning them, so they sent them with a group of them to Banu Qurayzah to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it and they said: If he orders you to flog and burn, then accept it, but if he orders you to stone, then do not. So he ordered them to stone, but they refused. So he appointed Ibn Suriya as a judge between him and them and said to him: I ask you by God, there is no god but Him, Who split the sea for Moses, and raised the mountain above you, and saved you and drowned the people of Pharaoh, and Who sent down to you His Book and what He permitted and what He prohibited, do you find in Him stoning for the married? He said: Yes. So they jumped on him and he said: I feared that if I lied to him, the punishment would come down upon us. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the two adulterers to be stoned at the door of the mosque. And whomever God desires to test" means his misguidance or disgrace. You will not possess for him anything from God so you will not be able to do anything for him from God to repel it. Those are the ones whose hearts God did not intend to purify from disbelief, and as you see, this is a text that proves the corruption of the Mu’tazila’s statement. For them in this world is disgrace is that by the jizya and fear of the believers. And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment which is eternity in the Fire, and the pronoun refers to those who were Jews if you start with and from those and if not, then it refers to both groups.
5:42: 42 Liars of lies Repeat it for emphasis. Eaters of ill-gotten gains meaning the forbidden, like bribery from its ill-gotten gains if he eradicates it because the blessing is taken away, and Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read in the three places with two dammahs and they are two languages like the neck and the neck, and it was read with the fathah of the seen in the form of the source. If they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them is a confusion for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, if they brought their case to him between ruling and turning away, and for this reason it was said: If two people of the Book brought their case to the judge, he is not obligated to judge, and this is the opinion of Al-Shafi'i and the most correct is that it is obligatory if the two litigants or one of them is a dhimmi because we are committed to defending them and repelling injustice from them, and the verse is not about the people of the covenant, and according to Abu Hanifa it is obligatory in all cases. And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all by making them hostile to you because you turned away from them, for God, the Most High, protects you from the people. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. That is, with the justice that God has commanded. Indeed, God loves those who act justly. So He protects them and raises their status.
5:43: 43 And how can they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of God?" It is astonishing that they make judgements of those they do not believe in, while the judgment is stated in the book they have, and it is a warning that they did not intend by the judgment to know the truth and establish the law, but rather they sought by it what would be easier for them, even if it is not the judgment of God, the Most High, in their opinion. "In which is the judgment of God" is a state of the Torah if you raise it with the circumstance, and if you make it the subject, then it is from its pronoun implied in it and its feminization because it is similar to the feminine in their speech in wording, such as "mumama and wadooda. Then they turn away after that then they turn away from your judgment that is in accordance with their book after the judgment, and it is an apposition to they make you judge" and is included in the judgment of astonishment. "And those are not believers" in their book because they turn away from it first and from what is in accordance with it second, or from you and with it.
5:44: 44 Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance that guides to the truth. And light that reveals what was unclear of the rulings. The prophets judged by it meaning the prophets of the Children of Israel, or Moses and those after him if we say that the law of those before us was law for us that which was not abrogated, and this verse is held by the speaker. Those who submitted is an attribute applied to the prophets in praise of them and in praise of the Muslims, and insinuating that the Jews are isolated from the religion of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, and following their guidance. For those who are Jews is related to sent down, or judges meaning they judge by it in their judgments and it indicates that the prophets are their prophets. And the rabbis and the scholars their ascetics and scholars who follow the way of their prophets is in apposition to the prophets. Because of what they were entrusted with of the Book of God because of God's command to them to protect His Book from loss and distortion, and it refers back to what was omitted and from the prophets. And they were witnesses over it watchers who would not allow anyone to change it, or witnesses who would clarify what was hidden from it, as Ibn Suriya did. So do not fear the people, but fear Me is a prohibition for the rulers to fear other than God in their governments and to be complacent in them out of fear of an oppressor or the supervision of a great one. And do not exchange My revelations and do not exchange My rulings that I have revealed for a small price is bribery and prestige. And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed disparagingly and denying it. Then those are the disbelievers for their disregard for it and their rebellion by ruling by other than it. That is why He described them by saying the disbelievers and the wrongdoers and the wicked. Their disbelief is due to their denial of it, their injustice is in ruling contrary to it, and their wickedness is in deviating from it. It is possible that each of the three attributes, in consideration of a situation that is combined with refraining from ruling with it, is appropriate for it, or for a group, as was said, this is in the Muslims due to their connection to their address, and the oppressors in the Jews, and the immoral in the Christians.
5:45: 45 And We prescribed for them and imposed on the Jews. In it in the Torah. A life for a life meaning that a life is killed for a life. And an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, and a tooth for a tooth Al-Kisa'i raised it as sentences connected to that and what is within its scope in consideration of the meaning, as if it was said: And We prescribed for them a life for a life, and an eye for an eye, for writing and reading occur on the most beautiful like saying, or it is resumed and its meaning is: Likewise the eye gouged out for the eye, and the nose cut off for the nose, and the ear cut off for the ear, and the tooth pulled out for the tooth, or that the raised from it is connected to what is implied in his saying for the life, and it is permissible because in the original it is separated from it by the end, and the preposition and the noun explain the meaning, and Nafi' read and the ear for the ear and in his ears with a sukoon on the dhal wherever it occurred. And wounds are subject to retaliation. Al-Kisa'i also read it with the nominative case, and Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir agreed with him that it is a summary of the ruling after the preference. But whoever gives charity from those who are entitled to it. With it with retaliation, meaning whoever pardons him. It is so the charity. It is an expiation for him for the one who gives charity, God expiates his sins with it, and it is said to the offender that what is required of him is dropped. It was also read It is an expiation for him so the one who gives charity has his expiation that he deserves by giving charity on his behalf, nothing is reduced from it. And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed of retaliation and other things. Then those are the wrongdoers.
5:46: 46 And We followed in their footsteps meaning, and We followed them in their footsteps, so the object was deleted because the preposition and noun indicate it, and the pronoun refers to the prophets. By Jesus, son of Mary is a second object to which the verb is transitive with the preposition Bi. Confirming what was before it and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel and it was read with the opening of the hamza In it is guidance and light in the accusative case as a state And confirming what was before it of the Torah is in apposition to it and so is his saying: And guidance and instruction for the righteous and it is permissible to put them in the accusative case as an object in apposition to something omitted or in connection with it and in apposition.
5:47: 47 And let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein "upon him" in the reading of Hamza, and according to the first, the lam is related to something omitted, i.e., We gave him to judge, and it was read: "And indeed, your Lord will judge on the basis that an" is connected to the command, like your saying: I ordered you to stand up, i.e., We ordered him to judge. "And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then those are the wicked" about his judgment, or about faith if he was disdainful of it, and the verse indicates that the Gospel includes the rulings and that Judaism was abrogated by the mission of Jesus, peace be upon him, and that he was independent in the law and carried it on "and let them judge by what God has revealed therein" of the obligation to act according to the rulings of the Torah contrary to the apparent meaning.
5:48: 48 And We have sent down to you the Book in truth meaning the Qur'an. Confirming what came before it of the Book of the same type as the revealed books, so the first lam is for the covenant and the second is for the type. And a guardian over it and a watcher over all the books, preserving it from change and testifying to its soundness and stability. It was read with the passive form, meaning He has authority over it and preserved it from distortion, and the guardian of it is God, the Most High, or the guardians in every age. So judge between them by what God has sent down meaning by what God has sent down to you. And do not follow their inclinations away from the truth that has come to you by deviating from it to what they desire, so it is a connection to following because it includes the meaning of do not deviate, or a state of its subject, meaning do not follow their inclinations, deviating from what has come to you. For each of you We have appointed O people. A law Shari'ah, which is the path to water, religion likened it to it because it is a path to what is the cause of eternal life. It was read with the opening of the shin. And a clear path and way in religion from the approach of the matter if it is clear. And it is used as evidence that we are not worshippers of the previous laws. And if God had willed, He would have made you one nation a group agreed upon one religion in all ages without abrogation or transformation. The object of if He had willed is omitted and indicated by the answer. It was said that the meaning is if God had willed for you to gather upon Islam, He would have forced you upon it. But that He may test you in what He has given you of the different laws appropriate for each age and century, do you act upon them in submission to them believing that their difference is in accordance with divine wisdom, or do you deviate from the truth and neglect work. So hasten to do good deeds so seize the opportunity and gain the advantage of precedence and progress. To God is your return all together a resumption in which the reason for the command to hasten is explained and a promise and a threat to those who hasten and those who fall short. Then He will inform you of that in which you used to differ with the recompense that distinguishes between the one who is right and the one who is wrong, the one who does good and the one who falls short.
5:49: 49 And that you judge between them by what God has revealed is in apposition to the Book, meaning that We revealed to you the Book and the judgment, or to the truth, meaning that We revealed it with the truth and that you judge, and it is permissible for it to be a sentence with the estimation and We commanded that I judge. And do not follow their desires and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what God has revealed to you meaning that they lead you astray and turn you away from it, and that its connection is a substitute for them, a substitute for inclusion, meaning beware of their temptation, or an object for it, meaning beware of them for fear that they tempt you. It was narrated that "the rabbis of the Jews said: Let us go to Muhammad, perhaps we can tempt him away from his religion. They said, O Muhammad, you know that we are the rabbis of the Jews, and that if we follow you, we will follow all the Jews. There is a dispute between us and our people, so we will bring our judgment to you so that you may judge for us against them, and we will believe in you and believe you. But the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused that," so it was revealed. If they turn away from the revealed judgment and wanted something else. Know that God only wants to afflict them for some of their sins, meaning the sin of turning away from the rule of God Almighty. He expressed it thus to indicate that they have many sins, and this, despite its greatness, is one of them counted among them, and in it is an indication of greatness, as in the indefiniteness and similar to it is the saying of Labid: Or some souls are linked to her bathroom And many of the people are wicked rebellious in disbelief and transgressing therein.
5:50: 50 Do they seek the judgment of the Age of Ignorance? which is the inclination and flattery in judgment, and what is meant by ignorance is the religion of ignorance which is following desires. It was said that it was revealed about Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to rule as the people of ignorance used to rule in differentiating between the dead. It was read with the ruling raised as a subject, and they seek is its predicate, and the referent is omitted as it was omitted in the relative clause in the Almighty's saying: Is this the one whom God sent as a messenger? This was considered weak in non-poetry, and it was read Do they seek the judgment of ignorance? meaning they seek a ruler like the rulers of ignorance who rules according to their desires. Ibn Amir read Tabghunu with the taa' on the basis of Say to them, do you seek the judgment of ignorance? And who is better than God in judgment for a people who are certain? That is, they have, and the lam is for clarification, as in the Almighty’s saying: Heyt laka meaning this question is for a people who are certain, for they are the ones who contemplate matters and verify things with their own eyes, so they know that there is no better judgment than God, glory be to Him, the Most High.
5:51: 51 O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. Do not rely on them and do not associate with them as friends. Some of them are allies of others. This is an allusion to the reason for the prohibition, that is, they agree on your disagreement and support each other because they are united in religion and unanimously oppose you. And whoever among you supports them, then indeed he is one of them. That is, whoever supports them, then indeed he is among them. This emphasis is the obligation to avoid them, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Their two fires will not appear to each other, or because those who supported them were hypocrites. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people, that is, those who wronged themselves by supporting the infidels or the believers by supporting their enemies.
5:52: 52 Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease meaning Ibn Abi and his ilk. Rushing into them meaning in their friendship and support. They say, 'We fear that a misfortune will strike us' They apologize by saying that they fear that a misfortune will strike them, that the matter will turn around and the state will be in the hands of the infidels. It was narrated that "Ubadah ibn al-Samit, may God be pleased with him, said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have many Jewish allies, and I declare before God and His Messenger that I am innocent of anyone who accuses me of being an ally of God and His Messenger. Ibn Abi said: I am a man who fears misfortunes, but I do not declare innocent of being an ally of my allies." So it was revealed. Perhaps God will bring victory for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, over his enemies and make the Muslims victorious. Or a command from Him that will cut off the Jews' desire to kill and expel them, or the command to reveal the secrets of the hypocrites and kill them. So they will become meaning these hypocrites. Regretting for what they concealed within themselves for what they concealed of disbelief and doubt regarding the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in addition to what they showed of their hypocrisy.
5:53: 53 And those who believe say in the nominative case, the reading of Asim, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i, that it is a new statement, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Ibn Amir in the nominative case without a waw, so that it comes in consideration of the meaning, and it is as if he said: Perhaps God will bring about the conquest, and those who believe say, or he makes it a substitute for the name of God Almighty, included in the name of perhaps, making the report unnecessary with what it includes of the event, or in the opening, meaning perhaps God will bring about the conquest and the saying of the believers, because bringing what it requires is like bringing it. Are these the ones who swore by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you? The believers say this to one another in amazement at the state of the hypocrites and boasting about the sincerity that God, the Most High, has bestowed upon them, or they say it to the Jews, for the hypocrites swore to support them, as God, the Most High, has narrated about them, And if you are fought, we will surely aid you. The most solemn oath is the most severe of oaths, and it is originally a source, and its accusative is in the state of the estimation, and they swore by God, they swore with their most solemn oaths, so the verb was deleted and the source was put in its place, and therefore it is permissible for it to be definite or in the source because it means they swore. Their deeds have become worthless, so they have become losers. Either from the statement or the statement of God, the Most High, as a testimony to them that their deeds have become worthless, and in it is the meaning of amazement, as if it was said, their deeds have become worthless, so what a loser they are.
5:54: 54 O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion Nafi' and Ibn Amir read it according to the original, and it is also in the Imam, and the rest with assimilation. This is one of the events that God the Almighty informed about before it happened. Three groups of Arabs apostatized at the end of the era of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Banu Mullaj, whose leader was Dhu al-Khimar al-Aswad al-Ansi, prophesied in Yemen and took over his country, then Fayruz al-Daylami killed him on the night of the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the next day. He informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that night, which pleased the Muslims, and the report came at the end of Rabi' al-Awwal. Banu Hanifa, the companions of Musaylimah, prophesied and wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: From Musaylimah, the Messenger of God, to Muhammad, the Messenger of God. As for what follows, half of the earth is mine and half is yours. He replied: From Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Musaylimah the Liar. As for what follows, the earth belongs to God, He gives it as an inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants, and the good end is for the righteous. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, fought him with an army of Muslims, and Wahshi, the killer of Hamza, killed him. Banu Asad, the people of Tulaiha bin Khuwaylid, prophesied, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid to him. He fled after the battle to the Levant, then converted to Islam and his conversion was good. During the reign of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, there were seven Fazza, the people of Ghaibnah bin Hisn, and Ghatafan, the people of Farah bin Salamah Al-Qushayri, and Banu Salim, the people of Al-Fuja’ah bin Abdullah Ya Layl, and Banu Yarbu’, the people of Malik bin Nuwayrah, and some of Tamim, the people of Sajah bint Al-Mundhir, the prophetess, the wife of Musaylima, and Kinda, the people of Al-Ash’ath bin Ghaith, and Banu Bakr bin Wa’il in Bahrain, the people of Al-Hattam bin Zaid, and God sufficed them with his help. During the reign of Umar bin Al-Hattab, may God be pleased with him, Ghassan, the people of Jabalah bin Al-Ayham, converted to Christianity and went to the Levant. God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him. It was said that they are the people of Yemen, because it was narrated that "he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pointed to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and said: They are the people of this." It was also said that they are the Persians, because he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about them, so he struck Salman's shoulder and said: This and his people. It was also said that those who fought on the day of al-Qadisiyyah were two thousand from the Nakha', five thousand from Kinda and Bajila, and three thousand from the people of the people. The reference to the omitted one is that God will bring a people in their place. God's love for His servants is the desire for guidance and success for them in this world and a good reward in the hereafter. The love of the servants for Him is the desire for His obedience and avoidance of His disobedience. Humble towards the believers is affectionate towards them and submissive to them, the plural of humiliated, not submissive, because its plural is humiliated. Its use with 'Ali is either to include the meaning of affection and tenderness, or to draw attention to the fact that despite their high status and superiority over the believers, they are submissive to them, or for the sake of contrast. Mighty against the disbelievers are strong and dominate them from izzu if he overpowers him. It is also read in the accusative case as a state. They strive in the cause of God is another description of a people, or a state of the pronoun in a’zza. “And they do not fear the blame of a blamer” is in apposition to they strive meaning that they are the ones who combine striving in the cause of God and being steadfast in His religion, or a state meaning that they are striving and their state is different from the state of the hypocrites, for they go out in the army of the Muslims fearing the blame of their Jewish allies and they do not do anything for which they will be blamed. The blame is from the blame in it and in the indefiniteness of blamer, two exaggerations. That is a reference to what came before from the descriptions. The bounty of God He gives it to whom He wills He grants it and makes it successful. And God is Bountiful is abundant in bounty. Knowing of who is worthy of it.
5:55: 55 Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe. When He forbade befriending the infidels, He mentioned those who are truly worthy of it. He only said, Your ally is God and did not say, Your ally is God to indicate that the allyship belongs to God, the Most High, in principle, and to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers in consequence. Those who establish prayer and give zakat is an attribute of those who believe, so it is like a noun, or a substitute for it. It is permissible to put it in the accusative or nominative case for praise. And they are bowing down are humble in their prayer and zakat. It was said that it is a specific state in which they give, or they give zakat while bowing down in prayer, eager to do good and hastening to do so. It was revealed about Ali, may God be pleased with him, when a questioner asked him while he was bowing down in prayer, so he threw his ring to him. The Shiites used it as evidence for his Imamate, that what is meant by the guardian is the one who is in charge of affairs and is entitled to dispose of them. What we have mentioned is apparent, although applying the plural to the singular is also contrary to what is apparent, and even if it is true that it was revealed about him, perhaps the plural was brought to encourage people to do the same as him so that they would be included in it. Based on this, it is evidence that a small action in prayer does not invalidate it, and that voluntary charity is called zakat.
5:56: 56 And whoever takes God and His Messenger and those who believe as allies and whoever takes them as allies, then indeed, the party of God will be the victorious" meaning, they will be the victorious, but the placement of the apparent in place of the implicit is an indication of the proof for it, so it is as if it was said: And whoever takes these as allies, they are the party of God, and the party of God will be the victorious, and to mention them and magnify their status and honor them with this name, and to expose whoever takes allies other than these as the party of Satan, and the origin of the party is the people who gather for a matter that upsets them.
5:57: 57 O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who take your religion in ridicule and amusement from among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers. This was revealed about Rifa'ah bin Zaid and Suwaid bin Al-Harith who outwardly became hypocrites, and there were men from among the Muslims who were friendly to them. The prohibition of befriending them was based on their taking their religion in ridicule and amusement, alluding to the reason and warning that whoever is like this is far from befriending and deserving of enmity and hatred. The distinction between those who mock the People of the Book and the disbelievers was made according to the reading of those who put it in the accusative case, and they are Abu Amr, Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub. The disbelievers, although they are general to the People of the Book, are applied to the polytheists in particular because their disbelief is doubled. Those who put it in the accusative case conjoined it with those who took as allies the prohibition of befriending those who are not upon the truth, whether they have a religion in which they follow their whims and distort it from the right path, like the People of the Book, or those who do not, like the polytheists. And fear God by abandoning the prohibitions. If you are believers, because true faith requires that. And it was said, If you are believers in His promise and His threat.
5:58: 58 And when you call to prayer, they take it in mockery and amusement. That is, they take the prayer, or the call, and in it is evidence that the call to prayer is prescribed for prayer. It was narrated that a Christian in Medina, when he heard the caller to prayer say, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, would say, May God burn the liar. One night, his servant entered with a fire while his family was asleep, and its sparks flew into the house and burned him and his family. That is because they are a people who do not reason. For foolishness leads to ignorance of the truth and mockery of it, and reason prevents that.
5:59: 59 Say, O People of the Scripture, do you hold a grudge against us? Do you deny and criticize us? It is said that someone denounced something from him if he denied it and that he took revenge if he rewarded him. It is also read tanqumoon with the opening of the qaf, which is a language. Except that we believe in God and in what was revealed to us and what was revealed before. Belief in all the revealed books. And that most of you are wicked is in apposition to that we have believed and it is as if the exception is necessary for both matters, which is opposition, meaning: What you disapprove of us is only your opposition, since we entered the faith and you have left it, or the original was and the belief that most of you are wicked, so the complement was deleted, or on what, meaning: And you do not blame us for anything except believing in God as He revealed and that most of you are wicked, and or on an omitted reason and the meaning is: Do you blame us for anything except that we believed due to your lack of fairness and your wickedness, or it is accusative with an implied verb indicating it, do you blame, meaning: And you do not blame that most of you are wicked, or it is raised as the subject and the predicate is omitted, meaning: And your wickedness is established and known to you, but the love of leadership and money prevents you from fairness. The verse is addressed to the Jews who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about who would believe in him, so he said: We believe in God and what was revealed to us until His saying: And we are Muslims to Him so they said when they heard the mention of Jesus: We do not know of a religion worse than your religion.
5:60: 60 "Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?" That is, of something that is destined for you. "A reward from God." A fixed recompense from God Almighty, and the reward is specific to goodness, just as the punishment is specific to evil, so it was placed here in its place in the manner of their saying: Greetings between them are painful And its accusative is from the distinction of human beings. He whom God has cursed and become angry with and made of them apes and pigs is a substitute for human beings with the deletion of an added word, meaning human beings from the people of that whom God has cursed, or human beings from that religion of Muhammad whom God has cursed, or a deleted predicate, meaning he is the one whom God has cursed and they are the Jews, God distanced them from His mercy and became angry with them for their disbelief and their immersion in sins after the verses became clear, and some of them were transformed into apes and they are the people of the Sabbath, and some of them into pigs and they are the disbelievers of the people of the table of Jesus, peace be upon him. And it was said that both of the transformed ones among the people of the Sabbath were transformed into apes, their young men and their old men into pigs. "And the slave of the taghut is in apposition to the relative clause of min and so is the slave of the taghut" in the passive form. The raising of "taghut and slave" means he became worshipped, so the referent is omitted, i.e. in them or among them. Whoever reads "and the slave of the taghut or slave as an adjective like intelligent and vigilant or slave of the taghut as a plural like servants or that its origin is slave" then the taa' is omitted for the addition and is in apposition to the monkeys. Whoever reads "and the slave of the taghut in the accusative case is in apposition to min, and what is meant by min" the taghut is the calf and it was said the priests and everyone who obeyed it in disobeying God Almighty. "Those" means the cursed ones. "Evil place made their place evil to be more eloquent in indicating their evil, and it was said place" is declined. "And astray from the right path" means the middle path between the extremism of the Christians and the criticism of the Jews. What is meant by the two superlative forms is the increase in general and not in relation to the believers in evil and misguidance.
5:61: 61 And if they come to you, they say, 'We believe.' This was revealed about the Jews who were hypocrites to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or about the generality of the hypocrites. And they entered with disbelief, and they have already left with it. That is, they will leave you as they entered, and what they heard from you did not affect them. The two sentences are states of the subject of they said. And with disbelief and with it are states of the subjects of entered and left. Although qad was used to bring the past closer to the state so that it could be a state, it also indicates what it contains of expectation that the sign of hypocrisy was evident among them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, thought so. Therefore, he said: And God knows best what they were concealing, that is, of disbelief, and in it is a warning to them.
5:62: 62 And you will see many of them meaning the Jews or the hypocrites. hastening into sin meaning the forbidden. It was said that it was lying, because of his saying: from their saying sin "and aggression" is injustice, or exceeding the limit in sins. It was said that "sin" is what is specific to them and aggression is injustice, or exceeding the limit in sins. It was said that "sin" is what is specific to them and aggression is what extends to others. "And their eating of ill-gotten gains" meaning the forbidden. He mentioned it specifically for emphasis. "How evil is what they used to do" How evil is what they did.
5:63: 63 Why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them from their sinful speech and their consumption of what is unlawful? This is an exhortation to their scholars to forbid that, because if lawla is used in the past tense, it indicates rebuke, and if it is used in the future tense, it indicates exhortation. How evil is what they used to do is more eloquent than saying How evil is what they used to do in that making is the work of a person after he has trained in it, pondered it, and sought to perfect it. For this reason, their elite were condemned for it, and because abandoning a good deed is uglier than committing a sin, because the soul takes pleasure in it and is drawn to it, but abandoning it is not the same, so it is more deserving of eloquent condemnation.
5:64: 64And the Jews said, 'The hand of God is chained.' That is, He is withholding and stingy with provision. The chaining of the hand and its extension are a metaphor for stinginess and generosity, and there is no intention in it to prove a hand, chaining, and extension. Therefore, it is used where that is not conceivable, such as his saying: Jad Al-Hama extended his hands in a shower of thanks to his dew, his valleys and valleys Its equivalent from the compound metaphors: The night’s gathering became gray. It was said that its meaning is that he is poor, based on the Almighty’s saying: God has certainly heard the statement of those who said, ‘God is poor, while we are rich.’ “Their hands are chained and they are cursed for what they said” is a supplication against them for miserliness and misery, or for poverty and destitution, or the hands are chained in reality, they are chained as prisoners in this world and dragged to the fire in the hereafter, so the correspondence is in terms of the wording and consideration of the origin, like your saying: He cursed me, God cursed his back. Rather, His hands are extended. The dual of the hand is an exaggeration in the response and negation of miserliness from Him, the Almighty, and an affirmation of the ultimate in generosity, for the most that the generous person gives of his money is to give it with his hands, and a reminder of the gifts of this world and the hereafter, and what is given to lure and what is given to honor. He spends as He wills is an emphasis on that, meaning He is free to choose how to spend, He sometimes expands and sometimes restricts according to His will and the requirements of His wisdom, not in succession, expansion and restriction in one hand, and it is not permissible to make it a state of the ha' to separate them with the report and because it is added to it, nor of the two hands, food, for they have no pronoun in it nor of their pronoun for that reason. The verse was revealed about Phinehas bin Azura, for he said that when God withheld from the Jews what He had expanded upon them of expansion due to the evil of their denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the association of others with Him because they were satisfied with His saying: And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief meaning they are transgressors and disbelievers and they increase in transgression and disbelief by what they hear from the Qur'an just as a sick person increases in illness from eating good food for the healthy. And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection so their hearts do not agree nor do their words match. Whenever they kindled the fire of war, God extinguished it. Whenever they wanted to fight the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and stir up evil against him, God, the Most High, repelled them by causing a dispute between them, thereby stopping their evil from him. Or whenever they wanted to fight someone, they were defeated. Because they disobeyed the ruling of the Torah, God gave power to Nebuchadnezzar over them. Then they corrupted, so He gave power to the Roman Pharoah over them. Then they corrupted, so He gave power to the Magians over them. Then they corrupted, so He gave power to the Muslims over them. War has the attribute of kindled or the attribute of fire. “And they strive to cause corruption in the land,” meaning to cause corruption, which is their efforts in plotting, stirring up wars and seditions, and violating sacred things. And God does not love corrupters, so He will only reward them with evil.
5:65: 65 And if the People of the Scripture had believed in Muhammad and what he brought. And feared what we have enumerated of their sins and the like. We would have removed from them their misdeeds which they committed and would not have held them accountable for them. And We would have admitted them to Gardens of Delight and made them enter them. This is a reminder of the enormity of their sins and the multitude of their transgressions, and that Islam wipes out what came before it, even though it is great, and that a People of the Book will not enter Paradise unless he submits to Islam.
5:66: 66 And if they had established the Torah and the Gospel by broadcasting what they contain of the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and implementing its rulings. And what was revealed to them from their Lord meaning all the revealed books, then they are charged with believing in them as if they were revealed to them, or the Qur'an they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet He would have expanded their provisions by bestowing blessings upon them from the sky and the earth, or increasing the fruits of the trees and the yield of the crops, or providing them with gardens full of ripe fruits. They would pick them from the tops of the trees and pick up what fell to the ground. Between that, what was withheld from them was due to the evil of their disbelief and their sins, not due to the deficiency of the abundance. If they had believed and established what they were commanded to do, He would have expanded for them and given them the best of the two abodes. Among them is a moderate nation just, neither excessive nor negligent, and they are those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that moderate was moderate in their enmity towards him. And many of them - evil is what they do. That is, what they do is evil. It contains the meaning of astonishment, that is, how evil is their work, which is obstinacy, distorting the truth, turning away from it, and excessive hostility.
5:67: 67 O Messenger, proclaim what has been revealed to you from your Lord all that has been revealed to you, not observing anyone or fearing harm. And if you do not even if you do not convey all of it as I have commanded you. Then you have not conveyed His message then you have not delivered any of it, because concealing some of it wastes what has been delivered of it, like omitting some of the pillars of prayer, for the purpose of the call is nullified by it, or it is as if you have not conveyed any of it, like His saying: Then it is as if he had killed all of mankind in terms of concealing some or all of it is similar in intercession and bringing punishment. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, and Abu Bakr read his messages in the plural and with a kasra on the ta'. And God will protect you from the people a promise and guarantee from God, the Most High, the Most Great, by protecting his soul, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the exposure of enemies and removing his excuses. Indeed, God does not guide the disbelieving people they cannot do what they want with you. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God sent me with His messages, and I was fed up with them. Then God revealed to me, ‘If you do not convey My message, I will punish you,’ and He guaranteed me protection, so I became strong.” On the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was guarding until this verse was revealed. Then he stuck his head out of his leather tent and said, ‘Go away, O people, for God has protected me from the people.’” The apparent meaning of the verse requires conveying what is related to the interests of the servants, and the intention behind its revelation was to inform them of it, for there are divine secrets that are forbidden to disclose.
5:68: 68Say, 'O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything' meaning a religion that is respected and it is correct to call it something because it is false. Until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord and establishing them includes believing in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and submitting to his rule, for the divine books in their entirety command belief in whoever believes in him and the miracle speaks of the obligation of obedience to him, and what is meant is establishing its principles and what has not been abrogated of its branches. And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief, so do not grieve over the disbelieving people do not grieve over them because of their increased transgression and disbelief in what you convey to them, for the harm of that will follow them and will not go beyond them, and in the believers there is an escape for you from them.
5:69: 69 Indeed, those who believe and those who are Jews and the Sabians and the Christians was previously explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. The Sabians are raised as a subject and its predicate is omitted, and the intention is to delay it from what is in the scope of in. The estimate is: Indeed, those who believe and those who are Jews and the Christians, their ruling is such and such, and the Sabians are likewise, as in His saying: I and Qiar are strangers to it And he said: Otherwise, know that you and I are rebels as long as we remain in discord. That is, know that we are rebels and you are the same. It is like an objection by which he indicated that since the Sabians, despite the appearance of their misguidance and their deviation from all religions, were forgiven if they were true in faith and righteous deeds, others were more deserving of that. It is possible that and the Christians is conjoined with it, and whoever believes is their predicate, and the predicate of if is understood and indicated by what follows it, like his saying: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs It is not permissible to connect it to the place of in and its noun, because it is conditional upon the completion of the predicate, because if it was connected to it before it, the predicate would be the predicate of the subject and the predicate of in together, so two factors would come together on it. Nor on the pronoun in Hadawa because of the lack of emphasis and separation, and because it requires the Sabians to be Hud. It was said that in means yes and what comes after it is in the nominative case as the subject. It was said that the Sabians is accusative with a fatha, just as it is permissible with a ya’ as it is permissible with a waw. Whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does righteousness is in the nominative case as the subject and its predicate. There is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve. The sentence is the predicate of in or the predicate of the subject, as mentioned above, and the referent is omitted, meaning: whoever believes among them, or in the accusative case as a substitute for the name of in and what is connected to it. It was read al-Sabi’in which is the apparent meaning, and al-Sabi’un by changing the hamza to a ya’, and al-Sabi’un by deleting it from saba’a by replacing the hamza with an alif, or from sabout because they were inclined to follow desires and did not follow the law or reason.
5:70: 70We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers to remind them and explain to them the matter of their religion. Whenever there came to them a messenger with what their souls did not desire with what contradicted their desires of laws and hardships of obligations. A party they denied and a party they killed is the answer to the condition and the sentence is an attribute of messengers and the referent is omitted, meaning a messenger from them. It was said that the answer is omitted and indicated by that and it is a resumption, and they kill was brought in place of they killed to narrate the past situation, to bring it to mind and to make killing horrific and to draw attention to the fact that this is their custom in the past and future and to preserve the beginnings of the verses.
5:71: 71 And they thought that there would be no trial meaning, the Children of Israel thought that no calamity or punishment would befall them because of killing the prophets and denying them. Abu Omar, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read not to be and inserted the verb to calculate into it, which is to confirm that it is a status of knowledge because it has taken hold of their hearts, and that or that with what is within its scope prevailed in place of its two objects. So they were blind to the religion or the evidence and guidance. And they were deaf to hearing the truth as they did when they worshipped the calf. Then God accepted their repentance meaning, then they repented, so God accepted their repentance. Then they were blind and deaf another time. And it was read with the dammah in both of them on the basis that God the Most High blinded them and deafened them, meaning He afflicted them with blindness and deafness, and it is rare, and the common language is blind and deaf. Many of them instead of the pronoun, or the subject and the waw is a sign of the plural, as in their saying: The fleas ate me, or the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning the blind and deaf are many of them. It was said that it is the subject and the sentence before it is its predicate, but this is weak because presenting the predicate in such a case is impossible. And God is Seeing of what they do, so He will reward them according to their deeds.
5:72: 72 They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'God is the Messiah, the son of Mary.' And the Messiah said, 'O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord.' That is, I am a servant who is being raised like you, so worship my Creator and your Creator. Whoever associates partners with God, that is, in worshipping Him or in what is specific to Him of attributes and actions. God has forbidden Paradise to him, that is, he is prevented from entering it just as the one who is forbidden is prevented from the one who is forbidden, for it is the abode of monotheists. And his abode is the Fire, for it is prepared for the polytheists. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers, that is, they have no one to protect them from the Fire. So the apparent was placed in place of the implicit as a record of the fact that they were wronged by associating partners with God and deviated from the path of truth.
