It is possible that it is part of the words of Jesus, peace be upon him, or that it is part of the words of God, the Most High, by which He drew attention to the fact that they said that out of respect for Jesus, peace be upon him, and to draw closer to Him, and he is their enemy in that and their opponent in it, so what do you think of anyone else?
5:73: 73 They have disbelieved who say that God is the third of three meaning one of three, and this is a narration of what the Nestorians and the Melkites said, among them those who believe in three hypostases, and what preceded what the Jacobites said, those who believe in union. And there is no god but one God and there is no entity in existence that is obligatory and deserving of worship in that He is the originator of all existences except one God, described as oneness, exalted above accepting partnership and from the addition of absorption. And if they do not desist from what they say and do not unite. A painful punishment will surely befall those of them who disbelieve meaning that it will befall those of them who remain in disbelief, or it will befall those of the Christians who disbelieved, he put it in place of will befall them to repeat the testimony to their disbelief and to draw attention to the fact that the punishment is upon those who persist in disbelief and do not abandon it, so he followed it with his saying:
5:74: 74 Will they not repent to God and seek His forgiveness? That is, will they not repent by abandoning those false beliefs and sayings and seek His forgiveness by believing in monotheism and being free from union and incarnation after this report and threat. And God is Forgiving and Merciful. He forgives them and grants them from His grace if they repent. In this questioning there is astonishment at their insistence.
5:75: 75 The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; many were the messengers who passed away before him. That is, he was no more than a messenger like the messengers before him. God Almighty singled him out with signs just as He singled them out with them. If he revived the dead at his hand, he revived the staff and made it a living, moving creature at the hand of Moses, peace be upon him, which is more amazing. If he created him without a father, he created Adam without a father or mother, which is even stranger. And his mother was a truthful woman, like all the other women who adhere to truthfulness, or who believe the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. They were eating food and they were in need of it as animals are in need. He first explained the utmost perfection they had and indicated that it did not necessitate divinity for them because many people share in the same. Then he pointed out their deficiency and mentioned what contradicts divinity and necessitates that they be among the corrupt existing compounds. Then he expressed amazement at those who claim divinity for them with such clear evidence, saying: See how We make clear to them the signs, then see how they are deluded. How are they turned away from listening to the truth and contemplating it? Then there is the difference between the two wonders, meaning that Our explanation of the signs is a wonder and their turning away from them is even more amazing.
5:76: 76 "Say: Do you worship besides God that which has no power to harm or benefit you?" meaning Jesus, peace be upon him, and even if he possessed that by God Almighty's giving him power, he does not possess it of his own accord, nor does he possess anything like what God Almighty harms with of afflictions and calamities, nor what he benefits with of health and abundance. Rather, he said what in view of what he is in his own right, as a prelude to denying power from him outright, and as a warning that he is of this kind, and whoever has a reality that accepts similarity and participation is isolated from divinity. Rather, he mentioned harm first because avoiding it is more important than seeking benefit. And God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing of words and beliefs, so He rewards for them, if good, then good, and if evil, then evil.
5:77: 77 "Say, O People of the Scripture, do not go to extremes in your religion beyond the truth." That is, go to extremes falsely, elevating Jesus, peace be upon him, to the point of claiming divinity for him, or belittling him, claiming that he is not on the right path. It was said that the word "al-Hattāb" refers to the Christians in particular. "And do not follow the inclinations of a people who have gone astray before," meaning their ancestors and imams who had gone astray before the mission of Muhammad, peace be upon him, in their religion. "And they led astray many," of those who followed them in their innovations and misguidance. "And they have gone astray from the straight path," from the straight path, which is Islam, after his mission, peace be upon him, when they denied him and rebelled against him. It was said that the first is an indication of their straying from the requirements of reason, and the second is an indication of their straying from what the religion brought.
5:78: 78 Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary meaning God cursed them in the Psalms and the Gospel by their tongues. It was said that when the people of Ayla transgressed on the Sabbath, God Almighty cursed them by the tongue of David, so God Almighty transformed them into monkeys. And when the people of the table disbelieved, Jesus, peace be upon him, called down curses upon them, so they became pigs, and they were five thousand men. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing meaning that this heinous curse required transformation because of their disobedience and transgression of what was forbidden to them.
5:79: 79 They did not forbid one another from the evil they were doing meaning they did not forbid one another from repeating an evil they were doing, or from doing a similar evil they were doing, or from doing an evil they wanted to do and were preparing for, or they did not desist from it, as they say he forbade the matter and stopped doing it if he refrained. How evil is what they were doing is an expression of astonishment at the evil of their action, confirmed by an oath.
5:80: 80 "You will see many of them" from the People of the Book. "Befriending those who disbelieve" they befriend the polytheists out of hatred for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers. "How evil is that which their souls have put forward for them meaning how evil is something they have put forward so that they will be increased in it on the Day of Resurrection that the wrath of God is upon them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally" is the one singled out for blame, and the meaning is the cause of the wrath of God and eternity in the punishment, or the reason for the blame and the singled out is omitted meaning how evil is that thing because it earned them wrath and eternity.
5:81: 81 And if they had believed in God and the Prophet meaning their Prophet, even though the verse is about the hypocrites, then what is meant is our Prophet, peace be upon him. And what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies since faith prevents that. But many of them are wicked outside their religion or rebellious in their hypocrisy.
5:82: 82 "You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God" because of their intense stubbornness, their increased disbelief, their preoccupation with following whims, their reliance on imitation and their distance from investigation, and their practice of denying and opposing the prophets. "And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, 'We are Christians'" because of their gentleness, the tenderness of their hearts, their lack of desire for this world, and their great interest in knowledge and action. He referred to this by saying: "That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant" about accepting the truth if they understand it, or they are humble and do not act arrogantly like the Jews. This is evidence that humility, turning to knowledge and action, and turning away from desires are praiseworthy, even if they are from a disbeliever.
5:83: 83 "And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears. This is in apposition to they are not arrogant." It is a statement of the tenderness of their hearts, the intensity of their fear, and their haste to accept the truth and their not refusing it. Overflowing is pouring out from fullness, so it was placed in place of fullness for emphasis, or their eyes were made from excessive crying as if they were overflowing with tears themselves. "From what they have known of the truth." The first is for the beginning and the second is to clarify what they have known, or to indicate that it is some of the truth. The meaning is that they have known some of the truth and it made them cry, so how would it be if they knew all of it? "They say, 'Our Lord, we have believed'" in that or in Muhammad. "Then register us among the witnesses," of those who have testified that it is the truth, or of his prophethood, or of his nation who are witnesses over the nations on the Day of Resurrection.
5:84: 84 And why should we not believe in God and in what has come to us of the truth and hope that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people?" A question of denial and exclusion of the absence of faith while the motive is present, which is the hope of joining with the righteous and entering into their presence, or an answer to a questioner who said, "Why did you believe? And we do not believe" is a state of the pronoun and the factor is what is in the lam of the meaning of the verb, i.e. what happened to us other than believing in God, i.e. in His Oneness, for they were triune. Or in His Book and His Messenger, for belief in them is true belief in Him, and its mention is an introduction and glorification, and we hope is in apposition to we believe or a deleted predicate, and the waw is for the state, i.e. and we hope and the factor in it is the workers of the first, restricted by it or we believe.
5:85: 85 So God rewarded them for what they said meaning for believing what you said, the saying of so-and-so, meaning his belief. "Gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. That is the reward of the doers of good" those who looked and acted well, or those who were accustomed to doing good in matters and the four verses. It was narrated that "it was revealed about the Negus and his companions. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him his letter and he read it, then he called Ja'far bin Abi Talib and the Muhajireen with him and brought the monks and priests, so he ordered Ja'far to recite the Qur'an to them. He recited Surat Al-Ma'idah and Maryam, so they wept and believed in the Qur'an." It was said that it was revealed about thirty or seventy men from his people who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he recited Surat Yasin to them, so they wept and believed.
5:86: 86 "And those who disbelieved and denied Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire." The denial of God's signs is linked to disbelief, which is a type of it because the intention is to explain the state of the deniers and mention them in the context of those who believe in them, combining encouragement and intimidation.
5:89: 87 "O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you" meaning whatever is pleasant and delicious from it. It is as if what preceded it included praise for the Christians for their monasticism and the urging to subdue the soul and reject desires, then it was followed by a prohibition against going to extremes in that and transgressing against what God, the Most High, has set by making what is lawful forbidden, so He said: "And do not transgress. Indeed, God does not like transgressors." It is possible that it is meant by it and do not transgress the limits of what God has made lawful for you to what He has forbidden you, so the verse is a prohibition against forbidding what is lawful and permitting what is forbidden, calling for moderation between them. It was narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, described the Day of Judgment to his companions one day and warned them in detail. They dispersed and gathered in the house of Uthman ibn Maz’un and agreed that they would continue to fast and stand in prayer, not to sleep on their beds, not to eat meat or fat, not to approach women or perfume, to reject the world, to wear hair-sackcloth, to roam the earth, and to remove their private parts. When this reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said to them: I did not command you to do this. Your souls have rights over you, so fast and break your fast, stand and sleep. I stand and sleep, fast and break my fast, eat meat and fat, and have intercourse with women. Whoever turns away from my way is not of me. So this was revealed. 89 God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths is what a person says without intending it, such as when a person says: No, by God, and yes, by God. This is what Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, said. It was also said that it is an oath based on what he thinks is the case but it was not, and this is what Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said. In your oaths there is a connection to He will hold you accountable or the unintentional because it is a source or a state of it. But He will hold you accountable for what you have pledged is for what you have pledged with intention and purpose. The meaning is But He will hold you accountable for what you have pledged if you break your oaths or violate what you have pledged, so it was deleted because it is known. Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Ibn Ayyash read on the authority of Asim aqaddum with a light vowel, and Ibn Amir, according to the narration of Ibn Dhakwan, aqaddum, which is from the active participle meaning to do. His expiation means the expiation for breaking the oath, i.e. the act that removes his sin and covers it. The apparent meaning is used as evidence for the permissibility of expiating with money before breaking the oath, which according to us is contrary to the Hanafi school of thought, due to the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever swears an oath and sees something better than it, let him expiate for his oath and do what is better. "Feeding ten poor people from the average of what you feed your families" is what I mean in type and amount, which is a mudd for each poor person according to us and half a sa' according to the Hanafi school of thought. Its place is in the accusative case because it is an attribute of a deleted object, the meaning of which is: that you feed ten poor people food from the average of what you feed, or in the nominative case as a substitute for feeding, and families are like lands. "Ahlikum" is read with a sukoon on the yaa according to the language of those who make it sukoon in the three cases like alif, and it is the plural of ahl like al-layali in the plural of lail and al-ardi in the plural of ard. It is also said that it is the plural of ahl. "Or their clothing" is in apposition to feeding or from awsat if it is made a substitute, which is a garment that covers the private parts. It is also said that it is a garment that includes a shirt, a cloak, or a loincloth. It is read with a damma on the kaf, which is a language like qudwa in qudwa and kasawatum meaning or like what you feed your families, whether it is extravagance or stinginess, you treat them equally if you do not feed them the middle, and the kaf is in the nominative case and its meaning is: or feeding them as their families. "Or freeing a slave" or freeing a person, and the condition of al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him, in oaths is based on analogy to the expiation for murder, and the meaning of or is obligating one of the three qualities absolutely and giving the expiator the choice in specifying. "So whoever does not find" means one of them. "Then fasting three days." Its expiation is fasting three days. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, stipulated that it be consecutive because it was read "three days." The exceptions are not considered evidence in our view if they are not proven in the Book or narrated in the Sunnah. "That" means what was mentioned. "The expiation for your oaths when you swear" and break your oaths. "And guard your oaths" by being stingy with them and not spending them for every matter, or by being righteous in them as much as you can and not missing any good, or by expiating them if you break your oaths. "Likewise" means like that explanation. "God makes clear to you His verses" the signs of His laws. "That you may be grateful" the blessing of teaching or the blessing of being grateful for, because such an explanation makes it easy for you to get out of it.
5:88: 88 And eat of what God has provided for you [that is] lawful and good. That is, eat what is lawful for you and good from what God has provided for you. Thus, lawful is the object of eat and of what is a preposition of it precedes it because it is indefinite. It is possible for min to be an introductory particle related to eat, or it is possible for it to be the object and lawful to be a preposition of the relative pronoun, or the omitted pronoun, or an attribute of a omitted source. According to the aspects, if the provision had not been unlawful, there would have been no additional benefit in mentioning lawful. "And fear God, in whom you are believers."
5:90: 90 "O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, idols, and divining arrows are but [all] evil deeds" meaning the idols set up for worship. "And divining arrows" were explained previously at the beginning of the surah. "Abomination" is filth that the minds reject. It was made singular because it is the predicate of intoxicants, and the predicate of the conjoined words is omitted or for an omitted complement, as if he said: Indeed, the consumption of intoxicants and gambling is but from the work of Satan" because it is caused by his temptation and beautification. So avoid it the pronoun refers to the abomination or to what was mentioned or to the consumption. That you may succeed so that you may succeed by avoiding it. Know that He, the Most High, has emphasized the prohibition of alcohol and gambling in this verse, by beginning the sentence with only and pairing them with idols and arrows, and calling them filth, and making them the work of Satan, as a warning that engaging in them is pure or predominant evil, and He has ordered avoiding them and made them a reason from which success can be hoped. Then He has established that by saying that while they contain worldly and religious corruptions that necessitate prohibition, the Most High has said:
5:91: 91 Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. He singled them out by repeating the mention and explaining what is in them of evil, to draw attention to the fact that they are the intended meaning of the explanation. He mentioned the idols and arrows to indicate that they are like them in sanctity and evil, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: The one who drinks alcohol is like the one who worships an idol. He singled out prayer from the mention by singling it out for the sake of glorification and to indicate that the one who averts it is like the one who averts faith in that it is its pillar and the difference between it and disbelief. Then he repeated the urging to desist in the form of a question, arranged according to what came before from the types of averting things, so he said: Will you then desist? as an indication that the matter of prohibition and warning has reached its climax and that the excuses have been cut off.
5:92: 92 And obey God and obey the Messenger in what they have commanded. And beware of what they have forbidden or disobeying them. But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification meaning, know that you have not harmed the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, by turning away, for he is only responsible for the notification and he has delivered it, and you have only harmed yourselves by it.
7:32: 93 There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten of what was not forbidden to them, according to His saying: If they fear God and believe and do righteous deeds meaning they fear what is forbidden and remain steadfast in faith and righteous deeds. Then fear what was forbidden to them after that, such as alcohol. And believe in its prohibition. Then fear then they continued and remained steadfast in avoiding sins. And do good and sought out beautiful deeds and occupied themselves with them. It was narrated that "when the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, the Companions, may God be pleased with them, said, O Messenger of God, what about our brothers who died while they were drinking alcohol and consuming gambling?" So it was revealed. This repetition may be in consideration of the three times, or in consideration of the three states of man’s use of piety and faith between himself and himself, between people and God Almighty, and therefore faith was replaced by goodness in the third instance, indicating what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said in his interpretation, or in consideration of the three levels, the middle principle and the end, or in consideration of what is avoided, for he should leave the forbidden things to avoid punishment and doubts, to guard against falling into the forbidden, and some of the permissible things to protect the soul from baseness and to refine it from the filth of nature. And God loves the doers of good, so He does not hold them accountable for anything, and in it is that whoever does that becomes a doer of good, and whoever becomes a doer of good becomes beloved to God. 32. "Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God" of clothing and other things with which one adorns oneself which He has produced for His servants of plants such as cotton and linen, and animals such as silk and wool, and minerals such as armor, and the good things of provision of the pleasures of food and drink. This is evidence that the basic principle regarding food, clothing, and types of adornment is permissibility, because the question in who is for denial. "Say: It is for those who believed in the worldly life" originally, and the disbelievers, even if they share it with them, then it is followed. Purely for the Day of Resurrection no one else shares it with them, and its accusative is in the state. Nafi' read it in the nominative case as report after report. Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know. That is, just as We detail this ruling, We detail all other rulings for them.
5:94: 94 O you who have believed, God will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and spears may reach. It was revealed in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. God, the Most High, tested them with hunting, and the wild beasts would overtake them in their camps, such that they could catch them by taking them by the hand and stabbing them with their spears while they were in the state of ihram. The belittling and disparaging of something is to draw attention to the fact that it is not one of the great things that destroy the feet, like the test of sacrificing lives and wealth. So how can someone who is not steadfast in it be steadfast in something more severe than it? That God may know who fears Him in the unseen. So that the one who fears His punishment while he is absent and awaiting it, due to the strength of his faith, may be distinguished from the one who does not fear Him due to the weakness of his heart and the lack of his faith. So He mentioned knowledge and meant the occurrence of the known and its appearance, or the attachment of knowledge. But whoever transgresses after that, after that test of hunting. He will have a painful punishment. The threat will follow him. If someone does not control his temper in such a matter and does not observe God’s ruling in it, then how will he be in what the soul is more inclined to and keen on?
5:95: 95 O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram meaning in a state of ihram, the plural of haram is radah and radah, and perhaps he mentioned killing without slaughtering and ritual slaughter for the sake of generalization, and he meant by game what its meat is eaten because it is the most common type of it according to custom, and this is supported by his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Five are to be killed in the sanctuary and outside of it: the kite, the crow, the scorpion, the mouse, and the rabid dog." In another narration, the snake is used instead of the scorpion, with what it contains of warning about the permissibility of killing any harmful thing, and there is a difference of opinion as to whether this prohibition cancels the ruling on slaughtering, so that the slaughtered animal of a person in a state of ihram is considered dead, and the slaughtered animal of a pagan is considered dead, or not, so it is like a sheep that has been usurped if the usurper slaughters it. And whoever among you kills him intentionally, mentioning his state of ihram, knowing that it was forbidden for him before he killed him. Most of them say that mentioning it is not to restrict the obligation of the penalty, since the intentional and accidental destruction are the same in requiring compensation, but because of His saying: And whoever returns, God will take vengeance on him. And because the verse was revealed regarding the one who did it intentionally, since it was narrated that during the Umrah of Hudaybiyyah, a wild donkey came across them, so Abu al-Yusr stabbed it with his spear and killed it. So it was revealed. Then the recompense is like that which he killed of livestock, raising the recompense. The recitation of the Kufians and Yaqub means upon him, meaning his obligation is a recompense similar to that which he killed of livestock. Accordingly, the preposition is not connected to recompense to separate between them by the description, since the object of the source is like its relative clause, so what is not completed by it is not described, but rather it is its description. The rest read by adding the source to the object and inserting the like of me as in their saying like me does not say such-and-such, and the meaning is then upon him is the recompense like that which he killed. It was read as fajaz mithlī ma qatal with the accusative case, as falijaz jaza’, or he must repay a penalty similar to what he killed, and his penalty is like what he killed. This resemblance is based on creation and appearance according to Malik and al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with them, and the value according to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, who said: The game is to be hunted where it is hunted. If it reaches the value, then it is sacrificed. He has the choice between sacrificing what is its value or buying food with it, so he gives each poor person half a sa’ of wheat or a sa’ of other food, or fasting for each poor person one day. If it does not reach the value, he has the choice between feeding and fasting. The wording for the first is more appropriate. Two just men among you shall judge by it is a description of jaza’ and it is possible that it is a state of its pronoun in its predicate or from it if you add it, or its description and raising it with the predicate of qadar for whom. Just as estimation requires consideration and effort, it requires similarity in creation and appearance to it, as the species are very similar. It was read dhu ‘adl to mean the genus or the imam. A gift is a state of the ha' in bih or of jaza' and if it is nun because it is specific to the description, or a substitute for mithl in consideration of its location or its wording in the one who put it in the accusative case. Reaching the Ka'bah is a description of a gift because its addition is verbal and the meaning of its reaching the Ka'bah is slaughtering it in the Sacred Sanctuary and giving it in charity. Abu Hanifa said that it is slaughtered in the Sacred Sanctuary and given in charity wherever he wants. Or expiation is in apposition to jaza' if you put it in the nominative case and if you put it in the accusative case then it is the predicate of an omitted word. Food for the poor is in apposition to an explanation or a substitute for them or the predicate of an omitted word, meaning it is food. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read the expiation of food with the addition of clarification like you say: a silver ring, and the meaning according to al-Shafi'i is or that he expiates by feeding the poor what is equal to the value of the gift from the most common food of the country, so he gives each poor person a mudd. Or the equivalent of that in fasting or what is other than that of fasting, so he fasts for the food of each poor person one day, and it is originally a source used for the passive participle. It is read with a kasra on the ‘ayn, which is what is equal to something in the estimated, like the equal of a load, and this is an indication of food, and fasting is a distinction for justice. So that he may taste the burden of his affair is related to mah, meaning that he must pay the penalty, or food, or fast, so that he may taste the weight of his action and the bad consequences of his violation of the sanctity of ihram, or the severe burden of disobeying the command of God Almighty. The origin of wabil is heaviness, and from it comes wabil food. God has pardoned what is past from killing game while it was forbidden in the pre-Islamic era or before the prohibition, or this time. And whoever returns to such a thing. So God will take revenge on him so God will take revenge on him, and there is nothing in it that prevents expiation for the one who returns, as was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Shuraih. And God is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution from what he persisted in disobeying Him.
5:96: 96 Lawful to you is the game of the sea means what is caught from it that lives only in water, and it is all lawful because of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, about the sea its water is pure and its dead are lawful. Abu Hanifa said that only fish is lawful. It was said that fish and what is eaten on land are lawful. And its food is what it throws up or evaporates from. It was said that the pronoun refers to the game and its food is eating it. Provision for you provision for you is in the accusative case of purpose. And for travelers means and for your travelers they stock up on dried meat. And forbidden to you is the game of the land means what is caught in it, or hunting in it. According to the first, what is hunted by the halal is also forbidden to the pilgrim even if he has no role in it. The majority are of the opinion that it is lawful because of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, The meat of the game is lawful to you, as long as you do not hunt it or it is hunted for you "As long as you are in the state of ihram" means in the state of ihram. It was read with a kasra on the dal from dam yadam. "And fear God to whom you will be gathered."
5:97: 97 God made the Kaaba He made it, and it was called the Kaaba because of its cube-like shape. The Sacred House is an explanatory apposition for the sake of praise, or the second object. Standing for people is a refreshment for them, meaning a reason for their refreshment in the matter of their livelihood and their afterlife. The fearful seek refuge in it and the weak are safe in it, and the merchants profit in it and the pilgrims and the worshippers head to it, or what their religious and worldly affairs are established by. Ibn Amir read standing as a source on a verb like satiety, raising its eye as it raises it as in its verb and making it accusative on the source or state. And the sacred month and the offerings and the necklaces This has been explained previously and what is meant is the month in which the Hajj is performed, which is Dhul-Hijjah because it is suitable for its peers and it was said the genus. That is an indication of the making, or what was mentioned about the command to preserve the sanctity of ihram and other things. So that you may know that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth. For the laws were legislated to prevent harm before it occurs and to bring about the benefits that result from it, which is evidence of the wisdom of the Lawgiver and the perfection of His knowledge. And that God is Knowing of all things. Generalization after specification and exaggeration after generalization.
5:98: 98 Know that God is severe in punishment and that God is Forgiving and Merciful. A warning and a promise to whoever violates His prohibitions and to whoever maintains them, or to whoever persists in them and to whoever does not desist from them.
5:99: 99 The Messenger has no duty except to convey the message. This is an emphasis on the obligation to carry out what he was commanded to do, i.e. the Messenger came with what he was commanded to convey, and you have no excuse for negligence. And God knows what you reveal and what you conceal of belief and denial, action and determination.
5:100: 100 "Say: The bad and the good are not equal." A general rule in denying equality before God, the Most High, between the bad people, deeds, and money and the good ones. He encouraged the interests of work and lawful money. "Even if the abundance of the bad pleases you." The point is in the good and bad, not the little and the much, because the little that is praised is better than the much that is blameworthy. The address is to everyone who considers, and for this reason He said: "So fear God, O you of understanding." That is, fear Him in seeking out the bad even if it is abundant, and prefer the good even if it is little. "That you may succeed." Hoping to attain success. It was narrated that it was revealed about the pilgrims of Yamamah when the Muslims intended to attack them, so they were forbidden from doing so, even though they were polytheists.
5:101: 101 "O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, will distress you. But if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be made clear to you." The conditional and what is conjoined to it are two descriptions of things, and the meaning is: Do not ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about things which, if they are made known to you, will distress you, and if you ask about them during the time of revelation, they will be made clear to you. They are like two premises that produce what prevents the question, which is that it is something that distresses them, and the wise person does not do what distresses him. Things are a collective noun like Ṭarfā’ except that its lam was changed and made fa’ā’. It was said that af’alā’ had its lam deleted, making it a plural for shay’, on the basis that its original form is shay’ like hayn, or shay’ like Ṣadiq, so it was lightened. It was said that af’al is a plural for it without change, like bayt and abaiyat, and this is rejected by the prevention of its inflection. God has pardoned them is another description, meaning about things that God has pardoned and is not obligated to do. It was narrated that “when the verse ‘Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind’ was revealed, Suraqah ibn Malik said: He ate one year and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him until he repeated it three times, then he said: No, even if I had said yes, it would have been obligatory, and if it were obligatory you would not have been able to, so leave me as I left you, so it was revealed, ‘or a resumption, meaning God has pardoned what you asked in the past, so do not return to the like of it. ‘And God is Forgiving and Forbearing’ He does not hasten to punish you for what you neglect, and He pardons much. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, ‘that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering a sermon one day and he was angry because of the many questions they asked about him that did not concern them, so he said: I will not be asked about anything except that I will answer, so a man said: Where is my father? He said: In the Fire, and another said: Who is my father? He said: Hudhafah, and he was called for someone else, so it was revealed.”
5:102: 102 "A people asked about it in the pronoun for the issue indicated by asked and therefore it did not return with about" or for things by deleting the preposition. "Before you is related to asked and is not an attribute of people, for the circumstance of time cannot be an attribute of the body nor a state of from" nor a predicate of it. "Then they became disbelievers in it" meaning because of it, as they did not follow what they asked in denial. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 9 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Māidah, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Anʿām. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. 6:143: 103Allah has not made any bahīrah, nor sā'ibah, nor wasīlah, nor Ḥām is a refutation and denial of what the people of ignorance innovated, which is that if a female camel gave birth to five offspring, the last of which was a male, they would slit its ear and set it free, so it could not be ridden or milked. A man among them would say: If I recover, my she-camel is ṣā'ibah, making it like a bahīrah in prohibiting benefit from it. If a sheep gave birth to a female, it is theirs, and if it gave birth to a male, it is for their gods, and if it gave birth to both of them, it would say the female joined her brother, so the male is not slaughtered for her. If ten offspring were born from the loins of a male, they would forbid its back and not prevent it from water or pasture, and they would say: its back has been protected. The meaning of what was made is what was prescribed and established, and for this reason it is transitive to one object, which is bahīrah, and from an additional verb. But those who disbelieve invent a lie against God by prohibiting that and attributing it to God, the Most High. And most of them do not reason, meaning the lawful from the unlawful, the permissible from the forbidden, or the command from the prohibition, but they imitate their elders. It is mentioned that some of them know the invalidity of that, but the love of leadership and imitating their fathers prevents them from acknowledging it. 143 "Eight pairs" instead of a load and a furnishing, or the object of eat, and do not follow an object between them or a verb that indicates it or a state of what means different or multiple and the pair is what has another of its kind with it to mate it. It may be said for their group and the first is meant. "Of the sheep two" two pairs, the ram and the ewe, and it is a substitute for eight and two was read as the beginning. And "the sheep" is a generic name like camels and its plural is two or the plural of a sheep like a merchant and a merchant. And it was read with the opening of the hamza and it is a language in it. "Of the goats two" the male goat and the female goat, and Ibn Kathir read Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Yaqub with the fat-ha, which is the plural of ma’iz, like sahib and sahab, haris and hars, and the goat was read Say, ‘Are the two males?’ The male of the sheep and the male of the goat Haram, or the two females? “Or their two females?” And the accusative of the two males and the two is with haram, Am Istamma alayhi arham al-antheen or what the females of both sexes carry, whether male or female, Inform me with knowledge with a known matter indicating that God Almighty has forbidden something of that, if you are truthful, claiming that it is forbidden.
5:104: 104 "And when it is said to them, Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger, they say, Sufficient for us is that which we found our fathers doing. This is a statement of the shortcomings of their minds and their preoccupation with imitation and that they have no support other than it. Or even if their fathers did not know anything and were not guided. The waw is for the state and the hamza was added to it to deny the action in this state, meaning, what they found their fathers doing is sufficient for them, even if they were ignorant and misguided. The meaning is that following the example is only valid for someone who is known to be knowledgeable and guided, and that is not known except by proof, so imitation is not sufficient.
5:105: 105 O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves meaning, protect them and adhere to their reform, and the preposition with the noun is made a noun for adherence and therefore the noun of yourselves is in the accusative case. It is read in the nominative case as a subject. He who goes astray will not harm you if you are guided Misguidance will not harm you if you are guided, and guidance includes denouncing evil according to one's ability as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Whoever among you sees an evil and is able to change it with his hand, let him change it with his hand, and if he is not able to, then with his tongue, and if he is not able to, then with his heart. The verse was revealed when the believers felt sorry for the disbelievers and wished for their faith, and it was said that when a man converted to Islam, they would say to him, You have made your fathers foolish, so it was revealed. La yadhirkum may be in the nominative case as a new sentence, and this is supported by the fact that it was read La yadhirkum and the jussive mood as an answer or a prohibition, but the ra' was added as a damma in imitation of the damma of the dad that was transferred to it from the assimilated ra', and this is supported by the reading of those who read La yadhirkum with a fatha, and La yadhirkum with a kasra of the dad and a damma from darah yadhiruhu and yadhuruhu. To God is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you used to do. A promise and a threat to both groups, and a warning that no one will be held accountable for the sin of another.
5:106: 106 O you who have believed, a testimony among you meaning in what you are commanded, a testimony among you, and what is meant by testimony is the witnessing of the will and its addition to the circumstance in the expansion, and testimony was read in the accusative and with the tanween on to stand. If death approaches one of you if he is close to it and its signs appear, and it is a circumstance of testimony. When the will is made is a substitute for it, and its substitution is an indication that the will is something that should not be taken lightly, or it is a circumstance of the present. Two is the subject of testimony, and it is possible for its predicate to be with the omission of the added. Two just men among you meaning from your relatives or from the Muslims, and they are two attributes of two. Or two others from other than you is in apposition to two, and whoever interprets other as the People of the Covenant made it abrogated, because his testimony against a Muslim is not heard unanimously. If you travel in the land meaning you travel in it. And the disaster of death befalls you meaning you are close to the appointed time. You detain them you make them stand and you make them patient is an attribute of the others and the condition with its deleted answer indicated by his saying or two others from other than you is an objection, the benefit of which is to indicate that two of you should testify, and if that is not possible as in the case of travel, then from other than you, or a resumption as if it was said how do we act if we are in doubt about the two witnesses and he said you detain them. After the prayer the afternoon prayer, because it is the time when people gather and the angels of the night and the angels of the day clash. And it was said any prayer it was. Then they swear by God if you are in doubt if the heir among you is in doubt. We will not buy with it a price sworn upon, and if you are in doubt is an objection indicating that the oath is specific to the case of doubt. The meaning is we will not exchange the oath or by God for a worldly gain, i.e. we will not swear falsely by God out of greed. Even if he is a relative even if the one to whom the oath is made is close to us, and its answer is also deleted, i.e. we will not buy. And we do not conceal the testimony of God meaning the testimony that God has commanded us to establish. It was narrated from Al-Sha’bi that he stopped at the testimony and then began with God with the extension, deleting the letter of the oath and replacing it with the letter of interrogation. It was narrated from him with other forms, such as their saying, God, I will do it. “Indeed, then we are among the sinners” meaning if we conceal it. It was read among the sinners by deleting the hamza and placing its vowel on the lam and assimilating the nun into it.
5:107: 107If he finds then if he appears. On the basis that they have both committed a sin i.e. they did something that necessitated a sin, such as distortion. Then two others then two other witnesses. They stand in their place from those who have been deserving of it from those who were wronged, and they are the heirs. Hafs read deserved in the active form, which is the first two. The first two are the most deserving of testimony due to their kinship and knowledge, and it is a deleted predicate, i.e. they are the first two, or the predicate of the last two or a subject whose predicate is the last two, or a substitute for them or for the pronoun in they stand. Hamza, Yaqub, and Abu Bakr read from Asim the first ones as an attribute of those, or a substitute for it, i.e. from the first ones from whom he has been deserving of it. The first ones was read in the dual form and in the accusative case for praise, and the first ones and its parsing is the parsing of the first two. And they shall swear by God, ‘Our testimony is more truthful than theirs’ is more truthful and more deserving of acceptance. And we have not transgressed and we have not exceeded the truth therein. Indeed, we would be among the wrongdoers putting falsehood in place of truth, or wrongdoers themselves if we transgressed. The meaning of the two verses is that if a dying person wants to make a will, he should have two just witnesses from his lineage or religion testify to his will, or he should make a bequest to them as a precaution. If he cannot find them, because he is on a journey, then others from outside them. Then, if a dispute or doubt arises, they should swear to the truth of what they say, making it more severe at the time. If it becomes clear that they lied due to an indication or suspicion, two other guardians of the deceased should swear. The ruling is abrogated if the two witnesses are present, for the witness is not contradicted, and his oath is not contradicted by the oath of the heir. It is established if they are guardians, and the oath is returned to the heirs, either because the betrayal of the guardians is apparent, for the guardian’s confirmation of the oath is due to his trustworthiness, or to change the claim. It was narrated that Tamim al-Dari and Adi ibn Zayd went to the Levant for trade, and they were Christians at the time, and with them was Badil, the freed slave of Amr ibn al-Aas, who was a Muslim. When they arrived in the Levant, Badil fell ill and wrote down what he had with him in a document and threw it in his belongings without telling them about it. He instructed them to give his belongings to his family and he died. They searched him and took from him a silver vessel containing three hundred mithqals engraved with gold, and they hid it. His family found the document and demanded the vessel from them, but they denied it. They brought their case to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed: O you who believe, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made them swear an oath after the afternoon prayer at the pulpit and released them. Then the vessel was found in their hands, and Banu Sahm came to them about that and said: We bought it from him, but we had no evidence against him, so we hated to bring it near. They brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed: But if he stumbles, so Amr ibn al-Aas and al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada’ah al-Sahmani stood up and swore and claimed it. Perhaps the number is allocated to both of them for the specific incident.

The pronoun is plural because it is a ruling that includes all witnesses. And fear God and listen what you are commanded to hear in response. And God does not guide the wicked people meaning if you do not fear God and do not listen, you will be a wicked people. And God does not guide the wicked people meaning He does not guide them to an argument or to the path to Paradise. So the Almighty says:
5:109: 109 The Day God will gather the messengers is an adverb for it. It was said that it is a substitute for the object of and fear as a substitute for inclusion, or the object of and listen with the deletion of the complement, meaning and listen to the report of the Day they are gathered, or it is accusative with the implication of remember. "He will say," meaning to the messengers. "What did you answer? meaning the answer you answered, on the basis that what" is in the place of the source, or with what did you answer, so the preposition was deleted. This question is to rebuke their people, just as the question of affection is to rebuke the one who is not familiar with it. Therefore, "They said, 'We have no knowledge,'" meaning we have no knowledge of what you do not know. "Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen." So You know what we know of what they answered us and showed us and what we do not know of what they concealed in their hearts. In it is the complaint against them and the matter is referred back to His knowledge for what they suffered from them. It was said that the meaning is we have no knowledge besides Your knowledge, or we have no knowledge of what they innovated after us, and the judgment is only for the conclusion. "Alam was read in the accusative case, indicating that the speech was completed by saying You are you, meaning that you are the one described by your known attributes, and Alam" is in the accusative case for specification or calling. Abu Bakr and Hamza read "al-Ghayub with a kasra on the ghayn" wherever it occurred.
5:110: 110"When God said, 'O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother' instead of the Day of Gathering, which is the way. And He called the companions of Paradise. The meaning is that He, glory be to Him, will rebuke the disbelievers on that Day by asking the messengers about their answer and enumerating the signs He showed them, so a group denied them and called them magicians, and others went too far and took them as gods. Or it was erected with the implication of remember. When I supported you I strengthened you, which is an adverb for My favor or a state of it, and it was read as I supported you. This is supported by His statement: "He spoke to people in the cradle and as an adult", that is, while he was in the cradle and as an adult. The meaning is that he spoke to them in childhood and adulthood alike, and the meaning is to connect his state in childhood to the state of adulthood in the perfection of reason and speech. This is evidence that he will descend, for he was raised before he was completed. "And when I taught you the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel. Nafi and Yaqub read "bird", and it can be singular or plural like Al Baqir. "And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you", meaning the Jews when they intended to kill him. "When you came to them with clear proofs" is an adverb for restrained. Then those who disbelieved among them said, ‘This is nothing but obvious magic.’ That is, what you have brought is nothing but obvious magic. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read, Except a magician, so the reference is to Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him.
5:111: 111 And when I inspired the disciples that is, I commanded them through the tongues of My messengers. To believe in Me and My Messenger. It is possible that an is a source or an explanatory particle. They said, 'We believe, and bear witness that we are Muslims' sincere.
5:112: 112 When the disciples said, O Jesus, son of Mary, is in the accusative case, or an adverb for they said, so it is an indication that their claim of sincerity, along with their statement, Can your Lord send down to us a table from the heaven? was not yet clear and well-known. It was said that this ability is based on what wisdom and will require, not on what ability requires. It was said that the meaning is Does your Lord obey? meaning Does He answer you? and Isti'a means obeyed, like Isti'a and Ijaba. Al-Kisa'i read Isti'a Rabbik, meaning Do you ask Him that without a diverter? The table is the tray if there is food on it, from the substance of water, it sways if it moves, or from the substance if it is given to it, as if it sways from those who come to it. Its equivalent is their statement, A grafted tree. "He said, 'Fear God,'" is similar to this question. "If you are believers," in the perfection of His power and the truth of my prophethood, you are truthful in your claim of faith.
5:113: 113"They said, 'We want to eat from it.'" An introduction to the excuse and explanation of what prompted them to ask, which was to enjoy eating from it. "And our hearts will be reassured." By adding the knowledge of observation to the knowledge of inference with the perfection of His power, glory be to Him. "And we will know that you have spoken the truth to us." In claiming prophethood, or that God answers our call. "And we will be among its witnesses." If you call us to witness, or among the witnesses of the eye, not the hearers of the report.
5:114: 114Jesus, son of Mary, said when he saw that they had a valid purpose in that, or that they would not give up, so he wanted to force them to submit the argument in its entirety. O God, our Lord, send down upon us a table from the heaven that will be for us a festival meaning that the day of its descent will be a festival that we will honor. It was said that the festival is the returning joy, and that is why the day of the festival was called a festival. Takun was read as an answer to the command. For our first and our last instead of for us by returning the factor, meaning a festival for our predecessors and our successors. And You are the best of providers meaning the best of those who provide, because He is the Creator of provision and the Giver of it without compensation.
5:115: 115 God said, 'I will send it down upon you' in response to your question. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, and 'Asim read its place with emphasis. But whoever among you disbelieves after that, I will punish him with a severe punishment meaning a punishment. It is permissible to make it a direct object, with flexibility. I will not punish him the pronoun refers to the source, or to the punishment if what is meant is what he is punished with, with the deletion of the preposition. Anyone from the worlds meaning from the worlds of their time or for the worlds in general, for they were transformed into monkeys and pigs, and no one else was punished with the like of that. It was narrated that a red table came down between two clouds while they were looking at it until it fell in their hands, so Jesus, peace be upon him, cried and said: O God, make me among the grateful. O God, make it a mercy and do not make it an example and a punishment. Then he stood up, performed ablution, prayed and cried, then uncovered the handkerchief and said: In the name of God, the best of providers. Then there was a grilled fish without scales or thorns, dripping with fat, and at its head was salt and at its tail was vinegar and around it were various kinds of vegetables except leeks, and there were five loaves of bread, on one of which were olives, on the second was honey, on the third was ghee, on the fourth was cheese, and on the fifth was dried meat. Simon said: O Spirit of God, is it from the food of this world or from the food of the Hereafter? He said: It is neither of them, but God Almighty invented it with His power. Eat what you asked for and be grateful, and God will provide for you and increase you from His bounty. They said: O Spirit of God, if you would show us Muhammad this sign as another sign. He said: O fish, come back to life by the permission of God Almighty. It was shaken, then He said to it, return to how it was, and it returned grilled, then the table flew away. Then they disobeyed and were transformed. It was said that it would come to them for forty days in a row, and the poor and the rich, the young and the old, would gather around it to eat, until when the shade was full, it would fly away while they looked at its shade. No poor person ate from it except a rich person for the rest of his life, and no sick person except that he recovered and never got sick again. Then God Almighty revealed to Jesus, peace be upon him, to make my table for the poor and the sick without the rich and the healthy. The people were upset because of this, so eighty-three men from them were transformed. It was said that when God promised to send it down with this condition, they refused and said: We do not want it, so it was not sent down. And Mujahid said that this is an example that God gave for those who propose miracles. And about the Sufis: The table here is an expression of the truths of knowledge, for it is the food of the soul just as food is the food of the body. Based on this, perhaps the case is that they desired truths that they were not prepared to stand upon, so Jesus, peace be upon him, said to them: If you have attained faith, then use piety until you are able to know about it. But they did not stop asking and insisted on it, so he asked because of their suggestion. So God, the Most High, the Most Great, explained that its revelation is easy, but there is danger and fear of consequences in it, for if the traveler is shown what is higher than his station, perhaps he will not be able to bear it and will not settle for it, so he will go astray far astray.
5:116: 116 "And when God said, O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as gods besides God?'" He means by this to rebuke and rebuke the disbelievers, and without is not an attribute of two gods or a connection to take me, and the meaning of without is either different, so it is an alert to the fact that worshipping God, the Most High, with worshipping someone other than Him is both worship, so whoever worships Him with worshipping them is as if he worshipped them and did not worship Him, or for the shortcoming, for they did not believe that they were independent in deserving worship, but rather they claimed that their worship leads to the worship of God, the Most High, as if it was said: Take me and my mother as gods who lead us to God, the Most High. "He said, Glory be to You," I declare You to be far removed from having a partner. "It is not for me to say what I have no right to say," it is not appropriate for me to say a statement that I have no right to say. “If you said it, then you knew it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in your soul.” You know what I conceal in my soul, just as you know what I declare, and I do not know what you conceal of your knowledge. His saying in your soul is for similarity, and it was said that what is meant by the soul is the self. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen is a confirmation of the two sentences in terms of their explicit and implied meanings.
5:117: 117 I only said to them what you commanded me to do is a statement of negating the questioner after presenting what indicates it. Worship God, my Lord and your Lord is an explanatory apposition for the pronoun in it, or a substitute for it. It is not a condition of the substitute to allow the substituted to be dropped absolutely, so that the relative pronoun remains without a referent, or an implied predicate or its object such as he or I mean. It is not permissible to replace it with what you commanded me to do because the source cannot be the object of the statement, nor can an be explanatory because the command is attributed to God Almighty, and He does not say Worship God, my Lord and your Lord and the statement is not explained, rather the sentence narrates after it unless the statement is interpreted as the command, so it is as if it was said: I only commanded them with what you commanded me to do, which is worship God. And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them meaning a watcher over them, preventing them from saying that and believing it, or witnessing their conditions of faith. When You took me by raising me to the heavens, as He said: Indeed, I will take you and raise you up. Taking is taking something in full, and death is a type of it. God Almighty said: God takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep. “You were the Observer over them” is the observer of their conditions, preventing those whom You wanted to protect from saying it by guiding them to the evidence and alerting them to it by sending messengers and revealing verses. And You are Witness over all things is aware of it and observing it.
5:118: 118 If You punish them, they are Your servants. That is, if You punish them, then You are punishing Your servants, and there is no objection to the absolute owner in what he does with his property, and it is a warning that they deserved that because they are Your servants and they worshipped other than You. And if You forgive them, then indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. There is no weakness or disgrace, for You are the Able, the Strong in reward and punishment, who does not reward or punish except with wisdom and correctness, for forgiveness is desirable for every criminal, so if You punish, then it is just, and if You forgive, then it is gracious. And the non-forgiveness of polytheism based on the threat, there is no impossibility in it in itself to prevent hesitation and the condition that.
5:119: 119Allah said, 'This is a Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness.' Nafi' read Day in the accusative case as an adverb for said and the predicate of this is omitted, or it is a permanent adverb that acts as a predicate and the meaning is this which was mentioned in the words of Jesus, it will occur on a Day when it will benefit. It was said that it is a predicate but it was built on the fat-ha by adding it to the verb and it is not correct because the complement to it is declined and what is meant by truthfulness is truthfulness in this world because what benefits is what is during the state of obligation. "For them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. That is the great attainment." Clarification of the benefit.
5:120: 120 To God belongs the kingdom of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them, and He is over all things competent. This is a warning against the lies of the Christians and the corruption of their claim that the Messiah is their mother. He did not say and whatever is in them in order to give precedence to rational people, but said and whatever is in them in order to follow them who are not rational, informing them that they are extremely deficient in the meaning of Lordship and have descended from the rank of servitude, and to insult them and warn against the similarity that contradicts divinity. Because what is mentioned includes all kinds, it is more appropriate to mean generality. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "Whoever recites Surat Al-Ma'idah will be given ten good deeds, ten bad deeds will be erased from him, and he will be raised ten degrees for the number of every Jew and Christian who breathes in this world." Surat al-An’am 6: 1 Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light. Then those who disbelieve equate others with their Lord. 1- Praise be to God, Who created the heavens and the earth. He informed that He, glory be to Him, is worthy of praise, and pointed out that He is the One who deserves praise or to be praised for these great blessings, to be an argument against those who equate their Lord. He gathered the heavens together without the earth, and they are like them because their layers are different in essence and their effects and movements vary, and He presented them for their honor, high place, and advanced existence. And He made the darkness and the light. He created them, and the difference between creating and making, which has one effect, is that creation has the meaning of estimation, and making has the meaning of inclusion, and therefore He expressed the creation of light and darkness with making, to point out that they do not exist by themselves as dualism claimed, and He gathered the darknesses together for the multitude of their causes and the bodies that carry them, or because darkness is misguidance, and light is guidance, and guidance is one and misguidance is multiple, and He presented them to precede annihilation over the faculties. Whoever claims that darkness is an accident that contradicts light, argues with this verse, and does not know that the absence of possession, like blindness, is not the mere absence, so that making is not connected to it. Then those who disbelieve in their Lord equate is in apposition to His statement, Praise be to God, meaning that God, the Most High, is worthy of praise for what He created as a blessing for His servants. Then those who disbelieve in Him equate, so they are ungrateful for His blessing, and it is with their Lord as a warning that He created these things as reasons for their existence and livelihood, so it is His right to be praised for them and not to be ungrateful. Or according to His statement, Created, meaning that He, the Most High, created what no one else is capable of, then they equate with Him what none of it is capable of. The meaning of then is: an enemy to them after this clarification. The ba in the first case is related to disbelieved, and the conjunction of equate is omitted, meaning they equate with Him so that the denial falls on the action itself. And in the second case, it is related to equate, and the meaning is that the disbelievers equate the idols with their Lord, meaning they equate them with Him, the Most High. Surat al-An’am 6: 2 It is He who created you from clay and then decreed a term, and a specified term is with Him. Then you are in doubt. 2- It is He who created you from clay meaning He began your creation from it, for it is the first material and Adam, who is the origin of mankind, was created from it, or He created your father, so the complement was omitted. Then He decreed a term the term of death. And a specified term with Him the term of resurrection. It was said that the first is between creation and death, and the second is between death and resurrection, for the term, as it is used for the last period, is used for its entirety. It was said that the first is sleep and the second is death. It was said that the first is for those who remain and for those who will come, and the term is indefinite and is specific to the description, and therefore it was dispensed with presenting the report and resuming with it to magnify it, and therefore it was indefinite and described as specified, meaning fixed, specific and does not accept change, and it was reported about it that it is with God, and no one else has any role in it, knowing or having power, and because it is the intended explanation. Then you are in doubt. This excludes their doubt after it has been proven that He is their Creator and the Creator of their origins and the One who will revive them until their appointed times. For He who is able to create and collect materials and deposit life in them and keep them as long as He wills is more able to collect those materials and revive them a second time. The first verse is evidence of monotheism and the second is evidence of resurrection. Doubt is doubt and its root is murri, which is extracting milk from the udder. Surat al-An’am 6: 3 And He is God in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and your public, and He knows what you earn. 3- And He is God the pronoun refers to God, the Most High, and God is its predicate. In the heavens and on the earth is related to the name God and the meaning is He is the One who deserves worship in them and no one else, like His, the Most High, saying: And He is God in the heaven and God on the earth or by His saying: He knows your secret and your public and the sentence is a second predicate, or it is the predicate and God is a substitute, and it is sufficient for the adverbial state to be valid that what is known in them is like your saying I shot the game in the sanctuary if you were outside it and the game was in it or a stable adverbial state that is the predicate, meaning that He, the Most High, due to His perfect knowledge of what is in them is as if He is in them, and He knows your secret and your public is a statement and confirmation of it and it is not related to the source because its description does not precede it. And He knows what you earn of good or evil, so He rewards for it and punishes, and perhaps what is meant by the secret and the public is what is hidden and what is apparent of the states of the souls and by what is acquired is the actions of the limbs. Surat al-An’am 6: 4 And there does not come to them a sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it. 4- And there never comes to them a sign from the signs of their Lord “from” the first is added for comprehensiveness and the second is for partiality, meaning: no evidence from the evidence or miracle from the miracles or a sign from the verses of the Qur’an appears to them except that they turn away from it leaving it to contemplate it and not paying attention to it. Surat al-An’am 6: 5 So they denied the truth when it came to them. So there will come to them report of that which they used to ridicule. 5- They denied the truth when it came to them meaning the Qur'an, and it is like the necessary preceding it, as if it was said: since they were turning away from all the signs, they denied it when it came to them, or as evidence for it on the meaning that since they turned away from the Qur'an and denied it, and it is the greatest of signs, how could they not turn away from anything else, and that is why it was arranged with the letter fa. Then there will come to them report of that which they used to ridicule meaning that what they used to ridicule will appear to them when the punishment descends upon them in this world and the hereafter, or when Islam appears and its matter is raised. Surat al-An’am 6: 6 Have they not seen how many generations before them We destroyed whom We had established upon the earth as We have not established you? And We sent down upon them abundant rain and made rivers flow beneath them. Then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them another generation. 6- "Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them?" That is, of the people of a time, and a century is the period of most people's lives, which is seventy years. It was also said eighty. It was also said that a century is the people of an era in which there is a prophet or someone who excels in knowledge. The period is short or long, and its derivation is from the word "Qarnat. We established them in the land." We made a place for them in it and settled them in it and gave them the strength and tools with which they were able to dispose of it. "What We did not establish for you?" What We did not give you of spaciousness and long stay, O people of Mecca, what We did not give you of strength and spaciousness in money and support in numbers and causes. "And We sent the sky upon them" That is, the rain or clouds, or the canopy, since the beginning of the rain is from it. "Profusely" That is, abundantly. "And We made the rivers flow beneath them" So they lived in fertility and the countryside among the rivers and fruits. "So We destroyed them for their sins" That is, that did not benefit them at all. And We created and brought about. After them another generation instead of them, and the meaning is that just as He, glory be to Him, was able to destroy those before you, such as ‘Aad and Thamud, and create in their place a country to populate with them, He is able to do that to you. Surat al-An’am 6: 7 And if We had sent down to you a book on parchment and they touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, This is not but obvious magic. 7- And if We had sent down to you a book on parchment written on paper. And they touched it with their hands they touched it. The specification of touching is because forgery does not occur in it, so they cannot say, Our eyes were only dazzled, and because sight precedes it where there is no obstacle. Its restriction to hands is to prevent exaggeration, as it may be exaggerated for examination, like His statement: And we have touched the heaven “Those who disbelieve would have said, This is not but obvious magic out of obstinacy and stubbornness. Surat al-An’am 6: 8 And they said, Why was an angel not sent down to him? But if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not have been reprieved. 8- And they said, 'Why was an angel not sent down to him?'" Why was an angel not sent down with him to speak to us that he is a prophet, as He said: "Why was an angel not sent down to him so that he would be with him as a warner? And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been accomplished." This is an answer to their statement and a clarification of what prevents what they suggested and the flaw in it. The meaning is that if the angel had been sent down so that they saw him as they suggested, their destruction would have been inevitable, for that is the way of God with those before them. "Then they would not be respite" after his descent for the blink of an eye. Surat al-An’am 6: 9 And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused for them that which they confused. 9- And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused for them what they confuse. A second answer: If the ha is made for the desired, and if it is made for the messenger, then it is a second suggestion answer, for sometimes they say, Why was an angel not sent down to him?, and sometimes they say, If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels. The meaning is, If We had made a companion for you an angel whom they could see, or the messenger an angel, We would have made him a man, just as Gabriel was made in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi. For human power is not strong enough to see the angel in his form, but only the individuals of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, saw them in this way with their holy power. And to confuse is an omitted answer, that is, if We had made him a man, We would have confounded them, that is, We would have confounded for them what they confuse for themselves, and they would say, This is nothing but a human being like you. And labsna is read with one lam and labsna with emphasis for emphasis. Surat al-An’am 6: 10 And messengers before you were mocked, but that which they used to mock encompassed those who mocked them. 10- And messengers before you were mocked to console the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what he saw from his people.
