Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 10 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Anʿām, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Aʿrāf. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. This is an answer to their saying, Follow our way, and We will bear your sins. "Then to your Lord is your return" on the Day of Resurrection. "And He will inform you about that over which you used to differ" by clarifying guidance from error and distinguishing the truth from the false.
6:165: 165 And it is He who has made you successors on the earth succeeding one another, or successors of God on His earth, disposing of it, as the address is general, or successors of the previous nations, as the address is to the believers. And He has raised some of you above others in degrees in honor and wealth that He may test you in what He has given you of status and money. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment because what is coming is near or because He hastens when He wills it. And indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful He described the punishment and did not attribute it to Himself, and He described Himself with forgiveness and added to it the description with mercy, and He used the construction of exaggeration and the emphatic lam to indicate that He, the Most High, is Forgiving in essence, punishing by accident, abundant in mercy, exaggerating in it, abundant in punishment, forgiving in it. On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Surat Al-An’am was revealed to me all at once, accompanied by seventy thousand angels who chanted glorification and praise. 7:1: Meccan, except for eight verses from His saying: And ask them to His saying: And when We removed the mountain, all of which are decisive. It was said that except for His saying: And turn away from the ignorant, and it has two hundred and five or six verses. 1. The word 'p' has been discussed previously.
7:2: 2. Book is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning it is a book, or the predicate of Alif Lam Meem, which means the surah or the Qur'an. It was revealed to you is its description. So let there not be in your breast any difficulty concerning it meaning doubt, for doubt is difficulty in the breast or constriction of the heart of the one who is trying to convey it for fear that you will lie about it, or fall short in fulfilling his duty towards it. Directing the prohibition to it is for exaggeration, like their saying: I do not see you here. The fa can be interpreted as conjunction or as an answer, so it is as if it was said: If it was revealed to you so that you may warn with it, then let there not be any difficulty in your breast. So that you may warn with it is related to It was revealed or So that you may not be afraid because if he is certain that it is from God, he will dare to warn, and likewise if he does not fear them or knows that he will be successful in conveying it. And a reminder for the believers may be in the accusative case due to the implication of its verb, meaning: to warn and remind, a reminder, for it means reminding, and the genitive case is in apposition to the place of warn and the nominative case is in apposition to book or as report of something omitted.
7:3: 3. Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord includes the Qur'an and the Sunnah, as God the Almighty says: "Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination. It is only a revelation revealed." And do not follow any protectors besides Him who would lead you astray from among the jinn and mankind. It was said that the pronoun in besides Him refers to what has been revealed, meaning: Do not follow any protectors besides the religion of God. It was also read and that you may seek "little what you remember, meaning little remembrance or a short time you remember when you abandon the religion of God and follow other than it, and ma is added to emphasize the little, and if it is made a source, little is not inflected with you remember". Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read "you remember without the ta', and Ibn 'Amir read they remember" on the basis that the address is after with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
7:4: 4. "And how many a town" and many a town. "We destroyed it" We wanted to destroy its people, or We destroyed it by abandoning it. "So it came to it" So its people came. "Our punishment" Our torment. "By night" Spending the night like the people of Lot, a source that takes the place of a state. "Or they are saying" is in apposition to it, meaning saying at noon like the people of Shu'ayb. The waw of the state was deleted because the two letters of expression were too heavy to come together, to exaggerate their heedlessness and their security from the punishment. For this reason, the two times were specified, and because they are a time of ease and rest, so the coming of the punishment in them would be more terrible.
7:5: 5. So their only call meaning their supplication and their cry for help, or what they were calling for in their religion. When Our punishment came to them was that they said, Indeed, we were wrongdoers" except their admission of their wrongdoing in what they were doing and its invalidity, out of regret for them.
7:6: 6. "We will surely question those to whom it was sent" about their acceptance of the message and their response to the messengers. "And We will surely question the messengers" about what they responded to, and the meaning of this question is to rebuke and reprimand the disbelievers, and what is negated in His statement: "And the criminals will not be asked about their sins" is a question of inquiry. Or the first in the situation of accountability, and this is when they receive the punishment.
7:7: 7. "So We will narrate to them to the messengers when they say, We have no knowledge. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen," or to the messengers and those to whom they were sent what they were like. "With knowledge" knowing their outward and inward aspects, or with what is known to us from them. "And We were not absent" from them, so that nothing of their conditions would be hidden from Us.
7:8: 8. "And the weight" means the judgment, or the weighing of deeds, which is their comparison with the reward. The majority are of the opinion that the scrolls of deeds are weighed on a scale that has a tongue and two pans, which the creation looks at to show justice and to cut off excuses, just as He asks them about their deeds, so their tongues confess to them and their limbs bear witness to them. This is supported by what was narrated: A man is brought to the scale, and ninety-nine records are spread out on it, each record as far as the eye can see, and a card is taken out for him with the two words of the testimony, so the records are placed on one pan and the card on the other, so the records fly away and the card becomes heavy. It was said that people are weighed because it was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Indeed, the great and fat one will come on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not weigh as much as a mosquito's wing in God's sight. On that Day" is the predicate of the subject, which is the weight. "The truth" is its attribute, or an omitted predicate, and its meaning is fair justice. "So whoever's scales are heavy" his good deeds, or what his good deeds are weighed with, it is the plural of weighed or scale, and its plural is based on the difference in the weighed and the multiplicity of the weight. "Then it is those who are the successful" those who win salvation and reward.
7:9: 9. And those whose scales are light - they are the ones who have lost themselves by wasting the sound nature with which they were created, and committing what exposes them to punishment. Because they were unjust to Our signs by denying instead of believing.
7:10: 10. And We have established you in the land meaning We have enabled you to inhabit it, cultivate it, and dispose of it. And We have made for you therein means of livelihood means by which you live, plural of livelihood. And according to Nafi’, he hamzated it as a likening to what the ya’ in it is extra like Saha’if. Little do you give thanks for what I have done for you.
7:11: 11. "And We created you, then We shaped you." That is, We created your father Adam from unshaped clay, then We shaped him. His creation and shaped him were placed in the same position as the creation and shaped of all things, or We began your creation and then shaped you by creating Adam, then shaped him. "Then We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam.' It was also said, Then" is to delay the information. "So they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was not among those who prostrated." Of those who prostrated to Adam.
7:12: 12. He said, 'What prevented you from prostrating?' That is, from prostrating, and there is no similar connection in lest he should know, emphasizing the meaning of the verb that it entered into, and alerting that the one being rebuked did not prostrate. It was said that the one who is prevented from something is compelled to do otherwise, so it is as if it was said: What compelled you not to prostrate? When I commanded you is evidence that the absolute command is for obligation and immediacy. He said, 'I am better than him.' An answer in terms of meaning, with which he resumed, ruling out that someone like him would be commanded to prostrate to someone like him, as if he said: The reason is that I am better than him, and it is not appropriate for the superior to prostrate to the inferior, so how is it appropriate for him to be commanded to do so? He is the one who established arrogance and spoke of rational good and evil first. You created me from fire and created him from clay is an explanation of His favor upon him. He made a mistake in that, as he saw all of the favor as being in consideration of the element and neglected what is in consideration of the agent, as He indicated in His Most High’s saying: What prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? meaning without an intermediary, and in consideration of the form, as He pointed out in His saying: And I breathed into him of My spirit, so fall down to him in prostration. And in consideration of the goal, which is his angel, and therefore He ordered the angels to prostrate to him because He showed them that he is more knowledgeable than them, and that he has properties that no one else has. The verse is evidence of existence and corruption, and that the devils are existing bodies. Perhaps adding the creation of man to clay and the devil to fire is in consideration of the predominant part.
7:13: 13. "He said, 'Then descend from it' from the sky or Paradise. 'What is it for you?' What is it that is not right. 'To be arrogant therein' and disobey, for it is the place of the humble and obedient. And in it is a warning that arrogance is not befitting of the people of Paradise and that God Almighty only expelled him and sent him down because of his arrogance, not merely because of his disobedience. 'Then get out, for you are among the debased' from those whom God has humiliated because of their arrogance. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, 'Whoever is humble, God will raise him up, and whoever is arrogant, God will humiliate him.'"
7:14: 14. He said, 'Give me respite until the Day they are resurrected.' Give me respite until the Day of Resurrection, so do not let me die, or do not hasten my punishment.
7:15: 15. He said, 'You are among those granted respite.' This apparently requires an answer to what he asked, but it is based on what came restricted by the Almighty's saying: Until the Day of the Known Time, which is the first blast, or a time when God knows when his term will end, and in His assistance to it, He tests the servants and exposes them to reward for disobeying Him.
7:16: 16. "He said: 'Because you have misled me'" meaning after you have given me time, I will strive to mislead them in any way I can because of your misleading me through them, by naming, or by making me stray, or by assigning me what I was misled for. The ba' is related to the deleted verb of the oath, "I will not sit down", because the lam prevents it. It was said that the ba' is for the oath: "I will sit down for them" lying in wait for them, as a highwayman sits down for travelers. "Your straight path" is the path of Islam. Its accusative is an adverbial phrase, like his saying: When he shakes his hand, his back becomes honeyed, just as the fox swallows honey on the road. It was said that its meaning is on your path, like their saying: Zaid struck the back and stomach.
7:17: 17. Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and on their right and on their left means from all four directions. Like his intention to tempt them and mislead them from any direction he could by approaching the enemy from the four directions, and that is why he did not say from above them and from beneath their feet. It was said that he did not say from above them because mercy descends from it and he did not say from beneath them because approaching from it frightens people. And from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: from before them from the direction of the Hereafter, and from behind them from the direction of the world, and from their right and from their left from the direction of their good deeds and bad deeds. It is possible to say from before them from where they know and are able to guard against it, and from behind them from where they do not know and are not able, and from their right and from their left from where it is easy for them to know and guard against it but they did not do so because of their lack of alertness and caution. The verb was transmitted to the first two with the letter of beginning because it was directed to them from them and to the last two with the letter of passing, for the one who comes from them is like the one who deviates from them and passes over their width. Similar to it is their saying, I sat on his right, and You will not find most of them grateful, obedient. He only said it as a supposition, because God Almighty said, And Iblis had certainly proven true about them his supposition, when he saw in them the origin of evil as multiple and the origin of good as one. And it was said that he heard it from the angels.
7:18: 18. He said, 'Get out of it blameworthy.' "Get out of it blameworthy. Get out of it blameworthy. It was read blameworthy like responsible in responsible or like measured in measured from blame him, defamed. Expelled" is expelled. "For whoever follows you from among them." The lam in it is for introducing the oath and its answer. "I will fill Hell with you all." It is the answer to the condition. "For whoever is read with a kasra on the lam as the report of I will fill" with the meaning: for whoever follows you, this threat, or the reason for "I will get out and I will fill is the answer to an omitted oath and the meaning of from you and from them," so the one being addressed prevailed.
7:19: 19. And O Adam meaning, We said, O Adam. Dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you wish, but do not approach this tree. It was read as hadi, which is the original, because it is diminutive of dhiyā, and the ha’ is a substitute for the ya’. Then you will be among the wrongdoers then you will be among those who wronged themselves, and the word tawkun may be in the subjunctive mood as a conjunction or in the accusative case as a response.
7:20: 20. "The devil whispered to them" meaning he whispered for them, and it is originally a low sound like a humming or rustling, and from it the whispering of jewelry. The manner of his whispering has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. "To show them" to appear to them, and the lam is for the consequence or to drown, as he also wanted with his whispering to make them feel bad by exposing their private parts, and for this reason he referred to them as the private parts. And in it is evidence that exposing the private parts in seclusion and with the husband without need is ugly and reprehensible in nature. "What was concealed from them of their private parts" is what was covered from them of their private parts and they did not see it of themselves nor one of them of the other, and the damma waw was not changed to a hamza in the well-known as it was changed in aw wasil, the diminutive of wasil because the second is a long vowel, and "sawā'athuma was read by deleting the hamza and placing its vowel on the waw, and sawā'athuma" by changing it to a waw and assimilating the quiescent letter into it. And he said, ‘Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree except that you should become angels or become of the immortals,’ except because he disliked that you should become. The answer to this is that it was known that truths do not change, and their desire was only to also obtain what the angels have of innate perfections, and to be independent of food and drink, and this does not indicate their superiority at all.

7:22: 22. 7:23: 23. They said, 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves.' We harmed ourselves by disobeying and exposing ourselves to expulsion from Paradise. The Mu'tazila said that it is not permissible to punish them while avoiding major sins. Therefore, they said: They only said that based on the custom of those who are close to God in considering minor sins as great and belittling major good deeds.
7:24: 24. He said, 'Go down.' The address was to Adam and Eve and their offspring, first of all, and to Satan. 7:26: 26. O children of Adam, We have sent down upon you clothing meaning, We created it for you through heavenly arrangements and revealed causes. It was narrated that the Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked and say, "We will not circumambulate in clothes in which we disobeyed God," so this was revealed. Perhaps he mentioned the story of Adam as an introduction to that so that he would know that the exposure of the private parts was the first evil that befell man from Satan, and that he led them astray in that as he led their parents astray. "And feathers" and clothing with which you adorn yourself, and feathers are beauty. It was said that it is full, and from this is the man's tarish if he is swayed. It was read riyashan, which is the plural of raysh like shu'ab and shu'ab. "And the clothing of piety" is the fear of God. It was said faith. It was said good appearance. It was said that the clothing of war and its raising by the beginning and its predicate: That is better or the predicate and that is its description as if it was said: And the clothing of piety referred to is better. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir and Al-Kisa’i read and the clothing of piety in the accusative case in apposition to clothing. “That” means sending down the clothing. From the signs of God indicating His grace and mercy. Perhaps they will remember so they will recognize His grace or be admonished and refrain from ugly things.
7:27: 27. "O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you" let him not test you by preventing you from entering Paradise by tempting you. "As he removed your parents from Paradise" just as he tested your parents by expelling them from it. The prohibition in the wording is for Satan, and the meaning is to make them greedy for following him and being tempted by him. "He strips them of their clothing to show them their private parts is a state of your parents or of the subject of expelled" and the attribution of the stripping to him is for the purpose of causing. "Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you do not see them" is a justification for the prohibition and an emphasis on the warning against his temptation, and his tribe are his soldiers and their seeing us from where we do not see them in general does not necessitate the impossibility of seeing them and their impersonation of us. "Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe" by what We found among them of compatibility, or by sending them against them and enabling them to fail them and push them to do what they tempted them to do. The verse is the purpose of the story and the gist of the tale.
7:28: 28. "And if they commit an immorality" an extremely ugly act such as worshipping an idol and exposing the private parts during the circumambulation. "They say, We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to do it. They apologized and argued with two things: imitating their fathers and slandering God, the Most High. So He ignored the first because its corruption was evident and responded to the second by saying. Say, 'God does not command immorality.' Because His habit, the Most High, is to command good deeds and encourage noble traits. There is no indication from it that the ugliest act in the sense of being condemned in the future is rational, because what is meant by immorality is that which a sound nature is repelled by and a straight mind finds wanting. It was said that they are the answers to two successive questions, as if they were asked why they did it. Why did you do it? They said: We found our fathers doing it. It was said: Where did your fathers take it from? They said: God has commanded us to do it. In both cases, imitation is prohibited if evidence is provided to the contrary, but not absolutely. Do you say about God what you do not know? is a denial that includes the prohibition of slandering God Almighty.
7:29: 29. Say, 'My Lord has commanded justice' with justice, which is the middle way of every matter, avoiding the two extremes of excess and deficiency. And set your faces and turn to His worship straight, not being unjust to anything else, or set them towards the Qiblah. At every masjid at every time of prostration or its place, which is prayer, or in any masjid you attend prayer, and do not delay it until you return to your masjids. And call upon Him and worship Him. Sincerely for Him in religion meaning obedience, for to Him is your final destination. As He began you as He created you in the beginning. You will return by His return, so He will reward you for your deeds, so be sincere in worship to Him. The repetition is similar to the beginning in order to confirm its possibility and ability. It was said that just as He began you from the dust, you will return to Him. It was said that just as He began you barefoot and naked, you will be Jews. It was said that just as He began you as believers and disbelievers, He will return you.
7:30: 30. A group He guided by granting them success in faith. And a group He decreed misguidance upon by virtue of the previous judgment. And its being in the accusative case is explained by what follows it, meaning He let down a group. Indeed, they took the devils as allies instead of God is an explanation for their being let down or a confirmation of their misguidance. And they think that they are guided indicates that the disbeliever who is mistaken The obstinate and the stubborn are equal in deserving blame, and the difference is that it is attributed to the one who is negligent in his appearance.
7:31: 31. O children of Adam, take your adornment your clothes to cover your private parts. At every masjid for circumambulation or prayer. It is Sunnah for a man to wear the best appearance for prayer, and this is evidence of the obligation to cover the private parts in prayer. And eat and drink whatever is good for you. It was narrated that Bani Amir during their Hajj days would only eat food as a means of subsistence and would not eat fatty food, thus glorifying their Hajj and thus they were Muslims. So this was revealed. And be not excessive by forbidding what is permissible, that is, by transgressing into what is forbidden, or by overeating and gluttony. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: Eat whatever you want, and wear whatever you want, as long as you do not miss two characteristics: extravagance and conceit. And Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Waqid said: God has gathered medicine in half a verse, saying: Eat and drink, but be not excessive. "Indeed, He does not like the extravagant" meaning He does not approve of their actions.
7:33: 33. Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden indecencies' that which is increasingly ugly, and it was said that it relates to the private parts. What is apparent of them and what is concealed its public and secret. Sin "and that which necessitates sin is a generalization after a specification, and it was said that it is drinking alcohol. And transgression is injustice, or arrogance, and he mentioned it alone for emphasis. Without right is related to transgression, emphasizing its meaning. And that you associate with God that for which He has not sent down authority mocking the polytheists and drawing attention to the prohibition of following that for which there is no proof. And that you say about God that which you do not know by blaspheming in His attributes, glory be to Him, and slandering Him, such as their saying, God has commanded us to do it.
7:34: 34. And every nation has a term a period, or a time for the punishment to descend upon them, and it is a threat to the people of Mecca. So when their term comes their term has expired, or their time has come. They will not delay an hour, nor will they advance it meaning they will not delay or advance it for the shortest time, or they will not seek to delay or advance it due to the intensity of the terror.
7:35: 35. O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you relating to you My verses, a condition mentioned with the letter of doubt to indicate that coming to the messengers is permissible and not obligatory as the people of education thought. And the letter ma was added to it to emphasize the meaning of the condition, and therefore its action was emphasized with the letter nun, and its answer is: But whoever fears God and does good, there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
7:36: 36. And those who denied Our verses and were arrogant toward them - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. The meaning is, "So whoever among you fears denial and corrects his deeds, and those among you who denied Our verses, and the inclusion of the letter fa in the first piece of report, not the second, is to exaggerate the promise and to forgive the threat."
7:37: 37. Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God or denies His signs? than he who says about God what He did not say or denies what He said. Those will receive their share of the Book of what was written for them of provisions and life spans. It was said that the Book is the Preserved Tablet, meaning that which was established for them in it. Until, when Our messengers came to them, they took their souls, meaning they took their souls, and it is a state of the messengers, and until is the goal of attaining them, and it is what the speech begins after. They said, is the answer to if, “Where are those you used to call upon besides God,” meaning where are the gods that you used to worship, and what is connected with where in the script of the Mushaf, and its right is to separate because it is connected. They said, ‘They have gone astray from us,’ they disappeared from us. And they testified against themselves that they were disbelievers, they admitted that they were astray in what they were upon.
7:38: 38. "He said, 'Enter.'" That is, God Almighty will say to them on the Day of Resurrection, or one of the angels. "Among nations that have passed on before you." That is, being among nations accompanying them on the Day of Resurrection. "Of the jinn and mankind." That is, the disbelievers of the past nations regarding both types. "Into the Fire is related to enter. Whenever a nation enters, that is, into the Fire, it curses its sister," the one who went astray by following it. "Until, when they have all overtaken it," that is, they have overtaken and caught up with each other and gathered in the Fire. "The last of them will say," entering or in a position, and they are the followers. "For their first," that is, for the sake of their first, since the address is with God, not with them. "Our Lord, these led us astray," they set a precedent for us to go astray, so we followed them. "So give them a double punishment from the Fire," doubled because they went astray and led others astray. He said to every weakness As for the leaders, it is due to their disbelief and misguidance, and as for the followers, it is due to their disbelief and imitation. But you do not know What is yours or what is for each group. Asim read it with the letter ya for separation.
7:39: 39. "And the first of them said to the last of them, 'You had no superiority over us.' They connected their words to the answer of God Almighty, for the last of them," and they based it on it, meaning that it has been proven that you have no superiority over us, and that we and you are equal in misguidance and deserving of punishment. "So taste the punishment for what you used to earn." This is the saying of the leaders or the saying of the two groups.
7:40: 40. Indeed, those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them that is, about believing in them. The gates of heaven will not be opened for them for their supplications and deeds, or for their spouses as they are opened for the deeds of the believers and their souls to connect with the angels. The ta' in opens is for the feminization of other than the doors and the emphasis is due to their abundance. Abu Amr read it with the lightening, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i with it and with the ya', because the feminization is not real and the verb is presented. Therefore:

7:121: 121. They said, 'We believe in the Lord of the worlds.'
7:122: 122. The Lord of Moses and Aaron. They replaced the second with the first so that it would not be thought that they meant Pharaoh.

7:126: 126. "And do not blame us" and do not disapprove of us. It is read with the kasra from هعدعاهع يهيدهwhich means he inclined him, and it is possible that it is a clarification of the agent and the object in the sense that we have given hope to ourselves and we have hope to You, and it is also possible that the damma is also built for the object of it in the language of the one who saysَعوتد الل دينع. "He said, My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will" his torment. "And My mercy encompasses all things" in this world, the believer and the disbeliever, even the accountable and others. "So I will write it" so I will establish it in the Hereafter, or I will write it as a special scribe from you, O Children of Israel. "For those who fear" disbelief and sins. "And give zakat" He mentioned it specifically because of its uniqueness and because it was more difficult for them. And those who believe in Our verses do not disbelieve in any of them.
7:157: 157. Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet is a subject whose predicate is he commands them, or a predicate of a subject whose meaning is they are those, or a substitute for those who fear God instead of some or all, and what is meant is those among them who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he only called him a Messenger in relation to God Almighty and a Prophet in relation to the servants. The unlettered is the one who does not write or read, he described him with this as a warning that the perfection of his knowledge with his state is one of his miracles. Which they find written down with them in the Torah and the Gospel is a noun and a description. He enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things of what was forbidden to them, such as fats. And prohibits for them the bad things such as blood and pork or like usury and bribery. And He removes from them their burden and the shackles which were upon them and lightens for them the difficult duties they were charged with, such as specifying retaliation for intentional and accidental killing, cutting off sinful limbs, and cutting off the site of impurity. The origin of isr is the weight that constrains its owner, i.e. prevents him from moving due to its weight. Ibn ‘Amir read ‘asarrahum So those who believed in him and supported him and glorified him with strength. It was read with the lightening, and its origin is prevention, and from it is the word ta’zir. “And supported him” for me. And followed the light that was sent down with him i.e. with his prophethood, meaning the Qur’an. He called it light because its miracle makes its matter apparent, or because it reveals the truths and reveals them. It is permissible for it to be with him related to followed i.e. and followed the light sent down with following the Prophet, which is an indication of following the Book and the Sunnah. Those are the successful ones the winners of eternal mercy. The meaning of the verse is the answer to the supplication of Moses, peace be upon him.
7:158: 158. Say, 'O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you.' The address is general. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent to all of mankind and all of the other messengers to their people. All of you is a state of to you. "To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth" is an attribute of God, even if it is separated from them by what is related to the complement, because it is like precedence over it, or praise in the accusative or nominative, or a subject whose predicate is "There is no god but He." This is in all aspects. The first is an explanation of what preceded it, because the One who owned the world was the god and no one else. In "He gives life and causes death" is further confirmation of His exclusive divinity. "So believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet who believes in God and His Words" what was revealed to him and to all of the other messengers of His books and revelation. And it was read and His word to mean the genus or the Qur’an, or Jesus, as an allusion to the Jews and to alert that whoever does not believe in him, his faith is not considered, but rather he changed from speaking to the absence to apply these attributes that call for belief in him and following him. And follow him that you may be guided. He made the hope of guidance the effect of the two matters, alerting that whoever believes him and does not follow him in adhering to his law is considered to be in the plans of misguidance.
7:159: 159. And from the people of Moses meaning from the Children of Israel. A nation guiding with the truth they guide people in truth or with the word of truth. And with it with the truth and do justice between them in judgment, and what is meant by it are those who are steadfast in faith and uphold the truth from the people of his time. Their mention is followed by the mention of their opposites, as is the custom of the Qur'an, to draw attention to the fact that the opposition of good and evil and the crowding of the people of truth and falsehood is a continuous matter. It was said that they are the believers of the People of the Book. It was said that they are a people beyond China whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw on the Night of the Ascension and they believed in him.
7:160: 160. And We cut them apart and We made them into distinct pieces, one from the other. Twelve is a second object of cut because it includes the meaning of made, or a state, and its feminization is for the sake of the nation or the piece. Tribes is a substitute for it, and therefore a plural, or a distinction for it, on the basis that each one of the twelve tribes is as if it was said: twelve tribes. And it was read with a kasra on the sheen and a sukoon on it. Nations on the first is a substitute after a substitute, or a description of tribes, and on the second is a substitute for tribes. And We inspired Moses when his people asked him for water in the wilderness. Strike the rock with your staff, and it gushed forth meaning, so he struck and it gushed forth, and its deletion is to indicate that Moses, peace be upon him, did not hesitate to comply, and that his striking was not effective and the action in itself depended on it. "From it are twelve springs. Every people have known" every tribe. Their place of drinking, and We shaded them with clouds to protect them from the heat of the sun. And We sent down upon them manna and quails, ‘Eat’ meaning, and We said to them, Eat “from the good things We have provided for you. And they did not wrong Us, but they were wronging themselves.” This was previously explained in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:161: 161. "And when it was said to them, 'Dwell in this city,'" implying remember the city of Jerusalem. "And eat from it wherever you will, and say, 'Forgiveness,' and enter the gate in prostration. The same meaning as in Surat Al-Baqarah, except that his saying and eat" in it with the letter fa indicates that their dwelling was due to eating from it, and he did not mention it here, as it was sufficient to mention it there, or because the state indicates it. As for presenting his saying say before enter, it has no effect on the meaning because it does not require order, and likewise the conjunction waw between them. "We will forgive you your sins. We will increase the doers of good." He promised forgiveness and increase it with reward, and the second was only brought out as a resumption to indicate that it is a pure favor, not in return for what they were commanded. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, and Ya'qub readتّفرwith the letter ta and the passive voice, and "خطياتكم" in the plural and nominative, except for Ibn 'Amir, as he used the singular form. Abu 'Amr readخطىكم.
7:162: 162. "But those who did wrong among them substituted other words than those that were said to them, so We sent upon them a punishment from the sky because they were wronging." Its interpretation has already been mentioned therein.
7:163: 163. And ask them to report and rebuke their ancient disbelief and disobedience, and to inform you of what is from their knowledge that is not known except through teaching or revelation so that this will be a miracle for you against them. About the village about its report and what happened to its people. Which was present on the sea close to it and it is Aila, a village between Madyan and Al-Tur on the seashore, and it was said Madyan, and it was said Tiberias. When they transgressed on the Sabbath they transgressed the limits of God by fishing on the Sabbath, and when is an adverb for was or present or for the deleted noun or a substitute for it as a substitute of inclusion. When their fishes come to them is an adverb for ya'dun or a substitute after a substitute. And it was read ya'dun and its origin is ya'tidun and ya'tidun from preparation, meaning they prepare fishing tools on the Sabbath, and they were forbidden to occupy themselves on it with anything other than worship. Their Sabbath day according to the Shari'ah is the day when they glorified the Sabbath. The source of the Jews' Sabbath is if they glorified their Sabbath by devoting themselves to worship. It was said that it is a name for blame and addition because they are specifically subject to the rulings in it. The first is supported if it is read as the day of their Sabbath. And his saying: And the day when they do not observe the Sabbath, do not come to them was read they do not Sabbath from I sabbat and they do not Sabbath in the passive form meaning they do not enter the Sabbath, and by the Shari'ah is a state of the whales and its meaning is apparent on the surface of the water from it came near to us if it came near and looked down. Thus do We test them for what they used to defy like that severe trial We test them because of their defamation. And it was said that it is connected to what preceded it, meaning it does not come to them like their coming on the Sabbath. And the ba' is connected to they count.
7:164: 164. And when she said is in apposition to when they were counting. "A nation of them" is a group of the people of the village, meaning their righteous ones who strove to preach to them until they despaired of being admonished. "Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy" is their chosen ones. "Or punish them with a severe punishment" in the Hereafter for their persistence in disobedience. They said it as an exaggeration that preaching is of no benefit to them, or as a question about the reason for preaching and its benefit, as if it was a discussion between them or the saying of someone who was frightened by preaching to those among them who were not frightened. It was said that what was meant was a group of the doomed sect who answered their preachers with it in response to them and mocking them. "They said, 'As an excuse to your Lord'" is an answer to the question, meaning our preaching is to end God's excuse so that we are not accused of being negligent in forbidding evil. Hafs read excuse me in the accusative case as a source or a reason, meaning we apologized with it as an apology and preached to them as an apology. And perhaps they will fear God because despair only occurs through destruction.
7:165: 165. When they forgot they left as one who forgets. What they were reminded of what their righteous ones reminded them of. We saved those who forbade evil and seized those who did wrong by transgressing and disobeying God's command. With a severe punishment fa'il from ba'usa yab'usa ba'san if it became severe. Abu Bakr read ba'isa with a kasra on the ba' and a sukoon on the hamza on the basis that it is ba'isa like ḍarḍ, as it was read with it, so he lightened its 'ayn by transferring its movement to the fa' like kabad in kabad. Nafi' read ba'isa karīs by changing the hamza and then assimilating it and ba'isa with a lightened kayna and ba'isa like fa'il. Because of their immorality because of their immorality.
7:166: 166. So when they were insolent about what they were forbidden They were arrogant about abandoning what they were forbidden, as God Almighty said: And they were insolent about the command of their Lord "We said to them, Be apes, despised, as He said: Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, Be, and it is. The apparent meaning requires that God Almighty first punished them with a severe punishment, then they were insolent after that, so He transformed them. It is possible that the second verse is a confirmation and explanation of the first. It was narrated that when the forbidding people despaired of the aggressors learning a lesson, they hated to live with them, so they divided the village with a wall in which there was a knocked-on door. One day, none of the aggressors came out to them, so they said: They have something to do with it. So they entered upon them and found that they were apes, so they did not recognize their relatives, but the apes recognized them, so they began to come to their relatives and smell their clothes and go around crying around them, then they died after three days. On the authority of Mujahid, their hearts were transformed, not their bodies.
7:167: 167. And when your Lord declared meaning He knew, it is done from the verb to declare with its meaning like threatening and warning, or he resolved because the one who resolves to do something declares himself to do it, so it is used in the manner of the verb of an oath. God knew and God witnessed and therefore it was answered with its answer which is: To send upon them until the Day of Resurrection and the meaning is and when your Lord made it obligatory upon Himself to give authority over the Jews. Who will afflict them with the worst of torment such as humiliation and imposing the jizya, because God sent upon them, like Solomon, peace be upon him, Nebuchadnezzar, so he destroyed their homes, killed their fighters, took their women and children captive, and imposed the jizya on those who remained of them, and they used to pay it to the Magians until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he did what he did, then imposed the jizya on them, and it will not cease to be imposed until the end of time. Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment He punished them in this world. And indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful for whoever repents and believes.
7:168: 168. And We divided them into nations throughout the earth and dispersed them in it so that there was hardly a country without them, completing their remnants so that they would never have a thorn. Nations is a second object of or mud. "And among them are those who are below that is understood to mean, And among them are people who are below that," meaning, they have deviated from righteousness, and they are their disbelievers and their immoral ones. "And We tested them with good and bad," with blessings and punishments. "Perhaps they will return," they will stop and return from what they were doing. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 11 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Aʿrāf, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Tawbah. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time.
