7:169: 169. And those who came after them succeeded after those mentioned. Khalaf is a bad source of description and therefore it applies to the singular and the plural. It was said that it is a plural and it is common in they inherited the Book and the Torah from their ancestors, they read it and understand what is in it. They take the goods of this lowest thing the debris of this lowest thing, meaning the world, and it is from lowliness or baseness, which is what they used to take as bribes in government and on the distortion of the word, and the sentence is a state of the waw. And they say, 'He will forgive us' God will not hold us accountable for that and overlook it, and it is possible for it to be a conjunction or a state and the verb is attributed to the preposition and the noun, or a source of they take. And if a similar goods comes to them, they take it is a state of the pronoun in for us meaning: they hope for forgiveness, persisting in sin, returning to the like of it and not repenting from it. Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them meaning in the Book. That they should not say about God except the truth is an explanatory apposition to the covenant, or related to it, that is, that they should say, and what is meant is to rebuke them for deciding on forgiveness without repenting, and to indicate that it is a slander against God and a departure from the covenant of the Book. And they studied what is in it is an apposition to Was it not taken in terms of meaning, as it is a confirmation, or to they inherited which is an interjection. And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God than what these people take. Do you not reason? So they know that and do not exchange the lowest and most contemptible that leads to punishment for eternal bliss. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, Hafs, and Ya’qub read it with the ta’ as a variation.
7:170: 170. And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer is in apposition to those who fear God. His statement, Do you not then reason? is an interruption or a subject whose predicate is, Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of the reformers, according to their estimation, or by placing the apparent in place of the implied, indicating that reform is like a deterrent from waste. Abu Bakr read hold fast with a light pronunciation and singular pronunciation because it is different from all other types of holding fast.
7:171: 171. And when We uprooted the mountain above them meaning We removed it and raised it up, separating them. The root of uprooting is attraction. As if it were a canopy a roof, which is what shades you. And they thought and were certain. That it would fall upon them falling upon them because the mountain does not remain in the air and because they were promised it, and the thought was only made general because it did not fall, related to that they refused to accept the rulings of the Torah because of its weight, so God raised the mountain above them. And it was said to them, If you accept what is in it, it will fall upon you. "Take with the implication of the saying, meaning and We said, Take or saying, Take. What We have given you" of the Book. "With strength" with diligence and determination to bear its hardships, and it is a state of the waw. "And remember what is in it" by acting upon it and do not leave it as if it is forgotten. "That you may guard against" ugly deeds and immoral morals.
7:172: 172. "And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants. That is, He brought forth from their loins their descendants as they reproduce, generation after generation, and from their loins is a substitute for from the children of Adam" as a substitute for some. Nafi', Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Ya'qub recited their descendants. "And made them testify of themselves, 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we testify.'" That is, He established for them the proofs of His Lordship and placed in their minds what calls them to acknowledge it until they became in the position of those who came before them: "They said, 'Yes.'" So He revealed enabling them to know it and enabling them to do so in the position of witnesses and acknowledgment in the manner of representation. This is indicated by His statement, "lest you say on the Day of Resurrection, that is, hating to say, Indeed, we were unaware of this." We did not draw attention to it with proof.
7:173: 173. Or say is in apposition to that you say and Abu Amr read both with a ya' because the beginning of the speech is about absence. Our fathers were polytheists before, and we were descendants after them so we followed their example because imitation when evidence is established and knowledge is possible is not a valid excuse. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did? meaning their fathers who were falsifiers by establishing polytheism. It was said that when God created Adam, He brought forth from his back offspring like ants and brought them to life and gave them reason and speech and inspired them with that according to a hadith narrated by Omar, may God be pleased with him, and I have investigated the discussion of it in my explanation of the book Al-Masabih. The purpose of citing this speech here is to oblige the Jews to abide by the general covenant after He obliged them to abide by the covenant specific to them, and to argue against them with auditory and rational arguments and prevent them from imitation and force them to think and reason as he said:
7:174: 174. And thus do We explain the verses in detail, that perhaps they will return meaning from imitation and following falsehood.
7:175: 175. And recite to them meaning to the Jews. The report of the one to whom We gave Our signs is one of the scholars of the Children of Israel, or Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt, for he had read the books and knew that God, the Most High, would send a messenger at that time, and he hoped that it would be him, but when Muhammad, peace be upon him, was sent, he envied him and disbelieved in him, or Balaam ibn Ba'oura from the Canaanites who was given knowledge of some of God's books. So he slipped away from them of the signs by disbelieving in them and turning away from them. So Satan pursued him until he caught up with him, and it was said that he followed him. So he was among the astray so he became among the misguided. It was narrated that his people asked him to invoke God against Moses and those with him, so he said: How can I invoke God against those who have angels with him? They persisted until he invoked God against them, so they remained in the wilderness.
7:176: 176. And if We had willed, We could have raised him to the ranks of the righteous among the scholars. With it because of those verses and their adherence, but he clung to the earth he inclined to the world or to baseness. And followed his desire in preferring the world and appeasing his people and turned away from the requirements of the verses. He only made his elevation dependent on the will of God the Most High, then he made up for it with the action of the servant, to draw attention to the fact that the will is the cause of his action that necessitates his elevation and that its absence is evidence of its absence, as the absence of the effect indicates the absence of its cause, and that the real cause is the will and that what we see of the causes are considered intermediaries in the occurrence of the effect in that the will is attached to it in this way. It would have been right for him to say, but he turned away from it and so he fell into place. He clung to the earth and followed his desire, exaggerating and drawing attention to what led him to do and that the love of the world is the root of every sin. So his example is his description which is an example in baseness. Like a dog is its description in the worst of its properties, which is if you attack it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants meaning it always pants, whether you attack it with reprimand and expulsion or leave it and do not deal with it, unlike other animals due to the weakness of its heart. Panting is the protrusion of the tongue from heavy breathing, and the conditional is in the position of the state and meaning. Panting in both cases, and the metaphor is in the position of the necessary structure, which is the negation of the nominative and the placement of the status for exaggeration and clarification. It was said that when he invoked against Moses, peace be upon him, his tongue stuck out and fell on his chest and he began to pant like a dog. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs, so relate the story the story mentioned about the Jews, for it is similar to their stories. Perhaps they will reflect reflection that will lead them to take heed.
7:177: 177. The example of the people is bad meaning the example of the people, and it was read the example of the people is bad with the deletion of the specific blame. Those who denied Our signs after the proof was established against them and they knew about them. And they were wronging themselves either it was included in the relative clause conjoined with it meaning: And they did not wrong by denying except themselves, for its consequences do not go beyond them, and therefore the object is not present.
7:178: 178. He whom God guides is the guided one, and he whom He sends astray - those are the losers. This is a statement that guidance and misguidance are from God, and that God's guidance is specific to some and not others, and that it necessitates guidance and the singular in the first and the plural in the second based on the wording, and the meaning is to alert that the guided are as one because their path is united, unlike those who are astray, and limiting the information about whom God has guided to the guided one is to magnify the importance of guidance, and alert that it is in itself a great perfection and a great benefit, if he did not obtain it, it would be enough for him, and that it is the necessitator of winning the blessings of the hereafter and the title for them.
7:179: 179. And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind meaning those who persist in disbelief in His knowledge. They have hearts with which they do not understand because they do not direct them to knowing the truth and looking into its evidence. And they have eyes with which they do not see meaning they do not look at what God has created with consideration. And they have ears with which they do not hear the verses and sermons are listening, contemplating and remembering. Those are like livestock in their lack of understanding and sight for consideration and listening for contemplation, or in that their feelings and powers are directed to the causes of livelihood and are limited to them. Rather, they are more astray because they perceive what they can perceive of benefits and harms and strive to bring them and repel them with the utmost effort, but they are not like that, rather most of them know that they are stubborn and so they rush into the Fire. Those are the heedless who are complete in heedlessness.
7:180: 180. And to God belong the best names because they indicate meanings that are the best meanings, and what is meant by them are the words and it was said the attributes. So call upon Him by them so call Him by those names. And leave those who blaspheme in His names and leave the naming of the deviants in them who call Him by what is not proven, because it may suggest a corrupt meaning like their saying O father of noble deeds O white-faced one, or do not care about their denial of what He called Himself like their saying: We do not know anyone but the Most Merciful of Yamamah, or leave them and their blasphemy in them by applying them to idols and deriving their names from them like Al-Lat from God, and Al-Uzza from Al-Aziz and do not agree with them on that or turn away from them because God will reward them as He said: They will be rewarded for what they used to do and Hamza read here and in Fussilat blaspheme with the fat-ha. It is said: Lahad and Alhad if he deviated from the right path.
7:181: 181. And among those We have created is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby. This was mentioned after he explained that He created for the Fire a group who were astray and atheists who turned away from the truth, to indicate that He also created for Paradise those who guide with the truth and are just in their commands. He used it as evidence for the validity of consensus, because what is meant by it is that in every century there is a group with this characteristic, based on his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, A group of my nation will continue to be upon the truth until the command of God comes. If it had been limited to the era of the Messenger or someone else, there would have been no benefit, because it is known.
7:182: 182. And those who deny Our signs - We will gradually lead them on We will gradually lead them on to destruction, little by little. The root of lead is to ascend or descend, step by step, from where they do not know what We want with them, and that is that blessings will be bestowed upon them one after the other, so they will think that it is a kindness from God Almighty to them, and they will become more arrogant and immersed in error until the word of punishment is justified against them.
7:183: 183. And I will give them respite and I will give them respite is in apposition to We will lead them on. “Indeed, My plan is firm” indeed, My punishment is severe, and He only called it a plan because its outward appearance is kindness but its inward essence is failure.
7:184: 184. "Have they not considered what is with their companion?" meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. "Of madness." Of insanity. It was narrated that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended the Safa and called them, group by group, warning them of the wrath of God Almighty. One of them said, "Your companion is mad and has spent the night in a state of confusion until morning. Then the verse was revealed, He is only a clear warner," making his warning clear so that it is not hidden from the observer.
7:185: 185. Have they not considered a look of evidence. In the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what God has created of things of the kinds that cannot be counted to indicate to them the perfection of the power of its Creator, the unity of its originator and the great status of its Owner and the One in charge of its affairs, to show the truth of what He is calling them to. And that perhaps their time has drawn near is in apposition to kingdom and that is a source or a lightened form of the heavy n and its subject is the pronoun of the matter and so is the subject of be and the meaning is: Or have they not considered the approaching of their times and the expectation of their coming so that they hasten to seek the truth and turn to what will save them before death overtakes them and the punishment descends. Then in what statement after it meaning after the Qur'an. They will believe if they do not believe in it, and it is the end of the statement as if it is informing about them by nature and determination to disbelieve after the obligation of the argument and guidance to consider. It was said that it is related to his saying: Perhaps it will be, as if it was said: Perhaps their time has drawn near. So why do they not hasten to believe in the Qur’an? And what are they waiting for after its clarity? If they do not believe in it, then what hadith is more true than it that they want to believe in? And his saying:
7:186: 186. He whom God sends astray, there is no guide for him as a statement and explanation for it. And We left them in their transgression in the nominative case as a resumption. Abu Amr, Asim, and Yaqub read it with the ya' because of his saying He whom God sends astray and Hamza and Al-Kisa'i with it and with the jussive in apposition to the place of He has no guide for him as if it was said: No one guides him but Him. And We left them "blindly" is a state of those who are.
7:187: 187. "They ask you about the Hour" meaning about the Resurrection, and it is one of the most common names and it is given to it either because it will happen suddenly or because of the speed of its reckoning, or because it is as long as an hour with God. "When will it be anchored?" When will it be anchored, meaning it will be established and settled? The anchoring of something means its stability and firmness, and from this the mountain anchored and the ship anchored. The derivation of "Ayyan is from Ay which means any time, and it is from Awwat ilayhi" because some people take refuge in all. "Say, 'Its knowledge is only with my Lord'" He has kept it to Himself, and no close angel or sent prophet has been informed of it. "None will reveal it at its time" Its matter will not be revealed at its time. "Except Him" and the meaning is that it will remain hidden from others until the time of its occurrence, and the lam is for timing like the lam in His statement: "Establish prayer at the decline of the sun. It is heavy in the heavens and the earth" It is great for its people from the angels and the two heavy ones because of its terror, and it is as if it is an indication of the wisdom in concealing it. "It will not come to you except suddenly" except suddenly, by surprise, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "The Hour will stir up people while a man is repairing his cistern, a man is watering his livestock, a man is setting his merchandise in his market, and a man is lowering his scales. They ask you as if you are knowledgeable about it" The verb is from hafa 'an al-shay' if he asks about it. For the one who goes to great lengths in asking about something and searching for it, his knowledge of it is perfected, and for this reason it is transitive with 'an. It is said that it is a conjunction of "they ask you" and it is said that it is from hafawah meaning compassion, for the Quraysh said to him: There is a kinship between us and you, so tell us when is the Hour, and the meaning is that they ask you about it as if you are knowledgeable, you are kind to them and you urge them because of their kinship by teaching them its time. It was said that its meaning is as if you love it by asking about it, from the root hafa bi al-shay’, meaning to be happy that you increase it because it is from the unseen that God has kept knowledge of. Say, ‘Its knowledge is only with God.’ He repeated it to repeat they ask you because of what was attached to it of this increase and for emphasis. But most people do not know. That its knowledge is with God, He did not give it to any of His creation.
7:188: 188. Say, 'I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm.' Bringing benefit or repelling harm, which is a demonstration of servitude and disavowal of claiming knowledge of the unseen. Except what God wills. Of that, He inspires me with it and grants me success in it. And if I knew the unseen, I would have increased in good, and no harm would have touched me. If I knew it, my condition would have been different from what it is, which is increasing in benefits and avoiding harm, so that no harm would have touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings. I am only a servant sent to warn and bring good tidings. For a people who believe. For they are the ones who benefit from them. It is possible that it is related to bringer of good tidings and the related to warner is omitted.
7:189: 189. It is He who created you from a single soul is Adam. And made from it from its body from one of its ribs, or from its kind, as He says: He made for you from yourselves mates. "His mate" is Eve. "To find tranquility in her" to be comforted by her and reassured by her as something reassures itself with its part or kind. The pronoun was mentioned in order to go to the meaning to suit. "So when he covered her" means he had intercourse with her. "She bore a light burden" was easy for her and did not encounter from it what pregnant women usually encounter of harm, or a light load, which is the sperm. "So she passed by it" means she continued with it, meaning she stood and sat. "So she passed by is read with a light vowel and she continued with it and she passed by is from mawr which means coming and going, or from mariyah" meaning she thought the pregnancy and doubted it. "So when it became heavy" became heavy due to the size of the child in her belly. It was read in the passive form, meaning that its load weighed them down. They called upon God, their Lord, ‘If You give us a good child’, we will surely be among the grateful ones,’ a healthy child with a healthy body.
7:190: 190. So when He gave them a righteous child, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. That is, He attributed to Him their children partners in what He had given their children, so they named him Abd al-Uzza and Abd Manaf, deleting the noun and replacing it with the noun to which it was attributed. This is indicated by His statement: So exalted is God above what they associate with Him.
7:191: 191. Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing, and they themselves are created? meaning idols. It was said: When Eve became pregnant, Satan came to them in the form of a man and said to her: How do you know what is in your belly? Perhaps it is an animal or a dog, and how do you know where it comes from? She was afraid of that and mentioned it to Adam, so they understood it. Then he returned to her and said: I am in a position with God, so if you ask God to make him a creation like you and make his exit easy for you, then name him Abd al-Harith. His name was Harith among the angels, so she accepted it. When she gave birth, they named him Abd al-Harith. Such things are not befitting of prophets. It is possible that the address in your creation was to the family of Qusayy from Quraysh, for they were created from the same Qusayy, and there was a husband from his tribe, an Arab Quraysh, and they asked God for a child, so He gave them four sons, and they named them: Abd Manaf, Abd Shams, Abd Qusayy, and Abd al-Dar. The pronoun in associate refers to them and their descendants who follow their example. Nafi’ and Abu Bakr read association meaning partnership, by associating others with Him or those who associate partners with Him, and they are the partners, and they are the pronoun for the idols, which was brought because they called them gods.
7:192: 192. And they cannot help them meaning their servants. Nor can they help themselves by repelling what befalls them.
7:193: 193. And if you call them meaning the polytheists to guidance to Islam, they will not follow you. Nafi' read it with a light sukoon and a fatha on the ba', and it was said that the address was to the polytheists and they are the pronoun for the idols, meaning that if you call them to guide you, they will not follow you to your desire and they will not answer you as God answers you. It is the same for you whether you call them or are silent. He did not say or are silent to emphasize the lack of benefit of the call, since it is equal to remaining silent, or because they did not call upon them for their needs, so it is as if it was said: It is the same for you whether you invent their call or continue to remain silent about their call.
7:194: 194. Indeed, those you call upon besides God meaning, you worship them and call them gods. are servants like you in that they are owned and subjugated. So call upon them and let them respond to you if you should be truthful that they are gods, and it is possible that when they carved them in the images of humans, He said to them: The most they can do is to be living, rational beings like you, so they do not deserve your worship, just as some of you do not deserve the worship of others. Then He returned to refuting him and said:
7:195: 195. "Do they have legs with which they walk, or do they have hands with which they strike? Or do they have eyes with which they see, or do they have ears with which they hear? It was read Indeed, those who with a light an and the accusative ibbad as a negative that worked like the Hijazi ma and nothing like it has been proven, and strike" with the deaf here and in Al-Qasas and Al-Dukhan. "Say, call upon your partners" and seek help from them in my enmity. "Then plot" so go to extremes in whatever you are able to of plotting, which is you and your partners. "So do not wait" do not delay, for I do not care about you because of my trust in the guardianship of God Almighty and His protection.
7:196: 196. My protector is God, who revealed the Book the Qur’an. And He takes care of the righteous meaning that it is His habit, the Most High, to take care of the righteous among His servants, in addition to His prophets.
7:197: 197. And those whom you call upon besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves. This is a complete explanation of His indifference to them.
7:198: 198. "And if you call them to guidance, they will not hear, and you will see them looking at you, but they do not see." They are like those looking at you because they are depicted in the image of someone looking at you, at someone facing him.
7:199: 199. Take what is easy means take what is easy for you from people's actions and make it easy and do not ask for what is difficult for them, from forgiveness which is the opposite of effort or take what is easy from sinners or the favor and what is easy from their charity, and that is before the obligation of zakat. And command what is good the good and desirable actions. And turn away from the ignorant do not argue with them and do not reward them with actions similar to theirs. This verse is a collection of noble morals and commands the Messenger to collect them.
7:200: 200. And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan He prompts you with a nudge from him, meaning a whisper that leads you to do something contrary to what you were commanded to do, such as the onset of anger and thought. The nudge, the spur, and the thrust are like a whisper to tempt them to commit sins and to disturb them, like the driver thrusting what he drives. Then seek refuge in God, for He is All-Hearing He hears your seeking refuge. All-Knowing He knows what is good for you and urges you to do it, or All-Hearing of the words of those who harmed you with their actions and punishes them for it, making you independent of revenge and following Satan.
7:201: 201. Indeed, those who fear God - when an impulse touches them from Satan is a plural of it, and it is an active participle from tafa yatawuf as if it had surrounded them and revolved around them but was unable to affect them, or someone who is surrounded by a phantom, yatif yafyan. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read tayf as a source or an alleviation of tayf both soft and easy, and what is meant by Satan is the genus and that is why its pronoun is plural. Remember what God has commanded and forbidden. Then they will see because of remembering the places of error and the tricks of Satan, so they are cautious about them and do not follow him in them, and the verse is an emphasis and confirmation of what preceded it, as well as His saying:
7:202: 202. And their brothers support them meaning, and the brothers of the devils who did not fear the devils' support. In error by embellishing and bearing it. N and it was read provide them from provide and provide them as if they are helping them with facilitation and enticement, and these help them with following and compliance. Then they do not fall short then they do not refrain from their temptation until they return them, and it is possible that the pronoun refers to the brothers, meaning they do not refrain from error nor fall short like the righteous, and it is possible that the devils are meant by brothers and the pronoun refers back to the ignorant so the report is in accordance with what it is for.
7:203: 203. And if you do not bring them a sign from the Qur'an or from what they suggested. They say, 'Why did you not select it?' Why did you not collect it and say it from yourself like everything else you read, or why did you not ask God for it? Say, 'I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord.' I am not inventing signs or suggesting them. These are insights from your Lord. This Qur'an is insights for the hearts by which one sees the truth and comprehends what is right. And guidance and mercy for a people who believe. Its explanation has been given previously.
7:204: 204. And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy. This was revealed regarding the prayer in which they were talking, so they were commanded to listen to the recitation of the imam and to be silent to him. The apparent meaning of the wording indicates that they are obligatory wherever the Qur'an is recited, and most scholars agree that they are recommended outside of prayer. It was used as evidence by those who do not believe that the recitation is obligatory for the person being led in prayer, but this is weak.
7:205: 205. And remember your Lord within yourself is general in remembrances of recitation, supplication, and others, or an order for the follower to recite silently after the imam has finished his recitation, as is the doctrine of Al-Shafi'i, may God be pleased with him. In humility and fear in humility and fear. And without speaking loudly and speaking a speech that distinguishes the secret and without speaking loudly, as it is more in humility and sincerity. In the mornings and the evenings at the times of running and the evenings. And it was read and the connection and it is a source of origin if it enters into the evening and it is identical to the morning. And do not be among the heedless of the remembrance of God.
7:206: 206. Indeed, those who are with your Lord meaning the angels of the highest assembly. are not too proud to worship Him, and they glorify Him and declare Him to be pure. And to Him they prostrate and they are singled out for worship and humility, and they do not associate anyone with Him. This is an allusion to those other than them who are accountable, and that is why prostration was prescribed for its recitation. And it was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "When the son of Adam recites a verse of prostration and prostrates, Satan withdraws weeping and says: Woe to him! This one was commanded to prostrate, and he prostrated, so Paradise is his; and I was commanded to prostrate, but I disobeyed, so Hell is mine." And it was narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-A'raf, God will place a veil between him and Satan on the Day of Resurrection, and Adam will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection.
8:1: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful 1. They ask you about the spoils of war meaning the spoils of war, meaning their ruling. The spoils of war are called nafl because they are a gift from God and a favor, just as what the Imam stipulates for a dangerous invader is called a gift for him and an increase in his share. “Say: The spoils of war belong to God and the Messenger” meaning their matter is specific to them, and the Messenger divides them as God commands him. The reason for its revelation was the disagreement of the Muslims about the spoils of Badr, how they should be divided and to whom they should divide them, the Muhajireen or the Ansar. It was said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stipulated that whoever had wealth should give it as a gift, so their young men rushed until they killed seventy and took seventy captive, then they asked for their gift - and the money was little - and the elders and notables who were with the banners said: We were a support for you and a group that would side with us, so it was revealed and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among them equally. For this reason it was said that the imam is not obligated to fulfill what he promised, and this is the saying of Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, and “On the authority of Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas, may God be pleased with him, he said: When the day of Badr came, my brother Umair was killed, so I killed Sa’id bin Al-’As with him and took his sword, so I brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him for it, so he said: This is not mine and it is not yours, throw it in the hand, so I threw it, and I have what only God knows about the killing of my brother and the taking of my spoils. I had not gone far until Surat Al-Anfal was revealed, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: You asked me for the sword, and it is not mine, and it has become mine, so go and take it.” And it was read yas’alunaka ‘alanfal without the hamza and the fa’. Its movement is on the lam and the assimilation of the nun from it, and they ask you about the spoils, meaning the young men ask you about what you stipulated for them. So fear God in the disagreement and quarrel. And set things right between you the situation between you by consoling and helping with what God has provided for you and submitting his matter to God and the Messenger. And obey God and His Messenger in it. If you are believers then faith requires that, or if you are complete in faith then the perfection of faith is in these three: obeying the commands and avoiding sins, and setting things right between people with justice and kindness.
8:2: 2. The believers are only those meaning those who are perfect in faith. Those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful are terrified at His mention out of great awe of Him and in awe of His majesty. It was said that it is a man who is about to commit a sin and is told, Fear God, so he refrains from it out of fear of His punishment. It was also read Wajalt with the fat-ha, which is a language, and Farqara means feared. And when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith to increase the believer in Him, or to reassure the soul and establish certainty through the manifestation of evidence, or by acting in accordance with it, which is the opinion of those who said that faith increases with obedience and decreases with disobedience, based on the fact that action is included in it. And upon their Lord they rely they entrust their affairs to Him and do not fear or hope except in Him.
8:3: 3. Those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them.
8:4: 4. Those are the true believers because they fulfilled their faith by adding to it the noble deeds of the heart, such as fear and sincerity. And trust, and the good deeds of the limbs which are the standard for them, such as prayer and charity. Truly is an attribute of a deleted source or A confirmed source, such as His saying: The promise of God is true. “For them are degrees with their Lord” of honor and high status. It was said that they ascend the degrees of Paradise through their deeds. And forgiveness for what they have neglected. And generous provision prepared for them in Paradise, its number will never be cut off and its duration will never end.
8:5: 5. Just as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth is the predicate of a deleted subject, the meaning of which is: "This situation in their hatred of it is like the situation of your being brought out for war in their hatred of it, and it is the hatred of what you saw of the spoils of war. Or the description of the source of the verb estimated in his saying: "For God and the Messenger" meaning the spoils were established for God and the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, with their hatred, as established as the establishment of your Lord bringing you out from your home, meaning Medina because it is his place of migration and his residence or his home in it with their hatred. "And indeed a party of the believers were averse" in the position of the state, meaning He brought you out in a state of their hatred, and that is because the caravan of Quraysh came from the Levant and in it was a great trade and with it were forty riders among them Abu Sufyan, Amr ibn al-Aas, Mukhramah ibn Nawfal, and Amr ibn Hisham, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he informed the Muslims, and they were amazed at its reception due to the abundance of money and the small number of men, so when they went out the report reached the people of Mecca, so Abu Jahl called out from above the Kaaba, O people of Mecca, escape, escape On every difficult and easy, your money is your caravan, if Muhammad strikes it, you will never succeed after that, and three days before that, Atika bint Abdul Muttalib saw that an angel descended from the sky and took a rock from the mountain and then circled it, and there was no house in Mecca that was not struck by something of them, so she told Al-Abbas about it and that reached Abu Jahl, so he said: We do not accept that their men prophesy until their women prophesy, so Abu Jahl went out with all the people of Mecca and went with them to Badr, which is a water body where the Arabs used to gather for their market one day a year. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Wadi Dhafran, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down to him with the promise of one of the two groups, either the caravan or the Quraysh, so his companions consulted about it, and some of them said: Why did you not mention the fighting to us so that we could prepare for it? We only went out for the caravan, so he responded to them and said that the caravan has gone to the seashore and Abu Jahl has come, so they said: O Messenger of God, take the caravan and leave the enemy, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry, so Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, stood up and said, and they did well, then Saad stood up Ibn Ubadah said: Look after your matter and go ahead with it, for by God, if you were to march to Aden, not a single one of the Ansar would stay behind you. Then Muqdad ibn Amr said: Go with what God has commanded you, for I am with you wherever you like. We will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Moses, “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.” Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are with you, fighting. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled and then said: Advise me, O people, meaning the Ansar, because they were their number and they had stipulated when they pledged allegiance to him at Al-Aqabah that they would be free from his protection until he reached their homes. He feared that they would not see his victory except against an enemy who had attacked him in Medina. Sa`d ibn Mu`adh stood up and said: It is as if you want us, O Messenger of God. He said: Yes. He said: “We have believed in you and we have spoken to you and we have testified that what you have brought is the truth, and we have given you our covenants and pledges to hear and obey. So go, O Messenger of God, with what you want, for by the One Who sent you with the truth, if you were to review…” “If you had crossed this sea with us, we would have crossed it with you. Not a single man of us would have stayed behind. We do not dislike that you should meet our enemy with us. We are patient in war and truthful in encounter. Perhaps God will show you from us something that will please your eyes. So go with us with the blessing of God Almighty.” His words encouraged him, then he said: “Go with the blessing of God Almighty and be glad, for God has promised me one of the two parties. By God, it is as if I am looking at the place where the people will fall.” It was said that when he, peace and blessings be upon him, finished at Bajr, it was said to him: Go with the camel. Al-Abbas called out to him while he was in his chains and he could not fit. He said: Because your promise is one of the two parties, and he has given you what he promised you. Some of them disliked his words.
8:6: 6. They argue with you about the truth about your preference for jihad by demonstrating the truth because they prefer throwing the caravan at it. After it became clear to them that they would be victorious wherever they went by informing the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. As if they were being driven to death while they were watching meaning they hated fighting with the hatred of someone who is being driven to death while he is watching its causes, and that was due to their small number and lack of preparation since it was narrated that they were infantry and there were only two horsemen among them, and in it is an allusion to the fact that their argument was only due to their extreme fear and terror.
8:7: 7. And when God promised you one of the two parties with the omission of remember, and one of the second objects of promised you and it was replaced with that it is for you as a substitute for inclusion. And you wish that the one without the power should be for you meaning the caravan, for there were only forty horsemen in it, and for that reason they wished for it and hated to meet the mobilization due to their large number, and their number and the power of the thorn are borrowed from the singular of thorns: And God intends to establish the truth meaning to establish it with His word. And to cut off the root of the disbelievers and to uproot them, and the meaning is: that you want to gain wealth and not encounter harm, and God intends to exalt the religion and make the truth apparent and what you obtain is the victory of the two abodes.
8:8: 8. So that the truth may be established and falsehood may be invalidated. That is, he did what he did, and it is not a repetition, because the first is to clarify what is intended and the difference between it and their intention, and the second is to clarify the motive for the Messenger to choose the one with power and support her against it. Even if the criminals hate it.
8:9: 9. When you seek help from your Lord instead of when He promises you or related to His saying to establish with His saying to establish the truth, or with the implication of mention, and their seeking help is that when they knew that there was no escape from fighting, they began to say: O Lord, grant us victory over Your enemy, help us, O Helper of those who seek help, and on the authority of Omar, may God be pleased with him, that he, peace be upon him, "looked at the polytheists, who were a thousand, and at his companions, who were three hundred, and he faced the qiblah and stretched out his hands supplicating: O God, fulfill for me what You promised me, O God, if You destroy this group, You will not be worshipped on earth and he continued like that until his cloak fell off, so Abu Bakr said, O Prophet of God: It is enough for you to implore your Lord, for He will fulfill for you what He promised you." So He responded to you, I am your supporter," that I am your supporter, so the preposition was deleted and the verb was applied to it. Abu Amr read it with a kasra, intending the statement or making it follow the path of "he responded," because the response is from the statement. "With a thousand angels in succession, following the believers or some of them with others from I followed him, if I came after him, or following some of the believers, they separated themselves from the believers from I followed him," so he replied. Nafi' and Ya'qub read mardifeen with a fatha on the dal, meaning following, meaning that they were the vanguard of the army or their rearguard. "Mardifeen was read with a kasra or damma on the ra', and its original form is murtadayfin meaning mutaradayfin," so the ta' was assimilated into the dal and two quiescents met, so the ra' was moved with a kasra according to the original or with a damma according to the imitation. It was read with thousands to agree with what is in Surat Al Imran. The way to reconcile it with the famous is that what is meant by the thousand are those who were in the vanguard or rearguard, or their faces and notables, or those who fought from them and there is disagreement about fighting them, and reports have been narrated that indicate this.
8:10: 10. And God has not made it meaning the support except as good report except as good report for you of victory. And that your hearts may be reassured thereby so that what is in them of fear due to your fewness and humiliation will be removed. "And victory is only from God. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise." The support of the angels and the large number and equipment and the like are intermediaries that have no effect, so do not think that victory comes from them and do not despair of it due to their loss.
8:11: 11. When drowsiness overtakes you is a second substitute for When He promises you to show a third blessing or related to victory or what is with God in the meaning of the verb, or makes or by implying remember. Nafi' read with the lightening of the word aghazatuhu from the thing if you overpowered it, and the subject in both readings is God Almighty. Ibn Kathir and Abu Omar read yaghshakum al-na'am with the nominative. Amanah minhu Amanah min God, and it is an object in consideration of the meaning, so his saying yasaa' overtakes you includes the meaning of you doze, and yasaa'kum has its meaning, and amanah is a verb for its subject, and it is permissible for it to mean faith, so it is the verb of the one who overpowers, and that you make according to the last reading the verb of sleep metaphorically because it is for his companions, or because it was his right not to overpower you due to the intensity of fear, so when he overpowered them, it is as if he obtained a security from God, and if it were not for it, he would not have overpowered them, like his saying: Sleep is afraid to cover eyes that fear you, so it is a repulsive absent-minded person. And Amanah was read as mercy, which is a language. And He sends down upon you from the sky water to purify you thereby from ritual impurity and major ritual impurity. And removes from you the impurity of Satan meaning major ritual impurity because it is from his imagination. Or his whispering and his frightening them with thirst. It was narrated that they camped in a sand dune where feet sink without water and they slept and most of them had wet dreams and the polytheists had overcome the water, so Satan whispered to them and said: How will you be victorious when you have overcome the water and you pray while in a state of ritual impurity and claim that you are the friends of God, and among you is His Messenger? So they feared, so God sent down rain, so it rained at night until the valley flowed and they built basins on its side and watered the riders and washed and performed ablution, and the sand between them and the enemy was pressed together until the feet were firm on it and the whispering was removed. And to strengthen your hearts with trust in God's kindness to them. And to strengthen thereby the feet meaning with the rain so that they do not sink in the sand, or by strengthening the hearts so that they are firm in battle.
8:12: 12. When your Lord inspires is a third substitute or related to confirm. "To the angels, I am with you in helping them and confirming them, and it is the object of inspires." It was read with a kasra to mean the saying or the revelation taking its course. "So make firm those who believe with the good report or by increasing their numbers, or by fighting their enemies, so his saying, I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve is like an explanation of his saying, I am with you, so be firm," and in it is evidence that they fought. Whoever prevents that made the address in it with the believers either by changing the address or by his saying, "I will cast to his saying, every fingertip" is teaching the angels what they will make firm the believers with, as if he said, say to them this saying of mine. "Then strike above the necks" the tops of them, which are the altars or heads. "And strike from them every fingertip" fingers, meaning cut off their necks and cut off their limbs.
8:13: 13. That refers to the beating or the command to do so, and the address is to the Messenger, or to each of those addressed before. That they have made opposition to God and His Messenger because of their opposition to them, and its derivation is from the word shaq because each of the two enemies is on a side other than the other, like enmity from adwah and quarrelling from khasim which is the side. And whoever opposes God and His Messenger, then indeed, God is severe in penalty is a statement of the reason or a threat of what is prepared for them in the Hereafter after what befell them in this world.
8:14: 14. That is addressed to the disbelievers in the manner of turning away and its place is in the nominative case, meaning: the matter is that or that is happening or it is in the accusative case with a verb that indicates it. So taste it or something else like engage or upon you, so the fa is a connective. And that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire is in apposition to that or it is in the accusative case as an object with it, and the meaning is taste what was hastened for you along with what was deferred for you in the Hereafter. The apparent in it is placed in the place of the pronoun to indicate that disbelief is the cause of the deferred punishment or to combine them. And is read with the kasra as a new sentence.
8:15: 15. O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing many, it is seen because of their large numbers as if they were advancing. It is the source of the boy's crawling when he crawls on his seat little by little, it was named with it and the plural is crawling and its accusative is in the state. Do not turn your backs to them in flight, let alone if they are like you or less than you, and it is more apparent that it is a specific ruling with His saying: Urge the believers to fight the verse. It is permissible for crawling to be in the accusative case as a state of the subject and the object, meaning: If you meet them advancing, they crawl towards you and you crawl towards them, do not flee, or from the subject alone and it is a notification of what will happen from them on the day of Hunayn when they turned away and they were twelve thousand.
8:16: 16. And whoever turns his back to them that day, except one who turns away for the sake of fighting meaning to attack after fleeing and deceive the enemy, for that is one of the tricks of war. Or withdrawing to a group or withdrawing to another group of Muslims in order to seek their help, and some of them did not consider the proximity because of what was narrated by Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both: "He was in a secret mission that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out and they fled to Medina, so I said, O Messenger of God, are we the ones who fled? He said: Rather, you are the troublemakers and I am your group". The accusative of mutaharifan and mahizan is in the state of otherwise and it is superfluous and has no function, or the exception from al-muwalleen means except a man who turns away or withdraws, and the weight of mutahir is mutafa'il not mutafa'il otherwise it would have been mutahawiz because it is munahaz and yuhuz. He has incurred the wrath of God, and his refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination. This is if the enemy does not increase more than twice as much, as he said: Now God has lightened your burden Nun. It was said that the verse is specific to his family and those present with him in the war.
8:17: 17. So why did you kill them with your strength. But God killed them with your victory and authority over them and casting terror into their hearts. It was narrated that "when the Quraysh rose from Al-Aqanqal, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: This is the Quraysh who came with their arrogance and pride, denying your Messenger. O God, I ask You for what You promised me. So Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said to him: Take a handful of dirt and throw it at them. So when the two armies met, he took a handful of pebbles and threw them in their faces and said May your faces be disfigured. There was not a single polytheist who was not preoccupied with his eyes, so they fled and the believers followed them, killing and taking them captive. Then when they turned back, they began to boast, and a man would say: I killed and took captive, so this was revealed." And the fa is the answer to an omitted condition, the meaning of which is: If you boasted about killing them, you did not kill them, but God killed them. And you did not throw, O Muhammad, a throw that would reach their eyes but you were not able to do so. When you threw means when you came with the image of throwing. But God threw He came with what is the ultimate throwing, so He delivered it to all their eyes until they were defeated and you were able to cut off its root. You have known that the word is used for the named and for what is like it and what is intended by it. It was said that its meaning is that you did not throw terror when you threw pebbles, but God threw terror into their hearts. It was said that it was revealed regarding a stab wound that Ubayy ibn Khalaf received on the day of Uhud, and no blood came out of him, so he began to moan until he died. Or a shot of an arrow that he threw on the day of Khabar towards the fortress, and it hit Kinanah ibn Abi al-Haqeeqi on his bed. The majority are on the first. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read but with a light vowel and raising what follows it in the nursing mothers. And that He may test the believers from Him with a good test and bestow upon them a great blessing of victory and booty, and the witness of the verses is that He did what He did. Indeed, God is Hearing of their cries for help and supplications. Knowing of their intentions and their conditions.
8:18: 18. "That" refers to the good test, or killing or shooting, and its place is in the nominative case, meaning that the intended or the matter is that. And his saying: "And that God will weaken the plot of the disbelievers" is conjoined to it, meaning that the intended is to test the believers and weaken the plot of the disbelievers and nullify their tricks. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu Amr read "muhan with emphasis, and Hafs read muhan khayd" with addition and alleviation.
8:19: 19. "If you ask for victory, victory has already come to you." This is addressed to the people of Mecca in mockery, because when they wanted to leave, they clung to the curtains of the Kaaba and said: O God, support the superior of the two armies, the most guided of the two groups, and the most honorable of the two parties. "And if you desist from disbelief and hostility to the Messenger, it is better for you" to ensure the safety of both abodes and the best of the two homes. "And if you return to fighting him, We will return" to support him against you. "And your group your congregation will not avail or prevent anything from you of enrichment or harm, even if" your group was many. "And that God is with the believers" with victory and assistance. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs read "and" with the opening, assuming that because God is with the believers, that was the case. It was said that the verse is addressed to the believers and the meaning is: If you seek victory, then the report has come to you, and if you stop being lazy in fighting and desiring what the Messenger monopolizes, then it is better for you, but if you return to it, then we will threaten you with denial or incitement of the enemy, and your great numbers will not be of any use then if God is not with you in victory, for He is with those who are perfect in their faith. This is supported by:
8:20: 20. O you who have believed, obey God and His Messenger and do not turn away from him. That is, do not turn away from the Messenger, for the intended meaning of the verse is the command to obey him and the prohibition against turning away from him. The mention of obedience to God is to pave the way and to draw attention to the fact that obedience to God is in obedience to the Messenger, as God the Most High says, Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God. It was said that the pronoun refers to jihad or to the command indicated by obedience. And you listen to the Qur'an and the sermons, listening with understanding and belief.
8:21: 21. And do not be like those who said, 'We hear.' Like the infidels and hypocrites who claimed to hear, but they do not hear, a hearing from which they benefit, as if they do not hear at all.
8:22: 22. Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God are the worst of what creeps on the earth, or the worst of beasts. The deaf of the truth. The dumb who do not understand it. He counted them among the beasts, then made them the worst of them because they nullified what distinguished them and for which they were preferred.
8:23: 23. And if God had known any good in them happiness that was written for them or benefit from the verses. He would have made them hear a hearing of understanding. And if He had made them hear and He knew that there was no good in them. They would have turned away and not benefited from it, or they would have apostatized after believing and accepting it. And they are turning away to their stubbornness. It was said that they were saying to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Bring Qusayy back to life for us, for he was a blessed old man so that he may bear witness for you and we may believe in you. The meaning is that He would make them hear Qusayy's speech.
8:24: 24. O you who believe, respond to God and the Messenger with obedience. When He calls you The pronoun is singular in it for what came before and because the call of God is heard from the Messenger. It was narrated that "he, peace and blessings be upon him, passed by my father while he was praying and called him, so he hurried in his prayer and then came and said: What prevented you from responding to me? He said: I was praying. He said: Have you not been informed of what was revealed to me "Respond to God and the Messenger"". There is a difference of opinion about it, and it was said that this is because responding to him does not interrupt the prayer, as prayer is also for boredom, and the apparent meaning of the hadith is appropriate for the first. For what gives you life of religious knowledge, as it is the life of the heart and ignorance is its death. He said: Do not be impressed by the ignorant's clothing, for he is dead and his clothing is a shroud. Or from what will give you eternal life in everlasting bliss from beliefs and deeds, or from jihad, for it is the reason for your survival, for if they were abandoned, the enemy would overcome them and kill them, or martyrdom, for the Almighty says: Rather, they are alive with their Lord, and they are provided for. “And know that God comes between a person and his heart” is a representation of the extent of His closeness to the servant, as the Almighty says: And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. And a warning that He is aware of the hidden secrets of hearts, which their owner may be unaware of, or an urging to hasten to purify hearts and cleanse them before God comes between him and his heart by death or otherwise, or an image and imagination of His possession of the servant’s heart, so He breaks his resolve and changes his intentions and comes between him and disbelief if He desires his happiness, and between him and faith if He decrees his misery. And it was read bayn al-mur with emphasis, deleting the hamza and placing its movement on the ra’ and performing the connection of the pause according to the language of those who emphasize it. And that to Him you will be gathered so He will reward you for your deeds.
8:25: 25. And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively. Fear a sin whose effect will spread to you, such as acknowledging evil among you, being complacent in enjoining what is right, division of opinion, the emergence of innovations, and laziness in jihad. His saying will not strike is either the answer to the command meaning that your affliction will not strike the wrongdoers among you exclusively, but will spread to you, and in it is that the answer to the condition is hesitant, so the emphatic nun does not suit it, but since it includes the meaning of prohibition, it is permissible in it, like the Almighty's saying: Enter your dwellings, lest they crush you. As for the description of trial, nor of negation, and in it is an anomaly because the nun does not enter the negated except in an oath, or for a prohibition on the intention of speech, like his saying: Even if darkness fell and mixed, they came with a taste. Have you ever seen a wolf? Or it is the answer to an omitted oath, like the reading of the one who read that you will surely be afflicted, even though they differ in meaning. It is possible that it is a prohibition after the command to avoid sin by not being exposed to injustice because its consequences affect the oppressor in particular and return to him. And among you in the first way is for partiality and in the last two ways is for clarification, and its benefit for the oppressor among you is worse than others. And know that God is severe in penalty.
8:26: 26. And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land the land of Mecca, oppressed by the Quraysh, and the address is to the Muhajireen. It was also said to all the Arabs, for they were humiliated in the hands of the Persians and the Romans. Fearing that people might snatch you away the infidels of the Quraysh or those other than them, for they were all hostile to them and opposed to them. So He gave you shelter to Medina, or made for you a shelter in which you could protect yourself from your enemies. And supported you with His victory over the infidels or with the support of the Ansar or with the support of the angels on the day of Badr. And provided you with good things from the spoils. That you might be grateful for these blessings.
8:27: 27. O you who have believed, do not betray God and the Messenger by neglecting the obligatory duties and traditions, or by concealing something other than what you reveal, or by misappropriating spoils. It was narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, besieged Banu Qurayzah for twenty-one nights. They asked him for peace as he had made peace with their brothers Banu al-Nadir against Sa`d ibn Mu`adh. They refused and said: Send Abu Lubabah to us. He was a sincere advisor to them because his family and wealth were in their hands. So he sent him to them and they said: What do you think? Should we submit to the judgment of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh? He pointed to his throat, meaning that he would slaughter. Abu Lubabah said: My feet did not move until I knew that I had betrayed God and His Messenger, so I submitted. He tied himself to a pillar in the mosque and said: By God, I will not taste food or drink until I die or God accepts my repentance. He remained seven days until he fell unconscious. Then God accepted his repentance and it was said to him: You have accepted your repentance, so release yourself. He said: No, by God, I will not release myself until the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, is the one who releases me. So he came to him and released him with his hand. He said: Part of my complete repentance is that I leave the home of my people in which I committed the sin, and that I give up my wealth. So he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: It is sufficient for you to give one-third of it in charity.” The root of betrayal is deficiency, just as the root of loyalty is completeness, and it is used in the opposite of trust because it includes it. And betray your trusts among yourselves, and it is in the jussive mood due to the conjunction of the first, or it is in the accusative case as an answer to the waw. And you know that you betray, or you are scholars who distinguish good from bad. And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial because they are the cause of falling into sin or punishment, or a trial from God Almighty to test you in them, so do not let your love for them lead you to betrayal like Abu Lubabah. And that God has a great reward for whoever prefers God’s pleasure over them and observes His limits regarding them, so entrust your efforts to what will lead you to Him.
8:28: 28. And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial because they are the cause of falling into sin or punishment or a trial from God Almighty to test you in them, so do not let your love for them lead you to betrayal like Abu Lubabah. And that God has with Him a great reward for whoever prefers God's pleasure over them and observes His limits in them, so attach your ambitions to that which leads you to Him.
8:29: . 29 O you who have believed, if you fear God, He will grant you a criterion a guidance in your hearts by which you can distinguish between truth and falsehood, or a victory that distinguishes between the truth and falsehood by honoring the believers and humiliating the disbelievers, or a way out from doubts, or salvation from what you fear in both abodes, or a manifestation that makes your matter famous and spreads your fame from their saying, I will do such and such until the criterion, meaning the morning, shines. And He will remove from you your misdeeds and conceal them. And He will forgive you by overlooking and pardoning you. It was said that the minor misdeeds and the major sins. It was said that what is meant is what came before and what came after because it was about the people of Badr and God Almighty forgave them. And God is the possessor of great bounty a reminder that what He promised them for their piety is a favor and kindness from Him, and that it is not something that requires their piety towards Him, like a master when he promises his servant a favor for his work.
8:30: 30. And when those who disbelieved plotted against you A reminder of the plot of the Quraysh against him when he was in Mecca, so that he would thank God for his salvation from their plot and control over them. The meaning is, remember when they plotted against you. To make you steadfast by tying you up or imprisoning you, or to inflict severe wounds, as they say, He struck him until he was steadfast, unable to move or rest. It was read to make you steadfast with emphasis and to spend the night there from to spend the night there and to tie you up. Or to kill you with their swords. Or they expel you from Mecca, because when they heard about the conversion of the Ansar and their pledge of allegiance, they were divided and gathered in the House of Assembly to consult about it. Then Satan entered upon them in the form of an old man and said: I am from Najd. I heard your gathering and wanted to attend to you, and you will not lack advice and counsel from me. Abu Al-Buhturi said: My opinion is that you should imprison yourself in a house and block its entrances except for a window through which you can throw his food and drink until he dies. The old man said: This is a bad opinion. Someone from his people will come to fight you and rescue him from your hands. Hisham bin Omar said: My opinion is that you carry him on a camel and expel him from your land, and what he has done will not harm you. He said: This is a bad opinion. He corrupts a people other than you and fights you with them. Abu Jahl said: I think that you should take a young man from each clan and give him a sharp sword and strike him once, so that his blood will be distributed among the tribes, so that the Banu Hashim will not be able to fight all of Quraysh. So if they ask for blood money, we will give it to them. He said, This young man is truthful. So they dispersed according to his opinion. Then Gabriel came to the Prophet, peace be upon them, and informed him of the report and ordered him to emigrate. So Ali, may God be pleased with him, spent the night in his bed and went out with Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, to the cave. And they plan, and God plans. By repelling their plan against them, or by punishing them for it, or by dealing with the planners with them by sending them out to Badr and making the Muslims appear small in their eyes until they attacked them and killed them. And God is the best of planners, since their plan is not taken into account more than His plan. Attributing such things is not appropriate for comparison and it is not permissible to say it initially because it implies blame.
8:31: 31. "And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, 'We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this.'" This is the statement of Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and his attribution to everyone is the attribution of what the leader of the people did to them, for he was their storyteller, or the statement of those who conspired against him, peace and blessings be upon him. This is the height of their stubbornness and extreme obstinacy, for if they were able to do that, then what prevented them from wishing to do so, when he challenged them and struck them with impotence for ten years, then he struck them with the sword, but they did not oppose a surah despite their arrogance and extreme disdain to be defeated, especially in the chapter of explanation. This is nothing but legends of the ancients. What the ancients wrote of stories.
8:32: 32. And when they said, 'O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.' This is also from the words of that speaker, more eloquent in denial. It was narrated that "when Al-Nadr said, 'This is nothing but legends of the ancients,' the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, 'Woe to you! It is the word of God.' He said that." The meaning is, if this is the truth revealed, then rain down stones upon us as punishment for denying it, or bring us a painful punishment other than it. What is meant by this is mockery and showing certainty and complete conviction that it is false. The truth was read in the nominative case, as it is a subject, not a separation. The benefit of the definition in it is to indicate that what is suspended upon it is the truth in the way that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, claims, which is its revelation, not the truth in general, because they allow it to be in accordance with reality and not revealed like the legends of the ancients.
8:33: 33. And God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness. A statement of what caused them to be given respite and to be delayed in answering their supplication. The lam is to emphasize the negation and to indicate that their punishment is a punishment of extermination, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, showed them to be outside his usual course and not upright in his judgment. What is meant by their seeking forgiveness is either the seeking of forgiveness by those believers who remained among them, or their saying, O God, Your forgiveness, or an opportunity, meaning that if they had sought forgiveness, they would not have been punished, as in His statement: And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly while their people were righteous.
8:34: 34. "And what is it to them that God should not punish them? And what is it to them that prevents their punishment when that is over and how can they not be punished? And they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque." Their situation and what prevented them from it was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers were forced to migrate and besieged in the year of Hudaybiyyah. "And they were not his guardians deserving of his authority despite their polytheism, and this is a refutation of what they used to say, We are the guardians of the House and the Sanctuary, so we prevent whomever we will and admit whomever we will. His guardians are only the righteous" from polytheism who do not worship anyone but Him in it, and it was said that the two pronouns refer to God. "But most of them do not know" that they do not have authority over him, as if he indicated by the majority that among them there are those who know and are stubborn, or he meant by it all as the few mean nonexistence.
8:35: 35. And their prayer at the House meaning their supplication or what they call prayer, or what they place in its place. Except whistling a verb from maka yamku if he whistles. And it is read with a short vowel like crying. And tasdiyan a clasping that you do from sada, or from sad by replacing one of the two doubling letters with ya. Their prayer was read in the accusative case as the predicate, and the context of the speech is to establish their deserving of punishment or their lack of guardianship of the mosque, as this is not befitting of someone whose prayer is like this. It was narrated that they used to circumambulate the House naked, men and women, interlocking their fingers, whistling and clapping. It was said that they used to do that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to pray, confusing him and making him think that they were also praying. Taste the punishment means killing and captivity on the day of Badr. It was said that it is the punishment of the Hereafter, and the lam may be for the covenant and the covenant: Bring us a punishment "for what you disbelieved" in belief and action.
8:38: 38. Say to those who disbelieve meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions, meaning say on their behalf. If they desist from opposing the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, by entering Islam, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them of their sins. It was read with a ta’ and a kaf, indicating that he addressed them, and forgives is in the active form, which is God Almighty. But if they return to fighting him, the precedent of the former peoples has already passed who plotted against the prophets to destroy them, as happened with the people of Badr, so let them expect the same. God
8:40: 40. And if they turn away and do not stop. Then know that God is your Protector Your Supporter, so trust in Him and do not care about their hostility. An excellent Protector He does not let down those who support Him. And an excellent Helper He who supports Him is not defeated.
8:41: 41. And know that whatever you have taken as spoils meaning that which you have taken from the infidels by force. Of anything of what the name of a thing applies to, even a thread. A fifth of it belongs to God is a subject whose predicate is omitted, meaning: it is established that a fifth of it belongs to God. It was read then with a kasra, and the majority are of the opinion that mentioning God is for glorification, as in His statement: And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should please Him, and that what is meant is dividing the fifth among the five conjoined words: And for the Messenger and for the near of kin and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, so it is as if he said: A fifth of it belongs to God and is spent on those who are most special to Him. And its ruling remains, except that the share of the Messenger, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, is spent on what he used to spend it on from the interests of the Muslims, as the two Sheikhs, may God be pleased with them, did. And it was said to the Imam. And it was said to the four categories. Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him said: His share and the share of his relatives were dropped upon his death, and all were allocated to the remaining three. Malik may God be pleased with him said: The matter is left to the opinion of the Imam, who allocates it to what he deems most important. Abu Al-Aaliyah took the apparent meaning of the verse and said: It is divided into six parts, and God’s share is allocated to the Kaaba, based on what was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to take a handful of it and put it for the Kaaba, then divide what remained among five. It was said that God made it for the public treasury. It was also said that it is included in the share of the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his relatives: Banu Hashim and Banu Al-Muttalib. It was narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, “divided the share of the relatives among them, and Uthman and Jubair bin Mut’im, may God be pleased with them, said to him: These are your brothers, Banu Hashim, we do not deny their virtue because of the position that God has placed you among them. Have you seen our brothers from Banu al-Muttalib, whom you have given and deprived us, and we and they are in one position?” He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: They did not leave us in ignorance or Islam, and he interlaced his fingers. “It was said: Banu Hashim alone. It was said: All of Quraysh, the rich and the poor, are equal in it. It was said: It is specific to their poor, like the share of the wayfarer. It was said: The fifth is all for them, and what is meant by the orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer is whoever is among them, and the conjunction is for specification. The verse was revealed at Badr.
