And those who gave shelter and aided are the Ansar who gave shelter to the emigrants to their homes and aided them against their enemies. Those are allies of one another in inheritance. The emigrants and the Ansar used to inherit through emigration and aid without relatives until it was abrogated by His statement: And those of kinship are more worthy of one another or in aid and support. And those who believed and did not emigrate - you have no part of their guardianship until they emigrate meaning from their guardianship in inheritance. Hamza read their guardianship with a kasra, likening it to work and industry like writing and leadership as if he was taking on the work of his companion. "And if they seek your aid in religion, then you must al-Nasr 110:It is your duty to support them against the polytheists. Except against a people between whom and you there is a covenant. For their covenant will not be broken because of their support for them. And God is Seeing of what you do.
8:73: 73. "And those who disbelieve are allies of one another" in inheritance or support, and in its concept it indicates the prevention of inheritance or support between them and the Muslims. "Unless you do it" unless you do what you have been commanded to do of communicating among yourselves and being allies of one another even in inheritance and severing ties between you and the disbelievers. "There will be a trial on earth" a great trial will occur in it, which is the weakness of faith and the appearance of disbelief. "And great corruption" in the religion, and it was read many times.
8:74: 74. And those who believed and emigrated and strove in the cause of God and those who gave shelter and aided - those are the believers, truly. When He divided the believers into three groups, He made clear that those who were perfect in faith among them were those who fulfilled their faith by achieving its requirements of emigration, jihad, spending money, and supporting the truth. And He promised them the noble appointment, saying, For them is forgiveness and noble provision, with no obligation or favor in it. Then He included with them in both matters those who would join them and bear their characteristics, saying:
8:75: 75. And those who believed afterward and emigrated and fought with you - those are from you meaning from your group, O Muhajireen and Ansar. And those of kinship are more worthy of one another in inheritance than strangers. In the Book of God in His ruling or in the Tablet or in the Qur'an and he used it as evidence for the inheritance of those of kinship. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things of inheritance and the wisdom in linking it to the relationship of Islam and manifestation, firstly and considering kinship secondly. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "Whoever recites Surat al-Anfal and Bara'ah, I will intercede for him on the Day of Resurrection, and I will witness that he is free from hypocrisy, and he will be given good deeds equal to the number of every hypocrite, male and female, and the Throne and its bearers will seek forgiveness for him during his life."
9:1: And it was said except for two verses from His saying: There has certainly come to you a Messenger and it is the last to be revealed and it has other names, Repentance and Al-Muqashqasha and Al-Buhuth and Al-Mubahathra and Al-Manqara and Al-Muthira and Al-Hafir and Al-Makhziyyah and Al-Fadihah and Al-Mankilah and Al-Musharjah and Al-Muddammamah and Surat Al-Adhab because of what it contains of repentance for the believers and Al-Qashqasha from hypocrisy which is disavowal of it, and searching for the state of the hypocrites and stirring it up, and digging about them and what disgraces them and exposes them and humiliates them and disperses them and scatters them and rumbles over them. It has one hundred and thirty verses, and it was said twenty-nine. The Bismillah was left out because it was revealed to remove security, and In the name of God is security. It was said that when a Surah or a verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would explain its location, and he died without explaining its location. Its story was similar to the story of Al-Anfal and was appropriate to it. Because in Al-Anfal the covenants were mentioned, and in Bara’ah they were discarded and added to it. It was said that when the Companions differed as to whether they were one Surah, the seventh of the seven long ones, or two Surahs, a space was left between them and In the name of God was not written. 1. Disclaimer from God and His Messenger meaning this is a disclaimer, and from is an introductory word related to an omitted word, the meaning of which is from God and His Messenger. It is permissible for disclaimer to be a subject for its specification by its description and the predicate is to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty. It was read in the accusative case on the basis of listen to disclaimer, and the meaning is that God and His Messenger are disclaimers of the treaty that you made with the polytheists. Rather, disclaimer was attached to God and His Messenger and the treaty to the Muslims to indicate that they must abandon the treaties of the polytheists to them, even if they were issued with the permission of God the Most High and the agreement of the Messenger, then they are disclaimers of them. This is because they made a treaty with the polytheists of the Arabs and broke it, except for some of them, Banu Damrah and Banu Kinanah, so he ordered them to abandon the treaty to the breakers and gave the polytheists four months to go wherever they wanted, so he said:
9:2: 2. So travel freely throughout the land for four months Shawwal, Dhul-Qi'dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram because it was revealed in Shawwal. It was said that it is the twentieth of Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, Rabi` al-Awwal, and ten days of Rabi` al-Akhir, because the notification was on the Day of Sacrifice, as it was narrated that “when it was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali, may God be pleased with him, riding Al-`Adhba` to recite it to the people of the season. He had sent Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, as a leader over the season, and it was said to him: If you send it to Abu Bakr, he said: No one will perform it on my behalf except a man from among me. When Ali, may God be pleased with him, approached, Abu Bakr heard the roaring, so he stopped and said: This is the roaring of the she-camel of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he caught up with him, he said: Leader or one who is commanded? He said: One who is commanded. When it was before Tarwiyah, Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, gave a sermon and told them about their rituals, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, stood on the Day of Sacrifice at Jamrat al-`Aqabah and said: It is for the people, for I am the Messenger of God to you. They said: What? So he recited to them thirty or forty verses, then he said: I have been commanded with four things: that no polytheist shall approach the House after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked, and no one shall enter Paradise except every believing soul, and that the Ka`bah be completed to “Everyone who has a covenant has his covenant.” Perhaps his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, None shall fulfil it on my behalf except a man from me is not general, “because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent so that many who were not from his family would fulfil it on his behalf.” Rather, it is specific to covenants, because the custom of the Arabs is that no one should undertake a covenant or break it for the tribe except a man from it, and evidence for this is that in some narrations, No one should convey this except a man from my family. “And know that you cannot frustrate God,” Do not escape Him even if He gives you respite, “And that God will disgrace the disbelievers,” with killing and captivity in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.
9:3: 3. And a call from God and His Messenger to the people meaning an effective notification in the sense of actions such as security and giving, and its raising is like the raising of innocence in both ways. The greater day of Hajj is the day of Eid because the Hajj is completed in it, most of its actions, and because the notification was in it and because it was narrated that "the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the day of sacrifice at the Jamarat during the Farewell Pilgrimage and said, This is the greater day of Hajj" and it was said the day of Arafah because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Hajj is Arafah and Hajj was described as the greater because Umrah is called the lesser Hajj, or because what is meant by Hajj is what occurs on that day of its actions, as it is greater than the rest of the actions, or because that Hajj brought together Muslims and polytheists and its Eid coincided with the Eids of the People of the Book, or because the glory of the Muslims and the humiliation of the polytheists appeared in it. That God means that God. is innocent of the polytheists meaning of their covenants. And His Messenger is in apposition to what is implied in is innocent, or to the position of if and its name in the reading of those who broke it, making the call to prayer run like a saying, and it was read in the accusative case in apposition to the name of if or because the waw means with and there is no repetition in it, so his saying innocence from God is report of the establishment of innocence and this is report of the obligation to inform about that, and for this reason he connected it to the people and did not specify it to those with whom a covenant was made. If you repent from disbelief and treachery, then repentance is better for you, but if you turn away from repentance or turn away from Islam and loyalty. Then know that you cannot escape God you will not miss a request from Him nor will you escape from Him in this world. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment in the Hereafter.
9:4: 4. Except for those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty. An exception from the polytheists or a correction, as if it was said to them after they were ordered to abandon the treaty to the covenant breakers, but those of them who made a treaty. Then they did not fail you in anything of the conditions of the treaty and did not break it or did not kill any of you or harm you at all. And they did not support anyone against you of your enemies. So fulfill their treaty with them until their term until the end of their term and do not treat them like the covenant breakers. Indeed, God loves the righteous. An explanation and a warning that fulfilling their treaty is a matter of piety.
9:5: 5. So when it is peeled off it is over, and the origin of peeling off is the removal of something from what it was wearing, such as the skinning of a sheep. The sacred months in which the faith-breakers are permitted to roam. It was said that they are Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram, and this is a violation of the system and contradicts the consensus, as it requires the sanctity of the sacred months to remain, since there is nothing in what was revealed after it abrogates them. Then kill the polytheists the faith-breakers wherever you find them whether in the sanctuary or outside. And capture them and take them captive. The capture is the captive. And besiege them and detain them or prevent them from the Sacred Mosque. And lie in wait for them at every place of ambush every passage so that they do not spread out in the land, and its accusative is in the context. If they repent from polytheism by faith. And establish prayer and give zakah confirming their repentance and faith. So let them go. So leave them alone and do not interfere with them in any of that. This is evidence that the one who abandons prayer and withholds zakat will not be let go. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. This is an explanation of the command, meaning, let them go because God is Forgiving and Merciful. He forgave them what had happened in the past and rewarded them for repentance.
9:6: 6. "And if one of the polytheists" who is commanded to be exposed to them. "Seeks your protection seeks your security and asks you for your protection then grant him protection" so grant him security. "Until he hears the word of God" and ponders it and learns the truth of the matter. "Then take him to his place of safety" a place of safety if he does not submit. "And one is raised by a verb that is explained by what follows it, not by the beginning because that is one of the factors of the verb. That is security or the matter. That they are a people who do not know what faith is and what the truth of what you are calling them to is, so their safety is necessary until they hear and ponder.
9:7: 7. How can there be a covenant for the polytheists with God and with His Messenger? An interrogative meaning denial and exclusion. They will not have a covenant and not break it despite the turmoil in their hearts, or that God and His Messenger will fulfill the covenant and they will break it. The predicate is how and it was presented for interrogation or for the polytheists or with God, and it is for the first two an attribute of the covenant or a circumstance for it. It is and how for the last two is a state of the covenant and for the polytheists if it is not a predicate then it is clarified. Except for those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque are the exceptions before and its location is the accusative as an exception or the genitive as a substitute or the nominative as the exception is disconnected, meaning: But those with whom you made a covenant at the Sacred Mosque. So if they are upright with you, then be upright with them meaning then wait for their affair, and if they are upright in the covenant, then be upright in fulfilling it, and it is like His saying Then complete their covenant with them until their term except that it is absolute and this is restricted and what the conditional and source clauses bear. Indeed, God loves the righteous was previously explained.
9:8: 8. How is repeated to exclude their adherence to the covenant or the continuation of its ruling, while pointing out the reason and deleting the verb because it is known, as in his saying: You told me that death is in the villages, so how about when there is a plateau and a well? That is, how did he die? And if they prevail over you, that is, if they are able to overcome you, they will not observe you, “they will not be observed in you,” except by alliance, and it was said by kinship. Hassan said: By your life, the people of Quraish are like the hump of an ostrich. It was said that it is lordship and perhaps it was derived for the oath from the word il which means to roar because when they made an alliance they raised their voices with it and made it loud, then it was borrowed for kinship because it establishes between relatives what an oath does not establish, then for lordship and education. It was said that it was derived from al-l of something if it defines it or from al-barq if it flashes. It was said that it is Hebrew meaning god because it was read il like Gabriel and Gabriel. And no covenant a covenant or right that is blameworthy for neglecting. They please you with their mouths is a resumption of explaining their state that contradicts their steadfastness in the covenant leading to their not being watched when they are victorious. It is not permissible to make it a state of the subject of they are not watched because after their appearance they are not satisfied. And because what is meant is to prove their pleasing the believers with the promise of faith, obedience and fulfilling the covenant in the present, and the internalization of disbelief and enmity such that if they are victorious they will not leave them alone, and the state contradicts it. And their hearts reject what their mouths utter. And most of them are wicked rebellious, with no belief to restrain them nor chivalry to deter them. The majority is specified for what some of the disbelievers have of avoiding treachery and refraining from what leads to bad talk.
9:9: 8. They exchanged the verses of God for a small price They exchanged the Qur'an for a small price A small gain, which is following whims and desires. So they turned away from His path His religion that leads to Him, or the path of His House by confining the pilgrims and the visitors. The fa indicates that their purchase led them to turning away. Indeed, evil was that which they were doing This action of theirs or what His statement indicates.
9:10: 10. They do not observe towards a believer any pact of kinship or covenant. This is an explanation, not a repetition. It was said that the first is general in the case of the transgressors, and this is specific to those who bought, and they are the Jews, or the Bedouins whom Abu Sufyan gathered and fed. And those are the transgressors in Al-Sharara.
9:11: 11. If they repent from disbelief. And establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. They are your brothers in religion. They have what you have and are subject to what you are subject to. And We detail the verses for a people who know. An interjection to encourage contemplation of what has been detailed of the rulings for those with whom a treaty has been made or the characteristics of those who repent.
9:12: 12. And if they break their oaths after their covenant And if they break what they pledged of faith or fulfillment of covenants. And attack your religion with explicit denial and ugly rulings. Then fight the leaders of disbelief meaning fight them. So the leaders of disbelief were put in the place of the pronoun to indicate that they thereby became those with leadership and precedence in disbelief and deserving of killing. It was said that what is meant by the leaders are the leaders of the polytheists, so the specification is either because killing them is more important and they are more deserving of it, or to prevent monitoring them. Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Ruh from Ya'qub read leaders with the two hamzas pronounced according to the original, and the explicit use of the ya' is a mistake. They have no oaths means they have no oaths in reality, otherwise they would not have stabbed him and broken it. It is evidence that if a dhimmi stabbed a non-Muslim, he has broken his covenant. The Hanafis cited it as evidence that the oath of a disbeliever is not an oath, but it is weak because what is meant is the negation of trust in it, not that it is not an oath, as God the Almighty says: And if they break their oaths. Ibn Amir read they have no oaths meaning no security or no Islam, and those who did not accept the repentance of the apostate clung to it, but it is weak because it is possible that it means they are not trusted in reporting about a specific people or they do not have faith, so they are watched for it. Perhaps they will desist is related to fight, meaning let your aim in fighting be that they desist from what they are doing, not to cause them harm, as is the way of those who cause harm.
9:13: 13. Do you not fight a people incites fighting because the hamza entered into the negation to deny, so it indicated exaggeration in the action. They broke their oaths which they swore with the Messenger, peace be upon him, and the believers not to help them against them, so they helped Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah. And they intended to expel the Messenger when they consulted about his matter in Dar al-Nadwa, as was mentioned in His statement: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you. It was said that they were the Jews who broke the covenant of the Messenger and intended to expel him from Medina. And they began with you the first time with hostility and fighting because he, peace be upon him, began with the call to them and obligated the argument with the Book and challenged them with it, so they turned away from opposing him to hostility and fighting, so what prevents you from opposing them and clashing with them. Do you fear them? Do you stop fighting them for fear that something bad will happen to you from them. God is more deserving that you should fear Him. So fight your enemies and do not abandon His command. If you are believers. The essence of faith is that one should fear none but Him.
9:14: 14. Fight them is an order to fight after explaining its reason and rebuking and threatening to abandon it. God will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them He promised them that if they fought, they would be victorious over them and be able to kill and humiliate them. And heal the hearts of a believing people meaning Banu Khuza'ah. It was said "clan from Yemen and Saba who came to Mecca and converted to Islam, but they were severely harmed by its people, so they complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Be of good cheer, for relief is near."
9:15: 15. And He removes the anger of their hearts for what they encountered from them, and God fulfilled what He promised them, and the verse is one of the miracles. And God turns in mercy to whom He wills beginning with the report that some of them repent from their disbelief, and that also happened, and and turns in repentance was read in the accusative case, with the implication that it is among the things that were answered with the command, for just as fighting caused the torment of a people, it caused the repentance of another people. And God is Knowing of what was and what will be. Wise He does not act or rule except in accordance with wisdom.
9:16: 16. Or did you think? is addressed to the believers when some of them hated fighting. It was said to the hypocrites, and or is disconnected and the meaning of the hamza in it is a rebuke for the calculation. That you should be left while God has not yet known those among you who strive and the sincere among you, who are those who strive, have not yet been distinguished from others, he denied knowledge and wanted to deny what is known for the sake of exaggeration, as it is like proof of it in that the connection of knowledge to it necessitates its occurrence. And they did not take is in apposition to struggled and is included in the connection. Besides God, His Messenger, and the believers, a close friend is a confidant who befriends them and divulges their secrets to them. What is in when of the meaning of expectation is an indication that the clarification of that is expected. And God is Acquainted with what you do He knows your purpose in it and it is like a mixture of what is imagined from the apparent meaning of his statement: And God has not yet known.
9:17: 17. It was not right for the polytheists it was not right for them. To maintain the mosques of God any of the mosques, let alone the Sacred Mosque. It was said that this is what is meant, and it was only collected because it is the direction of the mosques and their imam, so its maintainer is like the maintainer of all, and this is indicated by the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub with monotheism. Witnessing against themselves of disbelief by showing polytheism and denying the Messenger, and it is a state of the waw and the meaning is that it was not right for them to combine two contradictory matters, the maintenance of the House of God and the worship of other than Him. It was narrated (that when Al-Abbas was taken prisoner, the Muslims taunted him with polytheism and severing family ties, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, spoke harshly to him, so he said: What is the matter with you that you mention our faults and conceal our good deeds? We maintain the Sacred Mosque, block the Kaaba, provide water for the pilgrims, and free the captives) so it was revealed. Their deeds have become worthless which they boast about because of what accompanied them of polytheism. And in the Fire they will abide because of it.
9:18: 18. The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day and establish prayer and give zakat. That is, their maintenance is proper for those who combine the academic and practical perfections, and part of their maintenance is decorating them with carpets, lighting them with lamps, and continuing worship, remembrance, and lessons in knowledge in them, and maintaining them from what they were not built for, such as the hadith of this world. And from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: "God the Most High said: My houses on My earth are the mosques, and My visitors are their maintainers. So blessed is the servant who purifies himself in his house and then visits Me in My house. It is the duty of the one visited to honor his visitor." The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not mention faith because he knew that faith in God is a companion and its completion is faith in Him, and because His statement, and establishes prayer and gives zakat indicates this. And fears none but God, that is, in the chapters of religion, for fear of dangers is innate and the mind can hardly control itself from it. Perhaps those will be among the guided. He mentioned it in the form of expectation to cut off the polytheists’ desires for guidance and benefit from their actions, and to rebuke them by confirming that they are guided. For these people, with their perfection, if their guidance revolves around perhaps and perhaps, then what do you think of their opposites? And to prevent the believers from being deceived by their conditions and relying on them.
9:19: 19. Have you considered the provision of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day and strives in the cause of God? Watering and maintenance are the source of the verbs to water and to live, so they are not likened to corpses, but rather it is necessary to imply the meaning of Have you considered the people who provide water to the pilgrims equal to one who believes? or Have you considered the provision of water to the pilgrims equal to the faith of one who believes? The first reading is supported by the one who reads providing water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of the mosque. The meaning is to deny that the polytheists and their nullifying deeds are likened to the believers and their affirming deeds. Then He decided that by saying: They are not equal in the sight of God. And He clarified their inequality by saying: And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. That is, the unbelievers are wrongdoers in polytheism and enmity towards the Messenger, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, and are immersed in misguidance, so how can they be equal to those whom God has guided and granted success to the truth and right? It was said that what is meant by the wrongdoers are those who treat each other equally with the believers.
9:20: 20. Those who believed and emigrated and fought in the cause of God with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank with God higher in rank and more honorable than those who do not possess these qualities or those who provide water and construction for you. And those are the successful in reward and attainment of goodness with God, without you.
9:21: 21. Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and approval and gardens for them therein in the gardens. Eternal bliss forever. Hamza read gives them good tidings with a light pronunciation, and the indefiniteness of the one being given good tidings indicates that he is beyond specification and definition.
9:22: 22. They will abide therein forever. He emphasized eternity with perpetuity because it may be used for a long stay. Indeed, God has with Him a great reward. He considers what they deserved for it or the pleasures of this world insignificant compared to it.
9:23: 23. O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies. This was revealed about the emigrants, for when they were ordered to emigrate, they said: If we emigrate, we will cut off our fathers, our sons, and our tribes, and our trade will be lost, and we will remain lost. It was said that it was revealed as a prohibition against befriending the nine who apostatized and went to Mecca, and the meaning is do not take them as allies who will prevent you from believing and turn you away from obedience, because of His statement: If they prefer disbelief over belief, if they choose it and are keen on it. And whoever among you takes them as allies - then it is those who are the wrongdoers, by placing the allegiance in the wrong place.
9:24: 24. "Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your kindred, your kinsfolk are your relatives" is taken from the word ten. It is also said that it is from the word ten, because the kindred is a group that goes back to a contract like the contract of ten. Abu Bakr read and your kindreds and it was also read your kindreds. And wealth that you have acquired you have earned. And trade that you fear will decline the passing of the time for its hypocrisy. And dwellings that you like are dearer to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His cause is voluntary love rather than natural love, because it does not fall under the obligation to be cautious about it. Then wait until God brings about His command is an answer and a threat, and the command is a punishment, immediate or delayed. It is also said that it is the conquest of Mecca. And God does not guide the wicked people does not guide them, and in the verse there is great severity and few are those who can be freed from it.
9:25: 25. God has given you victory in many battles, meaning battles and situations. And the day of Hunayn and the place of the day of Hunayn and it is permissible to estimate it in the days of places or to interpret the place with the time like the killing of Al-Hussein and it does not prevent the substitution of his saying: When your great number pleased you from it to be connected to a place in places because it does not require their sharing in what the connected is added to until it requires their great number and her admiration of them in all places. Hunayn is a valley between Mecca and Taif where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims fought and they were twelve thousand, the ten who attended the conquest of Mecca and two thousand joined them from the freedmen Hawazin and Thaqif and they were four thousand so when they met the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, or another of the Muslims said: You will not be defeated today because of fewness, admiration of their great number and they fought a fierce battle so the Muslims realized their admiration and reliance on their great number so they were defeated until they reached Mecca and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained in his position with no one with him except his uncle Al-Abbas holding his reins and his cousin Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith. This is enough as a testimony to the extent of his bravery, so he said to Al-Abbas - and his fame spread among the people - so he called out: O servants of God, O people of the tree, O people of Surat Al-Baqarah, come together as one neck saying, Here I am, here I am. And the angels descended, so fear God with the polytheists. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said this when the battle became intense. Then he took a handful of dirt and threw it at them, then he said: Be defeated, by the Lord of the Kaaba. So they were defeated. And the earth, with all its vastness, became strait for you. With its vastness, meaning with its breadth, you could not find in it an escape that would reassure your souls from the intensity of the terror, nor could you remain in it like someone whose place cannot contain him. Then you turned to the infidels, running back in defeat, and turning back means going to the back, unlike advancing.
9:26: 26. Then God sent down His tranquility His mercy in which they rested and felt secure. Upon His Messenger and upon the believers who were defeated. The repetition of the preposition is to draw attention to the difference between their two states. It was said that they were those who stood firm with the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and did not flee. And He sent down soldiers you did not see with your eyes, meaning the angels, and they were five thousand or eight or sixteen according to the different opinions. And He punished those who disbelieved by killing, capturing, and taking captive. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers meaning what He did to them as recompense for their disbelief in this world.
9:27: 27. Then God will turn to whomever He wills after that of them by guiding them to Islam. And God is Forgiving and Merciful He overlooks them and is gracious to them. It was narrated that some people came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and became Muslims and said: O Messenger of God, you are the best of people and the most pious, yet our families and children have been taken captive and our wealth has been taken - and on that day six thousand people were taken captive and countless camels and sheep were taken - so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Choose, either your captives or your wealth. They said: We do not consider lineage equal to anything. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and said: These people have come as Muslims and we gave them the choice between children and wealth, but they did not consider lineage equal to anything. Whoever has captives in his possession and is willing to return them, let him do so, and whoever does not, let him give us and let it be a loan to us until we obtain something and we give him in its place. They said: We are satisfied and we have submitted. He said: I do not know, perhaps there are those among you who are not satisfied, so order your leaders to bring them to us. They brought them to us and said that they were satisfied.
35:10: 28. O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists are impure because of the filth of their interior, or because one should avoid them as one should avoid impurities, or because they do not purify themselves or avoid impurities, so they are often exposed to them. This is evidence that what is usually impure is impure. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that their bodies are impure like dogs. It was read Najis with a sukoon and a kasra on the noon, and it is like Kabd in Kabd, and most of what came is followed by Rijs. So do not approach al-Masjid al-Haram because of their impurity, and the prohibition of approaching is only for emphasis or to prevent entering the sanctuary. It was said that what is meant by it is the prohibition of Hajj and Umrah, not entering absolutely, and Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, went with this, and Malik compared all the mosques to al-Masjid al-Haram in the prohibition, and this is evidence that the disbelievers are addressed by the branches. After this year of theirs means the year of Bara'ah, which is the ninth. It was said that it was the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage. And if you fear poverty poverty due to their being prevented from entering the Sacred Sanctuary and the loss of what you had from their coming of earnings and companions. God will enrich you from His bounty from His giving or His favor in another way. He fulfilled His promise by sending rain from the sky upon them in abundance and guided the people of Tabalah and Jerash so they submitted and provided for them, then He opened up the lands and spoils to them and people headed to them from the corners of the earth. A’ila was read as a source like ‘afiyah or mud. If He wills He restricted it to the will so that hopes are cut off from God the Most High and to point out that He the Most High is generous in that and that the promised wealth will be for some and not others and in one year and not another. Indeed, God is Knowing of your conditions. Wise in what He gives and withholds. 10 - Whoever desires honor meaning honor and strength. To God belongs all honor meaning let him seek it from Him, for it is all his. Thus, the evidence is sufficient without meaning. To Him ascends the good words, and the righteous deed raises it is an explanation of what honor is sought by, which is monotheism and righteous deeds. Their ascension to Him is a metaphor for His acceptance of them, or the ascension of the scribes with their scroll. What is implied in raises it is for the words, for deeds are not accepted except with monotheism. This is supported by the fact that the deed is in the accusative case, or for the deed, for it confirms and strengthens faith, or for God, and deed is specifically designated for this honor because of the cost involved. Ascends is read as referring to the two constructs, and the ascender is God, the Most High, or the One who speaks it, or the angel. It is said that the good words includes remembrance, supplication, and reciting the Quran. “And on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: It is: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Great. When the servant says it, the angel ascends with it to the heavens and greets with it the face of the Most Merciful. If there is no righteous deed, it is not accepted.” And those who plot evil deeds means the evil plots of the Quraysh against the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, in Dar al-Nadwa, and they deliberated over one of three things: imprisoning him, killing him, or exiling him. For them is a severe punishment no attention will be paid to anything less than that. And the plotting of those is bound to fail it is corrupted and is not carried out because things are predestined and are not changed by it, as indicated by his saying:
9:29: 29. Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day meaning, they do not believe in them as they should, as we explained in the beginning of Al-Baqarah, for their belief is no belief. And they do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden what has been proven to be forbidden by the Book and the Sunnah. It was said that His Messenger is the one they claim to follow, and the meaning is that they contradict the original abrogated religion in belief and action. And they do not follow the religion of truth the established religion that abrogates all other religions and invalidates them. Of those who were given the Scripture is a statement of those who do not believe. Until they pay the jizyah what is decided upon them to give is derived from the verb jazi which means to pay off his debt. From his hand is a state of the pronoun, meaning from the hand of those who are submissive, or from their hand, meaning Muslims with their own hands and not sending with the hands of others, and for this reason it is forbidden to delegate it, or from wealth, and for this reason it is said: it is not taken from the poor, or from a hand that is dominant over them, meaning helpless and humiliated, or from the jizyah, meaning cash paid from hand to hand, or from a favor to them, for keeping them with the jizyah is a great blessing. And they are humiliated humiliated. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, he said: The jizyah is taken from the dhimmi and his neck is wound, and the meaning of the verse requires that the jizyah is specific to the People of the Book, and this is supported by the fact that Omar, may God be pleased with him, "that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it from the Magians of Hajar, and that he said: Establish a tradition with them." The People of the Book: This is because they have a semblance of a book, so they are included with the People of the Book. As for the rest of the infidels, the jizya is not taken from them according to us. According to Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, it is taken from them except for the polytheists of the Arabs, because al-Zuhri narrated that he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, made peace with the idol worshippers except for those who were from the Arabs. According to Malik, may God have mercy on him, it is taken from every infidel except the apostate, and the minimum amount each year is a dinar, whether rich or poor. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said that for the rich, it is forty-eight dirhams, for the average, half of it, and for the poor, who earns a living, a quarter of it, and nothing is due from the poor, who is not a living person.
9:30: 30. And the Jews said, 'Ezra is the son of God.' This was only said by some of their predecessors or those who were in Medina. They only said this because after the battle of Nebuchadnezzar, there was no one left among them who had memorized the Torah. When God revived him after a hundred years, He dictated the Torah to them by heart, so they were amazed by that and said, This is none other than the son of God. The evidence that this statement was among them is that the verse was read to them, and they did not lie, despite their insistence on lying. Asim, Al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read 'Aziz with the tanween, as if he were an Arab, being described by the word son, not described by it, and its deletion negates the other reading, either to prevent its being declined due to foreignness and definiteness, or because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, resembling the letter nun with soft letters, or because the son is a description and the predicate is deleted, like our god or our companion, which is false because it leads to accepting the lineage and denying the estimated predicate. And the Christians said, 'The Messiah is the son of God.' This is also the saying of some of them, and they only said it because it is impossible for Him to be born without a father or for Him to do what He did of healing the blind and the leper and raising the dead, who was not a god. That is their saying with their mouths. Either to confirm the attribution of this saying to them and to deny the metaphor for it, or to indicate that it is a saying devoid of proof and verification similar to the neglected that is found in mouths but its meaning is not found in objects. They imitate the saying of those who disbelieve. That is, their saying imitates the saying of those who disbelieve, so the complement was deleted and the complement to it was put in its place. Before means before them, and what is meant is their predecessors, meaning that disbelief is ancient among them, or the polytheists who said that the angels are daughters of God, or the Jews, since the pronoun refers to the Christians, and imitation is similarity and the hamza is a language in it. Asim read it, and from it is their saying, a woman who is like men in that she does not menstruate. May God kill them is a prayer for their destruction, for whoever God kills will perish, or it is amazement at the hideousness of their words. How are they turned away? How are they diverted from the truth to falsehood?
9:31: 31. They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God by obeying them in forbidding what God has permitted and permitting what God has forbidden or by prostrating to them. And the Messiah, the son of Mary by making him the son of God. And they were not commanded meaning what those who took or those who are taken as lords were not commanded, so it is like evidence of the invalidity of taking. except to worship to obey. One God which is God the Most High. As for obeying the Messenger and all those whom God has commanded to be obeyed, it is in reality obedience to God. There is no god but Him is a second attribute or a new statement of monotheism. Glory be to Him above what they associate with Him purifying Him from having a partner.
9:32: 32. They want to extinguish to put out the light of God His proof of His Oneness and His sanctity from having a son, or the Qur'an or the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace with their mouths with their polytheism or their denial. But God refuses that is, He is not pleased except to perfect His light by exalting monotheism and glorifying Islam. It was said that it is a metaphor for their situation in their seeking to invalidate the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by denial, in the situation of someone seeking to extinguish a great light spread in the horizons that God wants to increase by blowing it. The empty exception is correct and the verb is affirmative because it is in the meaning of negation. Even if the disbelievers hate it The answer is omitted because what preceded it indicates it.
9:33: 33. It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religions as an explanation of His statement: But God refuses except to perfect His light and for this reason He repeated even though the polytheists dislike it except that He put the polytheists in place of the disbelievers to indicate that they combined disbelief in the Messenger with polytheism in God, and the pronoun in to make it prevail refers to the true religion, or to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and the lam in religion refers to the genus, meaning over all other religions so that He abrogates them, or over their people so that He abandons them.
9:34: 34. O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis and the monks devour the wealth of people unjustly. They take it through bribery. In the rulings, taking money is called consuming because it is the greatest purpose of it. And they hinder [men] from the way of God His religion. And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of God may mean many of the rabbis and monks, so it is an exaggeration in describing them as greedy and stingy with money, and it may mean the Muslims who collect money and acquire it and do not pay its due, and its association with the bribe-takers from the People of the Book is for the sake of severity. Evidence for this is that when it was revealed, it became difficult for the Muslims, so Umar, may God be pleased with him, mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: God did not impose zakat except to purify what remains of your wealth. And his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whatever zakat is paid is not a hoard, meaning a hoard that has been threatened, because the threat is for hoarding without spending in what God has commanded to be spent in. As for his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever leaves a yellow or white thing, brand it with it, and the like, what is meant by it is what has not been paid its due, according to his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what the two sheikhs reported on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him: “There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay its due except if he is On the Day of Resurrection, plates of fire will be spread out for him, and his forehead, sides, and back will be branded with them. “So give them tidings of a painful punishment,” meaning branding with them. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 12 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Tawbah, and the first verses of Sūrat Yūnus. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time.
