9:35: 35. On the Day when it is heated in the Fire of Hell meaning on the Day when the Fire is lit with intense heat over it. Its original form is heated with fire, so heating up the fire was made an exaggeration, then fire was deleted and the verb was attributed to the preposition and noun to indicate the intended meaning, so it moved from the feminine form to the masculine form. He only said over it and what is mentioned are two things because what is meant by them are many dinars and dirhams, as Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Four thousand and what is less than that and what is above that is a treasure. And likewise the Almighty's saying: And they do not spend it and it was said that the pronoun in them refers to the treasures or to the money because the ruling is general and they are specifically mentioned because they are the law of wealth, or to silver and it is specifically mentioned because of its proximity and the indication of its ruling that gold is more deserving of this ruling. Then their foreheads, their flanks, and their backs will be branded with it. Because their gathering, their withholding of it, was to seek prestige through wealth and enjoyment of delicious foods and fine clothing, or because they turned away from the questioner and turned their backs on him, or because it is the most honorable of the visible organs, as it contains the main organs, which are the brain, heart, and liver, or because it is the origins of the four directions, which are the fronts, backs, and sides of the body. This is what you have hoarded, meaning for yourselves, for its benefit, and it was the very cause of its harm and the reason for its torment. So taste what you have been hoarding, meaning the consequences of your hoarding or what you hoard. It was read takanazon with a dammah on the nun.
9:36: 36. The number of months means the amount of their number. With God is the object of count because it is a source. Twelve months in the Book of God in the Preserved Tablet, or in its ruling, and it is an attribute of twelve. And His saying: On the Day He created the heavens and the earth is related to what is in it of the meaning of permanence or to the Book if it is made a fixed one, and the meaning is: that this is a matter that is permanent in the essence of the matter since God created the bodies and the times. Four of them are sacred one is Rajab and three are in succession Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram. That is the right religion meaning the sacredness of the four months is the straight religion, the religion of Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, and the Arabs inherited it from them. So do not wrong yourselves therein by violating their sanctity and committing their forbidden acts. The majority are of the opinion that the sanctity of fighting therein was abrogated, and those who commit injustice by committing sins therein are more sinful than committing them in the Sacred Sanctuary and in a state of Ihram. It was narrated from Ata’ that it is not permissible for people to wage war in the Sacred Sanctuary and in the sacred months unless they fight. The first is supported by what was narrated that “he, peace and blessings be upon him, besieged Taif and raided Hawazin at Hunayn in Shawwal and Dhul-Qi’dah.” And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together all together, and it is a source of refraining from something, as everyone is refrained from increasing, and it falls in the place of the state. And know that God is with the righteous is good report and a guarantee for them of victory because of their piety.
9:37: 37. Indeed, the postponement means delaying the sanctity of the month to another month. If a sacred month came while they were at war, they would make it permissible and forbid another month in its place, until they rejected the specificity of the months and considered the mere number. And from Nafi' with the narration of Warsh Indeed, the forgetfulness by changing the hamza to a ya' and assimilating the ya' into it. And the forgetfulness was read without it, and the nasa' and the women, and all three of them are sources of the nasa'ah if he delayed it. Addition to disbelief because it is the prohibition of what God has permitted and the permission of what God has forbidden, so it is another disbelief that they added to their disbelief. He misleads those who disbelieve thereby an additional misguidance. Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read yudhill in the passive form, and from Ya'qub yudhill on the basis that the action belongs to God the Most High. They make it permissible a year they make the forgotten sacred months permissible a year and forbid another month in its place. And they forbid it a year they leave it as sacred. It was said: The first one to do this was Junada bin Auf Al-Kinani. He would stand on a camel during the Hajj season and call out: Your gods have made the forbidden lawful for you, so make it lawful. Then he would call out to the tribes: Your gods have forbidden you the forbidden, so forbid it. Both sentences are an explanation of misguidance or confusion. So that they may agree with the number of what God has forbidden meaning that they may agree with the number of four forbidden days. The lam is related to they forbid or to what the two verbs indicate. So that they may make lawful what God has forbidden by agreeing with the number alone without taking into account the time. He has made their evil deeds seem good to them. It was read in the active form, which is God, the Most High, and the meaning is that He has let them down and led them astray until they considered their ugly deeds to be good. And God does not guide the disbelieving people guidance that leads to right guidance.
9:38: 38. O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that when you are told to go forth in the cause of God you are heavy-handed? You are slow. It was read َقاَقَقاْلُمaccording to the original andأَقاَقاْلُمas a question for rebuke. To the earth is related to it as if it included the meaning of devotion and inclination, so it was transitive with to. This was during the Battle of Tabuk, which they were ordered to do after their return from Taif at a time of hardship and heat with the distance and the large number of the enemy, so it was difficult for them. Are you satisfied with the life of this world and its delusion? From the Hereafter instead of the Hereafter and its pleasures. What is the enjoyment of the life of this world? What is the enjoyment of it? In the Hereafter in comparison to the Hereafter. Except a little insignificant.
9:39: 39. If you do not go forth If you do not go forth to that for which you have been called forth. He will punish you with a painful punishment By destroying you due to a terrible cause such as drought or the emergence of an enemy. And He will replace you with another people And He will replace you with others who are obedient such as the people of Yemen and the sons of Persia. And do not harm Him at all For your reluctance to support His religion does not detract at all, for He is independent of everything and in every matter. It was said that the pronoun refers to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning do not harm him, for God Almighty promised him protection and victory, and His promise is true. And God is over all things competent So He is able to change and alter the causes and to provide victory without support, as He said.
9:40: 40. "If you do not aid him, God has aided him." That is, if you do not aid him, God will aid him as He aided him: "When those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two." And there was only one man with him, so the penalty was omitted and what is like evidence for it was established in its place, or if you do not aid him, God has made victory obligatory for him until He aided him at that time, so He will not let him down at any other time. And attributing the expulsion to the disbelievers is because their intention to expel or kill him caused God to give him permission to go out. And "the second of two" was read with a sukoon in the language of those who treat the defective as a shortened form in grammar and place it in the accusative case as a state. "When they were in the cave is a substitute for when He expelled him" as a substitute for some, since what is meant by it is a long period of time, and the cave is a hole in the top of Thawr, which is a mountain to the right of Mecca, an hour's journey away, and they stayed in it for three days. "When he says is a substitute for second or an adverb for second." To his companion, who was Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, Do not be sad, God is with us, with protection and assistance. It was narrated that the polytheists climbed up to the cave and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, felt sorry for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you think of two when God is their third? So God blinded them from the cave, so they went around it and did not see him. It was said that when they entered the cave, God sent two doves that laid eggs at the bottom of it, and a spider that wove a web over it. So God sent down His tranquility, His security with which hearts are at peace. Upon him, upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or upon his companion, who is Al-Azhar, because he was disturbed. And supported him with soldiers you did not see, meaning the angels, whom He sent down to guard him in the cave or to help him against the enemy on the day of Badr, the Confederates, and Hunayn. So the sentence is connected to His statement, God aided him. “And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest,” meaning polytheism or the call to disbelief. And the word of God is the highest, meaning monotheism or the call to Islam, and the meaning is that He made that by freeing the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hands of the disbelievers to Medina, because it is the beginning for him, or By supporting him with the angels in this situation or by protecting and aiding him wherever he is. Jacob read and the word of God in the accusative case in apposition to the word those who, and the nominative case is more expressive because it contains the feeling that the word of God is high in itself, even if it surpasses others, so its superiority is not proven or taken into consideration, and therefore in the middle of the chapter, and God is Exalted in Might and Wise in His command and management.
9:41: 41. "March out, whether light or heavy, due to its difficulty for you, or because your children are few or many, or riding or walking, or light or heavy weapons, or healthy or sick. Therefore, when Ibn Maktoom said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Should I march out, he said: Yes. Until the verse was revealed: "There is no blame upon the blind. And strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of God" to the best of your ability, both or one of them. "That is better for you" than abandoning it. "If you should know" the good, you know that it is good, or if you know that it is good, then God Almighty's information about it is true, so hasten to it.
9:42: 42. "If it were an offer" meaning if what they called for was a worldly benefit. "Close" easy to take. "And a moderate journey" moderate. "They would have followed you" they would have agreed with you. "But the distance was too far for them" meaning the distance that is traveled with difficulty. It was read with a kasra on the 'ayn and the sheen. "And they will swear by God" meaning those who stayed behind when you returned from Tabuk apologizing. "If we were able" they say or we had the ability to provide the equipment or the body. It was read "If we were able" with a damma on the waw likening it to the waw of the pronoun in His statement: "They purchased error We would have gone out with you" prevailed in place of the answers to the oath and the condition, and this is one of the miracles because it is a report of what happened before it happened. "They destroy themselves by causing themselves to be tormented, and it is a substitute for they will swear" because the false oath causes the soul to be destroyed or a state of its doer. "And God knows that they are liars" in that, because they were able to leave.
9:43: 43. May God forgive you is a metaphor for his mistake in giving permission, for forgiveness is one of the pioneers of His knowledge. Why did you give them permission? is a clarification of what was referred to as forgiveness and a reproach for it. The meaning is why did you give them permission to stay when they asked your permission and made excuses with lies? Why didn't you stop? Until those who are truthful become clear to you in the apology. And you know the liars in it. It was said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did two things that he was not commanded to do: taking the ransom and giving permission to the hypocrites, so God reproached him for them.
9:44: 44. Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your permission to fight with their wealth and their lives. That is, it is not the custom of the believers to ask your permission to fight, for the sincere among them rush to it and do not hesitate to ask your permission to do so, let alone ask your permission to stay away from it, or ask your permission to stay away out of dislike for fighting. And God is Knowing of the righteous. This is a testimony to their righteousness and a promise to them of His reward.
9:45: 45. Only those who do not believe in God and the Last Day ask your permission to stay behind. These are those who do not believe in God and the Last Day. The specification of belief in God Almighty and the Last Day in both places is to indicate that the motive for jihad and the deterrent from it is faith and the promise of faith in them. And their hearts are in doubt, so they are wavering in their doubt. They are confused.
9:46: 46. "And if they had intended to go out, they would have prepared for it." For going out. "Prepared" is equipment. It was read "adda" without the taa' when adding, as in his saying: The mixture was very good, so they withdrew and broke their promise to you. He promised him with the kasra of the ‘ayn with the addition and promised him with something else. But God disliked their going out is a correction of the meaning of his statement: And if they had wanted to go out as if he said they did not go out but were held back because God disliked their going out, meaning their getting up to go out. So He held them back is enough for them with cowardice and laziness. And it was said, ‘Sit with those who sit’ is a representation of God casting dislike of going out into their hearts, or the devil’s whispering of the command to sit, or the narration of some of them saying to each other, or permission from the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, for them. And those who sit could mean those who are excused and others, and in both cases it is not without blame.
9:47: 47. "If they had gone out with you, they would not have increased you anything" by their going out. "Except corruption" corruption and evil. This does not entail that they would have had corruption even if they had gone out, because the increase is in consideration of the generality of the year from which the exception was made. For this reason, the exception was made discontinuous, but it is not so because it cannot be empty. "And they would have hastened their mounts among you with gossip and slander, or defeat and discouragement from the camel's putting if it hastens. They seek to cause you discord they want to tempt you by causing discord among you or terror in your hearts, and the sentence is a state of the pronoun in they put. And among you are those who listen to them weak who listen to their words and obey them, or slanderers who listen to your talk in order to convey it to them. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers He knows their inner selves and what comes from them.
9:48: 48. They sought discord to scatter your affair and disperse your companions. Before meaning the day of Uhud, for Ibn Abi and his companions, just as they had stayed behind from Tabuk after they had gone out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Dhi Jeddah, below Thaniyat al-Wada', returned on the day of Uhud. And they turned things upside down for you and plotted against you tricks and schemes and circulated opinions to invalidate your affair. Until the truth came with divine victory and support. And the command of God appeared and His religion was exalted. And they were averse meaning in spite of themselves. The two verses are to console the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers for their staying behind and to explain what God had discouraged them for and hated their going out for it and to tear down their veils and reveal their secrets and to remove their excuses in order to make up for what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had missed by taking the initiative to give permission. For this reason, he was rebuked for it.
9:49: 49. And among them is he who says, 'Give me permission' to stay. And do not tempt me and do not make me fall into temptation, meaning into disobedience and failure to give me permission, and in it is an indication that he will inevitably stay behind whether he gives him permission or not, or into temptation due to the loss of money and children since there is no one to support them after me. Or into temptation with the women of the Romans, as it was narrated that Jadd bin Qais said: The Ansar have known that I am fond of women, so do not tempt me with the daughters of the yellow man, but I will help you with my money, so leave me. Indeed, into temptation they have fallen meaning that it is the temptation into which they have fallen, which is the temptation of failure or the appearance of hypocrisy, not what they have guarded against. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers gathering them on the Day of Resurrection, or now because the encompassing of its causes by them is like its existence.
9:50: 50. If you are afflicted in some of your battles. Good victory and booty. It will make them sad because of their excessive envy. And if you are afflicted in some of them. Calamity a fracture or hardship as happened on the day of Uhud. They will say, 'We have taken our command beforehand' They boasted about their departure and praised their opinion in staying behind. And they turn away from the one who spoke about it and their gathering for it, or from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And they are happy delighted.
9:51: 51. "Say: Nothing will ever happen to us except what God has decreed for us" except what we have secured by affirming and obligating it of victory, or martyrdom, or what has been written for us in the Preserved Tablet, which does not change with your agreement or opposition. And it was read hal yasibna and it is from fa'il not from fa'l because it is from the daughters of waw, as they say saba al-sham yasub and its derivation is from as-sawb because something happens as it was intended. And it was said that as-sawb is from huwa mawlana "he is our supporter and the one in charge of our affairs. and upon God let the believers put their trust" because their right is not to put their trust in anyone other than Him.
9:52: 52. "Say: Do you await for us?" Except one of the two good outcomes? "Except one of the two good outcomes, Victory and martyrdom. And we await for you also one of the two evils that God will afflict you with a punishment from Himself by a calamity from the sky. or by our hands" or by a punishment by our hands, which is killing for disbelief. "Then await what is our outcome? Indeed, we are with you awaiting" what is your outcome.
9:53: 53. "Say: Spend willingly or unwillingly, it will never be accepted from you." A command in the sense of a statement, meaning that your spending will not be accepted from you whether you spend willingly or unwillingly. Its benefit is to exaggerate the equality of the two spendings in not being accepted, as if they were ordered to be tested and spend and see if it will be accepted from them. This is the answer to the statement of Jad bin Qais, And I will help you with my wealth. The denial of acceptance has two possible meanings: that it will not be taken from them and that they will not be rewarded for it. His statement, Indeed, you were a people of wickedness, is an explanation for it by way of resumption, and what follows is an explanation and confirmation of it.
9:54: 54. And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger. That is, nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted except their disbelief. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read an yaqbal with a ya' because the feminine of expenditures is not real. It was read yaqbal on the basis that the action is for God. And they do not come to prayer except while they are lazy. Slowly. And they do not spend except while they are reluctant. Because they do not hope for reward for them nor do they fear punishment for abandoning them.
9:55: 55. So let not their wealth or their children impress you, for that is a lure and a calamity for them, as He said. God only intends to punish them with them in the life of this world, because of what they struggle to collect and preserve it from the troubles and what they see in it of hardships and calamities. And their souls depart while they are disbelievers, so they die as disbelievers, exploiting the enjoyment without considering the consequences, so that is a lure for them. The root of destroying is exiting with difficulty.
9:56: 56. And they swear by God that they are of you that they are of the Muslims. And they are not of you because of the disbelief in their hearts. But they are a people who fear they fear that you will do to them what you do to the polytheists, so they show Islam out of caution.
9:57: 57. If they find a refuge a fortress to which they can resort or caves jealously. Or an entrance a tunnel in which they can dig, derived from the verb to enter. Jacob read an entrance from the verb to enter. It was also read an entrance meaning a place in which they can enter themselves. Mandakhilan is derived from tadakhalu and indakhul. Lawlu ilayhi means they would rush towards it. And they are running fast they are running fast, nothing can stop them like a runaway horse. It was also read Yajmuzon and from it is the verb al-Jamaazah.
9:58: 58. And among them is he who slanders you criticizes you. And the Qur'an says yalamzak with the dammah and Ibn Kathir yalamzak. In the charity in its division. If they are given from it, they are pleased, but if they are not given from it, at once they are angry. It was said that it was revealed about Abu al-Jawaz the hypocrite, who said: Do you not see that your companion only distributes your charity among the shepherds of the sheep and claims that he is just. And it was said about Ibn Dhi al-Khuwaysira, the leader of the Khawarij, "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was dividing the spoils of Hunayn, so he softened the hearts of the people of Mecca by providing them with the spoils, so he said: Be just, O Messenger of God. He said: Woe to you, if I am not just, then who will be just?" And if is for surprise, a substitute for the conditional fa.
9:59: 59. And if they had been satisfied with what God and His Messenger gave them what the Messenger gave them of spoils or charity, and God was mentioned for glorification and to draw attention to the fact that what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, did was by His command. And they said, 'God is sufficient for us' His bounty is sufficient for us God will give us from His bounty charity or other spoils and His Messenger He will give us more than what He has given us. Indeed, we are desirous towards God that He enrich us from His bounty, and the entire verse is within the scope of the condition, and the answer is with an omitted word, the meaning of which is better for them then He explained the expenditures of the charity to correct and confirm what the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, did, so he said:
9:60: 60. Zakat is only for the poor and the needy meaning zakat is for these people and not for others, and this is evidence that what is meant by slander is slandering them in the division of zakat and not the spoils of war. The poor person is the one who has no money or earnings and is in need of poverty as if his poverty has afflicted him. The needy person is the one who has money or earnings that are not enough for him from stillness as if inability has made him still, and this is indicated by the saying of God Almighty: As for the ship, it was for the needy and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to ask for poverty and seek refuge from poverty. It was said the opposite, based on the Almighty’s saying: A poor man covered with dust. “And those who work on it” those who strive to obtain and collect it. And those whose hearts are to be reconciled are people who have converted to Islam but whose intentions are weak, so their hearts are renewed, or nobles who may be required to give them and take care of their peers’ conversion to Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave to Uyaynah ibn Hisn, Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis, and Al-Abbas ibn Mirdas for this reason. It was said that they were nobles who were to be reconciled to Islam, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to give to them. The most correct view is that he used to give them from the fifth of the fifth that was his special wealth, and he counted among them those whose hearts he would reconcile with something from it to fight the infidels and those who withheld the zakat. It was said that the share of those who were to be reconciled was to increase the number of Muslims, but when God made it victorious and increased its people, it was dropped. And in the slaves is for spending in freeing slaves by helping the slave with something from it to pay the stars. It was said that the slaves should be bought and freed, and Malik and Ahmad said the same, or that the prisoners should be ransomed. The change from lam to fi indicates that the entitlement is for the party and not for the slaves. It was said to indicate that they are more entitled to it. And the debtors and those who are indebted to themselves, not for disobedience and not for extravagance, if they cannot pay, or to reconcile people even if they are rich, “according to the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “Charity is not permissible for a rich person except for five: for a fighter in the cause of God, or for a debtor, or for a man who bought it with his money, or for a man who has a poor neighbor and he gives charity to the poor person, so the poor person gives a gift to the rich person, or for a worker on it.” And in the cause of God and for spending in jihad by spending on volunteers and buying mounts and weapons. It was said that in the construction of bridges and factories, and the wayfarer is the traveler who is cut off from his wealth. A duty from God is a source for what the noble verse indicated, i.e. God imposed on them the obligatory charity, or a state of the pronoun implied in for the poor. It was read in the nominative case on that a duty. “And God is Knowing and Wise” places things in their places, and the apparent meaning of the verse requires specifying the entitlement to zakat to the eight categories and the obligation to spend it on each category found among them and to take into account equality between them as a matter of partnership. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, went to this, and from Umar, Hudhayfah, Ibn Abbas, and others from the Companions and Followers, may God be pleased with them all, the permissibility of spending it on one category, and the three imams said this and some of our companions chose it, and my sheikh and my father, may God have mercy on them, used to issue fatwas on it, that the verse is a clarification that charity does not come from them, not an obligation to divide it among them.
9:61: 61. And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say he is an ear He hears everything that is said to him and believes it, he was called the wound for exaggeration as if from his excessive listening9 his whole body became the instrument of hearing just as the spy was called an eye for that, or a verb was derived for him from the verb adhaan if he listened like a nose and paralysis. It was narrated that they said Muhammad is an ear, he hears us and we say what we want then we come to him and he believes us in what we say. Say an ear of goodness for you confirming for them that he is an ear but not in the way they were criticized for, rather from the point of view that he hears goodness and accepts it, then he explained that by saying: He believes in God he believes in him because of the evidence that he has established. And he believes in the believers and he believes them because he knows of their sincerity, and the lam is added to differentiate between belief in belief because it means submission and belief in security. And mercy meaning it is mercy. For those of you who believe for those who show faith such that He accepts it and does not reveal its secret. It is a warning that He does not accept your words out of ignorance of your situation, but rather out of gentleness and mercy towards you. Hamza read and mercy in the accusative case in apposition to good. It was said in the accusative case, as the cause of an action indicated by good permission meaning He gives you permission out of mercy. Nafi' read good permission with a light emphasis in both of them. Good permission was read so that good is an attribute of it or a second predicate. And those who harm the Messenger of God will have a painful punishment by harming him.
9:62: 62. They swear to you by God regarding your excuses for what they said or did not say. To please you so that you may be pleased with them. The address is to the believers. And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should please Him more deserving of being pleased with through obedience and agreement, and the unification of the conscience is due to the two being pleased or because the speech is about harming the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and pleasing him, or because the estimate is that God is more deserving that the Messenger be pleased with Him as well. If they are believers truly.
9:63: 63. Have they not known that the matter is and it was read with the letter taa. Whoever opposes God and His Messenger is quarreling, a reciprocal of the word hadd. "For him is the fire of Hell, wherein he will abide eternally in the deletion of the report, meaning that it is true that he has or on the repetition of that for emphasis, and it is possible that it is conjoined with that and the answer is deleted, its estimate is that whoever opposes God and His Messenger will perish, and it was read then" with the kasra. "That is the great disgrace" meaning eternal destruction.
9:64: 64. The hypocrites are afraid that a surah will be revealed to them to the believers. It will inform them of what is in their hearts and tear away their veils. It is possible that the pronouns refer to the hypocrites, for what is revealed to them is like what is revealed to them in that it is recited and used as evidence against them. This indicates their hesitation in their disbelief as well, and that they were not certain about anything concerning the matter of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that it is report of the sense of a command. It was said that they were saying it among themselves in mockery of His statement: Say, 'Mock on! God will bring forth.' Showing or revealing. What you fear means what you fear from the revelation of the surah to you, or what you fear from revealing your faults.
9:65: 65. And if you ask them, they will surely say, 'We were only conversing and joking.' It was narrated that the hypocrites' caravan passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the Battle of Tabuk and said, "Look at this man who wants to conquer the palaces and fortresses of Syria. No way, no way." So God Almighty informed His Prophet about him, so he called them and said, You said such and such. They said, "No, by God, we have nothing to do with your affair or the affair of your companions, but we were involved in something that caravans converse in so that some of us could shorten the journey for others." Say, 'Was it at God and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking?' This is a rebuke for their mockery of someone whom it is not right to mock, and to impose the argument on them and not to pay attention to their false excuses.
9:66: 66. Do not apologize. Do not be preoccupied with your apologies, for they are known to be false. You have disbelieved. You have shown disbelief by harming the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and slandering him. After your belief. After showing your belief. If We pardon a group of you for their repentance and sincerity, or to avoid harming and mocking them. We punish a group because they were criminals Egyptian for hypocrisy or for committing harm and mockery. Asim read them with the letter noon in both. It was read with the letter ya and the subject is built in both of them, which is God. And if you pardon with the letter ta and the subject is built to the meaning, as if he said: that you have mercy on a group.
9:67: 67. The hypocrites, men and women, are of one another meaning they are similar in hypocrisy and distance from faith, like parts of the same thing. It was said that it is a denial of their oath by God that they are of you and a confirmation of their statement that they are not of you and what follows it is like evidence for it, as it indicates the opposite of their state to the state of the believers, which is His statement: They enjoin what is wrong by disbelief and sins. And forbid what is right by faith and obedience. And they withhold their hands from righteousness, and withholding the hand is a metaphor for stinginess. They forgot God they neglected to remember God and abandoned His obedience. So He forgot them by leaving them out of His kindness and grace. Indeed, the hypocrites are the wicked who are complete in rebellion and wickedness from the circle of goodness.
9:68: 68. God has promised the hypocrites, men and women, and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally. They are destined for eternity. It is sufficient for them as punishment and recompense, and in it is evidence of the enormity of its torment. And God has cursed them He has distanced them from His mercy and humiliated them. And for them is an enduring torment that will not cease. What is meant by this is what they were promised or what they suffer from the fatigue of hypocrisy.
9:69: 69. Like those before you means you are like those, or you did as those before you did. They were stronger than you and had more wealth and children is a statement of their likeness to them and their situation is like theirs. Then enjoy their share is their portion of the pleasures of this world, and its derivation is from the word khalaf meaning estimation, for it is what is destined for its owner. Then you enjoyed your share as those before you enjoyed their share is a censure of the first ones for enjoying their deceived portions of fleeting desires and being distracted by them from considering the consequences and striving to obtain true pleasures, as a prelude to censuring those addressed for resembling them and following in their footsteps. And you plunged and entered into falsehood. Like those who plunged is like those who plunged, or like the group who plunged, or like the plunge they plunged. Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter. They do not deserve any reward for them in both worlds. And those are the losers. Those who have lost this world and the Hereafter.
9:70: 70. Has there not come to them the report of those before them - the people of Noah? They were drowned by the flood. And Aad They were destroyed by the wind. And Thamud They were destroyed by the earthquake. And the people of Abraham Nimrod was destroyed by a mosquito and his companions were destroyed. And the people of Midian The people of Midian, who are the people of Shuaib, were destroyed by the fire on the Day of Shadow. And the overturned The cities of the people of Lot were overturned by them, meaning they were turned upside down, and they were rained down with stones of baked clay. It was said that they were the cities of the disbelieving rebels, and their overturning was the reversal of their conditions from good to evil. Their messengers came to them meaning everyone. "With clear proofs. So God would not wrong them" meaning it was not His habit to do anything similar to wronging people, such as punishing without a crime. But they were wronging themselves as they exposed themselves to punishment by disbelief and denial.
9:71: 71. The believing men and believing women are allies of one another in contrast to His statement, "The hypocrites, men and women, are of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and establish prayer and give zakat and obey God and His Messenger" in all matters. Those - God will have mercy upon them inevitably, for the seen is an emphasis of occurrence. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might dominant over everything, nothing that He wills is impossible for Him. Wise He places things in their proper places.
9:72: 72. God has promised the believing men and believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and pleasant dwellings that the soul enjoys or in which life is pleasant. In the hadith, it is said that they are palaces of pearls, emeralds, and red rubies. In the Gardens of Eden residence and eternity. “And on his authority, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, ‘Eden is the abode of God which no eye has seen and no human heart has conceived. None inhabits it except three: the prophets, the truthful ones, and the martyrs. God Almighty says: ‘Blessed is he who enters you.’” The reference of the conjunction in it may be to the multiplicity of what is promised to each one or to all by way of distribution, or to the difference in its description, as if he described it first as being of the same type as the most splendid places they know, so that their natures incline toward it as the first thing that strikes their ears. Then he described it as being surrounded by good living, free from the impurities of turbidity that are not absent from any of the places of this world, and in it is what the souls desire and the eyes delight in. Then he described it as a place of residence and stability in the neighborhood of the highest, in which neither decay nor change befalls them. Then he promised them something greater than that, saying: ‘And the pleasure of God is greater,’ because it is the beginning of all happiness and honor and the one that leads to attaining arrival and winning the encounter. And on his authority, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, God Almighty says to the people of Paradise, ‘Are you satisfied?’ They say, ‘Why should we not be satisfied, when you have given us what you have not given to anyone else?’” Who created you? He says: I will give you something better than that. They say: What is it like that? He says: I will bestow My pleasure upon you, and I will never be angry with you. That meaning pleasure or all of the above. is the great success before which the world and everything in it are insignificant.
9:73: 73. O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers with the sword. And the hypocrites by obligating the argument and establishing the limits. And be harsh upon them in that and do not show favoritism towards them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination their destination.
9:74: 74. They swear by God that they did not say it. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed in the Battle of Tabuk for two months, and the Qur’an was revealed to him and he criticized those who stayed behind. Then Al-Jalas bin Suwayd said: If what Muhammad says to our brothers is true, then we are worse than donkeys. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he summoned him and he swore by God that he did not say it. Then this was revealed, and Al-Jalas repented and his repentance was good. And they said the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam and showed disbelief after showing Islam. And they intended what they could not achieve of killing the Messenger, which is that fifteen of them agreed upon his return from Tabuk to push him from his mount to the valley when he ascended the pass at night, so Ammar bin Yasir took hold of the reins of his mount and led it and Hudhayfah was behind it leading it, while they were like that, Hudhayfah heard the sound of the camels' hooves and the clatter of peace, so he said, Come, come, O enemies of God, so they fled, or expelled him and the believers from the city or that they crown Abdullah bin Ubayy even if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not pleased. And they did not resent and they did not deny or they did not find what would cause their resentment. Except that God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty for most of the people of Medina were in need and in difficult living conditions, so when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought them forward, they enriched themselves with the spoils and killed a freed slave of Al-Jallas, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his blood money of twelve thousand and he became independent. The exception is devoid of the most general effects or causes. If they repent, it will be better for them. This is what prompted the companions to repent, and the pronoun in it refers to repentance. But if they turn away by persisting in hypocrisy. God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter by killing and fire. And they will have no protector or helper on earth, so He will save them from the punishment.
9:75: 75. And among them are those who made a covenant with God, 'If He should give us from His bounty, we will surely give in charity and be among the righteous.' "This was revealed about Tha'laba bin Hatib. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Ask God to grant me wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Tha'laba, a little for which you can give thanks is better than a lot that you cannot bear. So he repeated it to him and said: By Him Who sent you with the truth, if God grants me wealth, I will give everyone his due. So he prayed for him and he acquired sheep, which grew like worms until the city became too small for them. So he went down into a valley and stopped attending the congregation and Friday prayers. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about him and it was said that his wealth had increased to the point that no valley could contain him. So he said: Woe to Tha'laba. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out tax collectors to collect the alms. The people met them with their alms and passed by Tha'laba and asked him for the alms. He read him the book that contained the obligatory duties. So he said: This is nothing but a jizya. This is nothing but The sister of the tribute, so go back until I see my opinion. So it was revealed. Then Tha`laba came with the charity, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has prevented me from accepting it from you. So he began to throw dirt on his head and said: This is your work. I ordered you and you did not obey me. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and he brought it to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, but he did not accept it. Then he brought it to Umar, may God be pleased with him, during his caliphate, but he did not accept it. He died during the time of Uthman, may God be pleased with him.
9:76: 76. So when He gave them of His bounty, they were stingy with it. They withheld God's right from it. And they turned away from obeying God and they were averse. They are a people whose habit is to turn away from it.
9:77: 77. "So He made hypocrisy in their hearts" meaning, God made the consequence of their action hypocrisy and bad belief in their hearts. It is possible that the pronoun refers to miserliness, and the meaning is, "So He caused miserliness to cause them to have hypocrisy firmly rooted in their hearts. Until the Day they meet Him" they will meet God with death or they will meet their deeds, meaning their punishment, which is the Day of Resurrection. "Because they broke their promise to God" because they broke their promise to Him of giving charity and righteousness. "And because they used to lie" and because they were liars in it, because breaking a promise includes a lie that is ugly from both sides or in general. It was read "they lie" with emphasis.
9:78: 78. Have they not known meaning the hypocrites or those who made a covenant with God? It was read with the letter ta' for emphasis. That God knows their secret what they concealed in their souls of hypocrisy or the intention to break it. And their private conversations and what they call to one another of slander, or calling the zakat a jizya. And that God is Knower of the unseen so that is not hidden from Him.
9:79: 79. "Those who slander" is a nominative or accusative denunciation or a substitute for the pronoun, so it pleases them. Yalmazun is read with a dammah. "The volunteers" are the volunteers. "Of the believers in charity" It was narrated: "That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged charity, so Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf came with four thousand jars and said: I had eight thousand, so I lent my Lord four and kept four for my family, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God bless you in what you gave and in what you kept, so God blessed him until one of his two wives agreed to give half the price for eighty thousand dirhams. Asim ibn Adi gave charity with one hundred wasqs of dates, And Abu Uqayl al-Ansari came with a sa' of dates and said: I spent the night squandering jars for two sa's, so I left a sa' for my family and brought a sa', so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to scatter it on charity, so the hypocrites slandered them and said: Abd al-Rahman and Asim did not give except Hypocrisy, and God and His Messenger were not in need of Abu Aqil’s Sa’, but he wanted to be mentioned about himself so that he could be given from the charity. So the following was revealed: And those who find nothing except their effort except their ability. It was read with the fat-ha, and it is the source of effort in the matter if he exaggerates in it. They mock them mocks them. God mocks them He rewarded them for their mockery, as God the Most High said: God mocks them “And for them is a painful punishment” for their disbelief.
9:80: 80. Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them He means by it the equality between the two matters in not benefiting them as stated in his saying: If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, God will not forgive them. It was narrated that Abdullah bin Abdullah bin Ubayy, who was one of the sincere ones, asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his father's illness to ask forgiveness for him, so he did, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse was revealed. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will add seventy to it, so the verse was revealed: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, God will not forgive them. This is because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, understood from the seventy the specific number because it is the origin, so it is permissible for it to be a limit that differs from the ruling of what comes after it, so he explained to him that what is meant by it is the increase without the specification, and the use of seventy, seventy, seven hundred and the like has become widespread in the use of the increase, because seven includes all the divisions of the number, so it is as if it is the entire number. That is because they disbelieved in God and His Messenger is an indication that despairing of forgiveness and not accepting your forgiveness is not due to stinginess. It is not from us, nor is there any deficiency in you, but rather due to their inability due to the disbelief that turns them away from it. And God does not guide the wicked people who rebel in their disbelief, and it is like evidence for the previous ruling, for the forgiveness of the disbeliever is by ceasing to disbelief and guiding to the truth, and the one who is immersed in his disbelief that is natural to him will not be stopped or guided, and the warning about the excuse of the Messenger in his seeking forgiveness is that he did not despair of their faith unless he knew that they were natural to misguidance, and what is forbidden is seeking forgiveness after knowledge, for God Almighty said: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire.
9:81: 81. "The ones who stayed behind rejoiced at their sitting behind the Messenger of God" by their sitting behind him from the conquest. It is said that he stayed behind the tribe, meaning after them. It is possible that it means opposition, so its accusative is based on the reason or the state. "And they hated to fight with their wealth and their lives in the way of God" preferring ease and comfort over obedience to God, and in it is an allusion to the believers who preferred to obtain His pleasure by spending their wealth and lives. "And they said, 'Do not go forth in the heat'" meaning some of them said to each other or they said it to the believers to discourage them. "Say, 'The fire of Hell is more intense in heat'" and you preferred it with this opposition. "If they had understood" that their destination is to it, or that it is how it is, they would not have chosen it by preferring ease over obedience.
9:82: 82. So let them laugh a little and weep much as recompense for what they used to earn. This is a report of what will happen to them in this world and the next. He presented it in the form of an imperative to indicate that it is an inevitable duty. It is possible that laughter and weeping are metaphors for joy and sorrow, and what is meant by little is nothingness.
9:83: 83. If God returns you to a group of them If He returns you to the city and there is a group of those who stayed behind, meaning their hypocrites, then not all of them were hypocrites, or those who remained from them, and the ones who stayed behind were twelve men. Then they asked your permission to go out to another raid after Tabuk, then say, 'You will never go out with me, nor will you fight with me an enemy.' A statement in the sense of prohibition for exaggeration. You were satisfied to sit back the first time is an explanation for it, and their exclusion from the register of the raiders was a punishment for them for staying behind, and the first time is the departure to the Tabuk raid. So sit with those who stayed behind meaning their staying behind because of their unfitness for jihad, such as the women and children. It was read with those who stayed behind on the basis of shortening those who stayed behind.
9:84: 84. "And never pray over any of them who dies." It was narrated that Abdullah bin Ubayy called upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his illness. When he entered upon him, he asked him to seek forgiveness for him and shroud him in his garment that was next to his body and to pray over him. When he died, he sent his shirt to be shrouded in it and went to pray over him, so the following was revealed: "And it was said that he prayed over him, then it was revealed. He did not forbid shrouding him in his shirt, but he forbade praying over him because being stingy with the shirt was a lack of generosity, and because it was a reward for Abbas wearing his shirt when he was taken prisoner at Badr. What is meant by prayer is supplication for the dead and seeking forgiveness for him, which is forbidden for the disbeliever. Therefore, the prohibition was based on his saying: He died forever, meaning death in disbelief, because bringing the disbeliever back to life for torture without enjoyment is as if he had never been brought back to life. And never stand at his grave, and Do not stand at his grave for burial or addition. They disbelieved in God and His Messenger and died while they were wicked. This is an explanation for the prohibition or for the perpetuity of death.
9:85: 85. "So do not let their wealth or their children impress you. God only intends to punish them thereby in the life of this world and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers." Repetition for emphasis, and the matter is true, for eyes aspire to wealth and children, and souls rejoice over them. It is possible that this is in a group other than the first.
9:86: 86. "And when a surah is revealed" from the Qur'an, and it is possible that it means some of it. "That they believe in God that they believe in God, and it is possible that the interpretative that. And strive with His Messenger, those of them of wealth ask your permission" those of grace and abundance. "And they say, Leave us to be with those who sit those who sit for an excuse.
9:87: 87. They were content to be with the ones who stayed behind. With the women, the plural of khalafah. The word khalafah may also be used for someone who is not good. And their hearts are sealed, so they do not understand. What happiness there is in jihad and agreeing with the Messenger, and what misery there is in staying behind him.
9:88: 88. But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their lives. That is, if these people stayed behind and did not strive, then those who were better than them strove. And those will have the good things. The benefits of both worlds: victory and spoils in this world, and Paradise and honor in the Hereafter. And it was said that they are the houris because of the Almighty's saying: In them are good and beautiful things. It is the plural of khayra, a lightening of khayra. "And those are the successful ones." The victors in their demands.
9:89: 89. "God has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. That is the great attainment." A statement of the good things they will have in the Hereafter.
9:90: 90. And the Bedouins who had excuses came to be given permission meaning Asad and Ghatafan who asked permission to stay behind, apologizing for the effort and the large number of children. It was said that they were the people of Amer bin Tufail who said that if we went out with you, Tayy will raid our families and livestock. The excuser is either one who excused himself in the matter if he fell short in it, giving the impression that he had an excuse when he did not, or one who apologized if he prepared the excuse by assimilating the taa into the dhal and transferring its movement to the 'ayn. It is permissible to break the 'ayn due to the meeting of two quiescent letters and to add a damma to follow, but they were not read with them. And the Qur’an says: The excusers are from the root a’dhar, meaning he made an effort to make an excuse. And the Qur’an says: The excusers are read with emphasis on the ‘ayn and the dhal, as it is from ta’aṭarā meaning he apologized, which is a mistake, as the ta’ is not assimilated into the ‘ayn. And there is a difference of opinion as to whether they were apologizing by pretense or by correctness, so his statement: And those who denied God and His Messenger sat refers to others, and they are the hypocrites of the desert Arabs who denied God and His Messenger in claiming faith, even though they were the first, so their lie was by way of an apology. A painful punishment will befall those among them who disbelieved from the desert Arabs or from the excusers, as some of them apologized for their laziness, not their disbelief, by killing and fire.
9:91: 91. "There is no blame upon the weak nor upon the sick" such as the elderly and the lame. "Nor upon those who do not find what they can spend" because of their poverty such as Juhaynah, Muzaynah and Banu Udhrah. "There is no blame" sin in delaying. "If they advise God and His Messenger" with faith and obedience in secret and in public, as the loyalists would do, or with whatever they are able to do in action or word that returns good to Islam and the Muslims. "There is no blame upon the doers of good" meaning there is no blame upon them nor is there a way to reproach them. Rather, the doers of good were placed in the place of the pronoun to indicate that they are included in the ranks of the doers of good and are not reproached for that. "And God is Forgiving and Merciful" to them or to the wrongdoer, so how about the doer of good.
9:92: 92. And not upon those who, when they come to you that you may carry them, is an apposition to the weak or to the doers of good, and they are the seven weepers from the Ansar: "Maqal bin Yasar, Sakhr bin Khansa, Abdullah bin Kaab, Salim bin Umair, Tha'laba bin Ghanima, Abdullah bin Mughaffal, and Aliyah bin Zaid. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We have vowed to go out, so carry us on the patched sandals and the woven sandals, and we will fight with you. So he, peace be upon him, said: I do not find anything to carry you on, so they turned away while they were weeping." It was said that they were the sons of Muqrin, Maqal, Suwaid, and Al-Nu'man. It was said that Abu Musa and his companions said: I said, ‘I do not find what to carry you on.’ is a state of the kaf in they came to you with the omission of had. “Turned away” is the answer to if. “And their eyes are overflowing” is flowing. Of tears means tears, because min is for clarification and it is with the majrur in the place of the accusative on the distinction and it is more eloquent than her tears overflow, because it indicates that the eye became overflowing tears. Sadness is the accusative as a cause or state or source of a verb indicated by what preceded it. That they do not find is related to sadness or overflowing. “What they spend” in their expedition.
9:93: 93. The only way is to reproach. On those who ask your permission while they are rich and have the means. They were satisfied to be with the disobedient ones." A resumption to explain what is the reason for their asking permission without an excuse, which is their satisfaction with baseness and being included in the group of disobedient ones, preferring ease. "And God has sealed their hearts" until they are heedless of the dire consequences. "So they do not know" its consequences.
9:94: 94. They apologize to you for staying behind. If you return to them from this journey. "Say, 'Do not apologize' with false excuses because: "We will not believe you" will not believe you because: "God has already informed us of your report" He informed us by revelation to His Prophet of some of your report, which is what is in your consciences of evil and corruption. "And God and His Messenger will see your deeds" Will you repent from disbelief or will you persist in it? It is as if it is a call to repentance and a respite for repentance. "Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen" meaning to Him. So the description was placed in place of the pronoun to indicate that He is aware of their secret and their public, nothing of their consciences and deeds escapes His knowledge. "Then He will inform you of what you used to do" with rebuke and punishment for it.
9:95: 95. They will swear to you by God if you turn back to them to turn away from them. So do not rebuke them. So turn away from them. "And do not rebuke them. Indeed, they are unclean." Reprimanding them is of no use, for the purpose of it is purification by making them repent. These are unclean and do not accept purification, so it is the reason for turning away and not reprimanding. "And their abode is Hell." is a complete explanation, and the meaning is: The fire is sufficient for them as reprimand, so do not bother to reprimand them. "As a recompense for what they used to earn." It is possible that it is a source or a reason.
9:96: 96. They swear to you so that you may be pleased with them by their oath, so that you continue to do to them what you used to do. But if you are pleased with them, then indeed, God is not pleased with the wicked people meaning that your pleasure does not necessitate the pleasure of God, and your pleasure alone will not benefit them if they are in the wrath of God and facing His punishment, and if they are able to confuse you, they cannot confuse God, so their cover will not be torn, nor will humiliation descend upon them. The purpose of the verse is to forbid being pleased with them and being deceived by their excuses after the command to ignore them and not pay attention to them.
9:97: 97. The Bedouins the Bedouins. More severe in disbelief and hypocrisy than the city dwellers because of their savagery and cruelty and their lack of interaction with people of knowledge and their lack of listening to the Book and the Sunnah. And it is more deserving that they do not know "and more deserving that they do not know. The limits of what God has revealed to His Messenger of the laws, their obligations and their Sunnah. And God is Knowing of the knowledge of the condition of every one of the people of the hair and the mud. Wise in what He afflicts their wrongdoers and their good-doers with, punishment and reward.
9:98: 98. "And among the Bedouins is he who takes after what he spends" he spends it in the way of God and gives it in charity. "as a fine" a fine and loss, since he does not consider it as a means of drawing closer to God nor does he hope for a reward for it, but rather he spends it for show or as a precaution. "And He awaits for you the circles" the circles of time and its turns so that the matter may turn against you and he may be freed from spending. "Upon them is the circle of evil" an objection by praying for them in the manner they are awaiting or informing about the occurrence of what they are awaiting for them, and the circle is originally a source or an active participle from the house that turns, and the obstacle of time was named after it, and "evil" with the fat-ha is a source added to it for emphasis like you say a man of truth. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read "evil" here. In the fat-ha with the damma on the seen. "And God is All-Hearing" of what they say when spending. "Knowing" of what they conceal.
9:99: 99. And among the bedouins are those who believe in God and the Last Day and take what they spend as means of drawing near to God is the reason for drawing near and it is the second object of takes and with God is its description or circumstance for takes. And the prayers of the Messenger and the reason for his prayers because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate for the givers of charity and ask forgiveness for them, and therefore it is the Sunnah of the one who is given charity to supplicate for the giver of charity when taking his charity, but he does not have to pray for him as he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, bless the family of Abi Awfa because it is his position, so he may bestow it upon others. Indeed, it is a means of drawing near to them is a testimony from God to the correctness of their belief and confirmation of their hope on the resumption with the letter of warning and in confirming the relation and the pronoun for their spending, and Warsh read qurbah with a damma on the ra'. God will admit them into His mercy and their justice by encompassing mercy upon them and the seen is for its confirmation and his saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful is for its confirmation. It was said that the first is in Asad, Ghatafan, and Banu Tamim and the second in Abdullah Dhi Al-Bijadain and his people.
9:100: 100. "And the first of the Muhajireen" are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs or those who witnessed Badr and those who converted to Islam before the migration. "And the Ansar" are the people of the first pledge of Aqaba. They were seven, and the people of the second pledge of Aqaba. They were seven, and those who believed when Abu Zurarah Mus'ab bin Umair came to them. It was read in apposition to "and the first of the Muhajireen". "And those who followed them in goodness" are those who will follow the first of the two tribes, or those who followed them in faith and obedience until the Day of Resurrection. "God is pleased with them" by accepting their obedience and approving their deeds. "And they are pleased with Him" by what they attained of His religious and worldly blessings. "And He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow" Ibn Kathir read underneath which rivers as in all other places. "They will abide therein forever. That is the great attainment".
9:101: 101. And among those around you meaning and among those around your town, meaning Medina. Among the bedouins are hypocrites they are Juhayna, Muzayna, Aslam, Ashja' and Ghifar who were settled around it. And among the people of Medina is an appositive to and among those around you or the predicate of an omitted word that I added. Accustomed to hypocrisy. Similar to it in deleting the described and replacing it with the adjective is his saying: I am the son of Jala and Talaa Al-Thanaia And the first is a description of the hypocrites, separated from it by the one conjoined to the good, or a statement of the beginning to clarify their cunning and their skill in hypocrisy. You do not know them you do not know them by their persons, and it is a confirmation of their skill in it and their skill in avoiding the sites of accusation to the extent that their condition is hidden from you despite your perfect intelligence and true insight. We know them and we are aware of their secrets. If they are able to confuse you, they are not able to confuse us. We will punish them twice with disgrace and killing or one of them and the punishment of the grave, or by taking the zakat and the exhaustion of bodies. Then they will be returned to a great punishment to the punishment of the Fire.
9:102: 102. And others confessed their sins and did not apologize for their absence with false excuses, and they are "a group of those who stayed behind and tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque when they heard what was revealed about those who stayed behind, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and entered the mosque as was his custom and prayed two rak'ahs and saw them and asked about them and it was mentioned to him that they swore that they would not release themselves until you released them, so he said: And I swear that I will not release them until I command them, so it was revealed and I released them." They mixed a good deed with another bad one. They mixed the good deed, which is showing remorse and admitting sin, with another bad one, which is staying behind and agreeing with the hypocrites, and the waw is either in the meaning of the ba as in their saying I sold the sheep for a sheep and a dirham, or to indicate that each one of them is mixed with the other. Perhaps God will accept their repentance that He accepts their repentance, which is indicated by His saying They confessed their sins. God is Forgiving and Merciful. He overlooks the repentant and is gracious to him.
9:103: 103. Take charity from their wealth. It was narrated: "When they were released, they said, 'O Messenger of God, this is our wealth that we left behind, so give it in charity and purify us.' He said, 'I was not commanded to take anything from your wealth.'" So it was revealed: purify them from sins or the love of money that leads them to the same. Purify them was read from purify him meaning purified him, and purify them was read in the subjunctive mood in response to the command. And purify them with it and increase their good deeds and raise them to the stations of the sincere. And pray for them and show them kindness by supplicating and asking forgiveness for them. Indeed, your prayer is a comfort to them their souls are comforted by it and their hearts are reassured by it. It was pluralized because of the multiplicity of those supplicated for. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read it in the singular. And God is All-Hearing of their confession. Knowing of their remorse.
9:104: 104. Have they not known? The pronoun either refers to those who have been repented to, meaning that it is possible in their hearts to accept their repentance and to consider their charity, or to others, meaning to incite them to do so. That God is the One who accepts repentance from His servants if it is correct and its transitive use is from because it includes the meaning of overlooking. And He takes the charity He accepts it as someone who takes something to give in exchange. And that God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful and that it is His nature to accept the repentance of those who repent and to be gracious to them.
9:105: 105. "And say, 'Do whatever you wish.' And God will see your deeds, for nothing, whether good or evil, is hidden from Him. And [so will] His Messenger and the believers, for nothing, as you have seen and become clear to you, is hidden from them. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, by death. Then He will inform you of what you used to do, by the recompense for it.
9:106: 106. And others of those who stayed behind. Marjoon is delayed, meaning their matter is suspended from arja'tuhu if you postpone it. Nafi', Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read Marjoon with the waw and they are two dialects. For the command of God in their matter. Either He punishes them if they persist in hypocrisy. Or He turns to them if they repent. And the repetition is for the servants, and in it is evidence that both matters are by the will of God the Most High. And God is Knowing of their conditions. Wise in what He does to them. And it was read And God is Forgiving and Merciful, and what is meant by these is Ka'b bin Malik, Hilal bin Umayya and Murarah bin Al-Rabi'. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his companions not to greet them or speak to them, so when they saw that, they purified their intentions and entrusted their matter to God, so God the Most High had mercy on them.
9:107: 107. "And those who have taken a mosque is in apposition to and others are deferred", or a subject with an omitted predicate, meaning, and among those we described who have taken, or it is in the accusative case for specificity. Nafi` and Ibn `Amir read without the waw, harming to the believers. It was narrated: “When Banu `Amr ibn `Awf built the Quba Mosque, they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come to them. So he came to them and prayed in it. Their brothers Banu Ghanim ibn `Awf envied them, so they built a mosque with the intention that Abu `Amir the monk would lead them in it when he came from Ash-Sham. When they had completed it, they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: We have built a mosque for those in need and illness, and on rainy and cold nights, pray in it until we make it a place of prayer. So he took his garment to stand with them, and this was revealed. So he called Malik ibn Ad-Dukhshum, Ma`n ibn `Adi, `Amir ibn As-Sakin, and Al-Wahshi and said to them: Go to this mosque whose people are oppressors, and demolish and burn it. So he did so and took a place of sweeping in its place.” And disbelief and strengthening the disbelief that they were harboring. And division among the believers destroying those who used to gather to pray in the Quba Mosque. And ambush in anticipation. "For those who fought God and His Messenger before" means the monk, for he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of UHud 11:I will not find any people fighting you except that I will fight you with them. So he continued to fight him until the day of Hunayn until he was defeated with Hawazin and fled to the Levant to bring Caesar soldiers to fight the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he died alone in Qinnasrin. It was said that he was gathering the armies on the day of the Confederates, and when they were defeated, he went out to the Levant. "Before is related to fought or took" meaning they took a mosque before these people were hypocrites by staying behind, because it was narrated that it was built before the Battle of Tabuk, so they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come to him, and he said: I am on the verge of a journey, and when we return, God willing, we will pray in it. So when he returned, he repeated it to him. So "and they will swear that we intended nothing but the best" was revealed. We intended by building it nothing but the best characteristic or intention, which is prayer, remembrance, and expansion for the worshippers. "And God bears witness that they are liars" in their oath.
9:108: 108. Never stand in it for prayer. For a mosque founded on piety means the Quba Mosque, which was founded by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in which he prayed during his stay in Quba from Monday to Friday because it is more in keeping with the story, or the Mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to the statement of Abu Saeed, may God be pleased with him, "I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it and he said, 'This is your mosque, this is the mosque of Medina.'" From the first day of the days of its existence and from what includes time and place, like his statement: Whose home is Qannah al-Hajar? Stronger than Hajj and Era It is more deserving that you stand in it It is more deserving that you pray in it. In it are men who love to purify themselves from sins and reprehensible traits seeking the pleasure of God, the Most High, and it was said from major ritual impurity, so they do not sleep on them. And God loves those who purify themselves He is pleased with them and brings them close to His side, the Most High, as a lover brings his beloved close. It was said that when this was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked with the Muhajireen until he stopped at the door of the Quba Mosque and saw the Ansar sitting. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you believers? They were silent. So he repeated it and Umar said: They are believers and I am with them. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you satisfied with the decree? They said: Yes. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you patient in the face of affliction? They said: Yes. He said: Are you grateful in times of ease? They said: Yes. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You are believers, by the Lord of the Kaaba. So he sat down and said: O group of Ansar, God, the Almighty, has praised you, so what do you do when performing ablution and when defecating? They said: O Messenger of God, we follow the excrement with the three stones, then we follow the stones with water. Then the Prophet recited: In it are men who love to purify themselves.
9:109: 109. Is he who founded his building the building of his religion on piety to God and good pleasure on a firm foundation, which is piety to God and seeking His pleasure through obedience, or he who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling precipice on a foundation that is the weakest and loosest of foundations, so it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell, leading him due to his weakness and lack of steadfastness to fall into the fire, and the brink of the precipice, which is what the raging valley swept away, was placed opposite to piety as a representation of what they built their religion upon in terms of invalidity and rapid obliteration, then he nominated it by its collapse with him into the fire and placed it opposite to pleasure, as a warning that the foundation of that is on a matter that protects him from the fire and leads him to the pleasure of God and its requirements, the lowest of which is Paradise, and the foundation of this is on what they are due to fall into the fire hour by hour, then their destiny is to the fire inevitably. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read founded in the passive form, and it was read foundation His building and he founded his building with the addition and foundations and foundation with the fat-ha and extension and foundations with the kasra and all three of them are the plural of as, and piety with the tanween on the basis that the alif is for attachment and not for feminization like tatra, and Ibn Amir, Hamza and Abu Bakr read jarf with the alleviation. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people to what is good for them and their success.
9:110: 110. Their building which they built will remain The building which they built is a source intended for the object and is not plural, and therefore the letter taa may enter it and it is described in the singular and it is reported about it by saying: Doubt in their hearts meaning doubt and hypocrisy, and the meaning is that their building will remain the cause of their doubt and the increase of their hypocrisy, as it led them to do that because the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, demolished it, and it became ingrained in their hearts and increased to the point that its mark will not be removed from their hearts. Unless their hearts are cut off cut off to the point that they no longer have the ability to perceive, and this is the ultimate exaggeration and exception. It is one of the most general of times. It was said that what is meant by cutting off is what happens by killing or in the grave or in the fire. It was said that cutting off is by repentance, regret and sorrow.
