10:49: 49. "Say, 'I do not possess for myself any harm or benefit.' So how can I possess any power over you and hasten to bring punishment upon you? Except what God wills.' But whatever God wills of that will happen. 'For every nation there is a term set for their destruction.' When their term comes, they will not delay it an hour, nor will they advance it.' They will not delay it or advance it, so do not hasten it, for your time will come and your promise will be fulfilled.
10:50: 50. "Say, 'Have you considered, if His punishment comes to you,' which you are hastening. 'By night', a time of sleeping and being occupied with sleeping. 'Or during the day', when you were occupied with seeking your livelihood. 'What do the criminals hasten from it?' That is, what kind of punishment do they hasten? All of it is abhorrent and does not suit hastening. It is related to 'have you considered' because it means tell me. The criminals were put in the place of the pronoun to indicate that they, due to their deprivation, should be terrified by the coming of the punishment, not hasten it. The answer to the condition is omitted, which is regret hastening, or recognize its error. It is permissible for the answer to be 'what', like your saying, 'If I come to you, what will you give me?' and the sentence is related to 'have you considered' or to His saying:
10:51: 51. Then when it comes to pass, will you believe in it? meaning that if His punishment comes to you, will you believe in it after it has happened when belief will not benefit you? What is the reason for the objection and the question letter entering then to deny the delay? Now is intended for the people, meaning it was said to them if they believed after the punishment had happened, will you believe in it now? And from Nafi': Now by deleting the hamza and placing its vowel on the lam. And you were hastening it as a denial and mockery.
10:52: 52. Then it will be said to those who did wrong, in apposition to the implied said. "Taste the eternal torment," which is painful forever. "Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn?" of disbelief and sins.
10:53: 53. And they ask you and Is it true is what you say of the promise or the claim of prophethood true, do you say it seriously or falsely, are you joking about it? Huyayy ibn Akhtab said it when he came to Mecca, and it is more apparent that the question in it is on its origin because of his saying: And they ask you and it was said that it is for denial and this is supported by the reading the truth is because it is an allusion to it being false, and more true is the subject and the pronoun is raised by it and it is used as the predicate or the predicate of a nonexistent thing and the sentence is in the accusative position they ask you. "Say: Yes, by my Lord, it is the truth" that the punishment is going to happen or what you claimed is established. It was said that both pronouns refer to the Qur'an, and Yes means Yes and it is one of the requirements of the oath and therefore it is connected with its waw in confirmation and it is said Yes, by God and it is said Yes alone. And you will not escape by escaping the punishment.
10:54: 54. "And if every soul that has wronged had all that is in the earth of its treasures and wealth, it would have ransomed itself with it, and would have made it a ransom for itself from the punishment, from their saying, 'He ransomed him,' meaning, 'He ransomed him.' And they kept their regret secret when they saw the punishment, because they were astonished by what they saw of what they had not anticipated of the horror and terror of the matter, so they were not able to speak. And it was said, 'They kept their regret secret,' they made it clear because concealing it is making it clear, or because it is said that something is secret to its special person in that it is hidden and withheld. And it was said that they made it clear, from their saying, 'He kept something secret and made it apparent,' and it will be judged between them with justice, and they will not be wronged.' This is not a repetition, because the first is a judgement between the prophets and those who denied them, and the second is the punishment of the polytheists for polytheism, or the government between the oppressors and the oppressed, and the pronoun only includes them because of the indication of injustice towards them.
10:55: 55. Indeed, to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. A confirmation of His Almighty power to reward and punish. Indeed, the promise of God is true. What He promised of reward and punishment will happen and will not be broken. But most of them do not know. Because they do not know, due to the deficiency of their minds, except the outward appearance of worldly life.
10:56: 56. He gives life and causes death in this world, so He has power over them in the Hereafter, because the One who is powerful in and of Himself does not lose His power, and matter that is capable of life and death in and of itself has them forever. And to Him you will be returned by death or resurrection.
10:57: 57. O mankind, there has come to you instruction from your Lord and a healing for what is in the hearts and guidance and mercy for the believers. That is, there has come to you a book that contains practical wisdom that reveals the good and bad aspects of deeds, encouraging good and deterring bad, and theoretical wisdom that is a healing for the doubts and bad beliefs in the hearts and guidance to the truth and certainty and mercy for the believers, as it was revealed to them and they were saved by it from the darkness of misguidance to the light of faith, and their seats from the levels of Hell were exchanged for ascents from the levels of Paradise. The indefinite article in it is for glorification.
10:58: 58. "Say: By the grace of God and by His mercy" by sending down the Qur'an, and the ba is related to a verb that is explained by His saying: So let them rejoice in that. The demonstrative pronoun is like a pronoun, its meaning is by the grace of God and by His mercy, so let them take care or let them rejoice, so let them rejoice in that. The benefit of that repetition is to emphasize and clarify after the generality and to require that grace and mercy be specific to joy or to a verb indicated by It has come to you. That is an indication of its source, meaning, by its coming, let them rejoice, and the fa has the meaning of a condition, as if it was said: If they rejoice in something in them, then let them rejoice, or to connect with what preceded it, and to indicate that the coming of the book that combines these attributes requires joy and its repetition is for emphasis, like His saying: And if you perish, then be sad On the authority of Yaqub let them rejoice with the ta’ according to the rejected original, and it has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, and it is supported by the fact that he read let them rejoice. It is better than what they collect of the debris of this world, for it is close to disappearing, and it is the pronoun for that. Ibn Amir read let them rejoice with the ta’ meaning, in that let the believers rejoice, for it is better than what you collect, O you who are being addressed.
10:59: 59. "Say, 'Have you seen what God has sent down to you of provision?' He made provision a place because it is predestined in the sky and obtained through causes including it. What is in the accusative case with "sent down or have you seen" means tell me, and it indicates that what is meant by it is what is permissible. Therefore, He rebuked the partiality and said, "So you made of it forbidden and permissible." Like: "These are livestock and crops of stone. [And when the Almighty said] What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives. Say, Has God permitted you?" in the prohibition and permissibility, so you say that by His ruling. "Or do you invent a lie against God? in attributing that to Him? It is permissible for the detailed particle to be connected to have you seen and say is repeated for emphasis and for the question to be for denial, and or" is disconnected and the meaning of the hamza in it is confirmation of their invention of God.
10:60: 60. "And what do those who invent falsehood against God think? What do they think? On the Day of Resurrection?" Do they think that they will not be punished for it? It is in the accusative case of thinking, and it is indicated by the fact that it was read in the past tense because it is happening. And in the vagueness of the threat is a great threat. "Indeed, God is full of grace to mankind," as He bestowed upon them reason and guided them by sending messengers and revealing books. "But most of them are not grateful" for this blessing.
10:61: 61. "And you are not in a matter nor are you in an affair, and its origin is the hamza from the word shanata meaning its intention, and the pronoun in and what you recite from it is for him because the recitation of the Qur'an is most of the Messenger's concern, or because the reading is for a matter, so the estimate is for its sake and the object of you recite from the Qur'an, on the basis that from is partial or additional to emphasize the negation or for the Qur'an", and its implication before the mention and then its clarification is to glorify it or for God. "And you do not do from the work" is a generalization of the address after specifying it to the one who is their leader, and for this reason it was mentioned where it specified what is in it is grandeur and mentioned where it was generalized to include the great and the insignificant. "Except that We are witnesses over you" watching over it. "When you overflow therein you plunge into it and rush. And what is hidden from your Lord" is not far from Him nor is it absent from His knowledge, and Al-Kisa'i read with a kasra on the zay here and in Saba. "From the weight of an atom" the weight of a small ant or dust. In the earth nor in the heaven meaning in existence nor possibility, for the common people do not know of anything possible other than them, neither in them nor related to them. The earth is presented first because the speech is about the state of its people and the purpose of it is to prove His comprehensive knowledge of it. And neither smaller nor greater than that except in a clear book is a statement in its own right confirming what came before it. La is a negative and smaller is its name and in a book is its predicate. Hamza and Ya’qub read the nominative case as the subject and predicate. Whoever conjoins the word the weight of an atom and makes the fat-ha instead of the kasra due to the impossibility of inflection or in its place with the preposition makes the exception disconnected. What is meant by the book is the Preserved Tablet.
10:62: 62. "Behold, the friends of God are those who obey Him and He honors them. They have no fear of any harm befalling them, nor will they grieve for the loss of what they hope for." The verse as a summary is explained by His saying:
10:63: 63. Those who believed and were fearing God. It was said, Those who believed and were fearing God, as a statement of their taking charge of it.
10:64: 64- For them is good tidings in the life of this world which is what the righteous were given good tidings of in His Book and on the tongue of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what He shows them of righteous visions and what is revealed to them, and the good tidings of the angels at the time of death. And in the Hereafter with the angels receiving them as Muslims, giving good tidings of victory and honor, a statement of His taking charge of them, and the location of those who believe is the accusative or nominative for praise or for describing the saints or for the beginning and its predicate for them is good tidings. There is no change in the words of God meaning no change in His words and no breach of His promises. That is an indication of their being given good tidings in both abodes. It is the great success This sentence and the one before it are an interruption to realize what was given good tidings and magnify its importance, and it is not a condition for it to be followed by a speech that is connected to what came before it.
10:65: 65. "And do not let their statement grieve you" their polytheism, their denial, and their threats. Nafi' read "grieves you from made him sad" and both have the same meaning. "Indeed, honor belongs to God entirely" a resumption with the meaning of explanation and the reading with the fat-ha indicates it as if it was said do not be saddened by their statement and do not care about them because victory belongs entirely to God and no one else possesses any of it so He subdues them and gives you victory over them. "He is the Hearing" of their statements. "The Knowing" of their intentions and rewards them for them.
10:66: 66. "Indeed, to God belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth" of the angels and two heavy things, and if these who are the most honorable of the possible are slaves, none of them are fit for divinity, then what is not rational from them is more deserving of not having a rival or partner for Him, so it is like the evidence for His statement: "And those whom they invoke besides God do not follow partners meaning partners in reality, even if they call them partners, and it is possible that partners is the object of they invoke and the object of follows is omitted and indicated by they follow nothing but conjecture meaning they do not follow with certainty and only follow their conjecture that they are partners, and it is possible that what is an interrogative in the accusative case with follows" or a relative in apposition to whom and they invoke is read with the second-person taa' and the meaning is: What follows those whom you invoke as partners from the angels and prophets, meaning that they do not follow except God and do not worship other than Him, so what is the matter with you that you do not follow them in it like His statement: "Those are the ones who They call upon God, seeking a means to their Lord. It is an obligation after proof, and what follows is diverted from addressing them to clarify their support and the origin of their opinion. “They are only guessing.” They lie in what they attribute to God, or they guess and estimate that they are partners, a false estimate.
10:67: 67. "It is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day to see." He made clear His perfect power and the greatness of His blessings, which He is unique in, to guide them to His uniqueness in deserving worship. He only said "seeing and did not say so that you may see" in it, to differentiate between the abstract circumstance and the circumstance that is the cause. "Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen." A listening of contemplation and consideration.
10:68: 68. They said, 'God has taken a son' meaning, He adopted him. Glory be to Him is to absolve Him from adoption, for it is not valid except from one who can imagine having a son. He was amazed at their foolish statement. He is the Rich is a reason for absolving Him, for taking a son is caused by need. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is a confirmation of His richness. Indeed, you have authority for this is a negation of the opponent of what he established from the proof, exaggerating their ignorance and confirming the invalidity of their statement, and with this is related to authority or a description of it or to with you as if it was said: You have authority for this. Do you say about God what you do not know? is a rebuke and rebuke for their differences and ignorance. It is evidence that every statement without evidence is ignorance and that beliefs must have a decisive factor and that imitation in them is not permissible.
10:69: 69. "Say: Those who invent lies about God" by taking a son and attributing a partner to Him. will not succeed they will not escape the Fire nor will they win Paradise.
10:70: 70. Enjoyment in this world is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning that they fabricated enjoyment in this world by which they establish their leadership in disbelief or their life or their change, Enjoyment is the subject whose predicate is omitted, meaning that they will have enjoyment in this world. Then to Us is their return by death, so they will encounter eternal misery. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment for what they used to disbelieve because of their disbelief.
10:71: 71. And recite to them the story of Noah his story with his people. When he said to his people, O my people, if my stay is too great for you" is too great for you and hard for me. "My presence" is like saying I did such and such for the sake of so-and-so, or my being and my residence among you for a long period or my standing up for the call. "And my reminding you of the signs of God, then upon God I have relied" I trusted. "So decide upon your affair So resolve upon it. And your partners" means with your partners. This is supported by the reading in the nominative case in apposition to the attached pronoun, and it is permissible without emphasis for the separation. It was said that it is conjoined with "your affair" by deleting the added word, meaning and the affair of your partners. It was said that it is accusative with a deleted verb, the meaning of which is "And call upon your partners" and it was read with it. According to Nafi', "So decide" is from the collection, and the meaning is their command to resolve or gather on his intention and strive to destroy him in any way they can, trusting in God and little Then let not your affair be a grief for you in my intention. A grief for you is concealed and make it apparent and exposed, from ghamahu if he concealed it or Then let not your condition be a grief for you if you destroy me and are freed from the burden of my position and my reminder. “Then decide” bring to me that matter which you want with me, and it was read Then come to me with fa meaning come to your good report or bring it out to me, from afda if he went out to judge. And do not wait and do not give me time.
10:72: 72. If you turn away you turn away from reminding me. Then I have not asked you for any reward that would require you to turn away because of its burden on you and your accusation of me because of it, or that I would miss out because of your turning away. My reward what is my reward for calling and reminding is only with God it has no connection to you with which He would reward me whether you believe or turn away. And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims those who submit to His rule, not disobeying His command and not hoping for anything other than Him.
10:73: 73. So they denied him. They persisted in denying him after he had made the proof binding upon them and made clear that their turning away was only due to their stubbornness and rebellion. Indeed, the word of punishment was justified against them. So We saved him from drowning. And those with him in the ship and they were eighty. We made you successors of those who perished by it. And We drowned those who denied Our signs with the flood. So see how was the end of those who were warned to magnify what happened to them and to warn and console those who denied the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
10:74: 74. Then We sent We sent. After him after Noah. Messengers to their people each messenger to his people. So they came to them with clear proofs with clear miracles confirming their claim. But they were not to believe it was not right for them to believe due to the severity of their stubbornness in disbelief and God's abandonment of them. Because of what they denied before meaning because of their habit of denying the truth and their training in it before sending the messengers, peace and blessings be upon them. Thus do We seal the hearts of the transgressors by abandoning them because they were immersed in misguidance and following the familiar. And in such things there is evidence that actions occur by the power of God Almighty and the gain of the servant, and the investigation of that has passed.
10:75: 75. Then We sent after them after these messengers. Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his establishment with Our signs with the nine signs. But they were arrogant from following them. And they were a criminal people habitually guilty. Therefore, they were lax about the message of their Lord and dared to reject it.
10:76: 76. So when the truth came to them from Us and they recognized it through the manifestation of dazzling miracles that removed doubt. They said out of their extreme rebellion. Indeed, this is clear magic It is clear that it is magic, or that it is superior in its art, clear among his brothers.
10:77: 77. Moses said, 'Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, It is magic?" So the reported statement was omitted because what preceded it indicated it. It is not permissible for it to be "Is this magic?" because they continued the statement, but rather it is a resumption of the denial of what they said, God willing, unless the question in it is for confirmation and the reported statement is the meaning of their statement. It is permissible for the meaning of "Do you say about the truth to be Do you criticize it for what they said, so-and-so fears the statement, like the Almighty's statement, We heard a young man mentioning them," so the object is dispensed with. And magicians will not succeed is part of Moses’ words to indicate that it is not magic, because if it were magic it would have been lost and the magic of magicians would not have been nullified, and because the one who knows that magicians will not succeed does not practice magic, or part of their saying that this magic is made a narration, as if they said, You have come to us with magic seeking success by it, and magicians will not succeed.
10:78: 78. "They said, 'Have you come to us to distract us?' To distract us, and distraction and twisting are two brothers. 'From what we found our fathers doing' of worshipping idols. 'And you two will have pride in the land.' The kingdom therein was named thus because kings are characterized by pride, or arrogance towards people by following them. 'And we are not believers in you.'
10:79: 79. And Pharaoh said, 'Bring me every magician.' Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read every magician. Knowledgeable is skilled in it.
10:80: 80. So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, 'Cast down what you are going to cast down.'
10:81: 81. So when they threw, Moses said, 'What you have brought is magic.' That is, what you have brought is magic, not what Pharaoh and his people called magic. Abu Amr read magic with what as an interrogative raised by the beginning, and you have brought it as its predicate, and magic as a substitute for it or as the predicate of a deleted subject, the meaning of which is is it magic? or as a subject whose predicate is deleted, that I am magic. It is permissible for what does to be in the accusative case, explained by what comes after it, and its meaning is what did you bring? "Indeed, God will invalidate it." He will destroy it or will reveal its invalidity. "Indeed, God does not amend the work of corrupters." He does not establish it or strengthen it, and in it is evidence that magic is corruption and deception and has no reality.
10:82: 82. And God establishes the truth and confirms it. With His words with His commands and His judgments. It was read with His word. Even if the criminals hate that.
10:83: 83. None believed in Moses that is, at the beginning of his command. Except the offspring of his people except the children of his people, the Children of Israel. He called them, but they did not answer him for fear of Pharaoh, except a group of their young men. It was said that the pronoun refers to Pharaoh and the offspring refers to a group of their young men who believed in him, or the believer of Pharaoh's family and his wife Asiya and the treasurer and his wife and his hairdresser for fear of Pharaoh and their chiefs that is, with fear of them. The pronoun refers to Pharaoh and its plural is as is customary in the pronoun of great people, or that what is meant by Pharaoh is his people, as is said: Rabi'ah and Mudar, or for the offspring or the people. That he might tempt them that Pharaoh might torment them, and it is a substitute for it or the object of fear, and its singular use of the pronoun is to indicate that the fear of the chiefs was due to him. And Pharaoh was indeed arrogant in the land. “And indeed, he was among the transgressors” in his arrogance and insolence until he claimed divinity and enslaved the tribes of the prophets.
10:84: 84. "And Moses said, when he saw the fear of the believers in him, O my people, if you have believed in God, then rely on Him." So trust in Him and rely on Him. "If you are Muslims," submitting to God's decree and being sincere to Him. This is not from suspending the ruling on two conditions, for what is suspended on faith is the obligation of reliance, for it is what requires it, and what is conditioned on Islam is its occurrence, for it does not exist with confusion. Its equivalent is if Zaid calls you, then answer him if you are able.
10:85: 85. "They said, 'In God we trust.'" Because they were sincere believers, and therefore their prayer was answered. "Our Lord, do not make us a trial." A place of trial. "For the wrongdoing people." That is, do not give them power over it so that they tempt us.
10:86: 86. "And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people" from their plot and from the evil of witnessing them. In presenting trust before supplication, there is an indication that the supplicant should first trust in You so that his supplication will be answered.
10:87: 87. "And We inspired Moses and his brother, saying, 'Take for your people in Egypt houses,' in which you may dwell or to which you may return for worship. 'And make, you and your people, your houses,' those houses, 'a place of prayer,' and it was said, mosques facing the qiblah, meaning the Kaaba, and Moses, peace be upon him, used to pray towards it. 'And establish prayer,' they were commanded to do this at the beginning of their affair lest the disbelievers should prevail over them and harm them and tempt them away from their religion. 'And give good tidings to the believers,' with victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. The pronoun was dual at first because taking up residence for the people and making temples is something that the leaders of the people do in consultation, then it was pluralized because making houses into mosques and praying in them is something that everyone should do, then it was singularized because the glad tidings are originally the function of the one who has the law.
10:88: 88. And Moses said, 'Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment' what he adorns himself with of clothing, mounts, and the like. And wealth in the life of this world and various kinds of wealth. Our Lord, that they may go astray from Your way a supplication against them in the form of a command with what is known from their practice that it cannot be as if it were like your saying: May God curse Satan. It was said that the lam is for the consequence and it is related to you have given and it is possible that it is for the reason because giving blessings for disbelief is a lure and confirmation of misguidance, and because when they made them a reason for misguidance, it was as if they were given them so that they would go astray, so our Lord is a repetition of the first, emphasizing and alerting that the intended meaning is to expose their misguidance and disbelief in advance of His saying: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth meaning destroy it, and obliteration is the realization. It was read atmṣwith the dammah. And harden their hearts meaning and make them hard on them so that they do not open up to faith. "So they do not believe. Until they see the painful torment. This is an answer to the supplication, or a supplication with the wording of prohibition, or in apposition to so that they may go astray. What is between them is an intervening supplication.
10:89: 89. "He said, 'Your prayer has been answered,' meaning Moses and Aaron because he believed. 'So be steadfast,' so remain steadfast in what you are upon of the call and the obligation of the proof, and do not be hasty, for what you have asked for will happen, but in its time. It was narrated that he remained among them for forty years after the call. 'And do not follow the way of those who do not know,' the way of the ignorant in hastening or not trusting and being reassured in the promise of God Almighty. And from Ibn Amir, with the narration of Ibn Dhakwan, 'And do not follow,' with the light noon, broken because of the meeting of the two quiescent letters, 'and do not follow,' from 'and do not follow,' also.
10:90: 90. And We took the Children of Israel across the sea meaning, We made them cross the sea until they reached the shore, protecting them. It was read We crossed and it is from the verb synonymous with the active participle like weakened and added up. "So he followed them" so he caught up with them. It is said, "I followed him until I followed him. Pharaoh and his soldiers, in oppression and enmity" in oppression and enmity, or for oppression and enmity. It was read "and they were attacked. Until, when drowning overtook him" it caught up with him. "He said, I believe that" meaning that. "There is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read that with a kasra on the implication of the statement or resumption instead and explanation of I believed" so he turned away from belief at the time of acceptance and exaggerated in it when it is not accepted.
10:91: 91. Now do you believe now that you have despaired of yourself and you have no choice left. And you disobeyed before before that for the duration of your life. And you were among the corrupters the misguided and those who lead astray from the faith.
10:92: 92. So today We will save you We will rescue you from what your people have fallen into, from the bottom of the sea and make you float, or We will cast you on a place of safety on the land so that the Children of Israel can see you. And Jacob read We will save you from Anja, and he read Nahhik with a ha meaning We will cast you on a side of the shore. With your body in the place of the state meaning with your body stripped of the soul, or complete and sound or naked without clothing. Or with your armor, and he had a gold armor by which he was known. And it was read with your bodies meaning with all parts of the body like their saying he fell with his crime or with your armor as if he was a manifestation between them. So that you may be a sign to those who come after you for those who come after you a sign and they are the children of Israel because there was in their souls from his greatness what they imagined that he would not perish, until they denied Moses, peace be upon him, when he told them of his drowning until they saw him thrown out from their passage on the coast, or for those who come after you from the generations if they hear the outcome of your matter from those who saw you as a lesson and a punishment for tyranny, or an argument that shows them that man, despite what he was in of great status and the pride of the king, is a subjugated slave far from the places of Lordship. And it was read for those who created you meaning for your Creator a sign, meaning like all the signs, for His singling you out by throwing you to the coast is evidence that he intended to expose your forgery and remove the doubt in your matter. And that is evidence of the perfection of His power, knowledge and will, and this aspect is also possible according to the famous. And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs they do not think about them nor They consider it. Introduction by the director of al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. In the online form of this book, it makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 13 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the end of Sūrat l-Ḥij'r, all of Sūrat l-Naḥl, and the first hundred verses of Sūrat l-Isrā. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. Portions of this work have been translated using AI (machine-assisted translation) and post-edited for clarity and accuracy. "Indeed, He is the Hearer of the prayer of those who seek refuge in God, the Knower" of their conditions and what is good for them.

The ruling is what is the ruling in the matter of worship. Except for God because He is the One who deserves it intrinsically, in that He is the One Who is obligated to Himself, the Creator of everything and the Owner of His command. Then it was stated what is the upright truth and the straight religion that reason does not require anything other than it and knowledge does not accept anything less than it. But most people do not know so they stumble in their ignorance.

The vision is expressed in a more authentic expression than its expression, and the lam is for clarification or to strengthen the agent, because the verb is weak when it is delayed from its object, so it is strengthened by the lam like the active participle, or to include you interpret the meaning of a verb that is transitive with the lam, as if it were said: If you are volunteering to interpret the vision.
12:44: 44. They said, 'Confused dreams' meaning these are confused dreams and their mixtures, the plural of 'daghth', which originally means what is collected from plant mixtures and bundles, so it was used as a metaphor for a false vision. And we are not knowledgeable about the interpretation of dreams they mean by dreams false dreams in particular, meaning they have no interpretation for us, but rather the interpretation is for true dreams, so it is as if it is a second introduction to the excuse, so they are ignorant of its interpretation.

12:50: 50.:"And the king said, 'Bring him to me.' 12:53: 53. 12:73: 73. They said, 'By God,' is a section that contains the meaning of astonishment, the ta' instead of the ba', specific to the name of God Almighty: You have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land, nor were we thieves. They cited their knowledge as evidence of their innocence, as they knew of their two occasions of coming and intervening with the king, which indicates their extreme trustworthiness, such as returning the merchandise that had entered their baggage and covering the animals so that they would not eat anyone's crops or food.
12:74: 74. They said, 'What is his punishment?' So what is the punishment for the thief, or the theft, or the sa'a with the omission of the added word, if you are lying in claiming innocence.
12:75: 75. They said, 'His punishment is whoever is found in his saddlebags, that is his punishment.' That is, the punishment for his theft is to seize whoever is found in his saddlebags and enslave him. This was the law of Jacob, peace be upon him. His saying, that is his punishment is a confirmation of the ruling and an obligation for it, or the predicate of whoever and the fa because it includes the meaning of a condition or an answer to it because it is a condition. The sentence, as it is, is the predicate of his punishment by establishing the apparent in it in place of the pronoun, as if it were said: His punishment is whoever is found in his saddlebags, that is him. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers for theft.
12:76: 76. So he began with their vessels. So the muezzin began. And it was said Joseph because they were returned to Egypt. He kissed his brother's vessel Benjamin to deny the accusation. Then he extracted it meaning the watering can or the measuring cup because it is masculine and feminine. From his brother's vessel and it was read with a dammah on the waw and by changing it to a hamza. Likewise is like that plot. We plotted against Joseph by teaching it to him and revealing it to him. It was not for him to seize his brother by the king's religion the king of Egypt because his religion was beating and a fine double what he took without enslavement, which is an explanation of the plot. Except that God wills that he made that ruling the ruling of the king, so the exception is from the most general of conditions and it is possible that it is discontinuous, meaning but he took him by the will of God Almighty and His permission. We raise by degrees whom We will by knowledge as We raised his degree. And above every possessor of knowledge is the All-Knower higher in degree than him, and it was used as evidence by those who claimed that God Almighty is knowledgeable of Himself because if He had knowledge then there would be above Him someone more knowledgeable than Him. The answer is that what is meant is every possessor of knowledge from among creation because the speech is about them and because the All-Knower is God Almighty, and its meaning is the one who has comprehensive knowledge linguistically and because there is no difference between it and our saying above all scholars is the All-Knower and it is specific.
12:77: 77. They said that if Benjamin steals, his brother had stolen before meaning Joseph. It was said that his aunt inherited from her father the belt of Abraham, peace be upon him, and she used to embrace Joseph and love him. When he grew up, Jacob wanted to take him away from her, so she tied the belt around his waist. Then she revealed her estate, so he examined it and found it tied to him, so she became more entitled to him in their judgment. It was said that his mother's father had an idol, so he stole it, broke it, and threw it in the carcasses. It was said that there was a goat or a chicken in the house, so he gave it to the beggar. It was said that he entered a church and took a small statue of gold. And Joseph kept it secret within himself and did not reveal it to them. He kept it secret and did not reveal it to them. The pronoun is for the answer or the statement or attributing the theft to him. It was said that it is a metaphor with the condition of interpretation, and it is explained by his saying: He said, 'You are in the worst place.' It is a substitute for he kept it secret. The meaning is that he said to himself, You are the worst in consideration of the word or the sentence, and there is a consideration in this, since the interpreter of the sentence can only be the pronoun of the matter. And God is most knowing of what you describe. And He knows that the matter is not as you describe. Introduction by the director of al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. In the online form of this book, it makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 14 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the end of Sūrat l-Isrā, all of Sūrat l-Kahf, Sūrat Maryam and the first verses of Sūrat Ṭā Hā. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 12:78: 78. "They said, 'O Aziz, indeed he has an old father,' meaning in age or status. They mentioned his condition to him in order to pity him. 'Take one of us in his place,' for his father has been bereaved of his deceased brother and he will find comfort in him. 12:79: 79. "He said, 'God forbid that we should take anything except from the one with whom we found our goods.'" If someone else took it, it would be unjust according to your fatwa, so why don't we take one of you in his place. "Indeed, then we would be unjust," according to your doctrine. What he meant is that God permitted us to take from the one with whom we found the sa' in his saddlebag for his benefit and His pleasure with him, so if you took someone else, you would be unjust.
12:80: 80. When they despaired of him they despaired of Joseph and his answer to them, and the addition of the age and the taa is for emphasis. They were separated and isolated. "Did you not know that your father took a firm covenant from you from God" a firm covenant, and he made their oath by God firm from him because with his permission and confirmation from him. "And before And before this. What you neglected in Joseph you fell short in his matter, and what" is an addition and it is permissible for it to be a source in the place of the accusative in conjunction with the object of you learned, and there is no problem in separating the conjunction and the conjoined by the circumstance, or on the name of "that and its predicate in Joseph or from before or raising by the beginning and the predicate from before and there is a consideration in it, because before" if it is a predicate or a connection, it is not cut off from the addition so that it does not decrease and that it is connected, meaning: what you neglected in the meaning of what you presented in his right of the crime and its place What was mentioned above. I will not leave the land “I will not leave the land of Egypt.” Until my father gives me permission “to return.” Or God rules for me “Or He decrees for me to leave it, or for my brother to be freed from them or for me to fight with them to free him.” It was narrated that they spoke to Al-Aziz about releasing him, so Reuben said: O king, by God, you must leave us alone or I will cry out a cry that will cause pregnant women to give birth. 12:81: 81. Go back to your father and say, 'O our father, your son has stolen,' based on what we have seen from the apparent meaning of the matter. 12:83: 83. "He said, 'Rather, it has been suggested to me.' That is, when they returned to their father and said to him what their brother had said to them, he said, Rather, it has been suggested to me." That is, it has been made attractive and easy. 12:84: 84."And he turned away from them and turned away from them, disliking what he had encountered from them. And he said, Oh, my grief over Joseph meaning, Oh, my grief, come, for this is your time. And grief is the most intense sorrow and regret, and the alif is a substitute for the ya of the speaker, and he only felt sorry for Joseph and not for his two brothers and the incident of their calamity because his calamity was the norm for calamities and he was young and took hold of the recesses of his heart, and because he was confident in their lives but not his own. In the hadith: No nation was given Indeed, to God we belong and to Him we shall return" at the time of calamity except the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace." Do you not see when what befell Jacob, may God bless him and grant him peace, be upon him, befallen him, he did not seek refuge and said, Oh, my grief and his eyes turned white from grief" because of his frequent crying from grief as if the tear had erased their blackness. And it was said that his eyesight weakened. It was said: My uncle, and it was read: from sadness, and in it is evidence of the permissibility of regret and crying when grieving, and perhaps such things do not fall under the obligation, for few control themselves during hardships. Indeed, “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cried over his son Ibrahim and said: ‘The heart grieves and the eye weeps, and we do not say what angers the Lord, and indeed, O Ibrahim, we are grieved over you. ’” So he is kazeem, filled with anger towards his children, holding it in his heart and not showing it.
