Of the report of the unseen which We reveal to you are two pieces of report for him, And you were not with them when they decided on their plan and they were plotting as evidence for them, and the meaning is: This report is unseen and you did not know it except through revelation because you were not present with Joseph's brothers when they decided to do what they intended to do, which was to put him in the bottom of the well, and they were plotting against him and his father to send him with them. And it is known and not hidden from those who deny you that you did not meet anyone who heard that and learned it from him, and this part was only omitted because it was sufficient to mention it in a story other than this, like His saying: You did not know it, you or your people, before this.
12:103: 103. And most people, even if you were keen on their belief and exaggerated in showing them signs would not be believers because of their stubbornness and determination to disbelieve.
12:104: 104. And what you ask them about about the report or the Qur’an. Of reward from whoever makes as the bearers of report do. It is only a reminder an admonition from God Almighty for the worlds in general.
12:105: 105. And how many a sign And how many a sign. The meaning is, and as many as you want of the evidence indicating the existence of the Creator and His wisdom and as for His power and His oneness. In the heavens and the earth they pass over them over the signs and witness them. And they turn away from them they do not think about them nor consider them. And the earth was read in the nominative case as a subject whose predicate is they pass, so the pronoun in over it is for it, and in the accusative case on they tread the earth. And it was read, And the earth they walk over meaning they frequent it and see the traces of the perished nations.
12:106: 106. "And most of them do not believe in God" in their acknowledgement of His existence and His creation. "Except that they associate others with Him" by worshipping other than Him or taking the rabbis as lords. And attributing adoption to Him, the Most High, or saying about light and darkness or looking at causes and the like. It was said that the verse was about the polytheists of Mecca, and it was said about the hypocrites, and it was said about the People of the Book.
12:107: 107. Do they then feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from God a punishment that will overwhelm them and encompass them. Or that the Hour will come upon them suddenly suddenly without any previous sign. And they perceive not its coming, not being prepared for it.
12:108: 108. Say, 'This is my way.' This means calling to monotheism and preparing for the afterlife. Therefore, the way was explained by saying, I call to God. It was said that it is a state of the ya'. On insight is a clear and not blind statement and argument. I is an emphasis on what is hidden in call or on insight because it is a state of it or a subject whose predicate is on insight. "And whoever follows me" is conjoined with it. "And glory be to God, and I am not of the polytheists." And I declare Him to be completely free from partners.
12:109: 109. And We did not send before you except men is a response to their saying If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels. It was said that its meaning is the denial of the women's request We reveal to them as He reveals to you and they are distinguished by that from others. Hafsun and Nuhayr read throughout the Qur'an and Hamza and Al-Kisa'i agreed with him in Surat Al-Anbiya. From the people of the towns because its people are more knowledgeable and patient than the people of the desert. Have they not traveled through the land and seen what was the end of those before them of those who denied the messengers and the signs so they would beware of denying you, or of those who are preoccupied with the world and are infatuated with it so they give up their love for it. And the home of the Hereafter and the home of the present or the hour or the life of the Hereafter. is better for those who fear polytheism and sins. Do you not understand? They use their minds to know that it is good. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, ‘Asim, and Ya’qub read with the letter ta’ based on his statement: Say, ‘This is my way’, meaning say to them, Do you not understand?
12:110: 110. Until the messengers despaired is an omitted goal indicated by the speech, meaning that the passing of their days should not deceive them, for those before them were given respite until the messengers despaired of victory over them in this world, or of their belief because they were immersed in disbelief, indulgent and persistent in it without restraint. And they thought that they had been denied meaning that they had lied to themselves when they told them that they would be victorious, or the people had lied to them about the promise of belief. It was said that the pronoun refers to those to whom it was sent, meaning that the ones to whom it was sent thought that the messengers had lied to them about the call and the threat. It was said that the first refers to those to whom it was sent and the second refers to the messengers, or that they thought that the messengers had lied and failed to fulfill what God had promised them of victory and had confused the matter for them. What was narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the messengers thought that they had failed to fulfill what God had promised them of victory, if it is true, then what he meant by suspicion is what comes to mind through whispers. This is what is meant by it is exaggeration in the delay and respite by way of example. Other than the Kufians, they read it with emphasis, meaning that the messengers thought that the people had lied to them in what they promised them. It was read they lied with emphasis and the active participle, meaning that they thought that they had lied in what they told their people when he delayed it from them and they did not see any trace of it. Our victory came to them, so We saved whom We willed the Prophet and the believers. He did not specify them to indicate that they are the ones who deserve that He will their salvation, and no one else shares it with them. And he read Ibn Amir, Asim and Yaqub on the past tense passive voice and it was read as Fanaja “And Our punishment is not repelled from the criminal people” if it befalls them and it contains a clarification of the two wills.
12:111: 111. There was in their stories in the stories of the prophets and their nations or in the story of Joseph and his brothers a lesson for those of understanding for those with minds - free from the impurities of familiarity and reliance on the senses. It was not a fabricated story the Qur'an was not a fabricated story. But the confirmation of what was before it of the divine books. And the details of everything needed in religion, since there is no religious matter except that it has a support from the Qur'an with or without a middle way. And guidance from misguidance. And mercy by which he attains the best of both worlds. For a people who believe who believe in him. "And from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, teach your slaves Surat Yusuf, for any Muslim who recites it and teaches it to his family and those his right hand possesses, God will make the throes of death easy for him and give him the strength not to envy a Muslim."
13:1: It was said that it was revealed in Mecca, except for His saying: And those who disbelieve say... the verse, which is forty-three verses. In the name of God, the most gracious, the most merciful 1. Al-Mar is said to mean: God knows best and sees. "Those are the verses of the Book means the Surah by the Book, and those" refers to its verses, i.e.: those verses are the verses of the complete Surah or the Qur'an. "And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the entire Qur'an, and its place is in the accusative case by conjunction with the Book by conjunction of the general with the specific or one of the two attributes with the other or by raising with the beginning or its predicate with the truth" and the sentence is like the argument for the first sentence, and the definition of the predicate, even if it indicates that the revealed is specific to being true, it is more general than the revealed explicitly or implicitly, like that which is established by analogy and other things that the revealed has spoken of as good to follow. "But most people do not believe" because of their failure to consider and reflect on it.
13:2: 2. God is He Who raised the heavens is the subject and predicate. It is possible that the relative pronoun is an adjective and the predicate manages the affair. "Without pillars" is pillars, plural of pillar, like hide and ahab, or a column, like adimm and adam. It was read "pillars" like rusul. "You see them is an adjective for pillars" or a resumption of the evidence of their seeing the heavens likewise, and it is evidence of the existence of the wise Creator, for their elevation over all the other celestial bodies has in reality the physicality, and their being distinguished by what requires that must be by a specifier that is not a body or physical that gives preference to some possibilities over others by His will. And on this path are all the other verses mentioned. "Then He established Himself on the Throne" with preservation and management. "And He subjected the sun and the moon" He made them subject to what He wanted from them, like the continuous movement at a certain speed that benefits the occurrence and survival of beings. "Everything runs for a specified term for a specific period in which its roles are completed, or a set goal before which the course of action is cut off, which is When the sun is wrapped up and when the stars are extinguished. He directs the affair" the affair of His kingdom of creation and destruction, life and death, and other things. "He details the signs" He sends them down and explains them in detail or creates the evidence one after the other. "Perhaps you will be certain of the meeting with your Lord" so that you may reflect on them and realize the perfection of His power and learn that He who was able to create these things and direct them was able to restore and reward.
13:3: 3. And it is He who spread out the earth He spread it out in length and breadth so that feet could stand firm on it and animals could turn around on it. And He placed therein firm mountains fixed mountains from rasa if something is firm, plural of rasiya and the taa is for the feminine as an adjective of ajbal or for exaggeration. And rivers He included it with the mountains and connected them to one action in terms of the mountains being the causes of its generation. And of all fruits is related to His statement: He placed therein two mates meaning and He placed therein from all types of fruits two kinds like sweet and sour, black and white, small and large. The night covers the day He covers it in its place so the atmosphere becomes dark after it had been bright. Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read yaghshy with emphasis. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect on it, for its formation and its specialization in one way rather than another is evidence of the existence of a wise Creator who managed its affair and prepared its causes.
13:4: 4. And in the earth are neighboring tracts some of which are good and some of which are salt marsh, some of which are soft and some of which are hard, some of which are suitable for planting but not for trees and some of which are the opposite. And had it not been for the Almighty's designation of a place for His actions in a way but not in a way, it would not have been so, because those tracts share in the earthly nature and what is necessary for it and are presented to it by means of what is presented of heavenly causes, in that they are intertwined and share in proportion and situations. And gardens of grapevines and crops and palm trees and orchards in which are all kinds of trees and crops, and the unification of crops because it is a source in its origin. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Yaqub, and Hafs read and crops and palm trees in the nominative case in apposition to gardens. In pairs are palm trees of one origin. And not in pairs are scattered and of different origins. Hafs read it with the dammah, which is the language of Banu Tamim, like qanawan in the plural of qanw. They are watered with one water, and We prefer some of them over others in eating in dates in shape, quantity, smell and taste. This is also what indicates the wise Creator, for their difference with the unity of origins and causes is not referred to except by the specification of the able and choosing. Ibn Amir, Asim and Yaqub read yasqa in the masculine form based on the interpretation of what was mentioned, and Hamza and Al-Kisa’i with the addition of the ya’ to match his saying He directs the matter “Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason” who use their minds to think.
13:5: 5. "And if you are amazed" O Muhammad, at their denial of the resurrection. "The amazement of their statement" is worthy of amazement, for whoever is able to create what He has narrated to you, then the easiest thing for him is to repeat it. The enumerated verses, as they indicate the existence of the beginning, indicate the possibility of the return in that they indicate the perfection of His knowledge and power and the acceptance of materials for the types of His actions. "If we are dust, will we then be in a new creation? is a substitute for their statement or an object for it, and the factor in if" is omitted and indicated by: "Will we then be in a new creation? Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord" because they disbelieved in His ability to resurrect. "And those are the shackles on their necks" bound by misguidance, with no hope of their release or being chained on the Day of Resurrection. "And those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein" they will never be separated from it, and the middle of the separation is to specify eternity for the disbelievers.
13:6: 6. "And they hasten you with the evil before the good" with the punishment before the well-being, and that is because they hastened the worldly punishment they were threatened with in mockery. "And before them there have been examples" punishments for their likes from the deniers, so why did they not take heed of them and not allow the like of them to befall them? The example with the opening of the thaa and its closing is like charity and charity, and the punishment because it is like the one being punished, and from it the example for retaliation and you took revenge on the man from his companion if you took revenge on him. And "al-Mithalāt was read with a lightened al-Mithalāt and al-Mithalāt following the fa with the ayn and al-Mithalāt with a lightened al-Mithalāt after following, and al-Mithalāt with a fathah on the tha as it is the plural of Mithalāt like Rukbah and Rukbāt. And indeed, your Lord is the possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing" with their wrongdoing of themselves, and its place is the accusative case as a state and the agent in it is forgiveness and the restriction to it is evidence of the permissibility of forgiveness before repentance, for the repentant is not on his wrongdoing, and whoever prevents that restricted wrongdoing to the minor sins that are expiated for the one who avoids the major sins, or the beginning of forgiveness by concealment and respite. "And indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty" for the disbelievers or for whomever He wills, and from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "If it were not for God's forgiveness and pardon, no one would enjoy life, and if it were not for His threat and punishment, not everyone would be tired."
13:7: 7. And those who disbelieve say, 'Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?' due to their lack of regard for the signs sent down to him and their suggestion of something similar to what was given to Moses and Jesus, peace be upon them. You are only a warner sent to warn like other messengers, and all you have to do is bring what confirms your prophethood from the type of miracles, not what is suggested to you. And for every people there is a guide a prophet specifically with miracles from the type that is prevalent among them, who guides them to the truth and calls them to what is right, or is able to guide them, and He is God Almighty, but He does not guide except whom He wills to guide by what He sends down to you of signs. Then He followed that with what indicates the perfection of His knowledge and power and the comprehensiveness of His judgment and decree, drawing attention to the fact that He Almighty is able to send down what they suggested, but He did not send down because He knew that their suggestion was out of stubbornness rather than seeking guidance, and that He is able to guide them, but He did not guide them because of His previous judgment of disbelief, so He said:
13:8: 8. God knows what every female carries meaning her pregnancy or what she carries in any case is from the present and anticipated conditions. And what the wombs decrease and what they increase and what they decrease and what they increase in Paradise and the duration and number, and the maximum duration of pregnancy is four years according to us and five according to Malik and two years according to Abu Hanifa. Ad-Dahhak narrated that Harim bin Hayyan was born at the age of two years and his maximum number is unlimited. It was said that the end of what is known is four and Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, went to him, and Ash-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, said that a sheikh in Yemen informed me that his wife gave birth to wombs in each womb five. It was said that what is meant is the decrease and increase of menstrual blood, and Ghadah came transitive and intransitive, and so did increase. God the Almighty said: And they increased by nine If you make them intransitive, it is necessary that they be either a source. And their attribution to the wombs is metaphorical, for they belong to God Almighty and are not in them. And everything with Him is in measure in a measure that does not exceed it or fall short of it, like His Almighty saying: Indeed, all things We created in measure. For God Almighty has specified every event with a specific time and condition, and has prepared for it causes that are delayed to it and require that. Ibn Kathir read Haad, “Wa-l,” and Wa-q, and Ma-ma-id-Lah-baaq with the tanween in the connection, so if he stops, he stops with the ya’ in these four letters wherever they occur and nothing else, and the rest connect and stop without the ya’.
13:9: 9. The Knower of the Unseen is absent from the senses and the witnessed. The Great is the One of great status from whose work nothing is excluded. The Most High is the One who is above everything by His power, or the One who is greater than the description of created beings and is exalted above them.
13:10: 10. "Whether among you is he who keeps his words secret to himself, and he who declares them to someone else, and he who is hidden at night seeking concealment in hiding at night, and a stealer who appears during the day, everyone sees him from a stealth if he appears, and it is in apposition to who or hidden on the basis that who is in the meaning of both, like his saying: We are like two wolves who accompany each other He said, The two of you are the same, one who hides by night and one who travels by day. The verse is connected to what preceded it, confirming the perfection and comprehensiveness of His knowledge.
13:11: 11. "For him" for whoever confides or speaks openly or hides or sneaks away. "Mu'aqabat are angels who follow him in his protection, the plural of mu'aqaba from aqaba as an exaggeration of aqaba if he comes after him as if some of them follow others, or because they follow his sayings and actions and write them down, or 'ataqab so the ta' was assimilated into the qaf and the ta' for exaggeration, or because what is meant by mu'aqabat is groups, and it was read mu'aqib as the plural of mu'aqabat or mu'aqabat" as a compensation for the ya' for deleting one of the two qafs. "From before him and behind him" from his sides or from the deeds that he presented and delayed. "They protect him from the command of God" from His wrath whenever he sins by asking for forgiveness or seeking forgiveness for him, or they protect him from harm or they monitor his conditions for the sake of the command of God Almighty. It was read with it and it was said that "min means ba". It was said that "min amr God is a second description of mu'aqabat". It was said that the guards and henchmen around the sultan protect him from the decree of God Almighty. God does not change the condition of a people of health and blessings until they change what is in themselves of beautiful conditions with ugly conditions and if God intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it so there is no repelling it, so the factor in if is what the answer indicates. And they have no protector besides Him of those who oversee their affairs and repel evil from them, and in it is evidence that going against the will of God Almighty is impossible.
13:12: 12. It is He who shows you lightning, for fear of its harm and for hope of rain. The two are in the accusative case with the estimation of the added word, meaning the will of fear and hope, or the interpretation of frightening and hope, or the state of lightning or the addressees with the omission of the possessor, or the use of the source in the sense of the subject or the agent for emphasis. It was said that the one who harms him fears the rain and the one who benefits him hopes for it. And He creates the clouds the clouds withdrawing into the air. The heavy ones is the plural of heavy, and it was only used to describe the clouds because it is a generic name in the sense of the plural.
13:13: 13. And the thunder glorifies and its listeners glorify. With His praise entwined with it, so they clamor with Glory be to God and Praise be to God, or the thunder itself indicates the oneness of God and the perfection of His power entwined with it by indicating His grace and the descent of His mercy. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about thunder, so he said: An angel is assigned to the clouds, with him are whips of fire with which he drives the clouds." And the angels, out of fear of Him out of fear of God Almighty and His reverence, and it was said that the pronoun refers to thunder. "And He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whomever He wills" and destroys him. "And they dispute about God" as they belie the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he describes of His perfect power and power and uniqueness in divinity and the return of people and their reward, and the dispute is the severity in the dispute from the argument which is the killing, and the waw is either to connect the sentence to the sentence or for the state, as it was "It was narrated that Amer bin Al-Tufayl and Arbad bin Rabi'ah The brother of Labid came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) with the intention of killing him. Aamer seized him by arguing and Arbad went around behind him to strike him with the sword. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) noticed him and said: O God, protect me from them however You wish. So God sent a thunderbolt on Arbad and killed him. Aamer was struck by a thorn and he died in the house of Saluliyah. He used to say: A thorn like a camel’s thorn and death in the house of Saluliyah. So the following was revealed: And He is severe in His plot. The plot is the plotting of one’s enemies, from mahal to plot someone with someone if he plotted against him and exposed him to death. From this comes tamahal to use a trick, and perhaps its origin is mahal to plot meaning drought. It was also said that fa’al is from mahal to use a trick meaning strength. It was also said that muf’al is from hawl to plot or haylah to plot which is not analogous to analogy. This is supported by the fact that it is read with the opening of the m as if it is muf’al from hal yahwul to plot, and it is possible that it means faqar drought, and it is an example of strength and ability, like their saying: So God helped more strongly and Moses was more severe.
13:14: 14. His is the true call The true call, for He is the One who deserves to be worshipped and called to His worship, and no one else, or His is the answered call, for whoever calls upon Him, He answers him, and what comes after it supports it. And the truth in both aspects is what contradicts falsehood and the addition of the call to it because of the connection between them, or according to the interpretation of the call of the true one called. It was said that the truth is God Almighty and every supplication to Him is a supplication to the truth. What is meant by the two sentences, if the verse is about Arbad and Amer, is that their destruction from where they did not feel it is impossible from God in response to the supplication of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or an indication that he is on the truth. If it is general, then what is meant is a threat to the infidels for arguing with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that His impossibility will come upon them and a threat to them that the supplication of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, against them will be answered, or a statement of their misguidance and the corruption of their opinion. And those whom they invoke means the idols whom the polytheists invoke, so the referent was omitted, or and the polytheists who invoke the idols so the object was omitted because besides Him indicates it. They do not respond to them with anything of the requests. Except as one who extends his hands except as a response like the response of one who extends his hands. To the water to reach his mouth He asks him to reach it. And it will not reach it because it is inanimate and does not feel his call nor is it able to answer him and come with something other than what it was created for, and so are their gods. And it was said that they likened in the little benefit of their call to them to someone who wanted to scoop up water to drink it so he extended his hands to drink it. And it was read you call with a taa and baset with a tanween. And the call of the disbelievers is only in error in loss, loss and falsehood.
13:15: 15. And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion. It is possible that prostration is in its true sense, for the angels and the believers of the two heavy burdens prostrate to Him, willingly in times of hardship and ease, and the disbelievers by compulsion in times of hardship and necessity. And their shadows by accident, and that He intends by it their submission to bring about what He wills from them, whether they will or not, and the submission of their shadows to His diversion of them by extension and contraction, and the erection of willingly and by compulsion by state or reason, and His saying: in the morning and the evenings is an adverb for prostrates, and what is meant by them is permanence or a state of the shadows, specifying the two times because the shadows are only great and numerous in them, and the morning is the plural of the morning like qana is the plural of qana, and the evenings is the plural of aseel, which is what is between the afternoon and the sunset. It was said that the enemy is a source, and this is supported by the fact that it was read and the connection which is entering the evening.
13:16: 16. "Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" Their Creator and the One in charge of their affairs. "Say: God." Answer them with that, since they have no answer other than Him, and because it is the clear thing that cannot be disputed about, or He taught them the answer with it. "Say: Have you taken besides Him?" Then He obligated them with that because taking them is an evil and far from the requirements of reason. Allies who possess neither benefit nor harm for themselves. They are not able to bring benefit to themselves or ward off harm from them, so how can they benefit others and ward off harm from them? This is a second proof of their misguidance and the corruption of their opinion in taking them as allies in the hope that they will intercede for them. "Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?" The polytheist who is ignorant of the reality of worship and the one who requires it, and the monotheist who knows that. It was said that the worshipped One is heedless of you and the worshipped One is aware of your conditions. Or are darkness and light equal? Polytheism and monotheism. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and Abu Bakr read with the letter yaa. “Or have they made partners for God?” Rather, make and the hamzah is for denial. His statement, created like His creation is an attribute of partners that falls under the ruling of denial. So the creation became similar to them means God’s creation and their creation, and the meaning is that they did not take partners for God who were creators like Him so that the creation would become similar to them and they would say, These were created as God created, so they deserved worship as He deserved it. But they took partners who were helpless and were not able to do what the creation is able to do, let alone what the Creator is able to do. Say, ‘God is the Creator of all things.’ That is, there is no creator other than Him so that He can be associated with worship. He made creation the wave of worship and the necessary reason for deserving it, then He denied it from anyone other than Him to indicate His statement, And He is the One the One in divinity. The Subduer the Victorious over all things.
13:17: 17. "He sent down water from the sky" from the clouds or from the side of the sky or from the sky itself, for the beginnings are from it. "And valleys flowed" rivers, plural of valley, which is the place where water flows abundantly and expands in it, and it is used for running water in it and its indefiniteness because the rain comes alternately between places. "According to its amount" according to its amount that God Almighty knew would be beneficial and not harmful or according to its amount in smallness and largeness. "So the torrent carried foam" He raised it, and foam and boiling harm. "Mounting" high. "And from what they kindle in the fire" includes metals such as gold, silver, iron and copper in a manner of belittling them, showing his pride. "Seeking adornment" meaning seeking adornments. "Or goods" such as utensils and tools of war and farming, and the purpose of that is to explain their benefits. Foam like it meaning, and from what they kindle is foam like the foam of water, which is its impurity, and from is for the beginning or for the part, and Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Hafs read with the ya’ on the basis that the pronoun refers to people and its implication is for working with it. Thus does God give an example of truth and falsehood for it is like the truth in its benefit and stability with the water that comes down from the sky, so the valleys flow with it according to the need and interest, so various kinds of benefits are benefited from it, and it remains in the earth by some of it remaining in its benefits and some of it passing through the veins of the earth to the springs and canals and wells, and with the metal that is benefited from in the making of jewelry and making various items, and this lasts for a long time, and falsehood in its little benefit and the speed of its disappearance with their foam, and he explained that by saying: As for the foam, it vanishes as scum yajfa bih meaning the flood throws it away and the molten metal and its accusative is in the state, and it was read jafal and the meaning is the same. As for what benefits people like water and the essence of metal. It remains in the earth is benefited from "Thus does God set forth parables" to clarify doubtful matters.
13:18: 18. For those who responded for the believers who responded. To their Lord is the best the best response and those who did not respond to Him and they are the disbelievers and the lam is related to striking as he made the striking of the example for the two groups the striking of the example for them. And it was said to those who responded the report of the best which is the reward or Paradise and those who did not respond the subject of his report. If they had all that is in the earth and the like thereof with it, they would ransom themselves with it and it is according to the first statement as a subject to explain the fate of those who did not respond those will have an evil reckoning which is the discussion in it that a man will be held accountable for his sin and nothing will be forgiven for it. And their abode their return Hell, and an evil resting place the stable and the one specifically blamed is omitted.
13:19: 19. Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth so he responds. Like one who is blind blind of heart does not see and responds, and the hamza is to deny that there is any doubt about its similarity after he struck the example. Only those of understanding will remember those with minds free from following the letter alif and opposing illusion.
13:20: 20. Those who fulfill the covenant of God is what they pledged to themselves in acknowledging His Lordship when they said, Yes, or what God Almighty pledged to them in His books. And they do not break the covenant is what they have confirmed of the covenants between them and God Almighty and between the servants, and it is a generalization after a specification.
13:21: 21. And those who maintain what God has commanded to be maintained of kinship, loyalty to believers, and belief in all the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 15 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Ḥij'r, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Isrā. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 16:2: 2. He sends down the angels with the spirit with the revelation or the Qur'an, for He revives with it the hearts that are dead due to ignorance, or He takes the place of the spirit in the body in religion. And His mentioning it after that is an indication of the way in which the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew what their promise was fulfilled and its proximity, and to remove their exclusion of his being the only one to know it. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read yanzal from anzala, and from Yaqub it is similar, and from him it means tanazal. Abu Bakr read it as tanzal in the present tense that indicates the object of the revelation. From his command by his command or for his sake. Upon whomsoever of His servants He wills to take him as a messenger. To warn to warn means know whom you have warned of such and such if you know him. There is no god but Me, so fear Me that the matter is There is no god but Me, so fear Me, or frighten the people of disbelief and sins with There is no god but Me. His saying so fear Me refers back to addressing them with what is intended and that is an explanation because the spirit means revelation indicating speech, or a source in the position of the accusative instead of the spirit or the accusative removes the preposition, or a lightened form of the heavy. The verse indicates that the revelation descends by means of the angels and that its result is to alert to monotheism which is the ultimate perfection of scientific power, and the command to fear God which is the ultimate as well as practical power. And that prophethood is a gift and the verses that follow it are evidence of His Oneness in that they indicate that He, the Most High, is the Creator of the origins of the universe and its branches in accordance with wisdom and interest, and if God were your partner He would have been able to do that, so there would be a contradiction.
16:3: 3. He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He created them in different quantities, shapes, positions, and characteristics that He determined and specified with His wisdom. He is exalted above what they associate with Him of them or of what is in need of them in its existence or continuity and of what He is not able to create. And in it is evidence that He, the Most High, is not like the celestial bodies.
16:4: 4. Man was created from a sperm-drop inanimate, without feeling or movement, fluid, not preserving position and shape. Then he is an adversary logical, disputing, explaining the argument or an adversary struggling with his Creator, saying: Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed? It was narrated that Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a decayed bone and said: O Muhammad, do you think God will give life to this after it has decayed? "So it was revealed.
16:5: 5. And the livestock camels, cows, and sheep, and their accusative case is explained by an implied pronoun. He created them for you or by apposition to man, and He created them for you is an explanation of what they were created for, and what follows is a detail of it. In them is warmth that which warms one and protects against the cold. And benefits their offspring, their being, and their appearance, and they were only expressed with benefits to include their compensation. And from them you eat meaning you eat what is eaten from them of meat, fat, and milk, and the presentation of the circumstance is to preserve the heads of the verses, or because eating from them is the usual and relied upon in livelihood, while eating from the rest of the edible animals is for the purpose of treatment or amusement.
16:6: 6. "And for you therein is beauty an adornment when you bring them back to their pastures in the evening. And when you send them out to pasture you take them out to the pastures in the morning, for the courtyards are adorned with them at both times and their people are majestic in the eyes of those who look at them. Resting is mentioned first because the beauty in them is more apparent, for they come with full bellies and udders, then they return to the pens ready for their people. It was sometimes read that Tiryoon and Tashroon are two descriptions of it with the meaning of Tiryoon in it and Tashroon in it.
16:7: 7. And carry your burdens your loads. To a land you would not have reached meaning if the livestock were not there and were not created, let alone carry them on your backs to it. Except with great difficulty except with cost and hardship. It was read with the fat-ha, which is a language for it, and it was said that the open is the source of the matter being difficult for him and its origin is the crack and the broken in Mina half, as if half of his strength was lost due to fatigue. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful as He had mercy on you by creating it for your benefit and making the matter easy for you.
16:8: 8. And horses, mules, and donkeys is in apposition to livestock. "That you may ride them and as adornment" meaning that you may ride them and adorn yourselves with them as adornment. It was said that it is in apposition to the place of "that you may ride them" and the change in the system is because adornment is by the action of the Creator and riding is not by His action, and because the purpose of their creation is riding, while adorning oneself with them is by chance. It was read without a waw, and on this basis it is possible that it is the reason for to ride it or a source in the place of the state of one of the two pronouns, i.e. adorned or adorned with it, and it was used as evidence for the prohibition of its meat, but there is no evidence for it, since it is not necessary to explain the action with what is usually intended by it that nothing else is intended by it at all, and what indicates this is that the verse is Meccan and most of the commentators and hadith scholars are of the opinion that domestic donkeys were prohibited in the year of Khaybar. And He creates what you do not know, because when He separated the animals that He usually needs, whether necessary or not, He made others general. It is possible that it is report that He has creatures that no one knows about, and that what is meant by it is what He created in the henna and fire, which has not occurred to the heart of man.
16:9: 9. And upon God is the direction of the path is a statement of the straight path that leads to the truth, or establishing the path and correcting it out of mercy and grace, or upon Him is the direction of the path that whoever follows it will inevitably reach it. It is said a path of direction and direction, meaning straight, as if he intends the direction that the traveler intends and does not deviate from it. What is meant by the path is the genus, and therefore He added the direction to it and said: And among them is one who deviates deviating from the direction or from God, and the change in style is because it is not right for God the Most High to explain the paths of misguidance, or because the intended meaning is to explain His path and divide the path into the direction and the deviant, but it came incidentally. And it was read and among you is one who deviates meaning from the direction. And if God had willed, He would have guided you all meaning if He had willed to guide you all, He would have guided you to the direction of the path, guidance that necessitates right guidance.
16:10: 10. It is He who sent down from the sky from the clouds or from the side of the sky water for you from it a drink what you drink, and for you is a relative clause of sent down or a predicate of drink and from is a partial noun related to it, and presenting it gives the impression that the drink is limited to it and there is nothing wrong with it because the waters of springs and wells are from it, as He said: And He made it flow as springs and His saying: And We settled it in the earth. "And from it is trees" and from it is a tree meaning the tree that livestock graze. It was said that everything that grows on the earth is a tree. He said: It feeds them meat if trees are scarce, and feeding them meat is harmful to horses. "Feih tasimoon means you graze, from the word samat al-mashiyah which means to graze and its root is sawmah" which means a mark because it has marks when grazing.
16:11: 11. "He causes the crops to grow for you thereby." Abu Bakr read with a nun for emphasis. "And olives, palm trees, grapes, and of all fruits." And some of all of them if not all possible fruits grow in the earth. Perhaps presenting what is permissible in it over what is eaten from it because it will become animal food is the most honorable of foods. From this is presenting the crops and stating the three types and their arrangement. "Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reflect" on the existence of the Creator and His wisdom. For whoever contemplates that the seed falls into the earth and moisture reaches it and penetrates it, its top splits open and the trunk of the tree emerges from it, and its bottom splits open and its roots emerge from it, then it grows and leaves, flowers, sleeves, and fruits emerge from it, and each of them includes bodies of different shapes and natures with the union of materials and the proportion of the lower natures and astronomical influences to the whole, he knows that this is nothing but the action of a chosen agent who is sacred from the dispute of opposites and equals. Perhaps the separation of the verse with it is for that reason.
16:12: 12. And He has subjected to you the night and the day and the sun and the moon and the stars by preparing them for your benefit. Subjected by His command is a state of all, meaning that He has benefited you with them while they are subjected to God Almighty, He created them and managed them as He willed, or for what they were created for by His creation and decree or for His wisdom, and in it is an indication of the answer to what may be said that what affects the formation of plants are the movements of the planets and their positions, for if that is accepted then there is no doubt that they are also possible in essence and attributes occurring in some possible ways, so they must have a creator who specifies and chooses and is necessarily existent to prevent the cycle and sequence, or a source of the letter m that is collective for the difference of species. Hafs read and the stars are subjected as a subject and predicate, so it is a generalization of the ruling after it was made specific. Ibn Amir also raised the sun and the moon. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason. He made the verse plural, and mentioned reason because it indicates types of evidence that are apparent to those with sound minds and do not require the completion of thought, like the conditions of plants.
16:13: 13. And what He has created for you on the earth is in apposition to the night, meaning He has subjected to you what He created for you in it of animals and women. Different in their colors its types, as they often differ in color. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember Its difference in natures, forms, and appearances is nothing but the work of a wise Creator.
16:14: 14. And it is He who has subjected the sea He made it such that you can benefit from it by riding, fishing and diving. That you may eat from it tender meat is fish, and He described it as tender because it is the moistest of meats and spoils quickly, so people hasten to eat it, and to demonstrate His power in creating it fresh and tender in turbulent water. Malik and al-Thawri held to it that whoever swears not to eat meat has broken his oath by eating fish. It was answered that faith is based on custom, and it is not understood from it when it is absolute. Do you not see that God Almighty called the disbeliever a beast, and the Creator does not break his oath by not riding a beast by riding it. And extract from it ornaments which you wear like pearls and coral, meaning that your women wear them, so it was attributed to them because they are part of them and because they adorn themselves with it for their sake. And you see the ships the ships moving through it its slits with their belts. From the opening, which is the splitting of water. It was said that it is the sound of the ship’s horn. And that you may seek of His bounty from the abundance of His provision by riding it for trade. And that you may be grateful meaning that you may recognize the blessings of God Almighty and fulfill their right. Perhaps the reason for specifying it with the following of gratitude is that it is stronger in the chapter on blessings, in that it made the calamities a reason for benefiting from obtaining a livelihood.
16:15: 15. "And He cast into the earth firm mountains" firm mountains. "lest it should sway with you" hating that it should tilt with you and be shaken, and that is because the earth before the mountains were created in it was a light ball with a simple nature, and it was right for it to move in a circular manner like the spheres, or to move with the slightest cause of movement, but when the mountains were created on its face, its sides varied and the mountains directed their weight toward the center, so they became like pegs that prevent them from moving. And it was said that when God created the earth, it began to sway, so the angels said: It is not for anyone to rest on its back, so it became anchored by the mountains. "And rivers and He made rivers in it because He cast in it means and paths that you may be guided" to your goals, or to the knowledge of God Almighty.
16:16: 16. "And signs" are landmarks by which travelers find their way, such as mountains, plains, winds, and the like. "And by the star they are guided" at night in the wilderness and seas, and what is meant by the star is the genus and it is indicated by the reading and by the star with two dammahs and a dammah and a sukoon for the plural. And it was said that the Pleiades and the Farqandan and the daughters of the coffin and the Capricorn, and perhaps the pronoun refers to the Quraysh because they traveled a lot for trade and were famous for being guided in their journeys by the stars, and taking the speech out of the traditions of address and presenting the star and inserting the pronoun for specificity is as if it was said: and by the star in particular these in particular are guided, so considering that and thanking for it is more necessary for them and obligatory for them.
16:17: 17. "Is He who creates like He who does not create?" Denial after establishing the abundant evidence of His power and the limit of His wisdom, and the uniqueness of creating what is numbered among His creations, so that He is equal to Him and deserves to share with Him what is not able to create anything of that, but rather to bring into existence something, and the right to speak is, is He who does not create like He who creates, but it was reversed, alerting that by associating partners with God, the Most High, they made Him from the category of helpless creatures, similar to them, and what is meant by He who does not create is everything that is worshipped besides God, the Most High, prevailing in it those of them who have knowledge or idols and they treated them as those of knowledge because they called them gods and it is the right of God to know, or to make similarity between Him and those who create or to exaggerate and it is as if it was said: He who creates is not like he who does not create from those of knowledge, so how about what he has no knowledge, "Do you not remember?" So recognize the corruption of that, for its clarity is like the result of the mind that attends to it with the slightest remembrance and attention.
16:18: 18. "And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them." You could not count their number, let alone be able to give thanks for them. This was followed by enumerating the favors and establishing the proof of His uniqueness in deserving worship, as a reminder that beyond what He enumerated are countless blessings, and that the right to worship Him is beyond our ability. "Indeed, God is Forgiving, as He overlooks any shortcoming in giving thanks for them, and Merciful," as He does not cut them off because of your negligence in Him, nor does He hasten to punish you for your ingratitude for them.
16:19: 19. And God knows what you conceal and what you declare of your beliefs and actions, and it is a threat and a falsification of polytheism in terms of knowledge after falsifying it in terms of power.
16:20: 20. And those who call upon besides God meaning the gods whom you worship besides Him. Abu Bakr read they call upon with a ya. Hafs read all three with a ya. They do not create anything because he denied the participation between the one who creates and the one who does not create, he made clear that they do not create anything to produce that they do not share with Him, then he confirmed that by establishing for them attributes that contradict divinity, so he said: And they create because they are possible entities whose existence is in need of creation, and the deity should be necessarily existent.
16:21: 21. Dead are dead who are not affected by life, or dead in the present or in the future. Not alive in itself to include every deity, and the deity should be alive in itself and not affected by death. And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected and they do not know the time of their resurrection, or the resurrection of their worshippers, so how can there be a time for them to be rewarded for their worship? The deity should be knowledgeable of the unseen and determine reward and punishment, and in it is a warning that resurrection is a consequence of the obligation.
16:22: 22. Your God is one God is a repetition of the claim after the proofs have been established. Those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial, and they are arrogant. An explanation of what necessitated their insistence after the truth became clear, which is their disbelief in the Hereafter. The believer in it is a seeker of evidence, contemplating what he hears and benefiting from it, while the disbeliever in it is in the opposite state, and their hearts deny what is only known by proof, following the forefathers and relying on what is familiar, for it contradicts contemplation and arrogance in following the Messenger and believing him and paying attention to his words. The first is the mainstay in the chapter, and therefore the proof of the others was based on it.
16:23: 23. There is no crime indeed. Indeed, God knows what they conceal and what they declare so He will punish them, and it is in the nominative case with crime because it is a source or a verb. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant let alone those who are arrogant about believing in His Oneness or following the Messenger.
16:24: 24. And when it is said to them, 'What has your Lord sent down?' Some of them say it out of mockery, or the visitors to them, or the Muslims. They say, 'Legends of the ancients.' That is, what you claim was sent down, or what was sent down is legends of the ancients. They only called it sent down out of mockery, or on the assumption that it was sent down, so it is legends of the ancients, with no verification in it. And the ones who said it were the dividers.
16:25: 25. That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection. That is, they said that to mislead people, so they bore the burdens of their misguidance in full, for their misguidance was the result of their persistence in misguidance. And of the burdens of those whom they misguide. And some of the burdens of the misguidance of those whom they misguide, which is the share of the cause. Without knowledge is a state of the object, meaning they misguide those who do not know that they are misguided, and its benefit is to indicate that their ignorance does not excuse them, since it was upon them to investigate and distinguish between what is right and what is wrong. How evil is that which they denounce. How evil is that which they denounce, their action. 61- "And God will save those who fear Him. It was read and He will save with their salvation" with their success, a verbal noun from victory, and its interpretation as salvation is its specification to its most important sections and to happiness and righteous work, applying it to the cause, and the Kufians other than Hafs read it in the plural, applying them to the complement to it, and the ba in it is for causality, a connection to "and He will save" or His saying: "No harm will touch them, nor will they grieve", which is a state or a resumption to explain the salvation.
16:26: 26. Those before them had already plotted meaning they had made plans to plot against the Messengers of God, peace and blessings be upon them. Then God attacked their structure from the foundations so His command came to it from the direction of the pillars on which they had built, so that they were weakened. Then the roof fell upon them from above and became the cause of their destruction. And the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive they did not expect nor anticipate, and it is by way of example. It was said that what is meant by it is Nimrod bin Canaan, who built the tower in Babylon, five thousand cubits thick, to watch the matter of the sky, so God blew the wind, so it fell upon him and his people, and they perished.
16:27: 27. Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them He will humiliate them or punish them with the Fire, as God Almighty says: Our Lord, whoever You admit to the Fire - You have disgraced him. "And he will say, 'Where are my partners?'" He added to himself in mockery, or a narration to add them to increase their rebuke. "Those about whom you were quarreling" You were hostile to the believers in their matter. And we read Fa' with a kasra on the noon meaning you were quarreling with me, for quarreling with the believers is like quarreling with God Almighty. "And those who were given knowledge said" meaning the prophets and scholars who called them to monotheism but they quarreled with them and were arrogant towards them, or the angels. "Indeed, disgrace today and evil" humiliation and torment. "On the disbelievers" The benefit of their saying is to show gloating over them and increase the humiliation, and his narration is to be a kindness and admonition to whoever hears it.
16:28: 28. Those whom the angels take in death Hamzah read it with a ya'. It was read with an assimilation in the ta' and the position of the relative pronoun is open to three aspects. Wrongdoers of themselves by exposing themselves to eternal torment. "So throw down peace" so they made peace and were humble when they saw death. We were not saying what we were. We do evil disbelief and aggression, and it is possible that it is an explanation of "peace" on the basis that what is meant by it is the statement indicating submission. Yes meaning the angels will answer them yes. Indeed, God is Knowing of what you used to do so He will reward you for it, and it was said that his saying: "So throw down peace" to the end of the verse is a resumption and a return to explaining their condition on the Day of Resurrection, and based on this the first one for whom lying is not permissible on that day We were not doing evil meaning that we were not, in our claim and belief, doing evil, and it is possible that the one who responded to them is God the Most High, or those with knowledge.
16:29: 29. Then enter the gates of Hell. Each type has its own gate prepared for it. It was said that the gates of Hell are the types of its punishment. To abide therein, so wretched is the abode of the arrogant. Hell.
16:30: 30. "And it was said to those who feared" meaning the believers. "What has your Lord sent down? They said, Good." That is, He sent down good. The accusative case is evidence that they did not falter in their answer, and they applied it to the question, acknowledging the revelation, unlike the infidels. It was narrated that the Arab tribes used to send someone during the season to bring them report of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the delegate came to divide, they would say to him what they said, and when the believers came, they would say that to him. "For those who do good in this world is good." A reward in this world. "And the home of the Hereafter is better." That is, their reward in the Hereafter is better than it, and it is a provision for those who feared God according to their statement. It is possible that what follows it is a narration of their statement instead of and explanation of "good, as it is accusative with they said. And excellent is the home of the righteous," the home of the Hereafter, so it was deleted because it was mentioned beforehand and His statement:
16:31: 31. Gardens of Eden is a predicate of a deleted subject, and it may be the one being praised. They will enter it, with rivers flowing beneath it, and they will have therein whatever they wish of the types of desires, and in presenting the adverb there is an indication that a person will not find everything he wants except in Paradise. Thus does God reward the righteous He rewards them with such a reward, and it supports the first aspect.
16:32: 32. Those whom the angels take in death while they are pure purified from wronging themselves through disbelief and sins because it is in contrast to those who wrong themselves. It was said that they are happy with the good report that the angels give them of Paradise, or that they are pure with the taking of their souls because their souls are directed completely to the presence of the Holy One. "They say, 'Peace be upon you.' No harm will befall you after that." Enter Paradise for what you used to do when you are resurrected, for it is prepared for you according to your deeds. It was said that this death is the death of the gathering because the command to enter is then.
16:33: 33. Do they wait what awaits the aforementioned disbelievers? Except that the angels should come to them to seize their souls. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read with a yaa. Or that the command of your Lord should come the Resurrection or the ultimate torment. Likewise such an act of polytheism and denial. The act of those before them so what befell them befell them. And God did not wrong them by destroying them. But they were wronging themselves by their disbelief and their sins that led to it.
16:34: 34. "So the evil consequences of what they did befell them" meaning the punishment for the evil consequences of their actions, with the addition omitted or the punishment named after it. "And that which they used to ridicule overtook them" and His punishment encompassed them. "Haqq" is only used to mean evil.
16:35: 35. And those who associate others with God said, 'If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything besides Him.' They only said that in mockery or to prevent the mission and the obligation, holding that what God wills is obligatory and what He does not will is forbidden, so what is the benefit in that? Or to deny the ugliness of what was denounced to them of polytheism and the prohibition of lakes and the like, arguing that if it were ugly, God would not have willed it to come from them and would have willed otherwise, forcing them to do so, not as an apology, since they did not believe in the ugliness of their actions. What follows is an alert to the answer to the two doubts. Thus did those before them. They associated others with God, prohibited what was lawful, and rejected His messengers. Is there anything upon the messengers except the clear conveyance? Except the clear conveyance of the truth, which does not affect the guidance of whomever God wills to guide, but it leads to it by way of intercession. And what God wills to happen must happen, not absolutely, but through causes that He has decreed for it. Then He explained that the mission is a matter. It was the divine law among all nations as a reason for the guidance of those who wanted to be guided and an increase in the misguidance of those who wanted to be misguided, like good food, for it benefits and strengthens the healthy temperament and harms the deviant and destroys him, as God Almighty says:
16:36: 36. And We have certainly sent to every nation a messenger, [saying], 'Worship God and avoid false gods.' He commands the worship of God the Most High and the avoidance of false gods. Some of them were guided by God, 'He guided them to faith through His guidance.' And some of them were destined to go astray,' because He did not guide them and did not intend to guide them. This is a warning about the corruption of the second doubt, as it indicates that misguidance was achieved and established by the action and will of God the Most High, in that it is a part of God's guidance, and this is clearly stated in the other verse. "So travel through the land, 'O people of Quraysh.' And see how was the end of those who denied, 'Aad and Thamud and others, that you may take heed.
16:37: 37. If you are keen O Muhammad on their guidance, then indeed God does not guide he who misguides he who wants to misguide him, meaning he who is destined to misguide. Other than the Kufians, they read does not guide in the passive form, which is more eloquent. And they have no helpers who can help them by repelling the punishment from them.
16:38: 38. And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that God will not resurrect him who dies is in apposition to And those who associate others with God said indicating that just as they denied monotheism, they denied resurrection, swearing by it to further confirm its corruption. And God responded to them with the most eloquent response, saying: Yes He will resurrect them. A promise is a source confirming Himself, which is what Yes indicates. So if He resurrects, it is God's promise. Upon Him is its fulfillment, because breaking His promise is impossible, or because resurrection is a requirement of His wisdom. Truly is another description of the promise. But most people do not know that they will be resurrected, either because they do not know that it is one of the duties of wisdom that His custom has been unable to observe, or because their vision of the familiar is limited, so they imagine its impossibility. Then He, the Most High, explained the two matters, saying:
16:39: 39. To make clear to them meaning to resurrect them to make clear to them "that in which they differ" which is the truth. "And that those who disbelieve may know that they were liars" in what they claim, and it is an indication of the reason calling for resurrection that requires it in terms of wisdom, and it is the distinguisher between truth and falsehood, the justified and the invalidated, by reward and punishment. Then he said:
16:40: 40. Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, 'Be,' and it is. This is a statement of possibility and its confirmation that God's creation by His pure power and will is not dependent on the precedence of materials and supplies, otherwise a sequence would be required. Just as it was possible for Him to create things in the beginning without a precedence of material and example, it was possible for Him to create them again after that. Ibn Amir and Al-Kisa'i put it in the accusative here and in Ya-Sin, so it is in apposition to We say or an answer to the command.
16:41: 41. And those who emigrated for the cause of God after they had been wronged They are the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, the emigrants who were wronged by the Quraysh, so some of them emigrated to Abyssinia, then to Medina, and some to Medina. The imprisoned and tortured in Mecca after the emigration of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were Bilal, Suhayb, Khabbab, Ammar, Abis, Abu Jandal, and Suhayl, may God be pleased with them. His statement: For the cause of God means for His right and for His sake. We will surely provide them with a good abode in this world A good abode is Medina or a good abode. And the reward of the Hereafter is greater than what is hastened for them in this world. On the authority of Omar, may God be pleased with him: When he gave a gift to a man from the immigrants, he would say to him, “Take it, may God bless you with it. This is what God promised you in this world, and what He has stored for you in the Hereafter is better.” If they had known, the pronoun refers to the disbelievers, meaning if they had known that God would gather for these immigrants the best of both worlds, they would have agreed with them, or to the immigrants, meaning if they had known that, they would have increased their efforts and patience.
16:42: 42. Those who were patient in the face of hardships, such as harm from the infidels and leaving their homeland, and its place is in the accusative or nominative case for praise. And upon their Lord they rely, turning to God and entrusting the entire matter to Him.
16:43: 43. And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed is a response to the Quraysh's statement: God is greater than for His Messenger to be a human being, meaning that the divine tradition is that He does not send for the general call except a human being to whom We revealed through the tongues of angels, and the wisdom in that has been mentioned in Surat Al-An'am. If you doubt it. Then ask the people of the message the people of the Book or the scholars of the report so that they may teach you. If you do not know and in the verse there is evidence that God did not send a woman or an angel for the general call, and His statement: Making the angels messengers means messengers to the angels or to the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. It was said that they were not sent to the prophets except in the form of men. It was responded to by what was narrated: that he, peace and blessings be upon him, saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, in the form that he is in twice. And on the necessity of referring to the scholars regarding what is not known.
16:44: 44. With clear proofs and scriptures meaning We sent them with clear proofs and scriptures meaning miracles and scriptures, as if it were an answer to: Someone said: With what were they sent? It is permissible to relate to what We sent as included in the exception with men, meaning: We sent only men with clear proofs like your saying: I did not strike anyone but Zaid with the whip, or a description of them, meaning men who are immersed in clear proofs, or by inspiration as a direct object or a state of the one who takes the place of its subject, on the basis that his saying, So ask is an objection, or without you know, on the basis that the condition is for rebuke and obligation. And We sent down to you the Reminder meaning the Qur'an, and it was only called a Reminder because it is an admonition and a warning. To make clear to the people what was sent down to them in the Reminder by means of its sending down to you of what they were commanded to do and forbidden from, or of what was ambiguous to them, and clarification is more general than stating the intended meaning, or guiding to what indicates it like analogy and the evidence of reason. Perhaps they will reflect and he wanted them to reflect on it and become aware of the facts.
16:45: 45. Do those who plot evil deeds feel secure that God will not cause the earth to swallow them up as He caused Korah to swallow up or that the punishment will come upon them from where they do not perceive suddenly from the side of the sky as He did with the people of Lot.
16:46: 46. "Or He takes them in their changing" meaning, changing in their paths and trades. "So they will not escape."
16:47: 47. Or He takes them with fear with fear that He will destroy a people before them and they will fear and the punishment will come to them while they are fearful, or with fear that He will diminish them little by little in their lives and their wealth until they perish from His fear if it diminishes them. It was narrated that Omar, may God be pleased with him, said on the pulpit: What do you say about it? They were silent, then an old man from Hudhayl stood up and said: This is our language, fear and diminishment. He said: Do the Arabs know that in their poetry? He said: Yes. Our poet Abu Kabir said, describing his she-camel: The nomads feared it as a monkey, just as the spring tree feared ships. Omar said: Stick to your diwan, do not go astray. They said: What is our diwan? He said: The poetry of the pre-Islamic era, for in it is the interpretation of your book and the meanings of your words. For your Lord is Most Kind and Most Merciful, as He does not hasten to punish you.
16:48: 48. Or have they not seen what God has created of things? An interrogative of denial, meaning that they have seen such creations, so why have they not thought about them so that His perfect power and might may be revealed to them, so that they may fear Him? And ma is an ambiguous relative pronoun. shades means that they have not looked at the creatures that have shady shadows. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a ta’ and Abu Amr read it with a ta’. From the right and the left from its right and from its left, meaning from the sides of each one of them, a metaphor from the right and left of a person. Perhaps the unification of the right and the plural of the left are based on the word and meaning, like the unification of the pronoun in his shadows, and its plural in his saying: prostrating to God while they are humbled. They are two states of the pronoun in his shadows. What is meant by prostration is submission, whether it is by nature or by choice. It is said that the palm tree prostrated when it leaned due to the abundance of the load, and the camel prostrated when it lowered its head to ride, and prostration is a state of the shadows, while they are humbled is a state of the pronoun. The meaning is that the shadows return with the rising and falling of the sun, or with the difference of its easts and wests by the decree of God Almighty from one side to another, obedient to what has been decreed for it of shade, or lying on the ground, clinging to it in the form of one prostrating. The bodies in themselves are also humbled, meaning submissive and obedient to the actions of God Almighty in them, and the plural is Daakhiroon with the letter waw because it includes those who have reason, or because dakhiroon is one of the descriptions of rational beings. It was said that what is meant by the right and left sides is the right side of the sky, which is its eastern side because the planets appear from it rising and shining, and its north is the western side opposite it from the Earth. For shadows at the beginning of the day begin from the east, falling on the western quarter of the Earth. And at noon, they begin from the west, falling on the eastern quarter of the Earth.
16:49: 49. And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth meaning it submits in a submission that includes submission to His will and influence by nature and submission to His command and order willingly so that it is correct to attribute it to all the people of the heavens and the earth. His saying: of any creature is an explanation of them because creeping is physical movement whether it is on the earth or the sky. And the angels is an apposition to what is explained by it, the apposition of Gabriel to the angels for glorification, or the apposition of abstract things to physical things, and this is what was used as evidence by those who said that the angels are abstract spirits or an explanation of what is in their angels of guardians and others, and since it was used for rational beings as it was used for others, its use where the two tribes met was more appropriate than the use of whoever, in order to give precedence to rational beings. And they are not too proud to worship Him.
16:50: 50. They fear their Lord above them. They fear that He will send a punishment from above them, or they fear Him while He is above them by force, as God Almighty says: And He is the Prevailing over His servants. The sentence is a state of the pronoun in they are not arrogant, or a clarification and confirmation of it, because whoever fears God Almighty is not arrogant about worshipping Him. And they do what they are commanded of obedience and management, and in it is evidence that the angels are charged and alternate between fear and hope.
16:51: 51. And God said, 'Do not take two gods.' The number was mentioned even though the counted thing indicates it, indicating that the prohibition is directed towards it, or hinting that duality contradicts divinity. We mentioned the one in His statement, He is only one God, to indicate that the intended meaning is to establish oneness without divinity, or to draw attention to the fact that oneness is one of the requirements of divinity. So fear Me. He transferred from the third person to the first person, exaggerating the intimidation and stating the intended meaning, as if he said: I am that one God, so fear Me and no one else.
16:52: 52. And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth in creation and dominion. And to Him belongs the religion meaning obedience. Constantly is necessary because it is established that He alone is God and is the only One worthy of being feared. It was said constantly from wasb meaning to Him belongs the religion with a burden. It was said that the religion is the reward meaning to Him belongs the reward always, His reward does not cease for those who believe and His punishment for those who disbelieve. Then do you fear other than God? And there is no one who can harm other than Him, just as there is no one who can benefit other than Him, as God Almighty said.
16:53: 53.
