And whatever blessing you have is from God meaning, whatever blessing you have is from God, and whatever is a conditional or relative clause that includes the meaning of a condition in consideration of the information without the occurrence, so the stability of the blessing in them is a reason for the information that it is from God, not because it occurred from Him. Then when harm befalls you, to Him you cry for help So you do not implore except to Him, and crying is raising the voice in supplication and calling for help.
16:54: 54. Then when He removes the hardship from you, at once a party of you - and they are your disbelievers - associate others with their Lord in worshipping other than Him. This is if the address is general. If it is specific to the polytheists, then min is for clarification, as if he said: When a party - and they are you. It is permissible for min to be for partiality, so that some of them may be considered, as in the Almighty's saying: Then when He delivered them to the land, some of them were moderate.
16:55: 55. So that they may disbelieve in what We have given them of the blessing of revelation from them, as if they intended by their polytheism to be ungrateful for the blessing, or to deny that it was from God Almighty. Then enjoy is a threatening command. Then you will know is more severe in its threat. And it was read they may enjoy in the passive form, in apposition to so that they may disbelieve, and based on this it is permissible for the lam to be the lam of the command that came for the threat and the fa for the answer.
16:56: 56. And they make for what they do not know meaning for their gods who have no knowledge because they are inanimate, so the pronoun is for what, or for which they do not know, so they believe in ignorance, such as that they benefit them and intercede for them, on the basis that the reference to what is omitted, or for them to make on the basis that what is a source and the unknown for it is omitted because of knowledge of it. A share of what We have provided for them of crops and livestock. By God, you will be asked about what you used to invent that they are real gods by drawing near to them, and this is a threat to them for it.
16:57: 57. And they attribute to God daughters. Khuza'ah and Kinanah used to say that the angels were daughters of God. Glory be to Him. This is to absolve Him from what they said, or to express amazement at it. And for them is what they desire. Meaning sons. It is permissible to raise the subject in the nominative case and to lower the subject in conjunction with daughters, on the basis that making means choosing. Although it leads to the subject and object pronouns being for one thing, it is not far-fetched to permit it in the conjoined.
16:58: 58. And if one of them is given the good report of a female he is informed of her birth. His face becomes or remains all day blackened from depression and shyness before people. The blackening of the face is a metaphor for grief and distress. And he is suppressing filled with anger towards the woman.
16:59: 59. He hides from the people He hides from them. From the evil of what he has been given good report. From the evil of the one given good report, according to custom. Should he keep him? Talking to himself, thinking about leaving him. With humiliation Humiliation. Or should he bury him in the dirt? That is, hide him in it and bury him alive. The pronoun is masculine for the word what and it was read with the feminine in both of them. How evil is what they judge where they attribute to the one who is too exalted for a child what this is his place with them.
16:60: 60. For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is an evil example. The evil characteristic is the need for children, which calls for death, and keeping males as a means of protection, and hating females and burying them alive for fear of poverty. And to God belongs the highest example. It is the intrinsic obligation, absolute wealth, superior generosity, and freedom from the attributes of created beings. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. The One Unique in perfect power and wisdom.
16:61: 61. And if God were to punish people for their wrongdoing for their disbelief and sins. He would not have left upon it on the earth, but He implied it without mentioning it to indicate to people and beasts about it. From a beast is a cat due to the evil of their wrongdoing. And on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, may God be pleased with him: The dung beetle almost perished in his lap due to the sin of the son of Adam or from a wrongdoing beast. And it was said that if the fathers were destroyed due to their disbelief, there would be no children. But He delays them for a specified term He named it for their ages or for their punishment so that they may reproduce. So when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour nor will they precede it Rather, they will perish or be punished at that time inevitably. And it is not necessary from the generality of people and the attribution of wrongdoing to them that all of them are wrongdoers, even the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, because it is permissible to attribute to them what is widespread among them and issued by most of them.
16:62: 62. And they attribute to God what they hate meaning what they hate for themselves of daughters and partners in leadership, and belittling the messengers and the lowest of wealth. And their tongues describe lying with its humiliation, which is. That they will have the best meaning with God, as in His saying: And if I return to my Lord, I will have with Him the best. And it was read lying is the plural of liar as an attribute of tongues. There is no doubt that they will have the Fire is a response to their words and confirmation of its opposite. And that they are excessive are brought to the Fire from excessive in seeking water if you advance it. And Nafi' read it with a kasra on the ra' as being from excess in sins. And it was read with a shaddah, open, from excessive in seeking water and broken, from excessive in acts of obedience.
16:63: 63. "By God, We sent to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds pleasing to them, but they persisted in their evil deeds and disbelieved in the messengers. So he is their protector today," meaning in this world. He used the word day to refer to its time, or he is their protector when he made them pleasing to them, or on the Day of Resurrection, as a narration of a past or future situation. It is possible that the pronoun refers to Quraysh, meaning Satan made their deeds pleasing to the disbelievers before him, and he is the protector of these people today, tempting them and leading them astray. If it is an added word, meaning he is the protector of their likes, and the protector is the companion or the helper, then it would be a negation of the helper for them in the most eloquent way. And for them is a painful punishment on the Day of Resurrection.
16:64: 64. And We have not sent down the Book to you except that you may make clear to them to the people. That over which they differed of monotheism, destiny, the conditions of the afterlife, and the rulings on actions. And as guidance and mercy for a people who believe are conjoined with the place of to make clear, for they are the verbs of the revealed, unlike to make clear.
16:65: 65. And God sends down water from the sky and revives the earth with it after its lifelessness. He causes all kinds of plants to grow in it after it has dried up. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen. Hearing with contemplation and fairness.
16:66: 66. And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you. An indication that expresses ignorance to knowledge. We give you to drink from what is in their bellies. A resumption to explain the lesson, and the pronoun was mentioned and made singular here for the sake of the word and made feminine in Surat Al-Mu'minun for the sake of the meaning, as Al-An'am is a collective noun and therefore Sibawayh counted it among the singular words built on verbs such as Akhlaq and Akisa. Whoever said that it is a collective noun made the pronoun for some, as the milk is for some of them and not all of them or for one of them or for him according to the meaning, as what is meant by it is the genus. And Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, Abu Bakr and Ya'qub read We give you to drink with the fatha here and in Al-Mu'minun from between excrement and blood milk as it creates from some parts of the blood generated from the subtle parts in the excrement, which are the eaten things that are partially digested in the rumen. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: When an animal feeds and the fodder is cooked in its rumen, its lower part is excrement, its middle part is milk, and its upper part is blood. Perhaps if this is correct, what is meant is that its middle part is the substance of milk and its upper part is the substance of blood that nourishes the body, because they are not formed in the rumen. Rather, the liver attracts the purest digested food in the rumen, and keeps its weight, which is excrement, then holds it until it digests it a second time, creating four mixtures with it, one of which is watery. The distinguishing power distinguishes that watery part from what is more than what is needed from the two times and pushes it to the kidney, gall bladder, and spleen. Then the rest is distributed to the organs according to them, so it flows to each one according to what is appropriate for it, according to the estimation of the All-Wise, All-Knowing. Then, if the animal is female, its mixtures increase in proportion to its food, due to the cold and moisture dominating its temperament. The excess is first pushed to the uterus for the sake of the fetus, and when it separates, that excess or some of it flows to the udders, where it lays eggs by being adjacent to their white glandular meats, and becomes milk. Whoever ponders the creation of God Almighty in creating the mixtures and milks and preparing their locations and channels and the causes that generate them and the powers that control them at all times in a manner befitting Him, will be compelled to acknowledge the perfection of His wisdom and the limit of His mercy. The first min is partial because milk is part of what is in their bellies, and the second is introductory, like your saying: I was given to drink from the basin, because between the excrement and the blood is the place from which the drinking begins, and it is related to He gave you to drink or a state of laban which was presented before it to make it indefinite and to draw attention to the fact that it is the place of the lesson. Pure means clear, not accompanied by the color of blood or the smell of excrement, or filtered from what accompanies it of the dense parts by narrowing its outlet. Saighan li-dharibiyn means easy to pass through their throats, and it was read as siighan with emphasis and without emphasis.
16:67: 67. And from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapes is related to something omitted, i.e., We give you to drink from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapes, i.e., from their juice. His saying, You take from it intoxicant is a resumption to explain the giving to drink or with you take, and from it is a repetition of the circumstance to emphasize or to predicate something omitted whose description is you take, i.e., from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapes, fruit from which you take, and the pronoun is masculine in the first two ways because it refers to the omitted complement which is the juice, or because the fruits means the fruit and intoxicant is a source by which wine is named. And good provision like dates, raisins, molasses, and vinegar. If the verse preceded the prohibition of wine, then it indicates its abhorrence, otherwise it combines reproach and favor. It was said that intoxicant is wine, and it was said that it is the taste. He said: The symptoms of the generous became sugar That is, it moved with their symptoms. It was said that what satisfies hunger is sugar, so the sustenance is what is obtained from its price. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason. They use their minds by looking at and contemplating the verses.
16:68: 68. And your Lord inspired the bee He inspired it and cast into its hearts, and it was read to the bees with two fat-has. That you take by taking, and it is possible that that is explanatory because in inspiration there is a meaning of saying, and the feminization of the pronoun is based on the meaning, as the bee is masculine. From the mountains, houses, and from the trees and from what they erect It was mentioned with the letter of partiality because it is not built on every mountain and every tree and everything that is erected from grapes or roofs, nor in every place of them. Rather, what you build to make honey in it is called a house, likening it to the construction of a human being, because of the fine craftsmanship in it and the share of the division that the most skilled of engineers cannot achieve except with precise tools and vision, and perhaps its mention is to draw attention to that, and it was read houses with a kasra on the ba, and Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read they erect with a damma on the ra.
16:69: 69. Then eat of all the fruits of every fruit you desire, its bitter and its sweet. So follow what you eat. The paths of your Lord in His paths in which He transforms, by His power, the bitter light into honey from within you, or So follow the paths by which He inspired you to make honey, or So follow, returning to your homes, the paths of your Lord", do not make it difficult for you or become confused. "Humbled is the plural of Humble" and is a state of the paths. Meaning, submissive, God has subdued it and made it easy for you, or from the pronoun in aslkun meaning, and you are submissive and obedient to what you are commanded to do. It comes out of their bellies as if he changed it from addressing the bees to addressing people, because it is the place of blessing upon them and the purpose of creating the bees and inspiring them for their sake. Drink means honey because it is something that they drink, and it was used as evidence by those who claimed that the bees eat flowers and fragrant leaves, which are transformed into honey in their bellies, then they store it for the winter. And by those who claimed that they pick up with their mouths small, sweet, powdery parts scattered on the leaves and flowers, and put them in their nests as storage, so if a large amount of it gathers in their nests, it becomes honey, so he interpreted the bellies as mouths. Its colors are different: white, yellow, red, and black according to the age of the bees and the season. In it is a cure for people, either by itself, as in the case of phlegmatic diseases, or with something else, as in all other diseases, since there is rarely a paste that does not have honey as a part of it, although the indefiniteness in it indicates that it is partial, and it is permissible for it to be for glorification. On the authority of Qatada, “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My brother is complaining of his stomach. He said: Give him honey to drink. He went and then came back and said: I gave him honey to drink but it did not help. He said: Go and give him honey, for God has spoken the truth and your brother’s stomach has lied. So he gave him honey to drink and God Almighty healed him and he recovered, as if he had been released from a shackle.” It was said that the pronoun refers to the Qur’an or to what God has explained about the conditions of the bee. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reflect. Whoever contemplates the specialization of the bee in those precise sciences and wondrous actions with true contemplation will know with certainty that it must have a Creator, Able and Wise, who inspires it with that and compels it to do it.
16:70: 70. And God created you, then He will take you at different terms. And among you is he who is returned to the worst of ages" the worst of it means old age that resembles childhood in the decrease of strength and mind. It was said that it is ninety-five years and it was said that it is seventy-five. "So that after knowing he will not know anything" to become in a state similar to the state of childhood in forgetfulness and misunderstanding. "Indeed, God is Knowing" of the measures of your ages. "Powerful" He kills the active youth and leaves the mortal old man. In it is a warning that the difference in people's terms is only by the estimation of the Powerful, the Wise, who constructed their structures and adjusted their temperaments according to a known measure. If that were what natures require, the difference would not have reached this level.
16:71: 71. "And God has favored some of you over others in provision. Some of you are rich and some are poor. Some of you are clients who take care of their own provision and the provision of others, and some of you are slaves whose situation is different from that. "So those who are favored are not those who give their provision to those whom their right hands possess." Over their slaves, for they only return it. Upon them is their provision which God has placed in their hands. They are equal in it. The clients and the slaves are equal in that God has provided for them. The sentence is necessary for the negative sentence or confirms it. It is permissible for it to be in the position of the answer as if it was said: Then what are those who have been favored who give their provision over those whom their right hands possess? So they are equal in provision. It is a response and denial to the polytheists, for they associate some of His creations with God in divinity and are not pleased for their slaves to share with them in what God has bestowed upon them, so it is a matter of doubt to them about it. Do they then deny the favor of God? Where they take partners for Him, for it requires that some of what God has bestowed upon them be attributed to them and they deny that it is from God, or where they denied such arguments after God has bestowed upon them by clarifying them. The ba is to include the meaning of denial as disbelief. Abu Bakr read you deny with the ta because of his saying: He created you and He favored some of you.
16:72: 72. And God has made for you mates from among yourselves meaning from your own kind so that you may be comforted by them and so that your children may be like you. It was said that He created Eve from Adam. And He has made for you from your mates sons and grandchildren and sons of sons or daughters, because the grandchild is the one who is quick to serve and the daughters serve in the homes in the most perfect service. It was said that they are the two sisters over the daughters. It was said that they are the stepdaughters and it is possible that it means the sons themselves and the conjunction is to differentiate the two descriptions. And He has provided for you from the good things from the pleasures or the lawful things and from is for the partial because the one provided for in this world is an example of it. Do they then believe in falsehood? That is, that idols benefit them, or that some natural things are forbidden, such as lakes and wild animals. And they disbelieve in the favor of God when they attribute a favor to idols, or forbid what God has made permissible for them. The relative clause is placed before the verb, either for emphasis or to give the impression of specificity, exaggeration, or to preserve the breaks.
16:73: 73. And they worship besides God that which possesses no provision for them from the heavens or the earth at all of rain and plants, and provision if you make it a source then something is accusative with it, otherwise it is a substitute for it. And they are not able to possess it or they have no ability at all, and the pronoun is plural in it and singular in does not possess because what is singular in the meaning of gods, and it is permissible for it to refer back to the infidels, meaning that these people are not able, although they are alive and dispose of anything of that, so how about inanimate objects.
16:74: 74. So do not make for God similitudes. So do not make for Him a similitude by associating Him with Him, or by comparing Him to Him, for making a similitude is likening one state to another. Indeed, God knows the corruption of what you rely on in analogy, because the worshippers of the king's slaves are more glorified than his worship, and the enormity of your crime in what you do. And you do not know that, and if you knew it, you would not have dared to do it, for He is All-Knowing of the prohibition, or that He knows the essence of things, and you do not know Him, so leave your opinion without His text. It is possible that it is meant, So do not make for God similitudes, for He knows how to make similitudes, and you do not know. Then He taught them how to make similitudes, so He made an similitude for the soul and for those below Him, and He said:
16:75: 75. "God has set forth a parable: a slave owned by someone who has no power over anything, and one whom We have provided from Us with a good provision, so he spends from it secretly and publicly. Are they equal?" He likened himself to the free owner whom God has provided with a lot of money, so he disposes of it and spends from it as he wishes. He argued that it is impossible to associate and equate between them, despite their sharing in nationality and creation, on the impossibility of equating idols, which are the most helpless of creation, with God, the Rich and All-Powerful. It was said that it is a representation of the forsaken infidel and the successful believer, and restricting the slave to being owned to distinguish him from the free man is a representation of the servant of God, and by taking away the ability to distinguish him from the one who is freed and the one who is authorized, and making him a partner to the disposing owner indicates that the slave does not own, and it is more apparent that from is an indefinite noun described to match a slave, and the pronoun in they are equal is plural because it is for both genders, so the meaning is: are the free and the slaves equal? Praise be to God All praise is due to Him, no one else deserves it, let alone worship, because He is the Master of all blessings. But most of them do not know so they attribute a blessing to someone other than Him and worship Him for its sake.
16:76: 76. "And God sets forth a parable: two men, one of them mute" A mute boy who neither understands nor comprehends. Not capable of anything Of crafts and measures due to his lack of intelligence. And he is a burden on his master A child and a burden on whoever is in charge of his affairs. Wherever he directs him Wherever his master sends him on a matter. He directs is read in the passive form and He directs means he directs, like his saying Wherever I direct, I find happiness and He directs in the past tense. He does not bring good He succeeds and suffices. Is he equal to the one who commands justice? “And he is a logical, sufficient, and wise man who benefits people in their search for justice that includes all virtues.” And he is on a straight path. “And he is in himself on a straight path that does not direct him to a goal except that he reaches it with the closest effort.” And he only contrasted those qualities with these two descriptions because they are the perfection of what they contrast with. This is a second representation that God Almighty struck for Himself and for the idols to invalidate the partnership between Him and them or between the believer and the disbeliever. 43- On the Day they emerge from the graves quickly quickly, plural of quick, as if they were to a monument erected for worship or knowledge, they hasten, Ibn Amir and Hafs read to a monument with a damma on the noon and the sad, and the rest of the seven read it with a fatha on the noon and a sukoon on the sad, and it was read with a damma as a lightening of monument or a plural.
16:77: 77. "And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth" His knowledge is exclusive to Him, not to anyone else's knowledge, and it is that which is hidden from the servants in them, such that it is not perceptible and no perceptible thing indicates it. And it was said about the Day of Resurrection, for His knowledge is hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth. "And the matter of the Hour" and the matter of the coming of the Hour in its speed and ease. "is only like the twinkling of an eye" except like the return of the eye from the top of the pupil to the bottom. "Or it is nearer" or its matter is nearer than that, in that it is in the time of half that movement, or in the moment in which it begins, for He, the Most High, revives the creatures all at once, and what is found all at once is at once, and "or is for choice or in the sense of rather". And it was said that its meaning is that the coming of the Hour, even if it is delayed, is with God like the thing about which you say it is like the twinkling of an eye, or it is nearer, an exaggeration in its approximation. "Indeed, God is over all things competent" so He is able to revive the creatures all at once, just as He was able to revive them gradually, then He indicated His power by saying:
16:78: 78. And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers. Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the hamza as a language or following what preceded it, and Hamza with a kasra on it and a kasra on the meem and the ha' is an addition like it in ahraq. You do not know anything ignorantly, continuing the ignorance of inanimate objects. And He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts a tool by which you learn, so you sense with your feelings the details of things and comprehend them, then you become alert with your hearts to the similarities and differences between them by repeating the sensation until you acquire the intuitive knowledge, and you are able to acquire the acquired features by looking at them. Perhaps you will be grateful so that you may know what He has bestowed upon you, stage after stage, and then thank Him.
16:79: 79. Have they not seen the birds? Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Yaqub read with the letter ta' as if it were addressed to the general public. Subjected tamed for flight with what was created for them of wings and the means that are conducive to it. In the atmosphere of the sky in the air far from the earth. What holds them up in it. Except God because the weight of their bodies necessitates their falling and there is no connection above them or support beneath them to hold them up. Indeed in that are signs subjecting the birds to flight by creating them in a way that allows them to fly, and creating the atmosphere in which they can fly and hold them up in the air contrary to their nature. For a people who believe because they are the ones who benefit from them.
16:80: 80. And God has made for you from your houses a place of rest a place in which you live during your stay, like houses made of stone and mud, a verb with the meaning of a passive participle. And He has made for you from the hides of livestock, houses are the domes made of leather, and it is permissible to include those made of fur, wool and hair, because since they grow on their hides, it is true that they are from their hides. You find them light you find them light, so carrying and transporting them is easy for you. The day of your departure is the time of your travel. And the day of your residence and placing or striking them at the time of settlement or disembarkation. The Hijazis and Basrans read the day of your departure with the fat-ha, which is a dialect for it. And from their wool and their fur and their hair wool for the sheep and fur for the camels and hair for the goats, and adding it to the pronoun livestock is because it is part of them. furniture is what is worn and furnished. and goods is what is traded Until a while means a period of time, because it is hard and lasts for a long time, or until a while, your death or until you have finished it or it has left you.
16:81: 81. And God has made for you from what He has created of trees, mountains, buildings, and other things. Shades to protect you from the heat of the sun. And He has made for you shelters from the mountains places where you live, from caves and carved houses in them, the plural of kan. "And He has made for you garments" garments of wool, linen, cotton, and other things. "To protect you from the heat" He mentioned it only to suffice with one of the two opposites, or because protection from the heat was more important to them. "And garments to protect you from your violence" means armor and cloaks, and the cloak includes everything that is worn. "Likewise" as a completion of these blessings that came before. "To complete His favor upon you that you may submit" meaning that you may look at His favors and believe in Him and submit to His judgment. It was read "taslamun" from safety, meaning that you are grateful and are saved from the punishment, or that you look at them and are saved from polytheism. It was said that "you are saved" from wounds by wearing armor.
16:82: 82. If they turn away they turn away and do not accept from you. Then your duty is only to convey the clear message so it will not harm you, for your duty is only to convey the message, and you have conveyed it. This is from establishing the cause in place of the effect.
16:83: 83. "They know the favor of God" meaning the polytheists know the favor of God which He enumerated upon them and others, as they acknowledge it and that it is from God the Most High. "Then they deny it" by worshipping other than the one who bestowed it and saying that it is through the intercession of our gods, or because of such and such, or by their turning away from fulfilling its rights. It was said that the favor of God is the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They knew it through miracles, then they denied it out of stubbornness, and the meaning of then is to exclude denial after knowledge. "And most of them are disbelievers" are the deniers out of stubbornness, and the majority were mentioned either because some of them did not know the truth due to a deficiency in reason or negligence in consideration, or the proof was not established against them because they did not reach the level of accountability, or because they are taken in place of all, as in His statement: "But most of them do not know."
16:84: 84. And the Day We raise up from every nation a witness and he is their prophet who will testify for them and against them regarding faith and disbelief. Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved to apologize, as they have no excuse. It was said about returning to the world. Then is to increase what will befall them from the severity of the prohibition of apologizing, because it includes complete despair of what they are blessed with from the testimony of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. Nor will they seek repentance nor will they seek approval, from repentance, which is satisfaction, and the nominative case of the day is with an omitted word, the meaning of which is remember, or their fear, or what will befall them will befall them. And likewise his saying:
16:85: 85. And when those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be given respite.
16:86: 86. And when those who associate others with God see their partners their idols which they called partners, or the devils who shared with them in disbelief by forcing it. They will say, Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You." We worship them or obey them. This is an admission that they were wrong in that, or a request to divide their punishment. "Then they will cast down to them the word, 'Indeed, you are liars.' That is, they will answer them with denial that they are partners with God, or that they did not truly worship them but rather worshipped their desires, as God Almighty says, No! They will disbelieve in their worship. It is not impossible for God to make the idols speak of it at that time, or that they forced them to disbelieve and oblige them to it, as He says, And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me."
16:87: 87. And they threw down, and those who did wrong threw down. To God, that Day, is peace. Submission to His rule after arrogance in this world. "And what they used to invent was lost to them and nullified." That their gods would support them and intercede for them when they denied them and disavowed them.
16:88: 88. Those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the path of God by preventing Islam and forcing people to disbelieve. We will increase their punishment for their aversion. On top of the punishment they deserved for their disbelief. Because they were corrupting for being corrupters by their aversion.
16:89: 89. "And the Day We shall raise up in every nation a witness over them from among themselves" meaning their prophets, for the prophet of every nation was sent from among themselves. "And We have brought you" O Muhammad. "as a witness over these" over your nation. "And We have sent down to you the Book is a resumption or a conjunction with the omission of already". "Explanation" an eloquent explanation. "for everything" of the matters of religion in detail or in general by referring to the Sunnah or analogy. "And guidance and mercy" for all. The prohibition of the forbidden is only due to his negligence. "And good tidings for the Muslims" in particular.
16:90: 90. God commands justice by moderation in matters, such as belief in monotheism, which is moderate between idleness and polytheism, and saying that earning is moderate between mere report and destiny, and by action, such as worshipping by performing duties, which is moderate between idleness and monasticism, and by character, such as generosity, which is moderate between miserliness and extravagance. And goodness is "goodness in acts of obedience, and it is either according to quantity, such as voluntary acts of worship, or according to quality, as the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, "Goodness is to worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. And giving to relatives" and giving relatives what they need, which is a specification after generalization for exaggeration. "And He forbids immorality" from excessive pursuit of the lustful force, such as adultery, for it is the ugliest and most heinous of human conditions. "And evil" is what is condemned for its practitioner in arousing the angry force. And oppression and arrogance and domination over people and tyranny over them, then it is the devilishness that is required by the imaginary power, and there is no evil in man except that it is included in these categories and issued by the mediation of one of these three powers, and for this reason Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, said: It is the most comprehensive verse in the Qur’an for good and evil. And it became the reason for the conversion of Uthman bin Maz’un, may God be pleased with him, to Islam, and if there was nothing in the Qur’an other than this verse, then it would have been true that it is an explanation of everything and a guidance and mercy for the worlds. Perhaps it was mentioned after his saying: And We have sent down to you the Book to draw attention to it. He admonishes you with commands and prohibitions and distinguishes between good and evil. Perhaps you will remember so that you may be admonished.
16:91: 91. And fulfill the covenant of God meaning the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, based on the Almighty's saying: Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are only pledging allegiance to God. It was said that every matter must be fulfilled and that His saying: When you have made a covenant does not fit with it. It was said that it is vows. It was said that it is belief in God. And do not break oaths meaning the oaths of allegiance or all oaths. After confirming them after documenting them with the mention of God, the Almighty, and from this it was confirmed by changing the waw to a hamza. And you have made God a guarantor over you witnessing that pledge, for the guarantor is mindful of the condition of the one guaranteed and is a watcher over him. Indeed, God knows what you do of breaking oaths and covenants.
16:92: 92. And do not be like the one who untwisted her spinning what she spun, a source meaning the object. After she had untwisted is related to untwisted meaning she untwisted her spinning after it was tight and perfect. Unwounds energies, unwound, twisted, plural of unwound, and its accusative is in the state of her spinning or the second object of untwisted because it means made, and what is meant by it is likening the unwound to someone like that. It was said that she is Raytah bint Saad bin Taym Al-Qurashiyyah, that she was a clumsy woman who used to do that. You take your oaths as a means of deception among yourselves is a state of the pronoun in and do not be or in the preposition in the position of the predicate, meaning do not imitate a woman like this, taking your oaths as a means of corruption and deception among yourselves. The origin of deception is that which enters something, and it was not from. That a nation is more numerous than another nation is because a group is more numerous and more abundant in wealth than a group, and the meaning is do not betray a people because of your large number and small number, because of the large number of their opponents and their strength like the Quraysh, for if they saw a thorn in the enemies of their allies, they would break their covenant and ally with their enemies. God only tests you with it is the pronoun will not be a nation because it means the source, meaning He tests you with their being more numerous to see. Do you hold fast to the rope of fulfilling the covenant of God and the pledge of allegiance to His Messenger, or are you deceived by the large number of Quraysh and their strength and the small number of believers and their weakness. It was said that the pronoun refers to hypocrisy, and it was said that it refers to the command to fulfill. And He will make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ, when He rewards you for your deeds with reward and punishment.
16:93: 93. And if God had willed, He could have made you one nation united in Islam. But He leaves astray whom He wills by abandoning. And He guides whom He wills by success. And you will surely be asked about what you used to do a question of rebuke and retribution.
16:94: 94. And do not use your oaths as a means of deception between you. This is an explicit prohibition of it after the inclusion, emphasizing and exaggerating the ugliness of what is prohibited. So that a foot slips, that is, from the path of Islam. After it has been firmly established on it, and what is meant is their feet. The singular and indefinite are used to indicate that the slip of one foot is great, so it is sufficient for many feet. And taste the evil the punishment in this world. Because you have turned away from the path of God by turning away from fulfilling it, because others have turned you away from it, for whoever breaks the pledge of allegiance and apostatizes, he makes that a tradition for others. And for you is a great punishment in the Hereafter.
16:95: 95. And do not exchange the covenant of God for a small price a small offer, which is what the Quraysh promised to the weak Muslims and stipulated for them in return for apostasy. What is with God of victory and spoils in this world and reward in the Hereafter is better for you than what they promise you, if you only knew if you were people of knowledge and discernment.
16:96: 96. What you have of worldly goods. It will run out will end and perish. And what is with God of the treasures of His mercy. It will remain will not run out, and this is an explanation for the previous ruling and evidence that the bliss of the people of Paradise will remain. And We will surely reward those who were patient with their reward in the face of poverty and the harm of the disbelievers, or in the face of the hardships of the obligations. Ibn Kathir and Asim read with the letter nun. "With the best of what they used to do" with what is most likely to be done of their deeds, such as the obligatory and recommended deeds, or with a reward better than their deeds.
16:97: 97. Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, He mentioned the two types to avoid specificity. And he is a believer, since the deeds of the infidels are not taken into account in deserving the reward, but rather what is expected of them is a lightening of the punishment. We will surely cause him to live a good life in this world, living a good life. If he is well-off, then it is apparent, and if he is poor, his life is good due to contentment and satisfaction with the division and expecting a great reward in the Hereafter, unlike the infidel, for if he is poor, then it is apparent, and if he is well-off, greed and fear of missing out do not allow him to enjoy his life. And it was said in the Hereafter. And We will surely give them their reward according to the best of what they used to do of obedience.
16:98: 98. "So if you recite the Qur'an "if you want to recite it, as God the Almighty says: "When you rise to prayer seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed" then ask God to protect you from his whispers so that he does not whisper to you in the recitation, and the majority are of the opinion that it is recommended. And in it is evidence that the one praying seeks refuge in every rak'ah because the ruling resulting from a condition is repeated by its repetition by analogy, and his following that with a good deed and a promise for it is an indication that seeking refuge when reciting is of this type. And on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud "I recited to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: I seek refuge in the All-Hearing, All-Knowing from Satan, the accursed, so he said: Say: I seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed. This is how Gabriel recited it to me from the pen from the Preserved Tablet."
16:99: 99. He has no authority authority and guardianship over those who believe and rely on their Lord over the friends of God Almighty who believe in Him and rely on Him, for they do not obey His commands nor accept His whisperings except in what they despise, rarely and out of heedlessness. For this reason they were commanded to seek refuge, so He mentioned authority after the command to seek refuge so that it would not be imagined that He has authority.
16:100: 100. His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian who love him and obey him. And those who associate others with Him with God or because of Satan associate others with Him.
16:101: 101. "And if We substitute a verse for another" by abrogation, so We make the abrogating verse in place of the abrogated one in wording or ruling. "And God knows best what is sent down" of interests. Perhaps what is an interest at one time becomes a corruption afterwards, so He abrogates it, and what is not an interest at that time is an interest now, so He establishes it in its place. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read "It is sent down" with a light pronunciation. "They said" meaning the disbelievers. "You are only a slanderer" who is making up false statements about God, commanding something and then it changes to you, so you forbid it. The answer to "if And God knows best what is sent down" is an objection to rebuke the disbelievers for what they say and to draw attention to the corruption of their chain of transmission. It is possible that it is a state. "Rather, most of them do not know" the wisdom of the rulings and do not distinguish between right and wrong.
16:102: 102. "Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down" meaning Gabriel, peace be upon him, and adding the spirit to the Holy, which is purity, is like their saying: Hatim al-Jud. Ibn Kathir read the Holy Spirit with a light pronunciation. In "yanzil and nazzaluhu" there is a warning that its revelation is gradual according to interests, which necessitates change. "From your Lord in truth" is mixed with wisdom. "To confirm those who believe" so that God confirms those who believe in the belief that it is His word, and that if they hear the abrogator and reflect on what is in it of taking care of righteousness and wisdom, their beliefs will be established and their hearts will be reassured. "And guidance and good tidings for the Muslims who submit to His rule, and they are conjoined with the place of lithbat" meaning confirmation, guidance and good tidings, and in it there is an allusion to the occurrence of the opposites of that for others. "lithbat" was read with a light pronunciation.
16:103: 103. And We know that they say, 'It is only a human being who teaches him.' They mean Jabran the Roman, the slave of Amir ibn al-Hadrami. It was said that Jabran and Yasar used to make swords in Mecca and read the Torah and the Gospel, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pass by them and listen to what they read. It was said that Aisha, the slave of Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza, had converted to Islam and was a bookkeeper. It was also said that Salman the Persian. The tongue of the one they incline to is foreign. The language of the man to whom they incline their speech away from righteousness, taken from the word lakhd al-grave. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read yalahdun with the opening of the ya’ and the ha’, a foreign tongue that is not clear. And this and this Qur’an “a clear Arabic tongue” with clarity and eloquence. The two sentences are resumed to refute their criticism, and its confirmation has two possible meanings: one of them is that what he heard from him was foreign speech that neither he nor you understand, and the Qur’an is Arabic, you understand it with the slightest contemplation, so how could what he received from him be? The second: Suppose that he learned the meaning from him by listening to his speech, but did not receive the wording from him, because that was foreign and this is Arabic, and the Qur’an, as it is miraculous in terms of meaning, is miraculous in terms of wording, although the many sciences in the Qur’an cannot be learned except by staying with an outstanding teacher, and those sciences are for a long period, so how could he learn all of that from a vulgar boy who heard from him during some of the times he passed by foreign words that they perhaps did not know their meaning, and their criticism of the Qur’an with such weak words is evidence of the utmost inability.
16:104: 104. Those who do not believe in the verses of God do not believe that they are from God. God does not guide them to the truth or to the path of salvation. It was said to Paradise. And for them is a painful punishment in the Hereafter. He threatened them for their disbelief in the Qur'an after he had removed their doubts and responded to their attacks on it, then he turned the matter back on them and said:
16:105: 105. Only those who do not believe in the signs of God invent lies because they do not fear a punishment that will deter them from it. And those referring to those who disbelieved or to the Quraysh, are the liars meaning the liars in truth, or the complete liars because denying the signs of God and attacking them with these superstitions is the greatest lie, or those whose habit is lying and neither religion nor chivalry turns them away from it, or the liars in their saying: You are only an inventer "only a human being knows it."
16:106: 106. Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief instead of those who do not believe and what is between them is an objection, or of those or of liars, or a subject whose predicate is omitted and indicated by his saying: upon them is wrath and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with a deleted answer and indicated by his saying: except for he who is forced to slander or the word of disbelief, a connected exception because disbelief in language includes speech and belief like faith. And his heart is reassured by faith his belief did not change, and in it is evidence that faith is belief in the heart. But whoever opens his chest to disbelief believes it and is pleased with it. Upon them is wrath from God and for them is a great punishment because there is nothing greater than his crime, "It was narrated that the Quraysh forced Ammar and his parents Yasir and Sumayyah to apostatize, so they tied Sumayyah between two camels and a spear was brought to her vagina and they said: You have converted to Islam for the sake of men So he was killed, and they killed Yasir, and they were the first two people to be killed in Islam, and Ammar gave them with his tongue what they wanted, by force. So it was said: O Messenger of God, Ammar has disbelieved. He said: No, Ammar is filled with faith from his head to his feet, and faith has mixed with his flesh and blood. So Ammar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was crying, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to wipe his eyes and say: What is the matter with you if they return to you? Return to them what you said. It is evidence of the permissibility of speaking blasphemy when forced, even though it is better to avoid it out of respect for the religion, as his parents did, because “It was narrated that Musaylimah took two men and said to one of them: What do you say about Muhammad? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you say about me? He said: You. So he left him alone. He said to the other: What do you say about Muhammad? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you say about me? He said: I am deaf. So he repeated it to him three times, and he repeated his answer, so he killed him. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: As for the first, he took God’s permission, and as for the second, he spoke the truth, so congratulations to him.”
16:107: 107. That refers to disbelief after faith or the threat. Because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter because they preferred it over it. And that God does not guide the disbelieving people meaning the disbelievers in His knowledge to what necessitates the steadfastness of faith, nor does He protect them from deviation.
16:108: 108. Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing and sight God has sealed, so they are unable to perceive the truth and contemplate it. And those are the heedless, completely heedless, as the current state has made them forget to consider the consequences.
16:109: 109. There is no doubt that in the Hereafter they will be the losers, because they wasted their lives and spent them on what led them to eternal torment.
16:111: 111. The Day every soul will come is governed by Raheem or by Remembrance. "It will argue for itself argues for itself and strives for its salvation, not caring about the affairs of others, so it will say, My soul, my soul. And every soul will be fully compensated for what it has done" the recompense for what it has done. "And they will not be wronged" their rewards will not be reduced.
16:112: 112. "And God sets forth a parable of a city" meaning He made it an example for every people upon whom God bestowed His blessings, but they were arrogant and disbelieved, so God sent down His punishment upon them, or upon Mecca. "Its people were safe and secure" no fear would disturb them. "Its provisions would come to it its food in abundance in abundance from every place" from its regions. "So it disbelieved in the blessings of God By His blessings" is the plural of blessing without considering the taa' like dir' and adra', or the plural of na'am like misery and misery. "So God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear" He borrowed taste to perceive the effect of harm, and clothing for what covered them and encompassed them of hunger and fear, and He made the taste appear on it by looking at what was borrowed for it like the saying of Kathir: Omar Al-Rada, if he smiles and laughs, the necks of money will be closed because of his laughter He borrowed the cloak for the good deed because it protects the honor of its owner as the cloak protects what is thrown at him, and he added to it the immersion, which is a description of the good deed and the bounty, not a description of the cloak, in view of what it is borrowed for. And the borrowed may be looked at as in his saying: My cloak is being disputed by Abd Amr. Take it easy, brother of Amr ibn Bakr. I have the half that my right hand possesses, and you can take half of it. He borrowed the cloak for his sword, then he said, looking at the borrowed garment, Because of what they were doing.
16:113: 113. And there had come to them a Messenger from among themselves meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the pronoun refers to the people of Mecca, referring back to their mention after mentioning their likes. But they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers meaning that the state of their confusion with wrongdoing and punishment was what befell them of severe drought, or the Battle of Badr.
16:114: 114. So eat of what God has provided for you, lawful and good. He commanded them to eat what God has made lawful for them and to be thankful for what He has bestowed upon them after He warned them against disbelief and threatened them with what He mentioned of the example and punishment that befell them, to deter them from the actions of ignorance and its corrupt doctrines. And be thankful for the favor of God if it is Him you worship. You obey, or if your claim is correct that you mean by worshipping the gods to worship Him.
16:115: 115. "He has only forbidden you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limits] - then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful." When He commanded them to eat what He had made lawful for them, He enumerated for them His prohibitions so that they would know that everything else was lawful for them. Then He emphasized that by forbidding what is forbidden and what is permitted according to their whims, saying:
16:116: 116. And do not say about what your tongues describe falsely, 'This is lawful and this is unlawful,' as they said, What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males, the verse. The context of the speech and the introduction of the sentence with "that the forbidden things are limited to the four types, except for what is added to it by evidence: such as wild beasts and domestic donkeys." The accusative of lie with and do not say and this is lawful and this is unlawful is a substitute for it or related to describe with the intention of saying, meaning: And do not say lies about what your tongues describe, so you say this is lawful and this is unlawful, or the object of do not say, and lie is accusative with describe and what is a source, meaning: And do not say this is lawful and this is unlawful due to your tongues describing lies, meaning: Do not forbid or permit based on a mere statement uttered by your tongues without evidence. And their tongues describing lies is an exaggeration, so their speech is described as lies as if the reality of the lie was unknown and your tongues describe it and know it. With their words, and therefore it is considered correct speech like their saying: her face describes beauty and her eyes describe magic. And lie was read in the accusative instead of what and lie is the plural of lieber or liar in the nominative as an attribute of tongues and in the accusative as a censure or in the sense of false words. To invent lies against God is an explanation that does not include the purpose. Indeed, those who invent lies against God will not succeed. Since the complainant invents lies to achieve a desired goal, he negated success from them and explained it by saying:
16:117: 117. A brief enjoyment means that what they invent for the sake of it or what they are in is a brief benefit that will soon cease. And for them is a painful punishment in the Hereafter.
16:118: 118. And We have forbidden to those who are Jews what We have related to you meaning in Surat Al-An'am in His statement: And We have forbidden to those who are Jews every animal with claws "before is related to Our stories or to We have forbidden". "And We did not wrong them" by prohibiting. "But they were wronging themselves" since they did what they were punished for, and in it is a reminder of the difference between them and others in prohibition and that just as there is harm, there is punishment.
16:119: 119. Then your Lord is for those who did evil in ignorance because of it or involved in it so that ignorance of God and His punishment and lack of contemplation of the consequences are widespread due to the dominance of desire, and evil includes slandering God and others. Then they repented after that and reformed - indeed, your Lord is after that after repentance Forgiving of that evil Merciful rewarding for repentance.
16:120: 120. Indeed, Abraham was a nation for his perfection and the collection of virtues that are hardly found except scattered in many people, such as his saying: It is not surprising that God should unite the world into one He is the leader of the monotheists and the role model of the investigators who argued with the groups of polytheists and invalidated their deviant doctrines with conclusive arguments. Therefore, his mention was followed by falsifying the doctrines of the polytheists of polytheism and attacking the prophethood and forbidding what he permitted, or because he was the only believer and the rest of the people were disbelievers. It was said that it is a verb with the meaning of a passive participle like the journey and the elite from his mother if he intended him or followed his example, then the people would go to him to benefit and follow his conduct, like his saying: Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people “obedient to God” obedient to Him and carrying out His commands Hanif inclined away from falsehood and he was not of the polytheists as they claimed, for the Quraysh claimed that they were on the religion of Abraham.
16:121: 121. Grateful for His blessings. He mentioned the word few to indicate that he did not fail to thank for the few blessings, but was content with the many. He chose him for prophethood. And guided him to the straight path in calling to God.
16:122: 122. And We gave him good in this world by making him beloved to the people, so that the leaders of religions would take him as their protector and praise him, and He granted him good children and a long life in abundance and obedience. And indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous among the people of Paradise, as He asked him by saying: And join me with the righteous.
16:123: 123. Then We revealed to you O Muhammad, and then either to glorify him and to draw attention to the fact that the lawful thing that Abraham was given was to follow the religion of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to indicate the shortness of his days. To follow the religion of Abraham, upright in monotheism and calling to it with kindness and presenting evidence time after time and arguing with everyone according to his understanding. And he was not of the polytheists rather he was an example for the monotheists.
16:124: 124. The Sabbath was made to glorify the Sabbath, or to devote it to worship. Only against those who differed about it meaning against their prophet, who were the Jews.
