The reason for the prohibition is the resumption and the pronoun is either for the one killed, for he is supported in this world by the establishment of retaliation for killing him and in the hereafter by the reward, or for his guardian, for God Almighty supported him by making retaliation obligatory for him and commanding the guardians to assist him, or for the one killed by the guardian excessively by making retaliation obligatory or punishment and sin upon the one who was excessive.
17:34: 34. And do not approach the property of an orphan let alone dispose of it. Except in a way that is best. Except in a way that is best. Until he reaches maturity. The limit for the permissibility of the disposal indicated by the exception. And fulfill the covenant with what God has promised you of its obligations, or what you have promised and other things. The covenant was asked about required, the covenanted one is asked not to waste it and to fulfill it, or he is responsible for it, the breaker of the covenant is asked and reprimanded for it, why did you break it, or the covenant is asked to rebuke the breaker, as it is said to the buried girl, For what sin were you killed? So it is an imaginary and it is permissible, or it is intended that the owner of the covenant was responsible.
17:35: 35. And give full measure when you measure and do not cheat therein. And weigh with a straight balance with a sound balance, and it is Roman and Arab, and that does not detract from the Arabic language of the Qur’an, because if the Arabs use a foreign word and make it follow their language in grammar, definiteness, indefiniteness, and the like, it becomes Arabic. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read with a kasra on the qaf here and in Ash-Shu’ara’: That is better and more suitable for interpretation and the best consequence is a verb from the root al if it returns.
17:36: 36. And do not stop and do not follow. It was read and do not stop from qaf athrahhu if he followed him and from it the qafah. That which you have no knowledge of unless your knowledge is related to it by imitation or guessing, and it was used as evidence by those who forbade following conjecture and their answer is that what is meant by knowledge is the preponderant belief derived from a chain of transmission, whether it is certainty or conjecture and its use in this meaning is permissible and common. It was said that it is specific to beliefs. It was said to be stoning and false testimony and it is supported by his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, Whoever follows a believer in what is not in him, God will imprison him in the mire of destruction until he brings a way out. Al-Kumait said: I do not accuse the innocent without guilt, nor do I follow the guards if we follow them. The hearing, the sight, and the heart, all those meaning all these organs, so He treated them as rational beings because they are responsible for their conditions and bear witness to their owner. This is even though they is often used in rational beings, but since it is a collective noun, and therefore it includes both tribes, it came for others, like His saying: And live after those days He was responsible for it in all three of them is the pronoun for each, meaning each one of them was responsible for himself, meaning for what his companion did to him. The pronoun in about him may be for the source of do not stop or for the one who has hearing and sight. It was said that responsible is attributed to about him like the Almighty's saying: not those who have incurred wrath and the meaning is that his companion will be asked about him, and this is wrong because the agent and what takes its place do not come before it, and in it is evidence that the servant will be held accountable for his intention to commit a sin. And and the heart was read by changing the hamza to a waw after the damma and then replacing it with a fatha. 8- Then you will surely be asked on that Day about the pleasures that distracted you. The address is specific to everyone who is distracted by his worldly life from his religion. Pleasures is what makes him busy, as is evident from the many texts, such as His saying: Whoever is deprived of the adornment of God “Eat of the good things.” It was said that it is Ya’man, since everyone will be asked about his gratitude. It was said that the verse is specific to the disbelievers. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites ‘Alahakum’, God Almighty will not hold him accountable for the blessings He bestowed upon him in this world, and he will be given a reward as if he had recited a thousand verses.
17:37: 37. And do not walk on the earth exultantly meaning with exultation, which is swaggering. It was also read exultantly, which is more eloquent in consideration of the ruling, even though the source is more emphatic than the explicit description. Indeed, you will never tear the earth You will not make a hole in it with the force of your tread. And you will never reach the mountains in height with your arrogance, which is a mockery of the arrogant, and the reason for the prohibition is that arrogance is sheer foolishness that does not return any benefit, not in humiliation.
17:38: 38. "All of that" refers to the twenty-five mentioned qualities. From the Almighty's saying: "Do not make with God another god." And from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them: that they are written in the tablets of Moses, peace be upon him. "His evil" means what is forbidden, for the mentioned things are commands and prohibitions. The Hijazis and Basrans read "his evil as the predicate of was and the noun is the pronoun of all, and that" refers to what he specifically forbade. And based on this, his saying: "With your Lord it is disliked instead of his evil or a description of it carried on the meaning, for it means bad and it has been read with it, and it is permissible for disliked to be erected as a state of what is implied in was or in the circumstance as a description of his evil", and what is meant by it is the hated opposite to the sick, not what is opposite to what is intended, so that the decisive proof is established that all events occur by His Almighty will.
17:39: 39. That refers to the previous rulings. From what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom which is knowing the truth for its own sake and the goodness to act upon it. And do not make with God another god repeated it to draw attention to the fact that monotheism is the beginning and end of the matter, for whoever has no intention, his knowledge is invalidated, and whoever intends to do it or someone else leaves it, his effort is lost, and that it is the head of wisdom and its angel, and He first arranged for it what will result in polytheism in this world and second what will be its outcome in the hereafter, so God Almighty said: Then you will be thrown into Hell, blamed blaming yourself. Rejected banished from the mercy of God Almighty.
17:40: 40. Has your Lord chosen you with sons? Addressing those who say that the angels are the daughters of God, the hamza is for denial and the meaning is: Your Lord has chosen you with the best of children, which are the sons. And He took from the angels females daughters for Himself, and this is contrary to what your minds and customs are based on. Indeed, you are saying a terrible word by attributing children to Him, which is specific to some bodies due to their quick disappearance, then by detailing yourselves to Him where you make for Him what you dislike, then He makes the angels, who are among the most noble of God's creation, the lowest of them.
17:41: 41. And We have certainly diverted We have repeated this meaning in several ways from the report. In this Qur'an in several places in it, and it is possible that what is meant by this Qur'an is the nullification of the addition of daughters to it on the assumption: And We have certainly diverted this statement in this for a meaning or We have placed diversion in it, and We have diverted was read with the alleviation. So that they may remember So that they may remember, and Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read here and in Al-Furqan So that they may remember from the remembrance which is in the meaning of remembrance. And it only increases them in aversion from the truth and lack of reassurance with it.
17:42: 42.. "Say, 'If there were with Him gods as they say,' O polytheists,' and Ibn Kathir and Hafs from Asim read with the letter 'ya' in it and what follows it on the basis that the speech is with the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he addresses the polytheists with it, and the second is from what he exonerated himself from their statement. Then they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne is an answer to their statement and a reward for if, and the meaning is: they would have sought a way to the One who is the Owner of the Kingdom by honoring one another as kings do with one another, or by drawing near to Him and obeying Him because of their knowledge of His power and their inability as God Almighty says: Those are the ones whom they call upon, seeking a means of access to their Lord.
17:43: 43. Glory be to Him. He is absolutely exalted. "He is far above what they say, far removed from what they say, for He is in the highest ranks of existence, which is that He is the Necessary Being and Eternal for Himself, and taking a son is from His lowest ranks, for it is from the special ones whose eternity is impossible.
17:44: 44. "The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise." He purifies Him from what is necessary for possibility and the consequences of occurrence by means of the language of the state, as it indicates its possibility and occurrence to the ancient Creator who is necessary for Himself. But you do not understand their glorification, O polytheists, because you have failed to use the correct consideration by which their glorification is understood. It is permissible to carry glorification on the common ground between the word and the meaning, as it is attributed to what the word can be imagined from and to what cannot be imagined from it, and on them according to those who permit the application of the word to its two meanings. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Nafi', and Abu Bakr read glorifying with the letter ya. "Indeed, He was Forbearing," as He did not hasten to punish you for your heedlessness and polytheism. "Forgiving" to whoever among you repents.
17:45: 45. "And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a veil" that prevents them from understanding what you recite to them. "Concealed" means concealment, as in the Almighty's saying: "His promise is coming. And their saying a torrential flood, or concealed from the senses, or with another veil that they do not understand", that they do not understand, is a denial from them that they understand what was revealed to them of verses after He denied them the understanding of the evidences that are established in the souls and horizons, confirming it and clarifying that they are imprinted with misguidance, as He stated in His saying:
17:46: 46. "And We placed over their hearts coverings" covering them and preventing them from realizing the truth and accepting it. "That they should not understand it" hating that they should understand it. It is permissible that it is the object of what is indicated by His statement: "And We placed over their hearts coverings" meaning that We prevented them from understanding it. "And in their ears deafness" preventing them from listening to it. Since the Qur'an is miraculous in terms of wording and meaning, it was proven to its deniers that which prevents them from understanding the meaning and realizing the wording. "And if you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an" one, not supported by their gods, a source that takes the place of a state and its origin is yahidun wahda meaning one alone. "And they turned their backs in aversion" fleeing from listening to monotheism and aversion or turning away, and it is permissible that it is the plural of nafir like qa'id and qa'ud.
17:47: 47. We know best what they listen to because of it and for its sake of mocking you and the Qur'an. When they listen to you is an adverb for I know and so is And when they are whispering meaning We know best their purpose in listening when they are listening to you, implying it and when they are whispering about it, and whispering is a source and it is possible that it is the plural of whispered "When the wrongdoers say, You follow none but a man bewitched is understood by mention, or instead of When they are whispering by placing the wrongdoers in place of the pronoun to indicate that their whispering about what they say is from the category of injustice, and the bewitched is the one who is bewitched so his mind is gone. It was said that he who has magic is the lung, meaning except a man who breathes and eats and drinks like you.
17:48: 48. "Look how they have given you examples." They have given you examples of the poet, the magician, the soothsayer, and the one who is tempted. "They have strayed" from the truth in all of that. "They cannot find a way" to a directed attack, so they rush and stumble like someone who is confused about his situation and does not know what to do or what to do.
17:49: 49. "And they said, 'When we are bones and debris, shall we then be resurrected as a new creation?'" In denial and exclusion of what is between the freshness of the living and the dryness of the decayed, of distance and contradiction, and the factor in if is what is indicated by resurrected, not itself, because what comes after if does not work on what comes before it, and "creation" is a source of mud.
17:50: 50. "Say" in response to them. "Be stones or iron."
17:51: 51. "Or a creation of that which is too great for you to accept life because it is the furthest thing from it, for His Almighty power is not short of reviving you because bodies share in accepting rejection, so how would it be if you were bones that were laid down and had been tender and lined with life before, and the thing is more receptive to what was known in it than what was not known. Then they will say, Who will bring us back? Say, He who created you the first time. And you were dust, and what is more distant than that is life. "Then they will shake their heads at you." They will move them toward you in amazement and mockery. "And they will say, When will it be? Say, Perhaps it will be soon. For everything that is coming is near. Its accusative is as a predicate or circumstance, meaning it will be in a near time. And is the name of perhaps or its predicate, and the name is implied.
17:52: 52. "The Day He calls you and you respond" meaning the Day He resurrects you and you are resurrected. He used the terms supplication and response to indicate their speed and ease, and that the purpose of them is to bring them to account and be rewarded. "With His praise" is a state of them, meaning praising God Almighty for the perfection of His power, as it was said that they shake the dust off their heads and say: Glory be to You, O God, and with Your praise, or submitting to His resurrection as those who praise Him submit. "And you think that you have remained only a little" and you think that the length of your stay in the graves is short, like the one who passed by a village. Or the length of your life because of what you see of the terror.
17:53: 53. "And tell My servants to say that which is best and not to be harsh with the polytheists. Indeed, Satan induces dissension among them, so perhaps being harsh with them will lead to stubbornness and increased corruption. Indeed, Satan has been to mankind a clear enemy."
17:54: 54. "Your Lord knows you best. If He wills, He will have mercy on you, or if He wills, He will punish you. This is an explanation of that which is best." And what is between them is an interruption, meaning say to them this word and something similar, and do not state that they are from the people of the Fire. For it will incite them to evil, even though the outcome of their affair is unknown and no one knows except God. "And We have not sent you over them as a guardian." You are entrusted with their affair and forcing them to believe. Rather, We have sent you as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, so be gentle with them and command your companions to bear with them. It was narrated that the polytheists went too far in harming them, so they complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this was revealed. It was said that one of them insulted Umar, may God be pleased with him, and he intended to do so, but God commanded him to forgive him.
17:55: 55. And your Lord is most knowing of those in the heavens and the earth and of their conditions, so He chooses from among them for His prophethood and guardianship whomever He wishes, and this is a response to the Quraish’s rejection of the orphan of Abu Talib being a prophet, and that the naked and hungry ones were his companions. And We have certainly preferred some prophets over others with spiritual virtues and disavowal of physical relationships, not with an abundance of wealth and followers, even David, peace be upon him, for his honor was in what was revealed to him of the Book, not in what he was given of kingship. It was said that it is an indication of the preference of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. His statement, And We gave David the Psalms is an indication of the reason for his preference, which is that he is the Seal of the Prophets and his nation is the best of nations, indicated by what was written in the Psalms that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants. Its indefiniteness here and its definition in the statement of God Almighty, And We have certainly written in the Psalms because it is originally a passive participle like milking, or a verbal noun like acceptance, and this is supported by the reading of Hamza with a dammah, which is like Abbas or Al-Fadl, or because what is meant is that We gave David some of the Psalms, or some of the Psalms in which the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, is mentioned.
17:56: 56. "Say, 'Call upon those whom you claim to be gods besides Him, such as the angels, the Messiah, and Ezra. But they have no power, nor can they remove harm from you, such as sickness, poverty, and famine. Nor can they transfer it from you to others.'
17:57: 57. Those who call upon God seek a means of approach to their Lord. These gods seek closeness to God through obedience. Which of them is nearest? instead of and "seek meaning whoever is nearest to God seeks a means of approach, so how can anyone but the nearest suffice? And they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment like all other servants, so how can you claim that they are gods? Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to be feared" truly, so that everyone should be wary of it, even the messengers and angels.
17:58: 58. "And there is no town but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection" by death and extermination. "Or punish it with a severe punishment" by killing and various types of affliction. "That was in the Book in the Preserved Tablet inscribed" written.
17:59: 59. And what prevented Us from sending the signs What prevented Us from sending the signs that the Quraysh proposed. Except that the former peoples denied them Except the denial of the former peoples who were like them in nature, such as Aad and Thamud, and that if it had been sent, they would have denied it as those people denied it, and they deserved to be exterminated according to what Our way has passed, and We have decreed that We should not exterminate them, because among them are those who believe or give birth to those who believe. Then he mentioned some of the nations that were destroyed by denying the proposed signs, so he said: And We gave Thamud the she-camel because of their question. Clear with sight or insight, or We made them people of insight. And it was read with the fat-ha. So they wronged themselves with it so they disbelieved in it, or they wronged themselves because of hamstringing it. And We do not send the signs meaning the suggested signs. Except as a warning of the descent of the exterminating torment, so if they do not fear, it will be sent down or with other than the suggested ones like the miracles and verses of the Qur’an except as a warning of the torment of the Hereafter, for the matter of those to whom it was sent is postponed until the Day of Resurrection, and the ya’ is added or in the position of the state and the object is deleted.
17:60: 60. And when We said to you, And remember when We revealed to you, Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people so they are in the grip of His power, or He encompassed the Quraysh in the sense that He destroyed them from the enemy's encirclement of them, so it is good report of the Battle of Badr and the expression in the past tense is to confirm its occurrence. And We did not make the vision which We showed you the night of the Ascension and it was interpreted by those who said that it was in a dream, and those who said that it was while awake interpreted the vision as a vision. Or the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah when he saw that he entered Mecca. And in it is that the verse is Meccan, unless it is said that he saw it in Mecca and narrated it at that time, and perhaps it was a vision that he saw during the Battle of Badr, as God Almighty said: When God showed them to you in your sleep, little by little. And as it was narrated that when he reached his water, he said, ‘It is as if I see the people’s deaths, this is the death of so-and-so, and this is the death of so-and-so.’ So the Quraysh heard about it and mocked him. And it was said, He saw a group of the Umayyads climbing his pulpit and jumping on it like monkeys, so he said, ‘This is their share of the world, which they give it through their Islam.’ And based on this, what was meant by his saying: Except as a trial for the people was what happened in their days. And the cursed tree in the Qur’an. In reference to the vision, which is the tree of Zaqqum, when the polytheists heard its mention, they said that Muhammad claims that Hell burns stones, then he says that trees grow in it. They did not know that He who was able to protect the fur of the salamander from being consumed by the fire, and the entrails of the ostrich from the harm of the embers and the pieces of red-hot iron that it swallows, was able to create a tree in Hell that would not burn it. And its curse in the Qur’an is the curse of those who eat it, and it was described as such by metaphor for exaggeration, or it was described as being at the bottom of Hell, for it is the furthest place from mercy, or as being hated and harmful, from their saying cursed food, for it is harmful. It was interpreted as referring to Satan, Abu Jahl, and Al-Hakam bin Abi Al-Aas, and it was read in the nominative case as the subject, and the predicate is omitted, meaning that the cursed tree in the Qur’an is likewise. And We frighten them with various types of frightening. But it only increases them in great transgression, except insolence that exceeds seriousness. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 16 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Isrā, and the first verses of Sūrat Maryam. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 17:61: 61. "And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He said, 'Shall I prostrate to one You created from clay?'" For one You created from clay, so the subject is removed by removing the preposition. It is possible that it is a state of the one referring back to the relative pronoun, meaning I created him while he was clay, or of it, meaning should I prostrate to him, and its root is clay. And in it, in all three ways, there is an allusion to the reason for the denial.
17:62: 62. He said, Have you seen this one whom You have honored over me?" The kaf is for emphasis of the address and has no syntactic position. This is the object of "or and whom" is its description, and the second object is omitted because its connection to it indicates it. The meaning is, "Inform me about this one whom You have honored over me by ordering me to prostrate to him, why have You honored him over me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection" is a subjective statement, and the lam is used to introduce the oath, and its answer is: "I will surely destroy his offspring, except for a few." That is, I will surely eradicate them by seduction, except for a few, whose strength I will not be able to resist. From the verb "ahtanaqat" the locusts to strip the earth of what is on it by eating. It is taken from "hanak" palate. Rather, it is known that this will be easy for him, either by deduction from the angels' statement, "Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein?" with the confirmation, or by insight into his creation, who is delusional, lustful, and angry.
17:63: 63. "He said, 'Go.' Go to what you intended, which was expulsion and leaving him alone with whatever his soul tempted him to do. 'And whoever follows you among them, then Hell is your recompense.' Your recompense and their recompense, so the one addressed predominated over the absent one, and it is possible that the address is to the followers on the shift. 'A full recompense.' Complementing their saying, 'Give your companion his honor.' The accusative of recompense is on the source by implying its action or by what is in 'your recompense.' Of the meaning that you will be recompensed, or a state that prepares for his saying, 'full recompense.'
17:64: 64.And provoke and belittle. Whom you can of them to provoke and the light fright. With your voice with your call to corruption. And bring them and shout at them from the noise which is shouting. If you withheld for fear of spending you would be stingy for fear of exhaustion through hypocrisy, since there is no one who does not choose benefit for himself, and if he prefers someone else with something, he only prefers it for a greater compensation, so he is stingy in comparison to the generosity and kindness of God Almighty. "On the authority of Safwan, that a Jew asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about them, and he said: That you do not associate anything with God, and do not be extravagant, and do not commit adultery, and do not kill the soul that God has forbidden except by right, and do not practice magic, and do not consume usury, and do not walk with an innocent person to a person in authority to kill him, and do not accuse a chaste woman, and do not flee from battle. These are the companions of the king’s right hand, and Marnoush, Dabarnoush and Shadhnush are the companions of his left hand, and he used to consult them. The seventh is the shepherd who agreed with them and the name of their dog is Qatmir and the name of their city is Ephesus. It was said that the three sayings are for the People of the Book and a few of them. Do not dispute about them except with an apparent dispute. So do not dispute about the youths except with an apparent dispute that is not deep, which is that you tell them what is in the Qur’an without making them ignorant or refuting them. And do not consult any of them about them. Do not ask any of them about their story with a question seeking guidance, for in what has been revealed to you there is an alternative to something else, even though they have no knowledge of it. Do not ask a stubborn question that wants to expose the one being asked and falsify what he has, for that is a violation of good morals.
18:23: 23. And do not say of anything, 'I will do that tomorrow', except, 'If God wills.' This is a prohibition of discipline from God Almighty to His Prophet when the Jews said to the Quraysh 106:Ask him about the Spirit, the People of the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn. They asked him, and he said: Come to me tomorrow, I will tell you. He did not make an exception, so the revelation was delayed for him by a dozen or so sleeps until it was difficult for him and the Quraysh denied him. The exception to the prohibition is that do not say of anything you intend to do, 'I will do it in the future' except with If God wills, that is, except when mixed with His will, saying, 'If God wills,' or except at the time when God wills that you say it, meaning that He gives you permission to do it. It is not permissible to make it conditional on an agent because the exception of the conjunction of the will with the action is not sound, and the exception of its objection without it does not suit the prohibition.
18:24: 24. And remember your Lord the will of your Lord and say, If God wills. As it was narrated that when it was revealed, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said, If God wills. "If you forget" if you forget something and then remember it, and from Ibn Abbas even after a year, as long as he did not break his oath, and therefore it is permissible to delay the exception from it. The majority of jurists are of the opposite view because if that were correct, then no acknowledgment, divorce, or emancipation would be established, and truthfulness or falsehood would not be known. The verse and the report do not indicate that the exception made up for by it is from the previous statement, but rather it is from an implied meaning, and it is permissible for the meaning to be, "And remember your Lord with glorification and seeking forgiveness if you forget the exception is an exaggeration in urging it, or remember your Lord and His punishment if you leave some of what He commanded you to do so that He may urge you to make up for it, or remember Him if you are overcome by forgetfulness so that He may remind you of what was forgotten. And say, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to a path nearer to right conduct than this.’ To a path nearer to right conduct and clearer evidence that a prophet is from the story of the People of the Cave. And He guided him to something greater than that, such as the stories of the prophets whose days were far from him, and the report of the unseen and the events that will befall in the coming ages until the Day of Resurrection. Or to a path nearer to right conduct and closer to good than that which was forgotten.
18:25: 25. And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine. That is, they remained in it alive, their ears covered with blood, and this is an explanation of what was summarized before. It was said that it is a narration of the speech of the People of the Book, for they differed in the length of their stay, just as they differed in their number. Some of them said three hundred, and some of them said three hundred and nine years. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read three hundred years with the addition of the plural in place of the singular, and what is good here is that the sign of the plural in it is a compensation for what was deleted from the singular, and that the origin of the number is its addition to the plural, and whoever did not add the years replaced three hundred.
18:26: 26. "Say: God knows best how long they stayed. To Him belong the unseen of the heavens and the earth." To Him belongs whatever is hidden in them and concealed of the conditions of their inhabitants, so no creation is hidden from Him in knowledge. I see it and I hear. It is mentioned in the form of astonishment to indicate that His command in perception is outside of what the hearers and seers perceive, since nothing veils Him and nothing differs from Him, subtle and dense, small and large, hidden and clear. The ha refers to God and its place is in the nominative case as an agent, and the ba is an addition according to Sibawayh. Its original form was absara meaning he became sighted, then it was transferred to the imperative form with the meaning of creating, so the pronoun appeared because the form was not suitable for it or because of the addition of ba as in the Almighty's saying And it is sufficient for Him. The accusative case is an object according to Al-Akhfash, and the agent is the pronoun of the one commanded, which is everyone, and the ba is an addition if the hamza is for transitivity and transitive if it is for becoming. They have no protector refers to the people of the heavens and the earth. Besides Him, there is no guardian who takes charge of their affairs. And He does not associate anyone of them in His judgment, nor does He give him any input in it. Ibn Amir and Qaloon read on the authority of Yaqub with the ta’ of the jussive, prohibiting everyone from associating partners. Then, when the Qur’an included the story of the People of the Cave, in that it is one of the unseen matters, in addition to the Messenger of God, indicating that it is a miraculous revelation, He commanded him to continue his studies and to stick with his companions, so He said:
18:27: 27. And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord of the Qur'an, and do not listen to their saying, Bring a Qur'an other than this or change it. "There is no changing His words" no one is able to change them or alter them except Him. "And you will not find any refuge other than Him" a refuge to Him if you intend to do so.
18:28: 28. "And be patient with yourself" and restrain it and make it steadfast. "With those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening" at their appointed times, or at the two ends of the day. Ibn Amir read "al-Ghadwah and in it that al-Ghadwah is a name in most cases, so the lam" in it is interpreted as indefinite. "They desire His countenance" the pleasure of God and His obedience. "And let not your eyes pass beyond them and let not your gaze pass beyond them to others, and its transitivity with an" is to include the meaning of report. And it was read "And let not your eyes pass and And let not the countenance from He prepared it and He prepared it". What is meant is that the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is forbidden to despise the poor believers and to look down on their shabby clothing in aspiration for the freshness of the clothing of the rich. You want the adornment of the worldly life is a state of the kaf in the famous and of the hidden in the verb in other than it. And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless “of Our remembrance” like Umayyah ibn Khalaf in your call to expel the poor from your gathering for the leaders of Quraysh. And in it is a warning that what prompted him to this call was his heart’s heedlessness of rational matters and his preoccupation with the sensible, until it was hidden from him that honor is in the adornment of the soul and not in the adornment of the body, and that if he had obeyed him, he would have been like him in stupidity. The Mu’tazilites, when they were angered by the attribution of heedlessness to God Almighty, said: It is like you answered him if you found him like that or attributed it to Him, or someone who neglected his camels if he left them without a mark, meaning we did not mark him with Our remembrance, like the hearts of those in whose hearts We wrote faith. And they argued that what is meant is not the apparent meaning of what was mentioned first by his saying: And follow His passion, and the answer to it was not mentioned more than once. And it was read Aghalana by attributing the action to the heart, meaning we considered his heart to be heedless of our reminding him of the punishment. And his affair was a fart, meaning he was ahead of the truth and cast it behind his back. It is said: a fart horse, meaning he is ahead of horses, and from it the fart.
18:29: 29. And say, 'The truth is from your Lord.' The truth is that which comes from God, not that which is dictated by desire. It is possible that the truth is the predicate of a deleted subject, and from your Lord is a state. So whoever wills - let him believe, and whoever wills - let him disbelieve. I do not care about the belief of whoever believes, nor the disbelief of whoever disbelieves. It does not require the servant to act independently, for even if it is by his will, his will is not by his will. Indeed, We have prepared. For the wrongdoers, a fire whose pavilion will surround them. Its pavilion is likened to what surrounds them of the fire. It was said that the pavilion is the room that is around the pavilion. It was said that its pavilion is its smoke, and it was said that it is a wall of fire. And if they call for help from thirst. They are helped with water like molten metal like a melted body. It was said that it is like the dregs of oil, and it is in the manner of His saying: So take refuge in the burning sand. "It burns faces" if it is presented to drink from its extreme heat, and it is a second description of water or a state of the mahal or the pronoun in the kaf. "Bad is the drink" the mahal. "And bad" the fire. "Resting place is reclining, and the origin of erfacing is the erection of the elbow under the cheek, and it is to meet his saying And good resting place" otherwise there is no erfacing for the people of the fire.
18:30: 30. Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - never will We allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds. The predicate of the first in and the second in is what is included in its scope, and the referent is omitted, its meaning being whoever did well in deeds among them or it is dispensed with by the generality of whoever did well in deeds as it is dispensed with in your saying: Yes, Zaid is a good man, or it is in its apparent position, for whoever did well in deeds is not appropriate to apply it in reality except to those who believed and did righteous deeds.
18:31: 31. "They will have gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow." What is between them is an objection, and the first is a resumption to explain the reward or a second piece of report. "They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold. The first is for the beginning and the second is for the explanation, describing bracelets," and its indefiniteness is to magnify its beauty from encompassing it, which is the plural of bracelet or aswar in the plural of bracelet. "And they will wear green garments" because green is the best and most refreshing of colors. "Of fine silk and brocade" from what is fine of brocade and what is thick of it. He combined the two types to indicate that therein is what the souls desire and the eyes delight in. "Reclining therein on couches" on beds as is the state of those who enjoy themselves. "Yes, the reward" of Paradise and its delights. "And good the couches resting" reclining.
18:32: 32. And give them an example of the disbeliever and the believer. Two men is the case of two men who are estimated or existent, they are two brothers from the Children of Israel, a disbeliever named Qatrus and a believer named Judah, they inherited eight thousand dinars from their father and they shared them, the disbeliever bought with them farms and real estate and the believer spent them on charitable causes, and their situation ended up as God Almighty narrated. It was said that the two examples were two brothers from Banu Makhzum, a disbeliever, who is Al-Aswad bin Abdul-Shadd, and a believer, who is Abu Salamah Abdullah, the husband of Umm Salamah before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. We made for one of them two gardens two orchards. Of grapes of vineyards, and the entire sentence is a statement of the example or a description of the two men. And We surrounded them with palm trees and We made the palm trees surround them, supporting their vineyards with them. It is said that the people surrounded him if they surrounded him and you surrounded him with them if you made them surround him, so the baa adds a second object. As you say: I covered it with it. “And We placed between them” in the middle of them crops so that each of them would be a collector of food and fruits, with continuous construction in a beautiful form and elegant arrangement.
18:33: 33. Both gardens produced their fruit their fruit, and the pronoun is singular because both is singular. It was read both gardens produced their fruit. "And they were not wronged by it and they did not decrease from their fruit. Anything is known in all orchards, as the fruits are complete in one year and usually decrease in the next. And We caused a river to gush forth within them so that their drinking would continue, as it is the origin and their splendor would increase. And from Yaqub, We caused a river with the lightening.
18:34: 34. And he had fruits of all kinds of wealth, other than the two gardens, from the fruits of his wealth if he increased it, and Asim read with the opening of the tha and the meem, and Abu Amr with the damma of the tha and the sukoon of the meem and the rest with the damma of them and likewise in his saying and his fruits were surrounded. "So he said to his companion while he was conversing with him" he is returning to him in speech from hara if he returned. "I am more wealthy than you and more honorable in men" retinue and helpers. And it was said male children because they are the ones who travel with him.
18:35: 35. And he entered his Paradise with his companion, walking around with him in it and boasting about it to him. The singular of Paradise is because what is meant is his Paradise and what he enjoyed of this world, indicating that he has no Paradise other than it and no share in the Paradise that the righteous are promised, or because each of his two Paradises is connected to the other, or because entering is in one by one. And he is unjust to himself harming it with his conceit and disbelief. He said, I do not think that this Paradise will ever perish that it will be destroyed. Ever because of the length of his hope, the persistence of his heedlessness, and his being deceived by his respite.
18:36: 36. And I do not think the Hour will ever come. "And if I am returned to my Lord" by resurrection as you claim. "I will surely find better than it" than his Paradise, and the Hijazis and the Shami read from them, meaning from the two Paradises. "Returning" as a return and consequence because it is transient and that is eternal, and he only swore by that because he believed that the Almighty only gave it to him because he deserved it and he deserved it for himself and he is with him wherever he meets him.
18:37: 37. "His companion said to him while he was conversing with him, 'Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust?' because it is the origin of your matter or the duration of your origin. 'Then from a sperm-drop,' because it is your immediate matter. 'Then He proportioned you as a man. 'Then He balanced you and made you a human being, a male, mature enough to be men.' He made his disbelief in the resurrection disbelief in God Almighty because its origin is doubt in the perfection of God Almighty's power. Therefore, He arranged the denial of His creation of him from dust, because He who was able to begin his creation from it was able to restore him from it.
18:38: 38. But He is God, my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord. Its original form is but I, so the hamza was deleted by transferring the vowel or without it, so the two nuns met, and there was assimilation. Ibn Amir and Yaqub read it in a narration with an alif in the connection to compensate for it from the hamza or to make the connection like a pause. It was read but I according to the original form, and it is the pronoun of the matter, and in the sentence it is the predicate of it, the predicate of I, or the pronoun God and God instead of it, and my Lord is its predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of I, and the correction from I disbelieve is as if he said: You are a disbeliever in God, but I am a believer in Him. It was read to you He is God, my Lord, but I, there is no god but He, my Lord.
18:39: 39. "And why did you not say, when you entered your garden, 'Whatever God wills'?" The matter is whatever God wills, or whatever God wills will be, on the basis that what is a relative pronoun, or whatever God wills will be, on the basis that it is conditional, and the answer is omitted, acknowledging that it and what is in it are by the will of God, if He wills He will keep it, and if He wills He will destroy it. "There is no power except with God" and I said there is no power except with God, acknowledging your inability to do anything with yourself and the power is with God, and that whatever is made easy for you of building it and managing its affairs is with His help and power. And from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "Whoever sees something and likes it and says what God wills, there is no power except with God, it will not harm him. If you see me, I am less than you in wealth and children It is possible that it is a separation and it is an emphasis of the first object, and less was read in the nominative case as the predicate of I" and the sentence is a second object of see. And in his saying and children is evidence for those who interpreted the group as children.
18:40: 40. Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden in this world or in the Hereafter for my faith, which is the answer to the condition. And send upon it upon your garden for your disbelief. A reckoning from the sky is the plural of hisbanah, which is thunderbolts. It was said that it is a source meaning reckoning, and what is meant by it is the estimation of its destruction or the punishment of the reckoning for bad deeds. So it becomes a slippery ground a smooth land on which it is slippery due to the uprooting of its plants and trees.
18:41: 41. Or its water becomes sunken meaning sunken into the ground. A source used to describe it as slippery. You will not be able to seek it for the sunken water, hesitating to return it.
18:42: 42. And his fruit was surrounded and his wealth was destroyed as his owner had expected and warned him of. It is taken from the word ahata bihu which means that if the enemy surrounded him, he overcame him, and if he overcame him, he destroyed him. Its equivalent is ahata alayhi if it destroyed him from ahata alayhim the enemy came to them if he came to them, superior to them. So he began to turn his hands from back to back in longing and regret. For what he spent in it in its construction, and it is related to turns over because turning the hands over is a metaphor for regret, so it is as if it was said: So he became regretful, or a state, i.e., regretting what he spent in it. And it is empty fallen. On its thrones because its thrones fell to the ground and the vines above it fell upon it. And he says in apposition to turns over or a state of his pronoun. Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord as if he remembered his brother’s sermon and knew that he had committed polytheism before, so he wished he had not been a polytheist so that God had not destroyed his garden. It is possible that it is repentance from polytheism and regret for what came before from him.
18:43: 43. And he had no group. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with the letter ya because it precedes it. They support him are able to support him by repelling destruction or bringing about the destroyer or bringing about something similar. Other than God because He alone is capable of that. And he was not victorious and he was not able by his strength to prevent God's vengeance against him.
18:44: 44. There in that position and that situation. The guardianship belongs to God the Truth Victory is His alone and no one else is able to do it, as is stated in His saying, And he had no company to help him or in which He helps His believing friends against the infidels, just as He helped his believing brother in what the infidel did, and this is supported by His saying, It is better in reward and better in outcome, meaning for His friends. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with the kasra, and its meaning is authority and kingship, meaning there is authority for Him, and it is not defeated or prevented, or no one else is worshipped, as in His saying, the Most High, So when they embark on a ship, they call upon God, sincere to Him in religion, so it is a warning that His saying, Oh, I wish I had not associated was out of compulsion and fear of what had befallen him. It was said, There is a reference to the Hereafter, and Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read the Truth in the nominative case as an attribute of guardianship, and it was read in the accusative case as a confirmed source, and Asim and Hamzah read Aqaba with the sukoon, and Aqba was read, and all of them mean the consequence.
18:45: 45. And give them the example of the life of this world. And mention to them what resembles the life of this world in its flowering and its quick passing or its strange characteristic. Like water is like water and it may be a second object for strike as if it means to make. We sent it down from the sky and the vegetation of the earth mingled with it so it became twisted because of it and mixed with each other because of its abundance and density, or it settled in the vegetation until it became moist and flourished. Based on this, it was right that it mingled with the vegetation of the earth, but since each of the mixed things was described by the characteristic of its companion, it was reversed to exaggerate its abundance. So it became dry straw shattered and broken. The winds scatter it scatter it, and it was read as dharā fromأذرىand the thing being compared is not the water nor its state but the quality extracted from the sentence, which is the state of the plant grown by water, it is green and lush then dry straw blown away by the winds so it becomes as if it had never been. And God is over all things from the creation And annihilation. Powerful is able.
64:14: 46. Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world. They adorn a person in his worldly life, and they will soon disappear from him. And the lasting good deeds are good deeds whose fruits will remain with him forever. It includes what was interpreted as the five daily prayers, the Hajj rituals, fasting Ramadan, Glory be to God, Praise be to God, There is no god but God, God is Greatest, and good speech. Better in the sight of your Lord than wealth and children. Reward is a return and better in hope because its owner will attain through it in the Hereafter what he hoped for in this world. 14- O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you who distract you from obeying God or quarrel with you in religious or worldly matters. So beware of them and do not feel secure from their tricks. But if you pardon their sins by not punishing them and overlook by ignoring them and not blaming them for them, and forgive by concealing them and paving the way for their excuse, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful He will treat you in the same way as you did and will be gracious to you.
18:47: 47. And the Day We set the mountains in motion And remember the Day We uproot them and set them in motion in the air, or We take them away and make them scattered dust. It is permissible to connect it to with your Lord, meaning the lasting good deeds are better with God and on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read Tasir with the ta' and the passive form. It was read Tasir from Sarat. And you see the earth exposed is apparent, protruding from beneath the mountains, with nothing covering it. It was read Watra in the passive form. And we gathered them and We have assembled them and We have gathered them to the place of standing. Its coming in the past tense after Nasir and Watra is to confirm the gathering or to indicate that their gathering was before the setting in motion so that they would witness and witness what was promised to them. According to this, the waw is for the state with the implication of qad. Falma nakharad means we did not leave. Anyone among them It is said that he left him and betrayed him if he abandoned him. From this comes the word treachery for abandoning loyalty and al-Ghadir for when the flood left it. It is also read with a ya.
18:48: 48. And they were presented to your Lord He likened their condition to the condition of soldiers presented to the ruler, not for him to know them, but for him to command them. In ranks, lined up, with no one blocking anyone else. You have come to Us on the implication of the statement in a way that is a state or an agent on the Day of Judgment. As We created you the first time naked, with nothing with you of wealth or children, as He said. And you have come to Us individually or alive, as He first created you, as He said: Rather, you claimed that We would not make for you an appointment a time to fulfill the promise of resurrection and revival, and that the prophets denied you about it, and rather to move from one story to another.
18:49: 49. And the Book was placed the records of deeds in the right and left hands or in the balance and it was said that it is a metaphor for the placement of the account. And you will see the criminals fearful afraid. of what is in it" of sins. "And they will say, Oh, woe to us calling out for their destruction which they have perished from among the destructions. What is this Book in amazement at its status. It does not leave out a small a small trifle. nor a great thing except that it has counted it except that it has enumerated it and encompassed it. And they will find what they did present written in the records. And your Lord does not wrong anyone by writing down for him what he did not do or increasing his punishment in proportion to his work.
18:50: 50. And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He repeated it in places because it is an introduction to the matters intended to be explained in that place, and here when He denounced the boasters and deemed their actions ugly, He decided that it was from the ways of Iblis, or when He explained the state of the one who is deceived by the world and turns away from it, and the reason for being deceived by it was the love of desires and the instigation of Satan. He first made them renounce the adornments of the world because they are subject to disappearance and righteous deeds are better and more lasting than themselves and are higher, then He turned them away from Satan by reminding them of the ancient enmity between them, and this is the doctrine of every repetition in the Qur’an. He was from the jinn is a state with the omission of had or a resumption of the explanation as if it was said: Why did he not prostrate, so it was said: He was from the jinn. So he disobeyed the command of his Lord so he went out of His command by not prostrating, and the fa’ is for the reason, and in it is evidence that the angel is not disobeyed at all, but Iblis disobeyed because he was originally a jinn, and the detailed discussion of it is in Surat Al-Baqarah, Do you then take him after what was found from him, you take him, and the hamza is for denial and astonishment. And his offspring his children or followers, and he called them offspring metaphorically. As allies instead of Me “So you would replace them with Me and obey them instead of obeying Me.” And they are an enemy to you, what an evil substitute for the wrongdoers for God Almighty, Iblis and his offspring,
18:51: 51. I did not make them witness to the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor to the creation of themselves. He denied bringing Iblis and his offspring to the creation of the heavens and the earth, and bringing some of them to the creation of others, to indicate the denial of relying on them for support in that, as He stated in His statement: And I would not have taken the misguiders as supporters, meaning as helpers, in response to their taking guardians other than God as partners with Him in worship, for deserving worship is a consequence of creation, and sharing in it necessitates sharing in it, so placing the misguiders in place of the pronoun is to criticize them and exclude relying on them for support. The pronoun was said to refer to the polytheists, and the meaning is: I did not make them witness to the creation of that, nor did I single them out with knowledge that no one else knows, so that if they believed, people would follow them as they claim. So do not pay attention to their statement, hoping for their support for the religion, for it is not appropriate for me to rely on the misguiders for my religion. It is supported by the reading of those who read and you were not as addressing the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was read the one who took the misguiders according to the original and ‘uddan with the alleviation and ‘uddan with the succession and ‘uddan like servants, the plural of ‘adhdh from ‘udhuhu if he strengthened him.
18:52: 52. And on the Day He will say meaning God the Most High to the disbelievers and Hamza read with the letter nun. "Call upon My partners whom you claimed" that they are My partners and your intercessors to protect you from My punishment, and adding partners according to their claim is for rebuke and what is meant is what is worshipped besides Him, and it was said that Iblis and his offspring. "So call upon them So they called upon them for relief. So they did not respond to them So they did not help them. And We made between them" between the disbelievers and their gods. "Destructive" is a destructive thing that they share in and it is the fire, or an enmity that is in its intensity destruction like the saying of Omar, may God be pleased with him: Let not your love be an obsession nor let your hatred be destruction. "Destructive is a place name or a source from to perish" if it perishes. It was said that the description is clear, meaning and We made their communication in this world destruction on the Day of Resurrection.
18:53: 53. And the criminals saw the Fire and thought and were certain that they would fall into it and mix with it, falling into it and they found no way out or place to which they could turn.
18:54: 54. And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an every kind of example of every kind that they need but man is the thing that most often comes up with argument. Argumentation" is a dispute with falsehood and its erection is a distinction.
18:55: 55. "And what prevented people from believing" from believing. "When guidance came to them" which is the messenger who calls and the clear Qur'an. "And to ask forgiveness of their Lord" from asking forgiveness for sins. "Except that the precedent of the ancients should come to them" except a request or waiting or estimation that the precedent of the ancients should come to them, which is extermination, so the noun was deleted and the noun to which it was added was placed in its place. "Or the punishment should come to them" the punishment of the Hereafter. "Qublan" clearly. The Kufians read "qablan" with two dammahs, which is a language in it or the plural of qabil meaning types, and it was read with two fathahs, which is also a language. It is said I met him, "qablan and qablan and qablan qabliyan, and its accusative is in the state of the pronoun or the punishment".
18:56: 56. "And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and warners to the believers and the disbelievers, and those who disbelieve argue with falsehood" by suggesting signs after the miracles have appeared, and asking about the story of the people of the cave and the like out of stubbornness. "To refute thereby" to remove by argument. "The truth from its place and invalidate it, from the refutation of the foot, which is its slipping, and that is their saying to the messengers You are only human beings like us And if God had willed, He would have sent down angels" and the like. "And they took My signs" meaning the Qur'an. "And what they were warned" and their warning or what they were warned of of the punishment. "in mockery" mockery. And it was read "in mockery" with sukoon, and it is what is mocked according to both estimates.
18:57: 57. And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord by the Qur'an. But turns away from them so he does not ponder them or remember them. And if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided then in fact and not by imitation because they do not understand or hear. "When they wronged" like Quraysh by denying and arguing and various types of sins. "And We appointed for their destruction an appointed time" for their destruction a time from which they will not delay an hour nor advance it, so let them take heed from them and not be deceived by the delay of the punishment from them. Abu Bakr read "for their destruction with the opening of the meem and the lam, meaning for their destruction, and Hafs read with the breaking of the lam based on what is unusual from the sources of the verb yaf'al" like the reference and the menstruation.
18:60: 60. "And when Moses said, It is estimated that I will mention. And it was said that the two seas were Moses and Al-Khidr, peace be upon them, for Moses was the sea of apparent knowledge, and Al-Khidr was the sea of hidden knowledge. And it was read with a kasra on the meem as an anomaly from the verb fa’ala like al-mashriq and al-matla’ or I pass a long time or I travel a long time, and the meaning is until it happens either the meeting is reached or the ages have passed or until I reach unless I pass a time with which I am certain that the meeting has passed, and the ages are the age and it was said eighty years and it was said seventy. It was narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, gave an eloquent sermon to the people after the destruction of the Copts and his entry into Egypt, and he was impressed by it, so it was said to him: Do you know anyone more knowledgeable than you? He said: Then which of your servants is most just? He said: The one who judges with truth and does not follow desire. He said: Then which of your servants is most knowledgeable? He said: The one who seeks the knowledge of the people to his knowledge, perhaps he will find a word that will guide him to guidance or turn him away from ruin. He said: If there is among your servants the most knowledgeable From me, so show me to him. He said, I know Al-Khidr better than you. He said, Where can I look for him? So they went walking.
18:61: 61. When they reached the junction between them meaning the junction of the two seas, and between them is a circumstance added to it for the sake of expansion or in the sense of connection. They forgot their fish Moses, peace be upon him, forgot to ask for it and find out about its condition, and Joshua forgot to mention to him what he saw of its life and its falling into the sea. It was narrated: Moses, peace be upon him, slept, and the grilled fish became agitated and jumped into the sea as a miracle for Moses or Al-Khidr. It was said that Joshua performed ablution from the spring of life, and the water gushed over him, so he came back to life and jumped into the water. It was said that they forgot to check on his condition and what would be a sign of attaining what was sought. So he took his way in the sea, a path. So the fish took his way in the sea, a path from His saying, and he traveled by day. It was said that God stopped the flow of water over the fish, so it became like a canopy over it, and poured it on the second object, and in the sea is a state of it or of the path, and it is permissible for it to be connected to took.

It is an apology for forgetting it because Satan occupied him with his whispers, and the situation, although it was amazing, the likes of which are not forgotten, but when he was harmed by seeing similar things with Moses and became accustomed to them, his interest in it decreased, and perhaps he forgot that because he was absorbed in insight and attracted by the evil of his evil to the side of holiness because of what he was stripped of from seeing the dazzling signs, and he attributed it to Satan to belittle himself or because the inability of strength to bear both sides and its preoccupation with one of them rather than the other is considered a deficiency. And he took his way in the sea a wonder a wonderful way, which is that it is like a flock or taking a wonder, and the second object is the circumstance and it was said that it is the source of his implied action, meaning he said at the end of his speech, or Moses in his answer a wonder of amazement at that situation. It was said that the action was attributed to Moses, meaning that Moses took the path of the whale in the sea as a wonder.
18:64: 64. "He said that meaning the matter of the fish what we were seeking" we seek because it is a sign of what was sought. "So they returned on their tracks" they returned on the path they came on. "Stories" they tell stories meaning they follow their tracks following, or retributing until they came to the rock.
18:65: 65. "So they found one of Our servants." The majority of scholars agree that he was Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, and his name was Balya bin Malkan. It was also said that he was Al-Yasa'. It was also said that he was Elias. "We gave him mercy from Us" which is revelation and prophethood. "And We taught him knowledge from Us" which is specific to Us and is not known except by Our guidance, which is the knowledge of the unseen.
18:66: 66. "Moses said to him, 'Shall I follow you on condition that you teach me?' On the condition that you teach me, and it is in the position of the state of the Kaf. It is the object of 'taught' and the object of 'I learned', the deleted pronoun, and both are transferred from 'ilm, which has one object. It is possible that 'guidance' is the cause of 'tab'bak' or a source with the implication of its action. It does not contradict his prophethood and his being the bearer of a Sharia that he learn from others what was not a condition in the chapters of religion, for the Messenger should be more knowledgeable than the one he was sent to in what he was sent with of the principles and branches of religion, not absolutely. He observed in that the utmost humility and politeness, so he considered himself ignorant and asked permission to be his follower, and asked him to guide him and bestow upon him the favor of teaching him some of what God had bestowed upon him.
18:67: 67. He said, 'You will not be able to have patience with me.' He denied that he could have patience with him in a number of emphatic ways, as if it were something that was not correct or right. He explained that and apologized for it by saying:
18:68: 68. And how can you be patient with that which you have no knowledge of? And the promise being suspended on God's will is either for good fortune, and breaking it forgetfully does not undermine his infallibility, or because he knew the difficulty of the matter, for witnessing corruption and patience contrary to what is usual is severe, so there is no breaking it, and in it is evidence that the actions of the servants occur by the will of God Almighty.

Hamza and Al-Kisa'il read to drown its people with attribution to the people. Indeed, you have done a terrible thing. You have done a great thing from the word amr if it is great.

It was said that he meant by forgetting to leave, i.e. do not hold me accountable for what I left out of your will the first time. It was said that it is one of the metaphors of speech and what is meant is something else that he forgot. "And do not overburden me with difficulty in my affair and do not deceive me with difficulty in my affair by making things difficult and holding me accountable for what I forgot, because that makes it difficult for you to follow up, and difficultly is a second object of to overburden", as it is said: "he overburdened him if he covered him and he overburdened him, and it was read hardly" with two dhammahs.

The letter fa is to indicate that as he met him, he killed him without deliberation or investigating the situation. Therefore, He said, 'Have you killed a pure soul without a soul?' meaning pure from sins. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu Amr, and Ruways read on the authority of Ya'qub, pure, and the first is more eloquent. Abu Amr said, pure is the one who has never sinned, and pure is the one who sinned and then was forgiven. Perhaps he chose the first for that reason, because she was young and had not reached puberty, or because he had not seen her commit a sin that would require punishment before her, or kill a soul so that she would be killed for it. He alerted with it that killing is only permitted as a prescribed punishment or as retaliation, and both matters are absent. Perhaps the change in the system by making its breach a punishment, and Moses' objection, peace be upon him, is a new beginning in the first in the second. Killing him is part of the condition and objecting to it is a punishment because killing is more ugly and objecting to it is more important, so it was worthy of being the main point of the speech. Therefore, he separated it by saying: You have certainly done something reprehensible, meaning reprehensible. Nafi’ read in the narration of Qalun, Warsh, Ibn Amir, Ya’qub, and Abu Bakr reprehensible with two dammahs.
18:75: 75. He said, 'Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?' He added to you to it, combating with reproach for refusing the commandment, and branding him with lack of steadfastness and patience because of his repeated disgust and disapproval, and he did not heed the reminder the first time until he increased his disapproval the second time.

And if I ask you to keep me company, and I mean Jacob, do not keep me company, meaning do not make me your companion. You have received an excuse from me. I found an excuse from myself for disobeying you three times. “And on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, may God have mercy on my brother Moses, he felt shy and said that, if he had stayed with his companion he would have seen the most amazing wonders.” And Nafi’ read from me with the nun moved and was satisfied with it instead of the nun of the pillar, as in his saying: Give me a share of the victory of the two lovers Abu Bakr Ladni with a sukoon on the nun and a sukoon on the dhad from udhud.
18:77: 77. So they set out until they came to the people of a village the village of Antioch, and it was said Ablah al-Basra. And it was said Bajrawan Armenia. And they found therein a wall about to collapse almost falling, so the will was borrowed for approaching, just as the concern and determination were borrowed for it. And it is said that it is taken from the verb to take, like to follow from to follow, and it is not from to take according to the Basrans. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God Almighty be pleased with them both: Najdah al-Haruri wrote to him how he killed him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of parents, so he wrote to him, If you know about the condition of children what the scholar of Moses was like, then you may kill. 18:82: 82. "As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city." It was said that their names were Asram and Sareem, and that the name of the murdered man was Jaysur. The blame for their treasure in the Almighty's statement: "And those who hoard gold and silver" is for those who do not pay their zakat and the rights attached to them. It was said that it was from the books of knowledge. It is possible that it is a cause or source for wanted because the will of good is mercy. It was said that it is related to an omitted word, the meaning of which is I did what I did as a mercy from your Lord. Perhaps the attribution of the will is first to himself because he is the one directly attributing the fault, and second to God and to himself because the change is by destroying the boy and God creating a replacement for him, and third to God alone because he had no role in the boys reaching maturity. Or because the first is evil in itself, the third is good, and the second is mixed. Or because of the difference in the state of the knower in paying attention to the intermediaries. And I did not do it and I did not do what I saw. Of my own accord of my opinion, and I only did it by the command of God Almighty, and the basis of that is that if two harms conflict, the lesser of the two must be borne in order to repel the greater of the two, and it is a paved principle, but the laws differ in its details. That is the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience meaning that you could not, so the ta’ was deleted for the sake of lightening. Among the benefits of this story is that a person should not be amazed by his knowledge and should not rush to deny what he does not like, for perhaps there is a secret in it that he does not know, and that he should continue to learn and humble himself before the teacher, and observe good manners in return, and that he should alert the criminal to his crime and forgive him until his persistence is confirmed, then he should abandon him.

18:85: 85. So he followed a means meaning he wanted to reach the Maghrib so he followed a means that would lead him to it. The Kufians and Ibn Amir read it with the alif cut off and the ta lightened.

A people it was said that their clothing was the skins of wild animals and their food was what the sea had thrown up, and they were infidels, so God gave him the choice between punishing them or calling them to faith, as He narrated in His saying: We said, O Dhul-Qarnayn, either you punish meaning by killing for their infidelity. Or you take good towards them by guiding and teaching the laws. It was said that God gave him the choice between killing and captivity and called it goodness in return for killing, and the first is supported by His saying:

That is, he chose the call and said: As for he whom I called, and he wronged himself by persisting in his disbelief or persisted in his wrongdoing, which is polytheism, then I and those with me will punish him in this world by killing him, then God will punish him in the Hereafter with a terrible punishment, the likes of which have never been known.
18:88: 88. "And as for he who believes and does righteous deeds, which is what faith requires, he will have" in both abodes. "The best reward" is his best deed. It is possible that "amma and ma" are for division without choice, meaning let your affair with them be either torture or kindness. And God's call to him, if he was a prophet, then by revelation, and if he was someone else, then by inspiration or on the tongue of a prophet. And We will say to him of Our command with what We command. Easy is easy, facilitated, not difficult. Its meaning is easy. It was read with two dammahs.
18:89: 89. Then I followed a path. Then I followed a path that would lead him to the East.

It was read with the opening of the lam to imply an added noun, meaning the place where the sun rises, as it is a source. 18:91: 91. Likewise meaning the matter of Dhul-Qarnayn as we described it in the loftiness of the place and the expansion of the kingdom, or his matter with them is like his matter with the people of the West in terms of choice and selection. And We have encompassed what he has of soldiers, machines, numbers and causes. report knowledge related to its outward and hidden aspects, and what is meant is that the abundance of that has reached a level that only the knowledge of the Gracious, the All-Knowing can encompass.
18:92: 92. Then I followed a path meaning a third path crossing between the east and the west, taking it from the south to the north.
18:93: 93. Until he reached between the two dams between the two mountains between which his dam was built, and they are the mountains of Armenia and Azerbaijan.
