He found, besides them, a people who could hardly understand a word because of the strangeness of their language and the lack of their intelligence. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read they do not understand, meaning that the listener does not understand their speech, nor do they make it clear because of their stuttering in it.
18:94: 94. They said, 'O Dhul-Qarnayn!' That is, their translator said, and in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud, he said, Those who are below them. "Indeed, Gog and Magog" are two tribes from the descendants of Japheth, son of Noah. It was said that Gog and Magog are from the Turks and Magog are from the generation. They are two foreign names, as evidenced by the prevention of inflection. It was said that they are Arabs from the word "aj" which means to hurry, and their origin is the hamza, as 'Aasim read, and their inflection was prevented for the purpose of definition and femininity. "Corrupting on the earth" That is, in our land, by killing, destruction, and damaging crops. It was said that they would go out in the spring, leaving nothing green without eating it, and nothing dry without carrying it. It was also said that they would eat people. "Shall we then make for you a tribute?" We would take it from our money. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read "kharaj, and both are the same, like an-nul and an-nawal". It was said that "kharaj is on the land, and dhimmah and kharaj" are the source. On the condition that you place a barrier between us and them to prevent them from coming out against us. It was included by those who included two barriers, except for Hamza and Al-Kisa’i.
18:95: 95. He said, 'What my Lord has empowered me with is better.' What He has empowered me with is better than what you give me in taxes, and I have no need for it. Ibn Kathir read empowered me according to the original. So help me with strength, meaning with the strength of his action or with whatever tools I am strengthened with. I will place between you and them a barrier, a strong barrier, and it is bigger than a dam, from their saying, a garment covered with patches upon patches.
18:96: 96. Bring me iron blocks cut it and the big piece of it, and it does not contradict returning the tax and limiting it to assistance because giving means handing over, and this is indicated by Abu Bakr's reading of bring me with a broken tanween and a connected hamza meaning bring me iron blocks, and the ba' is deleted because it was deleted in I ordered you good and because giving the tool is assistance by force without the tax on the work. Until when he leveled between the two mountain sides between the two sides of the mountains by arranging them. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir and the two Basrans read with two dammahs, and Abu Bakr with a dammah on the sad and a sukoon on the dal, and it was read with a fathah on the sad and a dammah on the dal, and all of them are languages from the sadaf which is the inclination because each of them is isolated from the other and from it the coincidence of the opposition. He said, Blow meaning he said to the workers, Blow into the jugs and iron. Until when he made it made the blown into a fire" like fire by heating. "He said, Bring me molten copper meaning bring me molten copper. He poured a drop on it, so the first was deleted because the second indicated it. The Basrans held to this, that it is more appropriate to use the second of the two operators directed towards one object, if the object of the verb poured was the object of poured to avoid confusion. Hamza and Abu Bakr read they came to me with the alif connected.
18:97: 97. Fama ista'u by deleting the ta' to avoid meeting two close letters. Hamza read it with idgham, combining two quiescent letters out of the ordinary. It was also read by changing the sin to a sad. An izharuhu means to ascend it due to its height and smoothness. And they were not able to tunnel due to its thickness and hardness. It was said that he dug for the foundation until he reached the water, and made it from rock and molten copper and the building from iron sheets between them firewood and coal until it was level with the tops of the two mountains, then he placed the bellows until it became like fire, so he poured molten copper on it, so it mixed and stuck together and became a solid mountain. It was said that he built it from rocks connected to each other with hooks of iron and molten copper in their cavities.
18:98: 98. He said this this dam or the destinies to level it. A mercy from my Lord to His servants. So when the promise of my Lord comes the time of His promise of the emergence of Gog and Magog, or the establishment of the Hour, as the Day of Resurrection approaches. He made it level flattened, spread out, leveled with the ground, a source with the meaning of a passive participle, and from it the sentence adka for someone with a flat hump. The Kufians read dakaa with a long vowel, meaning a level ground. And the promise of my Lord was true will inevitably happen, and this is the last story of the words of Dhul-Qarnayn.
18:99: 99. And We will let some of them surge against others on that Day. And We will make some of Gog and Magog, when they emerge from behind the dam, surge against others, crowded together in the land, or some of creation surge against others, so they will be disturbed and mixed, their humans and jinn confused. This is supported by His statement: And the Trumpet will be blown for the establishment of the Hour. So We will gather them together for the reckoning and recompense.
18:100: 100. And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, presenting it to them. And We will show it and make it apparent to them.
18:101: 101. "Those whose eyes were covered from My remembrance" from My signs that they looked at, so I remind with monotheism and glorification. "And they were unable to hear" to listen to My remembrance and My words due to their extreme deafness to the truth, for the deaf may be able to hear if he is called out to, but these are as if their ears were completely deaf.
18:102: 102. Do those who disbelieve think? They thought, and the question is for denial. That they would take My servants as they take the angels and the Messiah. Besides Me as protectors as deities who would benefit them, or that I would not punish them with it. So the second object was deleted as the predicate is deleted due to the context. That they would take was made the place of its two objects, and it was read, Do those who disbelieve think meaning a lie against them in salvation, and that with what is in its scope is raised as the subject of hasab, for if the description depends on the hamza, it is equal to the verb in action or predicate for it. Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as a lodging what is established for the inhabitant, and in it is mockery and a warning that they have behind it of punishment that is insignificant compared to it.
18:103: 103. "Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in respect of their deeds?" The word is in the accusative case as a distinguishing word and is plural because it is one of the active parts of the verb or because of the diversity of their deeds.
18:104: 104. Those whose efforts have been lost in worldly life was lost and in vain due to their disbelief and conceit, like the monks, for they lost their world and their afterlife. Its place is in the nominative case as a deleted predicate, for it is the answer to the question, or in the genitive case as a substitute, or in the accusative case as a blame. And they think that they are doing well with their conceit and belief that they are on the right path.
18:105: 105. Those who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord in the Qur'an or in its evidence established for monotheism and prophethood. And meeting Him in the resurrection as it is or meeting His punishment. So their deeds have become worthless because of their disbelief, so they will not be rewarded for them. So We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight so that we will despise them and do not give them any value or consideration, or we will not set for them a scale by which their deeds will be weighed because they have become worthless.
18:106: 106. That means that matter, and His saying: Their recompense is Hell is a sentence explaining it. It is possible that that is the subject and the sentence is its predicate and the pronoun is omitted, meaning their recompense with it, or their recompense is its substitute and Hell is its predicate or their recompense is its predicate. Hell is an explanatory apposition to the predicate. Because they disbelieved and took My verses and My messengers in ridicule meaning because of that.
18:107: 107. Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging. This is in reference to the previous ruling and promise of God. Paradise is the highest level of Paradise, and its origin is the garden that contains grapes and palm trees.
18:108: 108. "They will abide therein" is a predetermined state. "They will not seek to change from it" is a change, as they will not find anything better than it, until their souls strive for it. It is possible that it is intended to confirm eternity.
18:109: 109. "Say: If the sea were ink" what is written with, and it is the name of what extends something like ink for an inkwell and a sharpener for a lamp. For the words of my Lord for the words of His knowledge and wisdom. The sea would be exhausted the sea would be exhausted by His command because every body is finite. Before the words of my Lord are exhausted because they are infinite and will not be exhausted like His knowledge. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it with a ya. And if we brought something like it like the existing sea. Extension is an addition and assistance, because the sum of the finite is finite, rather the sum of what enters into existence from bodies cannot be except finite due to the conclusive evidence of the finiteness of dimensions, and the finite is exhausted before the infinite is exhausted inevitably. It was read extended with a ya and extension with a kasra on the meem, the plural of maddah, which is what the writer draws and ink. The reason for its revelation is that the Jews said in your book, And whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good, and you read, And of knowledge you have been given only a little.
18:110: 110. "Say, 'I am only a human being like you.' I do not claim to have complete knowledge of His words. 'It has been revealed to me that your God is one God.' I am distinguished from you by that. So whoever hopes to meet his Lord hoping for a good meeting with Him or fearing an evil meeting with Him, let him do righteous work that pleases God. And do not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord by showing off to Him or asking for a reward from Him. “It was narrated that Jundub bin Zuhair said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “I do a deed for God, and when I see it, it pleases me.” He said: God does not accept that in which you associate partners. So it was revealed confirming what he said, may God bless him and grant him peace: Beware of minor polytheism. They said: What is minor polytheism? He said: Showing off. The verse combines the essence of knowledge and action, which are monotheism and sincerity in obedience. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites it when he goes to bed will have a light in his bed that shines to Mecca, filled with angels who pray for him until he wakes up. If his bed is in Mecca, he will have a light that shines from his bed to the Frequented House, filled with angels who pray for him until he wakes up.” On his authority, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, Whoever recites Surat Al-Kahf from the end, it will be a light for him from his head to his feet, and whoever recites it in its entirety, it will be a light for him from the earth to the heavens.
19:1: 1- Khay’as Abu Amr inflated the ha’ because the alifs of the spelling names are ya’s, and Ibn Amir and Hamza inflated the ya’, and both al-Kisa’i and Abu Bakr, and Nafi’ bin Bayn and Nafi’ and Ibn Kathir and Asim inflated the dal of spelling with the dhal, and the rest assimilate it.
19:2: 2- Remember the mercy of your Lord is the predicate of what preceded it, whether it is the beginning of the surah or the Qur'an, then it includes it or the predicate is omitted, meaning: this recited is remember the mercy of your Lord, or the subject whose predicate is omitted, meaning in what is recited to you, its mention, and remember is read as a past tense and remember as a command. His servant is the object of mercy or the remembrance on the basis that mercy is its subject in the expansion like you say: Zaid's generosity reminded me. Zachariah is a substitute for it or an explanatory apposition for it.
19:3: 3- When he called upon his Lord in secret because concealment and public speaking are the same before God, and concealment is more subdued and more sincere, or so that he would not be blamed for asking for a child in his old age, or so that his masters whom he feared would not find out about him, or because the weakness of old age concealed his voice. There is disagreement about his age at that time, as some say sixty, some say seventy, some say seventy-five, some say eighty-five, and some say ninety-nine.
19:4: 4- "He said, 'My Lord, indeed my bones have become feeble'" is an explanation of the call, and weakness is weakness, and the bone is specified because it is the support of the body and the origin of its structure and because it is the hardest part of it, so if it weakens, what is behind it is weaker, and its singularity is because what is meant by it is the genus, and "hen and when" were read with damma and kasra, and its counterpart is Kamal with the three movements. "And the head was ignited with gray hair" He likened the gray hair in its whiteness and its illumination to the flames of fire and its spread and prevalence in the hair by its ignition, then he brought it out in the form of a metaphor and attributed the ignition to the head which is the place of the gray hair as an exaggeration, and made it distinctive to clarify the intended meaning, and he was satisfied with the lam for the addition to indicate that the speaker's knowledge of the specificity of the intended meaning suffices without restriction. And I have never been unhappy in my supplication to You, my Lord. Rather, whenever I supplicate to You, You answer me. This is a supplication based on what he had previously received in response, and a reminder that even if the one being supplicated to is not accustomed to, his response is accustomed, and that the Almighty has accustomed him to the response and has given him hope in it. It is the right of the Generous not to disappoint the one who gives him hope.
19:6: 6 - He inherits me and he inherits from the family of Jacob are two attributes of Him, and Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i confirmed them as the answer to the supplication, and what is meant is the inheritance of the law and knowledge, as the prophets do not inherit money. It was said that he inherits me the high priest, because he was a scholar, and he inherits from the family of Jacob the kingdom, and he is Jacob bin Isaac, peace be upon them. It was said that Jacob was the brother of Zakariya or Imran bin Mathan from the descendants of Solomon, peace be upon him. It was read (He inherits me, the heir of the family of Jacob) as a state of one of the two pronouns, or (he inherits) in the diminutive because of its smallness, and an inheritor from the family of Jacob as the subject of he inherits me, and this is called the stripped in the science of rhetoric because it is stripped of what was mentioned first, although it is what is meant. And make him, my Lord, pleasing please him in word and deed.
19:7: 7- O Zachariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. This is an answer to his call and a promise to answer his prayer. He named him to honor him. We have not made for him a namesake before. No one had been named John before him, and this is evidence that naming with strange names is a reference to the one being named. It was said that he was named after someone similar, as in the Almighty's saying: Do you know of any other namesake for him? because similar things share the same name. It is more apparent that it is foreign, and even if it is Arabic, it is derived from a verb such as to live and to prosper. It was said that he was named after him because his mother's womb was revived by it, or because the religion of God was revived by his call.
19:8: 8- He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?' Harshness and barrenness in the joints, and its root is 'atu and ka'ud, but they found the succession of the two dhammahs and the two waws heavy, so they broke the ta', and the first waw was changed to a ya', then the second was changed and assimilated, and Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read 'atiya with a kasrah, and the boy was amazed by an old man and a barren old woman, in recognition that the influence on him is the perfection of his power and that the intermediaries are nullified when investigated, and therefore:
19:9: 9- He said meaning God Almighty or the angel who conveyed the good report confirming it Likewise the matter is likewise, and it is permissible for the kaf to be in the accusative case with He said in: Your Lord said and that is an indication of an ambiguous thing that it explains. It is easy for Me and the first reading is supported by the one who read (And it is easy for Me) meaning the matter is as I said, or as I promised and it is easy for Me, or as I promised and it is easy for Me, I do not need reasons for what I want to do, and the object of the second said is omitted. And I created you before, and you were nothing. Rather, you were purely nonexistent, and in it is evidence that the nonexistent is nothing. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read And We have created you.
19:10: 10 - He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign' A sign by which I will know that what You have given me the good report will happen. He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, sound' Sound creation, you are neither mute nor dumb. The nights and days are mentioned here in (Al Imran) to indicate that he continued to be prevented from speaking to people and to devote himself to remembrance and gratitude for three days and their nights.
19:11: 11- So he came out to his people from the sanctuary from the prayer area or from the room. Then he inspired them so he gestured to them with his words except as a sign. It was said that he wrote for them on the ground. To glorify pray or praise your Lord. morning and evening the two ends of the day, and perhaps he was commanded to glorify and command his people to agree with him, and that could be a source or an explanatory.
19:12: 12- O Yahya on the assumption of the saying. Take the Book the Torah. With strength with diligence and memorization with success. And We gave him wisdom while he was a boy meaning wisdom and understanding of the Torah, and it was said that it was prophecy. God perfected his mind in his youth and made him a prophet.
19:13: 13- And compassion from Us and mercy from Us upon him or mercy and compassion in his heart towards his parents and others in apposition to the ruling. And purity and purification from sins or charity, meaning that God gave him charity to his parents, or enabled him and granted him success in believing in people. And he was pious obedient and avoiding sins.
19:14: 14- And dutiful to his parents. And dutiful to them. And he was not a disobedient tyrant. Disobedient or disobedient to his Lord.
19:15: 15- "And peace be upon him" from God. The day he was born from Satan's afflictions with what he afflicts the children of Adam with. And the day he dies from the torment of the grave. And the day he is raised alive from the torment of the Fire, which is the Resurrection.
19:16: 16- And mention in the Book in the Qur'an. Mary means her story. When she withdrew she secluded herself, a substitute for Mary a substitute of inclusion because the times include what is in them, or a substitute for the whole because what is meant by Mary is her story and by the circumstance the matter in which it occurs and they are one, or a circumstance for an estimated addition and it was said when means the source like you say: I honored you when you did not honor me so it is inevitably a substitute. From her people an eastern place east of Jerusalem, or east of her house, and for this reason the Christians took the east as a qiblah and a place a circumstance or an object because she withdrew includes the meaning of came.
19:17: 17- So she took a veil from them a covering. Then We sent to her Our Spirit, and he appeared to her as a well-proportioned man. It was said that she sat in a place of worship to bathe after menstruation, veiled with something to cover her - and she would move from the mosque to her aunt's house when she menstruated and return to it when she was pure - and while she was bathing, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to her in the form of a young, beardless, well-proportioned man so that she would be comforted by his words, and perhaps to arouse her desire with him so that her sperm would descend into her womb.
19:18: 18- She said, 'Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you' from the utmost of her chastity. If you are pious you fear God and celebrate seeking refuge, and the answer to the condition is omitted and indicated by what preceded it, i.e. then I seek refuge from you, or take heed from my seeking of refuge, or do not interfere with me. It is possible that it is for exaggeration, i.e. if you are pious and devout, then I seek refuge from you, so how about if you are not like that.
19:19: 19- He said, 'I am only the Messenger of your Lord'" in whom you sought refuge. "To give you a boy" meaning to be the cause of his gift by blowing into the shield. It is possible that it is a narration of the statement of God Almighty, and it is supported by the reading of Abu Amr and most of the people from Nafi' and Ya'qub with the letter ya'. "Pure" purified from sins or growing in goodness meaning advancing from age to age in goodness and righteousness.
19:20: 20- She said, 'How can I have a boy when no man has touched me?' and no man has touched me lawfully. These euphemisms are only used in this case. As for adultery, it is only said that it was wicked and immoral towards her and the like. This is supported by the conjunction of his saying: And I was not a rebel. It is a fa'ul from baghiyyah, its waw was changed to a ya' and assimilated, then the ghayn was broken in imitation of it, and for this reason the ta' was not added to it, or fa'il with the meaning of fa'il and the ta' was not added to it because it is for emphasis, or for relation like talaq.
19:21: 21- He said, 'Thus said your Lord: It is easy for Me. And We will make it.'" That is, we will do that to make it a sign or to demonstrate our power and to make it. It was said that it is in apposition to "to give" in the manner of turning away. "A sign for the people" is a sign for them and evidence of the perfection of our power. "And a mercy from Us" to the servants, so that they are guided by His guidance. "And it was a matter decreed." That is, the decree of God was related to it from eternity, or it was decreed and written on the tablet, or it was a real matter that it would be decreed and done because it is a sign and a mercy.
19:22: 22- So she carried him by blowing into her armour and the blowing entered her womb and the duration of her pregnancy was seven months, and it was said six, and it was said eight, and no child born after eight lived other than him, and it was said an hour after she carried him she threw him away and her age was thirteen years, and it was said ten years and she menstruated twice. So she withdrew with him so she separated from him while he was in her womb as he said: Skulls and turban trample us The noun and preposition are in the accusative case. A distant place far from its people, behind the mountain. It was also said that it was the furthest part of the house.
19:23: 23- So the labor pains came upon her so the labor pains forced her, and it is originally derived from came but it was used specifically as in to give and the labor pains were read with the kasra and they are the source of the woman's labor if the child moved in her womb to come out. To the trunk of the palm tree to hide behind it and lean on it during childbirth, which is the space between the root and the branch and it was a dry palm tree with no top or greenery and it was winter, and the definition is either for the genus or for the covenant if there was nothing else and it was like a learner among the people, and perhaps God Almighty inspired her to do that to show her from His signs what would calm her fear and feed her fresh dates which are the mute dates of the postpartum woman that are compatible with it. She said, 'Oh, I wish I had died before this' out of shyness from the people and fear of their blame, and Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read I died from mata yamout. And I was forgetful means that which is likely to be forgotten and not sought after. Its equivalent is slaughtering when it is slaughtered. Hamza and Hafs read it with the fat-ha, which is a dialect for it or a source named after it. It was read with it and with the hamza, which is milk mixed with water that its people forget because of its scarcity. Forgotten means forgotten in the sense that it does not cross their minds. It was read with the kasra on the meem, following the tradition.
19:24: 24- And he called to her from beneath her Jesus, and it was said Gabriel was kissing the child, and it was said beneath her, lower than her place. Nafi', Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, Hafs, and Ruh read (from beneath her) with the kasra and genitive, on the basis that in the word called there is a pronoun for one of them, and it was said that the pronoun in beneath her is the palm tree. That you do not grieve meaning do not grieve or that you do not grieve. Your Lord has placed beneath you a stream a brook. This is how it was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and it was said that it was a master of cypress trees, which is Jesus, peace be upon him.
19:25: 25- "And shake the trunk of the palm tree towards you and incline it towards you, and the Baa is added for emphasis or do the shaking and inclination with it, or shake" the fruit by shaking it and shaking is movement by pulling and pushing. "Taqata'alayka" means falling, so the second Taa was assimilated into the Seen and Hamza deleted it, and Ya'qub read with the Yaa and Hafs (Taqata'ala) from Qaqata meaning dropped, and it was read (Tatasaqta) and (Tasqutu) and (Yusqutu) so the Taa is for the palm tree and the Yaa is for the trunk. "Rabitan janya" is a distinguishing or passive participle. It was narrated that it was a dry palm tree with no head or fruit and it was winter, so I shook it and God gave it a head, palm leaves and fresh dates. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 17 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat Maryam, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Anbiyāa. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. 19:26: 26- Eat and drink meaning from the dates and the water of the spring or from the dates and their juice. And be cheerful and please yourself and reject from it what saddens you. (Waqri) was read with the kasra, which is the language of Najd, and its derivation is from the qarār, because when the eye sees what pleases the soul, it is calmed by it rather than looking at anything else, or from disgust. The tear of joy is cold and the tear of sadness is hot, and that is why it is said that the coolness of the eye is for the beloved and its heat is for the hated. If you see anyone from among mankind if you see a human being, and (tarā'an) was read in the language of those who say lbāt bi-al-hajj because of the brotherhood between the hamza and the soft letter. So say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast' silence, and it was read with it, or fasting, and they did not speak during their fast. I will not speak to any human being today after I informed you of my vow, but I speak to the angels and I commune with my Lord. It was said that she informed them of her vow by gesture and ordered them to do so out of dislike for argument and to be satisfied with the words of Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him, as they are decisive in cutting off the one who attacks.
19:27: 27- So she brought him meaning with her son. Her people returning to them after she had purified herself from childbirth. Carrying him carrying him. They said, O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented meaning something new and strange, such as scratching the skin.
19:28: 28- O sister of Aaron They mean Aaron the Prophet, peace be upon him, and she was from the descendants of those who were with him in the class of brothers, and it was said that she was from his lineage and there were a thousand years between them. And it was said that he was a wicked or righteous man who was in their time and they likened her to him in mockery or because they saw her righteousness before or they cursed her with it. Your father was not a bad man and your mother was not unchaste is a confirmation because what she came with is a lie, and a warning that the obscenities of the children of the righteous are more obscene.
19:29: 29- So she pointed to him to Jesus, peace be upon him, meaning speak to him so that he may answer you. They said, 'How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?' We have never known a child in the cradle to whom a rational person spoke. Was is redundant and the circumstance is a relative clause of from. "A child" is a state of what is implied in it, or complete or permanent, like the Almighty's saying: "And God is Knowing and Wise" or in the sense of became.
19:30: 30- He said, 'I am the servant of God.' God Almighty made him say it first because it is the first of the stations and to respond to those who claim His divinity. He gave me the Scripture the Gospel. And made me a prophet.
19:31: 31- And He made me blessed beneficial, teaching goodness. The expression in the past tense is either in consideration of what preceded in His judgment, or by making what is certain to happen as reality. It was said that God perfected his mind and made him a child. Wherever you are wherever you are. And He enjoined upon me and commanded me. To pray and to give zakat zakat on money if you own it or purifying the soul from vices. As long as I live.
19:32: 32- And dutiful to my mother and dutiful to her is in apposition to blessed, and it was read with the kasra as a source of description or accusative by a verb indicated by He commanded me, meaning He charged me with dutifulness, and this is supported by the reading with the kasra and genitive in apposition to (prayer). And He did not make me a wretched tyrant in the sight of God due to his excessive arrogance.
19:33: 33- "And peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I die and the day I am raised alive" as it is upon Yahya and the definition is for the covenant and it is more apparent that it is for the type and the allusion to cursing his enemies, because when he made the type of peace upon himself, he alluded to its opposite being upon them like the Almighty’s saying: "And peace be upon him who follows the guidance" for it is an allusion that the punishment is upon he who denied and turned away.
19:34: 34- That is Jesus, son of Mary meaning the one described above is Jesus, son of Mary, not what the Christians describe, and it is a denial of what they describe in the most eloquent and demonstrative way, as he made him described with the opposites of what they describe, then reversed the ruling. The word of truth is an omitted predicate, meaning it is the word of truth in which there is no doubt, and the addition is for clarification and the pronoun is for the previous statement or for the completion of the story. It was said that it is an attribute of Jesus or a substitute or a second predicate and its meaning is the word of God. Asim, Ibn Amir and Yaqub read speech in the accusative case as a confirmed source. It was read (said the truth) and it means the saying. about which they are in doubt in his matter, they doubt or dispute, so the Jews said he is a magician and the Christians said he is the son of God, and it was read with the ta' as a direct address.
19:35: 35- "It is not for God to take a son. Glory be to Him." A refutation of the Christians and a declaration of God's sanctity from what they have slandered. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is. A rebuke to them, for He who, when He wills a thing, brings it into existence with Be, is far removed from the likeness of creation to the need to take a son by impregnating females. Ibn Amir read so it is in the accusative case as an answer.
19:36: "And indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path." Its interpretation was previously mentioned in Surah Al Imran. The Hijazis and Basris read and with the fat-ha on and because and it was said that it is conjoined with prayer.
19:37: 37 Then the parties differed among themselves" the Jews and Christians. Or the Christian sects, the Nestorians said that he is the son of God, the Jacobites said that he is God who descended to earth and then ascended to heaven, and the Angels said that he is the servant of God and His prophet. "So woe to those who disbelieve from the sight of a tremendous day" from witnessing a tremendous day, its horror, its reckoning and its reward, which is the Day of Resurrection, or from the time of the witnesses or from its place in it, or from the testimony of that day against them, which is that the angels and prophets and their tongues and their limbs and their feet will testify against them with disbelief and immorality, or from the time of the testimony or from its place. It was said that it is what they testified about Jesus and his mother.
19:38: 38- I hear and see them means that their hearing and seeing. On the Day they come to Us meaning the Day of Resurrection is worthy of being amazed at after they were deaf and blind in this world, or the threat of what they hear and see on that Day. It was said that He ordered that they hear and see the appointments of that Day and what will surround them in it, and the preposition and the noun in the first case are in the nominative case and in the accusative case in the second case. But the wrongdoers today are in clear error. The wrongdoers were placed in the position of the pronoun to indicate that they wronged themselves since they neglected listening and seeing when it would benefit them, and their neglect was recorded as clear error.
19:39: 39- And warn them of the Day of Regret the day when people will regret the wrongdoer for his wrongdoing and the good-doer for his lack of goodness. When the matter is decided the reckoning is over and the two groups are destined for Paradise or Hell. When is a substitute for the Day or a circumstance for regret. And they are in heedlessness and they do not believe is a state related to His statement in manifest error and what is between them is an interruption, or to Warn them meaning warn them while they are heedless and not believing, so it is a state that includes the reason.
19:40: 40- Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it. No one will remain on it or over it except Us, nor will they have any dominion, or We will take the earth and whoever is on it by destruction and annihilation, and the heir will die of his inheritance. And to Us they will be returned. They will be returned for recompense.
19:41: 41- “And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth” who was always truthful, or who believed a lot due to the many things he believed in regarding the unseen of God Almighty, His signs, His books, and His messengers. A prophet whom God appointed as a prophet.
19:42: 42- When he said instead of Abraham and what is between them is an interruption, or related to was or to a truthful prophet. To his father, O my father the taa is a substitute for the yaa of addition and therefore it is not said O my father but it is said O my father, but it is mentioned to express sympathy and therefore it is repeated. Why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see so that it knows your condition and hears your remembrance and sees your submission. And it does not avail you at all in bringing benefit or repelling harm. He called him to guidance and showed him his misguidance and argued against him in the most eloquent and graceful manner, as he did not explicitly state his misguidance but rather asked for the reason that called him to worship what the clear mind belittles and refuses to rely on, let alone worshipping Him which is the ultimate in glorification and is only due to Him who has complete self-sufficiency and general bounty, and He is the Creator, the Provider, the Giver of Life, the Giver of Death, the Punisher, the Rewarder. He pointed out that the rational person should do what he does for a correct purpose, and if something were alive, distinct, hearing, seeing, and capable of benefit and harm but were possible, the sound mind would refuse to worship it, even if it were the most honorable of creation like the angels and prophets, because it does not see its like in need and submission to the necessary power, so how would it be if it were inanimate and neither hears nor sees? Then he called him to follow Him so that He would guide him to the correct truth and the straight path because he was not blessed with divine knowledge independently of sound consideration, so he said:.
19:43: 43- O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to a straight path. He did not call his father excessively ignorant nor himself superior in knowledge, but rather made himself like a companion to him on the journey who would be more knowledgeable about the path. Then he discouraged him from what he was doing by saying that despite its lack of benefit, it entailed harm, for it was in reality the worship of Satan since he was the one who ordered it, so he said:
19:44: 44- "O my father, do not worship Satan." And when he found this objectionable, he explained the harm in it, that Satan is stubborn with your Lord, the Master of all blessings, by saying: "Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful." And it is known that the one who obeys the disobedient is a disobedient, and every disobedient person is deserving of having blessings taken back from him and vengeance taken from him, and therefore he followed it by frightening him with the evil of his end and what it leads to, so he said:
19:45: 45- O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Gracious will afflict you, and you will be a friend of Satan a companion in cursing and punishment, following him and you, or steadfast in his friendship, for it is greater than the punishment, just as the pleasure of God is greater than the reward. The mention of fear and the touch and the indefiniteness of the punishment is either for the sake of flattery or to conceal the consequences. Perhaps his limiting it to the disobedience of Satan among his crimes is due to his high ambition in divinity, or because he is its angel, or because it is a result of his enmity towards Adam and his descendants, drawing attention to it.
19:46: 46- He said, 'Do you desire my gods, O Abraham?' He responded to his sympathy and kindness in guidance with rudeness and stubbornness, so he called him by his name and did not respond to O my father: O my son. He delayed it and presented the report before the subject and began it with a hamza to deny the desire itself in a kind of astonishment, as if it was something that no sane person would desire. Then he threatened him and said: If you do not desist from what you said about it or the desire for it. I will stone you with my tongue meaning cursing and slander or with stones until you die, or move away from me. 19:48: 48- And I will leave you and what you call upon besides God by emigrating for my religion. And I will call upon my Lord and worship Him alone. Perhaps I will not be in the call of my Lord unhappy disappointed and wasting my efforts like you in calling upon your gods. 19:49: 49- So when he had left them and what they worshipped besides God by migrating to Ash-Sham. We gave him Isaac and Jacob instead of the infidels he had left. Of the descendants of Adam is a substitute for it by repeating the preposition, and it is possible that of in it is for partiality because those upon whom favors are bestowed are more general than the prophets and more specific than the descendants. And of those whom We carried with Noah means and of the descendants of those whom We carried in particular, and they are those other than Idris, for Abraham was from the descendants of Sam, son of Noah. This is the predicate of those if you make the relative pronoun its attribute, and a resumption if you make it its predicate to clarify their fear of God and their humility before Him despite their high status in noble lineage, perfection of soul, and closeness to God Almighty. And from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Recite the Qur’an and weep, and if you do not weep, then pretend to weep. Weeping is the plural of baak, like prostration is the plural of sajid.
