19:59: 59- And after them came a generation So after them came a generation of evil. It is said a true generation with the fat-ha, and a bad generation with the sukun. They neglected the prayer They abandoned it or delayed it from its time. And followed desires such as drinking alcohol, making marriage to one's paternal sister permissible, and being immersed in sins. And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, in his saying And followed desires from the sons of the severe, and rode the visible, and wore the famous. Then they will meet with error evil like his saying: Whoever finds good, people praise him for his actions, and whoever goes astray will not lack someone to blame him for his error. Or a reward for error, as God Almighty says: He will receive sins, or error from the path to Paradise. It was said that it is a valley in Hell from which its valleys seek refuge.
19:60: 60- Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous deeds indicates that the verses are about the disbelievers. Then those will enter Paradise Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Abu Bakr and Yaqub read it in the passive form of adkhla. And they will not be wronged at all nor will they be deducted from the reward for their deeds. It is permissible for at least to be in the accusative case as a source, and in it is a warning that their previous disbelief will not harm them nor will it detract from their rewards.
19:61: 61- "Gardens of Eden" instead of Paradise, instead of some because it includes it, or it is directed to praise, and it was read in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, and Eden because it is the complement to it in the knowledge or knowledge of Eden in the sense of residence as a greatness, and therefore it is correct to describe what it was added to by saying: "which the Most Gracious has promised His servants in the unseen" meaning He promised it to them while it is absent from them, or they are absent from it, or He promised them with their belief in the unseen. "It is" God. "His promise which is Paradise was coming" its people who were promised it will inevitably come to it, and it was said that it is from the one who came to him with kindness, meaning done and accomplished.
19:62: 62- They will not hear therein idle talk idle talk. “Except peace” but they will hear a word in which they will be free from fault and deficiency, or the angels’ peace upon them or the peace of some of them upon others based on the discontinuous exception, or based on the fact that the meaning of peace if it is idle talk is that they will not hear idle talk other than it like his saying: There is no fault in them except that their swords have dents from the clashing of the battalions. Or that its meaning is a prayer for safety and its people are rich in need of it, so it is apparently a futile statement and its benefit is only honor. And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening, according to the custom of those who live in luxury and the middle ground between asceticism and desire. It was said that what is meant is the continuity and abundance of provision. 46- They are exposed to the Fire morning and evening is a new sentence, or the Fire is a deleted predicate, and they are exposed is a new explanation, or a substitute, and they are exposed is a state of it, or of the family, and it was read in the accusative case as a specification, or by implying a verb that explains they are exposed like they pray, so exposing them to the Fire means burning them in it, as they say: The prisoners were exposed to the sword if they were killed with it, and that is for their souls, as Ibn Mas`ud narrated that their souls are in the bodies of black birds that are exposed to the Fire morning and evening until the Day of Resurrection, and mentioning the two times may be specific or supportive, and in it is evidence of the continuity of the soul and the torment of the grave. And on the Day the Hour is established meaning this is as long as the world continues, and when the Hour is established, it will be said to them: Enter the family of Pharaoh O family of Pharaoh. The most severe torment is the torment of Hell, for it is more severe than what they were in, or the most severe torment of Hell. Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Nafi’, Ya’qub, and Hafs read Enter as an order to the angels to enter the fire.
19:63: 63- That is the Paradise which We give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were righteous. We keep it for them from the fruit of their righteousness, just as an heir keeps the wealth of his inheritor. Inheritance is the strongest word used for ownership and entitlement, as it is not followed by annulment or recovery, nor is it nullified by rejection or forfeiture. It was said that the righteous will inherit from Paradise the dwellings that would have belonged to the people of Hell had they obeyed, as an increase in their honor. And from Yaqub, We inherit with emphasis.
19:64: 64- And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. The story of Gabriel's words, peace be upon him, when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, was slow to respond to him when he was asked about the story of the People of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit, and he did not know what to answer, and he hoped that revelation would be revealed to him about it, but he was slow to respond to him for fifteen days, and it was said forty days until the polytheists said his Lord has forsaken him and detested him, then he came down with an explanation of that. And descending means descending slowly because it is the passive participle of nazala and it may be used to mean descending absolutely, just as nazala is used to mean sending down, and the meaning is we do not descend at any time except by the command of God according to what His wisdom requires, and it was read (and does not descend) with the letter ya and the pronoun refers to the revelation. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and what is between that which is where we are of places and times. We do not move from one place to another, nor do we descend at one time rather than another except by His command and will. And your Lord is not forgetful leaving you, meaning that the lack of descent was only due to the lack of command to do so, and it was not because of God leaving you and bidding you farewell as the disbelievers claimed, but rather it was for a wisdom that He saw in it. It was said that the beginning of the verse is a narration of the words of the righteous when they enter Paradise, and the meaning is that we are not sent down to Paradise except by the command of God and His kindness, and He is the Owner of all matters, past, future, and present. So what we found and what we find is from His kindness and grace. And His saying And your Lord is not forgetful is a confirmation from God of their saying, meaning that your Lord is not forgetful of the deeds of the workers and what He promised them of reward for them. And His saying:
19:65: 65- Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them is a statement of the impossibility of forgetting Him, and it is a deleted piece of report or a substitute for your Lord, so worship Him and be patient in worshipping Him. It is addressed to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, arranged according to it, meaning when you know your Lord because it is not appropriate for Him to forget you, or the deeds of the workers, then turn to worshipping Him and be patient in it and do not be confused by the delay of revelation and the mockery of disbelief. It was only transitive with the lam because it includes the meaning of steadfastness in worship in the hardships and difficulties that come upon him, like your saying to the warrior: Be patient for your horn. Do you know of anyone with a namesake? For example, someone who deserves to be called a god or someone who is called God? Even though the polytheists called the idol a god, they never called it God. This is because His Oneness is evident, and His Essence is exalted above likeness, such that He does not accept confusion or stubbornness. It is a confirmation of the matter, meaning that if it is true that there is no one like Him and no one else deserves to be worshipped, then there is no alternative but to submit to His command, engage in His worship, and be patient with its hardships.
19:66: 66- And man says what is meant by this is the entire species, for what is said is said among them even if not all of them said it, like when you say: The sons of so-and-so killed so-and-so and the killer was one of them, or some of them who are known and they are the infidels, or Abi bin Khalaf, for he took rotten bones and crushed them and said: Muhammad claims that we will be resurrected after we die. Will I then be brought forth alive? from the earth or from the state of death, and the presentation of the adverb and its declension are the letter of denial because what is denied is that what is after death is the time of life, and its being in the accusative case is by a verb that indicates it, brought forth, not by it, for what comes after the lam does not act on what comes before it, and here it is purely for emphasis and devoid of the meaning of the state, just as the hamza and lam in Ya God are purely for compensation, so it is permissible to couple it with the letter of the future. It was narrated from Ibn Dhakwan, If you die with a single hamza broken as report.
19:67: 67- Or does man not remember? is in apposition to says. The placement of the hamza of denial between it and the conjunction, although the original is that it precedes them, is to indicate that the object of denial is the conjoined object and that the object of denial arose from it. If he had remembered and contemplated: We created him before, and he was nothing, but rather he was pure nothingness, he would not have said that. Rather, it is more astonishing to gather the materials after the separation and create something similar to what was in them of accidents. Nafi', Ibn Amir, Asim, and Qaloon read on the authority of Ya'qub, remembers, from the remembrance that is intended to mean contemplation. The reading was, remembers, according to the original.
19:68: 68- By your Lord, We will surely gather them together. He swore by His name, the Most High, in addition to His Prophet, to fulfill the command and magnify the status of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the devils is an appositive or an object with it, because it was narrated that the disbelievers will be gathered with their companions from the devils who misled them, each with his devil in a chain. And even though this is specific to them, it is permissible to attribute it to the entire species, because if they are gathered and among them are the disbelievers accompanied by the devils, then they will all be gathered with them. Then We will surely bring them around Hell so that the happy ones will see what God has saved them from and their happiness and joy will increase, and the wretched ones will receive what they have stored up for their afterlife and their anger will increase because of the happy ones’ return from them to the abode of reward and their gloating over them on their knees because of the terror of the Day of Judgment that will overtake them, or because it is one of the consequences of standing for the reckoning before reaching the reward and punishment. The people of the gathering are on their knees because of the Almighty’s saying And you will see every nation on its knees as is customary in gatherings of exchange. If what is meant by humans are the disbelievers, then perhaps they will be driven on their knees from the gathering to the shore of Hell as a humiliation to them, or because of their inability to stand because of the severity that has befallen them. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read on their knees with a kasra on the jim.
19:69: 69- Then We will extract from every sect from every nation that spread a religion. Which of them is most rebellious against the Most Gracious? Whoever is more disobedient and rebellious than them, then We will throw them into it. Mentioning the most rebellious is an indication that the Almighty pardons many of the people of disobedience, even if He specifies that to the infidels. What is meant is that He distinguishes their groups, the most rebellious among them, and throws them into the Fire in order, or He places each of them in the class that suits him. Which of them is built on the damma according to Sibawayh because it is right for it to be built like all the other relative pronouns, but it is parsed based on all and some because of the necessity of the addition. If the beginning of its relative pronoun is deleted, its deficiency increases, so it returns to its right in the accusative case with we will remove, and for this reason it is read accusative and nominative according to others, either by beginning as an interrogative and its predicate is most, and the sentence is reported and the meaning of the speech is: we will remove from every sect about whom it is said which of them is most rebellious, or it is suspended from it we will remove because it includes the meaning of distinction necessary for knowledge, or it is a new sentence and the verb is based on from every sect with the addition of from or with the meaning of we will remove some of every sect, or with shia because it means sectarianism. And ala is for clarification or related to fa`ala and so is the ba in his saying:
19:70: 70 - Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of it - burning. That is, We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of burning, or burning them is most deserving of the Fire. They are the ones who are taken away, and it is possible that what is meant by them and the most stubborn of them are the leaders of the sects, for their punishment is doubled for their misguidance and leading them astray. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read burned with a kasra on the sad.
19:71: 71 - "And there is among you" and there is not among you is a reference to the human being and it is supported by the fact that it was read and there is among them. "Except he will pass through it" except he who continues to it and is present without it. The believers pass through it while it is dormant and collapses without them. And on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, that he, peace be upon him, "was asked about it and he said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, some of them will say to each other: Did not our Lord promise us that we would return to the Fire? And it will be said to them: You have entered it while it was dormant." As for the Almighty's saying: "Those are far from it," what is meant is from its punishment. And it was said that its passing is the passage over the bridge, for it is extended over it. "It was upon your Lord an inevitability decreed." Their passing was an obligation that God made obligatory upon Himself and decreed by Him by promising it a promise that cannot be broken. And it was said that He swore by it.
19:72: 72 Then We will save those who feared God and they will be led to Paradise and he recited Al-Kisa’i and Ya’qub said: Nanji with a light pronunciation, and it was read Thamma with a fatha on the tha meaning there. And He will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees, collapsing with them as they were, and it is evidence that what is meant by the arrivals is the kneeling around it and that the believers will leave the wicked for Paradise after their kneeling, and the wicked will remain therein collapsing with them in their forms.
19:73: 73 - And when Our verses are recited to them as clear proofs the words are recited, the meanings are made clear by themselves or by the explanation of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the clear miracles. Those who disbelieve say to those who believe because of them or with them. That is, the two groups the believers and the disbelievers. The best position a place to stand or a place. Ibn Kathir read it with the dammah, meaning a place to stay and a home. And the best assembly a gathering and a society. The meaning is that when they heard the clear verses and were unable to oppose them and enter upon them, they began to boast about their worldly fortunes and to infer from their increased fortune in them their virtue and good condition with God Almighty, due to their limited vision of the situation and their knowledge of the outward appearance of worldly life. So He responded to them with a threat of refutation by saying:
19:74: 74 - And how many generations have We destroyed before them who were better in furnishings and appearance. "How many is the object of we destroyed and of a generation" is its explanation. The people of each era are called a generation, meaning a leader from the horn of the beast. It is its leader because it comes after it, and they are the best description of you and furniture, distinguishing it from the proportion, which is the furnishings of the house. It was said that it is what is new from it, and the Kharthi is what is worn out, and the vision is the view, an action from vision for what is seen, such as grinding and bread. Nafi' and Ibn Amir read "riya with the hamza changed and its assimilation, or that it is from ray" which is the blessing. Abu Bakr read "riya with the change, and it was read with the hamza deleted, and zayya is from zay" which is the collection, for it is collected beauties. Then he explained that their enjoyment is an enticement and not an honor, but rather the standard for excellence and deficiency is what will be in the hereafter, with his saying:
19:75: 75 - "Say: Whoever is in error - let the Most Merciful extend for him a term." So He extends him and gives him respite with a long life and enjoyment of it. Rather, He brought it out in the form of a command to indicate that giving him respite is something that should be done as a lure and to cut off his excuses, as in the saying of the Most High: We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin. And as in His saying: Have We not given you life long enough for whoever will remember therein to remember? "Until, when they see what they are promised." The limit of the extension. It was said that the limit of the statement of those who disbelieved to those who believed is that they said, which of the two groups, until when they see what they are promised. "Either the punishment or the Hour." A detailing of what is promised, for it is either the punishment in this world, which is the Muslims’ victory over them and their torture of them by killing and capturing them, or the Day of Resurrection and the humiliation and punishment that will befall them therein. And they will know who is in worse position of the two groups, because they saw the situation as the opposite of what they had estimated, and what they enjoyed turned into failure and disaster for them. This is the answer to the condition, and the sentence is mentioned after until. “And weaker in soldiers” meaning a group and supporters, he met it with the best gathering, in that the gathering was good due to the gathering of the people’s notables and leaders, and the appearance of their power and their support.
19:76: 76 - And God increases those who are guided in guidance. This is an affixation to the conditional clause mentioned after the statement, as if when he explained that the respite of the disbeliever and his enjoyment of worldly life is not due to his grace, he wanted to explain that the shortcomings of the believer's share of it are not due to his deficiency, but rather because God, the Almighty, wanted for him what is better for him and compensated him for it. It was said that it is an affixation to let him be given more time because it is in the meaning of the report, as if it was said, whoever is in misguidance, God increases his misguidance and increases the equivalent of guidance for him. And the lasting good deeds are the acts of obedience whose benefits remain forever, and this includes what was said about the five daily prayers and saying Subhan God, Al-Hamdulillah, La ilaha illa God, and Allahu Akbar. Better in reward with your Lord refers to the transient blessings that the unbelievers have enjoyed, which they are proud of, especially since their end is eternal bliss, while the end of this is regret and eternal torment, as he indicated by his saying: And better in return. The good here is either simply an increase or in the manner of their saying, Summer is hotter than winter, meaning that its heat is more intense than its cold.
19:77: 77 - Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children?'" It was revealed about Al-'As bin Wa'il. Khabbab owed him wealth and demanded it from him. The verse said to him, "No, not until you disbelieve in Muhammad. He said, No, by God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad, alive or dead, nor when you are resurrected. He said, Then when you are resurrected, come to me and I will have wealth and children, and I will give you. Since seeing is the strongest support for reporting, Have you seen" was used in the sense of reporting. The root of the letter "fa" is in following, and the meaning is: He reported the story of this disbeliever after the story of those. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read "child, which is the plural of child like lion in lion, or a dialect in it like Arab and Arabs".
19:78: 78 - He has seen the unseen. He has reached such great status that he has ascended to the knowledge of the unseen, which is unique to the One, the Compeller, until he claimed that he would be given wealth and children in the Hereafter and he swore an oath to do so. Or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful? Or he took a covenant from the Knower of the Unseen about that, for one cannot attain knowledge of it except through one of these two paths. It has been said that the covenant is the word of testimony and righteous action, for God has promised reward for them like the covenant upon Him.
19:79: 79 - No is a deterrent and a warning that he is wrong in what he imagined for himself. We will write what he says. We will show him that we wrote what he said in the way he said it: If we were related, I would not have been born mean That is, it turns out that I was not born mean, or we will take revenge on him as he wrote the enemy’s crime and preserved it for him, for the writing itself does not delay the saying, according to the Almighty’s saying: Not a word does he utter but there is by him an observer ready to record it. “And We will prolong for him the punishment” and We will prolong for him the punishment he deserves, or We will increase his punishment and multiply it for him for his disbelief, slander, and mockery of God, may He be glorified and exalted. Therefore, He emphasized it with the infinitive to indicate the intensity of His anger with him.
19:80: 80 - And We inherit him upon his death. What he says meaning money and children. And he comes to Us on the Day of Resurrection. Alone not accompanied by money or children who had the advantage of being brought to us in this world, then more. And it was said alone rejecting this statement and being unique from it.
19:81: 81 - And they have taken gods besides God that they may be a source of strength for them so that they may be strengthened by them, as they may have a connection to God and intercessors with Him.
19:82: 82 - No is a deterrent and denial of their being strengthened by it. They will disbelieve in their worship. The gods will deny their worship and will say, You did not worship Us, according to the Almighty's saying: When those who followed disavowed those who followed. Or the disbelievers will deny the evil consequence of worshipping them, according to the Almighty's saying: Then their only trial was that they said, 'By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists.' "And they will be an opponent to them." The first is supported if the opposite is interpreted as the opposite of glory, meaning, and they will be humiliated by them, or their opposite in the sense that it will be an aid in their punishment by lighting their fires with it, or making the waw for the disbelievers, meaning, they will be disbelievers in them after they used to worship it, and its unification is due to the unity of the meaning by which they oppose it, so they are like one thing, and similar to it is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "And they are a hand against whoever is other than them. And No" was read with the tanween, by changing the alif to a nun when stopping, changing the alif of release in his saying: I blame the critic and the reproacher less Or on the meaning of all this opinion, both and both, on the implication of a verb that is explained by what follows, meaning they will deny, No, they will disbelieve in their worship.
19:83: 83 - Have you not seen that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers to give them power over them or to provide them with companions. To incite them to incite them and tempt them to sin with suggestions and to make lusts attractive. What is meant is the astonishment of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the sayings of the disbelievers and their persistence in error and their determination to disbelieve after the truth has become clear as stated in the previous verses.
19:84: 84 - So do not hasten their destruction until you and the believers are relieved of their evils and the earth is purified of their corruption. We only count for them the days of their appointed times. A count meaning do not hasten their destruction, for they only have a limited number of days and a limited number of breaths left.
19:85: 85 - The Day We shall gather the righteous We shall gather them. To the Most Gracious To their Lord Who has overwhelmed them with His mercy. And the testing of this name in this Surah is important, and perhaps because the context of this speech in it is to enumerate His great blessings and explain the state of those who are grateful for them and those who are ungrateful for them, as a delegation coming to Him as delegations come to kings, awaiting their honor and favors.
19:86: 86- And We will drive the criminals as animals are driven. To Hell, thirsty, for whoever wants water does not want it except because of thirst, or like the animals that want water.
19:87: 87- They do not possess intercession The pronoun in it refers to the servants indicated by the mention of the two sections, which is the subject of the Day. Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful Except for he who is adorned with what he prepares himself with and is worthy of interceding for the sinners from faith and righteous deeds according to what God the Most High has promised, or except for he who has taken permission from God for it, as in His saying the Most High: Intercession does not benefit except for he to whom the Most Merciful has given permission from their saying: The emir entrusted so-and-so with such-and-such if he ordered him to do it, and its place is the nominative as a substitute for the pronoun or the accusative as an estimated addition, meaning except the intercession of he who took, or as an exception. It was said that the pronoun refers to the criminals and the meaning is: They do not possess intercession for them except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, preparing himself to intercede for him with Islam.
19:88: 88- And they said, ‘The Most Gracious has taken a son.’ The pronoun has two possible meanings, because since this was said among people, it is permissible for it to be attributed to them.
19:89: 89- You have done something terrible to exaggerate the blame and record them for their audacity towards God Almighty. The word id with the fatha and kasra means great and reprehensible, and addah means severity and the least of the matter, and adni means it burdened me and was great for me.
19:90: 90- The heavens almost Nafi' and Al-Kisa'i read it with a ya'. They burst from it they split again and again, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza, Abu Bakr and Ya'qub read (they burst), and the first is more eloquent because the verb tafa'al is a passive participle of fa'l and the verb tafa'al is a passive participle of fa'l and because the root of the verb tafa'al is forced. And the earth splits and the mountains collapse in ruins "tahdaduhu or mahdhud, or because it is yadhadu meaning shattered" and it is a confirmation of its being an ad'a, and the meaning is that the horror of this word and its enormity are such that if it were imagined in a tangible form these huge bodies could not bear it and would crumble from its intensity, or that its horror brings about the wrath of God such that if it were not for His forbearance, He would have destroyed the world and scattered its pillars in anger at whoever uttered it.
19:91: 91- "That they invoke a son for the Most Gracious may be in the accusative case as a reason for almost or for guide" with the deletion of the lam and the verb leading to it, and the genitive case with the omission of the lam or by substitution of the ha in it and the nominative case as it is the predicate of a deleted word whose estimation is the reason for that "that they invoke, or the subject of guide" meaning he guided her with a supplication. The son belongs to the Most Gracious, and it is from the verb da’a meaning named which is transitive to two objects, and it was limited to the second object to include everything that was called a son for, or from the verb da’a meaning relative whose passive form is ada’a to someone if he is related to him.
19:92: 92- And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son. It is not befitting for Him to take a son, nor would it be required of Him if He asked, for example, because it is impossible. Perhaps the arrangement of the ruling with the attribute of the Most Merciful is to indicate that everything other than Him is a blessing and a blessing upon Him, so it is not similar to the One who is the originator of all blessings and the Master of their origins and branches. So how can He take a son? Then He stated it explicitly in His saying:
19:93: 93- Indeed, everyone in the heavens and the earth meaning, there is none of them. except that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant except that he is owned by Him, resorting to Him in servitude and submission. Coming to the Most Merciful was read according to the original.
19:94: 94- He has counted them He has confined them and encompassed them so that they do not go beyond the realm of His knowledge and the grasp of His power. And He has counted them precisely He has counted their persons, their breaths, and their actions, for everything with Him is measured.
19:95: 95- And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone, separate from the followers and supporters. Nothing of that is similar to Him for Him to take as a son, nor is it suitable for Him to associate partners with Him.
19:96: 96- Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love. He will create affection in their hearts without them being exposed to its causes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When God loves a servant, He says to Gabriel, 'I love so-and-so, so love him.' Gabriel loves him, then he calls out to the people of heaven, 'God has loved so-and-so, so love him.' The people of heaven love him, then love is placed for him on earth." The seen is either because the surah was revealed in Mecca and they were hated at that time among the disbelievers, so He promised them that when Islam spread, or because the promise is made on the Day of Resurrection when their good deeds are presented to all witnesses, and whatever rancor is in their hearts is removed.
19:97: 97- We have made it easy for you by sending it down in your language, and the ba has the meaning of upon or upon in its origin, so that We have made it easy includes the meaning of We have sent it down meaning We have sent it down in your language. That you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous. Those who are on the path to piety. And warn with it a people who are obstinate, who are fierce in their disputes and who engage in every kind of argument, due to their extreme obstinacy. So give good tidings and warn with it.
19:98: 98- And how many generations before them have We destroyed to frighten the infidels and to make the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, bold in warning them. Do you perceive any of them? Do you sense any of them and see them? Or do you hear a whisper of theirs? It was also read hear from hear and hear means a low sound. The origin of the construction is concealment, and from it the spear is hearkened if its tip is hidden in the ground, and treasure means buried money. On the authority of the Messenger of God, "Whoever recites Surat Maryam will be given ten good deeds for the number of those who denied Zachariah and believed in him, and John and Mary and Jesus and all the prophets, may God bless them and grant them peace, mentioned in it, and for the number of those who called upon God in this world and those who did not call upon God."
20:1: 1- Taha was pronounced with emphasis by Qaloon, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Hafs. And Jacob is on the original, and Abu Amr and Warsh emphasized the letter ta alone. Because of its superiority and the rest of it is inclined. They are from the names of letters. It was said that its meaning is O man in the language of Akk. If it is correct, then perhaps its origin is O this, so they changed it by changing it and abbreviating it and citing his saying: Foolishness is a prey to you. Where are your morals? May God not sanctify the morals of the cursed. It is weak because it is possible that it is an oath, like His saying, Ha Meem, they will not be helped. And Ta Ha was read as an order to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to tread the ground with his feet, because he used to stand in his night prayers on one of his feet, and its origin is ta’a so its hamza was changed to a ha’ or it was changed in ya’ta’a to an alif like His saying, La hunka al-murta’a. Then he built on it the order and added to it the ha’ of silence. Based on this, it is possible that the origin of Ta Ha is ta’a and the alif was changed from the hamza and the ha’ is a metaphor for the ground, but that is rejected by writing them in the form of a letter, and likewise the interpretation is ya rajul or he was satisfied with the two halves of the words and referred to them by their name.
20:2: 2- We have not sent down the Qur'an to you to make you miserable is the predicate of Ta-Ha if you make it the subject as interpreted by the surah, or the Qur'an and the Qur'an is in it the position of the pronoun and its answer if you make it the oath by it and the vocative if you make it a vocative, and a resumption if it is a verbal or nominal sentence with an implied subject, or a group of letters reported and the meaning is: We have not sent down the Qur'an to you to tire yourself out with your excessive regret over the disbelief of Quraysh since all you have to do is reach it, or with much exercise and much night prayer and standing on one leg. Misery is commonly used to mean exhaustion and from it is more miserable than the one who trains a mare, and the master of the people is the most miserable of them. Perhaps it was modified to indicate that it was sent down to him to make him happy. It was said that it was a response and denial of the disbelievers, for when they saw his much worship they said that you are miserable by abandoning our religion and the Qur'an was sent down to you so that you are miserable by it.
20:3: 3- Except a reminder but a reminder, and its accusative is due to the interrupted exception, and it is not permissible for it to be a substitute for the place of to be miserable due to the difference in genders, nor an object for We sent down, because one verb does not extend to two causes. It was said that it is a source in the position of a state of the kaf or the Qur'an, or an object for it on the basis that to be miserable is related to an omitted word which is an attribute of the Qur'an, meaning We did not send down to you the Qur'an revealed so that you would tire yourself by conveying it except as a reminder. For he who fears for he in whose heart there is fear and tenderness that is affected by the warning, or for he from whom God knows that he fears by frightening him, because he is the one who benefits from it.
20:4: 4- Tanzilan is in the accusative case with the omission of its verb or with yakhas, or for praise or in apposition to tadhkira if it is made a state, and if it is made an object for it in wording or meaning then no because a thing is not explained by itself or by its type. From Him who created the earth and the high heavens with what follows it to His saying To Him belong the best names is an exaggeration of the status of the one who sent it by excessively glorifying the one who sent it by mentioning its actions and attributes in the order that is with the mind, so He began with the creation of the earth. And the heavens, which are the origins of the world, and He put the earth first because it is closer to the senses and more apparent to Him than the highest heavens, and it is the plural of the highest, the feminine of the highest, then He indicated the way in which the creation of beings and the management of their affairs were created by intending the throne and from it He carried out the rulings and measures, and from it He sent down the causes in order and measures according to what His wisdom required and what His will was attached to, so He said:
20:5: 5- The Most Gracious is firmly established on the Throne to indicate the perfection of His power and will.
20:6: 6- To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is under the soil. Since power is subordinate to will and is inseparable from knowledge, then His knowledge encompasses the obvious and hidden aspects of things alike, so He said:
20:7: 7- And if you speak aloud, then indeed He knows the secret and what is even more hidden. That is, if you speak aloud in the remembrance of God and invoke Him, then know that He is independent of your speaking aloud, for He, glory be to Him, knows the secret and what is even more hidden than it, which is the conscience of the soul. And in it is a warning that the legislation of remembrance and invocation and speaking aloud in them is not to inform God, but to depict the negation in remembrance and to establish it in it and to prevent it from being occupied with anything other than Him and to digest it through supplication and invocation. Then, when it became clear by this that He is the One who has gathered the attributes of divinity, He explained that He is the One who is unique in them and is unique in their requirements, so He said:
20:8: 8- God, there is no god but He; to Him belong the best names. And whoever in of those who created the earth is a connection to a revelation or an attribute of to Him. The transition from speaking to the third person is to diversify speech and magnify the revelation from two aspects: attributing its revelation to the pronoun of the One, the Great in status, and attributing it to the One who is distinguished by the attributes of majesty and honor, and drawing attention to the fact that it is obligatory to believe in it and submit to it, since it is the speech of one of this status. It is possible that We revealed it as a narration of the speech of Gabriel and the angels who descended with him. The Most Gracious was read in the accusative case as an attribute of those who created, so He rose over the throne would be a deleted predicate. Likewise, if The Most Gracious is raised in praise without the beginning, and it is possible that it is a second predicate. The soil is the dusty layer of the earth and it is its last layer, and the best is the feminine of the best, and the superiority of the names of God the Most High over all other names in beauty is because they indicate meanings that are the most honorable and best of meanings.
20:9: 9- And has there come to you the story of Moses? He followed the introduction to his prophethood, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the story of Moses, so that he could follow his example in bearing the burdens of prophethood, conveying the message, and being patient in the face of hardships, for this surah was among the first to be revealed.
20:10: 10- When he saw a fire is an adverb for the hadith because it is an event or an action, not a mention. It was said that he asked permission from Shu'aib, peace be upon them, to go out to his mother, and he went out with his family. When he reached the valley of Tuwa, in which was the mountain, a son was born to him on a dark, snowy winter night. It was a Friday night, and he had lost his way and his livestock had scattered when he saw a fire on the side of the mountain. So he said to his family, 'Stay here.' Stay where you are. Hamza read to his family, stay here. In Al-Qasas, the ha' is pronounced with a damma in the connection, while the rest read it with a kasra. Indeed, I perceived a fire. I saw it with a sight that was without doubt. It was said that familiarity is seeing something that brings familiarity. Perhaps I can bring you a torch from it. A flame from the fire, and it was said a coal. Or I find guidance over the Fire a guide who shows me the way or guides me to the gates of religion, for the thoughts of the righteous are inclined towards it in everything that comes to mind for them. And since their occurrence is anticipated, the matter in them is built on hope, unlike familiarity, which was certain, and therefore He made it certain for them so that they would prepare themselves for it. The meaning of superiority in over the Fire is that its people are overlooking it or are superior to the place close to it, as Sibawayh said in: I passed by Zayd, for he is stuck in a place close to it.
20:11: 11- "So when he came to it" meaning the fire, he found a white fire burning in a green tree. "He was called, 'O Moses.'"
20:12: 12- I am your Lord Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr opened it, meaning that I am, and the rest closed it by implying the statement or making the call its course, and repeating the pronoun for emphasis and verification. It was said that when he was called, he said: Who is the speaker? He said: I am God, then Satan whispered to him, perhaps you hear the words of Satan, so he said: I know that it is the speech of God, meaning I hear it from all sides and with all limbs. It is an indication that he, peace and blessings be upon him, received the words of his Lord spiritually, then that speech was represented to his body and transferred to the common sense, so it was engraved with it without being specific to a limb or direction. Then take off your shoes he ordered him to do so because barefootness is humility and good manners, and that is why the predecessors circumambulated barefoot. It was said that it was due to the impurity of his shoes, as they were made of untanned pig skin. It was also said that it means empty your heart of family and money. You are in the sacred valley is an explanation for the command to respect the place, and the sacred is possible in both meanings. Tawwa is an apposition to the valley, and its nun is Ibn Amir and the Kufians interpreting it as a place. It was said that it is like thana from tayy, a source for nawadi or al-maqdis, meaning: he was called twice or sanctified twice.
20:13: 13- And I have chosen you I selected you for prophethood. Hamza read (And We have chosen you). So listen to what is revealed to what is revealed to you, or to the revelation, and the lam may be related to both verbs.
20:14: 14- Indeed, I am God, there is no god but Me, so worship Me instead of what is revealed, indicating that it is limited to establishing monotheism, which is the ultimate knowledge, and commanding worship, which is the perfection of action. 20:117: 117- So We said, 'O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so do not let him expel you both.' So that they do not become a cause for your expulsion. What is meant is to forbid them from being such that Satan causes them to be expelled from Paradise, so that you become miserable. And He singled him out by attributing the misery to him after making them share in the expulsion, as it is sufficient that his misery entails her misery, since he is responsible for her and maintains the separations, or because what is meant by misery is the fatigue in seeking a livelihood, and that is the job of men. This is supported by His saying:
20:118: 118- You will neither go hungry nor naked therein.
20:119: 119- And that you will neither be thirsty therein nor exposed to the sun is a statement and reminder of the reasons for sufficiency and the pillars of sufficiency that are satiety, quenching thirst, clothing, and housing for him in Paradise, without needing to acquire them or strive to attain goals that may be cut off and removed by mentioning their opposites, so that his ears may be struck by the types of misery that he has been warned against. And the conjunction, even though it replaces that, it replaces that, but it replaces that in terms of it being an agent, not in terms of it being a letter of confirmation, so its entry on that is not prevented by the entry of that on it. Nafi and Abu Bakr read (And that you will not be thirsty) with a kasra on the hamza, and the rest with a fatha on it.
20:120: 120- Then Satan whispered to him, and his whispering reached him. He said, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of immortality?' The tree from which whoever eats will become immortal and will never die. So he attributed it to immortality, meaning eternity, because it is its cause, according to his claim. And a kingdom that will not decay, that will not disappear or weaken.
20:121: 121- So they ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. They began to stick the leaves over their private parts to cover themselves, and they were fig leaves. And Adam disobeyed his Lord by eating from the tree. So he went astray. He went beyond what was desired and was disappointed when he sought immortality by eating from the tree, or from what was commanded, or from guidance when he was deceived by the words of the enemy. And it was read (Faghwa) from the word ghawa which means that a young camel becomes full of milk. In blaming him for his disobedience and misguidance despite the smallness of his mistake, there is a magnification of the mistake and a strong warning to his children about it.
20:122: 122- Then his Lord chose him He chose him and brought him close by encouraging him to repent and granting him success in it from ajba ila kadha faajtabituhu like jalayta ala al-aroos faajtalayha, and the original meaning of the word is plural. Fa'atu 'alayhi al-sallam So He accepted his repentance when he repented. And guided to steadfastness in repentance and to be certain of the reasons for infallibility.
20:123: 123- "He said, 'Descend from it, both of you.'" The address was to Adam and Eve, or to him and to Satan, since they were the original descendants. He addressed them as they would address them, saying, "Some of you are enemies to others," for the sake of livelihood, as people do, of attraction and war, or for the disruption of the state of each of the two types by means of the other. The first is supported by His statement, "But if there comes to you guidance from Me," a Book and a Messenger. "So whoever follows My guidance will not go astray, in this world, nor will he be miserable," in the Hereafter.
20:124: 124- And whoever turns away from My remembrance from the guidance that remembers Me and calls to My worship. He will have a depressed life. A narrow source that is described by it, and therefore it is the same for both males and females. It was read (Dhanka) like Sakra, because the focus of his ambition and the aspirations of his sight are on the worldly matters, he is obsessed with its increase and fears its decrease, unlike the believer who seeks the Hereafter, although the Almighty may be distressed by the evil of disbelief and expand by the blessing of faith, as He said, And humiliation and poverty were imposed upon them. "And if only they had established the Torah and the Gospel. And if only the people of the towns had believed and feared God." The verses. It was said that it is the thorn and the thorn in the Fire, and it was said that it is the torment of the grave. "And We will gather him. It was read with the ha' silent in the form of a pause and with the jazm in apposition to the place of He will have a depressed life," because it is the answer to the condition. "On the Day of Resurrection blind." Blind of sight or heart, and the first is supported.
20:125: 125- He said, 'My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was seeing?' Hamza and Al-Kisa'i made them inclined because the alif was changed from the ya', and Abu Amr made the distinction by saying that the first is the beginning of the verse and the place of the pause, so it is worthy of being changed.
20:126: 126- "He said, 'Likewise,' meaning you did the same thing, then you explain it. He said, 'Our signs came to you,' clear and bright. 'But you forgot them,' so you were blind to them and left them without looking at them. 'Likewise,' and like your leaving them, 'today you will be forgotten,' you will be left in blindness and torment.
20:127: 127- And thus do We recompense him who transgressed by being immersed in desires and turning away from the signs. And did not believe in the signs of his Lord but rather denied them and contradicted them. And the punishment of the Hereafter which is the gathering in blindness, and it was said the punishment of the Fire, meaning the Fire after that. is more severe and lasting than the hardship of life or from it and from blindness, and perhaps when he enters the Fire his blindness will go away so that he can see his place and state or from what he did of abandoning the signs and disbelieving in them.
20:128: 128- Have they not been guided? is attributed to God Almighty or the Messenger or what indicates it. How many generations before them have We destroyed? meaning our destruction of them or the sentence with its content, and the verb is dependent on the first ones and runs in the course of I know and is indicated by the reading with the letter nun. "They walk in their dwellings" and see the signs of their destruction. "Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding" for those with minds that prevent negligence and blindness.
20:129: 129- And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord which is the promise to delay the punishment of this nation until the Hereafter. It would have been inevitable, as was revealed to 'Aad and Thamud, it would have been inevitable for these disbelievers. It is a source described by it or a tool name that is called inevitable due to its extreme necessity, like their saying Lazzaz is an opponent. And a specified term is in apposition to the word, meaning, and had it not been for the promise to delay the punishment and a specified term for their lives, or for their punishment, which is the Day of Resurrection or the Day of Badr, the punishment would have been inevitable. The separation is to indicate the independence of each of them by negating the necessity of the punishment. It is permissible to apposition it to what is implied in was meaning, the immediate taking and a specified term would have been inevitable for him.
20:130: 130- "So be patient over what they say and exalt [God] with praise of your Lord." And pray while praising your Lord for His guidance and success, or absolving Him from polytheism and all the shortcomings they attribute to Him, praising Him for what He has distinguished you with through guidance, acknowledging that He is the Master of all blessings. "Before the rising of the sun" means dawn. "And before its setting" means noon and afternoon because they are at the end of the day or afternoon alone. "And during the hours of the night and during its hours, plural ana with kasra and shortening, or ana" with fatha and extension. "So exalt" means sunset and evening. Or the time of the night was brought forward because it is specifically for greater virtue, because the heart is more united in it and the soul is more inclined to rest, so worship is more intense in it. For this reason, the Almighty said: "Indeed, the hours of the night are most effective for concurrence and most suitable for saying." And the ends of the day is a repetition of the dawn and sunset prayers, intending to be specific, and it is used in the plural form to avoid confusion, as in his saying: Their backs are like the backs of two gears. Or he ordered the noon prayer, because it is the end of the first half of the day and the beginning of the other half, and he combined it by considering the two halves or because the day is a type, or by volunteering in parts of the day. Perhaps you will be satisfied is related to glorify, meaning glorify at these times in the hope that you will attain from God what will please you. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Bakr read it in the passive form, meaning that your Lord will please you.
20:131: 131- "And do not extend your eyes" meaning the sight of your eyes. "To that which We have given enjoyment with" approving of it and wishing that you would have the same. "Wives from them" and types of disbelievers. It is possible that it is a state of the pronoun in it and the object from them, meaning that which We have given enjoyment with, and it is types of some of them or people from them. "The flower of the life of this world is accusative by an omitted word indicated by We have given enjoyment or with it to include the meaning of We have given, or by a substitute for the place of with it or from wives" by estimating an added word and below it, or by blame, which is adornment and joy. Ya'qub read it with the fat-ha, which is a language like the loudness in loudness, or the plural of zahir, describing them as zahir of this world for their enjoyment and the splendor of their attire, unlike what the ascetic believers are upon. "To test them in it" to try them and examine them in it, or to torment them in the Hereafter because of it. “And your Lord’s provision” and what He has stored for you in the Hereafter, or what He has provided you with of guidance and prophethood. is better than what He has given them in this world. And more lasting for it is never interrupted.
20:132: 132- And enjoin prayer upon your family He commanded him to command his family or those who follow him from his nation to pray after he commanded it so that they would cooperate in using it to help them in their poverty and not be concerned with the matter of livelihood or pay attention to the attention of the wealthy. And be patient with it and continue to do it. We do not ask you for provision meaning that you provide for yourself or your family. We provide for you and them so devote your mind to the matter of the Hereafter. And the good end is praiseworthy. For piety for those who have piety. It was narrated that whenever his family was afflicted with harm, he would command them to pray and recite this verse.
20:133: 133- And they said, 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?' A sign indicating his truthfulness in giving prophethood, or a suggested sign denying the signs he brought, or to take it as an obstinate and stubborn belief. So he obliged them to bring him the Qur'an, which is the mother of miracles and the greatest and most lasting of them, because the reality of a miracle is the specialization of the claimant of prophethood with a type of knowledge or action in an extraordinary manner. There is no doubt that knowledge is the root of action and is higher in status and more lasting in effect, so is what is of this type. He also alerted them to a clearer aspect of the aspects of his miracle that are specific to this chapter, so he said: Did there not come to them a clear proof of what was in the former scriptures? From the Torah and the Gospel and all the other heavenly books, for its inclusion of the essence of what is in it of beliefs and general rulings, even though the one who brought it was illiterate and did not see it and did not learn from those who taught it, is a clear miracle, and in it is a notification that just as it indicates his prophethood, it is proof of what preceded it from the books in terms of it being a miracle, and that is not like that. Rather, it lacks what testifies to its authenticity. Al-Sahuf was read with a light pronunciation, and Nafi’, Abu Amr, and Hafs on the authority of Asim read Awlma ta’tuhum with a ta’, and the rest with a ya’.
20:134: 135- And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it before Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, or the evidence and reminder because it is in the sense of righteousness, or what is meant by it is the Qur’an. "They would have said, 'Our Lord, if only You had sent to us a messenger so we could have followed Your signs before we were humiliated' by being killed and taken captive in this world. "And disgraced' by entering the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. And it has been read in the passive form in both of them.
20:135: 135- "Say: Every one of us and you. Waiting is waiting for what will happen to us and you. Wait is also read as Fatamuu. You will know who are the companions of the straight path is the straight path. It was also read as as-sawaa meaning the good middle and as-sawaa and as-su'a meaning evil, and as-sawaa is its diminutive. And whoever is guided from misguidance and who in both places is for interrogation and its place is the nominative case as a subject. It is permissible for the second to be a relative unlike the first due to the lack of a pronoun, so it is conjoined with the place of the interrogative sentence from which the verb is suspended, on the basis that knowledge means knowledge or on the companions or on the path, on the basis that what is meant by it is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Ta-Ha will be given on the Day of Resurrection the reward of the Muhajireen and Ansar, may God be pleased with them all.
21:1: 1- The reckoning of the people has drawn near in addition to what has passed or what is with God, as God the Almighty says: Indeed, they see it far off, but We see it near. And His saying: "And they urge you to hasten the punishment, but God will not fail in His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count." Or because everything that is coming is near, and what is far is what has passed and is gone. The lam is a connection to drawn near or an emphasis on the addition, and its origin is that the reckoning of the people has drawn near, then the reckoning of the people has drawn near, then the reckoning of the people has drawn near. And He specified the people as the disbelievers to restrict them with His saying: And they are in heedlessness, meaning in heedlessness of the reckoning. Turning away from contemplating it, and they are two predicates of the pronoun. It is possible that the circumstance is a state of what is implied in turning away.
21:2: 2- "Whatever comes to them of a reminder" alerts them from the year of heedlessness and ignorance. "From their Lord is an attribute of reminder or a connection to comes to them". "Revealed" is sent down to repeat the reminder to their ears so that they may learn a lesson, and it was read in the nominative case based on the location. "Except that they listen to it while they are playing" mocking it and ridiculing it due to the extent of their heedlessness and their extreme aversion to considering matters and contemplating the consequences. "While they are playing" is a state of the waw. Likewise:
21:3: 3- Lahiyyat Qulubhum meaning they listened to it, combining mockery, distraction and forgetfulness from thinking about it. It is possible that it is from the waw of ya'aliboon and it was read in the nominative case as another predicate for the pronoun. And they kept the secret they exaggerated in concealing it or made it such that their secret conversation was hidden. Those who wronged is a substitute for the waw of and kept the secret to indicate that they were wrongdoers in what they kept secret, or it is the subject of it and the waw is for the sign of the plural or it is the subject and the previous sentence is its predicate and its origin is and these kept the secret so the relative pronoun was put in its place to record their action as being wrong or it is accusative for blame. Is this anything but a human being like you? Then do you practice magic while you see? With his command in the accusative case instead of the whispering secret, or as an object of an implied statement, as if they used his being a human as evidence of his falsehood in claiming the message, because they believed that the messenger could only be an angel, and they inferred from him that what he brought of miracles such as the Qur’an was magic, so they denied his presence, and they only kept it secret to consult about deducing what would destroy his matter and reveal his corruption to the people in general.
21:4: 4- He said, 'My Lord knows what is said in the heavens and the earth' whether it is public or secret, rather than what they concealed, so it is more emphatic than His statement, Say, 'He sent it down who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth' and that is why it was chosen here and to match His statement, And they whispered secretly in exaggeration. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read He said as a report on the authority of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing so nothing is hidden from Him what they conceal or what they conceal.
21:5: 5- Rather, they said, 'Confused dreams. Rather, he invented it. Rather, he is a poet.'" This is a diversion from their saying that it is magic to that it is a mixture of dreams, then to that it is the speech of a poet. It appears that the first "rather" is to complete the story and begin with another, or to divert from their dialogue about the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what appeared to him of the signs to their exchange of words about the Qur'an. The second and third are to divert from their saying that it is falsehoods that were imagined to him and mixed up to him, to that he invented them on his own, then to that it is poetic speech that imagines to the listener meanings that have no reality and makes him desire them. It is possible that all of this is from God, a revelation of their sayings in the degree of corruption, because its being poetry is further from being invented, because it is loaded with truths and wisdom, and there is nothing in it that suits the saying of poets. It is from being dreams because it includes many hidden things that match reality, and the inventor is not like that, unlike dreams. And because they tested the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, more than once. And forty years and they never heard a lie from him, and it is further from being magic because it is similar to it in that they are both miracles. Then let him bring us a sign as the former ones were sent meaning as the former ones were sent, such as the white hand, the staff, healing the blind, and bringing the dead back to life. The simile is correct in that sending includes bringing a sign.
21:6: 6- No town believed before them of the people of a town. We destroyed it by suggesting the verses when they came to them. Do they believe? if you brought them to them while they were more stubborn than them, and in it is a warning that not bringing what was suggested was to preserve them, because if it was brought and they did not believe, they would deserve the punishment of extermination like those before them.
21:7: 7- And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed, so ask the people of the message if you do not know. This is an answer to their saying, Is this anything but a human being like you? So He ordered them to ask the People of the Book about the state of the previous messengers in order to remove any doubt or referral to them, either for the sake of obligation, for the polytheists used to consult them about the matter of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and they trusted their words, or because informing a large crowd necessitates knowledge, even if they were disbelievers. Hafs read (Our revelation) with a noon.
21:8: 8- And We did not make them bodies that did not eat food, nor were they immortal. A denial of what they believed to be among the characteristics of the angels from the messengers, in confirmation, because they were human beings like them. And it was said that it is an answer to their saying, What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? "And they were not immortal." An emphasis and confirmation of it, because living on food is among the consequences of analysis that leads to annihilation and the unification of the body to will the species, or because it is a source in the original or on the deletion of the added or the interpretation of the pronoun with each one, and it is a body with a color, so it is not applied to water and air, and from it bodies for saffron. And it was said a body with a composition because its origin is to collect something and its intensity.
21:9: 9- Then We fulfilled the promise to them meaning in the promise. And We saved them and whomever We willed meaning the believers in them and whoever there is wisdom in keeping them alive, such as whoever will believe or one of his descendants, and for this reason the Arabs were protected from the punishment of extermination. And We destroyed the transgressors in disbelief and sins.
21:10: 10- We have sent down to you O Quraysh a Book meaning the Qur’an. In it is your remembrance your reputation as He says and indeed it is a reminder for you and your people or your admonition or what you seek through it to be a good mention of noble morals. Do you not then reason so you will believe.
21:11: 11- And how many a town have We destroyed meaning great wrath because destruction is a break that shows the harmony of parts, unlike separation. It was unjust is a description of its people and it was described by it when it was established in its place. And We brought forth after it after the destruction of its people. Another people in their place.
21:12: 12- So when they perceived Our punishment So when they realized the severity of Our punishment, realizing the tangible scenes, and the pronoun refers to the deleted family. At once they were running from it They fled quickly, running their animals, or they were likened to them due to their extreme speed.
21:13: 13- "Do not run on the intention of the statement, that is, it was said to them mockingly, Do not run" either by the tongue of the state or the statement, and the speaker was an angel or then one of the believers. "And return to what you were in luxury" of enjoyment, pleasure and luxury is the vanity of the blessing. "And your dwellings" that were yours. "Perhaps you will be questioned" tomorrow about your deeds or you will be punished, for questioning is one of the preludes to punishment, or you will intend to ask and consult about important matters and calamities.
21:14: 14- They said, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.' When they saw the punishment and did not see the way to escape, it did not benefit them. It was said that the people of Hadur, a village in Yemen, had a prophet sent to them, so they killed him. Then God empowered Nebuchadnezzar over them, so he put the sword to them, and a caller from the sky called out, Oh, revenge for the prophets! So they regretted it and said that.
21:15: 15- And that was their call" they kept repeating that, and he called it a call because the howling one is as if he is calling for woe and saying: Woe, come, this is your time, and both "that and their call" can be nominal or predicative. "Until We made them a harvest" like harvest, which is the harvested plant, and for this reason it was not pluralized. "Extinguished dead from the word khamdat an-nar and it is with harvested" in the position of the second object like you say: I made it sweet and sour, because the meaning is: And We made them gatherers, similar to harvest and extinction, or a description of it, or a state of its pronoun.
21:16: 16- And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play. Rather, We created them filled with various kinds of wonders as an insight for the observers, a reminder for those who consider, and a cause for what will organize the affairs of the servants in this world and the hereafter. So they should climb through them to attain perfection and not be deceived by their decorations, for they quickly disappear.
21:17: 17- If We had intended to take a diversion something to be diverted and played with. We would have taken it from Our Presence from the aspect of Our power, or from Us from what is appropriate for Our Presence from abstract things, not from raised bodies and spread out bodies as is your custom in raising ceilings and decorating them and leveling and beautifying the carpets. It was said that diversion is the child in the language of Yemen, and it was said that it is the wife, and what is meant by it is a response to the Christians if We were to do that, and it indicates the answer to the previous answer. It was said that if is negative and the sentence is like the result of the conditional.
21:18: 18- Rather, We cast the truth upon falsehood. This is a denial of taking amusement and purifying it from playing. That is, it is our nature to make the truth, which includes seriousness, prevail over falsehood, which includes amusement. And destroys it means annihilating it. He only used a metaphor for that, which is the distant throw that requires the hardness of the target, and the destruction, which is the breaking of the brain such that its membrane is torn, leading to the loss of the soul, as a depiction of its nullification and exaggeration. And destroys it was read in the accusative case, as in His saying: I will leave my home to Banu Tamim and go to Hijaz to rest His face with the burden on the meaning and the conjunction with (the truth). Then it will perish perishing and perishing is the departure of the soul and he mentioned it to suggest the metaphor. And for you is woe for what you describe from what you describe him with which is not permissible for him and it is in the position of the state and what is a source or relative or described. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of God, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 18 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Anbiyāa, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Mu'minūn. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time.
