22:10: 10- That is because of what your hands have put forth on the shift, or the intention of saying, that is, he will be told on the Day of Resurrection that this disgrace and torment is because of what he committed of disbelief and sins. And that God is not unjust to the servants, but rather He is rewarding them for their deeds, and the exaggeration is due to the large number of servants.
22:11: 11- And among the people is he who worships God on the edge on the edge of the religion, not steadfast in it, like the one who is on the edge of the army, if he wins something good he is reassured by it, otherwise he flees. If good befalls him he is reassured by it, but if a trial befalls him he turns back on his face. It was narrated that it was revealed about some Bedouins who came to Madinah. When one of them became healthy physically, his mare gave birth to a healthy foal, his wife gave birth to a healthy boy, and his wealth and livestock increased, he would say: I have not experienced anything since I entered this religion of mine except good and he would be reassured. But if things were otherwise, he would say: I have experienced nothing but evil and he would turn back. And on the authority of Abu Saeed, "A Jew converted to Islam and was afflicted with calamities, so he had a bad omen about Islam. So he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: "Excuse me." He said: "Islam is not to be excused." So it was revealed. He lost this world and the Hereafter by losing his protection and his deeds being in vain due to his apostasy. It was read as loser in the accusative case as a state and in the nominative case as an agent, and it was placed like the apparent in place of the pronoun, explicitly stating his loss or that it is the predicate of an omitted word. That is the manifest loss because there is no loss like it.
22:12: 12- He calls upon, besides God, that which neither harms him nor benefits him. He worships an inanimate object that neither harms nor benefits itself. That is the farthest error. From the goal, borrowed from the word delusion from the one who goes far astray in the wilderness.
22:13: 13- He calls upon whoever harms him by being worshipped because it requires killing in this world and torment in the hereafter. Closer than his benefit which is expected by worshipping him, which is intercession and seeking intercession through it to God Almighty, and the lam is attached to calls upon in that it means he claims, and the claim is a statement with belief, or it is included in the sentence that is said, making it run like a statement: that is, the disbeliever says that with a prayer and screaming when he sees that he is harmed by it, or it is a new sentence on the basis that he calls upon a repetition of the first and from the subject of its predicate What an evil protector is the helper. And what an evil companion is the friend.
22:14: 14- “Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Indeed, God does what He wills.” There is no repelling or preventing the reward of the righteous monotheist and the punishment of the wicked polytheist.
22:15: 15- Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter This is a brief statement, and the meaning is: God will support His Messenger in this world and the Hereafter. So whoever thinks otherwise and expects it out of his anger. It was said that what is meant by victory is provision, and the pronoun refers to whom. Then let him extend a rope to the sky and then cut it off. So let him strive to remove his anger or his impatience by doing everything that someone filled with anger or someone who is extremely impatient does, even extending a rope to the sky of his house and choking from cutting off when he chokes, because the one who is choking cuts himself by blocking his airways. It was said that let him extend a rope to the lowest heaven and then cut the distance with it until he reaches its reins, and strive to repel his victory or obtain his provision. Warsh, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read (li-yaqta`) with a kasra on the lam. Fal-yanzur let him imagine in his mind, Will his plot go away? He did that and called it plotting because it is the limit of what he is capable of. What enrages is his anger or what enrages him is God’s victory. It was said that it was revealed about a group of Muslims who were slow to receive God’s victory because of their haste and intense anger at the polytheists.
22:16: 16- And likewise and similar to that revelation. We sent it down We sent down the entire Qur'an. Clear signs clear. And that God guides with it or establishes upon guidance whoever He desires to guide him or establish him, He sent it down thus, making it clear.
22:17: 17- Indeed, those who have believed and those who are Jews or Christians or Sabeans or Magians or polytheists - indeed, God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection by judging them and showing the one who is right among them over the one who is wrong, or by retribution, so He will reward each one according to what is appropriate for him and admit him to the place prepared for him. Indeed, in was inserted on each of the two ends of the sentence for further emphasis. Indeed, God is Witness over all things Knowing of them and observing their conditions.
22:18: 18- Have you not seen that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth is subject to His power and cannot be achieved by His management, or His humility indicates the greatness of His Manager, and it is permissible to include those with reason and others on the predominance, so His saying: And the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the beasts is singling them out for mention due to their fame and the remoteness of that from them. And and the beasts was read with a light vowel to dislike doubling or combining two quiescent letters. And many people is a conjunction to it if it is permissible to apply one word to each of its concepts, and to attribute it based on one of them to a matter and based on the other to another, then specifying many indicates the particularity of the meaning attributed to them, or a subject whose predicate is deleted and indicated by the predicate of its counterpart such as the reward is due to him, or the subject of an implied verb, meaning and many people prostrate to Him in obedience. And many have the punishment justly deserved because of their disbelief and refusal to obey. It is permissible to make and many a repetition of the first, to exaggerate the number of those who deserve punishment, and to link it to those who prostrate in the general sense, described by what comes after it. Haqq was read with the damma and haqq with the implied verb. And he whom God humiliates with misery there is none to honor him to honor him with happiness. It was read with the fatha, meaning honor. Indeed, God does what He wills of honor and humiliation.
22:19: 19- These two are opponents meaning two quarreling factions. That is why He said: They disputed based on the meaning, and if it were reversed it would be permissible, and what is meant by them are the believers and the disbelievers. About their Lord about His religion or His essence and attributes. It was said that the Jews and the believers disputed, so the Jews said: We are more deserving of God and we have a book and a prophet before your prophet, and the believers said: We are more deserving of God, we believed in Muhammad and your prophet and in what God has revealed of a book, and you know our book and our prophet, then you disbelieved in it out of envy, so it was revealed. As for those who disbelieved is a section for their dispute, and it is what is meant by the Almighty's saying: Indeed, God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. "It was cut out for them" was measured for them according to the sizes of their bodies, and it was read with a light pronunciation. "Garments of fire" fires that surround them as clothes surround. He pours boiling water over their heads. This is a dream from the pronoun in for them or a second piece of report. Hot water is boiling water.
22:20: 20- It melts what is in their bellies and their skins. That is, its extreme heat in their bellies affects their exteriors, so their insides melt as their skins melt. The sentence is a state of the boiling water or of their pronoun. It is read with emphasis for emphasis.
22:21: 21- And they will have whips of iron - whips with which they flog. The plural of muqammah is muqamma, and its true meaning is muqamma, meaning to suppress, that is, to restrain violently.
22:22: 22- Whenever they want to get out of it from the fire. From grief from its generality is a substitute for the ha' by repeating the preposition. They are returned to it meaning they get out, they are returned because the return does not happen except after the exit, and it was said that the flames of the fire will strike them and raise them to the top of it, so they will be struck with the clubs and fall into it. And taste meaning and it was said to them taste. The punishment of the burning meaning the fire that is extremely burning.
22:23: 23- "Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. He changed the style in it and attributed the admission to God the Most High and emphasized it with in" in praise of the state of the believers and glorification of their status. "They will be adorned therein from the word halliyyat" meaning to dress a woman in jewelry, and it was read with the lightening and the meaning is the same. "Of bracelets" is an attribute of a deleted object. "Aswar is the plural of aswarah which is the plural of swarah". "Of gold" is an explanation of it. "And pearls is in apposition to it and not to gold because the bracelet was not known from it unless it is intended to be studded with it, and Nafi' and Asim made them accusative in apposition to its place or by implying the accusative like and they give", and it was read (lu'lu'an) by changing the second to a waw and (lawliyan) by changing them both, and (lawwayn) then the second is changed to a ya' and (laylya) by changing them both to ya' and (lawl) like adl. And their clothing therein will be silk. This is a different style of speech to indicate that silk is their usual clothing, or to preserve the appearance of the joints.
22:24: 24- And they are guided to the good of speech which is their saying Praise be to God who has fulfilled His promise to us or the word of monotheism. And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy the Praiseworthy Himself or His outcome which is Paradise, or the Truth or the One deserving of praise in and of Himself which is God Almighty and His path is Islam.
22:25: 25- Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of God does not mean by it a present or future state, but rather it means by it the continuation of their aversion, like their saying: So-and-so gives and withholds, and that is why when he conjoined it with the past. And it was said that it is a state of the subject of disbelieved and the predicate of indeed is omitted and indicated by the end of the verse, meaning they are being punished. And the Sacred Mosque is in apposition to the name of God and the Hanafis begin it with Mecca and they cited as evidence his saying: Which We have made for mankind equal, the one who dwells therein and the visitor meaning the resident and the visitor on the impermissibility of selling or renting its houses, and despite its weakness it is opposed by the saying of God Almighty: Those who were expelled from their homes and the purchase of the prison house in it by Omar, may God be pleased with him, without any objection, and equal is an advanced predicate and the sentence is a second object for We have made it if he made for mankind a state of the ha' otherwise it is a state of what is hidden in it, and Hafs put it in the accusative case as the object or the state and the one who dwells is raised by it, and the one who dwells was read in the genitive case as a substitute for people. And whoever enters therein is from what left its object so that every seeker may include it, and it was read in the fat-ha from the arrivals. By atheism means deviating from the intention. By injustice means unjustly. These are two synonymous states, or the second is a substitute for the first by repeating the preposition or connecting it to it: meaning an atheist because of injustice such as polytheism and committing sins. We will make him taste a painful punishment is an answer to whoever.
22:26: 26- And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House. That is, remember when We appointed him and made it a place of rest for him. It was said that the lam is redundant and place is a circumstance, that is, when We sent him down in it. It was said that the House was raised to the sky and was obliterated during the days of the flood, so God informed him of its location by a wind that He sent, which swept away what was around it, so he built it on its old foundation. That you do not associate anything with Me, and purify My House for those who perform Tawaf, and those who stand, and those who bow and prostrate. “That” is an explanation of established in that it includes the meaning of our worship, because establishing a place is for the sake of worship, or it is a source connected to the prohibition, meaning: We did that so that you do not associate anything with My worship, and purify My House from idols and filth for those who perform Tawaf around it and pray in it. Perhaps he expressed the prayer with its pillars to indicate that each one of them is independent, as required by that, how and when they came together? Associates was read with a ya, and Nafi’, Hafs, and Hisham read My House with a fatha on the ya.
22:27: 27- And proclaim to the people Call to them and it was read (And proclaim). To the Hajj with the call to the Hajj and the command to do it. "It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ascended Abu Qubais and said: O people, perform the Hajj to the House of your Lord, so God made him hear from the loins of men and the wombs of women between the east and the west from those who had previously known that they would perform the Hajj." It was said that the address was to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he ordered that in the Farewell Pilgrimage. They will come to you on foot Plural of Rajil like Qaim and Qiyam, and it was read with a damma on the ra' and a light and heavy jim and rajala like ajala. And on every lean camel meaning and riders on every emaciated camel that has become tired after the journey and has become emaciated. They come is an attribute of lean and is based on its meaning, and it was read (they come) as an attribute of the men and riders or a resumption, so the pronoun is for the people "from every pass" road. "Deep" means far away, and it is read as (Mu'iq) It is said a deep well and Mu'aq has the same meaning.
22:28: 28- "That they may witness" to be present. "Benefits for them" religious and worldly, and its indefiniteness is because what is meant by it is a type of benefit specific to this act of worship. "And mention the name of God" when preparing gifts and sacrifices and slaughtering them. It was said that the mention was used as a metaphor for slaughtering because the slaughtering of Muslims is inseparable from it, indicating that it is the intended meaning of what brings them closer to God Almighty. "On known days" are the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah, and it was said the days of slaughtering. "On what He has provided for them of the cattle" He connected the verb to the one provided for and made it clear to the animal, inciting them to draw closer and drawing attention to the requirement of mention. "So eat from it" from its meat, He ordered that to permit it and remove what the people of ignorance were embarrassed about it, or to encourage sympathy with the poor and to be equal to them, and this is in what is voluntary and not obligatory. "And feed the poor" the one who has been afflicted with poverty, meaning hardship. The poor is the needy, and the command in it is for obligation, and it was said in the first.
22:29: 29- Then let them complete their untidiness Then let them remove their dirt by trimming the moustache and nails, plucking the armpit hairs, and shaving the pubic hair when they enter ihram. And fulfill their vows What they vow of righteousness during their Hajj, and it was said the obligations of Hajj. Abu Bakr read with the opening of the waw and the strengthening of the fa. And let them circumambulate The circumambulation of the corner with which the release is completed, as it is an indication of completing the untidiness, and it was said the farewell circumambulation. Ibn Amir alone read with the breaking of the lam in both. By the ancient house The ancient because it is the first house established for the people, or the one freed from the domination of tyrants, so how many tyrants have sent to it to demolish it, but God Almighty prevented them. As for Al-Hajjaj, he only intended to remove Ibn Al-Zubayr from it, not to dominate it.
22:30: 30- That is an omitted predicate, meaning that is the matter, and it and its likes are used to separate between two statements. And whoever honors the sacred things of God His rulings and everything else that is not permissible to violate, or the sanctuary and what is related to the Hajj of obligations. It was said that it is the Kaaba, the Sacred Mosque, the Sacred City, the Sacred Month, and the sacred month. It is better for him so honoring is better for him "With his Lord" as a reward. "And grazing livestock have been made lawful to you except what is recited to you" except what is recited to you as forbidden, which is what was forbidden from them due to an obstacle: such as dead animals and what was dedicated to other than God, so do not forbid from them anything other than what God has forbidden, such as the bahīrah and the sā'ibah. "So avoid the uncleanness of idols" so avoid the uncleanness which is idols as you avoid impurities, and this is the ultimate exaggeration in the prohibition of honoring them and repelling from worshipping them. And avoid false statement is a generalization after a specification, for the worship of idols is the head of falsehood. It is as if when he urged the veneration of sacred things, he followed that with a response to what the infidels were doing of forbidding lakes and saba’i’ and venerating idols and slandering God Almighty by ruling with that. And it was said that false testimony is because “it was narrated that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said, ‘False testimony is equal to associating partners with God Almighty’ three times, and he recited this verse.” And falsehood comes from falsehood, which means deviation, just as slander comes from afk, which means diversion, for lying is a deviation from reality.
22:31: 31- Hanif for God sincere to Him. Not associating anything with Him and these are two states of the waw. And whoever associates anything with God, it is as if he had fallen from the sky because he fell from the height of faith to the depths of disbelief. Then the birds snatch him away because bad desires distribute his thoughts. Nafi' alone read Fatkhatafahu with a fatha on the kha and a shaddah on the ta. Or the wind throws him down into a remote place far away because Satan has thrown him into misguidance. And the waw is for choice as in the saying of God the Most High: Or like a rainstorm from the sky, or for variety because some of the polytheists have no salvation at all, and some of them can be saved by repentance but at a distance. It is possible that it is one of the compound similes, so the meaning is: And whoever associates anything with God, his soul has perished in a perdition similar to one of the two perditions.
22:32: 32- That is it, and whoever honors the symbols of God the religion of God or the obligatory acts of Hajj and the places of its rituals, or the gifts because they are among the landmarks of Hajj and it is more appropriate to the apparent meaning of what follows, and honoring them is to choose them beautiful, fat and expensive. "It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, presented one hundred camels, including a camel for Abu Jahl, in whose nose was a gold ring", and that Omar, may God be pleased with him, presented a noble female camel that was asked for three hundred dinars from him. For it is from the piety of the hearts for honoring it from him is from the actions of those with piety of hearts, so these additions and the one who returns to whom were omitted, and the hearts were mentioned because they are the source of piety and immorality or the one that commands them.
22:33: 33- For you therein are benefits for a specified term, then their place of destination is the Ancient House meaning, for you therein are benefits from their milk, offspring, wool, and back until they are slaughtered, then at the time of slaughter they end at the House, that is, the area next to it in the Sacred Sanctuary. Then may be interpreted as a delay in time or a delay in rank, meaning, for you therein are worldly benefits until the time of slaughter, and after that there are religious benefits greater than them. According to the first two, it is either connected to the hadith of the livestock and the pronoun in it refers to them, or according to the first, what is meant is for you therein are religious benefits from which you benefit until a specified term, which is death, then their place of destination is the Ancient House to which deeds are raised or in which their reward is, which is the Frequented House or Paradise. According to the second, For you therein are benefits from trade in the markets until the time of review, then at the time of exiting from them they end at the Kaaba by entering ihram with the circumambulation of the visit.
22:34: 34- And for every nation and for every people of a religion. We have appointed a place of worship an act of worship or an offering by which they draw near to God. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra, meaning a place of worship. That they may remember the name of God and not anything else and make their sacrifice for His sake. He explained making it as an indication that the purpose of the rituals is to remember the worshipped One. For what He has provided for them of the beast of cattle when slaughtering it, and in it is an indication that the sacrifice must be blessings. So your God is one God, so submit to Him be sincere in drawing near or remembering Him and do not taint it with polytheism. And give good tidings to the humble the humble or sincere, for humility is their characteristic.
22:35: 35- Those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful in awe of Him due to the rays of His majesty shining upon them. And those who are patient over what befalls them of hardships and calamities. And those who establish prayer at its appointed times. It was read (and those who establish prayer) according to the original. And from what We have provided them, they spend in the ways of good.
22:36: 36- Al-Badan is the plural of Badana like Khashab and Khashabah, and its origin is the Dammah and it has been read with it. Rather, camels were named with it because of the size of their bodies, taken from Badan Badana, and it is not necessary that the cow shares with it in its parts from seven by his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, the Badana from seven and the cow from seven" the name Badana includes it in the Sharia. Rather, the Hadith prevents that and its being in the accusative case is based on a verb that explains it. "We made it for you" and whoever raised it made it a subject. "From the symbols of God" from the signs of His religion that God the Most High has legislated. "For you in them is good" religious and worldly benefits. "So mention the name of God over them" by saying when slaughtering them God is the Greatest, there is no god but God and God is the Greatest, O God from you and to you. "Standing" standing, they have arranged their hands and feet, and it was read (Sawafin) from the row of the horse as it stands on three. And on the tip of the fourth hoof because the camel has one of its hands tied so it stands on three, and it was read (Sawafana) by replacing the tanween with the letter of generalization when stopping and (Sawafi) meaning purely for the sake of God, and (Sawafi) with a sukoon on the yaa according to the language of those who sukoon on the yaa absolutely like their saying: Give the bow to its maker. And when its sides fall it falls to the ground and it is a metaphor for death. So eat from it and feed the contented the satisfied with what he has and with what is given without asking and this is supported by the reading (Al-Qan`), or the questioner from Qana`at ilayhi qunu`an if she submits to him in asking. And the objector and the one who objects by asking, and it was read (And the objector) it is said ‘ara and ‘araha and ‘atarah and ‘atarah. Likewise like what we described of its slaughter standing. We have subjected it to you with its size and strength until you take it obedient then you tie it and detain it with its legs straight then you stab its core. "Perhaps you will be grateful" for our blessing upon you by drawing near to Him and being sincere.
22:37: 37- He will not attain God He will not attain His pleasure nor will He be accepted by it. Their meat given in charity. Nor their blood spilled by slaughtering, since it is meat and blood. But he will attain it through piety from you but he will attain what accompanies it of piety in your hearts that calls you to glorify His command, draw near to God, and be sincere to Him. It was said that when the people of ignorance slaughtered sacrifices, they would smear the Kaaba with their blood as an act of devotion to God, the Most High, so the Muslims understood it, so it was revealed. Thus has He subjected them to you He repeated it as a reminder of the blessing and as a justification for it by saying: That you may glorify God meaning that you may know His greatness through His ability to do what no one else is able to do, so you may unify Him with greatness. It was said that it is the glorification at the time of ihram or slaughter. On what He has guided you He has guided you to the path of harnessing it and how to draw near to Him through it. What can be a source or a predicate, and on is related to so that you may glorify to include the meaning of gratitude. And give good tidings to the doers of good who are sincere in what they do and leave.
22:38: 38- Indeed, God defends those who believe from the plot of the polytheists. Nafi', Ibn Amir, and the Kufians read (Yadafi') meaning He exaggerates in defending, exaggerating in the defense of someone who is struggling. Indeed, God does not like any traitor in the trust of God. Ungrateful for His blessings, like someone who draws near to idols with his sacrifice, but he does not approve of their actions nor does he support them.
22:39: 39- Permission is permission, and Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read it in the construction of the agent, which is God. For those who fight the polytheists, and the one who is permitted is omitted because it indicates it, and Nafi', Ibn Amir and Hafs read it with the opening of the ta', meaning those whom the polytheists fight. Because they were wronged because they were wronged and they were the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The polytheists used to harm them and they used to come to him from among those who were beaten and wounded and complained to him, so he would say to them: Be patient, for I was not commanded to fight until I migrated, so it was revealed. It is the first verse revealed about fighting after it was forbidden in more than seventy verses. And indeed, God is Able to give them victory He promised them victory just as He promised to repel the harm of the disbelievers from them. 14- Tell those who have believed to forgive. The predicate was omitted because the answer indicated it, and the meaning is, tell them to forgive, so they will forgive, i.e., pardon and overlook. For those who do not expect the days of God. They do not anticipate His attacks on His enemies, as they say, the days of the Arabs for their attacks, or they do not hope for the times that God has set for the victory of the believers and their reward and promised them. The verse is about Umar, may God be pleased with him, who was insulted by Ghaffari, so he intended to strike him. It was said that it was abrogated by the verse about fighting. That He may reward a people for what they used to earn. The reason for the command, and the people are the believers or the disbelievers or both, so the repetition is for glorification or belittling or commonality, and earning is forgiveness or offense or what includes both. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read lanjazi with a nun. It was also read lijazi qawm and lijazi qawman, meaning to reward good or evil or reward. I mean what one is rewarded with, not the source, because the attribution to it, especially with the direct object, is weak.
22:40: 40- Those who were expelled from their homes meaning Mecca. Unjustly without any reason they deserved it. Except that they say, ‘Our Lord is God’ in the manner of Al-Nabigha’s saying: There is no fault in them, except that their swords have dents from the shepherd of the battalions. It was said that it is disconnected. And had God not repelled some people by means of others by giving authority to the believers among them over the disbelievers. It would have been demolished would have been ruined by the polytheists taking control of the people of the religions. Nafi’ read defense and Nafi’ and Ibn Kathir read it would have been demolished with a light pronunciation. Monasteries are monasteries of the monks. And churches are churches of the Christians. Prayers are churches of the Jews, so called because they are prayed in. It was said that its origin is salwa in Hebrew and it was Arabized. And mosques are mosques of the Muslims. The name of God is mentioned therein much is an attribute of the four or of mosques that were specifically designated for them as a preference. And God will surely support those who support Him whoever is supported by his religion. He fulfilled His promise by giving authority to the Muhajireen and Ansar over the leaders of the Arabs and the Persian kings and their Caesars and He gave them their land and homes. Indeed, God is Powerful to support them. Mighty nothing can prevent Him.
22:41: 41- "Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer and give zakah and enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong." A description of those who were expelled, and it is praise before a trial, and in it is evidence of the correctness of the matter of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs, since none of the Muhajireen gathered that together. It was said instead of those who support him. "And to God belongs the outcome of matters," for their return is to His judgment, and in it is confirmation of what He promised.
22:42: 42 - And if they deny you, then before them the people of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud denied.
22:43: 43 - And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot.
22:44: 43- "And the people of Madyan" is a consolation for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that if his people denied him, then he is not the only one who denied, for these people had denied their messengers before his people. "And Moses was denied" He changed the system and made the verb passive because his people were the Children of Israel, and they did not deny him, but rather the Copts denied him, and because his denial was more heinous and his signs were greater and more widespread. "So I granted respite to the disbelievers" So I gave them respite until their appointed terms had passed. "Then I seized them, so how was My denial" meaning My denial of them by changing the blessing into a trial, life into destruction, and civilization into ruin.
22:45: 45- "How many a town have We destroyed" by destroying its people, and the two Basrans read it without the expression of glorification. "While it was unjust" meaning its people. "It is empty on its thrones" its walls have fallen on its roofs, so its construction was destroyed and its roofs collapsed and then its walls collapsed and fell on the roofs, or empty while its thrones remained intact, so the preposition is related to "empty", and it is permissible for it to be a predicate after a predicate, meaning it is empty and it is on its thrones, meaning: overlooking it because it fell and the walls remained leaning and overlooking it, and the sentence is conjoined with "We destroyed it not with While it is unjust because it is a state and destruction is not a state of its emptiness, so it has no place if it is accusative like any with an implied explanation that We destroyed it" explains, and if it raises it by the beginning, then its place is nominative. "And a well that is not in use is in apposition to a village", meaning, how many wells in the desert were left without water being drawn from because their inhabitants had perished. It was read with a light pronunciation from "atalah meaning made it inoperable". A drop of semen by creating him from it, or then We made the offspring a drop of semen, and the masculine pronoun is used to interpret it as a substance, a fluid, or water. In a firm resting place A secure resting place, meaning the womb, and it is originally an attribute of the settled place, describing the place for emphasis, as it was expressed by the settlement.
23:14: 14- "Then We created the sperm-drop into a clot" by transforming the white sperm into a red clot. "Then We created the clot into a lump of flesh" by hardening it. "Then We clothed the bones with flesh" from what remained of the sperm-drop or from what We grew on it that reached it. The difference in emotions is due to the difference in transformations and the plural is due to their difference in form and hardness. Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read in the singular form in both of them, sufficing with the name of the species instead of the plural. He read in the singular form of one and the plural of the other. "Then We produced him into another creation which is the form of the body or the soul or the faculties by breathing into it or the combination, and then" is due to the difference between the two creations. Abu Hanifa used it as evidence that whoever usurps an egg that hatched in his possession is liable for the egg, not the chick, because it was another creation. "So blessed be God" so His status is exalted in His power and wisdom. The best of creators is the one who determines the estimation, so the distinguishing feature was deleted because the creators indicates it.
23:15: 15- Then after that you will surely die. You will inevitably die, and for this reason the adjective for confirmation was mentioned without the active participle, and it was read with it.
23:16: 16- Then on the Day of Resurrection you will be resurrected for accountability and retribution.
23:17: 17- And We have certainly created above you seven paths heavens because they are paths, one above the other, like a sandal hitting another, and everything above it is like it, so it is its path, or because they are the paths of the angels or the planets, in which their path is. And We were not heedless of the creation of that created thing which is the heavens or of all the created things. Neglecting its matter rather We protect it from disappearance and disorder and manage its matter until it reaches the limit of what was destined for it of perfection according to what wisdom requires and what the will is attached to.
23:18: 18- And We sent down from the sky water in due measure by estimating that its benefit would increase and its harm would decrease, or by the amount of what We knew of their righteousness. And We settled it by making it firm and stable. "In the earth. And We are able to take it away" by removing it by corruption or by raising it or deepening it to the point that it would be difficult to extract it. We are able just as We were able to send it down. In the indefiniteness of taking away there is an allusion to the abundance of its paths and an exaggeration in the threat of it. Therefore it is made more eloquent than the Almighty's saying: "Say, Have you considered: if your water were to become sunken, then who could bring you flowing water?"
23:19: 19- So We produced for you thereby with water. Gardens of palm trees and grapevines, for you therein in the gardens. Many fruits with which you enjoy. And from them and from the gardens are their fruits and crops. You eat as nourishment or sustenance and obtain your livelihood from their saying: So-and-so eats from his craft. It is possible that the two pronouns refer to palm trees and grapes, meaning that their fruits are sufficient for you in the form of various types of fruits, such as fresh fruits, grapes, dates, raisins, juice, molasses, and other things, and food that you eat.
23:20: 20- And a tree is in apposition to gardens and it was read in the nominative case as a beginning, meaning: And among what We have created for you is a tree. It emerges from Mount Sinai the mountain of Moses, peace be upon him, between Egypt and Ayla, and it was said in Palestine. It may also be called Mount Sinai. It is not without the mountain being the mountain and Sinai the name of a place added to it, or the compound of them being a proper noun for it like Imru' al-Qais and it was prevented from being declined for the definite article and foreignness or the feminine according to the interpretation of the place and not for the alif because it is a fa'il like dimas from sana' with the extension which is the elevation, or with the shortening which is the light or attached to fa'ilal like ala'ba from seen since there is no fa'la with the feminine alif unlike Sinai according to the reading of the Kufians and the Shami and Ya'qub because it is a fa'il like kaysan or fa'la like desert not fa'la since there is no fa'la in their speech, and it was read with the kasra and the shortening. It grows with oil means it grows mixed with oil and accompanied by it. It is possible that the letter ba is a transitive conjunction for it grows as in your saying: I went with Zayd. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read in one narration it grows and it is either from anbat meaning to grow like the saying of Zuhair: I saw those in need at their homes, so he was attentive to them until the plants grew. Or on the assumption that its olives grow covered with oil, and it was read in the passive form, which is like the first, and it bears fruit with oil, and it produces oil, and it produces oil, and it grows with oil. And a dye for the eaters is conjoined with the oil, and its syntax is like conjoining one of the two descriptions of a thing with the other, meaning: it grows with the thing that combines being oily, with which it is smeared and from which it is lamps, and being a condiment in which the bread is dyed, meaning: it is dipped in it for condiment, and it was read (and a dyer) like a tanner in tanning.
23:21: 21- And indeed, in livestock there is a lesson for you. Consider their condition and use them as evidence. We give you drink from what is in their bellies. Of milk or fodder, since milk is formed from it. Min is for partiality or for beginning. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, Abu Bakr, and Ya'qub read We give you drink with a fat-ha on the nun. "And for you in them are many benefits" in their backs, wool, and hair. "And from them you eat" so you benefit from their essence.
23:22: 22- And upon it and upon the livestock, for among them are those upon which it is carried, such as camels and cows. It was said that what is meant are camels because they are what they are carried upon, according to them, and are suitable for the ship, for they are the ships of the land. Dhu al-Rummah said: A ship under my cheek is its reins The pronoun in it is like the pronoun in And their husbands have more right to take them back and And you are carried on ships on land and sea.
23:23: 23- And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, 'O my people, worship God.' to the end of the story, presented to explain the people's ingratitude for the blessings He had enumerated for them in succession and what had befallen them of their loss. You have no god other than Him. is a resumption of the reasoning behind the command to worship. Al-Kisa'i and others read it in the accusative case based on the wording. Do you not then fear? Do you not fear that He will remove His blessings from you and destroy you and punish you for your rejection of His worship in favor of the worship of someone other than Him and your ingratitude for His blessings that you cannot count.
23:24: 24- Then the chiefs the nobles who disbelieved among his people said to their common people, This is only a human being like yourselves who wants to do you a favor to seek favor over you and rule you. And if God had willed to send a messenger, He would have sent down angels as messengers. We have not heard of this among our forefathers meaning Noah, peace be upon him, that is, we have not heard of him being a prophet, or what he spoke to them of urging them to worship God Almighty and denying any god other than Him, or of claiming prophethood, and that was either due to their extreme stubbornness or because they were in a prolonged period.
23:25: 25- He is only a man possessed by madness meaning insanity, and for this reason he says that. So wait for him so endure him and wait. Until a time perhaps he will recover from his madness.
23:26: 26- He said after he despaired of their faith. My Lord, support me by destroying them or by fulfilling the punishment You promised them. Because they denied instead of their denying Me or because of it.
23:27: 27- So We inspired him, 'Make the ark under Our eyes' with Our protection, We protect it from making a mistake in it or spoiling it for you. And Our revelation and Our command and Our instruction on how to make. And when Our command comes to ride or the punishment descends. And the oven overflows It was narrated that it was said to Noah when the water overflowed from the oven, ride you and those with you, so when the water gushed from it, his wife informed him, so he rode and his place was in the mosque of Kufa to the right of the one entering from the door of Kinda. It was said that it was the spring of Warda in Ash-Sham and there are other aspects to it that I mentioned in (Hud). So walk therein so enter it. It is said that he walked therein and others walked. God Almighty said, What has brought you into Hellfire? "Of every pair two" from every nation, the male and female, one and double, and Hafs read (of every) with the tanween, meaning of every type, two and two for emphasis. "And your family" and your household or those who believed with you. Except for those against whom the word has already gone forth meaning the word from God Almighty to destroy them for their disbelief. The preposition ala was brought because the word that precedes is harmful, just as the preposition lam was brought when it was beneficial in the words of God Almighty: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us. “And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged” by praying for their salvation. Indeed, they will be drowned without a doubt because of their wrongdoing through polytheism and sins. And whoever is like this, there is no intercession for him and no intercession for him. How can it be when He commanded him to praise Him for being saved from them by their destruction, by His words:
23:28: 28- So when you and those with you are settled in the ship, say, ‘Praise be to God, who has saved us from the wrongdoing people.’ Like the Almighty’s saying: “So He eliminated the last of the people who did wrong. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.”
23:29: 29- And say, 'My Lord, drop me down' in the ship or on the earth. A blessed landing place that brings about more good in both worlds according to Abu Bakr's reading. It was also read (a landing place) meaning a landing or a place of landing. And You are the best of those who give landing places is praise that matches his supplication. He ordered him to intercede for him with it, exaggerating it and seeking through it an answer. He singled him out with the command and what was attached to it so that he and those with him would be equal, to demonstrate his favor and to indicate that in his supplication there is an alternative to their supplication, for He encompasses them.
23:30: 30- Indeed in that in what He did to Noah and his people. There are signs that are used as evidence and are considered by those who have insight and reflection. And indeed We were to test to afflict the people of Noah with a great affliction, or to examine Our servants with these signs. And indeed is the lightened one and the lam is the distinguishing one. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 19 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Mu'minūn, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Fur'qān. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 23:31: 31 - Then We produced after them another generation they are Aad or Thamud.
23:32: 32- So We sent among them a Messenger from among themselves He is Hud or Salih, and the statement was made the place of sending to indicate that he did not come to them from a place other than their place, but rather it was revealed to him while he was among them. That you worship God; you have no deity other than Him is an explanation of We sent meaning We said to them on the tongue of the Messenger, Worship God. "Will you not then fear" the punishment of God.
23:33: 33- And the leaders of his people who disbelieved said Perhaps it was mentioned with the waw because their speech was not connected to the speech of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, unlike the speech of the people of Noah, where it was resumed, so it is assumed to be a question. And they denied the meeting of the Hereafter in meeting what is in it of reward and punishment, or in their return to the second life by resurrection. And We provided them with luxury and and blessed them in the life of this world with an abundance of wealth and children. This is only a human being like you in description and condition. He eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink An estimate of the similarity and what is a report and what refers to the second is an accusative deleted or a genitive deleted with the preposition because what preceded it indicates it.
23:34: 34- And if you obeyed human beings like yourselves in what he commands you to do. You would then be losers since you would have humiliated yourselves, and if is a consequence of the condition and an answer to those of his people who spoke to them.
23:35: 35- Does He promise you that when you die and become dust and bones stripped of flesh and nerves, that you will be brought forth from the graves or from nothingness another time into existence, and that you is a repetition of the first, emphasized by it because of the long separation between it and its predicate, or that you will be brought forth is a subject whose predicate is the advanced circumstance, or the subject of the implied verb in response to the condition and the sentence is the predicate of the first, meaning: that you will be brought forth if you die, or that when you die your bringing forth will occur. It is possible that the predicate of the first is omitted because the predicate of the second indicates it, not that it is the circumstance because its name is a corpse.
23:36: 36- Hihat Hihat after confirmation or validity. Lama ta'awaddun or after you are promised, and the lam is for clarification as in Hayt laka as if when they voted with the word of exclusion it was said: What is this exclusion? They said: Lama ta'awaddun. It was said that Hihat means distance, and it is a subject whose predicate is Lama ta'awaddun. It was read with the fatha and a tanween for emphasis, and with the damma and a tanween as a plural of hayha and without a tanween likening to qabl and with the kasra in both ways, and with the sukoon as a word of stopping and by replacing the ta' with a ha'.
23:37: 37- It is nothing but our worldly life. Its original form is it is nothing but our worldly life." So the pronoun was used in place of the first because the second indicates it, to avoid repetition and to indicate that its specificity makes it unnecessary to state it explicitly, as in His saying: The soul bears what it can bear Its meaning is that there is no life but this life, because an is a negative that entered hi which has the meaning of life and indicates the genus, so it was like la which negates what comes after it with the negation of the genus. We die and we live some of us die and some are born. And we will not be resurrected after death.
23:38: 38- He is what he is. But a man who has fabricated a lie against God in what he claims of sending him and in what he promises us of resurrection. And we are not believers in him in believing.
23:39: 39- “He said, ‘My Lord, support me’ against them and take revenge for me from them. ‘Because they denied’ because of their denial of me.
23:40: 40- He said in a little while in a short time and ma is a relative pronoun to emphasize the meaning of fewness, or an indefinite noun described. They will surely regret the denial when they witness the punishment.
23:41: 41- So the blast seized them Gabriel's blast, he shouted a tremendous blast at them that cracked their hearts and they died, and it was used as evidence that the people were righteous. With truth in the third sense that has no repeller, or with justice from God, like when you say so-and-so judges with truth. Or with the true promise. So We made them scum He likened their destruction to the scum of a flood, which is its carrier, like the Arabs say: the valley flowed with it, for those who perished. So away with the wrongdoing people can mean report and supplication, and away is a source of after if he perished, and it is one of the sources that are made accusative by verbs that are not used to show it, and the lam is to clarify who was called away, and the apparent was placed in place of their pronoun for explanation.
23:42: 42- Then We produced after them other generations namely the people of Salih, Lot, Shuaib, and others.
23:43: 43- No nation can precede its term the time set for its destruction, and of is an additional word for comprehensiveness. Nor do they delay the term.
23:44: 44- Then We sent Our messengers in succession one after the other from the odd number, which is the individual, and the ta' is a substitute for the waw like tulj and tiqur and the alif is for the feminine because the messengers are a group, and Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read with the tanween as a source meaning continuous and it occurred as a state, and Hamza and Ibn Amir and Al-Kisa'i made it inclined. Whenever a messenger came to a nation, they denied him adding the messenger with sending to the sender and with coming to the ones to whom they were sent because sending which is the beginning of the command is from him and coming which is its end to them. So We made some of them follow others in destruction. And We made them stories We left nothing of them except stories to be told, and it is a collective noun for hadith or the collective noun for hadith which is what is spoken about for amusement. So away with a people who do not believe.
23:45: 45- Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs with the nine signs. And a clear authority and a clear argument binding on the opponent. It is possible that it refers to the staff and its parts because it is the first and mother of miracles. Various miracles were connected to it: such as its turning into a snake and its swallowing up what the magicians had fabricated, the splitting of the sea and the gushing of springs from the rock when they struck it, its guarding and its destination being a candle and a green fruitful tree and a rope and a bucket. It is possible that it refers to miracles and the signs to arguments, and that it refers to miracles because they are signs of prophethood and a clear argument for what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, claims.
23:46: 46- To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they were arrogant in believing and following. And they were a haughty people arrogant.
23:47: 47- And they said, 'Shall we believe in two human beings like ourselves?' Human beings are dual because they are used for one person, as in His saying, a well-proportioned human being, and they are also used for the plural, as in His saying, If you see among mankind one, and the like is not dual because it is in the position of a source. These stories, as we see, testify that the most extreme resemblance of those who deny prophethood is comparing the state of the prophets to their own states, because of the similarity between them in reality, and its corruption becomes apparent to the one who has insight with the slightest contemplation, for human souls, even if they share in the origin of powers and perception, are different in their feet in them, and as you see on the side of deficiency, they are stupid to whom thought does not return a cold. It is possible that on the side of excess, there are those who are rich in thinking and learning in most things and most conditions, so they perceive what others do not perceive and know what their knowledge does not reach, and to this He referred in His saying, the Most High: Say, 'I am only a human being like you, to whom it is revealed that your God is one God.' "And their people," meaning the Children of Israel. "We have servants" who are obedient and submissive like servants.
23:48: 48- So they denied them both, and were among those destroyed by drowning in the Sea of Qulzum.
23:49: 49- And We gave Moses the Book the Torah. Perhaps they the Children of Israel, and it is not permissible for the pronoun to refer to Pharaoh and his people because the Torah was revealed after they were drowned. They will be guided to knowledge and rulings.
23:50: 50- And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign by her giving birth to him without touching him, so the sign is one thing added to them, or We made the son of Mary a sign by speaking in the cradle and other miracles appeared from him and his mother a sign by giving birth without touching him, so the first was deleted because the second indicated it. And We settled them on a high place the land of Jerusalem, for it is high, or Damascus, or the sand of Palestine, or Egypt, for its villages are on the hills, and Ibn Amir and Asim read with the opening of the ra' and (Rabawa) was read with the damma and kasra. A place of settlement a stable, flat place on the land. And it was said that it has fruits and crops, for its inhabitants settle there for its sake. And a spring and a spring water is a visible, active participle from the meaning of water if it flows and its origin is the distance in something, or from the tool which is the benefit because it is useful, or the passive participle from `ana if he perceives it with his own eyes because of its appearance it is perceived by the eyes and its water was described as such because it is the combination of the reasons for recreation and the pleasantness of the place.
23:51: 51- O messengers, eat from the good things is a call and address to all the prophets, not that they were addressed with that at once because they were sent at different times, but rather in the sense that each of them was addressed with it in his time, so Jesus is included under it as a primary entry and the beginning of the speech is a warning that the preparation of the means of enjoyment was not specific to him, and that the permissibility of good things for the prophets is an ancient law and an argument against monasticism in rejecting the good things, or a narration of what was mentioned to Jesus and his mother when they were sheltered on the hill so that they would follow the example of the messengers in eating what they were provided with. It was said that the call is for him and the plural form is for glorification and good things are what are enjoyed from the permissible things. It was said that the permissible is the pure and consistent, so the permissible is that in which God is not disobeyed, and the pure is that in which God is not forgotten, and the consistent is that which controls the soul and preserves the mind. And do righteousness for it is what is intended from you and is beneficial to your Lord. I am aware of what you do, so I will reward you for it.
23:52: 52- And this meaning because this and the reason for it so fear God, or know that this, and it was said that it is conjoined with what you do and Ibn Amir read it with the alleviation and the Kufians with the kasra as a resumption. Your nation is one nation your religion is one religion meaning united in belief and the principles of the laws, or your group is one group agreed upon faith and monotheism in worship and the accusative of nation is in the state. And I am your Lord, so fear God in splitting the stick and contradicting the word.
23:53: 53- So they divided their affair among themselves So they divided their affair among themselves, they made it into different religions, or they dispersed and became parties, and their affair is in the accusative case by removing the preposition or the distinction, and the pronoun refers to what the nation indicates from its masters, the first of them. Zubran is definitely the plural of Zabur, which means division, and this is supported by the reading with the opening of the ba', as it is the plural of zabarah, and it is a state of their affair or of the waw, or a second object of So they divided, as it includes the meaning of making. And it was said that it is books from zabarat al-kitab, so it is a second object, or a state of their affair, based on the estimation of the like of kataba, and it was read with a light ba' like rusul in rusul. Every party of the parties. With what they have of religion. Rejoicing is admiring, believing that they are on the truth.
23:54: 54- Leave them in their ignorance in their ignorance, he likened it to water that submerges a person because they are immersed in it or playing with it, and it was read in (their ignorance) until a time until they are killed or die.
23:55: 55- Do they think that what We provide for them that what We give them and make for them is a support, of wealth and children is an explanation of what is not report of it, for he is not to be blamed for it, but rather what is to be blamed for is their belief that this is better for them, report of it.
23:56: 56- We hasten to them in good deeds. The referent is omitted, and the meaning is: Do they think that what We provide them with will be hastened to them in what is good for them and honors them? Rather, they do not perceive. Rather, they are like animals, they have no intelligence or awareness to reflect on it and know that this provision is a lure, not a hastening in good. The reading of Yamduhum is in the third person, as is Yasara'a and Yasra'a. It is possible that there is a pronoun for the one provided with in them, and Yasara'a is in the passive form.
23:57: 57- Indeed, those who are, out of fear of their Lord out of fear of His punishment. are apprehensive are cautious.
23:58: 58- And those who believe in the signs of their Lord the accusative and the subjunctive. By confirming their meaning.
23:59: 59- And those who do not associate anything with their Lord with obvious or hidden association.
23:60: 60- And those who give what they give they give what they give of charity, and it was read (they give what they give) meaning they do what they do of acts of obedience. 24:4: 4 - And those who accuse chaste women accuse them of adultery, describing the slandered women as chaste, and mentioning them after the adulteresses and considering four witnesses by saying: And if they do not produce four witnesses, flog them with eighty lashes. And accusing someone other than that, such as the perpetrator or the drinker of alcohol, requires discretionary punishment like accusing someone who is not chaste. Chastity here means freedom, puberty, reason, Islam, and chastity from adultery, and there is no difference between males and females in this regard. The specification of chaste women is for the specific incident or because slandering women is more common and more heinous, and it is not required that witnesses meet at the time of performance, and the testimony of the slandered woman's husband is not considered, contrary to Abu Hanifa. And let his lash be lighter than the lash for adultery because of the weakness of its cause and possibility, and therefore its number is reduced. And do not accept their testimony meaning that he is a slanderer. It was also said that their testimony in slander is not contingent upon the punishment being flogged, contrary to Abu Hanifa, for the command to flog and the prohibition against accepting them are the same in that they occur in response to the condition, with no sequence between them, so they are both connected to it at once. How could it be that his condition before the flogging is worse than after it? Forever unless he repents, and according to Abu Hanifa, until the end of his life. And those are the wicked who are judged to be wicked.
24:5: 5 - "Except for those who repent" from the slander. "After that, and amend" their deeds by making up for it, including submitting to the prescribed punishment or seeking forgiveness from the one slandered. The exception goes back to the original ruling, which is that the condition requires these matters, and it does not require the punishment to be dropped as it was said, because the completion of repentance is submitting to it or seeking forgiveness. The place of the exception is the accusative case as an exception. It was said to the prohibition, and its place is the genitive case as a substitute for "they in them." It was said to the last, and its place is the accusative case because it is from an obligation. It was said that it is disconnected and connected to what comes after it. "Then God is Forgiving and Merciful" is the reason for the exception.
24:6: 6 - And those who accuse their wives but have no witnesses except themselves was revealed about Hilal ibn Umayya who saw a man on his bed, and themselves is a substitute for witnesses or an attribute of them, on the basis that except means other. Then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies so the testimony of one of them is obligatory or the testimony of one of them is required, and four is an accusative of the source, and Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs raised it as the predicate of testimony "By God" is related to testimonies because it is closer and it was said that it is a witness because it came before. "He is of the truthful meaning in what he accused her of of adultery, and its origin is that he deleted the preposition and broke in" and suspended the agent from it with the lam for emphasis.
24:7: 7 - And the fifth and the fifth testimony. That the curse of God be upon him if he is among the liars. In slander, this is the man's cursing and the ruling on it is that the punishment for slander is dropped from him, and the separation between them itself is a separation that is annulled in our view, based on the saying of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, Two people who curse each other can never meet.
24:8: 8 - And the judge’s separation is a division of divorce according to Abu Hanifa and the denial of the child if he is exposed to it and the establishment of the punishment for adultery on the woman based on his saying: And the punishment is averted from her meaning the punishment. That she testifies four times by God that he is among the liars regarding what he accused me of.
24:9: 9 - And the fifth is that the wrath of God be upon her, if he is of the truthful. In that, the fifth was raised by the subject and what came after it was the predicate or by conjunction with that she testifies. Hafs lowered it in conjunction with four. Nafi' and Ya'qub read that the curse of God and that the wrath of God with a light nun in them, a kasra on the dad, a fatha on the ba' from anger, and a raising on the ha' from the name God. The rest read it with a shaddah on the nun in them, a nasb on the ta', a fatha on the dad, and a genitive on the ha'.
24:10: 10 - "And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy and that God is Forgiving and Wise" The answer is left for the sake of glorification, that is, He would have exposed you and hastened the punishment upon you.
24:12: 12 - "If only Why not? When you heard it, the believing men and believing women would think well of one another" of those among them, the believing men and believing women, as God Almighty said: "And do not criticize one another." The reason for changing the address from the third person to an exaggeration of the rebuke and to indicate that faith requires thinking well of the believers, refraining from slandering them, and defending those who slander them as they defend themselves. It is permissible to separate "if only" and its verb with the adverbial phrase because it is given its status in that it is inseparable from it, and that allows for more room for it than for anything else. This is because mentioning the adverbial phrase is more important, as the exhortation is not to neglect its beginning. "And they said, 'This is an obvious lie,'" as someone who is certain and aware of the situation says.
24:13: 13 - Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? But since they do not bring witnesses, then it is they who are the liars in the sight of God. This is part of what is said to confirm that it is a lie, for that which has no proof is a lie in the sight of God, that is, in His judgment, and for this reason He imposed the punishment on it.
24:14: 14 - And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter Were it not for this, a thing would have been impossible due to the existence of something else, and the meaning is had it not been for the grace of God upon you in this world with various blessings, including respite for repentance, and His mercy in the Hereafter with the pardon and forgiveness decreed for you. It would have touched you quickly. In what you have indulged you engaged in. Therein is a great punishment compared to which blame and flogging are insignificant.
24:15: 15 - When is an adverb for to touch you or you have poured out. You receive it with your tongues means some of you take it from others by asking about it. It is said to receive like to catch and to teach it. The reading you receive is to teach according to the original. You receive is from to catch if you catch it. You receive is with a kasra on the letter of the present tense. You receive is from some of them throwing it to others. You receive and you shine are from to shine and to shine which means lying. You seek is from you seek if you seek it and find it. You follow means you follow it. And you say with your mouths means you say words that are specific to the mouths without the help of the hearts. That of which you have no knowledge because it is not an expression of knowledge of it in your hearts like the Almighty's saying: They say with their mouths that which is not in their hearts. "And you think it is easy" is easy and of no consequence. And it is grave in the sight of God in terms of sin and the punishment it brings. These are three sins that are connected to the grave punishment: uttering falsehood with their tongues, speaking about it without verifying it, and belittling it, while it is grave in the sight of God.
24:16: 16 - And why, when you heard it, did you not say, 'It is not for us' It is not appropriate and not right for us. To speak of this It is permissible for the reference to be to the specific statement or to its type, for slandering individual people is forbidden by the Shari'ah, let alone the exposure of the truthful daughter of the truthful one to the sanctity of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Glory be to You is an expression of amazement at that slander or at the one who says that. Its origin is to be mentioned by every person who is amazed, to glorify God the Most High from the difficulty of something like it, then it became widespread and was used for every person who is amazed, or to glorify God the Most High from the sanctity of His Prophet being immoral, for her immorality repels Him and undermines the purpose of marriage, unlike her disbelief, so it is a confirmation of what came before it and a preparation for his saying, This is a great slander because of the greatness of the one slandered, for the insignificance and greatness of sins are considered in relation to their connections.
24:17: 17 - God admonishes you not to return to the like of it disliking that you return or in that you return. Never as long as you are alive and accountable. If you are believers for belief prevents it and it contains incitement and rebuke.
24:18: 18 - God makes clear to you the signs indicating the laws and the good manners so that you may learn a lesson and be disciplined. And God is Knowing of all conditions. Wise in His plans, and it is not permissible to be rude to His Prophet, nor does He approve of it.
24:19: 19 - Those who love want that immorality among those who believe will spread for them a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter” by the prescribed punishment and the Blaze and other things. And God knows what is in the minds. And you do not know so they were punished in this world based on what is indicated by the apparent meaning, and God Almighty punishes for what is in the hearts of the love of spreading.
24:20: 20 - And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy is a repetition of the favor of not hastening the punishment to indicate the enormity of the crime. Therefore, His statement, And that God is Kind and Merciful was connected to the occurrence of His grace and mercy upon them, and the answer was omitted, and it is dispensed with by mentioning it once.
24:21: 21 - O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan by spreading immorality. It was also read with a fatha on the ta', and Nafi', Al-Buzzi, Abu Amr, Abu Bakr, and Hamzah read it with a sukoon. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan - indeed, he enjoins immorality and wrongdoing is a statement of the reason for the prohibition of following him. Immorality is that which is extremely ugly, and wrong is that which is condemned by the Shari'ah. And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy by enabling repentance that erases sins and legislating the prescribed punishments that expiate them, not one of you would have been pure would not have been cleansed from its filth. None of you would ever be pure until the end of time. But God purifies whom He wills by urging him to repent and accepting it. And God is Hearing of their words. Knowing of their intentions.
24:22: 22 - And do not swear an oath and do not swear an oath is a causative verb from the root word aliyah, or do not shorten the word alo, and the first is supported by the fact that it was read and do not swear, and that it was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, when he swore that he would not spend on Mistah anymore, and his cousin was one of the poor emigrants. Those of virtue among you in religion. And plenty in wealth. This indicates the virtue and honor of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. That they should give on the basis that they should not give, or in that they should give. It was read with the letter ta to indicate shifting of opinion. The relatives, the needy, and the emigrants in the way of God are descriptions of one described, i.e. people who combine them because the speech is about someone who was like that, or descriptions that were used in their place, so it is more eloquent in explaining the intended meaning. And let them pardon what they have neglected. And let them overlook by ignoring it. Would you not love that God should forgive you? For your pardon, forgiveness, and kindness to those who wronged you? And God is Forgiving and Merciful. From the perfection of His power, so adopt His morals. It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) recited it to Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him and he said: Yes, I would, and he returned to Mistah’s expenses.
24:23: 23 - Those who accuse chaste women - those who are unaware of what they are accused of - believing women - in God and His Messenger - violating their honor and slandering the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and the believers like Ibn Abi. They are cursed in this world and the Hereafter because they slandered them. And they will have a great punishment because of the enormity of their sins. It was said that this is the ruling for every slanderer as long as he does not repent. It was said that it is specifically for those who slander the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Therefore, Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: There is no repentance for him. If you searched the warnings of the Qur'an, you would not find anything more severe than what was revealed about the slander of Aisha, may God be pleased with her.
24:24: 24 - The Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them is an adverbial phrase referring to the meaning of stability in them, not to the torment, because it is described. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with the letter ya for the sake of precedence and separation. Their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to do They will acknowledge it by God Almighty causing them to speak without their choosing it, or by His effects appearing on them, and in that there is more intimidation of the torment.
24:25: 25 - On that Day, God will pay them in full their due recompense. "And they will know, because they have witnessed the matter, that God is the evident truth." Established in His essence, His divinity is evident. No one shares that with Him, and no one is able to reward or punish except Him. Or the Possessor of the evident truth, meaning the Just One whose justice is evident. And whoever is like this will inevitably take revenge on the oppressor for the oppressed.
24:26: 26 - "Evil women are for evil men, and evil men are for evil women. Good women are for good men, and good men are for good women." That is, evil women marry evil women and vice versa, and so are good men. Thus, it is like evidence for his statement: Those meaning the family of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the Messenger, Aisha, and Safwan, may God be pleased with them. Abandoned from what they say, because if it were true, she would not have been his wife, peace be upon him, and it was not confirmed on her. It was said that evil women and good women are among the statements, and the reference is to good men, and the pronoun in they say is for the slanderers, that is, innocent of what they say about them, or the evil men and the evil women meaning innocent of saying what they say. For them is forgiveness and noble provision meaning Paradise. And God has acquitted four people with four things: He acquitted Joseph, peace be upon him, with a witness from among his people, and Moses, peace be upon him, from what the Jews said about him with the stone that took away his garment, and Mary with her son speaking, and Aisha, may God be pleased with her, with these noble verses with this exaggeration. And that is only to demonstrate the position of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and to raise his status.
24:27: 27 - "O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses" which you do not inhabit, for even the borrower and the borrower do not enter except with permission. "Until you have asked permission. You ask permission from istinās meaning to inquire from anas" if you see something.
