No good report that Day will be given to the criminals for it means that they will be prevented from the good report or will not receive it, and that Day is repeated or a predicate and for the criminals is an explanation or a second predicate or a circumstance for what the lam relates to, or for good report if it is considered definite and not explained with la then it does not work, and for the criminals it is either general and its ruling includes their ruling by way of proof and the denial of good report for all the criminals then necessitates the denial of good report of forgiveness and intercession at another time, or it is specific and is placed in the place of their pronoun as a record of their crime and a notification of what prevents good report and necessitates what is opposite to it. And they say, 'A forbidden stone' is in apposition to the meaning, meaning, the disbelievers will say at that time, this word is a seeking of refuge and a request from God Almighty to prevent meeting them. It is one of the things they used to say when meeting an enemy or an undesirable attack, or the angels say it meaning, 'Paradise or good report are forbidden to you.' A stone is also read with the damma, but its original form is the fatha, except that since it is specific to a specific place, unlike your sitting and your life, and therefore it is not modified and its accusative is not shown. It is described as forbidden for emphasis, like their saying, 'the death of a dead person.'
25:23: 23- And We shall turn to whatever deeds they did and make them as scattered dust. That is, We shall turn to whatever good deeds they did in their disbelief, such as hospitality, maintaining kinship ties, and helping the distressed, and We shall render them worthless due to the loss of what is required for their consideration. This is a comparison of their state and their deeds to the state of a people who rebelled against their ruler, so He turns to their things and tears them up and nullifies them, leaving no trace of them. Flare is dust that is seen in a ray that rises from the window of the hopah, which is dust. Scattered is an adjective that compares their frustrated work to the dust in its insignificance and uselessness, then to the scattered part of it in its dispersion such that it cannot be organized or dispersed towards the purposes they were directing it towards, or a third object in that it is like the predicate after the predicate, as in the Almighty’s saying: Be apes, despised.
25:24: 24- The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be in the best settlement. A place where people will settle most of the time to sit and talk. And the best place to rest. A place where people seek rest with their wives and enjoy them, a metaphor for a place for a siesta, as a metaphor, or because it is not usually devoid of that, as there is no sleep in Paradise. And in the best symbol of what distinguishes their siesta from the time of images and other sensations. It is possible that one of them is intended to mean the source or the time, indicating that their place and time are the best of all places and times imaginable. The preference is either to indicate an increase in general or in comparison to what the luxurious have in this world. It was narrated that the reckoning will be completed in the middle of that day, so the people of Paradise will rest in Paradise and the people of Hell will rest in Hell.
25:25: 25- And the Day the sky will split open. Its original form is it will split open, but the t was dropped and assimilated by Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, Ibn Amir, and Ya’qub. With clouds is because of the clouds rising from it. It is the cloud mentioned in His statement, Do they await anything but that God should come to them in canopies of clouds and the angels? “And He sends down the angels in a [gradual] descent” in that cloud with the records of the servants’ deeds. Ibn Kathir read, And We send down, and it was read, It was sent down, “And He sent down,” And He sent down the angels, without the nun. The word.
25:26: 26- The kingdom on that Day belongs to the Most Merciful which is established for Him because every kingdom will be nullified on that Day and nothing will remain except His kingdom. They are the report and the Most Merciful is its connection, or clarification, and on that Day is the object of the kingdom not the truth because it comes later or is its description, and the report is on that Day or the Most Merciful. “And it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers” severe.
25:27: 27- And the Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands out of extreme regret. Biting the hands, biting the fingertips, gnawing the teeth, and the like are metaphors for anger and regret because they are among their concomitants. What is meant by the wrongdoer is the genus. It was said that Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt used to sit with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) a lot, so he invited him to his hospitality, but he refused to eat from his food until he recited the two testimonies of faith, so he did. Ubayy ibn Khalaf was his friend, so he rebuked him and said, You have become an apostate. He said, No, but he swore that he would not eat from my food while he was in my house, so I felt shy of him and testified for him. He said, I see nothing from you except that you go to him, step on his back, and spit in his face. He found him prostrating in Dar al-Nadwa, so he did that, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, I will not meet you outside Mecca except that I will strike your head with my sword. He was captured on the day of Badr, so he ordered Ali to kill him and stabbed Ubayy in a duel at Uhud, so he returned to Mecca and died. He says, Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a path, a path to salvation or one path, which is the path of truth, and that I had not strayed into the paths of misguidance.
25:28: 28- Woe to me! It was read with a ya’ according to the original. Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend. That is, someone I led astray. So-and-so is a metaphor for proper names, just as here it is a metaphor for races.
25:29: 29- He has led me astray from the remembrance from the remembrance of God, or His Book, or the sermon of the Messenger, or the word of testimony. After it came to me and I had control over him. And Satan means the misleading friend or Iblis because he led him to oppose and disobey the Messenger, or everyone who has become devilish from among the jinn and humans. If it had been sent down to him all at once, his memorization would have been impaired, and perhaps it would not have been established for him, as grasping it only comes about little by little. And because its revelation according to events requires more insight and immersion in the meaning, and because if it is sent down in stages, and he challenges with every star, they are unable to oppose it, that increases the strength of his heart, and because if Gabriel sends it down, one moment after another, his heart is strengthened by it, and no matter how much knowledge it contains, it will be more difficult for him to understand. The abrogating and the abrogated, including the joining of the current contextual evidence to the verbal meanings, as it aids in eloquence, as well as the description of a deleted source and the reference to its being revealed in parts, as it is indicated by His statement, Why was not the Qur’an revealed to him all at once? It is possible that it is from the complete speech of the disbelievers and therefore he stopped at it, so it is a state and the reference is to the previous books, and the lam in both cases is related to something deleted. “And We recited it to you, little by little, slowly and deliberately, over twenty years or twenty-three. Except that We bring you the truth The conclusive answer to him. And a better explanation And what is better in explanation or meaning than their question, or They do not come to you with an amazing situation, saying: Why was this not the case, except that We gave you from the situations what is right for you in Our wisdom and what is the best revelation of what you were sent for.
25:34: 34- Those who will be gathered on their faces into Hellfire meaning upside down or dragged into it, or their hearts clinging to the lower parts, their faces turned towards it. “And it was narrated from him, peace and blessings be upon him, that people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in three categories: a category on beasts, a category on foot, and a category on their faces.” This is a blame in the accusative or nominative case, or as the beginning of its predicate. Those are the worst in position and most astray in path. The one preferred over him is the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, in the manner of the Most High’s statement: Say, ‘Shall I inform you of one worse than that as reward from God? One whom God has cursed and with whom He has become angry.’ It is as if it was said that what prompted them to ask these questions was to belittle his position and mislead him, and they did not know their condition, so that they would know that they were the worst in position and most astray in path. It was also said that it is connected to his statement, The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be the best settlement, and describing the path as astray is a metaphorical attribution for exaggeration.
25:35: 35- And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture and appointed with him his brother Aaron as a minister to assist him in the call and raising the word, and this does not contradict his participation in the prophethood, because those who share in the matter assist each other in it.
25:36: 36- “So We said, ‘Go both of you to the people who denied Our signs,’ meaning Pharaoh and his people. ‘And We destroyed them with [complete] destruction.’” That is, they went to them and they denied them, so We destroyed them. So He limited himself to the two margins of the story, contenting himself with what was intended from it, which is to oblige the argument to send the messengers and to deserving destruction because of their denial, and the follow-up by considering the ruling to occur. And it was read, And We destroyed them. (Fadamarahum Fadamarahum) with emphasis with the heavy nun. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 20 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Fur'qān, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Naml. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 25:45: 45- Have you not seen your Lord? Have you not looked at His creation? How He extended the shadow? How He spread it out? Or, have you not looked at the shadow, how your Lord extended it? And I have come to you from Sheba Ibn Kathir read it with the narration of Al-Bazzi and Abu Amr without a sukoon on the interpretation of the tribe, the town, and the bows with a silent hamza. With certain report with verified report it was narrated that when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, completed the construction of the Holy House in Jerusalem, he prepared for Hajj, so he arrived at the Sacred Sanctuary and stayed there as long as he wished. Then he headed to Yemen, leaving Mecca in the morning and arriving at Sana'a at noon. He was impressed by the purity of its land, so he stopped there and did not find water - and the hoopoe was his guide because it was good at searching for water - so he checked on it and did not find it. When Solomon landed, he flew and saw a hoopoe lying down, so he descended to it and they talked to each other. He flew with it to see what was described to him. Then he returned after the afternoon and narrated what he narrated. Perhaps among the wonders of God's power and what He has given to His special servants are things greater than that, which are considered too great by those who know them and are deemed too strange by those who deny them.
27:23: 23 - I found a woman ruling them, meaning Bilqis bint Shuraheel bin Malik bin Rayyan, and the pronoun refers to Sheba or its people. And she has been given of everything, that kings need. And she has a great throne, its greatness in relation to her or to thrones like hers. It was said that it was thirty cubits long by thirty cubits wide and thick, or eighty, of gold and silver, crowned with jewels.
27:24: 24 - I found her and her people prostrating to the sun instead of God as if they were worshipping it. And Satan made their deeds pleasing to them worshipping the sun and other ugly deeds. So he averted them from the path from the path of truth and righteousness. So they are not guided to it.
27:25: 25 - That they should not prostrate to God. So He prevented them from prostrating, or He made it seem good to them that they should not prostrate, as a substitute for their deeds, or that they should not be guided to prostrating with the addition of la. Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read illa with a light pronunciation, as it is for emphasis, and ya is for calling, and the one being called is omitted, meaning: O my people, prostrate, as He said: She said, Listen, I will advise you on a plan. I said, I am all-hearing, so speak and be right. And on this basis, it is correct that it is a resumption from God or from Solomon and the pause is at they are not guided, so it is an order to prostrate. And on the first, it is a blame for leaving it. And on both faces, it requires the obligation of prostration in the sentence, not when reciting it. And Hala and Hala were read by changing the hamza to a ha, and ala tasjudun and hala tasjudun are addressed. Who brings forth what is hidden within the heavens and the earth and knows what you conceal and what you declare is a description of Him, the Most High, with what necessitates that He be singled out for the deserving of prostration, from His uniqueness in perfect power and knowledge, urging prostration to Him and responding to whoever prostrates to someone other than Him. Hidden is what is hidden in something, and bringing it forth is revealing. It includes the shining of the stars, the sending down of rain, the sprouting of plants, and even creation, for it is bringing forth what is in something potentially to actuality and innovation. It is bringing forth what is in possibility and nonexistence to necessity and existence. And it is known that it is specific to what is necessary in and of itself. Hafs and Al-Kisa’i read what you conceal and what you declare with a ta’.
27:26: 26 - God, there is no god but He, Lord of the Mighty Throne, which is the first and greatest of all bodies and encompasses all of them. So there is a distance between the two great things.
27:27: 27 - He said, 'We will look.' We will know from looking in the sense of contemplation. Did you tell the truth or were you among the liars? That is, did you lie? The change is for emphasis and to preserve the pauses.
27:28: 28 - Go with this letter of mine and deliver it to them, then turn away from them. Then move away from them to a nearby place where you can hide. Then see what they will return. What they will return to one another in terms of saying.
27:29: 29 - She said, meaning after he had thrown it to her. O assembly, indeed a noble letter has been thrown to me, because of the nobility of its content or its sender, or because it was sealed, or because of the strangeness of its matter, as she was lying down in a house with closed doors, and the hoopoe entered through a window and threw it on her throat so that she did not feel it.
27:30: 30 - It is from Solomon is a resumption as if she was asked who it is from and what it is, so she said it is, meaning the book or title is from Solomon. And it is meaning that what is written or what is contained. It was read with the fat-ha as a substitution for book or as an explanation of his generosity. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 21 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Naml, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Rūm. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. 27:31: 31 - That you do not exalt yourself over me "that" is an explanatory or verbal noun, so its root is the predicate of an omitted word, i.e. it is he or what is meant is that you do not exalt yourself, or a substitute for "Book". "And come to me as Muslims" believing or obedient. This speech is extremely concise yet fully indicative of the intended meaning, as it includes the Basmalah, which indicates the essence of the Creator, the Most High, and His attributes, explicitly or implicitly, and the prohibition of haughtiness, which is the mother of vices, and the command to Islam, which includes the mothers of virtues. The command in it is not to submit before establishing proof of his message, so that it would be a call to imitation, as the Book to her in that state is one of the greatest indications.
27:32: 32 - "She said, 'O assembly, advise me in my affair.' Answer me in my affair, the young man, and state what you consider appropriate in it. 'I have not decided on a matter.' I have not refused a matter until you bear witness.' Except in your presence. She sought their sympathy with her in order to persuade her to answer.
27:33: 33 - They said, 'We are men of strength' in bodies and numbers. And men of great courage in bravery and bravery. And the matter is up to you is entrusted. So see what you command of fighting or peace. We will obey you and follow your opinion.
27:34: 34 - "She said, 'When kings enter a town by force and oppression, they corrupt it.'" This is a falsification of what she found to be good in them of their inclination to fight by claiming intrinsic and incidental powers, and a feeling that she sees peace for fear that Solomon might overstep their plans and quickly corrupt whatever he encounters of their wealth and buildings. Moreover, war is a tug of war whose outcome is unknown. "And they made the most honorable of its people humiliated." By plundering their wealth and destroying their homes, in addition to other humiliation and captivity. "And thus they do." This is an affirmation of what she described of their condition and a statement that this is one of their established and ongoing customs, or a confirmation of it from God Almighty.
27:35: 35 - And I am sending to them a gift is an explanation of what you see as being presented in the reconciliation, and the meaning is that I am sending messengers with a gift with which I will repel him from my kingdom. So I will see what the messengers return from his condition so that I may act accordingly. It was narrated that she sent Mundhir ibn Amr with a delegation and sent with them boys in the garb of slave girls and slave girls in the garb of boys, and a bag containing a pearl and a piece of leather with a crooked hole. She said: If he is a prophet, distinguish between boys and slave girls, and make a straight hole in the pearl and thread a thread through the bead. When they arrived at his camp and saw the greatness of his status, their souls shriveled up before him. When they stood before him, Gabriel had preceded them in the matter and sought the truth and informed them of what was in it, he ordered a termite to take a hair and pierce the pearl, and he ordered a white worm to take the thread and pierce the piece of leather. He called for water, and the slave girl would take water in one hand and put it in the other and then hit her face with it, and the boy would take it and hit his face with it. Then he returned the gift.
27:36: 36 - "When Solomon came" meaning the Messenger or what was presented to him. It was also read as (When they came). "He said, 'Do you provide me with wealth?'" Addressing the Messenger and those with him, or the Messenger and the one sent, with the addressee being predominant. Hamzah and Ya'qub read with assimilation, and it was read with one and two noons and the ya' was deleted. "What God has given me" of prophethood and kingship, which is not to be increased. Nafi', Abu Amr, and Hafs read with the ya' with a fatha, and the rest with a sukoon and with an imalah, only Al-Kisa'i read it with an imala. "Better than what He has given you" I have no need for your gift, and it has no meaning for me. Rather, you rejoice in your gift, because you only know the outward appearance of worldly life, so you rejoice in what is given to you out of a desire to increase your wealth, or because you consider it to be a source of pride over your peers. The rejection of denying the provision of wealth to him and belittling it is to explain the reason that led them to it, which is comparing his condition to their condition in the lack of ambition for this world and the increase in it.
27:37: 37 - "Return," O Messenger. "To them," to Bilqis and her people. "We will come to them with soldiers they cannot resist." They have no power to resist them nor the ability to confront them. It was also read "with them. And We will surely expel them from it," from Sheba. "Humbled," with the loss of their glory. "And they are humiliated," as humiliated captives.
27:38: 38 - "He said, 'O assembly, which of you will bring me her throne?'" He wanted to show her some of the wonders with which God Almighty had distinguished him, indicating the greatness of his power and the truthfulness of his claim to prophethood. He wanted to test her mind by having her deny her throne, to see if she would recognize it or deny it. "Before they come to me in submission," for if she came in submission, it would not be permissible to take it except with her consent.
27:39: 39 - An evil, rebellious demon said, 'Of the jinn,' an explanation of him, because it is said of a wicked, reprehensible man whose peers are covered in dust, and his name was Dhakwan or Sakhr. I will bring it to you before you rise from your seat from your seat of government, and he used to sit until noon. And indeed, I am for it for carrying it, strong and trustworthy I will not reduce anything from it nor change it.
27:40: 40 - He who has knowledge of the Book said, Asif bin Barkhiya, his minister, or Al-Khidr, or Gabriel, peace be upon them, or an angel whom God supported with it, or Solomon, peace be upon him, himself. The expression of it is to indicate the honor of knowledge and that this honor was because of it. The address in: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you is to the jinn, as if he was slow to do it and said that to him, or he wanted to show a miracle in conveying it, so he first challenged them, then showed them that he could do what was not possible for the jinn jinn, let alone others. What is meant by the Book is the type of revealed books or the tablet, and I will bring you in both places is suitable for both the verb and the noun, and the glance is the movement of the eyelids to look, so it was put in its place. And since the observer is described by sending the glance, as in His saying: If you send your eyes as a guide to your heart one day, the sights will tire you out. The description of the cooling of the eye and the eyelid as a recoil, meaning that you direct your eye towards something and before you return it, its throne is brought before you. This is the ultimate in haste and is used as an example. So when he saw it meaning the throne settled near him placed before him, he said receiving the blessing with gratitude in the manner of the sincere servants of God the Most High This is from the bounty of my Lord He favored me with it without me deserving it, and the reference is to the ability to bring the throne during the period of the eye’s recoil of a two-month journey, by himself or someone else, and the discussion of the possibility of something like this has already been mentioned in the verse Al-Isra’. That He may test me whether I will be grateful by seeing it as a favor from God the Most High without any power or strength from me and fulfill its duty. Or be ungrateful by finding myself in between, or falling short in fulfilling his duties. Its place is in the accusative as a substitute for the ya’. And whoever is grateful is grateful for himself because by doing so he brings to it the continuity of the blessing and its increase, and he removes from it the burden of duty and protects it from the stigma of ingratitude. "And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, my Lord is free of need" of thanks. "Generous" in bestowing blessings upon him secondly.
27:41: 41 - "He said, 'Disguise her throne for her.'" By changing its form and shape. "We will see." The answer to the command, and it was read in the nominative case as a resumption. "Will you be guided or will you be among those who are not guided?" To knowing it or the correct answer, and it was said to be to believing in God and His Messenger if she saw her throne advance and she had left it with the doors closed and guards assigned to it.
27:42: 42 - "So when she came, it was said, 'Is your throne like this?'" This was a comparison to her, to further test her mind, as she mentioned before him the foolishness of the mind. "She said, 'As if it were he' and she did not say, He is he" because of the possibility that he could be like him, and that was due to the perfection of her mind. "And we were given knowledge before her, and we were Muslims" is part of her speech, as if she thought that he wanted to test her mind and show her a miracle, so she said: "And we were given knowledge of the perfection of God's power and the truth of your prophethood before this situation, or the miracle from the previous verses." It was said that it was from the words of Solomon, peace be upon him, and his people, and they linked it to her answer because it indicates her faith in God and His Messenger, as she allowed that it was her throne, a common possibility, and the presence of some of the miracles that no one but God Almighty is capable of, and they do not appear except at the hands of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, meaning we were given knowledge of God and His power and the truth of what He brought before her, and we were obedient to His rule and we did not cease to adhere to His religion, and their purpose in it was to talk about what God had bestowed upon them in terms of progress in that, thanking God Almighty.
27:43: 43 - "And what she used to worship besides God prevented her" meaning her worship of the sun prevented her from advancing toward Islam, or God prevented her from worshipping it by granting her success in faith. "Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people. It was read with the fat-ha as a substitution of the agent of sadarha" according to the first, meaning her upbringing among the disbelievers prevented her or the explanation for it.
27:44: 44 - "She was told, 'Enter the palace'" The palace, or it was said, the courtyard of the house. "When she saw it, she thought it was a sea and uncovered her legs." It was narrated that before her arrival, he ordered the construction of a palace with a courtyard of white glass. He made water run underneath it and threw sea animals into it. He placed his bed at the front of it and sat on it. When she saw it, she thought it was stagnant water, so she uncovered her legs. Ibn Kathir, according to the narration of Qanbal, read "I will give her water with a hamza, based on the plural of suuq and asuq. He said, Indeed, what you think is water is a smooth palace" Smooth. "Of bottles" of glass. "She said, 'My Lord, I have wronged myself'" By worshipping the sun. It was also said, "Because I thought Solomon would drown her in the sea." And I submitted with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds, in what he commanded his servants. There is disagreement as to whether he married her or whether he married her to Dhu Tubba, the king of Hamdan.
27:45: 45 - And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], 'Worship God.' That is, worship God. It was read with a damma on the noon, following it with the ba. Then at once they became two parties disputing. So they were suddenly divided and disputing, so one party believed and one party disbelieved, and the waw refers to the two parties together.
27:46: 46 - He said, O my people, why do you hasten the evil with the punishment, saying, Bring us what you promise us "before the good before repentance, delaying it until the punishment descends, for they used to say, If his threat were true, then we would have repented at that time why do you not ask forgiveness of God before it descends that you may receive mercy" by accepting it, for it will not be accepted at that time.
27:47: 47 - They said, 'We have an ill omen,' they said, because of you and those with you,' since hardships have befallen us one after the other, or separation has occurred between us since you invented your religion. "Your omen said, 'Your cause from which your evil has come, is with God,' which is His decree or your deeds written down by Him. 'Rather, you are a people who are being tested,' they say, you are being tested by the succession of good and bad times." The transition from explaining their omen, which is the beginning of what will befall them, to mentioning what is the cause of it.
27:48: 48 - And there were in the city nine men Nine people, and it was used to distinguish the nine in terms of meaning, and the difference between it and a group is that it ranges from three or seven to ten, and a group ranges from three to nine. They cause corruption in the land and do not reform meaning their nature is pure corruption devoid of any taint of reform.
27:49: 49 - They said meaning some of them said to each other. They divided by God is a stated command or a predicate that occurred as a substitute or a state with the omission of al-qad. We will certainly surprise Salih and his family by night Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a ta' as if some of them were addressing each other, and it was read with a ya' as if they divided it as a predicate. Then we will surely say has the three readings. To his guardian to the guardian of his blood. We did not witness the destruction of his family let alone that we took charge of their destruction, and it is possible for the source, time and place, and so is muhalik in the reading of Hafs, since mufa'al came as a source as a reference. Abu Bakr read it with a fat-ha, so it is a source. And we are truthful in what we mentioned because the witness is for the thing that is not directly related to it according to custom, or because we did not witness their destruction alone, but rather his destruction and their destruction, like you say I did not see there a man, but two men.
27:50: 50 - And they plotted a plan with this agreement. And We plotted a plan by making it a reason for their destruction. And they did not perceive of that. It was narrated that Salih had a mosque in a valley in Al-Hijr where he used to pray. They said: He claimed that he would be free from us in three days, so we would be free from him and his family before three days. So they went to the valley to kill him, but a rock fell on them in front of them and closed the mouth of the valley over him. They perished there, and the rest perished in their places by the shout, as indicated by his saying:
27:51: 51 - "So see how was the consequence of their plot. Indeed, We destroyed them and their people, all together." If you make was incomplete, then its predicate is how. "We destroyed them is a resumption or a deleted predicate, not the predicate of was" due to the lack of a pronoun. If you make it complete, then "how" is a state. The Kufians and Ya'qub read "We destroyed them with a fat-ha, as if it is a deleted predicate or a substitute for the name of was or a predicate for it, and how" is a state.
27:52: 52 - Those are their houses, empty. Empty from khawa al-batn, meaning empty, or fallen and demolished from khawa an-Najm, meaning it fell. It is a state in which the meaning of indication works. It is read in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject. Because of their wrongdoing. Because of their wrongdoing. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know. So they are admonished.
27:53: 53 - And We saved those who believed Salih and those with him. And were fearful of disbelief and sins, and that is why they were singled out for salvation.
27:54: 54 - And Lot. And mention Lot, or And We sent Lot as evidence. And We had certainly sent him. "When he said to his people" is a proxy for the first and an adverbial phrase for the second. "Do you commit immorality while you see?" You know its immorality from the sight of the heart and committing shameful acts from the world is uglier because of its ugliness, or some of you see it from others because they were publicizing it, so it would be more immoral.
27:55: 55 - Do you indeed approach men with lust? Clarification of their committing the shameful act and its justification by lust to indicate its ugliness, and to draw attention to the fact that the wisdom in intercourse is to seek offspring, not to satisfy desire. Instead of women who were created for that. Rather, you are a people who are ignorant You do the actions of someone who is ignorant of its ugliness, or is a fool who does not distinguish between good and bad, or you are ignorant of the consequences. The taa' in it is because the one described by it is in the meaning of the one being addressed.
27:56: 56 - "And the only answer of his people was that they said, 'Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure.'" That is, they abstain from our actions, or from filth, and they consider our actions filthy.
27:57: 57 - "So We saved him and his family, except for his wife. We destined her to be among those who remained behind." We destined her to be among those who remained in the punishment.
27:58: 58 - And We rained down upon them a rain, and evil was the rain of those who were warned. A similar example has been mentioned.
27:59: 59 - "Say: Praise be to God, and peace be upon His chosen servants." He ordered His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, after He had related to him the stories indicating the perfection of His power, the greatness of His position, and the great signs and victory over the enemy that He had bestowed upon His Messengers, to praise Him and greet His chosen servants in thanks for what He had bestowed upon them, or to teach him what he did not know about their conditions and in recognition of their excellence, right to precedence, and striving in religion. Or to Lot, to praise Him for the destruction of the infidels of his people and to greet the one He had chosen to protect from immorality and save from destruction. Is God better than what they associate? This is an obligation upon them, a mockery of them, and a disparagement of their opinion, since it is known that there is no good in what they associate with Him at all until it is balanced against the One who is the originator of all good. Abu Amr, Asim, and Yaqub read it with the letter ta'.
27:60: 60 - Aman rather, Aman. He created the heavens and the earth" which are the origins of beings and the principles of benefits. "Aman is read with a light pronunciation as a substitute for God. And He sent down for you" for you. "From the sky water, and We caused to grow thereby gardens of delight." He changed it from the third person to the first person to emphasize the action's specificity to Himself, and to point out that the growing of the delightful gardens of different kinds and different natures from similar materials is not possible for anyone else to do, as He indicated in His statement: "It was not for you to cause its trees to grow The trees of gardens, which are the orchards, are from ihdaq" which means to encompass. "Is there a god with God?" Is there someone other than Him who is paired with Him and a partner is made for Him, while He is the One Who is unique in creation and formation. It is read (Alahihan) with an implied verb like "atada'unu or atashrikun" and with a long vowel between the two hamzas and the second one being placed in between. "Rather, they are a people who deviate" from the truth, which is monotheism.
