29:25: 25- And He said, ‘You have only taken idols besides God, out of affection between you in worldly life.’ That is, so that you may love one another and maintain contact by meeting to worship them. The second object of you have taken is omitted. It is possible that mawdah is the second object by estimating an added word, that is, you have taken idols as a cause of affection between you, or by interpreting it as the beloved. Nafi’ and Abu Bakr read it with a tanween, making between you the subject, and the correct view is what preceded. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Al-Kisa’i, and Ruways read it with a raised tanween, making between you the predicate of a deleted subject, that is, it is beloved or a cause of affection between you. The sentence is an attribute of idols or the predicate of inna on innama as a source or relative, and the pronoun is omitted, which is the first object. It was read with a raised tanween and added with a fatha on between you, just as it was read la qadda taqadah bainum and it was read it is only affection between you. Then on the Day of Resurrection, some of you will disbelieve in others and curse some of you. Some of them say: “That is, the discord and mutual cursing between you, or between you and the idols, is based on the dominance of those addressed, as God Almighty says: “And they will be against them.” And your refuge is the Fire, and you will have no helpers to save you from it.
29:26: 26- So Lot believed in him he is his nephew and the first to believe in him, and it was said that he believed in him when he saw the fire did not burn him. And he said, Indeed, I am an emigrant" from my people. "To my Lord" to where He has commanded me. "Indeed, it is He who is the Exalted in Might" who protects me from my enemies. "The Wise" who does not command me except with what is best for me. It was narrated that he emigrated from Kutha from the plains of Kufa with Lot and his wife Sarah, his cousin, to Harran, then from there to Ash-Sham and settled in Palestine, and Lot settled in Sodom.
29:27: 27- And We bestowed upon him Isaac and Jacob a son and an additional gift when he despaired of having children from a barren old woman. That is why Ishmael is not mentioned. And We bestowed upon his descendants prophethood so that the number of prophets increased among them. And the Book he means by it the genus to include the four books. And We gave him his reward for his migration to Us. In this world by giving him a son at an untimely time, and good offspring and the continuation of prophethood among them and the people of religions growing towards him and praising and praying upon him until the end of time. And indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous among those who are perfect in righteousness.
29:28: 28- And Lot is in apposition to Abraham or to what is in apposition to him. When he said to his people, ‘Indeed, you are committing an immorality’ the extremely ugly act. The two imams, Ibn Amir, and Hafs read it with a broken hamza as a statement, and the rest read it as a question, and they agreed on the question in the second. No one in the world had done it before you is a resumption establishing its immorality, as it is something that natures are disgusted with and souls avoid, until they committed it due to the wickedness of their nature.
29:29: 29- Do you indeed approach men and block the way? And you expose travelers to murder, theft of money, or indecency until the roads are blocked, or you block the way of offspring by turning away from tillage and doing what is not tillage. And you commit in your assemblies In your gatherings crowded with its people, and the club is only called for when its people are in it. The evil Such as sexual intercourse, farting, untying the garment, and other shameful acts, out of indifference to them. It was also said that it was slander and shooting rifles. And the only answer of his people was that they said, Bring us the punishment of God, if you should be of the truthful" In the ugliness of that or in the claim of prophethood understood from the rebuke.
29:30: 30- He said, ‘My Lord, support me’ by bringing down the punishment. Upon the corrupting people by following immorality and establishing it among those who came after them. He described them thus as an exaggeration in bringing down the punishment and indicating that they are more deserving of the punishment being hastened for them.
29:31: 31- And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, the good tidings of a son and the voluntary offering. They said, ‘Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city,’ the city of Sodom. The addition is verbal because the meaning is future tense. Indeed, its people were wrongdoers, an explanation for their destruction because of their insistence and persistence in their wrongdoing, which is disbelief and various types of sins.
29:32: 32- He said, ‘Therein is Lot.’ This is an objection to them that there are those in it who were not wronged, or a counter to the obligation with the deterrent, which is the Prophet being among them. “They said, ‘We know best who is in it. We will surely save him and his family.’” This is an acknowledgment of his statement while claiming greater knowledge of it and that they were not unaware of it, and an answer to it by specifying the family to those other than him and his family, or the timing of the destruction by expelling them from it, and in it is a delay in explaining the address. Except his wife, she was among those who remained behind, those who remained in the punishment or the village.
29:33: 33- And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed by them. He was distressed and grieved because of them, fearing that his people would intend evil against them. That is a conjunction to emphasize the two actions and their connection. And he felt straitened by them. He felt straitened by their situation and the management of their affairs, meaning he felt straitened by his ability, as they say, his hand became straitened, and in contrast, his ability was broadened by such-and-such, if he was able to bear it. This is because someone with long arms can attain what someone with short arms cannot attain. And they said, when they saw the signs of distress on him, Do not fear and do not grieve, about their ability to overpower us. Indeed, We will save you and your family, except for your wife, who is among those who remain behind. Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Ya’qub read lanjanjinah We will save him and manjook We will save you with a light pronunciation. Abu Bakr and Ibn Kathir agreed with the second pronunciation. The position of the kaf is the accusative according to the preferred opinion, and your family is the accusative with an implied verb or by being connected to its position according to the original.
29:34: 34- Indeed, We are going to send down upon the people of this city a punishment from the sky a torment from it that was called this because it disturbs the one being tormented by their saying irtajaz if he is shaken, meaning he is disturbed. Ibn Amir read manzilun with emphasis. Because they were sinning because of their sin.
29:35: 35- And We have certainly left of it a clear sign which is its common story or the traces of the ruined homes, and it was said that it was the rain-soaked stones, for they remained after that, and it was said that it was the remainder of its blackened rivers. For a people who understand who use their minds to gain insight and contemplate, and it is related to We left or sign.
29:36: 36- “And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu`ayb. He said, ‘O my people, worship God and hope for the Last Day.’ And do what you hope for reward for. So the effect was made in place of the cause. It was said that it is from hope in the sense of fear. “And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.”
29:37: 37- But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them the severe earthquake, and it was said that it was the cry of Gabriel, peace be upon him, because hearts tremble at it. So they became in their homes in their country or their houses, and it was not pluralized to avoid confusion. Kneeling kneeling on their knees, dead.
29:38: 38- ‘Aad and Thamud are in the accusative case due to the omission of remember or a verb indicated by what preceded it, such as we destroyed. Hamzah, Hafs, and Ya’qub read and Thamud without the accusative case, interpreting it as a tribe. And it has become clear to you from their dwellings meaning, some of their dwellings have become clear to them, or their destruction from the perspective of their dwellings if you look at them when you pass by them. And Satan made their deeds pleasing to them of disbelief and sins. So he averted them from the path the straight path that the messengers had shown them. And they were discerning able to see and discern, but they did not do so, or they were clear that the punishment would not befall them due to the messengers informing them, but they persisted until they perished.
29:39: 39- And Korah, Pharaoh, and Haman is in apposition to 'Aad, and Korah is mentioned first due to the nobility of his lineage. And Moses had already come to them with clear proofs, but they were arrogant upon the land, and they were not forerunners. Rather, the command of God overtakes those who seek it first if they miss it.
29:40: 40- So each of the masculine genders. We seized him for his sin We punished him for his sin. And among them were those upon whom We sent a violent storm a violent wind with pebbles in it, or an angel who pelted them with it, like the people of Lot. And among them were those whom the blast seized like Midian and Thamud. And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow like Qarun. And among them were those whom We drowned like the people of Noah, Pharaoh, and his people. And God would not wrong them to treat them as an oppressor, punishing them without a crime, since that is not His habit, the Almighty, the Majestic. But they were wronging themselves by exposing themselves to punishment.
29:41: 41- The parable of those who take protectors other than God is that they do not take Him as a trustee or a protector. Like the spider who has made a home in what he has woven out of weakness and frailty, but that is even weaker, for this has a reality and some benefit, or like them in relation to a man who built a house from stone and plaster. Spider is used for singular and plural, masculine and feminine, and the taa' is like the taa' of taghut and it is pluralized as anakeeb, anakeeb, 'akab, 'akabah and a'kab. And indeed, the flimsiest of houses is the spider's house There is no house weaker or less protective from heat and cold than it. If they only knew They would refer to knowledge, they would know that this is their example and that their religion is weaker than that. It is possible that what is meant by the spider's house is their religion, and he named it thus to achieve the example, so the meaning would be: And indeed, the flimsiest of what is relied upon in religion is their religion.
29:42: 42- Indeed, God knows whatever they call upon besides Him with the omission of the statement, meaning, say to the disbelievers, Indeed, God knows. The two Basrans read it with the letter ya based on what preceded it. Ma is an interrogative noun governed by you call upon and knows is suspended from it. Min is for clarification or negation. Min is an addition and Shay’ is the object of you call upon or a verbal noun. Shay’ is a verbal noun or relative pronoun, the object of you call upon and the object of you call upon is its omitted pronoun. The discussion of the first two is to make them ignorant and to emphasize the example. The discussion of the last two is a threat to them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise is an explanation of the two meanings, for it is extreme foolishness to associate something that is not considered anything with someone of this nature, and that inanimate things, in comparison to the One who is able and dominant over everything, who has attained the utmost knowledge and perfection of action, are like nonexistent things, and that the One with this description is able to punish them.
29:43: 43- And these examples meaning this example and others like it. We present them to the people to illustrate what is beyond their comprehension. And none understands them nor understands their beauty and benefit. Except those of knowledge who contemplate things as they should. “And it was narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited this verse and said: The knowledgeable one is he who understands God, acts in obedience to Him, and avoids His wrath.”
29:44: 44- God created the heavens and the earth in truth with the truth, not with the intention of falsehood, for the purpose of creating them is to convey goodness and indicate His essence and attributes, as He indicated by His saying: Indeed in that is a sign for the believers, because they are the ones who benefit from it.
29:45: 45- Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book to draw closer to God the Most High by reading it, memorizing its words, and exploring its meanings. The thoughtful reader may discover through repetition what was not discovered to him when he first heard it. "And establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing" by being a reason for refraining from sins while engaged in it and other things, as it reminds one of God and instills in the soul a fear of Him. It was narrated that "a young man from the Ansar used to pray with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would not leave any immorality without committing it. When he described it to him, peace be upon him, he said: His prayer will prohibit him, and it did not take long for him to repent." And the remembrance of God is greater and prayer is greater than all other acts of obedience. It was expressed thus to explain that its inclusion of His remembrance is the main reason it is preferred over good deeds and prevents bad ones, or because God’s remembrance of you through His mercy is greater than your remembrance of Him through His obedience. And God knows what you do in it and in all other acts of obedience, so He will reward you for it with the best reward.
29:46: 46- And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best except in the best characteristic, such as countering harshness with gentleness, anger with restraint, and quarreling with advice. It was said that this was abrogated by the verse of the sword, as there is no argument more severe than it. The answer to this is that it is the last resort. It was also said that what is meant by it is those among them who have a treaty. Except for those among them who have wronged by excessive aggression and stubbornness, or by claiming a son and saying, The hand of God is chained, or by breaking the treaty and refusing to pay the jizyah. And say, ‘We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you.’ This is from arguing in a way that is best. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “Do not believe the People of the Scripture, nor disbelieve them, but say, ‘We believe in God and in His Book and His Messengers.’ If they say something false, you will not believe them, and if they say something true, you will not disbelieve them.” Our God and your God is one, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him. We are obedient to Him in particular, and it is an allusion to their taking their rabbis and monks as lords besides God.
29:47: 47- And likewise and similar to that revelation. We have sent down to you the Book a revelation confirming all the other divine books, and it is the fulfillment of His statement: Those to whom We gave the Scripture believe in it They are Abdullah ibn Salam and his likes, or those who came before the time of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the People of the Book. And among these and from the Arabs or the people of Mecca or those who came during the time of the Messenger from the People of the Two Books. He who believes in it the Qur’an. And none rejects Our signs despite their clarity and the establishment of proof for them. Except the disbelievers except those who are deeply entrenched in disbelief, for their certainty about it prevents them from contemplating what would restrict its truthfulness to them due to it being a miracle in relation to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, as He indicated in His statement:
29:48: 48- And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand. The appearance of this book, which encompasses various noble sciences, while illiterate, is not known to be a miracle through reading and learning. The mention of the right hand is to further illustrate the negated and to negate the exaggeration in the chain of transmission. Then the falsifiers would have had doubts. That is, if you were among those who write and read, they would have said, Perhaps you learned it or picked it up from the books of the ancients. He only called them falsifiers because of their disbelief or because they doubted the denial of one aspect of the numerous miracles. It was said that the People of the Book would have had doubts because We would have found your description contrary to what is in their books. Thus, their falsification would be based on reality, not what is assumed. Rather, it is rather the Qur’an.
29:49: 49- Clear verses in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge They memorize it and no one is able to distort it. None reject Our verses except the wrongdoers Those who are deeply entrenched in injustice through stubbornness after the evidence of its miraculous nature has become clear, to the point that they do not pay attention to it.
29:50: 50- And they said, ‘Why were not signs sent down to him from his Lord?’ Such as the she-camel of Salih, the staff of Moses, and the table of Jesus. Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, the two Basrans, and Hafs read signs. “Say, ‘The signs are only with God.’” He sends them down as He wills. I do not own them, so I will bring you what you suggest. I am only a clear warner. My only concern is to warn and make it clear with the signs that I have been given.
29:51: 51- Was it not sufficient for them a verse that suffices them in what they suggested. That We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book which is recited to them its recitation to them continues, they unite with it, so it remains with them as a fixed sign that does not fade, unlike other signs. Or it is recited to them, meaning the Jews, by confirming what they have in their hands of your description and the description of your religion. Indeed in that the Book which is a continuous sign and clear proof. is mercy a great blessing. And a reminder for a people who believe and a reminder for those whose concern is belief without obstinacy. “It was said that some Muslims came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with books in which were written some of what the Jews say, so he said, “It is enough for a people to be misguided that they turn away from what their prophet brought them to what someone other than their prophet brought.” So this verse was revealed.
29:52: 52- Say, ‘God is sufficient as a witness between me and you’ with my truthfulness and He has confirmed me with miracles, or with my conveying what I was sent to you with and my advising you and your response to me with denial and stubbornness. He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, so my condition and your condition are not hidden from Him. And those who believe in falsehood, which is what is worshipped besides God, and disbelieve in God, among you. Those are the losers in their deal where they bought disbelief with faith.
29:53: 53- And they ask you to hasten the punishment by saying, Then rain down upon us stones from the sky. “And were it not for a specified term” for every punishment or people. The punishment would have come upon them quickly. And it will come upon them suddenly suddenly in this world, such as the Battle of Badr, or in the Hereafter when death descends upon them. And they are not aware of its coming.
29:54: 54- They urge you to hasten the punishment, while Hell will surely encompass the disbelievers. It will encompass them on the Day the punishment comes to them, or it will encompass them now due to the encompassing and disbelief and sins that they have committed. The lam is for the covenant, placing the apparent in place of the implicit to indicate the reason for encompassing, or for the genus, so it is an inference from the ruling of the genus to their ruling.
29:55: 55- The Day the punishment will cover them is an adverbial phrase for surrounding or implied, such as such and such. “From above them and from beneath their feet” means from all sides. And He says God or some of His angels by His command, according to the reading of Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and the two Basrans with the letter nun. “Taste what you used to do” means its reward.
29:56: 56- O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship Me. That is, if it is not easy for you to worship Me in one land and it is not easy for you to practice your religion openly, then migrate to wherever it is easier for you to do so. “And it was narrated from him, peace and blessings be upon him, that whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is evil, will deserve Paradise and will be a companion of Abraham and Muhammad, peace be upon them.” The fa is a conditional omitted letter, as the meaning is that My earth is spacious. If you do not worship Me sincerely in one land, then worship Me sincerely in another.
29:57: 57- Every soul will taste death It will inevitably reach it. Then to Us you will be returned for the recompense, and whoever has this consequence should strive to prepare for it. Abu Bakr read it with the letter yaa.
29:58: 58- And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely assign them lofty chambers in Paradise [Al-Ali]. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read lantahuwaynihum meaning We will surely establish them from their lodging, so the accusative case of ghurfana is because it is used in the same way as lanzallanahum or by removing the preposition or by likening the temporary circumstance to the ambiguous. “Underneath it rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. Excellent is the reward of the workers.” [Fana’am] was also read, and the one being praised is omitted, indicated by what preceded it.
29:59: 59- Those who were patient in the face of the harm of the polytheists and the migration for the sake of religion, along with other trials and hardships. And upon their Lord they put their trust and they put their trust in no one but God.
29:60: 60- "And how many a creature does not carry its own provision" It cannot carry it due to its weakness or it does not store it, but it wakes up and has no livelihood. "God provides for it and for you" Moreover, despite its weakness and reliance on Him, and despite your strength and striving, they are the same in that none provides for it and for you except God, because the provision of everyone is through causes that He alone is the cause of. So do not fear for your livelihood by emigrating, because when they were commanded to emigrate, some of them said, "How can we go to a land where we have no livelihood?" So this was revealed: "And He is the Hearing" of what you say. "The Knowing" of your conscience.
29:61: 61- And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?’ The people of Mecca are responsible for them. They will surely say, ‘God,’ since it is established in the minds that all possibilities must end with One, Necessarily Existent. How then are they deluded? They are turned away from His Oneness after having acknowledged that.
29:62: 62- God expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for whom He wills. It is possible that the one for whom He expands and restricts it is one and the same, so that the expansion and restriction are sequential and not by placing the pronoun in place of whomever He wills and making it ambiguous because whomever He wills is ambiguous. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things. He knows their interests and their harms.
29:63: 63- And if you ask them, ‘Who sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ They acknowledge that He is the Creator of all things, their origins and their branches. Then they associate with Him some of His creations who are not capable of any of that. Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ For what He has protected you from such misguidance, or for believing you and demonstrating your proof. Rather, most of them do not reason. They contradict themselves by acknowledging that He is the Originator of everything other than Him. Then they associate with Him an idol. It has been said that they do not understand what you mean by praising You when they say this.
29:64: 64- And what is this worldly life? A gesture of contempt. How could it not be, when it weighs nothing in the sight of God as much as a mosquito's wing? Except amusement and play. Except as children amuse themselves and play with it, gathering together and rejoicing in it for an hour, then dispersing, exhausted. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is life. It is the home of true life, as death is prevented from approaching it, or it is in itself life for the sake of exaggeration. Hayawan is a verbal noun meaning living, which is the name given to the one with life, and its root is hayyan, so the second ya was changed to a waw, and it is more eloquent than life because of the movement and disturbance in the structure of fa'laan necessary for life. That is why it was chosen over it here. If they had known, they would not have preferred this world over it, whose origin is non-life, and life in it is fleeting and quickly disappears.
29:65: 65- So when they embark on a ship is connected to what is indicated by the explanation of their condition, i.e. they are as they were described in terms of polytheism, so when they embark on the sea. They call upon God, devoting their religion to Him sincerely being in the image of the most sincere believers in their religion, as they do not mention anyone but God and do not call upon anyone other than Him, knowing that no one can remove hardships except Him. But when He delivers them to land, at once they associate others with Him they suddenly return to polytheism.
29:66: 66- That they may disbelieve in what We have given them. The lam in it is the lam of ki, meaning that they associate others so that they may be disbelievers in their association with the blessing of salvation. And that they may enjoy themselves by their gathering together to worship idols and to love one another for them, or the lam of command is for threatening, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Kathir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Qalun on the authority of Nafi’. (And let them enjoy) the tranquility. They will know the consequences of that when they are punished.
29:67: 67- Or have they not seen meaning the people of Mecca. That We have made a secure sanctuary meaning We have made their land safe from plunder and aggression, and its people safe from killing and captivity. And people are snatched away all around them they steal away killing and captivity, as the Arabs around it were treacherous and plundering. Then do they believe in falsehood? Beyond this revealed blessing and other things that only God has power over, they believe in idols or Satan. And they disbelieve in the favor of God since they have associated others with Him, and the two conjunctions are brought forward for emphasis or specificity by way of exaggeration.
29:68: 68- And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God by claiming that He has a partner. Or denies the truth when it comes to him meaning the Messenger or the Book. In when there is a mockery of them because they did not agree and never considered when it came to them, but rather they hastened to deny it the first time they heard it. Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers? It is a confirmation of their abode, as He says: Aren't you better than those who ride mounts? That is, do they not deserve to remain in it when they fabricated such a lie against God and denied the truth with such a denial, or because they dared, that is, did they not know that in Hell is a residence for the disbelievers so that they dared to commit such a bold act?
29:69: 69- And those who strive for Us for Our sake, and the term struggle is used to include striving against apparent and hidden enemies in all its forms. We will surely guide them to Our ways the ways of traveling to Us and reaching Our side, or We will increase their guidance to the path of goodness and grant them success in following it, as God the Most High says: And those who are guided - We will increase them in guidance. And in the hadith: Whoever acts upon what he knows, God will make him inherit knowledge of that which he does not know. “And indeed, God is with the doers of good” with victory and support. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites Surat Al-Ankaboot will have ten good deeds equal to the number of all the believers and hypocrites.
30:3: 3 - In the lowest part of the land the land of the Arabs because it is the land known to them, a, in the lowest part of their land of the Arabs and the lam is a substitute for the addition. And they, after their defeat from the addition of the source to the object, and it was read defeated them and it is in the language like the bringing and the bringing. They will be defeated.
30:4: 4 - In a few years. It was narrated that the Persians invaded the Romans and met them in Adhraat and Busra, and it was said in Al-Jazirah, which is the closest land of the Romans to the Persians. They defeated them and the report reached Mecca, so the polytheists rejoiced and gloated over the Muslims and said: You and the Christians are people of the Book, and we and the Persians are illiterate. Our brothers have triumphed over your brothers, and we will triumph over you. So it was revealed. Abu Bakr said to them: May God not comfort your eyes, for by God, the Romans will triumph over the Persians after a few years. Ubayy ibn Khalaf said to him: You have lied. Set a deadline between us for which I will compete with you. So he competed with him for ten she-camels from each of them, and they set the deadline for three years. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: A few is between three and nine. So he increased the risk and added to the deadline, so they set it at one hundred she-camels for nine years. Ubayy died from a wound inflicted on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after his return from Uhud. The Romans triumphed over the Persians on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah. Abu Bakr took the risk from my father’s heirs and brought it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said, Give it in charity. The Hanafis used it as evidence for the permissibility of invalid contracts in the land of war. It was answered that it was before gambling was prohibited, and the verse is one of the proofs of prophethood because it is a report of the unseen. The word ghalaba was read with a fat-ha and the word siyaghalbunu with a damma, meaning that the Romans had defeated the countryside of Syria and the Muslims would defeat them. In the ninth year of its revelation, the Muslims invaded them and conquered some of their lands. Based on this, the word ghalab is added to the subject. To God belongs the command before and after before they were victorious, which is the time when they were defeated, and after they were defeated, which is the time when they were victorious, meaning His is the command when they were defeated, and nothing of them is except by His decree. The word from before and after was read without estimating an object, as if it was said before and after, meaning first and last. And on that day and the day the Romans are victorious, the believers will rejoice.
30:5: 5 - By the victory of God for he who has a Book over he who does not have a Book, because it is a reversal of optimism and the manifestation of their truthfulness in what they told the polytheists and their victory in their bet and the increase of their certainty and steadfastness in their religion. It was said that God gives victory to the believers by demonstrating their truthfulness or by some of their enemies being allies of others until they are annihilated. He gives victory to whom He wills so He gives victory to these people at one time and to those people at another. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful He takes revenge on His servants by giving them victory at one time and bestows favor upon them by giving them victory at another time.
30:6: 6 - The promise of God is a source that confirms itself because what preceded it is in the meaning of a promise. God does not break His promise because lying to Him is impossible. But most people do not know His promise and the validity of His promise because of their ignorance and lack of thought.
30:7: 7 - They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, what they see of it and enjoy its adornments. And they are heedless of the Hereafter, which is its goal and intended purpose. They are heedless, it does not cross their minds. The second they is a repetition of the first or a subject, and heedless is its predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of the first. In both cases, it is a vocative of their complete heedlessness of the Hereafter, which is confirmed by the requirement of the previous sentence replaced by His statement, They do not know, as a confirmation of their ignorance and likening them to animals whose perception of this world is limited to some of its outward aspects. Part of knowing its outward aspect is knowing its realities, characteristics, properties, actions, causes, how they emanate from it, and how to act within it. For this reason, the outward aspect is denied. As for its inner aspect, it is a metaphor for the Hereafter and a connection to attaining it and a model for its conditions, and a notification that there is no difference between lack of knowledge and knowledge that is specific to the outward aspect of this world.
30:8: 8 - Have they not reflected upon themselves? Or have they not thought about themselves, or have they not thought about their own affairs, for they are closer to them than anything else and a mirror in which what is revealed to the one who has insight is made manifest to him in all possibilities, so that they may realize the ability of their Creator to restore them, just as He has the ability to bring them into being. God did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except in truth. Related to an omitted statement or knowledge indicated by the speech. And a specified term Ends with it and does not remain after it. And indeed, many of the people, in the meeting with their Lord Meeting His reward at the expiration of the specified term or the establishment of the Hour. Are disbelievers Deniers who think that this world is eternal and that the Hereafter will not come to pass.
30:9: 9 - Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? This is a report of their travels throughout the regions of the earth and their observation of the traces of the destroyers before them. They were mightier than them in strength, such as Aad and Thamud. And they tilled the earth and turned upside down to extract water, minerals, and plant seeds, etc. And they populated it and populated the earth. More than they populated it of the people of Mecca populating it, for they were people of a valley without crops that were not spread out for them elsewhere. This is a mockery of them, as they were deceived by the world and proud of it, while they were in a weaker state in it, since its affair revolved around expansion in the lands, dominating the servants, and disposing of the regions of the earth with various types of construction, while they were weak and forced into a home that had no benefit. And their messengers came to them with clear proofs with miracles or clear signs. God would not wrong them by doing to them what the oppressors do, destroying them without any crime or reminder. But they were wronging themselves because they did what led to their destruction.
30:10: 10 - Then the end of those who did evil was the worst meaning then their end was the bad end or the bad characteristic, so the apparent was placed in place of the pronoun to indicate what required that to be their end and that they did the same as their actions, and bad is the feminine of worst like good or a source like good report that is described by it. That they denied the signs of God and used to mock them is a reason, a substitute, or an apposition for the worst, or the predicate of was, and the worst is the source of they did evil or its object with the same meaning, then the consequence of those who committed the sin was that God sealed their hearts until they denied the signs of God and mocked them. It is possible that the worst is the relative clause of the verb and that they denied is its follower and the predicate is omitted for ambiguity and exaggeration, and that that is explanatory because if the offense is explained by denial and mockery, then it includes the meaning of the statement. Ibn Amir and the Kufians read consequence in the accusative case, on the basis that the noun is the worst and that they denied are in the aforementioned ways.
30:11: 11 - God begins creation He creates them. Then He repeats it He resurrects them. Then to Him you will be returned for recompense and the shift to address is to exaggerate the intended meaning. Abu Bakr, Abu Amr and Ruh read it with the letter ya according to the original.
30:12: 12 - And on the Day the Hour appears, the criminals will be in despair. They will be silent, desperate. It is said, I looked at him and he was in despair if he was silent and despaired of arguing. From this comes the word al-Mublis which means a she-camel that does not bray. It is also read with the opening of the lām from ablasa if he silenced him.
30:13: 13 - And they had no intercessors from among their partners from those whom they associated with God. Intercessors to protect them from the punishment of God. The past tense is used to indicate its realization. And they were disbelievers in their partners disbelieving in their gods when they despaired of them. It was said that they were disbelievers in this world because of them. It was written in the Qur'an (intercessors) and (they taught the Children of Israel) with the waw, as well as (the worst) with the alif to confirm the hamza in the form of the letter from which its movement is derived.
30:14: 14 - And on the Day the Hour comes, that Day they will be divided meaning the believers and the disbelievers, as God Almighty says:
30:15: 15 - As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, they will be in a garden a land with flowers and rivers. They will be delighted with a joy that will ruin their faces.
30:16: 16 - And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter - those will be brought to the punishment. They will be brought in and will not be absent from it.
30:17: 17 - So glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. This is a statement in the meaning of the command to glorify God the Most High and praise Him at these times when His power is evident and His blessings are renewed, or it is an indication that what occurs at these times of clear evidence of His glorification and His being deserving of praise is from those who have distinction among the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and the specification of glorification to the evening and morning is because the effects of power and greatness are more evident at these times. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 22 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Rūm, and the first verses of Sūrat Saba. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time.
