33:1: 1 - O Prophet, fear God. He called him the Prophet and ordered him to fear God, to glorify him and to magnify the importance of piety. What is meant by it is the order to adhere to it so that it would prevent him from what He forbade in His saying: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, with regard to what would result in weakness in religion. It was narrated that Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Abu al-A'war as-Sulami came to him regarding the truce that had been between him and them. Ibn Abi, Mu'tab ibn Qushayr, and al-Jadd ibn Qays stood with them and said to him: Refuse to mention our gods and say that they have intercession and we will leave you to your Lord. So the following was revealed: Indeed, God is Knowing of what is good and what is bad. Wise He only rules according to what wisdom dictates.
33:2: 2 - And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord as a prohibition against obeying them. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Knowing. So He revealed to you what will improve your deeds and make you not need to listen to the disbelievers. Abu Amr read it with the letter ya so that the letter waw refers to the disbelievers and hypocrites, meaning that God is aware of their plots and will repel them from you.
33:3: 3 - And put your trust in God and all your affairs are in His control. And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs Entrusting all matters to Him.
33:4: 4 - God has not made for any man two hearts within him meaning He has not combined two hearts in one chest because the heart is the repository of the animal spirit related to the human soul first and foremost and prevents all powers and that prevents polygamy. And He has not made your wives whom you declare to be your mothers nor has He made your adopted sons your sons He did not combine marriage and motherhood in a woman nor calling and sonship in a man, and what is meant by that is to refute what the Arabs claimed that the intelligent and well-informed person has two hearts and that is why Abu Ma'mar or Jamil ibn Asad al-Fihri was called the one with two hearts, and the wife whom he declared to be like a mother and the man was called his son and that is why they used to say of Zayd ibn Haritha al-Kalbi the freedman of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the son of Muhammad, or what is meant is to deny motherhood and sonship from the one who declared to be from her and the adopted one and to deny the two hearts to pave the way for a principle upon which they are based. The meaning is: Just as God did not make two hearts in one cavity to lead to contradiction, which is that each of them is the origin of all faculties, and not the origin, He did not make the wife and the adopted son who have no child with Him and his mother, and his son who have no child with Him. Abu Amr read al-lay with the letter ya alone, on the basis that its origin is la with a hamza, so it was lightened. The Hijazis narrated the same, and from them and from Ya’qub with the letter hamza alone. The origin of tazaharoon is tatazaharoon, so the second ta’ was assimilated into the dhaal. Ibn ‘Amir read tazaharoon with assimilation, Hamza and al-Kisa’i with deletion, and Asim read tazaharoon from dhahir. It was read tazhiroon from dhahir meaning dhahir like aqd meaning aqid and tazhiroon from dahur. The meaning of zihar is to say to the wife, you are to me like the back of my mother. It is taken from the back, considering the wording, like the talbiyah from labbayka, and its transitivity is with min to include the meaning of avoidance, because it was a divorce in the pre-Islamic era, while in Islam it requires divorce or prohibition until the expiation is performed, as it is transitive to sworn to it, and it has the meaning of an oath. The back is mentioned as a metaphor for the abdomen, which is the pillar, because mentioning it is similar to mentioning the vagina, or to emphasize the prohibition, because they considered it a crime to have intercourse with a woman while her back is towards the sky. Adiyaa is the plural of da’i, as an anomaly, and it is as if it was compared to fa’il in the sense of fa’il, so it was made plural. That is an indication of what was mentioned or the latter. Your saying with your mouths has no reality in objects, like the saying of the delirious one. And God speaks the truth has no reality in objects corresponding to it. And He guides to the way is the way of truth.
33:5: 5 - Call them by the names of their fathers. Attribute them to them. This is the singular meaning of his true statements. His statement, It is more just in the sight of God, is an explanation of it. The pronoun is for the source of call them. "More just is a comparative adjective intended to mean an absolute increase from justice," meaning fairness, and its meaning is the utmost in truth. "But if you do not know their fathers," then attribute them to them. "Then your brothers in religion," meaning they are your brothers in religion. "And your clients, and your clients in it, so say, This is my brother and my client," with this interpretation. "And there is no blame upon you for that in which you err," and there is no sin upon you for what you did by mistake before the prohibition or after it, whether due to forgetfulness or a slip of the tongue. "But [there is no blame] for what your hearts intended," but the blame is for what your hearts intended, or but what your hearts intended is the blame. "And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful," for His forgiveness of the one who errs. Know that adoption is not considered important in our view, but according to Abu Hanifa, it requires the emancipation of his slave and the establishment of lineage for an unknown person who can be attributed to him.
33:6: 6 - The Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves in all matters, as he does not command them or accept from them except what is good for them and successful, unlike the self. Therefore, it was stated in general terms, so it is necessary for them to be more beloved to them than themselves, and his command is more effective over them than their command, and their compassion for him is more complete than their compassion for the self. It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) wanted to go on the Battle of Tabuk, so he ordered the people to go out. Some people said, We should ask permission from our fathers and mothers. So this verse was revealed. It was read, And he is a father to them, meaning in religion, as every prophet is a father to his nation in that he is the foundation of eternal life, and therefore the believers became brothers. And his wives are their mothers, in status like theirs in terms of being forbidden and deserving of reverence, and in everything else, they are like foreigners. Therefore, Aisha may God be pleased with her said, We are not the mothers of women. "And those of kinship" and relatives. "Some of them are closer to others" in inheritance, which abrogated what was in the early days of Islam of inheritance through migration and loyalty in religion. In the Book of God in the Tablet or in what was revealed, which is this verse or the verse of inheritance or in what God has imposed. Of the believers and the emigrants is a statement of the relatives, or a connection to the relatives, meaning the relatives by right of kinship are more deserving of inheritance than the believers by right of religion and the emigrants by right of migration. Unless you do to your relatives a kindness is an exception to the most general of what priority is estimated in terms of benefit, and what is meant by doing a kindness is a recommendation or something interrupted. That was written in the Book what was mentioned in the two verses was established in the Tablet or the Qur’an. It was also said in the Torah.
33:7: 7 - And when We took from the prophets their covenant is understood as mention and their covenant is their pledges to convey The message and call to the true religion. And from you, and from Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary. He mentioned them specifically because they are famous masters of the laws, and He presented our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Peace be upon him, to glorify him and honor his status. And We took from them a solemn covenant of great importance. Or confirmed by an oath, and repetition to clarify this description to magnify it.
33:8: 8 - That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness. That is, We did that so that God may question on the Day of Resurrection the prophets who were true to their covenant about what they said to their people, or their belief in them, as a rebuke to them, or those who believed them about their belief, for the one who believes the truthful is truthful, or the believers who were true to their covenant when He made them witness against themselves about their truthfulness in their covenant. And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment. This is in apposition to We have seized, in that the sending of the messengers and the taking of the covenant from them was to reward the believers, or to what it indicates, So that He may question, as if He said, So He rewarded the believers and prepared for the disbelievers.
33:9: 9 - O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when there came to you armies meaning the Confederates, namely the Quraysh, Ghatafan, and the Jews of Qurayzah and Nadir, and they were about twelve thousand. Then We sent against them a wind the north wind. And armies you did not see the angels. It was narrated that when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) heard of their approach, he dug the trench around Madinah, then he went out to them with three thousand, with the trench between him and them. Nearly a month passed between the two groups, with no war between them except the throwing of arrows and stones, until God sent a cold wind on a winter night, which decimated them, threw dirt in their faces, extinguished their fires, toppled their tents, and the horses swarmed against each other. The angels shouted Allahu Akbar God is Great on the sides of the army, and Tulaiha ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadi said, As for Muhammad, he started you at dawn, so escape, escape. So they were defeated without a fight. And God is All-Seeing of what you do of digging the trench. The two Basrans read it with the letter ya meaning of what the polytheists do of forming parties and fighting. All-Seeing is All-Watching.
33:10: 10 - When they come to you instead of when it comes to you. "From above you" from the top of the valley from the east are Banu Ghatafan. "And from below you" from the bottom of the valley from the west are Quraysh. "And when the eyes swerve" they turn from the level of their vision in confusion and staring. "And the hearts reach the throats" in terror, for the lungs swell from the intensity of the terror, so the heart rises with its rise to the top of the throat, which is the end of the trachea, the entrance for food and drink. "And you think about God various thoughts." The types of thoughts are: The sincere ones with steadfast hearts thought that God would fulfill His promise to elevate His religion, or that He would test them, so they feared slipping and weakness of endurance. The weak-hearted and the hypocrites, as was reported about them. The alif is added in such verses to liken the breaks to the rhymes. Nafi`, Ibn `Amir, and Abu Bakr made the connection in it like the pause, and Abu `Amr, Hamza, and Ya`qub did not add it at all, which is the standard.
33:11: 11 - There the believers were tested. They were tested, and the sincere were distinguished from the hypocrites, and the steadfast were distinguished from the shaken. And they were shaken with a severe shaking. From the intensity of the fear, and it was read (Zalzalan) with the fat-ha.
33:12: 12 - And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say weak belief, What God and His Messenger promised us of victory and exaltation of religion is nothing but delusion a false promise. It was said that Mu'tab bin Qushair said, "Muhammad promises us the conquest of Persia and Rome, and one of us cannot even defecate out of fear. This is nothing but a delusional promise."
33:13: 13 - And when a party of them said, meaning Aws bin Qayzi and his followers, O people of Yathrib, meaning the people of Medina. It was said that it is the name of a land in a part of which Medina was located. No place to stay, meaning a place to stay. For you here, and Hafs read it with the dammah as a place or a verbal noun from aqama. "So return," fleeing to your homes. It was said that the meaning is "You have no place to stay upon the religion of Muhammad, so return to polytheism and submit to it so that you may be safe, or You have no place to stay in Yathrib, so return as disbelievers so that you may remain there. And a party of them ask the Prophet's permission," to return. "They say, 'Our houses are vulnerable,' not fortified, and its root is khalaal. It is possible that the lightening of awrah is from awrat al-dar" if it is disturbed, and it was read with it. "And it is not vulnerable," rather it is fortified. "They only want to flee," meaning that they only want to flee from the fighting.
33:14: 14 - And if you had entered upon them means entering the city or their homes. From its regions means from its sides. The subject was omitted to indicate that the entry of these partisans upon it and the entry of other armies are the same in requiring the ruling based on it. Then they were asked about the strife means apostasy and fighting the Muslims. They would have come to it means they would have given it. The two Hijazis read it with the short vowel meaning they would have resorted to it and done it. And they did not remain in it means strife or giving it. Except for a little while until the question and answer took place. It was said that they did not remain in the city after the apostasy was complete except for a little while.
33:15: 15 - And they had already made a covenant with God not to turn their backs. That is, Banu Haritha made a covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud when they failed, then they repented that they would not return to the like of it. And the covenant with God will be questioned about regarding fulfilling it, and one will be rewarded for it.
33:16: 16 - Say, 'Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing.' For every person must die a natural death, or be killed at a specific time, which has been decreed and recorded by the pen. And then you will not enjoy yourself except for a little. That is, if, for example, flight benefits you, then you are prevented by delay, then that enjoyment will only be a little enjoyment, or for a short time.
33:17: 17 - "Say: Who is it that can protect you from God if He intends to do you harm or intends to show you mercy?" That is, or afflict you with harm if He intends to show you mercy. So He shortened the speech as in His saying: Armed with a sword and a spear Or the second is based on the first, because infallibility has a meaning of prevention. And they will not find for themselves besides God a protector who will benefit them. And no helper who will ward off harm from them.
33:18: 18 - God knows those among you who hold back those who discourage people from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and they are the hypocrites. And those who say to their brothers from the inhabitants of Madinah, Come to us bring yourselves closer to us. Its origin is mentioned in (Al-An'am). And they do not come to battle except a little except for a little coming or time or battle, then they excuse themselves and hold back as much as they can, or they go out with the believers but they do not fight except a little like His statement They did not fight except a little and it was said that it is from the completion of their speech and its meaning is that the companions of Muhammad do not come to the war of the parties and they do not resist them except a little.
33:19: 19 - Stingy upon you are stingy with you in helping or spending in the way of God or victory or booty, the plural of stingy and it is accusative as a state of the subject of they come or the handicapped or as a blame. So when fear comes, you will see them looking at you with their eyes rolling in their pupils. Like one who faints like the look of the fainted or like the rolling of his eyes, or resembling him or resembling his eye. From death from dealing with the throes of death out of fear and seeking refuge with you. So when the fear is gone and the booty is obtained. They will smite you they will strike you. With sharp tongues sharp, seeking booty, and smiting is spreading out forcefully with the hand or tongue. Stingy upon good is accusative as a state or a blame, and this is supported by the reading of the nominative and not by repetition because each of them is restricted from one aspect. Those did not believe out of sincerity. So God rendered their deeds worthless, so He revealed their invalidity, since their deeds were not proven to be invalid, or He rendered their pretense and hypocrisy null and void. And that rendering worthless was easy for God, easy because the will was attached to Him and there was nothing preventing Him from it.
33:20: 20 - They think that the confederates have not gone away. That is, these people, out of cowardice, think that the confederates were not defeated, but they were defeated, so they fled into the city. And if the confederates come again, they wish that they were desert dwellers among the bedouins. They ask, everyone coming from the direction of the city, about your report, about what happened to you. And if they had been among you, this time and had not returned to the city and there had been fighting. They would not have fought except a little, out of hypocrisy and fear of reproach.
33:21: 21 - There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern to follow. A good quality that deserves to be emulated, such as steadfastness in war and enduring hardships. Or he is in himself a role model to follow, such as when you say, In an egg there are twenty iron minas, meaning it is in itself this amount of iron. Asim read it with a damma over the hamza, which is a dialect for it. For whoever hopes for God and the Last Day, meaning the reward of God or meeting Him and the bliss of the Hereafter, or the days of God and the Last Day in particular. It was said that it is like saying, I hope for Zayd and his bounty, because the Last Day is included in it according to the ruling, and hope may include hope or fear, and for whoever is a connection to a good deed or an attribute of it. It was said that it is a substitute for for you, and most of the scholars agree that the pronoun for the addressee cannot be substituted. And remember God often, and frequent remembrance is linked to hope, which leads to constant obedience, because the one who follows the Messenger is the one who is like that.
33:22: 22 - And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, 'This is what God and His Messenger promised us.' In His Most High's saying: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? The verse, and His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, The matter will become difficult when the confederates gather against you, and the [best] outcome will be for you against them. And His saying, peace and blessings be upon him, They will march toward you after nine or ten. Hamzah and Abu Bakr read with a kasrah on the ra' and a fathah on the hamzah. And God and His Messenger spoke the truth. The truth of the report of God and His Messenger became apparent, or they were truthful in victory and reward, just as they were truthful in the trial. The use of the name is for glorification. And it did not increase them in it is a pronoun when they saw, or the matter or the trial. except faith in God and His promises. And submission to His commands and decrees.
33:23: 23 - Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God of steadfastness with the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and fighting to raise the religion. Whoever believes in me when he speaks the truth to you, for if a covenantor fulfills his covenant, then he has fulfilled it. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow his vow to fight until he was martyred, such as Hamza, Mus'ab ibn 'Umair, and Anas ibn al-Nadr. A vow is a vow, and it is used metaphorically for death because it is like a vow binding on the neck of every animal. And among them is he who awaits martyrdom, such as 'Uthman and Talha, may God be pleased with them. And they did not change the covenant nor alter it. Alteration is any alteration. It was narrated that Talha remained steadfast with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud until his hand was injured, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Talha has fulfilled his vow and in it is an allusion to the people of hypocrisy and sickness of the heart by changing, and his saying:
33:24: 24 - That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites, if He wills, or accept their repentance. This is an explanation of the explicit and implied meanings. It is as if the hypocrites intended a bad outcome by changing the verse, just as the sincere intended a good outcome by remaining steadfast and faithful. Accepting their repentance is conditional upon their repentance, or what is meant by it is success in repentance. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful to whoever repents.
33:25: 25 - And God repelled those who disbelieved meaning the parties. In their fury in a rage. They did not attain any good except for being victorious, and these are two states that overlap or alternate. And God sufficed the believers in fighting with the wind and the angels. And God is Powerful over bringing about what He wills. Mighty over all things.
33:26: 26 - And He sent down those who supported them supported the confederates. of the People of the Scripture meaning Qurayza. from their fortresses from their strongholds, the plural of saysiyah is what one fortifies with, and that is why the horn of a bull or a gazelle and the fork of a rooster are called. And He cast terror into their hearts fear. And it is read with the dammah. A group you kill and a group you take captive. It was also read with a dammah on the seen. It was narrated that Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the morning of the night in which the Confederates were defeated and said: “Do you defend your nation while the angels have not laid down their weapons? God commands you to march to Banu Qurayzah, and I am heading towards them. So announce to the people that they should not pray the afternoon prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. Twenty-one or twenty-five besieged them until the siege was exhausting them. He said to them: “Will you accept my judgment?” They refused. He said: According to the judgment of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh. They refused. Sa`d ruled that their fighters should be killed and their women and children taken captive. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, exclaimed: You have ruled according to the judgment of God from above seven heavens. He killed six hundred or more of them and took seven hundred captive.
33:27: 27 - And He has given you as inheritance their land their farms. And their homes their fortresses. And their wealth their money, livestock and furniture. It was narrated that "the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) gave their property to the Muhajireen, and the Ansar spoke about it, so he said: You are in your homes." And "Umar may God be pleased with him said: Do you not give one-fifth as you gave one-fifth on the day of Badr? He said: No, I only gave this to me out of greed." And a land you have not trodden like Persia and Rome, and it was said Khaybar, and it was said a land that will be conquered until the Day of Resurrection. And God is over all things competent so He has power over that.
33:28: 28 - "O Prophet, tell your wives: If you should desire the life of this world" spaciousness and enjoyment therein, and its adornments its decorations, then come, I will provide for you give you enjoyment, and release you with gracious release a divorce without harm or innovation. It was narrated that they asked him for finery and increased maintenance, so this was revealed. He started with Aisha may God be pleased with her, so he gave her the choice, and she chose God and His Messenger. Then the rest of the women chose as she chose, so God thanked them for that, so He revealed: It is not lawful for you other women after that and linking the release to their desire for this world and making it a partner to their desire for the Messenger indicates that if the woman has the choice, she is not divorced, contrary to what Zayd, al-Hasan, Malik, and one of the two narrations from Ali said. This is supported by the statement of Aisha may God be pleased with her: "The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave us the choice, and we chose him." He did not consider it a divorce and preferred the enjoyment over the release caused by it due to generosity and good character. It was said that because the separation was by their will, like the choice of the woman who had free will herself, then it is a revocable divorce according to us and an irrevocable divorce according to the Hanafis. There was disagreement about its obligation for the one who has been consummated with her and there is nothing in it that indicates it. It was read (I will enjoy you and release you) in the nominative case as a new sentence.
33:29: 29 - And if you desire God and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, then indeed, God has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward. He despises the world and its adornments in comparison to it, and whom is for clarification, because they were all good-doers.
33:30: 30 - O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits an immorality a major obvious apparent ugliness according to the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr and the rest with a kasra on the yaa. The punishment will be doubled for her double the punishment of others, meaning double, because the sin on their part is uglier, as the increase in its ugliness follows the increase in the favor and blessing of the sinner. Therefore the punishment of a free man was made double the punishment of a slave, and the prophets were reprimanded in a way that others were not reprimanded. The two Basrans read yud'if in the passive voice, raising al-'adhaab, and Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read nud'if with a noon and in the active voice, and placing al-'adhaab in the accusative case. And that was easy for God does not prevent Him from doubling the punishment because they were the wives of the Prophet, and how is that its cause.
33:31: 31 - And whoever among you is obedient and who consistently obeys. To God and His Messenger Perhaps the mention of God is for the sake of glorification or because of His saying: And does righteousness - We will give her her reward twice once for her obedience and once for their seeking the pleasure of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) through contentment and good treatment. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read (and does righteousness) with a ya' based on the wording (from and gives it) as it contains the pronoun of God's name. And We have prepared for her a noble provision in Paradise in addition to her reward.
33:32: 32 - O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women. The root of ahad is wahd meaning one. Then it was placed in the general negation, including masculine and feminine, singular and plural, and the meaning is you are not like any other group of women in virtue. If you fear God means disobeying the command of God and the pleasure of His Messenger. Do not speak in a submissive tone means do not speak in a submissive and gentle tone like the speech of nurses. Let he in whose heart is a disease covet means immorality. It was read in the jussive mood, in apposition to the place of the verb of prohibition, as he is sick of heart and unable to covet, following their prohibition against speaking in a submissive tone. And speak in an appropriate manner means good and free from suspicion.
33:33: 33 - And abide in your houses from waqara yaqraan or from qara yaqraan. The first of the two ra's of iqran was deleted and its kasra was transferred to the qaf, so the hamzat al-wasl was dispensed with. This is supported by the reading of Nafi' and Asim with the fatha from qararat iqraan, which is a dialect in it. It is possible that it is from qar yaqar if it gathers. And do not display yourselves and do not strut in your walk. The display of the first ignorance is like the display of women in the days of ancient ignorance. It was said that it was between Adam and Noah, or it was said that it was the time when Abraham, peace be upon him, was born. Women would wear a pearl coat of mail and walk in the middle of the road, exposing themselves to men. The other ignorance was between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them. It was said that the first ignorance was the ignorance of disbelief before Islam, and the other ignorance was the ignorance of immorality in Islam. This is supported by the statement of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to Abu Darda’, may God be pleased with him, There is ignorance in you. He said, Islamic ignorance of disbelief or Islam? He said, Rather, it is ignorance of disbelief. “And establish prayer and give zakah and obey God and His Messenger” in all that He has commanded you to do and forbidden you to do. God only desires to remove from you the uncleanness the sin that defiles your honor. This is an explanation for the command and prohibition to them on the basis of resumption, and therefore the ruling was generalized. Ahl al-Bayt is in the accusative case as a call or a praise. And purify you from sins. Purification and the metaphor of impurity for disobedience and the nomination of purification to repel from it, and the Shiites’ specification of the people of the house to Fatima and Ali and their two sons, may God be pleased with them, because of what was narrated “that he, peace and blessings be upon him, went out one morning wearing a black hair cloak and sat down, and Fatima, may God be pleased with her, came and he put her in it, then Ali came and he put him in it, then Hassan and Hussein, may God be pleased with them, came and he put them in it, then he said: “God only desires to remove impurity from you, O people of the house.” The argument for this to support their infallibility and the fact that their consensus is a weak argument because specification to them does not fit what comes before and after the verse, and the hadith requires that they are from the people of the house, not that there is no one else.
33:34: 34 - And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom from the Book that combines the two matters and is a reminder of what God has bestowed upon them in terms of making them the people of the household of the Prophethood and the place of revelation and what they witnessed of the spaciousness of the revelation which necessitates the strength of faith and eagerness to obey, urging them to desist and adhere to what they are charged with. Indeed, God is Kind and Aware He knows and manages what is best in the religion and for this reason He chose you and admonished you, or He knows who is fit for His prophethood and who is fit to be the people of His household.
33:35: 35 - The Muslim men and Muslim women who have entered into Islam and are submissive to the rule of God. The believing men and believing women who believe in what must be believed. The obedient men and obedient women who are constant in obedience. The truthful men and truthful women in word and deed. The patient men and patient women in acts of obedience and avoiding sins. The humble men and humble women who are humble before God in their hearts and limbs. The charitable men and charitable women from what is required of their wealth. The fasting men and fasting women the obligatory fast. The men who guard their private parts and the women who guard from what is forbidden. The men who remember God often and the women who remember with their hearts and tongues - God has prepared for them forgiveness for the minor sins they have committed because they are expiations. And a great reward for their obedience. The verse is a promise to them and their likes for their obedience and for adopting these qualities. It was narrated that the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O Messenger of God, God mentioned men in the Quran with goodness, so there is no good in us to be mentioned with. So this was revealed. It was also said that when what was revealed about them was revealed, he said: The Muslim women, so nothing was revealed about us. So this was revealed: “And the females were joined to the males because of the difference in the sexes, which is necessary. And the two spouses were joined to the two spouses because of the difference in the two descriptions, so it is not necessary. That is why it was left out in His statement: “Muslim, believing women.” Its benefit is to indicate that the preparation of those prepared for it combines these qualities.
33:36: 36 - And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman what is correct for him. When God and His Messenger have decided a matter meaning the Messenger of God has decided. God was mentioned to magnify His matter and to indicate that His decision is God's decision, because it was revealed regarding Zaynab bint Jahsh, the daughter of his paternal aunt Umaimah bint Abdul Muttalib. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) proposed to her for Zayd ibn Haritha, but she and her brother Abdullah refused. It was also said that Umm Kulthum bint Uqbah offered herself to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he married her to Zayd. That they should have the option of their decision means that they should choose something in their decision. Rather, they should make their choice subject to the choice of God and His Messenger. The option is what is chosen. The first pronoun is plural for the generality of both male and female believers, as they are in the context of negation. The second is plural for emphasis. The Kufians and Hisham read (be) with a ya. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error between deviation from the right path.
33:37: 37 - "And when you said to him whom God had bestowed favor" by guiding him to Islam and your guiding him to free him and to single him out. "And you had bestowed favor" with what God had granted you, and he is Zayd ibn Haritha. "Keep your wife for yourself" Zaynab. That is because the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) saw her after he had married her to him, and she fell into his heart, so he said, "Glory be to God, the Changer of hearts." And Zaynab heard the glorification of God and mentioned it to Zayd, so he became aware of that and felt aversion to her company, so he came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: I want to leave my companion. He said: What is it that arouses your curiosity about her? He said: No, by God, I have only seen good in her, but because of her honor she acts haughtily toward me. So the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: "Keep your wife for yourself. And fear God" in her matter, so do not divorce her to cause harm and using her arrogance as an excuse. "And conceal within yourself that which God is to bring to light", which is marrying her if he divorces her or intends to divorce her. "And you fear people" that they might reproach you with it. "But God has more right that you should fear Him" if there is something feared in Him. The "and" indicates the state, and the reproach is not for concealing it alone, for that is good, but rather for concealing it for fear of people's gossip and revealing what contradicts what one conceals. In such cases, it is better for one to remain silent or entrust the matter to his Lord. "So when Zaid had no longer any need for her" a need such that he grew tired of her and had no longer any need for her, so he divorced her and her waiting period had ended. "We married her to you. It was said that the fulfillment of his need is a euphemism for divorce, like I have no need of you. It was also read I married her to you," meaning that he ordered her to be married to him or that he made her his wife without an intermediary contract. This is supported by the fact that she used to say to the other wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "God has taken care of my marriage, and your guardians will marry you." It was also said that Zaid was the ambassador in proposing marriage to her, and that was a great test and clear evidence of the strength of his faith. So that there will be no blame upon the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them. This is a reason for marriage, and it is evidence that his ruling and the ruling of the female slave are the same, except for what is specified by the evidence. And the command of God His command that He wants will be carried out inevitably formed, just as the marriage of Mary was.
33:38: 38 - There is no blame upon the Prophet for what God has ordained for him. He has ordained for him a portion and a decree, as they say, He has ordained for him in the register. This is like the provisions of the army for their provisions. The way of God He has established that as a way. In those who passed on before of the prophets, which is to negate any blame upon them for what He has permitted them. And the command of God is a decree decreed. A decree that has been decreed and a final judgment.
33:39: 39 - Those who convey the messages of God is an attribute of those who have been alone, or praise is given to them in the accusative or nominative case. It was read as the message of God. “And they fear Him and do not fear anyone except God.” An allusion after an explicit statement. And sufficient is God as Accountant Sufficient for fears or an Accountant, so one should only fear Him.
33:40: 40 - Muhammad is not the father of any of your men is true, so the same is true between him and his son due to the sanctity of marriage and other ties of kinship. Its generality is not invalidated by his being the father of At-Tahir, Al-Qasim and Ibrahim because they did not reach the age of men, and if they had, they would have been his men, not their men. But the Messenger of God - and every Messenger is the father of his nation, not absolutely, but rather because he is compassionate and sincere towards them, and it is obligatory upon them to respect and obey him, and Zayd is among them, with no birth between him and him. The Messenger of God is read in the nominative case as the predicate of a deleted subject, but with emphasis to delete the predicate, meaning But the Messenger of God is from those whom you know did not have a living male child. And the Seal of the Prophets and the last of them who sealed them or who were sealed with him according to the reading of Asim with the fat-ha, and if he had a grown son it would have been appropriate for his position to be a prophet as "the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said about Abraham when he died: If he had lived he would have been a prophet", and this does not detract from the descent of Jesus after him because if he descended he would have followed his religion, even though what is meant by it is that he is the last of those who were prophesied. And God is Knowing of all things so He knows who is appropriate for the prophethood to be sealed with him and how his affair should be.
33:41: 41 - O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance. It is most of the time and includes all types with what is due to it of sanctification, praise, glorification, and exaltation.
33:42: 42 - And glorify Him in the morning and the evening or the day and its end in particular, and mentioning them specifically for this purpose is to indicate their superiority over all other times because they are witnessed like the individuals of glorification from the group of remembrances because it is the mainstay of them. It was said that the two actions are directed to them. It was also said that what is meant by glorification is prayer.
33:43: 43 - It is He who sends blessings upon you with mercy. And His angels with seeking forgiveness for you and showing concern for what is best for you. What is meant by salat is the common denominator, which is concern for the betterment of your affairs and the appearance of your honor. It is borrowed from salat. It was said that mercy and spiritual turning are taken from prayer, which includes the formal turning which is bowing and prostrating. The angels' seeking forgiveness and supplication for the believers is mercy upon him, especially since he is the reason for mercy, as their supplications are answered. That He may bring you out from darknesses into the light from the darkness of disbelief and disobedience to the light of faith and obedience. And He is ever Merciful to the believers as He was concerned for the betterment of their affairs and the elegance of their status, and He used for that His closest angels.
33:44: 44 - Their greeting is from adding the verbal noun to the object or they greet. The day they meet Him is the day they meet Him upon death or upon emerging from the graves, or upon entering Paradise. "Peace" is report of safety from every harm and calamity. And He has prepared for them a noble reward is Paradise, and perhaps the difference in the system is to preserve the pauses and exaggerate what is more important.
33:45: 45 - O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness over those to whom you were sent, regarding their belief and denial, their salvation and their misguidance, and this is a predetermined state. And as a bringer of good tidings and a warner.
33:46: 46 - And calling to God to acknowledge Him, His Oneness, and the attributes that must be believed in. By His permission by making them easy for him. He made it general for him in that it is one of its causes, and he restricted the call to it, indicating that it is a difficult matter that cannot be achieved except with the help of His Holiness. And an illuminating lamp by which one may be enlightened from the darkness of ignorance, and from whose light one may draw the lights of insight.
33:47: 47 - And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from God great bounty over all other nations or over the reward for their deeds. Perhaps it is connected to something omitted, such as observe the conditions of your nation.
33:48: 48 - And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites is an incitement to his disobedience to them. And leave their harm is their harming you and do not celebrate it, or your harming them as a recompense or punishment for their disbelief, and for this reason it was said that it was abrogated. And put your trust in God for He will suffice you against them. And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs to whom the matter is entrusted in all circumstances, and perhaps when He, glory be to Him, described Him with five attributes, He contrasted each one with an address that suited it, so He omitted the opposite of the witness, which is the command to observe, because what follows it is like a detail for it, and He contrasted the bearer of good tidings with the command and the illuminating lamp with being satisfied with it, for whoever God illuminates as a proof for all of His creation, it is fitting that he be satisfied with him over others.
33:49: 49 - O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them you have intercourse with them, and Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with an alif and a damma on the ta'. Then you have no waiting period over them days during which they wait by themselves. You count it you complete its number from I counted the dirhams so count it like you say: I took it, so I took it, or you count it. And the chain of transmission to men indicates that the waiting period is the right of husbands, as I have indicated, so what is wrong with you? And from Ibn Kathir (you observe waiting period) in a lightened form by replacing one of the two dals with a ya’ or that it is from ‘iddah meaning you observe waiting period in it, and its apparent meaning requires that waiting period is not obligatory merely by seclusion and the specification of believing women and the ruling is general to indicate that it is the nature of the believer not to marry except a believing woman, giving his sperm a choice, and the benefit then is to remove what might be imagined as delaying divorce until consummation is possible, as it affects lineage and affects the waiting period. Then provide for them means if it is not obligatory for her, then what is obligatory for the one for whom it is obligatory is half of what is obligatory without the enjoyment, and it is permissible to interpret the enjoyment as what includes them both, or to command what is common between obligation and recommendation, as enjoyment is a Sunnah for the one for whom it is obligatory. And release them: Take them out of your homes, as you do not have a waiting period for them. A gracious release without causing harm or preventing a right, and it is not permissible to interpret it as a Sunnah divorce because it is conditional upon divorce and the pronoun refers to those who have not been consummated with.
33:50: 50 - O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their dowries their dowries because the dowry is a reward for sexual intercourse, and restricting the permissibility for him by giving her immediately is not because the permissibility depends on it, but rather to give him preference for what is better, like restricting the permissibility of the female slave to her being a cause in His statement: And what your right hand possesses of what God has bestowed upon you because the beginning of the matter of the purchased woman and what happened to her is not established, and restricting the female relatives to her being emigrants with him in His statement: And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and restricting the permissibility with that is possible in his right specifically and it is supported by the statement of Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to me and I apologized to him and he excused me, then God revealed this verse and I was not permissible for him because I did not emigrate with him, I was among those who were freed. And a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet is in the accusative case because of a verb explained by what precedes it or in apposition to what preceded it. It is not refuted by the restriction that an which is for the future tense, because the meaning is permissibility and informing about the permissibility, i.e., We have informed you of the permissibility of a believing woman who offers herself to you and does not ask for a dowry if it is agreed upon. That is why he denied it. There is disagreement about the agreement of that, and the one who says it mentioned four: Maymuna bint al-Harith, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah al-Ansariyyah, Umm Sharbak bint Jabir, and Khawlah bint Hakim. An is read with the fat-ha, meaning because she offered herself or the duration of that she offered herself, like saying: Sit as long as Zayd is sitting. If the Prophet wanted to marry her is a condition for the first condition for the permissibility to be fulfilled. If she gives herself to him, this does not make her permissible for him unless he wants to marry her. It is considered acceptance. The transition from addressing someone in the third person to addressing them in the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is repeated, then referring back to him in his saying: Purely for you, not for the believers, indicating that it is something that was singled out for him due to the honor of his prophethood and confirming that he deserved honor because of it. Our companions used it as evidence that marriage is not concluded by the wording of a gift, because the wording is subordinate to the meaning, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was singled out by the meaning, so it is singled out by the wording. Marriage is the request for marriage and the desire for it. Purely is a confirmed verbal noun, meaning that her permissibility was pure, or the permissibility of what We have made permissible for you according to the mentioned restrictions, they were pure for you. It is a state of the pronoun in she gave or an attribute of an omitted verbal noun, meaning a pure gift. We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives of the conditions of the contract, the obligation of dividing the dowry and intercourse where it is not named. And what their right hands possess is an expansion of the command in it, how should it be imposed on them, and the sentence is an interjection between His saying: so that there will be no difficulty for you and its object, which is pure to indicate that the difference between it and the believers in something like that is not merely to intend to expand upon it, but rather meanings that necessitate expansion upon it and restriction upon them at times and vice versa. And God is Forgiving for what is difficult to guard against. Merciful by expanding in places of difficulty.
33:51: 51 - "You may postpone whomever you wish of them" means delaying her and not sleeping with her. "And you may take to yourself whomever you wish" means taking to yourself whomever you wish and sleeping with her, or divorcing whomever you wish and keeping whomever you wish. Nafi', Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Hafs read "tarja" with a ya' and the meaning is the same. "And whoever you seek" means seeking. "From whom you have isolated" means divorcing with revocation. "There is no blame upon you" in any of that. "That is more likely that their eyes will be comforted and they will not grieve and will be satisfied with what You have given them all." This entrustment to Your will is closer to the comfort of their eyes, the reduction of their grief, and their satisfaction all together, because the judgment of all of them is the same in it. Then, if You treat them equally, they will find that to be a favor from You, and if You give preference to some of them, they will know that it is the judgment of God, the Most High, and their souls will be reassured by it. It was read (taqrur) with a damma on the ta’ and (‘ayinunna) in the accusative and (taqrur) in the passive voice and (kulhanna) to emphasize the noon of yurdain. It was read in the accusative to emphasize them. And God knows what is in your hearts, so strive to do good to Him. And God is Knowing of what is in the hearts. Forbearing He does not hasten to punish, so He is worthy of being feared.
33:52: 52 - "It is not lawful for you to marry other women" with a ya' because the feminine of the plural is not real, and the two Basrans read it with a ta'. "From after" from after nine, which in his case is like four in our case, or from after today, so that if one of them dies, it is not lawful for him to marry another. "Nor that you exchange them for other wives so that you divorce one and marry another in her place, and from" is added to emphasize the comprehensiveness. "And if their beauty pleases you the beauty of the exchanged wives, and it is a state of the subject of exchanged and not its object, which is from wives" because it is deeply indefinite, and its estimation is assuming you like them. There is disagreement as to whether the verse is definitive or abrogated by His statement: "You may put off whomever you wish of them and take to yourself whomever you wish" according to the second meaning, because even if it is a reading, it precedes it in revelation. It was said that the meaning is, it is not lawful for you to marry other women after the four types that He explicitly stated are lawful for you, nor that you exchange them for wives from other types. "Except what your right hand possesses" is an exception to women because it includes both wives and female slaves. It was also said that it is disjunctive. "And God is ever, over all things, a Watcher" so guard your affairs and do not transgress what He has set for you.
33:53: 53 - O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when permission is given to you except at the time when permission is given to you or unless you are given permission. To food is connected to is given permission because it includes the meaning of being invited to indicate that it is not appropriate to enter the food without being invited even if permission is given, as is indicated by his saying: not waiting for its time not waiting for its time, or its attainment as a state of the subject of do not enter or the noun in for you. It was read in the genitive case as an attribute of food, so it is governed by someone other than the one it belongs to without making the pronoun explicit, and this is not permissible according to the Basrans. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i made anah inclined because it is a source of the word ana meaning that the food is attained. But when you are invited, then enter, and when you have eaten, disperse disperse and do not stay. This is also addressed to people who used to wait for the food of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so they would enter and sit waiting for it to arrive. This is specific to them and their likes, otherwise it would not have been permissible for anyone to enter their homes with permission for anything other than food, nor would they remain after eating for them. nor seeking entertainment for conversation for the conversation of some of you with others, or for the conversation of the people of the house by listening to it, in apposition to watching or implied by a verb, meaning: do not enter or do not remain seeking entertainment. That staying used to annoy the Prophet because the house was cramped for him and his family and distracted him with things that did not concern him. so he would feel shy of you from expelling you, as He said: And God is not shy of the truth meaning that expelling you is a right, so shame should not be neglected, just as God did not leave it as shame left, so He ordered you to leave. The reading (la yastahy) was read by deleting the first ya and placing its vowel on the ha. And if you ask them for something something that may be of benefit. Ask them for something. From behind a partition a screen. It was narrated that “Umar may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, both the righteous and the wicked may enter upon you, so why don’t you order the Mothers of the Believers to wear a veil?” So this was revealed. It was also said that “he (peace and blessings be upon him) was eating food with some of his companions, and a man’s hand touched Aisha may God be pleased with her, so the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) disliked that, so this was revealed: “That is purer for your hearts and their hearts” from satanic, self-indulgent thoughts. And it is not for you and it is not right for you. To harm the Messenger of God to do what he dislikes. Nor to marry his wives after him, ever after his death or separation. He specifically mentioned the one with whom he had not consummated the marriage. It was narrated that Ash’ath ibn Qays married the woman who was seeking refuge during the days of Umar may God be pleased with him and he intended to stone her, but he was informed that he (peace and blessings be upon him) had divorced her before touching her, so he left her without objecting. That means harming him and marrying his women. was in the sight of God a great sin and it contains God’s glorification of His Messenger and the obligation of his sanctity, alive and dead. Therefore, He exaggerated the threat against him and said:
33:54: 54 - If you disclose anything such as their marriage on your tongues, or conceal it in your hearts, then indeed, God is ever Knowing of all things, so He knows that and will punish you for it. In this generalization, along with the proof of the intended meaning, there is further exaggeration and exaggeration in the threat.
33:55: 55 - "There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons." An exception for those from whom veiling is not obligatory. It was narrated that when the verse of veiling was revealed, fathers, sons, and relatives said: O Messenger of God, can we also speak to them from behind a screen? So it was revealed. The paternal uncle and maternal uncle were not mentioned because they are in the same position as parents. That is why the paternal uncle was called a father in His statement: "And the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac." Or because he disliked not veiling himself from them for fear that they would be described to their sons. "Nor their women" meaning the believing women. "Nor those their right hands possess" of male and female slaves. It was said specifically female slaves, and this was mentioned in Surat An-Nur. "And fear God" in what you have been commanded to do. "Indeed, God is ever, over all things, Witness" nothing is hidden from Him.
33:56: 56 - "Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet." They are concerned with showing his honor and magnifying his status. "O you who have believed, send blessings upon him. You too should be concerned with that, for you are more deserving of that, and say, O God, send blessings upon Muhammad. And greet him with peace. And say, Peace be upon you, O Prophet." It was said that they obeyed his commands, and the verse indicates the obligation of sending blessings and peace upon him in general. It was said that sending blessings is obligatory whenever he is mentioned, "because of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, 'May the nose of a man in whose presence I am mentioned be rubbed in the dust, and he does not send blessings upon me.' And his saying, Whoever is mentioned in whose presence I am mentioned and does not send blessings upon me, then he enters the Fire, so may God cast him far away." Sending blessings upon others is permissible as a consequence. It is disliked to send blessings on his own because in custom it is a symbol of mentioning the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and for this reason it is disliked to say, "Muhammad, the Mighty and Sublime," even if he is honored and venerated.
33:57: 57 - Indeed, those who harm God and His Messenger commit what they hate of disbelief and sins, or they harm the Messenger of God by breaking his front teeth, calling him a mad poet, and the like, and mentioning God to glorify Him. Whoever permits the use of the word in two meanings interpreted it in both meanings based on the two objects. God has cursed them He has distanced them from His mercy. In this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment that will humiliate them and cause them pain.
33:58: 58 - And those who harm believing men and believing women for no reason without any crime for which they deserved to be harmed. They have certainly borne upon themselves a slander and a manifest sin apparently. It was said that it was revealed about hypocrites who were harming Ali may God be pleased with him, and it was said about the people of slander, and it was said about adulterers who were following women against their will.
33:59: 59 - O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. They should cover their faces and bodies with their coverings when they go out for a need. Min is for partiality, as a woman may let down some of her outer garment and cover herself with the rest. That is more suitable that they will be known so that they will be distinguished from female slaves and singing girls. And they will not be harmed so that the people of doubt will not harm them by approaching them. And God is Forgiving of what has passed. Merciful to His servants, as He takes their interests into consideration, even the small ones.
33:60: 60 - If the hypocrites do not desist from their hypocrisy. And those in whose hearts is disease weakness of faith and lack of steadfastness in it, or immorality due to their wavering in religion or their immorality. And the slanderers in the city spread bad report about the Muslim raids and the like of their slander, and its origin is the movement from the shaking which means earthquake, and false report is called by it because it is unstable and unsteady. We will surely tempt you with them We will order you to fight them and expel them, or what will force them to request expulsion. Then they will not live near you is in apposition to We will surely tempt you, and then is to indicate that expulsion and separation from the Prophet's neighborhood is the greatest thing that will befall them. Therein in the city. Except for a little a time or a short period of time.
33:61: 61 - Cursed is in the accusative case as an insult or a condition, and the exception also includes it. A]: They do not live near you except as cursed. It is not permissible to use the accusative case for his statement: Wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed in a horrific manner because what comes after the conditional word does not affect what comes before it.
33:62: 62 - The way of God with those who passed on before is a confirmed source, meaning that God has prescribed that with the past nations, which is that those who were hypocrites would be killed, the prophets and sought to weaken them by spreading rumors and the like wherever they are found. "And you will not find any change in the way of God" because He does not change it and no one is able to change it.
33:63: 63 - "People ask you about the Hour" about the time of its occurrence, mockingly, stubbornly, or as a test. "Say, 'Its knowledge is only with God.'" No angel or prophet has been informed of it. "And what makes you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. Something near, or The Hour will be near." The accusative is a circumstantial adverbial. It is permissible for it to be a masculine form because "the Hour has the meaning of the day," and it contains a threat to those who are impatient and a silencing of those who are stubborn.
33:64: 64 - Indeed, God has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Blaze. A very blazing fire.
33:65: 65 - They will abide therein forever, finding neither a protector nor a helper to protect them. Nor a helper to ward off the punishment from them.
33:66: 66 - On the Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire. It will be turned from one side to another like meat being roasted in fire, or from one state to another. Turn over is read as turn over and turn over is related to the circumstance. They will say, ‘Oh, if only we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger’ so that we would not be afflicted with this punishment.
33:67: 67 - And they said, 'Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries' meaning their leaders who taught them disbelief. Ibn Amir and Yaqub read our masters in the plural to indicate large numbers. And they led us astray from the path with what they made attractive to us.
33:68: 68 - Our Lord, give them double the punishment double what You have given us because they have gone astray and led others astray. And curse them with a great curse great in number. Asim read it with the letter ba’, meaning a curse that is the most severe and greatest of curses.
33:69: 69 - O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but God cleared him of what they said. So He declared his innocence from what they said, meaning its meaning and content. This was because Korah incited a woman to accuse him of adultery, but God protected him, as mentioned in Al-Qasas. Or people accused him of killing Aaron when he went out with him to the mountain, and he died there. The angels carried him and passed by him until they saw that he had not been killed. It was also said that God revived him, so he informed them of his innocence. Or they accused him of a defect in his body, such as leprosy or pyrexia, due to his extreme modesty, so God informed them that he was innocent of it. And he was held in high esteem by God, of closeness and esteem. It was also read, And the servant of God was held in high esteem.
33:70: 70 - O you who have believed, fear God in committing what He hates, let alone what harms His Messenger. And speak words of appropriate justice intending the truth from sadd meaning to block, and what is meant is to forbid its opposite, like the hadith of Zaynab, without intending it.
33:71: 71 - He will make your deeds right for you He will guide you to do good deeds, or He will make them right by accepting them and rewarding them. And He will forgive you your sins and make them expiated by your uprightness in word and deed. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger in the commands and prohibitions, has certainly achieved a great victory He will live in this world with praise and in the Hereafter with happiness.
33:72: 72 - Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to undertake it and feared it; but man undertook it. This is a confirmation of the previous promise to magnify obedience. It is called a Trust because it is obligatory to fulfill. The meaning is that it is so great that if it were offered to these great bodies that had feeling and perception, they would have declined to undertake it and feared it, and man undertook it despite the weakness of his nature and the flimsiness of his strength. There is no doubt that the one who cares for it and fulfills its rights will win the best of both worlds. Indeed, he was unjust, since he did not fulfill it and did not consider its rights. Ignorant, of the nature of its consequences. This is a description of the genus in consideration of the majority. It was said that what is meant by trust is the obedience that includes the natural and the voluntary, and by its presentation it is called upon which includes the request for an action from the chosen one and the will for it to be issued by someone other than him, and by its bearing it is betrayal and abstention from performing it, and from this is their saying, The one who dreams of the trust and bears it for the one who does not perform it is absolved of responsibility, so refusing it is doing what can be done from him, and injustice and ignorance are betrayal and negligence. It was said that when He, the Most High, created these bodies, He created in them understanding and said to them: I have imposed a duty and created Paradise for those who obey Me in it, and Hell for those who disobey Me. They said: “We are determined to do what You created us. We do not bear a duty, nor do we seek a garment or a punishment.” When He created Adam, He offered him something like that, so he took it on. He was unjust to himself by taking on what was difficult for him, ignorant of the dire consequences. Perhaps what is meant by trust is the mind or the obligation, and by offering it to them, it is considered in relation to their readiness, and by their refusal, the natural refusal which is the lack of suitability and readiness, and by man taking on his ability and readiness for it, and his being unjust and ignorant because of what has overcome him of the angry and lustful power. Based on this, it is appropriate for it to be a reason for bearing it, because one of the benefits of the mind is that it dominates the two powers, protecting them from transgression and exceeding the limit, and most of the purpose of the obligation is to adjust them and break their wall.
33:73: 73 - That God may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women, and that God may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women. This is an explanation of the meaning of the sentence, as it is the result of a punishment, like a disciplinary action. The mention of repentance in the promise is an indication that they, being unjust and ignorant in their nature, will not be free from errors. And God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful, as He accepted their errors and rewarded victory for their obedience. "He, peace and blessings be upon him, said, 'Whoever recites Surat Al-Ahzab and teaches it to his family or those his right hand possesses, will be given safety from the punishment of the grave.'"
34:1: 1- Praise be to God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth in creation and blessings. To Him belongs praise in this world for the perfection of His power and the completion of His blessings. To Him belongs praise in the Hereafter because whatever is in the Hereafter is also like that. This is not an example of linking a restricted statement to an absolute statement, for the description that indicates that He is the Bestower of worldly blessings restricts praise to them, and the connection is presented for specificity, for worldly blessings may be through someone who deserves praise for them, but this is not the case with blessings in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise who has perfected the affairs of both abodes. The All-Aware of the inner workings of things.
34:2: 2- He knows what penetrates the earth such as rain that penetrates in one place and springs up in another, and such as treasures, buried goods, and the dead. And what comes forth from it such as animals, plants, metals, and spring water. And what descends from the sky such as angels, books, decrees, provisions, dew, and thunderbolts. And what ascends therein such as angels, the deeds of His servants, vapors, and fumes. And He is the Most Merciful, the Forgiving of those who are excessive in thanking Him for His blessings despite their abundance, or in the Hereafter with His wealth of previous blessings that are too numerous to count.
34:3: 3- And those who disbelieve say, ‘The Hour will not come to us.’ Denying its coming or impatiently delaying it, mocking the promise of it. Say, ‘Yes.’ A response to their words and confirmation of what they denied. And by my Lord, the Knower of the Unseen will surely come to you. A repetition of its affirmation, confirmed by the oath, establishing the description of the thing sworn by with attributes that establish its possibility and negate its improbability, as mentioned more than once. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read ‘Allam Al-Ghaib’ for emphasis, and Nafi’, Ibn ‘Umar, and Ruways read ‘Allam Al-Ghaib’ in the nominative case as a deleted predicate or a subject whose predicate is: Not an atom’s weight in the heavens or on the earth escapes Him. Al-Kisa’i read (Nothing is absent) with a kasra. Nor anything smaller than that or larger, except that it is in a clear book is a sentence emphasizing the negation of celibacy, and raising them by beginning is supported by the reading with a fatha to negate the genus, and it is not permissible to connect the raised to mithqal and the open to atom because it is a fatha in the place of the genus due to the impossibility of inflection because the exception prevents it, unless the pronoun in about it is made for the unseen and the established in the tablet is made outside of it due to its clarity to those who look at it, so the meaning is that nothing is separated from the unseen except that it is written in the tablet.
34:4: 4- That He may reward those who have believed and done righteous deeds. This is the reason for His saying, It will come to you, and an explanation of what necessitates its coming. For those is forgiveness and noble provision, without any effort or burden.
34:5: 5- And those who strive against Our verses by invalidating and making people lose interest in them. Failing to do so racing to escape from Us. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read Failing to do so meaning discouraging those who wanted to believe. For those is a punishment of severe torment of severe torment. Painful painful. Ibn Kathir, Ya’qub, and Hafs recited it with the chain of transmission ending with the Prophet. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 23 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat Saba, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Ṣāfāt. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time.
