34:6: 6- And those who have been given knowledge will see and those with knowledge from the Companions and those who followed them from the Ummah, or from the Muslims of the People of the Book, that which has been revealed to you from your Lord the Qur'an. It is the truth and whoever raises the truth makes it the subject and the truth its predicate and the sentence is the second object of sees, and it is raised, resuming the evidence of those with knowledge against the ignorant who strive in the verses. And it was said that it is accusative and conjoined with that He may reward meaning that those with knowledge will know when the Hour comes that it is the truth clearly as they have learned it now as proof. And guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, which is monotheism and wearing the garment of piety.
34:7: 7- And those who disbelieved said, they said to one another, Shall we direct you to a man meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, who will inform you will tell you of the most amazing wonders. When you are torn apart, you will indeed be in a new creation you will be created anew after your bodies have been torn apart and scattered to the point of becoming dust. The adverbial phrase is brought forward to indicate distance and to exaggerate it, and its agent is omitted and indicated by what follows it, as what precedes it does not accompany it and what follows is an addition to it, or it is hidden between it and it by that and torn could be a place meaning if you are torn apart and the torrents carry you away in every direction and you are thrown away in every place. New has the meaning of an active participle from jadda like hadad from hadd, and it was said that it means a passive participle from jadda the weaver cuts the garment.
34:8: 8- Does he invent a lie against God, or is he mad? Madness that makes him think that and puts it on his tongue. He used as evidence that they made it a counterpart to slander, not believing in its truthfulness, on the basis that there is a middle ground between truth and falsehood, and it is every report that is not based on insight into the one being reported, and its weakness is clear because slander is more specific than falsehood. Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in torment and far astray. This is a response from God Almighty to their hesitation and confirmation for them of what is more terrible than the two categories, which is the astray far from the truth such that there is no hope of salvation from it and what it leads to in terms of torment. He made it a messenger for it to occur and preceded it in the wording to exaggerate their deserving of it, and distance is originally a description of the astray and describing the astray with it on the metaphorical attribution.
34:9: 9- Have they not seen what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them up or cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon them. A reminder of what they witness, which indicates the perfection of God's power and what is likely to be a displacement due to their impossibility of bringing them back to life, until they made it a slander, a mockery, and a threat to them. The meaning is that they are blind to what they see of the heaven and the earth that surrounds them, and they have not considered which is more powerful in creation, or the heaven. And If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them up or cause a fragment of the sky to fall upon them, due to their denial of the signs after the clear proofs had become clear. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read Yash'a and (Yakhsuf) and (Yaqtutu) with the letter Ya’ because of his saying: He fabricated a lie against God. And Al-Kisa’i Alone by assimilating the fa’ into the ba’ and Hafs (kasfan) with the fat-ha. Indeed in that is looking and contemplating them and what they indicate. A sign is an indication. For every servant who turns back returns to his Lord, for he often contemplates his situation.
34:10: 10- And We had certainly given David bounty from Us meaning over all the other prophets, which is what was mentioned later, or over all the people, which includes prophecy, the Book, the kingdom, and a beautiful voice. O mountains, echo with him echo with him in glorification or lamentation over sin, either by creating a sound like his voice in them, or by making him glorify when he contemplates what is in them, or go with him wherever he goes. Obtain is read from awb, meaning return in glorification whenever he returns to it. It is a substitute for bounty or We have given by implying Our saying or We said. "And the birds" is in apposition to the location of the mountains, and this is supported by the reading in the nominative case in apposition to its wording. Likening the accidental structural movement to the syntactic movement or to fadla, or an object with it for ubi and on this basis it is permissible for the nominative to be in apposition to its pronoun and the original was: And We had certainly given David bounty from Us, the return of the mountains and the birds, so he replaced this system with what he understood from grandeur and the indication of the greatness of his status and the majesty of his power, as he made the mountains and the birds like rational beings obedient to his command in the penetration of his will in them. And We made iron soft for him We made it in his hand like wax so that he could change it as he wished without heating or pounding with its softness or its strength.
34:11: 11- Whoever does We command him to do, so that is an explanatory or a source. "Sabaghat" are wide coats of mail, and it was read (Sabaghat) and he was the first to make them. "And measured in the narrative" and measured in its weaving so that its rings would fit, or the size of its nails so that they would not be thin so that they would be loose, nor thick so that they would be torn. It was reported that his coats of mail were not nailed, and this is supported by his statement: "And We softened the iron for him. And work righteousness" the pronoun in it refers to David and his family. "Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do" so I will reward you for it.
34:12: 12- And to Solomon We subjected the wind meaning, We subjected the wind to him. The wind is read in the nominative case, meaning, and to Solomon the wind was subjected. It is also read (the winds). Its morning journey is a month and its evening journey is a month its journey in the morning is a month’s journey, and in the evening likewise. It is read (its morning journey) (And its spirit). And We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him The molten copper We caused to flow for him from its mine, so a spring of water gushed forth from it, and that is why He called it a spring. And that was in Yemen. And of the jinn were those who worked before him is in apposition to the wind. “And of the jinn” is an introductory adverbial phrase, or the sentence of is a subject and predicate. By the permission of his Lord by His command. And whoever deviates from among them is also read as and whoever turns away from among them “from Our command” from what We commanded of obeying Solomon. Deviates is read from made him deviate. “We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze” is the punishment of the Hereafter.
34:13: 13- "They make for him whatever he wishes of sanctuaries" Fortified palaces and noble dwellings, so named because they are defended and fought over. "And statues" and pictures, which are statues of angels and prophets according to their custom of worship, so that people may see them and worship them, and the sanctity of pictures is a renewed law. It was narrated that they made for him two lions at the bottom of his throne and two eagles above it, so when he wanted to ascend, the two lions would spread their arms for him, and when he sat, the two eagles would shade him with their wings. "And bowls" and plates. "Like a reservoir Like large basins, plural of jabiya from jabiya", which is one of the most common descriptions like a beast. "And fixed pots" Fixed on the fire places and do not move from them due to their size. Work, O family of David, in gratitude, narrating what was said to them. And be grateful is in the accusative case as a reason, meaning: Work for Him and worship Him in gratitude, or the source because the work is for Him in gratitude, or the description is for Him, or the state, or the object. And few of My servants are grateful. He is the one who constantly expresses gratitude with his heart, tongue, and limbs most of the time, yet he does not fulfill its right, because his ability to be grateful is a blessing that calls for more gratitude, not an end to it. Therefore, it was said that the grateful is the one who considers his inability to be grateful.
34:14: 14- So when We decreed death for him meaning for Solomon. What indicated his death to them? What indicated the jinn and it was said his family. Except the creature of the earth meaning the termite, attributed to its action. It was read with a fat-ha on the ra', which is the effect of the wood being affected by its action. It is said: the termite struck the wood with a strike, so it struck the ground, like the sharp teeth ate a gnawing, so it ate a gnawing. Its staff eats His stick from Nasa'at al-Ba'eer if you expel the camel because it is used to expel it. It is also read with a fatha on the meem and a light hamza, by changing and deleting it in a way that is not standard, as the standard is to put it in between. Mansa'atu is on the pattern of Maifa'ah like Mayda'ah in Mayda'ah and Mansa'atu means the tip of his stick, borrowed from the Sitat al-Qaws the bow's end. There are two pronunciations for it, as in Qahha and Qahha. Nafi' and Abu Amr read Mansa'atu with an alif instead of the hamza, and Ibn Dhakwan with a silent hamza, and Hamza, when he stops, makes it in between. So when he fell, the jinn became clear The jinn knew after the matter was confused for them. That if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment That if they had known the unseen, as they claim, they would have known his death when it happened, so they would not have remained a year in subjugation until he fell, or the jinn appeared and that what was in his possession was a substitute for it, meaning it became clear that if the jinn had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the punishment. David founded the Holy House in the place of Moses’ tent, peace be upon them both, but he died before its completion. He bequeathed it to Solomon, peace be upon him, who employed the jinn in it, but it was not yet completed, as his time was approaching and he was informed of it. He wanted to conceal his death from them so that they might complete it, so he called them and they built over him a palace of glass that had no door. He stood praying, leaning on his staff, and his soul was taken while he was leaning on it. He remained like that until termites ate it, so he fell. Then they opened it for him and wanted to know the time of his death, so they placed termites on the staff, and it ate an amount of money in a day and a night. They calculated based on that and found that he had died a year ago. He was fifty-three years old, and he had reigned when he was thirteen years old. He began the construction of the Holy House four years into his reign.
34:15: 15- "Indeed, it was for Saba'" for the sons of Saba' ibn Yashjub ibn Ya'rub ibn Qahtan. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr prohibited the inflection of this because it became the name of the tribe. Ibn Kathir changed the hamza to an alif, and perhaps he brought it out between them so the narrator did not recite it as it should have. "In their dwellings" in their places of residence, which is in Yemen and is called Ma'rib. Between it and Sana'a is a three-day journey. Hamzah and Hafs read it with the singular and the fat-ha, and Al-Kisa'i with the kasra based on what is an anomaly of analogy such as the mosque and the rising. "A sign" is a sign indicating the existence of the Creator, the Chosen One, and that He is able to do whatever He wills of wondrous matters, a metaphor for the good and the evil, supporting the previous proof as in the stories of David and Solomon, peace be upon them. "Two gardens is a substitute for a sign" or an omitted predicate, the meaning of which is the sign, two gardens. It is also read in the accusative case for praise, and what is meant is two groups of orchards. "On the right and left" A group on the right of their town and a group on its left, each one of them in its closeness and solidarity as if it were a single paradise, or a garden, each man on the right and on the left of his dwelling. "Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him" A narration of what their prophet said to them, or a statement of the situation or an indication that they were deserving of being told that. "A good land and a Forgiving Lord" A resumption to indicate the obligation of gratitude, meaning this town in which your provision is a good land and your Lord who provided for you and asked for your gratitude is a Forgiving Lord, the excesses of those who thank Him. And both are read in the accusative as an expression of praise. It was said that they were the most fertile and best of lands and there was no disease or calamity in them.
34:16: 16- So they turned away from gratitude. So We sent upon them the flood of the dam The flood of the dam, meaning the difficult, from the man's dam, so he is dam, and dam if he is fierce and difficult, or heavy rain or rats, he added to it the flood because it was pure sugar for them, which Bilqis struck for them, so she injected the water of the trees with it and left in it a hole the size of what they needed, or the drain that held sugar, as it is the plural of dam, which is the piled up stones. It was said that it is the name of a valley from which the flood came, and that was between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them. And We exchanged for them their two gardens two gardens of bitter fruit, ugly fruit, because every plant that takes a taste of bitterness, and it was said that it is the arak or every tree that does not have thorns, and the meaning is every bitter food, so the added word was deleted and the added to it was used in its place as a substitute, or an explanatory apposition. And tamarisk and some lote-trees, few of them are in apposition to ate and not to dried, because tamarisk is the tamarisk and it has no fruit. They were read in the accusative case in apposition to Two gardens. The description of the lote tree as a little, for its fruit, which is the jujube tree, is one of the things that are delicious to eat, and that is why it is planted in orchards. The naming of the substitute two gardens is for similarity and sarcasm. Abu Amr read my self as akal without the tanween on the lam, and he read al-Haramain with a light akal.
34:17: 17- That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief for their disbelief in the blessing or for their disbelief in the messengers, as it was narrated that thirteen prophets were sent to them but they denied them. The object is brought forward to indicate glorification, not specificity. And do We recompense anyone except the ungrateful? And is anyone recompensed with the like of what We did to them except the one who is eloquent in disbelief or disbelief? Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Ya’qub, and Hafs read Najaazi with a nun and Al-Kafur with the accusative.
34:18: 18- And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed by expanding upon their people, which are the towns of Ash-Sham. Towns visible connected, some of them visible to others, or mounted on a The road is clear to the wayfarers. And We have ordained therein the journey so that the traveler may rest in a village and the traveler may spend the night in another until he reaches Syria. Travel therein means to say it with the tongue of the state or the speech. Nights and days whenever you wish, night or day. Safe Security does not vary according to the time, or travel in safety, even if your journey is long, travel in it for the nights and days of your lives, and you will find therein nothing but safety.
34:19: 19- And they said, 'Our Lord, extend between our journeys.' They were pleased with the blessing and tired of the ease like the Children of Israel, so they asked God to make deserts between them and the Levant so that they could outstrip the poor by riding camels and marrying poor women. So God answered them by destroying the middle-class villages. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read And Hisham (after), and Jacob Our Lord distanced in the form of a report as a complaint from them for the length of their journey, excessive luxury and lack of appreciation for what God has bestowed upon them, and similar to it is the reading of those who read (Our Lord distanced) or (after) as a vocative and attributing the action to between. And they wronged themselves as they were arrogant about the blessing and did not appreciate it. So We made them stories people would talk about them in amazement and make an example and they would say: They were scattered like the hands of Saba’. And We tore them apart completely so We scattered them until Ghassan of them reached Ash-Sham, Anmar to Yathrib, Judham to Tihamah, and Azd to Oman. Indeed in that according to what was mentioned, are signs for everyone who is patient from sins. Grateful for the blessings.
34:20: 20- And indeed, Iblis proved true to their assumption meaning he was true to his assumption or he believed in the assumption of his assumption, just as he did, and it is permissible for the action to be transitive to it by itself, as in: We proved his promise because it is a type of saying. The Kufians stressed it to mean he verified his assumption or found it to be true. It was read with the accusative of Iblis and the nominative of the assumption from the stress meaning he found his assumption to be true, and the lightening meaning he told him his assumption was true when he imagined that they had led him astray. And by raising them and lightening it applies to the bodies, and that is either his assumption of Sheba when he saw their preoccupation with desires or of the children of Adam when he saw their father the Prophet weak in resolve, or what was inherent in them of desire and anger, or he heard the angels say, Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein? So he said, I will surely mislead them and I will surely lead them astray. “So they followed him, except for a group of the believers.” Except for a group, they are the believers who did not follow him, and their being reduced in relation to the disbelievers, or except for a group of the groups of believers who did not follow him in disobedience, and they are the sincere ones.
34:21: 21- And he had no authority over them means domination and control through whispering and seduction. Except that We may know who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it except that Our knowledge is connected to that in a way that results in recompense, or to distinguish the believer from the doubter, or for the one who believes to the extent of his faith to believe and the one who is misguided to the extent of his misguidance to doubt. What is meant by the attainment of knowledge is the attainment of a connected exaggeration. There is a clear point in the arrangement of the two clauses. And your Lord is Guardian over all things Guardian. And the two Zintan are sisters.
34:22: 22- Say to the polytheists: Call upon those whom you have alleged meaning you have alleged as gods. They are two direct objects of claimed, the first omitted due to the length of the relative pronoun and its clause, and the second because its attribute takes its place. It is not permissible for it to be the second direct object because it does not fit with the pronoun in speech, nor they do not possess because they do not claim it. besides God means call upon them regarding what concerns you of bringing benefit or warding off harm, perhaps they will respond to you if your claim is true. Then He answered on their behalf, indicating that the answer is necessary and that He does not accept stubbornness, so He said: they do not possess an atom’s weight of good or evil in the heavens or on the earth in any matter. He mentioned them for the common usage, or because some of their gods are heavenly like the angels and planets, and some are earthly like idols, or because the proximate causes of evil and good are heavenly and earthly, and the sentence is a resumption to explain their condition. And they have no share in them in creation or ownership. "And he has no supporter among them" to help him manage their affairs.
34:23: 23- And no intercession will benefit them with Him. So no intercession will benefit them either, as they claim, since intercession does not benefit with God. Except for him whom He permits. He permits him to intercede, or He permits that intercession be made for him due to his high status, but that has not been proven. The lam in the first case is like the lam in your saying: The generosity is for Zayd. And in the second case it is like the lam in your saying: I came to you for Zayd. Abu Amr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read it with a damma over the hamzah. Until fear is removed from their hearts. This is the limit of the meaning of the statement, that there is a pause and awaiting permission, meaning: they wait in a state of fear until fear is removed from the hearts of the intercessors and those for whom permission is granted. It was said that the pronoun refers to the angels, and they were previously mentioned implicitly. Ibn Amir and Ya'qub read fāz'a in the active form. It was read faḍarāq, meaning the fear is negated from faḍarāq al-ḍaḍwhen the provisions are used up. Qalā means some of them said to each other. What did your Lord say? about intercession? They said, ‘The truth.’ They said, He said the true word, which is permission to intercede for whomever He is pleased with, and they are the believers. It was read in the nominative case, meaning His word is the truth. And He is the Most High, the Grand, the Possessor of loftiness and majesty. No king or prophet from the prophets will speak on that day except with His permission.
34:24: 24- Say, ‘Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?’ He means by this to confirm his statement, They do not possess. “Say, ‘God,’” since there is no answer other than Him, and in it is a notification that if they are silent or falter in their answer for fear of being forced, they acknowledge it in their hearts. And indeed, either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. That is, one of the two groups, the monotheists who are unique in their provision and innate ability to worship, and the polytheists who are inanimate and have descended to the lowest levels of possibility, is upon one of the two matters of clear guidance or error. This, after what preceded from the eloquent confirmation indicating who is upon right guidance and who is in error, is more eloquent than explicit statement because it is in the form of fairness that silences the quarrelsome opponent. Similar to it is the statement of Hassan: I satirize him, but I am not his equal. May God sacrifice my life for you both. It was said that it is based on wrapping and spreading, and there is a problem with it, and the difference between the two letters is because the guide is like someone who has ascended. A lighthouse that sees things and looks at them, or he rides a horse that runs wherever he wants, and the lost one is as if he is immersed in confused darkness, not seeing anything, or imprisoned in a dungeon from which he cannot escape.
34:25: 25- Say, ‘You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you do.’ This is more fair and more blatant in its malice, as the crime is attributed to themselves and the action to those being addressed.
34:26: 26- “Say, ‘Our Lord will gather us together’ on the Day of Resurrection. Then He will judge between us in truth’. He will judge and decide by admitting those who are right into Paradise and those who are wrong into Hell. ‘And He is the Opener’. The Judge who decides in related cases. ‘The Knower’.
34:27: 27- Say, ‘Show me those whom you have associated with Him as partners.’ So that I may see by what attribute you have associated them with God in deserving of worship. This is an inquiry into their doubt after the proof has been imposed upon them, in order to further rebuke them. No! It is a deterrent to them from associating partners after invalidating the comparison. Rather, He is God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. He is described as having dominance and perfect power and wisdom. These who are associated with Him are characterized by humility, refusing to accept knowledge and power directly, and the pronoun refers to God or to the matter.
34:28: 28 - And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to mankind except as a general sending to them from the suffice, for if it is general to them then it has sufficed them from any important person leaving it, or except as a gathering of them in conveying the message, then it is a state of the kaf and the ta' for emphasis, and it is not permissible to make it a state of the people according to the chosen one. As a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of the people do not know so their ignorance leads them to disobey you.
34:29: 29- And they say, out of extreme ignorance, When will this promise come? They mean the one who brings good tidings and the one who warns. About him or the one promised by the Almighty’s saying: Our Lord will gather us together “if you are truthful” they are addressing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers with it.
34:30: 30- Say to you, ‘An appointment is made for you on a Day.’ A promise is a day or a time. Adding it to the day is for clarification. This is supported by the fact that it was read day as a substitute, and it was read day with an implied meaning. Do not delay it an hour, nor advance it. If it surprises you, it is an answer to a threat that came in accordance with what they intended with their question of obstinacy and denial.
34:31: 31- And those who disbelieve say, ‘We will not believe in this Qur’an, nor in that which was before it,’ nor in what preceded it of books indicating descriptions. It was said that the disbelievers of Mecca asked the People of the Book about the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they informed them that they found his description in their books, so they became angry and said that. It was also said that what was before him is on the Day of Resurrection. And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, that is, in the place of accountability. Referring to each other’s statement, they discuss and exchange statements. Those who were deemed weak will say, the followers say. To those who were arrogant, to the leaders. Had it not been for you, had it not been for your misguidance and turning us away from faith. We would have been believers, by following the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
34:32: 32- Those who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed, ‘Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals.’ They denied that they had averted them from faith and confirmed that they were the ones who averted themselves when they turned away from guidance and preferred imitation over it. Therefore, they based their denial on the name.
34:33: 33- And those who were oppressed said to those who were arrogant, ‘Rather, your plotting was night and day.’ This is an interruption of their interruption, meaning: It was not our crime, but your plotting against us that was constant, night and day, until you made us blind. When you ordered us to disbelieve in God and attribute to Him equals. The conjunction connects it to their first statement, and the addition of plotting to the adverbial phrase is for expansion. The plotting of the night was read in the accusative case as a source, and plotting of the night with the tanween and the accusative case of the adverbial phrase, and plotting of the night is from karur. “And they concealed their regret when they saw the punishment.” Both groups concealed their regret for misguidance and being led astray, and each group hid it from the eye of the other for fear of expressing it, or they made it apparent, as it is from opposites, as the hamza is suitable for affirmation and negation, as in I complained about it. “And We have placed shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved.” That is, on their necks. So the word came in the apparent form to highlight their condemnation and to indicate the effect of their shackles. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do? That is, what is done to them is not done except as recompense for their deeds. The transitivity of yajzi is either to include the meaning of qada or by removing the preposition.
34:34: 34- And We did not send to any city a warner but its affluent ones said, ‘We are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent,’ as a consolation to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what he had suffered from his people, and singling out those who were affluent for denial because the greatest motive for it is arrogance and boasting about the trappings of this world, being absorbed in desires, and belittling those who have not enjoyed them. For this reason, they combined mockery and boasting with denial and said, Indeed, we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers, contrasting the plural with the plural.
34:35: 35- And they said, ‘We are more in wealth and children.’ So we are more deserving of what you claim, if possible. And we will not be punished. Either because punishment will not happen, or because He has honored us with that and will not humiliate us with punishment.
34:36: 36- Say for their sake. Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it. Therefore, people who are similar in characteristics and attributes differ in it. If that were for the sake of honor and humiliation that they require, it would not be by His will. But most people do not know. They think that an abundance of money and children is for honor and dignity, and it is often for the purpose of enticement, as He said:
34:37: 37- And it is not your wealth and your children that will bring you near to Us. “Nearness” is either because what is meant is and what is the sum of your wealth and your children, or because it is an omitted description like piety and a characteristic. And it was read (By that) meaning by the thing that brings you closer. Except for he who believes and does righteous deeds is an exception to the object of brings you closer, meaning money and children do not bring anyone closer except the righteous believer who spends his money in the way of God and teaches his children good and raises them to be righteous, or from your money And your children is with the deletion of the noun. For those is a double reward that they will be rewarded double to ten or more, and the addition is the addition of the source to the object, and it was read with the works on the original and from Ya`qub they raised them on the substitution of the double, and the reward was placed in the accusative case on the distinction or the source for its action which it indicated for them. For what they did while they were in the chambers safe from the hardships, and it was read with the opening of the ra` and its sukoon, and Hamza read (in the chamber) to mean the genus.
34:38: 38- And those who strive against Our signs by rejecting and challenging them. To outshine by racing against Our prophets or thinking that they can evade Us. Those will be brought to the punishment.
34:39: 39- “Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for whom He wills.’ He expands it for him sometimes and restricts it for him other times. This is for one person considering two times, and what came before was for two people, so there is no repetition. “And whatever you spend, He will replace it.” in exchange, either sooner or later. And He is the Best of providers. For others are intermediate in delivering their provision, but their provider is not truly Him.
34:40: 40- And the Day We shall gather them all together the arrogant and the oppressed. Then He will say to the angels, ‘Was it these that they used to worship you?’ As a rebuke to the polytheists, to rebuke them, and to make them despair of what they expected from their intercession. The angels were singled out because they are the most honorable of their partners and the most worthy of being addressed, and because their worship is the beginning and root of polytheism. Hafs and Ya’qub read them with the letter ya in both of them.
34:41: 41- They said, ‘Glory be to You! You are our protector rather than them.’ You are the one we support rather than them. There is no support between us and them. It is as if they demonstrated with that their innocence of being pleased with their worship. Then they turned away from that and denied that they truly worshipped them by saying, Rather, they used to worship the jinn, meaning the devils, since they obeyed them in worshipping other than God. It was also said that they used to appear to them and imagine to them that they were angels, so they would worship them. Most of them are believers in them. The first pronoun refers to humans or polytheists, and most means all, and the second refers to the jinn.
34:42: 42- So today none of you has power to benefit or harm others as the whole matter is his, because the world is a place of recompense and He alone is the one who is rewarded. And We will say to those who did wrong, ‘Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.’ This is in apposition to does not have power, clarifying the purpose of its introduction.
34:43: 43- And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, ‘This is not but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship.’ They mean Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, so that he may follow you with what he has innovated. “And they said, ‘This is nothing but a lie,’” meaning the Qur’an, because what it contains does not match reality. Muftaray is attributed to God Almighty. And those who disbelieved said about the truth when it came to them regarding the matter of prophethood, or Islam, or the Qur’an. The first is based on its meaning, and the second is based on its wording and its miraculous nature. This is nothing but obvious magic. Its magic is apparent, and in the repetition of the action and the explicit mention of the disbelievers and what is in the two lams of the reference to the qayyin and the statement about it, and what is in lama of the rush to decide with this statement is a great denial of it and a profound astonishment from it.
34:44: 44- And We did not give them any books to study. This is evidence of the validity of polytheism. And We did not send to them before you any warner calling them to it and warning them against abandoning it. It had been made clear before that it had no basis, so how did they get this suspicion? This is the ultimate in making them ignorant and belittling their opinion. Then He threatened them, saying:
34:45: 45- And those before them denied, just as they denied. And they did not attain a tenth of what We gave them, just as they denied. And these did not attain a tenth of what We gave them, just as these did not attain a tenth of what We gave those of strength, long life, and abundant wealth, or those did not attain a tenth of what We gave them of clear proofs and guidance. So they denied My messengers, so how was My denial? So when they denied My messengers, My denial of destruction came to them, so how was My denial of them? So let these beware of the like of it. There is no repetition in lie, because the first is for emphasis and the second is for denial, or the first is absolute and the second is restricted, and that is why it is connected to it with fa.
34:46: 46- “Say, ‘I only admonish you of one thing.’ I guide you and advise you of one characteristic, which is what is indicated by: ‘That you stand up for God.’ This means standing up from the assembly of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or standing up in the matter purely for the sake of God, turning away from argument and imitation. "Two by two and one by one" Separated by two by two and one by one, for crowding confuses the mind and mixes up speech. "Then you reflect" on the matter of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and what he brought, so that you may learn its truth. Its place is in the accusative case as a substitute or clarification or nominative or accusative with the omission of "he" I mean. "There is no madness in your companion" so that you may learn what madness he has that drives him to do that, or a new statement alerting them that what they know of his sound mind is sufficient to support his truthfulness, for it does not allow him to undertake to claim a serious matter and a great matter without verification and confidence in proof, so he is disgraced in front of all witnesses and throws himself into destruction, so how is it when many miracles have been added to him? And it was said that "what" is an interrogative and the meaning is: Then you reflect on what traces of madness he has: "He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment" before him because he is sent in the breeze of the Hour.
34:47: 47- Say, ‘I have not asked you for any reward for the message.’ That is, what I have asked you for as a reward for the message. It is yours. What is meant is to negate the question about it, as if making prophethood entail one of two things: either madness or the expectation of worldly benefit from it, because it is either for a purpose or something else, and whatever is required of one of them, then he negated both of them. And before ma is a relative pronoun meaning what he asked them with His saying: I do not ask you for it any reward except for whoever wills to take a way to his Lord. And His saying: I do not ask you for it any reward except love for the relatives. And taking the way benefits them and his relatives are their relatives. My reward is only from God, and He is, over all things, Witness. He knows my truthfulness and the sincerity of my intention. Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read it with a sukoon on the ya’.
34:48: 48- Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord casts the truth’ He casts it and sends it down upon whomever He chooses from among His servants, or He casts it with falsehood and destroys it, or He casts it to the ends of the earth, so it is a promise to make Islam prevail and spread. Nafi’ and Abu Amr read it with the fatha on the ya’. Knower of the Unseen is an adjective carried over to the position of in and its noun, or a substitute for what is implied in He casts or a second predicate or a deleted predicate. It was read in the accusative as an adjective for my Lord or understood as I mean. Hamzah and Abu Bakr read the Unseen with the kasra like houses and with the damma like the tithes, and it was read with the fatha like patient as an exaggeration of the absent.
34:49: 49- “Say, ‘The truth has come,’ meaning Islam. ‘Falsehood can neither begin nor restore.’ And falsehood, meaning polytheism, has perished, such that no trace of it remains. This is taken from the destruction of a living thing, for when it perishes, it has no beginning or restoration. He said: I jump from his family slaves, for today neither shows nor returns It was said that falsehood is Satan or an idol, and the meaning is that it does not create a creation and does not repeat it, or does not initiate good for its people and does not repeat it. It was also said that “what” is an interrogative noun governed by what follows it.
34:50: 50- “Say, ‘If I go astray’ from the truth, ‘I go astray only to my own detriment’, for the consequences of my going astray are upon me because it is my own fault, for it is the one who is ignorant of itself and commands to evil. And with this consideration, He contrasted the conditional with His statement, ‘And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me’, for guidance is by His guidance and success. ‘Indeed, He is All-Hearing, All-Near’, He comprehends the words and actions of every person who is astray or guided, even if he conceals them.
34:51: 51- And if you could but see when they are terrified at death, or resurrection, or on the day of Badr, and the answer If is omitted, meaning you would have seen a terrible thing. There is no escape, so they do not escape God by fleeing or taking refuge. And they were seized from a nearby place, from the surface of the earth to its interior, or from the position to the fire, or from the desert of Badr to the well, and the conjunction is with They were terrified or there is no escape, and this is supported by the fact that it was read and took in apposition to its place, meaning: there is no escape there and there he took.
34:52: 52- And they said, ‘We believe in him,’ in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. This was mentioned previously in His statement, What is with your companion? “And how can they grasp it?” And how can they grasp it easily? “From a distant place,” for he was in the realm of obligation and it was far from them. It is a metaphor for their state in seeking salvation through faith after its time had passed them by and it had been far from them, like the state of someone who wants to grasp something from the extreme of grasping it from an arm’s length in impossibility. Abu Amr and the Kufians other than Hafs read it with a hamza, changing the waw because of its damma. Or it is from na’asht something if you seek it. Ru’bah said: My father's neighbor, Al-Jamoush, has brought me to you with the wrath of fate Or from naasht if she is late and from it his saying: Nashisha wished he had obeyed me, and after that, things happened. It means eating from a distance.
34:53: 53- And they disbelieved in him Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, or in the punishment. Before before that time of accountability. And they cast aspersions in the unseen and they cast aspersions based on conjecture and they rely on things that the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, did not reveal to them of accusations, or in the punishment of spreading his denial. From a distant place from a distant aspect of his affair, which is the doubts that they created in the affair of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, or the state of the Hereafter as mentioned before. Perhaps it is a metaphor for their state in that like the state of someone who casts something that he does not see from a distant place where there is no room for suspicion of its occurrence. It was read (and they cast aspersions) meaning that Satan casts that upon them and prompts them to do so. The conjunction with and they disbelieved is to narrate the past state or to they said, so it is a metaphor for their state like the state of the slanderer in obtaining what they lost of faith in this world.
34:54: 54- And they will be prevented from what they desire of the benefit of faith and salvation by it from the Fire. Ibn Umar and Al-Kisa’i read it with the dammah on the ha’. As He did with their followers before with their likes from the disbelieving nations of the common people. Indeed, they were in disturbing doubt is a place of doubt, or of doubt taken from the doubter, or doubt is a description of doubt for the sake of exaggeration. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Saba’, there will remain no messenger or prophet but that he will be his companion and friend on the Day of Resurrection.
35:1: 1 - Praise be to God, the Creator of the heavens and the earth. Their Creator comes from the word fatr meaning to split, as if He split nothingness by bringing them out of it. The addition is pure because it has a past tense meaning. Who has made the angels messengers. They are intermediaries between God and His prophets and righteous servants, conveying His messages to them through revelation, inspiration, and true visions, or between Him and His creation, conveying to them the effects of His creation. Those with wings, two, three, or four means those with multiple wings that vary in rank, with which they descend and ascend, or with which they hasten towards whatever God has entrusted them with, and they dispose of it as He commands them. Perhaps this does not mean that they are prepared specifically and that they do not still have them, because it was narrated that “He, peace and blessings be upon him, saw Gabriel on the night of the Ascension, and he had six hundred wings.” He increases in creation as He wills is a new indication that their variation in that is in accordance with His will and the effect of His wisdom, not something that their essences require, because the difference of classes and types in properties and divisions, if it were due to their common essences, would necessitate a contradiction in the implications of the agreed-upon matters, and that is impossible. The verse deals with additions in form and meaning, such as a beautiful face, a beautiful voice, a shrewd mind, and a generous soul. Indeed, God is over all things competent. The specific attainment of some things and not others is only from the aspect of the will.
35:2: 2 - What God opens to mankind means what He releases and sends to them, and this is from the use of the cause for the effect. Of mercy such as blessing, security, health, knowledge, and prophecy. There is none who can withhold it He thinks it is. And what He withholds, there is none who can send it He releases it, and the difference between the two pronouns is because the first relative pronoun is explained by mercy and the second is absolute in including it and anger, and in that is an indication that His mercy preceded His anger. After it means after His withholding. And He is the Exalted in Might He prevails over whatever He wills, no one has the right to dispute with Him in that. The Wise He does not act except with knowledge and mastery. Then after He explained that He is the One who created the kingdom and the kingdom of heaven and who disposes of them absolutely, He commanded the people to be grateful for His blessings, saying:
35:3: 3 - "O mankind, remember the favor of God upon you." Preserve it by knowing its right, acknowledging it, and obeying its Master. Then he denied that anyone other than Him had a role in that, and thus deserved to be associated with Him, by saying: "Is there a creator other than God who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no god but Him, so how are you deluded? So how are you turned away from monotheism to associating anyone other than Him with Him? The raising of other is to carry it on the place of who is the Creator as a description or a substitute, since the question is in the meaning of negation, or because it is the subject of Creator" and Hamza and Al-Kisa'i made it genitive based on its wording. It was made accusative as an exception, and "provides for you is an attribute of Creator" or a new explanation of it or a new statement. According to the latter, the use of "is there a Creator" prevents it from being applied to anyone other than God.
35:4: 4 - And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], [other] messengers were denied before you. That is, take them as an example in your patience with their denial. The use of you have been denied is to dispense with the effect, and the indefiniteness of messengers is to emphasize the importance of consolation and to encourage patience. And to God are returned all matters. So He will reward you and them for your patience and denial.
35:5: 5 - "O mankind, indeed the promise of God" of gathering and recompense. "is true" and will not be broken. "So do not let the worldly life delude you" so that its enjoyment distracts you from seeking and striving for the Hereafter. "And do not let the Deceiver delude you about God" the devil by promising you forgiveness while persisting in sin, for even if it is possible, the sin with this expectation is like taking poison relying on repelling nature. It is read with the dammah and it is a source or plural like qa'ud.
35:6: 6 - Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you an ancient, general enmity. So take him as an enemy in your beliefs and actions and be wary of him in all aspects of your life. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze is a confirmation of his enmity and a statement of his purpose in calling his followers to follow whims and incline to this world.
35:7: 7 - Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, and those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward. A warning to those whose prayers are answered, a promise to those who disobey him, and an end to empty hopes. The whole matter is based on faith and righteous deeds. His saying:
35:8: 8 - "Is he who has made his evil deeds seem good to him so he regards them as good?" A statement for him, that is, is he who has made his evil deeds seem good to him so that his imagination and desires overcome his mind until his opinion is distorted and he sees falsehood as truth and ugly as good, like he who has not made them seem good to him but rather has been guided until he knows the truth and approves of actions and disapproves of them as they are? So the answer was omitted due to the indication of: "Indeed, God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills." It was said that its meaning is: Is he who has made his evil deeds seem good to him so that your soul goes away in regret over them? So the answer was omitted due to the indication of: "So do not let yourself perish over them in regret" over it and its meaning is so do not destroy yourself over them in regret over their error and their insistence on denial. The three "fa"s are for causality, but the first two are used for the cause and the third is used for the effect. The plural of "regrets" is to indicate the doubling of his grief over their conditions or the many evils of their actions that require regret. "Over them" is not a connection because the connection of the source does not precede it, but rather a connection that goes away or a statement of what is regretted. "God is All-Knowing of what they do," and He will reward them for it.
35:9: 9 - And it is God who sends the winds. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read it as the wind. "And it stirs up clouds" as a narration of a past event, evoking that wonderful image indicating perfect wisdom, and because the intended meaning is to explain its events with this characteristic, and that is why He attributed it to it. It is also possible that the difference in the actions is to indicate the continuity of the matter. "So We drove it to a dead land." Nafi', Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read it with emphasis. "So We revived the earth thereby" with the rain descending from it, and the mention of the clouds is like its mention, or with the clouds, for they are the cause of the cause or the one that becomes rain. "After its death" after its drying up, and the shift in both of them from the third person to what is more appropriate in specificity is due to what they contain of further creation. "Likewise is the resurrection" meaning like the revival of the dead is the resurrection of the dead in the validity of the predestination, since there is nothing between them except the possibility of the difference in the matter in the comparison to which it is compared, and that has no bearing on it. It was said about the manner of revival that God Almighty sends water from under the throne from which the bodies of creation grow.
35:11: 11 - And God created you from dust by creating Adam, peace be upon him, from him. Then from a sperm-drop by creating his offspring from it. Then He made you mates males and females. And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge except that which is known to Him. And no one lives long nor is his life extended from his destiny to old age. And He does not decrease his lifespan from the lifespan of someone else by giving him a lifespan that is less than his own, or He does not decrease the lifespan of someone whose lifespan is less than his own by making it less than his own. The pronoun refers to him even though it is not mentioned to indicate its opposite or to the age in order to be lenient in it, trusting in the understanding of the listener, like their saying: God does not reward a servant nor punish him except with justice. It was said that the increase or decrease in a single lifespan is based on different reasons proven in the tablet, such as: that if Amr performs Hajj, then his lifespan is sixty years, otherwise it is forty. It was said that what is meant by decrease is what passes of his life and ends, for it is written in the book of his life day by day. And from Yaqub, nor does it decrease is in the active form. Except in a book is the knowledge of God Almighty or the Preserved Tablet or the book. Indeed, that, for God, is easy is an indication of preservation or increase or decrease.
35:12: 12 - The two seas are not alike. This is fresh and sweet, and its drink is pleasant, and the other is salty and bitter." An example is given for the believer and the unbeliever. The fresh is that which quenches thirst, the sweet is that which flows easily, and the bitter is that which burns with its saltiness. It is read (sigh) with emphasis and (sigh) without emphasis, and salt is on the pattern of fa’l. And from each you eat tender meat and extract ornaments which you wear. This is a digression into the description of the two seas and the blessings they contain, or a complete illustration and meaning: Just as they share some benefits, they are not equal, since they are not equal in what is intended in itself, namely water, because one of them has been mixed with that which corrupts it and changes its natural disposition, the believer and the disbeliever are not equal, even if they share some qualities, such as bravery and generosity, because they differ in what is the greatest characteristic, which is that one of them remains in his original nature while the other does not, or the preference of the brackish water over the disbeliever in what it shares with the fresh water of benefits. What is meant by ornament is pearls and rubies. And you see the ships therein in each. Watercourses that split the water, making it flow. That you may seek of His bounty of God’s bounty by moving therein. The lam is related to watercourses, and it is permissible for it to be related to what is indicated by the aforementioned actions. "And perhaps you will be grateful" for that, and the letter of hope is based on what the apparent situation requires.
35:13: 13 - "He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term." This is the duration of its cycle or its end or the Day of Resurrection. That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. This refers to the Doer of these things. This indicates that His dominion over them is required by the confirmation of the successive reports. It is possible that To Him belongs dominion is an introductory statement in the Qur'an. And those you invoke besides Him do not possess so much as a date stone. This indicates His uniqueness in divinity and lordship, and a date stone is the smallest particle.
35:14: 14 - If you call upon them, they do not hear your call because they are inanimate. And if they heard hypothetically. They would not respond to you because of their inability to benefit, or because they disavow you for what you call upon them. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association because of your association with them, they will acknowledge its falsehood or say, You did not worship us. "And none informs you like the All-Knowing and no one informs you about a matter like the All-Knowing" He informed you about it, and He is God, the Most High, the Most Great, for He is the All-Knowing about it in truth, unlike all other informants. The rebellious one is the one who confirms what he informed about the state of their gods and denies what they call upon them to do.
35:15: 15 - "O mankind, you are those in need of God" in yourselves and what is in your minds. The definition of "poor" is to exaggerate their poverty, as if they are the ones who are poor due to their extreme poverty and great need, and that the poverty of all other creatures is not taken into account in comparison to their poverty. Therefore, He said: "And man was created weak. And God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy", the One who is completely free of need, the One who bestows favors upon all other creatures, so He deserves praise from them.
35:16: 16 - If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation with another people more obedient than you, or with another world other than what you know.
35:17: 17 - And that is not difficult for God is not difficult or hard.
35:18: 18 - And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another and no sinful soul shall bear the sin of another soul. As for His statement, And they will bear their own burdens and burdens in addition to their burdens, this refers to those who have gone astray and lead others astray, for they will bear the burdens of their misguidance in addition to the burdens of their misguidance, and all of that is their burdens, with nothing of the burdens of others in it. And if a heavily burdened soul calls forth is a soul burdened with burdens. To bear it carries some of its burdens. Nothing of it shall be borne it is not necessary to bear anything of it. He negated that its sin be borne for it, just as he negated that the sin of others be borne for it. Even if he was a relative even if the one called was a relative of hers, so the one called was omitted to indicate that if she calls upon him. The reading (a relative) was read with the predicate omitted, which is more appropriate than making the complete kana because it does not fit the structure of the speech. You only warn those who fear their Lord unseen absent from His punishment, or from people in their private moments, or absent from them from His punishment. And establish prayer for they are the ones who benefit from the warning and no one else. The difference between the two actions is due to the continuity mentioned above. And whoever purifies himself and whoever cleanses himself from the filth of sins only purifies himself for [the benefit of] himself since it benefits him. It was also read and whoever purifies himself only purifies himself which is an emphasised objection to their fear and their establishment of prayer because they are part of purification. And to God is the final destination so He will reward them for their purification.
35:19: 19 - The blind and the seeing are not alike the disbeliever and the believer, and it was said that they are two examples of the idol and God Almighty.
35:20: 20 - Nor darkness nor light nor falsehood nor truth.
35:21: 21 - Nor shade nor heat nor reward nor punishment, and nor to emphasize the negation of the ascension and repeating it in both parts for more emphasis. Hurur is a noun from har which is predominantly used for samum. It is said that samum is what blows during the day and harur is what blows at night.
35:22: 22 - And the living are not alike to the dead. Another more eloquent representation of the believers and the disbelievers than the first, and that is why the verb was repeated. It was said to both the scholars and the ignorant. Indeed, God makes hear whom He wills. His guidance, enabling him to understand His verses and take heed from His sermons. And you cannot make hear those in the graves. This is a nomination to represent those who persist in disbelief with the dead and to exaggerate His despair of them.
35:23: 23 - You are only a warner. You are only responsible for warning. As for making them hear, you have no power over what is sealed in their hearts.
35:24: 24 - Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a truthful one, or a sending accompanied by the truth. It is permissible for it to be a connection to His saying: as a bringer of good tidings and a warner meaning as a bringer of good tidings of the true promise and a warner of the true threat. And there is no nation of a time but that there has passed “in it a warner” of a prophet or scholar who warns about it. It is sufficient to mention it because it is known that warning is a companion to good tidings, especially since it was coupled with it before, or because warning is the most important purpose of the mission.
35:25: 25 - "And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], those before them denied. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs" with miracles that testified to their prophethood. And with the scriptures such as the scrolls of Abraham, peace be upon him. And with the illuminating book such as the Torah and the Gospel, meaning the details and not the plural. It is possible that they both mean one thing, and the conjunction is due to the difference between the two descriptions.
35:26: 26 - Then I seized those who disbelieved, and how terrible was My punishment. That is, the denial of the punishment.
35:27: 27 - "Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors" their kinds and types, with each one of them having different kinds, or their forms of yellowness, greenness, and the like. "And among the mountains are lines" meaning lines, that is, lines and paths. It is said that a donkey has a line on its back, and it is read (jadda) with a damma, the plural of jadeeda, meaning newness, and (jadda) with two fathahs, which is the clear path. "White and red, of varying colors" with intensity and weakness. "And black crows is in apposition to white or to jadda", as if it was said: And among the mountains are lines of varying colors, and among them are "crows" of the same color, and it is an implied emphasis explained by what follows it, for the ghareeb is an emphasis of black, and it is the right of emphasis to follow the emphasized, and similar to that in the description is the saying of Al-Nabigha: And the faithful birds wipe it And in such a case there is further confirmation of what it contains of repetition, considering the concealment and the manifestation.
35:28: 28 - And among people and moving creatures and livestock are different colors likewise. Like the fruits and mountains. Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge. The condition of fear is knowledge of the one feared and of His attributes and actions. So whoever has more knowledge of Him is more fearful of Him. For this reason, "He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: 'Indeed, I fear God most of you and am most pious to Him.'" For this reason, he followed it with mentioning His actions that indicate the perfection of His power, and he presented the object first because the intention is to limit the effectiveness. If it were delayed, the matter would be reversed. It was read with the name of God in the nominative case and the scholars in the accusative case, on the basis that fear is borrowed to indicate glorification, for the one who is glorified is awe-inspiring. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Forgiving. This is an explanation for the necessity of fear, as it indicates that He will punish the one who persists in his transgression and forgive the one who repents from his disobedience.
35:29: 29 - Indeed, those who recite the Book of God are persistent in reading it or following what is in it until it became a characteristic and a title for them. What is meant by the Book of God is the Qur’an or the type of books of God, so it is praise for the believers from the nations after the state of the disbelievers has been recounted. And they establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly. How did it happen without intending them? It was said that the secret is in the recommended and the public is in the obligatory. They hope for a trade to obtain the reward of obedience, and it is the report of if. “It will never perish” will never be stagnant and will never be destroyed by loss, an attribute of the trade. His saying:
35:30: 30 - That He may pay them their wages is the reason for its meaning, that is, that it is free of stagnation and is spent with God, that He may pay them their wages for their deeds through its spending, or for the meaning of what is counted from their compliance, such as they did that, That He may pay them or as a consequence of they hope. "And increase them from His bounty" in return for their deeds. "He is Oft-Forgiving" for their excesses. "Appreciative for their obedience, that is, He will reward them for it, and it is the reason for the payment and increase or the predicate of that. And they hope is a state of the and and they spend."
35:31: 31 - And that which We have revealed to you of the Book meaning the Qur'an. Min is for clarification or type, and Min is for partiality. It is the truth, confirming what was before it The most deserving of confirming what was before it from the heavenly books is a confirmed adverbial because its truthfulness necessitates its agreement with it in beliefs and fundamental legal rulings. Indeed, God is All-Aware and All-Seeing of His servants Knowing of the inner and outer aspects. If there was in your circumstances something that contradicted prophethood, He would not have revealed to you such a miraculous book that is a standard for all other books. The mention of All-Aware is to indicate that the main point in that is spiritual matters.
35:32: 32 - Then We caused the Scripture to be inherited. We decreed that it be inherited from you or that you bequeath it, so it was expressed in the past tense to confirm its authenticity, or We caused it to be inherited from previous nations. The conjunction with Indeed, those who recite "and that which We have revealed to you" is an interjection to explain the manner of inheritance. "Those We have chosen from among Our servants" meaning the scholars of the nation from the Companions and those who came after them, or the nation as a whole, for God chose them over all other nations. "And among them is he who is unjust to himself" by falling short in acting upon it. "And among them is he who is moderate" who works for it most of the time. "And among them is he who is foremost in good deeds by God's permission" by including teaching and guidance with action. It was said that the unjust is the ignorant, the moderate is the learner, and the foremost is the knowledgeable. It was said that it refers to the wrongdoer who is criminal, the moderate who mixes good with bad, and the foremost one whose good deeds outweigh one another so that his bad deeds are expiated. This is the meaning of the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): “As for those who are foremost, they will enter Paradise and will be provided for therein without account. As for those who are moderate, they will be given an easy reckoning. As for those who wronged themselves, they will be detained for a long time at the gathering place, then God will meet them with His mercy.” It was also said that it refers to the wrongdoer and disbeliever, with the pronoun referring to the servants, and it was mentioned first because of the large number of wrongdoers and because injustice in the sense of ignorance and inclination to whims is required by human nature, and moderation and foremost are accidental. That is the great bounty refers to inheritance, selection, or foremost.
35:33: 33 - Gardens of Eden they shall enter is the subject and predicate. The pronoun refers to the three, or to those, or to the economist and preceder, since the object of both is the genus. It was read (Garden of Eden) and Gardens of Eden is in the accusative case with a verb that is explained by the apparent meaning. Abu Amr read (they enter it) in the passive form. They abide therein is a second predicate or an implied state. It was read (they abide therein) from the woman's adornment, so it is a state. Of bracelets of gold "Of" the first is for partiality and the second is for clarification. "And pearls is in apposition to gold meaning of gold studded with pearls, or of gold" in the purity of the pearls. Nafi' and Asim, may God have mercy on them, put it in the accusative case in apposition to the position of "of bracelets". "And their clothing therein will be silk."
35:34: 34 - And they said, 'Praise be to God, who has removed from us sorrow.' Their concern was due to fear of the consequences, or their concern was for livelihood and its troubles, or because of the whisperings of Satan, or other things. Sorrow was also read. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving to the sinners. Appreciative to the obedient.
