39:26: 26- So God made them taste disgrace humiliation in the life of this world such as transformation, sinking, killing, captivity and exile but the punishment of the Hereafter prepared for them is greater because of its severity and permanence if they only knew if they were people of knowledge and insight they would have known that and taken heed of it.
39:27: 27- And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an from every [kind of] example that perhaps they will be reminded.
39:28: 28- An Arabic Qur'an is a state of this and the reliance in it is on the description as you say: Zaid came to me as a righteous man, or he praised him without any crookedness with no defect in it in any way and it is more expressive than straight and more concise in meaning. And it was said with doubt, citing as evidence his saying: And there has come to you a certainty from God without crookedness and a word that is not false. It is a specification of some of its meaning, so that they may become righteous, for another reason based on the first.
39:29: 29- God has set forth an example for the polytheist and the monotheist: a man among whom are quarreling partners, and a man devoted to another man. The example of the polytheist, as required by his doctrine, is that each of his worshipped ones claims his servitude, and they dispute over him with a slave whom they share, a group that they pull at each other and take turns with in their various tasks in his confusion and the division of his heart. The monotheist is one who is devoted to one person and has no way over anyone else. A man is a substitute for an example, and in it is a connection to partners, and the quarreling and staring is the difference. Nafi`, Ibn `Amir and the Kufians read Ṣalmān with two fatḥahs. It was also read with a fatḥah on the seen or a kasrah on it with a sukoon on the lam. All three are masdars. Ṣalm is described by them, or mahā dha and rajul salim were deleted, meaning there is a healthy man. The man was singled out because he was more aware of harm and benefit. Are they both equal, for example? is an adjective and a state, and its accusative is a specification for that reason alone. Ṭamthalīn was read to indicate the difference in type, or because what is meant by are they equal in the two descriptions is that the pronoun refers to the two equals, since the meaning is like a man and like a man. “Praise be to God,” all praise is for Him, and no one else shares it with Him in reality, because He is the One who bestows blessings intrinsically and the absolute Owner. Rather, most of them do not know, so they associate others with Him due to their extreme ignorance.
39:30: 30- You will die and they will die. Everyone is about to die and is counted among the dead. It was read one hundred and one hundred because it is something that will happen.
39:31: 31- Then you will dispute before your Lord on the Day of Resurrection. So you argue with them by saying that you were on the truth in monotheism and they were in falsehood in associating partners with God, and you strove to guide and convey the message but they persisted in denial and stubbornness, and they make excuses with falsehoods such as We obeyed our masters and We found our fathers. It was said that what is meant by it is the general dispute, people dispute with each other over what happened between them in this world.
39:32: 32- "Who is more unjust than he who lies about God by adding a son and a partner to Him and denies the truth" which is what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came with. "When it came to him without stopping and thinking about his matter Is there not in Hell a residence for the disbelievers?" That is sufficient as a recompense for their deeds, and the lam can be interpreted as a covenant or a gender, and it is used as evidence for declaring the innovators to be infidels, as they lie about what they know to be true, and it is weak because it is specific to the one who is surprised by what he knows the Messenger will come with, by denying it.
39:33: 33- And he who brought the truth and was believed in The lam is for the genus to include the messengers and believers, as He said: Those are the righteous. It was said that it is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is he who followed him, as in the Almighty's saying: And We gave Moses the Scripture that they might be guided. It was said that the one who came is the Messenger and the one who believed is Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and that requires the omission of what is not permissible. It was read and was believed in with the lightening, meaning the people believed in it, so he conveyed it to them as it was revealed without distortion, or it became true because of it because it is a miracle that indicates its truthfulness and was believed in with it in the passive form.
39:34: 34- They will have whatever they wish with their Lord in Paradise. That is the reward of the doers of good for their good deeds.
39:35: 35- That God may remove from them the worst of what they have done. The word worst was used specifically for emphasis, because if someone removes the worst, then someone else is more deserving of that, or to indicate that because they consider their sins so great, they think that they are negligent and guilty, and that the minor sins they commit are the worst of their sins. It is also possible that it means bad, as in their saying: The deficient and the most just of the Banu Marwan. Worst was read as the plural of bad. “And He will reward them their wage” and give them their recompense. For the best of what they used to do, so the good deeds of their actions are counted for them with the best of them in increasing the reward and its greatness due to their extreme sincerity in them.
39:36: 36- Is not God sufficient for His servant? This is an interrogative of denial and exaggeration in affirmation. The servant is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The genus is possible and is supported by the reading of Hamza and Al-Kisa'i, His servants, and it was interpreted as the prophets, may God bless them. And they frighten you with those besides Him, meaning the Quraysh, for they said to him, We fear that our gods will confuse you because you find fault with them. It was said that he sent Khalid to break Al-Uzza, but its keeper said to him, Beware of it, for it is very strong. So Khalid went to it and smashed its nose. Khalid's frightening was taken to the same level as his frightening, because he is the one who commands him to do what he fears for. And he whom God sends astray, until he forgets God's sufficiency for him and frightens him with what neither benefits nor harms. There is no guide for him, to guide him to the right path.
39:37: 37- And whomsoever God guides, there is none to misguide him. For there is no one to prevent His action, as He said: Is not God Exalted in Might? Victorious and Impregnable, Possessor of Retribution. Who takes revenge on His enemies.
39:38: 38- And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ This is because the proof of His uniqueness in creation is clear. Say, ‘Have you considered what you invoke besides God? If God intended to harm me, could they remove His harm?’ That is, after you have realized that the Creator of the universe is God, the Most High, and that your gods, if God intended to afflict me with harm, could they remove it? Or if He intended to bestow mercy upon me? “Can they withhold His mercy?” So He would withhold it from me? Abu Amr read Kashifaat Darah Mumasqiat Rahmatuh with the tanween in both of them and with the accusative of Darah and Rahmatuh. Say, ‘God is sufficient for me.’ This is sufficient for attaining good and repelling harm, since this statement establishes that He is the Able, and there is no obstacle to what He intends of good or evil. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them and they remained silent, so this was revealed. He only said, revealing and holding in reference to the femininity with which they describe her, as a warning of her complete weakness. On Him do those who rely rely, because they know that everything comes from Him, the Most High.
39:39: 39- “Say, ‘O my people, work according to your position.’ According to your position, a noun for place borrowed for the state as here and where from place borrowed for time. And it was read ‘your positions’ as ‘I am working’ meaning according to my position, so it was deleted for the sake of brevity and exaggeration in the threat, and to indicate that his state does not stop, for the Almighty increases his strength and victory over time, and for this reason He threatened them with being victorious over them in both abodes, so He said, ‘Then you will know.’”
39:40: 40- Whoever is afflicted with a torment that disgraces him then the disgrace of his enemies is evidence of his victory, and God disgraced them on the Day of Badr and a lasting torment will befall him is permanent, which is the torment of the Fire.
39:41: 41- Indeed, We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book for mankind for their sake, for it is the basis of their interests in this life and the hereafter. With the truth embracing it. So whoever is guided, it is for the benefit of himself because he benefits from it. And whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment for its consequences will not pass it by. And you are not a guardian over them and you were not entrusted with them to compel them to guidance. Rather, you were commanded to convey the message, and you have conveyed it.
39:42: 42- God takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die during their sleep meaning He takes them from the bodies by severing their connection to them and their control over them, either outwardly or inwardly, and that is at death, or outwardly but not inwardly, while in sleep. Then He keeps those for whom He has decreed death and does not return them to the bodies. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read qada with a damma on the qaf and a kasra on the dad, and al-mawt with a damma on the qaf, and al-mawt with a damma on the qaf, and al-mawt with a damma on the dammah... What was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: That in the son of Adam there is a soul and a spirit between them like the rays of the sun. The soul is the one with the intellect and discernment, and the spirit is the one with the soul and life. They both die at death, and the soul alone dies at sleep. This is close to what we have mentioned. Indeed in that of taking, withholding, and sending are signs indicating the perfection of His power and wisdom and the comprehensiveness of His mercy for a people who give thought to how it is attached to bodies and how He takes them away from them completely at death, and how He keeps them alive and does not perish with their perishing, and what befalls them of happiness and misery, and the wisdom in taking them away from their outward appearances and sending them from time to time until their appointed terms are fulfilled.
39:43: 43- Or have they taken - rather, the Quraysh have taken intercessors besides God to intercede for them with God Say, Even if they did not possess anything nor reason" - even if they were in this state as you see them, inanimate objects that do not have power or knowledge.
39:44: 44- “Say: To God belongs all intercession.” Perhaps this is a response to what they might answer with, which is that the intercessors are close people who are their images, and the meaning is that He is the Owner of all intercession, and no one can intercede except with His permission and approval, and he does not have it independently. Then He confirmed that: To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, for He is the Owner of all dominion, and no one has the right to speak about His affair without His permission and approval. Then to Him you will be returned on the Day of Resurrection, and the dominion will be His also then.
39:45: 45- And when God alone is mentioned without their gods the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter are filled with disgust “they contract and are repelled “and when those besides Him are mentioned” meaning the idols at once they rejoice due to their extreme infatuation with them and their forgetting the right of God. He has exaggerated in both matters until he reached the point of them, for rejoicing is when his heart is filled with joy until the skin of his face expands, and revulsion is when he is filled with sorrow until the skin of his face contracts, and the factor in when he is mentioned is the factor in when which is surprise.
39:46: 46- "Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed." Turn to God in supplication when you are confused about their situation and fed up with their stubbornness and the severity of their resentment, for He is capable of all things and knows all conditions. You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differ. You alone are able to judge between me and them.
39:47: 47- And if those who did wrong had all that is in the earth and as much more with it, they would offer it as ransom from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. A severe threat and complete despair for them of salvation. And there will appear to them from God that which they had not reckoned upon. An exaggeration in it and it is similar to the Almighty’s saying: No soul knows what has been hidden for them in the promise.
39:48: 48- And the evils of what they had earned will become apparent to them the evils of their deeds or what they had earned when their records are exposed. And that which they used to ridicule will overtake them and their recompense will encompass them.
39:49: 49- But when harm befalls man, he calls upon Us is an account of the genus in which it is predominant, and the conjunction with His statement and when God alone is mentioned with the letter fa is to show their contradiction and reversal in the causation, meaning that they are disgusted by the mention of God alone and are pleased by the mention of the gods, so when harm befalls them, they call upon those whose mention they are disgusted by, not those whose mention they are pleased by, and what is between them is an objection confirming the denial of that to them. Then when We bestowed upon him a favor from Us We gave it to him as a favor, for the bestowal is specific to him. He said, "It was only given to me because of knowledge from me regarding how he earned it, or that I will give it to him because I deserve it, or from God through me and because I deserve it, and the ha" in it is because it was made a relative pronoun, otherwise it is for the blessing and the masculine because what is meant is something of it. "Rather, it is a trial is a test for him, whether he will be grateful or ungrateful, and it is a rejection of what he said and the feminine pronoun is in consideration of the good or the word blessing, and it was read in the masculine form, but most of them do not know" that, and it is evidence that the human being is for the species.
39:50: 50- Those before them had said it. The ha' is for his saying, It was only given to me because of knowledge, because it is a word or a sentence. It was read in the masculine form. And those before them Qarun and his people, because he said it and his people were satisfied with it. So what they were earning did not avail them of worldly pleasures.
39:51: 51- So the evil of what they earned will befall them as a recompense for the evil of their deeds or as a recompense for their actions. He called it evil because it is in contrast to their evil deeds, a symbol that all their deeds are like that. And those who did wrong through rebellion among these polytheists. From is for clarification or for partiality. The evil of what they earned will befall them as it befell those, and it has befallen them. They were afflicted with a drought for seven years and their leaders were killed at Badr. And they will not escape by escaping.
39:52: 52- Do they not know that God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Where He withheld provision from them for seven days and then expanded it for them for another seven days. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe that all events are not mediated by God or other than Him.
39:53: 53- Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves’ They have gone too far in transgressing against themselves by going too far in sins. The addition of servants is specific to the believers, as is the custom of the Qur’an. Do not despair of the mercy of God Do not despair of His forgiveness first and His pardon second. Indeed, God forgives all sins pardon, even after a while. Restricting it to repentance is contrary to the apparent meaning, and its generality is indicated in everything except polytheism, as God the Most High says: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him. The explanation given by His saying: Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful is an exaggeration and indicates limitation and the promise of mercy after forgiveness, and presenting what calls for the generality of forgiveness from what is in My servants of the indication of humiliation and exclusivity that require mercy, and specifying the harm of extravagance to themselves and forbidding despair absolutely of mercy, let alone forgiveness, and its generality and explanation given by saying that God forgives all sins, and placing the name God in place of the pronoun to indicate that He is the Self-sufficient and the Bestower of favors absolutely and the emphasis is on all. And what was narrated that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: I would not like to have the world and everything in it for me, so a man said: O Messenger of God, and who associates partners with God? He was silent for a moment, then he said: And who associates partners with God? Three times.” And what was narrated that the people of Mecca said: Muhammad claims that whoever worships idols and kills a soul unjustly will not be forgiven, so how can we not have emigrated when we worship idols and kill a soul? So it was revealed. And it was said that Ayyash and Al-Walid were in a group who were tempted or in Al-Wahshi, which does not negate its generality. And likewise his saying:
39:54: 54- And turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you and then you will not be helped. This does not indicate that forgiveness will be granted to everyone without repentance and prior punishment, as this would make repentance and sincerity in action unnecessary and contradict the threat of punishment.
39:55: 55- And follow the best of what was revealed to you from your Lord the Qur'an, or what is commanded rather than what is forbidden, or the obligations rather than the dispensations, or the abrogating verse rather than the abrogated verse. Perhaps it is what is more saving and safer, such as repentance and perseverance in obedience. before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive of its coming, so that you may make up for it.
39:56: 56- To say 'self' is disliked, and it is indefinite to say self because the speaker is some of the souls, or for the sake of multiplication, like the saying of Al-A'sha: By the Lord of Baqi', if I shouted in its interior, a generous man would come to me shaking his head in anger. Oh, my regret and it was read with a ya according to the original on what I neglected by what I fell short in the side of God in His side, meaning in His right, which is His obedience. Sabeq Al-Barbari said: Do you not fear God while you are with a man who has a heart that is worthy of being cut off? It is a metaphor that contains exaggeration, as in his saying: Generosity, chivalry and generosity are in a dome that was erected on Ibn al-Hashraj. It was said in itself, on the assumption of an addition like obedience, and it was said in its proximity to the Almighty’s saying: and the companion at your side. And it was read in the remembrance of God, And if you were among the mockers, mocking his family, and the location of if you were is accusative in the state, as if he said I was careless and I was mocking.
39:57: 57- Or you say, 'If God had guided me, I would have been among the righteous.' With guidance to the truth, I would have been among the righteous.
39:58: 58- Or you say when you see the punishment, 'If only I had another chance so I could be among the doers of good' in belief and action, and the or is to indicate that she is not free from these statements of confusion and excuses for what is of no benefit.
39:59: 59- Yes, My signs did come to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers. This is a response from God to him because of what is included in his statement, If God had guided me, of a meaning of negation and separating it from it because presenting it separates the evidence and delaying the beloved disrupts the order of existence because he regrets his negligence, then makes excuses for losing guidance, then wishes to return. It does not prevent the effect of God’s power on the servant’s action, nor what is in it of attributing the action to Him, as you know, and the masculinity of the address is based on the meaning, and it was read with the feminine for the soul.
39:60: 60- And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God by describing Him with what is not permissible, such as taking a son. Their faces will be blackened by the hardship that befalls them or by the darkness of ignorance that is imagined for them. The sentence is a state, since it appears that it is seen by sight, and the pronoun was sufficient for it instead of the waw.
