It was said that it was revealed regarding the sick and the decrepit if they are unable to obey God, then a reward will be written for them according to the best of what they used to do.
41:9: 9- Say, 'Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days?' In the amount of two days, or two turns, and created in each turn what He created as quickly as possible. Perhaps what is meant by the earth is what is in the lower part of the simple bodies, and the One who created it in two days means that He created for it a common origin, then created for it images through which it became types. Their disbelief in Him is their denial of His essence and attributes. And you attribute to Him rivals. It is not correct that He has a rival. That is the One who created the earth in two days. "Lord of the worlds" is the Creator of all that exists of possibilities and their Sustainer.
41:10: 10- "And placed therein firm mountains is a resumption not connected to created" to separate from what is outside the connection. "Above it" is raised above it to show what aspects of insight it contains and to expose its benefits to the seekers. "And blessed it" and increased its goodness by creating in it all kinds of plants and animals. "And measured therein its sustenance" the sustenance of its people by specifying for each kind what it needs and by which it lives, or sustenance that arises from it by specifying the occurrence of each sustenance to one of its regions. It was read and divided its sustenance therein. "In four days" is the completion of four days, like saying: I traveled from Basra to Baghdad in ten days, and to Kufa in fifteen days. Perhaps he said that and did not say in two days to indicate their connection to the first two days. The statement is for brevity. "Equally" means equal in the sense of being level, and the sentence is an attribute of days, and this is indicated by Ya'qub's reading in the accusative case. It was said that it is a state of the pronoun in its sustenance or in it, and it was read in the nominative case as it is the same as for the questioners related to an omitted word, the meaning of which is this restriction for the questioners about the duration of the creation of the earth and what is in it, or about the amount of sustenance in it for those seeking it.
41:11: 11- Then He directed Himself to the heaven He meant something similar to what they say He directed Himself to such and such a place if He turned towards it without looking to any other place. It appears that there is a difference between the two creations, not a delay in time, as He said: And the earth after that He spread out and they spread it out as He created the mountains above it. And it was smoke is a dark command, and perhaps He meant by it its substance or the small parts from which He wrote. Then He said to it and to the earth, 'Bring' with what It created in you of influence and being influenced, and He revealed what It deposited in you of different situations and diverse beings. Or Bring in existence, on the basis that the previous creation means estimation or arrangement of rank, or information or the coming of the heaven to its occurrence and the coming of the earth to become spread out. You have known what is in it, or for each of you to come to the other in the occurrence of what is wanted from you, and this is supported by the reading of coming in conjunction, meaning each one her sister in what is wanted from you. Willingly or unwillingly whether you like it or not. What is meant is to demonstrate the perfection of His power and the necessity of His will being fulfilled, not to prove that they both are willing or unwilling. These two sources are used in the place of a state. They said, ‘We have come willingly’ submissive to the Self. What is more apparent is that what is meant is to depict the effect of His power upon them and their being affected by the Self from it, and to represent them as the command of the obeyed and the answer of the obedient. Indeed, the obedient is like His saying, Be and it is. What was said about the Most High addressing them and enabling them to answer can only be conceived of in the first and last ways. Rather, He said willingly in the sense that they were addressed, like His saying, prostrating.
41:12: 12- And He ordained them as seven heavens. He created them with a creative creation and perfected their affair. The pronoun refers to the heaven in meaning or is ambiguous, and seven heavens is a state of the first and a specification of the second. In two days. It was said that He created the heavens on Thursday and the moon and stars on Friday. And He revealed to each heaven its command. Its affair and what results from it, by making it bear it by choice or by nature. It was also said that He revealed to its inhabitants His commands and prohibitions. And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps. All the stars are seen as if they are shining on it. And as protection. That is, We preserved it from harm, or from stealers, as protection. It was also said that it is an object of the verb, meaning, as if He said: And We specified the lowest heaven with lamps as decoration and protection. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. The One who is perfect in power and knowledge.
41:13: 13- If they turn away from faith after this explanation. Say, 'I have warned you of a thunderbolt.' So he warned them that a severe punishment would befall them, like the thunderbolt of 'Aad and Thamud. A thunderbolt was also read, like the thunderbolt of 'Aad and Thamud, and it is the first time from the thunderbolt or the lightning bolt. It is said that the thunderbolt struck him with a thunderbolt, so he was struck with a thunderbolt.
41:14: 14- When the messengers came to them is a state of the thunderbolt of 'Aad, and it is not permissible to make it an attribute of thunderbolt or an adverbial of I warned you because the meaning is corrupted. From before them and from behind them they came to them from all sides and strove with them from every direction, or from the past tense by warning of what happened to the disbelievers, and from the future by warning of what is prepared for them in the Hereafter, and both expressions are permissible, or from before them and after them since the report of those who came before them reached them and Hud and Salih informed them about those who came after them calling to believe in all of them, and it is possible that it is an expression of abundance like the saying of the Most High: Its provision will come to it in abundance from every place. "That you worship none but God" that you worship not or that is, do not worship. "They said, 'If our Lord had willed'" to send messengers. "He sent down angels" with His message. "We are, in that with which you were sent," you claim. "disbelievers," since you are like us and have no superiority over us.
41:15: 15- As for 'Aad, they were arrogant upon the land without right. They acted arrogantly therein over its people without justification. And they said, 'Who is stronger than us?' Arrogant of their strength and power. It was said that their strength was such that a man among them could pull out a rock with his hand. Did they not see that God, who created them, was stronger than them in strength? In strength, for He is capable in and of Himself, able to do what is infinite, powerful over what no one else is capable of. And they used to deny Our signs. They knew that they were true but denied them, and this is an apodosis to they were arrogant.
41:16: 16- So We sent upon them a furious wind cold, destroying with its intense cold from sarr which is the cold that gathers, or very loud in its blowing from sara'r. In unlucky days plural of nahasa from nahas nahasa naqis sa'd sa'dan, and the two Hijazis and Basrans read it with sukoon for alleviation or description on the basis of fa'l, or description with the source, it was said that the end of Shawwal was from Wednesday to Wednesday and no people were punished except on Wednesday. That We may make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world He added the punishment to disgrace which is humiliation with the intention of describing it with it, for His saying: And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgraceful and it is originally an attribute of the punisher, but it was described with the punishment on the basis of the metaphorical attribution for the sake of exaggeration. And they will not be aided by the punishment being warded off from them.
41:17: 17- And as for Thamud, We guided them. We showed them the truth by establishing proofs and sending messengers. Thamud is read in the accusative case with an implied verb explained by what follows it, and with a tanween in both cases, and with a damma on the tha'. So they preferred blindness to guidance. They chose misguidance over guidance. So the thunderbolt of a humiliating punishment seized them. A thunderbolt from the sky destroyed them. Adding it to the punishment and describing it as humiliating is for emphasis. For what they were earning of choosing misguidance.
41:18: 18- And We saved those who believed and were fearing God from that thunderbolt.
41:19: 19- And the Day when the enemies of God will be gathered to the Fire. It was read Yahshur in the active form, which is God, the Almighty. Nafi’ read Nahshur with a fatha on the noon, a damma on the sheen, and the accusative of enemies. “They will be distributed” means the first of them will be held back by the last of them so that they will not disperse, and it is an expression for the large number of people in the Fire.
41:20: 20- Until when they come to it if they attend it, and what is added to confirm the connection of the testimony to the presence. Their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them as to what they used to do by God Almighty making it speak, or showing signs on it that indicate what was committed with it by the tongue of the situation.
41:21: 21- And they will say to their skins, 'Why did you bear witness against us?' A question of rebuke or astonishment, but perhaps what is meant by it is the same as astonishment. They will say, 'God has made us speak, Who has made everything speak.' That is, we did not speak of our own choice, rather God has made us speak, Who has made everything speak. Or is our speaking a wonder at the power of God, Who has made every living thing speak? If the answer had been interpreted as speaking by implication of the circumstance, the thing would have remained general in all possible beings. And He created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned. It is possible that this is the completion of the skins' speech or that it is a new chapter.
41:22: 22- And you were not concealing yourself lest your hearing, your sight, and your skins should testify against you. That is, you were concealing yourself from people when committing immoral acts for fear of disgrace, and you did not think that your limbs would testify against you, so you did not conceal yourself from them. This is a warning that the believer should realize that nothing passes him by except that He is watching him. But you thought that God did not know much of what you do. That is why you were embarrassed by what you did.
41:23: 23- And that refers to their assumption, and it is a subject. His saying, Your assumption which you assumed about your Lord has ruined you is two predicates for it. It is possible that your assumption is a substitute and ruined you is a predicate. So you became among the losers because what they were given to seek refuge in the two abodes became a cause of misery in the two homes.
41:24: 24- "If they are patient, the Fire will be their abode." There is no escape for them from it. "And if they seek repentance," they ask for repentance, which is to return to what they love. "They will not be among those who seek repentance. Those who are granted repentance are similar to what God Almighty says in the narration of Are we impatient or patient? There is no escape for us. And it was read, And if they seek repentance, they will not be among those who seek repentance," meaning if they ask to please their Lord, then they will not do so due to the loss of the ability.
41:25: 25- "And We have ordained" and destined. "For them" for the disbelievers. "Companions" are taken by the devils who seize them as one seizes an egg, which is its shell. It was said that the origin of "qayd" is the exchange and from it comes the bartering for opposition. "So they made attractive to them what is before them" of the worldly matter and the following of desires. "And what is behind them" of the matter of the Hereafter and its denial. "And the word has come into effect upon them" meaning the word of torment. "Among nations" among nations like the poet's saying: If you are not good at what you do, then others have already done it. It is a state of the genitive pronoun. Before them, there were jinn and humans, and they did the same deeds as them. Indeed, they were losers, is an explanation of why they deserved the punishment, and the pronoun refers to them and to nations.
41:26: 26- "And those who disbelieved said, 'Do not listen to this Qur'an and speak noisily during it.'" And they opposed it with superstitions or raised their voices with them to confuse the reader. It was read with a damma on the ghain and the meaning is the same. It is said that someone blabbers and that someone talks nonsense. "Perhaps you will overcome" meaning that you will overcome him in his recitation.
41:27: 27- Then We will make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment. What is meant by them are those who say it, or all the disbelievers. And We will recompense them for the worst of what they used to do. Their evil deeds, and something similar has come before.
41:28: 28- That: refers to the worst. The recompense of the enemies of God is its predicate. The Fire is an apposition to recompense or a deleted predicate. For them therein is in the Fire. The eternal home is their abode, and it is like saying: In this home is the home of pleasure, and by the home you mean the home itself, although the intended meaning is the description. A recompense for what they used to deny Our verses they denied the truth or they used to ignore it, and the mention of denial is the cause of the idle talk.
41:29: 29- And those who disbelieved will say, ‘Our Lord, show us those who misled us among the jinn and mankind.’ Meaning the two types of devils who lead us astray and disobey. It was said that they are Iblis and Cain, for they set the example of disbelief and murder. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Yaqub, Abu Bakr, and Al-Soussi read show us with a light thigh like thigh in thigh. Al-Duri read it with a shortened kasra on the ra. “We will place them under our feet” means we will trample them in revenge for them. It was also said that we will place them in the lowest depths. So that they will be among the lowest in place or humiliation.
41:30: 30- Indeed, those who have said, ‘Our Lord is God,’ acknowledging His Lordship and affirming His Oneness. Then they have remained steadfast in action. Then is because it is a gradual progression from acknowledgment in rank, as it is the beginning of steadfastness, or because it is a difficulty that rarely follows acknowledgment. What has been narrated from the Rightly-Guided Caliphs regarding the meaning of steadfastness in faith, sincerity in action, and performance of the obligatory duties are its details. The angels will descend upon them, as they see fit, to expand their chests and remove fear and sadness from them, or upon death or emerging from the grave. That you should not fear what you are about to do. And do not grieve over what you have left behind. And that is a verbal noun or a lightened noun understood by the letter ya or explanatory. And receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised in this world on the tongues of the Messengers.
41:31: 31- We are your allies in this worldly life We inspire you with the truth and urge you to do good instead of what the devils used to do to the disbelievers. Whatever your souls desire with intercession and honor when the disbelievers and their peers are at odds. And for you therein in the Hereafter is whatever your souls desire of pleasures. And for you therein is whatever you ask for whatever you wish of supplication in the sense of request, which is more general than the first.
41:32: 32- A lodging from a Forgiving, Most Merciful is a state of what you are asking for to indicate that what they wish for in relation to what they are given is something that would not occur to them, like a lodging for a guest.
41:33: 33- And who is better in speech than one who invites to God to His worship. And does righteousness between himself and his Lord. And says, Indeed, I am of the Muslims"" boasting about it and adopting Islam as a religion and a way of life, as they say: This is what so-and-so says about his way of life. The verse is general for whoever possesses these qualities. It was said that it was revealed about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was said about the muezzins.
41:34: 34- "And not equal are the good deed and the bad" in reward and good outcome. The second "la" is added to emphasize the negation. "Repel evil with that which is better" Repel the evil wherever it comes your way with that which is better than it, which is the good. The meaning of "better" is the absolute excess, or with the best of the good deeds that can repel it. It was brought out as a resumption as an answer to someone who said: What should I do? For emphasis. That is why "better" was put in place of the good. "Then he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend." That is, if you do that, your hostile enemy will become like a compassionate friend.
41:35: 35- And none shall receive it and none shall receive this characteristic, which is responding to evil with good. Except those who are patient for it prevents the soul from taking revenge. And none shall receive it except one of great portion of goodness and perfection of the soul. It has been said that portion is Paradise.
41:36: 36- And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan Nakhsa is likened to his whispering because it prompts a person to do what is not appropriate, such as repelling with something worse. The suggestion is made into a new way, or it is meant to be Naghzegh, describing Satan with the verbal noun. Then seek refuge in God from his evil and do not obey him. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing of your seeking refuge. The All-Knowing of your intention or your righteousness.
41:37: 37- “And among His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon.” Because they are two created things that are commanded just like you. And prostrate to God, who created them. The pronoun refers to the four mentioned, and the intention is to connect the action to them to indicate that they are among what He does not know and does not choose. If you worship Him. Prostration is the most specific of acts of worship, and it is the place of prostration according to us because the command is coupled with it. According to Abu Hanifa, it is at the end of the other verse because it completes the meaning.
41:38: 38- But if they are arrogant about complying. Then those who are with your Lord of the angels. glorify Him night and day that is, always, according to His saying. And they do not become weary that is, they do not get tired.
41:39: 39- And among His signs is that you see the earth still dry and submissive, borrowed from khushu’ meaning humility. But when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells is decorated and swells with plants. It is also read as rabba’at meaning it increases. Indeed, He who gives it life after its death “is the Giver of Life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent” of giving life and causing death.
41:40: 40- Indeed, those who deviate deviate from the right path. in Our verses by challenging, distorting, falsely interpreting and nullifying them. They are not hidden from Us so We will punish them for their deviance. Is he who is thrown into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? He contrasted being thrown into the Fire with coming secure, exaggerating the praise of the believers. Do whatever you will is a severe threat. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do is a warning of retribution.
41:41: 41- Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message when it came to them is a substitute for his saying: Indeed, those who blaspheme Our verses or it is a new sentence and the predicate of indeed is omitted like obstinate or perishing, or those are the ones who call and the message is the Qur’an. And indeed, it is a noble Book of great similar benefit or impregnable and it is not possible to nullify or distort it.
41:42: 42- Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it. Falsehood cannot approach it from any direction or from what it contains of past and future report. A revelation from the Wise. That is, the Wise. Praiseworthy. Every creature praises Him for the blessings He bestows upon them.
68:48: 43- What is said to you means what the unbelievers of your people say to you. Except what was said to the messengers before you except like what the unbelievers of their people said to them. It is also possible that the meaning is what God says to you except like what He said to them. Indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for His prophets. And the Possessor of painful punishment for their enemies. According to the second opinion, it is possible that what is said means that the sum of what was revealed to you and to them is the promise of forgiveness to the believers and punishment to the unbelievers. 48- So be patient over the decision of your Lord which is giving them respite and delaying your victory over them and do not be like the companion of the fish Jonah, peace be upon him. When he called in the belly of the fish. While he was choked with anger filled with rage and impatience, so you are tested by his trial.
41:44: 44- And if We had made it a foreign Qur'an. This is an answer to their saying: Why was the Qur'an not revealed in the language of the non-Arabs? The pronoun refers to the male. "They would have said: Why were its verses not explained in detail?" It was explained in a language that we understand. A foreigner and an Arab? The speech of a foreigner and the addressee is an Arab. This is a denial confirming the specificity. A foreigner is said of someone whose speech is not understood. This is the reading of Abu Bakr, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i. Qaloon and Abu Amr read it with elongation and simplification, Warsh with elongation and replacing the second with an alif, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Dhakwan and Hafs without elongation and simplifying the second, and it was read as ‘ajami’, which is attributed to the non-Arabs, and Hisham read ‘ajami’ as a statement. Based on this, it is possible that what is meant is: Why are its verses not separated, so that some of them are made foreign to make the non-Arabs understandable and some of them Arabic to make the Arabs understandable? The intention is to invalidate their suggestion by entailing the objection, or to indicate that they do not cease from the description in the verses however they come. “Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guidance’ to the truth and a healing for what is in the hearts of doubt and suspicion. ‘And those who do not believe’ is a subject and its predicate is ‘in their ears is deafness’ based on the estimation that it is in their ears is deafness, as He said, ‘And it is blindness to them’, due to their deafness to hearing Him and their turning a blind eye to what He shows them of signs. Whoever permits the conjunction of two different factors conjunctions that with ‘for those who believe, a guidance’. ‘Those are called from a distant place’ meaning deaf, and it is a metaphor for them in their not accepting the truth and not listening to it from someone who is a great distance away.
41:45: 45- And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, but there was disagreement about it regarding belief and denial, just as there was disagreement about the Qur’an. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord which is the promise of the Day of Resurrection and the settlement of disputes at that time, or the estimation of the appointed times. It would have been decided between them by the extermination of the deniers. And indeed, they and the Jews or those who do not believe “are in doubt about it” of the Torah or the Qur’an, disturbing causing confusion.
41:46: 46- "Whoever does righteousness, it benefits himself. And whoever does evil, it harms himself. And your Lord is not unjust to His servants." He does to them what He has no right to do.
41:47: 47- To Him is returned the knowledge of the Hour meaning if he is asked about it since no one knows it except Him. And what fruits emerge from their coverings from their vessels, the plural of kam is in the kasra. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, and Hafs read min thmarat in the plural due to the difference in types. It was also read with the plural of the pronoun, and ma is negative and the first min is added for the sake of completeness. It is possible that it is a relative pronoun conjoined with the Hour and min is clarifying, unlike His statement: And no female conceives or gives birth in a place. Except with His knowledge except coupled with His knowledge, actually according to its connection to it. And the Day He will call to them, Where are My partners? according to your claim? They will say, We have informed you. "There is not from us a witness" from anyone who testifies to their partnership since we have disavowed them and witnessed the situation, so the question about them is for the sake of rebuke, or from anyone who witnesses them because they have gone astray from us. It was said that it is the partners’ statement, meaning that none of us can testify that they were right.
41:48: 48- "And what they used to call upon has vanished from them" they worship. "Before" it does not benefit them or they do not see it. "And they assumed" and were certain. "They have no escape" an escape and the assumption is suspended from it by the letter of negation.
41:49: 49- Man does not get tired does not get bored. From supplicating for good from asking for abundance in blessings, and it was read from supplicating for good. And if evil touches him narrowness. He despairs of God’s grace and mercy. This is a characteristic of the disbeliever, as He said: Indeed, no one despairs of relief from God except the disbelieving people. And he may be infatuated with his despair in terms of structure and repetition, and what is in despair of the appearance of the effect of despair.
41:50: 50- And if We let him taste mercy from Us after a hardship has befallen him by relieving him of it. He will surely say, 'This is mine,' my right, which I deserve because of my virtue and deeds, which are always due and will never end. And I do not think the Hour will ever come. "And if I return to my Lord, I will have with Him the best." That is, if it comes based on imagination, then I will have with God the best state of honor, because he believes that the blessings of this world that befell him were due to his deserving them and that he will never be separated from them. "We will surely inform those who disbelieve, We will inform them, of what they did," the reality of their deeds, and We will make them see the opposite of what they believed in them. "And We will surely make them taste a severe punishment," which they will not be able to investigate.
41:51: 51- And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away from giving thanks. And distances himself and deviates from it or goes away with himself and distances himself from it completely out of arrogance. The side is a metaphor for the soul, like the side in His statement: on the side of God. "And if evil touches him, then he is full of abundant supplication" Abundant, borrowed from something that has an extensive width to indicate its abundance and continuity. It is more expressive than long, since length is two extensions. So if its width is like that, then what do you think of its length?
41:52: 52- “Say, ‘Have you considered?’ Tell me. ‘If it is,’ meaning the Qur’an, ‘from God, and then you disbelieved in it,’ without considering or following any evidence. ‘Who is more astray than he who is in extreme dissension?’” meaning, who is more astray than you? The relative pronoun was placed in place of the pronoun to explain their condition and justify their further misguidance.
41:53: 53- "We will show them Our signs in the horizons" meaning what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had informed them of of upcoming events and the effects of past calamities, and what God facilitated for him and his successors of conquests and victory over the kingdoms of the East and the West in an extraordinary manner. "And within themselves" what appeared among the people of Mecca and what happened to them, or what is in the human body of wonders of creation that indicate the perfection of power. "Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth" the pronoun refers to the Qur’an, or the Messenger, or monotheism, or God. "And is not your Lord sufficient? meaning, Or is your Lord not sufficient? The fa" is added for emphasis as if it was said: "Or is sufficiency not achieved through Him? It is rarely added to the subject except with sufficiency. He is a Witness over all things" is a substitute for it, and the meaning is: Is it not enough for you that the Most High is a Witness over all things, fulfilling them and fulfilling your command by revealing the promised signs as He fulfilled all the promised things, or is He All-Knowing and knows your condition and their condition, or is it not enough for man to be deterred from sins that the Most High is All-Knowing over all things and nothing is hidden from Him?
41:54: 54- Indeed, they are in doubt doubt, and it is read with the dammah, which is a language like hidden and hidden. Indeed, He is, over all things, encompassing of the resurrection and the reward. “Indeed, He is, over all things, knowing the totality of things and their details, and is capable of them, nothing of them escapes Him. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Whoever recites Surat As-Sajdah, God will give him ten good deeds for every letter.”
42:2: 2- "`Ain Qaf" may be two names for the surah, and that is why they were separated and two verses were added. If they were one name, the separation was to match the rest of the Ha-Mim letters, and it was read as Ha-Mim-Saq.
42:3: 3- Thus does God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise, reveal to you and to those before you. That is, like what is in this Surah of meanings, or a revelation like its revelation was revealed to you and to the messengers before you. It was mentioned in the present tense as a narration of the past situation to indicate the continuity of the revelation and that revelation like it is his custom. Ibn Kathir read yuhashu with the fat-ha so that thus is the subject and yuhashu is its predicate attributed to its pronoun, or a source and yuhashu is attributed to you, and God is raised by what is indicated by yuhashu, and the Exalted in Might, the Wise are two of His attributes that are established due to the high status of the one revealed as mentioned in the previous Surah, or by the beginning as in the reading nuha with the nun and the Exalted and what follows are predicates or the Exalted in Might are two attributes. And his saying:
42:4: 4- To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great. These are two pieces of report for Him, and in other respects they are a resumption of His glory and wisdom.
42:5: 5- The heavens almost Nafi' and Al-Kisa'i read it with a ya'. They burst means they are cracked from the majesty of God, and it was said from claiming a son for Him. The two Basrans and Abu Bakr read it with a noon, and the first is more expressive because it is the passive participle of fatarah, and this is the passive participle of fatarah. It was read with a ta' to emphasize the feminine, and this is rare. From above them means the bursting begins from their upper side, and it was specified according to the first because the greatest signs and most indicative of the loftiness of His status are from that side, and according to the second to indicate the bursting from beneath them in the first way. It was said that the pronoun refers to the earth, as what is meant by it is the genus. And the angels exalt [God] with praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on the earth by striving to attain their forgiveness through intercession, inspiration, and the preparation of means that bring one closer to obedience. This generally includes both believers and disbelievers. Indeed, if seeking forgiveness were interpreted as meaning striving to remove an expected defect, it would include animals and even inanimate objects. Since it is specific to believers, what is meant by it is intercession. Unquestionably, it is God who is the Forgiving, the Merciful since there is no creature except that it has a share of His mercy. The verse, in the first case, is a further confirmation of His greatness, and in the second case, it is an indication of His holiness from what is attributed to Him. The fact that they were not punished hastened for that heinous word is due to the angels’ seeking forgiveness and the greatness of God’s forgiveness and mercy.
42:6: 6- And those who have taken protectors besides Him partners and equals. God is a Guardian over them Watching over their conditions and deeds and rewarding them for them. And you O Muhammad are not a guardian over them One who is entrusted with them or one whose affair is entrusted to you.
42:7: 7- "And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an The reference is to the source of inspires or to the meaning of the previous verse, as it is repeated in the Qur'an in many places, so the kaf is the direct object and an Arabic Qur'an" is a state of it. "That you may warn the Mother of Cities" The people of the Mother of Cities, which is Mecca, may God Almighty honor it. "And those around it" Of the Arabs. "And warn of the Day of Assembly" The Day of Resurrection, on which all creation, or spirits, or ghosts, or workers and deeds will be gathered. The second object of the first and the first two objects of the second were omitted for emphasis and to obscure the generalization. It was read "to warn" with the ya and the verb for the Qur'an. "There is no doubt about it" An objection that has no syntactic position. A group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze meaning that after they are gathered at the gathering place, they will be gathered first and then dispersed. The meaning is a group and the pronoun refers to those gathered because the gathering indicates it. They were read in the accusative case as a state of them meaning and you will warn of the Day of their gathering, dispersed, meaning on the verge of dispersion, or dispersed in the abode of reward and punishment.
42:8: 8- "And if God had willed, He could have made them one nation" guided or astray. "But He admits whom He wills into His mercy" by guidance and urging them to obey. "And the wrongdoers will have no protector or helper" meaning He will leave them without a protector or helper in His punishment. Perhaps the change in the contrast is to exaggerate the threat, as the speech is about warning.
42:9: 9- Or have they taken Rather, they have taken. besides Him protectors such as idols. Then God is the protector is an answer to an omitted condition, such as if they meant protectors in truth, then God is the protector in truth. And He gives life to the dead, and He is over all things competent as a confirmation of His being truly protectors.
42:10: 10- And whatever you differ over you and the disbelievers. of anything of worldly or religious matters. The judgment thereof is with God entrusted to Him. He distinguishes the truthful from the false by victory or by reward and punishment. And it was said, And whatever you differ over of ambiguous interpretation, refer it to the definitive part of God's Book. That is God, my Lord; in Him I have relied in the complexities of matters. And to Him I turn to Him I return in difficult matters.
42:11: 11- "The Creator of the heavens and the earth is another predicate for that" or a subject whose predicate is its predicate. "He made for you and it was read in the accusative case as a substitute for the pronoun or description of to God". "From yourselves" is from your kind. "Women" is women. "And from the livestock, wives" meaning, He created for the livestock from their kind, or He created for you from the livestock types or males and females. "He multiplies you is from dhar' which is spreading, and in its meaning are scattering and scattering and the pronoun in the first case refers to people, and the livestock" is to make the rational ones addressed predominantly. "In it" in this management, which is making people and livestock have offspring between them, so it is like a source for spreading and multiplying. "There is nothing like Him" means there is nothing like Him that can match or be compatible with Him. What is meant by "like Him" is His essence, as in their saying: "The likes of you cannot do such-and-such," with the intention of exaggerating in negating it from Him, because if it is negated from someone who is compatible with Him and takes his place, then it is more appropriate to negate it from Him. Similar to this is the saying of Ruqayqah bint Saifi about giving water to Abd al-Muttalib: "Behold, among them is the pure and good in and of itself. Whoever said that the kaf is redundant in it perhaps meant that it gives the meaning of there is nothing like Him," but it is more emphatic for what we have mentioned. It was said that "like Him" is His description, meaning there is no description like His description. "And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing" of everything that He hears and sees.
42:12: 12- To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth their treasuries. He expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it He expands and restricts it according to His will. Indeed, He is Knowing of all things He does it as it should be.
42:13: 13- He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. That is, He has ordained for you of religion the religion of Noah and Muhammad, peace be upon them, and what came between them of masters of religions. It is the common foundation between them, which is explained by His statement: Establish the religion. It is belief in what must be believed and obedience in the rulings of God. Its place is in the accusative case as a substitute for the object of He enjoined, or in the nominative case as a resumption as if it were an answer to what is that which is enjoined, or in the genitive case as a substitute for the ha of it. And do not be divided therein. And do not differ regarding this foundation. As for the branches of the religions, they are different, as He said: To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. "Grief upon the polytheists" is difficult for them. "What you call them to" of monotheism. "God chooses for Himself whom He wills. He brings to Himself," and the pronoun refers to what you call them to or to the religion. "And guides to it" by allusion and guidance. "Whoever repents" will be accepted.
42:14: 114- And they did not become divided means the previous nations. It was said that they were the People of the Book, because of His statement: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them knowledge that division is a threatened misguidance, or knowledge of the mission of the Messengers, peace and blessings be upon them, or the causes of knowledge from the Messengers, the Books, and other things, but they did not pay attention to them. Out of jealous animosity between themselves enmity or seeking worldly gain. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord regarding respite. Until a specified term which is the Day of Resurrection or the end of their allotted lives. It would have been judged between them by the extermination of the wrongdoers when they committed, due to the enormity of what they committed. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them means the People of the Scripture who were during the time of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, or the polytheists who were given the Qur'an after the People of the Scripture. It was read inherited and inherited. In doubt about it from their book, they do not know it as it is or they do not believe in it as it should be, or from the Qur’an. Suspicious is disturbing or causing doubt.
42:15: 15- Therefore Therefore, for that reason, the division, or the Book, or the knowledge that you have been given. So call to agreement on the Hanafi religion or following what you have been given. Based on this, it is permissible for the lam to be in the place of ila to indicate connection and causation. And stand firm as you are commanded and stand firm in the call as God the Most High has commanded you. And do not follow their desires the false ones. And say, 'I have believed in what God has revealed of the Book' meaning all the revealed books, not like the disbelievers who believed in some and disbelieved in others. And I have been commanded to be just between you in conveying the laws and governments. The first is an indication of the perfection of theoretical power, and this is an indication of the perfection of practical power. God is our Lord and your Lord the Creator of all and the One in charge of its affairs. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds and each will be rewarded for his deeds. There is no argument between us and you and there is no argument between us and you means no dispute, as the truth has become clear and there is no room for argument and no basis for disagreement except stubbornness. God will gather us together on the Day of Resurrection. And to Him is the final destination is the return of all for the final judgment. There is nothing in the verse that indicates abandoning the disbelievers completely, such that it would have been abrogated by the verse on fighting.
42:16: 16- And those who dispute about God about His religion. After it has been answered after the people responded to him and entered into it, or after God responded to His Messenger and made His religion manifest with His victory on the Day of Badr, or after the People of the Scripture responded to him by acknowledging his prophethood and seeking victory through him. Their argument is worthless before their Lord vanishing and false. And upon them is wrath for their obstinacy. And for them is a severe punishment for their disbelief.
42:17: 17- God is He Who sent down the Book is the type of Book. With the truth is ambiguous and far from falsehood, or with what is right to be sent down of beliefs and rulings. And the Balance is the law by which rights are weighed and people are treated equally, or justice by sending down the command with it or the weighing instrument by inspiring its preparation. And what makes you know? Perhaps the Hour is near its coming, so follow the Book and act according to the law and persevere in justice before the Day surprises you when your deeds are weighed and you are given your reward. It was said that the word near is mentioned because it means near, or because the Hour means resurrection.
42:18: 18- Those who do not believe in it are hastening it in mockery. And those who believe are fearful of it fearful of it while backbiting it in anticipation of reward. And they know that it is the truth meaning that it will inevitably happen. Behold, those who dispute about the Hour argue about it from doubt, or from the camel’s udder being stroked vigorously for milking because each of the disputants extracts what is in the other’s mind with harsh speech. are in extreme error from the truth, for the Resurrection is most similar of the unseen to the tangible. So whoever is not guided to its possibility is further from being guided to what is beyond it.
42:19: 19- God is Kind to His servants with their Lord with kinds of goodness that are beyond the comprehension. He provides for whom He wills that is, He provides for him as He wills, so He distinguishes each of His servants with a kind of goodness according to what His wisdom requires. And He is the Strong with dazzling power. The Mighty with impregnable power.
42:20: 20- Whoever desires the cultivation of the Hereafter its reward is likened to sowing in that it is a benefit obtained through work. That is why it is said: This world is the farm of the Hereafter. Sowing is originally sowing seeds in the ground and it is said of the sowing that results from it, We will give him an increase in his cultivation, so we give him ten for one to seven hundred and above. Whoever desires the cultivation of this world, We will give him thereof something of it according to what We have apportioned for him. And he will have no share in the Hereafter, because actions are by intentions and each person will have what he intended.
42:21: 21- "Or do they have partners?" Rather, they have inspired partners. The hamza is for confirmation and rebuke. Their partners are their devils. "They have legislated for them" by embellishing. "In religion that which God has not permitted" such as polytheism, denial of resurrection, and working for the world. It was said that their partners are their idols, and they are attributed to them because they have taken them as partners, and the law is attributed to them because they are the cause of their misguidance and their temptation with what they follow, or images from their tradition. "And were it not for the decisive word" meaning the previous decree to postpone the recompense, or the promise that the decision would be on the Day of Resurrection. "The matter would have been judged between them" between the disbelievers and the believers, or the polytheists and their partners. "And indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment. It was read an with a fat-ha in apposition to the word the decisive word meaning And were it not for the decisive word" and the estimation of the punishment of the wrongdoers in the Hereafter, it would have been judged between them in this world, for the painful punishment is predominant in the punishment of the Hereafter.
42:22: 22- You will see the wrongdoers on the Day of Resurrection. fearful afraid. of what they have earned of evil deeds. And it will befall them meaning, its consequences will overtake them, they feared. And those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the gardens of Paradise in the best and most pleasant places therein. They will have whatever they wish with their Lord meaning, whatever they desire is established for them with their Lord. That refers to the believers. That is the great bounty compared to which what others have in this world will be insignificant.
42:23: 23- That is what God gives good tidings of to His servants who have believed and done righteous deeds. That is the reward with which God gives them good tidings. So the preposition and the pronoun were omitted, or that is the good tidings with which God gives good tidings to His servants. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read yubashir min basharahu and it was read yubashir min absharahu. "Say, 'I do not ask of you for it,'" for what I do of conveying the message and giving good tidings. "Any benefit from you, except love for my kinship." That is, love my kinship. It was said that the exception is disjunctive and the meaning is: I do not ask of you any reward at all, but I ask of you love. "For my kinship is a state of it, that is, except love is established for those relatives, established in its people, or in the right of kinship and for its sake, as came in the hadith, Love for the sake of God and hatred for the sake of God." It was narrated that when this verse was revealed, it was said: O Messenger of God, who are these your relatives whose love is obligatory upon us? He said: Ali, Fatima, and their two sons. It was also said that relatives means drawing closer to God, meaning that you should love God and His Messenger by drawing closer to Him through obedience and righteous deeds. It was also read as except for love in kinship. “And whoever does a good deed” means whoever is recorded as doing an act of obedience, especially loving the family of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). It was also said that it was revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him and his love for them. We will increase for him therein good means doubling the reward. It was also read as He will increase meaning God will increase in goodness. Indeed, God is Oft-Forgiving to those who sin. Appreciative to those who obey by giving them the full reward and favoring them with an increase.
42:24: 24- Or do they say, rather, do they say, He has fabricated a lie against God, Muhammad fabricated a lie by claiming prophethood or the Quran. If God wills, He will seal your heart, to exclude such a fabrication by indicating that only someone whose heart is sealed and ignorant of his Lord would dare to do it. As for someone who has insight and knowledge, no. It is as if he said: If God wills to abandon you, He will seal your heart so that you would dare to fabricate against Him. It was said that He will seal your heart by withholding the Quran or the revelation from it, or by tying it down with patience so that their harm will not be difficult for you. “And God effaces falsehood and establishes the truth with His words. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.” This is a resumption of the denial of the fabrication of what he says, that if it were fabricated, He would have effaced it, since it is His habit, the Most High, to efface falsehood and establish the truth with His revelation, or His judgment, or His promise, by effacement of their falsehood and establishing His truth with the Qur’an, or with His judgment that cannot be reversed. The waw is omitted from efface in some copies of the Qur’an to follow the wording, as in the saying of the Most High: And He calls man to evil.
42:25: 25- And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants by overlooking what they have repented from. Acceptance is transitive with a second object with min and an to include the meaning of taking and clarifying. You have already known the reality of repentance. On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: It is a noun that has six meanings: regret for past sins, repetition for neglecting obligatory duties, returning wrongs, dissolving the soul in obedience as you raised it in disobedience, making it taste the bitterness of obedience as you made it taste the sweetness of disobedience, and crying instead of every laughter. And He pardons misdeeds, small and great, for whomever He wills. And He knows what you do, so He rewards and overlooks with perfection and wisdom. The Kufians other than Abu Bakr read what you do with a ta'.
42:26: 26- "And those who believe and do righteous deeds will respond meaning that God will respond to them, so the lam was omitted as it was omitted in and when they measure them", and what is meant is the response to the supplication or the reward for obedience, as it is like a supplication and a request for what results from it. And from this is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "The best supplication is praise be to God", or they respond to God with obedience if He calls them to it. "And He will increase them from His bounty" over what they asked for and deserved and were entitled to from Him by the response. "And for the disbelievers is a severe punishment" instead of what the believers have of reward and bounty.
42:27: 27- And if God were to expand the provision for His servants, they would surely rebel upon the earth They would have become arrogant and spread corruption therein out of insolence, or some of them would have rebelled against others out of dominance and haughtiness. This is most likely the case, and the root of rebellion is to seek to exceed the measure in what one seeks in quantity or quality. But He sends down in measure by estimation. What He wills as His will requires. Indeed, He is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of His servants He knows the hidden aspects of their affair and the apparent aspects of their condition, so He decrees for them what suits their condition. It was narrated that the people of the Suffa wished for wealth, so this was revealed. It was said that the Arabs used to fight each other when their land was fertile, and they used to migrate when it was barren.
42:28: 28- And it is He who sends down the rain the rain that relieves them from drought, and that is why it is specifically used to mean beneficial. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read it with emphasis. After they despaired they lost hope in it, and it was also read with a kasra on the noon. And spreads His mercy in everything, from plains and mountains, plants and animals. And He is the Protector the One who takes care of His servants with His kindness and spreading His mercy. The Praiseworthy the One who is deserving of praise for that.
42:29: 29- And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth for they, in themselves and their attributes, indicate the existence of a Creator, capable and wise. And what He has dispersed throughout them is in apposition to the heavens, the creation. “Of the moving creature” is of the living, by applying the name of the effect to the cause, or of what creeps on the earth and whatever is in one of the two things, it is true that it is in it in the sentence. And He has power to gather them when He wills meaning at any time He wills. Able is able to do it, and if as it is used with the past tense, it is used with the present tense.
42:30: 30- And whatever strikes you of disaster is for what your hands have earned is because of your sins, and the fa is because ma is conditional or includes its meaning, and Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir did not mention it because of the meaning of causation in the ba’. And He pardons many of the sins and does not punish for them. The verse is specific to the criminals, as what befalls others is for other reasons, including exposing them to a great reward for being patient with it. 7- So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it.
42:31: 31- And you will not escape on earth and will escape the calamities that have been decreed for you. And you will not have besides God any protector to protect you from them. And no helper to ward them off from you.
42:32: 32- And among His signs are the ships that sail the ships. in the sea like mountains like mountains. Al-Khansa' said: And Sakhr is the one whom the guides follow, as if he were a flag with fire on its head.
42:33: 33- If He wills, He can still the wind. And it was read as the winds. "So they remain motionless on its back." So they remain fixed on the back of the sea. "Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful person." For everyone who devotes his efforts and confines himself to contemplating the signs of God and reflecting on His blessings, or for every believer who has complete faith, for faith is two halves: half patience and half gratitude.
42:34: 34- Or He destroys them or He ruins them by sending a violent, overwhelming wind. What is meant is the destruction of its people, as God Almighty says: Because of what they have earned. Its root is or He sends it and destroys them because it is a definite noun that calms down, so it was restricted to what is intended, as in God Almighty's saying: And pardons many. The meaning is, Or He sends it and destroys people for their sins and saves people because of His pardoning them. It was read and He pardons as a new reading.
42:35: 35- "And He knows those who dispute about Our verses is in apposition to an implied cause such as to take revenge on them and to know", or to the reward. The accusative case is the accusative of the real object in proximity to the six things because it is also not obligatory. Nafi' and Ibn Amir read it in the nominative case as a resumption, and it was read in the jussive case in apposition to "he forgives" so the meaning is that He combines the destruction of a people and the salvation of a people and the warning of others. "For them is a refuge" is a refuge from the punishment and the verb is suspended from the sentence.
42:36: 36- Whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of worldly life You will enjoy it for the duration of your life. And what is with God of the reward of the Hereafter is better and more lasting for those who have believed and upon their Lord rely because of its pure benefit and permanence. The first ma is a relative pronoun that includes the meaning of a condition in that giving what they have been given is a reason for enjoying it in worldly life, so the fa came as its answer, unlike the second. On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, gave all of his money in charity, so he blamed him for gathering it, so the verse was revealed.
42:37: 37- And those who avoid major sins and immoralities, and when they become angry, they forgive. "And those with what follows is in apposition to those who believe or praise in the accusative or nominative case, and the construction of forgive on their pronoun as report to indicate that they are the ones who are specifically forgiven in the accusative case, and Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read major sin."
42:38: 38- And those who responded to their Lord was revealed about the Ansar. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to faith and they responded to him. And they establish prayer and their affairs are conducted by consultation among themselves Those who consult among themselves do not have a single opinion until they consult each other and agree upon it, and that is due to their extreme deliberation and vigilance in matters. It is a verbal noun like fatwa meaning consultation. And from what We have provided them they spend in the way of God, the good.
42:39: 39- And those who, when they are wronged, defend themselves based on what God has made for them, the hatred of humiliation, and it is their description of the inability of the forgiven with all the mothers of virtues, and it does not contradict their description of forgiveness, as it indicates the inability of the forgiven and the victorious to resist the opponent, and patience with the helpless is praiseworthy and with the victorious is blameworthy because it is a procedure and an enticement to the wrong, then after their description of victory to prevent the aggression.
42:40: 40- And the recompense for an evil act is an evil act like it. He called the second evil because of the duality, or because it harms the one who suffers from it. “But whoever pardons and makes peace” between himself and his enemy. His reward is due from God is a vague phrase indicating the enormity of the promise. Indeed, He does not like the wrongdoers who initiate evil and transgress in taking revenge.
42:41: 41- And for he who retaliates after being wronged after he was wronged, and it was read as such. There is no way against them with reprimand and punishment.
42:42: 42- The path is only against those who wrong people who begin by harming them and demanding what they do not deserve out of force against them. “And transgress upon the earth without right. Those will have a painful punishment” for their injustice and transgression.
42:43: 43- And for he who is patient in the face of harm. And forgives and does not retaliate. Indeed, that is of the matters of determination. That is, that is from him, so it was deleted as it was deleted in their saying: Butter is worth two dirhams, because of knowledge of it.
42:44: 44- "And he whom God sends astray - for him there is no protector after Him." No helper to take care of him after God has abandoned him. "And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment," when they see it, so it was mentioned in the past tense for emphasis. "They will say, 'Is there any way back?'" Is there any way back to this world?
42:45: 45- And you will see them exposed to it the Fire, and the punishment indicates it. Humbled by humiliation submissive and shrinking from the humiliation that will befall them. They will look from the corner of their eyes meaning their gaze will begin at the Fire with the movement of their eyelids, weak like someone who is patient looking at a sword. And those who believed will say, 'Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families' by exposing them to eternal punishment. On the Day of Resurrection is an adverbial phrase for lost and the statement is in this world, or he would have said, meaning they would say when they saw them in that state. Indeed, the wrongdoers will be in a lasting punishment is the completion of their statement or a confirmation from God for them.
42:46: 46- "And they had no protectors to help them other than God. And he whom God sends astray has no way" to guidance or salvation.
42:47: 47- Respond to your Lord before there comes a Day from God that cannot be repelled. God will not repel it after He has decreed it. Min is a conjunction to mard. It was said that it is a conjunction to ya’ti meaning before a Day comes from God that cannot be repelled. You will have no refuge is an escape. On that Day, you will have no denunciation is a denunciation of what you have done because it is recorded in your books of deeds, your tongues will bear witness to it, and your judgment will prevail.
42:48: 48- But if they turn away, then We have not sent you over them as a guardian an observer or an accountant. Your responsibility is only to convey the message and I have conveyed it. And indeed, when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it He meant by man the entire species, as He said: And if evil befalls them for what their hands have put forth, then indeed, man is ungrateful He is extremely ungrateful, forgetting the blessing completely, remembering the calamity and magnifying it, without considering its cause. Although this is specific to criminals, it is permissible to attribute it to the entire species due to their prevalence and inclusion in it. The first conditional clause is prefaced with if and the second with in because tasting the blessing is certain in that it is a habit inherently required, unlike the occurrence of a calamity. The cause of the recompense is established in its place and the apparent is placed in the place of the implicit in the second to indicate that this species is characterized by ingratitude.
42:49: 49- To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. So He has the power to divide blessings and calamities as He wishes. He creates what He wills without any need or room for objection. He gives to whom He wills female [children] and He gives to whom He wills males.
42:50: 50- Or He pairs them with males and females and makes whom He wills barren instead of He creates instead of some, and the meaning is that He makes the conditions of the servants with regard to children different according to the will, so He gives some either one type of male or female or both types and He makes others barren. Perhaps the females were presented first because they are more numerous to increase the offspring, or because the context of the verse is to indicate that the reality is related to the will of God and not the will of man, and the same applies to females, or because the speech is about calamity and the Arabs consider them a calamity, or to please the hearts of their fathers or to preserve the intervals and for this reason He specified the males, or to make up for the delay and change the conjunction in the third because it is the division of what is common between the two parts, and the fourth is not needed because it is eloquent that it is the division of what is common between the previous parts. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent so He acts with wisdom and choice.
42:51: 51- And it is not for a human being and it is not valid for him that God should speak to him except by revelation hidden speech that is understood quickly because it is a representation that is not in itself composed of disconnected letters that depend on successive waves, which is what is common to all people as narrated in the hadith of the Ascension, and what was promised in the hadith of the vision and the one who was called out to as happened to Moses in Tuwa and at the Mount, but the connection of His saying: or from behind a veil to it makes it specific to the first, so the verse is evidence of the permissibility of the vision, not of its impossibility. It was said that what is meant by it is inspiration and casting into the mind or the revelation sent down by the angel to the messengers, so what is meant by his saying, Or He sends a messenger who reveals by His permission what He wills is or He sends to him a prophet who conveys His revelation as He commanded him. According to the first opinion, what is meant by the messenger is the angel who reveals to the messengers, and revelation with what is conjoined to it is in the accusative case as a verbal noun because from behind a veil is a description of omitted speech, and sending is a type of speech. It is possible for it to be a revelation and send two verbal nouns, and from behind a veil is a circumstance that occurred as conditions. Nafi’ read or sends by raising the lam, He is exalted over the attributes of created beings. Wise does what His wisdom requires, so He speaks sometimes through an intermediary and sometimes without an intermediary, either clearly or from behind a veil.
42:52: 52- And thus We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], a spirit of Our command meaning what was revealed to him, and He called it a spirit because hearts are revived by it. It was also said that it was Gabriel, and the meaning is that We sent him to you with the revelation. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was meaning before the revelation, and this is evidence that he was not worshipping. It was said that prophethood was based on a law. It was also said that what is meant is belief in something that has no way to it except by hearing. But We made it meaning the spirit, the Book, or faith a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants by granting success in accepting and considering it. And indeed, you guide to a straight path which is Islam. It was read to be guided meaning that God guides you. 38- On the Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is right. This is a confirmation and emphasis of His statement, they do not possess, for if these people, who are the best of creation and the closest to God, are not able to speak what is right, such as intercession for whomever He is pleased with, except with His permission, then how can anyone other than them possess it? On the Day is a circumstance of they do not possess, or of they speak, and the Spirit is an angel assigned to the spirits or their kind, or Gabriel, peace be upon him, or a creation greater than the angels.
42:53: 53- The path of God instead of the first. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth in creation and dominion. Unquestionably, to God do all matters return with the removal of intermediaries and attachments, and in it is a promise and a threat to the obedient and the criminals. On the authority of the Prophet, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, Whoever recites Ha Mim Ain Sin Qaf will be among those upon whom the angels pray, seek forgiveness for him, and ask mercy for him.
43:3: 3- Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur’an. He swears by the Qur’an that He has made it an Arabic Qur’an. This is one of the most beautiful examples of the consistency between the oath and the thing sworn to, as in the saying of Abu Tammam: Your folds are a purpose Perhaps God’s swearing by things is evidence of what they contain in terms of what is sworn by, and of the Qur’an in terms of it being a miracle that clarifies the paths of guidance and what is needed in religion, or He explained to the Arabs what indicates that He, the Most High, made it thus so that you may understand so that you may understand its meanings. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 26 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Zukh'ruf, and the first verses of Sūrat Muḥammad. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time.
