43:4: 4- And indeed is in apposition to Indeed, and Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra as a new sentence. In the Mother of the Book is in the Preserved Tablet, for it is the origin of the heavenly books, and the Mother of the Book was read with a kasra. With Us is preserved with Us from being changed. For Ali is of high status among the books because it is a miracle among them. Wise is of profound wisdom, or definitive and cannot be abrogate by anything else. They are two pieces of report because in the Mother of the Book is connected to For Ali and the lam does not prevent it, or it is a state of it, and With Us is a substitute for it or a state of The Mother of the Book.
43:5: 5- Shall We turn away from you the Reminder? Shall We turn away from you and keep it away from you? This is a metaphor for their saying: He turned away the strange things from the pool. Tarafa said: I will strike away your worries, I will strike you with the sword, Qanus Al-Fars The letter fa is for conjunction with something omitted, meaning they neglected you, so we would turn away from you the remembrance. “Safhan” is a verbal noun from a different wording, for removing the remembrance from them is turning away, or an object for it, or a state meaning forgiving. Its origin is that you turn the side of something, so it is an adverbial phrase, and this is supported by the fact that it was read safhan with the damma. In this case, it is possible that the alleviation of safah is the plural of safuh meaning forgiving. What is meant is to deny that the matter is contrary to what was mentioned about the revelation of the Book in their language so that they would understand it. If you were a people who are extravagant means because you were, and it is in fact a reason requiring not turning away from them. Nafi’, Hamza, and al-Kisa’i read in with the kasra, on the basis that the sentence is conditional, taking the certain out of the doubtful to fool them, and what precedes it is evidence of the consequence.
43:6: 6- And how many a prophet We sent among the former peoples.
43:7: 7- And there came not to them a prophet but they used to ridicule him. This is to console the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the mockery of his people.
43:8: 8- "So We destroyed those who were more severe than them in punishment" meaning, than the transgressing people, because He diverted the address from them to the Messenger, informing about them. "And the example of the former peoples has passed" and the Quran has mentioned their amazing story, and in it there is a promise to the Messenger and a threat to them with the same as what happened to the former peoples.
43:9: 9- And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘The Exalted in Might, the Knowing created them.’ Perhaps this is the implication of what they said, or what indicated it in general terms was established in its place to establish the proof against them. It is as if they said, God, as was reported from them in other places, and He is the One whose description includes the attributes that were mentioned. It is possible that what they said and what follows is a resumption of He who made the earth a cradle for you, so that you settle in it. Other than the Kufians, it was read as cradle with the alif.
43:10: 10- And He made for you therein paths" that you may follow. "That you may be guided" so that you may be guided to your goals, or to the wisdom of the Creator by considering that.
43:11: 11- And He who sent down from the sky water in due measure in a measure that benefits and does not harm. Then We revived thereby a dead land from which the water departed. And its masculine form is because the land and the place. Likewise is like that resurrection. You will emerge you will emerge from your graves. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read you will emerge with a fatha on the ta' and a damma on the ra'.
43:12: 12- "And He who created in pairs all kinds of creatures. And made for you of the ships and the grazing livestock that which you ride." What you ride is based on the predominance of the transitive verb by itself over the transitive verb by something other than it, as it is said: I rode the animal and I rode in the ship, or the created thing for riding is over the one made for it, or the prevalent one over the rare one. For this reason He said:
43:13: 13- "That you may mount on their backs" meaning the backs of what you ride, and the plural is for the meaning. "Then remember the favor of your Lord when you are mounted on it" remember it in your hearts, acknowledging it and thanking God for it. "And say, 'Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it'" is from the verb aqrana to endure something, and its root is to find its companion, as the difficult cannot be a companion to the weak. It was read with emphasis and the meaning is the same. It was narrated from him, peace and blessings be upon him, "that when he put his foot in the stirrup, he would say: In the name of God, and when he was mounted on the mount, he would say: Praise be to God in every circumstance Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us" until his saying:
43:14: 14- And indeed, to our Lord we will return. That is, we will return. This is because riding is for transportation, and the greatest transportation is the return to God Almighty. Or because it is dangerous, so the rider should not neglect it and should prepare to meet God Almighty.
43:15: 15- And they attributed to Him from among His servants a portion is connected to His saying: And if you ask them meaning that after that recognition from His servants they attributed to Him a son, so they said the angels are the daughters of God. Perhaps He called him a part as he was called some because he is a piece of the father indicating the impossibility of him being the One True God in his essence. Abu Bakr read part with two dammahs. Indeed, mankind is clearly ungrateful The apparent ungratefulness and from that is attributing a son to God because they are from extreme ignorance of Him and belittling His status.
43:16: 16- Or has He taken from what He creates daughters and preferred you with sons? The meaning of the hamza in Am is to deny and express astonishment at their condition, as they were not satisfied with making a part of Him until they made for Him from His creations parts that were less worthy than what was chosen for them and more hateful to them, such that if one of them is given good report of it, his grief over it becomes intense, as he said:
43:17: 17- And when one of them is given good tidings of that which is presented to the Most Merciful as an example with the gender for which he made an example, since the son must resemble the father. His face darkens His face becomes extremely black because of the gloom that befalls him. And he is filled with inward grief His heart is filled with distress, and in that are indications of the corruption of what they said, and the definition of sons as mentioned previously in the males. It was read blackened and sawad on the basis that in shadow there is a pronoun for the one giving good tidings, and his face is blackened, a sentence that is the predicate.
43:18: 18- Or he who grows up in adornment meaning, or they made for him, or he took someone who would be raised in adornment, meaning girls. And he is in the dispute in the argument. Not clear is established for what he claims of a deficiency in the mind and weakness of opinion, and it is possible that it is from the subject with the predicate omitted, meaning, or from this is the state of his son, and in the dispute is related to clear, and adding not to it does not prevent it for what you know. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read yansha meaning he raises. Yansha and yansha'a were read with the same meaning, and similar to that are above it, above it, and above it, with the same meaning.
43:19: 19- And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females. This is another blasphemy included in their statement, which he denounced them for, which is that they made the most perfect and honored servants in the sight of God, the most deficient in opinion and the most contemptible in kind. Ubayd, Al-Hijaziyan, Ibn Amir, and Yaqub, according to Ali, read it as an example of their proximity. It was also read as female, which is the plural of the plural. Witness their creation. They brought God's creation of them and witnessed them as females, for that is something that is known by observation, and it is ignorance and mockery. Nafi' read ashhadu with an interrogative hamza and a damma hamza between them, and a'ashhadu with a period between them. Their testimony will be written down, which they testified against the angels. And they will be asked, meaning about it on the Day of Resurrection, and it is a severe threat. It was also read sayyaktu and sankatub with a ya' and a noon. Their testimonies are that God is a part of Him or that He has daughters who are the angels and they are questioned about questioning.
43:20: 20- And they said, ‘If the Most Gracious had willed, we would not have worshipped them.’ That is, if He had willed that the angels not be worshipped, we would not have worshipped them. They used the negation of His will not to worship as evidence for the impossibility of prohibiting it or for its being good. This is false, because the will gives precedence to some possibilities over others, whether they are commanded or prohibited, good or not. Therefore, He was ignorant of them, so He said, “They have no knowledge of that. They are only guessing.” They are making false assumptions. It is possible that the reference is to the origin of the claim, as if when He showed the aspects of its corruption and narrated their false doubt, He denied that they had knowledge of it by way of reason, then He turned away from it to deny that they had a basis in transmission, so He said:
43:21: 21- Or did We give them a scripture before it? Before the Qur'an, or their claim that proves the truth of what they said. So they cling to it. They cling to that scripture.
43:22: 22- Rather, they said, ‘We found our fathers following a religion, and we are guided by their footsteps.’ That is, they have no rational or transmitted proof, but rather they have inclined towards imitating their ignorant fathers. Ummah is the path that is followed like a mount for the one being traveled to. It is read with a kasrah, and it is the state that the mother, that is, the one intending, is in, and from it comes religion.
43:23: 23- And likewise, We did not send before you a warner to any city except that its affluent ones said, ‘Indeed, we found our fathers following a religion, and we will certainly follow in their footsteps.’ This is a consolation for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and an indication that imitation in such a matter is an ancient misguidance, and that their predecessors also did not have a reliable support, and singling out the affluent ones is an indication that indulgence and the love of idleness diverted them from looking at imitation.
43:24: 24- He said, Or even if I came to you with better guidance than what you found your fathers following? That is, would you follow your fathers even if I came to you with a religion better guided than the religion of your fathers? It is a narration of a past or present matter to the warner, or an address to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The first is supported by the fact that Ibn Amir and Hafs read, He said. And his statement, They said, ‘Indeed, in that with which you have been sent, we are disbelievers.’ That is, even if it was better guidance, to make the warner despair of them looking or thinking about it.
43:25: 25- So We took revenge on them by exterminating them. Then see how was the end of those who denied and do not pay attention to their denial.
43:26: 26- And when Abraham said, "And remember the time when he said this, so that they may see how he disavowed imitation and held fast to the evidence, or so that they may imitate him if they have no alternative but to imitate, for he is the most honorable of their forefathers. To his father and his people, 'Indeed, I am disassociated from what you worship.' Disassociated from your worship or your object of worship, is a source of description, and therefore it is the same for the singular and the plural, the masculine and the feminine, and it is read as bari' and bara' like karim and karram.
43:27: 27- Except He who created me is an exception, whether disjunctive or connected, that includes those with knowledge and others, and that they used to worship God, idols, and statues, or an attribute, that what is described, meaning I am innocent of any gods that you worship other than He who created me. For He will guide me He will make me steadfast in guidance, or He will guide me to what is beyond what He has guided me to.
43:28: 28- And He made it and made Abraham, peace be upon him, or God, the word of monotheism. a word remaining among his descendants among his offspring, so that there will always be among them those who unify God and call to His unification. A word and in his descendants were read for ease, and in his descendants means among those who come after him. Perhaps they will return those who associate others with God will return through the supplication of those who believe in monotheism.
43:29: 29- Rather, We gave enjoyment to these and their fathers these contemporaries of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Quraysh and their fathers, with long life and blessings, so they were deceived by that and became immersed in desires. It is read Manta'a with the fat-ha as an objection to Himself in His statement: And made it an enduring word as an exaggeration in taunting them. Until the truth came to them the call to monotheism or the Qur'an. And a clear Messenger the apparent message with his miracles, or clear of monotheism with arguments and signs.
43:30: 30- And when the truth came to them to alert them from their heedlessness, they said, 'This is magic, and indeed, we disbelieve in it.' They increased their wickedness and added to their polytheism their opposition to the truth and their disdain for it, so they called the Qur'an magic and disbelieved in it and despised the Messenger.
43:31: 31- And they said, ‘Why was this Qur’an not sent down to a man from the two cities?’ From one of the two cities, Mecca and Taif. Great with prestige and wealth, such as Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and Urwah bin Masoud Al-Thaqafi, for the message is a great position that only befits a great person, and they did not know that it is a spiritual rank that calls for greatness of the soul by being adorned with virtues and holy perfections, not adorned with worldly decorations.
43:32: 32- Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord? This is a denial that shows ignorance and astonishment at their control. What is meant by mercy is prophethood. We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world. They are unable to manage it, and it is the essence of their worldly life. So how can they manage the matter of prophethood, which is the highest human rank? The general meaning of livelihood requires that what is lawful and unlawful in it be from God. And We have raised some of them above others in degrees. And We have placed disparity among them in provision and other things. That they may take others in service. So that they may employ one another in their needs, and thus harmony and solidarity may occur between them, thus regulating the order of the world, not for the sake of perfection in the wealthy nor for the sake of deficiency in the poor. Moreover, they have no objection to Us in that regard, nor can they interfere with it, so how can it be in something higher than it? And the mercy of your Lord, meaning this prophethood and what follows it, is better than what they accumulate of the debris of this world and the great provision from it, not from Him.

He said meaning the evening person to the devil. Oh, would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts the distance between the east and the west, so the east was dominant and dual and the distance was added to them. Then what an evil companion you are.
43:39: 39- And it will not benefit you today meaning what you are wishing for. When you were unjust since it is true that you wronged yourselves in this world instead of today "that you are sharing in the punishment" because it is your right that you and your devils share in the punishment just as you were sharing in its cause. It is permissible for the action to be attributed to it with the meaning. And your sharing in the punishment will not benefit you as it benefits those who are in a difficult matter by helping them bear its burdens and dividing them to endure its suffering, because each of you has what he cannot contain. And "you" is read with a kasra, which strengthens the first.
43:40: 40- Can you make the deaf hear or guide the blind? Denial and astonishment that He is the One who is able to guide them after they have been trained in disbelief and have been immersed in misguidance to the point that their night became blindness coupled with deafness. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would tire himself out in calling his people, and they would only become richer, so the verse was revealed: And whoever is in manifest error is in apposition to blindness in consideration of the difference between the two descriptions, and in it is an indication that it is necessary for them to be able to remain in misguidance that is not hidden.
43:41: 41- Then if We take you away meaning if We take you before we see their punishment, and ma is an additional, emphatic letter in the position of the oath lam in bringing the emphatic nun then We will take vengeance on them with punishment in this world and the hereafter.
43:42: 42- Or We show you what We promised them or if We wanted to show you what We promised them of the punishment, and Ya’qub read with the narration of Rawis or We show you with a sukoon on the nun and likewise We go away. “For We are powerful over them” they will not escape Us.
43:43: 43- So hold fast to what has been revealed to you of the verses and laws. It has been revealed was read as the subject, which is God Almighty. Indeed, you are on a straight path with no crookedness.
43:44: 44- And indeed, it is a reminder for you an honor for you. And for your people, and you will be questioned that is, about it on the Day of Resurrection and about your fulfillment of its right.
43:45: 45- And ask those We sent before you of Our messengers meaning, ask their nations and their religious scholars. Ibn Kathir and Al-Kisa’i read it with a light hamza. Have We made other than the Most Merciful gods to be worshipped? Did We rule on the worship of idols and did it come in any of their religions? What is meant by it is to cite the consensus of the prophets on monotheism and to indicate that it is not an innovation that should be denied and opposed, because it was the strongest thing that drove them to deny and oppose.
43:46: 46- “And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs. He said, ‘Indeed, I am the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds.’” By his narration, he intended to console the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to contradict their saying, Why was this Qur’an not sent down to some great man from the two cities? And to cite Moses’ call, peace be upon him, to monotheism so that they might reflect upon it.
43:47: 47- So when He brought them Our signs, at once they laughed at them. They were surprised at the time of their laughter at them, or they mocked them when they first saw them and did not reflect on them.
43:48: 48- And We did not show them a sign except that it was greater than its sister except that it reached the highest degree of miraculousness, such that the one looking at it would think that it was greater than the signs that could be compared to it. What is meant is to describe the whole as being great, like your saying: I saw men, some of whom were better than others, and like His saying: Whoever receives from them, say, I have met their master, like the stars that a traveler carries. Or except, which is specific to a type of miracle and is preferred over others in that regard. And We seized them with punishment, such as years, floods, and locusts. Perhaps they would return, in a way that is hoped for.
43:49: 49- "And they said, 'O magician!'" They called him thus at that moment due to their extreme stubbornness and foolishness, or because they used to call a skilled scholar a magician. Ibn 'Amir read it with a damma on the ha'. "Call upon your Lord for us," so that He may remove the punishment from us. "By what He has promised you, by His promise to you of prophethood, or that He will answer your call, or that He will remove the punishment from those who are guided, or By what He has promised you," so you have fulfilled it, which is faith and obedience. "Indeed, we are [rightly] guided."
43:50: 50- So when We removed the punishment from them, at once they broke their covenant with guidance.
43:51: 51- And Pharaoh called out by himself or through his crier. Nor will they grieve over the loss of something beloved. The fa is to indicate that the noun includes the meaning of a condition.
46:14: 14- Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein eternally as reward for what they used to do of acquiring scientific and practical virtues, and abidingly is a state of what is implied in companions and reward is a source for a verb indicated by the speech, meaning they were rewarded.
46:15: 15- And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, good treatment. The Kufians read it as ihsan, and it was read hasan meaning a good recommendation. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship of hardship or a heavy load, which is hardship. The Hijazis, Abu Amr, and Hisham read it, and they are two languages like poverty and poverty. It was said that the damma is a noun and the fatha is a verbal noun. And his pregnancy and his weaning and the duration of his pregnancy and his weaning is n, and weaning is weaning, and this is indicated by the reading of Ya`qub, and his separation or his time, and what is meant by it is the complete breastfeeding that ends with it, and therefore he expressed it as the duration is expressed by the term. He said: Every living thing has completed its lifespan and dies when its term ends. Thirty months All of this is an explanation of what the mother suffers in raising the child, exaggerating in recommending it. It is evidence that the minimum period is six months because weaning reduces it to two years, as God the Almighty says: Two complete years for him who wishes to complete the suckling. This remains and this is what the doctors have said. Perhaps specifying the minimum period of pregnancy and the maximum period of suckling is due to their regularity and the realization of the connection between the rulings of lineage and suckling with them. Until when he reaches his full strength when he matures and his strength and mind are complete. And reaches forty years It was said that no prophet was sent until after forty. He said, 'My Lord, inspire me' Inspire me and inspire me with whom You inspire with such-and-such. That I may be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents meaning the favor of religion or what includes it and others. This supports what was narrated that it was revealed about Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him because no one from the Muhajireen and Ansar had converted to Islam, he and his parents, except him. And that I do righteousness of which You approve is indefinite for emphasis, or because He meant a type of action that attracts the pleasure of God the Almighty. And make my offspring righteous for me and make righteousness prevail in my offspring and be present in them. And similar to this is his saying: And if she apologizes in the place for her udder to the guest, he will be wounded in her heels, we pray I repent to You for what you do not like or that distracts you, and I am among the Muslims who are sincere to You.
46:16: 16- Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did meaning their acts of obedience, as what is permissible is good but is not rewarded for. And We overlook their misdeeds because of their repentance. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read them with the letter nun in both. Among the companions of Paradise being among them, or rewarded, or counted among them. The promise of truth is a source confirming itself, so it is accepted and overlooked which they were promised meaning in this world.
46:17: 17- And he who said to his parents, 'Fie upon you both,' is a subject and its predicate is those, and what is meant by it is the genus. Even if it is true that it was revealed about Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr before his conversion to Islam, the specific reason does not necessitate specification. Fie has readings mentioned in the case of the Children of Israel. Do you promise me that I will come forth? Hisham read Do you promise me with one doubled nun. "And generations before me have passed away," not one of them returned. "And they both seek help from God, they say, I seek help from God," or they ask Him to help him by granting him success in faith. "Woe to you! Believe, meaning they say to him, Woe to you," which is a call for destruction by urging him to do what he fears he will abandon. "Indeed, the promise of God is true. He says, This is nothing but legends of the ancients," their falsehoods that they wrote.
46:18: 18- Those are the ones upon whom the word has come into effect that they are the people of the Fire. This verse was revealed about Abd al-Rahman because it indicates that he is one of its people for that reason, and it was obligatory for him if it was due to his conversion to Islam. Among nations that have passed on before them is like his statement about the people of Paradise. Of the jinn and mankind is a clarification of the nations. Indeed, they were losers is an explanation of the ruling based on the resumption.
46:19: 19- And for each of the two groups. Degrees according to what they have done ranks of recompense for what they have done of good and evil, or for what they have done. Degrees is predominant in reward, and here it came in the form of predominance. And that He may fully recompense them for their deeds their recompense. Nafi`, Ibn `Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa`i, and Ibn Dhakwan read it with the letter nun. "And they will not be wronged" with a reduction in reward and an increase in punishment.
46:20: 20- And the Day those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire They will be tormented by it. It was said that the Fire will be exposed to them, but this was changed to indicate exaggeration, like their saying: The she-camel was exposed to the Cistern. You went away means it will be said to them, You went away, and it is the subject of the word today. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Ya'qub read it with the question mark, except that Ibn Kathir reads it with an extended hamza, and they both read it with it and with two definite hamzas. Your good things for your pleasures. In your worldly life by completing it. And you enjoyed it so nothing of it remains for you. So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation Humiliation has been read with this reading. Because you were arrogant upon the earth without right and because you were defiantly disobedient because of your false arrogance and defiantly refusing to obey God. You defiantly was read with the kasra.
46:21: 21- And mention the brother of Aad meaning Hud. When he warned his people in Al-Ahqaf the plural of Haqf which is a raised, oblong sand dune with a curve from Ahqaf when something is crooked. They used to live among the sand dunes overlooking the sea in Ash-Shihr in Yemen. And there have been warnings the messengers before him and behind him before Hud and after him. The clause is a state or an interruption. That you worship none but God meaning do not worship, or that you do not worship, for the prohibition of something is a warning of its harm. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day because of your polytheism.
46:22: 22- They said, Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? “Then bring us what you promise us,” of punishment for polytheism, if you should be truthful in your promise.
46:23: 23- He said, Knowledge is only with God. I have no knowledge of the time of your punishment, nor do I have any part in it, so hasten it. Its knowledge is only with God, and He will bring it to you at its appointed time. And I convey to you that with which I have been sent, to you, and the Messenger has no duty except to convey. But I see that you are a people behaving ignorantly, not knowing that the Messengers were sent as conveyors and warners, not as punishers and proposers.
46:24: 24- So when they saw it as a cloud a cloud that appeared on the horizon of the sky. facing their valleys heading towards their valleys, and the addition in it is verbal, and likewise in His statement: They said, 'This is a cloud bringing us rain' meaning it brings us rain. Rather, it is meaning Hud, peace be upon him, said, Rather, it is what you were hastening of the punishment. And it was read, Rather, it is a wind it is a wind, and it is permissible for it to be a substitute for what in it is a painful punishment its description, and likewise in His statement:
46:25: 25- Palmyra destroys. Everything of their souls and their conditions. By the command of its Lord, for there is no spring of movement or contraction of stillness except by His will. In mentioning the command and the Lord and adding to the wind there are benefits that have been mentioned before repeatedly. It was read that He destroys everything from the root word ḍammara ḍamān, if it is destroyed, then the pronoun is omitted, or the ha’ in its Lord, and it is possible that it is a resumption to indicate that every possible thing has a preordained annihilation that is neither advanced nor delayed, and the ha’ is for everything, for it means things. So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings, meaning the wind came upon them and destroyed them, so they became such that if you were to visit their country, nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisa’i read nothing could be seen except their dwellings, with the ḍammah ya’ and raising the dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people. It was narrated that when Hud, peace be upon him, felt the wind, he secluded himself with the believers in the enclosure, and the wind came and tilted the Ahqaf towards the disbelievers, and they were under it for seven nights and eight days, then it uncovered them and carried them, throwing them into the sea.
46:26: 26- And We have certainly empowered them in that in which We have empowered you. "In is a negative, and in is better than what here because it requires repetition in wording, and for this reason its alif was changed to a ha in whatever", or a conditional omitted answer, and the estimation, and We have certainly empowered them in that which is more complete. Something in which We have empowered you would have been more oppressive, or a connection as in His saying: One hopes for what one does not see and displays without the slightest trouble. The first is more apparent and more in accordance with His statement: They are better furnished “They were more numerous than them and stronger in strength and influence” And We gave them hearing and sight and hearts so that they would recognize those blessings and use them as evidence of their Giver, the Most High, and persevere in thanking Him. But their hearing and sight and hearts availed them nothing from enrichment, which is little. Because they denied the signs of God is a connection to so they availed nothing and it is a circumstance that takes the place of explanation in that the ruling is based on what it is attributed to, and likewise where that which they used to ridicule encompassed them of the punishment.
46:27: 27- And We have certainly destroyed what was around you O people of Mecca. Of the towns such as the towns of Thamud and the towns of the people of Lot. And We have diversified the signs by repeating them. Perhaps they will return from their disbelief.
46:28: 28- Why did not those whom they took as deities besides God aid them? Why did their deities, by whom they seek to draw near to God, prevent them from being destroyed? They said, These are our intercessors with God. The first two objects of took referring to the relative pronoun are omitted, and the second is sacrifice and deities as a substitute or apposition, or deities and sacrifice as a state or object of it, as it means drawing near. Qurbanan is read with a damma on the ra'. Rather, they have gone astray from them. They were absent from their support, and it was forbidden for them to seek help from them, as it is forbidden to seek help from one who has gone astray. That is their falsehood. That taking, the effect of which is to turn them away from the truth. Ifkahum is read with a shaddah for emphasis. Afkahum means to make them slanderers, and afkahum means their saying al-ifk means the one who has the slander. And they did not invent.
46:29: 29- "And when We directed to you a company of the jinn We gave them hope of reaching you, and the company is less than ten, and its plural is anfar. listening to the Qur'an" is a state carried by the meaning. "So when they attended it" meaning the Qur'an or the Messenger. "They said, Listen they said to each other, Be quiet so that we may hear it. "So when it was concluded" he completed and finished reciting it, and it was read in the form of the subject, which is the pronoun of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. "And they turned back to their people as warners" meaning warning them of what they heard. It was narrated that they met the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, in Wadi al-Nakhlah when he was returning from Ta'if, reciting in his night prayers.
46:30: 30- "They said, 'O our people, indeed we have heard a book revealed after Moses.'" It was said that they only said that because they were Jews or because they had not heard of the matter of Jesus, peace and blessings be upon him. "Confirming what was before it, guiding to the truth" of the beliefs. "And to a straight path" of the laws.
46:31: 31- "O our people, respond to the caller to God and believe in him, and He will forgive you some of your sins." Some of your sins, which are those that are purely in the right of God, because injustices are not forgiven by faith. "And He will save you from a painful punishment." This is prepared for the disbelievers. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, argued that limiting them to forgiveness and protection means that they have no reward, and what is more apparent is in the consequences of obligation, like the children of Adam.
46:32: 32- "And whoever does not respond to the call of God will not escape Him on earth" as there is no escape from him. "And he has no protectors besides Him" to protect him from it. "Those are in manifest error" as they turned away from responding to someone of this nature.
46:33: 33- Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not weary in their creation, and did not get tired or unable, and the meaning is that His power is necessary and does not decrease or cease with creation forever and ever. Able to give life to the dead means Able, and this is indicated by the reading of Ya’qub, is able, and the ba is added to emphasize the negation, as it includes that and what is within its scope. Therefore, He answered it by saying, Yes, He is over all things competent, confirming the power in a general manner that is like proof of the intended purpose, as if He began the surah by confirming the principle and wanted to conclude it by proving the resurrection.
46:34: 34- And the Day those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire is subject to an implied statement, the predicate of which is: Is this not the truth? and the reference is to the punishment. “They will say: Yes, by our Lord.” He will say: Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve. For your disbelief in this world, and the meaning of the command is to humiliate them and rebuke them.
46:35: 35- "So be patient, as were patient the messengers of strong will" those of steadfastness and seriousness among them, for you are among them. "From" is for clarification, and it was said for partiality. "Those of strong will" among them are the people of the religions who strove to establish and establish them and were patient in bearing their hardships and in the opposition to those who attacked them. The most famous among them are: Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them. It was said that those who are patient in the face of God's affliction are like Noah, who was patient in the face of the harm from his people who used to beat him until he fainted, and Abraham in the face of the fire and the slaughter of his son and the slaughtered one in the face of the slaughter, and Jacob in the face of the loss of his son and his sight, and Joseph in the well and prison, and Job in the face of hardship, and Moses, to whom his people said, "Indeed, we are to be overtaken. He said, No indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me." And David wept over his sin for forty years, and Jesus did not place brick upon brick. "And do not hasten them" for the disbelievers of Quraysh, for it will inevitably descend upon them at its appointed time. "On the Day they see what they are promised, it will be as if they had not remained [in the world] except for an hour" because of its horror, they will think their stay in this world was but an hour. "Prompt" This that you have been admonished with, or this surah is a pronouncement, meaning sufficiency, or a pronouncement from the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is supported by the fact that it was read as "balagh" enough. It was also said that "balagh is the subject, and its predicate is lahum for them, and ma" is between them, an interruption, meaning they have a time to reach which they will reach, as if when they reach it and see what is in it, they will think their lifespan was short. It was also read in the accusative, meaning they conveyed a pronouncement. "Then are none destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people? Those who turn away from admonition or obedience? It was read yahluka with a fatha or kasra from halaka to perish and nahlaka with a nun, and al-qawm" is the accusative. It was narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Whoever recites Surat al-Ahqaf, ten good deeds will be recorded for him, for the number of every sand grain in the world."
47:1: 1- Those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God refrained from entering Islam and following its path, or prevented people from it, such as those who were fed on the day of Badr, or the devils of Quraysh or the Egyptians from the People of the Book, or it is general for all who disbelieved and averted. He rendered their deeds worthless He rendered their good deeds, such as maintaining kinship ties, freeing prisoners, and protecting neighbors, lost, i.e., lost and surrounded by disbelief, or defeated and immersed in it as water is lost in milk, or misguidance since they did not intend thereby the face of God, or He nullified what they did of plotting against His Messenger and averting people from His way by supporting His Messenger and making His religion prevail over all religions.
47:2: 2- And those who have believed and done righteous deeds includes the Muhajireen, the Ansar, and those who believed from among the People of the Book and others. And have believed in what was revealed to Muhammad is a specification of what was revealed to him from what must be believed in, to glorify him and to indicate that faith is not complete without it, and that it is the foundation of it. Therefore, he emphasized it by saying: And it is the truth from their Lord in objection to the method of limitation. It was said that its reality is that it is an abrogator that cannot be abrogated. It was read revealed in the active form and revealed in the two forms and revealed in the light form. He removed from them their misdeeds covered them with faith and their righteous deeds. And set right their condition in religion and in this world with success and support.
47:3: 3- That refers to what was mentioned previously about misguidance, atonement, and reform. It is a subject whose predicate is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood and those who believed followed the truth from their Lord because of these people following falsehood and those following the truth. This is an explicit statement of what was indicated by what preceded it, and that is why it is called an explanation. Likewise is an example of that example. God sets forth for the people He explains to them their examples the conditions of the two groups or the conditions of the people, or He sets forth their examples by making following falsehood an example for the actions of the disbelievers and misguidance an example for their failure and following the truth an example for the believers, and expiation of bad deeds an example for their success.
47:4: 4- So when you meet those who disbelieve in battle. Then strike the necks its original form is strike the necks but the verb was dropped and the verbal noun was brought forward, and its place was added to the object for emphasis and brevity. Expressing it as killing indicates that it should be by striking the necks wherever possible, and depicting it in the most hideous image. Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them you have increased their killing and made it severe from thakhin which is thick. Then tighten the bonds so capture them and protect them. The bond with the fatha and kasra is what one secures with. Then either a favor from us or a ransom. Meaning, either you give us a favor or ransom us. What is meant is the choice after capture between a favor and release or taking a ransom. This is established according to us, because if a free, accountable male is taken prisoner, the imam has the choice between killing, a favor, or ransom. Enslavement is abrogated according to the Hanafi school, or is specific to the Battle of Badr, as they said that killing or enslavement is required. It was read as a ransom like a stick. Until war lays down its burdens means its tools and heavy equipment that cannot be sustained without them, such as weapons and mounts. That is, the war ends and no one remains except a Muslim or a peaceful person. It was also said that its sins, and the meaning is until the people of war lay down their polytheism and sins. This is the end of the striking or the tightening or the favor and ransom or the whole, meaning that these rulings apply therein until there is no more war with the polytheists with the removal of their power. It was also said that with the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, that means that command, or do that to them. And if God had willed, He could have taken revenge on them He would have taken revenge on them by exterminating them. But that He may test some of you by means of others. But He has commanded you to fight so that He may test the believers by means of the disbelievers, by striving against them and thus deserving of the great reward through the believers, by hastening them at their hands with some of their punishment, so that some of them may be deterred from disbelief. Those who were killed in the way of God means they fought. The two Basrans and Hafs read killed meaning they were martyred. He will not let their deeds go to waste means He will not let them go to waste. It was read yaddil from dalala and yadhil in the passive form.
47:5: 5- He will guide them to the reward, or He will confirm their guidance. And He will reform their condition.
47:6: 6- And He will admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them. He made it known to them in this world so that they longed for it and did what they deserved for it, or He made it clear to them so that each one would know his home and be guided to it as if he had been an inhabitant of it since He was created, or He made it fragrant for them from the fragrance, which is a pleasant smell, or He specified it for them so that each Paradise would have a separate section.
47:7: 7- O you who have believed, if you support God if you support His religion and His Messenger, He will support you against your enemy. And plant firmly your feet in fulfilling the rights of Islam and in jihad against the disbelievers. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 27 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat Muḥammad, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Ṭūr. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time.
