47:8: 8- And those who disbelieve - for them is wretchedness. So, a stumble and a decline for them, and its denial is a lie. Al-A'sha said: It is more appropriate for her to be miserable than for me to say to her Its being in the accusative case due to its verb, which must be implied by hearing, and the sentence is the predicate of those who disbelieved or implied for its accusative. And He rendered worthless their deeds is in apposition to it.
47:9: 9- That is because they hated what God revealed the Qur'an because of what it contains of monotheism and obligations that contradict what they were accustomed to and what their souls desired. This is a specification and explicit statement of the reason for disbelief in the Qur'an for misery and misguidance. So He rendered worthless their deeds He repeated it to indicate that it necessitates disbelief in the Qur'an and cannot be separated from it under any circumstances.
47:10: 10- Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? God destroyed them. He destroyed from them what was specific to them of their lives, their families, and their wealth. And for the disbelievers from placing the apparent in place of the implicit. The like thereof the likes of that consequence or punishment. Or destruction because destruction indicates it, or the way because the Almighty said: The way of God that has passed.
47:11: 11- That is because God is the protector of those who believe He supports them against their enemies. And because the disbelievers have no protector He will avert punishment from them. This does not contradict His statement: And they will be returned to God, their true protector because the protector in it means the owner.
47:12: 12- "Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But those who disbelieve will enjoy themselves and eat as livestock eat, greedy and heedless of the consequences. And the Fire will be their abode."
47:13: 13- And how many a city was mightier in power than your city which expelled you with the deletion of the noun and the application of its rules to the noun to which it is attached, and the expulsion is based on the consideration of causation. We destroyed them with various types of punishment. So there is no helper for them to ward off the punishment from them, and it is like the situation described.
47:14: 14- Is he who has clear evidence from his Lord proof from Him, which is the Qur’an, or what includes it and rational proofs, such as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers like he to whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive such as polytheism and sins. And they follow their desires in that they have no doubt about it, let alone proof.
47:15: 15- The parable of Paradise which has been promised to the righteous i.e. in what We have narrated to you is its amazing description. It was said that the subject is Khalid and its predicate is: Like one who is in the Fire, the meaning of the statement is the best of the people of Paradise is he who is immortal, or the best of Paradise is like the reward of one who is immortal, so he is free from denial and the deletion of what was deleted is sufficient, like it is a depiction of the stubbornness of one who equates the one who clings to the evidence and the followers of God, with the stubbornness of one who equates Paradise and the Fire, and according to the first it is a deleted predicate, its classification: Is one who is immortal in this Paradise like one who is immortal in the Fire, or a substitute for saying: Like one who adorned and what could be to clarify what distinguishes him from others in the Hereafter, a confirmation of denial. In it is that it is from water that is not stagnant and allows for an explanation of the parable or a state of the deleted words, or a suitable predicate, and stagnant is from asana of water with a fatha if its taste and smell change, or with a kasra meaning occurrence. Ibn Kathir read asana. And rivers of milk, pure and clear that has not become bitter or sour. And rivers of wine, a delight to those who drink delicious, with no taste, smell, or traces of intoxication. And wine is the feminine form of delicious or a verbal noun describing rivers, or it is an alternative reading, and it is read in the nominative case as a description of rivers, and in the accusative case as a reason. And rivers of purified honey that has not been mixed with wax or the remnants of lawful things or anything else. This represents what takes the place of drinks in Paradise with the types of what is enjoyed from them in this world, stripped of what diminishes or defiles them, and the specifications are such that it necessitates its abundance and continuity. And for them therein is from every kind of fruit a type according to this analogy. And forgiveness from their Lord is in apposition to the omitted type, or a subject whose predicate is omitted, meaning they have forgiveness. How much he will abide in the Fire and stand and be available the place of those drinks only their intestines from the excessive heat. 6- "They will have no food except from the thorny plant" The dried-up thorny plant, which is grazed by camels as long as it is moist. It was also said that it is a fiery tree similar to the thorny plant. Perhaps it is the food of these people, while the Zaqqum and the Ghaslin are the food of others. Or what is meant is that their food is what camels avoid and detest because of its harm and lack of benefit, as God Almighty said:
47:17: 17- "And those who are guided - He increases them in guidance." That is, God increases them in success and inspiration, or the words of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. "And gives them their piety." He explains to them what they should fear, or He helps them in their piety, or He gives them the reward for it.
47:18: منْاَْماًَََْْْةََُْْن ْأَفَلَون آخًَاََاَِفَلَون18- َُْْوقَئ َن ْأثث،َهًْاَعل"َاء ََْاُُاَْف: "وقوَه،" ًَاََا ُْومعَى َن ْأثََُْْ َُِْْا َْرَُْفاَى: "محَق َزئَاةََُْلى ََه واَْق، َْماراُْا ْمَعث اَََي اَصلة واََلَُُ ْلَه قًََْ ًَاََا وََْما، ًََْ ًَاََا" ََُِْا َمحَََُْْْيََُْْاَُْْماَاََم.ََفعََفَغ َه وَ <div id='div_ar1' style='text-align:left; direction:ltr; فجمجا َجَمُهَهونج ِإَن اََناَجًج َجنم ْجأمْإَجُهْم َإْجفجلجًة؟ وجقجْمfont-size:20px;'>18. فجأجَنى ِإَجا َجاءجْمُهْم َجَمْهَهونج ؟.َجاءجتم مهَجاْإئجاْهُجا
47:19: 19- "Know that there is no god but God, and ask forgiveness for your sin" meaning, if you know the happiness of the believers and the misery of the disbelievers, then remain steadfast in your knowledge of the Oneness of God and the perfection of the soul by correcting its conditions and actions and comprehending it through asking forgiveness "for your sin". "And for the believing men and believing women" and for their sins by supplicating for their great need and the abundance of their sins, and that they are of a different kind, for sin has its consequences, not for abandoning the first. "And God knows your [moving and] changing" in this world, for they are stages that must be completed. "And your abode" in the Hereafter, for it is your abode, so fear God, ask His forgiveness, and prepare for your return.
47:20: 20- And those who believe say, 'Why was a surah not sent down?' That is, why was a surah not sent down about the matter of jihad? But when a clear surah is sent down, making clear, with no ambiguity therein. "And fighting is mentioned therein," That is, the command to do it. "You will see those in whose hearts is disease," Weakness in religion, and it was said, hypocrisy. "They look at you with the look of one fainting from death, Out of cowardice and fear, So it is more fitting for them. Woe to them. Then w...
47:21: 21- Obedience and kind speech is a resumption, meaning their command obedience or obedience and kind speech is better for them, or a narration of their saying according to Abu's reading, they say obedience. So when he decides on the matter meaning he is serious, and it is for those in charge, and attributing it to him is a metaphor and the circumstantial factor is omitted. It was said, If they had been truthful to God meaning in what they claimed of eagerness for jihad or faith. Then truthfulness would have been better for them.
47:22: 22- So is it likely that you will cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship if you were given authority, or if you turned away and turned away from Islam, that you would cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship, quarreling over authority and arguing over it, or returning to what you were doing in the days of ignorance of enmity and fighting relatives? The meaning is that because of their weakness in religion and their eagerness for this world, they are deserving of being expected to do so from someone who knows their condition and says to them: Is it likely that you will? This is in the dialect of the Hijaz, for Banu Tamim do not attach the pronoun to it and its predicate is that you would cause corruption, and if you turn away is an interjection. And from Ya'qub, You turned away means that if oppressors took control of you, you would go out with them and help them in causing corruption and severing ties of kinship. And you were cut off is from cutting, and it was read You were cut off from cutting.
47:23: 23- Those refers to those mentioned whom God has cursed for their corruption and severing family ties. He has made them deaf from hearing the truth and blinded their sight so they are not guided to His path.
47:24: 24- Do they not then consider the Qur'an carefully? They skim through it and what it contains of admonitions and deterrents so that they do not dare to commit sins. Or are there locks upon their hearts? No remembrance can reach them and no matter can be revealed to them. It was said that or is disconnected and the meaning of the hamza in it is confirmation, and the hearts are indefinite because the hearts are meant to be the hearts of some of them or to indicate that it is due to the ambiguity of its matter in its harshness, or due to its extreme ignorance and indefiniteness as if it is vague and indefinite. The addition of the locks to it is to indicate locks appropriate to it and specific to it that do not resemble the usual locks. And its being closed is read as a source.
47:25: 25- Indeed, those who turned back on their heels meaning what they were upon of disbelief. After guidance has become clear to them with clear proofs and manifest miracles Satan enticed them making it easy for them to commit major sins from sawl which means relaxation. It was also said that he led them to desires from sawl which means wishing, and in it that sawl is a hamza and its hamza was changed to a waw due to the damma of what preceded it, and this is not the case with tasweel, and it can be refuted by their saying they both beg each other and sawl was read based on the estimation of an addition, meaning the trick of Satan enticed them. And he extended their hopes and wishes and extended their hopes and wishes, or God Almighty gave them respite and did not hasten their punishment according to the reading of Ya'qub and I extended my hope to them meaning I extended my hope to them, so the waw is for the state or resumption, and Abu Amr read and I extended my hope to them in the passive form which is the pronoun of Satan or them.
47:26: 26- "That is because they said to those who hated what God revealed" meaning the Jews said to those who disbelieved in the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, after his description had become clear to them, to the hypocrites, or the hypocrites to them, or one of the two groups to the polytheists. "We will obey you in some of the matter" in some of your affairs or in some of what you are commanded to do, such as sitting back from jihad and agreeing to go out with them if they are expelled, and joining forces against the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. "And God knows their secrets" including this statement of theirs which God revealed to them. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read their secrets as a source.
47:27: 27- How then, when the angels take their souls? How will they work and plan at that time? It was read as they take their souls and it is possible for it to be in the past tense or the present tense with one of its two ta's omitted. They strike their faces and their backs is a depiction of their taking their souls with what they fear and are cowardly about fighting for.
47:28: 28- That refers to the described death. Because they followed what angered God of disbelief, such as concealing the description of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and disobeying the command. And they hated His pleasure of what pleases Him of faith, jihad, and other acts of obedience. So He rendered their deeds worthless for that reason.
47:29: 29- Or do those in whose hearts is disease think that God will not bring forth their grudges that God will not reveal to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers. their rancor their grudges.
47:30: 30- And if We willed, We could have shown them to you We could have known you by signs by which you would know them by their identities. And you would have known them by their mark by the marks by which We name them, and the lam is the lam of the answer and was repeated in the conjoined. And you will surely know them by the tone of their speech is the answer to an omitted oath, and the tone of speech is its style, or its inclination towards allusion and ambiguity, and from this the one who makes a mistake is called a lahan because he deviates from the truth in his speech. And God knows your deeds so He will reward you according to your intentions, as deeds are judged by intentions.
47:31: 31- And We will surely test you with the command to fight and all other difficult tasks. Until We make evident those among you who strive [for the cause of God] and the patient in its hardships. And We will test your report with what is revealed about your deeds, revealing their goodness and badness, or their report about their faith and their loyalty to the believers in terms of their truthfulness and falsehood. Abu Bakr read the three verbs with a ya' to agree with what preceded them, and according to Ya'qub, and We will test with a sukoon on the waw, assuming that we test.
47:32: 32- Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God and opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them are the Qurayzah and the Nadir, or those who were fed on the day of Badr. Never will they harm God at all by their disbelief and averting [people], or they will never harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by opposing him. The complement was omitted to magnify it and to make opposing him terrible. And He will render worthless their deeds the reward for their good deeds thereby, or the plots they set up to oppose him, so they will not achieve their goals through them, and they will only produce death and expulsion from their homelands.
47:33: 33- O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds with what these people invalidated, such as disbelief, hypocrisy, arrogance, showing off, showing off, harming others, and the like. There is no evidence in it that acts of obedience are invalidated by major sins.
47:34: 34- Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of God and then died while they were disbelievers - never will God forgive them. This is general for everyone who died in disbelief, even though it was revealed about the Companions of the Well. Its implication indicates that the sins of someone who did not die in disbelief may be forgiven.
47:35: 35- Do not weaken do not become weak "and call for peace" and do not call for reconciliation out of weakness and humiliation. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case by implying in and it was read do not call from claim meaning call, and Abu Bakr and Hamza read it with a kasra on the seen. And you are the highest the victorious. And God is with you your supporter. And He will not let you go to waste from your deeds and He will not let your deeds go to waste, from watarat a man if you kill someone close to him or a close friend, so you separated it from it from watar, likening it to suspending the reward of the deed and separating it from it.
47:36: 36- The life of this world is only play and amusement. It is not stable. And if you believe and fear God, He will give you your rewards. “And He will not ask you for your wealth.” All of your wealth. Rather, He will limit it to a small portion, such as a quarter of a tenth or a tenth.
47:37: 37- "If they ask you for it, He will force you" He will exhaust you by asking for everything, concealing and insisting, exaggerating and achieving the goal. It is said: He shaved his mustache when he pulled it out. "Be stingy" so do not give. "And He will bring forth your grudges" He will bring forth your grudges against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The pronoun in "bring forth is for God Almighty, and this is supported by the reading with the letter nun or bukhl" because it is the cause of the grudges. It was read "and he will bring forth with the letter ta and the letter ya and raising your grudges".
47:38: 38- Here you are meaning you, O those being addressed, are those described. His statement, You are called to spend in the cause of God is a new chapter confirming that, or a connection to these as meaning those who, and it includes spending on military conquest, zakat, and other things. Among you are those who are miserly people who are miserly, and this is like the evidence for the previous verse. And whoever is miserly is only miserly to himself because the benefit of spending and the harm of miserliness return to him, and miserliness is transitive with an and ala because it includes the meaning of withholding and transiting, as it is withholding from one who is entitled to it. And God is the Rich, and you are the poor so whatever He commands you is due to your need for it, so if you comply, it is for you, but if you turn away, it is against you. And if you turn away is in apposition to if you believe. He will replace you with another people He will replace you with another people. Then they will not be like you in turning away and renunciation of faith, and they are the Persians because “he was asked about it, peace and blessings be upon him, and Salman was beside him, so he struck his thigh and said: This one and his people.” Or the Ansar, or Yemen, or the angels. On the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, Whoever recites Surat Muhammad, it is a right upon God to give him to drink from the rivers of Paradise.
48:1: 1- Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest. A promise to conquer Mecca, and expressing it in the past tense indicates its realization or what happened to it in that year, such as the conquest of Khaybar and Fadak, or reporting the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. It was called a conquest because it was after his victory over the polytheists until they asked for a peace treaty and it led to the conquest of Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, devoted himself to the rest of the Arabs, so he invaded them and conquered places and brought a great number of people into Islam. A great sign appeared to him in Hudaybiyyah, which is that its water drained completely, so he rinsed his mouth and spat into it, and it flowed with water until all who were with him drank. Or the conquest of the Romans, for they defeated the Persians in that year. You have known that it was a conquest for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Surat Al-Rum. It was said that conquest means decree, meaning We decreed for you that you would enter Mecca the next year.
48:2: 2- That God may forgive you is the reason for the victory, as it is caused by jihad against the infidels and striving to remove polytheism, elevate the religion, and perfect the deficient souls by force, so that this gradually becomes a choice, and the weak are freed from the hands of the oppressors. Whatever of your sin, past and future is all that you have neglected, for which you can be rebuked. And complete His favor upon you by elevating the religion and joining kingship to prophethood. And guide you to a straight path in conveying the message and performing the ceremonies of leadership.
48:3: 3- And God will grant you a mighty victory a victory that brings honor and strength, or by which the victorious person will be honored, so his description is an exaggeration.
48:4: 4- It is He who sent down tranquility stability and reassurance. Into the hearts of the believers until they were steadfast when souls are anxious and feet falter, that they may increase in faith along with their faith certainty along with their certainty in the firmness of the faith and the soul's reassurance in it, or He sent down tranquility into them according to what the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought so that they may increase in faith in the laws along with their faith in God and the Last Day. And to God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth He manages their affairs, sometimes giving some power over others and at other times establishing peace between them, as His wisdom dictates. And God is Knowing of what is in people's best interests. Wise in what He decrees and manages.
48:5: 5- That He may admit the believing men and believing women to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. The reason for what follows is based on what is indicated by the Most High's statement: To God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth, which is a meaning of management, meaning He managed what He managed of the dominance of the believers so that they may recognize God's blessing in it and be grateful for it, so He admits them to Paradise and punishes the disbelievers and hypocrites because of what angered them about that, or We opened or He sent down or all of what was mentioned, or that they may increase. It was said that it is a substitute for it, a substitute of inclusion. And He will cover their misdeeds from them, He will cover them and not show them. And that meaning the admission and the expiation, is with God a great attainment, because it is the ultimate attainment of benefit or the averting of harm, and at a state of attainment.
48:6: 6- And He punishes the hypocrites, men and women, and the polytheists, men and women is in apposition to enters unless you make it a substitute, in which case it is in apposition to what it replaces. Those who think evil of God thinks evil, which is that He will not support His Messenger and the believers. Upon them is a circle of evil is a circle of what they think and lie in wait for the believers, it will not pass them by. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the circle of evil with the damma, and they are two dialects, but the open one is more common in that what is intended to be condemned is added to it, and the closed one is used in the manner of evil, and both are originally a source. And God has become angry with them and has cursed them and prepared Hell for them is in apposition to what they deserved in the Hereafter with what they deserved in this world. The waw in the others and the position is the position of the fa, since the curse is a cause of the preparation, and the wrath is a cause of it, since all are independent in the threat without taking into account the relativity. And an evil destination is Hell.
48:7: 7- “To God belong the soldiers of the heavens and the earth. And ever is God Exalted in Might and Wise.”
48:8: 8- Indeed, We have sent you as a witness over your nation. And a bringer of good tidings and a warner regarding obedience and disobedience.
48:9: 9- That you may believe in God and His Messenger The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Ummah, or to them, as his address is given the same status as their address. And honor Him and strengthen Him by strengthening His religion and His Messenger. And respect Him and glorify Him. And glorify Him and praise Him or pray to Him morning and evening morning and evening or always. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the four verbs with the letter Ya, and it was read Ta'azruhu with a sukoon on the 'ayn and Ta'azruhu with a fatha on the ta' and a damma or kasra on the zay and Ta'azruhu with two Zays and Tawqarruhu from awqarah meaning he honored him.
48:10: 10- Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are only pledging allegiance to God because he is the one meant by his pledge. The hand of God is over their hands is a state or a renewed resumption confirming it by way of imagination. But whoever breaks his pledge breaks the covenant. He only breaks it to the detriment of his own soul so the harm of his breaking it will only come to him. And whoever fulfills what he has pledged to God in his pledge He will give him a great reward which is Paradise. It was read as Ahd and Hafs read upon him with a damma on the ha' and Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Ibn Amir and Ruh read Fasna'tuhi with a noon. The verse was revealed about the Pledge of Ridwan.
48:11: 11- The Bedouins who stayed behind will say to you, They are Aslam, Juhayna, Muzayna, and Ghifar. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called them to mobilization in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, but they stayed behind, claiming that they were busy with their wealth and families. What kept them behind was their failure, weakness of faith, and fear of fighting the Quraysh if they repelled them. Our wealth and families distracted us, as there was no one to take care of their concerns. It was read with a shaddah for emphasis. Then ask forgiveness for us, from God for staying behind. They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, denying their apology and seeking forgiveness. Say, 'Who can control anything for you against God?' So who can prevent you from His will and decree? If He intended to harm you, something that would harm you, such as killing, defeat, or loss of wealth and family, as punishment for staying behind. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a dammah. Or He intended to benefit you, something that contradicts that, and it is an allusion to rejection. Rather, God is All-Aware of what you do. He knows your failure and your intention in it.
48:12: 12- But you thought that the Messenger and the believers would never return to their families, because you thought that the polytheists would uproot them. Ahl is the plural of ahl and it can be pluralized as ahlat like ardhat because its root is ahla, while ahal is the plural of kiliyal. And that was made attractive to your hearts so it was firmly established in them, and it was read in the construction of the agent, which is God or Satan. And you thought an evil thought is the thought mentioned, and what is meant is to record it with evil or it and all the rest of what they think about God and His Messenger of the perverted matters. And you were a people who perished perished in the sight of God because of the corruption of your beliefs and the evil of your intentions.
48:13: 13And whoever does not believe in God and His Messenger - then indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers a Blaze. The disbelievers are placed in place of the pronoun to indicate that whoever does not combine belief in God and His Messenger is a disbeliever and that he deserves the Blaze because of his disbelief. The indefiniteness of the Blaze is for emphasis or because it is a specific fire.
48:14: 14- And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He manages it as He wills. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, since there is no obligation upon Him. And God is Forgiving and Merciful. For forgiveness and mercy are from His essence, and punishment is included under His judgment by accident. Therefore, it is stated in the divine hadith, My mercy precedes My wrath.
48:15: 15- Those who stayed behind will say meaning those mentioned When you set out to take the spoils meaning the spoils of Khaybar, for he (peace and blessings be upon him) returned from Hudaybiyyah in Dhul-Hijjah of the year six and stayed in Madinah for the rest of it and the beginning of Muharram, then he raided Khaybar with those who had witnessed Hudaybiyyah, so he conquered it and seized a lot of money which he designated for them. Leave us to follow you They want to change the word of God, meaning His promise to the people of Hudaybiyyah that He would compensate them from the spoils of Makkah with the spoils of Khaybar. It was also said that God the Almighty said: You will never go out with me and it appears that it was in Tabuk. Speech is a noun for addressing and is prevalent in the useful sentence. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read God spoke which is the plural of word. Say, 'You will never follow us' is a negation in the sense of prohibition. Thus said God before before they prepared to go out to Khaybar. And they will say, 'Rather, you envy us' that he shares with you in the spoils, and it was read with the kasra. Rather, they did not understand "they did not understand except a little" except a little understanding, which is their intelligence in worldly matters. The meaning of the first interruption is a response from them that God's ruling is that they should not follow them and confirmation of envy, and the second is a response from God to that and confirmation of their ignorance of matters of religion.
48:16: 16- Say to those of the Bedouins who stayed behind He repeated this name to exaggerate the blame and to indicate the enormity of staying behind. You will be called to a people of great strength Banu Hanifa or others who apostatized after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the polytheists, for He said: You will fight them or they submit meaning that it will be one of the two options: either fighting or Islam, nothing else, as indicated by the reading or they submit, and whoever is not them will be fought until he submits or pays the jizyah. This indicates the Imamate of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, if this call did not coincide with anyone else, unless it is proven that they were Thaqeef and Hawazin, for that was during the era of the Prophet. It was said that it was the Persians and the Romans, and the meaning of they submit is they submit, so as to include their acceptance of the jizyah. Then if you obey, God will give you a good reward which is the spoils of war in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter. And if you turn away as you turned away before from Al-Hudaybiyyah. He will punish you with a painful punishment to double your crime.
48:17: 17- There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the ill. When He threatened for staying behind, He negated the blame from these excused ones, excluding them from the threat. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow. He separated the promise and made the threat more general, exaggerating the promise for His prior mercy. Then He made up for that by repetition in the way of generalization, saying: And whoever turns away - He will punish him with a painful punishment. Since intimidation here is more beneficial than encouragement, Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read We will admit him and punish him with the letter nun.
48:18: 18- God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. It was narrated that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived at Al-Hudaybiyah, he sent Jawas ibn Umayyah Al-Khuza'i to the people of Mecca. They intended to attack him, but the Abyssinians prevented him, so he returned. Then he sent Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him who imprisoned him, and rumours spread of his death. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called his companions, who were 1,300, 400, or 500, and pledged allegiance to them to fight the Quraysh and not to flee from them. He was sitting under a tamarisk tree or lote tree. He knew what was in their hearts of sincerity, so He sent down tranquility upon them tranquility and peace of mind through encouragement or peace and rewarded them with an imminent victory the victory of Khaybar after their departure, and it was said that it was Mecca or Hajar.
48:19: 19- And they will take many spoils. Meaning, the spoils of the All-Knowing. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise. Dominant, observing the requirements of wisdom.
48:20: 20- God has promised you abundant spoils which you will take. This refers to the spoils of war that will be given to the believers until the Day of Resurrection. So He has hastened this for you. This refers to the position at Khaybar. And He has restrained the hands of the people from you. This refers to the hands of the people of Khaybar and their successors from Banu Asad and Ghatafan, or the hands of Quraysh due to the peace treaty. And that this balance or spoils may be a sign for the believers. This is a sign by which they know that they have a place with God, or the Messenger was truthful in his promise to them to conquer Khaybar upon his return from Hudaybiyyah, or the counting of the spoils or a title for the conquest of Mecca. The conjunction with something omitted is the reason for restraint, or hasten, such as so that you may submit, or so that you may take, or the reason for something omitted, such as do that. "And guide you to a straight path," which is trust in God's grace and reliance on Him.
48:21: 21- And another and other spoils are conjoined with these, or are in the accusative case by a verb that explains them. God has encompassed them like He has decided. It is possible for it to be in the nominative case because it is described, and for it to be in the genitive case because of the omission of Lord. "You were not able to control them" after what was in them of the round. "God has encompassed them" took control and made you triumph over them, and they are the spoils of Hawazin or Persia. "And God is over all things competent" because His power is intrinsic and is not specific to one thing over another.
48:22: 22- And if those who disbelieved from the people of Mecca fought you and did not make peace, they would turn their backs and be defeated. Then they would not find a protector to guard them. Nor a helper to support them.
48:23: 23- The way of God that has passed before meaning the way of His prophets’ victory is an ancient way for the nations that have passed, as God Almighty said: I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. “And you will not find in the way of God any change” any alteration.
48:24: 24- And it is He who restrained their hands from you meaning the hands of the infidels of Mecca and your hands from them in the valley of Mecca inside Mecca after He had given you victory over them He had made you victorious over them. This is because Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl went out with five hundred men to Al-Hudaybiyyah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid bin Al-Walid with an army and he defeated them until he brought them inside the walls of Mecca and then he returned. It was said that this was on the day of the conquest and it was used as evidence that Mecca was conquered by force, but this is weak since the surah was revealed before that. And God is All-Seeing of what you do of fighting them first in obedience to His Messenger and restraining them secondly to honor His House. Abu Amr read it with a ya' Baseer meaning He will reward them for it.
48:25: 25- They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from al-Masjid al-Haram and the sacrificial animal, prevented from reaching its destination. This indicates that this was in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, and the sacrificial animal is what is offered to Mecca. The word al-hady was also read, and it is a fa'il with the meaning of maf'ul, and its location is the place where it is permissible to slaughter it, and what is meant is its usual place, which is Mina, not its place where it is not permissible to slaughter it anywhere else. Otherwise, the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have slaughtered it when he was prevented. This does not constitute evidence for the Hanafis that the place of slaughtering the sacrificial animal of one who is prevented is the Sacred Mosque. And had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know you would not have known them by their identities because they had mixed with the polytheists. lest you trample them means that you would have overthrown them and destroyed them. He said: And our tread was a tread of anger, the tread of the chained, fixed-age man And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The last place God treaded upon was Waj. It is a valley in Taif, and it was the last battle of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in it. Its root is Ad-Daws, and it is a badal ishtilam from men and women or from their pronoun in you learn them. “Then you will be afflicted by them” from their side with shame something disliked, such as the obligation of blood money and expiation for killing them, and to feel sorry for them, and to reproach the infidels for that and the sin of neglecting to search for it, the active participle of ‘ara if he exposes him to something he dislikes. without knowledge is related to that you trample them, meaning that you trample them without knowing them. The answer to had it not been for is omitted because the speech indicates it, and the meaning is had it not been for because of the disbelief that you destroy believing people among the disbelievers, ignorant of them, and that an evil would befall you because of their destruction, because you had withheld your hands from them. That God may include in His mercy is the reason for what was indicated by withholding the hands from the people of Mecca, in order to protect the believers in it, meaning that it was for God to include in His mercy, that is, in His success, to increase good or for Islam. whoever He wills of their believers or polytheists. had they separated had they dispersed and distinguished themselves from one another. It was also read had they separated. "We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment" by killing and captivity.
48:26: 26- When those who disbelieved is understood as a mention or an adverbial phrase We would have punished you or turned you away. In their hearts is arrogance and haughtiness. The arrogance of the Age of Ignorance that prevents submission to the truth. So God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers. He sent down upon them steadfastness and dignity. This is what was narrated: “When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was about to fight them, they sent Suhayl ibn Amr or Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza and Mukraz ibn Hafs to ask him to return that year on the condition that the Quraysh would leave Mecca for him for three days. He agreed and they wrote a document among themselves. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Ali may God be pleased with him: Write: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. They said: We do not know this. Write: In your name, O God. Then he said: Write: This is what the Messenger of God made peace with the people of Mecca. They said: If we had known that you were the Messenger of God, we would not have prevented you from the House and we would not have fought you. Write: This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah made peace with the people of Mecca. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Write what they want.” The believers understood that they would refuse and be violent towards them, so God sent down tranquility upon them, so they were humbled and endured. And He made them adhere to the word of piety, the word of testimony or In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Muhammad is the Messenger of God, which He chose for them, or steadfastness and fulfillment of the covenant. And the word is added to piety because it is its cause or the word of its people. And they were more deserving of it than others, and its people, “and those deserving of it,” and God is Knowing of all things, so He knows the people of everything and makes it easy for them.
48:27: 27- God has fulfilled the vision of His Messenger. He saw, peace and blessings be upon him, that he and his companions had entered Mecca safely, having shaved and cut their hair. He related the vision to his companions, and they were happy and thought that it would happen that year. When he was delayed, some of them said, By God, we have neither shaved nor cut our hair, nor have we seen the House. So this verse was revealed, and the meaning is that his vision was true. By the truth is connected to it, because what he saw will inevitably happen at the appointed time, which is the next year. It is possible that by the truth is an attribute of a deleted source, meaning truthfulness connected to by the truth, which is the intention to distinguish between the one who is steadfast in faith and the one who is wavering in it, and that it is an oath either in the name of God Almighty or by the opposite of falsehood. His saying, You shall enter the Sacred Mosque is its answer, and the first two are the answer to a deleted oath. If God wills is a condition for the number. By the will of God, as an instruction to the servants, or as a notification that some of them will not enter due to death or absence, or as a narration of what the Angel of Dreams, or the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to his companions. Safe is a state of the and and the condition is an interjection. Shave your heads and cut your hair meaning some of you will shave and others will cut their hair. Do not fear is a confirmatory state or a new sentence, meaning you will not fear after that. Then He knew what you did not know of the wisdom in delaying that. Then He made something short of that before you entered the mosque or the conquest of Mecca. An imminent conquest is the conquest of Khaybar so that the hearts of the believers may find comfort in it until the promised thing is made possible.
48:28: 28- It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance whether associated with it, because of it, or for its sake. And the religion of truth and the religion of Islam to make it prevail over all religion to make it prevail over all religions by abolishing what was true and demonstrating the corruption of what was false, or by giving authority over its people, since there is no people of a religion except that the Muslims have subdued them. This is an affirmation of what He promised of conquest. And sufficient is God as Witness that what He promised will come to pass, or of his prophethood by demonstrating miracles.
48:29: 29- Muhammad is the Messenger of God is a clause explaining the thing being testified to. It is possible that the Messenger of God is an adjective and Muhammad is an omitted predicate or a subject: And those with him is conjoined to it and their predicate is harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. "harsh is the plural of harsh and merciful is the plural of rahim". The meaning is that they are harsh with those who oppose their religion and merciful among themselves, as in His statement: "humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers. You see them bowing and prostrating" because they are busy praying most of the time. "seek bounty from God and approval" reward and approval. "Their mark is on their faces from the traces of prostration" meaning the mark that occurs on their foreheads from frequent prostration. So whoever marks him, if he informs him, it has been read as an extended word and "from the traces of prostration" is its explanation or a state of what is implied in the preposition. "That" is an allusion to the descriptive mentioned. Or an ambiguous indication that is explained by like a plant. Their likeness in the Torah is their amazing description mentioned therein. And their likeness in the Gospel is an appositive to it, meaning that is their likeness in the two books. His saying like a plant is a renewed representation or an explanation or a subject and like a plant is its predicate. He brought forth its shoot its chicks. It is said that the plant sprouts if it sprouted. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir, according to the narration of Ibn Dhakwan, read its shoot with fathahs, which is a dialect in it. It was read shtaah with a light hamza, and shtaah with a long vowel, and shtaah with a movement of the hamza and its deletion, and shtahu by changing it to a waw. So He supported him he strengthened him from support and in seeing or from the belt, which is assistance. Ibn Amir read, according to the narration of Ibn Dhakwan, “so He supported him like his wage in his wage. “So he became thick” so it changed from thinness to thick. "And it stood firm on its stalk" meaning it stood straight on its reeds. The plural of "saq is suquq" its stalk is pronounced with a hamza. "The farmers are amazed" by its density, strength, thickness and good appearance. It is an example that God the Almighty used for the Companions who were few in number at the beginning of Islam, then they multiplied and became strong, and their affair progressed to a point that amazed the people. "To enrage the disbelievers with them" is a reason for likening them to crops in their zakat and strength, or because God the Almighty said: "God has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have forgiveness and a great reward because when the disbelievers heard it, it enraged them, and from them" is for clarification. It is narrated from the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): "Whoever recites Surat al-Fath, it is as if he was among those who witnessed the conquest of Mecca with Muhammad (blessings and peace of God be upon him)."
49:1: 1- O you who have believed, do not advance meaning do not advance a matter. The object was omitted to dispel the illusion of everything that is possible, or it was left because the intended meaning is to negate the precedence completely or do not advance, and from this is the vanguard of the army for those who advance, and this is supported by the reading of Yaqub, do not advance. It was read do not advance from arrival. In the hands of God and His Messenger is borrowed from what is between the two opposite directions of the hands of a human being, to mock what they were forbidden, and the meaning is do not decide a matter before they judge it. It was said that what is meant is in the hands of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioning God is to glorify Him and to indicate that He is with God in a place that requires His reverence. And fear God in presenting or opposing the ruling. Indeed, God is Hearing of your words. Knowing of your actions.
49:2: 2- O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet meaning, when you speak to him, do not raise your voices above his voice. And do not raise your voices to him as you raise your voices to one another and do not raise your voices to him as you raise your voices to one another. Rather, make your voices lower than his voice to protect your welcome and to be respectful. It was said that its meaning is, do not address him by his name or nickname as you address one another, but address him as the Prophet and the Messenger. Repeating the call is to evoke more insight, exaggerate the admonition, and indicate the independence of the one being addressed and to increase the attention paid to him. That your deeds may be rendered worthless. The dislike that they may be rendered worthless is a reason for the prohibition, or that they may be rendered worthless, as the prohibition is against an action whose justification is based on performance, because speaking loudly and raising one's voice is a belittling gesture that may lead to disbelief that renders the deed worthless. This is because the intention to humiliate and not care is added to it. It has been narrated that Thabit ibn Qays had a deafness in his ear and he spoke loudly. When this verse was revealed, he stayed behind from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) checked on him and called him, saying: O Messenger of God, this verse has been revealed to you, and I am a man with a loud voice, so I fear that my deeds may have been rendered worthless. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: "You are not there. You will live well and die well, and you are among the people of Paradise." And you do not perceive that it renders the deed worthless.
49:3: 3- Indeed, those who lower their voices lower them. In the presence of the Messenger of God out of respect for etiquette, or for fear of disobeying the prohibition. It was said that Abu Bakr and Umar after that would whisper to him until he asked them questions. Those are the ones whose hearts God has tested for piety. He tested them for piety and trained them for it, or He made them know that they were for piety and purely for it, for testing is the cause of knowledge, and the lam is a deleted connective, or for the verb in consideration of the origin, or God struck their hearts with various trials and difficult tasks for the sake of piety, for it does not appear except through patience in it, or He made them pure for piety like He tests gold when he melts it and separates its pure gold from its impurity. For them is forgiveness for their sins. And a great reward for their anger and all their acts of obedience. The indefiniteness is for emphasis, and the sentence is a second predicate because or is a resumption to explain what is the reward of the angry ones, praising their state as He informed about it in a sentence composed of two definite articles. The subject is a demonstrative pronoun that includes what was made a title for them, and the predicate is connected by a connective that indicates that they have reached the utmost perfection, exaggerating the respect for their anger and accepting it, and alluding to the hideousness of raising and declaring, and that the state of the one who commits them is contrary to that.
49:4: 4- Indeed, those who call you from behind the rooms from outside, behind or in front of it, and from the beginning, as the calling originated from the direction behind, and its benefit is to indicate that the one calling is inside the room, as the beginning and end must differ in direction. The rooms were read with a fatha on the jim, or a sukoon on it, and the three are the plural of room, which is a piece of land surrounded by a wall, and that is why the camel pen is called a room. It is a verb with the meaning of a passive participle like a room and a handful, and what is meant are the rooms of the wives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and it is a metaphor for his seclusion with the women and their calling from behind them, either that they came to her room by room and called from behind it, or that they dispersed to the rooms seeking him, so the action of the parts was attributed to all. It was said that the one who called him was Uyaynah ibn Hisn and Al-Aqra’ ibn Habis, who were a delegation to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with seventy men from Banu Tamim at noon while he was asleep. They said, O Muhammad, come out to us. It was attributed to all of them because they were satisfied with it or ordered it, or because it was found among them. Most of them do not understand, since reason requires good manners and observing modesty, especially for someone in this position.
49:5: 5- And if they had been patient until you came out to them meaning, even if their patience and waiting until you came out to them was proven, then even if an indicates a source in its context, it indicates permanence by itself, and therefore it is necessary to omit the verb. until indicates that patience should be sufficient for its coming out, because it is specific to the ultimate goal of the thing in itself. Therefore, you say: I ate the fish up to its head, and you do not say until half of it, unlike to, which is general. to them indicates that if he had come out not for their sake, they should be patient until he initiates the conversation with them or addresses them. It would have been better for them. Patience would have been better for them than hastening, because it includes preserving good manners and respecting the Messenger, which necessitate praise and reward, and helping with the matter, since it was narrated that they came as intercessors for the prisoners of Banu al-Anbar, so He released half and ransomed the other half. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, as He limited Himself to advising and reprimanding these ill-mannered people who neglected to respect the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
49:6: 6- O you who have believed, if there comes to you a wicked person with information, verify it. So, know and investigate. It was narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, sent Al-Walid bin Uqba as a tax collector to Banu Al-Mustaliq, and there was enmity between him and them. When they heard about him, they welcomed him, thinking they were his fighters. He returned and said to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, that they had apostatized and refused to pay the zakat, so he intended to fight them, so this was revealed. It was also said that he sent Khalid bin Al-Walid to them and found them calling for prayer and performing voluntary night prayers, so they handed over the zakat to him, so he returned. The indefiniteness of the wicked person and the report is for generalization, and the connection of the command to verify to the wickedness of the informant requires the permissibility of accepting the report of a just person, since something is connected with the word if when it does not exist. And if the report of one person was required to be verified from the point of view of what it is, it would not have been based on wickedness, since the order indicates the reason, and what is specific is not explained by something else. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read fat-habatu meaning, then wait until the situation becomes clear to you, that you may strike. Hatred of your afflicting a people out of ignorance who are ignorant of their condition. So you become “so you become” regretful over what you did, grieving a necessary grief, wishing that it had not happened. The combination of these three letters is always in use.
49:7: 7- And know that among you is the Messenger of God that what is within its scope takes the place of the two objects of know in consideration of what it restricted to of the state, which is His saying: If he were to obey you in much of the matter, you would be in trouble because it is a state of one of the two pronouns of among you, and if it were made a resumption, the benefit of the command would not appear. The meaning is that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is in a state among you that must be changed, which is that you want him to follow your opinion in events. If he did that, you would be cursed, meaning you would fall into great hardship. This indicates that some of them suggested that he target Banu al-Mustaliq. His statement, But God has endeared faith to you and made it pleasing in your hearts and has made disbelief, immorality and disobedience hateful to you, is a correction to clarify their excuse, which is that it was due to their excessive love for faith and hatred of disbelief that they were driven to do that when they heard al-Walid’s statement, or due to the description of those among them who did not do that, praising their action and alluding to censuring those who did. This is supported by His statement, Those are the rightly guided, meaning those who are exempt are the ones who have followed the right path. And hated is transitive by itself to one object, and if it is stressed, another is added to it. However, since it includes a partial meaning, hated is relegated to the status of hatred, so it is transitive to another with to, or it is relegated to you as another object. Disbelief is covering up the blessings of God with ingratitude. Islamic depravity means deviating from the intended purpose, and disobedience means refusing to obey.
49:8: 8- A favor and blessing from God is an explanation for dislike or endearment and what is in between is an objection, no, no. The rightly guided ones because favor is the action of God, and right guidance, even if it is caused by an action attributed to their pronoun or a source other than an action, then endearment and right guidance are a favor and blessing from God. And God is Knowing of the conditions of the believers and the differences between them, Wise as He favors and bestows success upon them.
49:9: 9- And if two parties among the believers should fight they fight, and the plural is in consideration of the meaning, as each party is a plural. "Then make peace between them" by advising and calling to the judgment of God the Most High. But if one of them transgresses against the other transgresses against it. Then fight against the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of God returns to His judgment or what He has commanded. The word shadow is used to refer to shadow because it returns after the sun is abrogated, and the spoils because they return from the disbelievers to the Muslims. "But if it returns, then make peace between them with justice" by separating what is between them according to what God has decreed. The restriction of reconciliation to justice here is because it is likely to cause injustice, as it is after the fighting. And act justly and act justly in all matters. Indeed, God loves those who act justly He praises their actions with good reward. The verse was revealed regarding a fight that took place between the Aws and the Khazraj during his time, peace and blessings be upon him, with palm leaves and sandals. It indicates that the aggressor is a believer and that if he refrains from fighting, he should be left alone, as stated in the hadith, because he is subject to the command of God Almighty. It is also necessary to help the one who has been aggressed against after offering advice and striving for reconciliation.
49:10: 10- The believers are but brothers in that they are related to one origin, which is faith, which necessitates eternal life. This is a justification and confirmation of the command to make peace. That is why He repeated it in order with the letter fa, saying: "So make peace between your two brothers." He placed the apparent in place of the pronoun added to those commanded to exaggerate the confirmation and specification. He mentioned the two specifically because they are the ones least likely to cause discord between them. It was said that what is meant by the two brothers are the Aws and the Khazraj. It was read between your brothers and your brothers. "And fear God" in disobeying His rule and neglecting it. "Perhaps you will receive mercy" for your fear of God.
49:11: 11- O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. That is, let not some believing men and women ridicule others, for the one ridiculed may be better in the sight of God than the one ridiculing. The word people is specific to men because it is either a source of description, which is common in the plural for standing, like visitor and visitor. Caring for affairs is the job of men, as God the Most High said, Men are the protectors and maintainers of women. And when it was interpreted as the two tribes, like the people of Aad and Pharaoh, it is either by predominance or by sufficing with mentioning men over women, because they are subordinates. The plural was chosen because ridicule is prevalent in gatherings, and perhaps in its name is a resumption due to the reason that requires the prohibition, and it has no predicate because the name is sufficient for it. It was read perhaps that they will be and perhaps that they will be, so on this basis it has predicate. And do not backbite yourselves, that is, do not backbite each other, for the believers are as one soul, or do not do what you backbite, for whoever does what deserves Whoever backbites has backbitten himself. Backbiting is slander. Yaqub read it with the dammah. And do not insult one another by nicknames and do not call one another by bad nicknames, as backbiting is specifically used for bad nicknames according to custom. How evil is the name of immorality after faith meaning, how evil is the reputation of the believers to be mentioned for immorality after they have entered faith and are known for it. What is meant by this is either to disparage the attribution of disbelief and immorality to the believers in particular, as it was narrated that the verse “was revealed about Safiyyah bint Huyayy may God be pleased with her, who came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and said: ‘Women say to me, “O Jewess, daughter of two Jewesses.” He said to her, “Why did you not say, ‘My father is Aaron, my uncle is Moses, and my husband is Muhammad, peace be upon them?’” Or to indicate that backbiting is immorality and associating it with faith is reprehensible. And whoever does not repent from what God has forbidden. Then those are the wrongdoers by placing disobedience in place of obedience and exposing oneself to punishment.
49:12: 12- O you who have believed, avoid much [negative] assumption. Be on the side of it, and the ambiguity of much is so that one is cautious in every assumption and ponders until he knows which type it is from, for there is some assumption that must be followed, such as assumption when there is no decisive factor in actions and good opinion of God, the Most High, and what is forbidden, such as assumption in matters of divinity and prophethood when there is a decisive factor, and bad opinion of the believers, and what is permissible, such as assumption in everyday matters. Indeed, some assumption is sin is a new command, and sin is the wrongdoing for which one deserves punishment. The hamza in it is a substitute for the waw, as if it means that deeds are sinful, meaning by breaking them. And do not spy and do not search for the faults of Muslims. The verb is derived from jass considering what it contains of a meaning of seeking, like groping. It is read with a ha from hass which is the effect of groping and its goal. That is why the five senses are called spyers. In the hadith: Do not pursue the faults of Muslims, for whoever pursues their faults, God will pursue his faults until He disgraces him, even if it is in his own home. “And do not backbite one another” and do not speak badly of one another in their absence. “The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was asked about backbiting, so he said: ‘To mention your brother in a way that he dislikes. If that is true then you have backbitten him, and if that is not true then you have slandered him.’” Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? This is an example of what the backbiter gets from exposing the backbiter in the most obscene way, with the exaggerations of the established question, and attributing the action to someone for the sake of generalization and attaching love to what is extremely detestable, and the example of backbiting is eating human flesh and making what is eaten a brother and a dead person, and following that with his saying: And you hated it as a confirmation and confirmation of that. The meaning is that if that is true or this is presented to you, then you hated it and you cannot deny hating it, and the accusative of dead is in the state of the flesh or the brother, and Nafi' stressed it. “And fear God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” For whoever fears what He has forbidden and repents from what He has imposed. The emphasis is on the Forgiving because it is eloquent in accepting repentance, as it makes its owner as if he had not sinned, or because of the large number of those who are repented to or because of the large number of their sins. It was narrated: “Two men from the Companions sent Salman to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to get them some food. Usamah was at his table, so he said: I have nothing. Salman told them, and they said: If we sent him to the well of Samiha, its water would boil away. When they went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said to them: Why do I see meat in your mouths? They said: We have not eaten meat. He said: You have backbitten each other. So this was revealed.”
49:13: 13- O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female from Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, or We created each one of you from a father and a mother, so all are equal in that, so there is no point in boasting about lineage. It may be a confirmation of brotherhood that prevents backbiting. And We made you peoples and tribes The people is the great group related to one origin and it includes the tribes. The tribe includes the buildings. The building includes the clans. The clan includes the thighs. The thigh includes the factions, so Khuzaymah is a people, Kinanah is a tribe, Quraysh is a building, Qusay is a clan, Hashim is a thigh, and Abbas is a faction. Before the peoples are the clans of the Persians and the tribes are the clans of the Arabs. That you may know one another so that you may know one another, not to boast about fathers and tribes. It was read that you may know one another with assimilation, and that you may know one another and that you may know one another and that you may know one another and that you may know one another The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. For righteousness is what perfects souls and distinguishes people. So whoever desires honor, let him seek it from it, as the Prophet, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: Whoever wants to be the most honorable of people, let him fear God. And he, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: “O people, people are of two types: a believing, righteous man who is honored in the sight of God, and a wicked, wretched man who is insignificant in the sight of God.” Indeed, God is All-Knowing of you and Aware of your inner selves.
49:14: 14- The Bedouins said, 'We have believed.' This was revealed about a group of Banu Asad who came to Madinah during a year of drought and declared the two testimonies of faith. They used to say to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), "We have come to you with our heavy loads and our children, and we have not fought you as Banu so-and-so fought you, seeking charity and as a favor. "Say, 'You have not believed.'" Faith is belief coupled with trust and peace of mind, and you did not achieve it except when you bestowed Islam upon the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and abandoned fighting, as indicated by the end of the Surah. "But say, 'We have submitted.'" Islam is submission, entering into peace, declaring the two testimonies of faith, and abandoning fighting. This is indicated by the way the verse was structured so that it would not be said, "Do not say, 'We have believed,' but say, 'We have submitted,' or You have not believed, but you have submitted." So he shifted to this structure as a precaution against the prohibition of saying faith and being certain of their Islam, which has lost the condition for it to be considered valid in Islamic law. "And when faith has not yet entered your hearts is a timing for say" as it is a state of its pronoun, meaning: "but say, 'We have submitted,'" and your hearts have not yet agreed with your tongues. "And if you obey God and His Messenger" with sincerity and abandoning hypocrisy. "He will not deprive you of anything of your deeds" will not deprive you of their reward. "Anything from La yalayta" if it decreases. The two Basrans read "La yalayta from alat" which is the language of Ghatafan. "Indeed, God is Forgiving" for what the obedient have neglected. "Merciful" in His favor towards them.
49:15: 15- The believers are only those who have believed in God and His Messenger and then have not doubted. They did not complain about the doubt of the one who obeyed him, as it caused him to fall into doubt and suspicion, and in it is an indication of what required denying faith from them, and then is to indicate that the condition of not doubting in considering faith is not only in the state of faith, but also in it and in what is to come, as in His statement: then they remained steadfast. “And strive with their wealth and their lives in the cause of God” in His obedience. Striving with wealth and their lives is suitable for all financial and physical acts of worship. Those are the truthful, those who were truthful in their claim of faith.
49:16: 16- "Say, 'Do you inform God of your religion?' Do you inform Him of it by saying, 'We believe?' And God knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and God is Knowing of all things.' Nothing is hidden from Him, and this is to make them ignorant and to rebuke them. It was narrated that when the previous verse was revealed, they came and swore that they were believers and had faith, so this verse was revealed.
49:17: 17- They consider their Islam a favor to you. They consider their Islam to be a favor to you, which is a blessing for which the one who bestowed it does not seek recompense from the one who bestowed it upon him. It is from the word mann meaning to cut off, because what is meant by it is to cut off his need. It was also said that a heavy blessing is from the word mann. "Say, 'Do not consider your Islam a favor to me.'" That is, their Islam. The word is in the accusative case by removing the preposition or by including the meaning of moderation in the verb. "Rather, God bestows a favor upon you that He has guided you to faith," as you claim, even though guidance does not necessitate being rightly guided. It was read "if He guides you with a kasra, and when He guides you." If you are truthful in your claim of faith, and the answer to it is omitted and indicated by what precedes it, i.e., then God is the one who bestows favor upon you. And in the context of the verse there is a kindness, which is that when they heard what came from them as faith and they believed in it, then He denied that it was faith and called it Islam by saying, They bestow favor upon you with what is in reality Islam, and it is not worthy of His bestowing it upon you. Rather, if their claim of faith is true, then God is the one who bestows favor upon them by guiding Him, not them.
49:18: 18- Indeed, God knows the unseen in the heavens and the earth what is hidden in them. And God is Seeing of what you do in secret and in public, so how could what is in your hearts be hidden from Him? Ibn Kathir read it with the letter ya because of the absence in the verse. On the authority of the Prophet, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, Whoever recites Surat Al-Hujurat will be given a reward equal to the number of those who obeyed God and those who disobeyed Him.
50:1: 1- “Qaf. By the Glorious Qur’an.” The discussion of it is as mentioned in “Sad. 50:2: 2- Rather, they were amazed that a warner had come to them from among themselves. This is a denial of their amazement at something that is not a wonder, which is that someone from their own race or from their own skin should warn them. Then the disbelievers said, 'This is an amazing thing.' This is a narration of their amazement, and this is an indication of God's choice of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, for the message, and the omission of their mention and then its manifestation is to indicate their stubbornness in this statement, then the recording of their disbelief in that or linking their amazement at the resurrection to their amazement at the mission, and exaggerating it by placing the apparent in place of their pronoun and narrating their amazement in a vague manner if the reference was to from among them it is explained by what follows it, or in a general manner if it is easier than what they see of his doing.
50:3: 3- If we die and become dust meaning, will we return if we die and become dust? The omitted word is indicated by his statement: That is a far-fetched return meaning far from imagination, custom, or possibility. It was said that return means what is returned.
50:4: 4- We know what the earth takes from them what it eats from the bodies of their dead, and it is a response to their exclusion by removing what is the origin of it, and it was said that it is the answer to the oath and the lam is omitted due to the length of the speech. And with Us is a Preserving Book that preserves the details of all things, or preserved from change, and what is meant is either a representation of His knowledge of the details of things with the knowledge of one who has a preserved book that he looks at, or an emphasis on His knowledge of them by their being recorded in the Preserved Tablet that He has.
50:5: 5- Rather, they denied the truth meaning the prophethood established by miracles, or the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the Qur'an when it came to them, they understood and it was read as lamma with a kasra. in a confused matter disturbed from the shaking of the ring on his finger if it came out, and that is their saying sometimes that he is a poet and sometimes that he is a magician and sometimes that he is a soothsayer.
50:6: 6- Have they not looked when they disbelieved in the resurrection. at the sky above them at the traces of God Almighty’s power in creating the world. How We constructed it We raised it without pillars. And adorned it with planets. And it has no rifts. So beware that He created it smooth, its layers adhering together.
50:7: 7- And the earth We have spread out We have expanded it. And We have cast therein firm mountains “firm mountains.” And We have caused to grow therein of every kind “delightful” beautiful.
50:8: 8- An insight and a reminder for every penitent servant who returns to his Lord, contemplating the wonders of His creation. They are two causes for the meaning of the aforementioned verbs, even though they are in the accusative case for the last verb.
50:9: 9- And We sent down from the sky blessed water with many benefits and We caused to grow thereby gardens of trees and fruits. And the grain for the harvest and the grain for the crops that are meant to be harvested, such as wheat and barley.
50:10: 10- And tall palm trees Tall or pregnant from the verb absaqat when the sheep becomes pregnant, so it is from the verb af'al which is fa'il. 50:11: 11- Provision for the servants is a reason for We caused to grow or a source, for the affirmation is provision. And We revived thereby with that water. A dead land is a barren land with no growth in it. Likewise the exit as You revived this land, so will your exit be alive after your death.
50:12: 12- The people of Noah, the companions of Ar-Rass, and Thamud denied before them.
50:13: 13- And Aad and Pharaoh He meant by Pharaoh himself and his people to fit what came before and after it. And Lot's brothers were his brothers because they were his in-laws.
50:14: 14- And the companions of the thicket and the people of Tubba' previously mentioned in Al-Hijr and Ad-Dukhan. All denied the messengers meaning each one or a group of them or all of them, and the pronoun is singular because its wording is singular. 50:15: 15- Are We weary with the first creation? That is, are We unable to create, so that We are unable to repeat it? That is, they do not deny Our ability to create the first creation, rather they are in confusion and doubt about a renewed creation because it violates custom. 50:17: 17- When the two receivers receive is understood by mention or related to closer, meaning He knows his condition better than any close one when he receives, meaning the two guardians receive what he says, and in it is an indication that He is independent of the guardianship of the two angels, for He knows better than them and is aware of what is hidden from them, but it is due to a wisdom that required it, which is what it contains of severity that discourages the servant from disobedience, and an emphasis on considering and controlling deeds for the reward and the obligation of the proof on the Day when the witnesses arise. 50:18: 18-No word is uttered "No word is thrown out of his mouth. Except that there is a watcher by him "An angel watches his work. 50:19: 19- And the intoxication of death will come in truth. 50:32: 32- This is what you are promised implying the people and pointing to the reward or the source of azalfat and Ibn Kathir read it with the letter ya.
