50:40: 40- "And during part of the night, glorify Him" meaning, glorify Him during some of the night. "And during the ends of prostration" and the aftermath of the prayers is the plural of dabr from adbara. The two Hijazis, Hamzah, and Khalaf read it with kasra from adbarat al-salat when it has ended. It was said that what is meant by tasbeeh is the prayer, so the prayer before sunrise and before sunset is the noon and afternoon prayers, and during the night are the two evening prayers, and the tahajjud and after prostration are the voluntary prayers after the obligatory prayers. It was said that the witr is after the evening prayer.
50:41: 41- "And listen to what He has informed you of regarding the conditions of the Resurrection, and in it is awe and glorification of the one who is informed of it, On the Day when the caller will call" Israfil or Gabriel, peace be upon them both, and he will say: "O you rotten bones, torn flesh, and scattered hair, indeed God commands you to gather for the passing of judgment. From a place nearby" such that His call will reach everyone equally, and perhaps in repetition it is similar to yours in manifestation, and the Day is set up by what is indicated by the Day of Resurrection.
50:42: 42- "The Day they hear the Shout is a substitute for it, and the Shout" is the second blast. "In truth is related to the Shout" and what is meant by it is resurrection for recompense. "That is the Day of Resurrection" from the graves, and it is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, and it may be said of the servant.
50:43: 43- Indeed, it is We who bring to life and cause to die in this world, and to Us is the final destination for recompense in the Hereafter.
50:44: 44- "The Day it will split Split, and it was read as Split". Asim, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, Khalaf and Abu Amr read it with a light shin. "The earth will be removed from them quickly" Hurrying. "That is a gathering" Bahath and gathering. "For Us is easy" Easy. The adverbial phrase is brought forward for specificity, as that is not easy except for the All-Knowing, All-Powerful in and of Himself, and no matter distracts Him from another matter, as God the Most High said: "He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul."
50:45: 45- "We know best what they say" as a consolation to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a threat to them. "And you are not a compeller over them" with authority to make them believe, or do with them what you want, you are only a caller. "So remind with the Qur'an whoever fears My threat" because no one will benefit from it except him. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Whoever recites Surat Qaf, God will make the times of death and its agonies easy for him." And God knows best.
51:1: 1- "And the scatterers scatter" meaning the winds that scatter dust and other things, or the fertile women who scatter children, or the causes that scatter creation from angels and others. Abu Amr and Hamza read it by assimilating the taa' into the dal.
51:2: 2- "Those who carry a burden" means the clouds carrying rain, or the winds carrying the clouds, or pregnant women, or the reasons for that. It was read "burden" based on the naming of the carrier by the source.
51:3: 3- "And those that run smoothly" means ships that run smoothly in the sea, or the winds that run in their directions, or the planets that run in their mansions. "Smoothly" is an adjective of a deleted noun, meaning running smoothly.
51:4: 4- And those who divide a matter are the angels who divide matters such as rain, provisions, and other things, or what is common to them and others from the reasons for division, or the wind divides the rain by distributing the clouds. If it is carried on different entities with the letter fa to arrange the divisions with it in consideration of what is between them of the difference in indicating the perfection of power, otherwise the letter fa is for arranging the actions since the winds, for example, scatter vapors into the atmosphere until they form clouds, then they carry it and run with it, spreading it to where they are commanded to do so, then they divide the rain with.
51:6: 6- "And the religion is certain" is the answer to the oath, as if he used his ability to do these amazing things that contradict the requirements of nature as evidence of his ability to resurrect for the promised reward. "Ma is a relative pronoun or a verbal noun, and the religion" is the reward and the actual occurrence.
51:7: 7- "And the heaven of interwoven paths" of paths, and what is meant is either the tangible paths which are the path of the planets or the rational paths which the observers follow and by which they reach knowledge, or the stars which have paths or they are like what the embroiderer adorns the paths of embroidery. Plural of Ḥabīkah like Ṭarīq and Ṭarūq or Ḥabbak like mithl and mithl. Perhaps the point in this section is to liken their opinions in their differences and contradiction of their purposes to the ways of the heavens in their distance and the difference in their goals.
51:9: 9- Whoever turns away from him turns away from him turns away from him and the pronoun refers to the Messenger or the Qur’an or faith, from turning away since there is no turning away more severe than it, so it is as if there is no turning away in relation to it, or turning away from turning away in the knowledge and judgment of God and it is possible that the pronoun refers to speech in the sense that Afka comes from Afka about the different speech and because of it like his saying: They forbid eating and drinking That is, their prohibition stems from them and their cause. 51:10: 10- "The liars were killed" are the ones who have different opinions. Its origin is a prayer for killing that was treated as a curse.
51:11: 11- Those who are in the midst of ignorance in the midst of ignorance. Heedless oblivious to what they have been commanded to do.
51:12: 12- "They ask, 'When is the Day of Judgment?' That is, they say, When is the Day of Judgment? That is, when will it occur? When" is read with a kasra.
51:13: 13- "The Day they are on the Fire and are tested." They are burned. This is an answer to the question, meaning it occurs "The Day they are on the Fire and are tested, or it is The Day they are on the Fire and are tested. The opening of the Day" is because it is added to something that is not established, and this is indicated by the fact that it was read in the nominative case.
51:14: 14- "Taste your trial" meaning this statement will be said to them. "This is what you were hastening for This is the punishment that you were hastening for, and it is possible that this is a substitute for your trial and which" is its description.
51:15: 15- Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs.
51:16: 16- taking what their Lord has given them accepting what He has given them and being satisfied with it, meaning that everything He has given them is good, pleasing, and accepted. Indeed, they were before that doers of good they did good deeds, and this is an explanation of why they deserved that.
51:17: 17- They slept but little of the night is an explanation of their good deeds, and ma is an additional word meaning they slept in a part of the night, or they slept a little sleep, or it is a verbal noun or a relative pronoun, meaning in a little of the night they slept, or in which they slept, and it is not permissible for it to be negative because ma after it does not act on what preceded it. And in it are exaggerations to diminish their sleep and rest, the mention of little and the night which is the time of hibernation, and slumber which is escaping from sleep and the addition of ma. 18- And in the hours of the pre-dawn hours they seek forgiveness. That is, despite their little sleep and much prayer, when they wake up in the early hours of the morning they begin to seek forgiveness as if they had committed crimes in the night. The construction of the verb with the pronoun indicates that they are more deserving of that due to their abundant knowledge of God and their fear of Him. God
51:19: 19- And in their wealth is a right a share that they deserve for themselves as a way of drawing closer to God and out of compassion for people. For the beggar and the deprived for the one who begs and the one who is too chaste to accept charity, who thinks he is rich. God
51:20: 20- And on the earth are signs for those of certain faith meaning that there are signs in it of the types of minerals and animals, or aspects of signs of rolling and stillness and the elevation of some of them above the water and the difference in their parts in qualities, properties and benefits, which indicate the existence of the Creator and His knowledge, power, will, unity and the abundance of His mercy. God
51:21: 21- And in yourselves meaning, and in yourselves are signs, since there is nothing in the world except that in man there is a counterpart that indicates its significance, along with what he has uniquely possessed of beneficial forms, beautiful sights, and wondrous compositions, the ability to perform strange actions, deduce various crafts, and gather diverse perfections. Do you not see? Do you not look with the gaze of one who considers. God
51:22: 22- And in the sky is your provision means the causes of your provision or its determination. It was said that what is meant by the sky is the clouds and by provision is the rain because it is the cause of sustenance. And what you are promised of reward because Paradise is above the seventh heaven, or because the deeds and their reward are written and determined in the sky. It was said that it is a new verse, the predicate of which is:
51:23: 23- By the Lord of the heaven and the earth, it is the truth. Based on this, the pronoun refers to what. According to the first opinion, it could refer to it and to what was mentioned about the signs, provision, and promise. Like your speech. That is, like your speech. Just as you have no doubt that you speak, you should not doubt that this is true. The accusative is in the state of the implied in the truth or the description of a deleted source, that is, it is the truth, like your speech. It was said that it is built on the fat-ha because it is added to something that is not established, which is what if it means something, and in with what is in its scope if it is made redundant, and its place is the nominative as an attribute of the truth. This is supported by the reading of Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr in the nominative case.
51:24: 24-"Has there come to you the story of Abraham's guests?" This emphasizes the importance of the story and points out that it was revealed to him. The word "guest" is originally a verbal noun and therefore it is used for both singular and plural forms. It was said that there were twelve angels. It was also said that there were three: Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil. They were called "guests" because they were in the form of guests. "The honored ones" means honored by God or by Abraham, as he served them himself and his wife.
51:25: 25- "When they entered upon him is an adverbial phrase for speech or guest or honored ones". "They said, 'Peace'" meaning, we greet you with peace. "He said, 'Peace'" meaning, upon you be peace. He changed it to the nominative case in the beginning in order to make it steadfast so that his greeting would be better than theirs. They were both read as nominatives. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read, "Peace be upon you", and it was read as accusative, but the meaning is the same. "A people who are unknown" meaning, you are a people who are unknown. He did not recognize them because he thought they were the sons of Adam and did not recognize them, or because peace was not their greeting, for he knew Islam, which is like getting to know them.
51:26: 26- He went back to his family" so he went to them secretly from his guest, because it is part of the etiquette of a host to hasten to offer hospitality, in order to avoid the guest being bored or having to wait. "So he brought a fat calf" because most of his property was cows.
51:27: 27- So he brought it near to them by placing it in front of them. He said, 'Will you not eat?' meaning from it, and this indicates that it was Haneeth. The hamza in it is for display and urging people to eat in a polite manner, as he said it the first time he placed it, and for denial, as he said it when he saw their aversion.
51:28: 28- So he felt fear of them." So he concealed his fear of them when he saw them turning away from his food, thinking that they had come to him for evil. It was said that it occurred to him that they were angels sent to be punished. "They said, 'Do not fear.' We are messengers of God." Gabriel stroked the calf with his wing, and it rose and ran until it joined its mother. He recognized them and felt safe from them. "And they gave him good tidings of a boy." He was Isaac, peace be upon him. "Knowing." He completed his knowledge when he reached maturity.
51:29: 29- So his wife Sarah came to her house and was in a corner watching them in a shriek with a creaking cry, and its place is the accusative case as a state or a direct object if so she came begins with took. So she slapped her face so she slapped her forehead with the tips of her fingers, the action of someone who is astonished. It was said that she felt the heat of menstrual blood so she slapped her face out of shyness. And a barren old woman said meaning I am old, so how can I give birth?
51:30: 30-"They said, 'Likewise,' like that which He gave us good tidings of. Your Lord said, We only inform you of it from Him. Indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing." So His words are true and His actions are decisive.
51:31: 31- He said, 'What is the matter with you, O messengers?' When he knew that they were angels and that they did not descend together except for a great matter, he asked about it.
51:32: 32- They said, 'We have been sent to a people of criminals.' They meant the people of Lot.
51:33: 33- We will send upon them stones of clay. He means the baked clay, for it is petrified clay.
51:34: 34- Marked with your Lord sent from the word marked for cattle, or marked from the word mark, which means sign. “For the transgressors” who exceed the limit in immorality.
51:35: 35- So We brought out whoever was in it in the villages of Lot’s people, and its being omitted and not mentioned because it was known. Of the believers from among those who believed in Lot.
51:36: 36- And we did not find in it anything but a house of Muslims except for the people of a house of Muslims. This was used as evidence for the unity of faith and Islam, but it is weak because this only requires the truth of the believer and the Muslim regarding those who follow him, and this does not require the unity of their two concepts because it is permissible for different concepts to be true regarding one person.
51:37: 37- And We left therein a sign a mark. For those who fear the painful punishment they are the ones who will take heed from it. It is those stones, or a rock poured into it, or a black, stinking water.
51:38: 38- And in Moses is in apposition to and in the earth, or We left in it meaning and made in Moses, as in His saying: I fed her straw and cold water. When We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority. It is a miracle like the staff and the hand.
51:39: 39- So he turned away with his support meaning he turned away from believing in Him, as in His statement, And he distanced himself from his side or he turned away with what he used to strengthen himself with from His soldiers, and it is a name for what something relies on and is strengthened by. It was read with a damma on the kaf. And a magician said meaning he is a magician. Or a madman as if he attributed the miracles that appeared to him to the jinn, and there was some doubt as to whether that happened by his choice and effort or by something else.
51:40: 40- So We seized him and his soldiers and threw them into the sea. So We drowned them in the sea. And he was blameworthy. He committed what he was blamed for of disbelief and stubbornness, and the sentence is a state of the pronoun in So We seized him.
51:41: 41- And in the tribe of Aad, when We sent upon them the barren wind. He called it barren because it destroyed them and cut off their roots, or because it did not include any benefit, and it is the wasp, the south, or the calamity.
51:42: 42- It leaves nothing that it has passed over except that it has turned it into ashes. Like ashes from ram, which means decay and disintegration.
51:43: 43- And to Thamud, when it was said to them, 'Enjoy yourselves for a time.' Its interpretation is his saying: Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days.
51:44: 44- So they rebelled against the command of their Lord, so they were too arrogant to obey Him. So the thunderbolt seized them, meaning the punishment after the three times. Al-Kisa'i read the thunderbolt as the first time from the word sawq. "And they were looking" at it, for it came to them in plain sight during the day.
51:45: 45- And they were not able to stand up is like his saying: And they became kneeling in their homes. It was said that it is from their saying what he stands up for when he is unable to repel it. And they were not victorious is to refrain from it.
51:46: 46- And the people of Noah meaning, We destroyed the people of Noah because what preceded it indicates it. Or remember, and it is permissible for it to be in apposition to the place of in Aad, and this is supported by the reading of Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i in the accusative case. Before before those mentioned, Indeed, they were a wicked people who deviated from the straight path through disbelief and disobedience.
51:47: 47- And the heaven We constructed with power with strength. And indeed, We are expanding “Able” from expansion meaning energy, and expander means able to spend. Or expander the heaven or what is between it and the earth or the provision.
51:48: 48- And the earth We have spread out We have leveled it for you to settle on. And excellent are the levelers meaning We are.
51:49: 49- And of everything of the species We created pairs two kinds that you may remember so that you may know that multiplicity is one of the characteristics of possibilities and that the Necessary in and of itself does not accept multiplicity and division.
51:50: 50- So flee to God from His punishment through faith, monotheism, and constant obedience. Indeed, I am to you from Him that is, from His punishment prepared for those who associate others with God or disobey. A clear warner to you. He explained that he was a warner from God through miracles, or a warner of what one should beware of.
51:51: 51-And do not make with God another god is a singular statement of the greatest thing that must be fled from. Indeed, I am to you from it a clear warner is a repetition for emphasis, or the first is arranged according to abandoning faith and obedience and the second according to polytheism.
51:52: 52- Likewise meaning the matter is like that, and the reference is to their denial of the Messenger and their calling him a magician or a madman and His saying: There came not to those before them a messenger except that they said, ‘A magician or a madman’ is like an explanation of it, and it is not permissible to make it accusative with came or what explains it because what comes after the negative ma does not affect what comes before it.
51:53: 53- They enjoin it upon one another. That is, as if the first and the last of them enjoined this saying upon one another until they all said, Rather, they are a transgressing people. This is a departure from the fact that the enjoining of one another is what unites them due to the distance between their days, to the fact that what unites them in this saying is their participation in the transgression that leads to it.
51:54: 54- Then turn away from them so turn away from arguing with them after you repeatedly called them to the truth, but they refused except to persist and be stubborn. You are not to be blamed for turning away after you have made your effort to convey the message.
51:55: 55-And remind "And do not neglect the reminder and the admonition. For the reminder benefits the believers. Whoever God has strengthened his faith or whoever believes, his insight will increase through it.
51:56: 56- "And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me." Since He created them in an image directed towards worship and predominantly towards it, He made their creation obscured by it as an exaggeration in that, even if it was taken at face value, even though the evidence prevents us from doing so in the apparent meaning of His statement: "And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind." And it was said that its meaning is except to command them to worship or for them to be My servants.
51:57: 57- I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed me. That is, I do not want to direct you to earn my provision, so occupy yourselves with what you are like those created for Him and commanded to do. What is meant is to make clear that His affair with His servants is not the affair of masters with their slaves, for they only own them so that they may use them to earn their living. It is possible that it is understood as say, and it is in the meaning of His saying: Say, ‘I do not ask of you any payment for it.’
51:58: 58- Indeed, God is the Provider who provides for everyone who needs sustenance, and this indicates that He is independent of it. It was read Indeed, I am the Provider “of strength, the Mighty” of great strength, and the Mighty was read in the accusative case as an attribute of strength.
51:59: 59- For those who have wronged are sins meaning for those who wronged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by denying him, there is a share of punishment. Like the sins of their companions like the share of their peers from previous nations. This is taken from the sharing of water by buckets by the water-bearers, as the sin is the large, filled bucket. So let them not be impatient is an answer to their saying, When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?
51:60: 60- So woe to those who disbelieve from the Day they are promised from the Day of Resurrection or the Day of Badr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever recites Surat Adh-Dhariyat, God will give him ten good deeds for the number of every wind that blows and swirls in the world.
52:1: 1- And the Mount means Mount Sinai, which is a mountain in Madyan where Moses, peace be upon him, heard the words of God Almighty. And the Mount in Syriac means the mountain or what flew from the height of creation to the depths of matter, or from the world of the unseen to the world of witness.
52:2: 2- And an inscribed Book" written, and the line is the arrangement of the written letters. What is meant by it is the Qur’an or what God wrote in the Preserved Tablet, or the Tablets of Moses, peace be upon him, or in the hearts of His saints of knowledge and wisdom, or what is written by the guardians.
52:3: 3- On an open parchment The parchment is the leather on which the book is written. It is borrowed for what the book is written on. The indefiniteness of them is to show respect and to indicate that they are not common among people.
52:4: 4- And the Frequented House means the Kaaba and its population with pilgrims and visitors, or Ad-Dharah, which is in the fourth heaven and its population is the large number of angels who visit it, or the hearts of believers and its population with knowledge and sincerity.
52:5: 5- The raised ceiling means the sky.
52:6: 6- "And the sea that is set ablaze" means the filled one, which is the ocean, or the ignited one from His saying: "And when the seas are set ablaze" It was narrated that the Almighty will make the seas a fire on the Day of Resurrection with which the fire of Hell will be set ablaze, or the mixed one from the sajir which is the mixture.
52:7: 7- The punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass.
52:8: 8- He has no one to repel him that repels him. The meaning of these matters that are sworn by is that they are matters that indicate the perfection of God Almighty’s power, His wisdom, the truth of His report, and His control of the actions of His servants for recompense.
52:9: 9- The Day the sky will sway violently It will tremble, and turbulence means to be erased or gone, and it was said that it moved in waves, and Day is a circumstance.
52:10: 10- And the mountains will move meaning they will move off the face of the earth and become dust.
52:11: 11- So woe on that Day to the deniers. That is, if that happens, then woe to them.
52:12: 12- Those who are engaged in idle talk meaning engaging in falsehood.
52:13: 13- The Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, a summoning. They will be violently pushed into it, by having their hands chained to their necks and their forelocks gathered to their feet, and they will be pushed into the Fire. It is read they will be summoned from the supplication, so they will be summoned is a state of being, meaning they are summoned. "The Day is a substitute for the Day of Dates," or a circumstance of an implied, reported statement.
52:14: 14- This is the fire which you used to deny. That is, they will be told that.
52:15: 15- Is this magic? That is, you were saying to the revelation, This is magic. Is this also magic? The report was presented because it is the intended meaning of the denial and rebuke. Or do you not see? This is also just as you did not see in the world. What it indicates is a rebuke and mockery. Or: Or have your eyes been blinded as they were blinded in the world, according to your claim, when you said, Only our eyes have been dazzled.
52:16: 16- "Enter it, and be patient or do not be patient." That is, enter it in whichever way you wish, whether with patience or without it, for there is no escape for you from it. "It is the same for you." That is, both matters, patience or without it. "You will only be recompensed for what you used to do." This is an explanation for the equality, for since the recompense must occur, patience or without it is bad in that it does not benefit you.
52:17: 17- Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and delights. In which gardens and what delights, or in gardens and delights specific to it.
52:18: 18- Feasting softly and enjoying themselves. With what their Lord has given them It was read Feasting and Feasting as the predicate and the adverbial phrase is superfluous. And their Lord has protected them from the punishment of Hellfire is in apposition to He has given them if what is made a source, or in gardens or a state by implying from hidden in the adverbial phrase or state, or from the subject of coming or its object or both of them.
52:19: 19- Eat and drink at ease meaning food and drink. Enjoyably, or food and drink. Enjoyably means that which is not spoiled. For what you used to do because of it or instead of it. It was said that the ba is redundant and what is the subject of Enjoyably, and the meaning is that He blessed you with what you used to do as a reward for it.
52:20: 20- Reclining on couches lined up lined up. And We will marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes. The ba is because of the meaning of marriage which means connection and attachment, or because of the causality, as the meaning is that We made them spouses because of them, or because of the meaning of marriage which means attachment and joining, and therefore it is connected.
52:21: 21- And those who believed with houris, meaning We joined them with houris spouses and believing companions. It was said that it is the subject of We joined them and His statement, and their offspring followed them in faith is an objection for the reason. Ibn Amir and Ya'qub read their offspring in the plural and with a damma on the ta' of exaggeration in their large number and to make it clear, because offspring can be used for both singular and plural. Abu Amr read We followed them their offspring meaning We made them follow them in faith. It was said that with faith is a state of the pronoun or the offspring or both of them and its indefiniteness is for emphasis, or to indicate that following in the origin of faith is sufficient for joining. We joined them their offspring in entering Paradise or the degree, because it was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Indeed, God raises the offspring of the believer in his degree even if they are below him, so that his eye may be comforted by them. Then he recited this verse. Nafi', Ibn Amir and the two Basrans read their offspring. "And We did not deprive them" nor did We diminish them. "of their work of anything" with this attachment, as it could have been a reduction in the status of the fathers or by giving some of their rewards, and it could have been a detailing of them, which is more fitting for the perfection of His kindness. Ibn Kathir read it with a kasra on the lam of "alta ya'alat, and from him latanahum from lata yalayta and alatanahum from alta yawlat, and walatanahum from walat", and the meaning of all is the same. "Every soul is pledged for what it has earned" for its work, pledged to God the Most High, so if he does righteousness, He will release him, otherwise He will destroy him.
52:22: 22- And We provided them with fruits and meat of whatever they desired. That is, We increased for them, time after time, the types of pleasures they desired.
52:23: 23- They quarrel over it They and their companions drink it in a jostling manner. A cup of wine, He named it after its place, and that is why you are the pronoun in His statement: Therein is no idle talk nor sin meaning they do not speak idle talk while drinking it, nor do they do anything for which the doer is sinful, as is the custom of drinkers in this world. This is like the statement of God Almighty: Therein is no threat Ibn Kathir and the two Basrans read it with the fat-ha.
52:24: 24- "And there will circulate among them meaning with the cup boys of theirs" meaning slaves specifically for them. It was said that they are their sons who preceded them. "As if they were hidden pearls" preserved in shells of their whiteness and purity. And it was narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, "By the One in whose hand is my soul, the superiority of the master over the servant is like the superiority of the moon on the night of the full moon over all the other stars." Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 28 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Ṭūr, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Wāqiʿah. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 52:25: 25- And some of them turned to others, asking each other about their conditions and deeds.
52:26: 26- They said, 'Indeed, we were before among our families fearful.' Fearful of disobeying God, concerned with obeying Him, or fearful of the consequences.
52:27: 27- So God bestowed His favor upon us with mercy and success and protected us from the torment of the poisonous winds the torment of the fire that penetrates the poisonous winds, and it was read and protected us with emphasis.
52:28: 28- Indeed, we were before before that in the world. We used to call upon Him we used to worship Him or ask Him for protection. Indeed, He is the Most Barrier the Beneficent. Nafi’ and Al-Kisa’i read it with the fat-ha. The Most Merciful the One with abundant mercy.
52:29: 29- So remind So persist in reminding and do not pay attention to what they say. So you are not, by the grace of your Lord by the praise and blessings of God. Neither a soothsayer nor a madman as they say.
52:30: 30- Or do they say, 'He is a poet for whom we are waiting for the misfortune of death?' What worries the souls about the events of time, and it was said, death is the active participle of minhu if it cuts it off.
52:31: 31- Say, 'Wait, for I am with you among those who wait.' I wait for your destruction as you wait for my destruction.
52:32: 32- Or do their dreams their minds command them to do this with this contradiction in speech, for the soothsayer is intelligent and has keen insight, and the madman has his mind covered, and the poet has balanced, consistent, imaginative speech, and this does not come from the madman, and the dream commanding him is a metaphor for its performance to him. Or are they a transgressing people who have exceeded the limit in stubbornness, and it was read rather they are.
52:33: 33- Or do they say, 'He made it up'? He invented it on his own. Rather, they do not believe. They accuse him of these accusations because of their disbelief and stubbornness.
52:34: 34- Let them produce a hadith like it like the Qur’an. If they are truthful in their claim, since there are many among them who are considered eloquent. This is a refutation of the aforementioned statements by way of challenge, and it is possible that it is a refutation of the fabrication, since the rest of the categories are clearly corrupt.
52:35: 35- "Or were they created from nothing?" Or were they created and decreed without an initiator or decreer, so that is why it is not far-fetched, or for the sake of nothing of worship and reward. "Or are they the creators? supports the first, as its meaning is, Or did they create themselves?" Therefore, He followed it with His saying:
52:36: 36- Or did they create the heavens and the earth? "Or" in these verses is disconnected and the meaning of the hamza in it is denial. "Rather, they are not certain." If they are asked who created you and who created the heavens and the earth, they will say God, because if they were certain of that, they would not have turned away from worshipping Him.
52:37: 37- Or do they have the treasures of your Lord? The treasures of His provision so that they may grant prophethood to whomever they wish, or the treasures of His knowledge so that they may choose for it whomever His wisdom has chosen. Or are they the ones in control? The ones who have dominion over things, managing them as they wish. Qanbal and Hafs recited it differently from him, and Hisham recited it with a sin, and Hamzah recited it differently from Khallad, between the sad and the zay, and the rest recited it with a sad only.
52:38: 38- Or do they have a ladder ascending to the heaven wherein they listen ascending to the speech of the angels and what is revealed to them of the knowledge of the unseen until they know what is to come? Then let their listener produce clear authority with a clear argument that confirms his listening.
52:39: 39- Or does He have daughters and you have sons? This is a mockery of them and a sign that someone with this opinion is not considered rational, let alone that his soul ascends to the world of the kingdom and he can see the unseen.
52:40: 40- Or do you ask them for a reward for conveying the message? They are burdened from the obligation of a debt. They are burdened are carrying a heavy load, so they have given up on following you.
52:41: 41- Or do they have the unseen? The Preserved Tablet in which the unseen is recorded so they write from it.
52:42: 42- Or do they intend a plot? This is their plot against the house of prophecy against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then those who disbelieved can be general or specific, so it is placed in the place of the pronoun to record their disbelief and to indicate that it is the reason for the aforementioned ruling. They are the ones who are plotted against are those who are beset by plots or who are the victims of their plots, which is their killing on the day of Badr, or those who are defeated in the plot of someone who plotted against him, so he plotted against him.
52:43: 43- Or do they have a god other than God? Who helps them and protects them from His punishment. Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him. Above their association or partnership with what they associate with Him.
52:44: 44- And if they see a fragment of the sky falling, they say, out of their excessive transgression and obstinacy, 'A heaped-up cloud.' This is a cloud, some of it piled up on top of others, and it is the answer to their saying, Then let down upon us a fragment of the sky.
52:45: 45- So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck dead. This is at the first blast. It was read they will meet. Ibn Amir and Asim read they will be struck dead in the passive form of saqah or I struck him dead.
52:46: 46- The Day their plotting will not avail them at all meaning at all in repelling the punishment. Nor will they be aided will they be prevented from the punishment of God.
52:47: 47- And indeed, for those who have wronged may be general or specific. There is a punishment less than that meaning less than the punishment of the Hereafter, which is the punishment of the grave, or the punishment in this world, such as their killing at Badr and the seven-year famine. But most of them do not know that.
52:48: 48- And be patient over the decision of your Lord by granting them respite and keeping you in their distress for indeed, you are under Our eyes in Our protection so that we see you and watch over you. The plural of eye is to pluralize the pronoun and to emphasize the many reasons for protection. And exalt the praises of your Lord when you rise from wherever you rise, or from your sleep or to prayer.
52:49: 49- And during part of the night, glorify Him. For worship during that time is more difficult for the soul and further from showing off, and that is why He singled it out for mention and mentioned it before the verb. And by the setting of the stars. And when they set at the end of the night, and it is read with the fat-ha, meaning in their wake when they set or are hidden. On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat At-Tur, it is incumbent upon God to keep him safe from His punishment and to bless him in His Paradise.
53:1: 1- The star when it sets He swears by the type of stars or the Pleiades, for it is predominant in them if it sets or is scattered on the Day of Resurrection or falls or rises, for it is said: it set, with the fat-ha, if it fell and set, and it rose with the damma if it rose and ascended, or by the star from the stars of the Qur’an if it descends or the plant if it falls to the ground, or if it grows it rises according to his saying.
53:2: 2- Your companion has not gone astray Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not deviate from the straight path. The address is to the Quraysh. nor has he gone astray he did not believe in falsehood. The address is to the Quraysh, and the intention is to deny what they attribute to him.
53:3: 3- And he does not speak from [his own] inclination and he does not recite the Qur’an from [his own] inclination.
53:4: 4- It is what the Qur'an is or what he speaks. Except a revelation revealed meaning, except a revelation revealed to him by God. This was used as evidence by those who did not see it as his duty to exert himself. The answer to this is that if it was revealed to him to exert himself, then his effort and what he relies on is revelation, and there is a view on this because that in that case would be by revelation, not revelation.
53:5: 5- He was taught by a mighty angel - a mighty angel, Gabriel, peace be upon him, for he is the intercessor in the beginning of miracles. It was narrated that he uprooted the villages of the people of Lot and raised them to the sky, then turned them upside down and shouted a shout at Thamud, so they became prostrate.
53:6: 6- Once is wise in his mind and opinion. He rose so he was upright in his true image in which God Almighty created him. It was said that none of the prophets saw him in his image except Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, twice, once in heaven and once on earth. And it was said that he rose with his strength over the matter that was made for him.
53:7: 7- And he is on the highest horizon in the horizon of the sky, and the pronoun refers to Gabriel, peace be upon him.
53:8: 8- Then he drew near to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He hung down and clung to him, which is a metaphor for his ascension to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. It was said, Then he hung down from the highest horizon and drew near, so it was from the Messenger, indicating that he ascended with him without being separated from his place, confirming the strength of his strength, for hanging down is continuity with hanging like the hanging of a fruit, and it is said that he hung his feet from the bed and lowered his bucket, and the buckets are the hanging fruit.
53:9: 9- So it was Gabriel, peace be upon him, as you say: He is from me, tied up in a garment, or the distance between them. Two bow lengths is their amount. Or less according to your estimation, as he said, or they increase, and the intended meaning is to represent the ability to connect and to realize his hearing of what was revealed to him by denying the confusing distance.
53:10: 10- "So Gabriel, peace be upon him, inspired" to his servant, Abdullah, and he omitted it before mentioning it because it is known, like his saying: on its back "what Gabriel, peace be upon him, inspired", and in it is the glorification of the one inspired or God to him, and it was said that all the pronouns are for God Almighty, and He is the one meant by emphasizing the powers, as in his saying, the Almighty: "Indeed, God is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Sturdy" and his closeness to Him by raising his status and his hanging down, pulling him with his evils to the side of the sanctuary.
53:11: 11- The heart did not lie about what it saw What he saw with his sight of the image of Gabriel, peace be upon him, or God Almighty, meaning his sight did not lie about what was narrated to him, because holy matters are first instilled in the heart and then transferred from it to the sight, or what his heart said when he saw him, I did not recognize you, and if he had said that, he would have been lying because he knew him with his heart as he saw him with his sight, or what he saw with his heart, meaning that it was not a false imagination. This is indicated by "that he, peace and blessings be upon him, was asked, 'Did you see your Lord?' He said, 'I saw Him with my heart.'" Hisham read He did not lie, meaning he believed him and did not doubt him.
53:12: 12- Do you argue with him about what he sees? Do you argue with him about it? From the root word maraa which means argument, and its derivation is from the word mara a she-camel as if each of the disputants is showing what the other has. Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, and Ya'qub read it aftamaroohu meaning do you overcome him in the argument from maraituhu I argued with him, or aftajadhuhu from maraituhu I showed him his right if he denied it. And because the verb includes the meaning of victory, because victory is intended by the one who argues with him and the one who denies with their actions to defeat the opponent.
53:13: 13- And indeed, he saw him on another descent. Once again, the verb to descend is used in place of one time and its accusative case is used to indicate that the vision this time was also with a descent and nearness. The discussion is about what is seen and nearness as mentioned previously. It was said that its interpretation is And indeed, he saw him descending on another descent, and its accusative case is in the source, and what is meant by it is to negate doubt about the last time.
53:14: 14- At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary which is the place where the deeds and knowledge of creation end, or what descends from above it and ascends from beneath it. Perhaps it was likened to the Lote Tree, which is the Nabq tree, because they gather in its shade. It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet that it is in the seventh heaven.
53:15: 15- There is the Garden of Refuge The Garden to which the righteous or the souls of the martyrs take refuge.
53:16: 16- "When that which covers the lote tree covers it" is a glorification and multiplication of what covers it, such that no description can encompass it nor can any number count it. It was also said that a great multitude of angels covers it, worshipping God there.
53:17: 17- The sight did not swerve The sight of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not deviate from what he saw. And it did not go beyond What did it exceed, but rather it established it with correct and certain confirmation, or it did not deviate from seeing the wonders that he was commanded to see and what went beyond them.
53:18: 18- He saw some of the greatest signs of his Lord meaning, by God, he saw some of His royal and heavenly signs and wonders on the night of the Ascension. It has been said that this is what is meant by what he saw. It is possible that the greatest is an attribute of the signs on the condition that the object is omitted, meaning something of the signs of his Lord or some additional.
53:19: 19- Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza?
53:20: 20- And Manat, the third, the other are idols that they had. Al-Lat belonged to Thaqeef in Taif or to Quraysh in Nakhl. It is a verb from lawa because they used to circle around it. Hibat God, on the authority of Al-Bazzi and Ruways, on the authority of Yaqub, read Al-Lat with emphasis, that it was named thus because it was the image of a man who used to mix gruel with ghee and feed the pilgrims. Al-Uzza with emphasis is a samura of Ghatafan that they used to worship. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, sent Khalid bin Al-Walid to it, and he cut it down. Its origin is the feminine of Al-A'zz. Manat is a rock that belonged to Hudhayl and Khuza'ah or Thaqif. It is a verb from manat if you cut it, for they used to slaughter sacrifices there, and from it is Mina. Ibn Kathir read Manat, which is a verb from the word naw, for they used to seek rain from it, seeking blessings from it. His saying the third other are two descriptions for emphasis, like the saying of God Almighty: flies with its two wings or the other from the delay in rank.
53:21: 21- Do you have males and He has females? A denial of their saying that the angels are daughters of God, and that these idols were inhabited by jinn who are His daughters, or the skeletons of the angels, which is the second object of His saying, Have you seen?
53:22: 22- That is an unfair division is unjust because you gave him what you would disdain. It is a fa'li form of dhayz, which means injustice. However, it broke the fa' to preserve the ya' as it did in bayd, because fa'li with the kasra does not come as a description. Ibn Kathir read it with a hamza from da'azahu if he wronged him, as it is a source of description.
53:23: 23- They are nothing but names The pronoun refers to the idols, meaning that they are nothing in terms of divinity but names that you give them because they say that they are gods, but they do not contain anything of the meaning of divinity, or because of the description that you give them of them being gods, daughters, and intercessors, or because of the names mentioned, for they used to call them Al-Lat because they deserved to be devoted to their worship, and Al-Uzza because of her might, and Manat because they believed that she deserved to be approached with sacrifices. You named them You named them with it. You and your fathers by your desires for which God has sent down no authority a proof to which you cling. They follow and it was read with a ta’ except assumption except the imitation that what they are upon is right through imitation and false imagination. and what their souls desire and what their souls desire and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance the Messenger or the Book, but they abandoned it.
53:24: 24- Or does man have whatever he desires? "Or" is disconnected and the meaning of the hamza in it is denial, and the meaning is that he does not have everything he desires, and what is meant is the denial of their hope in the intercession of the gods and their saying: "If I were to return to my Lord, then indeed I would have with Him the best" and his saying: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities" and similar to them.
53:25: 25- To God belongs the Hereafter and the First. He gives of them whatever He wills to whomever He wants, and no one has the right to control Him in either of them.
53:26: 26- And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all. And many of the angels whose intercession will not avail at all and will not be of any benefit. Except after God gives permission for intercession. For whomever He wills from among the angels to intercede or from among the people to intercede for. And is pleased and deems him worthy of that. So how can idols intercede for their worshippers?
53:27: 27- Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels meaning each one of them with a female name by calling them daughters.
53:28: 28- And they have no knowledge of it meaning of what they say, and it was read with it meaning with the angels or with the name. They follow nothing but conjecture, and conjecture is of no avail against the truth for the truth, which is the reality of a thing, is only perceived through generality, and conjecture is not taken into account in true knowledge, but rather what matters is in the operations and what is connected to them.
53:29: 29- So turn away from he who turns away from Our remembrance and desires only the life of this world. So turn away from his call and concern for his affairs, for whoever is heedless of God and turns away from His remembrance, and is engrossed in this world to the point that it is the end of his ambition and the extent of his knowledge, the call will only increase his obstinacy and insistence upon falsehood.
53:30: 30- That meaning the matter of this world or its being desirable is the extent of their knowledge their knowledge does not exceed it, and the sentence is an interjection confirming the inadequacy of their aspirations for this world. His statement: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who has been guided is an explanation for the command to turn away, meaning that God only knows who will respond and who will not, so do not tire yourself in calling them, since you are only required to convey the message, and you have conveyed it.
53:31: 31- And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, in creation and dominion. That He may recompense those who do evil for what they have done, with the punishment for what they have done of evil, or with something similar to it, or because of what they have done of evil, and what preceded it indicated something similar to it, meaning He created the world and proportioned it for recompense, or distinguished the astray from the guided and preserved their conditions for that reason. And He will reward those who do good with the best, with the best reward, which is Paradise, or with something better than their deeds or because of the good deeds.
53:32: 32- "Those who avoid the major sins" are the sins whose punishment is great and for which the threat was specifically imposed. It was said that it is what requires the prescribed punishment. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read "major sin" to mean the genus or polytheism. "And immoralities" are the major sins that are especially obscene. "Except for the slightest" except for what is small and minor, for it is forgiven for those who avoid major sins. The exception is disjunctive and the place of "those" is the accusative as an attribute or praise or the nominative as it is the predicate of an omitted word. "Indeed, your Lord is Vast in forgiveness" as He forgives minor sins by avoiding major sins, or He has the power to forgive whatever sins He wishes, small and great. Perhaps He followed this with a threat to the wrongdoers and a promise to the doers of good so that the one who commits a major sin does not despair of His mercy or imagine that punishment is obligatory upon God the Most High. "He knows you best" knows your conditions better than you do. "When He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs" He knew your conditions and the dispositions of your affairs when He began your creation from the dust by creating Adam and when He formed you in the wombs. "So do not praise yourselves" do not praise yourselves with the purity of deeds and the increase of good, or with purity from sins and vices. "He knows best who fears Him" for He knows the fearing and others among you before He brought you out from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him.
53:33: 33- Have you seen him who turned away from following the truth and adhering to it?
53:34: 34- And he gave a little and was reluctant. Giving is derived from the saying the digger became reluctant when he reached a hillock, which is a solid rock, so he stopped digging. Most of the scholars agree that it was revealed about Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, who was following the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so some of the polytheists taunted him and said: You have abandoned the religion of the elders and led them astray. He said: I fear the punishment of God Almighty. So he guaranteed that he would bear the punishment on his behalf if he gave him some of his money, but he apostatized and gave some of the stipulated amount, then was stingy with the rest.
53:35: 35- Does he have knowledge of the unseen so that he sees? He knows that his companion will bear the burden on his behalf.
53:36: 36- Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses?
53:37: 37- And Abraham who fulfilled fulfilled and completed what he pledged and was commanded to do, or he went to great lengths to fulfill what he promised God, and he was singled out for that because he endured what no one else could endure, like the patience of Nimrod’s fire until Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him when he was thrown into the fire and said, Do you have a need? He said, But not to you. And he slaughtered the boy, and he used to walk a league every day seeking out a guest, and if he agreed with him, he would honor him, otherwise he would intend to fast. And Moses, peace be upon him, came first because his scrolls, which are the Torah, were more famous and larger among them.
53:38: 38- No soul bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another an is the lightened form of the heavy form and with what follows it is in the accusative case instead of in the scriptures of Moses, or the nominative case is that no soul bears as if it was said what is in its scriptures? So he answered with it, and the meaning is that no one will be held accountable for the sin of another and that does not contradict his statement: We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption in the land - it will be as if he had slain mankind entirely and his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, Whoever establishes a bad precedent will bear its burden and the burden of those who act upon it until the Day of Resurrection for that is for the indication and the cause which is his burden.
53:39: 39- And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for except his own striving, meaning that just as no one is held accountable for the sin of another, he shall not be rewarded for his own actions. What is mentioned in the hadiths that charity benefits the dead is because the one who intends it for him is like his representative.
53:40: 40- And that his effort will be seen.
53:41: 41- Then He will reward him with the fullest reward meaning the servant will be rewarded for his efforts with the fullest reward, so it is in the accusative case by removing the preposition. It is permissible for it to be a source and for the ha’ to be for the reward indicated by He will be rewarded and the reward is its substitute.
53:42: 42- And to your Lord is the final destination The end of creation and their return. It was read with a kasra as if it were separated from what is in the scriptures, as well as what comes after it.
53:43: 43- And it is He who makes laugh and cry.
53:44: 44- And that it is He who causes death and brings to life. No one else is able to cause death and bring to life, for the murderer refutes the evidence, and death occurs in his view by the action of God Almighty, as is customary.
53:45: 45- And that He created the two mates, the male and the female.
53:46: 46- From a sperm if it is desired flows in the womb or is created, or the child is destined from it from semen if it is destined.
53:47: 47- And that upon Him is the other creation Resurrection after death in fulfillment of His promise. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the word the creation as a period, and it is also the source of the word created.
53:48: 48- And that He is the Most Rich and the Most Compassionate. And He gave contentment, which is what is derived from money, and it is singled out because it is the most honorable and most satisfying of money, and its realization makes contentment for him contentment.
53:49: 49- And that He is the Lord of Sirius meaning the crossing, and it is brighter than Al-Ghamisa’. Abu Kabsha, one of the grandfathers of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, worshipped it, and he differed from the Quraysh in worshipping idols. That is why they called the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, Ibn Ati Kabsha. Perhaps it was specified to indicate that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, even if he agreed with Abu Kabsha in their differences, also differed from him in worshipping it.
53:50: 50- And that He destroyed the former 'Aad the ancients because they were the first nations to be destroyed after the people of Noah, peace be upon him. And it was said that the former 'Aad were the people of Hud and the other 'Aad were Iram. And it was read 'Aad lawli without the hamza and the damma of it was transferred to the lam of the definite article. And Nafi' and Abu Amr read 'Aad lawli with the damma of the lam and the movement of the hamza and the assimilation of the tanween. And Qalun after the damma of the lam with a silent hamza in place of the waw.
53:51: 51- And Thamud is in apposition to Aad because what comes after it does not affect it. Asim and Hamza read it without tanween and stop without alif, and the rest read it with tanween and stop with alif. So what did He leave is the two groups.
53:52: 52- And the people of Noah is also connected to it. Before before Aad and Thamud. Indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious than the two groups because they used to harm him, alienate him, and beat him until he could not move.
53:53: 53- And the overturned and the villages that were overturned with their people, that is, they were turned upside down, and they are the villages of the people of Lot. He overturned after he raised it and turned it upside down.
53:54: 54- And what befell them befell them This is an exaggeration and generalization of what befell them.
53:55: 55- So which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute? You doubt, and the address is to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or to everyone, and the enumerated things, even if they are blessings and punishments, He called them favors because of the lessons and gifts in His punishment for those who take heed, and the vengeance for the prophets, may God bless them and grant them peace, and the believers.
53:56: 56- This is a warner from among the first warners. That is, this Qur’an is a warning from among the previous warnings, or this Messenger is a warner from among the first warners.
53:57: 57- The hour has drawn near." The hour described as being near has drawn near, as in the Almighty’s saying: "The Hour has drawn near."
53:58: 58- "There is no one to uncover it except God." There is no soul capable of uncovering it if it occurs except God, but no one uncovers it, or delays it except God, or there is no one to uncover its time except God, since no one knows about it except Him, or there is no one to uncover it except God, as it is a source like well-being.
53:59: 59- “Do you then marvel at this statement meaning the Qur’an in denial?
53:60: 60- "And you laugh" in mockery. "And you do not cry" in grief over what you have neglected.
53:61: 61- "And you are steadfast" not being humiliated or arrogant from the camel's stumbling in its path when it raises its head, or singing to distract people from listening to it from the Thamud which is singing.
53:62: 62- "So prostrate to God and worship" meaning, worship Him without any other gods. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Whoever recites Surat An-Najm, God will give him ten good deeds for the number of those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and denied him in Mecca.”
54:1: 1- The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. It was narrated that the infidels asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a sign, and the moon split. It was also said that its meaning is that it will split on the Day of Resurrection, and the first is supported by the fact that it was read, And the moon has split, meaning that the Hour has drawn near, and among the signs of its approach has occurred the splitting of the moon. And His saying:
54:2: 2- And if they see a sign, they turn away from contemplating it and believing in it. And they say, 'Persistent magic' is continuous and indicates that they saw other signs before it in succession and successive miracles until they said that, or it is a well-established word from the time, it is said I made it bitter so it continued if I made it perfect so it became strong, or it is ugly from the thing continued if its bitterness became intense or it is gone and does not remain.
54:3: 3- And they denied and followed their desires which is what Satan made attractive to them of rejecting the truth after it had appeared. He mentioned them in the past tense to indicate that they were from their old habit. And every matter is settled ends at a goal of failure or victory in this world and misery, or happiness in the hereafter. For when something reaches its goal, it is established and settled. It was read with the fatha, meaning settled, meaning stable, and with the kasra and jar as an attribute of a matter. And every is conjoined with the hour.
54:4: 4- And there has certainly come to them in the Qur'an of report report of past centuries or report of the Hereafter that in which there is a deterrent Deterrent of torture or threat and the taa of the ifti'al is changed to a dal with the dhal, the dal and the zay for the sake of consistency, and it was read as muzajr by changing it to a zay and assimilating it.
54:5: 5- A profound wisdom, its purpose is clear and it is a substitute for what or a predicate for something omitted. It was read in the accusative case as a state of what, for it is a relative pronoun or specific to the adjective, the state of which is in the accusative case. So what use can vows make? Negation or a question of denial, meaning what use can vows make? It is the plural of nadhir meaning warner or warner from it, or a source meaning warning.
54:6: 6- Turn away from them because you know that warning will not avail them On the Day the Caller will call Israfil, and it is possible that the call in it is like the command in His saying Be and it is and the omission of the yaa is sufficient with the kasra for the sake of alleviation and the accusative of On the Day with they go out or with the implication of remember to something monstrous terrible that souls will reject because they have not known the like of it and it is the horror of the Day of Resurrection, and Ibn Kathir read it with alleviation, and it was read monstrous meaning to reject.
54:7: 7- They will emerge from the graves with humbled eyes meaning they will emerge from their graves with humbled eyes from the terror. It is singular and masculine because its subject is apparent and not truly feminine. It was read Khashi'a according to the original form. 55:60: 60- Is the reward for goodness in work anything but goodness in reward, which is Paradise.
55:61: 61- Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:62: 62- And below them are two gardens And below those two sides promised to the fearful and those brought near. Two gardens for those below them from the companions of the right hand.
55:63: 63- Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:64: 64- Two dark green gardens that are almost black from the intensity of the greenery. This indicates that the predominant thing in these two gardens is the plants and herbs spread out over the surface of the earth, and the first two have trees and fruits, indicating the disparity between them.
55:65: 65- Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:66: 66- In them are two gushing springs gushing with water. This is also less than what was described in the first two, and so is what comes after it.
55:67: 67- Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:68: 68- In them are fruits, date palms, and pomegranates. He linked them to the fruit to explain their virtue, as the fruit of the date palm is a fruit and the food of the pomegranate is a fruit and a medicine. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, used it as evidence that whoever swears not to eat fruit and then eats dates or pomegranates has not broken his oath.
55:69: 69- Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:70: 70- "In them are good things meaning good things, so it was lightened because good which means last" is not pluralized, and it was read according to the original. "Hassan" is good in character and disposition.
55:71: 71- Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:72: 72- Houris confined to tents They were confined to their tents. It is said that a woman is short, short, and confined, meaning secluded, or those who confine their gaze to their husbands.
55:73: 73- Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:74: 74- No man or jinn has touched them before them like the houris of the first people, who are the owners of the two gardens, as they point to them.
55:75: 75- Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:76: 76- Reclining on a cushion Pillows or throws, plural of cushion. It is said that cushion is a type of rug or the hem of a tent and it may be said for every wide garment. Khader and Abqari Hassan Abqari is attributed to Abqar. The Arabs claim that it is the name of a country for the jinn, so they attribute everything amazing to it. What is meant by it is the genus, and that is why the plural Hassan is based on the meaning.
55:77: 77- Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
55:78: 78- Blessed be the name of your Lord. His name is exalted in that it is absolute in its essence, so what do you think of its essence? It was said that the name means an attribute or is inserted as in His saying: Until the year, then peace be upon you both Possessor of majesty and honor. Ibn Amir read it with the nominative case as an attribute of the noun. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Ar-Rahman will be grateful for the blessings God Almighty has bestowed upon him.

56:7: 7- And you were pairs of three kinds. "And each kind is or is mentioned with another kind as a pair. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 29 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Wāqiʿah, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Ḥashr. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 56:8: 8- The companions of the right, what are the companions of the right?
56:9: 9- And the companions of the left - what are the companions of the left? The companions of the high station and the companions of the low station are those who take the right as auspicious and the left as pessimistic, or the companions of the right and the companions of the left are those who are given their scrolls with their right hands and those who are given them with their left hands, or the companions of right and bad luck, for the happy ones are auspicious for themselves with their obedience and the wretched ones are unlucky for themselves with their disobedience. The two interrogative sentences are report of what preceded them by making the apparent the pronoun, and their meaning is astonishment at the state of the two groups.
56:10: 10- And the foremost, the foremost and those who preceded in faith and obedience after the truth appeared without hesitation or hesitation, or who preceded in acquiring virtues and perfections, or the prophets, for they are the leaders of the people of religions, they are those whose state and destiny you know, like the saying of Abu al-Najm: I am the father of the star and my hair is my hair Or those who preceded to Paradise.
56:11: 11- Those who are close to God.
56:12: 12- In the Gardens of Delight those whose degrees in Paradise are brought near and whose ranks are raised.
56:13: 13- A group of the ancients meaning they are many of the ancients, meaning the previous nations from Adam to our master Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
56:14: 14- And a few of the others means the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. This does not agree with his statement, peace and blessings be upon him, My nation will outnumber all other nations. It is possible that the forerunners of all other nations will be more than the forerunners of this nation, and the followers of this nation will be more than their followers. This is not refuted by his statement regarding the companions of the right hand, A group of the first ones * and a few of the others, because the large number of both groups does not contradict the majority of one of them. It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they are from this nation, and its derivation is from the word thal which means to cut off.
56:15: 15- On woven couches is another good example of the omitted pronoun, and woven is woven with gold, interlaced with pearls and rubies, or continuous from wadhan, which is the weaving of a shield.
56:16: 16- Reclining on them, facing each other are two states of the pronoun in on couches.
56:17: 17- Immortal youths will circulate among them to serve them, remaining forever in the form and freshness of youths.
56:18: 18- With cups and pitchers when drinking or otherwise. A cup is a vessel without a handle or spout, and a pitcher is a vessel that has that. And a cup of pure wine of wine.
56:19: 19- They will not have a headache from it because of alcohol. And they will not have a drain nor will their minds be drained, or their drink will not run out. The Kufians read with a kasra on the zay La yasda'un meaning they will not have a headache, that is, they will not disperse.
56:20: 20- And fruits of whatever they choose.
56:21: 21- And the meat of birds, whatever they desire.
56:22: 22- And houris with wide, beautiful eyes is in apposition to boys, or a subject with an omitted predicate, meaning, and in it or for them are houris. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it in the accusative case in apposition to gardens with the estimation of an added word, meaning, they are in gardens and in the company of houris, or on cups because the meaning of immortal boys will circulate among them with cups is that they will enjoy cups. Both were read in the accusative case on and they will be given houris.
56:23: 23- Like hidden pearls that are protected from anything that may be detrimental to their purity and clarity.
56:24: 24- As a reward for what they used to do" meaning that all of this will be done to them as a reward for their actions.
56:25: 25- They will not hear therein any idle talk falsehood. Nor any sin nor any relation to sin, meaning they will not be told, You have sinned.
56:26: 26- Except a little meaning a word. "Peace, peace" instead of a little like the Almighty's saying: "They will not hear therein any idle talk except peace" or its description or its object meaning except that they say peace, or a source and the repetition is to indicate the prevalence of peace among them. And it was read as peace, peace as a narration.
56:27: 27- And the companions of the right - who are the companions of the right?

56:32: 32- And many fruits of many kinds.

56:47: 47- And they used to say, 'When we die and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?' The hamza was repeated to indicate the denial of resurrection absolutely, especially at this time, just as the conjunction entered into his saying:

56:49: 49- Say, ‘Indeed, the first and the last.’
56:50: 50- They will be gathered together and it was read as gathered together "to the appointed time of a known day" to what the world has appointed and what happened on a specific day with God that is known to him.

56:53: 53- And they will fill their bellies with it from intense hunger.

56:55: 55- They will drink the drink of the heem The camels that are afflicted with heem, which is a disease similar to dropsy, the plural of which is aheem and heema.
