It was said that sand is the plural of hiyam with a fat-ha, which is the sand that does not stick together. It was pluralized as haym like sahab, then it was lightened and what was done to it was done to the plural of abyad. Each of the conjoined and the one it is conjoined to is more specific than the other in some way, so there is no union. Nafi’, Hamza, and Asim read sharab with a damma on the shin.

56:57: 57- We created you, so why do you not believe in creation, certain and certain of belief through deeds indicating it, or in resurrection, for He who is able to create is able to bring back.
56:58: 58- Have you seen what you wish for? That is, what you ejaculate in the wombs of sperm. It was read with the opening of the ta’ from minā meaning we wished for it.
56:59: 59- Do you create it? You make it into a normal human being. Or are We the creators?
56:60: 60- We have decreed death among you We have divided it among you and have determined the death of each at a specific time. Ibn Kathir read it with a light dal. 56:61: 61- That We may replace your likes in the first case is a state or cause of We have decreed and on has the meaning of lam, and We are not to be outdone is an objection and in the second case it is a connection, and the meaning is that We may replace you with your likes and create in your place, or We may replace your attributes, given that your likes is the plural of like in the meaning of an attribute. And We will create you in what you do not know in a creation or attributes that you do not know.
56:62: 62- And you have certainly known the first creation, so why do you not remember? That whoever has power over it has power over the other creation, for it is less of a creation due to the acquisition of materials, the specification of parts, and the precedence of the example, and in it is evidence of the validity of analogy.
56:63: 63- Have you seen what you sow? You sow its seed.
56:64: 64- Do you plant it? "Do you cause it to grow? Or are We the planter? The one who causes it to grow?"
56:65: 65- If We willed, We could have made it into debris shattered. Amusement is moving around with various kinds of fruit, and it is used metaphorically to mean moving around in conversation. 56:68: 68- Have you seen the water that you drink? That is, the fresh water that is suitable for drinking.

56:70: 70- If We willed, We could have made it bitter salty or from bitterness, for it burns the mouth. The deletion of the separating lam between the answer to what is purely for the condition and what includes its meaning is due to the listener knowing its location, or it is sufficient to have mentioned it previously, or what is intended for itself is specific, so it is more important and its loss is more difficult with more emphasis. Why do you not give thanks are examples of these necessary blessings.
56:71: 71- Have you seen the fire which you kindle? You kindle.
56:72: 72- Did you create its tree, or were We the creator? Meaning the tree from which the spark came.
56:73: 73- We made it We made the fire of the flint. A reminder insight into the matter of resurrection as in Surat Yasin, or in the darkness or a reminder and model for the fire of Hell. 56:74: 74- So glorify the name of your Lord, the Great. And one of the requirements of His mercy is that He does not leave His servants in vain. 56:96: 96- So glorify the name of your Lord, the Most Great. So we declare Him, by mentioning His name, the Most High, free from what is not befitting of His greatness and status. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Waqi’ah every night will never be afflicted with poverty.
57:1: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies God. It is mentioned here, in Al-Hashr and Al-Sanaf, in the past tense, and in Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Taghabun in the present tense, indicating that what is attributed to it glorifies Him at all times, because it is an innate indication that does not differ with different situations. The use of the source in general in Bani Israel is more expressive in that it indicates that everything and in every situation deserves glorification. It is transitive with the preposition lam, and it is transitive in itself, like I advised him in I advised him, indicating that the action was performed for the sake of God and purely for His sake. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise is a state indicating that He is the originator of glorification.
57:2: 2- To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, for He is their Creator and Disposer of them. He gives life and causes death is a new statement or report of something omitted. And He has power over all things, from giving life and causing death and other things. Powerful is completely powerful.
57:3: 3- He is the First who precedes all other beings in that He is their Creator and Originator. And the Last who remains after their annihilation, even if only in view of themselves, disregarding everything else. Or He is the First from whom causes begin and effects end. Or the First externally and the Last mentally. And the apparent and the hidden. The apparent is His existence due to the abundance of His proofs, and the hidden is the reality of His essence, so the minds cannot fathom it. Or the One who is predominant over everything and the Knower of its interior. The first and last and are for combining the two descriptions, and the middle one is for combining the two groups. And He is Knowing of all things. The apparent and the hidden are equal to Him.
57:4: 4- “It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself on the Throne. He knows what penetrates the earth” like seeds, and what emerges from it like crops, and what descends from the sky like rain, and what ascends therein like vapors. And He is with you wherever you are His knowledge and power are never separate from you. And God is Seeing of what you do so He will reward you for it. Perhaps He mentioned creation before knowledge because it is evidence of Him.
57:5: 5- To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He mentioned it with repetition as he mentioned it with completion because it is like an introduction to them. And to God all matters return.
57:6: 6- “He causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night. And He is Knowing of that within the breasts.”
57:7: 7- Believe in God and His Messenger and spend from that over which He has made you successors. From the wealth that God has made you successors to dispose of, it is in reality His, not yours, or that which He has made you successors to own and dispose of from those before you. It encourages spending and makes it easy for oneself. So those among you who have believed and spent will have a great reward. It contains exaggerations, making the sentence a nominal sentence, repeating the mention of faith and spending, basing the ruling on the pronoun, making the reward indefinite and describing it as great.
57:8: 8- And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in God? That is, what are you doing without believing in Him? Like saying: What is the matter with you that you are standing? And the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord. The meaning is: What excuse do you have for abandoning belief while the Messenger invites you to Him with arguments and signs? And He has taken your covenant. That is, God has taken your covenant to believe before that by putting the evidence in the accusative case and enabling you to look. The waw is for the accusative case of the object of invites you. Abu Amr recited it in the passive form and raised your covenant. If you are believers. For a reason, then this is a reason and nothing more.
57:9: 9- It is He who sends down to His Servant clear signs that He may bring you out meaning God or the servant. from darkness into the light from the darkness of disbelief to the light of faith. And indeed, God is to you Kind and Merciful as He alerted you through the Messenger and the signs and did not limit Himself to the rational arguments He set up for you.
57:10: 10- And what is [the matter] with you that you should not spend? And what is [the matter] with you that you should not spend. In the way of God in that which brings one closer to Him. And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth He inherits everything in them, so no one has any wealth left. And if that is the case, then spending it in such a way that he replaces it with something that will remain, which is the reward, is more appropriate. "Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought. Those are greater in degree." A clarification of the difference between those who spend according to their circumstances, such as precedence and strong certainty, and seeking out needs, urging them to seek out the best of them after urging them to spend. The mention of fighting is for digression, and a particle of spend is omitted due to its clarity and the indication of what comes after it. The conquest is the conquest of Mecca, as Islam was strengthened by it, its people increased in number, and the need for fighting and spending decreased. Of those who spent after meaning after the conquest and fought - to all of them God has promised the best meaning God has promised to all of the spenders the best reward, which is Paradise. Ibn ‘Amir read and to all in the nominative case as a subject, meaning God promised to all of them to match what it was conjoined to. And God is Acquainted with what you do knowing its outward and inward aspects, so He will reward you according to it. The verse was revealed about Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, as he was the first to believe and spend in the way of God and he argued with the disbelievers until he was struck with a blow that brought him to the brink of destruction.
57:11: 11- Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? That is, who is it that spends his money in His cause hoping that He will reward him? It is as if someone lends Him and spends it well by being sincere in it and seeking the most honorable money and the best path for it. So He will multiply it for him. That is, He will give him his reward many times over. And he will have a noble reward. That is, the reward that is multiplied is noble in itself and should be sought even if it is not multiplied, so how about when it is multiplied many times over? Asim read so He will multiply it in the accusative case as an answer to the question based on the meaning, so it is as if he said: Would God lend to someone so He could multiply it for him? Ibn Kathir read so He will make it weak in the nominative case, and Ibn Amir and Ya'qub read so He will make it weak in the accusative case.
57:12: 12- The Day you see the believing men and believing women is an adverbial phrase for His statement and for Him or He will multiply it or it is implied by mention "their light will proceed" what necessitates their salvation and guidance to Paradise. "Before them and on their right" because the blessed ones will be given their records of deeds from these two directions. "Good tidings to you today are gardens meaning the angels who meet them will say to them Good tidings to you meaning the one who is given the good tidings are gardens, or Good tidings to you" is entering gardens. "Underneath them rivers flow, wherein you will abide eternally. That is the great attainment" the reference is to what came before of the light and good tidings of the eternal gardens.
57:13: 13- The Day the hypocrites, men and women, will say instead of The Day you see. "For those who have believed, 'Wait for us.' Wait for us, for they will be hastened to Paradise like a flash of lightning. Or, look at us, for when they look at them, they will face them and be illuminated by a light before them. Hamza read Wait for us, meaning that their being given time to catch up with them is a respite for them. We will take from your light. The subject is from it. It will be said, 'Go back behind you.' To this world. Then seek a light. By acquiring divine knowledge and virtuous morals, for these are generated from it, or to the station, for from there it is taken. Or wherever you wish, seek another light, for you have no way to this. This is a mockery of them and disappointment from the believers or the angels. So a wall was placed between them, between the believers and the hypocrites. With a wall. "It has a door," through which the believers enter. Its interior is the interior of the wall or the door. In it is mercy because it is next to Paradise. And its exterior is torment from its side because it is next to Hell.
57:14: 14- They will call out to them, ‘Were we not with you?’ They will say, Yes, but you tempted yourselves with hypocrisy. And you waited for the believers to face calamities and you doubted and cast doubt on the religion. And wishful thinking deceived you like the extension of life until the command of God came which is death. And the Deceiver deceived you about God Satan or the world.
57:15: 15- "So today no ransom will be taken from you" ransom. Ibn Amir and Yaqub read it with a taa. "Nor from those who disbelieved" outwardly and inwardly. "Your refuge is the Fire. It is your protector" It is more deserving of you, as Labid said: So both vaginas began to think that he was the master of fear behind and in front of them. The reality of your course, that is, your place in which it is said that he is more deserving of you, like your saying: he is the place of the generous, that is, the place where the speaker says that he is generous, or your place is close to the guardian, which is closeness, or your supporter, in the manner of his saying: Greetings between them, hitting and kicking Or your guardian will take care of you as you took care of its obligations in this world. And wretched is the destination - the Fire.
57:16: 16- Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? Has not its time come? It is said, Any matter is coming, just now or Anna if it comes, and it is read Alm ya'in with a kasra on the hamza and a sukoon on the noon from An ya'in meaning it came, and Alm ya'in is not coming. It was narrated that the believers were suffering from drought in Mecca, and when they migrated, they were blessed with provision and blessings, so they stopped doing what they had been doing, so the verse And what has come down of the truth was revealed, meaning the Qur'an, and it is in apposition to the remembrance, in apposition of one description to the other. It is possible that what is meant by remembrance is to remember God. Nafi', Hafs, and Ya'qub read nazzal with a light sukoon. And it was read anzalla. And let them not be like those who were given the Scripture before is in apposition to humble themselves. Ruways read it with a ta', and what is meant is the prohibition of imitating the People of the Scripture in what was reported about them in His statement: So a long period passed over them, and their hearts hardened. That is, the period passed over them because of the length of their lives and hopes, or what was between them and their prophets, so their hearts hardened. "And many of them are wicked," is another reading, meaning they have gone beyond their religion and rejected the extreme harshness in their Scripture.
57:17: 17- Know that God revives the earth after its death. This is an example of reviving hard hearts through remembrance and recitation by bringing them to life and killing them, encouraging humility and deterring them from being hard. We have made clear to you the verses that you may understand. So that your minds may be perfected.
57:18: 18- Indeed, the men who give charity, men who give charity Indeed, the men who give charity, men who give charity, and it has been read with both, and Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr read it with a soft sad meaning those who believed in God and His Messenger. And loan God a goodly loan is in apposition to the meaning of the verb in the place with the lam because its meaning is: those who gave charity, or were truthful, and it is according to the first to indicate that what is considered is the charity coupled with sincerity. It will be doubled for them, and for them will be a noble reward its meaning and the reading in It will be doubled as mentioned before, except that it is not in the jussive mood because it is the predicate of in and it is attributed to for them or to the pronoun of the source.
57:19: 19- And those who believe in God and His messengers - those are the truthful and the martyrs in the sight of their Lord. That is, those are in the sight of God as the truthful and the martyrs, or they are the ones who are most truthful, for they believed and confirmed all the report of God and His Messenger, and they bear witness for God and for them, or for the nations on the Day of Resurrection. It was said that and the martyrs are in the sight of their Lord is a subject and predicate, and what is meant by it are the prophets from His statement: How will it be when We bring from every nation a witness or those who were martyred in the cause of God for them is their reward and their light like the reward of the truthful and the martyrs and like their light, but it is without doubling to allow for disparity, or the reward and light promised to them. And those who disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of Hellfire. This is evidence that eternity in Hell is specific to the disbelievers, as the structure indicates specificity and companionship indicates constant association.
57:20: 20- Know that the life of this world is only play and amusement and adornment and boasting to one another and competition in increase of wealth and children. When he mentioned the state of the two groups in the Hereafter, he belittled the matters of this world, I mean that which does not lead to ultimate victory, by explaining that they are imaginary matters of little benefit and quickly disappear because they are games in which people tire themselves out greatly, like children in playgrounds without benefit, and amusement with which they distract themselves from what concerns them, and adornment like fine clothes, splendid processions, and lofty houses, and boasting about lineage or competition in numbers and numbers. Then he confirmed that by saying: Like the example of rain whose growth pleases the disbelievers, then it dries up and you see it turn yellow; then it becomes debris. This is a metaphor for its speed and little benefit, like the state of plants that rain grows, so they become straight and the farmer is pleased with it, or the disbelievers in God, because they are more impressed by the adornments of this world, and because when the believer sees something impressive, his thoughts move to the power of its Creator and he is impressed by it, while the disbeliever’s thoughts do not go beyond what he senses and become absorbed in it. Admiration, then it became agitated, that is, it dried up with a defect and turned yellow, then it became debris. Then He magnified the eternal matters of the Hereafter by saying: And in the Hereafter is a severe punishment, discouraging from being absorbed in this world and urging on that which brings about a dignified outcome. Then He emphasized that by saying: And forgiveness from God and approval, that is, for whoever turns to it and seeks nothing but the Hereafter. And the life of this world is only the enjoyment of delusion, that is, for whoever turns to it and does not seek the Hereafter with it.
57:21: 21- Race one another Hasten as racers race in a racetrack. To forgiveness from your Lord To its requirements. And a Paradise as wide as the heaven and the earth That is, its width is like their width. And if the width is like that, then what do you think of length? And it was said that what is meant by it is the vastness, like His statement: Then the possessor of a broad supplication "Prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers" This is evidence that Paradise was created and that faith alone is sufficient for deserving it. "That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills" That which is promised, He bestows it upon whom He wills without requiring it. "And God is the possessor of great bounty" From Him is the bounty of that, even if His status is great.
57:22: 22- No disaster strikes upon the earth such as drought or affliction. nor within yourselves such as sickness or disease. except it is in a register except it is written on the tablet and recorded in the knowledge of God the Most High. before We bring it into being We create it. The pronoun refers to calamity or the earth or theselves. “That” meaning its recording in a register. is easy for God because He the Most High does not need a number or a period.
57:23: 23- So that you will not grieve means, it was written so that you will not be sad over what you have missed of worldly blessings and do not rejoice in what He has given you because God has given you of them, for whoever knows that everything is predestined, the matter becomes easy for him. Abu Amr read with what He has given you from the coming to equal what you have missed, and according to the first, it indicates that its loss will overtake it since it is left with its nature, and as for its occurrence and continuation, there must be a reason that brings it into existence and sustains it, and the intended meaning is to negate the sorrow that prevents submission to God's command and the joy that causes arrogance and deceit, and for this reason he followed it with his saying: And God does not love every arrogant boaster because few are steadfast in the states of adversity and prosperity.
57:24: 24- "Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess on people" is a substitute for every arrogant person, for the one who is arrogant with money is usually guaranteed by it, or it is a subject whose predicate is omitted and indicated by His statement: "And whoever turns away - then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy" because its meaning is, and whoever turns away from spending - then indeed, God is Free of need of him and of his spending, and is praiseworthy in and of itself. Turning away from thanking Him does not harm Him, nor does drawing near to Him by thanking Him for His blessings benefit him. It contains a threat and a notification that the command to spend is for the benefit of the spender. Nafi' and Ibn Amir read, "then indeed, God is Free of need."
57:25: 25- We have certainly sent Our messengers meaning the angels to the prophets or the prophets to the nations. with clear proofs with arguments and miracles. And We sent down with them the Scripture to make clear the truth and distinguish between correct actions. And the Balance to level rights and establish justice, as God Almighty said: That people may uphold justice. Its sending down means sending down its causes and commanding its preparation. It was said that the Balance was sent down to Noah, peace be upon him, and it is possible that it means justice. That people may uphold justice to establish politics and repel enemies, as He said: And We sent down iron, in which is great might because the tools of war are made from it. And benefits for people because there is no craft except that iron is its tool. And that God may make evident who will support Him and His messengers by using weapons in fighting the disbelievers. The conjunction with an omitted word indicated by what preceded it is a state that includes a reason, or the lam is a connection to an omitted word, meaning He sent it down so that God may make evident. In the unseen is a state of the hidden one who supports him. Indeed, God is Powerful, to destroy whomever He wants to destroy. Mighty does not need support, but rather He ordered them to fight in order to benefit from it and deserve the reward for obeying it.
57:26: 26- And We had certainly sent Noah and Abraham and placed among their descendants prophethood and the Book by asking them to prophesy and revealing to them the Book. It was said that what is meant by the Book is writing. And among them are the descendants or those to whom the message was sent, and We sent indicates them. Some are guided, but many of them are wicked deviating from the straight path and deviating from the Sunnah, which is susceptible to exaggeration in blame and indicates that misguidance is predominant.
57:27: 27- Then We followed up their footsteps with Our messengers, and followed up with Jesus, the son of Mary. That is, We sent messenger after messenger until we reached Jesus, peace be upon him. The pronoun refers to Noah and Abraham and those to whom they were sent, or to the messengers who were their contemporaries, not to the offspring, for the messengers will be met by the offspring. And We gave him the Gospel. It is also read with a fat-ha on the hamza, and its matter is easier than the matter of al-Bartil because it is foreign. And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion. It is also read with compassion on the basis of fa'ala. And mercy and monasticism, which they innovated. That is, they innovated monasticism, which they innovated, or innovated monasticism, as it is one of the fabrications, which is exaggeration in worship, asceticism, and seclusion from people. It is attributed to al-Burhan, which is exaggeration in fear from rahab, like khashiyan from khashi. It is also read with a damma as if it is attributed to al-Burhan, which is the plural of rahabib, like rakib and rakban. We did not prescribe it for them We did not impose it on them. Except seeking the pleasure of God is a disjunctive exception, meaning, but they innovated it seeking the pleasure of God. It was also said that it is connected, because We did not prescribe it for them means We did not command them to do it. Just as it negates the obligation intended to avert punishment, it negates the recommendation intended to merely seek God’s pleasure. This contradicts His statement, They innovated it, unless it is said, They innovated it, then they were encouraged to do it, or They innovated it means they introduced it and brought it, or because they invented it on their own. They did not observe it means they did not observe it all. Its due observance by adding the trinity, saying the union, intending to seek fame, and disbelief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the like. So We gave to those who believed they came with the correct faith, including belief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and they preserved its rights. From them are those who are known for following him. Their reward is great, but many of them are wicked. They are outside the state of following.
57:28: 28- O you who have believed in the previous messengers. Fear God in what He has forbidden you. And believe in His Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. He will give you a double portion two shares of His mercy for your belief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, as you believed in those before him. It is not far-fetched that they will be rewarded for their previous religion, even if it was abrogated by the blessing of Islam. It was said that the address was to the Christians who were in his time, peace and blessings be upon him. And He will make for you a light by which you will walk means what is mentioned in His statement: Their light will run or the guidance by which one will be led to the side of holiness. And He will forgive you, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.
57:29: 29- So that the People of the Scripture may not know means so that they may know, and there is no additional word. This is supported by the fact that it was read li-ya'lam, la-ki-yalama, and la-la'ilama, with the assimilation of the nun into the ya'. Do they not have power over anything of the bounty of God is an, and the meaning is that they will not attain anything of what was mentioned of His bounty, nor will they be able to attain it because they did not believe in His Messenger, which is conditional upon belief in him, or they will not have power over anything of His bounty, let alone dispose of the greatest of it, which is prophethood, and they will allocate it to whomever they want. This is supported by His statement: And that bounty is in God's hand; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty. It was said that la is nothing but additional, and the meaning is so that the People of the Scripture will not think that the Prophet and the believers in him are not able to attain anything of God's bounty, so and that bounty is in apposition to so that he may not know. It was also read layla ya'lam, and the reason for this is that the hamza was deleted and the nun was assimilated into the lam, then it was replaced with a ya'. It was read at night, as the original form of the single letters is the fat-ha. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Hadid will be recorded among those who believed in God and His Messenger, all of them.
58:1: 1- "God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God." It was narrated that Khawlah bint Tha'labah divorced her husband Aws ibn al-Samit, so she sought a fatwa from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: "I am forbidden to him." She said: "He did not divorce me." He said: "I am forbidden to him." She was distressed because of the smallness of her children and complained to God, the Most High, so these four verses were revealed. The Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the one arguing with her expected that God would hear her argument and complaint and relieve her distress. Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Abu Amr, and Hisham, on the authority of Ibn Amir, assimilated its dal into the seen. "And God hears your dialogue" You both exchange speech, and it is predominantly in the direct address. "Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing" of statements and conditions.
58:2: 2- Those of you who swear off their wives zihar is when a man says to his wife, You are to me like my mother's back, derived from back, and the jurists added to it a comparison of her to a forbidden female part, and in of you there is a mockery of their custom in it, as it was from the faith of the people of ignorance, and the origin of yazhirun is yataḥāhirūn, and Ibn Amir, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read yazhirun from aḥāhir, and Asim read yazhirun from ẓāhir. They are not their mothers meaning in reality. Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them, so they are not likened to them in sanctity except by those who include them like the wet nurses and the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from Asim, their mothers in the nominative case according to the language of Banu Tamim, and it was read as their mothers, which is also according to the language of those who put the accusative. And they say an abominable thing because the law denied it. And falsely deviating from the truth, as the wife is not like the mother. And indeed, God is Forgiving and Forgiving for what he has done in the past absolutely, or if he repents from it.
58:3: 3- And those who pronounce zihar declaration of divorce concerning their wives and then go back on what they said meaning to their statement by making up for it. From this is the proverb: The rain has returned to what he spoiled. It is by nullifying what it requires. According to Al-Shafi'i, it is by the one who pronounced zihar refraining from her in marriage for a period of time during which he can separate from her, as the likening includes its sanctity due to the validity of her exception from it, which is the least that can be nullified. According to Abu Hanifa, it is by permitting one to enjoy her, even with a lustful glance. According to Malik, it is by intending to have intercourse, and according to Al-Hasan, it is by intercourse. Or by zihar in Islam, on the basis that his saying they pronounce zihar means they are accustomed to zihar, as they used to pronounce zihar in the pre-Islamic era, which is the opinion of Al-Thawri. Or by repeating it verbally, which is the opinion of the Zahiris, or meaning by swearing an oath to what he said, which is the opinion of Abu Muslim. Or to what is said about her, by keeping her, or permitting one to enjoy her or have intercourse with her. Then the freeing of a slave means that it is upon them, or it is obligatory to free a slave, and the fa is for causality. Among its benefits is the indication of the recurrence of the obligation of freeing a slave with the recurrence of the zihar, and the slave is restricted by faith in our view by analogy to the expiation for murder. Before they touch each other means that each of the two who zihar has enjoyed the other, due to the generality of the wording and the implication of the simile, or that he has intercourse with her, and in it is evidence of the prohibition of that before the expiation. That meaning that is the ruling of expiation. You are admonished thereby because it indicates the commission of the crime that warrants a fine and deters from it. And God is Acquainted with what you do nothing is hidden from Him.
58:4: 4- But whoever does not find meaning a slave and the one whose wealth is lost, then he should fast for two consecutive months before they touch each other If he breaks his fast without an excuse, he must start over, but if he breaks his fast due to an excuse, there is a difference of opinion regarding this. If he has intercourse with the woman who has sworn to divorce her at night, the continuity is not interrupted in our view, contrary to the opinion of Abu Hanifa and Malik may God be pleased with them. But whoever is unable meaning to fast due to old age, chronic illness, or excessive sexual desire, then the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) specifically stated that the Bedouin who broke his fast should make up for it. Then he should feed sixty poor persons Sixty mudds according to the mudd of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), which is a pound and a third because it is the least that has been said about expiations and its type is what is taken out in the fitrah. Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him said that he should give each poor person half a sa' of wheat or a sa' of other food. He did not mention touching each other with food because it was sufficient to mention it with the others, or because it is permissible during feeding, as Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with him said. That meaning the explanation or teaching of the rulings, and its place is in the accusative case due to a verb explained by His statement, that you may believe in God and His Messenger, meaning that this was made obligatory so that you may believe in God and His Messenger by accepting His laws and rejecting what you were doing in your ignorance. And these are the limits set by God, which may not be transgressed. And for the disbelievers, meaning those who do not accept them, is a painful punishment. This is similar to His statement, the Most High, And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds.
58:5: 5- Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger are hostile to them, for each of the two enemies has a different limit than the other, or they set or choose limits other than their own. They were humbled they were disgraced and destroyed. The root of humiliation is to humiliate. “As those before them were humbled” meaning the disbelievers of past nations. And We have certainly sent down clear signs indicating the truth of the Messenger and what he brought. And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment their glory and arrogance will be taken away.
58:6: 6- The Day God will resurrect them is in the accusative case because of humiliating or because of the implied mention. "All together" means all of them, leaving no one except to be resurrected, or together. "Then He will inform them of what they did" means in front of all witnesses, publicizing their condition and confirming their punishment. "God has counted it" means He has encompassed it in number, nothing of it is hidden. "And they forgot it" because of its large number or their cooperation in it. "And God is Witness over all things" nothing is hidden from Him.
58:7: 7-Have you not seen that God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth completely and partially. Whatever happens of three people whispering meaning what happens of three people whispering, and it is permissible to estimate an addition or interpret whispering as whispering and make three an attribute of it, and its derivation is from the word najwa which is what rises from the earth, for the secret is something that is brought to the mind and not everyone can be aware of it. Except He is their fourth except God makes them four in that He shares with them in knowing it, and the exception is from the most general of conditions. Nor five nor is there a whispering of five. Except He is their sixth. The specification of the two numbers is either for a particular incident, as the verse was revealed regarding the hypocrites' secret conversation, or because God Almighty is odd and loves odd numbers, three being the first of odd numbers, or because consultation requires two people who are like two people in dispute and a third who mediates between them. Three and five were read in the accusative case as a state by implying they are secretly talking or interpreting secret conversation as two people secretly talking. And no less than that and no less than what was mentioned, like one and two. And no more like six and above. Except He is with them He knows what goes on between them. Jacob read and no more in the nominative case in apposition to the place of secret conversation or the place of no less by making no to negate the genus. Wherever they are because His knowledge of things is not due to spatial proximity such that it varies according to the difference in places. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection, as a disgrace to them and a confirmation of the punishment they deserve. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things, because the relation of His essence, which requires knowledge, is to all equally.
58:8: 8- Have you not considered those who were forbidden from secret conversation, then they return to that which they were forbidden? This was revealed about the Jews and the hypocrites. They used to whisper among themselves and wink at each other when they saw the believers. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade them, but they returned to the same action. And they whisper about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger meaning that it is sin and aggression towards the believers and they whisper to each other to disobey the Messenger. Hamzah read it as and they produce which is from the word whispering and a similar narration was narrated from Ya'qub. And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you they say As-Samu 'Alaykum or Good morning and God the Most High says: "And peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen." And they say within themselves among themselves. Why does God not punish us for what we say? Why does God not punish us for that if Muhammad had been a prophet? Sufficient for them is Hell as a punishment. They will enter it. "What an evil destination!" Hell.
58:9: 9- "O you who have believed, when you confer privately, do not confer about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger" as the hypocrites do, and from Jacob, do not conspire. "And confer privately about righteousness and piety" which includes the best of the believers and avoiding disobeying the Messenger. "And fear God, to whom you will be gathered" regarding what you do and leave, for He will reward you for it.
58:10: 10- The private conversation meaning the private conversation about sin and aggression is only from Satan for he is the one who makes it look attractive and encourages it. That he may cause grief to those who believe by making them think that it is a disaster that has befallen them. And it will not meaning Satan or the private conversation harm them by harming the believers at all except by permission of God except by His will. And upon God let the believers put their trust and not worry about their private conversation.
58:11: 11- O you who have believed, when you are told to make room in assemblies, make room in it and let some of you make room for others, from their saying: Make room for me, meaning step aside. It was also read as tafasahu, and what is meant by assembly is the type, and this is indicated by the reading of Asim in the plural, or the assembly of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, as they used to squeeze in it, competing to be close to him and eager to listen to his speech. So make room, and God will make room for you, in whatever you want to make room in, such as space, provisions, chests, etc. And when it is said, 'Rise up,' stand up to make room or for what you have been commanded to do, such as prayer or jihad, or rise from the assembly. Rise up, Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, and Asim read it with a damma on the sheen in both of them. God will raise those who have believed among you, with victory and good reputation in this world, and their shelter in the rooms of Paradise in the Hereafter. And those who have been given knowledge will have degrees. The scholars among them are raised in degrees because of the knowledge and action they have accumulated, because knowledge, while its degree is high, requires the action that accompanies it to further elevate them. Therefore, one follows the actions of a scholar and does not follow anyone else. In the hadith, The superiority of a scholar over a worshipper is like the superiority of the moon on a full night over all the other planets. “And God is All-Aware of what you do.” This is a threat to those who do not understand the matter or are forced to do it.
58:12: 12- "O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation a charity." So give charity before it is borrowed from someone who has two hands. In this matter is the reverence of the Messenger and benefiting the poor and the prohibition of excessive begging, distinguishing between the sincere and the hypocrites, the lover of the Hereafter and the lover of this world. There is a difference of opinion as to whether it is recommended or obligatory, but it was abrogated by the saying: "Did you fear?" And if it was connected to it in recitation, it was not connected to it in revelation. And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that in the Book of God there is a verse that no one acted upon except me. I had a dinar, so I spent it, and whenever I conferred with him, I would give a dirham in charity. And according to the opinion of obligation, it does not detract from others. Perhaps the rich did not have a private conversation during his life, as it was narrated that he only remained ten, and it was said only an hour. "That" means that charity. It is better for you and purer meaning for yourselves from suspicion and according to the money. This indicates a recommendation, but his saying: But if you do not find it, then God is Forgiving and Merciful meaning for those who do not find it, as He has permitted them to pray in private without giving charity, is more indicative of the obligation.
58:13: 13- Did you fear to offer alms before your private conversation? Did you fear poverty from offering alms, or did you fear offering them because of what Satan threatens you with of poverty? The plural of alms is to gather those being addressed, or because of the frequency of your private conversation. Then when you did not do it, and God has turned to you in forgiveness by permitting you not to do it, and in it is a notification that their fear was a sin that God overlooked because of what He saw from them that took the place of their repentance. When is in its context, and it was said to mean if or if. Establish prayer and give zakah so do not be negligent in performing them. And obey God and His Messenger in all the commands, because carrying them out is like a remedy for being negligent in that. And God is Acquainted with what you do outwardly and inwardly.
58:14: 14-Have you not seen those who turned back and befriended. A people with whom God has become angry meaning the Jews. They are neither of you nor of them because they are hypocrites who waver between that. And they swear to a lie which is claiming to be a Muslim. And they know that what is sworn to is a lie, like someone who swears by the dust. This restriction is evidence that lying includes what the informant knows will not be true and what he does not know. It was narrated that "the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was in one of his rooms and he said, "A man will enter upon you now whose heart is the heart of a tyrant and who looks with the eye of a devil." Then Abdullah ibn Nabtal, the hypocrite, entered and he was blue-eyed. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him, "Why are you and your companions gloating over me?" He swore by God that he had not done so. Then he came with his companions and they swore, so this was revealed."
58:15: 15- God has prepared for them a severe punishment a type of punishment that is more severe. Evil indeed is what they used to do so they practiced evil deeds and persisted in them.
58:16: 16- They took their oaths meaning the oaths they swore, and it was read with a kasra, meaning the oaths they declared. A shield as a protection against their blood and wealth. So they averted from the path of God they averted people from the religion of God during their security by incitement and discouragement. So for them is a humiliating punishment and a second threat with another description of their punishment. It was said that the first is the punishment of the grave and this is the punishment of the Hereafter.
58:17: 17- "Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God. Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally." A similar hadith has already been narrated.
58:18: 18- The Day God will resurrect them all, they will swear to Him meaning God the Most High that they are Muslims. as they swear to you in this world and say that they are from you. And they think that they are on something in their false oaths, because hypocrisy has taken root in their souls to the point that it will seem to them in the Hereafter that false faith will spread lies about God as it spreads them to you in this world. Unquestionably, they are the liars who have reached the extreme of lying, as they lie to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and they swear by Him.
58:19: 19- Satan has taken over them takes over them from the verb to seize which means to take control of a camel, and this is based on the original text. And He made them forget the remembrance of God they do not remember Him in their hearts or with their tongues. Those are the party of Satan his soldiers and followers. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers because they have missed out on eternal bliss and exposed themselves to everlasting torment.
58:20: 20- "Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger - those are among the most humiliated." Among the most humiliated of God's creation.
58:21: 21 God wrote on the tablet. I will surely prevail, I and My messengers. That is, with the argument. Nafi' and Ibn Amir read my messengers with a fatha on the ya'. God is Powerful to grant victory to His prophets. Mighty, nothing can overcome Him in His will.
58:22: 22- You will not find a people who believe in God and the Last Day having affection for those who oppose God and His Messenger. That is, you should not find them befriending the enemies of God, meaning that they should not befriend them. Even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kindred. Even if the opponents were their closest people. Those means those who did not befriend them. He has ordained faith in their hearts. He has established it therein, which is evidence that deeds are not part of the concept of faith, since that which is fixed in the heart is fixed therein, while the actions of the limbs are not fixed therein. And He supported them with a spirit from Him. That is, from God, which is the light of the heart or the Quran, or with victory over the enemy. It was said that the pronoun refers to faith, because it is a cause for the heart to live. "And He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. God is pleased with them." And they are pleased with Him. "Those are the party of God," His soldiers and supporters of His religion. "Indeed, the party of God - they are the successful ones." The winners of the best of both worlds. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Mujadalah will be recorded as one of the party of God on the Day of Resurrection.
59:1: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. It was narrated that when he, peace be upon him, came to Medina, he made peace with Banu Nadir on the condition that they would neither be for him nor against him. When the day of Badr appeared, they said: He is the prophet described in the Torah as the victor. When the Muslims were defeated on the day of Uhud, they doubted and broke their promise. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf went out to Mecca with forty riders and formed an alliance with Abu Sufyan. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, ordered Ka'b's foster brother to kill him by treachery. Then he attacked them with battalions and besieged them until they agreed to evacuate. Most of them fled to Syria, and a group reached Khaybar and al-Hirah. Then God Almighty revealed: Glorify God until His saying: And God is over all things competent.
59:2: 2- It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering meaning at the beginning of their gathering from the Arabian Peninsula, since this humiliation had not befallen them before, or at the beginning of their gathering for fighting or exile to Syria, and the last of their gathering was the expulsion of Omar, may God be pleased with him, from Khaybar to him, or at the beginning of the gathering of the people to Syria, and the last of their gathering, they will be gathered to him at the establishment of the Hour, and it will overtake them there, or that a fire will come out from the east and gather them to the west. Gathering is the expulsion of a group from one place to another. You did not think that they would leave because of their great strength and power. And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God meaning that their fortresses would protect them from God's strength and change of order. The presentation of the report and the attribution of the sentence to their pronoun is to indicate their extreme confidence in their strength and their belief in themselves that they are in honor and power because of them. It is possible that their fortresses is the subject of protected them. "Then God came to them" meaning His punishment, which is terror and the compulsion to flee. It was said that the pronoun refers to "the believers", meaning God's victory came to them. It was read "Then God came to them" meaning the punishment or victory. "From where they did not expect" because of the strength of their confidence. "And He cast terror into their hearts" and instilled in them the fear that terrifies them and fills them. "Destroying their houses with their own hands" out of spite for the Muslims and removing whatever equipment they liked. "And the hands of the believers" because they also used to remove their outer parts to spite and expand the scope of the fighting. It was conjoined with "their hands" because the destruction of the believers was caused by their demolition, so it was as if they used them in it. The sentence is a state or explanation of "the terror". Abu Amr read "they destroy" with a shaddah, which is more expressive because of the emphasis it contains. It was said that destruction means disabling or leaving something in ruins, and destruction means demolition. So take heed, you who have insight. So take heed from their condition, so do not betray and do not rely on anyone other than God. It is used as evidence that analogy is a proof in that it is a command to move from one condition to another and to apply it to a ruling based on the commonality between them that requires it, as we have established in the books of jurisprudence.
59:3: 3- And had it not been that God decreed for them exile leaving their homelands. He would have punished them in this world by killing and captivity as He did with Banu Qurayzah. And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire is a resumption, the meaning of which is that if they were saved from the punishment of this world, they would not be saved from the punishment of the Hereafter.
59:4: 4- "That is because they opposed God and His Messenger. And whoever opposes God - then indeed, God is severe in penalty." The reference is to what was mentioned of what befell them, what they were about to do, and what was prepared for them, or to the end.
59:5: 5- What you cut down of the soft palm tree meaning whatever you cut from the palm tree, the verb is from color and the plural is colors, and it was said that it is from softness and its meaning is the noble palm tree and its plural is alyyan. Or you left it the pronoun refers to lamma and its feminine gender is because it is explained by the soft one. Standing on its roots and its root was read as sufficient with the damma instead of the waw or because it was disliked. Then by God's permission The word is by His command. And to disgrace the wicked is the reason for an omitted word, meaning and you did or He gave you permission to cut it down so that He may punish them for their wickedness by what angered them. It was narrated that when he (peace and blessings be upon him) ordered the cutting down of their palm trees, they said: O Muhammad, you used to forbid corruption on earth, so what is the matter with cutting down and burning palm trees? So this was revealed. It was used as evidence for the permissibility of demolishing the homes of the infidels and cutting down their trees to increase their anger.
59:6: 6- "And what God has bestowed upon His Messenger" and what He has returned to him means that He made it his or returned it to him, for it was truly his because He created people to worship Him and created what He created for them so that they would seek His obedience through it, so it is truly his to be for the obedient. "Of them" from Banu Nadir or from the disbelievers. "For what you have urged is what you have rushed to obtain from wajeef" which is speed of travel. "Of horses or camels" what is ridden from camels is predominant in it just as a rider is predominant over his rider, and that is if what is meant is the spoils of Banu Nadir, because their villages were two miles from Madinah so they walked to them on foot, except for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), for he rode a camel or a donkey, and no further fighting took place, and for this reason the Ansar were not given anything from it except for three who had a need. "But God gives power to His messengers over whom He wills" by casting terror into their hearts. "And God is capable of everything" He means sometimes through intermediaries and sometimes without them.
59:7: 7- What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns is an explanation of the first, and that is why it was not conjoined with it. Its the spoils are for God and for the Messenger and for near relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer. There is a difference of opinion regarding the division of the spoils. Some say that it is to be divided into a sixth based on the apparent meaning of the verse, and God's share is to be spent on the maintenance of the Kaaba and other mosques. Others say that it is to be divided into a fifth because mentioning God is for glorification, and now the share of the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) is to be spent on the Imam, according to one opinion, and on the armies and borders, according to another opinion, and on the interests of the Muslims, according to another opinion. It is also said that it is to be divided into a fifth like spoils of war, because the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to divide the fifth in this way and spend the four-fifths as he wished, and now according to the aforementioned difference of opinion. So that it will not be meaning the spoils that should be for the poor. Hisham read it in his narration with a ta'. A state among the rich among you. State is what the rich circulate among them, as it was in the pre-Islamic era. It was read state meaning so that the spoils would not be circulated among them or taken by force between them. Hisham read state with the nominative case based on the perfect kan, meaning so that a pre-Islamic state would not occur. And whatever the Messenger has given you, and whatever he has given you of the spoils or of the command, take it, because it is lawful for you, or hold fast to it because it is obligatory to obey. And what he has forbidden you, from taking it from him, or from doing it, refrain from it. And fear God in disobeying His Messenger. Indeed, God is severe in penalty for those who disobey Him.
59:8: 8- For the poor emigrants instead of for the near of kin and what is in apposition to it, for the Messenger is not called poor, and whoever gives to the rich of his kin is specifically replaced by what follows it, and the spoils of war are the spoils of Banu Nadir. Those who were expelled from their homes and their properties for the disbelievers of Mecca expelled them and took their properties. Seeking bounty from God and approval is a condition restricting their expulsion in a way that requires their status to be glorified. And they support God and His Messenger with themselves and their properties. Those are the truthful in their faith.
59:9: 9- And those who settled in the home and in faith is in apposition to the Muhajireen, and what is meant by them are the Ansar whose truthfulness was evident, for they adhered to Madinah and faith and were established in them. It was said that the meaning is they settled in the home of migration and the home of faith, so the noun in the second and the noun to which it was added in the first were deleted and replaced by the lam, or they settled in the home and were sincere in faith, as in His saying: I fed her straw and cold water. It was said that the city was named after faith because it is a manifestation and destination. Before them is before the migration of the emigrants. It was said that the meaning of the speech is and those who settled in the home before them and faith. They love those who emigrated to them and it does not burden them. And they find not in their hearts in themselves. A need what need leads to, such as seeking, grudge, envy, and anger. Of what they were given of what the emigrants were given from the spoils of war and other things. And they give preference over themselves and they give preference to the emigrants over themselves, so that if he has two wives, he gives up one and marries her to one of them. Even if they are in privation is a need from the privations of construction, which is a relief. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul until he contradicts it in what overwhelms it of loving money and hating spending, it is those who are the successful the victors of immediate praise and deferred reward.
59:10: 10- And those who came after them are those who migrated when Islam became strong, or those who followed them in righteousness, who are the believers after the two groups until the Day of Resurrection. Therefore, it was said that the verse includes all believers. They say, 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith.' That is, our brothers in religion. And put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. "Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful." So it is fitting that You answer our supplication.
59:11: 11- "Have you not seen those who are hypocrites saying to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture meaning those who had a brotherhood of disbelief or friendship and allegiance between them, If you are expelled from your homes, we will surely go out with you and we will never obey anyone concerning you in fighting you or abandoning you, ever" meaning from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers. "And if you are fought, we will surely aid you" we will assist you. "And God bears witness that they are liars" because He knows that they will not do that, as He said:
59:12: 12- "If they are expelled, they will not go out with them. And if they are fought, they will not aid them." And it was so, for Ibn Abi and his companions corresponded with Banu Nadir about that, then they broke their promise. And in it is evidence of the authenticity of the Prophethood and the miraculous nature of the Qur'an. And if they aid them assuming and estimating. They will turn their backs in defeat. Then they will not be aided after that, but rather God will abandon them and the aid of the hypocrites, or their hypocrisy, will not benefit them, since the pronoun in both verbs could possibly refer to the Jews or the hypocrites.
59:13: 13- "For you are more feared" meaning more feared is a verbal noun for the passive verb. "In their hearts" because they were concealing their fear of the believers. "Of God" despite what they showed hypocritically. So, concealing your fear is a reason for showing the fear of God. "That is because they are a people who do not understand" they do not know the greatness of God until they fear Him with the fear He should be feared and know that He is the One truly to be feared.
59:14: 14- They will not fight you the Jews and the hypocrites all together" together in agreement. "Except in fortified villages" with paths and trenches. "Or from behind walls" due to their extreme fear. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read "jidar" and Abu Amr made the fatha of the dal inflected. "Their violence among themselves is severe" meaning that this is not due to their weakness and cowardice, for their violence is intense when they fight each other, but rather because God has cast terror into their hearts and because the brave becomes a coward and the honorable is humiliated when they fight God and His Messenger. "You think they are all together together in agreement but their hearts are diverse" divided due to the separation of their beliefs and the difference of their intentions. "That is because they are a people who do not understand" what is good for them, even though the scattering of hearts weakens their strength.
59:15: 15- "Like those before them meaning the Jews are like the people of Badr, or Banu Qaynuqa if it is true that they were expelled before Nadir, or the destroyed nations of the past near in a recent time and its accusative is like like since the meaning is like the existence of like. They tasted the evil consequences of their deed" the bad consequences of their disbelief in this world. "And for them is a painful punishment" in the Hereafter.
59:16: 16- Like Satan meaning like the hypocrites in tempting the Jews to fight, like Satan. When he said to man, 'Disbelieve' He tempted him to disbelieve as one who is commanded is tempted. "Then when he disbelieved, he said, 'Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.'" He disassociated himself from him for fear that he would share in the punishment, but that did not benefit him, as he said:
59:17: 17- "So their end was that they were both in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. That is the recompense of the wrongdoers." What is meant by human is the human race. It was said that Satan said to Abu Jahl on the day of Badr, "No one among the people can overcome you today, and I am your protector." It was also said that he was a monk who led him to immorality and apostasy. "Their end and they will abide eternally were read as the predicate of that and in the Fire" is superfluous.
59:18: 18- O you who have believed, fear God and let a soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow. He called the Day of Resurrection thus because it is near or because this world is like one day and the Hereafter is like its tomorrow. The indefiniteness is for emphasis. As for the indefiniteness of the soul, it is because the souls are independent and look to what they have put forth for the Hereafter. It is as if He said: Let a single soul look to that. And fear God is repeated for emphasis, or the first is in performing obligations because it is coupled with action and the second is in abandoning forbidden things because it is coupled with His statement: Indeed, God is Acquainted with what you do which is like a threat for sins.
59:19: 19- And do not be like those who forgot God forgot His right. So He made them forget themselves so that they did not hear what would benefit them and did not do what would save them, or He showed them on the Day of Resurrection such terror that they forgot themselves. Those are the wicked the complete in wickedness.
59:20: 20- The companions of the Fire are not equal to the companions of Paradise those who perfected their souls and thus deserved Paradise and those who mocked them and thus deserved Hell. Our companions used this as evidence that a Muslim is not killed for killing a disbeliever. The companions of Paradise are the successful ones of eternal bliss.
59:21: 21- If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God. This is a metaphor and imagery, as mentioned previously in His statement: Indeed, We offered the Trust… That is why He followed it with His statement: And these examples We present to the people that perhaps they will give thought. The reference is to Him and to His examples. What is meant is to rebuke man for his lack of humility when reciting the Qur’an due to the hardness of his heart and lack of contemplation, and cracked means splitting. It is read as musaddaqan with assimilation.
59:22: 22- He is God, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. What is hidden from the senses of the sacred substances and their conditions, and what is present to it of the bodies and their accidents, and the presentation of the unseen is due to its precedence in existence and the attachment of eternal knowledge to it, or the non-existent and the existent, or the secret and the public. And it was said, the world and the hereafter. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
59:23: 23- He is God, other than whom there is no deity, the Sovereign, the Holy. The One who is completely free from any deficiency. It is also read with the fat-ha, which is a language for it. As-Salam (Peace) the One who is free from every deficiency and affliction, a verbal noun used for emphasis. Al-Mu'min the Giver of security, and it is also read with the fat-ha, meaning the one believed in, with the preposition omitted. Al-Muhaymin the Guardian (the Preserver) the Watcher and Preserver of all things, derived from al-Aman security, whose hamza was changed to a ha. Al-Mighty, Al-Jabbar the Compeller (the One who compelled His creation to do what He willed), or compelled their condition with what He improved. Al-Muttakabbir the Proud (the One who is too proud to do anything that would cause need or deficiency). Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him they do not associate anything with Him.
59:24: 24- He is God, the Creator Who determines all things according to His wisdom. The Inventor Who brings them into existence free from any inequality. The Fashioner Who brings into existence their forms and qualities as He willed. And whoever wants to elaborate on explaining these names and their sisters, he should refer to my book called The Ultimate Desired. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names all of them. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise Who encompasses all perfections, for they all return to perfection in power and knowledge. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever recites Surat Al-Hashr, God will forgive him his past and future sins. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 30 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Mum'taḥanah, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Ḥāqah. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 60:1: 1-O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies. "This verse was revealed about Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah. When he learned that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was going to attack the people of Mecca, he wrote to them that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted you, so take your precautions. He sent his letter with Sarah, the slave girl of Banu al-Muttalib. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down and informed the Messenger of God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali, Ammar, Talhah, al-Zubayr, al-Miqdad, and Abu Marthad and said: Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman there with Hatib's letter to the people of Mecca. Take it from her and leave her. If she refuses, then strike off her head. They caught up with her there, but she denied it. They intended to return, but Ali, may God be pleased with him, drew his sword, but she took it out of her tie. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, summoned Hatib and said: What made you do that? He said: O Messenger of God, I have not disbelieved since I became Muslim, nor have I deceived you since I advised you, but I “I was a matter stuck among the Quraysh and I had no one among them to protect my family, so I wanted to take a hand with them, and I knew that my letter would not avail them at all, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, believed him and excused him.” You extend to them affection “You extend affection to them by writing to them.” The ba is an additional particle or it is the Messenger of God’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, information because of the affection. The sentence is a state of the subject of Do not take or an attribute of allies that was applied to someone other than the one to whom it belongs. There is no need to make the pronoun explicit because it is conditional on the noun and not the verb. And they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth is a state of the subject of one of the two verbs. They expel the Messenger and you that is, from Mecca, and it is a state of they disbelieved or a resumption of its explanation. That you believe in God, your Lord “that you believe in Him, and in it is the predominance of the one being addressed and the shift from speaking to the third person to indicate what requires belief. If you have gone forth from your homelands in jihad in My cause and seeking My pleasure is a reason for going forth and a basis for the condition, and the answer to the condition is omitted and indicated by do not take "confidentially to them with affection is a substitute for receive" or a resumption of the meaning: that is, there is no benefit for you in secretly expressing affection or informing about the reason for the affection. "And I know what you have concealed and what you have declared" that is, from you. It was said that "I know is a present tense verb and the ba is an additional verb and ma" is a relative pronoun or a verbal noun. "And whoever among you does it that is, whoever takes it, has certainly strayed from the right path" has missed it.
60:2: 2- If they gain control of you they will defeat you. They will be your enemies and showing them affection will not benefit you. And they will stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil that will harm you, such as killing and cursing. And they would like you to disbelieve and they wish you would turn away. The use of would like alone in the past tense is to indicate that they would like before anything else, and that their friendship is present even if they have not gained control of you.
60:3: 3- Your kinship will not benefit you your relatives nor your children for whose sake you befriended the polytheists. On the Day of Resurrection He will judge between you He will judge between you by what has befallen you of terror, so some of you will flee from others. So why do you today reject the right of God for those of you who flee in enmity?" Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the sad and a shaddah and a fatha on the fa'. Ibn 'Amir read "yufasil in the passive form, which is between you, and 'Aasim read yufasil". "And God is Seeing of what you do" so He will reward you for it.
60:4: 4- "There has certainly been for you an excellent pattern." Example is the name for something to be emulated. "In Abraham and those with him is a second description or predicate of was and for you is meaningless or a state of what is implied in good or a description of it, not of model" because it is a description. "When they said to their people is a circumstance of the predicate of was Indeed, we are disassociated from you the plural of baree like zarif and zarifa' and from what you worship besides God, we have disbelieved in you" meaning in your religion or in your deity, or in you and with Him, so we do not consider your status and your gods. "And there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone" so the enmity and hatred turn into meaningless and love. "Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, I will surely ask forgiveness for you is an exception to his saying an excellent pattern. Abraham's asking forgiveness for his disbelieving father is not something that they should follow, because it was before the prohibition or because of a promise that He made to him. And I do not possess for you anything from God is part of the statement of the exception. Excluding the whole does not necessarily exclude all of its parts. Our Lord, in You we have put our trust, and to You we have turned, and to You is the final destination is connected to what came before the exception or a command from God to the believers to say it in completion of what He commanded them to do regarding severing ties between themselves and the disbelievers.
60:5: 5- Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve by giving them power over us so that they tempt us with a punishment we cannot bear. And forgive us for what we have neglected our Lord, for You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. And whoever is like this is worthy of protecting the trustful and answering the supplicant.
60:6: 6- Indeed, in them you have an excellent example to follow. This is a repetition to further emphasize the example of Abraham. Therefore, it begins with an oath and replaces the statement, For whoever hopes in God and the Last Day, with For you. This indicates that a believer should not abandon their example, and abandoning it is a sign of bad faith. Therefore, it is followed by the statement, And whoever turns away - then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy. This is because it is worthy of being promised to the unbelievers.
60:7: 7- It may be that God will establish between you and those among them with whom you have been enemies affection when the verse Do not take was revealed. The believers became enemies of their polytheist relatives and disowned them, so God promised them that and fulfilled it, as most of them converted to Islam and became their allies. And God is Able to do that. And God is Forgiving and Merciful for what you neglected in your friendship with them before and for what remained in your hearts of kinship.
