60:8: 8- God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes meaning He does not forbid you from being kind to these people because His statement, that you be kind to them is a substitute for those who and and act justly toward them and act justly toward them meaning justice. Indeed, God loves the just the just. It was narrated that Qutaylah bint Abd al-Uzza came as a polytheist to her daughter Asma bint Abi Bakr with gifts, but she did not accept them and did not give her permission to enter, so this was revealed.
60:9: 9- God only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion such as the polytheists of Mecca, some of whom sought to expel the believers and some of them aided those who were expelled. That you take them as allies instead of those is a substitute for inclusion. Whoever takes them as allies - then it is those who are the wrongdoers because they put the alliance in the wrong place.
60:10: 10- "O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them." Test them with what you think is most likely to agree with their hearts and tongues in faith. "God knows best about their faith," for He is the One who knows what is in their hearts. "And if you ascertain that they are believers," the knowledge that you can acquire, which is the most likely assumption through oaths and the appearance of signs. He only called it knowledge to indicate that it is like knowledge in that it is obligatory to act upon it. "Then do not return them to the disbelievers," meaning to their disbelieving husbands, because He said: "They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them." The repetition is for consistency and emphasis, or the first is to cause separation and the second is to prevent a new marriage. "And give them what they spent," what they paid to them of dowries, because the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was based on: "Whoever among you comes to us, we will return him." But when it was impossible for him to pledge it, because of the prohibition of that, he was obliged to return their dowries. It was narrated that, peace and blessings be upon him, “After Al-Hudaybiyyah, Subay’ah bint Al-Harith Al-Aslamiyyah came to him as a Muslim. Her husband, Musafir Al-Makhzumi, came seeking her, so the verse was revealed.” The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, made her swear an oath, and she swore. He gave her husband what he had spent, and Umar, may God be pleased with him, married her. There is no blame upon you if you marry them, for Islam prevented them from marrying their disbelieving husbands. When you have given them their due compensation stipulated the condition of giving the dowry in their marriage, indicating that what their husbands were given does not take the place of the dowry. And do not hold on to the bonds of disbelieving women to which disbelieving women hold on, such as a contract and a reason for the plural of bonds. What is meant is to forbid believers from continuing to marry polytheistic women. The two Basrans read and do not hold on with emphasis. And ask what you have spent of the dowries of your wives who joined the disbelievers. And let them ask what they have spent of the dowries of their emigrant wives. That is the decree of God meaning all of what was mentioned in the verse. He judges between you is a resumption or a state of judgment based on the omission of the pronoun, or making the judgment a judge based on exaggeration. And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise He legislates what His wisdom requires.
60:11: 11- And if one of your wives escapes you and one of your wives gets away from you and escapes from you. Something of your wives one of your wives, and it has been read with this reading and the placement of something is for disparagement and exaggeration in generalization, or something of their dowries. to the disbelievers and you take turns so it came, meaning your turn to pay the dowry, the ruling was likened to these paying the dowries of the women of those times and those paying the dowries of the women of those other times by a matter in which they take turns, just as one takes turns in riding and other things. Then give those whose wives have gone away the equivalent of what they spent of the dowry of the emigrant woman, and do not give it to her disbelieving husband. It was narrated that when the previous verse was revealed, the polytheists refused to pay the dowry of the disbelieving women, so it was revealed. It was said that its meaning is if one of your wives escapes you and you take a consequence from the disbelievers, which is the spoils, then give instead of the lost spoils, and fear God, in whom you are believers because belief in Him requires fear of Him.
60:12: 12- O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God was revealed on the day of the conquest, for when he (peace and blessings be upon him) had finished the pledge of allegiance of the men, he took up the pledge of allegiance of the women. "And they shall not steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children" meaning burying girls alive. "And they shall not bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and feet, nor disobey you in what is right" in a good deed that you command them to do. The restriction to what is right, even though the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) only commands it, is a warning that it is not permissible to obey a creature in disobeying the Creator. "Then take their pledge" if they pledge you with the guarantee of reward for fulfilling these things. "And ask forgiveness for them from God. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful."
60:13: 13- "O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry." Meaning the disbelievers or the Jews, as it was narrated that it was revealed about some poor Muslims who used to maintain relations with the Jews in order to obtain some of their fruits. "They have despaired of the Hereafter." Due to their disbelief in it or due to their knowledge that they have no share in it due to their stubbornness against the Messenger described in the Torah, who is supported by the verses. "Just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves," that they will be resurrected, rewarded, or that anything better than them will reach them. According to the first interpretation, the apparent is placed in place of the implied to indicate that disbelief has made them despair. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Mumtahanah, the believing men and women will intercede for him on the Day of Resurrection.
61:1: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Its interpretation has been previously mentioned.
61:2: 2- O you who have believed, why do you say that which you do not do? It was narrated that the Muslims said: If we knew what the most beloved deeds to God Almighty were, we would spend our wealth and our lives in it. Then God revealed: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks. So they turned back on the day of Uhud, and so it was revealed. Lam is composed of the preposition lam and the interrogative ma, and most of the times its alif is deleted with the preposition due to their frequent use together and their use to indicate the thing being asked about.
61:3: 3- It is most hateful to God that you say what you do not do. Hatred is the most intense hatred, and it is in the accusative case as a specification to indicate that their saying this is pure hatred. Great to those who belittle everything great below Him, as an exaggeration in forbidding it.
61:4: 4- Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in ranks lined up, as described by it. As if they were a solid structure in their closeness with no gaps, a state of what is hidden in the first state. And closeness is the connection of some parts of the structure to others and its solidity.
61:5: 5- And when Moses said to his people implied by mention or it was so O my people, why do you harm me by disobeying and pelting with stones. And you know that I am the Messenger of God to you by what I have brought you of miracles, and the sentence is a state of confirmation of denial, for knowledge of his prophethood requires him to be glorified and prevents harming him. And is to confirm knowledge. So when they deviated from the truth, God made their hearts deviate He turned them away from accepting the truth and inclining towards what is right. And God does not guide the wicked people guidance leading to knowledge of the truth or to Paradise.
61:6: 6- And when Jesus, son of Mary, said, 'O Children of Israel,' and perhaps he did not say O my people as Moses, peace be upon him, said because it was attributed to him in their case, Indeed, I am the Messenger of God to you, confirming what came before me of the Torah and bringing good tidings in my confirmation of what came before me of the Torah and giving good tidings of a Messenger to come after me. The operative in both cases is what is in the Messenger of the meaning of sending, not the preposition because it is superfluous since it is a relative clause of the Messenger and thus does not apply. of a Messenger to come after me whose name is Ahmad means Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the meaning is that my religion is to believe in the books of God and His Prophets, so he mentioned the first of the famous books that the Prophets ruled by and the Prophet who is the Seal of the Messengers. So when he came to them with clear proofs, they said, 'This is obvious magic.' The reference is to what he came with or to him, and calling it magic is for emphasis. This is supported by the reading of Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i, magician, on the basis that the reference is to Jesus, peace be upon him.
61:7: 7- And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God while he is invited to Islam? That is, no one is more unjust than he who is invited to Islam, the truth of which is apparent and necessitated by the report of the two abodes. So he puts in place of his answer the invention of God by denying His Messenger and calling His signs magic, as it includes affirming the negated and negating the established. It was read he is called and it is said he called him and he claimed him like he touched him and he sought him out. "And God does not guide the wrongdoing people" He does not guide them to what will bring them success.
61:8: 8- They want to extinguish means they want to extinguish, and the lam is added because it contains a meaning of will to emphasize it, just as it was added because it contains a meaning of addition to emphasize it in La Aba Lak, or they want the slander to extinguish. The light of God means His religion, His book, or His proof. With their mouths by their attack on it. And God will perfect His light by spreading it and making it exalted. Ibn Kathir, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, and Hafs read it with the addition. Even if the disbelievers dislike it to humiliate them.
61:9: 9- It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance with the Qur’an or the miracle and the religion of truth and the pure faith. to make it prevail over all religions to make it prevail over all religions. even though the polytheists hate it because it contains pure monotheism and the nullification of polytheism.
61:10: 10- O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? Ibn Amir read tanjikum with emphasis.
61:11: 11- You believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives. This is a clear resumption of trade, which is the combination of faith and jihad that leads to the perfection of their honor. What is meant by it is the command, and the wording was brought to indicate that this is something that should not be abandoned. That is better for you, meaning what was mentioned of faith and jihad. If you only knew, if you were people of knowledge, because the actions of the ignorant are not taken into account.
61:12: 12- "He will forgive you your sins" is an answer to the command indicated by the wording of the report, or to a condition or question indicated by the speech, the meaning of which is that you believe and strive, or do you accept that I guide you so that He may forgive you? It is far-fetched to make it an answer to "did I guide you" because its mere indication does not necessitate forgiveness. "And He will admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual bliss. That is the great attainment." The reference is to what was mentioned about forgiveness and admission to Paradise.
61:13: 13- And another that you love." And for you, in addition to this mentioned blessing, is another blessing that is immediate and beloved. In "you love it" there is an allusion to the fact that they prefer the immediate to the deferred. It was said that "another is in the accusative case with the omission of He gives you, or you love, or a subject whose predicate is victory from God," and according to the first it is a substitute or clarification. According to the saying of the accusative case it is a deleted predicate. It was read with what it was conjoined to in the accusative case as a substitute, or specificity, or source. "And a near opening," immediate. "And give good tidings to the believers," in conjunction with something that was omitted, such as: Say, "O you who believe, And give good tidings, or according to you believe," because it is in the meaning of a command, as if he said: Believe and strive, O believers, and give them good tidings, O Messenger of God, with what He promised them for them, deferred and immediate.
61:14: 14- "O you who have believed, be supporters of God." Al-Hijaziyan and Abu Amr read it with the tanween and the lam because the meaning is be some of God's supporters. "As Jesus, son of Mary, said to the disciples, 'Who are my supporters to God?'" That is, who is a soldier directed to support God, to match the Almighty's saying: "The disciples said, 'We are supporters of God.'" The first addition is the addition of one of the partners to the other because of the specialization between them, and the second is the addition of the subject to the object and the likening in consideration of the meaning, since the intended meaning is say to them as Jesus, son of Mary, said, or be supporters as the disciples said when Jesus said to them, "Who are my supporters to God?" The disciples were his chosen ones and they were the first to believe in him and they were twelve men from the houris, which is white. "So a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved," that is, in Jesus. "So We supported those who believed against their enemy," with argument and war, and that was after Jesus was taken up. "So they became apparent" so they became victorious. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Saff, Jesus will pray for him and seek forgiveness for him as long as he is in this world, and he will be his companion on the Day of Resurrection.
62:1: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies God, the Sovereign, the Holy, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. The four attributes were read in the nominative case as a sign of praise.
62:2: 2- It is He who has sent among the unlettered ones meaning among the Arabs because most of them do not write or read. A Messenger from among themselves from among them, an illiterate person like them. Recites to them His verses because he was an illiterate person like them, he was not known to read or learn and purifies them from the evils of beliefs and deeds and teaches them the Book and wisdom the Qur’an and the Shari’ah, or the landmarks of the religion from the transmitted and rational sources. If He had no other miracle, it would have been sufficient for Him. And they were before in manifest error from polytheism and the evil of ignorance. This is a statement of their great need for a prophet to guide them, and to remove any illusion that the Messenger learned that from a teacher. In is the lightened one and the lam indicates it.
62:3: 3- And others among them is in apposition to the unlettered ones, or the subject of He teaches them and they are those who came after the Companions until the Day of Judgment, for his call and teaching include everyone. When they have not yet joined them they have not yet joined them and they will. And He is the Exalted in Might in enabling him to do this extraordinary matter. The Wise in choosing and teaching him.
62:4: 4- That is the bounty of God That is the bounty by which He is distinguished from His peers. He gives it to whom He wills As a favor and gift. And God is the possessor of great bounty Compared to which the pleasures of this world, or the pleasures of the Hereafter, or both of them, are insignificant.
62:5: 5- The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah they were taught it and were charged with acting in accordance with it then they did not uphold it they did not know it or did not benefit from what was in it. Like a donkey who carries volumes books of knowledge with the effort of carrying them but does not benefit from them. The state and the agent in it carry the meaning of a simile or a description since what is meant by the donkey is not a specific person. How evil is the example of the people who deny the signs of God meaning the example of those who denied, and they are the Jews who denied the signs of God indicating the prophethood of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. It is possible that those is an description of the people and the one specifically blamed is omitted. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
62:6: 6- "Say, 'O you who are Jews!' Become Jews. 'If you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of the people,' since they used to say, 'We are the children of God and His beloved.' Then wish for death,' wish that God would cause you to die and transfer you from the abode of affliction to the abode of honor, 'if you should be truthful,' in your claim."
62:7: 7- And they will never desire it, because of what their hands have put forth because of what they have put forth of disbelief and sins. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers and He will reward them for their deeds.
62:8: 8- "Say, 'Indeed, the death you flee from' and fear to wish for with your tongues for fear that it might befall you and you would be seized by your deeds - it will surely meet you' will catch up with you, you will not miss it. The 'fa' is to include the meaning of a condition in the noun based on the description, as if their flight hastens its catching up with them. It has been read without 'fa', and it is possible for the relative pronoun to be a predicate and the 'fa' a conjunction. 'Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the seen, and He will inform you of what you used to do' by rewarding you for it.
62:9: 9- "O you who have believed, when the call is made for the prayer" meaning when the permission for it is given. "On Friday is an explanation of when" and it is called Friday because people gather for prayer on it. The Arabs used to call it Al-Aruba. It was also said that Ka'b bin Lu'ay called it because people gathered to it on it. The first Friday that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gathered was when he came to Madinah, he stopped at Quba' there for the Friday prayer, then he entered Madinah and prayed the Friday prayer in a valley belonging to Banu Salim bin Awf. "Then hasten to the remembrance of God so proceed to it quickly, for striving is not a race, and remembrance" is the sermon. It was also said that the prayer and the command to hasten to it indicate its obligation. "And leave off business" and leave off dealings. "That meaning striving to the remembrance of God is better for you than dealings, for the benefit of the Hereafter is better and more lasting if you only knew" the true good and evil, or if you are among the people of knowledge.
62:10: 10-So when the prayer is completed it is performed and completed. Then disperse throughout the land and seek from the bounty of God is a generalization of what was prohibited to them, and it was used as evidence by those who made the command after the prohibition to be permissible. In the hadith: Seek from the bounty of God, not by seeking this world, but rather it is visiting the sick, attending a funeral, and visiting a brother in God.
62:11: 11- And if they see business or entertainment, they disperse to it. It was narrated that "the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was delivering the Friday sermon and a caravan carrying food passed by him. The people came out to them except for twelve men, so the following was revealed." The mention of business as a metaphor was used because it was the intended meaning. What is meant by entertainment was the drum with which they would greet the caravan. The repetition is to indicate that some of them dispersed merely upon hearing or seeing the drum, or to indicate that dispersing to business when there is a need for it and benefiting from it, if it is reprehensible, then dispersing to entertainment is more appropriate. It was said that its meaning is that if they see business, they disperse to it, and if they see entertainment, they disperse to it. And they left you standing meaning on the pulpit. Say, 'What is with God' of reward. Better than amusement and trade. This is certain and eternal, unlike what you imagine about their benefit. And God is the best of providers. So put your trust in Him and seek provision from Him. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat al-Jumu’ah will be given ten good deeds for the number of those who come to Friday prayers and those who do not come in the Muslim countries.
63:1: 1- If the hypocrites come to you, they say, 'We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of God.' The testimony is information about the knowledge of the witnesses, which is presence and awareness. Therefore, the famous one believed in it and they lied in the testimony by saying: And God knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars, because they did not believe that.
63:2: 2- They took their oaths their false oath or their testimony, for it is considered an oath in confirmation, and their oath was read as a shield as protection from killing and captivity. So they turned away from the path of God turning away or turning away. Indeed, evil was what they were doing of their hypocrisy and turning away.
63:3: 3- "That" refers to the previous statement, that statement which testifies to the evil of their deeds, or to the mentioned state of hypocrisy, lying, and pretending to believe. "That they believed because they believed outwardly, then disbelieved" secretly. "They believed when they saw a sign, then disbelieved" whenever they heard doubts from their devils. "So a seal was placed upon their hearts" until they became accustomed to disbelief and became ingrained in it. "So they do not understand" the truth of faith, nor do they know its validity.
63:4: 4- And when you see them, you will be impressed by their bodies because of their size and beauty. And when they speak, you will listen to their speech because of their smoothness and the sweetness of their speech. Ibn Abi was a large and eloquent man who would attend the gathering of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a group like his, and he would be impressed by their build and listen to their speech. As if they were propped up pieces of wood is a state of the genitive pronoun in their saying, meaning he heard what they said, likening them to pieces of wood propped up against a wall in that they are ghosts devoid of knowledge and insight. It was said that wood is the plural of khashaba, which is a piece of wood whose interior has been eaten away. They were likened to it in their beautiful appearance but ugliness of their report. Abu Amr, Al-Kisa'i, and Qanbal read it on the authority of Ibn Kathir with a sukoon on the sheen for emphasis, or that it is like kabdan in the plural of badana. They think every shout is against them means that it will befall them due to their cowardice and accusation. So against them is the second object of they think, and it is possible that its relative clause and the object are they are the enemy. Based on this, the pronoun refers to all of them and their plural in view of the predicate, but the fact that his statement beware of them is based on it indicates that the pronoun refers to the hypocrites. May God fight them is a supplication against them, and it is a request from Himself to curse them, or a teaching to the believers to supplicate against them with that. How are they deluded?
63:5: 5- “And when it is said to them, ‘Come, that the Messenger of God may ask forgiveness for you,’ they turn their heads away, refusing to do so and being arrogant about it. Nafi’ read it with a light ‘waw’. “I saw them turning away” turning away from asking forgiveness. And they are arrogant about apologizing.
63:6: 6- It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them - God will never forgive them because of their entrenched disbelief. Indeed, God does not guide the wicked people who have gone beyond the expectation of reform because of their immersion in disbelief and hypocrisy.
63:7: 7- They are the ones who say, meaning to the Ansar, Do not spend on those with the Messenger of God until they disperse, meaning the poor emigrants. And to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, in His hand are provisions and division. But the hypocrites do not understand, that is, because of their ignorance of God.
63:8: 8- They say, 'If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble.' It was narrated that a Bedouin disputed with the Ansar over some water, so the Bedouin struck his head with a piece of wood. He complained to Ibn Abi Talib, who said, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until they disperse. And when we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble." By the more honorable, he meant himself and the more humble, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was read liyakharunna with a fat-ha on the ya', and liyakharunna with a passive participle, and liyakharunna with a noon. The accusative of the more honorable and the more humble, according to these readings, is a source or a state, with an estimated addition, like khurooj or akhrij or something like. To God belongs honor and to His Messenger and to the believers. To God belongs victory and strength, and to whomever He honors among His Messenger and the believers. But the hypocrites do not know because of their extreme ignorance and arrogance.
63:9: 9- O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God Do not let managing and taking care of them distract you from remembering Him, the prayers and all the other acts of worship mentioned for the One Who is worshipped, and what is meant is to forbid them from being distracted by them. Directing the prohibition to them is for emphasis, and that is why He said: And whoever does that meaning distracting himself with it, which is preoccupation. Then it is those who are the losers because they sold the great and everlasting for the insignificant and fleeting.
63:10: 10- Spend from what We have provided you" some of your wealth to save for the Hereafter. "Before death comes to one of you that is, he sees its signs and says, 'My Lord, if only You would delay me' Why did You not give me respite? Until a near term" a period not far away. "So I will give charity So I will give charity. And I will be among the righteous" by making up for it. "I will be is in the jussive mood to connect with the position of So" and what follows it. Abu Amr read "And I will be in the accusative case in apposition to So I will give charity, and it was read in the nominative case on And I will be" so it is a number for righteousness.
63:11: 11- And God will not delay a soul nor will He give it respite. When its time comes the end of its life. And God is Aware of what you do so it is a metaphor for it, and Abu Bakr read it with the letter ya to agree with what came before it in the absence. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever recites Surat Al-Munafiqun will be free from hypocrisy.
64:1: 1- Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God indicating His perfection and independence. To Him belongs dominion and to Him belongs praise He brought forward the two adverbials to indicate that both matters are exclusively His in reality. And He has power over all things because the relation that requires power applies to all equally. Then He began what He claimed, saying:
64:2: 2- It is He who created you, and among you is he who disbelieves. His disbelief is understood and what compels him to do it is directed at him. And among you is he who believes. His faith is understood and he is guided to what He calls him to. And God is Seeing of what you do. So He deals with you in a manner that suits your actions.
64:3: 3- He created the heavens and the earth in truth with perfect wisdom. And He shaped you and perfected your shapes So He shaped you from among what He created in them in the best form, as He adorned you with the best descriptions of beings, and singled you out with the essence of the characteristics of the Creators, and made you a model for all creation. And to Him is the final destination So improve your inner selves so that your outer selves will not be distorted by the torment.
64:4: 4- “He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you declare. And God is Knowing of that within the breasts.” Nothing that He can know, whether completely or partially, is hidden from Him, because the proportion of the necessitating factor for His knowledge to the whole is one, and the presentation of the report of ability over knowledge is because the evidence of the creatures is of His ability first and foremost and intrinsically and of His knowledge of what is in them of perfection and specialization in some aspects.
64:5: 5- Has there not come to you O disbelievers. the report of those who disbelieved before such as the people of Noah, Hud, and Salih, peace be upon them. So they tasted the evil consequences of their deed the harm of their disbelief in this world. Its root is heaviness, from which comes the word wabil for food that is heavy on the stomach, and wabil for heavy rain. And for them is a painful punishment in the Hereafter.
64:6: 6- That meaning the aforementioned calamity and torment is because their messengers came to them with clear proofs with miracles. They said, 'Shall human beings guide us?' They denied and were amazed that the messengers were human beings, and human beings are used for both singular and plural. So they disbelieved in the messengers and turned away from contemplating the clear proofs. And God is independent of everything, let alone their obedience. And God is independent of their worship and anything else. Praiseworthy indicates that every creature praises Him.
64:7: 7- Those who disbelieve claim that they will not be resurrected. To claim is to claim knowledge, and therefore it takes two objects, and that has taken their place, including what is within its scope. "Say, 'Yes,' meaning, yes, you will be resurrected. 'By my Lord, you will surely be resurrected.'" An oath with which He confirms the answer. Then you will surely be informed of what you did. With accountability and recompense. And that is easy for God.
64:8: 8- So believe in God and His Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. And the light which We have sent down meaning the Qur'an, in which, with its miraculous nature, it is a manifestation of something else in which it explains and clarifies. And God is All-Aware of what you do so it is a reward for him.
64:9: 9- The Day He will gather you is an adverbial phrase for that you will surely be informed" or a predestined Lord. Jacob read "We will gather you. For the Day of Assembly" is because of the accounting and recompense it contains, and the gathering is the gathering of the angels and the two heavy burdens. "That is the Day of Loss" in which some will lose out to others, because the happy will be in the homes of the miserable, had they been happy, and vice versa. It is borrowed from the word "taghabun" traders lose and the lam in it is to indicate that the true taghabun is the loss in matters of the Hereafter, due to its greatness and permanence. "And whoever believes in God and does righteousness" meaning righteous deeds. "He will remove from him his misdeeds and admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever." Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read them with the letter nun in both. "That is the great attainment" refers to the combination of the two matters, and therefore He made it the great attainment because it combines interests, such as warding off harm and bringing benefits.
64:10: 10- And those who disbelieved and denied Our verses - those are the companions of the Fire, abiding eternally therein, and wretched is the destination. It is as if the previous verse and it are an explanation of al-Taghabun and a detailing of it.
64:11: 11- No disaster strikes except by permission of God except by His decree and will. And whoever believes in God - He will guide his heart to make him steadfast and seek refuge in Him when it happens. He guides his heart is read in the nominative case, making it the subject, and in the accusative case, in the manner of he fooled himself. “He calms down” with the hamza, meaning He makes it calm. And God is Knowing of all things, even the hearts and their conditions.
64:12: 12- "And obey God and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification." That is, if you turn away, then there is no harm upon him, since his duty is to convey, and he has conveyed.
64:13: 13- God, there is no god but He, and in God let the believers put their trust. Because their belief that everything comes from Him requires that.
64:15: 15- Your wealth and your children are but a trial a test for you. And God has with Him a great reward for whoever prefers the love of God and obedience to the love of wealth and children and striving for them.
64:16: 16- So fear God as much as you are able meaning, exert your effort and energy in fearing Him, and listen to His admonitions, and obey His commands, and spend in good causes, purely for His sake, that which is good for yourselves meaning, do what is best for yourselves, and this is an emphasis on urging compliance with these commands. It is possible that it is an attribute of a deleted source, the meaning of which is: good spending, or report, as it would have been understood as an answer to the commands. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. This has been explained previously.
64:17: 17- If you lend to God spend the money in the manner He has commanded. A good loan coupled with sincerity and a good heart. He will multiply it for you He will make for you for one ten to seven hundred and more. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Yaqub read He will multiply it for you. “And forgive you” by the blessing of spending. And God is Appreciative He gives generously for little. Forbearing He does not hasten to punish.
64:18: 18- The Knower of the unseen and the witnessed and nothing is hidden from Him. The Exalted in Might, the Wise is perfect in power and knowledge. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat At-Taghabun, sudden death will be warded off from him. And God knows best.
65:1: 1- O Prophet, when you divorce women He made the call specific and the address general in the ruling because he is in front of his nation, so his call is like their call, or because the speech is with him and the ruling is general to them. The meaning is if you want to divorce them according to the status of the legislator in it. Then divorce them during their waiting period meaning at its time, which is purity, because the lam in times and the like is for timing, and whoever counts the waiting period to menstruation attaches the lam to an omitted word like future ones, and its apparent meaning indicates that the waiting period is according to purity and that divorcing a woman in waiting period according to menstrual periods should be during purity, and that it is forbidden during menstruation because ordering something necessitates forbidding its opposite and does not indicate its non-occurrence, since the prohibition does not necessitate corruption. How can it be when it is authentic that "when Ibn Umar may God be pleased with him divorced his wife while she was menstruating, the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ordered him to take her back" and this is the reason for its revelation. And count the waiting period and control it and complete it as three menstrual periods. And fear God, your Lord in lengthening the waiting period and harming them. Do not turn them out of their houses from their dwellings at the time of separation until their waiting period is over. Nor should they leave by their own will. However, if we agreed to move, it would be permissible because the right does not extend beyond them. Combining the two prohibitions indicates their entitlement to residency and their obligation to remain in the separation residence. His statement, Unless they commit a clear immorality is an exception to the first, and the meaning is unless she is excessive towards the husband, for it is like rebellion in forfeiting her right, or unless she commits adultery, in which case she is taken out to have the prescribed punishment carried out on her, or to the second, to emphasize the prohibition and indicate that her going out is an immorality. And those are the limits set by God is a reference to the aforementioned rulings. And whoever transgresses the limits of God has wronged himself by exposing himself to punishment. You do not know meaning the self, or you, O Prophet, or the divorced one. Perhaps God will bring about something new after that, which is the desire for the divorced woman to return or resume.
65:2: 2- And when they have reached their term approaching the end of their waiting period then keep them "and take them back on acceptable terms" with good treatment and appropriate spending. "Or part from them on acceptable terms" by fulfilling their rights and avoiding harm, such as taking her back then divorcing her to lengthen her waiting period. "And have two just men among you witness" of the taking back or separation to absolve oneself of suspicion and to end disputes. It is recommended, as God the Almighty says: "And take witnesses when you make a sale" and Al-Shafi'i said that it is obligatory in the case of taking back. "And establish the testimony" O witnesses when necessary. "For God" sincerely for His sake. "This is admonished" He means to urge the taking of witnesses and establishing them, or all of what is in the verse. "Whoever believes in God and the Last Day" then he is the one who will benefit from it and is the one intended by its mention. "And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out."
65:3: 3- And will provide for him from where he does not expect is an interjectional clause confirming what came before with the promise to avoid what He explicitly or implicitly forbade, such as divorce during menstruation, harming a woman in her waiting period and expelling her from her home, transgressing the limits of God, concealing testimony, and expecting that God will make a way out for him from the hardships and sorrows that spouses face, and will provide him with relief and a replacement from a source he had not imagined, or with the promise to all the righteous of deliverance from the harms of this world and the next and winning their good from where they do not expect. Or it is a digression when mentioning the believers. It was narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), "I know of a verse that, if people were to adhere to it, it would suffice them. 'And whoever fears God,' he will continue to recite it and repeat it." It was narrated that Salim ibn Awf ibn Malik Al-Ashja’i was captured by the enemy, so his father complained to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said to him, “Fear God and say often, ‘There is no power nor strength except with God.’ So he did so, and while he was in his house, his son knocked on the door with a hundred camels. The enemy had ignored them, so he drove them away.” In another narration, He returned with sheep and provisions. “And whoever relies upon God, then He is sufficient for him” is sufficient. Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose means He will accomplish what He wants, and nothing He desires will escape Him. Hafs recited the addition, and balagha’ amruhu was recited, meaning effective, and balagha as a state. The report is, God has set for everything a [decreed] extent, an estimation or a predetermined amount, or a term that cannot be changed. This is a clarification of the obligation of reliance and a confirmation of what came before regarding the timing of divorce according to the time of the waiting period and the command to count it, and a prelude to what will come regarding its amounts.
65:4: 4- "And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation" because of their old age. "If you are in doubt" if you are ignorant about their waiting period, that is, if you are ignorant of them. "Their waiting period is three months. It was narrated that when the verse And divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods was revealed, it was said, What is the waiting period of those who have not menstruated?" So it was revealed. "And those who have not menstruated" meaning, and those who have not yet menstruated are the same. "And those who are pregnant, their term" is the end of their waiting period. that they give birth is a ruling that includes divorcees and those whose husbands have died. Maintaining its generality is more appropriate than maintaining the generality of the Almighty’s statement: And those of you who die and leave wives behind because the generality of those who are pregnant is specific and the generality of wives is incidental, and the ruling is extended here, unlike it there. And because it was authenticated that “Subai’ah bint al-Harith gave birth a few nights after the death of her husband, so she mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said, “You are permissible, so marry.” And because it was revealed later, its precedence in practice is a specification, and the precedence of the other based on the general over the specific, and the first is more likely to be agreed upon. And whoever fears God in His rulings and takes her rights into account. He will make for him a way out makes his matter easy for him and guides him to what is good.
65:5: 5- That is the command of God referring to what was mentioned of the rulings “He has sent it down to you. And whoever fears God” in His rulings and observes their rights He will remove from him his misdeeds for good deeds eliminate misdeeds and will make great for him his reward by multiplying it.
65:6: 6- Lodge them where you live meaning a place of your residence according to your means meaning what you can bear, or an explanatory apposition to His statement from where you live. And do not harm them in housing in order to make things difficult for them so as to force them to leave. And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth and they have finished their waiting period. This indicates that the right to maintenance is specific to the pregnant woman in her waiting period, and the hadiths support this. If they breastfeed for you after the marital bond has been severed. Then give them their payment for breastfeeding. And consult together in what is right so that you may enjoin upon one another what is fair in breastfeeding and payment. And if you are in difficulty you are in difficulty. Then another woman will breastfeed him, and in it is a rebuke to the mother for being difficult.
65:7: 7- Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance, and he whose provision is restricted - let him spend from what God has given him. That is, let both the wealthy and the poor spend according to their ability. God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. Indeed, the Almighty does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity, and in this is a good description of the one with an abundance of wealth, and for this reason He promised him ease, saying: God will bring about, after hardship, ease, that is, sooner or later.
65:8: 8- And how many a town [people of a town] was insolent toward the command of its Lord and His messengers "turned away from it as the insolent, obstinate one turns away So We brought it to a severe account" with investigation and discussion. "And We punished it with a terrible punishment" terrible, and what is meant is the accounting of the Hereafter and its punishment, and the expression is in the past tense for emphasis.
65:9: 9- So she tasted the evil consequences of her deed the punishment for her disbelief and sins. And the outcome of her deed was loss with no profit in it at all.
65:10: 10- God has prepared for them a severe punishment. This is a repetition of the threat and an explanation of what necessitates the piety commanded in His statement: So fear God, O you of understanding. It is possible that what is meant by the reckoning is the exhaustive examination of their sins and their recording in the records of the guardians, and by the punishment is what they will be afflicted with immediately. Those who believe - God has sent down to you a reminder.
65:11: 11- A Messenger means by the mention Gabriel, peace be upon him, because of his frequent mention, or because he descended with the mention, which is the Qur’an, or because he is mentioned in the heavens or has mention, meaning honor, or Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, because of his regular recitation of the Qur’an, or his conveyance of it. He expressed his sending with the word sending down as a recommendation, or because he was caused by the revelation being sent down to him. He substituted a Messenger for it to clarify, or he meant the Qur’an by it. A Messenger is in the accusative case with an implied word such as sent or mention as a source, and a Messenger is its object, or he substituted it as meaning the message. He recites to you the clear verses of God is a state of the noun God or an attribute of Messenger, what is meant by those who believe in His statement, That He may bring forth those who believe and do righteous deeds is those who believed after it was revealed, that is, that He may grant them what they are upon now of faith and righteous deeds, or that He may bring forth whoever He knows or has decreed will believe from darkness into the light from misguidance to guidance, And whoever believes in God and does righteousness - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read We will enter it with the letter nun. God has certainly given him good provision in it is amazement and glorification of the reward they have been given.
65:12: 12- God is He who created seven heavens is a subject and predicate. And of the earth the like of them meaning He created the like of them in number on the earth. It is read in the nominative case as a subject and predicate: The command descends between them meaning He executes the command and decree of God between them and implements His rule among them. That you may know that God has power over all things and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge is a reason for created or for descends, or an implied word that includes them both, as each of them indicates the perfection of His power and knowledge. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Whoever recites Surat At-Talaq will die according to the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.”
66:1: 1- "O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you? It was narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was alone with Maria during the turn of Aisha may God be pleased with her or Hafsa. Hafsa found out about that and reprimanded him, so he forbade Maria, so this was revealed. It was also said that He drank honey in Hafsa's house, so Aisha conspired with Sawda and Safiyya, so they said to him, 'We smell the odor of perfumes from you, so he forbade honey.' So this was revealed: Seeking the pleasure of your wives, as an explanation of forbid or a state of the doer or a resumption to clarify the motive for it. And God is Forgiving for you for this slip, as it is not permissible to forbid what God has made lawful. Merciful He was merciful to you since He did not hold you accountable for it and reprimanded you to protect your chastity.
66:2: 2- "God has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths." He has prescribed for you the expiation of your oaths, which is the expiation of what you have bound by expiation, or the exception in it by the will so that you do not break your oath, from their saying: He made his oath expiated if he made an exception in it. It was used as evidence by those who saw the prohibition absolutely or the prohibition of a woman by an oath, and it is weak because the obligation of expiation for an oath in it does not necessarily mean that it is an oath, with the possibility that he, peace and blessings be upon him, used the wording of the oath, as it was said: "And God is your Master, the Guardian of your affairs, and He is the All-Knowing, what is good for you, the Wise," the Perfect in His actions and rulings.
66:3: 3- And when the Prophet confided in one of his wives meaning Hafsah a statement" about the prohibition of Maria or honey, or that the caliphate after him would be for Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them both. "And when she informed him of it" meaning when Hafsah informed Aisha, may God be pleased with them both, about the statement. "And God revealed it to him" and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, learned about the statement, meaning about its disclosure. "He knew some of it" the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, knew some of what Hafsah did. "And he ignored some" about some of the signs out of generosity, or he rewarded her for some by divorcing her and overlooked some. This is supported by Al-Kisa'i's reading with the light vowel, as it does not allow for anything else here, but the heavy vowel is from the category of using the name of the effect to the cause, and the light vowel is the opposite. The first is supported by his statement: "And when he informed her of it, she said, 'Who informed you of this?' He said, 'The Knowing, the Acquainted informed me.'" This is more in keeping with Islam.
66:4: 4- "If you both repent to God" is addressed to Hafsa and Aisha, highlighting the exaggeration in the reproach. "Your hearts have already turned away" He found in you that which necessitates repentance, which is the inclination of your hearts from what is required of you to be sincere to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, by loving what he loves and hating what he hates. "But if you both back up against him" If you both back up against him in what they do wrong, the Kufians read it with a light pronunciation. "Then God is his Protector, and [so will be] Gabriel and the righteous believers" He will not lack those who will support him from among God, the angels, and the righteous believers, for God is his supporter, and Gabriel, the chief of the Cherubim, is his companion, and the righteous believers are his followers and helpers. "And the angels after that are supporters" Supporters, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, was singled out to glorify him, and what is meant by "righteous" is the genus, and therefore it was generalized by the addition, and by His saying after that, it is glorified by the angels' support as part of the things with which God, the Most High, supports him.
66:5: 5- "Perhaps if he divorces you, his Lord will substitute for him wives better than you" based on the majority, or the general address, and there is nothing in it to indicate that he did not divorce Hafsah and that there are better women than them because the condition of divorcing all of them does not contradict the divorce of one, and what is conditional on what has not happened does not have to happen. Nafi' and Abu Amr read "He will substitute him" with a light pronunciation. "Muslim women, believers" affirming, sincere, or submissive, believing. "Qanitat" praying or regularly performing acts of obedience. "Repentant" for sins. "Abidat" devoutly or humbled to the command of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. "Sa'ihat" fasting. The fasting person is called a traveler because he glorifies God during the day without food, or emigrants. "Married women and virgins" the conjunction is in the middle because of their contradiction because they are ruled by the same description since the meaning includes married women and virgins.
66:6: 6- O you who have believed, protect yourselves by abandoning sins and performing acts of obedience and your families with advice and discipline. It was read and your families in apposition to the and of protect, so yourselves is the selves of the two tribes, with the emphasis on those being addressed. A Fire whose fuel is men and stones A Fire whose fuel is men and stones" A Fire whose fuel is like wood for others. "Over it are angels" who follow its command, which are the Zabaniyyah. "Harsh and severe" Harsh in speech and severe in deeds, or harsh in character and severe in character, strong in severe actions. "They do not disobey God in what He commands them" in the past. "And they do what they are commanded" in the future, or they do not refrain from accepting and abiding by the commands and they do what they are commanded.
66:7: 7- "O you who have disbelieved, make no excuses today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do." That is, this will be said to them when they enter Hell, and the prohibition of making excuses is because they have no excuse or the excuse will not benefit them.
66:8: 8- "O you who have believed, repent to God with sincere repentance." This is an extreme form of sincere advice, which is a characteristic of the repentant, as he advises himself to repent. It is described with a metaphorical attribution, exaggerating or in sincere advice. It is the sewing, as if she is repairing what the sin has torn. Abu Bakr read it with a damma on the noon, which is a source meaning advice, like thanks and gratitude. Sincerity, like steadfastness and perseverance, is estimated as the essence of sincere advice, or you advise sincerely, or repent sincerely for yourselves. Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asked about repentance, and he said: It includes six things: regret for past sins, and for obligatory duties, repetition, returning wrongs, seeking forgiveness from opponents, resolving not to return, and raising yourself in obedience to God as you raised it in disobedience. "Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow." This is mentioned in the form of hope, following the custom of kings, and indicating that it is a favor and that repentance is not required, and that the servant should be between fear and hope. "The Day when God will not disgrace the Prophet is an adverbial phrase for will admit you. And those who believed with him" is in apposition to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to praise them and compensate those who opposed them. It was also said that it is a subject and predicate. "Their light proceeds before them and on their right," meaning on the path. "They say, when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished, Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent." It was also said that their lights vary according to their deeds, so they ask for its completion as a favor.
66:9: 9- O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers with the sword and the hypocrites with argument and be harsh upon them and use harshness in striving against them if gentleness reaches its limit. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination. Hell or their refuge.
66:10: 10- "God sets forth an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot." God, the Most High, sets forth their situation in that they are punished for their disbelief and do not show favoritism because of the relationship between them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers, in their situation. They were under two of Our righteous servants. He means by this to glorify Noah and Lot, peace be upon them. But they betrayed them by hypocrisy. So they did not avail them at all against God. "So the two prophets did not avail them at all by the right of marriage. It was said, That is, for them at their death or on the Day of Resurrection. Enter the Fire with those who enter" with all the disbelievers who enter who have no connection to the Prophets, peace be upon them.
66:11: 11- "And God presents an example to those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh." He likened their situation in that the connection with the disbelievers does not harm them to the situation of Asiya, may God be pleased with her, and her status with God, even though she was under the most hostile of God's enemies. When she said is an adverbial phrase for the omitted example. My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise close to Your mercy or in the highest degrees of those brought near. And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds from his evil self and his bad deeds. And save me from the wrongdoing people from the Copts who followed him in wrongdoing.
66:12: 12- And Mary, the daughter of Imran is in apposition to the wife of Pharaoh as a consolation for the widows who guarded her chastity from men so We breathed into him into her chastity, and it was read in her, meaning in Mary or in the sentence. of Our spirit from a spirit We created without an intermediary origin. and she believed in the words of her Lord in His revealed scriptures or in what He revealed to His prophets. and His books and what was written in the Preserved Tablet, or the type of revealed books, and the reading of the two Basrans and Hafs indicates this in the plural. It was read with the word of God and His book, meaning with Jesus, peace be upon him, and the Gospel. and she was among the devout among those who were constant in obedience. The masculine is for emphasis and to indicate that her obedience did not fall short of the obedience of perfect men so that she was counted among them, or among their descendants, so of is an introductory particle. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “Many men attained perfection, but only four women attained perfection: Asiya bint Marahim, the wife of Pharaoh; Mary bint Imran; Khadija bint Khuwaylid; and Fatimah bint Muhammad. The superiority of Aisha over other women is like the superiority of tharid over all other foods.” And on his authority, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat At-Tahrim, God will give him a sincere nut.
67:1: 1- Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion with the power to control all matters. And He is over all things competent over all that He wills.
67:2: 2- Who created death and life He determined them or brought life into existence and took it away according to what He determined. He mentioned death first because He said: And you were dead and He gave you life and because it is more likely to lead to good deeds. To test you so that the one who is tested will deal with you, O you who are charged. Which of you is best in deed is the most correct and sincere. It came in the nominative case: the best in mind, the most pious in avoiding what God has forbidden, and the quickest in obeying Him. It is a sentence that acts as the second object of the verb of trial, which includes the meaning of knowledge. This is not a case of suspension, because it would be invalidated by the sentence being good when the verb is not suspended from it, unlike when it acts as two objects. And He is the Exalted in Might The Prevailing Whom no one who does evil deeds can render Him helpless. The Forgiving for whoever repents among them.
67:3: 3- He who created seven heavens in layers matching one above the other, the source of the verb tatabaqat an-na'l is to mix them layer upon layer, describing them, or to layer them in layers, or having layers, the plural of tabaq like jabal and jibal, or tabaqa like rāhbah and rāhab. What do you see in the creation of the Most Gracious any discrepancy? Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it from tafawwat and their meanings are the same, like ta'ahud and al-'ahudhu, which is the difference and lack of proportion from fat as if each of the two dissimilar things missed out on some of what was in the other. The sentence is a second description of seven in which the creation of the Most Gracious was placed in the place of the pronoun for glorification and to indicate that the Almighty creates such a thing with His dazzling power out of mercy and favor, and that in its creation there are great blessings that are countless. The address in it is to the Messenger or to every addressee and His saying, Then look again - do you see any flaw? is connected to it in the sense of causing, meaning you have looked at it repeatedly, so look at it once again, contemplating it to witness what it has been informed of of its proportionality, straightness, and its being gathered together as it should be. Futuur is the cracks and what is meant is the defect from fatarahu if he splits it.
67:4: 4- "Then return your sight twice" meaning two more returns to search for the fault. What is meant by repetition is repetition and multiplication as in "Labbaik and Sa'dayk". Therefore, he answered the command by saying: "The sight will return to you, humbled far from hitting the desired goal, as if it had been driven away from it by being driven away by smallness while it is weary" exhausted from the length of the repetition and the many returns.
67:5: 5- And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven the heaven closest to the earth. with lamps with shining stars at night lighting lamps therein. The indefinite form is for emphasis, and this does not prevent some of the stars from being stationed in heavens above them, as adornment is by showing them therein. And We have made them missiles against the devils and We made for them another benefit, which is to stone your enemies. The word rajum is the plural of rajm with a fat-ha, and it is a verbal noun that is used to name what is stoned by the falling of meteors caused by it. Its meaning is: We made them missiles and assumptions for the devils among mankind, who are the astrologers. And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze in the Hereafter after the burning by the meteors in this world.
67:6: 6- And for those who disbelieve in their Lord from the devils and others. The punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination. It was read in the accusative case, so that for those is in apposition to for them and punishment is in apposition to the punishment of the Blaze.
67:7: 7- If they are thrown into it, they will hear its roaring a sound like the sound of donkeys. And it will boil boiling with them like a boiling cauldron with everything in it.
67:8: 8- It almost bursts with rage It scatters with rage against them, and it is a metaphor for the intensity of its burning with them, and it may be intended to mean the rage of the guards. Whenever a group is thrown into it A group of disbelievers. Its keepers asked them, Did there not come to you a warner?" To frighten you with this punishment, and it is a rebuke and a reprimand.
67:9: 9- "They said, 'Yes, a warner has come to us, but we denied it and said, "God has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error."' That is, we denied the messengers and went to extremes in our denial until we denied the revelation and sending altogether, and we went astray in attributing them to error. So the warner is either in the plural sense because it is a verbal noun or a verbal noun understood by an adjective, i.e., people of warning, or it is described by it for emphasis, or it is singular and the address is to it and its likes by emphasis, or the denial of the singular is made in place of the denial of all, or the meaning is that the groups said, A messenger from God has come to every group of us, but we denied them and led them astray. It is possible that the address is from the words of the guards to the disbelievers, meaning the statement, so the error is what they were upon in this world, or the punishment in which they will be.
67:10: 10- "And they said, 'If only we had listened' to the words of the Messengers and accepted them completely without research or investigation, relying on what was evident of their truthfulness through miracles. 'Or reasoned' and contemplated its wisdom and witnessed the thinking of those who have insight. 'We would not have been among the companions of the Blaze' among them and among their number.
67:11: 11- So they acknowledged their sin when it would not benefit them, and admission is an acknowledgment with knowledge, and sin was not pluralized because it is originally a source, or what is meant by it is disbelief. So, destruction to the companions of the Blaze So God crushed them with a crushing that removed them from His mercy, and the predominance is for brevity, exaggeration and explanation, and Al-Kisa'i read it with emphasis.
67:12: 12- Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen fear His punishment in a way that is hidden from them and that they have not yet witnessed, or hidden from Him or from the eyes of people, or hidden from them, which is their hearts. For them is forgiveness for their sins. And a great reward compared to which the pleasures of this world are insignificant.
67:13: 13- And whether you conceal your speech or declare it publicly, He is Knowing of that within the breasts with the pronouns before expressing them secretly or publicly.
67:14: 14- Does He not know who created? Does He not know the secret and the manifest who brought things into existence according to His wisdom? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware. Whose knowledge reaches what is apparent and what is hidden, or does God not know who He created? In this position and with this restriction to this state, it is necessary for knows to have an object to benefit. It was narrated that the polytheists used to speak among themselves about things, and God would inform His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of them, and they would say: Keep your speech secret so that the God of Muhammad does not hear. So God pointed out their ignorance.
67:15: 15- It is He who made the earth subservient to you soft and easy for you to walk in it. So walk in its slopes in its sides or mountains. This is an example of extreme subservience, as the shoulder of a camel refuses to be trodden by a rider and does not become subservient to him. So when He made the earth in such a way that he can walk in its slopes, nothing will remain that will not be subservient. And eat of His provision and seek from the blessings of God. And to Him is the resurrection, and He will ask you to be grateful for what He has bestowed upon you.
67:16: 16- Do you feel secure against Him who is in the heaven? meaning the angels who are assigned to manage this world, or God, the Most High, according to the interpretation of who is in the heaven, His command is His judgment, or according to the claim of the Arabs, for they claimed that He, the Most High, is in the heaven. Ibn Kathir said, And you felt secure, by changing the first hamza to a waw because of the sukoon of what preceded it, and you felt secure by changing the second to an alif, and this is the reading of Nafi', Abu Amr, and Ruways. That He will cause the earth to swallow you up, by making you disappear into it as He did with Qarun, and it is a badal al-ishtmal. And behold, it is turbulent, by which one comes and goes.
67:17: 17- Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send upon you a storm of stones? That He will rain down upon you pebbles. Then you will know how My warning is. How My warning is when you see the one being warned, but knowledge will not benefit you then.
67:18: 18- And those before them denied, so how was My reproach. My reproach to them by sending down the punishment, which is a consolation to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a threat to his polytheist people.
67:19: 19- “Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading out their wings in the air when flying, for when they spread them out, they line up their tiptoes. And they fold them in” and bring them together when they strike their sides with them time after time to show that they are moving. Therefore, it was changed to the verb form to differentiate between the original flight and that which is imposed upon it. What holds them up in the air contrary to nature except the Most Gracious whose mercy encompasses everything, for He created them with shapes and characteristics that prepared them to fly in the air. Indeed, He is Seeing of all things He knows how to create the strange and manage wonders.
67:20: 20- Is this the one who is your army that will aid you against the Most Merciful? is similar to His statement, Have they not seen, meaning, Have you not considered such crafts, so you do not know Our ability to punish them by means of a landslide or the sending of a hailstorm? "Or do you have an army that will aid you against God if He sends His punishment upon you? It is like His statement, Or have they gods that can protect them against Us?" except that it was used as a question to identify who will aid them, indicating that they believed in this oath. "Who is the subject, this is its predicate, who is its predicate, and aids you is a description of army" based on its wording. "The disbelievers are only in delusion," they have no support.
67:21: 21- Is this the one who provides for you? Or the one who is pointed to and it is said, This is the one who provides for you. "If He withholds His provision" by withholding the rain and all other means that purify and lead it to you. "Rather, they persisted in stubbornness obstinacy boiling" straying from the truth so that their natures would be repelled by it.
67:22: 22- Is he who walks prone on his face better guided? It is said, I made him fall down, so he fell down. This is one of the strange words, like God scattered the clouds, so they scattered. The truth is that they are both from the same root as anfaḍ, meaning he became those who stumbled and those who scattered. The passive forms of kab and qasha'a are not the passive forms of kab and qasha'a, but rather the passive forms of both are akba and anqaba. The meaning of those who stumbled is that he stumbles every hour and falls on his face due to the roughness of his path and the difference in his parts. Therefore, he contrasted it with his saying, Is he who walks upright, standing, safe from stumbling. On a straight path, whose parts and direction are level. The intended meaning is to represent the polytheist and monotheist with the travelers, and the religious people with the two paths. Perhaps the indication in kab of the state of the path is sufficient to indicate that what the polytheist is on does not deserve to be called a path, like the walking of someone who is arbitrarily in a different, uneven place. It was said that the one who is stuck is the blind one, for he is thrown down and the one who is sighted is the one who walks stuck and is thrown down on his face to the Fire, and the one who walks upright is the one who is thrown down on his feet to Paradise.
67:23: 23- "Say, 'It is He who created you and gave you hearing, and sight, so that you may see His creations, and hearts, so that you may reflect and consider. Little do you give thanks,' for using them for the purpose for which they were created."
67:24: 24- Say, 'It is He who dispersed you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.' For recompense.
67:25: 25- And they say, 'When will this promise come to pass?' That is, the gathering or what they were promised of subsidence and stones. If you should be truthful, meaning the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the believers.
67:26: 26- "Say, 'Knowledge is only with God,' meaning knowledge of its time. 'And I am only a clear warner.'" Warning requires knowledge, or even a suspicion, that what is warned against will occur.
67:27: 27- So when they saw it meaning the promise, for it means the promised thing. Close meaning close to them. The faces of those who disbelieved were made ugly because they were overcome by sadness and the sight of the punishment made them sad. And it was said, 'This is what you were calling for' you were asking for and hastening, you are making the invocation from the word supplication, or you are calling that there is no resurrection, for it is from the word claim.
67:28: 28- "Say, 'Have you considered: if God should destroy me and those with me of the believers, or have mercy on us by delaying our appointed times, then who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?'" That is, no one can save them from the punishment, whether we die or live. This is an answer to their saying, We are waiting for him to be struck by a misfortune of time.
67:29: 29- Say, ‘He is the Most Gracious’ to whom I invite you, the Master of all blessings. We have believed in Him knowing that. And upon Him we have relied putting our trust in Him and knowing that no one other than Him in and of Him can harm or benefit. The relative clause is presented for specification and to indicate it. Then you will know who is in manifest error from among us and from you. Al-Kisa’i read it with a ya’.
67:30: 30- Say, ‘Have you considered if your water were to become sunken in?’ Sunken into the ground so that buckets could not reach it. Then who would bring you flowing water? Running or apparent, easy to access. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever recites Surat Al-Mulk, it is as if he has revived the Night of Decree.
68:1: 1- Nun" is one of the names of letters. It was said that it is the name of the whale and what is meant by it is the genus or the Bahamut which is the one on which the earth is, or the inkwell, as some whales extract something blacker than the soul and write with it. The first is supported by its stillness and its writing in the form of a letter. "And the Pen" is what wrote the tablet, or what is written with. God swore by it due to its many benefits. Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub concealed the nun to make the separate waw act like the connected one, as the still nun is concealed with the letters of the mouth if it is connected to it. This was narrated from Nafi' and Asim, and it was read with the fatha and kasra like "Sad". "And what they write and what they write, and the pronoun refers to the pen" in the first meaning to glorify, or in the second meaning to mean the genus and to attribute the action to the evidence and to make it act like the people of knowledge to take their place, or to its companions or the memorizers. "Ma" is a source or a relative pronoun.
68:2: 2- "You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman." The answer to the oath, and the meaning is that you are not a madman, and that He has blessed you with prophecy and sound judgment. The agent in the state has the meaning of negation. It was said that "a madman" does not prevent its function in what precedes it because it is an additional letter, and there is a consideration in this regard from the point of view of meaning.
68:3: 3- "And indeed, you will have a reward" is an assumption and a statement. "Ungrateful" is either certain or grateful to you from people, for God Almighty gives it to you without any intermediary.
68:4: 4- And indeed, you are of a great moral character as you endure from your people what your peers would not endure. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, was asked about his character, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she said: His character was the Qur’an. Do you not read the Qur’an: The believers have succeeded.
68:5: 5-You will see and they will see.
68:6: 6- Which of you is afflicted? Which of you is afflicted with madness? The ba is an additional word, or which of you is mad, given that the afflicted is a source like the rational and the flogged, or which of the two groups among you is the madman, the group of believers or the group of disbelievers, meaning in which of them is there someone who deserves this name.
68:7: 7- Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of those who have strayed from His way - they are the truly insane. And He is most knowing of the rightly guided - those who are victorious with perfect reason.
68:8: 8-Do not obey the deniers is an incitement to resolve to disobey them.
68:9: 9- And they wish that you would be lenient with them that you would abandon their prohibition of polytheism, or that you would agree with them sometimes. So that they would be lenient so they would be lenient with you by abandoning their criticism and agreeing. The fa is for conjunction, meaning that they wished to be lenient and desired it, but they delayed their lenientness until you were lenient. Or it is for causality, meaning that they wish that you would be lenient so they would be lenient then, or they wished that you would be lenient, so they are lenient now, hoping for it. In some copies of the Qur'an, so that they would be lenient is the answer to the wish.
68:10: 10- And do not obey every swearer who swears a lot, whether right or wrong, insulting, low-minded, from insulting which means lowliness.
68:11: 11- A backbiter, a slanderer, a gossiper, someone who spreads gossip.
68:12: 12- An obstacle to goodness": He prevents people from doing good, such as faith, conviction, and righteous deeds. "Aggressor": He who transgresses in injustice. "Atheem": He who commits many sins.
68:13: 13- Atal is dry and rough from Atalah if he led someone violently and roughly. Badhalka after he was counted among his faults Zanim is a pretender taken from the two humps of a sheep which are the two hanging from its ear and throat. It was said that he is the child of Al-Mughira and his father claimed him eighteen years after his birth. It was said that Al-Akhnas bin Shuraiq was originally from Thaqeef and his number is in Zahra.
