68:14: 14- If he has wealth and children.
68:15: 15- When Our verses are recited to him, he says, 'Legends of the ancients.' He said that because he was wealthy and boasted of having children out of his excessive arrogance. However, the agent is the meaning of said not itself, because what comes after the condition does not affect what comes before it. It is possible that it is the reason for do not obey, meaning do not obey someone like this, for example, because he had wealth. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Yaqub, and Abu Bakr read that it was as a question, except that Ibn Amir made the hamza between now he had wealth, meaning would you obey him?, or would you obey him because he had wealth. It was read that it was with a kasra, on the basis that the condition of wealth in the prohibition of obedience is like the reason of poverty in the prohibition of killing children, or that made it a condition for the addressee, meaning do not obey him, stipulating his wealth, because if he obeys the wealthy, then it is as if he made it a condition for his obedience.
68:16: 16- We will brand him with a cautery on the nose on the nose. Al-Walid's nose was injured on the day of Badr, and its mark remained. It was said that it is an expression for humiliating him to the utmost degree, like their saying: Cut off his nose, in spite of his nose, because the mark on the face is a mark on the nose that is an obvious disgrace, or blacken his face on the Day of Resurrection.
68:17: 17- Indeed, We tested them We tested the people of Mecca, may God Almighty honor it, with famine. As We tested the companions of the garden He means the garden that was two farsakhs from Sana'a, and it belonged to a righteous man who used to call out to the poor at harvest time and leave for them what the sickle missed and what the wind blew, or after the rug that was spread out under the palm tree and a large amount was gathered for them. So when he died, his sons said, If we do what our father used to do, the situation will become difficult for us. So they swore to harvest it in the morning, secretly from the poor, as He said, When they swore to harvest it in the morning to cut it down entering in the morning.
68:18: 18- And they do not make an exception nor do they say God willing, but he called it an exception because of what it contains of giving out, except that the one giving out by it is different from what was mentioned and the one giving out by exception is the same, or because the meaning of I give out God willing and I do not give out until God wills is the same, or and they do not make an exception is the share of the poor as their father used to give out.
68:19: 19- And a plague swept over them on Paradise a plague swept over them. "From your Lord" is the subject of it. "And while they were asleep."
68:20: 20- So it became like a barren land like an orchard whose fruits have been cut off so that nothing remains in it. Fa'il means maf'ul, or like the guide in its burning and blackening, or like the day in its whitening from excessive dryness. They were called barren land because each of them is cut off from the other, or like sand.
68:22: 22- That you go out to your tillage in the morning means that you go out or that you go out to it in the morning, and the verb is transitive with the preposition 'ala either because it includes the meaning of approach or because the morning is likened to the morning of the enemy, which includes the meaning of seizure. If you are decisive cutting him off.
68:23: 23- So they set out, speaking in low voices. They consulted among themselves. The word khafa, khafafat, and khafad mean to conceal, and from this comes the word khafdud for the bat.
68:24: 24- That no poor person should enter it upon you today. "That" is an explanatory particle, and it was read with its omission, implying the statement. What is meant by prohibiting the poor person from entering is the exaggeration of the prohibition against allowing him to enter, like their saying: I do not want to see you here.
68:25: 25- And they went out in the morning with a heavy heart, able to do so. And they went out with a heavy heart, able to do so only for misery, from haradt as-sana if there is no rain in it, and haradt al-ibil if its milk is withheld. The meaning is that they decided to make things difficult for the poor, but things became difficult for them to the point that they were unable to do anything except misery, or they went out with misery and deprivation instead of being able to benefit. It was said that harad means harad and it was read with it, meaning they were unable to do anything except anger some of them to others, like his saying: They blame each other. It was also said that harad, intention, and speed. He said: A torrent came from God’s command, roaring like the roar of the enslaved Paradise. That is, they went quickly to their paradise, capable in their own minds of its severity. It was said that it was a sign of paradise.
68:26: 26- So when they saw it the first time they saw it. They said, 'Indeed, we are astray' the path to our Paradise and what it is in.
68:27: 27- "Rather, we meaning after they contemplated it and knew that it was her, they said, Rather, we are deprived" we were deprived of its goodness because of our crime against ourselves.
68:28: 28- The one of them who was most moderate in opinion or age said, 'Did I not tell you why you would not glorify God?' Why would you not remember Him and repent to Him for your evil intentions? He said this when they decided to do that, and it indicates this meaning.
68:29: 29- They said, ‘Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.’ That is, why do you not make an exception? The exception is called glorification because they share in the glorification, or because it is a declaration that He is not to allow anything to happen in His kingdom that He does not want.
68:30: 30- So they turned to one another, blaming one another. Blaming one another, some of them indicated that, some of them approved of it, some of them remained silent, satisfied, and some of them denied it.
68:31: 31- "They said, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors.'" They transgressed the limits of God Almighty.
68:32: 32- Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us one better than it through the blessing of repentance and confession of sin. It has been narrated that they substituted one better than it, and it was read Yubdallana with a light pronunciation. Indeed, we are desirous of our Lord seeking forgiveness and seeking good, and to me indicates the end of the desire, or because it includes the meaning of returning.
68:33: 33- Such is the punishment Like the punishment with which We afflicted the people of Mecca and the companions of Paradise, the punishment in this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater Greater than it. If they had known They would have beenware of what would lead them to the punishment.
68:34: 34- Indeed, for the righteous are with their Lord meaning in the Hereafter, or in the vicinity of Jerusalem Gardens of Delight Gardens in which there is nothing but pure enjoyment.
68:35: 35- Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals? A denial of the words of the infidels, for they used to say: If it is true that we will be resurrected as Muhammad and those with him claim, then they will not prefer us, but rather we will be in a better state than them, as we are in this world.
68:36: 36- What is the matter with you? How do you judge? This is a turn of expression expressing astonishment at their judgment and rejecting it, and indicating that it is the result of a disordered mind and a crooked opinion.
68:37: 37- Or do you have a book from the heaven. In it you study you read.
68:38: 38- Indeed, you will have in it whatever you choose. You will have whatever you choose and desire. Its origin is that it is for you with the fat-ha because it is studied, but when the lam was brought, it was broken. It may be a narration of what is studied or a resumption. To choose something and select it means to take its best.
68:39: 39- Or do you have oaths upon Us? Confirmed covenants of faith. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 31 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Jin, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Naba. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 70:8: 8- The Day the sky will be like molten metal is an adverbial phrase for soon, meaning it could be the Day it will be or for an implied word indicated by occurring or a substitute for on the Day if it is attached to it, and molten metal is what is melted in molten metal like metals or dregs of oil.
70:9: 9- "And the mountains will be like wool" like wool dyed in different colors because the mountains are of different colors, so when they dry up and fly in the air they will resemble carded wool when the wind blows it.
70:10: 10- And no intimate friend will ask a intimate friend. And no relative will ask a relative about his condition. According to Ibn Kathir, and he will not ask is in the passive form, meaning that no intimate friend will ask him about his condition.
70:11: 11- They will see them is a resumption or a state indicating that the reason for this question is preoccupation rather than concealment or something that would suffice to observe the situation such as the whiteness or blackness of the face. The two pronouns are used together for the sake of the general meaning of the intimate word The criminal would like "if he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his children."
70:12: 12- And his companion and his brother is a state of one of the two pronouns or a resumption indicating that every criminal is preoccupied with himself such that he wishes to ransom himself with the people closest to him and the wisest of them in his heart, let alone care about his condition and ask about him. Nafi` and Al-Kisa`i read with a fat-ha on the m of that day and it was read with a tanween of torment and the accusative of that day because it means torment.
70:13: 13- And his clan and his tribe from whom he was separated that shelters him includes him in lineage or in times of hardship.
70:14: 14- And all those on earth of the two heavy burdens or creation. Then He will save him is in apposition to He will ransom him meaning then the ransom will save him and then is for exclusion.
70:15: 15- "No" is a deterrent to the criminal from friendship and an indication that ransom will not save him. "It is the pronoun for the fire or an ambiguous one explained by flame which is the predicate or a substitute or for the story and flame" is the subject of its predicate.
70:16: 16- Naz'at il-Shuwa which is pure flame. It was said that it is a name for fire transferred from latha meaning flame. Hafs read on the authority of Asim Naz'atan in the accusative case as a specification or a confirmed or transferred state on the basis that latha means scorched and the grill and the extremities or the plural of shawat which is the scalp.
70:17: 17- It invites attracts and brings, as Dhu al-Rummah said. His nose calls suspicion A metaphor for attracting and bringing those who fled from it. It was said that it calls its guards and it was said that it calls for destruction, from their saying the callers of God if He destroys him whoever turns away from the truth and turns away from obedience.
70:18: 18- And he gathered and stored He gathered the money and put it in a container and hoarded it out of eagerness and hope.
70:19: 19- Indeed, mankind was created impatient. Very anxious and impatient.
70:20: 20- If evil touches him harm. Anxious He becomes very impatient.
70:21: 21- And if goodness touches him "abundance diverse he exaggerates in holding back and the three descriptions are conditions that are estimated or realized because they are the natures that human beings are created with and the first if is a circumstance for impatient and the other for diverse.
70:22: 22- Except those who pray is an exception for those described with the attributes mentioned after who are naturally endowed with the conditions mentioned before, due to the opposition of those attributes to them in that they indicate absorption in obeying the Truth, compassion for creation, belief in reward, fear of punishment, suppression of desire, and preference of the hereafter over the present. These arise from being preoccupied with the love of the present and shortsightedness regarding them.
70:23: 23- Those who are constant in their prayers nothing distracts them from it.
70:24: 24- And those in whose wealth there is a known right such as zakat and designated charity.
70:25: 25- For the beggar who asks and the deprived who does not ask and considers himself rich but is deprived.
70:26: 26- And those who believe in the Day of Judgment believing in their deeds, which is that he exhausts himself and spends his money in the hope of the reward in the Hereafter, and that is why religion was mentioned.
70:27: 27- And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord are afraid for themselves.
70:28: 28- Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not safe. An objection indicating that no one should be safe from the punishment of God, even if he exaggerates in his obedience to Him.
70:29: 29- And those who guard their private parts.
70:30: 30- Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed.
70:31: 31- But whoever seeks beyond that - then those are the transgressors. This was previously explained in Surat Al-Mu'minun.
70:32: 32- And those who are to their trusts and their covenants attentive. Ibn Kathir read to their trusts, meaning they do not betray, deny, or conceal what they know of the rights of God and the rights of the servants.
70:33: 33- And those who stand by their testimonies. Yaqub and Hafs read with their testimonies because of the difference in types.
70:34: 34- And those who maintain their prayers They observe its conditions and complete its obligatory and recommended acts, and the repetition of the mention of prayer and their description of it first and last are two considerations to indicate its virtue and its superiority over other prayers. There are exaggerations in the organization of this prayer that are not hidden.
70:35: 35- Those will be in gardens, honoured with the reward of God Almighty.
70:36: 36- So what is the matter with those who disbelieved before you, that they are rushing around you, rushing.
70:37: 37- On the right and on the left, two groups different groups, izza and its root is izzwa from azwa and it is as if each group is proud of someone other than the one to whom the other is proud. The polytheists would gather around the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in circles and mock his words.
70:38: 38- Does every one of them aspire to enter the Garden of Delight? without faith, which is a denial of their saying, If what he says is true, then we would have a better share in it than they did in this world.
70:39: 39- No is a deterrent from this greed. Indeed, We created them from that which they know is an explanation for it. The meaning is that they were created from a drop of sperm that is not suitable for the world of holiness. So whoever is not perfected by faith and obedience and is not endowed with royal morals is not prepared to enter it. Or you were created for what you know, which is the perfection of the soul through knowledge and action. So whoever does not perfect it will not be among the stations of the perfect. Or the evidence from the first creation is the possibility of the second creation, which they built greed upon supposing it as an impossible supposition for them after being deterred from it.
70:40: 40- "So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests that We are indeed Able."
70:41: 41- That We may replace them with better ones meaning that We will destroy them and bring forth better people than them, or that We will give Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, someone better than you in your place, namely the Ansar. And We will not be outdone will We be defeated if We will that.
70:42: 42- So leave them to indulge in idle talk and play until they meet the Day they are promised. This was mentioned at the end of Surat At-Tur.
70:44: 44- Their eyes will be humbled, and humiliation will cover them. Its interpretation was mentioned, That is the Day which they were promised in this world. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Isra, God will give him the reward of those who are attentive to their trusts and covenants.
71:1: 1- Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Warn,' meaning, to warn, or by saying to him, Warn. It is possible that it is an explanation to include in sending the meaning of saying, and it was read without that to mean saying. Your people before there comes to them a painful punishment, the punishment of the Hereafter or the flood.
71:2: 2- He said, 'O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner.'
71:3: 3- Worship God, fear Him, and obey me. A similar example was mentioned in Al-Shu’ara’, and in that both interpretations are possible.
71:4: 4- "He will forgive you some of your sins" He will forgive you some of your sins, which is what was mentioned previously, so Islam will fulfill it, so He will not hold you accountable for it in the Hereafter. "And He will give you respite for a specified term" is the furthest that has been decreed for you, provided that you have faith and obedience. "Indeed, the term that God has decreed" if it comes in the manner decreed, it is a term, and it was said that it comes when the longer term comes. "He will not give you respite" so hasten to the times of respite and delay. "If you only knew" if you were people of knowledge and contemplation, you would have known that. It includes that because they are immersed in the love of life, it is as if they are doubting death.
71:5: 5- "He said, 'My Lord, I have called my people night and day.'" That is, constantly.
71:6: 6- My supplication only increased their flight from faith and obedience. Attributing the increase to the supplication is causal, as in His saying: It only increased their faith.
71:7: 7- And whenever I called them to faith, so that you might forgive them because of it, they put their fingers in their ears blocked their ears from listening to the call. And they covered themselves with their garments covered themselves with them so that they would not see me, out of aversion to looking at me due to their extreme aversion to my call, or so that I would not recognize them and call them. The expression in the form of a request is for exaggeration, and they persisted and were arrogant in disbelief and sins, borrowed from the donkey’s persistence on its pubic hair when it presses its ears and turns towards them. And they were arrogant about following me, with great arrogance.
71:9: 9- Then I declared to them and whispered to them secretly meaning I called them time after time and time after time in whatever way I could, and then is for the difference in the ways, as speaking out loud is more severe than speaking secretly, and combining them is more severe than singling them out because they are delayed from each other, and publicly is an accusative of the source because it is one of the two types of supplication, or its description is a deleted source with the meaning of supplication publicly meaning declaring it openly, or the state is in the meaning of declaring openly.
71:10: 10- So I said, 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord' by repenting from disbelief. He is indeed Oft-Forgiving to those who repent. It is as if when He commanded them to worship, they said, If we are on the truth, we will not abandon it, but if we are on falsehood, how can He accept us and be kind to us when we disobey Him? So He commanded them with what would make their sins worthy and bring them to Him, and their persistence led to God withholding rain from them for forty years, and making the wombs of their women barren. So He promised them that in return for seeking forgiveness for what they were upon, by saying:
71:11: 11- He sends down abundant rain upon you.
71:12: 12- And He will provide you with wealth and children and provide for you gardens and provide for you rivers. That is why seeking forgiveness for rain was prescribed. The sky may mean a canopy or clouds, and the rain means abundant rain. In this construction, both masculine and feminine are equal. What is meant by gardens are orchards.
71:13: 13- What is the matter with you that you do not expect reverence for God? You do not expect reverence for Him, that is, to magnify the one who worshipped and obeyed Him, so you are in a state in which you hope that He will magnify you. God is an explanation of the one who is revered, and if it had been delayed, it would have been a connection to reverence. Or you do not believe that He has greatness, so you fear disobeying Him. Rather, the belief was expressed with the hope that follows the slightest suspicion, as an exaggeration.
71:14: 14- And He has created you in stages is a state that establishes denial in that it is affirmative, for He created them in stages, that is, at times, since He created them first as elements, then compounds that nourish man, then mixtures, then sperm, then clots, then chewed flesh, then bones and flesh, then He created them another creation. This indicates that He can bring them back another time and magnify them with reward, and that He, the Most High, is of great power and perfect in wisdom. Then He followed that with what supports it, which is the verses of the horizons, so He said:
71:15: 15- Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers?
71:16: 16- And He made the moon a light therein meaning in the heavens, and it is in the lowest heaven, and it is only attributed to them because of its association. And He made the sun a lamp is like it because it removes the darkness of the night from the face of the earth just as a lamp removes it from what is around it.
71:17: 17- And God caused you to grow from the earth as a plant. He created you from it, so the word growth was used as a metaphor for creation because it is more indicative of occurrence and formation from the earth. Its original form is He caused you to grow from the earth as a plant, so you grew as a plant. So He shortened it to be satisfied with the implied meaning.
71:18: 18- "Then He will return you to it" buried. "And He will bring you forth a bringing forth" by the gathering. He emphasized it with the source as He emphasized the first, indicating that the return is certain like the beginning, and that it will inevitably happen.
71:19: 19- And God has made the earth a carpet for you on which you roll.
71:20: 20- So that you may take from it wide paths. Wide is the plural of wide and from, so that the verb includes the meaning of taking.
71:21: 21- “Noah said, ‘My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me’ in what I commanded them. ‘And they followed one whose wealth and children only increase him in loss.’ They followed their leaders who were arrogant with their wealth and conceited about their children, such that this became a reason for their increased loss in the Hereafter. It indicates that they only followed them out of prestige, which led them to loss. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and the two Basris read “and his son” with a damma and sukoon, as a language like sadness or a plural like a lion.
71:22: 22- And they plotted is in apposition to It did not increase him and the pronoun refers to whom and its plural is for the meaning. A great plot is extremely significant as it is more expressive than big and it is from big, and that is their deception in religion and inciting people to harm Noah, peace be upon him.
71:23: 23- "And they said, 'Do not abandon your gods,' meaning, to worship them. 'And do not abandon Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr. 'And do not abandon' these in particular. It was said that they are names of righteous men who were between Adam and Noah. When they died, they were made into statues to seek blessings from them. As time passed, they were worshipped. This was passed on to the Arabs, so Wadd was for Kalb, Suwa' for Himyar, Yaghuth for Madhhij, Ya'uq for Murad, and Nasr for Himyar. Nafi' read Wadd with the dammah, and Yaghuth and Ya'uq were read for the sake of appropriateness. They were not declined because they are proper nouns and foreign.
71:24: 24- And they have led many astray. The pronoun refers to the leaders or the idols, as in His statement: Indeed, they have led many astray. "And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error. This is in apposition to My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed Me." Perhaps what is meant is misguidance in promoting their deceit and worldly interests, not in matters of their religion, or loss and destruction, as in His statement: "Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness."
71:25: 25- "of their sins because of their sins, and ma is added for emphasis and glorification, and Abu Amr read of their sins they were drowned" by the flood. "so they were brought into a Fire" meaning the torment of the grave or the torment of the Hereafter, and the follow-up is because what is between drowning and bringing in is not taken into account, or because the effect is like what follows the cause even if it is delayed due to the lack of a condition or the presence of an obstacle, and the indefiniteness of the Fire is for glorification or because what is meant is a type of Fire "so they did not find for themselves besides God supporters" exposing them to taking gods besides God who are not able to support them.
71:26: 26- And Noah said, 'My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller.' That is, not a single one. It is one of the forms of general negation that is used in the form of a verb from the word 'dar' or 'dawr'. Its root is 'diwar', so what is derived from the root 'sayyid' is used in it. Otherwise, it would have been 'dawwar'.
71:27: 27- If you leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not give birth to anyone but wicked disbelievers. He said that after he had tested them and studied their conditions for a thousand years minus fifty years, so he knew their characteristics and natures.
71:28: 28- My Lord, forgive me and my parents to the king of Methuselah and Shamkha son of Enosh, and they were believers. And whoever enters my house my house, my mosque, or my ship. As a believer, and for the believing men and believing women until the Day of Resurrection. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction destruction. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Nuh will be among the believers who will be overtaken by the supplication of Nuh.
72:1: 1- "Say, 'It has been revealed to me.' It was also read 'Ahya', and its root is 'Waha' from 'Waha'i ilaihi', so the 'Waw' was changed to a 'Hamza' due to its 'Damma'. 'Waha' is in the original form, and its subject is: "that a group of jinn listened. A group is between three and ten, and the jinn" are subtle rational bodies, mostly fiery or airy. It was said that they are a type of abstract spirits, and it was said that they are human souls separate from their bodies. This indicates that he, peace and blessings be upon him, did not see them and did not recite to them, but rather their presence happened to be at some of the times of his recitation, so they heard it, and God informed His Messenger about it. "They said," when they returned to their people. "Indeed, we have heard a Qur'an," a book. "Amazing," unique, different from the speech of people in the beauty of its composition and the precision of its meaning. It is a source of description for exaggeration.
72:2: 2- It guides to the right path to the truth and rightness. So we believed in it in the Qur'an. And we will not associate anyone with our Lord as stated by the conclusive evidence of monotheism.
72:3: 3- And that He, the Most High, is the Lord of our Lord. Ibn Kathir and the two Basrans read it with a kasra, as if it were part of what was narrated after the statement, and so is what follows it except for His statement: And if they had been steadfast. "And that the mosques, and that when he stood up" are among the things that were revealed. Nafi' and Abu Bakr agreed with them except for his saying: "and that when he stood up" as a new sentence or a statement. The rest opened all of them except what began with the letter "fa on the basis that what was from their saying is conjoined to the place of the preposition and the noun in with it" as if it was said: We have believed "that He, the Most High, is the grandfather of our Lord" meaning His greatness is from the greatness of so-and-so in my eyes if he is great, or his authority or his wealth is borrowed from the grandfather which is luck, and the meaning is describing Him as being above having a companion or a son due to His greatness or authority or his wealth. His saying: "He has not taken a companion or a son" is an explanation of that. It was read "Jadd as a distinction Jadd Rabbina" with the kasra meaning He believed in His Lordship, as if they heard from the Qur'an what alerted them to the error of what they believed of polytheism and taking a companion and a son.
72:4: 4- "And that our foolish one, Satan or the rebellious jinn, used to say something outrageous about God." An outrageous statement, which is going far and exceeding the limit, or it is an outrage due to the extreme amount of exaggeration in it, which is attributing a companion and a son to God.
72:5: 5- And we thought that mankind and the jinn would never tell a lie about God. This is an apology for following the fool in that, as they thought that no one would lie about God. A lie is in the accusative case as a source because it is a type of omitted statement or description, meaning a statement in which there is a lie. Whoever reads that you would never tell a lie like Jacob makes it a source because the statement can only be a lie.
72:6: 6- And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn. For when a man spent the evening in a desert, he would say, I seek refuge with the master of this valley from the evil of the fools of his people. "So they increased them." So they increased the jinn by seeking refuge with them. "In oppression," in arrogance and transgression, or they increased the jinn and mankind in transgression by attacking them until they sought refuge with them. In origin, oppression means covering something.
72:7: 7- And that they and that mankind thought as you thought O jinn or vice versa, and the two verses are from the speech of the jinn to each other or a resumption of the speech of God Almighty, and whoever opens that in them makes them from what was revealed. That God will not resurrect anyone prevailed as the two objects of thought.
72:8: 8- "And we touched the heaven" We sought to reach the heaven or experience it. Touching is borrowed from "mass to request, like jass". It is said "touch, seek, and tamasuhu, like talabhu, attalibhu, and tattalabhu". "So we found it filled with guards, guards is a collective noun, like servants, strong", and they are the angels who prevent them from it. "And shooting stars, the plural of shihab", which is the shining light generated by fire.
72:9: 9- "And we used to sit therein in stations to listen Stations free of guards and meteors, or suitable for watching and listening, and to listen is a connection to we sit or an attribute of stations". "So whoever listens now will find a meteor watching him" meaning a meteor watching him and for his sake preventing him from listening by stoning, or those with a meteor watching, as it is a collective noun for the watcher, and the explanation of that was mentioned in As-Saffat.
72:10: 10- And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on the earth by the protection of heaven or whether their Lord intends for them a right course or good.
72:11: 11- And among us are the righteous the righteous believers. And among us are those who are less than that meaning a people less than that, so the described word was omitted, and they are the moderate ones. We were ways those with ways, meaning schools of thought, or like ways in the difference of circumstances, or our ways were ways. Scattered different, plural of qadda from qad, meaning to cut.
72:12: 12- And we thought we knew. That we would not be unable to defeat God on earth being on earth wherever we were in it. And we would not be unable to defeat Him by escaping fleeing from it to the sky, or we would not be unable to defeat Him on earth if He wanted something from us and we would not be unable to defeat Him by escaping to our request.
72:13: 13- And when we heard the guidance, meaning the Qur’an, “we believed in it. So whoever believes in his Lord will not fear,” meaning he will not fear. It was also read will not fear, and the first is more indicative of the certainty of the salvation of the believers and that it is specific to them. Without loss or burden, meaning a deficiency in the reward, nor that he should be burdened with humiliation, or a small reward, because no one’s right was withheld from him, nor was anyone burdened with injustice, because it is the right of the believer in the Qur’an to avoid that.
72:14: 14- And among us are Muslims, and among us are the unjust those who deviate from the path of truth, which is faith and obedience. And whoever submits - then those have sought the right path they have sought the great path that will lead them to the abode of reward.
72:15: 15- As for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hellfire. It will be kindled by them as it is kindled by the thoughts of mankind.
72:16: 16- And if they had been upright meaning that if the jinn or mankind or both had been upright. On the way meaning on the best way. We would have given them abundant water We would have provided them with abundant sustenance. The mention of abundant water, which is plentiful, is specific because it is the basis of livelihood and abundance and because of the scarcity of its existence among the Arabs.
72:17: 17- To test them therein To test how they will thank Him. It was said that its meaning is that if the jinn had adhered to their old way and did not submit to listening to the Qur’an, We would have provided them with abundant provision, luring them into temptation and punishing them for their disbelief. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord From His worship, His admonition, or His life. He will lead him He will make him enter. Other than the Kufians, he read it with the letter nun. A severe punishment Hard, rising above the one being punished and overpowering him, a source described with it.
72:18: 18- And that the mosques are for God are specific to Him. So do not invoke anyone with God so do not worship therein other than Him. Whoever makes that implied by the lam a reason for the prohibition has nullified the benefit. It was said that what is meant by the mosques is the whole earth because it was made a mosque for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that it is the Sacred Mosque because it was said that the mosques and the places of prostration are on the basis that what is meant is the prohibition of prostrating to other than God, and its seven arabs or prostrations on the basis that it is the plural of mosque.
72:19: 19- And that when Abdullah stood up meaning the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He was only mentioned with the word servant for humility, as it is the same as speaking about himself, and to indicate what is required for his standing up. calling upon Him worshipping Him. They almost the jinn almost. to be upon him in a crowd piling up from crowding around him in amazement at what they saw of his worship and heard of his recitation, or the people almost gathered around him to invalidate his command. It is the plural of labdah which is what is matted together like the mane of a lion. Ibn Amir said that labdan with a damma on the lam is the plural of labdah and it is a language. It is read labdan like sajdah the plural of labdhu labdan like sabr the plural of labood.
72:20: 20- Say, 'I only call upon my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with Him.' This is not an innovation or something reprehensible that would cause you to be amazed or to agree with my hatred. Asim and Hamza read Say as a command to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to agree with what came after it.
72:21: 21- “Say, ‘I do not possess for you any harm or benefit,’ nor any evil. He expressed one of them by its name and the other by the name of its cause or effect, to indicate both meanings.
72:22: 22- "Say, 'No one can protect me from God' if He intends harm for me. And I will find no refuge besides Him' a refuge or a shelter, and its root is the entrance to the grave.
72:23: 23- Except a message from God is an exception to His statement, I do not possess," for the message is guidance and benefit, and what is in between is an objection confirming the negation of ability, or from someone who is united, or its meaning is I do not convey, and what precedes it is evidence of the answer. "And His messages is in apposition to a message, and from God is its description, for its connection is from," like his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: "Convey from me, even if it is one verse. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger," in the command to monotheism, since the discussion is about it. "Then for him is the fire of Hell. And it was read, then on, then his recompense is that they will abide therein forever," combining the meaning.
72:24: 24- Until, when they see what they are promised in this world, such as the Battle of Badr, or in the Hereafter. The purpose is for His saying: They will be upon it in droves in the second meaning, or for an omitted word indicated by the state of the disbelievers' weakness and their disobedience to Him. Then they will know who is weaker in helpers and less in number - he or they.
72:25: 25- "Say, 'I do not know.' I do not know. 'Is that which you are promised near, or will my Lord set for it a term?'" It is as if when the polytheists heard until they see that which they are promised, they said, When will it be? in denial. It was said, Say, 'It will inevitably happen, but I do not know when it will be.'
72:26: 26- The Knower of the Unseen is the Knower of the Unseen. He does not reveal so He does not inform. about His Unseen to anyone meaning about the Unseen that is specifically His knowledge.
72:27: 27- "Except for he whom He approves" for knowledge of some of it so that it would be a miracle for him. "From a Messenger is an explanation of from", and it was used as evidence to invalidate miracles, and the answer to that is that the Messenger is limited to the kingdom and the manifestation of what happens without an intermediary, and the miracles of the saints over the unseen are only received from the angels like our knowledge of the conditions of the Hereafter through the intermediaries of the prophets. "Then He will send before him from before the one who is approved and behind him are watchers" guards of angels who guard him from the snatching of the devils and their mixing with them.
72:28: 28- That he may know that they have conveyed meaning that the prophet to whom revelation has been sent may know that Gabriel and the descending angels have conveyed the revelation, or that God Almighty may know that the prophets have conveyed the message, meaning that His knowledge may be attached to it as it exists. The messages of their Lord as they are protected from change. And He encompasses what they have what the messengers have. And He has taken account of everything in number even the rain and the sand. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Jinn will have a slave freed for every jinn who believed in Muhammad or denied him.
73:1: 1- O you who is wrapped in a blanket Its origin is Al-Mutazzammil from tamamul bi-thabaihi if he wraps himself in it, so the taa was assimilated into the zay and it was read with this, and with Al-Muzzammil with the open meem or closed meaning the one who was wrapped by someone else, or wrapped himself, the prophet peace be upon him was called by this name as a mockery of what he was like as he was sleeping, or trembling from what amazed him at the beginning of the revelation while wrapped in a blanket or to improve it as it was narrated: "That he peace be upon him was praying wrapped in a blanket spread on Aisha may God be pleased with her so it was revealed" Or likening him in his sluggishness to Al-Mutazzammil because he was not yet trained in praying at night or from tamamul az-Zamil if he carried the load meaning the one who carried the burdens of prophethood.

75:6: 6- He asks when the Day of Resurrection will be When will the Day of Resurrection be, excluding him or mocking him.
75:7: 7- So when the sight flashes he is startled by the lightning and his sight is dazzled. Nafi' read it with the fat-ha, which is a language, or from the sparkle meaning it flashed with the intensity of its flashing. It was read as balq from balq of the door if it opened.

And for the one who carries that as a sign of death, he can interpret the eclipse as the disappearance of the light of sight and the gathering as the consequence of the sensory spirit in the disappearance, or as its arrival to the one from whom the light of reason was taken from the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and the verb is masculine because of its advancement and the predominance of the conjoined.
75:10: 10- Man will say on that Day, ‘Where is the escape?’ That is, the escape is said by the comforting words of his desire for it. It is read with the kasra, which is the place.
75:11: 11- No is a deterrent from seeking escape. No burden is no refuge, borrowed from the word rope and derived from the word wazr which means weight.
75:12: 12- To your Lord, that Day, is the final destination. To Him alone is the final destination of the servants, or to His rule is the final destination of their affairs, or to His will is the place of their settlement. He admits whomever He wills into Paradise and whomever He wills into Hell.
75:13: 13- On that Day, man will be informed of what he sent forward and what he left behind. What he sent forward of deeds and what he left behind that he did not do, or what he sent forward of deeds and what he left behind of good or bad practices that he practiced after it, or what he sent forward of money that he gave in charity and what he left behind and succeeded to, or what he did at the beginning and end.
75:14: 14- Rather, man is a witness against himself. His proof is clear evidence of his actions because he witnessed them. He described him as having sight metaphorically, or a seeing eye, so he does not need to be informed.
75:15: 15- And if he presents his excuses Even if he comes with everything that he can apologize with, the plural of excuse is excuse, or the plural of excuse is not based on the standard of insight into it, so he does not need to be informed. And if he presents his excuses. And if he comes with everything that can be excused, he collects an excuse, which is an excuse, or collects an apology without analogy, like the reprehensible in the reprehensible, then his analogy is excuses, and that is more appropriate, and there is consideration in it.
75:16: 16-"Do not move O Muhammad your tongue with it the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to hasten it to take it quickly for fear that it will slip away from you.
75:17: 17- It is for Us to collect it in your chest and to recite it and to confirm its recitation on your tongue, which is your emphasis on the prohibition.
75:18: 18-So when We have recited it to you by the tongue of Gabriel, then follow its recitation its recitation and repeat it, explaining it in your mind.
75:19: 19- Then it is for Us to explain it. Explaining whatever is unclear to you of its meanings. It is evidence for the permissibility of delaying the explanation beyond the time of the address. It is an objection to emphasize the rebuke of the love of haste if it is reprehensible in what is the most important of matters and the foundation of the religion, so how is it in other matters? Or by mentioning what happened during the revelation of these verses. It was said that the address is to the man mentioned and the meaning is that he will be given his book and his tongue will falter from reading it quickly out of fear, so it will be said to him, "Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it, for it is for Us, by virtue of the promise, to collect what is in it of your deeds and read it. So when We read it, follow its reading with acknowledgment or contemplation of it. Then it is for Us to explain the command to him to be rewarded for it."
75:20: 20- No" is a deterrent to the Messenger from the habit of haste or to man from being deceived by the immediate. "Rather, you love the immediate."
75:21: 21- And you abandon the Hereafter is a generalization of the address, indicating that the children of Adam are naturally inclined to haste, even though the address is to humans, and what is meant by it is the species, so the pronoun is plural for the meaning, and this is supported by the reading of Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and the two Basrans with the letter ya in both of them.
75:22: 22- Some faces, that Day, will be radiant. Bright and cheerful.
75:23: 23- Looking to her Lord She sees Him absorbed in contemplating His beauty to the point that she neglects everything else. That is why the object was brought forward. This is not the case in all cases, so that her looking to something else contradicts it. It was said: Waiting for His favor. It was responded that waiting is not attributed to the face, and its interpretation in the sentence is contrary to what appears, and that what is used in its meaning is not transitive with to. And the poet said: If I look at you from the king and the sea without you, you increase my blessings In the sense of asking, waiting does not entail giving. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 32 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Qiyāmah, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Takwīr. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 75:24: 24- And faces that Day will be gloomy Very frowning. Al-Basel is more eloquent than Al-Baser, but it is used predominantly for a brave person if he is very intense and gloomy.

75:27: 27- And it was said that he who performs incantation said the one present and the one who performs incantation over him from what he has from incantation, or he said the angels of death, which of you will perform incantation over his soul, the angels of mercy, or the angels of torment from incantation.

75:31: 31- There is no truth in what must be believed, or there is no truth in his money, meaning there is no zakat. And he did not pray, what was imposed on him, and the pronoun in both of them refers to the human being mentioned in Does man think?

75:34: 34- It is more appropriate for you, then more appropriate. Woe to you from the guardian. Its original form is May God give you what you hate. The lam is an extra letter, as in He has given you or It is more appropriate for you to perish. It is said that the root of the word wail after al-qalb is closer than adun, or fa`la from al is interpreted as meaning your end is the Fire.
75:35: 35- Then it is better for you, and better for you meaning that this is repeated to him time after time.

This includes a repetition of his denial of the resurrection and an indication of it, in that wisdom requires commanding good deeds and forbidding bad deeds, and duties are not achieved except through reward, which may not be in this world, but rather in the hereafter.
75:37: 37- Was he not a drop of ejaculated semen?
75:38: 38- Then he was a clot, then He created and proportioned him. Then He proportioned him and balanced him.
75:39: 39- And He made from it the two pairs for the two classes the male and the female and this is another proof of the beginning of the repetition as was previously stated repeatedly and therefore He based on it His saying:
75:40: 40- Is He not able to bring the dead to life? On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, When he recited it, he would say, ‘Glory be to You! Yes indeed!’ And on his authority, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Qiyamah, Gabriel and I will bear witness for him on the Day of Resurrection that he was a believer in him.
76:1: 1- Has there come upon man a period of time? is a question of confirmation and approximation, and therefore it was interpreted as qad and its root is ahl like his saying: People saw us at the foot of the valley of the hills A time of time is a limited segment of the unlimited extended time. It was not a thing mentioned rather it was something forgotten and not mentioned in humanity like the element or the sperm, and the sentence is a state of the human being or a description of a time by deleting the referent and what is meant by the human being is the species, as He said:
76:2: 2- Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop or Adam first explained his creation then mentioned the creation of his sons. Mixtures are mixtures, plural of mix or mix or mixture from mix something if you mix it, and the plural of sperm is because what is meant by it is the sum of the semen of the man and the woman, and each of them has different parts in delicacy and texture properties, and therefore each part of them becomes the substance of an organ. It was said to be singular like tenths and rams. It was said to be colors, because the man's semen is white and the woman's semen is yellow, so when they differ it becomes green, or stages, because the sperm becomes a clot then a lump of flesh until the creation is complete. We test him is in the place of the state, meaning testing him, meaning wanting to test him or transferring him from one state to another, so the test was used metaphorically for it. So We made him hearing and seeing so that he could observe the evidence and verses, so he is like the one caused by the test, and therefore the verb that it restricts is connected with the letter fa and the statement is based on it:
76:3: 3- Indeed, We guided him to the way meaning by setting up proofs and sending down verses. Either grateful or ungrateful are two states of the ha'. Either is for detail or division, meaning We guided him in both of his states or divided into them, some of them grateful by being guided and taking it, and some of them ungrateful by turning away from it, or from the way and describing him with gratitude and ungratefulness is a metaphor. Ama was read with the fat-ha, deleting the answer, and perhaps he did not say ungrateful to match its counterpart, to preserve the pauses, and to indicate that man is not free from ungratefulness in most cases, but rather the one who is held accountable for it is the one who delves into it.
76:4: 4- Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains with which they will be led, and shackles with which they will be bound, and a Blaze with which they will be burned. The threat is presented before their mention, and their mention was delayed because the warning is more important and beneficial, and starting and ending the speech with a mention of the believers is better. Nafi’, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Bakr read chains for the appropriateness.
76:5: 5- The righteous is the plural of barr like arbab or bar like ashhad. They will drink from a cup of wine, which is originally the cup in which it is kept. Its mixture is what it is mixed with, camphor because of its coolness, sweetness, and pleasant fragrance. It is said that it is the name of water in Paradise that resembles camphor in its scent and whiteness. It is said that the qualities of camphor are created in it, so it is as if mixed with it.
76:6: 6- Ainan instead of Kafur if it is made into water or from the place of Min Kas on the assumption of an addition, meaning water or its wine or accusative of specificity or by a verb explained by what follows it. The servants of God drink from it meaning enjoying it or mixed with it. It was said that the ba is an addition or in the meaning of from because drinking is initiated from it as it is. They make it gush forth they make it flow wherever they want with easy flow.
76:7: 7- They fulfill their vows is a resumption of the statement of what they were provided for, as if he was asked about it and was answered with that, and it is more expressive in describing them as being diligent in fulfilling their duties, because whoever fulfills what he has obligated upon himself for the sake of God the Most High, will be more fulfilling of what God the Most High has obligated upon him. And they fear a Day whose evil is its hardships. Wildly spreading is widespread, extremely widespread, like the spreading of fire and dawn, and it is more expressive than flew, and it indicates the goodness of their belief and their avoidance of sins.
76:8: 8- And they feed the poor, the orphan, and the captive, in spite of their love for Him. The love of God Almighty, or food, or feeding. The poor, the orphan, and the captive, meaning the captives of the infidels. "For the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would bring the captive, and he would hand him over to some of the Muslims, and he would say, 'Be kind to him.'" Or the believing captive, which includes the slave and the prisoner. In the hadith, Your debtor is a captive, so be kind to your captive.
76:9: 9- "We feed you only for the sake of God" is intended to be said with the intention of action or speech, to remove the illusion of favor and the expectation of a reward that diminishes the reward. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: She used to send charity to a household and then ask the one sent to her what they said. If he mentioned a supplication, she would supplicate for them with the same one so that the reward of the charity would remain purely for her with God. "We do not want from you any reward or thanks" meaning thanks.
76:10: 10-Indeed, we fear our Lord, so we treat you well or do not ask for a reward from you. A Day is a day of torment. Frowning is a day in which faces frown or resemble a frowning lion in its ferocity. Qamtarir is someone who frowns intensely like someone who gathers what is between his eyes from the word aqmatar, meaning the she-camel raises her tail and gathers her earrings, or it is derived from qatar and the mim is an additional word.
76:11: 11- So God saved them from the evil of that Day because of their fear and caution against it. And He met them with radiance and joy instead of the frowning and sadness of the wicked.
76:12: 12- "And He rewarded them for what they patiently endured" for their patience in fulfilling obligations, avoiding forbidden things, and giving up wealth. "A garden" a garden from which they eat. "And silk" they wear. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain, may God be pleased with them both, fell ill, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited them with some people. They said: O Abu Al-Hasan, if you make a vow on behalf of your two sons, so Ali and Fatima, may God be pleased with them both, and a silver slave girl of theirs vowed to fast for three days if they recovered. They recovered and they had nothing with them, so Ali borrowed three sa’s of barley from Sham’un Al-Khaibari, so Fatima ground a sa’ and baked five loaves of bread, and they placed them in front of them to break their fast. A poor man stopped by them, and they preferred him. They spent the night without tasting anything but water, and in the morning they fasted. When they reached the evening and set the food aside, an orphan stopped by them, and they preferred him. Then a prisoner stopped by them the third time, and they did the same. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down with this surah and said: Take it, O Muhammad. May God be with your family.
76:13: 13- "Reclining therein on couches is a state of those who are in their reward or an attribute of Paradise". "They will see therein neither sun nor freezing cold is possible, and it is a state of what is implied in reclining", and the meaning is that a moderate breeze passes over them therein, neither hot nor harmfully cold. It was said that freezing cold is the moon in the language of Tayy. Their rajaz poet said: And the night is dark, and the cold has not yet blossomed Meaning that its air itself does not need a sun or moon.
76:14: 14- And its shades will be within easy reach for them is a state or another description in apposition to what precedes it, or in apposition to Paradise, meaning a garden within easy reach, as they were promised two gardens, like His statement: And for him who fears standing before his Lord are two gardens. It was read in the nominative case as the predicate of its shades, and the sentence is a state or description. And its fruits will be made easy to reach is in apposition to what precedes it, or a state of within easy reach, and making the fruits within easy reach means that they are made easy to reach, not forbidden to pick as they wish.
76:15: 15- And there will be passed around among them vessels of silver and cups and pitchers without handles. They were glass.
76:16: 16- Qawarir min silver meaning it was formed combining the clarity and transparency of a bottle with the whiteness and softness of silver. The nun of Qawarir was taken from the nun of Salasilan and Ibn Kathir said the first because it is the beginning of the verse. The reading of Qawarir min silver is as Qawarir. They estimated it by an estimate meaning they estimated it in themselves so its measurements and shapes came out as they wished, or they estimated it by their good deeds so it came out according to them, or the circumambulators estimated it, referred to by His statement, its drink will be circulated according to the amount of their desires. 76:17: 17- And they will be given to drink there a cup whose mixture is of ginger. It tastes like ginger, and the Arabs used to enjoy a drink mixed with it.
76:18: 18- "A spring in it called Salsabil" because of its smooth flow into the truth and its ease of swallowing. It is said that it is a drink of Salsal, Salsal, and Salsabil. 76:19: 19- And there will circulate among them immortal youths. “When you see them, you will think them to be scattered pearls.” From the purity of their colors, their dispersion in their gatherings, and the reflection of their rays on one another.
76:20: 20- And if you saw then has no explicit or implied object because it is general and means that wherever your sight falls, you will see bliss and a great kingdom vast. In the hadith, The lowest in status in Paradise will look at his kingdom for a thousand years' journey, seeing its farthest point as he sees its lowest point. This is greater than that for the knower, which is that his soul will be engraved with the manifestations of the kingdom and the hidden aspects of the kingdom, so he will be illuminated by the lights of the holiness of the Almighty.
76:21: 21- Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. Upon them will be green silk garments, both fine and coarse. The accusative case is in the state of those who are above them or sufficient for them or kingdom based on the estimation of an added word, meaning and people of a great kingdom above them. Nafi' read upon them Hamzah in the nominative case as the predicate of garments. Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr read Khader in the genitive case based on sands in the sense that it is a generic noun, and and heavy brocade in the nominative case as an apposition to garments. Hafs, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read them in the nominative case. And brocade was read with the hamza connected and the fatha on the basis that it is an istaf'ala from brilliance and was made a name for this type of garment. And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver is in apposition to and will circulate among them. His statement bracelets of gold does not contradict this, as it is possible to combine, punish, or separate them. The adornments of the people of Paradise will differ according to their deeds, so perhaps God Almighty will bestow upon them, as a reward for what they have done with their hands, adornments and lights of varying degrees of gold and silver. Or it is a state of the pronoun in above them by implying may. Based on this, it is possible that this refers to the servants and that to those who are served. And their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink, meaning by it another type that is superior to the two types mentioned above. That is why He attributed its giving to God Almighty, and described it as pure, as it purifies its drinker from inclination toward sensual pleasures and from inclining toward anything other than the Truth. So he devotes himself to contemplating His beauty, enjoying meeting Him, remaining with His remaining. It is the highest degree of the truthful, and that is why He concluded the reward of the righteous with it.
76:22: 22- This was indeed a reward for you with the implication of the statement and the reference to what was counted as their reward and your effort was appreciated rewarded for it and not wasted.
76:23: 23- Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur’an to you gradually in parts, for a reason that required it, and the repetition of the pronoun with an is an addition to the specificity of the revelation to it.
76:24: 24- So be patient over the decision of your Lord by delaying your victory over the disbelievers of Mecca and others and do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate meaning anyone who commits the sin that calls you to it or anyone who is extreme in disbelief that calls you to it. If the prohibition is based on the two descriptions, it indicates that it is for them, and that requires obedience to be in sin and disbelief, because obeying them in what is not sin or disbelief is not prohibited.
76:25: 25- And remember the name of your Lord in the morning and the evening. And be persistent in remembering Him, or be persistent in praying the dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers, for the evening includes their times.

Perhaps what is meant by it is the sunset and evening prayers, and the context is brought forward because of the additional effort and sincerity involved in the night prayer. And glorify Him for a long time during the night. And perform the night prayers for a long time during the night.
76:27: 27- Indeed, these people love the immediate and leave behind them in front of them or behind their backs. A heavy day is borrowed from the heavy burden of the one carrying it, and it is like an explanation for what he commanded and forbade.
76:28: 28- We created them and strengthened their bonds and made their joints tightly connected with nerves. And if We will, We can replace them with others like them with a complete replacement and if We will, We can destroy them and We can replace them with others like them with a complete replacement in creation, and the strength of the bond means the second creation, and for this reason if was brought or We can replace them with others like them who obey and if to realize the ability and strength of the caller.
76:29: 29- Indeed, this is a reminder referring to the Surah or the verses nearby, so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way drawing closer to Him through obedience.
76:30: 30- And you do not will except that God wills. You do not will that except when God wills your will. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read yashu'un with a ya. Indeed, God is All-Knowing of what each person deserves. Wise He wills only what His wisdom requires.
76:31: 31- He admits whom He wills into His mercy with guidance and success in obedience. And for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment is in the accusative case. The wrongdoers is a verb that explains He has prepared for them like He threatened and He rewarded to match the conjoined clause. It is read in the nominative case as a start. These are the attributes of the angels of death, for they extract the souls of the unbelievers from their bodies by drowning, that is, by drowning in the death, for they extract them from the furthest reaches of the bodies, or souls that have been drowned in the bodies, and they are animated, that is, they extract the souls of the believers gently, as a bucket is animated from a well when it is drawn out, and they swim in extracting them as a diver swims when he extracts something from the depths of the sea, so they race with the souls of the unbelievers to the Fire and with the souls of the believers to Paradise, and they manage the matter of its punishment and reward by preparing it to attain what has been prepared for it of pains and pleasures, or the first two are for them and the remaining ones are for groups of angels who swim in its passage, that is, they hasten in it and they race to what they are commanded to do and they manage its matter, or the attributes of the stars, for they are drawn from the east to the west by drowning in the death, by cutting the celestial sphere until it descends in the farthest west, and they are animated from one constellation to another, that is, they emerge from the vigour of the bull when it emerges from one country to another, and they swim in the celestial sphere, and some of them precede in movement because they move faster, so they manage a matter assigned to them. Like the difference of seasons and the estimation of times and the appearance of the times of worship, and since their movements from east to west are forced and their movements from one sign to another are appropriate, He called the first a withdrawal and the second an activity. Or the qualities of the virtuous souls in the state of separation, for they are withdrawn from the bodies by drowning, that is, by a strong withdrawal from the drowning of the withdrawer in the bow, and they are active towards the world of the kingdom and swim in it, so they race to the enclosures of holiness and become, due to their honor and strength, among the managers. Or in the state of their behavior, for they are withdrawn from desires and are active towards the world of holiness, so they swim in the ranks of ascension and race to perfections until they become among the complete ones. Or the qualities of the souls of the invaders, or their hands withdraw the bows by drowning the arrows and they are active with the arrow for shooting and they swim on land and sea and race to the war of the enemy and manage its affairs. Or the qualities of their horses, for they are withdrawn in their reins by a withdrawal in which the reins are drowned due to the length of their necks and they go out from the abode of Islam to the abode of disbelief, and they swim in their war and race to the enemy and manage its affairs. 79:23: 23- So he gathered the magicians or his soldiers. So he called in the assembly himself or through a crier.
79:24: 24- He said, 'I am your highest lord.' The highest of all those who are in charge of your affairs.
79:25: 25- So God seized him with the punishment of the Hereafter and the first as a punishment for whoever saw him or heard him in the Hereafter by burning and in this world by drowning, or according to his word the Hereafter which is this and his first word which is his saying: I have not known for you any god other than Me or as a punishment in both of them, or for them and it is possible that it is a confirmed source estimated by his action.
79:26: 26- Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears because it was his nature to fear.
79:27: 27- Are you more difficult to create? More difficult to create. Or the heaven? Then he explained how he created it, saying: He constructed it. Then he explained the construction, saying:
79:28: 28- He raised its thickness meaning he made its height from the ground or its thickness so that it goes up high, thin. 79:29: 29- And He covered its night means He covered it with darkness. It is derived from the word ghashāsh which means it became dark. He only added it to it because it causes its movement. 79:30: 30- And the earth after that He spread out He extended it and prepared it for habitation.
79:31: 31- He brought forth from it its water by bursting the springs and its pasture and its grazing, which is originally for the place of grazing, and the sentence is stripped of the conjunction because it is a state by implying qad or an explanation of the rolling.
79:32: 32- And the mountains He has fixed firmly. He established them. It was read and the earth and the mountains in the nominative case as the subject, and it is returned because the conjunction is based on a verbal noun.
79:33: 33- For your enjoyment and for your livestock For your enjoyment and for your livestock.
79:34: 34- "And when the Calamity comes" the catastrophe that is overwhelming, that is, greater than all other calamities. "The Greatest" which is the greatest of all calamities, which is the Resurrection, or the second Trumpet blast, or the hour in which the people of Paradise will be led to Paradise and the people of Hell to Hell.
79:35: 35- The Day when man will remember what he strove for by seeing it recorded in his record, even though he had forgotten it due to excessive heedlessness or a long period of time. It is a substitute for So when it comes and what is a relative pronoun or a verbal noun.
79:36: 36- And Hell will appear and be made manifest. For whoever sees is for every seer, such that it will not be hidden from anyone. It was read And will appear and For whoever sees, as if it contains the pronoun for Hell, like the Most High's statement: When it sees them from a distant place, or that it is addressing the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning to whoever you see from the disbelievers. The answer to When it comes is omitted, indicated by The Day he remembers or what follows it of preference.
79:37: 37- But as for he who transgressed until he disbelieved.
79:38: 38- And he preferred the life of this world so he was preoccupied with it and did not prepare for the afterlife through worship and self-discipline.
79:39: 39- Then Hellfire will be his refuge. It is his refuge, and the lam in it is a substitute for the addition, because it is known that the owner of the refuge is the tyrant, and it is a chapter or a subject. But as for he who feared the position of his Lord, his position before his Lord, because of his knowledge of the beginning and the end.
79:40: 40- And he forbade the soul from desire because he knew that he would be afflicted.
79:41: 41- For Paradise is his refuge.
