79:43: 43- What is it to you regarding its remembrance? What is it to you regarding mentioning its time to them? That is, what is it to you regarding mentioning it to them, and clarifying its time in any way, because mentioning it only increases their error. And its time is something that God the Most High has kept to Himself in His knowledge. And it was said that what is it is a denial of their question and you regarding its remembrance is a new sentence, and its meaning is that you are a mention of its mention, that is, a sign of its portents, because his being sent as the Seal of the Prophets is a sign of its portents. And it was said that it is connected to their question and the answer.
79:44: 44- To your Lord is its destination meaning the destination of its knowledge.
79:45: 45- You are only a warner of those who fear it. You were only sent to warn those who fear its terror, and it is not appropriate to specify the time and the one who fears because he is the one who benefits from it. And on the authority of Abu Amr and Mundhir with the tanween and the work on the original because it means the state.
79:46: 46- It will be as if, on the Day they see it, they had not remained in this world or in the graves. Except for an evening or its morning. That is, the evening of a day or its morning, as in His saying, Except for an hour of a day. That is why He added the morning to the evening because they are from one day. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat An-Nazi’at will be among those whom God will consider worthy of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection, equal to the amount of an obligatory prayer.
80:2: 2- If the blind man came to him It was narrated that Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and there were the leaders of Quraysh calling them to Islam. He said: O Messenger of God, teach me from what God has taught you, and he repeated that and he did not know that he was busy with the people, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not like him interrupting his speech, so he frowned and turned away from him, so this verse was revealed. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to honor him and say when he saw him: Welcome to the one about whom my Lord rebuked me, and whom He appointed as His successor over Medina twice. It was read with emphasis for emphasis, and if he came to him is the reason for turned away, or frowned according to the two schools of thought. It was read with two hamzas and an alif between them, meaning that if the blind man came to him, he would do that. The blind man was mentioned to indicate his excuse for rushing to interrupt the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) speaking to the people and to indicate that he deserved compassion and kindness, or to increase the denial, as if he said: He turned away because he was blind, like the turning around in His saying:
80:3: 3- "And what do you know? Perhaps he will be purified." That is, something that makes you aware of his condition, perhaps he will be purified from sins by what he receives from you. This indicates that his turning away was to purify someone else.
80:4: 4- Or he remembers and the reminder benefits him or he is admonished and your admonition benefits him. It was said that the pronoun in perhaps refers to the disbeliever, meaning that you hoped to be purified by Islam and reminded of the admonition, and for that reason you turned away from others. How do you know that what you hoped for will come to pass? Asim read so that it will benefit him in the accusative case as an answer to perhaps.
80:5: 5- But as for him who is self-sufficient.
80:6: 6-So you confront it means you approach it by turning towards it. Its root is tatasaddadi. Ibn Kathir and Nafi' read tasaaddadi with assimilation. It was also read tasaaddadi, meaning you expose yourself and are invited to confront it.
80:7: 7- "And there is nothing wrong with you if he does not purify himself with Islam, until your eagerness for him to become a Muslim leads you to turn away from someone who has become a Muslim. "Your only duty is to convey the message."
80:8: 8- And as for he who comes to you striving he hastens seeking good.
80:9: 9- And he fears God or the harm of the infidels in coming to you, or the stumble on the road because he is blind and has no guide.
80:10: 10- So you are distracted from him you are preoccupied, it is said to her that she is distracted from him and is distracted, and perhaps the mention of giving charity and being distracted is to indicate that the reproach is for his heart being preoccupied with the rich and being distracted from the poor, and someone like him should not do that.
80:11: 11- No" is a deterrent against the one being reprimanded or against repeating the same thing. "It is a reminder."
80:12: 12- Whoever wishes to remember it will memorize it or take heed from it. The two pronouns refer to the Qur’an, or the mentioned reproach. The first is feminine because its predicate is feminine.
80:13: 13- In the pages in which there is an established description of a reminder, or a second piece of report, or report of something omitted. An honor with God.
80:14: 14- Exalted in power. Purified and free from the hands of the devils.
80:15: 15- In the hands of scribes are scribes from the angels or prophets who copy books from the tablet or revelation, or ambassadors who travel with the revelation between God Almighty and His messengers, or the nation is the plural of traveler from travel, or embassy and the construction of revealing, it is said that a woman traveled if she revealed her face.
80:16: 16- Generous are dear to God or compassionate towards the believers, speaking to them and asking forgiveness for them. Pious are pious.
80:17: 17- How ungrateful man is! Kill him! This is a supplication against him with the most heinous supplications and an expression of astonishment at his extreme ungratefulness. Despite its brevity, it indicates great anger and severe condemnation.
80:18: 18- From what thing did He create it? This is a statement of what He bestowed upon it, especially the beginning of its occurrence. The question is for disparagement, and so He answered it by saying:
80:19: 19- From a sperm-drop He created him and proportioned him. He prepared him for the appropriate limbs and forms, or proportioned him in stages until his creation was complete.
80:20: 20- Then the way is made easy for him. Then He made his exit from his mother’s womb easy by opening the opening of the womb and inspiring him to repent, or He made the way of good and evil easy for him. He made the way easy with a verb that is explained by the apparent meaning to exaggerate the facilitation, and defining it with the lam without the addition to indicate that it is a general way, and in it, in the last meaning, is an indication that the world is a way and the destination is other than it, and therefore He followed it with His saying:
80:21: 21- Then He caused him to die and buried him.
80:22: 22- Then if He wills, He will resurrect him. He promised death and burial in the blessings because death is a connection in general to eternal life and pure pleasures, and the command to be buried is an honor and protection from wild beasts. In if He wills, there is a notification that the time of resurrection is not specific in itself, but rather it is entrusted to His will, the Most High.
80:23: 23- No is a deterrent to man regarding his condition. He has not yet fulfilled what he was commanded. Up to this point, Adam had not fulfilled what God commanded him to do, as no one is free from some shortcoming.
80:24: 24- Let man look at his food following the intrinsic blessings with the external blessings.
80:25: 25- We poured the water out in torrents is a resumption explaining how the food was created. The Kufians read it with the fat-ha as a substitute for it, a substitute for inclusion.
80:26: 26- Then We split the earth open meaning with plants or vines. The splitting is attributed to the split itself as the action is attributed to the cause.
80:27: 27- Then We caused to grow therein grain such as wheat and barley.
80:28: 28- And grapes and reeds meaning fresh dates. It is named after the root word qadbah which means to cut it because it is cut again and again.
80:30: 30- And gardens of great abundance is a description of gardens due to their density and the abundance of their trees, or because they have thick trees borrowed from the description of necks.
80:31: 31- Fruit and pasture and pasture from ab if it is mother because it is used for grazing and pasture, or from ab for something if it is prepared for it because it is prepared for grazing, or dry fruit that returns for the winter.
80:32: 32- For your enjoyment and for your livestock. Some of the mentioned types are food and some are fodder.
80:33: 33- So when the Deafening Blast comes meaning the blast, it was described as such metaphorically because people listen to it.
80:34: 34- The Day when a man will flee from his brother.
80:35: 35- And his mother and his father.
80:36: 36- And his wife and his children because he was preoccupied with his own affairs and knew that they would not benefit him, or to be wary of demanding from them what he had neglected to do to them and delaying the most beloved, then the most beloved, for the sake of exaggeration, as if it was said: He flees from his brother, rather from his parents, rather from his wife and his children.
80:37: 37- Every man among them, that Day, will have enough to concern him. It is sufficient for him to care about it. It was read to concern him, meaning it concerns him.
80:38: 38- Some faces, that Day, will be radiant shining from the light of dawn.
80:39: 39- Laughing and cheerful at what she sees of bliss.
80:40: 40- And faces that Day will be covered with dust. Dust and gloom.
80:41: 41-A period of time exhausts her and she is covered by blackness and darkness.
80:42: 42- Those are the disbelieving immoral people who combined disbelief with immorality, and therefore dust was added to the blackness of their faces. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 33 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Takwīr, and the first verses of Sūrat l-Shams. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 82:2: 2-And when the stars are scattered they fall in separate places.

82:4: 4-"And when the graves are scattered" their soil is turned upside down and their dead are brought out. It is said that it is composed of "ba'ath and ba'athir like Bismillah" in wording and meaning.
82:5: 5- A soul will know what it has put forward of work or charity. And what it has delayed of bad deeds or left behind. It is possible that what is meant by delay is wasting, and this is the answer to if.
82:6: 6- O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? That is, what has deceived you and made you dare to disobey Him? The mention of the Generous is to exaggerate the prohibition against being deceived, for pure generosity does not necessitate neglecting the oppressor and treating the loyalist and the hostile, the obedient and the disobedient equally. So how would it be if the attribute of coercion and revenge were added to it, indicating what Satan is deceiving him with? He would say to him, Do whatever you wish, for your Lord is Generous, He does not punish anyone, nor does He hasten to punish. The indication is that the abundance of His generosity calls for seriousness in obeying Him, not immersion in disobeying Him out of deceit at His generosity.
82:7: 7- Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you. This is a second attribute of Lordship, explaining generosity and pointing out that whoever was able to do that first is able to do it a second time. Proportioning means making the limbs sound, proportionate, and prepared for their benefits. Modification means making the structure proportionate, with the limbs proportionate, or proportionate with what powers make it happy. The Kufians read fa-adlaka with a light m meaning He made some of your limbs proportionate with others until you were balanced, or He turned you away from His creation other than you and distinguished you with a creation that differed from the creation of all other animals.
82:8: 8- In whatever form He willed, He assembled you. That is, He assembled you in whatever form He willed. Ma is an additional word, and it was said that it is conditional. Rakabak is its answer, and the adverbial phrase is the relative clause of Your justice. The sentence was not connected to what preceded it because it is a statement of Your justice.
82:9: 9- No is a deterrent against being deceived by God's generosity. His statement, Rather, you deny the Recompense is a diversion to explain what is the original cause of their deception. What is meant by the Recompense is the reward or Islam.
82:12: 12- They know what you do is a confirmation of what they lie about and a response to what they expect of tolerance and neglect, and the scribes are glorified by being honored by God to magnify the reward.
82:13: 13- Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss.
82:14: 14- And indeed, the wicked will be in Hellfire. An explanation of what they are being written for.
82:15: 15- They will reach it and suffer its heat. On the Day of Judgment.
82:16: 16- And they will not be absent from it because they will remain in it forever. It was said that its meaning is that they will not be absent from it before that, as they would find its poisons in the graves.

88:1: 1- Has there come to you the report of the overwhelming event? The disaster that will overwhelm people with its hardships, meaning the Day of Resurrection, or the Fire, as God Almighty says, And the Fire will cover their faces.
88:2: 2- Some faces, that Day, will be humbled.
88:3: 3- A working, exhausted woman does what tires her out, such as dragging chains and wading through fire as camels wade through mud, and climbing and descending its hills and valleys. She did what she did, and she was exhausted in tasks that will not benefit her on that day.
88:4: 4- "You will be burned with a fire" means you will enter it. Abu Amr, Yaqub, and Abu Bakr read it as "you will be burned with a fire from God burned him", and it was read with emphasis for emphasis. "Hot" extremely hot.
88:5: 5- She is given to drink from a spring that reached its peak in the heat.
88:7: 7- It neither fattens nor satisfies hunger. What is meant by food is one of two things.
88:8: 8- On that Day, faces will be radiant cheerful or pampered.
88:9: 9- She was satisfied with her efforts. She was satisfied with her work when she saw its reward.
88:10: 10-In a high paradise high place or status.
88:11: 11- Do not listen O you who are being addressed or the faces, and Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ruways read it in the passive form with the letter Ya and Nafi' with the letter Ta. In it is idle talk idle talk or a word with idle talk or a soul that is idle, for the speech of the people of Paradise is remembrance and wisdom.
88:12: 12- There is a flowing spring in it Its water flows and does not stop. The indefinite article is for emphasis.
88:13: 13- Therein are raised couches of high thickness or capacity.
88:14: 14- And cups is the plural of cup, which is a vessel without a handle, placed in their hands.
88:15: 15- And cushions are pillows, plural of namariqah with fat-ha and damma, arranged one next to the other.
88:16: 16- Zarabi luxurious rugs, plural of Zariba "Mabthatha" spread out.
88:17: 17- Do they not then look with contemplation at the camels - how they are created a creation indicating the perfection of His power and the goodness of His management, as He created them to pull heavy loads to distant lands, then made them large, stable for the place, able to carry the load, obedient to those who lead them, long necks so that they cannot bear the loads, grazing on all plants and enduring thirst for ten days or more so that they can cross the deserts and wildernesses, along with other benefits. Therefore, they were specifically mentioned to explain the signs spread in animals, which are the most noble of vehicles and the most well-crafted, and because they are the most amazing of this type among the Arabs. It was said that what is meant by them is the clouds, as a metaphor.
88:18: 18- And to the sky, how it was raised without pillars.
88:19: 19- And to the mountains, how they are erected. They are firmly rooted and do not sway.
88:20: 20- And to the mountains, how they were spread out until they became cradles. The four verbs were read in the active form for the speaker and the accusative referent was deleted. The meaning is Do they not look at the types of creation, from simple and compound things, to realize the perfection of the power of the Creator, glory be to Him, so that they do not deny His ability to resurrect. Therefore, He followed it with the command of the return and arranged the command to remind upon it, saying:
88:21: 21- So remind, for you are only a reminder. So do not worry if they do not look or remind, for your only duty is to convey.
88:22: 22- I have no control over them with mustaṭalit and from Al-Kisa’i with sin according to the original and Hamza with ishmaan.
88:23: 23-Except for he who turns away and disbelieves. But he who turns away and disbelieves.
88:24: 24- Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment meaning the punishment of the Hereafter. It was said that it is connected, because jihad and killing the disbelievers is a form of domination, and it is as if He promised them jihad in this world and the punishment of Hellfire in the Hereafter. It was said that it is an exception to His statement, Then he will remember, meaning, he will remember, except for he who turns away and persists, so he deserves the greatest punishment. What is between them is an objection. The first is supported by the fact that it was read, Except for he who turns away, as a warning.
88:25: 25- "Indeed, to Us is their return" is their return. It was read with emphasis, as if it were fa'ilal, a source of fa'il from i'yaab, or fa'al from awba. The first waw was changed, then the second for assimilation.
88:26: 26- Then it is up to Us to bring them to account at the gathering place. The report is presented for specification and exaggeration in the threat. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Ghashiya, God will hold him to an easy account.
89:1: 1- And the dawn He swore by the dawn or its break, as in his saying: And the dawn when it breathes or by his prayer.
89:2: 2- And ten nights are the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. Therefore, the dawn was interpreted as the dawn of Arafah, or the day of sacrifice, or the last ten days of Ramadan. The indefinite form is used for emphasis. It was read and ten nights in addition to the fact that what is meant by the ten days.
89:3: 3- And the even and the odd and all things are even and odd, or creation, as He said: And of everything We created pairs and the Creator because He is individual, and whoever interprets them as the elements and the spheres or the zodiac and the planets or the even and odd prayers, or the two days of sacrifice and Arafah, and it has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, or with something else, then perhaps he mentioned separately from the types of meaning what he saw as most clearly indicating monotheism, or an introduction to the religion or a connection to what came before them or more beneficial and requiring gratitude, and and the odd was read with a kasra on the waw, and they are two languages like ink and ink.
89:4: 4- And the night when it departs when it passes, like his saying: And the night when it departs and the restriction to that is because of what is in the succession of the strength of the indication of the perfection of power and the abundance of blessing, or he sees in it from their saying he prayed the place and deleted the ya' to suffice with the kasra for the sake of alleviation, and Nafi' and Abu Amr specified it for the pause to take into account the pauses and Ibn Kathir and Ya'qub did not delete it at all, and Yusra was read with the tanween that was replaced by the letter of generalization.
89:5: 5- Is there in that the oath or the thing sworn by an oath or the thing sworn by. For one with reason he considers it and confirms with it what he wants to achieve, and the reason stone is called thus because it prevents from what is not appropriate, just as it is called reason, prohibition, and pebble from statistics, which is control, and the thing sworn by is omitted, which is that he will punish, indicated by his saying:
89:6: 6- Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the 'Aad? meaning the sons of 'Aad, son of 'Aws, son of Iram, son of Sam, son of Noah, peace be upon him. The people of Hud were named after their father, just as the Banu Hashim were named after him.
89:7: 7- Iram is an apposition to Aad with the assumption of an added word, meaning the tribe of Iram, or the people of Iram if it is true that it is the name of their town. It is said that their first ones, who are Aad the First, were named after their grandfather, and it was prevented from being declined due to being a proper noun and feminine. That of the Pillars is the one with the high build or tall stature, or dignity and steadfastness. It is said that "Aad had two sons, Shaddad and Shadid, and they fought and conquered, then Shadid died and the matter was given to Shaddad, and he ruled the inhabited world and its kings submitted to him. He heard about Paradise, so he built a paradise like it in some of the deserts of Aden and named it Iram. When it was completed, he marched to it with his family, but when he was a day and a night's journey from it, God sent a shout from the sky upon them and they perished. It was narrated from Abdullah bin Qilabah that he went out in search of his god and came upon it.
89:8: 8- "The like of which has not been created in the land is another description of Iram and the pronoun refers to it whether you make Iram" the tribe or the town.
89:9: 9- And Thamud who hewed out the rock they cut it and made it into homes, as He said: And you carved out of the mountains, houses “in the valley” Wadi al-Qura.
89:10: 10- And Pharaoh of the stakes because of the large number of his soldiers and the stakes they used to strike when they came down, or because of his torture with the stakes.
89:11: 11- Those who transgressed in the land is an attribute of the aforementioned Aad, Thamud, and Pharaoh, or a condemnation in the accusative or nominative case.
89:12: 12- And they increased corruption therein through disbelief and injustice.
89:13: 13- So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment - what He mixed for them of various types of punishment. Its origin is mixing, and the braided skin with which they are struck is called that because its energies are mixed together. It was said that what was brought upon them in this world was likened to a scourge to indicate that it is the comparison to what is prepared for them in the Hereafter of punishment, like the whip when compared to the sword.
89:14: 14- Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful refers to the place where He watches for surveillance. The verb mif`al comes from raṣadahu like miqāt from miqāt, and it is a metaphor for His surveillance of the disobedient with punishment.
89:15: 15- As for man is connected to his saying: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful as if it was said that he is ever watchful of the Hereafter, so he only wants to strive for it. As for man, he is only concerned with this world and its pleasures. When his Lord tests him tests him with wealth and ease then honors him and bestows favors with prestige and money. He says, 'My Lord has honored me' favored me with what He has given me, and it is the predicate of the subject, which is man. The fa is because of the meaning of the condition in amma, and the intermediate adverbial phrase in estimating the delay, as if it was said: As for man, he says, My Lord has honored me at the time of his test with favors. And likewise his saying:
89:16: 16- And if He tests him and restricts his provision If the restriction is as for man, if He tests him with poverty and stinginess to balance his counterpart. He says, 'My Lord has humiliated me' Because of his limited vision and bad poverty, stinginess may lead to honor in both abodes, and expansion may lead to intending enemies and being absorbed in the love of this world. That is why He, the Most High, rebuked him for his saying, and deterred him from it by saying:
89:17: 17- "No although his first statement is in agreement with akramahu and he did not say fa-humiliated him and was able to control him" as he said: "fa-humiliated him and was favoured" because generosity is a favour and failing to do so is not an insult. Ibn Amir and the Kufians read "akramanu and ahanna without a ya" in connection and stopping. Abu Amr said the same and Nafi' agreed with them in stopping and Ibn Amir read "fa-humiliated" with emphasis. "Rather, you do not honour the orphan."
89:18: 18- And do not encourage the feeding of the poor meaning, rather, their actions are worse than their words and more indicative of their wasting of money, which is that they do not honor the orphan with spending and charity, and they do not urge their families to feed the poor, let alone others. The Kufians read and do not encourage.
89:19: 19- And you consume the inheritance inheritance, the root of which is warath. "Eating what" means combining what is permissible and what is forbidden, for they did not give inheritance to women and children and they ate their shares or they ate what the testator had combined of what was permissible and what was forbidden, knowing that.
89:20: 20- And you love money with an intense love a lot with greed and greed. Abu Amr, Sahl, and Yaqub read they do not honor except and they love with the letter ya, and the rest with the letter ta.
89:21: 21- No is a deterrent to them from that and a denial of their action and what comes after it is a threat against them. When the earth is pounded to a pounding meaning pounded after pounding until it becomes low mountains and hills, or scattered dust.
89:22: 22- And your Lord has come meaning the signs of His power and might have appeared, just as is evident when the Sultan is present, with the effects of his majesty and his rule. And the kings, rank upon rank according to their stations and ranks.
89:23: 23- And Hell will be brought forth on that Day as God Almighty says: And Hell will come forth and in the hadith: Hell will be brought forth on that Day with seventy thousand reins, and with each rein seventy thousand angels pulling it. “On that Day” is a substitute for when the earth and the workers in them are leveled. “Man will remember” meaning he will remember his sins or he will be admonished because he knows how ugly they are and regrets them. And how will he remember meaning what benefit will there be in remembering so that what came before it is not diminished. This is used as evidence for the non-obligation of accepting repentance, because this remembrance is an unacceptable repentance.
89:24: 24- He says, Oh, I wish I had put forth for my life meaning for this life of mine, or the time of my life in this world, righteous deeds. This wish does not indicate the independence of the servant in his action, for the one who is prevented from doing something may wish for it if it were possible for him.
89:25: 25- On that Day no one will be punished as He punished him.
89:26: 26- And no one will bind him as he is bound. The ha refers to God, meaning that no one will be responsible for God's punishment and binding on the Day of Resurrection except Him, as the whole matter is His, or for man, meaning that no one among the guards will be punished as they punish him. Al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read them in the passive form.
89:27: 27- O tranquil soul meaning that it is tranquilized by the remembrance of God, for the soul ascends in the chain of causes and effects to the Necessary in and of itself, so it is aroused without knowing Him and is independent of others through Him, or to the truth such that no doubt disturbs it, or to the security that is not aroused by fear or sadness, and both have been recited with it.
89:28: 28- Return to your Lord to His command or His appointment of death. This is indicated by the statement of the one who said: The souls were present before the bodies in the world of holiness or resurrection, satisfied with what they were given, pleasing to God Almighty.
89:29: 29- So enter among My servants among My righteous servants.
89:30: 30- And enter My Paradise with them or in the group of those brought near, so that you may be illuminated by their light, for the sacred jewels are like facing mirrors, or enter the bodies of My servants from which you have departed, and enter the abode of My reward that I have prepared for you. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever recites Surat Al-Fajr during the first ten nights will be forgiven, and whoever recites it during the other days, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection.
90:2: 2- And you are a resident of this city. God Almighty swore by the Sacred City and restricted it to the residence of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in it, to show more of His favor, and to indicate that the honor of the place is in the honor of its people. It was said that a resident means that it is permissible for you to wander around in it, just as it is permissible for hunting to wander around in other places, or it is permissible for you to do whatever you want in it for an hour of the day, so it is a promise of what was made permissible for him in the year of the conquest.
90:3: 3- And the father is in apposition to this country and the father is Adam or Abraham, peace be upon them. And what was born is his offspring or Muhammad, peace be upon him. The indefiniteness is for emphasis and preferring what over whom for the meaning of astonishment as in his saying And God knows best what you have placed.
90:4: 4- Indeed, We created man into hardship. Toil and hardship from the man’s liver, if his liver is in pain, and from it is the struggle, and man is not ceased to be in hardships, the beginning of which is the darkness of the womb and its narrowness and its end is death and what comes after it, and it is a consolation for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, from what he was suffering from the Quraysh, and the pronoun in Does he think refers to some of them who were suffering from more, or slackening like Abu Al-Ashd bin Kalada, for he would spread out a leather skin of Ukaz under his feet and ten would pull it until it broke and his feet would not move, or for each one of them or for the human being.
90:5: 5- No one will be able to do anything to him. So he will take revenge on him.
90:6: 6- He says meaning at that time. I spent a lot of money, from the word talabad which means to gather something, and what is meant is what he spent for fame and boasting, or enmity towards the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
90:7: 7- Does he think that no one sees him when he was spending or after that and asks him about it, meaning that God Almighty sees him and rewards him, or finds him and holds him accountable for it. Then He explained that by saying:
90:8: 8- Did We not give him two eyes with which he could see?
90:9: 9- And a tongue with which he translates his conscience. And two lips with which he covers his mouth and uses them to help him speak, eat, drink, and other things.
90:10: 10- And We showed him the two ways the path of good and evil, or the two breasts, and its origin is a high place.
90:11: 11- So he did not storm the obstacle meaning he did not thank those hands by storming the obstacle, which is entering into a difficult matter, and the obstacle is the path in the mountain. He borrowed it as the Almighty interpreted it with regard to release and feeding in His saying:
90:12: 12- And what can make you know what the obstacle is?
90:14: 14- Or feeding on a day of famine.
90:16: 16- Or a poor person covered with dust because of the struggle of the soul in them and the multiplicity of what is intended by them, the good occurrence, not the location of lam, as it is almost never repeated, since the meaning is: neither freeing a slave nor feeding an orphan or a poor person. And famine, proximity, and dust are Mafa'ilat from saghb if he is hungry and close in lineage and taraba if he is poor, and Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read the freeing of a slave as a substitution of iqtama and the saying of God the Almighty: And what will make you know what the difficult obstacle is is an objection meaning that you do not know its difficulty and reward.
90:17: 17- Then he was among those who believed is in apposition to stormed, or released with then because faith is far removed from emancipation and feeding in rank due to its independence and the condition of all other acts of obedience to it. And they enjoin one another and they enjoined one another to patience in obeying God Almighty. And they enjoin one another to mercy with mercy upon His servants, or with the requirements of God Almighty’s mercy.
90:18: 18- Those are the companions of the right hand the right or the right.
90:19: 19- And those who disbelieve in Our signs in what We have established as evidence of the truth from the Book and the argument or the Qur’an. They are the companions of the left the left or the bad luck. The repetition of mentioning the believers with the demonstrative pronoun and the disbelievers with the pronoun is a matter that is not hidden.
90:20: 20- A closed fire will be upon them from the root word awsadat al-bab, meaning to close and lock the door. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Hafs read it with the hamza from aasidatuhu. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites ‘I swear by this city’, God Almighty will grant him safety from His wrath on the Day of Resurrection.
91:1: 1- "And the sun and its brightness" its brightness when it rises, and it was said that the morning is the height of the day and the morning is above that, and the morning with the opening and extension when the day is extended and almost midday.
91:2: 2- And the moon when it follows it Its rising follows the rising of the sun at the beginning of the month or its setting on the night of the full moon, or in the fullness and perfection of light.
91:3: 3- And the day when it reveals it It reveals the sun, for it is revealed when the day spreads out or darkness falls, or the world or the earth, even if it is not mentioned because it is known.
91:4: 4- And the night when it covers it covers the sun, covering its light, or the horizons, or the earth. Since the conjunctions of conjunction are for the first conjunction of the oath, the prepositional conjunction itself, which replaces the verb of the oath, since it necessitates its being dropped with it, the nouns and adverbials are connected to the noun and adverbial that came before, connecting the conjunction of the conjunction to what comes after it in your saying: Zaid struck Amr and Bakr struck Khalid, on the subject and the object, without connecting it to two different operators.
91:5: 5- And the heaven and He who built it and He who built it and it was preferred over whom to mean the descriptive meaning as if it was said: And the able thing that built it and its construction indicated its existence and the perfection of its power, and for this reason it was mentioned alone and so is the speech in his saying:
92:6: 6- And the earth and what He spread out. 6- And believed in the best is a clear explanation of the dispersion of efforts. The meaning is whoever gives obedience and avoids disobedience and believes in the best word, which is what indicates the truth, such as the word of monotheism.
92:7: 7-And the soul and He who proportioned it and making the waters a source removes the verb from the subject and disrupts the system of his saying: 7- Then We will ease him toward ease. We will prepare him for the companionship that leads to ease and comfort, like entering Paradise. He who eases the horse when he prepares it for riding with a saddle and bridle.
92:8: 8- And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness by His saying: And He proportioned it unless the name of God is implied in it for knowledge of it and the indefiniteness of soul is for multiplication as in the saying of the Most High: A soul knew or for glorification and what is meant is the soul of Adam and the inspiration of wickedness and righteousness is understanding them and defining their state or enabling them to be done. 8- But as for he who is miserly with what he was commanded and considers himself independent of the pleasures of this world over the bliss of the Hereafter.
92:9: 9- He has succeeded who purifies it He has developed it through knowledge and action. This is the answer to the oath. The lam was deleted for length, as if when he wanted to urge people to perfect the soul and exaggerate it, he swore by it what would show them knowledge of the existence of the Creator, the necessity of His Essence and the perfection of His attributes, which is the highest degree of theoretical power. He reminds them of His great favors to make them immerse themselves in thanking Him for His blessings, which is the ultimate perfection of practical power. It was said that it is a digression by mentioning some of the states of the soul, and the answer is omitted, its meaning is that God may destroy the disbelievers for denying His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as He destroyed Thamud for denying Salih, may God bless him and grant him peace. 9- And he denied the best and denied its meaning.
92:10: 10- And he who concealed it has failed. He diminished it and hid it through ignorance and immorality. The root of dasa is dasas, like taqda and taqaddad. 10- We will ease him toward difficulty for the trait that leads to difficulty and hardship, such as entering the Fire.
92:11: 11- Thamud denied the truth due to their transgression because of their transgression, or because of the punishment they promised to the transgressor, as God Almighty said: So they were destroyed by the transgressor, and its original form is their transgression, but its ya was changed to a waw to differentiate between the noun and the adjective, and it was read with a dammah like al-raj'i. 11- And his wealth will not avail him Negation or interrogative denial. If he falls Perishes, it is done from the ruin, or falls into the pit of the grave or the bottom of Hell.
92:12: 12- When he arose when he stood up is an adverb for lied or transgressed. Their most wretched is the most wretched of Thamud, who is Qadar bin Salif, or he is the one who supported him in killing the she-camel, because if you add the comparative, it is suitable for the singular and the plural, and their wretchedness is preferred for their taking charge of hamstringing. Introduction by the director of the al-Maehad al-Sadiqin (the Al-Sadiqin Institute). In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful. Our research at Al Sadiqin necessitated a translation of the tafsir (commentaries) on the Holy Qur'an that allowed easy searching, comparison between similar ahadith and immediate reference to the original Arabic text for those not fluent in Arabic. Al Sadiqin contributes to fulfilling this need by providing this publication. The online form of this book makes for easy “copy and paste” of ahadith for use in research papers. In the printed form, it allows the reader who may not be fluent in Arabic to find references to the original Arabic text. The Tafsir Al-Qur’an: A Complete English Translation of Classical Qur’anic Commentaries Volume 34 presents a simple, but complete English translation of the major classical commentaries on the Qur’an, covering the last verses of Sūrat l-Shams, and the last chapter of the Qur'an, Sūrat l-Nās. These tafsir works are foundational to Islamic scholarship, each offering a distinct methodology and historical perspective: • Tafsir al-Tabari (923 CE) – One of the earliest and most comprehensive tafsirs, authored by Imam al-Tabari. It is based on tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (interpretation through transmitted reports) and includes extensive narrations from the Prophet (pbuh), the Sahabah, and early scholars. • Tafsir al-Baghawi (1122 CE) – Written by Imam al-Baghawi, this tafsir is known for its conciseness and reliance on authentic hadith and narrations. It is widely used in Sunni circles as a balanced and straightforward commentary. • Tafsir al-Qurtubi (1273 CE) – Authored by Imam al-Qurtubi, this tafsir is famous for its focus on fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and legal interpretations, making it essential for scholars studying Qur’anic law. • Tafsir al-Baidawi (1286 CE) – A concise and refined commentary by Imam al-Baidawi, often studied in traditional madrasahs. It is particularly valuable for its linguistic analysis and summarization of earlier tafsirs like al-Zamakhshari’s. • Tafsir Ibn Kathir (1372 CE) – One of the most widely read tafsirs today, written by Ibn Kathir, emphasizing tafsir bi’l-ma’thur and the use of hadith and narrations from the Sahabah. • Tafsir al-Jalalayn (1505 CE) – A brief yet highly regarded tafsir written by Jalal al-Din al-Mahalli and completed by Jalal al-Din al-Suyuti. It is a widely studied introductory tafsir, particularly in traditional Islamic education. • Tafsir al-Suyuti (1505 CE) – Compiled by Imam al-Suyuti, this tafsir is a rich source of tafsir bi’l-ma’thur (narrative-based exegesis), incorporating extensive hadith and historical reports. • Fath al-Qadir (1834 CE) – Written by Imam al-Shawkani, this tafsir combines tafsir bi’l-ma’thur with rational analysis and legal insights, making it a comprehensive and independent work. This book serves as an essential resource for students, researchers, and general readers seeking a comprehensive understanding of the Qur’an through classical scholarship. As part of a 34-volume complete translation, this work aims to make these monumental Islamic commentaries accessible to English readers for the first time. 114:6: 13- "Then the Messenger of God said to them: 'The she-camel of God' - that is, leave the she-camel of God and beware of hamstringing her - and her watering place - and her watering place, so do not drive her away from it. Surat Ash-Shams: 14 But they denied him and hamstrung her. So their Lord destroyed them for their sin and leveled them. 14- "But they denied him" in what he warned them of the punishment that would befall them if they did so. "So they hamstrung her, so their Lord destroyed them so the punishment was brought down upon them, which is from their repeated use of the term a fatted she-camel" when He covered it with fat. "For their sin" because of it. "So He leveled it" so He leveled the tumbling among them or upon them, so that none of them, young or old, escaped, nor did Thamud escape by destruction. Surat Ash-Shams: 15 and he does not fear its consequences. 15- "And he does not fear its consequences" meaning the consequence of the rumbling or the consequence of the destruction of Thamud and its consequences, so some of the preservation remains, and the waw is for the state, and Nafi` and Ibn `Amir read not as a conjunction. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever recites Surat Ash-Shams, it is as if he has given in charity everything that the sun and moon rise upon. 6- From the jinn and mankind is an explanation of the whisperer, or the one who or related to whispers, meaning he whispers in their hearts from the side of the jinn and mankind. It was said that it is an explanation of the people on the basis that what is meant by it is what includes both humankind, and this is arbitrary unless what is meant by it is the forgetful one, as in the saying of God the Almighty: The Day the Supplicant will call, for forgetting the right of God the Almighty includes both humankind. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites the two Mu’awwidhat, it is as if he has recited the books that God Almighty revealed.
92:1: 1- And the night when it covers meaning it covers the sun or the day or everything that it conceals with its darkness.
92:2: 2- And the day when it appears It appears when the darkness of the night disappears, or becomes clear when the sun rises.
92:3: 3- "And He created the male and the female and the Able One who created the two types of male and female from every kind that has reproduction, or Adam and Eve and it was said that what" is a source.
92:4: 4- Your efforts are diverse. Your efforts are diverse.
92:5: 5- But as for he who gives and fears God.
92:13: 13- And indeed, to Us belongs the Hereafter and the first life. So We give in both abodes whatever We will to whom We will, or the reward of guidance to those who are guided, or your abandonment of guidance does not harm Us.
92:14: 14- So I have warned you of a blazing Fire.
92:15: 15- He shall not be punished for it means he shall not be bound by it because of its severity. Except the most wretched except the disbeliever, for even if the immoral person enters it, he shall not be bound by it. That is why He called him the most wretched and described him by saying:
92:16: 16- He who denied and turned away meaning he denied the truth and turned away from obedience.
92:18: 18- He who avoids polytheism and sins, then he will not enter into them, let alone enter into them and pray them. The meaning of that is that whoever avoids polytheism without sinning does not avoid them and is not required to pray them, so it does not contradict the previous restriction. He gives his wealth he spends it on charitable causes, because his saying is purified is a substitute for he gives or a state of its subject.
92:19: 19- And no one has a favor with Him for which he can be rewarded. By giving Him, He means that He will reward him for it.
92:20: 20- Except seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High is an exception, whether disconnected or connected, from something omitted, such as He is not given except seeking the face of his Lord, not as a reward for a blessing.
92:21: 21- And he will be satisfied. He promised the reward that will please him. The verses were revealed about Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, when he bought Bilal among a group of people who had been taken over by the polytheists, and he freed them. Therefore, it was said that the one meant by the most wretched is Abu Jahl or Umayyah ibn Khalaf. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever recites Surat Al-Layl, God Almighty will give him until he is satisfied, and He will spare him from hardship and make things easy for him.
93:1: 1- And the forenoon and the time of sunrise and its specification because the day is strong in it, or because in it Moses, peace be upon him, spoke to his Lord and the magicians fell down in prostration, or the day and this is supported by the Almighty's saying: That Our punishment may come to them in the forenoon in contrast to at night.
93:2: 2- And the night when it covers its inhabitants become still or its darkness subsides from the sea covering itself when its waves become still. The presentation of the night in the previous surah is based on the origin, and the presentation of the day here is based on honor.
93:3: 3- Your Lord has not forsaken you He has not severed you as one who bids farewell cuts off. It is read with a light pronunciation meaning He has not abandoned you and it is the answer to the oath. And He did not hate you He did not detest you. The object was omitted as it was mentioned before and in consideration of the pauses. It was narrated that the revelation was delayed for days because he left out the exception as mentioned in Surat Al-Kahf, or because he was warned by a persistent beggar, or because a dead puppy was under his bed or something else, so the polytheists said: Muhammad has been forsaken and hated by his Lord, so it was revealed in response to them.
93:4: 4- And the Hereafter is better for you than the first. For it is everlasting and pure from impurities, and this is fleeting and tainted with harm. It is as if, when He, Glory be to Him, the Most High, made clear that He continues to provide him with revelation and honor in this world, He promised him what is higher and more sublime than that in the Hereafter, or that the end of your affair is better than its beginning, for he, may God bless him and grant him peace, continues to ascend in elevation and perfection.
93:5: 5- "And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied." A comprehensive promise for what He has given of the perfection of the soul, the manifestation of the matter, and the elevation of religion, and for what He has stored for him of what is known in its essence, and the lam is for the beginning, the predicate entered after the subject was deleted, and the meaning is: And your Lord will give you, not for the oath, as it does not enter into the present tense except with the emphatic nun, and its combination with sawaf is to indicate that the giving will inevitably happen even if it is delayed due to its ruling.
93:6: 6- Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? An enumeration of the blessings He bestowed upon him, indicating that just as He was good to him in the past, He will be good to him in the future, even if it is delayed. He finds you is from existence, meaning knowledge, and orphan is the second particle or befriending, and orphan is a state.
93:7: 7- And He found you lost with knowledge of wisdom and rulings. So He guided so He taught you through revelation, inspiration, and success in contemplation. It was said that He found you lost on the road when Abu Talib took you to Syria or when Halima weaned you and came to return you to your grandfather, so He removed your misguidance from your uncle or grandfather.
93:8: 8- And He found you poor poor with children. And He made you rich with the profits you gained from trade.
93:9: 9- As for the orphan, do not oppress him. Do not force him to take his money because of his weakness. It was also read as do not oppress him, meaning do not frown at him.
93:10: 10- And do not repel the beggar. Do not rebuke him.
93:11: 11- And speak of the favor of your Lord. Speaking of it means thanking Him for it. It was said that what is meant by the favor of prophecy is speaking of it and conveying it. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “Whoever recites Surat Ad-Duha, God Almighty will place him among those for whom Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is pleased to intercede, and he will receive ten good deeds, which God Almighty will write down for the number of orphans and needy people.”
94:1: 1-Have We not expanded your breast for you? Have We not expanded it so that it can commune with the Truth and call upon creation, so that it was absent and present? Or, Have We not expanded it with what We have deposited in it of wisdom and removed from it the narrowness of ignorance? Or with what We have made easy for you to receive the revelation after it had been difficult for you? And it was said that it is a reference to what was narrated, "Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, in his youth or on the day of the covenant, and took out his heart, washed it, then filled it with faith and knowledge." Perhaps it is a reference to something similar to what came before, and the meaning of the question is to deny the negation of expansion, exaggerating in affirming it, and that is why it was conjoined with it.
94:2: 2- And We removed from you your burden your heavy burden.
94:3: 3- He who broke your back means the one who carried it, on the contrary, which is the sound of the saddle when it breaks from the weight of the load, which is what weighed down on him from his excesses before the mission, or his ignorance of the ruling and the provisions, or his confusion, or receiving the revelation, or what he saw of the misguidance of his people from his inability to guide them, or from their insistence and their devotion to harming him when he called them to faith.
94:4: 4- And We have raised your remembrance through prophethood and other things. Any raising is like linking his name with His name, the Most High, in the two testimonies of faith, making obedience to him obedience to Him, praying for him with His angels, commanding the believers to pray for him, and addressing him with titles. But for you was added to be vague before clarification, thus indicating exaggeration.
94:5: 5 For indeed, with hardship such as constriction of the chest, burdensome loss, people going astray and being harmed by them. There is ease such as explanation, placement, and success in guidance and obedience. So do not despair of the spirit of God if something that distresses you befalls you. The indefiniteness is for glorification, and the meaning in for with is the exaggeration of the accompaniment of ease to hardship, and its connection to it is the connection of those who are close.
94:6: 6- Verily, with hardship comes ease is a repetition for emphasis or to resume His promise that hardship is followed by another ease such as the reward in the hereafter, as in your saying: Verily, for the fasting person there is joy. "Verily, for the fasting person there is joy," meaning joy when breaking the fast and joy when meeting the Lord. And based on this, his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, "Hardship will not overcome two eases." Hardship is definite and therefore not multiple, whether it is for a covenant or a type, and ease is indefinite, so it is possible that the second is intended to mean an individual that differs from what was intended by the first.
94:7: 7-And when you have finished conveying the message, then devote yourself to worship in gratitude for the blessings We have enumerated for you in the past and the blessings We have promised you in the future. And it was said that when you have finished the conquest, devote yourself to worship, or when you have finished the prayer, devote yourself to supplication.
94:8: 8- And to your Lord turn with questions and do not ask anyone other than Him, for He alone is able to help you. It was read so turn meaning that people turn to seeking His reward. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever recites Surat Alam Nashrah, it is as if he came to me when I was distressed and relieved me.
95:1: 1- The fig and the olive He singled them out from the fruits by section because the fig is a delicious fruit with no season and a pleasant food that is easily digested, and a very beneficial medicine as it softens the temperament, dissolves phlegm, cleanses the kidneys, removes sand from the bladder, opens blockages in the liver and spleen, and fattens the body. In the hadith, It cuts off hemorrhoids and is beneficial for gout. The olive is a fruit, a condiment, and a medicine and it has a pleasant oil that is very beneficial, although it may grow where there is no oil in it like mountains. It was said that what is meant by them are two mountains of the Holy Land or the mosques of Damascus and Jerusalem, or countries.
95:2: 2- Mount Sinai means the mountain on which Moses, peace be upon him, spoke to his Lord. Sinin and Sinai are two names for the place where it is.
95:3: 3- This is the safe city meaning the safe city from the security of a man, so he is trustworthy, or the one who is safe in it is safe in it for whoever enters it, and what is meant by it is Mecca.
95:4: 4- Indeed, We created man meaning by it the species in the best stature is an amendment by specifying upright stature, a beautiful appearance, and the collection of the characteristics of beings and the likes of all other possibilities.
95:5: 5- Then We returned him to the lowest of the low by making him one of the people of the Fire or to the lowest of the low, which is the Fire. It was said that it is the most decrepit age, so his saying:
95:6: 6- "Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds" is an interrupted exception. "For them is a reward uninterrupted" is not interrupted at first, and it is a ruling based on the exception and established for it.
95:7: 7- So what would make you lie? That is, what would make you lie, O Muhammad, in terms of evidence or speech? After the Recompense with the reward after the appearance of these proofs. It was said that what means who. It was said that the address is to humanity, with a shift in attention. The meaning is, what drives you to this book?
95:8: 8- Is not God the most just of judges? This is a confirmation of what came before, and the meaning is, is not the one who did that of creation and return the most just of judges in making and planning? And whoever is like that is able to restore and reward, as has been mentioned repeatedly. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Whoever recites Surat At-Tin, God will give him well-being and certainty as long as he lives. When he dies, God will give him a reward equal to the number of people who recited this surah.”
96:1: 1- Read in the name of your Lord meaning read the Qur'an beginning with His name, glory be to Him, or seeking His help. Who created meaning the One to whom creation belongs or the One who created everything. Then He singled out what is more noble and more evident in its making and management and more indicative of the obligation of the worship intended by reading, saying:
96:2: 2- He created man or He who created man was vague at first then explained to glorify his creation and indicate the wonder of his nature. From the one who connected He pluralized it to man in the sense of plural. And since the first duty is to know God Almighty, He first revealed what indicates His existence, His great power and the perfection of His wisdom.
96:3: 3- Read is a repetition for exaggeration, or the first is absolute and the second is for conveying or in prayer. Perhaps when he was told: Read in the name of your Lord, he said: I am not a reader. So he was told: "Read: And your Lord is the Most Generous," the one who is more generous than every generous person, for He, glory be to Him, the Most High, bestows blessings without compensation and is patient without fear. Rather, He alone is truly generous.
96:4: 4- Who taught by the pen meaning writing with a pen. It was read with it to restrict knowledge and teach the distant with it.
96:5: 5- He taught man that which he did not know by creating powers, establishing proofs, and sending down verses. He teaches you to read even if you are not a reader. The Almighty has enumerated the beginning and end of man's affair, demonstrating what He has bestowed upon him, that He has moved him from the lowest of ranks to the highest, confirming His Lordship and realizing His honor. He first pointed to what indicates his knowledge by reason, then He alerted to what indicates it by hearing.
96:6: 6- No is a deterrent to those who disbelieve in God's blessings through their transgression, even though it is not mentioned because the words indicate this. Indeed, man transgresses.
96:7: 7- If he saw him, he would be independent If he saw himself, and independent is its second object because it means he knew, and therefore it is permissible for its subject and object to be two pronouns for one person.
96:8: 8- Indeed, to your Lord is the return. The address is to the human being to pay attention, as a threat and warning against the consequences of tyranny. Return is a source like good report.
96:9: 9-Have you seen the one who forbids?
96:10: 10- A slave when he prays was revealed about Abu Jahl who said, If I saw Muhammad prostrating, I would step on his neck. So he came to him and turned back on his heels. So he was asked, What is the matter with you? He said, Between me and him is a trench of fire, terror, and wings. So it was revealed, and the word slave and its indefiniteness are to emphasize the ugliness of the prohibition and to indicate the complete servitude of the one prohibited.
96:11: 11- Have you seen if he is on the right path?
96:12: 12- Or he commanded piety. Have you seen the repetition of the first and the same in his saying:
96:13: 13- Have you seen if he lies and turns away?
96:14: 14- Does he not know that God sees? The conditional is its second object, and the answer to the condition is omitted, indicated by the answer to the second condition, which is in the position of its divisor. The meaning is, tell me about someone who forbade some of God's servants from praying, if the one who forbade was guided in what he forbade, or commanding piety in what he commanded of worshipping idols, as he believes, or if he was denying the truth and turning away from what is right, as you say, Does he not know that God sees and is aware of his conditions, whether he is guided or misguided. It was said that the meaning is, Have you seen the one who forbids * a servant from praying, and the one who is forbidden is guided, commanding piety, and the one who forbade is a denier and turned away. What is more amazing than that? It was said that the address in the second verse is to the disbeliever, for He, glory be to Him, is like a judge who has two opponents present, addressing this one once and the other another time, as if he said, O disbeliever, tell me if his prayer is guidance and his supplication to God, glory be to Him, is an order to piety, should I forbid him? Perhaps He mentioned the order to piety, so He limited himself to mentioning the prayer as an invitation to action, or because the prohibition of the servant if he prays could possibly be for it or for something else, and its general conditions are confined to completing himself with worship and others with supplication.
96:15: 15- No! is a deterrent to the one who forbids. If he does not desist from what he is doing. We will surely seize him by the forelock. We will seize him by the forelock and drag him by it to the Fire. Seizing means grasping and pulling something forcefully. It was read lansafan'a with a doubled nun and lasfa'an and it is written in the Qur'an with an alif according to the rule of stopping and sufficing with the lam instead of the addition because it is known that what is meant is the forelock of the aforementioned.
96:16: 16- A lying, sinful forelock instead of the forelock, but it is permissible to describe it, and it was read in the nominative case as it is a forelock and in the accusative case as a censure and description of it as a lie and a mistake, and they are for its owner on the metaphorical attribution of exaggeration.
96:17: 17- So let him call his group meaning the people of his group to help him, which is the council in which the people meet. It was narrated that Abu Jahl, may God curse him, passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying and said: Did I not forbid you? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was harsh with him, and he said: Are you threatening me when I am the most prominent group of people in the valley? So this was revealed.
96:18: 18- "We will call the guards" to drag him to the fire. It is originally a condition, and its singular is zayna like afariya from zaban, which means pushing, or zayni according to the lineage, and its root is zabani, and the taa is a substitute for the yaa.
96:19: 19- No is also a deterrent to the one who forbids. Do not obey him means remain steadfast in your obedience. And prostrate means continue in your prostration. And draw near means draw near to your Lord. In the hadith, The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he prostrates. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Alaq will be given a reward as if he had recited the entire Mufassal.
97:1: 1- Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. The pronoun refers to the Qur’an, which is emphasized by the implication of from without mentioning it, as evidence of its greatness, which does not require mentioning it explicitly. He also glorified it by attributing its revelation to it, and he glorified the time in which it was revealed by saying:
97:2: 2- And what can make you know what the Night of Decree is?
97:3: 3- "The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months" and its being sent down in it means that it was sent down in it, or it was sent down all at once from the Tablet to the lowest heaven to the Scrolls, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, would send it down to the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, in stages over twenty-three years. It was also said that the meaning of "We sent it down" is in its virtue, and it is in the odd-numbered nights of the last ten nights of Ramadan, and perhaps it is the seventh of them. The reason for concealing it is that whoever wants it stays up for many nights, and it is called that for its honor or to determine matters in it, as God, the Most High, said: "In it is decreed every matter of wisdom" and the mention of the thousand is either for emphasis, or because it was narrated that he, peace be upon him, "mentioned an Israelite who would wear arms in the way of God for a thousand months, so the believers were amazed and their deeds fell short to them, so they were given the Night of Decree, which is better than the duration of that warrior."
97:4: 4- The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord. This is an explanation of why it is separated over a thousand months and brings them down to the earth, or to the lowest heaven, or brings them close to the believers. For every matter is for every decree in that year. It was read for every person, meaning for every human being.
97:5: 5- "Peace is" It is nothing but safety, meaning that God decrees nothing but safety in it, and decrees safety and affliction in other than it, or it is nothing but safety due to the frequency with which they greet the believers. Until the break of dawn meaning the time of its break, that is, its rising. Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra as if it is like a reference or a time name not according to analogy like the east. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Qadr will be given a reward as if he fasted Ramadan and stayed up during the Night of Decree.
98:1: 1- Those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture the Jews and Christians, for they disbelieved by blaspheming the attributes of God, the Most High, and from is for clarification. and the polytheists and idol worshippers will not be separated from their religion, or the promise to follow the truth when the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, came to them. until there came to them clear evidence the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, or the Qur’an, for it explains the truth, or the miracle of the Messenger with his morals, and the Qur’an with its silencing of those who challenged him with it.
98:2: 2- A Messenger from God instead of proof itself or by estimating an added word or a subject. Recites purified pages is its description or predicate, and the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, even though he was illiterate, but when he recited what was in the pages, he was following them. And it was said that what was meant was Gabriel, peace and blessings be upon him, and the pages being purified means that falsehood does not come to what is in them, or that none touch them except the purified.
98:3: 3- It contains valuable books upright writings that speak the truth.
98:4: 4- “And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided from what they were upon, whether some of them believed or hesitated about their religion, or from their promise by persisting in disbelief. “except after there came to them clear proof.” So it is like His saying: And before, they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved, but when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it. And singling out the People of the Scripture after grouping them together with the polytheists is to indicate the hideousness of their state, and that when they became divided despite their knowledge, others were more deserving of that.
98:5: 5- And they were not commanded that is, in their books, including what is in them, except to worship God, devoting religion to Him alone not associating anything with Him. Hanun turning away from deviant beliefs. And to establish prayer and give zakat but they distorted and disobeyed. And that is the right religion the right religion.
98:6: 6- Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. That is, on the Day of Resurrection, or in the present situation, due to their involvement in what necessitates that. The fact that both groups share the same type of punishment does not necessitate that they share the same type, so perhaps it will differ due to the difference in their disbelief. Those are the worst of creation. That is, of creation. Nafi' read al-Bari'ah with a hamza, according to the original.
98:7: 7- Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the best of creation.
98:8: 8- "Their reward is with their Lord: Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever." This contains exaggerations in presenting praise and mentioning the reward, indicating that what they were granted is in contrast to what they were described with and the ruling on it being from their Lord. The plural of gardens is a resumption of what they will have in addition to their reward. They were described from it because it made them attain their utmost desires. That meaning the mentioned reward and pleasure, is for him who fears his Lord, for fear is the essence of the matter and the motive for all good. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Kafiru will be with the best of creation on the Day of Resurrection, in the evening and at rest.
99:1: 1- When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake is the disturbance that is destined for it at the first blast, or the second, or what is possible for it, or what is appropriate for it in wisdom. It is read with the fat-ha, and it is the name of the movement, and it is not in the structures fa`lal except in the doubled form.
99:2: 2- And the earth brought forth its burdens what was in its interior of buried treasures or the dead, the plural of thaqal is the household furnishings.
99:3: 3- And man said, 'What is wrong with her?' because of the terrible matter that astonished them. It was said that what is meant by man is the disbeliever, because the believer knows what is wrong with her.
99:4: 4- On that Day it will speak It will speak to the creation with the tongue of the state. Its report is what caused its earthquake and its emergence. It was said that God Almighty will make it speak, so it will inform of what He did with it, and On that Day is a substitute for if and its subject is spoken, or it is the origin and if is subject with an implied word.
99:5: 5- That your Lord inspired her meaning that it happened because your Lord inspired her by creating in her what indicated the report, or made her speak it. It is possible that it is a substitute for informing her, as it is said: I told him such and such, and the lam means to or according to its origin, as she has in that relief from the disobedient.
99:6: 6- On that Day people will proceed from their exits from the graves to the gathering place. in separate groups according to their ranks to see their deeds the reward for their deeds. It was read with the opening of the ya’.
99:8: 8- And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. A detailed explanation of that they may see. That is why yarrahu was read with a damma, and Hisham read it with a sukoon on the ha’. Perhaps the good deeds of the disbeliever and the bad deeds of the one who avoids major sins affect the reduction of reward and punishment. It was said that the verse is conditional on not being frustrated or forgiven, or from the first it is specific to the happy and the second to the wretched, because of His saying in scattered parts, and the atom is the small ant or dust. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Whoever recites Surat Al-Zalzala Al-Ard four times, it is as if he has recited the entire Qur’an.
100:1: 1- And the charging steeds panting. God Almighty swears by the horses of the invaders that gallop and pant, which is the sound of their breathing at the enemy. He made it accusative with its deleted verb, or by the charging steeds, as it indicates by implication the panting ones, or panting is a state meaning panting.
100:2: 2- Those who kindle sparks means those who kindle fire, and expiation is the removal of fire. It is said that the flint was struck and ignited.
100:3: 3- Al-Mughirat Its people attack the enemy. In the morning meaning at the right time.
100:4: 4- They stirred up so they became agitated. With it at that time. Dust or shouting.
100:5: 5- And he was surrounded by it so they were surrounded by that time or by the enemy, or by the dust, meaning they were entangled in it. A group from the groups of enemies. It was narrated: "That he, peace and blessings be upon him, sent out cavalry and months passed without any report from them, so it was revealed." It is possible that the oath by ordinary souls has an effect as they have those who illuminate with their thoughts the lights of knowledge, and those who attack according to desire and aggression when something like the lights of holiness appears to them, they were affected by it with longing, and he was surrounded by it by a group from the group of the Most High.
100:6: 6- Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord. Ungrateful comes from kanada ingrate, or disobedient in the language of Kinda, or miserly in the language of Bani Malik, and it is the answer to the oath.
100:7: 7- And indeed, he is a witness to that and indeed, man is a witness to his ingratitude. He bears witness against himself because of the effect of it appearing on him, or that God Almighty is a witness to his ingratitude, so it is a threat.
